encodingDesc.p: Each of the 36491 entries keeps its Perseus id as its xml:id (an entry the print has and Perseus lost is added with the id of the entry it follows plus ".1"); n is the homograph number where Perseus gives one, and bn:strong the Strong's Greek numbers whose headword is the same word. The note of type forms is the headword line (endings, article, principal parts); etym is the etymology (Perseus writes Liddell and Scott's "Hence" at the end of an entry as "from ..." on the next), and each sense a numbered sense, with its level in bn:level. gloss is a translation, usg an author or usage label (bn:title gives the author an "Id." refers to), and foreign a Greek, Latin or English word. A ref of type entry links to one entry; a ref of type lemma links to every entry with the headword in bn:lemma. Greek is converted from Perseus's Beta Code to Unicode (NFC).

A headword beginning with * is one Liddell and Scott print with an asterisk, a form not found in use, such as their roots (11 entries; Perseus writes the asterisk after the word). It is looked up without the asterisk.
English words Perseus left in the bare text of its Greek headword-line notes (such as "fut." and "or") are kept as English.

Left out: Perseus's machine-made stem analysis (1008 groups), the notes its linking tool left ("#skipped" and a word, 24), the alphabet headings, and 147 breves or macrons that no vowel can carry where they stand.

entry.sense: ἀάᾱτος: in Il. with penult. long, not to be injured, inviolable, νῦν μοι ὄμοσσον ἀάᾱτον Στυγὸς ὕδωρ, because the gods swore their most binding oaths thereby.
ἀάατος: in Od. with penult. short, hurtful, perilous, aweful; ἄεθλος ἀάατος.
unbroken, not to be broken, hard, strong, Od., Theocr.
not to be touched, resistless, invincible, χεῖρες ἄαπτοι Hom., Hes.
insatiate, c. gen., Ἄρης ἆτος πολέμοιο Il.

entry.etym: The quantities vary: ᾱασεν, ᾱᾱσαν, part. ἀασας: ᾱ̓ασάμην, ᾱ̓ᾱσατο: ᾱ̓ασθην, ἀασθη.
entry.sense: properly to hurt, damage; then to mislead, infatuate, of the effects of wine, sleep, divine judgments, Od.; so in Mid., Ἄτη ἣ πάντας ἀᾶται Il.
aor1 mid. and pass., to act recklessly or foolishly, ἀασάμην I was infatuated Il.; μέγ’ ἀάσθη Id.

entry.etym: epic Verb only used in aor1.
entry.sense: to be speechless, epic Verb only used in aor1, οἱ δ’ ἀβάκησαν πάντες Od.
speechless, infantine, Sapph..
uninitiated in the Bacchic orgies, generally, joyless, Eur.
properly ἆ βάλε, expressing a wish, O that! Lat. utinam, c. inf., Anth.
without weight: not burdensome, of persons, NTest.
not examined by torture, untortured; of things, unexamined, Plut.; adv. -τως, without examination, Thuc.
not ruled by a king, Thuc., Xen.
not subject to enchantment; adv. -τως, Anth.
not to be carried, Plut.
untrodden, impassable, inaccessible, of mountains, Hdt., Soph., etc.; of a river, not fordable, Xen.
of holy places, not to be trodden, like ἄθικτος, Soph.: metaph. pure, chaste, ψυχή Plat.
of horses, not ridden, Luc.
act., ἄβ. πόνος a plague that hinders walking, i.e. gout, Luc.
Hebr. word, father, NTest.
a man of Abdera in Thrace, proverb. of simpletons. Dem.
like an Abderite, i.e. stupid, Luc.
uncertain, unsteady; τὸ ἀβέβαιον = ἀβεβαιότης, Luc.
of persons, unstable, Dem., etc.
not profane, inviolable, Plut.
silliness, stupidity, fatuity, Plat.
good for nothing, silly, stupid, fatuous, Ar., etc.;—Sup. -ώτατος, Id.
unforced, without violence, Plat.
= ἀβίωτος, Anth.
without a living, starving, Luc.
of the Ἱππημολγοί, simple in life, Il.
not to be lived, insupportable, ἀβ. πεποίηκε τὸν βίον Ar.; ἀβίωτον χρόνον βιοτεῦσαι Eur.; ἀβίωτόν [ἐστι] life is intolerable, Eur., Plat.; adv., ἀβιώτως ἔχειν to find life intolerable, Plut.
freedom from harm, Plut.
act. harmlessness, Lat. innocentia, Cic.
without harm, i.e.,
pass. unharmed, unhurt, secure, Aesch., etc.
act. not harming, harmless, innocent, Aesch., Plat.
averting or preventing harm, Theocr.
adv. in attic formularies, ἀβλαβῶς σπονδαῖς ἐμμένειν without doing harm, Thuc.; so the σπονδαί themselves are entitled ἄδολοι καὶ ἀβλαβεῖς, Id.
without eye-lids, Anth.
not thrown or shot, ἰὸν ἀβλῆτα an arrow not yet used, Il.
not hit by darts, Il.
without bleatings, Anth.
weak, feeble, Il.; ἀβλ. θάνατος an easy death in ripe old age, opp. to a violent one, Od.
of sheep, Babr.
helpless, Plut.
without summons, Pind.
not loudly lamented, Anth.
ungrazed, ὄρη Babr.
untended by herdsmen: metaph. unheeded, Aesch.

entry.etym: ἀβουλέω is an exception to the rule that α privat. cannot be comp. directly with Verbs.
entry.sense: to be unwilling, Plat.
want of counsel, thoughtlessness, Hdt., Soph., etc.
inconsiderate, ill-advised, Soph., etc.; τέκνοισι ἄβουλος taking no thought for them, Id.: comp. -ότερος, Thuc.; adv. -ως, inconsiderately, Hdt.; Sup. ἀβουλότατα, Id.
without oxen, i.e. poor, Hes.
of no weight, Eur.
softly or delicately stepping, Aesch.
living delicately, effeminate, Plut.
wailing womanishly, Aesch.
living delicately, Aesch.; τὸ ἁβροδίαιτον effeminacy, Thuc.
with delicate or luxuriant leaves, φοῖνιξ Eur., Anacreont.
without Bacchus, Anth.
noiseless; epith. of the Trojans in Il., v. αὐίαχος.
with soft sandals, Anth.
of delicate texture, Aesch.
richly luxuriant, Eur.

entry.etym: perhaps the same root as ἥβη?
entry.sense: delicate, graceful, beauteous, pretty, Anacr., etc.: of things, splendid, Pind.—Very early the word took the notion of over-delicate, dainty, luxurious; hence neut. as adv. ἁβρὰ παθεῖν to live delicately, Solon; ἁβρὰ παρηΐδος = ἁβρὰν παρηΐδα, Eur.; ἁβρῶς and ἁβρὸν βαίνειν to step delicately, Id.

entry.etym: From same Root with ἀμβροτεῖν, ἁμαρτεῖν, μ being rejected.
entry.sense: to miss, c. gen., only in aor1 subj., μήπως ἀβροτάξομεν (epic for -ωμεν) ἀλλήλοιϊν that we may not miss one another, Il.
delicacy, luxury, Pind.; οὐκ ἐν ἁβρότητι κεῖσαι thou art not in a position to be fastidious, Eur.
delicate and costly, Aesch.
immortal, divine, holy, νὺξ ἀβρότη, either holy Night, as a divinity, (like ἱερὸν κνέφας, ἱερὸν ἦμαρ), or never failing (like ἄφθιτος ἠώς), Il.; ἔπη ἄβροτα holy hymns, Soph.
without men, solitary, Aesch.
in soft tunic, softly clad, Anth.; εὐνὰς ἁβροχίτωνας beds with soft coverings, Aesch.
unwetted, unmoistened, Aeschin.: wanting rain, waterless, Eur.

to make delicate, treat delicately, Aesch.: to deck or trick out, εἰς γάμον ἁβρῦναί τινα Anth.; Mid. or Pass. to live delicately; then to wax wanton, give oneself airs, Aesch.; c. gen. rei, to pride or plume oneself on a thing, Eur.
from Abydos, Il.
at Abydos, Il.
Abydos, the town on the Asiatic side of the Hellespont.
with no bottom, bottomless, unfathomed, Hdt.; generally, unfathomable, enormous, Aesch.
ἡ ἄβυσσος, the great deep, the abyss, bottomless pit, NTest.
seeming good, Plat.
to do good, NTest.
a good deed, service rendered, Lat. beneficium, Hdt.
doing good: — οἱ Ἀγαθοεργοί, at Sparta, the five oldest and most approved knights, who went on foreign missions for the state, Hdt.
to do good, NTest.; ἀγ. τινά to do good to, Id.
to do well, act rightly, Id.
well doing, NTest.
doing good, beneficent.
good, Lat. bonus:
of persons,

in early times, good, gentle, noble, in reference to birth, opp. to κακοί, πατρὸς δ’ εἴμ’ ἀγαθοῖο, θεὰ δέ με γείνατο μήτηρ Il.; ἀγαθοὶ καὶ ἐξ ἀγαθῶν, Lat. boni bonis prognati, Plat.; with this early sense was associated that of wealth and power, like Lat. optimus quisque in Sallust and Cicero; esp. in the phrase καλοὶ κἀγαθοί (v. καλοκἀγαθός).

good, brave, since these qualities were attributed to the Chiefs, Il.; ἀγαθὸς ἐν ὑσμίνῃ, βοὴν ἀγαθός, πὺξ ἀγαθός, etc., Hom.; ἀγ. τὰ πολέμια, τὰ πολιτικά Hdt., etc.;—also c. dat., ἀγ. πολέμῳ Xen.;—and, ἀγ. εἴς τι, περί τι, πρός τι Plat., etc.; lastly, c. inf., ἀγ. μάχεσθαι, ἱππεύεσθαι, good at fighting, etc., Hdt.
good, in moral sense, Plat., etc.
ἀγαθοῦ δαίμονος, as a toast, "to the good Genius," Ar.
of things,
good, serviceable, Ἰθάκη ἀγαθὴ κουροτρόφος Od.; ἀγ. τοῖς τοκεῦσι, τῇ πόλει Xen.; c. gen., εἴ τι οἶδα πυρετοῦ ἀγ. good for fever, Id.; ἀγαθόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it is good to do so and so, Hom., etc.

ἀγαθόν, τό, a good, of persons, φίλον, ὃ μέγιστον ἀγ. εἶναι φασι Xen.; ἐπ’ ἀγαθῷ τοῖς πολίταις Ar.; τὸ ἀγαθόν or τἀγαθόν, the good, summum bonum, Plat., etc.; in pl., ἀγαθά, τά, the goods of fortune, wealth, Hdt., etc.; also good qualities, of a horse, Xen.

instead of the regular degrees of comparison, many forms are used,—comp. ἀμείνων, ἀρείων, βελτίων, κρείσσων, λωΐων , epic βέλτερος, λωΐτερος, φέρτερος; — Sup. ἄριστος, βέλτιστος, κράτιστος, λώϊστος, epic βέλτατος, κάρτιστος, φέρτατος, φέριστος.
the adv. is usually εὖ: ἀγαθῶς in late writers.
goodness, kindness, NTest.

entry.etym: epic and ionic for ἄγαμαι, only in pres. and in bad sense (cf. ἄγη II).
entry.sense: c. gen. rei, to be indignant at, Od.
c. dat. pers. to be indignant with, Hdt.
very glorious, famous, Lat. inclytus, Il., Pind.
= ἀγακλεής, Hom., etc.
of things, ἀγακλειτὴ ἑκατόμβη Od.
Lat. inclytus, of men, Hom., Hes.
of things, Od.
well-built or placed, πόλις Pind.
without milk, getting no milk, i.e. taken from the mother's breast, Horace's jam lacte depulsus, Aesch.
great joy, exultation, NTest.
to rejoice exceedingly, NTest.
the iris or flag, Hhymn.

entry.etym: Pass., mostly in pres. and imperf.
entry.sense: to make glorious, glorify, exalt, c. acc. : esp. to pay honour to a god, ἀγ. τινὰ θυσίαισι Ar.; to adorn, deck, γαμηλίους εὐνάς Eur.; Pass. to glory, take delight, exult in a thing, c. dat., Hom., attic; absol., Hdt., etc.
a glory, delight, honour, Il., attic; ἀγάλματ’ ἀγορᾶς mere ornaments of the agora, Eur.
a pleasing gift, esp. for the gods, Od.
a statue in honour of a god, Hdt., attic; an image, as an object of worship, etc., Aesch.; then generally,= ἀνδριάς, any statue, Plat.: also a portrait, picture, ἐξαλειφθεῖς’ ὡς ἄγαλμα Eur.
a maker of statues, a sculptor, statuary, Hdt., Plat., etc.
absol. to wonder, be astonished, Hom.
c. acc. to admire a person or thing, Id., Hdt.; so in attic, ταῦτα ἀγασθείς Xen.; c. acc. pers. et rei, to admire one for a thing, Plat., Xen.
c. gen. rei only, often in Com., to wonder at, λόγων Ar.
c. acc. rei et gen. pers., οὐκ ἄγαμαι ταῦτ’ ἀνδρός I admire not this in a man, Eur.
c. gen. pers., foll. by a part., to wonder at one's doing, ἀγ. αὐτοῦ εἰπόντος Plat.
c. dat. to be delighted with a person or thing, Hdt., Eur., etc.
in bad sense, to feel envy, bear a grudge against a person, c. dat., Hom.
c. acc. to be jealous or angry at a thing, Od. Cf. ἀγαίομαι.
of or having to do with Agamemnon, Hom., Pind., Aesch.
Agamemnon's son, Orestes, Od.
the very steadfast, name of the leader of the Greeks against Troy, Hom.
part. pres. of ἄγαμαι, with admiration, respect or deference, Plat.
celibacy, Plut.; ἀγαμίου δίκη, ἡ, an action against one for not marrying, Plut.
unmarried, unwedded, single, Lat. caelebs, Il., Trag.
γάμος ἄγαμος, a marriage that is no marriage, a fatal marriage, Soph., Eur.
to feel irritation: metaph. to be vexed, annoyed, angry, discontented, Ar., Plat.; c. dat. rei, to be vexed at a thing, Id.; ἐπί τινι Isocr., ὑπέρ τινος, διά τι Plat.
to be vexed at or with a person, τινί Xen.; πρός τινα Plut.; κατά τινος Luc.: c. acc. pers., ἀγ. τινὰς ἀποθνήσκοντας to be angry at their dying, Plat.
irritation, of the irritation caused by teething, Plat.: metaph., ἀγανάκτησιν ἔχει the thing gives ground for annoyance or displeasure, Thuc.
irritable, Plat.
irritating, Plat.
much snowed on, snow-capt, Il.
mild-eyed, Anth.
mild, gentle, kindly, of words, Hom., Pind.; in Hom. of the shafts of Apollo and Artemis, as bringing an easy death; Sup. ἀγανώτατος, Hes.: adv. -νῶς, Eur.
gentleness, kindliness, Hom.
poet. adj. gentle of mood, Hom.

entry.etym: ἄγᾱν properly, but ἄγαν in Anth.
entry.sense: very, much, very much, Theogn., Attic, the word λίην being its equiv. in epic and ionic: in bad sense, too, too much, Lat. nimis, as in the famous μηδὲν ἄγαν, ne quid nimis, not too much of any thing, Theogn., etc.
admiring, Hes.
to treat with affection, shew affection to a person, caress, c. acc., Hom.; so in Mid., Od.
of persons, to treat with affection, to caress, love, be fond of, c. acc., attic for ἀγαπάζω, Plat., etc.; Pass. to be beloved, Id., Dem.
in NTest. to regard with brotherly love, v. ἀγαπή.

of things, to be well pleased or contented at or with a thing, c. dat., Dem., etc.; also c. acc. rei, Id.; absol. to be content, Luc.: —ἀγ. ὅτι.., εἰ.., ἐὰν.., to be well pleased that . . ., Thuc., etc.
a delight, darling, Anth.
= ἠνορέην ἀγαπῶν, loving manliness, manly, Il.
love: esp. brotherly love, charity; the love of God for man and of man for God, NTest.
in pl. a love-feast, Id.
to be loved, desired, Plat.
affectionate, Plut.
beloved, of an only son, Hom., Dem.
of things, worthy of love, loveable, dear, Plat., etc.
to be acquiesced in (as the least in a choice of evils), ἀγαπητόν [ἐστι] one must be content, εἰ.., ἐάν.., Id., Xen., etc.
adv. -τῶς, cheerfully, contentedly, Plat., Dem., etc.
just enough to content one, only just, barely, scarcely, Plat.
strong-flowing, swift-flowing, Il.
much groaning, howling, of waves, Od.: loud-wailing, Aesch.

entry.etym: ἀγατός poet. for ἀγαστός, as θαυματός for θαυμαστός, Hhymn.; verb. adj. of ἄγαμαι
entry.sense: deserving admiration, later form of the Hom. ἀγητός, admirable, Eur., Xen.; adv. -τῶς, Id. poet. for ἀγαστός, as θαυματός for θαυμαστός, Hhymn.
illustrious, noble, Hom.; Sup. -ότατος, Od.
stately, proud, Hes.: superl. adv. ἀγαυρότατα, Hdt.
to press one to serve as a courier, to press into service, NTest.
ἀγγαρήϊος, Ionic form of ἄγγαρος, Hdt.
neut. ἀγγαρήϊον, post-riding, the Persian system of mounted couriers, Id.
Persian word, a mounted courier, such as were kept ready at regular stages throughout Persia for carrying the royal despatches; cf. ἀγγαρήϊος, and v. Xen. Cyr. 8. 6, 17.
as adj., ἄγγαρον πῦρ the courier flame, said of beacon fires used for telegraphing, Aesch.

a message, tidings, news, Hom., Hdt., etc.; ἀγγελίη ἐμή a report of me, concerning me, Il.; ἀγγελίην πατρὸς φέρει ἐρχομένοιο he brings news of or about thy father's coming, Od.: — ἀγγελίην ἐλθεῖν, to go a message, i. e. on a message, like Lat. legationem obire, Il.;—so also epic in gen., ἀγγελίης οἴχνεσκε went on account of a message, Id.; ἤλυθε σεῦ ἕνεκ’ ἀγγελίης ( i. e. ἀγγελίης σοῦ ἕνεκα) Id., Hes.
a proclamation, command, Hhymn., etc.
a messenger, Hdt.: title of the Persian minister who introduced people to the king, Id.
to bear a message, τινί to a person, Hom.; c. acc. et inf. to make proclamation that, Il.
c. acc. rei, to announce, proclaim, report, Hom., attic
c. acc. pers. to bring news of, Od.; περί τινος Soph.
Mid. to announce oneself, Id.
Pass. to be reported of, Id., etc.; τὰ ἠγγελμένα the reports, Thuc.
a message, tidings, news, Eur., Thuc., etc.
a messenger, envoy, Hom., Hdt., attic
generally, one that announces, of birds of augury, Il.; Μουσῶν ἄγγελος, of a poet, Theogn.; Διὸς ἄγγ., of the nightingale, Soph.; c. gen. rei, ἄγγ. κακῶν ἐμῶν Id.
a divine messenger, an angel, NTest.
a vessel of various kinds, a jar to hold milk, etc., Hom.: a vat for the vintage, Hes.; a vase, pitcher, pail, Hdt., attic
a coffer or ark, in which children were laid, Hdt., Eur.: a chest for clothes, Soph.: a cinerary urn, Id.
the cell of a honeycomb, Anth.
to bring together, gather together, c. acc., Hom., attic; Pass. to come together, gather, assemble, Hom.; ἀγρόμενοι σύες herded swine, Od.; θυμὸς ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἀγέρθη, ἐς φρένα θυμὸς ἀγέρθη Il.
of things, to get together, collect, gather, Od.; so in Mid., Id.
to collect by begging, Id.
ὀφρύας εἰς ἓν ἀγείρειν to frown, Anth.
without neighbour, neighbourless, Aesch.; φίλων ἀγ. with no friends as neighbours, Eur.
belonging to a herd, feeding at large, Hom., attic.
in herds or shoals, gregarious, ἰχθύες Hdt.; ἀγελαῖα, τά, gregarious animals, Plat.
of the herd or multitude, i.e. common, Id., etc.
to lead a company, c. gen., Plut.
the leader of a company, captain, Plut., Luc.
without laughter, Plut.
not laughing, grave, gloomy, sullen, Hhymn., Aesch.
pass. not to be laughed at, not trifling, Id.
epic epith. of Athena, driver of spoil, forager, Il.
in herds or companies, Il., Hdt.:— doric ἀγελᾱδόν, Theocr.
a herd, of horses, of oxen and kine, cf. βούνομος; of swine, Hes.
any herd or company, Soph., Eur.; metaph., πόνων ἀγέλαι Id.
of unrecorded descent, NTest.
beardless; ἀγένειόν τι εἰρηκέναι to speak like a boy, Luc.
unborn, uncreated, unoriginated, Plat.
of things, not done, not having happened, ἀγένητον ποιεῖν, Lat. infectum reddere, Soph.
of no family, low-born, Hdt., Plat., etc.
low-minded, Hdt., Ar., etc.
of things, much like βάναυσος, illiberal, sordid, Plat.; adv. -νῶς, Eur.
unbegotten, unborn, ἀγ. τότ’ ἦ Soph.
like ἀγεννής, low-born, Id.

entry.etym: properly imperat. of ἄγω, used as adv.
entry.sense: come! come on! well! Lat. age! Hom., attic.
without a gift of honour, unrecompensed, unrewarded, Il., Eur.
a gathering, mustering, Hdt.
poet. adj. high-minded, lordly, Hom., etc.; in Pind. of noble actions.
in bad sense, haughty, arrogant, insolent, Archil., Luc.: so adv. -χως, Anth.
host-leading, Hes.
without taste of, fasting from, c. gen.; metaph., κακῶν ἄγευστος αἰών Soph.; τῶν τερπνῶν ἄγευστος Xen.
to drive out a curse, i.e. an accursed or polluted person, Lat. piaculum exigere, Hdt., Soph.
anything led, a division of an army, corps, Xen.
manliness, manhood, courage, Il.
poet. adj., manly, courageous, heroic, Il.; in bad sense, headstrong, arrogant, Hom., Hes.
wonder, awe, amazement, Hom.
envy, malice, Hdt.; and of the gods, jealousy, Aesch.
a fragment, piece, splinter, Aesch., Eur.
not waxing old, undecaying,
of persons, Hom., Hes.; so, ἀγήρως χρόνῳ Soph.
of things, Il., attic
leader of people, conductor of men, Aesch.; so, ἡγησίλεως and ἀγησίλας, ἀγησίλα, Anth.
leading the chorus, Pind.
admirable, wondrous, c. acc. rei, εἶδος ἀγητός admirable in form, Il.; εἶδος ἀγητοί wonderful in form only, as a reproach, Id.; c. dat. rei, ἀγ. χρήμασι Solon.
consecration, sanctification, NTest.
to hallow, dedicate, Soph.
to lead, bring, carry, Il., Hdt.; Mid. to cause to be brought, Id.
devoted to the gods, sacred, holy, Lat. sacer:
of things, esp. temples, Hdt., Xen., etc.: τὸ ἅγιον the Temple, τὰ ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων theHoly of Holies, NTest.
of persons, holy, pure, Ar.; adv. ἁγίως, Isocr., NTest.—The word never occurs in Hom. or Trag., ἁγνός being used instead.
mostly in pl. holy rites, temple-worship, Isocr.
to perform sacred rites, Plat.
to live piously or chastely, Eur.
holiness, sanctity, NTest.
Mid. to lift up in the arms, Il.
like ἀγκάς, in the arms, Aesch.
with bent arm, resting on the arm, Id.
entry.etym: not for ἀνέκαθεν, since ἀγκ- stands for ἀνακ-, never for ἀνεκ-.

entry.sense: the bent arm, Hdt., etc.; mostly in pl., ἐν ἀγκάλαις in the arms, Aesch., Eur.; ἐν ταῖς ἀγκ. Xen.;—in sg., φέρειν ἐν τῇ ἀγκάλῃ Hdt.
metaph. anything closely enfolding, πετραία ἀγκάλη Aesch.; πόντιαι ἀγκάλαι bights or arms of the sea, Id.; κυμάτων ἐν ἀγκάλαις Ar.
to embrace, Anth.
ἀγκαλιζόμενος in pass. sense, Aesop.
that which is embraced or carried in the arms, Luc.
an armful, bundle, Hhymn.
in or into the arms, Hom., Theocr.
a fish-hook, Theocr.
with a hook, Anth.
a fish-hook, Od., Hdt., etc.
the hook of a spindle, Plat.
Pass. to be furnished with barbs, Plut.
poet. for ἀγκάλη or ἀγκών, the bent arm, only in pl., Hom.
a bend: hence a mountain glen, dell, valley, Hom., Hdt., Eur.
a loop or noose in a cord,Eur., Xen.
the thong of a javelin, by which it was hurled: the javelin itself, Eur.
a bow-string, Soph.
Dim. of ἀγκύλη; τὰ ἀγκύλια, the Roman ancilia, Plut.
of a cock, with hooked spurs, Babr.
crook-toothed: barbed, Anth.
crooked of counsel, wily, epith. of Κρόνος, Hom.; of Prometheus, Hes.
with bent legs, ἀγκ. δίφρος, Rom. sella curulis, Plut.
crooked, curved, of a bow, Il.: beaked, of the eagle, Pind.: of greedy fingers, hooked, Ar.
metaph., of style, crooked, intricate, Luc.
with curved bow, Il., etc.
with hooked beak, αἰετός Od.; αἰγυπιοί Il.
with crooked claws, Batr.
to crook, bend, τὴν χεῖρα: Pass., ὄνυχας ἠγκυλωμένος with crooked claws, Ar.
of javelins, furnished with a thong (ἀγκύλη) for throwing, Eur.

Lat. ancora, an anchor, first in Alcae. and Theogn., for in Hom. we hear only of εὐναί, i. e. stones used as anchors; ἄγκυραν βάλλεσθαι, καθιέναι, μεθιέναι, ἀφιέναι to cast anchor, Pind., Hdt., etc.; so, ἐπὶ δυοῖν ἀγκύραιν ὁρμεῖν, i. e. "to have two strings to one's bow," Dem.; cf. ὀχέω; ἐπὶ τῆς αὐτῆς (sc. ἀγκύρας) ὁρμεῖν τοῖς πολλοῖς, i. e. "to be in the same boat" with the many, Id.
to throw by the hook-trick, i. e. by hooking your leg behind the other's knee, in wrestling, Ar.
a small anchor, Luc.
the bend of the arm, the elbow, Hom.
generally the arm, like ἀγκάλη, Pind., Soph.
any bend, as the jutting angle of a wall, Il.: the bend or reach of a river, Hdt.; ἕσπεροι ἄγκωνες, in Soph., seem to be the angle of the bay of Rhoeteium.
bright-haired, Hhymn.
splendour, beauty, adornment; ἀγλαΐηφι πεποιθώς (epic dat.) Il.: in bad sense, pomp, show, vanity, and in pl. vanities, Od., Eur.
triumph, glory, Pind., Soph.: in pl., festivities, merriment, Hes.
to make bright or splendid, Plut.
Mid. and Pass. to adorn oneself or be adorned with a thing, take delight in, σέ φημι ἀγλαϊεῖσθαι I say that thou will take delight in them (sc. τοῖς ἵπποις), Il.
an ornament, honour, Aesch., Eur.
with beauteous limbs, Pind.
with beautiful trees, Pind.
giving splendid gifts, Hhymn.
noble-hearted, Anth.
bearing beautiful or goodly fruit Od.: in Hhymn. of Demeter, giver of the fruits of the earth.
of beauteous form, Anth.
splendid, shining, bright, beautiful, Hom., Hes.
of men, either beautiful or famous, Il.; c. dat. rei, famous for a thing, Id.
god of the bright trident, Pind.
bright-eyed, beaming, Soph.
a head of garlic, made up of several cloves, Ar.
without tongue, of the crocodile, Arist.
tongueless, ineloquent, Lat. elinguis, Pind., Ar.: then = βάρβαρος, Soph.
a fragment, Plut.
a broken cliff, crag, Eur.
unbending, inflexible, Plut.
uncarded, NTest.
purity, chastity, Soph., NTest.: in pl. purifications, Isocr.
chastity, Eur.

to consider as part of purity, make it a point of religion, c. inf., ἁγνεύουσι ἔμψυχον μηδὲν κτείνειν Hdt.: absol. to be pure, Aesch.; χεῖρας ἁγνεύει is clean in hands, Eur.: to keep oneself pure from a thing, c. gen., Dem.
to cleanse away, esp. by water, Soph.
to cleanse, purify, from a thing, c. gen. Eur.
ἁγν. τὸν θανόντα to hallow the dead by fire, so that he may be received by the gods below, Soph.; Pass., σώμαθ’ ἡγνίσθη πυρί Eur.
a purification, expiation, Aesch.
to be purified, Eur.

Passive not to perceive or know, ἄνδρ’ ἀγνοιήσας’ from not recognising him, Od.: mostly with negat., οὐκ ἠγνοίησεν, i. e. he perceived or knew well, Il.; μηδὲν ἀγνόει learn all, Eur.: —c. acc. to be ignorant of, Hdt., attic; ἀγν. περί τινος Plat.; dependent clauses are added in part., τίς ἀγνοεῖ τὸν πόλεμον ἥξοντα; Dem.; or with a Conjunct., οὐδεὶς ἀγνοεῖ ὅτι.., Id.; Pass. not to be known, Plat., etc.
absol. to go wrong, make a false step, etc.; ἀγνοῶν ignorantly, by mistake, Xen.
a fault of ignorance, error, NTest.
want of perception, ignorance, Aesch., Thuc., etc.; ἣν ὑπ’ ἀγνοίας δρᾷς, i. e. whom seeing you pretend not to know, Soph.
= ἀγνόημα, a mistake, Dem.
pure-flowing, ποταμός Aesch.
a willow-like tree, vitex agnus castus, Hhymn.
full of religious awe:
of places and things dedicated to gods, hallowed, holy, sacred, Od., Att.
of divine persons, chaste, pure, Od.
of persons, undefiled, chaste, pure, Aesch., Eur.: c. gen. pure from a thing, Eur.
pure from blood, guiltless, Soph.; ἁγνὸς χεῖρας Eur.
in moral sense, pure, upright, Xen.; adv., ἁγνῶς ἔχειν to be pure, Id.
purity, chastity, NTest.

to break, shiver, Hom.; Pass. to be broken or shivered, ἄγη ξίφος Il.; ἐάγη δόρυ Id.; πάλιν ἄγεν ὄγκοι (for ἐάγησαν) the barbs were broken backwards, Id.; καμπὰς πολλὰς ἀγνύμενος, of a river, with a broken, i. e. winding, course, Hdt.; ἄγνυτο ἠχώ the sound spread around, Hes.
to act without right feeling, act unfairly, Xen., Dem.; Pass. to be unfairly treated, ἀγνωμονηθείς Plut.
want of sense, folly, Theogn.: senseless pride, arrogance, Hdt., Eur.
want of feeling, unkindness, unfairness, Dem.
in pl. misunderstandings, Xen.
ill-judging, senseless, Pind., Plat., etc.; adv. -όνως, senselessly, Xen.
headstrong, reckless, arrogant, (in comp. -ονέστερος) Hdt.; in Sup., Xen.
unfeeling, unkind, hardhearted, Soph., Xen.
of things, senseless, brute, Soph., Aeschin.
ignorance, Eur.; διὰ τὴν ἀλλήλων ἀγν. from not knowing one another, Thuc.
pass. unknown, of persons, Aesch.; ἀγνὼς πατρί clam patre, Eur.: of things, unknown, obscure, unintelligible, Aesch., Soph.; ἀγν. δόκησις a dark suspicion, Id.
not known, obscure, ignoble, Eur.
act. not knowing, ignorant, Soph.
c. gen., where the sense fluctuates between pass. and act., ἀγνῶτες ἀλλήλων Thuc.
unknown, τινί; ἄγνωτον ἐς γῆν Eur.; γνωτὰ κοὐκ ἄγνωτά μοι Soph.
not to be known, ἄγνωστόν τινα τεύχειν Od.; ἀγνωστότατοι γλῶσσαν most unintelligible in tongue, Thuc.
unfruitfulness, Plut.
pass. unborn, Il.: not yet born, Eur.
act. not producing, unfruitful, barren; τόκοισιν ἀγόνοις travail without issue, bringing no children to the birth, Soph., etc.
c. gen. not productive of, barren in a thing, Plat.
childless, Eur.
unmourned, Aesch.
(also in mid. sense); to be in the ἀγορά, frequent it, Hdt.: to occupy the market-place, Thuc.
to buy in the market, buy, purchase, Ar., Xen.; Mid. to buy for oneself, Id., etc.
as a mark of idle fellows, to lounge in the ἀγορά, Thuc.; cf. ἀγοραῖος.
in, of, or belonging to the ἀγορά, Hdt., attic; Ἑρμῆς Ἀγ. as patron of traffick, Ar.
frequenting the market, etc.; ἀγοραῖοι, οἱ, loungers in the market, Lat. circumforanei, subrostrani, Hdt.; hence generally, the common sort, low fellows, Ar., Plat., etc.
of things, low, mean, vulgar, Ar.
generally, proper to the ἀγορά, skilled in, suited to forensic speaking, Plut.
ἀγοραῖος (sc. ἡμέρα), a court-day, Strab., NTest.
adv. -ως, in forensic style, Plut.
of or for the ἀγορανόμος or his office, Plat.; used to translate Lat. aedilicius, Plut.
a clerk of the market, who regulated buying and selling there, Ar.; used to translate Lat. Aedilis, Plut.

entry.etym: almost wholly used in epic forms.
entry.sense: to meet in assembly, sit in debate: then, like ἀγορεύω, to speak in the assembly, harangue, Hom.
to speak, utter, Il.
to talk with, τινι Soph.

an assembly of the people, opp. to the Council of Chiefs, Hom.: —καθίζειν ἀγορήν to hold an assembly, opp. to λύειν ἀγ. to dissolve it; ἀγορήνδε καλέειν, κηρύσσειν, Hom.; so, ἀγορὰν συνάγειν, συλλέγειν Xen.

the place of Assembly, Hom.; used not only for debating, trials, and other public purposes, but also as a market-place, like the Roman Forum, attic; but to lounge in the market was held to be disreputable, cf. ἀγοραῖος.
the business of the ἀγορά, public speaking, gift of speaking, mostly in pl., Hom.
things sold in the ἀγορά, the market, Lat. annona; ἀγορὰν παρασκευάζειν to hold a market, Thuc.
as a mark of time, ἀγορὰ πλήθουσα or ἀγορᾶς πληθώρη the forenoon, when the market-place was full, Hdt.; opp. to ἀγορῆς διάλυσις, the time just after mid-day, when they went home, Id.
will lounge in the ἀγορά, without a beard, Ar.
that which is bought: in pl.goods, wares, merchandise, Dem., etc.
the slave who bought provisions for the house, the purveyor, Xen.

entry.etym: in correct attic writers, this Verb (and its compds.) is for the most part confined to pres. and imperf.; the other tenses being borrowed.
entry.sense: to speak in the assembly, harangue, speak, Hom.; κακόν τι ἀγορεύειν τινά to speak ill of one, Od.; of the κῆρυξ in the Ecclesia, τίς ἀγορεύειν βούλεται; who wishes to address the people? Ar., Dem., etc.
μή τι φόβονδ’ ἀγόρευε counsel me not to flight, Il.
to proclaim, declare, mention, Hom.; in aor1 mid., ἀγορεύσασθαι ὡς . . . to have it proclaimed that . . ., Hdt., etc.: metaph., δέρμα θηρὸς ἀγ. χειρῶν ἔργον tells a tale of. . ., Theocr.
Pass., of a speech, to be spoken, Thuc.
from the Assembly or market, Il., etc.
to the Assembly or market, Il.
a speaker, orator, Il.
the gift of speaking, eloquence, Od.
in the Assembly, Hes.
a leader, chief, Il., etc.
any matter of religious awe:
like Lat. piaculum, that which requires expiation, a curse, pollution, guilt, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
the person or thing accursed, an abomination, Soph., Thuc.
an expiation, Soph.
in good sense, = σέβας, awe, Hhymn.
the flat of the hand, Il.
the arm, = ἀγκάλη, Theocr., Anth.
without learning (γράμματα), unlettered, Xen., Anth.
unwritten, Soph.
a catching, hunting, ἄγραν ἐφέπειν to follow the chase, Od.; ἐς ἄγρας ἰέναι Eur.: also of fishing, Soph.
a way of catching, Hes., Hdt.
that which is taken in hunting, the booty, prey, Hes., Trag.: game, Hdt.: of fish, a draught, haul, NTest.
to dwell in the field, NTest.
dwelling in the field, of shepherds, Il., Hes.; ἄγρ. ἀνήρ a boor, Anth.
of oxen, Hom., etc.
of things, rural, rustic, Eur.
unwritten, Thuc.; ἄγραφοι νόμοι unwritten laws, i. e.
the laws of nature, moral law, Dem.
laws of custom, common law, Thuc.
not registered, Id. ἄγρει, ἀγρεῖτε, v. ἀγρέω.
of or in the country, Anth.
clownish, boorish, Ar.
clownishness, a rude, vagrant life, Anth.
a harrow, rake, Anth.
that which is taken in hunting, booty, prey, spoil, Eur.
a means of catching, Aesch.; of the net thrown over Agamemnon, Id.
a hunter, Pind., Eur.
of an arrow, Anth.
a hunter, like ἀγρεύς, Soph.
as adj., ἀγρ. κύνες hounds, Solon; ἀγρ. κάλαμοι a trap of reeds, Anth.
to take by hunting or fishing, to catch, take, Hdt., Eur.; also in Mid., θύματ’ ἠγρεύσασθ’ ye caught or chose your victim, Eur.; Pass. to be taken in the chase, Xen.
metaph. to hunt after, thirst for, Eur.; but ἀγρεύειν τινὰ λόγῳ to catch him in or by his words, NTest.
to capture, seize, Sapph., Aesch.
imperat. ἄγρει, = ἄγε, come, come on Il.; ἀγρεῖτε Od.
intr. to be angered, provoked, chafed, Plat.; τινί with one, Id.; metaph. of rivers, Plut.
Causal, to make angry: Pass. to be angered, Id.
wild, ἄμπελον ἀγριάδα Anth.
of a wild olive, Anth.
as Subst. a wild olive, Lat. oleaster, Theocr., NTest.
writing wild poetry, Ar.
living in the fields, Lat. agrestis:
of animals, wild, savage, αἴξ, σῦς Il.; ἵπποι, ὄνοι Hdt., etc.; of men, Id.; of a countryman, as opp. to a citizen, Mosch.
of trees, wild, Hdt., etc.; μητρὸς ἀγρίας ἄπο made from the wild vine, Aesch.; ἄγρ. ἔλαιον, Soph.
of countries, wild, uncultivated, Plat.
of men and animals, having qualities incident to a wild state:
in moral sense, savage, fierce, Lat. ferus, ferox, Hom., etc.
wild, brutal, coarse, boorish, rude, Hom., etc.; ἀγριώτατα ἤθεα Hdt.; ἐς τὸ ἀγριώτερον to harsher measures, Thuc.
of things and circumstances, cruel, harsh, Aesch., etc.; νὺξ ἀγριωτέρη more wild, stormy, Hdt.; ἀγρ. νόσος a malignant disease, Soph.
adv. -ίως, savagely, Aesch., etc.: also ἄγρια as neut. pl., Hes., Mosch.
wildness, savageness, Xen., etc.
in moral sense, savageness, fierceness, cruelty, Plat., etc.
with wild rough voice, Od.
to make wild or savage; τινί against one, Eur.
Pass., imperf. ἠγριούμην, aor1 ἠγριώθην: perf. ἠγρίωμαι; to grow wild or savage, and in perf. to be so, Eur.
in moral sense, to be savage, fierce, Soph., etc.
wild-looking, Eur.
feeding in the field, dwelling in the country, Soph., Eur.
a country neighbour, Plut.
a giver of booty or prey, Anth.
from the country, Od., Eur., etc.
rusticity, boorishness, coarseness, Plat.
Mid. to be rude and boorish, Plat.
of or in the country, Ar., etc.
of men, dwelling in the country, a countryman, rustic, Id.; then, opp. to ἀστεῖος, clownish, boorish, rude, Id.; the character of the ἄγροικος is described by Theophr.
adv. -κως, Ar.; comp. -οτέρως, Plat., Xen.; but -ότερον, Plat.
of land, rough, uncultivated, Thuc.
a countryman, Hom., Hes., etc.
as adj. rustic, Anth. ἀγρόμενος, epic aor2 part. pass. of ἀγείρω.
to the country, Od.
haunting the country, rural, wild, Od., Aesch.; of places, Soph.
as Subst., overseer of public lands, a magistrate at Athens, Plat.
Lat. ager, a field, in pl. fields, lands, Hom., etc.: in sg. a farm, Od.
the country, opp. to the town, Id.: ἀγρῷ or ἐπ’ ἀγροῦ in the country, Id.; κατ’ ἀγρούς Id.; ἐπ’ ἀγρῶν Soph.
poet. for ἄγριος, wild, of animals,Hom., etc.
of countrymen, Anth.
of plants, wild, Id.
fond of the chase; Ἀγροτέρα, the Huntress, i. e. Artemis, Il., Xen.
= ἀγρότης, Eur.; fem. ἀγρότειρα, as adj. rustic, Id.
a country-man, rustic, Eur.
= ἀγρευτής a hunter, Od.; fem. ἀγρότις, i. e. Artemis, Anth.
a watcher of the country, Anth.
to lie awake, be wakeful, Theogn.; ἀγρυπνεῖν τὴν νύκτα to pass a sleepless night, Xen.
metaph. to be watchful, NTest.
wakeful, Plut.
sleeplessness, waking, watching, Plat.; ἀγρυπνίῃσιν εἴχετο Hdt.
hunting after sleep, i. e. sleepless, wakeful, Plat., etc.: metaph., Ζηνὸς ἄγρ. βέλος Aesch.; τὸ ἄγρυπνον = ἀγρυπνία, Plat.
act. keeping awake, μέριμναι Anth.
to catch fish, Od.
Subst. and adj., Soph., Eur., a grass that mules fed on.
adj., wild, Eur.: rustic, Anth.

entry.etym: a quasiparticipial form from ἄγω cf. ὄργυια
entry.sense: a street, highway, Hom., etc.
adj., ἀγυιάτιδες θεραπεῖαι the worship of Apollo Agyieus, Eur.
name of Apollo, guardian of the streets, Eur.
a pillar set up at the street door, Ar.
want of training, Ar.
unexercised, untrained, Xen.
unpractised, τινός in a thing, Eur., Xen., etc.; also εἴς, πρός or περί τι Plat., etc.
unharassed, Soph.
adv., ἀγυμνάστως ἔχειν πρός τι to be unpractised in a thing, Xen.
a gathering, crowd, Hom.
to collect by begging, Od.
a collector: esp. a begging priest of Cybele, Anth.: then,
a beggar, mountebank, vagabond, juggler, Soph., Eur.
fit for an ἀγύρτης, vagabond, Plut.
fighting hand to hand, Il., Hes.; τὰ ἀγχ. ὅπλα arms for close fight, Xen.
near the sea, of cities, Il.; of islands, sea-girt, Aesch., Soph.
deep near shore, of the sea, Od.
neighbouring, Aesch.
near the gods, i. e. like the gods or dwelling with them, Od.; later, a demigod, Luc.
next door, Theogn., Theocr.
coming near, c. gen., Theocr.: —in Hom. only in as adv. near, close at hand; so ἐξ ἀγχιμόλοιο Il.
near the clouds, Anth.
readiness of mind, ready wit, sagacity, Plat., etc. From
ready of wit, sagacious, shrewd, Od., Plat., etc.
of Place, near, nigh, close by, absol. or c. gen., Hom.; comp. ἄγχιον, ἆσσον: Sup. ἄγχιστα (v. ἆσσον, ἄγχιστος).
near by sea, ἀγχ. πόρος a short voyage, Eur.
passing near, always near, Anth.
poet. for ἀγχίπολις, near the city, dwelling hard by, Aesch., Soph.
nearness of kin, Plat.
rights of kin, right of inheritance, Ar.
mostly in pl. ἀγχιστεῖς, closely akin, of nations, Hdt.: next of kin, Luc.
to be next or near, c. dat., Eur.
to be next of kin, Isae.
one who brings near, the immediate author, Soph..
close together, crowded, in heaps, Hom.
Sup. adj., nearest, Pind., Trag.; γένει ἄγχιστος πατρός nearest of kin to him, Eur.
in Hom. only neut. as adv., ἄγχιστον or ἄγχιστα most nearly like, c. gen., Διὸς ἄγχ. next to Zeus, Aesch.; ἄγχ. τοῦ βωμοῦ Hdt.
of Time, most lately, but now, most recently, Il., Hdt.
turning closely, quick-wheeling, of a hawk, Theogn.
quick-changing, sudden, Thuc.; neut. pl. as adv. suddenly, Hdt.
near the borders, neighbouring, Soph.
in the pangs of child-birth, Anth.
from nigh at hand, Hdt.
near, c. gen., Hom.; absol., Theocr.

a throttling, strangling, hanging, Trag., etc.; ἔργα κρείσσον’ ἀγχόνης deeds beyond (i.e. too bad for) hanging, Soph.; τάδ’ ἀγχόνης πέλας ’tis nigh as bad as hanging, Eur.; in pl., ἐν ἀγχόναις θάνατον λαβεῖν to die by hanging, Id.
fit for strangling, βρόχος Eur.

Sup. of ἀγχοῦ, like ἄγχιστα, nearest, next, c. gen., Hdt.; ἀγχ. τινός very near, i. e. very like, some one, Id.; also τινί Id.:— οἱ ἀγχοτάτω προσήκοντες the nearest of kin, Id.:— so, ἀγχότατα ἔχειν τινός to be most like one, Id.
comp. of ἀγχοῦ, nearer, c. gen., Hdt.
= ἄγχι, near, nigh, ἀγχοῦ δ’ ἱσταμένη Hom.;c. gen. Id., Hdt.
neighbouring, Anth.
nearly equal, ἀγχώμαλοι ἐν χειροτονίᾳ Thuc.; ἀγχ. μάχη a doubtful battle, Id.: — as adv., ἀγχώμαλα ναυμαχεῖν, Lat. aequo Marte pugnare, Id. adv. -λως, Luc.

to compress, press tight, esp. the throat, to strangle, throttle, choke, ἄγχε μιν ἱμὰς ὑπὸ δειρήν Il.; τὸν Κέρβερον ἀπῇξας ἄγχων Ar.: metaph. of creditors, Id., NTest.; of a guilty conscience, τοῦτο ἄγχει Dem.
fit for leading by, of a dog's leash, Anth.
one that draws or drags, Hdt.
a leading-rein, leash, Soph., Xen.
a carrying away, carriage, Hdt., etc.; πρὸς τὰς ἀγωγὰς χρῆσθαι ὑποζυγίοις Plat.
intr., τὴν ἀγωγὴν ἐποιεῖτο pursued his voyage, Thuc.: movement, τοῦ ποδός Plat.
a bringing to or in, ὑμῶν ἡ ἐς τοὺς ὀλίγους ἀγ. your bringing us before the council, Thuc.
a carrying off, abduction, Aesch., Soph.
a leading towards a point, guiding, ἵππου Xen.
the leading of an army, Plat.; ἐν ταῖς ἀγ. on marches, Xen.
a training, education, Plat., etc.; of plants, culture, Theophr.
easy to be led or carried, τρισσῶν ἁμαξῶν ἀγώγιμον βάρος weight enough to load three wains, Eur.; τὰ ἀγώγιμα things portable, wares, Xen., etc.
of persons, to be carried off, delivered into bondage, Dem.
easily led, complaisant, Plut.
the load of a wagon, Xen.
leading, and as Subst. a guide, Hdt., etc.: c. gen., δύναμις ἀνθρώπων ἀγωγός power of leading men, Plut.
leading towards a point, εἴς, πρός or ἐπί τι Plat., etc.
drawing forth, eliciting, χοαὶ νεκρῶν ἀγωγοί Eur.; δακρύων ἀγ. Id.
absol. attractive, Plut.
judge of a contest, Soph.
a contest, struggle for victory, διὰ πάσης ἀγωνίης ἔχειν to embrace every kind of contest, Hdt.; πολεμίων ἀγωνία Eur.; ἐν δημοτικῇ ἀγ. Xen.
gymnastic exercise, wrestling, Plat., etc.: generally, exercise, Id.
of the mind, agony, anguish, ἐν φόβῳ καὶ πολλῇ ἀγωνίᾳ Dem.
like ἀγωνίζομαι, to contend eagerly, struggle, Dem., etc.
to be distressed, be in an agony, Plat.; περί τινος Arist.; ἐπί τινι Plut.
as Dep. to contend for a prize, esp. in the public games, Hdt.; πρός τινα Plat.; τινί Id., etc.; περί τινος about a thing, Hdt., etc.: c. acc. cogn., ἀγ. στάδιον Id.; ἀγῶνα περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς ἀγ. Dem.
to fight, Hdt., Thuc.; περὶ τῶν ἁπάντων ἀγ. Id.; πρός τινα Id.: c. acc cogn., ἣν [μάχην] ἀγωνίζεσθε Eur.
to contend for the prize on the stage, both of the poet, Hdt., etc., and of the actor, Dem.: generally to contend for victory, καλῶς ἠγώνισαι Plat.
of public speaking, Xen.

to contend against, as law-term, Antipho; c. acc. cogn., ἀγ. δίκην, γραφήν to fight a cause to the last, Dem.; ἀγ. ψευδομαρτυριῶν (sc. γραφήν) Id.; ἀγ. ἀγῶνα Andoc., etc.; but ἀγ. φόνον to fight against a charge of murder, Eur.
generally, to struggle, to exert oneself, c. inf., Thuc.; c. acc. cogn., ἃ μὲν ἠγωνίσω Dem.

as Pass. to be won by a contest, to be brought to issue, mostly in perf., πολλοὶ ἀγῶνες ἀγωνίδαται (ionic for ἠγωνισμένοι εἰσι) Hdt.; τὰ ἠγωνισμένα the contested points, Eur., etc.; ὁ ἀγωνιζόμενος νόμος the law under debate, Dem.; fut. mid. in pass. sense, ἀγωνιεῖται τὸ πρᾶγμα it shall be brought to issue, Id.

of or belonging to the contest, ἄεθλος ἀγ. its prize, Pind.; of Hermes, as president of games, Id.; of Zeus as decider of the contest, Soph.;—the ἀγώνιοι θεοί, in Aesch., etc., are prob. the gods who presided over the great games (Zeus, Poseidon, Apollo, Hermes).
ἀγωνίῳ σχολᾷ in Soph. Aj. 195 is prob. an oxymoron, rest full of conflict, uneasy rest.
contest for a prize, Thuc.
a contest, in pl. deeds done in battle, brave deeds, feats, Hdt.
in sg., ἀγ. τινός a feat for him to be proud of, Thuc.; ξυνέσεως ἀγ. a fine stroke of wit, Id.; ἀρᾶς ἀγ. the issue of the curse, Eur.
ἀγ. ποιεῖσθαί τι to make it an object to strive for, Hdt.; οὐ μικρὸν τὸ ἀγ. προστάττεις Luc.
that with which one contends, a prize-essay, declamation, ἀγ. ἐς τὸ παραχρῆμα Thuc.
rivalry, Thuc.
one must contend, Xen., etc.
a rival at the games, competitor, Hdt., etc.:—as adj., ἀγ. ἵπποι race- horses, Plut.
a debater, opponent, Plat.
c. gen. one who struggles for a thing, τῆς ἀρετῆς Aeschin.
fit for contest or debate, Arist.
of persons, contentious, eager for applause, Plat.:—adv. -κῶς, contentiously, ἀγ. ἔχειν to be disposed to fight, Plut.
the office of ἀγωνοθέτης, direction of games, Plut.
to direct the games, exhibit them, Thuc.; ἀγ. Ὀλύμπια Anth.
c. acc., ἀγ. στάσιν to stir up sedition, Plut.
generally, to act as judge, decide, Dem. From
judge of the contests, director of the games, or (later) an exhibitor of games, Hdt., attic
generally, a judge, Xen., etc
a number of people brought together, a gathering, assembly, like ἀγορά, ἵζανεν εὐρὺν ἀγῶνα, λῦτο δ’ ἀγών, ἐν ἀγῶνι νεῶν Hom.: esp. an assembly met to see games, Id., etc.
a place of contest, the arena, Id., etc.; βήτην ἐς μέσσον ἀγῶνα Il.
an assembly of the Greeks at their great national games, ὁ ἐν Ὀλυμπίῃ ἀγών Hdt.; ὁ Ὀλυμπικὸς ἀγών Ar.

the contest for a prize at the games, ἀγὼν ἱππικός, γυμνικός Hdt., etc.; ἀγὼν τῶν ἀνδρῶν, in which the chorus was composed of men, opp. to τῶν παίδων, Dem., etc.:— hence, ἀγῶνα ἄγειν, καθιστάναι, τιθέναι, προτιθέναι, ποιεῖν, to hold or propose a contest; ἀγῶν or ἐν ἀγῶνι νικᾶν, to win one or at one.

generally, any struggle, trial, or danger, πολλοὺς ἀγῶνας ἐξιών, of Hercules, Soph.; ἀγὼν προκέαται, c. inf., it is hard or dangerous to do a thing, Hdt.:— also, ἀγὼν περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς, περὶ μεγίστων a struggle for life and death, for one's highest interests, Eur.
a battle, action, Thuc.
an action at law, trial, Plat., etc.
metaph., οὐ λόγων ἔθ’ ἁγών now is not the time for speaking, etc., Eur.; οὐχ ἕδρας ἀγ. ’tis no time for sitting still, Id.

entry.etym: on the augment in the Doric form ἆγον, see Chantraine, MHG, 311.
entry.sense: to lead or carry, to convey, bring, with living creatures as the object, φέρω being used of things, δῶκε δ’ ἄγειν ἑτάροισι γυναῖκα, καὶ τρίποδα φέρειν Il. (v. infr. 3); ἄγ. εἰς or πρὸς τόπον; poet. also c. acc. loci, ἄγει Ἀχέροντος ἀκτάν Soph.
intr. of soldiers, to march, Xen., etc.; so, ἄγωμεν let us go, NTest.
part. ἄγων is used in sense, taking, στῆσε δ’ ἄγων, where we should use two Verbs, took and placed, Hom.
to take with one, ἑταίρους Id.

to carry off as captives or booty, Id., etc.; mostly in phrase ἄγειν καὶ φέρειν to sweep a country of all its plunder (where φέρειν refers to things, ἄγειν to men and cattle); then c. acc. loci, φέρων καὶ ἄγων τὴν Βιθυνίδα plundering all Bithynia, Xen.; in Pass., ἀγόμεθα, φερόμεθα Eur.
ἄγειν εἰς δίκην or δικαστήριον, ἄγ. ἐπὶ τοὺς δικαστάς to carry one before a court of justice, Lat. rapere in jus, attic; so, simply ἄγειν, Plat.
to fetch, ἄξεθ’ ὑῶν τὸν ἄριστον Od.: of things, to bring in, import, οἶνον νῆες ἄγουσι Il.
to draw on, bring on, πῆμα τόδ’ ἤγαγον Οὐρανίωνες Id.; Ἰλίῳ φθοράν Aesch.
to bear up, φελλοὶ δ’ ὥς, ἄγουσι δίκτυον Id.
to lead towards a point, lead on, τὸν δ’ ἄγε μοῖρα κακὴ θανάτοιο τέλοσδε Il.; also, c. inf., ἄγει θανεῖν leads to death, Eur.: —ὁδὸς ἄγει the road leads, εἰς or ἐπὶ τόπον Soph., Plat.
metaph. to lead, as a general, Il.; ἄγ. στρατιάν, ναῦς, etc., Thuc.; ἄγ. τὴν πολιτείαν to conduct the government, Id.
to bring up, train, educate, Plat.
to draw out in length, τεῖχος ἄγειν to draw a line of wall, Lat. ducere, Thuc.:— Pass., ἦκται ἡ διῶρυξ Hdt.; κόλπου ἀγομένου a bay being formed, Id.
to keep in memory, καί μευ κλέος ἦγον Ἀχαιοί Od.
like agere, to hold, celebrate, ἑορτήν, τὰ Ὀλύμπια Hdt., etc.
also to hold, keep, observe, σπονδὰς ἄγ. πρός τινας Thuc.; εἰρήνην Plat.: often c. acc., as periphrasis for a Verb, σχολὴν ἄγειν = σχολάζειν, Eur.; ἡσυχίαν ἄγ. = ἡσυχάζειν, Xen.
to keep, maintain, ἐλευθέραν ἦγε τὴν Ἑλλάδα Dem.
of Time, to pass, ποίας ἡμέρας δοκεῖς μ’ ἄγειν; Soph.

like ἡγέομαι, Lat. ducere, to hold, account, reckon, ἐν τιμῇ ἄγειν, ἐν οὐδεμιῇ μοίρῃ, περὶ πλείστου ἄγειν Hdt.; θεοὺς ἄγειν to believe in gods, Aesch.; τιμιώτερον ἀγ. τινά Thuc.: —so with Adverbs, δυσφόρως ἄγ. to think insufferable, Soph.; ἐντίμως ἄγειν Plat.
to weigh so much, ἄγειν μνᾶν, τριακοσίους δαρεικούς to weigh a mina, 300 darics, Dem., where the acc. is the weight which the thing weighs or draws down: cf. ἕλκω.
on ἄγε, ἄγετε, v. sub vocc.
Mid. ἄγομαι, to carry away for oneself, take with one, χρυσόν τε καὶ ἄργυρον οἴκαδ’ ἄγεσθαι Od.

ἄγεσθαι γυναῖκα, Lat. uxorem ducere, to take to oneself a wife, Id.; in full, ἄγ. γυναῖκα ἐς τὰ οἰκία Hdt.; and simply ἄγεσθαι, to marry, Il., etc.;—also of the father, to bring home a wife for his son, Od.
διὰ στόμα ἄγεσθαι μῦθον to let pass through the mouth, i. e. to utter, Il.
ἄγεσθαί τι ἐς χεῖρας to take a thing into one's hands, and so to undertake, Hdt.
ignorance or unskilfulness in doing, c. inf., Od.
unknowing, ignorant of a thing, c. gen., Il.; κακῶν ἀδαήμονες Od.
= ἀδαήμων, c. gen. pers., Hdt.; c.gen. rei, Id.; c. inf. unknowing how to do, Soph.: absol., Xen.
unknown, Hes.
of which none might eat, Aesch.
without tears, Isocr., Plut.
without tears, i. e.
act. tearless, ἀδ. καὶ ἀπήμων Il.; ἀδακρύτω ἔχεν ὄσσε Od.: —εὐνάζειν ἀδακρύτων βλεφάρων πόθον to lull the desire of her eyes so that they weep no more, Soph.; cf. ἄδερκτος,
pass. unwept, unmourned, Id.
costing no tears, τρόπαια Plut.
adamantine, Aesch., etc.: —metaph. hard as adamant, σιδηροῖς καὶ ἀδαμαντίνοις λόγοις Plat.; οὐκ ἀδ. ἐντί, of a girl, Theocr.:—adv. -νως, Plat.
iron-bound, Aesch.
properly the untamed, unconquerable:
as Subst. adamant, i. e. the hardest metal, prob. steel: metaph. of any thing unalterable, ἔπος ἐρέω ἀδάμαντι πελάσσας having fixed it firm as adamant, Orac. ap. Hdt.
the diamond, Theophr.
as adj., metaph., the inflexible, of Hades, Theocr.
epith. of Hades, inflexible, Il.:—later in the proper sense, untamed, unbroken, ἵππος Xen.
unconquered, Aesch., etc.; of females, unwedded, Soph.: of beasts, untamed, v. sub πέσημα. [ᾱδαματω in Theocr.]
without expense, costing nothing, γλυκέα κἀδάπανα (crasis for καὶ ἀδάπανα) Ar.:— adv., ἀδαπάνως τέρψαι φρένα Eur.
undivided, Soph.
without fear, fearless, εἴ περ ἀδειής τ’ ἐστί, of Hector, Il.; κύον ἀδδεές Id.
fearless, secure (v. ἀλεής), τὸ ἀδεές, security, Thuc.; ἀδεὴς θανάτου without fear of death, Plat.; ἀδεὲς δέος δεδιέναι to fear where no fear is, Id.
causing no fear, not formidable, πρὸς ἐχθρούς Thuc.
adv. ἀδεῶς, without fear, confidently, Hdt., etc.
without stint, freely, Thuc.

freedom from fear, ἀδείην διδόναι to grant an amnesty, indemnity, Hdt.; ἐν ἀδείῃ εἶναι Id.; τῶν σωμάτων ἄδειαν ποιεῖν Thuc.; ἄδειάν τινι παρασκευάζειν, παρέχειν Dem.; opp. to ἄδειαν λαμβάνειν to receive indemnity, Id.; ἀδείας τυγχάνειν Id.
fearless, dauntless, Pind., etc.:—adv. -τως, Aesch.
where no fear is, οἰκία Luc.
supperless, Xen., etc.
unbribed, Arist.:—comp. adv. -ότερον Luc.
not tithed, tithe-free, Ar.
fem. of ἀδελφός, a sister, Trag., etc.
a sister (as a fellow Christian), NTest.
a brother's or sister's son, a nephew, Hdt.
a brother's or sister's daughter, a niece, Ar., etc.
murdering a brother or sister, Hdt. (in ionic form ἀδελφεοκτ-) , Plut.

entry.etym: α copul. , δελφύς; cf. Lat. couterinus
entry.sense: ἀδελφοί are properly sons of the same mother:

as Subst., ἀδελφός, ὁ, voc. ἄδελφε (not -φέ), ionic ἀδελφεός, epic -ειός:—a brother, or generally, a near kinsman, ἀδελφοί brother and sister, like Lat. fratres, Eur.; ἀδελφεοὶ ἀπ’ ἀμφοτέρων brothers by both parents, i. e. not half-brothers, Hdt.
a brother (as a fellow Christian), NTest.
adj., ἀδελφός, ή, όν, brotherly or sisterly, Trag., Plat.
like Lat. geminus, gemellus, of anything in pairs, twin, Xen.:—then, just like, c. gen. or dat., ἀδελφὰ τῶνδε, ἀδελφὰ τούτοισι Soph.
the brotherhood, NTest.
left-handed, awkward, Luc.
unseen, invisible, Anth.
not seeing, ἀδέρκτων ὀμμάτων τητώμενος reft of thine eyes so that they see not, Soph.; adv. -τως, without looking, Id.
unfettered, unbound, ἄδ. φυλακή, Lat. libera custodia, our "parole," Thuc., etc.; δεσμὸς ἄδεσμος bond that is no bond, of a wreath, Eur.
without master, Plat., etc.
unbound, free, Dem.
a word used by Hom. only in Od. as epith. of ὄλεθρος, πότμος, φῆμις, commonly expl. not sweet, bitter, cruel (from an old word δευκής sweet); but more prob. it means unexpected, sudden (from δοκ-έω).
untanned, of a raw hide, Od.

entry.etym: only found in two Homeric forms, aor1 opt. and perf. part.
entry.sense: to be sated, μὴ ξεῖνος δείπνῳ ἀδήσειε lest he should be sated with the repast, feel loathing at it; καμάτῳ ἀδηκότες ἠδὲ καὶ ὕπνῳ sated with toil and sleep.
unassailed, unravaged, Soph.
unbitten, not gnawed or worm eaten , Hes.; adv. ἀδήκτως, Plut.
to be in the dark about a thing, Soph.
uncertainty, Anth.
not seen or known, unknown, obscure, Hes., Soph., Plat.
of things, ἄδ. θάνατοι death by an unknown hand, Soph.; ἄδ. ἔχθρα secret enmity, Thuc.; ῥεῖ πᾶν ἄδηλον melts all to nothing, Soph.; ἄδ. τινι unseen, unobserved by him, Xen.
neut. ἄδηλόν [ἐστι] εἰ . . , ὅτι . . , it is uncertain whether . . , unknown that . . , Plat., etc.; so, ἄδηλον μή . . , Id.:— absol., ἄδηλον ὄν it being uncertain, Thuc.; so, ἐν ἀδηλοτέρῳ εἶναι Xen.
ἄδηλος often agrees with the subject (like δίκαιός εἰμι), παῖδες ἄδηλοι ὁποτέρων = ἄδηλόν ἐστιν ὁποτέρων παῖδες εἰσίν Lys., etc.
adv. -λως, secretly, Thuc., etc.; Sup. -ότατα, Id.
to be sorely troubled, Plat.; ἀδημονῆσαι τὰς ψυχάς Xen.
trouble, distress, Anth., Plut.

entry.etym: α short, except in first place cited from Il., where it is commonly written ἄδδην.
entry.sense: adv., Lat. satis, to one's fill, ἔδμεναι ἄδην to eat their fill, Il.

c. gen., οἵ μιν ἄδην ἐλόωσι πολέμοιο who may drive him to satiety of war, Id.; ἅδην ἔλειξεν αἵματος licked his fill of blood, Aesch.; καὶ τούτων μὲν ἅδην enough of this, Plat.; c. part., ἄδην εἶχον κτείνοντες Hdt.
without strife, Anth.
without strife or battle, Il.
unconquerable, ἀνάγκης σθένος Aesch.

entry.etym: αιδης in Hom., attic ᾱͅδης; but in Trag. also ᾱιδας:— gen. αιδεω as an anapaest in Hom.; gen. αιδᾱο Id=Hom.; gen. ᾱιδος before a vowel, Il.
entry.sense: Hades or Pluto (cf. Πλούτων), the god of the nether world, son of Kronus and Rhea, brother to Zeus, Ζεὺς καὶ ἐγώ, τρίτατος δ’ Ἄιδης Il.; called Ζεὺς καταχθόνιος Id.; εἰν or εἰς Ἀΐδαο (sc. δόμοις, δόμους) in, into the nether world, Hom.; εἰν Ἄϊδος Il.; ἐν Ἅιδου, ἐς Ἅιδου (sc. οἴκῳ, οἶκον) attic:— also Ἄϊδόσδε adv., Il.
as appellative,Hades, the world below, εἰσόκεν ἄϊδι κεύθωμαι Id.; ἐπὶ τὸν ᾅδην Luc.; εἰς ἀΐδην Anth.; ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ NTest.
the grave, death, ᾅδης πόντιος death by sea, Aesch., etc.
eating one's fill, gluttonous, ἀδ. ἀνήρ, of an athlete, Theocr.; τὴν ἀδ. νόσον this devouring sore, Soph.
not ravaged, Xen.
not to be passed, ποταμός, νάπος Xen.
not listening to slander, Plut.
intestate, Plut.
undecided, Luc.
unintermitting, incessant, NTest.; adv. -τως, Polyb., NTest.
undissolved, indissoluble, Plat.
unwetted, Simon.
ἀδίαντον, τό, a plant, maiden-hair, Theocr.
with no way back, of Hades, Eur.
incorruption, uprightness, NTest.
uncorrupted, Plat., etc.:— adv. -ρως, Aeschin.
of judges and witnesses, incorruptible, Plat., etc.: Sup. adv. -ώτατα, Id.
imperishable, Id.
untaught, ignorant, c. gen., ἀδ. ἐρώτων Anth.
untrained, of a chorus, Dem.
of things, untaught, Plut., Luc.
act., unable to get out, Anth.
unquestioned, Plut.
indescribable, Xen., Dem.
undecided, Luc.

to do wrong, Hdt., etc.; τἀδικεῖν wrong-doing, Soph.; τὸ μἀδικεῖν righteous dealing, Aesch.; but, σχήσει τὸ μἀδικεῖν will restrain wrong-doing, Aesch.:—in legal phrase the particular case of wrong is added in part., Σωκράτης ἀδικεῖ διδάσκων Plat., Xen.:—c. acc. cogn., ἀδικίαν, ἀδίκημα, Plat., or a neut. adj., ἀδικεῖν πολλά, μέγαλα, Id.; οὐδέν, μηδὲν ἀδ., Plat.:—also, ἀδ. περὶ τὰ μυστήρια Dem.

trans. c. acc. pers. to do one wrong, to wrong, injure, Hdt., etc.:—c. dupl. acc. to wrong one in a thing, Ar., etc.; τὰ μέγιστα ἀδ. τινά Dem.; ἀδ. τινὰ περί τινος Plat.:—Pass. to be wronged, μὴ δῆτ’ ἀδικηθῶ Soph.; ἀδικεῖσθαι εἴς τι Eur.
to spoil, damage, ἀδ. γῆν Thuc.
a wrong done, a wrong, Lat. injuria, Hdt., etc.:—c. gen. a wrong done to one, Dem.
that which is got by wrong, ill-gotten goods, Plat.
one must do wrong, Plat.
wrong-doing, injustice, Hdt., etc.
like ἀδίκημα, a wrong, injury, Id., Plat.
a wrong, wrong-dealing, Hdt.
ἀδικίου γραφή, an action against public wrong-doers, Plut.
of persons, wrong-doing, unrighteous, unjust, Hes., Hdt., etc.; ἀδικώτατος Soph.:— ἄδ. εἴς τι unjust in a thing, ἔς τινα towards a person, Hdt.; περί τινα Xen.; c. inf. so unjust as to . . NTest.
ἄδ. ἵπποι obstinate, unmanageable, Xen.
of things, wrongly done, wrong, unjust, ἔργματα Theogn., Hdt., etc.; τὸ δίκαιον καὶ τὸ ἄδ., τὰ δίκαια καὶ ἄδικα right and wrong, Plat.
adv. -κως, Solon, etc.; τοὺς ἀδ. θνήσκοντας Soph.; εἴτε δικαίως εἴτε ἀδ. jure an injuria, Hdt.; οὐκ ἀδ. not without reason, Plat.
close-packed: (v. ἁδρός):— hence,
crowded, thronging, of bees, flies, sheep, Hom.; ἀδινὰ δάκρυα thick-falling tears, Soph.

vehement, loud, of sounds, Il.; Σειρῆνες ἀδιναί the loud-voiced Sirens, Od.:—adv. -νῶς, frequently, or loudly, vehemently, Il.; so ἀδινόν and ἀδινά as adv., ἀδινὸν κλαίειν, μυκᾶσθαι, στοναχῆσαι Hom.: comp. ἀδινώτερον Od.
not corrected, not set right, Dem.:—of books, unrevised, Cic.
not doubted; adv. -τως, Anth.
not suffering from thirst, Eur., etc.
untamed, of cattle, Od.
of maidens, unwedded, Id.
in Hom. only in fem. and of cattle, unbroken, βοῦν ἀδμήτην, ἢν οὔ πω ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἤγαγεν ἀνήρ Il.; ἵππον ἑξέτε’ ἀδμήτην Id.
like ἀδμής, unwedded, of maidens, Hhymn.
unexpected, Hes., Soph., etc.; τὸ ἀδ. the unexpectedness, Thuc.
adv. -τως, Id.; so ἀδόκητα as adv., Eur.; ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀδοκήτου Thuc.
untried, unproved, in regard to civic rights, Lys., etc.
not standing the test, spurious, properly of coin, Plat.
metaph. of persons, rejected as false, disreputable, reprobate, Eur., Xen., etc.
to talk idly, prate, Plat., Xen.

entry.etym: Prob. from ἄδην λέσχη, talking to satiety.
entry.sense: a garrulous fellow, idle talker, Ar., Plat.
garrulity, idle talk, Ar., Plat., etc.; Theophr. wrote περὶ ἀδολεσχίας.
without fraud, guileless, of treaties, σπονδαὶ ἄδ. καὶ ἀβλαβεῖς Thuc.:—adv., often in the phrase ἀδόλως καὶ δικαίως, Lat. sine dolo malo, Id.
of liquids, unadulterated, genuine, Aesch.; metaph. guileless, pure, Eur.
unshaken, Anth.
not matter of opinion, i. e. certain, Plat.
to be held in no esteem, to stand in ill repute, Eur., Dem.
trans. to hold in no esteem, τινα Plut.
ill-repute, disgrace, Thuc., Plat.; obscurity, Plut.
inglorious, disreputable, Xen., Dem.: —of persons, obscure, ignoble, Xen., etc.:—adv. -ξως, Plut.
satiety, loathing, Il.
without gifts, Hhymn.
unattended by slaves, Eur.
noiseless, Anth.
inactive, powerless, Babr., Anth.
intractable, of iron, Plut.

entry.etym: Perhaps from α privat. , διδράσκω a name of Nemesis.
entry.sense: Aesch., the Inevitable.
not running away, not inclined to do so, of slaves, Hdt.
from the Adriatic; Ἀδριᾱκός ἀμφιφορεύς, i. e. a cask of Italian wine, Anth.
Adriatic, Eur.
the Adriatic, Hdt., etc.
to come to one's strength, Plat.
in the primary sense it seems to mean thick: (akin to ἀδ-ινός, as κυδρός to κυδνός):
of things, χιόνα ἁδρὴν πίπτουσαν falling thick, Hdt.:— strong, great in any way, ἁδρὸς πόλεμος Ar.
of persons, large, fine, well-grown, Hdt., Plat.; of animals, Xen., Babr.; of fruit or corn, full-grown, ripe, Hdt.
= ἁδροτής, of ears of corn, Hes.
strength, Il.
abundance, NTest.

entry.etym: = Ἁμαδρυάς, a kind of nymph, Hamadryad, Anth.

entry.sense: to make ripe, ripen, Xen.
Pass. to grow ripe, ripen, of fruit or corn, Hdt., etc.
want of strength or power, inability, incapacity, Hdt., etc.; c. gen., ἀδ. τοῦ ἀδικεῖν for wrong-doing, Plat.
poverty, Xen., Dem., etc.
Hdt., etc.; c. gen., ἀδ. τοῦ λέγειν Thuc.
of persons, to want strength, Plat., etc.; c. inf. to be unable to do, Xen.
of things, to be impossible, NTest.
of persons, unable to do a thing, c. inf., Hdt., Eur., etc.

absol. without strength, powerless, Hdt., Eur., etc.; οἱ ἀδύνατοι men disabled for service, incapable, Aeschin., etc.; ἀδύνατος χρήμασι poor, Thuc.; εἴς τι Plat.:—of ships, disabled, Hdt.:— τὸ ἀδ. want of strength, Plat.; τὰ ἀδ. disabilities, Dem.
of things, that cannot be done, impossible, Eur., Plat., etc.; ἀδύνατόν or ἀδύνατά [ἐστι], it is impossible, Hdt., etc.: τὸ ἀδ. impossibility, Id.; τολμᾶν ἀδύνατα, ἀδυνάτων ἐρᾶν Eur.
the innermost sanctuary, Il., etc.
not to be entered, Il., etc.
Ἀδωνιάζουσαι, αἱ, those who keep the Adonia, the title of the 15th Id. of Theocr.
the mourning for Adonis, celebrated yearly by Greek matrons:
Adonis, favourite of Aphrodite, Sapph.; ὥδωνις, crasis for ὁ Ἄδ., Theocr.:—generally, an Adonis, a darling, Luc.
Ἀδώνιδος κῆποι, quick-growing herbs grown in pots for the Adonia, Plat.
Aeschin.: adv. -τως, Dem.
incorruptible, Anth.
without gifts, taking none, incorruptible, c. gen., ἀδωρότατος χρημάτων Thuc.
giving no gifts, ἀδώροις ἐλαφηβολίαις by hunting from which no gifts were offered, Soph.
ἄδωρα δῶρα gifts that are no gifts, like βίος ἀβίωτος, Id.
one who gives nothing, Hes.
continually thrown, Anth.
epith. of the gods, like αἰὲν ἐόντες, everlasting, immortal, θεῶν αἰειγενετάων, θεοῖς αἰειγενέτῃσιν Il.
everlasting, Plat., Xen.
without form, incorporeal, Plat.
ever-revolving, Anth.

entry.etym: compare the morphological problems with ἀείρω
entry.sense: to sing, Il., etc.:—then of any sound, to twang, of the bowstring, Od.; to whistle, of the wind, Mosch.; to ring, of a stone struck, Theocr.
trans.,
c. acc. rei, to sing, chant, μῆνιν, παιήονα, κλέα ἀνδρῶν Hom.:—absol., ἀείδειν ἀμφί τινος to sing in one's praise, Od.:—Pass., of songs, to be sung, Hdt.; ᾆσμα καλῶς ᾀσθέν Xen.
c. acc. pers. to sing, praise, attic
ever-living, φύτλη Anth.
ever-green, Anth.

unseemly, shameful, ἀεικέα λοιγὸν ἀμύνειν Il.; ἀεικέα [εἵματα] Od.; δεσμὸς ἀεικής Aesch.; στολή Soph.; ἀεικέστερα ἔπεα Hdt.; οὐδὲν ἀεικὲς παρέχεσθαι to cause no inconvenience, Hdt.:—adv. ἀεικῶς; ionic -έως, Simon.; ἀεικές as adv., Od.
unseemly, shabby, μισθός, ἄποινα Il.
οὐδὲν ἀεικές ἐστι, c. inf., it is nothing strange that . . , Hdt., Aesch. Cf. attic αἰκής.
unseemly treatment, outrage, Hom., Hdt.:—Cf. attic αἰκία.
to treat unseemly, injure, abuse, Hom.; οὐ γὰρ ἐγώ σ’ ἔκπαγλον ἀεικιῶ I will do thee no great dishonour, Il.:—Mid. in act. sense, Id.
a continual talking:— as attic law-term, τὴν ἀ. προτείνεσθαι or παρέχειν to court continual inquiry into one's conduct, Dem.
ever to be remembered, Trag., Thuc. adv. -τως, Aeschin.
ever-fasting, Anth.
ever a virgin, Sapph.

entry.etym: The Root is ΑΕϜ ; cf. Lat. aevum, aetas, i. e. aeuitas.
entry.sense: always, for ever, Hom., etc.; often with other words of time, διαμπερὲς αἰεί, συνεχὲς αἰεί, ἐμμενὲς αἰεί, Id.; ἀεὶ καθ’ ἡμέραν, καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀεί, ἀεὶ καὶ καθ’ ἡμέραν, ἀεὶ κατ’ ἐνιαυτόν, ἀεὶ διὰ βίου, etc., Plat., etc.; v. εἰσαεί:—ὁ ἀεὶ χρόνος eternity, Hdt., Plat.; οἱ ἀεὶ ὄντες the immortals, Xen., etc.:—but, ὁ αἰεὶ βασιλεύων the king for the time being, Hdt.; τοῖσι τούτων αἰεὶ ἐκγόνοισι to their descendants for ever, Id.
ever-flowing, κρήνη Soph.

entry.etym: ᾱ̓ρῶ contr. as if from ἀερῶ, which is not in use. Compare the morphological problems of ἀείδω.
entry.sense: to lift, heave, raise up, Hom., etc.; ἱστία στεῖλαν ἀείραντες furled the sails by brailing them up, Od.:—esp. to lift for the purpose of carrying, to bear away, carry, Il.; ἄχθος ἀείρειν, of ships of burden, Od.; μή μοι οἶνον ἄειρε offer me not wine, Il.
to raise, levy, λεκτὸν ἀροῦμεν στόλον Aesch.
Mid. to lift up for oneself, i. e. bear off, c. acc. rei, Il.
to raise or stir up, ἀείρασθαι πόλεμον to undertake a long war, Hdt.; βαρὺς ἀείρεσθαι slow to undertake, Id.
ἀείρασθαι τὰ ἱστία to hoist sail, with or without ἱστία, Id.
Pass. to be lifted or carried up, Od.; ἀείρεσθαι εἰς . . to rise up and go to a place, Hdt.;—mostly of seamen, but also of land-journeys, Id.
to be suspended, πὰρ κουλεὸν αἰὲν ἄωρτο [the dagger] hung always by the sword-sheath, Il.
metaph. to be lifted up, excited, Soph.
poet. and ionic for ᾆσμα, Hdt., etc.
ever-burning, Anth.
ever-watching, i. e. ever-lasting, οἴκησις ἀείφρ., of the grave, Soph.
perpetual exile, Plat.
everlasting, Anth.
particip. form = ἀέκων,against one's will, unwilling Od.; πόλλ’ ἀεκαζόμενος, Virgil's multa reluctans, Id.
against one's will, Hom.; c. gen., σεῦ ἀέκητι, ἀέκητι σέθεν, Lat. te invito, and θεῶν ἀέκητι, ἀέκητι θεῶν, Id.
against one's will, involuntary, of acts, Hdt., etc.
of persons, only in adv. ἀκουσίως, involuntarily, Thuc.
against one's will, unwilling, of persons, ἀέκοντος ἐμεῖο Il.; πόλλ’ ἀέκων, Virgil's multa reluctans, Id.; ἄκοντος Διός, invito Jove, Aesch., Xen.:—adv. ἀκόντως, unwillingly, Plat.
like ἀκούσιος, of acts, involuntary, ἔργα Soph.
storm-swift, πελειάς Soph.
a stormy wind, whirlwind, eddy, Hom.; ἄελλαι ἀνέμων Id.
metaph. of any whirling motion, ὠκυδρόμοις ἀέλλαις, of an animal, Eur.; ἄστρων ὑπ’ ἀέλλαισι Id.
eddying, Il.
struggling with the storm, Anth.

entry.etym: poetic for ἀελλόπους, compare ἀρτίπος, Οἰδίπος
entry.sense: storm-footed, storm-swift, Il., etc.
storm, a Harpy, Hes.
to have no hope, only in part., ἀελπτέοντες σόον εἶναι Il.; ἀ. ὑπερβαλέεσθαι Hdt.
unhoped for, unexpected, Od.
an unlooked for event, ἐξ ἀελπτίης unexpectedly, Archil.
= ἀελπτής, Hhymn.; ἐξ ἀέλπτου unexpectedly, Hdt.; so, ἐξ ἀέλπτων Soph.
beyond hope, despaired of, Solon.
act. hopeless, desperate, Hhymn., Aesch.
adv. -τως, beyond all hope, Lat. insperato, Id=Aesch.:—neut. pl. as adv., Eur.
ever-flowing, Hes., Hdt., Trag.
generally, everlasting, ἀρετᾶς ἀέναον κλέος Simon.;—rare in attic Prose, Xen., Plat.
nourishing leaves, leafy, Aesch.
nourishing plants, Ἠώς Anth.

entry.etym: poetic form of αὔξω, compare αὐξάνω
entry.sense: to increase, enlarge, foster, strengthen, μένος μέγα θυμὸς ἀέξει Il.; θυμὸν ἀέξειν Id.; πένθος ἀ. to cherish woe, Od.; υἱὸν ἀ. to rear him to man's estate, Id.; ἔργον ἀέξουσι θεοί they bless the work, Id.
to exalt by one's deeds, to magnify, τὸ πλῆθος ἀέξειν Hdt.; to magnify, exaggerate, [ἀγγελίαν] μῦθος ἀέξει Soph.

Pass. to increase, grow, ἀέξετο he was waxing tall, Od.; οὐ ποτ’ ἀέξετο κῦμα no wave rose high, Id.; χόλος ἐν στήθεσσιν ἀέξεται rises high, Il.; τόδε ἔργον ἀ. it prospers, Od.; ἀέξετο ἱερὸν ἦμαρ was getting on to noon, Il.; so, κέρδος ἀέξεται Aesch.
a not working, idleness, Od., Hes.:—Cf. attic ἀργία.
not-working, idle, Hom., Hes., etc.;— ἀεργοὶ δόμοι idle houses, i. e. where people are idle, Theocr.—Cf. attic ἀργός.
lifting up, Aesch.—Cf. attic ἄρδην.
in the mist or thick air of morning, Eur.
in the air, high in air, Id.
to walk the air, Ar., Plat.
one who walks the air, Plut.
wheeling in air, Anth.
air-tossed, soaring, Ar.
to traverse the air, Luc.
an air-raven, Luc.
an air-gnat, Luc.
an air-battle, Luc.
to measure the air: to lose oneself in vague speculation, Xen.
floating in air, of clouds, Ar.
roaming in air, Aesch. ap. Ar.
high-soaring, Hes., Anth.
lifting the feet, brisk-trotting, ἵπποι Il.

entry.etym: ἀερτάζω is a lengthd. epic form of ἀείρω.
entry.sense: to lift up:— imperf. ἠέρταζον, Anth.

entry.etym: from a form ἀέω, not in use. Akin to ἄημι, ἄω1, ἰαύω.
entry.sense: to sleep, Od.
silliness, folly, Od., Hes.
damaged in mind, witless, silly, Hom., Hes.
an eagle, Hom., etc.:—proverb., ἀετὸς ἐν νεφέλαισι, of a thing quite out of reach, Ar.
an eagle as a standard, of the Persians, Xen.; of the Romans, Plut.
in architecture, the pediment of a temple, Ar.
a standard-bearer, Plut.
eagle-like, Luc.
dry, parched, Hom.; βῶν ἀζαλέην the dry bull's-hide, Il.
metaph. dry, harsh, Anth.
act. parching, scorching, Σείριος Hes.
to dry, parch up, Hhymn.
drought: in Od. an old shield is said to be πεπαλαγμένον ἄζῃ coated with dry dirt or mould.
freedom from jealousy, Plut.
not subject to envy, unenviable, dreary, Simon., Aesch., etc.
generally, sorry, inconsiderable, Plut.
free from jealousy, envy, Plut.
not to be envied, Plat.
free from further payment: without loss, scot-free, Lat. immunis, Hdt., etc.:—unpunished, not deserving punishment, Soph., Eur.
act. harmless, of sour looks, Thuc.

entry.etym: epic word, perhaps an old dialectic form for ἀδιεχής, α copulat. , διέχω, v. sub ζα-.
entry.sense: unceasing, excessive, Il.; neut. as adv., ἀζηχὲς φαγέμεν καὶ πιέμεν Od.; ὄϊες ἀζ. μεμακυῖαι Il.
to stand in awe of, dread, esp. the gods and one's parents, Hom.; followed by inf., to shrink from doing, Id.; also ἅζομαι μὴ . . , Il.
absol. in part. awe-struck, Od., Soph.
unwedded, κοίτη Luc.
of bread, unleavened, ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀζύμων or τὰ ἄζυμα the feast of unleavened bread, NTest.
unyoked, unpaired, unmarried, Eur.; of Pallas the virgin goddess, Id.: with a gen. added, ἄζυξ λέκτρων, γάμων, εὐνῆς, Lat. nuptiarum expers, Id.
to dry up, parch, Hes.:—Pass., αἴγειρος ἀζομένη κεῖται the poplar lies drying, Il.
ungirt, from hurry, Hes.
unpleasant to the taste, distasteful, of food, Plat.
generally, unpleasant, οὐδὲν οἱ ἀηδέστερον ἔσεσθαι Hdt.: in Plat. of talk, ἀηδές or οὐκ ἀηδές ἐστι.
of persons, disagreeable, odious, Id.
adv. -δῶς, unpleasantly, Id.; ἀηδῶς ἔχειν τινί to be on bad terms with one, Dem.
without pleasure to oneself, unwillingly, Plat.
unpleasantness, nauseousness, of drugs, Hipp.
of persons, odiousness, Dem., etc.
a being ill-pleased, disgust, dislike, Plat.
a young nightingale, Theocr., in epic pl. ἀηδονιδῆες.
of a nightingale, γόος, νόμος ἀ. the nightingale's dirge, Aesch.
a nightingale, Eur., Theocr.; Μουσάων ἀηδονίς, of a poet, Anth.
the songstress, i. e. the nightingale, Hes., etc.; of the daughter of Pandareus, who was changed into a nightingale, Hom.
unaccustomedness, Batr.; ἀήθ. τινος inexperience of a thing, Thuc.
to be unaccustomed to a thing, c. gen., Il.
unwonted, unusual, Aesch.:—adv. -θως, unexpectedly, Thuc.
of persons, unused to a thing, c. gen., Id., Dem.
a blast, gale, Aesch., Soph.
to breathe hard, blow, of winds, Hom.:—Pass. to be beaten by the wind, ὑόμενος καὶ ἀήμενος Od.: metaph., to toss or wave about, as if by the wind, δίχα θυμὸς ἄητο, i. e. was in doubt or fear, Il.

the lower air, the air that surrounds the earth, opp. to αἰθήρ the upper air (v. Il. 14. 288, where a tall pine μακροτάτη πεφυυῖα δι’ ἠέρος αἰθέρ’ ἵκανεν); hence mist, gloom, περὶ δ’ ἠέρα πουλὺν ἔχευεν Il.; ἠέρα μὲν σκέδασε Id.; cf. ἠέριος, ἠεροειδής.
generally, air, Soph., etc.; ἀέρα δέρειν (cf. Virg. verberat auras), NTest.
a blowing, Eur.
unconquered, Thuc., Dem.
unconquerable, Plat.
wicked, Il.
light as air, small, little, Aesch.
a blast, gale, Hom., etc.
stormy, furious, θάρσος ἄητον Il.
unused to the sea, a land-lubber, Ar.
not verdant, withered, Plut.
without warmth, Anth.
fearless, Ibyc., Plut.
immortality, Plat., etc.
to make immortal, to hold oneself immortal, Hdt.
undying, immortal, Hom., etc.:— ἀθάνατοι, οἱ, the Immortals, Hom., etc.; ἀθάναται ἅλιαι, i. e. the sea goddesses, Od.: comp. -ώτερος, Plat.
of immortal fame, Tyrtae.
of things, everlasting, Od., Hdt., etc.
ἀθ. θρίξ the hair on which life depended, Aesch.
οἱ ἀθάνατοι the immortals, a body of Persian troops in which every vacancy was at once filled up, Hdt.
adv., ἀθανάτως εὕδειν Anth.
entry.etym: ᾱθ- always in the adj. and all derivs., v. A α, fin.

entry.sense: unburied, Il., etc.
unworthy of burial, Anth.
groats or meal, porridge, Ar., etc.
discouraged, downhearted, Plut.: τὸ ἀθαρσές want of courage, Id. adv. -σῶς, Id.
unseen, invisible, Plut., Luc.
that may not be seen, secret, Plut.
act. not seeing, blind to a thing, c. gen., Xen.
without the aid of God, οὐκ ἀθεεί, Hor.'s non sine Dis, Od.
uninspired, Plut.
implacable, Aesch.
lawless, Pind., Eur.
lawless, godless, ἀθεμίστια εἰδώς versed in wickedness, Od.
lawless, without law or government, of the Cyclopes, Od.; ἀθεμιστότεροι Xen.
of things, lawless, unlawful, ἀθέμιτα ἔργα, ἀθέμιτα ἔρδειν Hdt.; ἀθ. ποιεῖν, εὔχεσθαι Xen.
without God, denying the gods, Plat.
godless, ungodly, Trag.:—comp. -ώτερος Lys.; Sup. -ώτατος Xen.
abandoned of the gods, Soph.
adv. -ως, impiously, Id.; Sup. -ώτατα, in most unholy wise, Id.
ungodliness, Plat.
uncared for, of animals, Xen.: τὸ ἀθ. neglect of one's appearance, Luc.
unhealed, incurable, Id.
to slight, make light of, Lat. nihil curare, c. acc. pers., Hom.
not heated by strife or passion, Aesch.
without heat: τὸ ἄθερμον want of heat, Plat.
beyond even a god's power to express: ineffable, aweful, ὄμβρος, θάλασσα, νύξ Hom.; also marvellous in quantity, ἀθ. οἶνος, σῖτος, βόες Od.
to set aside: ἀθ. τινα to deny one, refuse his request, NTest.
set aside:— adv. -τως, = ἀθέσμως, lawlessly, despotically, Aesch.
without observation:— adv. -τως, Plut.
unfeminine, Plut.
to Athens, Thuc., Xen.
the temple of Athena, Hdt.
Athenian, of or from Athens, Il., etc
the city of Athens, used in pl., because it consisted of several parts (cf. Θῆβαι, Μυκῆναι, Hom., etc.; the sg. (like Θήβη) Od.
from Athens, Lys., etc.; poet. Ἀθήνοθεν Anth.
Athena, goddess of wisdom, warlike prowess, and skill in the arts, often called Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη.
at Athens, Dem.
to long to be at Athens, Luc.
not hunted, Xen.
consumer of ears of corn, of a winnowing fan, Od.
without wild beasts or game, Hdt.: τὸ ἄθηρον absence of game, Plut.
an ear of corn, Hes.
husks, chaff, Luc.
the point of a weapon, Aesch., etc.
untouched, of a virgin, Anth.
untouched: c. gen. untouched by a thing, Soph.; κερδῶν ἄθικτον βουλευτήριον untouched by gain, i. e. incorruptible, Aesch.; also c. dat., νόσοις ἄθ. Id.
not to be touched, holy, sacred, of Delphi, Soph.; ἄθικτα holy things, Aesch.
to contend for a prize, combat, wrestle, Il.; ἀθλεύων πρὸ ἄνακτος struggling or suffering for him, Id.
Λαομέδοντι ἀθλήσαντες having contended with him, Il.; πολλά περ ἀθλήσαντα having gone through many struggles, Id.: to contend in battle, πρός τινα Hdt.
a contest, Plat., etc.
an implement of labour, Theocr.
a contest, struggle, NTest.
a prizefighter, Lat. athleta: as adj., ἀθλ. ἵππος a race-horse, Lys.
c. gen. rei, practised in a thing, Plat.

entry.etym: attic contr. of epic ἀέθλιος, see also ἄεθλον, ἆθλον
entry.sense: gaining the prize, or running for it (this sense only in epic form) ἵππος ἀεθλίη a race-horse, Theogn.; μῆλον ἀέθλ. the apple of discord, Anth.

metaph. struggling, wretched, miserable (this sense only in attic form), of persons Aesch., etc.: comp. -ιώτερος Soph.: Sup. -ιώτατος Eur.:—also of states of life, γάμοι, βίος, τύχη Trag.: —adv. -ίως, miserably, Soph.
in moral sense, pitiful, wretched, Dem.
without any moral sense, wretched, sorry, θηρσὶν ἀθλία βορά Eur.:—adv., ἀθλίως καὶ κακῶς with wretched success, Dem.
suffering, wretchedness, Plat., etc.
one who awards the prize, the judge in the games, Plat., etc.

entry.etym: contr. from epic and ionic ἄεθλον
entry.sense: the prize of contest, Hom., etc.; ἄεθλα κεῖται or πρόκειται prizes are proposed, Hdt.; ἆθλα προφαίνειν, προτιθέναι, τιθέναι to propose prizes, Xen.; ἆθλα λαμβάνειν or φέρεσθαι to win prizes, Plat.; ἆθλα πολέμου, τῆς ἀρετῆς Dem.
= ἆθλος, a contest, Od.:—metaph. a conflict, struggle, Aesch., Soph.

entry.etym: contr. from epic and ionic ἄεθλος
entry.sense: a contest for a prize, Hom., etc.; ἄεθλος πρόκειται a task is set one, Hdt.; ἄεθλον προτιθέναι to set it, Id.;—metaph. a conflict, struggle, Aesch.
bearing away the prize, victorious, ἵππος Il.; in ionic form ἀεθλ-, Id., Hdt.
not turbid, clear, Luc.
untroubled, of water, Hes.
undisturbed: τὸ ἀθ. tranquillity, Xen.
without uproar, Plat.:—adv. -βως, Eur.
unbroken, unhurt, Eur., etc.
to look at, gaze at, observe, perceive, Hom., etc.
absol., or with a prep., to look, gaze, Il.; δεῦρ’ ἄθρησον Eur.; οὐ γὰρ ἴδοις ἂν ἀθρῶν by observing, Soph.
of the mind, to look into a thing, consider, Id., Eur., etc.:—foll. by an interrog. or rel. clause, ταῦτ’ ἄθρησον, εἰ . . consider this also, whether . . , Soph.; ἄθρει Plat.
one must consider, Eur., Xen.

to gather together, to muster forces, Soph., Xen.; Τροίαν ἀθρ. to gather the Trojans together, Eur.; πνεῦμα ἄθροισον collect breath, Id.:—Mid. to gather for oneself, collect round one, Id., Xen.:—Pass. to be gathered together, ἐς τὴν ἀγορήν Hdt.; ἀθροισθέντες having rallied, Thuc.; τὸ ξύμπαν ἠθροίσθη δισχίλιοι the whole amounted collectively to 2000, Id.
in Pass. also of the mind, ἀθροίζεσθαι εἰς ἑαυτόν to collect oneself, Plat.; φόβος ἤθροισται fear has gathered strength, arisen, Xen.
a gathering, mustering, στρατοῦ Eur.; χρημάτων Thuc.
a gathering, λαοῦ Eur.
one must collect, Xen.

in crowds or masses, crowded together, mostly in pl.; πάντες ἁθρόοι Od., etc.; ἀθρόοι, of soldiers, in close order, Lat. conferto agmine, Hdt., Xen., etc.; also, πολλαὶ κῶμαι ἀθρόαι close together, Id.

taken together, ἁθρόα πάντ’ ἀπέτισεν he paid for all at once, Od.; ἁθρόα πόλις the citizens as a whole, Thuc.; τὸ ἀθρόον their assembled force, Xen.; ἀθρόωι στόματι with one voice, Eur.; ἁθρόους κρίνειν to condemn all by a single vote, Plat.; κατήριπεν ἀθρόος he fell all at once, Theocr.
multitudinous, δάκρυ Eur., Plat.
comp. ἁθροώτερος Thuc., etc.; later ἀθρούστερος Plut.
not broken, not enervated, Plut.; ἄθρυπτος εἰς γέλωτα never breaking into laughter, Id. adv. -τως, Id.

to be disheartened, lose heart, Aesch., etc.; τινι at or for a thing, Soph.; ἐπί τινι, εἴς τι, πρός τι, attic Prose:—foll. by a relat. word, to be sore afraid, ἀθυμῶ δ’ εἰ φανήσομαι Soph.; δεινῶς ἀθυμῶ μὴ βλέπων ὁ μάντις ἦι Id.
one must lose heart, Xen.
want of heart, faintheartedness, Hdt., Soph., etc.; εἰς ἀθυμίαν καθιστάναι τινά Plat.; ἀθυμίαν παρέχειν τινί Xen.; ἐν ἀθυμίαι εἶναι Id.; ἀθυμία ἐμπίπτει τινί Id.
without heart, fainthearted, Od., Hdt., etc.; ἄθ. εἶναι πρός τι to have no heart for a thing, Xen.; so adv., ἀθύμως ἔχειν πρός τι Id.
without passion, Plat.
a plaything, toy: a delight, joy, Hom., etc.
one that cannot keep his mouth shut, a ceaseless babbler, Eur.
without door, Plut.
ever-babbling, Soph.
without thyrsus, Eur.
to play, sport, of children, Il., Eur.; c. acc. cogn., μοῦσαν ἀθύρων singing sportive songs, Hhymn.:—Mid., simply, to sing, Id.
c. acc., ἔργα φωτῶν ἀθ. to play the deeds of men, of an actor, Anth.
never closed, Ar.
not offered, i. e. neglected, ἱερὰ ἄθ., Lat. sacra inauspicata, Aeschin.
act. without sacrificing, ἄθυτος ἀπελθεῖν Xen.
of mount Athos, Aesch.
unpunished, scot-free, Eur., etc.; ἀθώιους καθιστάναι τινάς to secure their immunity, Dem.; ἀθῶιον ἀφιέναι Id.; ἀθῶιος ἀπαλλάττειν to get off scot-free, Plat.
free from a thing, c. gen., Ar.
unharmed by a thing, c. gen., Dem.
not deserving punishment, without fault, Id.
not flattered, without flattery, τῆς ἐμῆς γλώσσης from my tongue, Eur.
act. not flattering, discourteous, Anth.
without breastplate, Xen.
mount Athos, Il., etc.
a wail, Eur.
to cry αἰαῖ, to wail, Trag.; c. acc. to bewail, Aesch., Eur.
exclam. of grief, ah! Lat. vae! c. gen., αἰαῖ τόλμας Eur.; and repeated, αἰαῖ αἰαῖ μελέων ἔργων Aesch.:—later c. acc., αἰαῖ τὰν Κυθέρειαν Bion.
son of Aeacus, Il.
bewailed, lamentable, Aesch., Ar.
wailing, miserable, Aesch.
dreary, dismal, direful, horrid, νυκτὸς αἰανῆ τέκνα, νυκτὸς αἰανὴς κύκλος, αἰανὴς νόσος Aesch., Soph., etc.
of Time, εἰς τὸν αἰανῆ χρόνον Aesch.; and so in adv. αἰανῶς for ever, Id.
entry.etym: The prob. deriv. is from αἰεί, everlasting, whence may come the notion of neverending, wearisome, dreary.

entry.sense: epic form used for γαῖα metri grat., Hom., Trag.; never in pl.
Ajax, pr. n., borne by two heroes, the Greater son of Telamon, the Less son of Oileus, Hom.
bah! exclam. of disgust or astonishment; but αἰβοῖ, βοῖ, of laughter, Ar.
the wild goat, Babr.
Aegaean, πέλαγος Aesch.; ὄρος Αἰγ. mount Ida, Hes.
Αἰγαῖος (sc. πόντος), the Aegaean, Plat., etc.
Aegaeon, the name given by men to the hundred-armed son of Uranus and Gaia, called by gods Βριάρεως, Il.
the Aegaean sea, Eur.
a hunting-spear, javelin, Hom., Anth.
of Aegeus, Aesch.
of a goat or goats, Lat. caprinus, αἴγειος τυρός goats-milk cheese, Il.; ἀσκῶι ἐν αἰγείωι in a goat's skin, Id.; αἰγείη κυνέη a helmet of goatskin.
the poplar (cf. λεύκη), Od.
a goatherd, Plut., Anth.
= αἴγειος, Od.
as Subst. αἰγέη (sc. δορά), a goat's skin, Hdt.
one who haunts the shore, Anth.
the sea-shore, beach, strand, Hom., Hdt.; αἰγιαλὸν ἔνδον τρέφει, i. e. he has a whole sea-beach (i. e. quantities of voting-pebbles, ψῆφοι) in his house, Ar.
a goat-pasture, Anth.
feeding goats, Anth.
browsed by goats, Od.
the titmouse, Lat. parus, Ar.
goat-shanked, Anth.
goatherds; name of one of the four old Attic Tribes, Hdt., Eur.
entry.etym: If from αἴξ, κορέννυμι, the literal sense would be goatfeeders.

entry.sense: destitute even of goats, hence steep, sheer, πέτρη Il.
a herb of which goats are fond, Theocr.
(sc. νῆσος) Aegina, Hdt.
of Aegina, Thuc., etc.
Aegina, Il., etc.
an Aeginetan, Hdt., etc.
a goatherd, Anth.
pass. browsed by goats, βοτάνη Id.
feeding goats: as Subst. a goatherd, Anth.
Aegis-bearing, of Zeus, Hom.
goat-footed, Hhymn.
a plant of which goats were fond, perh. buckwheat, Theocr.

the aegis or shield of Zeus, described in Il. 5. 738 sqq. the aegis on statues of Athena is a short cloak of goat-skin, covered with scales, set with the Gorgon's head, and fringed with snakes, v. Hdt. 4. 189.
a goatskin coat, Eur.
（αἴξ II) a rushing storm, hurricane, Aesch.
dazzling, radiant, lustrous, Hom.
the light of the sun, radiance, Od.:—then simply daylight, λευκὴ αἴγλη Id.; εἰς αἴγλαν μολεῖν, i. e. to be born, Pind
any dazzling light, lustre, gleam, χαλκοῦ Il.
radiant, Anth.
goat-horned, Anth., Plut.
as Subst. Capricorn in the Zodiac, Luc.
goat-faced, Hdt.
a vulture, Hom., etc.:— αἰγυπιός is the vulture which preys on live animals, γύψ the carrion vulture.
to speak Egyptian, Luc.
of or for the Egyptians, Plut., etc.
Egyptian, Hom., etc.
entry.etym: Αἰγυπτίη, Αἰγυπτίων, etc., are trisyll. in Hom.

entry.sense: in the Egyptian tongue, Hdt.
in Egyptian fashion, craftily, Theocr.
of Egyptian race, Aesch.
to Egypt, Od.
the river Nile, Od.; called Νεῖλος first in Hes.
Egypt, Od.
goat-hoofed, Anth.
to be ashamed to do a thing, c. inf., Hom., etc.; rarely c. part., αἴδεσαι μὲν πατέρα προλείπων feel ashamed of deserting him, Soph.:—absol., αἰδεσθείς from a sense of shame, Il.
c. acc. pers. to stand in awe of, fear, respect, αἰδεῖο θεούς Id., Hom., etc.; and of things, αἴδεσσαι μέλαθρον respect the house, Il.; ὅρκον αἰδεσθείς Soph.
to feel regard for a person, μήδε τί μ’ αἰδόμενος μήδ’ ἐλεαίρων Od.
exciting shame, venerable, Luc.
respect, Dem.
making unseen, annihilating, destroying, Il.:—adv. -λως, = ὀλεθρίως, Id.
pass. unseen, obscure, Hes.
bashful, modest, Xen.: Sup. αἰδημονέστατος, Id.: adv. -μόνως, Id.
unseen, annihilated, Hes.
everlasting, eternal, Hes. and attic:— ἐς ἀΐδιον for ever, Thuc.
unseen, dark, Hes.
mostly in pl. αἰδοῖα, τά, the genitals, pudenda, Il., etc.
of persons, regarded with reverence, august, venerable, and of women, deserving respect, tender, Hom.
act. shamefaced, reverent, Od.:—adv. -ως, reverently, Id.
comp. αἰδοιότερος, Od.; Sup. αἰδοιέστατος, Pind.
respectful in mind, compassionate, Soph.; πρός τινα Eur.
want of knowledge, ignorance, Od., Hdt.
poet. adj. unknowing, ignorant, Il.; c. gen., Od., etc.
unsettled, vagabond, Ar.; δρόμοις ἀν. in vagabond courses, Eur.

entry.etym: poets used the obl. cases Ἀϊδονῆος, ῆϊ, ῆα, with ᾱ, metri grat.

entry.sense: a sense of shame, shame, modesty, self-respect, Hom., etc.:—personif., Ζηνὶ σύνθακος θρόνων Αἰδώς Shame that shares his throne with Zeus, Soph.
regard for others, respect, reverence, Theogn.; τὴν ἐμὴν αἰδῶ respect for me, Aesch.
that which causes shame, and so,
a shame, Il.; as an exclam., shame! αἰδώς, Ἀργεῖοι, κακ’ ἐλέγχεα! Id.; αἰδώς, ὦ Λύκιοι· ποῖ φεύγετε; Id.
= τὰ αἰδοῖα, Id.
lulling in eternal sleep, of Death, Soph.
strong, lusty, vigorous, Hom.
strong, lusty, vigorous, Hom.
in Il. Vulcan is πέλωρ αἴητον, = ἄητον, terrible, mighty monster.
soot, Luc.
epith. of the τέττιξ, swarthy, dusky, Theocr.
smoky, sooty, Il., Theocr.; κόνις αἰθ. black ashes that are burnt out, Hom.
burning, Hes., Aesch.
soot, Eur.
to soil with soot or smoke, Eur.
Epic for εἴθε, αἴθ’ ὄφελες would that Hom.; cf. αἰ.
to walk in ether, Anth.
of or in the upper air, high in air, on high, Aesch., Soph., etc.; αἰθερία ἀνέπτα flew up into the air, Eur.
ether-skimming, Anth.

entry.etym: in Hom. fem; in Hes., Aesch., and attic Prose masc; in Soph. and Eur. masc or fem.
entry.sense: ether, the brighter purer air, the sky, above the ἀήρ (q. v.); Ζεὺς αἰθέρι ναίων Il.
a clime, region, Eur.
Ethiopia, Hdt.
Ethiopian, Hdt., etc.
in literal sense, sun-burnt, Anth.
properly burnt-face, i. e. an Ethiop, African, Hom., etc.
adj. Ethiopian, Hdt., etc.
