a burning heat, fire, Eur.

entry.etym: sc. στοά, αἴθουσα being partic. of αἴθω
entry.sense: in the Homeric house, the corridor, open in front like a verandah, looking E. or S. to catch the sun, whence the name; the sleeping place of travellers, Od.
fiery-looking, of metal, flashing, Il., etc.; of wine, sparkling, Id.; of smoke, mixed with flame, Od.
swart, dark, Anth.
metaph. fiery, keen, eager, Lat. ardens, Hes., Soph.
epith. of Boreas, born in ether, sprung from ether, Il.
not αἴθρα even in attic; clear sky, fair weather, Lat. sudum, Hom.

entry.etym: later form of αἴθρη, Solon, etc.
entry.sense: αἰθρίης, attic -ίας, in clear weather, Hdt., Ar.; ὑπὸ τῆς αἰθρίας in the open air, Lat. sub dio, Xen.
the clear cold air of night, Hdt.
to be clear, of the sky, ὡς δ’ ᾐθρίᾱσε Babr.
to sleep in open air, Theocr.
clear, bright, fair, of weather, Hhymn., Hdt.; epith. of Ζεύς, Theocr.
the clear chill air of morn, Od.; cf. αἰθρία.
a sea-bird, a gull or diver, Od.
one that darts swiftly, Anth.
to put in rapid motion, stir up, kindle, Soph.:—Pass. to quiver, of leaves, Sapph.
fiery, burning, blazing: of metal, flashing, glittering, Hom., etc.
in Hom. of the horse, lion, bull, eagle, —where it is either fiery, fierce, or tawny.
metaph. ablaze, fiery, Aesch., Soph.
entry.etym: The penult. of the obl. cases may be shortd. in Poets, metri grat., αἴθονος Soph.; αἴθονα Hes.

entry.sense: to light up, kindle, Hdt., Trag.
intr. to burn or blaze, Soph.:—in this sense the Pass. αἴθομαι is used by Hom. in part., πυρὸς μένος αἰθομένοιο Il., Od., etc.; so metaph., ἔρωτι αἴθεσθαι Xen.
to flatter, wheedle, fondle, c. acc., Soph., Eur.
absol., of a dog, to wag the tail fawningly, Babr.: (this is prob. the orig. sense).
rapid flight, rush, impetus, Il.
adv. ἀϊκῶς, Il.:—in Trag., αἰκής, αἰκῶς.
injurious treatment, an affront, outrage, Aesch., etc.
in Prose mostly as law-phrase, αἰκίας δίκη an action for assault, less serious than that for ὕβρις, Plat., etc.
Act. only in pres., to treat injuriously, to plague, torment, τινά Soph.; of a storm, αἰκίζων φόβην ὕλης Id.:—Pass. to be tormented, Aesch.
Dep. in same sense as Act., c. acc., Soph., etc.; c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, αἰκίζεσθαί τινα τὰ ἔσχατα Xen.
an outrage, torture, Aesch.:—in pl. mutilated corpses, Eur.
adverb of ἀϊκής.
a plaintive dirge, Trag.; (said to be from αἶ Λίνον, ah me for Linus! v. Λίνος II.)
adj. αἴλινος, ον, mournful, plaintive, Eur.:— neut. pl. αἴλινα as adv., Mosch.
a cat, Hdt., attic
mingled with blood, of blood, Eur.
bloody, blood-red, Anth.
blood, Hom., etc.; in pl. streams of blood, Trag.
bloodshed, murder, Aesch., etc.: —ἐφ’ αἵματι φεύγειν to avoid trial for murder by going into exile, Dem.; so, αἷμα φεύγειν Eur.
like Lat. sanguis, blood-relationship, kin, Soph., Hom., etc.; ὁ πρὸς αἵματος one of the blood or race, Soph.; μητρὸς τῆς ἐμῆς ἐν αἵματι akin to her by blood, Aesch.
a wall of dry stones, Lat. maceria, Od., etc.
a gush or stream of blood, Soph.
to make bloody stain with blood, Aesch.:—hence to smite so as to make bloody, Soph., Eur.; so in Mid., Anth.:—Pass. to welter in blood, be slain, Soph.
shedding of blood, NTest.
bloody, bloodstained, murderous, Trag.
of blood, consisting thereof, Aesch., Eur.
bringing blood, bloody, Aesch.
contr. αἱματοῦς, οῦσσα, οῦν, = αἱματηρός Il.
blood-red or of blood, Id.
bloody, murderous, Id.
licking blood, ἔρως αἱμ. thirst for blood, Aesch.
a blood-drinker, Ar.
blood-drinking, Aesch.
blood-streaming, αἱμ. ῥανίδες a shower of blood, Eur.
blood-dripping, Aesch.
blood-stained, Anth.
delighting in blood, Anth.
to make bloody, stain with blood, Aesch., Eur.
blood-red, Thuc.
bloody to behold, Eur.
bathed in blood, Soph.
blood-sucking, greedy of blood, Theocr.
bloodthirsty, Luc.
bleeding violently, Soph.
blood-sprinkled, Eur.
to have a αἱμόρροια, discharge of blood.
a discharge of blood.
blood-streaming, Aesch., Anth.
defiled with blood, κρέα Od.
winning, wily ways, Plut.
of winning wiles, Hhymn.
flattering, wheedling, wily, Hes., Aesch.; τὸν αἱμυλώτατον Soph.
bloody, blood-red, Luc.
skilful in a thing, c. gen., αἵμονα θήρης Il.
（αἷμα) bloody, Aesch., Eur.
terribly brave, Il.
praise, NTest.
praiseworthy, Arist., Anth.
This is a Poet. and ionic Verb, while ἐπαινέω is used in attic Prose
properly, to tell or speak of (cf. αἶνος), Aesch.
commonly, to speak in praise of, praise, Lat. laudo, c. acc., Hom., Hdt.
to allow, recommend, Od.: c. inf. to recommend to do a thing, Aesch.; also c. part., αἰνεῖν ἰόντα to commend one's going, Id.
like ἀγαπάω, to be content, acquiesce, Eur.:—c. acc. rei, to be content with, acquiesce in, γάμον Pind., etc.; θῆσσαν τράπεζαν Eur.
to decline courteously, Hes.
to promise or vow, τί τινι or τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Soph., Eur.
praise, fame, ἐν αἴνηι ἐών Hdt.

a dark saying, riddle, Aesch., etc.; ἐξ αἰνιγμάτων in riddles, Id.; δι’ αἰνιγμάτων Aeschin.; αἴνιγμα προβάλλειν, ξυντιθέναι to propose a riddle, Plat.; opp. to αἴνιγμα λύειν, εὑρίσκειν to solve it, Soph., etc.
riddling, dark, Aesch.
a riddle, δι’ αἰνιγμῶν ἐρεῖν Ar.; ἐν αἰνιγμοῖσι σημαίνειν Eur.

entry.etym: usually dep., = αἰνέω, Hom.:—act. αἰνίζω, Anth.

entry.sense: known from the adv. -ίως, in riddles, Aesch.
expressed in riddles, riddling, Soph.

to speak in riddles, Soph., Eur.; γνωρίμως αἰνίξομαι I will speak in riddles but so as to be understood, Soph.; αἰνίσσεσθαι ἔπεα to speak riddling verses, Hdt.:—c. acc. rei, to hint a thing, intimate, shadow forth, Plat.
as Pass. to be wrapt up in riddles, only in aor1 ἠινίχθην, perf. ᾔνιγμαι, Theogn., Plat., etc.
awefully strong, Anth.
fatally wedded, Eur.
adv. only in phrase αἰνόθεν αἰνῶς, from horror to horror, right horribly, Il.
sadly enervated, Theocr.
horrid-gleaming, Aesch.
fatally wedded, Aesch.
a dreadful lion, Theocr.
unfortunate in life's thread, in allusion to the Parcae, Anth.
a horrible wolf, Anth.
doomed to a sad end, Hom.
suffering dire ills, Od., Anth.
like Δύσπαρις, unlucky Paris, Eur.
unhappy father, Aesch.
dread, dire, grim, terrible, Hom.; αἰνότατε Κρονίδη most dread son of Cronus, Il.
adv. -νῶς, terribly, i. e. strangely, exceedingly, Hom., Hdt.; also αἰνά as adv., Il.; Sup. -ότατον, Id.
= μῦθος, a tale, story, Od.; αἰνεῖν αἶνον to tell a tale, Aesch., Soph.: generally, a saying, proverb, Theocr.
= attic ἔπαινος, praise, Hom., Trag.
unhappy in being a mother, Mosch.
a dreadful tyrant, Anth.
to take, take off, take hold of, Hom.; c. gen. partit., τυρῶν αἰνυμένους taking of the cheeses, Od.
a goat, Lat. caper, capra, Hom.
αἲξ ἄγριος the wild goat, the ibex, Id.
αἶγες, old name for waves.
entry.etym: Prob. not from ἀΐσσω, of which the root is ΑΙΚ.

entry.sense: an Aeolian; pl. Αἰολέες, attic Αἰολεῖς or -ῆς Hdt., Thuc.
to speak Aeolian, Plut.
of or like the Aeolians, Theocr.
to shift rapidly to and fro, Od.:—Pass. to shift colour, of grapes, Hes.
wielder of lightning, Ζεύς Pind.
with glancing breastplate, Il.
full of various wiles, Hes., Aesch.
with glancing or glittering girdle (for it was plated with metal), Il.
with variegated turban, Theocr.
with quick-moving steeds, Il., Theocr.

entry.etym: The penult. is lengthd. in the gen. Αἰόλου μεγαλήτορος, metri grat., Od.
entry.sense: quick-moving, Il.; αἰόλαι εὐλαί wriggling worms, Id.; so of wasps and serpents, Id.

changeful of hue, gleaming, glancing, of arms and armour, Id.; (but here also it may be explained moving with the body, manageable, Lat. habilis);— also, αἰόλα νύξ star-spangled night, Soph.; Aesch. calls smoke flushed by fire-light αἰόλη πυρὸς κάσις; αἰόλα σάρξ discoloured from disease, Soph.
metaph.,
changeful, shifting, varied, κάκα Aesch.; of sounds, ἰαχή Eur.
shifty, wily, slippery, ψεῦδος Pind.
as prop. n., proparox. Αἴολος, ου, ὁ, lord of the winds, properly the rapid or the changeable, Od.
shifting in speech, of an oracle, Aesch.
Exclam. of astonishment, ha! αἲ τάλας Ar.
if:— αἴ κε or κεν if only, so that, Lat. dummodo, with subj., Hom.; so doric αἴκᾱ, Theocr.
αἲ γάρ (with accent), epic for εἰ γάρ, to express a wish, O that! would that! Lat. utinam! with opt., Hom.; cf. αἴθε.
high, lofty, Hom.
metaph.,
precipitate, hasty, Pind.
hard to win, difficult, Pind., Eur.
to tend goats, Theocr.: —Pass., of the flock, Aesch.
of or for goatherds, Anth.
a herd of goats, Il., etc.
a goat-pasture, Anth.

entry.etym: αἰπόλος is for αἰγοπόλος from αἴξ, πολέω.
entry.sense: a goatherd, Od., etc.
a height, a steep, Aesch.:— πρὸς αἶπος ἔρχεσθαι, metaph. of a difficult task, Eur.
high, lofty, of cities, Il.; αἰπὰ ῥέεθρα streams falling sheer down, Il.
with high thoughts, Θέμιδος αἰπυμῆτα παῖ Aesch.
high-backed, on a high mountain-ridge, of Dodona, Aesch.
high and steep, lofty, of cities on heights, as Troy, Od.; of hills, Il.; βρόχος αἰπ. a noose hanging straight down, Od.
metaph. sheer, utter, αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος Hom. (death being regarded as the plunge over a precipice); so, φόνος αἰπύς Od.; also αἰπὺς χόλος towering wrath, Il.
arduous, difficult, Id.
that can be taken, Xen.
a taking especially, esp. of a town, Hdt., etc.; ἡ βασιλῆος αἵρ. the taking by the king, Hdt.
means for taking a place, Thuc.

（αἱρέομαι) a taking for oneself, a choosing, choice, νέμειν, προτιθέναι, προβάλλειν to give or offer choice, Hdt., attic; αἵρ. γίγνεταί τινι a choice is allowed one, Thuc.; αἵρεσιν λαμβάνειν to have choice given, Dem.
choice or election of magistrates, Thuc., etc.
a choice, deliberate plan, purpose, Plat., etc.
a sect, school, etc.: esp. a religious sect, such as the Sadducees and Pharisees, NTest.
a heresy, Eccl.
to be taken, desirable, Xen.
αἱρετέον, one must choose, Plat.
to choose, select, Babr., NTest.
able to choose, Plat.
heretical, NTest.
that may be taken or conquered, Hdt.; that may be understood, Plat.
（αἱρέομαι) to be chosen, eligible, Id., Hdt., etc.; ζοῆς πονηρᾶς θάνατος αἱρετώτερος Menand.
chosen, elected, Plat., etc.

entry.etym: The forms εἷλον etc. come from the stem ἑλ-.
entry.sense: Act. to take with the hand, grasp, αἱρ. τι ἐν χερσίν, μετὰ χερσίν to take a thing in hand, Od.; αἱρ. χερσὶ δόρυ Il.; αἱρ, τινὰ χειρός to take one by the hand, Id.:—part. ἑλών is sometimes used as adv., by force, Soph.
to take away, Hom.
to take by force, to take a city, Il., etc.; to overpower, kill, Hom., etc.:—often of passions, etc., to seize, Id., etc.:—to conquer (in a race), Il.
to take, catch, as in hunting, in good sense, to win over, Xen., etc.:—c. part. to catch or detect one doing a thing, Soph.
to win, gain, κῦδος Il.; of the public games, Simon., etc.

as attic law-term, to convict a person of a thing, τινά τινος Ar., etc.: also c. part., αἱρεῖν τινὰ κλέπτοντα to convict of theft, Id.; ἡιρῆσθαι κλοπεύς (sc. ὤν) Soph.; τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ὃ ἐμὲ αἱρήσει Plat.
ὁ λόγος αἱρέει, Lat. ratio evincit, reason proves, Hdt.
Mid. to take for oneself, Hom., etc.; αἱρ. δόρπον, δεῖπνον to take one's supper, Id.:—so in most senses of Act.

to choose, Id.: to take in preference, prefer one thing to another, τι πρό τινος Hdt.; τι ἀντί τινος Xen.; also, τί τινος Soph.; τι μᾶλλον ἢ . . , or μᾶλλόν τινος attic:—c. inf. to prefer to do, Hdt., etc.
αἱρεῖσθαι τά τινος or τινά to take another's part, join his party, Id., etc.
to choose by vote, elect to an office, Plat., etc.
Pass. to be taken, Hdt.; but ἁλίσκομαι is used in attic for Pass.
as Pass. to the mid. sense, to be chosen, in perf. ᾕρημαι (which is also mid.), Hdt., attic
Od. 18. 73 Ἶρος ἄϊρος, Irus unhappy Irus, — a play upon his name, like δῶρα ἄδωρα.

entry.etym: distinguish ἀρῶ from ᾱ̓ρῶ, contr. of ἀερῶ.
entry.sense: Act.
to take up, raise, lift up, Il., etc.; αἴρειν βῆμα to step, walk, Eur.; αἴρ. σημεῖον to hoist a signal, Xen.:—Pass. to mount up, ascend, Id.
often of armies and ships, αἴρ. τὰς ναῦς to get the fleet under sail, Thuc.:—also intr. to get under way, start, set out, ἆραι τῶι στρατῶι Id.;—so in Mid. and Pass., Hdt., etc.
to bear, sustain, μόρον Aesch.; ἆθλον Soph.
to raise up, exalt, Aesch.:—of passion, to exalt, excite, ὑψοῦ αἴρειν θυμόν to grow excited, Soph.; αἴρειν θάρσος to pluck up courage, Eur., etc.: Pass., οὐκ ἤρθη νοῦν ἐς ἀτασθαλίην Simon.
to raise by words, to extol, exaggerate, Eur., Dem.
to lift and take away, to remove, Aesch., etc.:—to take off, kill, NTest.

Mid., with perf. pass. ἦρμαι, to take up for oneself: to carry off, win, gain, κλέος Il.; ἀέθλια (of horses) Id.; κῦδος Hom.:—hence simply to receive, get, ἕλκος ἀρέσθαι Il.; also, δειλίαν ἀρεῖ wilt incur a charge of cowardice, Soph.
to take upon oneself, undergo, carry, bear, Il., etc.
to undertake, begin, πόλεμον Thuc., etc.; φυγὴν ἀρέσθαι, Lat. fugam capere, Aesch.
to raise up, σωτῆρά τινι Soph.: of sound, αἴρεσθαι φωνήν to raise, lift up one's voice, Ar.
like Μοῖρα, the goddess of destiny, Lat. Parca, Il.
as appellat.
the decree, dispensation of a god, Διὸς αἴσηι, ὑπὲρ Διὸς αἶσαν Id.; θεοῦ αἶσα Eur.:— κατ’ αἶσαν fitly, duly, Il., etc.; κατ’ αἶσαν, οὐδ’ ὑπὲρ αἶσαν Id.
one's appointed lot, destiny, Hom., etc.
one's share in a thing, Od.; ληΐδος αἶσα Id., etc.
to perceive, apprehend by the senses, to see, hear, feel, Hdt., attic

to perceive by the mind, understand, hear, learn, often in attic: absol., αἰσθάνει, Lat. tenes, you are right, Eur.:—Construct., c. gen. to have perception of, τῶν κακῶν Id., etc.; also c. acc., Soph., etc.:—dependent clauses are mostly added in part. agreeing with subject, αἰσθάνομαι κάμνων Thuc.; or agreeing with object, τυράννους ἐκπεσόντας ἠισθόμην Aesch.
perception of a thing, κακῶν Eur.
perception by the senses, αἴσθ. πημάτων perception, sense of calamities, Eur.— The phrase αἴσθησιν ἔχειν is used
of persons, αἴσθ. ἔχειν τινός, = αἰσθάνεσθαί τινος or τι, to have a perception of a thing, perceive it, Plat.
of things, to give a perception, i. e. to become perceptible, serving as a Pass. to αἰσθάνομαι, Thuc.; more freq. αἴσθησιν παρέχειν Id., Xen.
one of the senses, Plat.: and in pl. the senses, Id.
a perception, αἰσθήσεις θεῶν visions of the gods, Id.
in hunting, the scent, Xen.
an organ of sense, Arist., etc.; τὰ αἰσθ. the senses, faculties, NTest.
of or for perception by the senses, perceptive, Plat., etc.:—adv. αἰσθητικῶς ἔχειν to be quick of perception, Arist.
of things, perceptible, Plut.
perceptible by the senses, Plat.
to breathe out, like ἀποπνέω, θυμὸν ἄϊσθε he was giving up the ghost, Il.
happiness, αἰσιμίαις πλούτου Aesch.
Lat. fatalis, appointed by the will of the gods, destined, αἴσιμον ἦμαρ the fatal day, day of death, Il., etc.; αἴσιμόν ἐστι it is fated, Id.
agreeable to fate, meet, right, αἴσιμα εἰπεῖν, αἴσιμα εἰδώς Od.
boding well, auspicious, Il., etc.:—adv. -ίως, Eur.
unlike, unequal, Pind.
to move with a quick shooting motion, to shoot, dart, glance, Lat. impetu ferri, Il., etc.; so in aor. mid., ἀΐξασθαι, and aor. pass. ἀϊχθῆναι Id.; κόμη δι’ αὔρας ἀίσσεται floats on the breeze, Soph.
to turn eagerly, be eager, εἴς τι Eur.
trans. to put in motion, Eur.
not to be seen, unseen.
act. unconscious of, c. gen., Eur.
to make unseen, to annihilate, Hom., etc.
unknowing, unconscious, Plat.; τινός of a thing, Eur.
unseemly, evil, Il.
to rule over, c. gen., Eur.
an elective monarchy, Arist.
a prince, Il.
a regulator of games, a judge or umpire, Od.: a president, manager, Theocr.
an elective prince, Arist.
shame, disgrace, Hom., etc.:—in pl. shameful deeds, Od.
ugliness or deformity, of mind or body, Plat., Xen.
shameful, Anth.
base covetousness, Soph.
sordidly greedy of gain, Hdt., Eur.—adv. -δῶς, NTest.
foul language, abuse, Xen.
forming base designs, Aesch.
doing foully, Eur.
causing shame, abusive, ἔπεα Il.; so in adv., αἰσχρῶς ἐνένισπε Id.
opp. to καλός:
of outward appearance, ugly, ill-favoured, of Thersites, Id.

in moral sense, shameful, disgraceful, base, infamous, Hdt., etc.; αἰσχρόν [ἐστι], c. inf., Il.: —τὸ αἰσχρόν, as Subst., dishonour, disgrace, Soph., etc.; τὸ καλὸν καὶ τὸ αἰσχρόν, Lat. honestum et turpe, virtue and vice, Arist.:—adv. shamefully, Sup. αἴσχιστα, Trag.
awkward, Xen.
instead of the regul. comp. and Sup. αἰσχρότερος, -ότατος, the forms αἰσχίων [ῑ], αἴσχιστος (formed from αἶσχος) are used.
ugliness, deformity, Plat.
shameless conduct, Eur.
shame done one, disgrace, dishonour, Hdt., attic
a disgrace, of a person, Aesch.
shame for an ill deed, personified in Aesch.
generally, like αἰδώς, shame, the sense of shame, Soph., etc.
one must be ashamed, Xen.
bashful, modest, Plat.
a dishonourer, Aesch.
shameful, Arist.
to make ugly, disfigure, mar, πρόσωπον, κόμην Il.
in moral sense, to dishonour, tarnish, γένος πατέρων Id., etc.
to dishonour a woman, Aesch., etc.
Pass. to be dishonoured, νέκυς ᾐσχυμμένος, of Patroclus, Il.
to be ashamed, feel shame, absol., Od., Hdt., etc.

to be ashamed at a thing, c. acc. rei, Od., etc.; also c. dat. rei, Ar., etc.; and with Preps., αἰσχ. ἐπί τινι Xen.; ἔν τινι Thuc.; ὑπέρ τινος Dem.:—c. part to be ashamed at doing a thing, Aesch., Soph., etc.:—but c. inf. to be ashamed to do a thing, Hdt., etc.
c. acc. pers. to feel shame before one, Eur., etc.
doric word for a beloved youth, favourite, Theocr.: generally a lover, Anth.
to ask, beg, Od., etc.

c. acc. rei, to ask for, crave, demand, Hom., etc.; ὁδὸν αἰτ. to beg one's departure, i. e. ask leave to depart, Od.:—c. acc. pers. et rei, to ask a person for a thing, Hom., etc.; δίκας αἰτ. τινὰ φόνου to demand satisfaction from one for murder, Hdt.
c. acc. pers. et inf. to ask one to do, Od., etc.
Mid. to ask for oneself, to claim, Aesch., etc.:—but often used just like Act.
Pass.:
of persons, to have a thing begged of one, Hdt., Thuc.
of things, to be asked, τὸ αἰτεόμενον Hdt., etc.
a request, demand, Plat., NTest.
a request, demand, Hdt.
one must ask, Xen.
fond of asking, c. gen., Arist.
asked for, Soph.
to be accused, Xen.
a charge, guilt imputed, λαβεῖν ἐπ’ αἰτιάματί τινα Aesch.; τοιοῖσδε ἐπ’ αἰτιάμασιν on such charges, Id.

to charge, accuse, censure, blame, c. acc. pers., τάχα κεν καὶ ἀναίτιον αἰτιόωιτο Il.; αἰτ. τινά τινος to accuse of a thing, Hdt., etc.;—c. inf., αἰτ. τινα ποιεῖν τι to accuse one of doing, Id.:—in this signf., certain tenses are used in pass. sense, to be accused, aor1 ἠιτιάθην Thuc., Xen.; perf. ἠιτίαμαι Thuc.
c. acc. rei, to lay to one's charge, impute, τοῦτο αἰτ. Xen.; ταῦτα Dem.; c. dupl. acc., τί ταῦτα τοὺς Λάκωνας αἰτιώμεθα; Ar.
to allege as the cause, αἰτ. τινα αἴτιον Plat.; φωνάς τε καὶ ἄλλα μυρία αἰτ. Id.; τῆς ἱερᾶς χώρας ἠιτιᾶτο εἶναι he alleged that it was part of the sacred territory, Dem.

a charge, accusation, Lat. crimen, and then the guilt or fault implied in such accusation, Pind., Hdt.:—Phrases: αἰτίαν ἔχειν to be accused, τινός of a thing, Id., etc.;—reversely, αἰτία ἔχει με Id.; ἐν αἰτίαι εἶναι or γίγνεσθαι Xen., etc.; αἰτίαν ὑπέχειν to lie under a charge, Plat.; αἰτίαν φέρεσθαι Thuc.; αἰτίαις ἐνέχεσθαι Plat.:—opp. to these are ἐν αἰτίαι ἔχειν or δι’ αἰτίας to hold one guilty, accuse, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; ἐν αἰτίαι βάλλειν Soph.; αἰτίαν νέμειν τινί Id., etc.
in good sense, εἰ εὖ πράξαιμεν, αἰτία θεοῦ the credit is his, Aesch.; οἳ ἔχουσι ταύτην τὴν αἰτίαν who have this as their characteristic, Plat.
expostulation, μὴ ἐπ’ ἔχθραι τὸ πλέον ἢ αἰτίαι Thuc.
a cause, Lat. causa, Plat., etc.; dat. αἰτίαι, like Lat. causa, for the sake of, κοινοῦ ἀγαθοῦ Thuc.
an occasion, opportunity, αἰτίαν παρέχειν Luc.
the head under which a thing comes, Dem.
one must accuse, Xen.
one must allege as the cause, Plat.
to ask, beg, c. acc. rei, σῖτον Od.
c. acc. pers. to beg of, μνηστῆρας Id.
absol., αἰτίζων βόσκειν ἣν γαστέρα to fill one's belly by begging, Id.
inquiring into causes: τὸ αἰτιολογικόν, investigation of causes, Strab.
to blame, blameworthy, culpable, Il., etc.: comp., αἰτιώτερος more culpable, Thuc.; Sup., τοὺς αἰτιωτάτους the most guilty, Hdt.; τινος for a thing, Id.
as Subst., αἴτιος, ὁ, the accused, culprit, Lat. reus, Aesch., etc.; οἱ αἴτιοι τοῦ πατρός they who have sinned against my father, Id.:—c. gen. rei, οἱ αἴτ. τοῦ φόνου those guilty of murder, Id.
being the cause, responsible for, c. gen. rei, Hdt., etc.; c. inf., Soph.: Sup., αἰτιώτατος ναυμαχῆσαι mainly instrumental in causing the seafight, Thuc.
αἴτιον, τό, a cause, Plat., etc.
of or belonging to Etna (Αἴτνη), Pind., Aesch., etc.
metaph. like Etna, enormous, Eur.; some explain it so when used of horses, but better Etnean, i. e. Sicilian (for the Sicilian horses were famous), Soph.
unforeseen, sudden, Aesch., Thuc.:—adv. -ίως, Id=Thuc.; also -ιον Plut.
to throw the spear, Il.; ἔνδον αἰχμάζειν to play the warrior at home, Aesch.
to arm with the spear, ἤιχμασας χέρα Soph.
captivity: a body of captives, Diod., NTest.
to take prisoner, NTest.
of or for a prisoner, Eur.
taken by the spear, captive to one's spear, taken prisoner, Hdt., etc.; αἰχμάλωτον λαμβάνειν, ἄγειν to take prisoner, Xen.; αἰχμ. γίγνεσθαι to be taken, Id.; τὰ αἰχμάλωτα booty, Id.
= αἰχμαλωτικός, δουλοσύνη αἰχμ. such as awaits a captive, Hdt., Aesch.
armed with the spear, Aesch.
the point of a spear, Lat. cuspis, Il., etc.
a spear, Id., etc.; τοξουλκὸς αἰχμή, of an arrow, Aesch.
a body of spearmen, Pind., Eur.; cf. ἀσπίς.
war, battle, κακῶς ἡ αἰχμὴ ἐστήκεε the war went ill, Hdt.
warlike spirit, mettle, Pind.; so, in Aesch., γυναικὸς or γυναικεία αἰχμά seems to be a woman's spirit.
a sceptre, Id.
a spearman, Hom.
In Pind. as adj.,
pointed, κεραυνός.
warlike, θυμός.
one who trails a pike, a spearman, Hdt.:—esp. like δορυφόρος, of body-guards, Id.
quick, with speed, on a sudden, Hom.
swift-speeding, of Boreas, Hes.
quick, speedy, in haste, Hom.
to perceive by the ear, to hear, c. acc. rei, Il.; c. gen., Trag.:—also to perceive by the eye, to see, Od.
to listen to, give ear to, δίκης Hes.: to obey, Aesch.; cf. ἐπαΐω.
entry.etym: Hom. has αιω; but ᾱιεις, ᾱιων Soph.

entry.sense: to breathe, only in imperf., ἐπεὶ φίλον ἄϊον ἦτορ when I was breathing out my life, Il.
lasting for an age (αἰών 3), Plat.: ever-lasting, eternal, Id.
a period of existence:
one's life-time, life, Hom. and attic Poets.
an age, generation, Aesch.; ὁ μέλλων αἰών posterity, Dem.
a long space of time, an age, ἀπ’ αἰῶνος of old, for ages, Hes., NTest.; τὸν δι’ αἰῶνος χρόνον for ever, Aesch.; ἅπαντα τὸν αἰ. Lycurg.
a definite space of time, an era, epoch, age, period, ὁ αἰὼν οὗτος this present world, opp. to ὁ μέλλων, NTest.:—hence its usage in pl., εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας for ever, Id.
a machine for suspending bodies: a noose for hanging, a halter, Soph. in the form ἐώρα).
suspension in the air, oscillation, plat.
to lift up, raise, ὑγρὸν νῶτον αἰωρεῖ, of the eagle raising his feathers, Pind.; τοὺς ὄφεις ὑπὲρ τῆς κεφαλῆς αἰωρῶν Dem.:—cf. ἐωρέω.
to hang, Plut., Luc.
Pass. to be hung, hang, Hdt.; αἰωρουμένων τῶν ὀστῶν being raised, lifted, Plat.; αἷμα ἠιωρεῖτο spouted up, Bion.
to hang suspended, float in air, hover, oscillate, Soph., Plat.
metaph. to be in suspense, Thuc.; αἰωρεῖσθαι ἐν ἄλλοις to depend upon others, Plat.; αἰωρηθεὶς ὑπὲρ μεγάλων playing for a high stake, Hdt.
that which is hung up: a hanging cord, a halter, Eur.
a hovering, Anth.
the Academy, a gymnasium near Athens, where Plato taught: hence Platonic philosophers were called Ἀκαδημικοί, Academics.
uncleanness, impurity, Dem.
uncleansed, unclean, impure, Plat.:—adv., ἀκαθάρτως ἔχειν Id.
of things, not purged away, Soph.
a thorn, goad, Anth.
unfitness of times: unseasonableness, Plat.
want of opportunity, τὴν ἀκαιρίαν τὴν ἐκείνου καιρὸν ὑμέτερον νομίσαντες Dem.
ill-timed, unseasonable, inopportune, ἐς ἄκαιρα πονεῖν, Lat. operam perdere, Theogn.; οὐκ ἄκαιρα λέγειν Aesch.; ἄκ. προθυμία Thuc.:—adv. -ρως, Aesch., etc.; neut. pl. as adv., Eur.
of persons, importunate, Lat. molestus, Theophr.
poet. for ἄκακος, Aesch.
guileless, gracious, epith. of Hermes, Hom., Hes.
guilelessness, Dem., etc.
unknowing of ill, guileless, Aesch., Plat.
innocent, simple, Dem.:—adv. -κως, Id.
soft-flowing, of Ocean, Hom.
a nettle, Lat. urtica, Ar.
without charms, Luc.
ill-omened, ἱερά Aeschin.
unadorned, Luc.
uncovered, unveiled, Soph.
unwearied at the spear, Pind.
unwearied in fight, Pind.
untiring of foot, unwearied, Pind.
untiring, unresting, Il., etc.
without sense of toil: hence — untiring, unresting, Hom.; ἀκ. γῆ earth that never rests from tillage, Soph.:—neut. ἀκάματα, as adv., Id.
entry.etym: ἀκάματος, Soph.; but ᾱ̓κάματος in dactylics.

entry.sense: unbent, that will not bend, rigid, Plat.:—metaph. unbending, unflinching, inexorable, Pind.; ψυχὰν ἄκαμπτος Id.; ἀκάμπτωι μένει Aesch.; ἄκαμπτον Plut.
a thorn, prickle, Theocr., etc.
a prickly plant, thistle; in pl. thistledown, Od.:—also a kind of acacia, Hdt.
the backbone or spine of animals, Id., etc.
metaph., ἄκανθαι, thorny questions, Luc.
of thorns, NTest.
of acacia wood, Hdt.
a bird, the goldfinch, or the linnet, Arist., Theocr.
as fem. adj. prickly, Anth.
walking among thorns, nickname of grammarians, Anth.:—fem. ἀκανθοβάτις, ιδος, Anth.
gathering thorns, nickname of quibblers, Anth.
Lat. acanthus, brank-ursine, a plant imitated in Corinthian capitals, Theocr.
full of thorns, thorny, Hdt.
metaph., λόγοι ἀκ. thorny arguments, Luc.
without smoke, θυσία ἄκαπνος an offering but no burnt offering, Luc.; a poem is called Καλλιόπης ἄκαπνον θύος Anth.
softly, gently, Pind.
wanting the heart, Plut.
headless, Anth.
of hair, too short to be cut, very short: mostly in neut. ἀκαρές,
of Time, a moment, ἐν ἀκαρεῖ χρόνου Ar.; ἀκαρῆ διαλιπὼν (sc. χρόνον) having waited a moment, Id.; ἀκαρὲς ὥρας a moment, Plut.
the acc. ἀκαρῆ is used adverbially without reference to Time, οὐκ ἀκαρῆ or οὐδ’ ἀκαρῆ not a bit, Ar.
momentary, brief, Dem., etc.
unfruitfulness, barrenness, Aesch.
where nothing is to be reaped, unfruitful, of the sea, like ἀτρύγετος, Eur.
without fruit, barren, Eur.
metaph. fruitless, unprofitable, Id.:—adv. -πως, Soph.
act. making barren, blasting, Aesch.
not made fruitful, without fruit: of an oracle, fruitless, unfulfilled, Aesch.; νίκας ἀκάρπωτον χάριν because of victory which yielded no fruit, Soph.
gentle, Aesch.
not to be overthrown, irrefragable, Ar.
not to be condemned, NTest.
uncovered, NTest.
uncondemned, NTest.
irreconcileable:— adv. -τως, ἀκ. πολεμεῖν Dem.
indissoluble, NTest.
unstable, unsettled, Dem.
not to be checked:— adv. -τως, Plut.
not to be despised, important, Lat. haud spernendus, Xen., Plut., etc.
not fabulous, Hdt.
a light boat, Thuc., etc.
a small sail, perh. a top-sail, Xen., Luc.
a light vessel, Lat. actuaria, Hdt., etc.; cf. ἀκάτιον.
generally, a ship, Eur.
unburnt, Xen.
to trouble, grieve, τινά Od.:—Pass., μὴ λίην ἀκαχίζεο θυμῶι be not troubled in mind, Il.; μήτι θανὼν ἀκαχίζευ be not grieved at death, Od.
a part. (as if from a Verb *ἄκω, v. ἀκή Ι), sharpened, of axes and swords, Hom.
unbidden, Trag., Plat.
needing no goad or spur, Pind.
without sting, stingless, Plat.

entry.etym: The form ἀκέο is for ἀκέεο.
entry.sense: trans. to heal, cure, ἕλκος ἄκεσσαι heal the sore, Il.; or of part healed, βλέφαρον ἀκέσαιο Eur.; also to heal a person, Il.
to stanch, quench, δίψαν Id.
generally, to mend, repair, νῆας Od.; applied to a tailor or cobbler, like Lat. resarcire, Luc.
metaph. to repair, make amends for, ἁμαρτάδα Hdt.; κακόν Soph.:—absol. to make amends, ἀλλ’ ἀκεώμεθα, ἀλλ’ ἀκέσασθε Hom.
unmixed, pure in blood, Eur.

entire, unharmed, unravaged, of cities or countries, Hdt., Thuc.; ἀκ. δύναμις an army in full force, Id.; ἀκ. λέχος inviolate, Eur.; of persons, uncontaminated, guileless, Id.: c. gen., ἀκέραιος κακῶν ἠθῶν uncontaminated by bad habits, Plat.
not lightning-struck, Luc.
want of gain, loss, Pind.
without gain, bringing loss, Soph., Plat.
not greedy of gain, Plut.
unwoven, Anth.
without a tail, Arist.
want of money, Ar.
with unshorn hair (the Greek youths wore their hair long till they reached manhood), epith. of Phoebus, Il., etc.
not horned, Anth.
a healing, cure, Hdt.
a remedy, cure, Pind., Aesch.
a healer: metaph. as adj., ἀκ. χαλινός the rein that tames the steed, Soph.
ἀκεσταὶ ἱματίων ῥαγέντων menders of torn clothes, Xen.
the healing art, Anth.
curable:— metaph., easily revived, Il.
a darning-needle, Luc.
a sempstress, Luc.
a healer, saviour, Eur.
bringing a cure, healing, Eur.
allaying pain, Anth.
without head, Hdt.
without beginning, λόγος Plat.

a participial form, used as adv. like ἀκήν, softly, silently, Hom.; also dual ἀκέοντε Od. —Though ἀκέουσα occurs in Hom., yet ἀκέων stands with fem., Ἀθηναίη ἀκέων ἦν Il.; and though he has dual ἀκέοντε, yet ἀκέων occurs with pl. Verbs.
uncared for, unburied, Il.: adv., -τως, without due rites of burial, or (perh.) without care for others, recklessly, remorselessly, Id.
unburied, Plut.
to take no care for, no heed of, c. gen., Il., Aesch.
pass. uncared for, unburied, Hom.
act. without care or sorrow, careless, heedless, Id.
to be won by no charms, proof against enchantment, inexorable, Od., Soph.
a cure, relief, ὀδυνάων for pains, Il.
softly, silently, Il.
a Subst. cited in two senses,
a point, (whence ἀκίς, ἄκων, ἀκόνη, ἀκαχμένος, ἀκωκή, αἰχμή; cf. Lat. acus, acuo, acies).
silence, calm, (whence ἀκήν, ἀκέων, ἀκασκαῖος, ἦκα): a lulling, healing (whence ἀκέομαι).
unmixed, οἶνος Od.
untouched, Lat. integer, ἀκ. λειμῶνες meadows not yet grazed or mown, Hhymn.; ἄνθος ἀκ. fresh, Anth.
unmixed, uncontaminated, undefiled, ὕδωρ Il.; ποτόν Aesch.; ὄμβρος Soph.; ἀκ. χρυσός pure gold, Hdt.
metaph.,
of things, untouched, unhurt, undamaged, Lat. integer, Hom.; ἀκ. κόμη unshorn hair, Eur.; ἀκ. λειμών an unmown meadow, Id., etc.
of persons, undefiled, Id.; c. dat., ἀκήρατος ἄλγεσι untouched by woes, Id.; c. gen., ἀκ. κακῶν without taint of ill, Id.
unharmed by the Κῆρες, unharmed, Od.
act. unharming, harmless, Hhymn., Hes.
（κῆρ) without heart, i. e.,
lifeless, Il.
heartless, spiritless, Id.
without needing a flag of truce, Thuc.
unannounced, unproclaimed, ἀκ. πόλεμος a sudden war, Hdt.; but also a war in which no herald was admitted, implacable, Xen., Dem.:—adv. -τως, without needing a flag of truce, Thuc.
not proclaimed by heralds, inglorious, Eur.
with no tidings, not heard of, Soph.
unwaxed, Luc.
unadulterated, genuine, Plat., Luc.
metaph. of men, guileless, honest, Hdt.
weak, feeble, faint, Hom. always in the comp., ἀκιδνότερος Od.
powerless, feeble, Od.
Persian word, a short straight sword, Hdt., who declines it -εος, -εϊ, -εα; but Xen. has ἀκινάκην, ἀκινάκας as acc. sg. and pl.
without danger, free from danger, Eur., Thuc., etc.
adv. -νως, Eur., etc.: comp., ἀκινδυνότερον with less danger, Plat.; Sup., ἀκινδυνότατα most free from danger, Xen.
unmoved, motionless, of Delos, Orac. ap. Hdt.; ἐξ ἀκινήτου ποδός without stirring a step, Soph.
idle, sluggish, Ar.
unmoved, unaltered, of laws, Thuc., etc.
immovable, hard to move, Plat., Luc.:—adv., ἀκινήτως ἔχειν to be immovable, Plat., etc.
not to be stirred or touched, inviolate, Lat. non movendus, τάφος Hdt.: proverb. of sacred things, κινεῖν τὰ ἀκίνητα Id.; also τἀκίνητα φράσαι Soph.
of persons, not to be shaken, steadfast, stubborn, Id.
not worm-eaten: Sup. ἀκιώτατος Hes.
a point, the barb of an arrow or hook, Plut., Anth.:—an arrow, dart, Ar.
metaph., πόθων ἀκίδες the stings of desire, Anth.
not to be reached, unattainable, Il.
of persons, not to be reached by prayer, inexorable, Aesch.
to affect indifference or coyness, dissemble, Plat.
a bugbear or a silly woman.
unbroken, Anth.
unlamented, Hom.: (κλαίω):
pass. unwept, φίλων by friends, Soph.; ἄκλαυτα τέκνα, i. e. children not liable to death, Eur.
act. not weeping, tearless, Od.
Soph. = χαίρων, with impunity.
without fame, inglorious, unsung, Hom., etc. adv. ἀκλεῶς, Hdt., epic ἀκλειῶς, Il., etc.: also neut. ἀκλεές as adv., Id.
ingloriousness, Anth.
not closed or fastened, Eur., Thuc.
without lot or portion, poor, needy, Od., Xen., etc.: c. gen. without lot or share in a thing, Aesch., etc.
unallotted, without an owner, Eur.
without lot or portion in a thing, c. gen., Pind.
uncalled, unbidden, Aesch., etc.
bending to neither side, unswerving, Plat.: steadfast, regular, Anth., etc.:— adv. -νῶς, ionic -νέως, Id.
unwashed by waves, Plut., etc.; as fem., Αὖλιν ἀκλύσταν Eur.
to be in full bloom, be at one's prime or perfection,
of persons, cities and states, Hdt., etc.
c. dat. to flourish or abound in a thing, πλούτωι Id.; παρασκευῆι Thuc.
c. inf. to be strong enough to do, Xen.
of things, ἀκμάζει ὁ πόλεμος, ἡ νόσος the war, the plague is at its height, Thuc.; ἀκμάζον θέρος mid-summer, Id.; of corn, to be just ripe, Id.
impers. ἀκμάζει, c. inf., it is high time to do, Aesch.
in full bloom, at the prime, blooming, vigorous, Aesch.; ἀκμαῖος φύσιν in the prime of strength, Id.
in time, in season, Lat. opportunus, Soph.
full-grown, Od.
fasting, Il.; c. gen., ἄκμηνος σίτοιο fasting from food, Id.
a point, edge: proverb., ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἀκμῆς on the rasor's edge (v. ξυρόν); ἀμφιδέξιοι ἀκμαί the fingers of both hands, Soph.; ποδοῖν ἀκμαί the toes, Id.

the highest point of anything, the bloom, flower, prime, of man's age, Lat. flos aetatis, ἀκμὴ ἥβης Id.; ἀκμὴ βίου Xen.; ἐν ἀκμῆι εἶναι =ἀκμάζειν, Plat.; ἀκμὴν ἔχειν, of corn, to be ripe, Thuc.; also of time, ἀ. ἦρος the spring-prime, Pind.; ἀ. θέρους mid-summer, Xen.; ἀ. τῆς δόξης Thuc.; periphr. like βία, ἀκμὴ Θησειδᾶν Soph.

like καιρός, the best, most fitting time, Trag.; ἔργων, λόγων ἀκμή the time for doing, speaking, Soph.; ἀκμή ἐστι, c. inf., 'tis high time to do, Aesch.; ἐπ’ ἀκμῆς εἶναι, c. inf., to be on the point of doing, Eur.; ἐπ’ αὐτὴν ἥκει τὴν ἀκμήν ’tis come to the critical time, Dem.
ἀκμήν, acc. of ἀκμή, used as adv., just, Xen.
yet, still, Theocr., NTest.
untiring, unwearied, Il., Soph.
orig. prob. a thunderbolt, ἄκμων οὐρανόθεν κατιών Hes.
an anvil, Hom., etc.: metaph., λόγχης ἄκμονες very anvils to bear blows, Aesch.
the spine or backbone, Od.
without the fat of sacrifices, Anth.
a hearing, the sound heard, Il.
the thing heard, hearsay, report, news, tidings, μετὰ πατρὸς ἀκουήν in quest of tidings of his father, Od.; ἀκοῆι ἱστορεῖν, παραλαβεῖν τι to know by hearsay, Hdt.; so, ἐξ ἀκοῆς λέγειν Plat.
the sense of hearing, Hdt., etc.
the act of hearing, hearing, ἀκοῆι κλύειν, ἀκοαῖς δέχεσθαι, εἰς ἀκοὰς ἔρχεταί τι Soph., Eur.; δι’ ἀκοῆς αἰσθάνεσθαι Plat.
the ear, Sapph., Aesch.
sleepless, of the sea, Aesch.
not shared with another, c. dat., Eur.
act. having no share of or in, c. gen., Plat.: absol. unsocial, inhuman, Id.
a spouse, wife, Hom., etc.
licentiousness, intemperance, Thuc., etc.
to be licentious, intemperate, Ar., Plat., etc.
an act of ἀκολασία, Plut.
Lat. non castigatus, unchastised, undisciplined, unbridled, Hdt., attic, etc.
licentious, intemperate, opp. to σώφρων, Soph., etc.:— so in adv., ἀκολάστως ἔχειν Plat.; comp., ἀκολαστοτέρως ἔχειν πρός τι to be too intemperate in a thing, Xen.
a bit, morsel, Od.
to follow one, go after or with him, c. dat. pers., Ar., etc.; also, ἀκ. μετά τινος Plat.; σύν τινι Xen.; κατόπιν τινός Ar.:— absol., Plat., etc.
metaph. to follow, obey, τινι Thuc., etc.; ἀκ. τοῖς πράγμασιν to follow circumstances, Dem.
to follow the thread of a discourse, Plat.
of things, to follow upon, be consequent upon, τοῖς εἰρημένοις Id.
one must follow, Xen., etc.
a following, train, Soph., Plat.
a following upon, conformity with, τοῖς πράγμασι Id.
following, attending on; as Subst. a follower, attendant, Lat. pedisequus, Ar., Thuc., etc.; οἱ ἀκόλουθοι the camp-followers, Xen.
following after, c. gen., Νηρήιδων ἀκ. Soph.
following or consequent upon, in conformity with, c. gen., Ar.; also c. dat., Plat.:—absol. agreeing with one another, Xen., etc.:— adv. -θως, in accordance with, τοῖς νόμοις Dem.
unable to swim, Batr., Plut.
want of tending or care, Od.
untended.
without hair, bald, Luc.
not boastful, Aesch.
not boasting, Aesch.
unadorned, boorish, ἐγὼ δ’ ἄκομψος "rude I am in speech," Eur.
to sharpen, whet, μαχαίρας Ar.; λόγχην Xen.:—Mid., ἀκονᾶσθαι μαχαίρας to sharpen their swords, Id.
without knuckles:—without blows, Luc.
a whetstone, hone, Pind., etc.
made of aconite, Xen.
without the dust of the arena, i. e. without a struggle, without effort, Lat. sine pulvere, Thuc., Xen.
aconite, a poisonous plant, Theophr.
to hurl a javelin, τινός at one, Il.; ἐπί τινι Id.:—the weapon is put in dat., ἀκόντισε δουρί darted with his spear, Id.; also in acc., ἀκόντισαν ὀξέα δοῦρα darted their spears, Od.
c. acc. pers. to hit with a javelin, Hdt., etc.; Pass. to be so hit or wounded, Eur., Xen.
to shoot forth rays, of the moon, Eur.
intr. to pierce, εἴσω γῆς Id.

entry.etym: Dim. of ἄκων, Hhymn., Hdt., etc.
adverb of ἄκων, contr. for ἀεκοντί, Plut.

entry.sense: javelin-throwing, Xen.
a javelin's throw, Xen.
the thing thrown, a dart, javelin, Plut.
in pl. = ἀκοντισταί, Id.
a darter, javelin-man, Hom., Hdt., etc.
skilled in throwing the javelin, Xen.
the game of throwing the javelin, Il.
without weariness, and so,
pass. untired, Plat.
act. not wearying, of a horse, easy, Xen.
removing weariness, refreshing, Plat.
insatiate, Trag.; c. gen. insatiate in a thing, Aesch.:—in Soph. (πάντων ἀκορέστατος, most insatiate, most shameless), the word is either sync. for ἀκορεστότατος, or Sup. of ἀκορής, = ἀκόρεστος.
of things,
insatiate, unceasing, Lat. improbus, Trag.
act. not satiating, Aesch.
not liable to surfeit, φιλία Xen.
insatiate, unsated in or with a thing, c. gen., Il.
（κορέω) unswept, ungrimmed, ungarnished, Ar.
untiring, ceaseless, Lat. improbus, εἰρεσία Pind.
to be disorderly, to offend, Soph., Dem., etc.
unarranged, unorganised, Plat.:—adv. -τως, Id.
unfurnished with, c. dat., Xen.
disorder, Plat.: extravagance, Eur.:—in moral sense, disorderliness, disorderly conduct, Soph.
without order, disorderly, Aesch.:—in Hom. of Thersites' words, disorderly:— adv. -μως, Hdt., etc.
κόσμος ἄκοσμος, a world that is no world, Anth.; also of an inappropriate ornament, Id.
a cure, relief, remedy for a thing, c. gen., Od., etc.:—absol., ἄκος εὑρεῖν Il., Soph.; ἐξευρεῖν, λαβεῖν, ποιεῖσθαι, Hdt., etc.:—by a medical metaph., ἄκος ἐντέμνειν, τέμνειν, cf. ἐντέμνω II.
a means of obtaining a thing, c. gen., Eur.
only in aor1 part. ἵππος ἀκοστήσας ἐπὶ φάτνηι a horse corn-fed at manger, a stalled horse, Il.
barley.
to hearken or listen to, c. gen., Od.; δαιτὸς ἀκουάζεσθον ye are bidden to the feast, Il.
without male heir, Od.
（κουρά) unshaven, unshorn, Ar.
heard of God, Anth.
a thing heard, such as music, Xen.
a rumour, tale, Soph.
one must hear or hearken to, c. gen. pers., Hdt., etc.; c. acc. rei, Plat.
ἀκουστέος, α, ον, to be hearkened to, Soph.
heard, audible, Hhymn., Plat., etc.
that should be heard, Soph., Eur.

to hear, Hom., etc. —Construct., properly, c. acc. of thing heard, gen. of pers. from whom it is heard, ταῦτα Καλυψοῦς ἤκουσα Od.; the gen. pers. may be omitted, ἀκήκοας λόγον Soph., or the acc. rei, ἄκουε τοῦ θανόντος Id.:—often however c. gen. rei, to have hearing of a thing.
c. gen. objecti, to hear of, hear tell of, ἀκ. πατρός Od.; so c. acc., Od.:—so, ἀκ. περί τινος.
the pers. from whom the thing is heard takes a prep., ἀκούειν τι ἀπό, ἔκ, παρά, πρός τινος, Il., attic
to know by hearsay, εἴ που ἀκούεις Od.; so Plat., etc.
absol. to hearken, give ear, to begin a proclamation, ἀκούετε λεώι hear, O people.
to listen to, give ear to, Il.
to obey, c. gen., or more rarely c. dat., Id.
to hear and understand, κλύοντες οὐκ ἤκουον Aesch.

in pass. sense, with an adv., to hear oneself called, be called so and so, like Lat. audire, κακῶς ἀκ. πρός τινος to be ill spoken of by one, Hdt.; εὖ, κακῶς, ἄριστα ἀκ., Lat. bene, male audire, Id., attic
with a Noun, ἀκούειν κακός, καλός Soph., Plat.; κόλακες ἀκούουσι Dem.
c. acc. rei, ἀκ. κακά to have evil spoken of one, Ar.; φήμας κακὰς ἤκουσεν Eur.
unfulfilled, fruitless, Lat. irritus, Hom.
not barking, Aesch.
blowing strongly, fresh-blowing, of the north and west wind, Od.; si ἀκραὲς erit, if it shall be clear weather, Cic.
dwelling on the heights, Eur.
unmixed, pure, Eur., Ar.: metaph., πενία ἀκρ. utter poverty, Anth.
unharmed, entire, Lat. integer, Eur., Thuc.
c. gen. untouched by a thing, Soph.
unfulfilled, fruitless, Pind., Aesch.:—neut. pl. as adv., in vain, Id., Eur.
a headland, foreland, cape, Hom., etc.
a mountain-top, summit: used by Hom. only in the phrase κατ’ ἄκρης from top to bottom, i. e. utterly, πόλιν αἱρέειν κατ’ ἄκρης Hdt.; so in attic, κατ’ ἄκρας utterly, Trag., Plat.
the citadel of a city, Lat. arx, Xen.
bad mixture, ill temperature, Theophr.
incontinence, want of self-control, Plat.:—the later form is ἀκρασία.
powerless, impotent, Soph.
c. gen. rei, not having power or command over a thing, Lat. impotens, γλώσσης Aesch.; ὀργῆς Thuc.:—also, intemperate in the use of a thing, οἴνου Xen., Arist.; περὶ τὰ πόματα Id.
absol. without command over oneself, incontinent, Lat. impotens sui, Id.
of things, immoderate, δαπάνη Anth.
to drink wine unmixed with water: hence, to breakfast, because this meal consisted of bread dipped in wine, Ar.
a breakfast, Arist.
having breakfasted, Theocr.
a drinking of sheer wine, Hdt.
a drinker of sheer wine, Hdt.
of liquids, unmixed, sheer, of wine, Od.:—esp., οἶνος ἄκρητος wine without water, Lat. merum, Hdt.; and ἄκρατος without (οἶνος), Ar., etc.
metaph., ἄκρ. μέλαν pure black, Theophr.; ἄκρατος νύξ sheer night, Aesch.; ἄκρ. νοῦς pure intellect, Xen.
of conditions or states, pure, untempered, absolute, ἐλευθερία, ἡδονή Plat.; ἄκρ. ψεῦδος a sheer lie, Id.:—adv. -τως absolutely, Luc.
of persons, intemperate, excessive, violent, ἄκρατος ὀργήν Aesch.: so of things we feel, ἄκρ. ὀργή, ἄκρ. καῦμα, etc.
comp. ἀκρατέστερος, Sup. -έστατος (as if from ἀκρατής).
= ἀκρατής I, Soph.
= ἀκρατής II, Plat.
to be passionate, Plat.
quick to anger, passionate, Ar.
in passionate distress, Theocr.
a branch, twig, spray, Eur., Theocr.
at eventide, Anth.: neut. ἀκρέσπερον as adv., Theocr.
a youth in his prime, Anth.
in earliest youth, Theocr.

exactness, minute accuracy, precision, Thuc., etc.; with Preps. in adv. sense, δι’ ἀκριβείας, = ἀκριβῶς, with minuteness or precision, Plat.; so, εἰς τὴν ἀκρ., πρὸς τὴν ἀκρ. Id.:— ἡ ἀκρ. τοῦ ναυτικοῦ its perfect condition, Thuc.
parsimony, frugality, Plut.
exact, accurate, precise, made or done to a nicety, Eur., etc.
of persons, exact, precise, strict, consummate, Thuc., etc.:—esp. painfully exact, over-nice, precise, curious, Plat.:— τὸ ἀκριβές = ἀκρίβεια, Thuc.:—adv. -βῶς, to a nicety, precisely, Hdt., etc.
parsimonious, frugal, Menand.
to be exact or precise in language or thought, Plat.; c. acc. rei, to weigh accurately, Id.
precise in argument.
to make exact or accurate, Eur.; ἀκρ. τάδε to be perfect in bearing these hardships, Xen.:—Pass. to be or become perfect, Ar.
to investigate accurately, to understand thoroughly, οἱ τάδ’ ἠκριβωκότες Eur.; τοὔνομά μου σὺ ἀκριβοῖς; are you sure of my name? Plat.
a locust-cage, Theocr.
want of distinctness, Xen.
a locust, Il.
a hill-top, Od.
shedding floods of tears, Anth.
recklessly or confusedly babbling, Il.
hard of interpretation, Od.
undistinguishable, unarranged, disorderly, Hom.; τύμβος ἄκριτος one common undistinguished grave, Il.
continual, unceasing, ἄχεα Id.; neut. as adv., πενθήμεναι ἄκριτον αἰεί Od.:— ὄρος ἄκρ. a continuous mountain-range, Anth., Babr.
undecided, doubtful, νείκεα, ἄεθλος Il.; ἀκρίτων ὄντων while the issue was doubtful, Thuc.:—adv. ἀκρίτως, without decisive issue, Id.
unjudged, untried, of persons and things, ἄκριτόν τινα κτείνειν to put to death without trial, Lat. indicta causa, Hdt., etc.
act. not giving a judgment, Id.: without judgment, ill-judged, rash, Eur.
of undistinguishable, i. e. closely blending, leafage, Il.
undistinguishably mixed, Aesch.
anything heard with pleasure, as a play or musical piece, Xen.
designed for hearing only, Plut.
to hearken to, listen to, c. gen. pers., acc. rei, Thuc., etc.; c. gen. rei, Id.
absol. to listen, ὁ ἀκροώμενος a hearer, disciple, Plat., Xen.
to attend to, obey, τινός Thuc., etc.
a hearing or listening, Thuc., etc.
obedience to another, c. gen., Id.
one must listen to, τινός Ar.
a place of audience, NTest.
an audience, Plut.
a hearer, Lat. auditor, Thuc., etc.: a disciple, Arist.
a lecturer, Plut.
of or for hearing, μισθὸς ἀκρ. a lecturer's fee, Luc.
tinged at the point, Anth.
with a point at the end, Anth.
to sling, Anth.
a slinging, skirmishing, Appian.
to throw from afar, to fight with missiles, to skirmish, πρός τινα or absol., Thuc., Xen.:—metaph., ἀκρ. ἔπεσι Hdt.—The Act. in Anth.
a skirmishing, Xen., etc.
pass., struck from afar, Aesch.
act. a slinger, skirmisher.
the foreskin, NTest.
circumcision, Id.;—and as collect. the uncircumcision, i. e. the uncircumcised, Id.
at the extreme angle, ἀκρ. λίθος the corner foundation-stone, NTest.
bound at the end or top, Anth.
fruit-trees, Xen.
fruits, Arist.
touching on the surface, touching the lips, Anth.
to take of the best, pick out for oneself, Eur.
the topmost part of a heap, the choice part, first-fruits, taken as an offering to the gods, Hdt., etc.
only in epic part.; growing black on the surface, of a swollen stream, Il.
at the beginning of night, in twilight, Hes.
with hair on the crown, of the Thracians, who seem to have shaved all the head except the crown, Il.
with leaves at the top, Eur., Theocr.
the citadel of Corinth, Eur., Xen.
with the ends made of stone; ξόανον ἀκρ. a statue with the head, arms, and legs marble, the rest wood, Anth.
to gather at top, στάχυας Anth.
a mountaineer, Anth.
high-crested, peaked, Anth.
as Subst. a mountain crest, Plut.
to untie at the ends, Anth.
on the verge of madness, Hdt.
leaded at the edge, of a net, Anth.
the highest or furthest point:
a mountain-top, peak, Hom., etc.
a headland, foreland, cape, Od.
an end, extremity, Plat.; ἄκρα χειρῶν the hands, Luc.
metaph. the highest pitch, height, Pind.; εἰς ἄκρον exceedingly, Theocr.; τὰ ἄκρα τοῖς ἄκροις ἀποδιδόναι the highest place to the highest men, Plat.; ἄκρα φέρεσθαι to win the prize, Theocr.
of persons, Ἄργεος ἄκρα the oldest rulers of Argos, Id.
with the tip of the nail, Anth.
at night-fall, at even, Theocr., etc.
exceeding sad, Aesch.
on tiptoe, Luc.
the upper city, i. e. the citadel, Lat. arx, Od., Hdt.:—esp. the Acropolis of Athens, which served as the treasury, Thuc.
metaph. of men, a tower of defence, Theogn.
high-ranging, lofty, Hom.
piercing with the point, Od.
the end of a ship's prow, Strab.
the tip of the wing, Anth.
pointed or shod with iron, Anth.
high in wisdom, Pind.
at the furthest point, and so either topmost = Lat. summus, or outermost = Lat. extremus:
highest, topmost, ἐν ἄκρηι πόλει = ἐν ἀκροπόλει, Il.; μέλαν ὕδωρ ἄκρον at its surface, Id., etc.

outermost, ἄκρη χείρ, ἄκροι πόδες, ἄκρος ὦμος the end of the hand, ends of the feet, tip of the shoulder, Id., Thuc.; ἐπ’ ἄκρων [δακτύλων] on tiptoe, Soph.; ἄκροισι λαίφους κρασπέδοις with the outermost edges of the sail, i. e. under close-reefed sails, Eur.
of Time, it denotes completeness, ἄκραι σὺν ἑσπέραι when eve was fully come, Pind.; ἄκρας νυκτός at dead of night, Soph.

of Degree, the highest in its kind, exceeding good, consummate, excellent: of persons, Hdt., etc.; ἄκρος μάντις Soph.:—often with an acc. modi added, ψυχὴν οὐκ ἄκρος not strong in mind, Hdt.; ἄκροι τὰ πολέμια, skilful in war, Id., etc.; also c. gen. modi, οἱ ἄκροι τῆς ποιήσεως Plat.; also, ἄκρος εἰς or περί τι Id.
as Subst., v. ἄκρα, ἄκρον.
neut. as adv. on the top or surface, just, ἄκρον ἐπὶ ῥηγμῖνος on the very edge of the surf, il.
exceedingly, Theocr.
utterly, completely, Plat.
the gunwale of a ship, Plut.
apt to trip, unsteady, precarious, Plat.
the fag-end of a verse, Thuc.
to lop off, shave the surface, Xen.
cut off sharp, abrupt, Polyb.
the snout or pipe of a pair of bellows, Thuc.
yawning at top, Anth.
to struggle at arm's length, of a kind of wrestling, in which they grasped one another's hands, without clasping the body, Plat., etc.
a wart with a thin neck, Plut.
unhidden, Eur.
free from ice, ἡ χώρη Hdt.
the point of the shoulder; in a horse, the withers, Xen.
a dub. word in Aesch., perh. = ἀκρωτηριασμός, mutilation.
the tip of the nail: metaph. the ridge of a mountain, Xen.
with nails at the extremities, χερὸς ἀκρώνυχα the tips of the fingers, Anth.
a mountain-ridge, Xen., Theocr.

to cut off the extremities, mutilate, τὰς πρῴρας ἠκρωτηρίασαν cut the beaks off the prows, Hdt.:—so in Mid., τὰς τριήρεις ἀκρωτηριασάμενοι Xen.; perf. pass. in mid. sense, ἠκρωτηριασμένοι τὰς πατρίδας having mutilated their countries, Dem.
any prominent part, ἀκρ. τοῦ οὔρεος a mountain-peak, Hdt.
a cape, promontory, Id., Thuc.
the extremity of anything, ἀκρ. νηός a ship's beak, Hdt.
in pl. the extremities of the body, hands and feet, fingers and toes, Thuc., etc.; τὰ ἀκρ. τῆς Νίκης her wings, Dem.
to lift up, raise, ἀκταίνειν στάσιν to raise oneself so as to stand, to stand upright, Aesch.; so in the form ἀκταινόω, Plat.
on the coast, of Ionian cities, Thuc.: so, Ἀκταία (sc. γῆ), coast-land, an old name of Attica, Id.
haunting the coast, βάτραχοι Babr.
without property, poor, τίνος in a thing, Anth.
the elder-tree, Luc.
uncombed, unkempt, Soph.
one must lead, Plat., etc.; εἰρήνην ἀκτέον one must keep peace, Dem.
one must go or march, Xen.
unhallowed by funeral rites, Soph.
without property, poor, χρυσοῖο in gold, Il.: absol., ἀκτ. πενία Theocr.
a headland, foreland, promontory, shore, Od., etc.: of the banks of rivers, ἀκταὶ Σιμόεντος Aesch.; Ἀχέροντος Soph.
generally, coast-land, ἀκταὶ διφάσιαι of the N. and S. coasts of Asia Minor, Hdt.; of Attica (cf. ἀκταῖος), Soph.
generally, any edge or strand, like the sea-coast, Lat. ora, χώματος ἀκτή of a sepulchral mound, Aesch.; βώμιος ἀ. of an altar, Soph. (Perh. from ἄγνυμι, cf. ῥηγμίν.）
corn or meal, Δημήτερος ἀκτή Il.; ἀλφίτου ἀκτή Od.
not worth getting, Plat.
like a ray, Luc.
haunting the shore, of Pan, Theocr.
a ray, beam, of the sun, Hom.; ἀνὰ μέσσαν ἀκτῖνα, i. e. from the south, Soph.; ἀκτῖνες τελευτῶσαι sunset, Eur.
metaph. brightness, splendour, glory, Pind.
like Lat. radius, the spoke of a wheel, Anth.
a dweller on the coast, Anth.
untilled, Hhymn.
a leader, Aesch.
without steersman, Plut.
an acorn, the fruit of the ilex, Od.
not washed by the waves, ψαμάθοις ἐπ’ ἀκυμάντοις on sands washed by no waves, i. e. on the sands of the stadium, Eur.
waveless, calm, πέλαγος Luc.
tranquil, ἀκ. βίοτος Eur.
without fruit, barren, of women, Eur.
without authority:

of laws and contracts, invalid, ἄκυρον ποιεῖν, Lat. irritum facere, to set aside, and ἄκυρον γίγνεσθαι, to become of no force, to be set aside, Plat.; νόμοις ἀκύροις χρωμένη, i. e. having laws, but not enforcing them, Thuc.
of persons, having no right or power, ἄκ. ποιεῖν τινά Xen.; c. gen., ἄκυροι πάντων γενήσεσθε Dem.
unconfirmed, Eur.
a point, Hom., etc.
unhindered, Luc.: adv. -τως, Plat.
not ridiculed: adv. -τως, Luc.
a javelin, dart, Hom., etc.
without oars, Anth.
the office of Ἀλαβάρχης, in Egypt, ἐξ Ἀλαβαρχίης , Anth.
a case for alabaster ornaments, Dem.
a box or casket of alabaster, Hdt., Ar., etc.: ἀλάβαστρος is a later form in Lxx., NTest., Plut.
a box or casket of alabaster, in NTest., pl. ἀλάβαστρα or -τα in Theocr. and Anth.
adverb of ἅλς, to or into the sea, Il., etc.; also, εἰς ἅλαδε Od.
either from ἅλλομαι, the bounding race; or from ἅλς, a race over the sea.
false pretension, imposture, quackery, Ar., Plat., etc.
an imposture, piece of quackery, Ar., etc.
to make false pretensions, of the Sophists, Xen.
boastful, braggart, Xen. adv. -κῶς, Plut.
properly a vagabond: then, a false pretender, impostor, quack, of Sophists, Ar., Plat., etc.
as adj. swaggering, boastful, braggart, Lat. gloriosus, Hdt., Plat.
to wander about, Aesch., Eur.; ἀλ. πόδα to wander on foot, Id.
a shouting, Soph., Hdt.
= ἀλαλαγή, a shouting.
a loud noise, τυμπάνων, αὐλοῦ Eur.

entry.etym: (formed from the cry ἀλαλαί as ἐλελίζω, ὀλολύζω from similar sounds)
entry.sense: to raise the war-cry, Xen.; c. acc. cogn., νίκην ἀλαλάζειν to shout the shout of victory, Soph.
generally, to cry or shout aloud, of Bacchus and the Bacchae, Eur.
rarely of a cry of pain, ἠλάλαζε δυσθνῆσκον Id.
rarely also of other sounds than the voice, to sound loudly, clang, NTest.
exclam. of joy, Ar.

entry.etym: perf. of ἀλάομαι, only used in pres. sense
the part. ἀλαλήμενος takes the accent of pres.
entry.sense: to wander or roam about, like a beggar, Od.; of seamen, Id.
a loud cry, Eur.:— esp. the cry with which battle was begun, hence the battle-cry, Pind.
the shout of victory, Il.: war-cry, Id., Hes.
rarely, a cry of woe or wailing, Il.
a loud noise, αὐλῶν Anth.
unutterable, Anth., NTest.

entry.etym: From ΑΛΚ, come ἄλαλκε, ἀλκή, ἄλκαρ, ἄλκιμος, ἀλέξω: identical with ΑΡΚ, whence ἀρκέω, Lat. arceo, arx, arca.
entry.sense: to ward or keep off, τί τινι something from a person, Il., etc.; more rarely τί τινος Id.
name of Athena, prob. from ἀλαλκεῖν, the Protectress, Il.
a Boeot. month, answering to attic μαιμακτηριών, Plut.
speechless, NTest.

entry.etym: a perf. formed by redupl. from *ἀλυκτέω.
entry.sense: to be sore distressed, Il.
without light, darksome, Hhymn.; of the nether world, Soph.
ἀλ. ἡλίου out of the sun's light, Soph.
metaph. obscure, Plut.
to wander, stray or roam about, Hom., etc.: to wander from home, be banished, Soph.; c. acc. loci, ἀλ. γῆν to wander over the land, Id.
c. gen. to wander away from, cease to enjoy, εὐφροσύνας Pind.; τῆς πάροιθ’ εὐπραξίας Eur.
metaph. to wander in mind, be distraught, Soph.
a blind, i. e. useless, careless, watch, Hom., Hes.

entry.etym: Commonly regarded as a compd. of α privat. and λάω video.
entry.sense: not seeing, blind, Od., Trag., etc.; ἕλκος ἀλαόν a blinding wound, i. e. blindness, Id.
to blind, ὀφθαλμοῦ of an eye, Od.
exhausted, powerless, feeble, Hom., Hes.; Comp. ἀλαπαδνότεροι Il.

entry.etym: From Root ΛΑΠ, with α prefixed, cf. λαπάσσω.
entry.sense: to empty, drain, exhaust, Od.; ἀλ. πόλιν to plunder it, Il.; and of men, to destroy, Id.
salt, NTest., Plut.
to be full of wrath, Il.
under the influence of an ἀλάστωρ: suffering cruelly, Soph.
not to be forgotten, insufferable, unceasing, πένθος, ἄχος Hom.: neut. as adv., incessantly, Od.
of persons, ἄλαστε accursed wretch! Il., Soph.
the avenging deity, destroying angel, Trag.; ἀλ. οὑμός Soph.; βουκόλων ἀλάστωρ the herdsmen's plague, of the Nemean lion, Id.
pass. he who suffers from such vengeance, an accursed wretch, Aesch., Dem.
entry.etym: Either from ἄλαστος, or from ἀλάομαι, he that makes to wander.

entry.sense: a blinding, Od.
attic for epic ἀλεγεινός, giving pain, painful, grievous, Trag., Thuc.:—adv. -νῶς, Soph., Plat.
rare in pass. sense, feeling pain, grievously suffering, suffering, Soph. —Cf. ἀλγίων, -ιστος.
to feel bodily pain, suffer, Il., Hdt., etc.; the suffering part in acc., ἀλγ. ἧπαρ Aesch.; τὸν δάκτυλον, τὰ ὄμματα Plat.
to suffer hardship, Od.

to feel pain of mind, to grieve, be troubled or distressed, ἀλγεῖν ψυχήν, φρένα Hdt., Eur., etc.; ἀλγ. τινί to be pained at a thing, Hdt., Soph.; ἐπί τινι Id.; διά τι Hdt.; περί τι or τινος Thuc.; c. gen., Aesch.; c. acc., ἀλγῶ μὲν ἔργα Id.; c. part., ἤλγης’ ἀκούσας Hdt.
a sense of pain, pain, suffering, Hdt., Eur., etc.
of mind, pain, grief, Soph., Eur., etc.
pain, suffering, Soph., Eur.
sense of pain, Soph.
painful, grievous, Hes.

entry.etym: irreg. comp. and Sup. of ἀλγεινός, formed from ἄλγος (as καλλίων, -ιστος from κάλλος, αἰσχίων, -ιστος from αἶσχος）
In Hom. ἄλγιον, ι short, but ῑ always in attic.
entry.sense: more or most painful, grievous or distressing:— of the comp., Hom. has only neut. ἄλγιον, so much the worse, all the harder; ἀλγίστη δαμάσασθαι (of a mule), Il.
pain of body, Il., Soph.
pain of mind, grief, distress, Hom.
anything that causes pain, Bion., Anth.

entry.etym: The future middle ἀλγυνοῦμαι is used in a passive sense.
entry.sense: to pain, grieve, distress, τινά Aesch., etc.:—Pass. to be grieved at a thing, τινι Soph.; ἐπί τινι Eur.; τι Soph.: c. part., εἰσιδοῦσα ἠλγύνθην Aesch.

entry.etym: Only in pres. and imperf., except epic 3rd sg. aor2 ἤλδανε.
entry.sense: to make to grow, μέλε’ ἤλδανε she filled out his limbs, Od.: to increase, multiply, ἀλδαίνειν κακά Aesch.
to grow, wax, Il.
trans. = ἀλδαίνω, Theocr.
to warm, make warm, Arist.
intr. to grow warm, be warm, Ar.
an escape, Il.; c. gen. shelter from ὑετοῦ Hes.
warmth, heat, Od., Ar. (Deriv. uncertain.)
c. inf., ἵπποι ἀλεγεινοὶ δαμήμεναι hard to break, Il.

entry.etym: epic Verb, only in pres. and imperf.
entry.sense: to trouble oneself about a thing, to care for, in Hom. always with negat., c. gen. rei, τῶν μὲν ἄρ’ οὐκ ἀλέγιζε πατήρ Il.: absol. to take heed, Id.
to care for, furnish, c. acc., ἄλλας δ’ ἀλεγύνετε δαῖτας find your meals elsewhere; δαῖτ’ ἀλέγυνον, of invited guests; but, δαῖτας ἐΐσας ἀλ. to prepare a meal for guests, all in Od.

entry.etym: Prob. from Root ΛΕΓ, = LIG in Lat. religio, α being euphonic.
entry.sense: to trouble oneself, have a care, mostly with negat.:
absol., οὐκ ἀλ. to have no care, heed not, Lat. negligo, Hom.; κύνες οὐκ ἀλέγουσαι careless, reckless dogs, Od.; without negat., ἀλέγουσι κιοῦσαι are heedful in their course.
with a case,
c. gen. to care for, Od., Aesch.
c. acc. to heed, regard, respect, Il.:—without a negat., ὅπλα ἀλέγουσιν take care of, Od.
open to the sun, warm, hot, χώρη Hdt., Xen.

entry.etym: epic Verb, only in pres. and imperf.
entry.sense: to avoid, shun, c. acc., Od.; c. inf., κτεῖναι ἀλέεινε he avoided killing him, Il.
in the sun, ὕπνος Soph.
wheaten flour, Od.; cf. ἄλευρον.
anything used for anointing, unguent, fat, oil, Plat.
an anointer, a teacher of gymnastics, Arist.:—metaph. a teacher, Plut.
a cup, goblet, χρύσειον Hom.
one who flees from punishment, a culprit, a sinner, Hom.
anointing-oil, unguent, oil, Hom.
generally, anything used for smearing, pitch or resin, to seal wine-jars, Hes., Aesch., Theocr., etc.

entry.etym: From Root !lip, with α prefixed, v. λίπος
entry.sense: to anoint with oil, oil the skin, as was done after bathing, or before gymnastic exercises, the Act. referring to the act of another, Mid. to oneself, Il.; often with λίπα added (v. λίπα):— metaph. to prepare as if for gymnastics, to stimulate, Plat., etc.
like ἐπαλείφω, to plaster, οὔατα ἀλεῖψαι to stop up the ears, Od.
an anointing:—a method or custom of anointing, Hdt.
a cockerel, Babr.
cock-crow, i.e. the third watch of the night, Aesop., NTest.
unbedded, unwedded, Soph., etc.; ἄλεκτρ’, ἄνυμφα γάμων ἁμιλλήματα, much like γάμος ἄγαμος, i. e. a lawless, unhallowed marriage, Id.; ἄλεκτρα, as adv., Id.
a hen, Ar.
masc., a cock, Theogn., etc.
fem. = ἀλεκτρύαινα, a hen, Ar.
a cock, Aesch., etc.
to ward off, Anth.
a partisan of Alexander, Plut.
defending men, πόλεμος Inscr. ap. Diod.
the usual name of Paris in Il., cf. Aesch. Ag. 61, 363.
Alexander-like, Menand.
keeping off the wind, Od.
a defence, remedy, Aesch.
a keeping off, defence, Hdt.
able to keep off, of the gods, Lat. Averrunci, Aesch.; ξύλον ἀλ. a club for defence, Eur.
ἀλεξητήριον (sc. φάρμακον), a remedy: protection, Xen.
one who keeps off, ἀλ. μάχης a stemmer of battle, a champion, Il.

entry.etym: from ἀλέξω and ἀπά or Ἄρης
entry.sense: (from ἀρά) she that keeps off a curse, or (from Ἄρης) she that guards from death and ruin, Hes.
keeping off darts, Anth.
keeping off evil or mischief, Il.: c. gen., δίψης ἀλ. Anth.
protecting mortals, Pind.
warding off death, Soph.
an antidote, remedy, Plat.:— τινός against a thing, Id.

entry.etym: Note that some stems are formed from ἀλεξέω and others from ἀλέκω.
entry.sense: to ward or keep off, turn away or aside; c. acc. rei, Ζεὺς τό γ’ ἀλεξήσειε Od.; c. acc. rei et dat. pers., Δαναοῖσιν ἀλεξήσειν κακὸν ἦμαρ will ward it off from them, Il., etc.: —then c. dat. pers. only, to assist, defend, Id., Xen.; absol. to lend aid, Il.: —Mid. to keep off from oneself, defend oneself against, c. acc., Id.: absol. to defend oneself, Id., Soph.
Mid., also, to recompense, requite, τοὺς εὖ καὶ κακῶς ποιοῦντας ἀλεξόμενος Xen.

entry.etym: Prob. from same root as ἀλάομαι.
entry.sense: to avoid, shun, c. acc. rei, ἔγχεα ἀλεώμεθα, ἠλεύατο ἔγχος, ἀλεύατο κῆρα, ἀλεώμεθα μῆνιν, τὸ κῆτος ἀλέαιτο, — all in Il.; rarely c. acc. pers., θεοὺς ἀλέασθαι, Id.:—c. inf. to avoid doing; ἀλεύεται (epic 3rd sg. subj. for -ηται) ἠπεροπεύειν Od.
absol. to flee for one's life, flee, τὸν μὲν ἀλευάμενον τὸν δὲ κτάμενον Il.; οὔτε φυγέειν δύνατ’ οὔτ’ ἀλέασθαι Id.
a grinder, v. ὄνος II. 2.
a grinding, Plut.
to grind, Od.
that which grinds or pounds, a pestle, Ar.
a female slave who grinds corn, γυνὴ ἀλετρίς Od.
wheaten flour, distinguished from ἄλφιτα (barley-meal), Hdt., etc.
to remove, keep away; aor1 imperat., ἄλευσον ὕβριν Aesch.; κακὸν ἀλεύσατε Id.: absol. in pres. ἄλευ, for ἄλευε, avert the evil, Id.:—Mid., ἀλεύομαι, v. ἀλέομαι.

entry.etym: From Root ΑΛ, came also ἀλήθω, ἀλείατα, ἄλευρον, ἄλως, ἀλωή.
entry.sense: to grind, bruise, pound, Od.
avoidance, escape, Il., Hdt.
c. gen. a means of avoiding, a defence or shelter from δηΐων ἀνδρῶν Il.: absol. a defence, Id., Hdt.
truth, as opp. to a lie, παιδὸς πᾶσαν ἀλ. μυθεῖσθαι to tell the whole truth about the lad, Od.; so, χρᾶσθαι τῇ ἀλ. Hdt.; ἡ ἀλ. περί τινος Thuc.
truth, reality, opp. to appearance, τῶν ἔργων ἡ ἀλ. Thuc.
adverb. usages, τῇ ἀληθείᾳ in very truth, Thuc.; rarely ἀληθείᾳ Plat.; ἐπ’ ἀληθείας in truth and reality, Dem.; μετ’ ἀληθείας Xen.; κατ’ ἀλήθειαν Arist.
the character of the ἀληθής, truthfulness, sincerity, frankness, candour, Hdt., etc.
to speak truth, Aesch., etc.; τὰς δέκα ἡμέρας ἠλήθευσε he was right about the 10 days, Xen.; ἀλ. τοὺς ἐπαίνους to prove their praises true, Luc.
Pass. to come true, of predictions, Xen.
unconcealed, true:
true, opp. to ψευδής, Hom.; τὸ ἀληθές, by crasis τἀληθές, ionic τὠληθές, and τὰ ἀληθῆ, by crasis τἀληθῆ the truth, Hdt., attic
of persons, truthful, Il., attic
of oracles and the like, true, coming true, Aesch., etc.
adv. ἀληθῶς, ionic -θέως, truly, Hdt., etc.
really, actually, in reality, Aesch., Thuc., etc.; so, ὡς ἀληθῶς Eur., Plat., etc.
neut. as adv., proparox. ἄληθες; itane? indeed? really? in sooth? ironically, Soph., Eur., etc.
τὸ ἀληθές really and truly, Lat. revera, Plat., etc.; so, τὸ ἀληθέστατον in very truth, Thuc.
agreeable to truth:
of persons, truthful, trusty, Xen., Dem.
of things, true, real, Plat.; ἐς ἀλ. ἄνδρ’ ἀποβῆναι to turn out a true man, Theocr.:—adv. -νῶς, truly, really, Plat., etc.
prophet of truth, Aesch.
Ἀλήϊον πεδίον the plain of wandering (over which Bellerophon wandered), in Lycia or Cilicia, Il.
poor in lands, Il.
fine meal: metaph. of a wily knave, such as Ulysses, Soph.
a wanderer, rover, Od., Anth.
ceaseless wandering, Od., etc.
wandering of mind, distraction, Eur.
act., ἄλαι βροτῶν δύσορμοι, of storms such as keep men wandering without haven and rest, Aesch.; cf. ἀλύω.
not to be laid hold of, hard to catch, Plut.; comp. ἀληπτότερος less amenable, Thuc.
incomprehensible, Plut.

entry.etym: εἴλω, cf. ἀολλής; ionic word equiv. to attic ἀθρόος,
entry.sense: assembled, thronged, in a mass, all at once, Lat. confertus, Hes., Hdt.; either in pl., ὡς ἁλέες εἴησαν οἱ Ἕλληνες, or with collective nouns, ἁλὴς γενομένη πᾶσα ἡ Ἑλλάς Id.
a wandering, roaming, Aesch., Eur.
to wander, roam about, of beggars, Od.; of exiles, Eur.
a wanderer, stroller, rover, vagabond, of beggars, Hom.; of exiles, Trag.; τὸν μακρῶν ἀλάταν πόνων one who has wandered in long labours, Soph.
as adj. vagrant, roving, βίος Hdt.
Pass., to become whole and sound, ἄλθετο χείρ (epic 3rd sg. imperf.) Il.
a seaman, Soph.
the sea-eagle, osprey, Ar.
blowing seaward, Od.
properly sea-blooming: then = ἁλιπόρφυρος, purple, Anth.
an assembly of the people, in doric states, answering to attic ἐκκλησία, Hdt., etc.
unshrinking, unabating, Il.; neut. as adv., μηδ’ ἀλίαστον ὀδύρεο nor mourn incessant, Id.; so, φρὴν ἀλίαστος φρίσσει Eur.
of persons, undaunted, Id.
a dead body, corpse, Plat.
washed by the sea, Anth.
resembling, like, Hom.:—cf. the compd. ἐναλίγκιος.
sea-tossed, Aesch.
fishing, Arist.
sea-fenced, sea-girt, Pind.
one who has to do with the sea, and so,
a fisher, Hom., etc.
a seaman, sailor, Od.; with another Subst., ἐρέτας ἁλιῆας sea-faring rowers, Id.
of or for fishing, Xen., Arist.; —ἡ ἁλιευτική (with or without τέχνη) the art of fishing, Plat.
to be a fisher, Plut., Luc., etc.
to fish, go fishing, NTest.
to gather together, to muster, military forces, Hdt.:—Pass. to meet together, assemble, Id.
to salt, and Pass. to be salted, Arist., NTest.
sea-girt, Anth.
living on or in the sea, Anth.
sweeping the sea, κώπη Eur.
without stones, not stony, of land, Xen.
a Halicarnassian, Id.
from Halicarnassus, Luc.
a Doric city of Caria, Hdt., etc.
sea-washed, Soph.
groaning at sea, of ships in bad weather, Soph.
of waves, roaring on the sea, Eur.
surrounded by waves, Anth.
without harbour, harbourless, Aesch., Thuc., etc.
metaph. without shelter, inhospitable, Eur.
want of harbours, Xen.
flowing into the sea, of rivers, Hom.
sea-flowing, of the sea, Anth.
to make to roll (but Act. only occurs in compos. with ἐξ):— Pass. to roll in the dust (cf. ἀλινδήθρα):— metaph. to roam about, Anth.
a sandy place for horses to roll in, Lat. volutabrum: metaph., ἀλινδήθραι ἐπῶν, i. e. words big enough for rolling places, Ar.

entry.etym: ἅλς, νήχω, fem. as if from *ἁλινηκτήρ
entry.sense: swimming in the sea, Anth.
swimming in the sea, Anth.
of salt, Hdt.
without a net, ἄλ. θήρα a chase in which no net is used, Anth.
worn by the sea, Anth.
of the sea, Lat. marinus, of sea-gods and nymphs, Hom., etc.; ἅλ. ψάμαθοι the sea sand, Od.
fruitless, unprofitable, vain, idle, Hom.: neut. ἅλιον as adv., in vain, Il.; regul. adv. ἁλίως, Soph.
sea-bred, φῶκαι Od.
to make fruitless, frustrate, disappoint, Διὸς νόον Od.; οὐδ’ ἁλίωσε βέλος nor did he hurl the spear in vain, Il.
not fit for a suppliant, Soph.
a plain by the sea:— as the plain near Piraeeus was called, Xen.
roaming the sea, Soph., Anth.
sea-wandering, Anth.
a wandering voyage, Anth.
sea-beaten, Pind.
covered with water, Il.
sailing on the sea, ναῦς Arion.
through which the sea flows, Luc.
of sea-purple, of true purple dye, Od.
against which the sea breaks, Anth.
sea-surging, Anth.
dashed over by the sea, Anth.
ἁλ. πόροι the pathways of the raging sea, Aesch.
washed by the sea, Anth.
to pollute.
a pollution, NTest.

entry.etym: a defect. Pass., the Act. being supplied by αἱρέω
entry.sense: to be taken, conquered, of persons and places, Hom., etc.; ἁλίσκεσθαι εἰς πολεμίους to fall into the hands of the enemy, Plat.
to be caught, seized, θανάτῳ ἁλῶναι or without θανάτῳ, to die, Hom.; ἑάλωσαν εἰς Ἀθήνας γράμματα letters were seized and taken to Athens, Xen.
in good sense, to be won, achieved, attained, Soph., etc.
with part. to be caught or detected doing a thing, Hdt.; ἐὰν ἁλῷς τοῦτο πράττων Plat.; also with a Subst. or adj., the part. ὤν being omitted, οὐ γὰρ δὴ φονεὺς ἁλώσομαι Soph., Ar.
as attic law-term, to be convicted and condemned, Plat., Dem.:—c. gen. criminis, to be convicted of, ἁλῶναι ψευδομαρτυριῶν, etc.
in heaps, crowds, swarms, in abundance, in plenty; and then, sufficiently, enough, Lat. satis:
with Verbs, ἅλις πεποτήαται [μέλισσαι] Il.; περὶ δὲ Τρωαὶ ἅλις ἦσαν fly in swarms, Id.:—also just enough, in moderation, like μετρίως, Eur.
attached to a Noun, χαλκόν τε χρυσόν τε ἅλις gold and silver enough, Od.
ἅλις (sc. ἐστι) 'tis enough, Il.; ἢ οὐχ ἅλις, ὡς . . ; is it not enough that . . ? Hom.
like an adj., ἅλις ἡ συμφορά (sc. ἐστι) Eur.:—also, ἅλις (sc. εἰμί) with a part. added, ἅλις νοσοῦς’ ἐγώ enough that I suffer, Soph.
c. gen. rei, enough of a thing, ἅλις ἔχειν τινός Hdt., attic
sea-resounding, Aesch.
salted, pickled, Anth.
sea-tossed, Anth.

entry.etym: ἀλιτήμενος is formed as if from ἀλίτημι
entry.sense: c. acc. pers. to sin or offend against a god, Hom., Aesch.
c. acc. rei, to transgress, Διὸς ἐφετμάς Il.
the part. ἀλιτήμενος is used as an adj., sinful, Od.
stretching along the sea, level, flat, Plut.
bounded by the sea, Anth.
a sin, offence, Anth.
sinning or offending against, a god, c. gen., Ar., Thuc.
absol. sinful, guilty, Lys., etc.
abominable, accursed, Plat.
sinning against one's friend, Pind.
a wicked mind, Anth.
to sin, offend, Hes., Anth.
sinfulness, mischief, Soph.
sinful, sinning; and as Subst., δαίμοσιν ἀλιτρός a sinner against the gods, Hom.: in milder sense, a knave, rogue, Od.
sea-beaten, sea-worn, γέρων Theocr.; κύμβη Anth.
sea-beaten, ἁλ. βάρη griefs for sea-tossed corpses, Aesch.
as Subst. a seaman, fisherman, Eur.
a sort of salt-cheese, Anth.
a disaster at sea, shipwreck, Anth.
destroying on the sea: as Subst. a pirate, Anth.
strong, mighty, Eur.
only in nom. and acc., a safeguard, defence, c. dat., Τρώεσσιν ἄλκαρ ἔσεσθαι Il.; c. gen. ἄλκαρ Ἀχαιῶν defence of the Achaeans, Id.; but, γήραος ἄλκαρ a defence against old age, Hhymn.
valiant, warlike, Hhymn., Anth.
strength displayed in action, prowess, courage, boldness, ἐπιειμένος ἀλκήν clad in prowess, Il.; δύεσθαι ἀλκήν Id.: in pl. feats of strength, Pind.

strength to avert danger, a defence, succour, Hom.; ἀλκή τινος defence or aid against a thing, Hes., Pind., etc.; ἐς or πρὸς ἀλκὴν τρέπεσθαι to turn and resist, stand on one's guard, Hdt., etc.; so, ἀλκῆς μεμνῆσθαι Id.
battle, fight, Aesch., Eur.
bravely fighting, Anth.
strong, stout, of men and weapons, Hom.; ἄλκιμος τὰ πολεμικά Hdt.

entry.etym: heteroclit. of ἀλκή as if from ἄλξ
entry.sense: might, strength, ἀλκὶ πεποιθώς, of wild beasts, Hom.
stout-hearted, Aesch.
a protector from a thing, c. gen., Hom.
the 14 winter days during which the halcyon builds its nest, and the sea is calm, the halcyon days, proverb. of undisturbed tranquillity, Ar.
the kingfisher, Lat. alcedo, Hom., etc. (halcyon with h is a wrong form.)
a change, Aesch., etc.
exchange, barter, whether in buying or selling, Plat.
that which is given or taken in exchange: the price of a thing, Anth.
to deal in sausages, Ar.
a sausage-dealer, Ar.

entry.etym: Conjunct., properly neut. pl. of ἄλλος (with changed accent)
entry.sense: otherwise, but, stronger than δέ:

to oppose single clauses, but, Lat. autem, the preceding clause being negat., οὐ μόνον ἅπαξ, ἀλλὰ πολλάκις Plat.; so, οὐχ (or μὴ) ὅτι, οὐχ (or μὴ) ὅπως, are followed by ἀλλά or ἀλλά καὶ . . . , not only . . . , but . . .
after a negative ἀλλά sometimes = ἀλλ’ ἤ, except, but, ἔπαισεν οὔτις ἀλλ’ ἐγώ Soph.
to oppose whole sentences, but, yet, Lat. at:— used by Hom., with imperat. or subj., to remonstrate, encourage, persuade, like Lat. tandem, ἀλλ’ ἴθι, ἀλλ’ ἄγε, ἀλλὰ ἴωμεν, Hom.
joined with other Particles, ἀλλ’ ἄρα, or, ἀλλ’ οὖν, but then, however, Hdt., etc.
ἀλλὰ γάρ, Lat. enimvero, but really, certainly, attic
ἀλλ’ ἦ in questions, Lat. an vero? ergo? Plat.: cf. ἀλλ’ ἤ (suo loco).
a sausage, Ar.
to make other than it is, to change, alter, Eur., Plat., etc.
ἀλλ. τί τινος to give in exchange for, barter one thing for another, Aesch.; τι ἀντί τινος Eur.: so in Mid., Thuc.
to repay, requite, φόνον φονεῦσιν Eur.
to give up, leave, quit, οὐράνιον φῶς Soph.

to take one thing for another, κάκιον τοὐσθλοῦ Theogn.; ἀλλ. θνητὸν εἶδος to assume mortal form, Eur.:—Mid., ἀλλάσσεσθαι τί τινος one thing for another, εὐδαιμονίας Hdt., etc.:—hence, to buy, τι ἀντ’ ἀργυρίου Plat.
to interchange, alternate, σκῆπτρ’ ἀλλάσσων ἔχειν to enjoy power in turn, Eur.:—Pass., ἀρεταὶ ἀλλασσόμεναι in turns, Pind.
elsewhere, in another place, ἄλλος ἀλλαχῆ one here, another there, Xen.; ἄλλοτε ἀλλαχῆ now here, now there, Id.
from another place, Antipho.
elsewhere, Xen.
elsewhither, to another place, Id.
elsewhere, Soph., Xen.
to speak so as to imply something other than what is said, to interpret allegorically, Plut.:—Pass. to be spoken allegorically, NTest.
an allegory, i. e. description of one thing under the image of another, Cic.
unceasing, ceaseless, Od., Soph.
implacable, Il.
an eating one another, Hdt.
eating each other, Arist.
mutual slaughter, Pind.
murdering one another, Aesch., Xen.
of one another, to one another, one another, Hom., etc.
of Place,
in another place, elsewhere, Hom., etc.: —c. gen. loci, ἄλλος ἄλλῃ τῆς πόλεως one in one part of the city, one in another, Thuc.
to another place, elsewhither, Hom., etc.
of Manner, in another way, somehow else, otherwise, Id., etc.; ἄλλῃ γέ πῃ Plat.; ἄλλῃ πως Xen.
inexorable, Anth.
inexorable, Anth.
of another race, a stranger, NTest.
using a strange tongue, Hdt.
to take one for another, not know, ἀλλογνώσας (ionic for ἀλλογνοήσας) Hdt.
mis-known, unknown, Od.
belonging to another people or land, foreign, strange, Hom., etc.
of strange appearance, neut. pl. ἀλλοειδέα (which must be long-long-long), or ἀλλοϊδέα (which must be long-short-short-long), Od.
from another place, ἄλλοθεν ἄλλος one from one place, another from another, Il., etc.; ἄλλοθεν from abroad, Od.; οὐδαμόθεν ἄλλοθεν Id.

elsewhere, in another place, in a strange or foreign land, Od.: c. gen., ἄλλοθι γαίης in another or strange land, Id.; but, ἄλλοθι πάτρης elsewhere than in one's native land, i. e. away from home, Id.
in other ways, from other causes, Thuc., Plat.
speaking a strange tongue, Od.; generally, foreign, strange, alien, Hdt., Trag.

of another sort or kind, different, Hom.; ἀλλοῖόν τι, euphem. for κακόν τι, other than good, Hdt.:—from its comparative force, it may be foll. by ἤ . . , Id., Plat., etc.:—but an actual comp. ἀλλοιότερος occurs in Hdt., Thuc., etc.
adv. -ως, otherwise, Plat.: comp. -ότερον Xen.
to make different, to change, alter, Plat., etc.
Pass. with fut. mid. ἀλλοιώσομαι and pass. ἀλλοιωθήσομαι:—to become different, be changed, Thuc., Xen.
to be changed for the worse, Id. Hence
a change, alteration, Plat., etc.

of unusual nature or form, strange, monstrous, Ar., Plat., etc.; ἀλλ. πρᾶγμα an unwelcome business, Thuc.: c. gen., ἀλλοκότῳ γνώμαι τῶν πάρος with purpose utterly different from . . , Soph. adv. -τως, Plat.
entry.etym: From ἄλλος, the termin. -κοτος being uncertain.

entry.sense: to spring, leap, bound, of living beings, Hom., etc.:—metaph. of things, ἆλτο ὀϊστός Il.; the eye, to throb, Theocr.
i. e. ἄλλοτε πρὸς ἄλλον, leaning first to one side, then to the other, of Ares, Il.; πλοῦτος Anth.
to another place, elsewhither, Od.; ἄλλος ἄλλοσε one one way, one another, Aesch.
alius, another, one besides, ἄλλος μέν . , ἄλλος δέ . , one . , another . , Il.; ἄλλος τις or τὶς ἄλλος, any other, some other; οὐδεὶς ἄλλος no other; εἴ τις ἄλλος, Lat. si quis alius, any one else.
repeated, ἄλλος ἄλλο λέγει one man says one thing, one another, i. e. different men say different things; ἄλλος ἄλλῃ ἐτράπετο Xen.; λείπουσι τὸν λόφον ἄλλοι ἄλλοθεν Id.;—v. ἀλλαχῆ.
ἄλλος καὶ ἄλλος, one or two; ἄλλο καὶ ἄλλο one thing after another, Id.

joined with the Art., ὁ ἄλλος, the other; in pl., οἱ ἄλλοι (ionic ὧλλοι), all the others, the rest; Lat. ceteri; τὰ ἄλλα, contr. τἆλλα or τἄλλα Lat. cetera, reliqua, not alia;— οὕ τε ἄλλοι καὶ . . both all the others and . . , i. e. especially . .
with Numerals, yet, still, πέμπτος ποταμὸς ἄλλος yet a fifth river, Hdt.: with a Sup., ὀϊζυρώτατος ἄλλων most wretched of all besides, Od.
rarely like ἀλλοῖος, of other sort, different, Il.: hence
sometimes like a comp., c. gen., ἄλλα τῶν δικαίων other than just, Xen.; followed by ἤ . . , when a negat. goes before, οὐδὲν ἄλλο, ἤ . . , nothing else than . . , Hdt., etc.

at another time, at other times, ἄλλοτε . . , ἄλλοτε . . , at one time . . , at another . . , Hom.; so, ἄλλως ἄλλοτε at one time one way, at another another, Aesch.; ἄλλοτ’ ἄλληι, ἄλλοθι, ἄλλοσε, etc.
a busy-body in other men's matters, NTest.
to speak of things foreign to the matter, Strab.
a meddling with other people's business, Plat.

opp. to ἴδιος, of or belonging to another, Lat. alienus, Hom., etc.; ἀλλ. γυνή another man's wife, Aesch.; γναθμοῖσι γελοίων ἀλλοτρίοισιν, of the suitors, laughed with a face unlike one's own, of a forced, unnatural laugh, Od. (Horace's malis ridere alienis is different); ἀλλ. ὄμμασιν by the help of another's eyes, Soph.; ἀλλοτριωτάτοις τοῖς σώμασιν χρῆσθαι to deal with one's body as if it absolutely belonged to another, Thuc.
opp. to οἰκεῖος, foreign, strange, Lat. peregrinus, Hom.; often with the notion of hostile, Il.
adv., ἀλλοτρίως ἔχειν or διακεῖσθαι πρός τινα to be unfavourably disposed towards one, Lys.: comp. -ιώτερον less favourably, Dem.
alienation, estrangement, opp. to οἰκειότης, Plat., etc.
changing colour, Anth.
c. gen. pers. to estrange from, τῶν σωμάτων τὴν πόλιν Thuc.
c. dat. pers. to make hostile to another, τὴν χώραν τοῖς πολεμίοις Xen.:—Pass. to be made an enemy, τινι Thuc.
in Pass. of things, to be alienated, fall into other hands, Hdt.
estrangement, τῆς ξυμμαχίας οὐχ ὁμοία ἡ ἀλλ. its estrangement, its loss, Thuc.
to think of other things, to give no heed, Od.; of one in a swoon, to be senseless, Il., Theocr.: to be seized with frenzy, Hdt.
to be of another mind, have other views, Id.
of another tribe, foreign, Lat. alienigena, Aesch., Thuc.; πόλεμος ἀλλ. war with foreigners, Plut.
changed in colour, Eur.
looking strange or foreign, Id.
elsewhither, ἄλλυδις ἄλλος one hither, another thither, Hom.; ἄλλυδις ἄλλῃ changes now one way, now another, Il.
in another way or manner, otherwise, Hom., etc.: in attic, ἄλλως πως in some other way; ἄλλως οὐδαμῶς in no other wise; καὶ ἄλλως and besides; ἀρίστου καὶ ἄλλως φρονιμωτάτου Plat.
ἄλλως τε καί . . , both otherwise and so, . . , i. e. especially, attic, etc.
otherwise, differently, ἄλλως εἶπαι to say otherwise, i. e. to deny, Hdt.
in far other manner, i. e. better, Hom., etc.
otherwise than should be, i. e. without aim or purpose, without reason, Od., Hdt., etc.:—also fruitlessly, in vain, Il.
a spring, leap, bound, Od.; ἅλμα πέτρας a leap or fall from the rock, Eur.; κυνῆς ἅλμα the leap of the lot from the helmet, Soph.
sea-water, brine, Od., etc.: spray that has dried on the skin, Id.: a salt incrustation on soil, Hdt.
the brine, i. e. the sea, Pind., Aesch.
salt, briny, Od.
of taste, salt, brackish, Thuc., Xen.
metaph. bitter, distasteful, Lat. amarus, Plat., etc.; ἁλμυρὰ κλαίειν to weep bitterly, Theocr.
to thresh, thresh out, Plat.
to thresh, cudgel, beat, Il., Ar.
with a lobe wanting, of victims' livers, Xen.
to pay no regard to a thing, Lat. rationem non habere rei, c. dat., Il.; c. gen. to be disregardful of, Hdt.
to be out of one's senses, Luc.
want of respect or regard, ἀλογίην εἶχον τοῦ χρηστηρίου took no heed of it, Hdt.; so, ἐν ἀλογίῃ ἔχειν or ποιεῖσθαί τι Id.
in attic want of reason, unreasonable conduct, absurdity, Thuc., Plat.
thoughtlessness, rashness, Polyb., Plut., etc.
unreasoning, inconsiderate, thoughtless, heedless, Thuc., etc.: τὸ ἀλόγιστον unreason, Id.:—adv. -τως, Id., Plat., etc.
not to be reckoned, Soph.: not to be taken into account, vile, Eur.
without λόγος, i. e.,
without speech, speechless, infans, Plat.:—adv. ἀλόγως, Soph.
unutterable, Lat. infandus, Plat.
without reason, irrational, Id., etc.: τὰ ἄλογα brutes, animals, Id., Xen.; (in modern Greek ἄλογον is a horse).
not reckoned upon, unexpected, Thuc.
a threshing, Xen.
from the sea, ἐξ ἁλόθεν (showing that it is an old gen.) Il.
not reviling or railing, Aesch.
a thresher, grinder, ἀλ. ὀδόντες the grinders, Anth.
anything used for anointing, hog's-lard, grease, unguent, Hom.
laying on of unguents or paint, ἀλ. μύρων Plat.
to trace furrows in waxen tablets, to write, draw (cf. Lat. ex-arare), Ar.
a furrow: v. αὖλαξ.
Sea-born, a name of Amphitrite, Od.
a pestle to pound salt, Anth.
wrought in the sea, sea-purple, i. e. genuine purple, Plat.; ἁλουργῆ purple cloths, Aesch.
a purple robe, Ar.: as adj., ἐσθὴς ἁλουργίς Luc.
a being unwashen, want of the bath, Hdt., Eur.
unwashen, not using the bath, Hdt., Eur., etc.
without crest, Il.
a bedfellow, spouse, wife, Hom., Trag.
sweetest, loveliest, Pind.
a leaping, Arist.
a glade or grove, Lat. saltus, Hom.; grove, Od., Hdt., etc.
as neut., a lump of salt, Hdt.: generally, salt, oft. in pl., Hom., etc.; ἁλὸς μέταλλον a salt-mine, Hdt., Od., etc.
as fem. sg., the sea, Hom.
like a grove, Eur.
good at leaping, Xen.; ἁλτ. ὄρχησις, of the Salii, Plut.
a salt spring, Strab.
to be in distress, Hdt.
galling bonds, Hes.; in sg., Anth.
an escape, Aesch.
not pained or grieved, Soph.
act. not causing pain, Id.
without pain, Soph., etc.; c. gen., ἄλ. γήρως without the pains of age, Id.; τὸ ἄλυπον = ἀλυπία, Plat.—adv., ἀλύπως ζῆν to live free from pain, Id.
act. not paining, causing no pain, Id.
without the lyre, ὕμνοι ἄλυροι, i. e. wild dirges accompanied by the flute, not the lyre, (cf. ἀφόρμικτος), Eur., etc.
a chain, Hdt., Eur.
unprofitable, Xen. adv. ἀλυσιτελῶς, Id.
