to shun, shirk, avoid, Hom.
to flee from, shun, avoid, forsake, c. acc., Hom., etc.: rarely c. gen. to flee from, Soph.:— absol. to escape, Hom.
listlessness, ennui, Plut.
to be uneasy, be in distress, Il.
not to be loosed, indissoluble, Hom., etc.:—continuous, ceaseless, κύκλος Pind.

entry.etym: υ short in Hom., ῡ once in Od. and in Trag.
entry.sense: to wander in mind .
from grief, to be ill at ease, be distraught, Il.: to be beside oneself, Hom., Soph.
from perplexity, to be at a loss, not know what to do, ἀλύει δ’ ἐπὶ παντί Id.; ἀλ. λύπαι, ἐν πόνοις, Id.
from joy or exultation, to be beside oneself, Od., Aesch.
to wander or roam about, Luc., Babr.
to bring in, yield, earn, Hom.:—metaph., φθόνον ἀλφάνειν to incur envy, Eur.
bringing in oxen, παρθένοι ἀλφεσίβοιαι maidens whose parents receive many oxen as presents from their suitors, i. e. much-courted, Il.
working for one's daily bread, laborious, enterprising, Od.; esp. of trading, seafaring people, Id.
a dealer in barley-meal, Ar.
peeled or pearl-barley; sg. only in phrase ἀλφίτου ἀκτή, barley-meal, Lat. polenta, Hom.: in pl. ἄλφιτα, barley-groats, barley-meal, opp. to ἄλευρα, Hom., attic
metaph. one's daily bread, Ar.; πατρῶια ἄλφ. one's patrimony, Id.
a making of barley-meal, Xen.
to eat barley-bread, Xen.

entry.etym: From same Root comes Lat. albus, and also ἄλφιτον, because of the whiteness of meal.
entry.sense: whiteness: white leprosy, Hes., Plat., etc.
goddess of the threshing-floor, Theocr.
of or for the threshing-floor, Anth.
a threshing-floor, ἱερὰς κατ’ ἀλωάς Il.; μεγάλην κατ’ ἀλωήν, ἐϋκτιμένην κατ’ ἀλ. Id.
a garden, orchard, vineyard, v. γουνός.
a thresher, husbandman, Anth.

entry.etym: found in the obl. cases, Arist.

entry.sense: of a fox: ἀλωπεκέη, attic -κῆ (sub. δορά), a fox-skin, Hdt., Plut.
branded with a fox, Luc.
a young fox, Ar.
to play the fox, Ar.
a little fox, Ar.
= κυναλώπηξ, Xen.
a foxskin cap, Id.
a fox, Solon, Hdt., etc.
easy to take, win, or conquer, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
of the mind, easy to apprehend, Soph.
（ἅλωσις) of or for capture, παιὰν ἁλ. a song of triumph on taking a city, Aesch.; βάξις ἁλ. tidings of the capture, Id.
a taking, capture, conquest, destruction, Pind., Aesch., etc.; δαΐων ἅλ. conquest by the enemy, Id.: means of conquest, Soph.: ἁλῶναι ἰσχυρὰν ἅλωσιν to be taken without power to escape, Plut.
as law-term, conviction, Plat.
a threshing-floor, Xen., etc.:—then, from its round shape,
the disk of the sun or moon, or of a shield, Aesch., etc.
to be taken or conquered, Thuc.
attainable, Soph.
unremitting, Plut.
of or like the Amazons, Plut.

entry.etym: Commonly derived from α privat. , μαζός, from the fable that they got rid of the right breast, that it might not interfere with the use of the bow.
entry.sense: mostly in pl. Ἀμάζονες, αἱ, the Amazons, a warlike race of women in Scythia, Il., Hdt., etc.
to be untaught, stupid, Plat.

unlearned, ignorant, stupid, boorish (v. ἀμαθία), Hdt., etc.; ἀμαθὴς τὴν ἐκείνων ἀμαθίαν stupid with their stupidity, Plat.; ἀμαθέστερον τῶν νόμων ὑπεροψίας παιδεύεσθαι to be educated with too little learning to despise the laws, Thuc.:—adv., ἀμαθῶς ἁμαρτεῖν to err through ignorance, Eur.
c. gen. rei, without knowledge of a thing, Id.; περί τινος, πρός τι Plat.
not heard of, unknown, ἀμ. ἔρρει Eur.:—adv., ἀμαθῶς χωρεῖν of events, to take an unforeseen course, Thuc.
ignorance, Soph., etc.; ἀμ.τινός ignorant of a thing, Xen.; περί τι Id.
sandy soil, opp. to sea-sand (ψάμαθος), Il.; in pl. the links or dunes by the sea, Hhymn.
to level with the sand, utterly destroy, Il., Aesch.
to spread smooth, level, κόνιν h. Hom.
irresistible, Hom., Soph.
strong, stubborn, of a mast, Od.
to soften: then to destroy, efface, Il.: to use up, squander, χρήματα Theocr.:— Pass., ὥς κεν τεῖχος ἀμαλδύνηται Il.; ἀμαλδυνθήσομαι Ar.
metaph. to conceal, disguise, Hhymn.
not to be softened, Anth.
cut corn, a sheaf, Soph., Plut.
a binder of sheaves, Il.

entry.etym: From Root ΜΑΛ, μαλακός, with α euphon. .
entry.sense: soft, weak, feeble, Hom., Eur.
a vine trained on two poles, Sapph., etc.
a wagon, wain, opp. to the war-chariot (ἅρμα), Lat. plaustrum, Hom.
c. gen. a wagon-load of, πετρῶν, σίτου Xen.
the carriage of the plough, Lat. currus, Hes.:—Charles' wain in the heavens, the Great Bear (ἄρκτος), Hom.
= ἁμαξιτός, Anth.
for a wagon: βοῦς ἁ. a draught ox, Plut.
to traverse with a wagon: Pass. to be traversed by wagon-roads, of a country, Hdt.
metaph., ἁμαξεύειν βίοτον to drag on a weary life, Anth.
intr. to be a wagoner, Plut., Anth.
of or on a carriage, Aesch.; ἁμ. τρίβος a high-road, Eur.
large enough to load a wagon, λίθος Xen., etc.
a little wagon, Lat. plostellum, Hdt., Ar.
of or for a wagon, Anth.
traversed by wagons, ἁμ. ὁδός a carriage-road, high-road, Pind., Xen.; and without ὁδός, as Subst., Il.
dwelling in a wagon, Strab.
a cartwright, Plut.
large enough to fill a wagon, like ἁμαξιαῖος, Eur.
= ἁμαξοπηγός
ἐξ ἁμαξουργοῦ λέγειν to talk cartwrights' slang, Ar.
at once, at the same time, Hom., etc.
prep. c. dat. at the same time with, together with, ἅμ’ ἠοῖ at dawn, Il.; ἅμα ἕῳ, ἅμα ἕῳ γιγνομένῃ Thuc.
Lat. amaracum, amaracus, Anth.
of amaranth:— metaph. unfading, imperishable, NTest.
unfading, undecaying, NTest.
as Subst. amaranth, an unfading flower, Diosc.
a trench, conduit, channel, for watering meadows, Il., Theocr.
to miss, miss the mark, c. gen., ἑκὼν ἡμάρτανε φωτός he missed the man on purpose, Il.; ἁμ. τῆς ὁδοῦ to miss the road, Ar.; τοῦ σκοποῦ Antipho.

generally, to fail of doing, fail of one's purpose, to miss one's point, fail, go wrong, Od., etc.; c. gen., νοήματος ἤμβροτεν failed in hitting upon the thought, Id., etc.; ἁμ. τοῦ χρησμοῦ to mistake it, Hdt.
to fail of having, i. e. to be deprived of, lose, c. gen., ἁμαρτήσεσθαι ὀπωπῆς that I should lose my sight, Od.; ἁμ. πιστῆς ἀλόχου Eur.

to fail, do wrong, err, sin, Hom., etc.; c. dat. modi, γνώμῃ ἁμ. to err in judgment, Hdt.; or ἐν λόγοις Id., Plat.; with a neut. adj., τόδε γ’ ἤμβροτον I erred in this, Od.; in Prose, ἁμ. περί τι ἁμ. περί τι to do wrong in a matter, Plat., etc.
Pass., ἁμαρτάνεταί τι a sin is committed, Thuc.:—impers., ἁμαρτάνεται περί τι Plat.
a failure, fault, sin, Soph., Plat.
a bodily defect, malady, Id.
together, at once, Hom.
prone to error, Arist.
a failure, fault, sin, Aesch., etc.; ἁμ. τινός a fault committed by one, Id.; ἁμ. δόξης fault of judgment, Thuc.
generally, guilt, sin, Plat., Arist., NTest.
erring in mind, distraught, Hes., etc.
erring in words, speaking at random, Il.
needing no witness, Eur.
without witness, unattested, Thuc., etc.:—adv. -ρως, Dem.
sinful:— as Subst. a sinner, NTest.
a sparkling, glancing, of the eye, Hhymn.; of horses' feet, Ar.
a sparkle, twinkle, changing colour and light, Anth.; quivering, of the lip, Theocr. From
to sparkle, glance, of the eye, Hes.:—Mid. of light, colour, Anth.
to run together, in epic part. ἁματροχόων, Od.
a jostling or clashing of wheels, ἁματροχιὰς ἀλεείνων Il.
living in darkness, Ar.
dimly seen, dim, faint, baffling sight, εἴδωλον ἀμ. a shadowy spectre, Od.
having no light, darksome, νύξ Luc.:—blind, sightless, Soph.; so, ἀμαυρῶι κώλωι with blind foot, said of a blind man, Id.
metaph.,
dim, obscure, uncertain, κληδών Aesch.; ἐλπίς Plut.
obscure, unknown, Hes., Soph., Eur.
gloomy, troubled, φρήν Aesch.
act. enfeebling, νοῦσος Anth.
to make dim, faint, or obscure, Xen.; metaph. to impair, Eur., etc.:—Pass. to become dim, suffer eclipse, of the sun, Hdt.; to disappear, Hes.
obscuration, Plut.
without resistance, Thuc.
without battle, Il., Hdt.
not to be fought with, unconquerable, Soph.
not having fought, not having been in battle, Xen.
without battle:
of a person, with whom no one fights, unconquered, unconquerable, invincible, Hdt., etc.; of places, impregnable, Id.; of things, irresistible, Pind., Aesch.
act. not having fought, taking no part in the battle, Xen.
disinclined to fight, peaceful, Aesch.: not contentious, NTest.

entry.etym: From Root ΜΑ, with α euphon. ; cf. Lat. MET-O, to mow.
entry.sense: to reap corn, absol., Il., Hes.; metaph., ἤμησαν καλῶς they reaped abundantly, Aesch.:—so c. acc. to reap, λήϊον Od.; σῖτον Hdt.
generally, to cut reeds, etc., Il., Theocr.
in Mid. to gather together, collect, as reapers gather in corn, ἀμησάμενοι [γάλα] having collected milk:—so in Act., ἀμήσας κόνιν, having scraped together earth over a corpse, Anth.
with sudden bursts, ἀμβλ. γοόωσα Il.
to cause to miscarry, Soph., Plat.
of the woman, to miscarry, Plut.
to blunt, take the edge off a sharp instrument, and metaph. to make dull, ὄμματος αὐγήν Anth.:—Pass. to become dull, lose its edge or force, Aesch., Thuc.

blunt, dulled, with the edge taken off, of a sharp instrument, Plat., etc.:—metaph. dull, dim, of sight, ἀμβλὺ ὁρᾶν, βλέπειν Id.; of the feelings, ἀμβλυτέραι τῆι ὀργῆι with anger less keen, Thuc.; ἀμβλύτερον ποιεῖν τι less vigorous, Id.
in Aesch. Eum. of Orestes, having lost the edge of guilt: but of persons, generally, dull, spiritless, having lost the keenness of one's feelings, Thuc.
act. darkening, of a cloud, Anth. Hence
bluntness: metaph. dullness, Plut.
to be dim-sighted, Xen.
dim-sightedness, Plat.
to be dim-sighted, Plat., etc.; ἀμβλ. πρὸς τὸ φῶς to be blind to it, Luc.
bedimmed, dark, Aesch.
bubbling up, Il.: metaph. by jets, capriciously, Anth.
like a prelude, Hhymn., Pind.
thrown up, of earth, Xen.
putting off a work, dilatory, Hes., Plut.
ambrosia (i.e. immortality), the food of the gods, Hom., etc.

immortal, Hhymn.:—in Hom. night and sleep are called ambrosial, divine, as gifts of the gods; so of everything belonging to the gods, as their hair, robes, sandals, the fodder and the mangers of their horses.
with coursers of immortal strain , Eur.

entry.etym: α privat. , βροτός with μ inserted; like lengthd. form ἀμβρόσιος.
entry.sense: immortal, divine, Hom., Aesch.
νὺξ ἄμβροτος, like ἀμβροσίη νύξ, Od.;— then of all things belonging to the gods, Hom.
unenviable:
melancholy, direful, Hom., Eur.
of persons, unhappy, miserable, Od.
of amethyst, Luc.
not drunken, Plut.
as Subst., ἀμέθυστος, ἡ, amethyst, the precious stone, supposed to be a remedy against drunkenness, NTest.

entry.etym: From Root ΜΕΙΒ, or ΜΕΥ, with α prefixed, cf. ἀμεύομαι Lat. MOV-eo.
entry.sense: Act. to change, exchange, ἔντε’ ἄμειβεν Il.; ἀμ. τί τινος, as γόνυ γουνὸς ἀμείβων changing one knee for the other, i. e. walking slowly, Il.:—and so, either
to give in exchange, τεύχε’ ἄμειβε χρύσεα χαλκείων exchanged golden armour for brasen, Id.; or
to take in exchange, πόσιν ἀντὶ σᾶς ἀμεῖψαι ψυχᾶς to redeem him at the price of thine own life, Eur.
of place, to change it, and so to pass, cross, Aesch., Eur.: —then, either to pass out of a place, leave it, or to pass into, enter it, Hdt., attic
simply, to change, alter, χρῶτα one's colour, Aesch.
Causal, to make others change, τεύχε’ ἄμειβον Il.: to pass on, hand on from one to another, Eur.
like Mid. I. 3, to repay, return, ἀμ. χάριν Aesch.
intr. in part., ἀμείβοντες, οἱ, interchangers, i. e. the rafters that meet and cross each other, Il.; ἐν ἀμείβοντι = ἀμοιβαδίς, Pind.
ἀμείβει καινὸν ἐκ καινῶν one new thing comes on after others, Eur.
Mid. to change one with another, ἀμειβόμενοι by turns, alternately, Hom.: to come in turn, Eur.
often of dialogue, to answer one another, Od.; often in part. ἀμειβόμενος, answering, in answer, Hom.; c. acc., ἀμ. τινα μύθωι, μύθοις, ἐπέεσσι Id.; even, ταῦτα τοὺς φίλους ἠμείψατο Hdt.
to repay, requite, δώροισιν ἀμ. τινα Od.; χρηστοῖσι Hdt.; also c. acc. et dat. rei, ἀμ. εὐεργεσίας χάρισιν Xen.
to get in exchange, λώιους φρένας τῶν νῦν παρουσῶν Soph.
like Act. to change a place, to pass either out of or into, Hom., etc.
unsoftened, cruel, Hom., Hes.
implacable, relentless, Il.
of things, unmitigated, Aesch.
better, abler, stronger, braver, Hom., etc.; v. ἀγαθός.
of things, better, fitter, Id.
ἄμεινόν [ἐστι] 'tis better, c. inf., ἐπεὶ πείθεσθαι ἄμεινον Il., etc.; with negat., οὐ γὰρ ἄμεινον 'twere better not, Hdt.
τὰ ἀμείνω φρονέειν to choose the better part, Id.
to bereave of a thing, c. gen., Pind.
exchange, interchange, Plut.
change, succession, Id.

entry.etym: From Root ΜΕΛΓ, with α prefixed, comes also ἀμολγεύς; cf. Lat. mulg_eo.
entry.sense: to milk sheep and goats; βόας Theocr.: —Mid., in metaph. sense, ἀμέλγεσθαι τοὺς ξένους to milk them dry, Ar.
to draw milk from the animals, ἀμ. γάλα Hdt.; Pass., ὄϊες ἀμελγόμεναι γάλα having milk drawn from them, milch-ewes, Il.
metaph. to squeeze out like milk, to press out, ἐκ βοτρύων ξανθὸν ἄμελξε γάνος Anth.
to drink, Theocr.
indifference, negligence, Thuc., etc; τινος towards a person, περί τινος about a thing, Plat.
imperat. of ἀμελέω, never mind, Ar., Xen.; aor1 ἀμέλησον Luc.
as adv. by all means, of course, Ar., Plat., etc.
want of practice, Plat.
unpractised, Plat., etc.
to have no care for, be neglectful of, c. gen., Hom., Hdt., etc.
absol. to be careless, heedless, negligent, Hes., etc.; τὸ μἀμελεῖν (crasis for μὴ ἀμελεῖν) carefulness, Aesch.
c. acc. et part. to overlook, and so to let, allow, suffer, παῖδας θνήσκοντας ἀμελεῖ he lets them die, Eur.:—Xen. has gen. in same sense.
c. inf. to neglect to do, Hdt., Plat.
Pass. to be slighted, overlooked, Soph., etc.; οἱ ἠμελημένοι ἄνθρωποι Thuc.:—adv. ἠμελημένως, carelessly, Xen.
careless, heedless, negligent, Ar., Xen., etc.:—adv. ἀμελῶς, carelessly, Thuc.; comp. ἀμελέστερον, Id.
c. gen. careless of a thing, Plat., etc.; περί τινα Isocr.:—adv., ἀμελῶς ἔχειν to be careless, πρός τι πρός τι Xen.
pass. uncared for, unheeded, Id.
one must neglect, τινός Isocr.
ἀμελητέος, α, ον, to be neglected, Luc.
not to be cared for, Theogn.
not to be put off, Luc.
not to be blamed, blameless, Eur., Dem.; ἄμεμπτος χρόνου in regard of time, Aesch.; ἀμεμφής Aesch.
of things, perfect in its kind, Xen.; ἄμ. ἐκείνηι without blame to her, Plut.: comp. ἀμεμπτότερος, less blameworthy, Id.:—adv. -τως, so as to merit no blame, right well, Soph., Xen.
act. not blaming, content, ἀμεμφής Plut., ἄμεμπτόν τινα ποιεῖσθαι Xen.:—so adv., ἀμέμπτως δέχεσθαί τινα without censure, Id.
freedom from blame, Aesch., Soph.
powerless, fleeting, feeble, of ghosts, Od., etc.; of dreams, Id.; of one wounded, Il.
of mortal men generally, Hhymn., Ar.
to deaden the force of a thing, Il.
to pluck or pull, Lat. decerpo, Sapph., Eur.:—Mid. to pluck for oneself, Theocr.
to deprive of, bereave of, a thing, c. gen., Hes., Od.:—Pass. to be bereft of a thing, αἰῶνος, δαιτός Hom.

c. acc. pers. only, to bereave of his rights, to rob, Il.; ὄσσε δ’ ἄμερδεν αὐγή the glare bereft the eyes of power, blinded them, Id.; ἔντεα καπνὸς ἀμέρδει the smoke robs the arms of lustre, tarnishes them, Od.
without parts, indivisible, Plat.
free from care, unconcerned, Anth.
pass. uncared for, unheeded, Soph.
driving away care, Anth.
immovable: adv. ἀμετακινήτως, Arist.
not to be repented of, Plat.
of persons, unrepentant, Arist.
not to be repented of, Luc.
act. unrepentant, NTest.
not to be transposed, unchangeable, unchanging, Plat.
not to be got rid of or put away, Id.
adv. ἀμεταστρεπτῑ́ , or ἀμεταστρεπτεί, without turning, straight forward, ἰέναι, φεύγειν Plat.
without turning about.
unalterable, Plat., Plut.
having no share of a thing, c. gen., Thuc.
unmeasured, immeasurable, immense, Od., etc.
unnumbered, countless, Eur.
excess, disproportion, Plat., etc.
of immensely long life, Anth.
unmeasured in words, Il.
drinking to excess, Anth.
without measure, immense, excessive, boundless, Plat.:—adv. ἀμέτρως, Id.; neut. pl. ἄμετρα as adv., Babr.
immoderate, in moral sense, Plat.:—adv. ἀμέτρως, Xen., etc.
to conquer, Pind.
with interchanging paths, Pind.
not angry or wrathful, Hdt.; χειμὼν οὐκ ἀμήνιτος θεοῖς sent not but by the special wrath of heaven, Aesch.:—adv. -τως, Id.

entry.etym: for ἁμῆι, dat. fem. of ἁμός = τὶς
entry.sense: Hebr. adv. verily, of a truth, so be it, NTest.:— τὸ ἀμήν, certainty, Id.
a shovel or mattock, Ar., Xen.
in a certain way: ἁμη-γέ-πη ἁμη-γέ-πηι or other, Plat.
a kind of milk-cake, Ar.
a reaper, Il.
a reaping, harvesting, Il. (metaph. of slaughter).
harvest, harvest time, Hes., Hdt.
the crop or harvest reaped, Lat. seges, Anth.
without mother, motherless, Hdt., Eur.
unmotherly, μήτηρ ἀμήτωρ Soph.
to be at a loss for, or in want of a thing, c. gen., Hdt.; περί τινος about a thing, Eur.; ὅπα τράπωμαι which way to turn, Aesch.
absol., ἀμηχανῶν βιοτεύω I live without the necessaries of life, Xen.
want of means, helplessness, impotence, Od., etc.; ὑπ’ ἀμηχανίας Ar.
of things, hardship, trouble, Hes.
without means or resource, at a loss, τινος about one, Od.; ἀμ. εἴς τι awkward at a thing, Eur.:—adv., ἀμηχάνως ἔχειν = ἀμηχανεῖν, Aesch., Eur.
c. inf. at a loss how to do, unable to do, Soph., Dem., etc.
in pass. sense,

impracticable, difficult, c. inf., ἀμήχανός ἐσσι πιθέσθαι Il.; ὁδὸς ἀμ. εἰσελθεῖν a road hard to enter on, Xen.; ἀμήχανόν ἐστι, c. inf. 'tis impossible, Hdt., etc.:—absol., ἀμήχανα impossibilities, Aesch., etc.
against whom nothing can be done, irresistible, of gods, Il.:—of things, ἀμήχανα ἔργα mischief without resource or remedy, Id., Hes., Trag.; of dreams, inexplicable, Od.

extraordinary, immense, Plat.; ἀμήχανον εὐδαιμονίας an extraordinary amount of happiness, Id.:—often c. acc., ἀμήχανος τὸ μέγεθος, τὸ κάλλος, τὸ πλῆθος, i. e. inconceivable in point of size, etc., Id., Xen.:—Plat. often adds the relatives οἷος, ὅσος, and ὡς, as, ἀμήχανον ὅσον χρόνον an inconceivable length of time, ἀμηχάνως ὡς εὖ extraordinarily well.
undefiled, Theogn.; Aesch. calls the sea simply ἡ ἀμίαντος.
unmixed, pure, Arist.

entry.etym: by epic metath. for ἀριθμέω, Theocr.

entry.sense: unmingled, that will not mingle or blend, Aesch.
unmixed, pure, Plat.

of persons, not mingling with others (cf. μιγῆναι to have intercourse), unsociable, of Centaurs and Cyclopes, Soph., Eur.:— ἀμ. τινι having no intercourse with others, Id.; so of laws and customs, ἄμ. νόμιμα τοῖς ἄλλοις Thuc.
of places, inhospitable, Eur.
to compete, vie, contend with another, Lat. aemulari, c. dat. pers., Hdt., etc.; πρός τινα Eur.; c. dat. rei, to contend in or with a thing, Hdt.; περί τινος about a thing, Luc.
in pass. sense, τὸ πεζὸν πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἁμιλληθέν being matched one against another, Thuc.
of a single person, to strive, struggle, ἐπί τι to a point, Xen.; πρός τι to obtain a thing, Plat.
a contest for superiority, a conflict, Hdt., etc.

c. gen. rei, ἰσχύος ἅμ. a trial of strength, Pind.; ποδοῖν, λόγων ἅμ. Eur.; ἀρετῆς Plat.; c. gen. objecti, ἅμ. λέκτρων a contest for marriage, Eur.; so with an adj., ἅμ. φιλόπλουτος, πολύτεκνος a striving after wealth or children, Id.
a conflict, v. ἄλεκτρος.
a competitor in the race, v. τρόχος B.
inimitable in one's life, Plut.
inimitable, Anth.; τινί in a thing, Plut.:—adv. -τως, Id.
of persons, want of intercourse, ἀλλήλων with one another, Thuc.; πρός τινα Luc.; ἀμιξίη χρημάτων want of money dealings, Hdt.
keeping up with horses, i. e. fleet as a horse, Soph.
ἅμιπποι, οἱ, infantry mixed with cavalry, Thuc., Xen.
Eur., Dem., χρημάτων ἀμ. without reward of money, Plut.
without hire or pay, unhired, Aesch.
bringing in no rent, Dem.
a chamber-pot, Ar.
epith. of Lycian, wearing no girdle (μίτρα) with their coat of mail (χιτών), Il.
epith. of Lemnos, inaccessible, inhospitable, Il.
anything tied or made to tie, and so,
a knot, Hdt.
a noose, halter, Eur.
a band, Id.; ἅ. παρθενίας the maiden girdle, Anth.
in pl. the wrestler's arms or hug, Plut.
poet. for ἀνὰ μέσον.
what is not one's fate, bad fortune, Od.
without share of a thing, c. gen., Il., Soph.:—free from, without, ὠδίνων Anth.
absol. unhappy, Il.
sand (v. ἄμαθος), Plat., etc.
sandy ground, a race-course, Xen.
growing in sand, Anth.
Ἀ. ἕδρα the seat of Ammon, i. e. Libya, Eur.
the Libyan, Zeus-Ammon, Hdt., Pind., etc.
a lamb, Theocr.
of a lamb, ἀμν. χλαῖνα a lambskin cloak, Theocr.
unmentioned, unheeded, Eur.
to be unmindful, absol., Aesch., Eur.
c. gen. to make no mention of, not speak of, Id., etc.; so, ἀμν. τι περί τινος Thuc.
forgetfulness, Eur.
unmindful, forgetful, Soph., Plat.; τινός of a thing, Aesch., etc.
pass. forgotten, not mentioned, Eur.
pass. to be forgotten, Thuc.
forgetfulness of wrong: an amnesty, Plut.
unremembered, Theocr.
a bowl in which the blood of victims was caught, Od.
a ewe-lamb, Theocr.
sheep-minded, i. e. a simpleton, Ar.
a lamb, Soph., Ar.; ἄμνοι τοὺς τρόπους, lambs in temper, Id.:—for the oblique cases, ἀρνός, ἀρνί, ἄρνα are used; v. ἀρνός.
without toil or effort, Il.
unwearied, untiring, Hhymn.
without quarrel, Lacon. word in Thuc.
from some place or other, from what source soever, Od.; ἁμόθεν γέ ποθεν Plat.
by turns, alternately, ἀμ. ἄλλοθεν ἄλλος one after another, Theocr.
giving like for like, retributive, Pind., Anth.:—adv. -ως, in requital, Luc.
interchanged, alternate, Hdt.; ἀμοιβαῖα, alternating verses, sung by two persons one in answer to the other, Plat.; ἀμοιβαίη ἀοιδή Theocr.
for a change of raiment, Od.
alternately, in succession, Hom.
a requital, recompense, compensation, return, payment, Od.; ἑκατόμβης for the hecatomb, Id.
an answer, Hdt.
change, exchange, of money, Plut.
alternation, κακῶν Eur.
one who exchanges, ἀμοιβοί soldiers that relieve others, Il.
as adj. in return or in exchange for a thing, c. gen., Soph.
to have no share in a thing, c. gen., Plut.
without share in a thing, c. gen., Aesch., etc.
absol. = ἄμμορος, unfortunate, Eur.
of milk, made with milk, or (from ἀμολγός an old word for ἀκμή), of the best flour, Hes.
a milk-pail, Lat. mulctra, Theocr., Anth.
a milk-pail, Theocr.

a word of uncertain sense:—Hom. always joins νυκτὸς ἀμολγῶι, in the hours before daybreak, or the hours after sunset, i. e. generally, at night-time, Il. (The supposition that ἀμολγός meant milking-time (from ἀμέλγω) will not suit the sense. It is said that ἀμολγός was an old word for ἀκμή, so that νυκτὸς ἀμ. means the dead of night.)
blameless, Aesch.
made of Amorgian flax, Ar.
fine flax from the isle of Amorgos, Ar.
= ἄμοιρος c. gen., Eur.
absol., unlucky, wretched, Soph.
unshapeliness, unsightliness, Eur.
misshapen, unsightly, Hdt., Eur.: —Sup. ἀμορφέστατος (as if from ἀμορφής), Hdt.; but regul. form -ότερος, -ότατος, Xen., Plut.
= ἡμέτερος, our, ours, Hom., etc.
attic = ἐμός, when a long penult. is required.
an old word equiv. to εἷς or τις, only found in the adv. forms ἁμοῦ, ἁμῆ, ἁμοῖ, ἁμῶς, ἁμόθεν.
as, when, Theocr.
raging, savage, Theocr.
in Hom. as adv. ἄμοτον, insatiably, ἄμ. μεμαώς, striving incessantly; ἄμ. κλαίω I weep continually; τανύοντο they struggled restlessly forwards.
ἀμοῦγέ που, somewhere or other, Lys.: cf. ἀμόθεν, ἀμῆ, ἀμοῖ.
want of refinement, rudeness, grossness, Eur., Plat.
want of harmony, Eur.
without the Muses, without taste, unrefined, inelegant, rude, gross, Eur., Ar.:—adv. ἀμούσως Plat.
unmusical, Eur.; ἀμουσόταται ὠιδαί Id.
without effort.
crasis for ἃ ἐμόχθησα.
free from toil and trouble, Soph.:— shrinking from toil, Pind.
not tired, Xen.
as ἄμ-παλος, poet. for ἀνάπαλος, Pind.
as ἄμπ-αλος, ον, doric for ἀμφίαλος, Theocr.
poet. for ἀνά, before a word beginning with the labials e. g. ἂμ βωμοῖσι, ἂμ μέσον, ἂμ πεδίον ἂμ φυτά.
of the vine, Hdt.
of persons, given to wine, Anth.
a vine-plant, Ar.
the bird ἀμπελίων, Id.
rich in vines, Il., etc.

entry.etym: Perh.from ἀμπί (aeolic for ἀμφί), ἕλιξ, from its clasping tendrils.
entry.sense: a vine, Lat. vitis, Od., etc.
to dress vines, Theophr., Luc.
a vine-dresser, Ar., etc.
a vine-planter, Anth.
a vineyard, Aeschin., etc.
a fine robe: generally, clothing, clothes, Plat., Xen.
to surround, cover, Lat. cingere, c. acc., Od., Soph., etc.:—absol., σκότος ἀμπίσχων surrounding darkness, Eur.
to embrace, Id.
to put round, Lat. circumdare, esp. to put on another, c. dupl. acc., Ar., etc.
Mid. to put round oneself, to wear, χλαίνας οὐκ ἀμπισχοῦνται Id.; ἀμπισχόμενος with your cloak round you, Id.

entry.etym: pres. in use is ἀμπλακίσκῶ ἁμαρτάνω
entry.sense: c. gen. to come short of, Pind., Soph.
to lose, be bereft of, παιδός Id.; ἀλόχου Eur.
absol. to sin, err, do wrong, Id., etc.; ὡς τάδ’ ἤμπλακον when I committed these sins, Aesch.
an error, fault, offence, Aesch., etc.:—also, metri grat., ἀπλάκημα, Id.
to bind the hair with a band, Anth.
a horse's head-band, Aesch.
a woman's head-band, snood, Il., etc.
anything circular, a wheel, Soph.
a being sucked back, the ebb-tide, Hdt., etc.
of almonds, Xen.
an almond-tree, Luc.
a scratching, tearing, Soph., Eur.
of Time, together, at the same time, Od.
of Place, together, all together, Il.
indistinct, dim, obscure:
ἀμ. γράμματα scarce legible letters, Thuc.
ἀμ. πρὸς ἀλήθειαν faint in comparison with truth, Id.; ἀμ. ἐλπίς Plut.
uninitiated, Plat., etc.
in Plat. Gorg. as if from μύω, = οὐ δυνάμενος μύειν, unable to keep close, leaky.
unspeakable, unspeakably many or great, Dem.
where no herds low, of places, Anth.
from Amyclae, Pind.
to speak in the Amyclean (i. e. Laconian) dialect, Theocr.
the temple of Amyclaean Apollo, Thuc.
a Lacon. city, famous for the worship of Apollo, Il., etc.
a sort of shoes, made at Amyclae, Theocr.
not ground at the mill, i. e. ground by hand:— as Subst. a cake of fine meal, Ar., etc.
blameless, noble, excellent, used by Hom. as an honorary epithet, like our honourable, excellency, not implying virtue; never used of gods.
of things, Hom.

entry.etym: the forms assigned to this verb belong to an aor2, ἠμύναθον, hence the irregular infinitive and imperative (cf. ἐργαθεῖν, σχέθω): the inf. therefore is ἀμῡναθεῖν not ἀμῡνάθειν, while the imperative is ἀμῡναθοῦ, not ἀμῡνάθου.
entry.sense: to defend, assist, c. dat., Eur., Ar.:—Mid. to ward off from oneself, repel, ψόγον Aesch.: to take vengeance on, τινα.
personal name.
as appellat., ἦν ἀμυνίας was on its guard, Ar.
one must assist, c. dat. pers., Xen.; so pl. ἀμυντέα, Soph.
a means of defence, Plat., etc.
defensive, Plat., etc.
a defender, helper, Hom.
an avenger, πατρός Eur.

entry.etym: From Root ΜΥΝ, with α prefixed, cf. Lat. munio, moenia.
entry.sense: to keep off, ward off, Hom.:

c. acc. of the person or thing to be kept off, c. dat. of pers. for or from whom the danger is kept off, Δαναοῖσιν λοιγὸν ἀμύνειν to ward off ruin from the Danai, Il.:— the dat. is often omitted, λοιγὸν ἀμύνει Id.
c. dat. pers. to defend, assist, aid, succour, Hom., etc.
c. gen. from whom danger is kept off, Τρῶας ἄμυνε νεῶν he kept the Trojans off from the ships, Il., etc.
absol. to repel assaults, to aid, Id.; τὰ ἀμύνοντα means of defence, Hdt.
rarely c. acc., like Mid. 11, to requite, repay, Soph.
Mid. to ward off from oneself, defend oneself against:
c. acc., Il.
c. gen. of that from which danger is warded off, to fight for or in defence of, Id.: so, ἀμύνεσθαι περὶ πάτρης Id.; ὑπέρ τινος Xen.
absol. to defend oneself, Il.
ἀμύνεσθαί τινα also to avenge oneself on an enemy, to requite, repay, punish, Soph., Thuc., etc.; also, ἀμύνεσθαί τινά τινος or ὑπέρ τινος to punish for a thing, Id.

entry.etym: from root ΜΥΚ, with α prefixed, cf. Lat. mucro.
entry.sense: to scratch, tear, wound, lacerate, mangle, Il., Hdt.; also to prick, sting, Luc., scratch with both hands.
metaph., θυμὸν ἀμ. to tear the heart, Il., Aesch.; φρὴν ἀμύσσεται Id.
to drink deep, perf. ἠμύστικα Eur.
without closing the mouth, i. e. at one draught, Luc.
a long draught, Anacr., Eur., etc.
deep drinking, tippling, Id.
a large cup, used by the Thracians, Ar.
a scratch, skin-wound, Dem.; in sign of sorrow, ἀμυχὰς κοπτομένων ἀφεῖλεν Plut.
to embrace warmly, treat kindly, greet warmly, Od., etc.; so in Mid., Il.
Mid. to gather round, θεαὶ δέ μιν ἀμφαγέροντο (aor2) Il.: hence pres. ἀμφαγέρομαι, Theocr.
public, γάμος Od.
acc. fem. ἀμφαδίην as adv., = ἀμφαδόν, Il.
publicly, openly, without disguise, Hom.
discovered, known, Od.
to rush on from all sides, ἀμφὶ δέ τ’ ἀΐσσονται Il.; ἀμφὶ δὲ χαῖται ὤμοις ἀΐσσοντο floated around his shoulders, Id.
to rattle or ring around, Il.
speechlessness, Hom.
to ring around, Il.
to touch or feel all round, to handle, Hom.; so in Mid., Od.
μαλακώτερος ἀμφαφάασθαι easier to deal with, manage, Il.
coiled round, Eur.
to wrap or twine round, χέρας Eur.:—Mid., Pind.
to cover up, Anth.
Dep. to come round one, surround, Od.
two-edged, Il., Aesch.
metaph., ἀμφ. γλῶττα a tongue that will cut both ways, i. e. maintain either right or wrong, Ar.; of an oracle, ambiguous, Luc.
covered on both sides, close-covered, epith. of Apollo's quiver, Il.
fitted on both sides, well-fitted, ἀμφῆρες δόρυ, of the double rudder used in Greek ships (v. πηδάλιον), Eur.
rowed on both sides, worked by sculls, of a boat, Thuc.
contested on both sides, ἀμφήριστον ἔθηκεν, i. e. made it a "drawn" race, Il.
to clothe, τινά Plut.: metaph. of a grave, ὀστέα ἠμφίασεν Anth.
sea-girt, of islands, Od., Soph.
of Corinth, between two seas, Horace's bimaris, Xen.
Amphiaraus, the Theban seer, Aesch., etc.
a garment, Ctes., Luc.
of a bird, to fly shrieking about, in irreg. part. perf. ἀμφιαχυῖα, Il.
to go about or around, Il.
to bestride, Od.:—esp. to bestride a fallen friend, so as to protect him, Il.; hence of tutelary deities, to protect, Id.
to encompass, wrap round, c. acc., νεφέλη σκόπελον ἀμφιβέβηκε Od.: also c. dat., νέφος ἀμφιβέβηκε νηυσίν Il.:—metaph., σε πόνος φρένας ἀμφιβέβηκεν Id., etc.

to throw or put round: of clothes, to put them on a person, Lat. circumdare, c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, ἀμφὶ δέ χλαῖναν βάλεν Od.; also c. dat. pers., ἀμφὶ δέ μοι ῥάκος βάλον Il.:—Mid. to put round oneself, put round one, put on, Od.
ἀμφιβαλὼν θάλαμον having thrown a chamber over him, Id.; ζυγὸν Ἑλλάδι ἀμφ. Aesch.:—Mid., λευκὴν ἀμφιβάλλομαι τρίχα I put on, get white hair, Soph.
for the Mid. the Act. is sometimes used, κρατερὸν μένος ἀμφιβαλόντες [ἑαυτοῖς] Il.
to throw the arms round, to embrace, c. dat. pers., Od.
also, c. acc. pers. to embrace, Eur.
a going round, encompassing, ἀμφίβασιν Τρώων = τοὺς ἀμφιβαίνοντας Τρῶας, Il.
living a double life, i. e. both on land and in water, amphibious, Batr., Anth.
something thrown round:
an enclosure, Eur.
a garment, cloak, Id.
anything thrown round:
a casting-net, Hes., Hdt.:—metaph. of the garment thrown like a net over Agamemnon, Aesch.
a fetter, bond, Id.
of walls, encompassment of city-walls, Eur.
noised abroad, Anth.
the state of being attacked on both sides, Hdt.
put round, encompassing, Eur.
attacked on both or all sides, Aesch.; ἀμφ. εἶναι to be between two fires, Thuc.
act. hitting at both ends, double-pointed, Anth.
doubtful, ambiguous, Plat., Xen., etc.; τἀγαθὰ ἐς ἀμφίβολον ἔθεντο accounted their good fortune as doubtful, Thuc.; ἐν ἀμφιβόλωι in doubt, Luc.:—adv., οὐκ ἀμφιβόλως Aesch.
half-minded to do a thing, c. inf., Aesch.
covering the whole man, of a large shield, Il.
thoroughly soaked, Anth.
round the altar, Eur.
to rejoice around or exceedingly, Hhymn.

to be doubtful about a thing, not know or understand, c. acc., Plat.; ἐπί τινος, περί τινος Id., etc.; ἠμφεγνόουν ὅ τι ἐποίουν they knew not what they were about, Xen.:—Pass., ἀμφιγνοηθείς being unknown, Id.
bewailed all round, Anth.
of Hephaestus, he that halts in both feet, the lame one, Il.

entry.etym: The termin. -γυος, as in ὑπόγυος, is of uncertain sense.
entry.sense: pointed at each end, double-pointed, Hom.; in Soph., of persons, armed at all points, practised combatants.
used in intr. perf. and plup. to burn or blaze around, Il.
to bite all round: to grip close, Anth.
all-tearful, Eur.
fringed all round, of the Aegis, Il.
things bound round, bracelets or anklets, Hdt.
with two right hands, very dextrous, Lat. ambidexter, Arist.
like ἀμφήκης, two-edged, Eur.
metaph. double-meaning, ambiguous, Lat. anceps, χρηστήριον Hdt.
= ἀμφότερος, ἀμφ. ἀκμαῖς with both hands, Soph.; ἀμφ. πλευρόν each side, Id.
to look round about one, Anth.
bound or set all round, Anth.
disputed, νίκη Thuc.
to moisten all around, Anth.
to be put round, fitted closely round, Hom.
to lie in wait for, τινά Bion.
to agitate violently, Theocr., Anth.
to be doubtful:— Pass. to be matter for doubt, Plut.
with doubtful mind or of double sense, doubtful, Polyb., etc.
quite flayed, Anth.
as large as can be grasped, λίθος Xen.; cf. χειροπληθής.
running round, encompassing, inclosing, Soph.
having torn both cheeks, in grief, Il.
torn on both sides, Il.

entry.etym: The term. -δυμος recurs in δίδυμος, τρίδυμος.
entry.sense: two-fold, double, λιμὴν ἀμφ. Od.
to put on another:—Mid. to put on oneself, Soph.
of ships, rowed on both sides; or, rather, swaying to and fro, rolling.
to put round or on, like Lat. circumdare, Il.: but mostly, c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, ἐμὲ χλαῖναν ἀμφιέσασα Od.:— Pass., ἠμφιεσμένος τι clothed in, wearing, Ar., etc.
c. dat. rei, ἀμφ. τινά τινι to clothe one in or with a thing, Plat.
Mid. to put round one, put on oneself, Hom.

entry.etym: Forms such as ἀμφίεπον or ἄμφεπον could be interpreted as either imperfect or as second aorist.
entry.sense: to go about, be all round, encompass, Hom.
like διέπω, to be busy about, look after, Id.:—to do honour or reverence to, Pind.
to tend, Id.; to guard, protect, Soph., Eur.
ἀμφ. κῆδος to court an alliance, Lat. ambire, Id.
absol. in partic. with good heed, heedfully, carefully, Hom.
in Mid. to follow and crowd round, Il.
a garment: in pl. clothes, Plat.
to sit on, settle upon, c. dat., Il.
joined from both sides, Aesch.
with sea on both sides, sea-girt, Pind., Xen.
blooming on both sides, of children who have both parents alive, Il.
all abounding, of the gods, Aesch., Ar.:—metaph. abounding in, c. dat., Aesch.
to be in full bloom, Anth.
to warm on both sides, or thoroughly, Eur.
a double theatre, amphitheatre.
of a cup, either that will stand on both ends, or, with handles on both sides, Il.
to run round about, c. acc., Od.
sharpened on both sides, two-edged, Soph.
clotted round a wound, Soph.
with double entrance, Soph.
as Subst., ἀμφίθυρον, τό, a hall, Theocr.
c. acc. to cover all round, enwrap, enfold, of garments, Il.; of a coffin, Id.; ἀμφ. ἵππον to receive within the walls, Od.; of death, sleep, Id.
ἀμφ. τί τινι to put a thing round any one as a cover or shelter, ἀμφ. σάκος τινί, νέφος τινί Id.
after Hom., ἀμφ. τινά τινι to surround one with a thing, Batr.:—Pass., ἀμφεκαλύφθη κρᾶτα he had his head covered, Eur.
to cleave asunder, Od.
Pass. to lie round, ἐπ’ ἀλλήλοισιν ἀμφικείμενοι locked in each other's arms, Soph.; ἐπ’ ὀλέθρωι ἀμφικεῖσθαι φόνον that one murder lies close upon another, Id.
to shear all round, Anth.
with pillars all round, Soph.
broken all round, Anth.
washed on both sides by the waves, Soph.
to tend on all sides or carefully, Anth.
with hair all round, Anth.
thick-leafed, Il.
two headed, Eur.
surrounding the head, Anth.
to hang round, Pind.
hanging round or over, Anth.
with cliffs all round, Eur.
to cover or hide on every side, τοῖον νέφος ἀμφί σε κρύπτει Eur.
they that dwell round, next neighbours, Hdt., Pind.

entry.etym: The word was orig. the same as ἀμφικτίονες.
entry.sense: the Amphictyons, a Council composed of deputies chosen by the States of Greece, the Amphictyonic League, which met at Delphi and Anthela, Hdt., etc.
the Amphictyonic League, Dem.
Amphictyonic, of the Amphictyons, Dem.
fem. of Ἀμφικτυονικός; Ἀμφ. (sc. πόλις), a state in the Amphictyonic League, Aeschin.
a name of Demeter at Anthela, a meeting-place of the Amphictyonic Council, Hdt.
to encircle, surround, Aesch.
to roll around, to be pierced by a sword, Pind.
in Hom. ἀμφικύπελλον δέπας, a double cup, i. e. one that forms a cup both at top and bottom, Il., etc.
of double speech (Greek and Thracian), Ar.
taking in on all sides, widespreading, of large trees, Hdt.
generally, abundant, excessive, enormous, Id., etc.; γόος ἀμφ. a universal wail, Aesch.:—adv. -φῶς, copiously, Plut.
of size, bulky, huge, Hdt.
to dig round, c. acc., Od.
to dispute about, τι Xen.; ἀμφ. μή . . , to dispute, question that a thing is, Id.
discussed on all hands, doubtful, Aesch.: so adv. -τως, Id.
act. disputatious, Eur.; ἀμφ. εἶναί τινι to quarrel for a thing, Aesch.
Dep. to dispute, περί τινος Plut.
dispute, debate, Hes., Plut.
disputed, disputable, Xen.; τὰ ἀμφίλογα disputed points, Thuc.; ἀμφίλογον γίγνεταί τι πρός τινα a dispute on a point takes place with some one, Xen.; neut. pl. ἀμφίλογα as adv., Eur.
act. disputatious, contentious, Soph., Eur.
encompassing the neck, Soph.
associated with ἡ νύξ, the morning-twilight, gray of morning, Il.
to wipe all round, assumed as pres. of an epic aor1 ἀμφιμάσασθε, Od.
round both arms, two-sleeved, Ar.
fought for, Anth.
Dep., only in pres. and imperf., to fight round:
c. acc. to besiege, Il.
c. gen. to fight for, Id.
black all round: φρένες ἀμφιμέλαιναι, prob. referring to the φρένες or midriff being wrapped in darkness, dark-seated.
Pass. to be completely parted, Anth.
brothers or sisters by different mothers, Eur.
Dep. to bellow around: metaph., δάπεδον ἀμφιμέμῡκε (perf. 2) the floor echoed all round, Od.
contested on all sides, eagerly wooed, Aesch., Soph.
Mid., of cattle, to feed around: then, of men, to dwell round, c. acc. loci, Il.
to nod this way and that way, Anth.
to think both ways, be in doubt, Soph.
to smooth all round with an axe or plane, Od.
polishing all round, Anth.
tossed about, re-echoing, Anth.
to strike on both sides, Anth.
prep. with gen., dat., and acc.—Radic. sense, on both sides (cf. ἄμφω, Lat. ambo), whereas περί properly means all round.
c. gen.:
Causal, about, for, for the sake of a thing, ἀμφὶ γυναικός Aesch.
about, i. e. concerning or of a thing, ἀμφὶ φιλότητος ἀείδειν to sing about or of love, Od.
of Place, about, around, ἀμφὶ τῆς πόλιος Hdt.
C. DAT.:

of Place, on both sides of, about, ἀμφὶ ὤμοις, στήθεσσι Hom.; likewise, ἀμφὶ περὶ στήθεσσι Od.:—then, just like περί, all round, κρέα ἀμφὶ ὀβελοῖς ἔπειραν they fixed the meat round, i. e. upon, the spits, Id.
generally, about, near, at, ἀμφὶ πύληισι Il.
about, regarding, ἔρις ἀμφὶ μουσικῆι Hdt.; for the sake of, for, ἀμφ’ Ἑλένηι μάχεσθαι Il., etc.
like Lat. prae, ἀμφὶ τάρβει, ἀμφὶ φόβωι, prae pavore, for very fear, Aesch., Eur.
C. ACC.:
of Place, about, around, mostly with a sense of motion, ἀμφί μιν φᾶρος βάλον Il.
about, near, ἀμφὶ ῥέεθρα somewhere by the banks, ib.

of persons who are about one, οἱ ἀμφὶ Πρίαμον Priam and his train, Id.; oi( a)mfi\ *je/rceaοἱ ἀμφὶ Ξέρξεα his army, Hdt.; in attic, οἱ ἀμφὶ Πρωταγόραν the school of Protagoras or Protagoras himself, Plat.
κλαίειν ἀμφί τινα to weep about or for one, Il.
εἶναι, διατρίβειν ἀμφί τι to be engaged about it, Xen.
as a loose definition of Time, about, Pind.; ἀμφὶ Πλειάδων δύσιν Aesch.:—so of Number, Lat. circiter, ἀμφὶ τὰς δώδεκα μυριάδας about 120, 000, Xen.
WITHOUT CASE, as adv., on both sides, about, around.
= ἀμφίς A. 11, apart, Hhymn.
IN COMPOS.:
about, on both sides, as ἀμφίστομος, = δίστομος.
all round, on all sides, as ἀμφιλαμβάνω, ἀμφιλαφής.
Causal, for, for the sake of, as ἀμφιμάχομαι.
surrounded by a plain, Pind.
Dep. to float around, of music, Od.
Dep. to be busied about, take charge of, c. acc., Hom.; τὸν κύνες ἀμφεπένοντο the dogs made a meal of him, Il.
twined round, Anth.
Pass. to be put round as a crown, Od.
to keep turning about all ways, Il.
to chirp or twitter round about, Anth.
to decay all round, Hhymn.
to squeeze all round, hug closely, Theocr.
to fall around, i. e. to embrace, c. acc., Od.; c. dat., ἀμφιπίπτων στόμασιν embracing so as to kiss, Soph.
intertwined, Soph.; cf. κλῖμαξ.
beaten on both sides.
act. dashing on both sides, Soph.
striking with both sides, double-edged, Soph.
to be busied about, take care of, c. acc., Od., Hdt.; absol., δοῦναί τινά τινι ἀμφιπολεύειν to give one over to another, to take care of, Od.
c. acc.
to attend constantly, to attend on, watch, guard, Pind.
to tend, treat gently, Lat. fovere, Id.
c. dat. to minister to, θεαῖς Soph.
c. gen. rei, to be ministers of, Pind.
encompassing a city, of a city taken by blockade, Aesch.
as fem. Subst. a city between two seas or rivers, Thuc.
busied about, busy, epith. of Κύπρις, Soph.:—as fem. Subst. a handmaid, Od.:— sometimes joined with another Subst., ἀμφ. ταμίη, ἀμφ. γραῦς the housekeeper, the old woman in waiting, Hom.
as masc. an attendant, follower, Pind.: —also a priest, Plut.
in pass. sense, as adj. much-frequented, Pind.
to attend to a thing, c. acc., Il.
Dep. to fly round and round, Il.
double-faced, Plut.
a folding round, embrace, Eur.
with two entrances, Eur.
with fire at each end, of the thunder-bolt, Eur.; of Artemis as bearing a torch in either hand, Soph.
with fire all round, Id.
flowed around, sea-girt, of islands, Od., Hes., Soph. etc.
Pass. to toss about, as on the sea, Anth.
a kind of serpent, that can go either forwards or backwards, Aesch.
literally, to stand apart, and so to disagree with an argument, c. dat., Hdt.:—c. dat. pers. to dispute or argue with, τινι Plat.
absol. to dispute, wrangle, argue, Id., etc.:— οἱ ἀμφισβητοῦντες the opponents, in a lawsuit, Dem.
c. gen. rei, to dispute for or about a thing, Id.; also περί τινος Plat.:— to lay claim to the property of a deceased person, τοῦ κλήρου Dem.
c. acc. rei, to dispute a point, Plat.
c. acc. et inf. to argue that, Id.
Pass. to be the subject of dispute, Id.; or impers., ἀμφισβητεῖται περί τι or περί τινος Id.; ἀμφισβητεῖται μὴ εἶναί τι it is disputed, Id. Hence
a point in dispute, Plat., etc.
disputed, disputable, Plat., etc.; χώρα ἀμφ. debatable ground, Xen.; οὐκέτ’ ἐν ἀμφισβητησίμωι no longer in doubt, Dem.
a dispute, controversy, debate, ἀμφ. γίγνεται (or ἐστι) περί τινος Plat.; ἀμφισβήτησιν ἔχει it admits of question, Arist.
debatable, γῆ Thuc.
as adv.
on or at both sides, Il.; with both hands at once, Id.
generally, around, round about, Id.

apart, asunder, γαῖαν καὶ οὐρανὸν ἀμφὶς ἔχειν to keep heaven and earth asunder, Od.; ἀμφὶς ἀγῆναι to snap in twain, Il.; ἀμφὶς φράζεσθαι or ἀμφὶς φρονεῖν to think separately, i. e. to be divided, take opposite parts, Id.
as prep., like ἀμφί,
c. gen. around, ἅρματος ἀμφίς all round his chariot, Il.
apart from, ἀμφίς τινος ἧσθαι Id.; ἀμφὶς ὁδοῦ out of the road, Id.
c. acc. about, around, always following its case, Id.
Mid. to fold round oneself, c. acc., Theocr.
Pass. to stand all round like a crown, Hhymn.
to place round; only used in Pass. ἀμφίσταμαι, with intr. aor2 act. ἀμφέστην, epic 3rd pl. ἀμφέσταν; syncop. 3rd pl. perf. ἀμφεστᾶσι (for ἀμφεστήκασι):— to stand around, Hom.; c. dat., Soph.
with double mouth, of a tunnel, Hdt.; λαβαὶ ἀμφίστομοι handles on both sides of the bowl, Soph.
Dep. to beleaguer, besiege, epic pl. impf. ἀμφεστρατόωντο πόλιν Il.
turning all ways, of a dragon's heads, Il.
quite round, Luc.
to stretch all round, Hhymn.
encompassing the walls, Aesch.
to cut off on all sides, intercept, Il.

entry.etym: the other forms of this are under τίθημι
entry.sense: to put round, Lat. circumdo, ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ κυνέην ἔθηκε (in tmesi), Hom.; κόσμον ἀμφ. χροΐ Eur.; also, στέφανον ἀμφὶ κρᾶτα Id.:—Mid. to put round oneself, Od.:—Pass. to be put on, Il.
to cover with a thing, κάρα πέπλοις Eur.
to swing round, Anth.
to twitter or chirp around, Ar.
cutting with both sides, two-edged, Aesch., Eur.
well-rounded, Eur.
to tremble round one, in tmesi, Il.
to run round, surround, Pind.
pierced from end to end, ἀμφιτρής [sc. πέτρα], i. e. a cave with double entrance, Eur.; with a neut. noun, ἀμφιτρὴς αὔλιον Soph.
pierced through, Anth.
to tremble for, c. gen., Od.
to beam around, c. acc., Hhymn.
with double crest (v. φάλος), Il.
visible all round, known to all, Eur.
Pass. to tremble all round, ἀμφεφόβηθεν (epic for -ήθησαν, 3rd pl. aor1) Il.
a large jar with two handles, Lat. amphora, Hom.; cf. ἀμφορεύς.
Mid. to consider on all sides, consider well, Il.
to gape round, gape for, c. acc., Il.; of a child, ἀμφ. μαστόν Aesch.; of an army surrounding a city, Soph.
to pour around, to pour or spread over, Od.
Pass. to be poured or shed around, Il.; c. acc., Hom.
of persons, to embrace, c. acc., Od.
to dance around, Eur., Anth.
Mid. to anoint oneself all over, Od.
gilded all over, Eur.
poured around; thrown up around, of an earthen wall, Il.
lame in both feet, Anth.
a road round houses, a street, NTest.
an amphora, jar, urn, Hdt., etc.
a liquid measure, = μετρητής = 1 1/2 amphorae, or nearly 9 gallons, Id.
Dim. of ἀμφορεύς, Dem.
in both ways, Hdt.
sailing both ways:— τὸ ἀμφοτερόπλουν (sc. δάνειον), money lent on bottomry, when the lender bore the risk both of the outward and homeward voyage, Dem.
each or both of two, Lat. uterque, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
neut. ἀμφότερον as adv., ἀμφότερον βασιλεύς τ’ ἀγαθός κρατερός τ’ αἰχμητής both good king and stout warrior, Il.; so in neut. pl., ἀμφότερα μένειν πέμπειν τε Aesch.

κατ’ ἀμφότερα on both sides, utrinque, Hdt.; ἐπ’ ἀμφότερα, both ways, in utramque partem, Id.; ἀπ’ ἀμφοτέρων from both sides, ex utraque parte, Id.; ἀμφοτέραις, epic -ηισι (sc. χερσί), Od.; ἐπ’ ἀμφοτέρων βεβᾱκώς (sc. ποδῶν) Theocr.
from or on both sides, utrinque, Il., Hdt., etc.
at both ends, Od.
on both sides, Xen.
to both sides, Il.
in both ways, Plat.
adv., seems to mean off or from the ground, Od.
a javelin or spit with double point, Eur.
Lat. ambo, both, Hom., etc.
two-eared, two handled, Od.
unblamed, blameless, Il., etc.:—adv. -τως, Hdt.
without blame, blameless, Hdt., Aesch.

entry.etym: from obsol. ἁμός = τὶς, only in compd. ἀμωσ-γέ-πως
entry.sense: in some way or other, Ar., Plat.
conditional Particle. In attic, it is not joined with pres. or perf. ind., nor with imperat. of any tense. Three uses of ἄν must be distinguished in practice:
in combination with Conjunctions and Relatives.
in Apodosis.
in Iterative sentences.
in combinations with Conjunctions and Relatives:

such words are regularly foll. by the subj., viz. ἐάν (= εἰ ἄν) ἤν, ἄν , ἐπήν; ὃς ἄν quicunque, πρὶν ἄν, etc.; ἐπειδάν, ὅταν, ὁπόταν: the protasis generally has a fut. in apodosis, εἰ δέ κεν ὣς ἔρξηις, γνώσηι if perchance thou do thus, thou shalt know, Il.
in epic sometimes with Opt., ὥς κε δοίη ὧι κ’ ἐθέλοι that he might give her to whomsoever he might please, Od.: in such cases κε or ἄν does not affect the Verb.
in epic, sometimes with εἰ and Ind., οἵ κέ με τιμήσουσι Il.
in late Greek, ἐάν, etc., take Ind., ἐὰν οἴδαμεν NTest.
combined IN APODOSIS with the Verb, denoting that the assertion is dependent on some condition; ἦλθεν he came, ἦλθεν ἄν he would have come; ἔλθοι may he come, ἔλθοι ἄν he would come:
with Ind.:

with imperf. and aor., the protasis implies non-fulfilment of a condition, and the apod. expresses what would be or would have been the case if the condition were or had been fulfilled. The imperf. with ἄν refers to continued action in present or past time, the aor. generally to action in past time; οὐκ ἂν νήσων ἐκράτει, εἰ μὴ ναυτικὸν εἶχεν he would not have been master of islands if he had not had a fleet, Thuc.; εἰ ταύτην ἔσχε τὴν γνώμην, οὐδὲν ἂν ἔπραξεν if he had come to this opinion, he would have accomplished nothing, Dem.:—the protasis is often understood, οὐ γὰρ ἦν ὅ τι ἂν ἐποιεῖτε for there was nothing which you could have done (i. e. if you had tried), Id.:—hence the Ind. with ἄν represents a potential mood; ἦλθε τοῦτο τοὔνειδος τάχ’ ἄν this reproach might perhaps have come, Soph.
in epic, with fut. ind., so as to modify the simple fut.; καί κέ τις ὧδ’ ἐρέει and some one will perchance speak thus, Il.
with Subj., in epic, much like fut. ind., εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώηισιν, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι, i. e. I will take her myself, Id.
with Opt.:

after protasis in opt. with εἰ or some relative word, εἴ μοί τι πίθοιο, τό κεν πολὺ κέρδιον εἴη if he should obey me, it would be much better, Id.; sometimes with ind. in protasis, καί νύ κεν ἔνθ’ ἀπόλοιτο, εἰ μὴ νόησε he would have perished, had she not perceived, Id.:—sometimes the tense in protasis is pres. or fut., and the opt. with ἄν in apodosis= fut., φρούριον εἰ ποιήσονται, βλάπτοιεν ἄν if they shall build a fort, they might perhaps damage, Thuc.

the protasis is often understood: τὸν δ’ οὔ κε δύ’ ἀνέρε ὀχλίσσειαν two men could not heave the stone (i. e. if they should try), Il.:—hence the opt. with ἄν becomes a potential mood, βουλοίμην ἄν I should like, Lat. velim (but ἐβουλόμην ἄν I should wish, if it were of any avail, vellem).
the opt. with ἄν comes to have the force of a mild command or entreaty, χωροῖς ἂν εἴσω you may go in, Soph.; κλύοις ἂν ἤδη hear me now, Id.

with inf. and part.:—the pres. inf. or part. represents imperf. ind., φησὶν αὐτοὺς ἐλευθέρους ἂν εἶναι, εἰ τοῦτο ἔπραξαν he says they would (now) be free, if they had done this, Dem.; ἀδυνάτων ἂν ὄντων [ὑμῶν] ἐπιβοηθεῖν when you would have been unable to assist, Thuc.;—or represents pres. opt., φησὶν αὐτοὺς ἐλευθέρους ἂν εἶναι, εἰ τοῦτο πράξειαν he says they would (hereafter) be free, if they should do this, Xen.;—the aor. inf. or part. represents aor. ind. or opt., οὐκ ἂν ἡγεῖσθ’ αὐτὸν κἂν ἐπιδραμεῖν; do you not think he would even have run thither? Dem.; οὐδ’ ἂν κρατῆσαι αὐτοὺς τῆς γῆς ἡγοῦμαι I think they would not even be masters of the land, Thuc.; οὔτε ὄντα οὔτε ἂν γενόμενα, i. e. things which are not and never could happen, Id.:—so the perf. (or plup.) inf. or partic., πάντα ταῦθ’ ὑπὸ τῶν βαρβάρων ἂν ἑαλωκέναι [φήσειεν ἄν] he would say that all these would have been destroyed by the barbarians, Dem.

with imperf. and aor. ind. in the ITERATIVE construction, to express a condition fulfilled whenever an opportunity offered; εἶτα πῦρ ἂν οὐ παρῆν then there would be no fire at hand, i. e. there never was, Soph.; διηρώτων ἂν αὐτοὺς τί λέγοιεν Plat.
GENERAL REMARKS:
Position of ἄν.

ἄν may be separated from its inf. by such verbs as οἴομαι, δοκέω, so that ἄν has the appearance of belonging to the pres. ind., καὶ νῦν ἡδέως ἄν μοι δοκῶ κοινωνῆσαι I think that I should, Xen.:—in the peculiar case of οὐκ οἶδ’ ἂν εἰ, ἄν belongs not to οἶδα but to the Verb which follows, οὐκ οἶδ’ ἂν εἰ πείσαιμι = οὐκ οἶδα εἰ πείσαιμι ἄν, Eur.
ἄν never begins a sentence.
Repetition of ἄν:— in apodosis ἄν may be repeated with the same verb, ὥστ’ ἄν, εἰ σθένος λάβοιμι, δηλώσαιμ’ ἄν Soph.

entry.etym: = ἐάν, ἤν, often in Plat., etc.; cf. κἄν.

entry.sense: going up, mounting: — in Ar., aloft, upstairs.

to go up, mount, to go up to, c. acc. loci, Hom.; φάτις ἀνθρώπους ἀναβαίνει a report goes up among men, Od.; with a prep., ἀν. ἐς δίφρον Il.; ἀν. ἐπὶ οὔρεα Hdt.:—c. dat. to trample on, Il.:— c. acc. cogn., ἀν. στόλον to go up on an expedition, Pind.
Special usages:
to mount a ship, go on board, embark, Hom.; ἐς Τροίην ἀν. to embark for Troy, Od., etc.
to mount on horseback, ἀν. ἐφ’ ἵππον, ἐφ’ ἵππου Xen.; absol., ἀναβεβηκώς mounted, Id.
of land-journeys, to go up from the coast into Central Asia, Hdt., Xen.; cf. ἀνάβασις 1. 2.
of rivers, to rise, Hdt.; ἀν. ἐς τὰς ἀρούρας to overflow the fields, Id.
in attic, ἀν. ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα, ἀν. ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα, alone, to mount the tribune, Dem.; ἀν. ἐπὶ ἀν. ἐπὶ πλῆθος, τὸ δικαστήριον to come before the people, before the court, Plat.
of things and events, to come to an end, turn out, like ἀποβαίνω, ἐκβαίνω, Hdt., etc.
to come to, pass over to, εἴς τινα Id.
aor1 ἀνέβησα is used as aor. to ἀναβιβάζω in causal sense, to make to go up, esp. to put on shipboard, Il., Pind.; so mid. ἀνεβήσετο Od.
to rouse to Bacchic frenzy, Eur.; cf. ἀναβακχιόω.
intr. to break into Bacchic frenzy, Id.
to throw or toss up, Thuc., Xen.
to put back, put off, Od.; ἀν. τινα to put him off with excuses, Dem.:—Pass. to be adjourned, Thuc.
to run a risk, ἐγώ σφε θάψω κἀνὰ κίνδυνον βαλῶ, = καὶ ἀναβαλῶ, Aesch.
Mid. to strike up, begin to play or sing (cf. ἀναβολή 11), Od., Ar.
to put off, delay, Il., Ar., etc.
to throw back or refer a thing to another, Luc.
to throw one's cloak back, throw it over the shoulder, Ar., Plat.; ἀναβεβλημένος with one's cloak thrown up or back, Dem.; cf. ἀναβολή 1. 2.
to dip repeatedly, Plut.
a going up, mounting on horseback, Xen.:— πᾶσα ἄμβασις = πάντες ἀναβάται, all the horsemen, Soph.
an expedition up from the coast into Central Asia, as that of the younger Cyrus, Xen.
a way up, ascent of a tower or mountain, Hdt., Thuc.
to raise or lift up, carry, Luc.
one mounted, of Pentheus in the tree, Eur.: a horseman, rider, Xen.
skilled in mounting, ἐπὶ τοὺς ἵππους Xen.
to be mounted or scaled, easy to be scaled, Hom.

entry.etym: perf. with no pres. ἀνα-βρύζω in use
entry.sense: ἀναβέβρυχεν ὕδωρ the water gushed or bubbled up, Il.
to make go up, cause to mount, ἐπὶ πύργον Hdt., Xen.
Special usages:
ἀν. τινα ἐφ’ ἵππον to mount one on horseback, Id.; ἐπ’ ἅρμα Hdt.
ἀν. ναῦν to draw a ship up on land, Xen.
Mid., ἀναβιβάζεσθαί τινας ἐπὶ τὰς ναῦς to have them put on board ship, Thuc.; absol., ἀναβιβασάμενοι Id.
at Athens, to bring up to the bar as a witness, Plat., etc.: Mid., of a culprit, to bring up his wife and children to raise compassion, Id.
Pass., ἀναβιβάζεσθαι εἰς τιμήν to ascend to honour, Plut.
ἀν. τοὺς φθόγγους, to moderate them, Id.
one must cause to mount, Plat.
to come to life again, return to life, Ar., Plat.
a reviving, Plut.
as Pass. = ἀναβιόω, Plat.
as Dep., Causal of ἀναβιόω, to bring back to life, Id.; aor1 ἀνεβιωσάμην Id.
to shoot up, grow up again, of Plants, Plat.; of a city, Hdt.; of misfortunes, to spring up, be rank, Id.
to look up, Ar., Plat., etc.; ἀν. πρός τινα to look him in the face, Xen.
to look up at, c. acc., Eur.; also c. dat., Id.
c. acc. cogn., ἀν. φλόγα to cast up a glance of fire, Id.
to recover one's sight, Hdt., Plat.; πάλιν ἀν. Ar.
a looking up, Arist.
recovery of sight, NTest.
a putting off, delay, Il.
to spout up, c. acc., Anth.
intr. to gush forth, Theocr.
to go through, c. acc., Eur.
a loud cry, Aesch.

entry.etym: The form ἀναβοάσω is aor1, not future.
entry.sense: to shout aloud, utter a loud cry, Hdt., Eur.; of a war-cry, Xen.; c. inf. to call out that . . , Id.
c. acc. rei, to cry out something, Eur.; also to wail aloud over a misfortune, Aesch., Eur.
c. acc. pers. to call on, Id.
a groom who helps one to mount, Plut.
of the thing,
that which is thrown up, a mound, Xen.
that which is thrown back over the shoulder, a mantle, cloak, Plat.:—also the fashion of wearing it, Luc.; cf. ἀναβάλλω B. 111.
as an action,
a prelude on the lyre, Pind.; a dithyrambic ode, Ar.; v. ἀναβάλλω B. I.
a putting off, delaying, Hdt., Thuc.; οὐκ ἐς ἀμβολάς without delay, Eur.; V. ἀναβάλλω B. II.
intr. a bursting forth, Arist.
to boil well, seethe, c. acc., Ar.; absol., ἀναβράττετ’, ἐξοπτᾶτε Id.
boiled, Ar.
to neigh aloud, of horses, Ar.
Dep. to roar aloud, Plat.
to carry back tidings of, report, Aesch., Eur.; τῶι Βρασίδαι τὴν ξυνθήκην Thuc.:—Pass., c. part., ἀνηγγέλθη τεθνεώς was reported dead, Plut.
from which no messenger returns, Anth.
to laugh loud, ἀναγελάσας Xen.
to beget anew, regenerate, NTest.
to give one a taste, c. acc. pers., Ar.
epic usage, esp. in aor2 ἀν-έγνων, to know well, know certainly, Hom., Hdt.
to know again, recognise: to acknowledge, own, Lat. agnoscere, Hom., Hdt.

attic usage, fut. ἀναγνώσομαι: aor2 ἀνέγνων: perf. ἀνέγνωκα:— Pass., fut. -γνωσθήσομαι: aor1 ἀνεγνώσθην: perf. ἀνέγνωσμαι, etc.:—of written characters, to know them again, and so to read, Ar., etc.; ἀναγνώσεται (sc. ὁ γραμματεύς), ἀνάγνωθι, Dem.:— οἱ ἀναγιγνώσκοντες students, Plut.

ionic usage, aor1 ἀνέγνωσα, to persuade or induce one to do a thing, c. acc. et inf., Hdt.: the inf. is sometimes omitted, ὡς ἀνέγνωσε when he had persuaded him, Id.;—the pres. is once so used, ἀναγιγνώσκεις στρατεύεσθαι βασιλέα Id.:—so in aor1 pass. ἀνεγνώσθην, to be persuaded to do a thing, c. inf., Id.

to force, compel, mostly c. acc. pers. et inf., ἀν. τινὰ ποιεῖσθαι τι, λέγειν, etc., Hdt., etc.:—so Pass., ἠναγκάζοντο ἀμύνεσθαι Id.;—without the inf., ἀναγκάζεσθαί τι to be forced to do a thing, Plat., etc.:—also, ἀναγκάζειν τινὰ ἔς τι Thuc.
c. acc. pers. only, to constrain by argument, Plat.: Pass., ἠναγκάσθην I was constrained, tortured, Soph.; ἠναγκασμένος, ἀναγκασθείς under compulsion, Thuc.
c. acc. rei only, to carry through by force, Eur.
c. acc. rei et inf. to prove that a thing is necessarily so and so, Plat.
a place of constraint, a prison, Xen.:—others read Ἀνακεῖον.
with or by force:

act. constraining, applying force, Il.; ἦμαρ ἀν. the day of constraint, i. e. slavery, Ib.;so, ἀναγκαία τύχη the lot of slavery, or a violent death, Soph.; τῶι τῆς ἀρχῆς ἀναγκαίωι by the compulsory nature of our rule, Thuc.; ἐξ ἀναγκαίου under compulsion, Id.
of arguments, forcible, cogent, Id.
pass. constrained, forced, πολεμισταὶ ἀν. soldiers perforce, whether they will or no, Od.
necessary, ἀναγκαῖόν [ἐστι], like ἀνάγκη ἐστί, c. inf., it is necessary to do a thing, Hdt., etc.; but, ἔνιαι τῶν ἀποκρίσεων ἀναγκαῖαι ποιεῖσθαι necessarily requiring to be made, Plat.
τὰ ἀναγκαῖα necessary things, needs, as food, sleep, Id., Xen.; τὰ ἐκ θεοῦ ἀν. the appointed order of things, laws of nature, Id.

absolutely necessary, indispensable, barely sufficient; ἀν. τροφή = ἡ καθ’ ἡμέραν, Thuc.; τὸ ἀναγκαιότατον ὕψος the least height that was absolutely necessary, Id.; ἡ ἀναγκαιοτάτη πόλις the least that could be called a city, Plat.
of persons, connected by necessary ties, i. e. related by blood, Id., etc.:— οἱ ἀναγκαῖοι, Lat. necessarii, kinsfolk, Xen., etc.
adv. -ως, necessarily, of necessity, perforce, ἀναγκαίως ἔχει it must be so, Hdt.; ἀν. φέρειν to bear as best one can, opp. to ἀνδρείως, Thuc.
ἀν. λέγειν only so far as is necessary, Plat.
to be compelled, Plat.
neut. ἀναγκαστέον one must compel, Id.
forced, constrained, Hdt.; ἀν. στρατεύειν pressed into the service, Thuc.

force, constraint, necessity, Hom., etc.; ἀνάγκηι perforce, of necessity, or in act. sense, forcibly, by force, Id.; so, ὑπ’ ἀνάγκης, ἐξ ἀνάγκης, δι’ ἀνάγκης, πρὸς ἀνάγκην, κατ’ ἀνάγκην, attic:— ἀνάγκη ἐστί, c. inf., it is matter of necessity to do a thing, Hom., etc.; c. dat. pers., ἀν. μοι σχεθεῖν Aesch.:—in Trag., πολλή γ’ ἀνάγκη, πολλή στ’ ἀνάγκη or πολλή μ’ ἀνάγκη, with which an inf. must be supplied.
actual force, violence, torture, Hdt., etc.; metaph., δολοποιὸς ἀν., i. e. the stratagem of Nessus, Soph.
bodily pain, anguish, distress, κατ’ ἀνάγκην ἕρπειν painfully, Id.; ὑπ’ ἀνάγκης βοᾶν Id.
like Lat. necessitudo, the tie of blood, relationship, kindred, Lys., etc.
to bend back: Pass., αἰχμὴ ἀνεγνάμφθη the spear-point was bent back, Il.
to undo, loose, δεσμόν Od.
impure, unclean, unholy, defiled, Aesch., etc.
recognition, Plat.; in a tragedy, recognition, Arist.
recognition, Hdt.
reading, Plat.
a passage read aloud, a lecture, Luc.
a reader, a slave trained to read, Plut.
suitable for reading, opp. to ἀγωνιστικός, Arist.
a public proclamation, Decret. ap. Dem.

entry.etym: fut. and aor. are mostly supplied by ἀν-ερῶ, ἀν-εῖπον.
entry.sense: to proclaim publicly, Aeschin.:—Pass. to be proclaimed, ἀναγορευέσθω νικηφόρος Plat.
one must register, εὐεργέτην ἀν. τινά Luc.
inscribed, registered, Thuc.
a registrar, Lysias.
a registering, of treaties and the like, Arist.
a register, Plat.
to engrave and set up, of treaties, laws, etc., to inscribe, register, ἀν. τι ἐν στήληι or ἐς στήλην, Thuc., Dem.
of persons, to register his name, Isocr.:—Pass., ἀναγραφῆναι πατρόθεν to be registered with his father's name, Hdt.; ἀναγράφεσθαι εὐεργέτης to be registered as a benefactor, Id.
to describe mathematically, Plat. (in Mid.).
to entitle, Plut.
to keep muttering, Ar.
to strip naked, unveil, Plut.
a leading up, esp. taking a ship into the high sea, a putting to sea, Thuc., etc.
a bringing back: restitution by law, Plat.
ill-trained, of horses, ill-broken, unmanageable, Xen., etc.
without conflict, Thuc.: never having contended for a prize, Xen.
to lead up from a lower place to a higher, Theogn., etc.
to lead up to the high sea, to carry by sea, Hom., etc.; ἀν. ναῦν to put a ship to sea, Hdt.; absol. in the same sense, Id.; —this is more common in Mid.
to take up from the coast into the interior, Od., Hdt.; esp. from Asia Minor into Central Asia, Xen.
to bring up from the dead, Hes., Aesch.
ἀν. χορόν to conduct the choir, Hes., Eur., etc.; also, ἀν. ὁρτήν to celebrate a festival, Hdt.
to lift up, raise, κάρα, τὸ ὄμμα Soph., etc.
ἀν. παιᾶνα to lift up the paean, Id.
in various senses, ἀν. αἷμα to bring up blood, Plut.; ἀν. ποταμόν to bring a river up [over its banks], Luc.; ἀν. φάλαγγα, like ἀναπτύσσειν, Plut.; to bring up a prisoner for examination, Xen., etc.
to bring back, Hom., etc.
to refer a matter to another, Dem.
to rebuild, Plut.
to reckon or calculate, Id.
intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν) to draw back, withdraw, retreat, Xen.; ἐπὶ πόδα ἀν. to retreat facing the enemy.
to reduce in amount, contract, Dem.
Mid. and Pass. to put out to sea, set sail, Il., etc.; ἀναχθῆναι Hdt.; ἀναχθείς Aesch.
metaph. to make ready, prepare oneself, ὡς ἐρωτήσων Plat.
to light up, Aesch.
re-distribution or partition of land, among colonists, Hdt., Plat., etc.
divided anew, re-distributed, ἀν. γῆν ποιεῖν (cf. ἀναδασμός) Plat.
ἀν. ποιεῖν τι to rescind, Luc.
to divide anew, redistribute, Thuc.:—Pass. ἀναδαίομαι, to be distributed, Orac. ap. Hdt.
a mouthpiece used by public criers, Anth.

to lift up and shew, πύλας ἀναδεικνύναι to display by opening the gates, i. e. throw wide the gates, Soph.; (so in Pass., μυστοδόκος δόμος ἀναδείκνυται Ar.); ἀναδέξαι ἀσπίδα to hold up a shield as signal, Hdt.; ἀνέδεξε σημήϊον τοῖς ἄλλοις ἀνάγεσθαι made signal for them to put to sea, Id.
to consecrate, Anth.
a proclamation of an election, an appointment, Lat. designatio, Plut.
(from Pass.) a manifestation, NTest.
without brother or sister, Eur.
Dep. to look up, Il.
to strip the skin off: metaph. to lay bare, τι Luc.:—so in Mid., ἀναδέρεσθον Ar.
a binding on, στεφάνων Plut.
a binding up, τῆς κόμης Luc.
a band for the hair, a head-band, Il., Eur.:—so,
binding up the hair, Eur.
to moisten: metaph. to imbue, Plut.
Dep. to take up, catch, receive, Il.
to take upon oneself, submit to, ὀϊζύν Od.; ἀν. τι ἐφ’ ἑαυτόν Dem.
to undertake, promise to do, c. fut. inf., Hdt., Xen.:—so, ἀν. τοὺς δανειστάς to undertake to satisfy them, Plut.:— to be surety to one, τινι Thuc.
to bind or tie up, Pind.: Mid., ἀναδέεσθαι τὰς κεφαλάς to bind their heads, Hdt.; κρώβυλον ἀναδεῖσθαι τῶν τριχῶν to bind one's hair into a knot, Thuc.
c. acc. pers. to crown, Pind., Thuc.; εὐαγγέλια ἀναδεῖν τινα to crown him for good tidings, Ar.:—metaph. in Pass., τροφῆι ἀναδοῦνται are well furnished with food, Plat.
ἀναδῆσαι τὴν πατρίην ἔς τινα to attach one's family to a founder, trace it back, Hdt.
Mid., of a ship, ἀναδούμενος ἕλκειν to take in tow, Thuc.
metaph. in Pass., ἀναδεδέσθαι ἔκ τινος or εἴς τι to be dependent upon, Plut.
to teach otherwise or better, Lat. dedocere, Hdt.:—Pass. to be better instructed, change one's mind, Id.
to shew clearly, Thuc.: to expound, interpret, λόγια ἀν. τινά to expound them to one, Ar.
to hold up and give, Pind., Xen.
to give forth, send up, yield, καρπόν Hdt., etc.: of a river, to yield, ἀναδιδόναι ἄσφαλτον Id.
intr., of springs and fire, to burst forth, Id.
to deal round, spread, Plut.
intr. to retrograde, Arist.
tried over again, Andoc., Plat.
Pass. to be made double, Xen.
a distribution: digestion, Polyb.: metaph. of knowledge, Plut.
to be given up, Thuc.
a taking up, undertaking, πόνων Soph.
to come to the top of water, Batr.
to come up, rise from the sea, c. gen., Hom.; so c. acc., ἀνεδύσατο κῦμα θαλάσσης Il.
to draw back, retire, Hom.: to shrink back, hesitate, Ar.:—of springs, to fail, Plut.
c. acc. to draw back from, shun, πόλεμον Il.
a drawing back, retreat, Plat.: a holding back from service, Plut.
without bridal gifts, Il.

entry.etym: only in pres. and imperf.; ἀναερτάω is a lengthd. form of ἀν-αείρω, Anth.
entry.sense: to lift up, of a wrestler, Il.; to carry off, τάλαντα Id.
unlooked for, Hes.
to return to life, be alive again, NTest.
to yoke again, ἀναζευγνύναι τὸν στρατόν to move off the army, Hdt.; ἀν. τὸ στρατόπεδον to break up the camp, Id.; ἀν. τὰς νῆας to move Them back, Id.
absol. to break up, shift one's quarters, Thuc., Xen.
a marching off, return home, Plut.
to boil up or bubble up, Soph.
ἀναζ. εὐλάς to swarm with worms, a kind of disease, Plut.; also, εὐλαὶ ἀναζέουσιν Id.
to examine into, investigate, τὰ ὑπὸ γῆς Plat.: Pass., Hdt., etc.
to recall to life, Anth.
to gird up:— Mid., ἀν. τὰς ὀσφύας to gird up one's loins, NTest.
to rekindle, Eur.:—Pass. to gain fresh life and courage, Plat., Xen.; so, intr. in Act., Plut.
to shoot up again: so in fut. mid., ἀναθαλήσεται Anth.
to regain courage, Ar., Thuc.; τινι at a thing, Thuc.; πρός τι Plut.
to fill with fresh courage, Xen.
intr. = ἀναθαρσέω, Plut.
† ἀνάθημα, Theocr., Anth.
esp anything devoted to evil, an accursed thing, NTest.
a curse, Id=NTest.
to devote, ἀναθέματι ἀν. ἑαυτούς to bind themselves by a curse, NTest.
intr. to swear, Id.
to warm up, heat again, Anth.
one must attribute, τί τινι Plat.
to sprout afresh, Il.
a votive offering set up in a temple, Hdt., Soph., etc.
a delight, ornament, Od.
to press hard, Anth.
without contest, not warlike, Luc.
to cry out loudly, shout in applause, Plat., Xen.
c. acc. to applaud, Plat.
a nursling, Theocr.
to look up at, observe closely, Eur., Plat.:—Pass., τὰ ἔργα ἐκ τῶν λόγων ἀναθρούμενα their deeds compared with their words, Thuc.
to spring up, bound up, rebound, Il., Hdt., etc.; ἀναθρώσκει ἐπὶ τὸν ἵππον springs upon it, Hdt.
to make to rise in vapour:— Pass. to rise in vapour, Arist., Luc.
shamelessness, impudence, effrontery, Hom., Plat., etc.
Dep. to behave impudently, Ar.
shameless, Hom., Soph.
c. gen., ἀναιδέα δηϊοτῆτος insatiate of strife, Il.
of things, λᾶας ἀναιδής the reckless stone, of Sisyphus, Od.; ἔργ’ ἀναιδῆ Soph.: —τὸ ἀναιδές, contr. τἀνειδές, = ἀναίδεια, Eur.; ἐπὶ τὸ ἀναιδέστερον τραπέσθαι Hdt.
adv. -δῶς, Soph., etc.
to stir up, rouse, Soph., Eur.
to light up, set on fire, Eur.: to inflame to love, Mosch.
intr. to blaze up, Aesch.
unstained with blood, Aesch., Eur.
drained of blood, Aesch.
without blood, bloodless, Plat., etc.
without blood, bloodless, of the gods, Il.
adv., without shedding blood, Il.
Dep. c. acc. to reject with contempt, turn one's back on, spurn, Hom.: also simply to refuse, decline, Od., Xen.
to renounce, disown, Aesch., Eur.
c. inf. to refuse, decline to do, Il.; and with pleon. negat., ἀναίνετο μηδὲν ἑλέσθαι he said no, he had received nothing, Id.
absol. to refuse, deny, Hom.
a taking up of dead bodies for burial, Eur., Thuc.:—so, in a sea-fight, ναυαγίων ἀν. Thuc.
destruction, Xen., Dem.: abrogation of laws, Plut.
to take up, raise, Lat. tollere.
to take up and carry off, bear away, Il., Hdt.
to take up bodies for burial, Ar., Xen.; this is more common in Mid.
to make away with, to destroy, kill, Hom., Hdt., etc.
of things, to abolish, annul, Xen., etc.
to destroy an argument, confute, Plat.
to appoint, order, of an oracle, c. inf., ἀνεῖλε παραδοῦναι Thuc.; also c. acc. et inf., ἀνεῖλε μιν βασιλέα εἶναι Hdt.
absol. to answer, give a response, Id., attic
Mid. to take up for oneself, take up; and then to gain, win, get, achieve, Hom., etc.; ποινήν τινος ἀν. to exact penalty from one, Hdt.
to take up and carry off, snatch away, Od.
to take up dead bodies for burial, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
to take up in one's arms, Il.: hence, to take up new-born children, own them, Lat. tollere, suscipere, Plut.
to conceive in the womb, like συλλαμβάνω, Hdt.
to take upon oneself, undertake, πόνους Id.; πόλεμόν τινι war against one, Id.; ἀν. δημόσιον ἔργον to undertake, contract for the execution of a work, Plat.
to accept as one's own, γνώμην Hdt.; ἀν. φιλοψυχίην to entertain a love for life, Id.
to take back to oneself, cancel, Dem.
to lift up: in Mid., Eur.; in Pass., ἀναρθείς carried up, Anth.
want of feeling or perception; insensibility to pleasure or pain, Arist.
to want perception, Dem.
insensate, unfeeling, Xen., etc.:— adv., ἀναισθήτως ἔχειν to be indifferent, Isocr.
senseless, wanting tact, stupid, Thuc., Dem.: —τὸ ἀναίσθητον insensibility, Thuc.
pass. unfelt, θάνατος Id.
to use up, use, consume, Hdt.:—Pass., ἀναισιμοῦσθαι ἔς τι to be used for a purpose, or spent upon a thing, Id.; ποῦ ταῦτα ἀναισιμοῦται; where (i. e. how) have these been disposed of? Id.
consumption, expenditure, Hdt.
to start up, rise quickly, Il.; of thought, Id.; of a spring, to gush forth, Id.
c. acc. to leap up into, ἅρμα Id.
to be shameless, behave impudently, Thuc.; πρός τινα Xen.
shamelessness, Ar., Plat.
shameless, impudent, Eur., Ar., etc.: —τὸ ἀναίσχυντον, = ἀναισχυντία, Eur.:—adv. -τως, Plat.
of things, abominable, Eur.
of persons, not being the cause of a thing, guiltless, Hom., etc.
c. gen. rei, guiltless of a thing, Hdt., Aesch., etc.: —οὐκ ἀναίτιόν ἐστι, c. inf. it is blamable to do, Xen.
to burst out laughing, Plat.
to clear completely:— Pass., of the air, to become quite clear, Plut.
Mid. to clear or sweep away, Plat.
Pass. to sit upright, Luc.
to set up: Mid. to sit up, Plat.
intr. to sit up, Xen.
to renew, restore:— Pass. to be renewed, Anth., NTest.
renewal, NTest.
to light up, Od., Hdt., etc.:—Mid. to light oneself a fire, Hdt.
Pass., metaph. to fire up, with anger, Id.
to call up the dead, Aesch.; so in Mid., Eur.
to call again and again:
to invoke, appeal to, θεούς Hdt., etc.;—so in Mid., Soph., Eur.
to summon, cite, Hdt.:—Mid. to call to oneself, send for, summon, Id., Thuc.
to call by a name, ἀν. κακούς Eur.; Δαναούς Thuc.:—Pass., Ἀργεῖος ἀνακαλούμενος Soph.
to call on, so as to encourage, Thuc.; Mid., ἀνακαλεῖσθαι τὰς κύνας to cheer on the hounds, Xen.
to call back, recall, mostly in Mid., Aesch.; esp. from exile, Plat.; ἀνακαλεῖσθαι τῆι σάλπιγγι to sound a retreat, Xen.
presents made by the bridegroom, when the bride first took off her veil, Lys.
to uncover, ἀν. λόγους to use open speech, Eur.:—Mid. to unveil oneself, unveil, Xen.: —Pass., of a veil, to be uplifted, NTest.
to bend back: mostly intr. to bend one's steps back, return, Hdt.
without spine, of certain fish, Hdt.
to gulp down, Hdt.

entry.etym: for rest of morphology see article on κεῖμαι
entry.sense: to be laid up as a votive offering, to be devoted or dedicated, Hdt., etc.
to be set up as a statue, Dem., Theocr.
to be ascribed or offered, τινι Plut.

to be referred to a person, depend on his will, Hdt.; πάντων ἀνακειμένων τοῖς Ἀθηναίοις ἐς τὰς ναῦς since they had their whole fortunes dependant on their ships, Thuc.; ἐπὶ σοὶ τάδε πάντ’ ἀνάκειται Ar.; σοὶ ἀνακείμεσθα Eur.
the temple of the Dioscuri, Andoc., etc.; cf. ἀναγκαῖον.
a loud shout or din, Eur.
to mix up or again, κρητῆρα Od.; οἶνον Ar.:—Pass., aor1 ἀν-εκεράσθην Plat.; ἀν-εκράθην [ᾱ] Plut.
the Dioscuri, Castor and Pollux, Plut.
to sum up the argument:— Pass. to be summed up, NTest.
to spout up, gush forth, ἀνακήκιεν αἷμα Il.
to proclaim by voice of herald, publish abroad, Soph., Xen.
c. acc. pers. to proclaim as conqueror, Ar.:—Pass., aor1 inf. ἀνακηρυχθῆναι Hdt.
to put up to auction, Id.
to run into danger again, to run a fresh risk, Hdt.
to sway or swing to and fro, Hdt.
to stir up, awaken, νόσον Soph.; πόλεμον Plut.
a swinging to and fro: metaph., excitement, emotion, Soph.
Dep. to mix well: metaph., φιλίας ἀνακίρνασθαι to join in closest friendship, Eur.
to cry aloud, scream out, Eur.; of a dog, to bark, bay, Xen.

entry.etym: Note also that there is another verb ἀνακλάω
entry.sense: to weep aloud, burst into tears, Hdt.
c. acc. to weep for, Id.; so in Mid., Soph.

entry.etym: Note also that there is another verb ἀνακλάω
entry.sense: to bend back, δέρην Eur.
to break short off, Thuc.
a calling on, invocation, θεῶν Thuc.
a recalling: retreat, Plut.
fit for exhorting, Plut.
fit for recalling, τὸ ἀνακλητικὸν σαλπίζειν to sound a retreat, Anth.
to lean one thing upon another, [τόξον] ποτὶ γαίηι ἀγκλίνας having laid it on the ground, Il.:—Pass. to lean back, to lie on one's back, recline, Lat. resupinari, Od.
to push back a trap-door, to open it, Hom., Hdt. Hence
leaning back: ἀν. θρόνος a seat with a back, Plut.
of the Fates, to undo the thread of one's life, to change one's destiny, Luc.
to open and counterfeit a seal, Ar.
to communicate a thing to another, τί τινι Plat.
c. dat. pers. to communicate with, take counsel with, ἀν. τοῖς θεοῖς περί τινος Xen.
Mid., with perf. pass. ἀνακεκοίνωμαι, properly, to communicate what is one's own to another, ἀνακοινοῦται τῶι Ἴστρωι τὸ ὕδωρ mingles its water with the Ister, Hdt.
much like Act., either ἀνακοινοῦσθαί τί τινι to impart a thing to one; or ἀν. τινι to consult one, Xen.: absol. to hold communication, Ar.
to rule or command ina place, Anth.
a carrying away again, recovery, τῶν πλοίων Decret. ap. Dem.
to carry up, Xen.:—Pass. to be carried up stream, or up the country, Hdt.
to bring back, recover, Xen.: —Mid. (with perf. pass.) to take back with one, Hdt.:— Pass. to be brought back, and of persons, to return, Id., Thuc.
Mid. also, to bring to pass, Pind.:— to bring back upon oneself, Eur.
intr., to dart or shoot up, Il., Hdt.
a beating back: the recoil of the waves, and the water left after flood-tide, Plut.
to drive back, Od.
to beat back an assailant, Thuc.
to stop:— Pass. to be stopped, stop short, τινός from a thing, Luc.
to lift up, Eur.; of a ship, ἀν. κάρα Soph.:—Pass. to be lifted up or lightened, aor1 ἀνεκουφίσθην Eur.: to rise in spirits, Xen.
relief from a thing, c. gen., Soph.
to cry out, lift up the voice, Od., attic
a mixing with others, Plut.
Mid., to tune up, Anth.
to hang up on a thing, c. dat., Od.; ἐς . . or πρός. . . Hdt.:—Pass. to be hung up, Id.
to make dependent, Plat.
to examine closely, to question, interrogate, τινά Thuc., Plat.
to inquire into a fact, Antipho:—Mid., Pind.
used at Athens in technical sense:
to examine magistrates, as to their qualification, Dem.
of the magistrates, to examine persons concerned in a suit, so as to prepare the matter for trial, Id.
Mid., ἀνακρίνεσθαι πρὸς ἑαυτούς to dispute one with another, Hdt.
examination of parties concerned in a suit, a preparation of the matter for trial, Xen.; μηδ’ εἰς ἄγκρισιν ἐλθεῖν, i. e. not even to begin proceedings, Aesch.
to lift up and strike together, τὼ χεῖρε Ar.; τὰς χεῖρας Aeschin.: absol. to applaud vehemently, Ar.
a pushing back: of a ship, backing water, Thuc.
one must check, Xen.
to push back, stop short, check, ἵππον χαλινῶι Xen.
Mid., ἀνακρούεσθαι πρύμνην to put one's ship astern, by backing water, Ar.; so ἀνακρούεσθαι alone, Thuc.; also, ἐπὶ πρύμνην ἀν., Hdt.:—metaph. to put back, Plat.
in Music, to strike up, Theocr.
Dep., to regain for oneself, get back again, recover, Hdt., Aesch.
c. acc. pers. to win a person over, gain his favour or friendship, Hdt., Xen.
management of horses, Hhymn.
belonging to a lord or king, royal, Od.
a palace; of gods, a temple, Hdt., Eur.
to stir up and mix, mix up, Ar.
to turn round again, Eur.: metaph. to revolve in one's mind, Luc.
Pass., to revolve, Anth.
to fall rattling over, of chariots, Il.
to lift up the head, Hdt.; ἀνακεκυφώς with the head high, of a horse, Xen.
to come up out of the water, pop up, Ar., Plat.: metaph. to emerge, Plat.
to wail aloud, Aesch.; ἀνακωκύει φθόγγον utters a loud wail, Soph.
carefully, ἀνακῶς ἔχειν τινός to look well to a thing, give good heed to it, Hdt., Thuc.
Dep. only in pres., to take again, Mosch.
to raise a war-cry, cry aloud, Eur., Xen.
to take up, take into one's hands, Hdt.: to take on board ship, Id., Thuc.: generally, to take with one, Thuc.
to take up, for the purpose of examining or considering, Plat.
to take upon oneself, assume, τὴν προξενίαν Thuc., etc.
Mid. to take upon oneself, undertake, engage in, κίνδυνον, μάχην Hdt.
to learn by rote, Plut.
to get back, regain, recover, τὴν ἀρχήν Hdt., Xen.
to retrieve, make good, τὴν αἰτίην Hdt.; ἁμαρτίαν Soph.
to restore, repair, Hdt.; ἀν. ἑαυτόν to regain strength, revive, Thuc.
to take up again, resume, τὸν λόγον Hdt., Plat.: to recollect, Plut.
to pull short up, to check a horse, Xen.: ἀν. τὰς κύνας to call them back, Id.
to gain quite over, win over, Ar.
to flame up, take fire, Xen.
metaph. to break out anew, as war, Plut.
to come to oneself again, revive, Id.
want of feeling, insensibility, Dem.
painless, Plut.
without pain, and so:
of persons, insensible to pain, Arist.
unfeeling, hard-hearted, ruthless, Soph.; ἀναλγητότερος εἶναι to feel less grieved, Thuc.: c. gen., ἀν. εἶναί τινος to be insensible to, Plut.:—adv. -τως, unfeelingly, Soph.
of things, not painful, Id.
cruel, πάθος Eur.
not thriving, feeble, Ar.
to pick up, gather up, ὀστέα Il.:—Mid. to pick up for oneself, Hdt.; ἀν. πνεῦμα to collect one's breath, Anth.
to reckon up, τὸν χρόνον Plut.: —Pass., ἀναλεγόμενον being recounted, Xen.
to lick up, τὸ αἷμα Hdt.
a taking up of a child, to acknowledge it, Luc.
pass. a being taken up, the Ascension, NTest.
a taking back, a means of regaining, Plut.
a making good, making amends for a fault, Thuc.: a refreshing, Luc.
powerless to heal, Bion.
doric for ἀν-ήλιος.
doric for ἀν-ήλιπος.

entry.etym: The quantity of the 2nd syllable and the active form make it doubtful whether this verb is a compound of ἀνά, ἁλίσκομαι.
entry.sense: to use up, to spend, lavish or squander money, Thuc.; εἴς τι upon a thing, Plat., etc.; πρός τι Dem.; ὑπέρ τινος Id.:—Pass., τἀνηλωμένα the monies expended, Id.
metaph., ἀνάλωσας λόγον hast wasted words, Soph.; ἀν. σώματα πολέμωι Thuc.
of persons, to kill, destroy, Trag.:—Mid. to kill oneself, Thuc.
want of strength, feebleness, epic dat. pl. ἀναλκείησι Il.; sg. ἀναλκίη [with ῑ] Theogn.
without strength, impotent, feeble, of unwarlike persons, Hom., Aesch., etc.
Dep. , to leap or spring up, Ar., Xen.
not salted, Xen.
proportion, Plat., etc.
Dep., to reckon up, sum up, Plat., Xen.
to calculate, consider, τι Thuc.
foll. by a Conj., ἀναλ. ὡς, ὅτι, to recollect that, Id., Xen.
reconsideration, Thuc.:— a course or line of reasoning, Xen.
κατὰ τὸν ἀναλογισμόν according to proportionate calculation, ap. Dem.
proportionate, Plat.: neut. as adv. in proportion, analogously, Arist.
not to be filled, insatiate, Od.
a loosing, releasing, κακῶν from evils, Soph.
(from Pass.) retirement, departure, death, NTest.
a deliverer, Aesch.
to unloose, undo, of Penelope's web, Od.
to unloose, set free, release, ἐκ δεσμῶν Id.
after Hom., ἀν. ὀφθαλμόν, φωνάν, i. e. to restore to a dead man the use of his eyes and voice, Pind.
to analyse, Arist.
to put an end to a thing, Xen.:— to abolish, cancel, Dem.:—Mid. to cancel faults, Xen., Dem.
intr. to loose a ship from its moorings, weigh anchor, depart, Polyb.: —metaph., of death, NTest.
to return, Id.
expenditure, cost, in pl. expenses, Thuc., etc.
outlay, expenditure, Theogn., Thuc.
a spender, waster, Plat.
expensive, Plat.
not to be taken, invincible, impregnable, Hdt.: also, not taken, still holding out, Thuc.
of persons, ἀν. ὑπὸ χρημάτων incorruptible, Xen.
to rage through, c. acc., Il.
to inquire closely, Hdt.
impassable for wagons, Hdt.
without missing, unfailing, unerring, Xen.

in moral sense, without fault, blameless, Plat., etc.; ἀν. πρός τινα or τινι having done no wrong to a person, Hdt.; ἀν τινός guiltless of a thing, Id.; τὸ ἀναμάρτητον innocence, Xen.:—adv. ἀν-αμαρτήτως, without fail, unerringly, Id.
Dep. to chew over again, ruminate, Ar

to wipe off, ἔργον ὃ σῆι κεφαλῆι ἀναμάξεις a deed which thou wilt wipe off on thine own head (as if it were a stain), Od.; so, ταῦτα ἐμῆι κεφαλῆι ἀναμάξας Hdt.:—Mid., ἀναμάττεσθαι τῶι προσώπωι τοῦ αἵματος to have [some of] the blood wiped on one's face, Plut.
Dep., to renew the fight, retrieve a defeat, Hdt., Thuc.; ἀν. τὸν λόγον to fight the argument over again, Plat.
of a horse, that one cannot mount, Xen.
to begin to sing, ἀοιδάν Theocr.
to wait for, await, c. acc., Od., Hdt., etc.:—c. acc. et inf., ἀν. τινὰ ποιεῖν to await one's doing, Hdt.; ἀν. τι γίνεσθαι a thing happening, Id.:—absol to wait, stay, Soph., etc.
to await, endure, τί Xen.
to put off, delay, Id.
in the midland or interior, Lat. mediterraneus, Hdt.
filled full, τινός of a thing, Dem.
to fill up, fill full, Ar., in Pass.
to re-measure the road one came by, retrace one's steps to a place, ὄφρα ἀναμετρήσαιμι Χάρυβδιν Od.
to recapitulate, Eur., in Mid.
to measure over again, to measure carefully, take the measure of, τι Hdt.; ἀν. ἑαυτόν Ar.:—Mid., ἀνεμετρησάμην φρένας τὰς σάς took the measure of thy mind, Eur.
ἀναμετρεῖσθαι δάκρυ εἴς τινα to measure out (i. e. pay) to him the tribute of a tear, Id.
a measurement, τινος πρός τι of one thing by another, Plut.
to chew the cud, Luc.
promiscuously, Soph., Anth.
