to mix up, mix together, Od., Hdt., etc.:—Pass. to be mixed with others, Hdt., attic: to have intercourse, Plut.
ἀναμίσγω, poet. and ionic for ἀναμίγνυμι, only in pres. and imperf.
to mix one thing with another, τί τινι Od.: —Pass. to have intercourse, τινι Hdt.
to remind one of a thing, c. dupl. acc., ταῦτά μ’ ἀνέμνησας Od.; c. gen. rei, ἀν. τινά τινος Eur.:—c. acc. pers. et inf. to remind one to do, Pind.
c. acc. rei, to recall to memory, make mention of, Dem.
in Pass. to remember, τινός Hdt., etc.; more rarely τι Ar., Plat.; περί τι Plat.
intercourse, Plut.
adv., promiscuously, Hdt., Thuc.
to serve again for pay, Plut.
a calling to mind, recollection, Plat., etc.
that which one can recollect, Plat.
to roar loudly, boil up, πᾶς’ ἀναμορμύρεσκε (ionic imperf.) of Charybdis, Od.
to raise by a lever, to force open, πύλας Eur.
unerring, unfailing, Soph.
of a man, without error or crime, Aesch., Soph.
to moan loudly, Aesch.
unambiguous: adv. -λως, Luc.
undisputed, undoubted, Xen. adv. ἀναμφιλόγως, indisputably, Id.
undisputed, indisputable, Thuc.; ἀν. χώρα a place about which there is no dispute, i. e. well-known, Xen.
want of manhood, Eur., Plat., etc.
unmanliness, cowardice, Aesch., etc.
= ἄνευ ἀνδρός husbandless, Trag.
= ἄνευ ἀνδρῶν, without men, Id.
wanting in manhood, unmanly, Hdt., Plat.; τὸ ἄνανδρον = ἀνανδρία, Thuc.
widowed, εὐναί Soph.
to renew one's youth, Ar.
to divide anew: Mid. to count up, Hdt. (in ionic fut. -νεμέεται).
to rehearse, read, Theocr.
to mount up, ἀννεῖται (epic for ἀνανεῖται) Od.
to renew, Thuc., etc.
to throw the head back, in token of denial (which we express by shaking the head), Hom., Hdt., etc.
c. acc. rei, to deny, refuse, Il.
a renewal, Thuc.
to return to sobriety of mind, NTest.
trans. to make sober again, Luc.
without bloom, past its bloom, Plat.
without a rival, without a struggle, Thuc.: uncontested, unalloyed, Id.:—adv. -τως.
irresistible, Plut.
up-hill, Il.
up-hill, steep, Hdt., Plat., Xen.; πρὸς τὸ ἄναντες to the highest point, Plat.
incontestable, Luc.
to tear open, a wound, Babr.
to dry up things, of the wind, Il.; to dry up a stream, Hdt.
a command, behest, Pind.
of persons,
unworthy, not deemed or held worthy of, c. gen., Hdt.; ἀνάξιον σοῦ too good for thee, Soph.; c. inf., ἀνάξιος δυστυχεῖν undeserving to suffer, Id.:—adv., ἀναξίως ἑωυτῶν Hdt.
absol. unworthy, worthless, Id., Soph.:—adv. -ίως, Soph.
undeserving of evil, Id., Eur.
of things, undeserved, ἀνάξια παθεῖν Eur., etc.
ruled by the lyre, Pind.
a lord, master, being applied to the gods, esp. to Apollo and Zeus, Hom.; to the latter in voc., Ζεῦ ἄνα Il.
among the Homeric heroes Agamemnon is ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν; but ἄναξ is a title given to all men of rank and note, as to Teiresias, Od.; βασιλεὺς ἄναξ lord king, Id.
the master of the house, esp. as denoting the relation of master to slave, Id.
metaph., κώπης, ναῶν ἄνακτες lords of the oar, of ships, Aesch.; ἄν. ὅπλων Eur.
the trousers worn by eastern nations, Hdt., Xen.; by the Scythians, Hdt.
to scrape up or off:— Pass., ἀναξυσθείς (aor1 part.) having the surface scraped off, Plut.
to educate afresh, Ar.
struck back, rebounding: as Subst. an anapaest (i. e. a dactyl reversed), an anapaestic verse, Ar.; ἀνάπαιστα, τά, anapaestics, satire, Plut.
to strike back.
back again, Plat., etc.
over again, Id.
contrariwise, reversely, Id.

to swing to and fro, ἀμπεπαλὼν ἔγχος, having poised and drawn back the spear before throwing it, Il.: to set in motion, urge on, Eur.; ἀμπάλλειν τὰ κῶλα Ar.:—Pass. to spring up, ὡς ὅτε ἀναπάλλεται ἰχθύς, ὣς πληγεὶς ἀνέπαλτο(3rd sg. epic aor2) as when a fish springs up, so he smitten sprang up, Il.
to sprinkle upon, τί τινι Pind.
repose, rest, Soph.; κατ’ ἀναπαύλας διηιρῆσθαι to be divided into reliefs, of workmen, Thuc.
c. gen. rei, rest from a thing, Soph., Thuc., etc.
a resting-place, an inn, Lat. deversorium, Eur., Ar.
a repose, rest, Hes.; μεριμνῶν from cares, Theogn.
a resting-place, Anth.
repose, rest, Pind., Xen.: relaxation, recreation, Xen.
rest from a thing, c. gen., Thuc.
of or for resting, Hdt.
as Subst. ἀναπαυστήριον, τό, a time of rest, Xen.
a place of rest, Luc.
to make to cease, to stop or hinder from a thing, c. gen., Il.; ἀν. τινά τινος to give him rest or relief from a thing, Soph., Dem.
c. acc. only, to stop, put an end to, βοήν Soph.:—more commonly, to rest, halt, τὸ στράτευμα, τοὺς ναύτας Xen.
rarely intr. in sense of Mid. to take rest, ἀναπαύοντες Thuc.; ἀνέπαυεν Xen.
Mid. and Pass. to desist from a thing, ἀπὸ ναυμαχίας Thuc.
absol. to take one's rest, sleep, Lat. pernoctare, Hdt., Eur., etc.; of the dead, Theocr.: —of soldiers, to halt, rest, Xen.
to regain strength, Id.
prep. governing gen., dat., and acc. Radic. sense, up, upon, opp. to κατά.
WITH GEN., ἀνὰ νηός on board ship, Od.
WITH DAT., on, upon, ἀνὰ σκήπτρωι upon the sceptre, Il.; ἀνὰ ὤμωι upon the shoulder, Od.
WITH ACC., the comm. usage, implying motion upwards:
of Place, up to, up along, ἀνὰ τὸν ποταμόν Hdt.; ἀνὰ δῶμα up and down the house, throughout it, Il.; so, ἀνὰ στρατόν, ἄστυ, ὅμιλον Hom.; ἀνὰ στόμα ἔχειν to have continually in the mouth, Id.
of Time, throughout, ἀνὰ νύκτα Il.; ἀνὰ τὸν πόλεμον Hdt.; ἀνὰ χρόνον in course of time, Id.; ἀνὰ πᾶσαν τὴν ἡμέραν Id.; but, ἀνὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν, distributively, day by day, Id.

distributively also with Numerals, ἀνὰ πέντε παρασάγγας τῆς ἡμέρας [they marched] at the rate of 5 parasangs a day, Xen.; κλισίας ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα companies at the rate of 50 in each, NTest.; ἔλαβον ἀνὰ δηνάριον a denarius apiece, Id.
ἀνὰ κράτος up to the full strength, with all might, ἀνὰ κράτος φεύγειν, ἀπομάχεσθαι Xen.; ἀνὰ λόγον in proportion, Plat.
WITHOUT CASE as adv. thereupon, Hom., etc.
all over, μέλανες δ’ ἀνὰ βότρυες ἦσαν all over there were clusters, Il. [E.] IN COMPOS.,
upwards, up, as ἀναβαίνω, ἀνίστημι.
with a sense of increase or completeness, as ἀνακρίνω.
again, as ἀναβλαστάνω, ἀναγινώσκω.
back, backwards, ἀναχωρέω.
ἄνα by anastr. for ἀνάστηθι, up! arise! ἀλλ’ ἄνα Hom.
ἄν apocop. for ἀνέστη, he stood up, Il.
the negat. Prefix (of which α priv. is a shortened form) before vowels, ἀν-αίτιος, ἀν-ώδυνος (but see ἀ-έκων, ἄ-ελπτος, ἄ-εργος): the complete form remains in ἀνά-εδνος, ἀνά-ελπτος.
to bring over, convince, Xen.:— Pass., Thuc.
to persuade, move to do a thing, c. acc. pers. et inf., Hdt., attic; ἀν. τινά τι to persuade one of a thing, Ar.
to seduce, mislead, τινά Hdt., etc.
Dep., to try or attempt again: as a military and naval term, to renew or continue their exercises, Hdt., Thuc.
to pierce through, fix on a spit, Il., Ar.
to impale, ἐπὶ ξύλου τινά Hdt.: Pass., ἀποθανεῖν ἀναπαρείς (aor2 part.) Id.
persuasive, Ar.
Dep., to count again, count over, Plat.
to send up from below, Aesch.: to send forth, Pind.:—Mid. to send up from oneself, Xen.
to send up, from the coast inland, esp. into Central Asia, Thuc., Xen.
to send back, Pind.

to spread out, unfold, unfurl sails, Il.; ἀν. βόστρυχον to let the hair flow loose, Eur.; φάος ἀμπετάσας having shed light abroad, Id.; ἀν. τὰς πύλας to throw wide the gates, Hdt.:— Pass., ἀναπεπταμένος thrown open, Il.; ἀλώπηξ ἀναπιτναμένη a fox lying on its back, Pind.:—the part. perf. pass. ἀναπεπταμένος, η, ον, is often a mere adj. open, of the sea, Hdt.; of eyes, Xen.; δίαιτα ἀν. life in the open air, Plut.
to fly up, fly away, Hdt., etc.
metaph. to be on the wing, ἀνεπτόμαν Soph.; ἀνέπταν φόβωι Id.
to transfix, impale, Plut.
to leap up, start up, Il., Hdt., etc.
to leap back, from fear, Ar.; ἀνεπήδησεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἑστίαν, for protection, Xen.
much maimed, crippled, Plat., etc.
of ground, to send forth water, Plut.
to fill up, Lat. explere, Epigr. ap. Luc.
metaph., πότμον ἀναπλήσαντες having filled up the full measure of misery, Il.; so, ἀναπλῆσαι οἶτον, κακά, ἄλγεα, κήδεα Hom., Hdt., etc.
c. gen. rei, to fill full of a thing, Ar., etc.
with a notion of defiling, infecting, ὡς πλείστους ἀναπλῆσαι αἰτιῶν Plat.; so Pass. to be infected with disease, Thuc., Plat.
to fall back, Aesch.
to fall back, give ground, Thuc.: to flag, lose heart, Lat. concidere animo, Dem.
of a plan, to be given up, Id.
to recline at table, like ἀνάκειμαι, NTest.
to form anew, remodel, Ar.:—Mid., ἀναπλάσασθαι οἰκίην to rebuild one's house, Hdt.
metaph. to invent, in Mid., Anth.
to plaster up: Pass., κηρὸν ἀναπεπλασμένος having wax plastered, Ar.
to enwreath, Pind.:—Mid. to braid one's hair, Luc.
metaph. of writing verses, Anth.
Pass., ἀναπεπλεγμένοι closely engaged, Plut.
quite full of a thing, c. gen., Hdt., Plat.
infected with or by a thing, c. gen., Plat.
to sail up, to go up stream, c. acc., Od.
to put out to sea, Il., Dem.
to sail the same way back again, sail back, Hdt., Xen.:—of fish, to swim back, Hdt.
to fill up a void, Plat.
to make up, supply, Id.:—Mid., δώματ’ ἀν. to fill their houses full, Eur.
to fill up the numbers of a body, τὴν βουλήν Plut.; ἀν. τὴν συνηγορίαν to fill the place of advocate, Id.
to pay in full, in Mid., Dem.
Pass. to be restored to its former size, of the sun, after an eclipse, Thuc.
a filling up, Arist., Plut.
one must fill up, Plut.
a sailing upstream, Hdt.
a putting out to sea, Polyb.
to unfold, open, Mosch., Babr.
a resting-place, Pind.
recovery of breath, respite from a thing, c. gen., Il.
without breath, breathless, Hes.

entry.etym: besides the common tenses, we have three Homeric forms as if from ἀμπνύω
entry.sense: to breathe again, take breath, Il., etc.: to recover from a thing, c. gen., Id., Soph., etc.; so, ἔκ τινος Hdt.:— absol. to revive, Xen.; and in this sense Hom. uses ἄμπνυτο, ἀμπνύνθη.
to draw breath, breathe, Pind., Plat.
to breathe forth, send forth, καπνόν Pind.
recovery of breath, revival, Pind., Plat.; μόχθων ἀμπνοά rest from toils, Pind., Eur.
a drawing breath, respiration, Ar., Plat.; ἀμπνοὰς ἔχειν = ἀναπνέειν, to breathe, Soph.; τὴν ἀν. ἀπολαβεῖν τινος to strangle him.
a breathing organ, of the mouth, Luc.; an air-hole, Plut.
to make to step back, call back, cross-examine, Hdt., Aeschin.; ἀν. ἑωυτόν to correct himself, Hdt.
without ransom, only in neut. ἀνάποινον as adv., Il.
properly to turn up the ground again: hence to go over again, repeat, reconsider, Pind., Soph.
of a field, Pind.
a sending up: ἀν. θησαυρῶν a digging up of treasures, Luc.
sent back, Luc.
one that sends up or back, of Hades, sending up the shade of Darius, Aesch.
unwashen, Ar.
to exact, levy money or debts, Ar., Thuc.; ἀν. ὑπόσχεσιν to exact the fulfilment of a promise, Thuc.
to blow forth, to let burst forth, δάκρυ’ ἀναπρήσας with tears bursting forth, Hom.
properly of a bird, to raise its feathers: hence, ἀν. ἐθείρας Eur.
metaph. to set on the wing, excite vehemently, Hdt., Eur., etc.:— Pass. to be in a state of excitement, Aesch., Xen., etc.
to scare exceedingly, Mosch.:—Pass. to be scared, Plut.
to unfold the rolls on which books were written; and so, to unrol, open for reading, ἀν. βιβλίον Hdt.:— to undo, open, πύλας Eur.; ἀναπτύξας χέρας with arms outspread, Id.
to unfold, disclose, reveal, Lat. explicare, Trag.

as military term, τὴν φάλαγγα ἀναπτ. to fold back the phalanx, i. e. deepen it by wheeling men from both flanks to rear, French replier, Xen.; but conversely, τὸ κέρας ἀναπτ. to open out the wing, i. e. extend the line by wheeling men from rear to front, French deployer, Id.
αἰθέρος ἀμπτυχαί, the expanse of heaven, Eur.; ἡλίου ἀναπτυχαί the sun's expanse, Id.
to spit up, sputter, Soph.

to make fast on or to a thing, ἐξ ἱστοῦ πείρατ’ ἀνῆπτον made fast the rope to the mast, Od.:—Mid., ἐκ τοῦδ’ ἀναψόμεσθα κάλων to him will we make fast our cable, i. e. he shall be our protector, Eur.:—Pass. to fasten oneself on to, cling to a thing, c. gen., Id.; ἀμφί τινι Id.; ἀνῆφθαί τι to have a thing fastened on one, Id.
to hang up in a temple, offer up, ἀγάλματα Od.
metaph. to attach to, μῶμον ἀνάψαι Id.; αἷμα ἀν. τινί a charge of bloodshed, Eur.
to light up, light, λύχνα Hdt.; πῦρ Eur.; also, πυρὶ ἀν. δόμους Id.:—metaph., νέφος οἰμωγῆς ὡς τάχ’ ἀνάψει Id.
to inquire closely into, ascertain, Hdt.; τὸν ποιήσαντα Id.
to learn by inquiry, Id., Xen.
ascertained, notorious, Od., Hdt.
without joints, not articulated, Plat., etc.
without strength, nerveless, Soph.
of sound, inarticulate, Plut.
Mid. to enumerate, Dem.
not to be counted, countless, Hdt., attic: of time, immeasurable, Soph.
unregarded, Eur.

without number, countless, numberless, Sapph., Trag.: c. gen., ἀνάριθμος θρήνων without measure in lamentations, Soph.; μηνῶν ἀνήριθμος without count of months, Id.; πόλις ἀνάριθμος = πολῖται ἀνάριθμοι, Id.
not governed or subject, Thuc.: not submitting to be governed, Aesch.
unequipped, Anth.
not to fit or suit, τινί or πρός τι Plat.
discord, of musical sounds, Plat.
unsuitable, incongruous, disproportionate, Hdt., Xen.:—of sound, out of tune, Plat.:—adv. -τως, Id.
of persons, impertinent, absurd, Ar.
unfitted, unprepared, πρός τι Thuc.
re-capture, Eur.
to snatch up, Il., Xen.
to snatch away, carry off, Hom., etc.; of slave-dealers, to kidnap, Od.:—Pass., Soph.: in Prose also, to be dragged before a magistrate, carried off to prison, Lat. rapi in jus, Dem.
in good sense, to rescue, Plut.
to take by storm, plunder, Eur.; of persons, ἀναρπασόμενος τοὺς Φωκέας to take them by storm or at once, Hdt.
to carry off, steal, Xen., Dem.
snatched up, carried off, Eur., Plat.
carried up the country, i. e. into Central Asia, Xen.
to break up the ground, Il., Hdt.
to break through a wall, Il., Eur.:—Pass., ἡ ναῦς ἀναρρήγνυται τὴν παρεξειρεσίαν the ship has its bow broken through, Thuc.
to tear open a carcase, of lions, Il.; of Ajax, δίχα ἀνερρήγνυ was cleaving them asunder, Soph.
to make to break forth, utter, like Lat. rumpere voces, Ar., Theocr.; ἀν. πόλιν to make it break out, excite greatly, Plut.:—Pass. to burst forth; metaph. of persons, ἀναρρήγνυσθαι πρὸς ὀργήν Id.
intr. to break forth, Soph.
breakage, Plut.
a proclamation, Dem.; cf. ἀνεῖπον.
to throw up, ἀν. ἅλα πηδῶι to throw up the sea with the oar, i. e. row with might and main, Od.; also without πηδῶι, οἱ δ’ ἅλα πάντες ἀνέρριψαν Id.

ἀν. κίνδυνον, a phrase from the game of dice, to run the hazard of a thing, run a risk, Hdt., Thuc.; περί or ὑπέρ τινος Plut.;— also without κίνδυνον, ἐς ἅπαν τὸ ὑπάρχον ἀναρρίπτειν to throw for one's all, stake one's all, Thuc.; with a second acc. ἀν. μάχην to hazard a battle, Plut.
to clamber up with the hands and feet, scramble up, Ar.
to suck down again, of Charybdis, Od.
rescue: name of the second day of the festival Ἀπατούρια, Ar.
to strengthen afresh:— Pass., to regain strength, ἀναρρωσθέντες, Thuc.
intr. in aor1 act. to recover, Plut.
not fitting, incongruous: hence,
of persons, hostile, unpropitious, implacable, Hom., Trag.
of events, untoward, strange, monstrous, Hdt.
to hang to or upon, to attach to, make dependent upon, ἐς θεοὺς ἀν. τι to leave it depending upon them, Eur.; ἀν. ἑαυτὸν εἰς δῆμον Dem.
Pass. to be hung up, Plat.
metaph. to hang or depend upon, ἔκ τινος Id., Dem.:— ἀνηρτῆσθαι εἰς . . to be referred or referable to . . , Plat.; ἀνηρτημένοι ταῖς ὄψεσιν πρός τινα hanging on one with their eyes, Plut.
Mid. to attach to oneself, make dependent upon one, τινά Xen.

entry.etym: ionic Verb, only used in perf. pass.
entry.sense: to be ready, prepared to do, c. inf., Hdt.: cf. ἀρτέομαι.
uneven, odd, opp. to ἄρτιος (even), Plat.
to make old again, Anth.
lack of a leader, Hdt.
the state of a people without government, anarchy, Aesch., Thuc., etc.:—at Athens this name was given to the year of the thirty tyrants (B. C. 404), when there was no archon, Xen.
without head or chief, Il., Eur.: τὸ ἄναρχον = ἀναρχία, Aesch.
to shake up, stir up, Luc.
to draw back with a rein, to hold in check, Anth.
to draw aside from the road, Eur.
to shake back, swing to and fro, move up and down, Hes.: esp. as a signal, Thuc.
to stir up, NTest.
Pass., only in syncop. aor2, αἷμα ἀνέσσυτο the blood sprang forth, spouted up, Il.
bristling hair, Plut.
to dig up, to dig up ground, Plut.
to scatter abroad, Plut.
to pack up the baggage (τὰ σκεύη), Lat. vasa colligere: to carry away, Xen.:—Mid. to break up one's camp, march away, Thuc., Xen.
to disfurnish, dismantle a place, Thuc.: Mid. to dismantle one's house or city, Id.
to waste, ravage, destroy, Xen.
Pass. to be bankrupt, break, of bankers, Dem.; metaph., ἀνεσκευάσμεθα we are ruined, Eur.
unpractised, unexercised, Xen.

entry.etym: The middle future form ἀνασκολοπιοῦμαι has a passive meaning.
entry.sense: to fix on a pole or stake, impale, Hdt.
to look at narrowly, examine well, Ar., Thuc.
to scare and make to start up, to rouse, Plat.:—Pass., ἀνασεσοβημένος τὴν κόμην with hair on end through fright, Luc.
to tear up, Eur.
drawn up, Ar.
dragged up the country, of tribes compelled to emigrate into Central Asia, Hdt.
of a door or gate, drawn back, opened, Soph.
to draw up, pull up, Solon, Hdt.:—Mid., ἐκ χροὸς ἔγχος ἀνεσπάσατο he drew his spear forth again, Il.
to draw a ship up on land, Hdt., Thuc.
to draw or suck up greedily, αἷμα Aesch.: but, ὕδωρ ἀν. to draw water, Thuc.
to tear up, Hdt., attic
metaph., ἀνασπᾶν λόγους to draw forth words, to utter violent, offensive words, Soph.
τὰς ὀφρῦς ἀνασπᾶν to draw up the eyebrows, and so put on a grave important air, Ar.; so, τὰ μέτωπα ἀν. Id.
to draw back, τὴν χεῖρα Id.
to carry away from home, Luc.
a queen, lady, mistress, addressed to goddesses, Od., Aesch.; also to a mortal, Od., Trag.
generally, like ἄναξ IV, ἄνασσα ὀργίων Ar.

to be lord, master, owner, to rule, in a place, c. dat., Ἄργεϊ, νήσοισι ἀν.; or c. gen. to be lord of, rule over, Τενέδοιο, Ἀργείων Hom.: also, μετ’ ἀθανάτοισι ἀν. to be first among the immortals, Il.:—Mid., τρὶς ἀνάξασθαι γένεα ἀνδρῶν to have been king for three generations, Od.:—Pass. to be ruled, Id.
in Trag. metaph. of things, κώπης ἀνάσσειν, etc., Eur., cf. ἄναξ IV:—Pass., παρ’ ὅτῳ σκῆπτρον ἀνάσσεται by whom the sceptre is held as lord, Soph.
standing up, upright, Il.
act. a raising up of the dead, Aesch.
a making men rise and leave their place, removal, as of suppliants, Thuc.; ἀν. τῆς Ἰωνίας the removal of all the Greeks from Ionia, Hdt.:— an overthrow, destruction, ruin, Aesch., Eur.
a setting up, restoration, τειχῶν Dem.
（ἀνίσταμαι) a standing or rising up, in token of respect, Plat.
a rising and moving off, removal, Thuc.
a rising up, ἐξ ὕπνου Soph.
a rising again, the Resurrection, NTest.
a destroyer, Aesch.
made to rise up and depart, driven from one's home, Hdt.
of cities and countries, ruined, laid waste, Id., Soph., etc.
to unsettle, upset, NTest.
to impale, Hdt.: — Pass., Thuc.
in the Rom. times, to affix to a cross, crucify, Plut.
to crucify afresh, NTest.
strengthd. for στείβω, Anth.
to raise up:— Mid. to gird up one's clothes, Eur., Ar.
to keep back, repulse an attack, Eur., Thuc.:—Pass. to retire, Thuc.
Hdt.; τοιάδ’ ἀνεστέναζες ἐχθοδοπά such hateful words didst thou groan forth, Soph.
c. acc. pers. to groan for, lament, Aesch., Eur.
to groan aloud, Il.
c. acc. pers. to groan aloud over, bemoan, c. acc., Il.; so in Mid., Id.
to groan aloud, Aesch.
like ἀναστενάχω, c. acc., Eur.
to crown, wreath, κρᾶτα Eur.:—Pass., ἀνέστεμμαι κάρα I have my head wreathed, Id.
to set up firmly, Anth.
a putting back, τῆς κόμης Plut.
to furnish with a mouth, ἀν. τάφρον to clear out a trench, Xen.:—Mid., φάρυγος ἀναστόμου τὸ χεῖλος open the lips of your gullet wide, Eur.
to turn upside down, upset, Il., Eur., etc.; ἀν. καρδίαν to upset the stomach, i. e. cause sickness, Thuc.:—Pass., ὄρος ἀνεστραμμένον ἐν τῆι ζητήσει turned up by digging, Hdt.
to turn back, bring back, τινὰ ἐξ Ἅδιου Soph.; ὄμμ’ ἀν. κύκλωι to roll one's eye about, Eur.: to rally soldiers, Xen.
intr. to turn back, return, retire, Hdt., attic
Pass. to be or dwell in a place, Lat. versari, ἄλλην γαῖαν ἀν. to go to a place and dwell there, Od.; ἀν. ἐν Ἄργει Eur.:— to conduct oneself, ὡς δεσπότης Xen.
to revolve, of the sun, Id.
of soldiers, to face about, rally, Id.
ignorant of astrology, Strab.
a turning upside down, upsetting, Eur.; εἰς ἀναστροφὴν διδόναι = ἀναστρέφειν, Id.
a turning back, return, Soph.: a wheeling about, of soldiers, whether to flee or rally, Xen.; of a ship, Thuc.
(from Pass.) a dwelling in a place, Plut.: a mode of life, conversation, NTest.
the place where one tarries, an abode, haunt, Aesch.
intr., to keep turning about, Od.
to pull up one's clothes, Hdt.; perf. part. ἀνασεσυρμένος obscene, Theophr.
intr., to rise from a fall or illness, to recover, Babr.
a taking on oneself, endurance, τῶν δεινῶν Plut.
to rip up, τὴν γαστέρα Hdt.: to rend, Theocr.

to recover what is lost, rescue, Soph.: Mid., ἀνασώζεσθαί τινα φόβου to recover one from fear, Id.:—Mid. in proper sense, ἀν. τὴν ἀρχήν to recover the government for oneself, Hdt.:—Pass. to return safe, of exiles, Xen.
in Mid. also to preserve in mind, remember, Hdt.
to disturb greatly, rouse to frenzy, confound, Soph., Plat.:—Pass., ἀνατεταραγμένος in disorder, Xen.
to stretch up, hold up, χεῖρα ἀν. to lift up the hand in adjuration or in prayer, Pind.; or as token of ascent in voting, Xen.
to stretch forth, τὴν μάχαιραν ἀνατεταμένος with his sword stretched out, Id.; οὐδὲν ἀνατείνασθαι φοβερόν to hold out no alarming threat, Dem.
to hold up as a prize, Pind.
to lift up, exalt, Id.
to stretch out, extend, e. g. a line of battle, Xen.; ἀετὸς ἀνατεταμένος a spread eagle, Id.
intr. to reach up, πέδιλα ἐς γόνυ ἀνατείνοντα Hdt.: to extend out, οὖρος ἀν. ἐς τὴν Οἴτην Id.
to rebuild, Xen.
a rebuilding of the walls, Xen.
to make to rise up or to grow up, Il.:—Pass., φλὸξ ἀνατελλομένη a flame mounting up, Pind.
to give birth to, bring to light, Id.: of events, Soph.
intr. to rise, of the sun and moon, Hdt., Soph., etc.
of a river, to take its rise, Hdt.
to grow, of hair, Aesch.
to cut open, Hdt., Luc.
to lay upon (as a burden), Il., Ar.

to refer, attribute, ascribe a thing to a person, Hdt., etc.; οὐ γὰρ ἂν οἱ πυραμίδα ἀνέθεσαν ποιήσασθαι would not have attributed to him the erection of the pyramid, Id.; ἐμοὶ ἀναθήσετε will give me the credit of it, Thuc.:—also, ἀν. τινὶ πράγματα to lay them upon him, entrust them to him, Ar., Thuc.
to set up as a votive gift, dedicate, τί τινι Hes., Hdt., etc.; hence the votive gift itself was ἀνάθημα:— Pass., aor1 inf. ἀνατεθῆναι Ar.; but ἀνάκειμαι is more freq. as the Pass.
metaph., ἀν. τι λύραι to commit a song to the lyre, Pind.
to set up and leave in a place, Ar.
to put back, remove, προσθεῖσα κἀναθεῖσα τοῦ γε κατθανεῖν by adding or putting off somewhat of the necessity of death, Soph.
Mid. to put upon for oneself, τὰ σκεύη ἐπὶ τὰ ὑποζύγια Xen.
to impart something of one's own, τί τινι NTest.
to place differently, change about, Orac. ap. Hdt., Plat.
metaph. to retract one's opinion, Xen.
to raise in price, Hdt.
to shake up and down, brandish, Eur.; of the wind shaking about a sail, Id.
without harm, with impunity, Trag.
to bear up against, endure, Od., attic; φάρμακ’ ἀνέτλη resisted the strength of the magic drink, Od.
a rising, rise, of the sun, often in pl., Od.; of the stars, Aesch.
the quarter of sunrise, East, Lat. Oriens, Hdt.
to regain courage, Plut.
unharmed, Aesch.; c. gen., κακῶν ἄνατος harmed by no ills, Soph.
one must overthrow, Luc.
likely to upset a thing, c. gen., Plat.

entry.etym: Note that aor2 middle is used in a passive sense.
entry.sense: to turn up or over, overturn, upset, Archil., etc.:—Pass., ἀνετράπετο = ὕπτιος ἔπεσεν, Il.; of ships, Plat., etc.
to overthrow, Lat. evertere, Hdt., attic
to upset in argument, refute, Ar.:—Pass. to be upset, disheartened, ἀνετράπετο φρένα λύπαι Theocr.
to stir up, awaken, Soph.
to feed up, nurse up, educate, Aesch., Ar., Xen.
to run back, Il.
c. acc. to retrace, Lat. repetere, Pind.
to jump up and run, start up, of men, Hdt., Thuc.
of things, ἐγκέφαλος ἀνέδραμε ἐξ ὠτειλῆς the brains spurted up from the wound, Il.; σμώδιγγες ἀνέδραμον weals started up under the blow, Id.
to run up, shoot up, of plants, Id.; then of cities and peoples, to shoot up, rise quickly, Hdt.
ἀναδέδρομε πέτρη the rock ran sheer up, Od.
a trepanning, Plut.
to rub well, rub clean, κύνας Xen.
Pass. to be worn away, Hdt.
an upsetting, overthrow, Aesch., Plat.
to unroll, βιβλία Luc.
to impress again, Luc.
to stir up, confound, Ar.
rayless, sunless, Aesch.
not to be spoken, unutterable, ineffable, Lat. infandus, Aesch., Eur.
unspoken, impossible, Soph.
speechless, Id.
speechless, silent, Od., Aesch., etc.
preventing speech, silencing, Aesch.
like ἀναύδητος, unutterable, Soph.
without the flute, i. e. joyless, melancholy, Eur.: neut. pl. ἄναυλα as adv., Babr.
unskilled in flute-playing, Luc.
a river in Thessaly, Hes.
as appellat. ἄναυρος, ὁ, a torrent, Mosch.
without ships, νᾶες ἄναες ships that are ships no more, Aesch.
to cry aloud, Theocr.
to make to give light, make to blaze up, ξύλα Od.
to bring to light, shew forth, display, Hom., attic; ἀν. μελέων νόμους Ar.

to proclaim, declare, βασιλέα ἀν. τινά Pind.; ἀν. πόλιν to proclaim it victor in the games, Id.:—c. inf., ἀναφανῶ σε τόδε ὀνομάζειν I proclaim that they call thee by this name, i. e. order that thou be so named, Eur.
of things, to appoint, νόμους Ar.
ἀναφάναντες τὴν Κύπρον having opened, come in sight of, Cyprus, NTest.
Pass., with fut. mid. ἀναφανήσομαι or -φανοῦμαι : perf. ἀναπέφαμμαι, or in mid. form -πέφηνα:— to be shewn forth, come to light or into sight, appear plainly, Hom., etc.
to reappear, Hdt.
ἀναφανῆναι μούναρχος to be declared king, Id.; ἀναφαίνεσθαι σεσωσμένος to be plainly in safety, Xen.
bald in front, Luc.
visibly, openly, Od.
to bring or carry up, Od., etc.; ἀν. τινὰ εἰς Ὄλυμπον Xen.:— to carry up the country, esp. into Central Asia, Hdt.:—Mid. to carry up to a place of safety, take with one, Id.
to bring up, pour forth, tears, Aesch.:—Mid., ἀνενείκασθαι, absol. to fetch up a deep-drawn breath, heave a deep sigh, Il., Hdt.:—c. acc. rei, to utter, ἀνενείκατο φωνάν, μῦθον Theocr.
to uphold, take upon one, ἄχθος Aesch.; κινδύνους Thuc.
to offer, contribute, εἰς τὸ κοινόν Dem.:— to offer in sacrifice, NTest.
intr. to lead up, of a road, Xen.
to bring or carry back, Eur., etc.; ἀν. τὰς κώπας to recover the oars, at the end of the stroke, Thuc.
to bring back tidings, report, Hdt., etc.
to bring back from exile, Thuc.
to carry back, trace up one's family to an ancestor, Plat.

to refer a matter to another, Hdt., etc.: to ascribe, Eur., etc.:—without acc., ἀν. εἴς τινα to appeal to another, make reference to him, Hdt., Plat.:—of things, ἀν. εἴς τι to have reference to a thing, Plat.
to bring back, restore, recover, Thuc.:—Pass. to recover oneself, come to oneself, Hdt.:—so also intr. in Act. to come to oneself, recover, Id., etc.
to return, yield, as revenue, Xen.
to recall a likeness, Plut.
to flee up, Xen.
to escape, Id.
of a report, to disappear gradually, Plut.
not to be touched, impalpable, Plat.
Dep. to call out aloud, Plut.
Pass. to be undone, κατὰ τί δεῦρ’ ἀνεφθάρης; by what ill luck came you hither? Ar.
to inflame and swell up, Plut.
to light up, rekindle, Eur.: metaph., ἀν. ἔρωτα Plut.:—Pass. to be inflamed, excited, Anth.
a lighting up, Plut.
to bubble or boil up, Il.
to frighten away, Ar.
a carrying back, reference, Theophr., Plut.
recourse to another [in difficulty], Dem.
a means of repairing a fault or loss, a means of recovery, Eur., Plut.

entry.etym: Frequent. of ἀναφέρω Ι, Hdt., Thuc.

entry.sense: a pole or yoke for carrying things, Ar.
Mid. to be ware of a thing, perceive, Od.
without the favour of Venus, Plut., Luc.
Lat. invenustus, without charms, Plut.
to come back to one's senses, Xen.
c. inf., to meditate how to do a thing, Pind.
escape from a thing, c. gen., Aesch.
a retreat, Plut.
to mix up, confound:— Pass., ἦν πάντα ἀναπεφυρμένα Hdt.
to defile, αἵματι ἀναπεφυρμένος Id.
to blow up or forth, eject, of volcanoes, Plat.
metaph. in Pass. to be puffed up, Xen.
to blow upwards, of a dolphin, Hes.
to produce again, to let grow, πώγωνα Theocr.
Pass., with aor2 act. ἀν-έφυν, pf. ἀμ-πέφῡκα, to grow up, Hdt., etc.
to grow again, of the hair, Id.
to call aloud, declaim, Plut.
a proclamation, Plut.
an outcry, ejaculation, Plut.
to make to recoil, force back, only 3rd pl. poet. aor1 ἀνέχασσαν, Pind.
Mid: to draw back, retire, Hom.; ἐπὶ πόδα ἀναχάζεσθαι to retire slowly, of soldiers, Xen. (who also uses Act. in same sense).
of a horse, to throw back the mane, rear up, Eur.: metaph. of men, to become restive, Plut.
c. acc. to rear up and throw the rider, Eur.:—metaph. to upset, Id., Dem.
c. gen., ἀν. τῶν πραγμάτων to shake off the yoke of business, Plut.

entry.etym: only in pres. and imperf., the other tenses being formed from *ἀναχαίνω
entry.sense: to open the mouth, gape wide, Ar., Luc.
to pour forth.
Pass. to get the first down (χνόος), Ar.
to begin a choral dance, ἀν. θίασον Eur.
to celebrate in the chorus, Βάκχιον Id.
οὐκ ἄν με ἀνεχόρευ’ Ἐρινύσι would not scare me away by a band of Furies, Id.
intr. to dance for joy, Id.
effusion: metaph. excess, NTest.
to fuse again, Strab.
to heap up into a mound, Anth.
to go back, Hom.: esp. to retire or withdraw from battle, Hom., Hdt., attic
to retire from a place, c. gen., Od.
to come back or revert to the rightful owner, ἐς τὸν παῖδα Hdt.
. to withdraw from the world, Ar., Plat.
a drawing back, retiring, retreating, Hdt., Thuc.
a means or place of retreat, refuge, Thuc.
one must withdraw, retreat, Plat.
to make to go back or retire, Xen.
to wipe up:— Mid. to wipe up for oneself, Plut.
to put to the vote again, Thuc.
a cooling, refreshing: relief, recovery, respite, Plat.: from a thing, c. gen., Eur.
to cool, to revive by fresh air, to refresh, Hom., Eur.:—Pass. to be revived, refreshed, Il.
ναῦς ἀν. to let the ships rest and get dry, relieve them, Hdt., Xen.; so, ἀν. τὸν ἱδρῶτα to let it dry off, Plut.
metaph. c. gen., ἀν. πόνων τινα to give him relief from toil, Eur.
intr. in Act. to recover oneself, revive, Anth., Babr.
to please, delight, gratify, c. dat. pers., Hom., etc.:—absol., ἑᾱδότα μῦθον a pleasing speech, Id.
ἁνδάνει, Lat. placet, expressing opinion, οὔ σφι ἥνδανε ταῦτα Hdt.; c. inf., τοῖσι μὲν ἕαδε βοηθέειν it was their pleasure to assist, Id.:—impers., ἐπεί νύ τοι εὔαδεν οὕτως (sc. ποιεῖν) Hom.
a raised border, flower-bed, Theocr., Anth.:— any raised bank, a dyke, Mosch.
asunder, in twain, Il.
= ἀνδραγαθίζομαι:— Pass., ἠνδραγαθημένα = brave deeds, Plut.
a brave deed, Plut.
bravery, manly virtue, the character of a brave honest man, Hdt., Ar.
Dep. to act bravely, honestly, play the honest man, Thuc.
the spoils of a slain enemy, Il.
man by man, = κατ’ ἄνδρα, Od.

entry.etym: the middle future form ἀνδραποδιεῦμαι is used in a passive sense.
entry.sense: to reduce to slavery, enslave, esp. to sell the free men of a conquered place into slavery, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—Pass. to be sold into slavery, Hdt., Xen., etc.:—the Mid. was also used in act. sense, Hdt.
a selling free men into slavery, enslaving, Thuc., etc.
a slave-dealer, kidnapper, Ar., Plat.; ἀνδρ. ἑαυτοῦ one who sells his own independence, Xen.
a slave-dealer, Luc.
one taken in war and sold as a slave, a captive, Il., Hdt., attic
generally, a slave, a slavish low fellow, Plat., Xen.
slavish, servile, abject, Plat., Xen. adv. -δῶς, Plat.
a manikin, Ar.
loading a man, as much as a man can carry, Od.
the public meals of the Cretans, also the older name for the Spartan φειδίτια, Alcman, Plut.
manliness, manhood, manly spirit, Lat. virtus, Trag., etc.
an image of a man, Plat.
a flesh-coloured pigment, Id.
like a man, Plut.
of or for a man, Aesch., etc.; for αὐλοὶ ἀνδρεῖοι, v. αὐλός.
manly, masculine, Hdt., attic; in bad sense, stubborn, Luc.:—neut. τὸ ἀνδρεῖον, by crasis τἀνδρεῖον, = ἀνδρεία, Eur., Thuc.
of things, strong, vigorous, Ar.
= ἀνδρεία, Xen.
man-slaying, Il.
to banish from house and home, Aesch., Soph.
he that drives one from home, the avenger of blood, Aesch.
a puppet, Plut.
to make statues, Xen.
the sculptor's art, statuary, Plat., Xen.
a statue-maker, statuary, sculptor, Pind., Plat.
the image of a man, a statue, Hdt., attic
to make a man of: Pass. or Mid. to come to manhood, behave like a man, play the man, Plat.
of or for a man, masculine, manly, Lat. virilis, Plat.; ἀνδρ. ἱδρώς the sweat of manly toil, Ar.:—adv. -κῶς, like a man, comp. -ώτερον, Sup. -ώτατα, Id.
composed of men, χορός Xen.
a manikin, Ar., Theocr.
one must play the man, Plat.
like a man, like men, Ar., Theocr.
man-devouring, Anth.
of manly counsel, man-minded, Aesch.
man-eating, Eur.
begetting males, Hes.
a man-woman, hermaphrodite, Plat.
a womanish man, effeminate person, Hdt.
as adj. common to men and women, Anth.
man-slaying, Aesch.
man-taming, Pind.
the man-goddess, i. e. Athena, Anth.
from a man or men, Anth.
murderous, Aesch.
man-wearying, Aesch.: man-slaying, Id.
wrought by men's hands, Il.
slaughter of men in battle, Il., Aesch.
to slay men, Aesch.
man-slaying, murdering, Hdt., Eur.
a murderess, Aesch.
seizure of men guilty of murdering a citizen abroad, Lex. ap. Dem.
fighting with men, Anth.; fem. ἀνδρομάχη Id.
of man or men, human, κρέα Hom.; ψωμοὶ ἀνδρ. goblets of man's flesh, Od.
of a man's height, Xen.
a man-boy, i. e. a youth near manhood, Aesch.
a multitude of men, Aesch.
hurtful to men, Anth.
a slaughter-house of men, Aesch.
a man-sphinx, sphinx with the bust of a man, not (as usually) of a woman, Hdt.
manliness, manhood, courage, = ἀνδρεία: cf. ἁδροτής.
getting a husband, ἀνδρ. βίοτος wedded life, Aesch.
to eat men, Hdt.
eating men, Od., Hdt.
ἀνδρόφθορον αἷμα the blood of a slain man, Id.
man-destroying, murderous, Soph.
slaughter of men, Arist., Plut.
man-slaying, Il.
of women, murdering husbands, Pind.
as law-term, one convicted of manslaughter, a homicide, Plat., Dem.
to rear up into manhood, Anth.: —Pass. to become a man, reach manhood, Hdt., Eur.
in Pass. also of a woman, to be of marriageable age, Eur.
like a man, manly, Isocr. adv., -δῶς, Sup. -δέστατα, Xen.
the men's apartment in a house, the banqueting hall, etc., Hdt., Aesch., etc.; ionic ἀνδρεών, Hdt.; epic -ειών, Anth.:—also ἀνδρωνῖτις, ιδος, ἡ Xen.
clashed or rung loudly, of armour, Il.; creaked or grated loudly, of a door, Od.
not accredited, Plat.; of a woman, unwedded, Plut.
to wake up, rouse, ἐξ ὕπνου, ἐκ λεχέων Hom.:—Pass., Eur., Xen.
metaph. to wake up, raise, Pind.
metaph. also to rouse, encourage, Od.
of buildings, to raise, Anth.
wakeful, Anth.
not accused, without reproach, void of offence, Xen., etc.:—adv. -τως, Dem.
let loose, freely, without restraint, Plat., Dem.:— remissly, carelessly, Soph.
without more ado, absolutely, Plat.
unwished for, unwelcome, Hdt.
without the aid of Eileithuia, Eur.
to roll up together:— Pass. to crowd or throng together, Thuc.
ἀνείλω, Pass. to shrink up or back, Plat.

entry.etym: part. perf. pass. of ἀνίημι, used as adj.
entry.sense: let go free, released from labour, of animals dedicated to the gods, Soph.: metaph., ἀν. ἔς τι devoted to a thing, Hdt.
remiss, slack, unconstrained, Thuc.; ἐν τῶι ἀνειμένωι τῆς γνώμης when their minds are unstrung, Id.:—adv. ἀνειμένως, at ease, carelessly, without restraint, Thuc., Xen.

entry.etym: εῖμι, ibo, in attic serving as fut. to ἀνέρχομαι.
entry.sense: to go up, Hom., etc.; ἅμ’ ἠελίωι ἀνιόντι at sun- rise, Il.
to sail up, i. e. out to sea, Od.
to go up inland, esp. into Central Asia, Plat.
to approach, esp. as a suppliant, Il.
to go back, go home, return, Od., Hdt., etc.
without clothing, unclad, Od.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use, ἀναγορεύω being used instead.
entry.sense: to say aloud, announce, proclaim, Pind., Xen.: —c. acc. et inf. to make proclamation that . . , Ar., Thuc.:—in the Athen. assemblies, ἀνεῖπεν ὁ κῆρυξ Thuc., etc.:—Pass. to be proclaimed, ἀναρρηθέντος τοῦ στεφάνου when the crown was proclaimed, Dem.
to call upon, invoke, Plut.
to keep back, restrain, Hom., Xen.
to fasten on or to, to string, Hdt.; ἀν. στεφάνους to twine or wreathe them, Ar.
without entrance or access, Plut.
exemption from the εἰσφορά, Plut.
exempt from the εἰσφορά, Plut.
adv. of Place, from above, Hdt., Aesch.
of Time, from the first, by origin, Hdt.; so with Art., τὸ ἀνέκαθεν Id.
upwards, Lat. sursum, Pind., attic
without outlet, Thuc.
ineffable, NTest.
not given in marriage, Dem., etc.
inevitable, Anth.
unspeakable, NTest.
to fill up or again, Xen.
undaunted, intrepid, Plat.:— τὸ ἀνέκπληκτον intrepidity, Xen.
to be borne, Soph.
bearable, sufferable, tolerable, mostly with a negat., Il., attic
without a negat. that can be endured, Od., Thuc.
adv. -τως, Hom.; οὐκ ἀνεκτῶς ἔχει it is not to be borne, Xen.
not cross-questioned, safe from being questioned, Thuc.: unconvicted, Id.
not refuted, irrefutable, Plat.:—adv. -τως, without refutation, Plut.
to convince or convict utterly, Eur.
merciless, without mercy, NTest.
unmerciful, NTest.
illiberality, Plat.
not fit for a free man, Aesch., Arist.
illiberal, servile, Plat., etc.
in money matters, niggardly, stingy, Ar.
adv. -ρως, meanly, Xen.
anything rolled up, a ringlet, Anth.
an unfolding, Plut.
to unroll a book written on a roll, i. e. to unfold, read, interpret, Xen.; ἀν. βίον to pass one's whole life, Plut.
to cause to move backward, πόδα Eur.
to cause to revolve:— Pass. to revolve, move glibly, Ar.
to draw up, τάλαντα ἀνέλκει holds them up (in weighing), Il.; ἀνελκύσαι ναῦς to haul them up high and dry, Hdt., Thuc.
to drag up, drag into open court or into the witness-box, Ar.:— Mid., ἀνέλκεσθαι τρίχας to tear one's own hair, Il.
to draw a bow, in act to shoot, Hom.:—Mid., ἔγχος ἀνελκόμενος drawing back his spear [out of the corpse], Od.
without hope, hopeless, Eur.
unhoped for, unlooked for, Trag., etc.; τὸ ἀνέλπιστον τοῦ βεβαίου the hopelessness of security, Thuc.
act.,
of persons, having no hope, hopeless, Theocr.; c. inf. having no hope or not expecting that . . , Thuc.
of things or conditions, leaving no hope, hopeless, desperate, Soph., Thuc.; τὸ ἀνέλπιστον despair, Thuc.:—comp. -ότερος more desperate, Id.
inaccessible, Babr., Plut.
act. not going to or visiting, Anth.
free from blame, without offence, Plat.
not distributed, Dem.
act. having no share, Plut.
Pass. to be driven with the wind, NTest.
running with the wind, Luc.
to go through, c. acc., Eur.
sheltering from the wind, Il.

wind, Hom., etc.; ἀνέμου κατιόντος a squall having come on, Thuc.; ἄν. κατὰ βορέαν ἑστηκώς the wind being settled in the north, Id.; ἀνέμοις φέρεσθαι παραδοῦναί τι to cast a thing to the winds, Lat. ventis tradere, Eur.:—Hom. and Hes. mention only four winds, Boreas, Eurus, Notus (or Argestes), Zephyrus; Arist. gives twelve, which served as points of the compass.
echoing to the wind, Pind.
fed by the wind, of a wave, Il.; ἔγχος ἀνεμ. a spear from a tree reared by the wind, i. e. made tough by battling with the wind, Id.
to expose to the wind:— Pass., of the sea, to be raised by the wind, Anth.
intrepid: in adv. -τως, Plut.
unembarrassed, Arist.
swift as the wind, Eur., Ar.

windy: metaph., ἀνεμώλια βάζειν to talk words of wind, Hom.; οἱ δ’ αὖτ’ ἀνεμώλιοι are like the winds, i. e. good for naught, Il.; τί νυ τόξον ἔχεις ἀνεμώλιον; why bear thy bow in vain? Id.; ἀνεμώλιος empty fool! Anth.
the wind-flower, anemone, Bion.
in want of naught, Anth.
impossible, NTest.
indubitable, Luc.
indelible, Isocr., Plut.
unquestioned, impossible to be questioned or refuted, of statements or arguments, Thuc.; ἀν. ἔχει τὸ ἀνδρεῖον leaves their courage without proof, Id.
of persons, not to be convicted, irreproachable, Xen., etc.
unfinished, Luc.
not inquired into or examined, Dem.
uninquiring, Plat.
not to be found out, Thuc.
enduring evil, forbearing, long-suffering, NTest., Luc.
not to be traced, unsearchable, inscrutable, NTest.
with no outlet, allowing no return, Lat. irremeabilis, Theocr.
without festival, c. gen., ἀν. ἱερῶν without share in festal rites, Eur.
unperceived, imperceptible, Plut., Luc.
having no cause for shame, NTest.
untouched, ἀν. παρέχειν τι rem integram praestare, Dem.
not burdensome, without offence, Plut., Luc.:—adv. -θῶς, Thuc.
without plots, τὸ ἀνεπιβούλευτον the absence of intrigue, Thuc.
without title or inscription: metaph. without noticeable features, Luc.
not disputed by legal process, undisputed, Dem.
unfairness, unkindness, Dem.
unreasonable, unfair, Thuc.
unaccused, unblamed, Xen.
without preferring any charge:— adv. -τως, Thuc.
not open to attack, not censured, blameless, Eur., Thuc.: adv. -τως, Xen.
not mixing with others, unsocial, Plut.
not polished or finished, Hes.
without connexion with others, isolated, Strab.
not dedicated.
inattentive, inconsiderate: adv. -τως, Hdt.
pass. not examined, unregarded, Xen.
want of knowledge, ignorance, unskilfulness, Thuc.
not knowing, ignorant, unskilful, Hdt., Thuc.; ναῦς ἀνεπιστήμονες ships with unskilful crews, Thuc.;—c. gen. rei, unskilled in a thing, Plat.; c. inf. not knowing how to do a thing, Xen.
without knowledge, unintelligent: comp. ἀνεπιστημονέστερος less intelligent, Hdt.
subject to no control, Thuc.
unserviceable, unfit, Xen., Plat., etc.:— mischievous, prejudicial, hurtful, Hdt., Thuc.
unkind, unfriendly, Thuc., Xen.
made without care or design, simple, artless, Luc.
unpractised, untried, Plut.
not to be censured, τινος for a thing, Dem.
without reproach, Soph.; ἀν. ἐστι πᾶσιν ’tis no reproach to any one, Thuc.; ἀνεπιφθονώτατον least invidious, Dem. adv. -νως so as not to create odium, Thuc.
to love again, love anew, c. gen., Andoc., Xen.
not loved, Luc.
act. not loving, Anth.
unwrought, untilled, Luc.
not done, Eur.
to stir up, excite, Plut.:—Pass. to be in a state of excitement, Thuc., Xen.
Dep., only used in aor1, to snatch up and carry off, ἀνηρείψαντο Hom.; ἀνερειψαμένη Hes.
to examine closely, investigate, Plat.
not investigated, Plat.
that cannot be found out, inscrutable, Eur.
c. acc. pers. to enquire of, question, Od., Soph.
c. acc. rei, to ask about, Od., Plat.
c. dupl. acc. to ask a person about a thing, Il., Soph.
to creep up or upwards, Ar., Luc.
to go quite away: ἄνερρε away with you, Lat. abi in malam rem, Eur.
to begin to blush, blush up, Xen.
to draw up, haul up sails, Od.: to haul ships up on land, Hdt.: —Mid. to deliver, Anth.
to go up, Od., attic: absol. to mount the tribune, Plut.:— to go up from the coast inland, Od.:— to come up from the nether world, Theogn., Soph.
of trees, to grow up, shoot up, Od.: of the sun, to rise, Aesch.:—metaph., ὄλβος ἀν. Eur.
to go or come back, go or come home again, return, Hom.
to come back to a point, recur, Eur., Plat.
νόμος εἴς σ’ ἀνελθών a law brought home or having relation to you, Eur.
c. acc. pers. to ask or inquire of, question, Od., Plat.
c. acc. rei, to ask about, inquire into, Plat.; so, ἀν. περί τινος Hdt.
c. dupl. acc. to question a person about a thing, ask it of him, Eur., Ar.
a loosening, relaxing of strings, Plat., etc.
metaph. remission, abatement, κακῶν Hdt.; ἄν. φόρων, τελῶν remission of tribute, taxes, Plut.
relaxation, recreation, Plat., Arist.
a letting loose, indulgence, license, Plat., Arist.
without hearth and home, homeless, Il., Ar.
to examine closely, NTest.
one must dismiss, Plat.
relaxed, slack, loose, Luc.
prep. c. gen., without, Hom.
away from, Il.
adv. far away, distant, Hom.
inconvenient, NTest.
not having to render an account, irresponsible, Hdt., Thuc.
guiltless, because such a one is not liable to trial, Luc.; c. gen. guiltless of . . , Id.
not wishing, not praying, Anth.
prep. c. gen. without, οὐκ ἄνευ θεῶν, Lat. non sine Diis, not without divine aid, Od.; ἄνευ ἐμέθεν without my knowledge, Il.; ἄνευ πολιτῶν without their consent, Aesch.
away from, far from, ἄνευ δηΐων Il.
in Prose, except, besides, like χωρίς, Xen.
a discovery, Eur., Plut.
to find out, make out, discover, Hdt., attic: —Pass. to be found out or discovered, Thuc.; c. part. to be discovered to be . . , Hdt.
to shout εὐφήμει or εὐφημεῖτε: as this was mainly done on sorrowful occasions, to cry aloud, shriek, Eur., etc.; ἀνευφήμησεν οἰμωγῆι Soph.
unclouded, cloudless, Od.: metaph. not to be veiled or concealed, Soph.
not giving surety or confidence, Thuc.
trans. to hold up one's hands in fight, Od.; also in token of defeat, Theocr.:— to lift up the hands in prayer, Il., etc.
ἀν. φλόγα to hold up a torch at weddings, Eur.; hence ἄνεχε, πάρεχε (sc. τὸ φῶς), i. e. make ready, go on, Id.; also, ἀν. φῶς σωτήριον to hold up a signal fire, Thuc.
to lift up, exalt, τινά Pind.
metaph. to uphold, maintain, Od., Thuc.; ἀνέχων λέκτρα remaining constant to the bed, Eur.; so, ἀν. κισσόν Soph.
to put forth, πτόρθους Eur.
to hold back, Il.; ἀν. Σικελίαν μὴ ὑπό τινα εἶναι to keep it from being subject, Thuc.
intr. to rise up, rise, emerge from water, Od., Hdt.:—esp. in form ἀνίσχω, of the sun, Hdt., Xen.
of events, to arise, happen, Hdt.
to appear, shew oneself, Soph.
to project, Il.; of a headland, to jut out, Hdt., Thuc.
to hold on, keep doing, c. part., Thuc.; στέρξας ἀνέχει is constant in his love, Soph.; c. acc. et inf. to aver constantly that . . , Id.
to hold up, cease, Theogn.:—generally, to wait, delay, Thuc.
c. gen. to cease from suffering, get rest from pain, Soph.
Mid. to hold up what is one's own, ἔγχος, χεῖρας Il.; hence ἀνασχόμενος absol. (sub. ἔγχος etc.), Id.
to hold oneself up, bear up, hold out, Il.; aor2 imperat. ἀνάσχεο, epic ἄνσχεο, be of good courage, Id.:—in part., ἀνεχόμενοι with patience, Hdt.
c. acc. to bear up against, Il., Hdt., attic:— so, c. gen., Od., Plat.
the dependent clause is added in part., οὔ σε ἀνέξομαι ἄλγε’ ἔχοντα I will not suffer thee to have . . , Il., etc.; οὐ σῖγ’ ἀνέχει (sc. ὤν); Soph.
c. inf. to suffer, Aesch.
a first-cousin's son, or second cousin, Dem.

entry.etym: From α euphon. or α copul. , and ΝΕΠ, whence also Lat. nepos, neptis.
entry.sense: a first-cousin, cousin, Il., Hdt., attic
a nephew, Hdt.
entry.etym: When the ult. is long, Hom. lengthens also the penult., ἀνεψῑοῦ κταμένοιο.

entry.sense: without a sound, in silence, in Od. certainly an Adv.; in other places it may be nom. pl. ἄνεωι, from ἄν-εως = ἄν-αυος
to grow young again, Theogn., Eur., etc.
returning as in youth, Eur.
not yet come to man's estate, beardless, Plat., Theocr.
without leader, Luc.
Dep. to tell as in a narrative, relate, recount, Pind., Hdt.
intr. to advance, Pind.
not sweetened or seasoned, Arist.: unpleasant, Plut.
made of anise or dill, Theocr.
anise, dill, Ar., Theocr.; ionic ἄννησον or ἄνησον Hdt.; aeolic ἄννητον, or ἄνητον, Sapph..
not to be healed, incurable, irreparable, fatal, Il., Hdt., attic; ἀνήκεστα ποιεῖν τινα to do one irreparable injuries, Xen.; ἀνήκεστα πάσχειν Thuc.
of persons, implacable, Xen.
act. damaging beyond remedy, deadly, Soph.:—adv., ἀνηκέστως διατιθέναι to treat with barbarous cruelty, Hdt.
without hearing, of the dead, Mosch.
c. gen. not hearing a thing, never having heard it, ignorant of it, Xen., etc.:—absol., σκαιὸς καὶ ἀν. ignorant, Dem.
to be unwilling to hear, to disobey, c. gen., Il., Aesch., Thuc.; c. dat., Hdt.; absol., Id.
unheard of, Lat. inauditus, ἤκους’ ἀνήκουστα Soph.
act. not willing to hear: τὸ ἀνήκουστον disobedience, Xen.
to have come up to a point, reach up to, of persons, αἱμασιὴν ἀνήκουσαν ἀνδρὶ ἐς τὸν ὀμφαλόν a wall reaching up to a man's middle, Hdt.; ἀν. ἐς τὰ μέγιστα to reach up to the highest point, Id.

of things, τοῦτο ἐς οὐδὲν ἀν. amounts to nothing, Id.; αἱ πολλαὶ [ζημίαι] ἐς τὸν θάνατον ἀν. have gone as far as death, Thuc.; ἀν. ἔς σε ἔχειν it has come to you to have, has become yours to have, Hdt.
to appertain, be fit or proper, NTest.; τὸ ἀνῆκον what is fit and proper, Id.
without pity, unmerciful:— adv. -εῶς, Andoc.
without sun, sunless, Trag.
unshod, barefoot, Theocr.
unmilked, Od.
not tame, wild, savage, of persons and countries, Aesch.
= νηνεμία, Anth.
without wind, ἀνήνεμος χειμώνων without the blast of storms, Soph.

entry.etym: Formed as if from *ἀνέθω (ἀνά) to rise up; cf. ἐνήνοθε.
entry.sense: αἷμα ἀνήνοθεν ἐξ ὠτειλῆς blood gushed forth from the wound, Il.; κνίση ἀνήνοθεν the savour mounted up, Od.
ineffectual, Od.
= ἀνήνυστος, Soph., Plat.
endless, Plat.
unmanly, Od., Hes.
to cry aloud, roar, Mosch.
fulfilment, Aesch.
unploughed, untilled, Od., Aesch.
a man, Lat. vir (not homo):
a man, opp. to a woman, Hom., etc.
a man, opp. to a god, πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε Id.
a man, opp. to a youth, a man in the prime of life, Id., etc.; εἰς ἄνδρας ἐγγράφεσθαι to be enrolled among the men, Dem.
a man emphatically, a man indeed, ἀνέρες ἔστε, φίλοι Il.; πολλοὶ μὲν ἄνθρωποι, ὀλίγοι δὲ ἄνδρες many human beings, but few men, Hdt.
a man, opp. to his wife, a husband, Hom., etc.; αἰγῶν ἄνερ, Virgil's vir gregis, Theocr.
without real fire, πῦρ ἀνήφαιστον, i. e. the fire of discord, Eur.
Dep.:— to choose one person or thing instead of another, τινά (or τί) τινος Eur.; to prefer, choose rather, Id.
to dispute, lay claim to, τι Id.
Pass. to be captured in turn, ἁλόντες αὖθις ἀνθαλοῖεν ἄν Aesch.
Dep. to vie one with another, to race one another, Xen.
vying with, rivalling, Eur.
Dep. to lay hold of in turn, c. gen., Hdt., Eur.
simply to lay hold of, grapple with, engage in, c. gen., Hdt., Thuc.: generally, to reach, attain, τερμόνων Eur.
to lay hold of, attack, πλευμόνων, φρενῶν, Soph., Eur.
a flower, blossom, Ar.
one must cleave to, c. gen., Plat.; so in pl. ἀνθεκτέα, Thuc.
to draw or pull against, Thuc.; ἀνθ. ἀλλήλαις to pull against one another, Plat.
ἀνθέμιον ἐστιγμένος tattooed with flowers, Xen.
flowery, of meadows, Il.
of works in metal, bright, burnished, or wrought with flowers, Hom.; of tapestry, flowered, Anth.
ἄνθεμα χρυσοῦ, i. e. the costliest gold, Pind.
flowing from flowers, of honey, Eur.
working in flowers, of bees, Aesch.
flowery, blooming, Aesch., Eur.
the chin or part on which the beard grew, Lat. mentum, Il.
the beard of an ear of corn, the ear itself, Lat. spica, Il.
= the stalk of asphodel, Hdt., Theocr.
the feast of flowers, i.e. the three days' festival of Dionysus at Athens, in the month Anthesterion.
the month Anthesterion, eighth of the Attic year, answering to the end of February and the beginning of March.
to entertain in return or mutually, Plut.
bearing flowers, flowering, Eur.
to blossom, bloom, of the youthful beard, Od.; of flowers and plants, Hes., etc.
metaph.,
to be bright with colour, ἀνθεῖν φοινικίσι Xen.
to be in bloom, Pind.; ἐν ὥραι, ἐφ’ ὥραι ἀνθεῖν to be in the bloom of youth, Plat.
to flourish in wealth and prosperity, Hes., Hdt., attic; c. dat., ἀνθ. ἀνδράσι to abound in men, Hdt.
to be at the height or pitch, Aesch., Soph.
full bloom, Plat.
flowering, blooming, Ar.
metaph. blooming, fresh, Eur., Xen.
ἀνθηρὸν μένος rage bursting into flower, i. e. at its height, Soph.
bright-coloured, bright, Eur.; τὸ ἀνθ. brightness, Luc.
Pass. to give way in turn, τινί Thuc.
to strew or deck with flowers, Eur.
to dye with bright colour: Pass., Hdt.; metaph., ἠνθισμένος dyed, disguised, Soph.
like flowers, blooming, fresh, ἄνθινον εἶδαρ, of the lotus, Od.
bright-coloured, Lat. floridus, of women's dress, Plut.
a sham-fight of horse, Xen.
to ride against, ἀλλήλοις Xen.
to set against, Ar., Thuc.: to set up in opposition, Thuc.
to match with, compare, Plut.

Pass., with intr. aor2 act. ἀντέστην, perf. ἀνθέστηκα, attic contr. part. ἀνθεστώς: fut. mid. ἀντιστήσομαι, aor1 ἀντεστησάμην and pass. ἀντεστάθην [α]:— to stand against, esp. in battle, to withstand, oppose, τινι Il., Hdt., attic; also, πρός τινα Thuc., etc.: rarely c. gen., φρενῶν ἀνθίσταται (al. ἀνθάπτεται) Aesch.
absol. to make a stand, Il., Hdt.
to bestrew with flowers, Anth.:— Pass. to have flowers showered upon one, Plut.
garlanded with flowers, Anth.
living on flowers, Anth.
holding flowers, Mosch.
to produce flowers, Anth.
decked with flowers, flowery, Anth.
to govern flowers, Luc.
worked with flowers or brightcoloured, Eur.
a pulling in the contrary direction, resistance, Plut.
a flower-gathering, Luc.: Ἀνθολογίαι were collections of small Greek poems and epigrams by several authors, which the editor made up into a posy or nosegay.
flower-gathering, Anth.; c. gen. culling the flower of . . , Id.
Mid. to make a mutual agreement, πρός τινα Dem.
to confess freely and openly, Plut.
to return thanks, NTest.
to arm against: Pass. to be arrayed against, τινί Eur.:—Mid. to arm oneself, Xen.
to lie at anchor opposite to, τινί Thuc.; πρός τινα Id.
redolent of flowers, of wine, οἶνος ἀνθ. with a fine "bouquet", Ar.; so ἀνθοσμίας alone, Xen., Luc.

entry.etym: note that ἀνθέων shows up even in Attic.
entry.sense: a blossom, flower, Hom., etc.
generally, anything thrown out upon the surface, froth, scum.

metaph. the bloom or flower of life, ἥβης ἄνθος Il.; ὥρας ἄνθος Xen.; χροιᾶς ἄνθος the bloom of complexion, Aesch.:—also, the flower of an army and the like, Aesch., Thuc.; τὸ σὸν ἄνθος thy pride or honour, Aesch.
the height or highest pitch of anything, bad as well as good, ἔρωτος Id.; μανίας Soph.
brightness, brilliancy, Theogn.; in pl. bright colours, Plat.; ἁλὸς ἄνθεα, i.e. purple, Anth.
bloom, luxuriant growth, Anth.
to bear flowers, Anth.
bearing flowers, flowery, Ar., Anth.
party-coloured, Anth.
a heap of charcoal, hot embers, Il.; ἀνθρακιᾶς ἄπο hot from the embers, Eur.
black sooty ashes, Anth.
a man black as a collier, Luc.
to make charcoal of, to roast or toast, Ar.
Pass. ἀνθρακόομαι, to be burnt to cinders, Aesch.
charcoal, coal, Ar., Thuc.
a hornet, wasp, Ar.
a wasp's nest, Ar.
a man-pleaser, NTest.
Dim. of ἄνθρωπος, a manikin, Ar.
a man's skin, Hdt.

of or belonging to man, human, Hdt., etc.; ἀνθρώπεια πήματα such as man is subject to, Aesch.; ἀνθρωπήϊα πρήγματα human affairs, man's estate, Hdt.; τὸ ἀνθρώπειον either mankind or human nature, Thuc.
human, of which man is capable, Hdt., Plat.
human, as opp. to mythical, Hdt.
adv. -ως, humanly, in all human probability, Thuc.; ἀνθρ. φράζειν to speak as befits a man, Ar.
Dep. to be or act as a human being, Arist.
to be or act like a man, Luc.
of or for a man, human, Plat. adv. -κῶς, Luc.
of, from or belonging to man, human, Hdt., etc.; ἅπαν τὸ ἀνθρώπινον all mankind, Id.; τὸ ἀνθρ. γένος Plat.; τὰ ἀνθρ. πράγματα or τἀνθρώπινα human affairs, man's estate, Id.
human, suited to man, Id., Arist.
adv., ἀνθρωπίνως ἁμαρτάνειν to commit human, i. e. venial, errors, Thuc.
humanely, gently, Dem.
Dim. of ἄνθρωπος, a manikin, Lat. homuncio, Eur., Xen.: a paltry fellow, Xen.
a man-god, i. e. a deified man, Eur.
like a man, in human form, Hdt.
a human sacrifice, Strab.
murdering men, a homicide, Eur.
furnished by slaughtered men, Eur.
speaking of man, Arist.
a making of man or men, Luc.
making men, Luc.
man, Lat. homo (not vir), opp. to gods, ἀθανάτων τε θεῶν, χαμαὶ ἐρχομένων τ’ ἀνθρώπων Il.
with or without the Art. to denote man generally, Plat., etc.
in pl. mankind, ἀνθρώπων, ἀνδρῶν ἠδὲ γυναικῶν Il.; ὁ ἄριστος ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὄρτυξ the best quail in the world, Plat.; μάλιστα, ἥκιστα ἀνθρώπων most, least of all, Hdt., etc.

with another Subst., to give it a contemptuous sense, ἄνθρ. ὑπογραμματεύς, συκοφάντης, Oratt.; so homo histrio Cic.:—so, ἄνθρωπος or ὁ ἄνθρωπος was used alone, the man, the fellow, Plat.:— also in vocat. it was addressed contemptuously to slaves, ἄνθρωπε or ὦ ’νθρωπε, sirrah! you sir! Hdt., Plat.
fem. (as homo also is fem.), a woman, Hdt., etc.; with a sense of pity, Dem.
to slay men, Eur.
to eat men or man's flesh, Hdt.
an eating of men, Arist.
man eating, Arist.
of man's nature, Hdt.
to abuse one another, abuse in turn, Eur., Plut.
to bring to trial in turn, Thuc.
to be proconsul, Plut.
proconsular.
a proconsul, Lat. pro consule, Polyb., etc.
to yield in turn, τινί Plut.
a mutual yielding, Plut.
to serve in turn, τινί Arist.
Mid.
to answer in return, Hdt.
to put on in turn, ὀργήν Luc.
Mid. to make a counter-affidavit, Dem.
to suspect mutually:— Pass., ἀνθυποπτεύεται he is met by the suspicion that . . , Thuc.
to return a kindness, τινί τι Hdt., Eur.
to undertake to serve as choragus instead of another, Dem.
to grieve, distress, c. acc. pers., Hom.
intr. to be grieved or distressed, feel grief, Id.; c. dat. at or for a thing, Il.
Dep. to cure again, repair, Hdt.

entry.etym: In Hom. and Soph. ῑ: in other Poets ι or ῑ.
entry.sense: grief, sorrow, distress, trouble, Od., Hes., etc.
actively, δαιτὸς ἀνίη the bane of our feast, Od.
a rein.

entry.etym: In Hom and Soph. always ανῑ-, in other Poets ανι-.
entry.sense: grievous, troublesome, annoying, of persons, Od.; ἐχθροῖς ἀνιαροί Ar., of animals, Hdt.:—adv. ἀνιαρῶς Soph.
of things,
painful, grievous, distressing, Theogn., etc.; irreg. comp. ἀνιηρέστερος Od.
pass. grieved, distressed, Xen.:—adv. -ρῶς wretchedly, Id.
incurable, Plat., etc.
of persons, incorrigible, Id.; ἀνιάτως ἔχειν to be incurable, Id.
to cry aloud: c. acc. to praise loudly, Anth.

entry.etym: ῑ in Hom. and Soph., ι or ῑ in other Poets.
entry.sense: Like ἀνιάζω, to grieve, distress, c. acc., Od., etc.; c. dupl. acc., ὁ δρῶν σ’ ἀνιᾶι τὰς φρένας Soph.:—Pass. to be grieved, distressed, Od., etc.; with neut. adj., τοῦτ’ ἀνιῶμαι I am vexed at this, Soph.; aor1 part. as adj., a sorrowful man, Hom.
without sweat: metaph. without toil, Il.: lazily, slowly, Xen.
without having sweated or exercised oneself, Xen.
unholy, unhallowed, Aesch.; ἀνίερος ἀθύτων πελάνων unhallowed because of unoffered sacrifices, Eur.
unconsecrated, Plat.
to dedicate, devote, τί τινι Plut.

entry.etym: For quantities, ἀνι epic, ἀνῑ- attic; but Hom. has ἀνῑει, ἀνῑέμενος.
The forms ἀνιεῖς, -εῖ are formed as if they were from ἀνιέω.
The Homeric forms in ἀνεσ- are created as if from ἀν-έζω.
The Ionic form ἀνέωνται is formed as if from ἀν-εόω.
entry.sense: to send up or forth, Hom., etc.; of the earth, to make spring up, Hhymn.; of females, to produce, Soph.:— Pass. to be sent up, produced, Aesch., etc.; to send up from the grave or nether world, Id., etc.
to send back, put back, open, Hom., Eur.
to let go, leave, Hom., etc.; c. gen. rei, δεσμῶν ἀνίει loosed them from bonds, Od.: to let go unpunished, Xen.
ἀν. τινί to let loose at one, ἀν. κύνας, Lat. canes immittere, Xen.; hence, ἄφρονα τοῦτον ἀνέντες Il.: c. inf. to set on or urge to do a thing, Hom.
ἀν. τινὰ πρός τι to let go for any purpose, Hdt.; ἀν. τινὰ μανίας to set free from madness, Eur.
to let, allow one to do a thing, c. acc. et inf., Hdt., etc.: —so, ἀν. κόμην to let it hang, loosen, Eur.
Mid., c. acc., κόλπον ἀνιεμένη baring her breast, Il.; αἶγας ἀνιέμενοι flaying goats, Od.

to let go free, leave untilled, of ground dedicated to a god, Thuc.:—Pass. to devote oneself, give oneself up, Hdt.; of animals dedicated to a god, which are let range at large, Id.; esp. in perf. pass. part. ἀνειμένος, Soph., etc.
to slacken, relax, let down, unstring, Hdt., Plat.:—then, to remit, neglect, give up, Soph., Thuc., etc.:—Pass. to be treated remissly, Thuc.

so intr. in Act. to slacken, abate, of the wind, Soph., etc.; οὐδὲν ἀνιέναι not to give way at all, Xen.:—c. part. to give up or cease doing, ὕων οὐκ ἀνίει [ὁ θεός] Hdt.:—c. gen. to cease from a thing, Eur., Thuc.
insufficient, incapable, Babr.
without prayer, not entreating, Eur.
unconquered, unconquerable, Hes., etc.
unmerciful, NTest.
to draw up water, by means of leather straps: generally, to draw out or up, Xen.: also Mid. ἀνιμῶμαι, Luc., etc.
intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν), to mount up, Xen.
without horse, not serving on horseback, Hdt., Soph.: without a horse to ride on, Ar.
of countries, unsuited for horses, Hdt.
with unwashen feet, Il.
unwashen, Il.
not to be washed out, Aesch.
unequal, uneven, Plat., etc.:—adv., ἀνίσως, unfairly, Dem.
inequality, Plat., etc.
to make equal, equalise, Xen.:—Pass. to be made equal, Hdt.
Causal in pres., imperf. to make to stand up, raise up, χειρός by his hand. Il.:— to raise from sleep, wake up, Il.: metaph., ἀν. νόσον Soph.:— to raise from the dead, Il., Aesch.; from misery, Soph.
of things, to set up, build, Hdt., etc.; so, ἀν. τινὰ χαλκοῦν to set up a bronze statue of him, Plut.;—aor1 mid., ἀναστήσασθαι πόλιν to build oneself a city, Hdt.
to build up again, restore, Eur., Dem.
to put up for sale, Hdt.
to rouse to action, stir up, Il.:— to rouse to arms, raise troops, Thuc.; ἀν. πόλεμον ἐπί τινα Plut.
to make people rise, break up an assembly, Il., Xen.
to make people rise from their home, make them emigrate, transplant, Od., Hdt., etc.
to make suppliants rise and leave sanctuary, Hdt., Thuc.
of sportsmen, to put up game, spring it, Xen.

Intr. in pres. and imperf. ἀνίσταμαι, -μην, in fut. ἀναστήσομαι, in aor2 ἀνέστην, perf. ἀνέστηκα, attic plup. ἀνεστήκη; also in aor1 pass. ἀνεστάθην [α]:— to stand up, rise, to speak, Hom., etc.:— to rise from one's seat as a mark of respect, Lat. assurgere, Il.:— to rise from bed, Id., etc.:— to rise from the dead, Id.:— to rise from an illness, recover, Hdt.
to rise as a champion, Il., Soph.: c. dat. to stand up to fight against, τινι Il.; πᾶσιν ὃς ἀνέστη θεοῖς Aesch.
of buiildings and statues, to be set up, to rise up, rear itself, Eur., Plut., etc.
of a river, to rise, Plut.
to rise to go, set out, go away, Eur., Thuc., etc.
to be compelled to migrate, Thuc.; of a country, to be depopulated, Hdt., Eur.; οὐκέτι ἀνισταμένη no longer subject to migration, Thuc.
of a law-court, to rise, Dem.
of game, to be put up, Xen.
to make inquiry into, ask about, Soph.: c. acc. pers. et rei, to ask a person about a thing, Aesch., Soph.; so, ἀν. τινὰ περί τινος Eur.
ignorant of history:— adv., ἀνιστορήτως ἔχειν τινός to be uninformed about a thing, Plut.
equalisation, Thuc.
to trace back, as a hound, Il.: generally, to trace out, Plut.
to side with Hannibal, Plut.
to guide back, Babr.
having no road, impassable, Eur., Xen.
a way up, as to the Acropolis, Hdt.:— a journey inland, esp. into Central Asia, Id., Xen.
Dep. to set up a wailing, Xen.
without understanding, Od.
not thought on, unheard of, Hhymn.
not within the province of thought, unintelligent, Plat.
act. not understanding, unintelligent, Lat. ineptus, Hdt., attic; ὠνόητε oh you fool, Ar.; ἀνόητα follies, Id.:—adv. -τως, Plat., etc.
want of understanding, folly, Hdt., etc.; ὑπ’ ἀνοίας Aesch.; πολλὴ ἄνοιά [ἐστι] πολεμῆσαι Thuc.
to open doors, etc., ἀναοίγεσκον κληῖδα they tried to put back the bolt so as to open the door, Il.; πύλας, θύραν ἀν., Aesch., Ar.
to undo, open, πῶμ’ ἀνέωιγε took off the cover and opened it, Il.; metaph., ἀνοίξαντι κληῖδα φρενῶν Eur.; ἀν. οἶνον to tap it, Theocr.
to lay open, unfold, disclose, Soph.
as nautical term, absol. to get into the open sea, get clear of land, Xen.
Pass. to be open, stand open, of doors, Hdt., Plat.; κόλποι δ’ ἀλλήλων ἀνοιγόμενοι opening one into another, Plut.
to swell up, of a wave, Eur.
metaph. of passion, Hdt.

to remove up the country:— Pass. and Mid. to shift one's dwelling up the country, to migrate inland, Ar.; and of cities, to be built up the country, away from the coast, Thuc.:—generally, to migrate, δεῦρ’ ἀνοικισθείς Ar., Thuc.
to resettle:— Pass. to be re-peopled, Plut.
to build up, Hdt.
to wall up, Ar.
to build again, rebuild, Thuc., Xen.
houseless, homeless, Hdt.
one must open, Eur.
pitiless, merciless, Soph., Anth.
unpitied, unmourned, Anth.
pitiless, ruthless, Eur.:—adv. -τως, without pity, without being pitied, Soph., Eur.
opened, Babr., Luc.
to wail aloud, Aesch., Thuc.
without need to wail, with impunity, Soph.
unlamented, Aesch.
an opening, πυλῶν Thuc.
one must report, Soph., Eur.:— one must refer, τι πρός τι Plut.
referred, ἔς τινα to some one for decision, Hdt.
to goad to madness, Eur.
to hold back, ἀν. τὰς νέας to keep them at anchor, Hdt.: of a chariot, to hold it in, keep it back, Soph.
ἀν. τὸν τόνον τῶν ὅπλων to keep up the tension of the ropes, keep them taut, Hdt.
intr. to keep back, keep still, Id.

entry.etym: formed by redupl. from ἀνοχή (cf. ὄκωχα perf. of ἔχω). The forms ἀνακωχή, ἀνακωχεύω are late and corrupt.
entry.sense: a stay, cessation, κακῶν Thuc.: absol. a cessation of arms, truce, δι’ ἀνοκωχῆς γίγνεσθαί τινι to be at truce with one, Id.
a hindrance, Id.
misery, Hes.
unblest, wretched, luckless, Theogn., Trag.
a hauling up, λίθων Thuc.
to cry aloud, shout (with joy), Trag.
c. acc. to bewail loudly, Soph.
in a causal sense, to excite by Bacchic cries, Eur.
Dep. to break into loud wailing, Thuc., Xen.
to restore to equality, equalise, 1 perf. pass. inf. ἀνωμαλίσθαι Arist.
without rain, of countries, Hdt.; ἄν. ῥοαί streams not fed by showers, Eur.
to act lawlessly, περί τι Hdt.
lawlessness, Hdt., Eur., etc.
having no communion with others, unsociable, Plat.
c. gen., ἀνομ. παιδείας unacquainted with education, Luc.
eyeless, sightless, Soph.
of unlike kind, heterogeneous, Arist.
and α, ον, unlike, dissimilar, Pind., Plat.; ἀν. τινι unlike it, Plat.:—adv. -ως, Thuc.; ἀν. ἔχειν to be unlike, Xen.
dissimilarity, Plat.
to make unlike or dissimilar, Plat.: —Pass. to be or become so, Id.
Dep. to agree upon a thing, come to an understanding, περί τινος Plat.; πρός τινα with one, Id.
to sum up one's conclusions, τὰ εἰρημένα Id.
perf. in pass. sense, ἀνωμολόγημαι πράττειν I am allowed to be doing, Dem.
one must admit, Plat.
disagreement, Plut.
not agreeing .
not agreeing, inconsistent, Plat.
without law, lawless, Hdt., Trag., etc.:— adv. -μως, Eur., etc.; comp. -ώτερον, Plat.
（νόμος II) musical, Aesch.
unprofitable, useless, Soph., Eur., etc.; neut. pl. ἀνόνητα as adv. in vain, Eur.
c. gen. making no profit from a thing, Dem.
without understanding, foolish, silly, Il., Soph., etc.:—comp. ἀνούστερος, Aesch.
either from ἀν-priv., * ὄπτομαι she flew away unseen; or = ἄνω, up into the air; or ἀν’ ὀπαῖα ( = ἀνὰ ὀπήν) up by the smoke-vent, Od.:—others write ἀνόπαια, ἡ, a kind of eagle.
without the ὅπλον or large shield, Hdt., Plat.
to look up, Aesch
without instruments, Plut.
doric for ἠνορέη.
to set up again, restore, rebuild, Hdt., Thuc.
to restore to health or well-being, πόλιν Soph.
to set straight again, set right, correct, τινα Eur.
without harbour: metaph., ὑμέναιον ἄν. εἰσπλεῖν to sail into a marriage that was no haven for thee, Soph.
to rouse, stir up, Pind.:—Pass., epic aor2 ἀνῶρτο, to start up, Hom.
to start up, leap up, Hom.; of the sun, ἀνόρουσεν οὐρανὸν ἐς went swiftly up the sky, Od.; ἀνορούσαις (doric part. aor1) Pind.
roofless, Eur.
to clap the wings and crow, like a cockrel, Ar.
to dig up what has been buried, Hdt., Ar.
ἀν. τάφον to dig it up, break open, Hdt.
Dep. to leap up and dance, Eur.
unholy, profane, Lat. profanus, of persons and things, Hdt., attic; ἀνόσιος νέκυς a corpse with all the rites unpaid, Soph.:—adv. -ίως, in unholy wise, Id.: without funeral rites, Eur.
profaneness, Plat.
without sickness, healthy, sound, Od., Hdt., attic
c. gen., ἄνοσος κακῶν untouched by ill, Eur.
of a season, free from sickness, Thuc.
of things, not causing disease, harmless, Eur.
boneless, of the polypus, Hes.
whence none return, Anth.
not returning, κεῖνον ἀν. ἔθηκεν cut off his return, Od.
not to be retraced, Eur.
unreturning, without return, Od.; Sup., ἥβη ἀνοστοτάτη never, never to return, Anth.
to break out into wailing, Aesch., Eur.
without ear: without handle, Theocr.
unwounded by sword, Il.
without wound, Il.
a holding back, stopping, esp. of hostilities: pl., like Lat. induciae, an armistice, truce, Xen.
（ἀνέχομαι) forbearance, NTest.
to hoist, lift up, Anth.
to be borne, sufferable, endurable, Theogn., Soph.; mostly with negat., οὐκ ἀνσχετά insufferable, Od.; πτώματ’ οὐκ ἀνασχετά Aesch.: —οὐκ ἀνασχετόν [ἐστι], c. inf., Hdt., Soph.
to buy with money received in payment for something else, Xen.:—Pass., aor1 part. ἀνταγορασθείς Dem.
to speak against, reply, Pind.:— to gainsay, contradict, τινί Ar.
as Dep. to struggle against, prove a match for, τινί Hdt., Thuc.:—generally, to struggle or dispute with, τινί Thuc.:— οἱ ἀνταγωνιζόμενοί τι the parties in a lawsuit, Xen.
to oppose, be a rival, Arist.
an opponent, competitor, rival, Xen., etc.; ἀντ. ἔρωτος a rival in love, Eur.
Mid., ἀνταείρεσθαι χεῖράς τινι to raise one's hands against one, Hdt.
contending against, rivalling, τινος Anth.
Dep. to respect in return, Xen.
set over against, right opposite, ἀνταία πληγή a wound in front, Soph., Eur.
opposed to, hostile, hateful, Eur.; τινι to one, Aesch.; τἀνταῖα θεῶν their hostile purposes, Id.
to raise against, χεῖράς τινι Anth.; so in Mid., Thuc.
intr. to rise up against, τινί Plat., Dem.; πρός τι or τινα, Dem., etc.
of a cliff, to rise opposite to, πρὸς τὴν Λιβύην Plut.
to demand in return, Thuc.
a sort of sturgeon, Hdt.
to hear in turn, τι ἀντί τινος Soph.: absol. to hear in return, Aesch., Xen.
to return a shout, Aesch.
that which is given or taken in exchange, φίλου for a friend, Eur.; τῆς ψυχῆς for one's soul, NTest.
one must give in exchange, τινός for a thing, Dem.
to exchange one thing with another, τί τινι Eur.; τὴν ἀξίωσιν τῶν ὀνομάτων ἀντ. to change the signification of the names, Thuc.

Mid. to take in exchange, τί τινος one thing for another, Eur., Dem.; τι ἀντί τινος Dem.; θάνατον ἀνταλλάξεται shall receive death in exchange, i. e. as a punishment, Eur.:—Pass., ἀντηλλαγμένος τοῦ ἑκατέρων τρόπου having made an interchange of each other's custom, i. e. having each adopted the other's way, Thuc.
Mid. to exchange one thing with another, τί τινι Archil.
c. acc. pers. to repay, requite, punish, Id., Aesch., etc.
to answer again, Hdt.; ἀντ. τι πρός τινα Soph.
Mid. to defend oneself against, resist, Thuc.
to requite, τινὰ κακοῖς Soph.
to make go up in turn, Xen.
to lead up against, ἀντ. νέας to put ships to sea against, Hdt.; but also, ἀντ. ναυσί with ships, Thuc.;—so, ἀντανάγειν or ἀντανάγεσθαι alone, Id., Xen.
to bring up or out instead, Anth.
to take away from the opposite sides of an account, to cancel, Dem.
to destroy in return, Eur.
to wait instead of taking active measures, Thuc.
to fill up in return, Xen.
to plait in rivalry with, τινί Anth.
to supply as a substitute or balance, τινὰ πρός τινα Dem.
instead of a man, as a substitute, Luc.
to rise so as to balance, τινί Thuc.
to set up against, τί τινι Plut.
Pass., with aor2 act., to rise up against, τινι Soph.
worth just as much as, c. gen., Il., Hdt., attic
absol. worth as much, worth no less, Il.
to demand as equivalent, or in turn, Thuc.
to demand in return, Thuc.:— Pass. to be called on for a thing in turn, τι Plut.
Mid. to obey in turn, τινι Tyrtae.
to keep off in turn, Anth.
to prove in return or answer, Xen.
to give back, repay, tender in repayment or requital, Batr., Hdt., attic:—absol. to make a return, Thuc.
to make correspondent, Plat.
intr. to answer to, correspond with, τοῖς ἑτέροις Id.
to give back words, answer, τινί Id.
to deliver in turn, τὸ σύνθημα Xen.
to give back a sound, Plut.
repayment, requital, NTest.
a giving back in turn, Thuc.: a rendering, requiting, repayment, reward, NTest.
Mid. to answer again, NTest.: to argue against, τινι Id.
to kill in return, Hdt., attic
to receive or accept in return, Plat., Dem.
to destroy in return, Eur., Plat.
Pass. and Mid., with perf. 2 act. -απόλωλα, to perish in turn, Eur.; ὑπὲρ ἀνδρὸς ἑκάστου δέκα ἀνταπόλλυσθαι that ten be put to death in revenge for each man, Hdt.
to requite, repay, Anth.
to shew on the other hand, Thuc.
over against, face to face, ἄντα μάχεσθαι to fight man to man; ἄντα ἰδεῖν to look before one; θεοῖς ἄντα ἐώικει was like the gods to look at, Hom.; ἄντα τιτύσκεσθαι to aim straight at them, Od.
as prep. with gen., over against, Hom.; ἄντα παρειάων before her cheeks; ἄντ’ ὀφθαλμοῖϊν Od.; ἄντα σέθεν before thee, Id.
in hostile sense, against, Διὸς ἄντα Il.
to hold out against, τινι Thuc.; πρός τι Plut.
absol. to hold out, persist, Ar.
Dep. to welcome or greet in turn, Xen.; to receive kindly, Id.
reflexion of light, Xen.
to reflect light, φάσγανον ἀνταυγεῖ φόνον flashes back murder, Eur.
to speak against, answer, τινα Soph.
to sound in turn, answer, τινί Pind.
to let go or let fall in turn, Eur.
c. dat. pers. to come opposite to, meet face to face, meet with, Il., Trag.
c. gen., either
gen. pers. to meet in battle, Hom.; or

gen. rei, to take part in, partake in or of, Id.; ὅπως ἤντησας ὀπωπῆς how thou hast sped in getting sight of him, Od.; so, ἀντ. ξεινίων Hdt.; κακῶν Soph.; so, ἄντασεἘρεχθειδᾶν partook of their blood, Id.
to insert one name instead of another, Dem.
to accuse in turn, Dem.
to compare in return, τινά τινι Ar.; absol., Plat.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres, ἀνταγορεύω being used instead, cf. ἀντερῶ
entry.sense: to speak against or in answer, gainsay, c. dat., οὐδὲν ἀντ. τινι Aesch., etc.:—absol. to speak in answer, Thuc., etc.; ἀντ. ἔπος to utter a word of contradiction, Eur.
ἀντ. τινί τι to set one thing against another, Plat.
κακῶς ἀντ. τινά to speak ill of him in turn, Soph.
to introduce instead, substitute, Dem.
to bring into office in turn, Plut.
to steal away in return, Ar.
to knock out in return, Dem.
to send out in return, Xen.
to sail out against, τινί Thuc.
to stretch out in opposition, ἀν. αὑτόν τινι to match oneself with another, Ar.
to set forth or state instead, Plut.
to sally out against, Xen.
to sail against, Plut.
to hope instead or in turn, Thuc.
to make an inroad in turn, Xen.: to attack in turn, Plut.
to put on board instead, Thuc.
Pass. to stick right in, τινί Ar.
to fill in turn, Xen.: to fill in return, by way of compensation, τί τινος Id.
to set on fire in return, Hdt.
difference of appearance, Strab.
to give way in turn, of sawyers, Ar.
to export in turn or instead, Xen.
to demand in return, Plut.
to drive, ride, sail out against, Plut.
to go out against, Xen.
to try one by the standard of another, Aeschin.; τι πρός τι Plut.:—Mid. to measure oneself against another, τινί Luc.:— to dispute with him at law, Id.
to ride out against, Plut.
a sailing against, Thuc.: a mode of attack, Plut.
to lead against: intr. to advance against, Thuc.
to praise in return, Xen.
Pass., ἀντ. τινί to be extolled in comparison with, Luc.
Pass. to put to sea against, πρός τινα Thuc.
to let slip against, τινί Luc.
to rush upon, meet an advancing enemy, c. dat. or absol., Thuc.
intr., to go out against, Thuc.
to march out to meet an enemy, πρός τινα Thuc.; absol., Xen.
to march out to meet an enemy, Thuc.
to clamour against one, Luc.
to form counter-designs, Thuc.
to write something instead, Dem.
to exhibit in turn, Xen.; so Mid., Plut.
to desire a thing in rivalry with another, c. gen. rei, Andoc.:—Pass., ἀντεπιθυμεῖσθαι τῆς ξυνουσίας to have one's company desired in turn, Xen.
to help in return, τινι Xen.
Dep. to attend or give heed in turn, τινός to one, Xen.
to write an answer, Luc.
to take the field against, Xen.
to order in turn, τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Thuc.
Dep. with pf pass to build a fort in retaliation, Thuc.
to entrust a letter in answer, πρός τινα Thuc.
to attack in turn, τινι Plut.
to rival another in love for a person, τινί τινος Luc.
to contribute in turn; Pass. to be repaid, Anth.
a rival in love, τινός for another, Ar.: a rival, Plat.
to love in return, Aesch.; ἀντερᾶν τινός Luc.
ἀντ. τινί τινος to rival one in love for another, Eur.: absol., τὸ ἀντερᾶν jealous love, Plut.
to set firmly against, τί τινι Eur.; ἀντ. ξύλα [τῶι πύργωι] to set wooden props against it, Xen.; ἀντ. βάσιν to plant it firm, Soph.
intr. to stand firm, resist pressure, Xen.
resistance, Plut.
Dep. to ask in turn, Hdt., Xen.
to make equal in weight with, to value equally with, c. gen., Theogn.

entry.etym: fut. with no pres. in use.
entry.sense: to speak against, gainsay, Soph.; τι πρός τινα Ar.; c. inf. to refuse, Aesch.:—Pass., οὐδὲν ἀντειρήσεται no denial shall be given, Soph.
return-love, Plat.
to question in turn, ἐρωτώμενος ἀντερωτᾶν Plat.
to return a kindness, Xen.
to wish well in return, τινί Xen.

to hold against, c. acc. et gen., χεῖρα ἀντ. κρατός to hold one's hand against one's head, so as to shade the eyes, Soph.; c. dat., ὄμμασι δ’ ἀντίσχοις τάνδ’ αἴγλαν may'st thou keep this sunlight upon his eyes (al. off his eyes), Id.
to hold out against, withstand, c. dat., Hdt., Thuc.; πρός τινα Thuc.; c. acc. to endure, Anth.
absol. to hold out, stand one's ground, Hdt., attic: to hold out, endure, last, Hdt., etc.; of the rivers drunk by the Persian army, to hold out, suffice, Id.
Mid. to hold before one against something, c. acc. et gen., Od.
c. gen. to hold on by, cling to, Hdt., attic:—metaph., ἀντ. τῶν ὄχθων to cling to the banks, keep close to them, Hdt.; ἀντ. ἀρετῆς, τοῦ πολέμου Id.; τῆς θαλάσσης Thuc.
absol. to hold out, Soph.
c. dupl. gen. pers. et rei, ἀνθέξεταί σου τῶν χρημάτων will lay claim to the property from you, dispute it with you, Ar.
hostile, Pind.

entry.etym: Note that it is not not ἀνθ-ήλιος
entry.sense: opposite the sun, i. e. facing east, Soph.; δαίμονες ἀντήλιοι statues of gods which stood in the sun before the door, Aesch.
like the sun, formed like ἀντίθεος, Eur.

against, over against, ἄντην στήσομαι I will confront him, Il.; ὁμοιωθήμεναι ἄντην to match himself against me, Hom.; ἄντην ἔρχεσθαι to go straight forwards, Il.; ἄντην βάλλεσθαι to be struck in front, Id.; ἄντην εἰσιδέειν to look him in the face, Id.; ἄντην λόεσθαι to bathe before all, Od.; θεῶι ἐναλίγκιος ἄντην like a god in presence, Id.
instead of a man, σποδὸς ἀντ. dust for men, Aesch.
properly, one who rows against another: generally an adversary, Aesch.
set over against, opposite, face to face, Eur.:—c. gen. over against, facing, Id.; ἀντήρεις στέρνων πληγάς aimed straight at the breast, Soph.:—c. dat., ἀντ. τινί opposite to a thing, Eur.
a prop, stay, support, Eur., Xen.; in Thuc., ἀντηρίδες are stay-beams, fixed so as to strengthen the timbers of the bow.
a meeting, Od.
to sound or sing in answer, Eur.
of a musical string, to sound responsively, Plut., Luc.
to meet face to face,
c. acc. pers. to encounter, whether as friend or foe, Hdt., Aesch.: absol. to meet, answer, Pind.
to approach as suppliants, to entreat, supplicate, Hdt., Soph.
c. dat. pers. to meet in fight, Pind.
fem. adj. a match for men, of the Amazons, Il.
στάσις ἀντιάνειρα faction wherein man is set against man, Pind.
to go for the purpose of meeting:

c. gen. rei, to go in quest of, Hom.; of an arrow, to hit, Il.; of the gods, to come (as it were) to meet an offering, to accept it, or to partake of it, Hom.; then, generally, to partake of, enjoy, obtain, Od., Soph.; so in Mid., Il.
c. gen. pers. to match or measure oneself with, Id., Theogn.
c. dat. pers. to meet with, encounter, Hom.
c. acc. rei, to come to, visit, share, ἐμὸν λέχος ἀντιόωσα Il.

to go against, withstand, resist, c. dat., Hdt., Aesch.; πλευραῖσιν ἀντιβᾶσα having set her foot against, Eur.; also absol., Hdt., etc.; ἀντιβάς reluctant, Soph.; but, ἀντιβὰς ἐλᾶν to pull stoutly against the oar, going well back, Ar.
to throw against or in turn, return the shots, Thuc.
to put one against the other, λόγους ἀντ. πρὸς ἀλλήλους to exchange words in conversation, NTest.
resistance, Plut.
contrary, opposite, Plut.
Dep. to use force against, Anth.
against, face to face, Il.
opposing force to force, ἀντιβίοις ἐπέεσσι with wrangling words, Hom.:—neut. as adv. = ἀντιβίην, Il.
one must look in the face, Luc.
to look straight at, look in the face, c. dat. pers., Xen.
a looking in the face, a look, Xen.
to return a cry, Bion.
to help in turn, τινι Thuc., Xen.
to meet by chance, esp. in battle, c. dat. pers. or absol., Hom.
c. dat. rei, to be present at, φόνωι ἀνδρῶν, τάφωι ἀνδρῶν Od.
c. gen. rei, to partake of, have one's share of, μάχης Il.; τάφου Od.
to fall to one's lot, c. gen. pers., γάμος ἀντιβολήσει ἐμέθεν Id.
c. acc. pers. to meet as a suppliant, entreat, supplicate, Ar.; c. acc. et inf., Id.:—absol. to supplicate, entreat, Id.
entreaty, prayer, Thuc.
to rival in thundering, τινί Luc.
to return a cry, Anth.
ionic form, to rival in pedigree, Hdt.
to be of a different opinion: ἀντ. τι μὴ οὐκ εἶναι to think that a thing is otherwise, Xen.
= ἀντίγραφον, Luc.
a check-clerk, controller, Aeschin.; ἀντ. τῶν εἰσενεγκόντων one who keeps a check upon their accounts, Dem.
a reply in writing, such as Caesar's Anticato in reply to Cicero's Cato, Plut.
as law-term, a plea, indictment, Plat., Dem.
copied, Dem.:—as Subst., ἀντίγραφον, τό, a transcript, copy, counterpart, Id.
to write against or in answer, write back, Thuc., Plut.
Mid., with perf. pass., as law-term, to put in as a plea, to plead against, Dem.
to bite in turn, Hdt.
taking another's place at dinner, Luc.
Dep. to salute in return, τινα Xen.
Dep. to entreat in return, Plat.
Dep. = ἀντιβλέπω, c. acc., Eur.
Dep. to receive or accept in return, Aesch., Eur.
to rival as a demagogue, Plut.
to cross over in turn, Xen.
