to attack in return, Arist.
to retort, Aeschin.
to offer resistance, τοὺς ἀντιδιατιθεμένους opponents, NTest.
to teach in turn or on the other side, Anth.:—of poets, to contend for the prize, Ar.
to give in return, repay, τί τινι Hdt., attic
to give for or instead of, τί τινος Eur.; τι ἀντί τινος Ar.
at Athens, ἀντ. [τὴν οὐσίαν] to offer to change fortunes with one (cf. ἀντίδοσις), Dem., etc.
to go through in turn, Aeschin.
to dispute, go to law, περί τινος Xen.; οἱ ἀντιδικοῦντες the parties to a suit, Plat.; absol. of the defendant, Ar.; ἀντ. πρός τι or πρός τινα, to urge one's suit against . . , Dem.
an opponent in a suit, defendant or plaintiff, Plat., etc.: generally an opponent, Aesch.
of a different opinion or sect, Luc.
clothed with something instead of a skin, Anth.
a giving in return, exchange, Arist., Luc.

at Athens, a form by which a citizen charged with a λειτουργία or public charge might call upon any other citizen whom he thought richer than himself either to exchange properties, or to take the charge upon himself, Xen., Dem., etc.
given in lieu of, πυρός Anth.
given as a remedy for, κακῶν Id.:—as Subst., ἀντίδοτος, ἡ, an antidote, Id.
to serve in place of, τινός Eur.
treated as a slave, Aesch.
re-echoing, Aesch.; ἀντίδουπά τινι Id.
to act against, retaliate, Soph., Eur.
c. acc. pers. to repay, requite, Soph., Eur.
Dep. to present in return, τινά τινι one with a thing, Hdt., Plat., etc.; also, ἀντ. τινί τι to present a thing in turn to one, Eur.
to seek one who is seeking us, Xen.
to save alive in turn, Babr.
to bury opposite: Pass., aor2 ἀντετάφην [ᾶ], Anth.
equal to the gods, godlike, Hom.
to take care of in return, Xen.
opposition, resistance, Plat., Anth.
antithesis, Isocr.
to run against another, compete in a race, Hdt.
to run contrary ways, Anth.
to whet against another, ὀδόντας ἐπί τινα Luc.
echoing, Anth.
opposite the door: as neut. Subst., ἀντίθυρον, ου, τό, the part facing the door, the vestibule, Od., Soph.
the side of a room facing the door, Luc.
to sleep again or instead. Anth.

entry.etym: perf. of ἀντικαθίζομαι, but used as pres.
entry.sense: to be set over against; of armies or fleets, to lie over against, so as to watch each other, Hdt., Thuc.

entry.etym: here you need to generate ἀντικατίζομαι
entry.sense: Mid. to sit or lie over against, or armies or fleets watching one another, Hdt., Thuc.
to lay down or establish instead, substitute, replace, Hdt., Thuc.
to set against, oppose, τινὰ πρός τινα Thuc.; τινά τινι Plat.
to bring back again, restore, Thuc.
Pass., with aor2 and perf. act., and aor1 pass. κατεστάθην [ᾰ], to be put in another's place, reign in his stead, Hdt., Xen.
to stand against, resist, τινί Xen.; absol., Thuc.
to damage in turn, τινά Plat.
to invite in turn, Xen.
to die or be slain in turn, Aesch.
to leave in one's stead, Plat.
Mid., to exchange one thing for another:
to give one thing for another, τί τινος Dem.; τι ἀντί or ὑπέρ τινος Oratt.
to receive one thing in exchange for another, τι ἀντί τινος Isocr.
to stretch out or set directly in contrast, τι παρά τι Plat.
to accuse in turn, recriminate upon, τινός Aeschin.
Anticato, name of a book written by Caesar in reply to the Cato of Cicero, Plut.
to be set over against, lie opposite, Plat.: adv. part. ἀντικειμένως, by way of opposition, Arist.
to command in turn, Thuc.:— Pass. to be bidden to do a thing in turn, Id.
something acting as a goad, Aesch.
to tend instead of another, τινός Eur.
to proclaim in answer, Eur.
to sound against, to be echoed by a thing, Eur.:— ἀντ. ἀλλήλαις μέλος to sing against one another, Id.
to weep in return, Hdt.
the part of the leg opposite the κνήμη, the shin, Ar.
Pass. to be punished in return, Luc.
to flatter in turn, Plut.
to bring back as an answer, Plut.
to boast in opposition, τινί Plut.
to beat back, resist, oppose, Xen.
impers., ἤν τι ἀντικόψηι if there be any hindrance, Id.
Mid. to take arms against, τινί Anth.
to hold instead of another, Anth.
a striking against, hindrance: a repartee, Aeschin.
to strike against, to be a hindrance, counteract, τινί Thuc.; πρός τι Plut.; absol., Dem.
= ἄντην, over against, right opposite, c. dat., θεοῖς ἀντικρὺ μάχεσθαι Il.; c. gen., Ἕκτορος ἀντικρύ Id.
= ἄντικρυς, straight on, right on, Hom.; followed by a prep., ἀντικρὺ ἀν’ ὀδόντας, ἀντικρὺ δι’ ὤμου Id.; ἀντικρὺ κατὰ μέσσον right in the middle, Il.
outright, utterly, ἀντικρὺ δ’ ἀπόφημι Id.
straight on, right on, Thuc., etc.
outright, openly, without disguise, Aesch., Thuc., etc.; ἀντ. δουλεία downright slavery, Thuc.; οὐκ ἄντικρυς not at all, Ar.
later, = ἀντῑκρύ, opposite, Arist., Plut.
in requital for murder, Aesch.
to ring, clash against, τινί Anth.
to hit upon, meet, τινί Pind., Soph.
to ridicule in turn, Plut.
a thing to hold by, a handle, Lat. ansa, Thuc.:—metaph., πολλὰς . . ἔχει ἀντιλαβάς gives many handles against one, points of attack, Plat.
as a law-term, ἀντ. δίαιταν to have a new arbitration granted, i. e. to get the old one set aside, Dem.; ἀντ. ἔρημον (sc. τὴν δίκην) to get it set aside by default, Id.
to take hold of, hold by, c. gen., Eur.; to partake in, πόνων Id.
c. acc. to receive in turn, Id.
to kick against, τινί Ar.
to receive instead of, τί τινος Eur.: to receive in turn or as a return, τι Id., etc.
Mid., with perf. pass. -είλημμαι, like ἀντέχομαι, c. gen. to lay hold of, Theogn., etc.; χώρας ἀντ. to gain or reach it, Thuc.
to help, take part with, assist, Eur.; c. gen. rei, to help towards a thing, Thuc.; c. gen. pers., NTest.
to lay claim to, τοῦ θρόνου Ar.
to take part, or share in a thing, take in hand, Lat. capessere, τῶν πραγμάτων Xen., etc.
to take hold of for the purpose of finding fault, to reprehend, ἡμῶν Plat.
to take fast hold of, to captivate, ὁ λόγος ἀντιλαμβάνεταί μου Id.
in Mid. also, to hold against, hold back, ἵππου Xen.
to kindle a light in turn, Aesch.
intr. to reflect light, shine, Xen.
to shine opposite to or in the face of, ὁ ἥλιος ἀντ. τινί Plut.

entry.etym: the common fut. is ἀντερῶ; the aor. commonly used is ἀντεῖπον
entry.sense: to speak against, gainsay, contradict, τινί Thuc., etc.; τινὶ περί τινος Xen.; ὑπέρ τινος Id.; πρός τι Ar.:— ἀντ. ὡς . . to declare in opposition or answer that . . , Hdt., etc.; c. inf. to reply that . . , Thuc.; ἀντ. μὴ ποιεῖν to speak against doing, Id.
c. acc. rei, to allege in answer, Soph., Thuc.:—Pass. to be disputed, Xen.; of a place, to be counter-claimed, Id.
absol. to speak one against the other, speak in opposition, Hdt., etc.; οἱ ἀντιλέγοντες Thuc.
one must gainsay, Eur.
disputably, Thuc.
lion-like, formed like ἀντίθεος, Ar.
a motion for a new arbitration, Dem.
one must take part in a matter, Ar.; τῶν πραγμάτων αὐτοῖς ἀντ. Dem.
a receiving in turn or exchange, Thuc.: a counter-claim, Xen.
(from Mid.), a hold, support, defence, succour, Id.
a claim to a thing, Id.
an objection, Plat.
(from Pass.) a being seized, a seizure, attack of sickness, Thuc.
=ἀντιλέγω to deny, Soph.
= ἀντ. λέγω 3, Ar.
contradiction, controversy, disputation, Hdt., Thuc.; in pl. opposing arguments, answering speeches, Ar., Thuc.
Dep. to count up or calculate on the other hand, Xen.
given to contradiction, contradictory, disputatious, Ar., etc.:— ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη) the art of contradiction or of arguing from contradictories, Plat.
contradictory, reverse, Eur.
to rail at or abuse in turn, NTest.; Mid., c. acc. rei, Luc.
to vex in return, Plut.
responsive to the lyre, Soph.
a ransom, NTest.
Pass. to rage or bluster against, τινί Anth.
to learn instead, Ar.
to appear as witness against, to contradict solemnly, τινί Plut.
Dep. to protest on the other hand, Luc.
Dep. to fight against one, Thuc.
to drag different ways, Anth.
to move from one side to the other, to revolutionise, Ar.
Pass., with aor. 2 and perf. act., to pass over to the other side, Luc.
Dep. to behave petulantly in return, πρός τινα Plut.
to wait and watch against one, aor1 inf. ἀντιμελλῆσαι, Thuc.
Dep. to blame in turn, Hdt.
Dep. to impart in turn, Anth.
to compete: οἱ ἀντιμετιόντες competitors, Plut.
to measure out in turn, to give in compensation, Luc.: Pass. to be measured in turn, NTest.
front to front, Xen.
to contrive against or in opposition, Hdt., Thuc.
close imitation of a person in a thing, c. dupl. gen., Thuc.
a requital, recompense, NTest.
as a reward, Aesch.
by way of compensation, Dem.
sounding instead of, differing in sound from, c. gen., Eur.; ὕπνου ἀντίμολπον ἄκος song, sleep's substitute, Aesch.
corresponding to, τινί Luc.
to build ships against, Thuc.
to conquer in turn, Aesch.
ambiguity in the law, ἐν ἀντινομίαι γίγνεσθαι to be in a strait between two laws, Plut.
to set oneself against, Pind.
opposed, adverse, Hdt.:— τὸ ἀντίξοον opposition, Id.
Dep. to resist, oppose, τινί Hdt., Aesch.:— οἱ ἀντιούμενοι = οἱ ἐναντίοι, Hdt.:—c. acc., once in Hdt.
set against, and so
in local sense, face to face, opposite, esp. in battle, Hom., etc.; ἀντίος ἦλθε went to meet him, Il.; c. gen., Ἀγαμέμνονος ἀντίος Id.; usually c. dat., Od., Hdt., attic
opposite, contrary, Aesch., Eur.: οἱ ἀντίοι = οἱ ἐναντίοι, Pind., Hdt.: ἐκ τῆς ἀντίης contrariwise, Hdt.
as adv. in neut. ἀντία and ἀντίον, against, straight at, right against, ἀντίον ἷζεν Od., etc.; c. gen., ἀντί’ ἐμεῖο Il.; so, ἀντία σευ in thy presence, Hdt.; ἀντία τῆς ἵππου opposite it, Id.
against, ἀντίον τινος εἰπεῖν Od.; c. dat., ἀντία τοῖς Πέρσηισι Hdt.
τὸν δ’ ἀντίον ηὔδα = ἠμείβετο, answered, Od., attic
=ἀνθίσταμαι,to be contrary, of a wind, Soph.
Pass. to drive against, Anth.
in return for suffering, Aesch.: felt mutually, Luc.
as Subst., ἀντιπαθές, a remedy for suffering, Plut.
to play one with another, Xen.
like a boy or child, Aesch., Eur.

properly wrestling against: then, generally, struggling against, antagonistic, rival, Aesch.; c. dat. rivalling, a match for another, Eur.; c. gen., ὑμεναίων γόος ἀντίπαλος Id.:—as Subst., ἀντίπαλος, ὁ, an antagonist, rival, adversary, mostly in pl., Hdt., attic; τὸ ἀντίπαλον the rival party, Thuc.

of things, like ἰσόπαλος, nearly balanced, Id.; ἀντ. τριήρης equally large, Id.; ἀντ. δέος fear equal on both sides, mutual fear, Id.; ἤθεα ἀντίπαλα [τῆι πόλει] habits corresponding to the constitution, Id.:— τὸ ἀντίπαλον τῆς ναυμαχίας the equal balance, undecided state of the action, Id.:—adv. -λως, and in neut. pl. ἀντίπαλα, Id.
[II.] τὸν ἀμὸν ἀντ. him who fights for me, my champion, Aesch.
to hold side by side, to compare or contrast, τι πρός τι or παρά τι Plat., etc.
close comparison or contrast, Arist.
competition for a public office, Plut.
to command in turn or also, Xen.
to compete for a public office, τινί with one, Plut.
to lead the army against, advance to meet the enemy, Xen.
to outflank, Xen.
to summon in turn or contrariwise, Thuc., etc.
Dep. to exhort in turn or contrariwise, Thuc., etc.
to annoy in turn, Thuc.
to sail along on the other side, Thuc.
Mid. to prepare oneself in turn, arm on both sides, Thuc.; ἀντ. ἀλλήλοις ὡς ἐς μάχην Id.
mutual preparation, Thuc.
Mid. and Pass. to stand in array against, τινι Thuc.; πρός τι Aeschin.:—absol. to stand in hostile array, Thuc.; ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀντιπαραταχθέντος in hostile array, Id.
to stretch side by side, so as to compare, τι πρός τι Plat.
to contrast and compare, τινί τι Plat.
to march so as to meet, of armies on opposite sides of a river or the like, Xen.
to lead on against, Plut.
(sub. στρατόν) to march against, Philipp. ap. Dem.
to march parallel with, τινί Plut.
Dep. to pass by on the opposite side, NTest.
to supply in turn, Thuc.:—Mid., Xen.; ἀντ. πράγματα to cause trouble in return, Dem.
to suffer in turn, ἀντιπάσχω χρηστά I receive good for good done, Soph.; ἀντ. ἀντί τινος Thuc.: absol. to suffer for one's acts, Xen.
absol., τὸ ἀντιπεπονθός reciprocity, Arist.
to clatter so as to drown other sounds, Thuc.
c. gen. orig.:— sense over against, opposite.
Usage,
of Place, instead, in the place of, Hom., etc.
as good as, equal to, ἀντὶ πολλῶν λαῶν ἐστίν he is as good as many men, Il.; ἀντὶ κασιγνήτου Od.
at the price of, for, ἀντὶ χρημάτων for money paid, Hdt., etc.
for the sake of, Soph.
to mark comparison, ἓν ἀνθ’ ἑνός one set against the other, compared with it, Plat.: so, after Comparatives, πλέον ἀντὶ σοῦ Soph.; also (esp. after a negative), ἄλλος ἀντ’ ἐμοῦ Aesch.
Position: ἀντί rarely follows its case, and then does not suffer anastrophe.
IN COMPOS.,
over against, opposite, as ἀντίπορος.
in return, as ἀντιβοηθέω.
instead, as ἀντήνωρ.
equal to, like, as ἀντίθεος.
counter, as ἀντίτυπος.
to send back an answer, Hdt.
to send in repayment, Soph.
to send against, στρατιάν τινι Thuc.
to send in the place of another, στρατηγούς Id.
causing grief in turn, Aesch.
lying over against: ἀντιπέραια the lands just opposite, Il.
the opposite coast, Mosch.
over against, on the other side, c. gen., Thuc.; absol., ἡ ἀντ. Θράικη Id.
from the opposite side, c. gen., Anth.
to embrace in turn, Xen.
to sail round on the other side, Strab.
to move round in turn or in opposition, Plut.
like stone, rocky, Soph.
a kind of cradle for infants, on wheels, Eur.
to fall against, resist, τινί NTest.
to sail against an enemy, Thuc.
beaten by the opposing waves, Soph.
to man ships against the enemy, Thuc.
to fill up by new members, Xen.
to strike in turn, Arist.
of winds to be contrary, Plut., Luc.
caused by adverse winds, Aesch.: adverse, hostile, Id.
to long for in turn, τι Xen.
to do in return, τι Plat.: absol. to retaliate, Xen.
Mid. to exert oneself about a thing, seek after, lay claim to, c. gen., Thuc., Plat., etc.; c. inf., ἀντ. ἐπίστασθαί τι to lay claim to knowing, Plat.
to contend with one for a thing, ἀντ. τινὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς Xen.; τινι περί τινος Id.

requital, retribution, ἀντίποινα τίνειν = ἀντιτίνειν, to atone for, c. acc., Aesch.; ἀντίποινά τινος πράσσειν to exact retribution for a thing, Id.; ἀντίποιν’ ἐμοῦ παθεῖν to suffer retribution forthe wrong done me, Soph.
to urge war against others, Thuc., etc.; c. dat., Xen.
warring against, οἱ ἀντιπολέμιοι enemies, Thuc.
to besiege in turn, Thuc.
a rival city, τινι Strab.
Dep. to be a political opponent, Arist.; ἀντ. τινι to oppose his policy, Plut.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use
entry.sense: to give instead, Anth.
Pass. to march to meet another, Xen.
to ravage in return, Eur.
over the straits, on the opposite side of the straits, Aesch., Eur.
on the opposite coast, Aesch.; Ἄρτεμιν Χαλκίδος ἀντίπορον, i. e. her temple at Aulis over against Chalcis, Id.:—simply, over against, opposite to, τινι Xen.
counteraction, resistance, Plut.
to act against, seek to counteract, τινί Xen.:— absol. to act in opposition, Hdt., etc.; so in Mid., Xen.
Mid. to send counter-ambassadors, Thuc.
to come forward against or
to meet, τινί Thuc.
for next to nothing, cheap, Xen.
Mid. to retort a legal challenge (πρόκλησις), Dem.
to salute in turn, Plut.
to go against, Xen.
serving as aor2 to ἀντιπροσαγορεύω, Theophr.: aor1 pass. ἀντιπροσερρήθην, Xen.
to summon in turn, Dem.
to bring near in turn, τί τινι Xen.
with the face towards, facing, τινι Xen.: face to face, Id.
to offer in turn, τὴν δεξιάν Xen.
with the prow towards, Hdt., Thuc.: prow to prow, Thuc.
like ἀντιπρόσωπος, face to face, Soph.
with gates opposite, ἀλλήληισι Hdt.
like a tower, Eur.
to build a tower over against, πόλιν τήνδ’ ἀντεπύργωσαν reared up this rival city, Aesch.
to counterpoise, balance, Aesch.
counterpoising, compensating for, τινός Dem.; λύπης ἀντ. ἄχθος the counterpoising weight of sorrow, Soph.:—adv., ἀντιρρόπως πράττειν τινί so as to balance his power, Xen.
Mid. to meet pride with pride, Arist.
to counterbalance, compensate for, c. dat., Aesch.; c. gen., Eur.
Mid. to furnish for oneself in turn, Xen.
equipoise, compensation, Hdt.
to mock in return, Plut.
Pass to oppose on equal terms, Thuc.
drawn in the contrary direction: spasmodic, convulsive, Soph.
to draw the contrary way, hold back, Aesch., Ar.: Pass. to suffer a check, Arist.
to draw to itself, Xen.
counterpoising: in compensation for, c. gen., Soph.
to form a party against, τινί Xen.; οἱ ἀντιστασιάζοντες = οἱ ἀντιστασιῶται, Id.
an opposite party, Plat.
a standing against, resistance, Plut.
one of the opposite faction or party, Hdt., Xen.
to resist, oppose, τινί Plat.; absol., Hdt.
an opponent, adversary, Aesch.
to stand opposite in rows or pairs, ἀλλήλοις Xen.: to stand vis-a-vis in a dance, Id.
ranged opposite in rows or pairs, Arist.: standing over against, Eur.
Dep. to make war against, τινι Xen.
to be Propraetor, Plut.
the enemy's general, Thuc.
the Propraetor or Pro-consul, Polyb.
an encamping opposite, Polyb.
to encamp over against, τινί Isocr., Polyb.; mostly in Mid. with perf. pass., Hdt., attic
to turn to the opposite side: intr. to wheel about, face about, Xen.
a turning about: the antistrophe or returning of the chorus, answering to a previous στροφή, except that they now moved from left to right instead of from right to left.

turned so as to face one another: correlative, coordinate, counterpart, τινι to a thing, Plat.: also ἀντίστροφός τινος, as if ἀντ. were a Subst., the correlative or counterpart of, Id.; adv. -φως, coordinately, τινί Id.
a counter-senate, Plut.
to answer by syllogism, Arist.
to meet face to face, Anth.
to play at ball against, οἱ ἀντισφαιρίζοντες the parties in a game at ball, Xen.
an opposing force, Plut.
= ἀντισηκόω, to counterbalance, compensate for, Anth.
counter-array, Thuc.
to set opposite to, range in battle against, τινά τινι Hdt., Aesch., etc.; τι πρός τι Aeschin.:—so in Mid., Thuc.
Mid. also to set oneself against, meet face to face, meet in battle, Eur., etc.; τινι Dem.:—Pass. to be drawn out against, τινι Hdt., Xen.; πρός τινα Hdt., Xen.; κατά τινα Xen.
to stretch out in return, to offer in return, to repay, τι ἀντί τινος Eur.
intr. to strive against, counteract, resist, τινί, or absol., Hdt., attic
of places, to lie over against, τινί Plut.
a counter-fortification, Thuc.
to cut against, i. e. to provide a remedy or antidote, Eur.
Dep to contrive in opposition, counterplan, c. acc., Hdt.
counter-manoeuvring, emulation, Thuc.
rivalling in an art or craft, Ar., Plat.; c. dat., Plat.
to set against, oppose, c. dat., Simon.: to contrast, compare, τί τινι Hdt., Eur.; also τί τινος, Thuc.; τι πρός τι Dem.
ἀντ. τινά τινι to match one against the other in battle, Lat. committere, ἴσους ἴσοισι ἀντιθείς Eur.:—Pass. to be matched one against another, Hdt.
to retort, rejoin, Eur., Thuc.
to deposit in return, Eur., Xen.:— to give in return or as a recompense, τί τινος one thing for another, Eur.
to honour in return, τινά, Xen.:—f. mid. in pass. sense, Id.
Mid as law-term, to fix a counter-estimate of damages, c. gen. pretii, Plat.
Dep. to avenge oneself on, τινα Eur., Thuc.; absol. to take vengeance, Ar.
to pay or suffer punishment for a thing, τι Theogn.; absol., Soph.
Mid. to exact or inflict in turn, τί τινος one thing for another, Aesch., Eur.
to avenge, punish, σὸν φόνον Eur.
to dare to stand against another, πρός τινα Thuc.
boldly attacking, Aesch.
cut as a remedy for an evil: —ἀντίτομον, ου, τό, a remedy, antidote, Hom.; τινος for a thing, Pind.
strained against, resisting: as Subst., ἀντίτονα, τά, cords for a ballista, Plut.
to shoot arrows in turn, Xen.
to bore right through, c. gen., Il.; c. acc. to break open, Id.
paid back, requited, avenged: ἄντιτα ἔργα the work of revenge or retribution, Od.; παιδός for her son, Il.
to maintain in turn, Xen.
to meet with in return, τινός Theogn., Thuc.
repelled by a hard body, τύπος ἀντ. blow and counter-blow, of hammer and anvil, Orac. ap. Hdt.:—of sound, echoed, echoing, στόνος Soph.; κατὰ τὸ ἀντ. by repercussion, of an echo, Luc.
corresponding, as the stamp to the die, ἀντ. τῶν ἀληθινῶν figuring or representing the true, NTest.
act., of a hard body, repellent, rigid, Xen.; of hard ground, ἀντιτύπᾳ ἐπὶ γᾶι πέσε Soph.
metaph. of men, stubborn, obstinate, Xen.
opposed to, τινός Aesch.: adverse, of events, Xen.
to express as by a figure, Anth.
to beat in turn, Ar., Plat.
to set oneself against, measure oneself with, τινί Il., Ar.; παρά τινα Pind.
instead of a dower, Aesch.
to set against, τι ἐπί τινι Anth.:—Dep or Pass. to set oneself against, fight against, Hom.
to go into exile in turn, Eur.
to speak against, to contradict, Plat.
to return a sound, echo, Pind., Eur.
to speak against, Luc.
of answering sound, imitative, Anth.
to love in return, Plat., Xen.
return of affection, Arist.
to hold contrary tenets, Luc.
Pass. to be moved by jealousy against, πρός τι Plut.
Dep to receive kindly in turn, Plut.
in return for slaughter, in revenge for blood, Aesch., Soph.
θάνατοι ἀντ. deaths by mutual slaughter, Aesch.
Mid. to take in a return cargo, Dem.
to import in exchange for exports, Xen.: also as Pass., to be received in exchange for the cargo, Id.
to barricade, block up, Xen.
a watching one against another, Thuc.
one posted to watch another, Luc.
to watch in turn, Plat.:—Mid. to be on one's guard against, τινά Xen.
to sound in answer, reply, Trag.
c. acc. rei, to utter in reply, Soph.:—c. acc. pers. to reply to, answer, Id.
sounding in answer, responsive to, c. gen., Eur.
to rejoice in answer to, τινί Soph.
to shew kindness in turn, τινί Hdt., Xen.
to vote against doing a thing, ἀντ. μὴ παρέχειν Ar.; absol., Thuc.
to be a rival choragus, τινί to another, Dem.
a rival choragus, Dem., etc.
to be sufficient, like ἀποχράω, Hdt.
Antichrist, NTest.
to play a lyre in accompaniment to, τινί Ar.
responsive, harmonious, Eur.
Dep to vote against, πρός τι Plut.
to bale out bilge-water, bale the ship, Theogn., Eur.
generally, to draw water, Hdt.
metaph. of toil or suffering, to exhaust, come to the end of, like Lat. exantlare or exhaurire labores, Aesch., Eur.
to squander, Soph.
a bucket for drawing water, NTest.
the hold of a ship, Soph., Ar.
bilge-water, filth, Ar.

entry.etym: perhaps for ἀνά-τλος, the Root of -τλος being ΤΛΕ, τλάω
entry.sense: the hold of a ship, where the bilgewater settles, Lat. sentina, Od.
the bilge-water in the hold, Eur.; ἄντλον οὐκ ἐδέξατο let in no bilgewater, metaph. for "let no enemy come in, " Aesch.; εἰς ἄντλον ἐμβαίνειν πόδα, metaph. for getting into a difficulty, Eur.
to pity in return, τινά Eur.

entry.etym: Dep. only in pres. and impf.
entry.sense: =ἀντάω to meet, in battle, c. dat., Il.:—absol., διπλόος ἤντετο θώρηξ the breastplate doubled (by the belt) met or stopped (the dart), Id.
= ἀντιάζω 1. 2, c. acc. pers. to approach with prayers, entreat, Soph., Eur.
to swear in turn, c. fut. inf., Xen.
to name instead, call by a new name, Thuc.
to owe one a good turn, Thuc.
to meet face to face, to face, τινί Polyb., NTest.
Pass. to drive or ride against, Mosch.
*Fem. adj. of a grotto, Anth.
Lat. antrum, a cave, grot, cavern, Od., Trag.
full of caves, Xen.
like ἴτυς, the edge or rim of anything round or curved:
the rim of the round shield, Il.
the rail round the front of the chariot, the chariot-rail, Id.; sometimes double, and therefore ἄντυγες in pl., Id., Soph.
post-Hom.,
in pl. the chariot itself, Soph., Eur.
the frame of the lyre, Eur.
the orbit of a planet, Hhymn.; the disk of the moon, Mosch.
singing in answer, responsive, Ar., Anth.
an oath or affidavit made one against the other, i. e. by plaintiff and defendant, Plat., etc.
Dep to buy instead, Xen.
to bid against, ἀλλήλοις Lys.; ὁ ἀντωνούμενος a rival bidder, Dem.
with the eyes opposite, facing, fronting, Luc., Anth.
to assist or benefit in turn, τινά Xen.:—Pass. to derive profit in turn, Id.
not insulted, Plut.
act. not insolent, decorous, Id.
wanting water, waterless, of arid countries, Hdt.:—of a corpse, deprived of funeral lustrations, Eur.
without the nuptial song, unwedded, Soph., Eur.: neut. pl. as adv., Soph., Eur.
to praise in song, c. acc., Eur.
unwedded, Soph.; ἀν. γονή birth from an ill-starred marriage, Id.
not bridal, unwedded, Soph.; νύμφη ἄνυμφος a bride that is no bride, unhappy bride, Eur.
without bride or mistress, μέλαθρα Id.
not to be surpassed or outdone, Xen., etc.:—adv. -τως, Arist.
not liable to give account, irresponsible, Ar., Plat.
a going barefoot, Plat., Xen.
to go barefoot, Luc.
unshod, barefoot, Plat.
not liable to action, Plut.
without dissimulation, NTest.
unsuspected, Dem.
without suspicion, unsuspected, Thuc., Xen.:—adv. -τως, unsuspectedly, Thuc.
not to be withstood, irresistible, Xen., etc.
not made subject, τινι NTest.
unruly, refractory, of persons, Id.
finishing work, industrious, Theocr.
efficacious, effectual, εἴς τι Xen.: adv. -μως, Sup. -ώτατα, Plat.
accomplishment, Hom.
to be accomplished, practicable, Eur.; ὡς ἀνυστόν, like ὡς δυνατόν, σιγῆι ὡς ἀν. as silently as possible, Xen.
to be accomplished, practicable, Xen.
to weave anew, renew, Plat.
to raise up, exalt, Anth., in Mid.

to effect, achieve, accomplish, complete, Lat. conficere, c. acc. rei, Hom., etc.; absol., οὐδὲν ἤνυε he did no good, Hdt.; c. acc. et inf. to bring to pass that . . , Soph.:—Mid. to accomplish for one's own advantage, Od., Plat., etc.
to make an end of, destroy, Hom., etc.
to finish a journey, ὅσσον νηῦς ἤνυσεν much as a ship can do, Od.; so, ἀν. θαλάσσης ὕδωρ to make its way over the sea water, Id.

in attic absol. to make one's way, πρὸς πόλιν Soph.; ἐπὶ ἀκτάν Eur.; also, θάλαμον ἀνύτειν to reach the bridal chamber, Soph.; with inf., ἤνυσε περᾶν succeeded in crossing, Aesch.; and with an adj., εἶναι being omitted, εὐδαίμων ἀνύσει will come to be happy, Soph.
Pass. of Time, to come to an end, Theocr.
in Pass. also of persons, to grow up, Aesch.
to get, procure, φορβάν Soph., etc.
with a partic., οὐκ ἀνύω φθονέουσα I gain nothing by gruding, Il.

to do quickly, make haste, Ar.; then, like φθάνω, ἄνυε πράττων make haste about it, Id.; ἄνυσον ὑποδησάμενος make haste and get your shoes on, Id.; also ἀνύσας with an imperat., ἄνοιγ’, ἄνοιγ’ ἀνύσας make haste and open the door, Id.; ἀνύσας τρέχε, λέγ’ ἀνύσας Id., etc.
to accomplish, achieve, finish, ὁδόν Od.; οὐδὲν ἦνον Eur.
Pass., of the close ofa period of time, νὺξ ἄνεται night is drawing to a close, Il.; ἔτος ἀνόμενον the waning year, Hdt.:—generally to be finished, Il.; ἤνετο τὸ ἔργον Hdt.
implying Motion,
up, upwards, Hom., etc.; ἄνω ἰόντι going up the country, (i.e. inland), Hdt.
implying Rest, up, aloft, on high, Soph., Plat., etc.
on earth, as opp. to the world below, Soph.; οἱ ἄνω the living, opp. to οἱ κάτω the dead, Id.
in heaven, as opp. to earth, οἱ ἄνω θεοί the gods above, Lat. superi, Id.
generally of position, ἄνω καθῆσθαι to sit in the upper quarter of the city, i. e. the Pnyx, Dem.; ἡ ἄνω βουλή, i. e. the Areopagus, Plut.
geographically, on the north, northward, Hdt.
inward from the coast, Id., Xen.; ὁ ἄνω βασιλεύς the king of Persia, Hdt.
of Time, formerly, of old, Plat., etc.
above, like Lat. supra, in referring to a passage, Id.
of tones in the voice, Plut.
ἄνω καὶ κάτω, up and down, to and fro, Eur., Ar., etc.
upside down, topsy-turvy, Lat. susque deque, τὰ μὲν ἄνω κάτω θήσω, τὰ δὲ κάτω ἄνω Hdt.; ἄνω τε καὶ κάτω στρέφων Aesch., etc.
as prep. with gen. above, Hdt.
comp. ἀνωτέρω, absol. higher, Aesch.; further, Hdt.
c. gen. above, beyond, Id.
Sup. ἀνωτάτω highest, Id., etc.
anything raised from the ground; the upper floor of a house, used as a granary, Xen.; as a dining-room, Lat. coenaculum, NTest.

entry.etym: The verb ἄνωγα is a perfect form with present sense. The pluperfect is used with imperfect sense.
entry.sense: to command, order, also to advise, desire, urge:— c. acc. pers. et inf., σιωπᾶν λαὸν ἀνώγει bade the people keep silence, Il.; also c. dat. pers., Od.; c. acc. pers., without inf., θυμὸς ἄνωγέ με my spirit bids me, Hom.
free from pain, Soph.
act. allaying pain, Anth.
adv. of place from above, from on high, Hdt., Trag., etc.; ὕδατος ἄνωθεν γενομένου, i. e. rain, Thuc.: from the upper country, from inland, Id.
= ἄνω, above, on high, Trag.; οἱ ἄν. the living, opp. to οἱ κάτω, Aesch.:—c. gen., Hdt.
of Time, from the beginning, Plat., Dem.:— by descent, Theocr.; τὰ ἄν. first principles, Plat.
over again, anew, NTest.
to push up, push off from shore, Od.
Mid. to push back from oneself, to repel, repulse, Hdt.
unlooked for, Od.
unlooked for, unexpected, Il., Mosch.
indestructible, Plat.; epic ἀν-όλεθρος having escaped ruin, Il.
unevenness, Plat., etc.
of persons, irregularity, Aeschin.
uneven, irregular, Plat.: τὸ ἀν. unevenness of ground, Thuc.
of fortune, Id.
without oath, Hdt.
unsworn, not bound by oath, Eur.; θεῶν ἀνώμοτος without swearing by the gods, Id.
not sworn to, εἰρήνη Dem.
nameless, indescribable, ineffable, Eur., Ar.
without name, nameless, Od., Hdt., etc.
nameless, inglorious, Pind., Eur., Plat.
untimeliness, ἀν. τοῦ ἔτεος the bad season of the year, Hdt.
Dep to howl aloud, Anth.
Sup. adj. formed from ἄνω, topmost, Hdt.
upper, inland, NTest.
higher, Arist.
unprofitable, useless, Aesch., Soph., etc.
hurtful, prejudicial, Thuc.; τινι to one, Plat.: adv. -λῶς, Arist.
unprofitable, useless, Soph.; τινι to one, Aesch.
not fortified, Xen.
inhospitable, of persons, Hes., Plat.; of places, Soph., Eur.:—comp. and Sup. -ώτερος, -ώτατος, Eur.
sc. πόντος, the Axine, afterwards called the Euxine (Euxeinus qui nunc Axenus ille fuit Ov.), Pind., Eur.
unhewn, unwrought, Soph., Anth.
worth admiring, admirable, Xen.
worth hearing, Xen.
worth listening to, Xen.
the worth or value of a thing, c. gen., Hdt., Eur.; money-value, price, amount, Hdt.; τῆς ἀξίας τιμᾶσθαι to estimate the penalty at the real amount, Plat.; κατ’ ἀξίαν τῆς οὐσίας Xen.
of persons, worth, reputation, rank, Thuc., etc.

generally, a man's due, his deserts, τὴν ἀξίαν λαμβάνειν, τῆς ἀξίας τυγχάνειν to get one's deserts, Hdt., Ar.; κατ’ ἀξίαν according to desert, duly, Eur., Plat.; παρὰ τὴν ἀξίαν, οὐ κατ’ ἀξίαν Thuc., Dem.
worth telling, Hdt.
praiseworthy, Xen.
worthy of love, Xen.
an axe-head, Il.: battle-axe. Id.: generally, an axe, Xen., NTest.
worth living for, Xen.
capable of work, Xen.
enviable, Plut.
wonder-worthy, Xen.
well worth seeing, Hdt., Xen.
worthy of lamentation, Eur.
worthy of one's society, Plat.
worth getting, Xen.
worthy of mention, noteworthy, Hdt., Plat., etc.; πόλεμος ἀξιολογώτατος Thuc.:— adv. -γως, Xen.
of persons, of note, important, Thuc.
worthy to be deemed happy, Xen.
a match for another in battle or war, τινι Hdt., Thuc.; πρός τινα Plut.: absol., Hdt., etc.
c. inf. sufficient in strength or number to do a thing, Id. adv. -χως, Plut.
worthy of mention, Plat., Xen.; shapely, beautiful, Manetho.
worthy of victory, Xen.; c. inf., ἀξιονικότερος ἔχειν τοῦτο τὸ κράτος more worthy to hold this power, Hdt.
lamentable, Eur.
trustworthy, Plat., Dem.; εἴς τι in a thing, Xen.
becoming, goodly, Xen.
worth seeing, Luc.
worth considering, Xen.
worthy of zealous endeavours, Xen.

entry.etym: ἄγω IV, and so properly weighing as much.
entry.sense: weighing as much, of like value, worth as much as, c. gen., Il., Hdt.; οὐδ’ ἑνὸς ἄξιοί εἰμεν Ἕκτορος we are not worth one Hector, Il.; πάντων ἄξιον ἦμαρ, Lat. instar omnium, Id.; πολλοῦ ἄξιος worth much, Xen.; πλείστου ἄξιον, quantivis pretii, Thuc.; so, παντός, τοῦ παντὸς ἄξιον Plat.; λόγου ἄξιος, = ἀξιόλογος, Hdt., etc.:—opp. to these are οὐδενὸς ἄξ. Theogn.; ὀλίγου, σμικροῦ ἄξ. Plat., etc.
c. dat. pers., σοὶ δ’ ἄξιόν ἐστιν ἀμοιβῆς ’tis worth a return to thee, i. e. will bring thee a return, Od.; πολλοῦ or πλείστου ἄξιον εἶναί τινι Xen., etc.
absol. worthy, goodly, of persons and things, Od., etc.; in attic it sometimes has an opposite sense, of a proper value, cheap, Ar.
of things, deserved, meet, due, δίκη Soph.; χάρις Xen.
sufficient for, c. gen., Dem.

worthy of, deserving, meet for, c. gen. rei, φυγῆς, γέλωτος Eur.; c. gen. pers., ποιεῖν ἄξια οὔτε ὑμῶν οὔτε πατέρων Thuc.:—c. gen. rei et dat. pers., ἡμῖν δ’ Ἀχιλλεὺς ἄξιος τιμῆς is worthy of honour at our hands, Eur.; πολλῶν ἀγαθῶν ἄξιος ὑμῖν Ar.
c. inf., πεφάσθαι ἄξιος worthy to be killed, Il.; ἄξιός εἰμι πληγὰς λαβεῖν I deserve a flogging, Ar.

ἄξιόν [ἐστι] ’tis meet, fit, due, Il., Hdt.; c. dat. pers. et inf., τῆι πόλει ἄξιον ξυλλαβεῖν τὸν ἄνδρα ’tis meet for the city, is her duty, to arrest the man, Ar.:—the inf. is sometimes omitted, ἄξιον γὰρ Ἑλλάδι ’tis meet in the eyes of Hellas [so to do], Id.
adv. ἀξίως, c. gen., worthily of, Hdt.:—absol., Soph.
worthy of being general, Xen.
worthy of being brought in evidence, credible, Xen.
worth loving, Xen.
worthy of a thing, and so,
absol., like ἀξιόλογος, note-worthy, considerable, notable, Hdt., Thuc.
serviceable, sufficient, αἰτίη Hdt.; ἀξ. ἐγγυηταί trustworthy, substantial, Plat.
c. inf. able, sufficient to do, Hdt., Eur., etc.
c. gen. rei, worthy, deserving of, Hdt., Dem.
to think or deem worthy of a thing, whether of reward, Eur., Xen.; or of punishment, Hdt., Plat.:— Pass. to be thought worthy, τινός Hdt., Eur., etc.
c. acc. pers. to esteem, honour, Trag.
c. acc. pers. et inf. to think one worthy to do or be, Eur., etc.:—Pass., Aesch., etc.
to think fit, expect, require, demand that, Lat. postulare, ἀξ. τινα ἐλθεῖν Hdt., etc.
c. inf. only, ἀξ. κομίζεσθαι, τυγχάνειν to think one has a right to receive, expect to receive, Thuc.:—Pass. to be required to do, Dem.

to think fit, expect, consent, resolve, ἀξιῶ θανεῖν Soph.; εἴ τις ἀξιοῖ μαθεῖν if he deigns to learn, Aesch.:—so in Mid., ἀξιοῦσθαι μέλειν to deign to care for, Id., etc.; also as a real Mid., οὐκ ἀξιούμενος not deeming himself worthy, Hdt.
to claim, νικᾶν ἠξίουν claimed the victory, Thuc.: absol. to make a claim, Id.
to hold an opinion, Dem.; ἐν τῶι τοιῶιδε ἀξιοῦντι in such a state of opinion, Thuc.
that of which one is thought worthy, an honour, Eur.; γάμων ἀξ. honour of marriage, Id.
honour, reputation, Lat. dignitas, Eur., Thuc.
rank, position, Thuc.:—of things, worth, quality, Id.
that which is thought fit, a decision, purpose, Soph., Dem.
in Mathematics, a self evident theorem, an axiom, Arist.
a thinking worthy, Hdt.
a being thought worthy, reputation, Thuc.
a demand or claim, Id.
a thinking fit, an opinion, principle, maxim, Id.
ἀξ. τῶν ὀνομάτων the meaning of words, Id.
without carved images, Luc.
belonging to the axle, Anth.
not welded together by the hammer:— metaph. of rowers, not trained to keep time, Thuc.
with no timber, timberless, ἄξυλος ὕλη a coppice, brushwood, Il.:—others take it to be a wood from which no timber has been cut, a thick wood.
without wood, Hdt.
an axle, Lat. axis, Il., etc.
οἱ ἄξονες, the wooden tablets of Solon's laws, made to turn upon an axis, Plut.

entry.etym: Perh. from α copul., ὁδός; cf. ἀκόλουθος.
entry.sense: a servant, attendant, Aesch.
song, a singing, whether the art of song, Hom.; or the act of singing, song, Il.
the thing sung, a song, Hom., etc.
the subject of song, Od.
to sing, Od.
sung of, famous in song, Hdt.: in bad sense, notorious, infamous, Il.
a lyric poet, Anth.
fighting with verses, Anth.
one busied with song, a poet, Anth.
a singer, minstrel, bard, Lat. vates, Hom., Hdt.; c. gen., χρησμῶν ἀοιδός Eur.; of the cock, Theocr.
as fem. songstress, of the nightingale, Hes.; of the Sphinx, Soph.
an enchanter, Lat. incantator, Id.
as adj. tuneful, musical, ὄρνις ἀοιδοτάτα Eur.
inspiring song, Anth.
uninhabited, Hdt.
houseless, Dem.
houseless, homeless, Hes., Soph., etc.
ἄοικος εἰσοίκησις a homeless, i. e. miserable, home, Soph.
without wine, ἄοινοι χοαί, such as were offered to the Erinyes, Aesch.; hence Soph. calls the Erinyes ἄοινοι;—ἀοίνοις ἐμμανεῖς θυμώμασιν frantic with sober, deliberate rage, Soph.
of men, drinking no wine, sober, Xen.; of a place, having none, Id.
without hesitation, untiring, Hes., Soph., Thuc.
all together, in throngs, shoals or crowds, Hom., Soph., etc.
to gather together, Il.:—Pass. to come together, assemble, Id.
of things, to gather together, heap up, Anth.
without shields (ὅπλα), without heavy armour, Thuc., etc.: generally, unarmed, Plat.; ἅρμα ἄοπλ. a chariot without scythes, Xen.
unseen, not to be seen, invisible, Plat., etc.
act. without sight, Luc.
a defect in the passion of anger, "lack of gall", Arist.
incapable of anger, Arist.
without boundaries, Thuc.
undefined, indefinite, Dem., etc.
without birds, Soph.
Ἄορνος, ὁ, lake Avernus, Strab.

entry.etym: ᾰ in ἄορ; but in trisyll. cases also ᾱ.
entry.sense: a hanger, sword, Hom.: he also uses a masc. acc. pl., ἄορας.

entry.etym: lengthened form of ἀείρω, only in aor.1 pass. part. ἀορτηθείς
entry.sense: suspended, Anth.
a strap to hang anything to, a sword-belt, Hom.: a knapsack-strap, Od.
to help, τινί Mosch.
an assistant, helper, aider, Hom.
unwounded, unhurt, Il.
undisturbed, calm, Luc.
a report, as of an ambassador, Dem.
a narrative, recital, Thuc., Plat.

of a messenger, to bring tidings, report, announce, τί τινι Il., Hdt., etc.; τι πρός τινα Aesch., etc.; ἀπ. τι οἴκαδε to carry a report home, Plat.:—absol., πάλιν ἀπ. to bring back tidings, report in answer, Od.:—Pass., ἐξ ὧν ἀπηγγέλλετο as he was reported, Dem.; c. part., ἀπηγγέλθη ἐκκεκλεμμένος was reported to have been stolen away, Hdt.
of a speaker or writer, to relate, narrate, Id., attic
a messenger, Anth.

entry.etym: properly the imperat of ἀπάγω, in intr. sense.
entry.sense: away! begone! hands off! Lat. apage! Eur., Ar.
not firm or stiff, of Persian caps, Hdt.
esp of paying tribute, Hdt.
failure of strength, exhaustion, Plut., Luc.
one must give up, Luc.
to forbid, ἀπ. τινὰ μὴ ποιεῖν τι Hdt., attic; τινά Xen.
to dissuade, Hdt.

intr. to bid farewell to, c. dat., ἀπαγ. τῶι πολέμωι to give up, renounce war, Plat.; c. part. to give up doing, Xen.:—absol. to give up, fail, sink, Id.; of things, τὰ ἀπαγορεύοντα worn out and useless, Id.
to become wild or savage, Soph.
to strangle, Anth.
to strangle, throttle, Od., Ar.; to choke with anger, Ar.:—Mid. and Pass. to hang oneself, to be hanged, Hdt., attic: to be ready to choke, Ar.
a leading away, Xen.
payment of tribute, Hdt.
as attic law-term, a process by which a person caught in the act (ἐπ’ αὐτοφώρωι) might be arrested and brought before the Magistrates, Oratt.: — the written complaint laid before the Court, Lys.
to lead away, carry off, Od., Trag.:— Mid. to take away for or with oneself, Hdt., Trag.:— Pass., ἐς ὀξὺ ἀπηγμένος brought to a point, tapering off, Hdt.
intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν) to retire, withdraw, march away, Id., Xen.; cf. ἄπαγε.
to bring back, bring home, Hom., attic
to return what one owes, render, pay, τὸν φόρον Ar., Thuc.
to arrest and carry off, παρά τινα Hdt.:—esp. as attic lawterm, to bring before a magistrate and accuse, Dem.:— then, to carry off to prison, Plat., etc.
to lead away from the subject, Id., etc.
to sing out of tune, be out of tune, Plat.
metaph. to dissent, ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων Id.
to wander away, ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐρωτήματος Id.
poet. for ἀπαίρω, to depart, Eur.:—Mid. to depart from, c. gen., Il.
to aim at immortality, Plat., Arist.
want of sensation, insensibility, Arist.
not suffering or having suffered, without experience of a thing, c. gen., Theogn., Hdt., attic:—absol., Id.attic
without passion or feeling: — adv., ἀπαθῶς ἔχειν to be without feeling, Plut.
Pass. to be changed into a poplar, Strab.
without teacher or guide, Arist.: uneducated, untaught, τινος in a thing, Id.
want of education, Thuc., Plat.
ignorance, boorishness, coarseness, Plat., etc.
c. gen., ἀπαιδευσίαι ὀργῆς from want of control over passion, Thuc.
uneducated, Eur., Plat.:— c. gen. uninstructed in a thing, Xen.
ignorant, boorish, coarse, Eur., Plat.
adv., ἀπαιδεύτως ἔχειν to be without education, Eur.
childlessness, Hdt., Soph.
to clear away clouds from the sky, Ar.
to take away, withdraw, τί τινος Od.: to pluck off, Mosch.
to perplex, confound, Eur.
cheating, fraud, personified in Ar.
to lift off, carry off, take away, to remove from, τί τινος Eur.: absol., Hdt.

to lead away a sea or land force, Id.:—intr. (sub. ναῦς, στρατόν, etc.), to sail or march away, depart, Id., attic; c. gen., ἀπαίρειν χθονός to depart from the land, Eur.: c. acc. cogn., ἀπ. πρεσβείαν to set out on an embassy, Dem.
childless, Hdt.; τὰς ἄπαιδας οὐσίας her childless estate, Soph.:—c. gen., ἄπ. ἔρσενος γόνου without male heirs, Hdt.; τέκνων ἄπαιδα Eur.; etc.
Νυκτὸς παῖδες ἄπαιδες children of Night, yet children none, Aesch.
to spring from aheight, c. gen., Il.
to dart away, Soph.
to refuse through shame, Plat.
to demand back, demand, Hdt.:— ἀπ. τί τινα to demand something of one, Id., attic; ἀπ. ὅπλα τοῦ πατρός Soph.; also, χάριν ἀπ. τινα Plat.
Pass., of things, to be demanded in payment, Hdt.
of persons, to have demanded of one, ἀπαιτεῖσθαι εὐεργεσίαν Xen.
a demanding back, Hdt.; ἀπ. ποιεῖσθαι to make a formal demand, Dem.
only in pres. part., = ἀπαιτέω, to demand back, χρήματα Od.
Pass. to hang down from above, hang suspended, hover about, Hes.
Pass. to be finished off, highly finished, Plat., Isocr.
as Mid. to finish off, Anth., Luc.
not trained in the palaestra, unskilled in wrestling, Anth.: awkward, Cic.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use, v. ἄλαλκε
entry.sense: to ward off something from one, τί τινος Hom.; epic inf. ἀπαλαλκέμεν, Theocr.
without hands, helpless, good for naught, Il.
impracticable, reckless, lawless, ἔρδειν ἔργ’ ἀπάλαμνα Solon.; ἀπάλαμνόν τι πάσχειν Eur.
like ἀπάλαμνος, helpless, Hes., Pind. [ᾱπ - metri grat.]
Pass. to go astray, wander, Hes.
to feel no more pain at a thing, τι Thuc.; ἀπ. τὸ πένθος to put away sorrow, Plut.
to wipe off, expunge from a register, Dem.; ἀπ. τι to cancel it, Aeschin.
to ward something off from a person, τί τινος Il.
reversely to keep a person from suffering something, τινά τινος Od.
Mid. to defend oneself, ἀπαλέξασθαί [τι] Soph.
to speak the whole truth, Xen., in Mid.
Dep to heal thoroughly, Il.
deliverance, release, relief from a thing, riddance of it, πόνων, ξυμφορᾶς Aesch., Soph., etc.
absol. a divorce, Eur.
(from Pass.) a going away, a means of getting away, an escape, departure, Hdt.; ἡ ἀπ. ἀλλήλων separation from one another, of combatants, Thuc.
ἀπ. τοῦ βίου departure from life, Xen.; ψυχῆς ἀπὸ σώματος Plat.
one must release from, τινά τινος Plut.
(from Pass.) one must withdraw from, get rid of, τινός Plat.
to wish to be delivered from or get rid of, τινός Thuc.

entry.etym: The middle future ἀπαλλάξομαι has a passive sense.
entry.sense: Act.
to set free, release, deliver a person from a thing, τινά τινος Hdt., attic
to put away or remove a thing from a person, τί τινος Eur., etc.
c. acc. only, to put away, remove, dismiss, τι or τινα Id., Thuc., etc.: to destroy, ἑαυτόν Plut.
intr. to get off, come off, end so and so, οὐκ ὡς ἤθελε Hdt.; κακῶς ἀπ. Plat.; χαίρων Hdt.:—c. gen. to depart from, βίου Eur.
Pass. and Mid. to be set free or released from a thing, get rid of it, c. gen., Hdt., attic
to get off, καλῶς Eur.; ἀζήμιος Ar.
absol. to be acquitted, Dem.
to remove, depart from, ἐκ χώρης Hdt., etc.; γῆς Eur.
ἀπαλλάσσεσθαι τοῦ βίου to depart from life, Id.; and without τοῦ βίου, to depart, die, Id., Thuc., etc.
ἀπ. λέχους to be divorced, Eur.
ἀπ. τοῦ διδασκάλου to leave school, Plat.
ἀπ. ἐκ παίδων to become a man, Aeschin.
πολλὸν ἀπηλλαγμένος τινός far inferior to him, Hdt.

to leave off or cease from τῶν μακρῶν λόγων Soph.; σκωμμάτων Ar.:—absol. to have done, give over, cease, Soph., Plat.:—c. part., εἰπὼν ἀπαλλάγηθι speak and be done with it, Plat.; also in part. with a Verb, οὐκοῦν ἀπαλλαχθεὶς ἄπει; have done and begone, Soph.
to depart from enmity, i. e. to be reconciled, Plat.
to estrange, alienate, Aeschin., Arist.
alienation, Arist.
to thresh out, σῖτος ἀπηλοημένος (perf. pass. part.) Dem.:—metaph. to bruise, crush, Il.
soft-haired, Eur.
soft to the touch, tender, of the body, Hom., Soph.; of fresh fruit, Hdt.; of tender meat, Xen.
metaph. soft, gentle, ἁπαλὸν γελάσαι to laugh gently, Od.; ἁπ. δίαιτα soft, delicate, Plat.
softness, tenderness, Xen., etc.
well-fed, plump, Il.
soft-hearted, Anth.
soft-skinned, Hhymn., Hes., etc.
to soften, Xen.
to make tender, τοὺς πόδας Id.
to bring to naught, Anth.
to cut off, Od., Soph.
to make abortive, Plut.
intr. to miscarry, Id.
to blunt the edge of a sword: metaph., τεθηγμένον τοί μ’ οὐκ ἀπαμβλύνεις λόγωι Aesch.:—Pass. to be blunted, lose its edge, Id., Plat.
to reply, answer, Hom.
to deprive one of share in a thing:—Pass. to be bereft, τινός of a thing, Hes.
Pass. to be neglected utterly, perf. part. ἀπημελημένος Hdt., Soph.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use
entry.sense: to fail utterly, Soph.
to keep off, ward off, τί τινι something for (i. e. from) another, Il.; τί τινος Luc.: c. acc. to ward off, κακά Hdt.; ἀπ. τὸν βάρβαρον to repulse him, Id.
Mid. to keep off from oneself, to drive back, repel, τινά Od., Hdt.
absol. to defend or protect oneself, Hom.
to disown, reject, Hom., Aesch.
to have the effrontery to do or say a thing, Plat.
to deny shamelessly, Dem.
to use quite up, utterly consume, Thuc.
Pass. to become manly, come to maturity, Eur., Luc.
afar off, far away, Il.
prep. c. gen. far away from, aloof from, τῶν ἄλλων θεῶν Id.; ἀπ. θεῶν without their knowledge, Id.
out from, issuing from, Id.
to leave off blooming, fade, wither, Plat., Luc.
to pluck off flowers, Lat. decerpere: metaph., ματαίαν γλῶσσαν ἀπανθίσαι to cull the flowers of idle talk, i. e. talk at random, Aesch.:—Mid. to gather honey from flowers, to cull the best of, Luc.
to broil on the coals, Ar.
to burn to a cinder, Luc.
far from man:
of places, desert, desolate, Aesch.
of men, inhuman, Plut.
to make rise up and depart, send away, τὴν στρατιήν Hdt., Thuc.
Pass., with aor2 and perf. act., and fut. mid., to arise and go away, depart, leave one's country, emigrate, Hdt., Thuc.
everywhere, Eur.
from all sides, Luc.
everywhere, Luc.
to every place, Plut.
everywhere, Eur.

to move from a place to meet a person; then, generally, to meet, encounter, τινί Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—absol., ὁ ἀεὶ ἀπαντῶν anyone that meets you, any chance person, Plat.:—often with a prep., ἀπ. τινι εἰς τόπον to come or go to a place to meet him, meet him at a place, Hdt.: —without a dat. pers., to present oneself at a place, Xen.
often in hostile sense, to meet in battle, Eur.; ἀπ. Ἀθηναίοις ἐς Τάραντα Thuc.: to oppose in any way, Plat.:—absol. to present oneself in arms, Eur.
as a law term, to meet in open court, Plat., Dem.:— absol. to appear in court, Dem.
ἀπ. εἰς or πρός τι to enter upon a thing, attempt or approach it, Plat., Aeschin.; to have recourse to . . , Dem.
of things, to come upon one, happen to one, Eur., Plat., etc.
a meeting, Eur.
everywhere, Hom.
right opposite, Xen.; c. gen., Dem.
right opposite, ἐς τὴν ἀπ. ἀκτήν Hdt.
to draw off water from a ship's hold: metaph., ἀπ. ὕβρισμα χθονός Eur.:—c. acc. only, to draw off, Aesch.: to lighten, lessen, πόνους Id.; βάρος ψυχῆς Eur.
to finish entirely, νῆες ἀπήνυσαν (sc. ὁδόν) the ships performed the voyage, Od.
all at once, mostly in pl., Ar.
in general, Luc.
to disclaim as unworthy, disown, τι or τινα Thuc.
ἀπ. τί τινος to deem a thing unworthy of one, Luc.:—Mid. to banish from one's house, Aesch.

entry.etym: α copul. and root παγ, πήγνυμι, cf. lat. simplex.
entry.sense: once, once only, once for all, like Lat. semel, Od., Hdt., attic
c. gen., ἅπ. τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ once in the year, Hdt.
without any notion of number, after εἴπερ, ἤν, ἐπεί, ὡς, ὅταν, like Lat. ut semel, εἴπερ ἐσπείσω γ’ ἅπαξ if once you have made a treaty, Ar.; ὡς ἅπαξ ἤρξατο once he had begun, Xen.
with no grandfather: metaph. unfathered by a thing, Aesch.
not passing over to another, not passing away, unchangeable, NTest.
of persons, not to be moved by prayer, inexorable, Plat., etc.:—adv. -τως, Thuc.
of punishments, not to be averted by prayers, inevitable, unmerciful, Dinarch.
uncovered: adv. -τως, undisguisedly, Plat.
unsummoned, volunteering, Thuc.
unchanged, unchangeable, Plut.
not to be persuaded, inconsolable, ἀθυμία Plut.
inexorable, Aesch.
without preparation, unprepared, Thuc., Xen.
to strike off, cut off, Il., Hdt.: to sweep off from the deck of a ship, ἀπὸ τῆς νηός Hdt.; ἀπὸ τοῦ καταστρώματος Thuc.
to be disagreeable to, τινί Thuc.
Mid. to shew displeasure, Il.
inconsolable, Plut.
not to be advised or controlled, Id.
unmaidenly, unfitting a maiden, Eur., in neut. pl. as adv.
no more a maid, Theocr.; νύμφην ἄνυμφον παρθένον τ’ ἀπάρθενον "virgin wife and widow'd maid, " Eur.
to count over, reckon up, Xen.
to reckon or pay back, repay, Id.
a counting over, recounting, Thuc.
to suffice, be sufficient, Trag.
to be contented, acquiesce, Aesch.
to deny utterly, deny, Hdt.; followed by μή and inf., Eur., etc.: ἀπαρνηθῆναί τι to refuse, reject, Thuc.
fut. ἀπαρνηθήσεται in pass. sense, shall be denied or refused, Soph., NTest.
denying utterly, ἄπαρνός ἐστι μὴ νοσέειν he denies that he is ill, Hdt.: c. gen., ἄπαρνος οὐδενός denying nothing, Soph.
not speaking freely, Luc.
to hang up from, ἀπ. δέρην to strangle, Eur.:—Pass. to hang loose, Xen.
metaph. to make dependent upon, ἐξ ἑαυτοῦ Luc.
to detach, separate, τί τινος Dem.:—Pass., ἀπηρτημένοι detached, disunited, Id.
intr. in Act. to remove oneself, go away, Thuc.
to make even, move regularly, Aesch.
to get ready, complete, Arist.
intr. to be even or exact, Id.
an even number or sum, Hdt.
a sale of goods by auction, Plut.
completely, of numbers, exactly, just, Hdt.
of Time, from now, from this time, henceforth, Ar., NTest.
just now, even now, NTest.
completion, NTest.
to draw off, skim off cream, Hdt.: metaph. to draw off the force of a thing, in verb. adj. ἀπαρυστέον, Ar.
mostly in pl. ἀπαρχαί, the beginning of a sacrifice, the primal offering (of hairs cut from the forehead), Eur.
the firstlings for sacrifice, first-fruits, Hdt., attic:—metaph., ἀπαρχὴ τῆς σοφίας Plat.
Dep.

to make a beginning, esp. in sacrifice, τρίχας ἀπάρχεσθαι to begin the sacrifice with the hair, i. e. by cutting off the hair from the forehead and throwing it into the fire, Il.: to begin the sacrificial rites, Od.
c. gen. to cut off part of a thing, to offer it, to offer part of a thing, Hdt., Eur.
to offer the firstlings or first-fruits, Hdt., Ar.
metaph. to take as the first-fruits, as the choice or best, Theocr.
ἀπάρχω Act., to be the first, be leader, dance, Anth.
to gasp away life, Eur.
quite all, the whole, and in pl. all together, Hom., etc.
with an Adj., ἀργύρεος ἅπας all silver, i.e. of massive silver, Od.; ἅπαν κακόν altogether evil, Ar.
in sing., like πᾶς, everyone, Lat. unusquisque, πᾶν everything, unumquodque, Hdt., Attic
an abstaining from food, a fast, Ar.
not having eaten, fasting, Il.: c. gen., ἄπαστος ἐδητύος ἠδὲ ποτῆτος without having tasted meat or drink, Od.
to flash forth, Luc.
to leave one no leisure, Luc.:—Pass. to be wholly occupied, Id.
detention by business, Strab.
to cheat, trick, outwit, beguile, Hom., etc.: Pass. to be deceived, Soph.; ἀπατᾶσθαι, ὡς . . , to be deceived into thinking that . . , Plat.
apart, aloof, Il.
prep. c. gen. far away from, ὁμίλου Id.
a cheat, rogue, quack, Plat., Xen.
guileful, wily, ἀπατήλια εἰδώς skilled in wiles, Od.; ἀπ. βάζειν Id.
a trick, fraud, deceit, Il.: a stratagem, Thuc.: in pl. wiles, Hom.
guile, fraud, deceit, treachery, Hdt., attic
fraudulent, Xen.
untrodden, Anth.
to dishonour greatly, Il.
the Apatouria, a festival at Athens in the month Pyanepsion, at which the grown-up youths (κοῦροι) were enrolled in the φρατρίαι, Oratt.
entry.etym: Prob. from πατρία, = φρατρία, with α euphon.

entry.sense: without father, fatherless, Soph., Eur.: c. gen., ἀπ. ἐμοῦ not having me for a father, Soph.
to beam forth, Call. (in Mid.)
efflux of light, effulgence, NTest.
to forbid, Soph.; ἀπ. μή c. inf. to prohibit from doing a thing, Id., Eur.
to decline, shun, πόνους Eur.: to deny, renounce, νεῖκος Theocr.
to be wanting towards, fail, φίλοισι Eur.; ἀπ. ὑπὸ λιμοῦ Luc.
Mid. to speak or act boldly, speak out, Plat.
to return the same day, Xen.
to take away or wrest from, rob of, c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, ἄμφω θυμὸν ἀπηύρα Il.; τοὺς μὲν τεύχε’ ἀπηύρα Id.
c. gen. pers., κούρην Ἀχιλῆος ἀπούρας Id.
c. dat. pers., πολέσσιν θυμὸν ἀπηύρα Id.
Mid., ἀπουράμενοι ψυχάς having lost their lives, Hes.
to receive good or ill, to enjoy or suffer, Id., Eur. Cf. ἐπαυρίσκομαι.
unceasing, never-ending, Aesch., Soph.
not to be stopped or assuaged, insatiable, δίψα Thuc.
c. gen. never ceasing from, γόων Eur.
to go of one's own accord, desert, Thuc.
like ἀπατάω, to cheat, beguile, Od.
Mid. to be grievous, τινι Sapph.
exclamation, like Latin and English ah! ἆ δειλέ, ἆ δειλώ, ἆ δειλοί, Hom.; doubled ἆ ἆ Aesch.
unshod, Aesch.
even, level, flat, Hdt., Thuc., etc.: —ἄπεδον, ου, τό, a plain, flat surface, Hdt.
to disaccustom, ἀπ. τινὰ μὴ ποιεῖν Aeschin.; part. perf. ἀπειθικώς, Plut.
to look away from other things at a thing, and so simply to look at, ἔς or πρός τι Thuc.
disobedience, Xen., NTest.
to be disobedient, refuse compliance, Aesch.; c. dat. to disobey, Eur., Plat.
disobedient, τοῖς νόμοις Plat.; of ships, τοῖς κυβερνήταις ἀπειθεστέραι less obedient to them, Thuc.
act. not persuasive, incredible, Theogn.
to form from a model, to express, copy, of painters, Xen., etc.:—Pass. to become like, resemble, ἀπεικασθεὶς θεῶι in a god's likeness, Eur.
to express by a comparison, Plat.:— Pass. to be copied or expressed by likeness, Id.
to liken, compare with, τί τινι Eur., Plat.
ὡς ἀπεικάσαι as one may guess, to conjecture, Soph.
one must represent, Xen.
to represent in a statue, Anth.
to force back; mostly in Pass., ἐς ἀπορίην ἀπειλημένος forced into great difficulties, Hdt.
to hold out either in the way of promise or threat:
in good sense, to promise, ἠπείλησεν ἄνακτι ῥέξειν ἑκατόμβην Il.; ἠπείλησας εἶναι ἀρίστους didst profess that they were best, Od.
commonly in bad sense, to threaten, Lat. minari, absol. or c. dat. pers., Hom., etc.; c. acc. cogn., ἠπείλησεν μῦθον spake a threatening speech, Il.:—also in Mid., NTest.
c. acc. of the thing threatened, θάνατον ἀπ. τινι Hdt.
dependent clauses added in inf. fut., γέρας ἀφαιρήσεσθαι ἀπειλεῖς Il., etc.; attic also in inf. aor.:—also ἀπ. ὅτι . . , ὡς . . , attic
Pass. ἀπειλοῦμαι, of persons, to be terrified by threats, Xen.
mostly in pl., boastful promises, boasts, Il.
in bad sense, threats, Hom., etc.:—in sg. a threat of punishment, Soph., Thuc.
of or for threatening, λόγοι Hdt.
a threatener, boaster, Il.
to be away or far from, τινος Od., etc.; ἀπό τινος Thuc.: c. dat. to be wanting, φίλοισιν Eur., etc.
absol. to be away or absent, and of things, to be wanting, Soph., etc.; of the dead, Eur.

to go away, depart, Od., etc.; οὐκ ἄπει; = ἄπιθι, be gone, Soph.; ἀπ. πάλιν to return, Xen.; ἄπιτε ἐς ὑμέτερα return to your homes, Hdt.; ἄπιμεν οἴκαδε Ar.; ἐπ’ οἴκου Thuc. —of the Nile, to recede, Hdt.; ἀπ. ἐπί τι to go in quest of a thing, Xen.

entry.etym: for εἶπον orig. had a digamma ϝεῖπον
entry.sense: to speak out, tell out, declare, μῦθον, etc., Hom.; ῥῆσιν Hdt.
to deny, refuse, Il., Plat.
to forbid, ἀπ. τινι μὴ ποιεῖν to forbid one to do, tell him not to do, Hdt., attic:—Pass., ἀπείρηταί τινι ποιεῖν τι it is forbidden him to do, Hdt.; τὸ ἀπειρημένον a forbidden thing, Id.

to renounce, disown, give up, μῆνιν Il.; τὴν συμμαχίην Hdt.; ἀπ. τὴν στρατηγίαν to resign it, Xen.:—Pass., αἱ σπονδαὶ οὐκ ἀπείρηντο had not been renounced, Thuc.:—so in Mid., ἀπείπασθαι ὄψιν to avert a vision (by sacrifice), Hdt.

intr. to give up, to be worn out, fail, sink from exhaustion, Soph., etc.; ἀπεῖπεν φάτις the word failed, was unfulfilled, Aesch.:—c. dat. pers. to fail or be wanting to one, οὐκ ἀπειρηκὼς φίλοις Eur.:—c. dat. rei, ἀπειρηκότων χρήμασι, i. e. when they were bankrupt, Dem.; also, ἀπ. κακοῖς, ἄλγει to give way to, sink under them, Eur.; φέροντες ἀπεροῦσιν they will be tired of paying, Thuc., Plat.
Apeiraean, Od.; Apeire = limitless-land, an imaginary place.
incapable of being tempted by a thing, c. gen., NTest.
to keep away, keep off from, τινά τινος Il.; ῥάκεα ἀποέργαθε οὐλῆς pushed back the rags from the scar, Od.; μή σε τῆσδε γῆς ἀπειργαθῇ Soph.
to keep away from, debar from, τινά τινος Hom., attic; τινὰ ἀπό τινος Hdt.
to keep from doing, prevent, hinder, c. acc. et inf., ἀπ. τινὰ ποιεῖν or μὴ ποιεῖν τι Soph., Eur.

c. acc. to keep back, keep off, ward off, Od., Soph., etc.; absol., ἀλλ’ ἀπείργοι θεός heaven forfend! Soph.: νόμος οὐδεὶς ἀπ. no law debars, Thuc.: of the Nile, ἀπεργμένος barred or shut off from its old channel, Hdt.
to part, divide, separate, κληῒς ἀποέργει αὐχένα τε στῆθός τε Il.:—and so to bound, Hdt.
of persons travelling, ἐν ἀριστερῆι ἀπέργων ῥοίτειον keeping Rhoeteium on the left, Id.
to shut up, confine, Id.
boundless, immense, countless, Hom., Od.
from Apeire, Od.
Act., without making trial of a thing, without making an attempt upon, c. gen., Il.
without trial or experience of a thing, Hhymn., Pind. : —absol. inexperienced, Od.
pass. untried, unattempted, Il., Hdt., Dem.
want of skill, inexperience, Plat.; τινός of or in a thing, Eur.
infinity, Plat.
unused to dew, unbedewed, Eur.
without experience of evil, unused to evil, Eur. τὸ ἀπ. ignorance of evil, Thuc.
ignorance of the beautiful, want of taste, Plat.: in pl. vulgarities, Xen.
ignorant of the beautiful, without taste, tasteless, vulgar, Plat.: τὸ ἀπ., = ἀπειροκαλία, Xen. adv. -λως, Plat.
ignorant of navigation, Luc.
without trial or experience of a thing, unused to, unacquainted with, Lat. expers, c. gen., ἄθλων Theogn.; τυράννων Hdt., etc.
absol. inexperienced, ignorant, Pind., Aesch., etc.
adv., ἀπείρως ἔχειν τινός to be ignorant of a thing, Hdt.
boundless, infinite, countless, πλῆθος Hdt., Plat.
in Trag., of garments, endless, i. e. without end or outlet, inextricable, Aesch., Eur.
inexperience, Eur.
not having brought forth, virgin, Anth.
= ἄπειρος1, without experience, ignorant, Soph.
= ἄπειρος2 1, boundless, endless, countless, Hom.
= ἄπειρος2 2, without end, inextricable, δεσμοί Od.
Dep. to expect anxiously, to look for, await, NTest.
to strip off from, τί τινος Babr.
to strip off oneself, to put off, as in preparing for single combat, NTest.
to strip off for oneself, to despoil, τινα Id.
a putting off (like clothes), NTest.
Mid. to forget entirely, c. gen., only in imperat. of epic aor2 ἀπεκλελάθεσθε, Od.
prep. c. gen. away out of, Hhymn.
uncombed, Anth.
to drive away, expel from a place, τινὰ δόμων, πόλεως, Eur., etc.; ἀπὸ τόπου Xen.: ἀπ. τινά to drive away, banish, expel, Soph., Xen.
ἀπ. στρατιήν to lead away an army, Hdt.: then absol. to march or go away, depart, Id.; (sub. ἵππον) to ride away, Xen.
Pass. to be driven away, Hdt., attic:— to be excluded from a thing, Hdt., etc.
refutation: disrepute, NTest.
to refute thoroughly, Antipho.
immeasurable, Hom.: neut. as adv. immeasurably far, Il.
the enfranchisement of a slave, Aeschin.
in the condition of a freedman, Plut.
an emancipated slave, a freedman, Lat. libertus, Plat., Xen.
to emancipate a slave, Plat.
emancipation, Dem.
Laconic for ἐκκλησιάζω, Plut.
to give up in despair, to despair, NTest.; (others to hope to receive from another); to drive to despair, τινά Anth.
to spit up, vomit forth, Lat. evomere, Il.
to sell, Eur.; ἀπ. τί τινος or ἀντί τινος to sell for a thing, Xen., Eur.; ἀπ. τινὰ χθονός to smuggle one out of the country, Eur.:—Pass., ἀπεμπολώμενοι "bought and sold, " Ar.
= ἀπέναντι, the opposite shore, Hdt.
opposite, against, c. gen., NTest.
to strip one of arms, despoil one of a thing, c. dupl. acc., Il.
free from grief, Aesch.
to go into banishment for a year, Xen.
to forbid, Aesch.; ἀπ. τι to forbid it, Soph.; c. acc. et inf., ἀπ. τινὰ ποιεῖν or μὴ ποιεῖν τι Eur.:— ἀπ. τινὰ θαλάμων to order him from the chamber, Id.
to deprecate, τι Aesch.
to take out, remove, τί τινος Eur.
unreasonable, Antipho:—adv. ἀπ-εοικότως or -εικότως, unreasonably, Thuc.
not ripened, unripe, Anth.
unripe, untimely.
unrobed, clad in the tunic only, Pind.: λευκῶν φαρέων ἄπεπλος not clad in white robes, i. e. in black, Eur.
talking without end.
boundless, infinite, of space, Pind., Eur., etc.:—of Time, endless, Ar.;—of Number, countless, Plat.; generally of events, ἀπέραντον ἦν there was no end to it, Thuc.
allowing no escape, Aesch.
to finish off, turn out complete, Ar., Plat.
of a painter, to fill up with colour, express perfectly, Plat.
to finish a contract, Xen.
c. dupl. acc. to make so and so, ἀγαθὸν ἀπ. τινα Id.:—so perf. in pass. sense, ἀπειργασμένος τύραννος a finished tyrant, Plat.
a finishing off, completing, of painters, Plat.
a making, producing, Id.
a business, trade, Id.
fit for finishing, causing, c. gen., Plat.
to bring to an end, finish, Hdt.
to rest, fix, settle, τὴν ὄψιν πρός τι Luc.
intr. = Pass. to rest upon, Id.
mostly as Pass., with fut. and aor1 mid., to support oneself upon, rest upon a thing, c. dat., Xen., etc.; εἴς τι Plat.
ἀπερείσι’ ἄποιναcountless ransom.
not to be out-talked, Ar.
uncircumscribed, Plut.
free from care:— adv. -νως, unthinkingly, Ar.
unregarding, reckless of, πάντων Thuc.
inconsiderate, thoughtless, Thuc. adv. -τως; comp. -ότερον, Id.
uncircumcised, NTest.
not returning or taking heed, Soph.
to go away, be gone, Eur.: ἄπερρε away, begone, Lat. abi in malam rem, Ar.
to put away blushes, to be past blushing, Ar.

to keep off or away, c. acc., Hom.; c. acc. et gen. to keep away from, Theogn.; c. acc. et inf. to prevent one from doing, οὔτε σε κωμάζειν ἀπερύκομεν Id.; also, ἀπ. τινί τι to keep off from, Hdt.; τι ἀπό τινος Xen.:—Mid., ἀπερύκου (sc. φωνῆς) abstain from speech, Soph.
to tear off from, ῥινὸν ἀπ’ ὀστεόφιν ἐρύσαι Od.:—Mid., Anth.
to go away, depart from, c. gen., Hom., attic; ἀπό or ἐκ τόπου Thuc.
when used with εἰς, departure from one place and arrival at another is implied, ἀπ. ἐς Σάρδις Hdt., etc.
absol. to depart, Id., Thuc., etc.: to depart from life, Anth.
a thwarter, Il.
to retire or withdraw from, πολέμου Il.
loveless, unloving, ἔρως ἀπέρωτος, like γάμος ἄγαμος, Aesch.
to eat. or gnaw off, Ar., Dem.
he is gone off, Lacon. for ἀπ-εσσύη or ἀπ-εσσύθη, 3rd sg. aor1 pass. of ἀποσεύω, Xen.
a being away, absence, Hdt.
leafless, Anth.
not inquired into, unknown, Od.
act. not inquiring, ignorant, Id.
to make straight again, Plat.; χέρας δεσμοῖς ἀπ. to bind his arms straight, i. e. behind him, Soph.
to guide aright, to direct, govern, Id.; to correct, chastise, Eur.: c. inf. to direct one to do a thing, Aesch.
to be deprecated, abominable, Aesch.
to lull to sleep, Soph.
Dep. to wish a thing away, wish it may not happen, deprecate, c. acc. rei, Eur., Dem.; c. inf., ἀπ. τι γενέσθαι or μὴ γενέσθαι to pray that it may not happen, Dem.
to reject, despise, τι Aesch.
boiled down, ἀπ. χρυσός refined gold, Hdt., Thuc.
to hate utterly, detest, τινά Il.
to make utterly hateful, τι Od.

to be hated, incur hatred, be roused to hatred, Od.; c. dat. pers. to be or become hateful to one, Il., Hdt.; ἀπ. πρός τινα to be hateful in his eyes, Eur.:—c. dat. rei, to be hated for a thing, Plat.
Dep., in causal sense, λόγοι ἀπεχθανόμενοι language that causes hatred, Xen.
felt towards another, πρός τινα Eur., etc.
felt by others towards one, enmity, odium, opp. to χάρις (popularity), and in pl. enmities, Plat., Dem.; δι’ ἀπεχθείας τινὶ ἐλθεῖν to be hated by him, Aesch.
an object of hate, Eur.
hateful, hostile, Soph., Theocr., etc.: adv., ἀπεχθῶς ἔχειν τινι to be at enmity with him, Dem.
to keep off or away from, τινά or τί τινος Il.: absol. to keep off, Eur.
to keep apart, part, κληῖδες ἀπ’ ὤμων αὐχέν’ ἔχουσιν the collar-bones part the neck from the shoulders, Il.
Mid., ἀπὸ χεῖρας ἔχεσθαί τινος (in tmesi) to hold one's hands off or away from, Od.: also, ἀπέχεσθαί τινος to hold oneself off a thing, abstain or desist from it, Hom., Hdt., etc.
c. inf., ἀπέχεσθαι ποιεῖν or μὴ ποιεῖν τι to abstain from doing a thing, Thuc., etc.
intr. in Act. to be away or far from, c. gen. loci, Id.; also, ἀπ. ἀπὸ Βαβυλῶνος, etc., Hdt.: absol. to be distant, Xen.
of actions, to be far from, ἀπεῖχον τῆς ἐξευρέσιος were far from the discovery, Hdt.; πλεῖστον ἀπ. τοῦ ποιεῖν to be as far as possible from doing, Xen.
to have or receive in full, τὸν μισθόν NTest., Plut.
impers., ἀπέχει it sufficeth, it is enough, NTest.
to strain off, filter, Ar.
without caring for anything, reckless of consequences, bluntly, μῦθον ἀπηλεγέως ἀποειπεῖν Hom.
one who keeps away from the Ἡλιαία, i. e. an enemy to law, with a play on ἥλιος, not fond of basking in the sun, Ar.
the wind that comes from the rising sun, the east wind, Lat. subsolanus, Hdt., Thuc.
unharmed, unhurt, Od.: ἔστω δ’ ἀπήμαντον be misery far away, Aesch.
freedom from harm, Theogn.
unharmed, unhurt, of persons, Hom.; νόστος ἀπ. a safe, prosperous return, Od.: c. gen., ἀπήμων οἰζύος free from distress, Aesch.
act. doing no harm, harmless, and so kindly, propitious, of a fair wind, of sleep, Hom.; c. gen., νεῶν ἀπ. free from harm to them, Eur.
a four-wheeled wagon, Hom.: any car or chariot, Aesch., Soph.:—metaph., ναΐα ἀπ. a ship, Eur.; τετραβάμων ἀπήνη, of the Trojan horse, Id.
metaph. also, like ζεῦγος, a pair, e. g. of brothers, Id.

entry.etym: Deriv. of -ηνης, as in προσηνής, uncertain.
entry.sense: ungentle, harsh, rough, hard, of persons, Hom.
hanging on high, high in air.
unmaimed, Hdt.
discordant, ill-sounding, Luc.
high in air, Od.
Laconic word for ἀποπέμπω, to dispatch, Thuc.
not winning belief, incredible, unlikely, improbable, Plat.:—of arguments, not persuasive, unconvincing, Id.
of persons, not to be trusted, Aeschin.
not having confidence to do a thing, c. inf., Plut.
improbability, Aeschin.
οὐκ ἀπίθησει μύθωι he disobeyed not the words, Il.
disobedient epic for ἀπειθής, Anth.
to bar the way, Lys.
only in pres. to lack understanding, be senseless, Hom.
a pear, Lat. pirum, Plat.
a pear-tree, Lat. pirus, Arist.

entry.etym: The first sense has short α, the latter ᾱ.
entry.sense: far away, far off, distant, ἐξ ἀπίης γαίης Hom.
Ἄπιος, η, ον, Apian, i. e. Peloponnesian (said to be derived from Ἆπις, a king of Argos), Ἀπία γῆ, Ἀπία χθών, or Ἀπία alone, the Peloponnese, esp. Argolis, Aesch., Soph.; so Ἀπίς, ίδος, ἡ, Theocr.
to press the juice from anything, Hdt.
to make equal, τινά τινι Plut.:—Pass. to be made equal, τινί to a thing, Hdt.
Apis, a bull worshipped in Egypt, Hdt.
to be ἄπιστος, and so,
to disbelieve, distrust, mistrust, c. acc., Od., Eur.:—Pass. to be distrusted, Thuc., Xen.
c. dat. pers., Hdt., attic; ἀπ. τινί τι to disbelieve one in a thing, Hdt.; τινι περί τι Id.:—absol. to be distrustful, incredulous, Id.
c. inf. to doubt that . . , Soph.; ἀπ. μὴ γενέσθαι τι to doubt that it could be, Thuc.
= ἀπειθέω, to disobey, τινί Hdt., attic: —absol. to be disobedient, refuse to comply, Soph., Eur.
τὸ σῶμ’ οὐκ ἀπιστήσω χθονί, i. e. I will not hesitate to commit it to the earth, Eur.
disbelief, distrust, mistrust, Hes., Hdt., etc.; ὑπὸ ἀπιστίης μὴ γενέσθαι τι from disbelief that it had happened, Hdt.; ἀπιστίαν ἔχειν περί τινος to be in doubt, Plat.
of things, ἐς ἀπιστίην ἀπῖχθαι to have become discredited, Hdt.; πολλὰς ἀπιστίας ἔχει it admits of many doubts, Plat.; εἰς ἀπ. καταπίπτειν Id.
want of faith, faithlessness, unbelief, Soph.: treachery, Xen.
pass. not to be trusted, and so,
of persons and their acts, not trusty, distrusted, faithless, Il., etc.; θράσος ἄπ. groundless confidence, Thuc.
of reports and the like, incredible, Hdt., Aesch.; τὸ ἐλπίδων ἄπιστον what one cannot believe even in hope, Soph.

act. not believing or trusting, mistrustful, incredulous, suspicious, Od.; ἀπιστότερος less credulous, Hdt.; ἄπιστος πρὸς Φίλιππον distrustful towards him, Dem.; ἄπιστος σαυτῶι not believing what you say yourself, Plat.; τὸ ἀπ. = ἀπιστία, Thuc.:—in NTest., unbelieving, an unbeliever,
not obeying, disobeying, c. gen., Aesch.
adv. ἀπίστως,
pass. beyond belief, Thuc.
act. distrustfully, suspiciously, Id.
Dep. to set oneself to oppose firmly, give a flat denial, πρός τινα Thuc.
to keep off, hold off, Od.
one must go away, Xen.
not wandering, steady, fixed, Plat.:—of stars, fixed, opp. to πλανῆται, Id., Anth.
of a line, straight, Anth.
that cannot go astray, Babr.
not moulded, i. e. in its natural state, natural, unaffected, Plut.
for ἀπέλατος, unapproachable, terrible, Hes., Trag.
unplaited, χαίτη Anth.
boundless, immense, Hdt., attic
not navigated: τὸ ἄπλ. a part of the sea not yet navigated, Xen.
unstricken, of a horse needing no whip or spur, Plat.:— unwounded, Eur.
insatiable, Luc., Anth.
insatiate desire, greediness, Plat.; τινός of or for a thing, Eur., Plat.
not to be filled, insatiate, Soph., etc.
c. gen., ἄπλ. χρημάτων insatiate of money, Hdt., etc.
adv., ἀπλήστως ἔχειν to be insatiate, Plat.; ἀπλ. διακεῖσθαι or ἔχειν πρός τι Xen.
impossibility of sailing, detention in port, esp. from stress of weather, Aesch., Thuc.; ἴσχον αὐτὸν ἄπλοιαι Hdt.
to deal openly or frankly, πρὸς τοὺς φίλους Xen.
simple, single, of a cloak, Hom.
with unbraided hair, Anth.
nickname of a Cynic who wore his coat single instead of double, Plut.
act., of ships, not sailing, unfit for sea, not sea-worthy, Thuc.:—comp., ἀπλοώτεραι ναῦς less fit for sea, Id.
pass., of the sea, not navigable, Dem.

entry.etym: from ἅμα as Lat. simplex from simul, opp. to διπλόος, duplex, twofold.
entry.sense: single, Soph., Thuc.
simple, natural, plain, sincere, frank, Trag., Plat., etc.: in bad sense, simple, Isocr.
simple, opp. to compound, Plat.; ἁπλῆ δημοκρατία sheer democracy, Id.
simple, absolutely true, Id.
adv. ἁπλῶς, v. sub voc.
comp. and Sup. ἁπλούστερος, ἁπλούστατος, Id.
singleness: simplicity, frankness, Xen., etc.
liberality, NTest.
without riches, Soph., Plut.
to make single, to unfold, stretch out, Batr., Anth.:—Pass., ἡπλώθη [the fish] lay stretched out, Babr.
filthiness, filth, Anth.
unwashen, unwashed, Ar.
Adv. of ἁπλοῦς, Lat. simpliciter
singly, in one way, Plat.
simply, plainly, openly, frankly, Aesch., etc.
simply, absolutely, ἁπλῶς ἀδύνατον Thuc.; οὐδεμία ἁπλῶς none at all, Id.; ὅς’ ἐστιν ἁπλῶς simply all there are, Ar.
in a word, Lat. denique, Eur., Xen.
Adv. of ἄπνευστος, ἀπ. ἔχειν to hold one's breath, Plat.; without drawing breath, Dem.
breathless, Od.
without breath, lifeless, Anth.
a ladder for disembarking, a gangway, Hdt., Thuc.
to step off from a place, to alight or disembark from a ship, Hom., etc.; absol. to disembark, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:— to dismount from a chariot, ἵππων or ἐξ ἵππων Il.
to go away, depart, Id., attic;—c. gen., ἀπ. πεδίων Eur.; of hopes, to come to naught, Id.

of events, to issue or result from, τὰ ἔμελλε ἀποβήσεσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς μάχης Hdt.; τὸ ἀποβαῖνον, contr. τἀποβαῖνον, the issue, event, and τὰ ἀποβαίνοντα, τὰ ἀποβάντα the results, Id., Thuc.; τὰ ἀποβησόμενα the probable results, Thuc.
to turn out so and so, παρὰ δόξαν Hdt.; τοιόνδε Eur.; ὡς προσεδέχετο Thuc.:—absol. to turn out well, succeed, Id.
of persons, to end by being, ἀπ. κοινοί to prove impartial, Id.; so, ἐς ἀλαθινὸν ἄνδρ’ ἀπ. Theocr.; ἀπέβη ἐς μουναρχίην things ended in a monarchy, Hdt.
Causal in aor1 ἀπέβησα, to make to dismount, disembark, land, (in which sense ἀποβιβάζω serves as pres.), ἀπ. στρατιήν Hdt.
to throw off, Il.; c. gen. to throw off from, ἀπ. ὀμμάτων ὕπνον Eur.
to throw away, τὴν ἀσπίδα Ar.; τὸν ἄνδρα ἀπ. to reject him, Eur.:—Mid. to cast from one, reject, Theocr.
to lose, τὰ πατρῶια, τὸν στρατόν Hdt.; τὴν οὐσίαν Ar.; πολλοὺς τῶν στρατιωτῶν Thuc.
to dip quite or entirely, ἑωυτόν Hdt.; τι εἴς τι Id.
a stepping off, disembarking, ἀπὸ τῶν νεῶν Thuc.; ἡ ναυτικὴ ἐπ’ ἄλλους ἀπόβασις landing from ships in the face of an enemy, Id.; absol., ποιεῖσθαι ἀπόβασιν to disembark, land, Id.
a landing, landing-place, οὐκ ἔχει ἀπόβασιν does not admit of landing, or has no landing-place, Id.; pl., Id.
a way off, escape, Plut.
one who rode several horses leaping from one to the other, Lat. desultor, Plut.
Dep. to force away:— Pass. to be forced away or back, Xen.
absol. to use force, Id.
Causal of ἀποβαίνω, to make to get off, esp. from a ship, to disembark, put on shore, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—Mid., ἀποβιβάσασθαί τινας to cause them to be put on shore, Hdt.
to ruin utterly:— Pass., ἀποβλαφθῆναι φίλου to be robbed of a friend, Soph.
to shoot forth from, spring from, c. gen., Soph.
a shoot, scion, Plat.
gazed on by all, admired, Eur.
to look away from all other objects at one, to look or gaze steadfastly, ἔς τινα or τι Hdt., Eur.; πρός τινα or τι Hdt., Plat.
to look to, pay attention or regard, ἔς τι Eur., etc.; πρός τι Plat.
to look upon with love or admiration, Lat. observare, suspicere, c. acc., Soph.; with a prep., ἔς or πρός τινα Eur., Xen.
to be thrown away, rejected, Plat.
to be thrown away as worthless, Il.
to cut out the comb from the hive: hence to steal, Ar.
to spirt out, c. gen. partit., ἀπ.οἴνου to spirt out some wine, Il.
a throwing away, Plat.
a losing, loss, Lat. jactura, Id.
apt to throw away a thing, c. gen., Ar.
Mid. to feed upon, καρπόν Ar.
to let cattle stray: to lose (as a bad shepherd does his sheep), εἰ τῆι θυγατρὶ τὸν παῖδα ἀποβουκολήσαιμι if I were to lose my daughter her son, Xen.:—Pass. to lose one's way, Luc.
to go off to sleep, go sound asleep, Od.
to strangle, Anth.
far from an altar, godless, Eur.
from land: ἀπόγειον or ἀπόγαιον, ου, τό, a morning cable, Luc.
to make to jut out like a cornice (γεῖσον), ὀφρύσι ἀπ. τὰ ὑπὲρ τῶν ὀμμάτων Xen.
to give one a taste of a thing, c. gen., Anth.:—Mid. to take a taste of a thing, c. gen., Plat., Xen.
to bank off, fence with dykes, τὴν Μέμφιν Hdt.
to grow old, Theogn.
to be away from, have no part in a thing, c. gen., Hdt., Thuc.
absol. to be taken away, opp. to προσγίγνομαι, Thuc.: generally, to be away, absent, Plat., etc.

of death, ἀπ. ἐκ τῶν οἰκιῶν to depart from the house, die out of it, Hdt.; ἀπογενέσθαι alone, to be dead, οἱ ἀπογενόμενοι the dead, Thuc.; ὁ ὕστατον αἰεὶ ἀπ. he who died last, Hdt.; ὁ ἀπογινόμενος one who is dying, Id., Thuc.
to be lost, ἀπ. οὐδὲν τοῦ στρατοῦ Thuc.
depart from a judgment, give up a design or intention of doing, ἀπ. τὸ μάχεσθαι Xen.; ἀπ. μὴ βοηθεῖν to resolve not to help, Dem.
c. gen. rei, to despair of a thing, c. gen., Lys.:—absol. to despair, Dem.
c. acc. to give up as hopeless, Id.:—Pass. to be so given up, Dem.

as law-term, to refuse to receive an accusation, reject, Id.:— ἀπ. τινος (sc. δίκην vel γραφήν) to reject the charge brought against a man, i. e. acquit him, opp. to καταγιγνώσκειν τινός, Id.: also, ἀπ. τινά (sc. τῆς δίκης vel γραφῆς) to judge one free from the accusation, to acquit him, Id.
despair of a thing, c. gen., Thuc.
born or descended from, Lat. oriundus, Hdt.: in pl. descendants, Id., Thuc.; ἀπόγονοι τεαί thy offspring, Soph.
a writing off: a register, list, of lands or property, Plat., etc.: a register of persons liable to taxation, Lat. census, NTest.
as attic law-term, the copy of a γραφή, a deposition, Oratt.
to write off, copy: to enter in a list, register, Hdt., Plat.:—Mid. to have names registered by others, or to register for one's own use, Hdt., Plat.
Mid. also to give in one's name, register, or enlist oneself, Xen.
as attic law-term,
ἀπογράφειν τινά to enter a person's name as accused, give in a copy of the charge against him, to inform against, denounce, Id.

to give in a list of property alleged to belong to the state, but held by a private person, Oratt.:—also, ἀπέγραψεν ταῦτα ἔχοντα αὐτόν gave a written acknowledgment that he was in possession of this property, Dem.
to deprive one of the use of his limbs, to enfeeble, μή μ’ ἀπογυιώσηις Il.
to bring into hard exercise, to ply hard, Aesch.
to strip quite bare of arms: Pass. to be so stripped, Od.:—Mid. to strip oneself, Xen.
to bite off a piece of a thing, c. gen.:—Pass., μῆλα ἀποδεδηγμένα with pieces bitten out, Luc.
absol. to bite hard, gnaw, Xen.
to weep much for, lament loudly, τινά Plat.
ἀπ. γνώμην is to weep away one's judgment, Ar.
to sleep a little, Plut.
parted from the rest, Hdt.
a division, part of a whole, Thuc.
to portion out to others, to apportion, τί τινι Il.
to part off, separate, Hdt.
wanting much, not fully manned, Plut.
Dep. to frighten away, Il.
to point away from other objects at one, and so,
to point out, shew forth, exhibit, make known, by deed or word, τί τινι Hdt.; τι Aesch.
to bring forward, shew, produce, Lat. praestare, μαρτύρια τουτέων Hdt.; παῖδας Soph.; ὑγιέα τινὰ ἐόντα ἀπ. to produce him safe and sound, Hdt.
to produce or deliver in accounts, λόγον Id., Thuc.
to publish a law, Lat. promulgare, Xen.
to appoint, assign, τέμενος, βωμὸν ἀπ. τινί Hdt.:—Pass., χῶρος ἀποδεδεγμένος an appointed place, Id.
to shew by argument, prove, demonstrate, Ar., Plat., etc.; ἀπ. τινὰ οὐδὲν λέγοντα to make it evident that he says nothing, Hdt.
to appoint, name, create, ἀπ. τινὰ βασιλέα Id., Xen.
to make, render, ἀπ. τινὰ μοχθηρόν to make him a rascal, Ar.; ἀπ. τινὰ κράτιστον Xen.
to represent as, ἀπ. παῖδα Hdt.:—Pass., οὐκ ἐν τοῖσι θεοῖσι ἀποδεδέχαται (ionic 3rd pl. perf.) have not been considered, admitted among, Id.
Mid. to shew forth, exhibit something of one's own, ἀποδέξασθαι τὴν γνώμην to deliver one's opinion, Hdt.; μνημόσυνα ἀπ. memorials of oneself, Id.:—Pass., ἔργα μέγαλα ἀποδεχθέντα Id.
just like Act., ἀποδ. ὅτι . . , to declare that . . , Xen.
one must prove, Plat.
c. dupl. acc. one must make one so and so, Luc.
great cowardice, Plut.
one must flinch, Plat.
to play the coward, to flinch from danger or toil, Xen., Plat.
a shewing forth, exhibiting, Eur.
a setting forth, exposition, publication, Hdt., Thuc.
a shewing, proving, proof, Hdt., attic; pl. proofs, arguments in proof of, τινος Dem.
(from Mid.) ἀπ. ἔργων μεγάλων a display, performance of mighty works, Hdt.
of or from supper, Anth.
to slaughter by cutting off the head or cutting the throat, Hom.
to tithe, pay tithes of, πάντα NTest.; ἀπ. τινά to take tithe of him, Id.
one must receive from others, τι Xen.
one must accept, allow, admit, τι Plat.; c. gen. pers. et part., ἀπ. τινὸς λέγοντος Id.
a receiver, Xen.
a receiver, name of a magistrate at Athens who paid the dicasts, Dem.
acceptable, NTest.
Pass. to be turned into a tree, Luc.
a hide stripped off, Hdt.
to flay or skin completely, τὸν βοῦν Hdt.; ἀπ. τὴν κεφαλήν to take off the scalp, Id.:—Pass., πρόβατα ἀποδαρέντα Xen.
ἀπ. τὴν δορήν to strip off the skin, Hdt.
a breastband, girdle, Luc.
a bundle, bunch, Plut.
to accept from another, to accept, Il., attic
to accept as a teacher, follow, Xen.
to admit to one's presence, Plat.

to receive favourably, approve, allow, accept, admit, Thuc., etc.; οὐκ ἀπ. not to accept, reject, Hdt.:—the person from whom one accepts in gen., ἀπ. τί τινος Thuc., etc.; but acc. being omitted, gen. pers. becomes dependent on the Verb, with a partic. added, ἀπ. τινὸς λέγοντος to accept [a statement] from him, i. e. to accept his statements, Plat.: —absol. to accept a statement, be satisfied, Dem.
to take a thing in a certain way, with an adv., Xen.; ὑπόπτως ἀπ. τι Thuc.; δυσχερῶς Plat.
to receive back, recover, Hdt., Thuc.
to bind fast, Plat.
to be in want of, lack, τριακοσίων ἀποδέοντα μύρια 10, 000 lacking 300, Thuc.: to fall short of, be inferior to, τινός Luc.
to be away from home, be abroad or on one's travels, Hdt., attic
to go abroad, ἀπ. παρά τινα to visit him, Hdt.; ἀπ. ἐς Αἰγίναν κατά τι to go abroad to Aegina to fetch a thing, Id.
one who goes abroad, Thuc.
fond of travelling: παράστασις ἀπ. banishment to foreign parts, i. e. ostracism, Arist.
a being from home, a going or being abroad, Hdt., attic; περὶ τῆς ἀπ. τῆς ἐκεῖ as to my life in that foreign land, i. e. beyond the grave, Plat.
away from one's country, from home, abroad, Pind., Plut.
to decide for one in an arbitration, opp. to καταδιαιτάω (to decide against), Dem.
to wear quite away, to waste utterly, Aeschin.
to run away or off, escape, or flee from, esp. by stealth, Od., Hdt., attic; of runaway slaves, Xen.; of soldiers, to desert, Id.
c. acc. to flee, shun, Hdt., Thuc.

to give up or back, restore, return, τί τινι Hom., attic: esp. to render what is due, to pay, as debts, penalties, submission, Il.; ἀπ. τινὶ λώβην to give him back his insult, i. e. make atonement for it, Id.; ἀπ. ἀμοιβήν τινι Theogn., etc.
to return, render, yield, of land, ἐπὶ διηκόσια ἀποδοῦναι (sc. καρπόν) to yield fruit two hundred-fold, Hdt.
c. inf. to suffer or allow a person to do a thing, ἀπ. τισὶ αὐτονομεῖσθαι Thuc., etc.:—so in Pass., ὁ λόγος ἀπεδόθη αὐτοῖς right of speech was allowed them, Aeschin.
to render so and so, ἀπ. τὴν τέρψιν βεβαιοτέραν Isocr.
to deliver over, give up, as a slave, Eur.; ἀπ. ἐπιστολήν to deliver a letter, Thuc.
λόγον ἀπ. to render or give in an account, Lat. rationes referre, Dem.: to give an account of a thing, Eur.
ἀπ. ὅρκον, v. ὅρκος.
