intr. to increase, much like ἐπιδίδωμι III, ἢν ἡ χώρη ἐπιδιδῶι ἐς ὕψος καὶ ἀποδιδῶι ἐς αὔξησιν Hdt.;—unless here it means the contrary, if the land increase in height and decrease in productiveness.

Mid. to give away of one's own will, to sell, Hdt., attic; ἀπ. τι ἐς Ἑλλάδα to take to Greece and sell it there, Hdt.; ἀπ. τοῦ εὑρίσκοντος to sell for what it will fetch, Aeschin.: at Athens, to farm out the public taxes, Dem.

entry.etym: inf. of ἀπέδικον, aor2 with no pres. in use.
entry.sense: to throw off or away, Aesch., Eur.
to defend oneself on trial, Xen.
to thresh corn (v. δῖνος II), Hdt.
= ἀποδιώκω, only in pres., Il.
Dep. to avert threatened evils by offerings to Zeus, to conjure away, Plat.
to mark off by dividing, to separate, NTest.
to chase away, Thuc.; οὐκ ἀποδιώξει σαυτόν; i. e. take yourself off, Ar.
it seems good not to do a thing, c. inf., ἀπέδοξέ σφι πράττειν or μὴ πράττειν Hdt., Xen.; sometimes with the inf. omitted, ὥς σφι ἀπέδοξε when they resolved not (to go on), Hdt.
to reject on scrutiny, to reject for want of qualification, Hdt., attic:—generally, to reject as unworthy or unfit, Plat., Xen.
one must reject, Xen.
-έος, έα, έον, to be rejected, Arist., Luc.
to reject, Hdt.
a giving back, restitution, return, τινος of a thing, Hdt., attic
payment, τοῦ μισθοῦ Thuc.
one must give back, refer, assign, τί τινι Plat.
one must describe, Id.
a receiving back, having restored to one, Thuc.
a running away, escape, Hdt.: c. gen. escape from, στρατείας Dem.
to pluck off, Pind.; ἀπόδρεπε οἴκαδε βότρυς pluck and take them home, Hes., Anth.
to tear off the skin, lacerate, Hom.:—Pass., of the skin, to be torn off, Od.
to lament bitterly, Hdt., attic
one must strip, τινά Luc.
from Pass., ἀπ. ταῖς γυναιξίν they must strip off their clothes, Plat.
an undressing room, Plat., Xen.
to strip off clothes or armour, Il.:—Pass., fut. -δυθήσομαι: aor1 -εδύθην [υ]: perf. -δέδυμαι.
to strip a person of clothes, ἀπέδυσε τὰς γυναῖκας Hdt., etc.:—Pass. to be stripped of one's clothes, Ar.

Mid., fut. -δύσομαι [ῡ]: aor1 -εδυσάμην; also intr. aor2 act. ἀπέδυν, perf. ἀποδέδῡκα:— to strip off oneself, take off, εἵματα Od.:—absol., ἀποδυσάμενος having stripped, Id.; ἀποδύντες stripped naked, Thuc.; ἀποδύεσθαι εἴς or πρός τι to strip for gymnastic exercises, Plut.:—metaph., ἀποδύντες ἐπίωμεν let us strip and attack, Ar.
to strip off, βοείην Od.
to withdraw from the path, c. gen., Il.
old epic aor1 only found in 3 pers. ἀπόερσε, swept away, subj. ἀποέρσηι, opt. ἀποέρσειε, all in Il.
to live off, ὅσον ἀποζῆν enough to live off, Thuc.
to live poorly, Luc.
Pass.:— to be parted from, γυναικός Eur.; εἰ γάμων ἀπεζύγην if I were free from wedlock, Id.; ἀπεζύγην πόδας I started on foot, Aesch.
to smell of something, τινος Ibyc.:— impers., ἀπόζει τῆς Ἀραβίης there comes an odour from Arabia, Hdt.
to lose the bloom, Anth.
to have full confidence, Xen.
to marvel much at a thing, c. acc., Od.:—absol. to wonder much, Hdt., Aesch.
from afar, Thuc., Xen.
afar off, Thuc., Xen.
to deify:— Pass., epic aor1 part. ἀποθειωθείς Anth.
regular worship, θεῶν Arist.
to cut off, κόμας Eur.
a laying up in store, Plat.
a putting aside, getting rid of a thing, c. gen., NTest.
= ἀποδυτήριον, Luc.
despised, Od.
a place in Lacedaemon, into which misshapen children were thrown, Plut.
laid by, stored up, Plut., Luc.
hidden, secret, mysterious, ἔπη Plat.
reserved for occasions, special, Dem.
to run away, Hdt., Xen.
serious contemplation, Plut.
deification, Strab.
any place wherein to lay up a thing, a barn, magazine, storehouse, Thuc.
anything laid by, a store, ἀποθήκην ποιεῖσθαι ἔς τινα to lay up store of favour with him, Hdt.
to make effeminate, enervate, Plut.
to store, hoard up, Luc.
to press upon, press, squeeze out, Eur.
of a crowd, NTest.
a squeezing out of one's place, Luc.
to die off, die, Hom., attic:— to be ready to die of laughter, Ar.
serving as Pass. of ἀποκτείνω, to be put to death, to be slain, ὑπό τινος Hdt., Plat.
Mid. to be very bold, dare all things, Dem.
to break off, Aesch.:—Pass. to be broken off: metaph., ἀποθραυσθῆναι τῆς εὐκλείας to be broken off from one's fair fame, make shipwreck of it, Ar.
to lament much, Babr., Plut.
properly, to cut off fig-leaves: to cut off, curtail, Ar.
to crush in pieces:— metaph. in Pass., ἀποτεθρυμμένος broken, enervated, Plat.
to leap off from, νηός Il.; ἀφ’ ἵππου, ἀπὸ νεός Hdt.
to leap up from, rise from, καπνὸν ἀποθρώσκοντα γαίης Od.:—absol. to rise sheer up, of rocks, Hes.
not according to the mind, unpleasant, hateful, ἀποθύμια ἔρδειν τινί to do one a disfavour, Il.; ἀποθύμιόν τι ποιῆσαι Hdt.
to offer as a votive sacrifice, Xen.
abatement of a swelling, Strab.
not done, undone, Pind.: not to be done, impossible, Plut.
to go away from home, to settle in a foreign country, emigrate, ἐς Θουρίους Plat.
to dwell afar off, to live or be far away, Eur., Thuc.: Pass., ἡ Κόρινθος ἐξ ἐμοῦ μακρὰν ἀπωικεῖτο Corinth was inhabited far away from me, i. e. I settled far from Corinth, Soph.
a settlement far from home, a colony settlement, Hdt., etc.; εἰς ἀπ. στέλλειν to send away so as to form a settlement, Id.; ἀπ. ἐκπέμπειν Thuc.
to send away from home, Od., Soph., etc.:—Pass. to be settled in a far land, to emigrate, Plat.
to colonise a place, send a colony to it, c. acc., Hdt., Thuc.
the settlement of a colony, Arist.
a colony, Hdt.
to cut off by building, wall up, barricade, τὰς θύρας, τὰς ὁδούς Thuc.
away from home, ἀπ. πέμπειν τινὰ γῆς to send away from one's country, Soph.
as Subst.,
a settler, colonist, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
ἄποικος (sub. πόλις), a colony, Xen.
Dep. to complain loudly of a thing, c. acc., Hdt.
unfed, untended, Anth.
to bewail loudly, c. acc., Trag.

entry.etym: α copul. or α euphon. , ποινή
entry.sense: a ransom or price paid, whether to recover freedom or to save one's life or to redeem the corpse of a friend, Il.; c. gen., ἄποινα κούρης, υἷος ransom for them, Id.
generally, compensation, requital, recompense for a thing, c. gen., Aesch., Eur.
to demand the fine due from the murderer, Lex ap. Dem.:—Mid. to hold to ransom, Eur.
exacting penalty, Eur.
to kill with arrows, Anth.
to be gone away, to be far from, c. gen., Il., attic
absol. to be gone, to have departed, to be absent, Od.: hence, to be gone, to have perished, ἀποίχεται χάρις Eur.: of persons, to be dead and gone, Pind., Ar.
to cleanse or clean quite, ἀπ. τὴν χεῖρα εἰς τὰ χειρόμακτρα upon the towels, Xen.
to refine from dross, Strab.: metaph. in Pass., ἀποκεκαθάρθαι τὴν φωνήν to be pure in dialect, Luc.
to clear away, τὰς τραπέζας Ar.:—Mid., ἀποκαθήρασθαί τινος to rid oneself of a thing, Xen.
a clearing off, purging, Thuc.
lustration, Plut.
Pass. to sit apart, ἀτιμώμενοι ἀποκατέαται (ionic for -κάθηνται) Hdt.
to re-establish, restore, reinstate, Xen.
Pass. to surpass or vanquish, c. acc., Od.
unseasonable, Soph.
to burn off, of cautery, Xen.: of intense cold (like Virgil's frigus adurit), to shrivel up, Id.:— Pass., ἀπεκαίοντο αἱ ῥῖνες their noses were frozen off, Id.
to call back, recall, from exile, Hdt., Xen.
to call away or aside, Xen.
to call by a name, esp. by way of disparagement, to stigmatise as, τὸν τοῦ μανέντος ξύναιμον ἀποκαλοῦντες Soph.; σοφιστὴν ἀπ. τινα Xen.
to uncover, τὴν κεφαλήν Hdt., etc.
to disclose, reveal, Plat.:—Mid. to reveal one's whole mind, Plut., NTest.:—Pass. to be disclosed, made known, NTest.
an uncovering, a revelation, NTest.: — the Apocalypse, Id.
to grow quite weary, fail or flag utterly, Soph., Plat.; c. part., ἀπ. ζητῶν to be quite weary of seeking, Plat.
c. inf. to cease to do, Eur., Plat.
c. acc., ἀπ. πόνον to flinch from toil, Xen.
intr. to turn off or aside, Xen.
a turning off the road, Theophr.
to breathe away, ἀπὸ δὲ ψυχὴν ἐκάπυσσεν (epic aor1 in tmesi) she gasped forth her life, Il.
earnest expectation, NTest.
to kill oneself by abstinence, Plut.
to reconcile again, NTest.
to break off by the stalk: to break short off, Eur., Thuc.
a breaking short off, snapping, Luc.
used as Pass. of ἀποτίθημι, to be laid away, absol. to be laid up in store, Soph., Xen.; πολύς σοι [γέλως] ἐστὶν ἀποκείμενος you have great store of laughter in reserve, Xen.

to clip or cut off hair, mostly in Mid., ἀπεκείρατο χαίτην cut off his hair, Il.; ἀποκείρασθαι τὰς κεφαλάς to have their hair shorn close, Hdt.; and absol., ἀποκείρασθαι to cut off one's hair, Ar.:—Pass., perf. part. ἀποκεκαρμένος with one's hair cut short, Id.
metaph. to cheat, τοὺς παχεῖς Luc.
generally, to cut through, sever, Il.
to cut off, slay, Aesch.
to have benefit, enjoyment from or of a thing, c. gen., Eur.; absol., Luc.
to change for small coin: metaph., ἀπ. τὸν βίον to dissipate one's substance, Anth.
to cease to mourn for, τινά Hdt.
to put away care, be careless, Il.
disinherited, Luc.
public renunciation of a son, disinheriting, Plut., Luc.
to sell by auction, Hdt.
to renounce publicly, to disinherit, Plat.
to forbid by proclamation: impers. in perf. pass., ἀποκεκήρυκται μὴ στρατεύειν Xen.
a venturous attempt, Thuc.
to make a bold attempt or venture, try a forlorn hope, πρός τινα against another, Thuc.; c. inf., ἀποκινδυνεύετον σοφόν τι λέγειν Ar.:—Pass., to be put to the uttermost hazard, Thuc.
to remove or put away from, c. gen., Hom.
a comic dance:— metaph., ἀπόκινον εὑρέ find some way to dance off, Ar.
to ring or shout forth, Aesch.
to bend one's knees.
to weep aloud, Hdt.; c. acc. cogn., ἀπ. στόνον Soph.
ἀπ. τινα or τι to bewail much, mourn deeply for, Aesch., Plat.; so in Mid., ἀποκλαίεσθαι κακά Soph.; τὴν πενίαν Ar.
Mid., also, to cease to wail, Luc.
to break off:— Mid., Anth.: —Pass., aor1 part. ἀποκλασθέντα Theocr.
a shutting up, ἀπόκλ. μου τῶν πυλῶν a shutting the gates against me, Thuc.
a shutting out, ἀποκλήισεις γίγνεσθαι (sc. ἔμελλον) there would be a complete stoppage to their works, Id.
to shut off from or out of, debar, τινὰ πυλέων Hdt.; δωμάτων Aesch.; ἀπ. τινά to shut him out, Ar.:—Mid., ἀπ. τινα τῆς διαβάσεως to get him debarred from passing, Thuc.
to shut out or exclude from a thing, τινός Hdt., etc.; ἀπό τινος Ar.
to shut up a gate and the like, to bar, close, Hdt.:—Pass. to be closed, Id.
to shut up one in prison, Soph., Ar., etc.
to shut out, intercept, bar, Hdt., Ar.:—Pass., ἀπ. ὑπὸ τῆς ἵππου Hdt.
without lot or share of a thing, c. gen., Pind.
to choose by lot from a number, Hdt., Thuc.: to choose or elect by lot, Thuc.
to allot, assign by lot, χώραν τινί Plut.
to turn off or aside, τι Od.: to turn back, Hhymn.:—Pass., of the day, to decline, get towards evening, Hdt.
Pass. to be upset, Dem.
intr. in Act. to turn aside or off the road, Xen.; πρὸς τὴν ἠῶ ἀποκλίνοντι as one turns to go Eastward, Hdt.
often in bad sense, to fall away, decline, degenerate, Soph.; ἐπὶ τὸ ῥαιθυμεῖν Dem.:—and without bad sense, to have a leaning, be favourably disposed, πρός τινα Id.
a turning off, declension, sinking, Plut.
to wash away: metaph. in Mid. to purge, Plat.: to avert by purifications, Ar.
to wear one out, worry to death, Plat., etc.:—Pass. to be worn out, Id., Xen.
to shrink from danger, c. acc., Thuc.: —c. inf. to shrink from doing, Id., Plat.
absol. to shrink back, hesitate, Thuc., Plat., etc.
a shrinking from, c. gen., Thuc.
verb. adj. of ἀποκνέω, Plat.
to nip off.
that which is nipt off, a little bit, Ar.
Pass.
to sleep away from home, Plat.
to get a little sleep, Hdt., Ar.
to sleep away from one's post, Decret. ap. Dem.
sleeping away from others, c. gen., Aeschin.
to dive and swim away, Thuc.
a getting away, getting back, Thuc.
to carry away, escort, Xen.: to carry away captive, Thuc.:—Pass. to take oneself off, get away, Id.: to return, Hdt.
a splinter, chip, shred, Theocr., Luc.
of lyre strings, to break with a snap, Anth.
a cutting off, Aesch.; ἀπ. χρεῶν, = the Rom. tabulae novae, a cancelling of all debts, Plat.
in Gramm. apocope, the cutting off letters from a word.
to cut off, hew off, of men's limbs, Il., Hdt.; also, ἀπέκοψε παρήορον he cut loose the tracehorse, Il.:—Pass., ἀποκοπῆναι τὴν χεῖρα to have it cut off, Hdt.
ἀπ. τινὰ ἀπὸ τόπου to beat off from a strong place, Xen.
Mid. to smite the breast in mourning: c. acc. to mourn for, νεκρόν Eur.
to bring to a point:— metaph., ἀπεκορύφου σφι τάδε gave them this short answer, Hdt.
to restore order by clearing away, to clear away, Od.
to dash out the last drops of wine, as in playing at the cottabus, Xen.
to lighten, set free from, relieve, τινὰ κακῶν Eur.
plucked from the fig-tree, Anth.
to sleep off a debauch, Plut.
to strike off from the head, Anth.
to exceed all others, Lat. superare, Hdt.
to let hang down, Il.; χορδὰν πλῆκτρον ἀπεκρέμασε the plectrum broke the string so that it hung down, Anth.
to hang up, suspend, Hdt.
broken sheer off, precipitous, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—metaph. full of difficulties, Dem.
a judicial sentence, NTest.
to separate, set apart, Plat.:— Pass., ἀποκρινθέντε parted from the throng, of two heroes coming forward as champions, Il.; ἀποκεκρίσθαι εἰς ἓν ὄνομα to be separated and brought under one name, Thuc.
to mark by a distinctive form, distinguish , Hdt.; perf. pass. part. ἀποκεκριμένος distinct, Plat.
to choose out, choose, Hdt., Plat.

Mid. ἀποκρίνομαι, fut. -κρινοῦμαι: perf. -κέκριμαι both in mid. and pass. sense:— to give answer to, reply, Eur., etc.; ἀπ πρός τινα or πρός τι to reply to a questioner or question, Thuc., etc.:—c. acc., ἀποκρίνεσθαι τὸ ἐρωτηθέν to answer the question, Id.: so in Pass., τοῦτό μοι ἀποκεκρίσθω let this be my answer, Plat.
to answer charges, defend oneself, Ar.
aor1 pass. ἀπεκρίθη, = ἀπεκρίνατο, he answered, first in NTest.
a separating.
(from Mid.) an answer, Thuc., Xen.
one must reject, Plat.
one must answer, Id.
beaten or trodden hard, of ground, Thuc.
to beat off from a place, Xen.:—Mid. to beat off from oneself, beat off an attack, Hdt., Thuc.: —Pass. to be beaten off, Thuc., Xen., etc.
Pass., κοτυλίσκιον τὸ χεῖλος ἀποκεκρουμένον a cup with the lip knocked off, Ar.
to hide from, keep hidden from, c. acc. et gen., θανάτοιο ἀπ. τινα Il.; c. dupl. acc., like Lat. celare aliquem aliquid, to keep back from one, Hdt.; so in Mid., ἀποκρύπτεσθαί τινά τι Xen., etc.
to hide from sight, keep hidden, conceal, Od., attic:—Mid., ἀποκρύπτεσθαι μὴ ποιεῖν τι to conceal one's doing, Thuc.
to obscure, throw into the shade, Plat.
ἀπ. γῆν to lose from sight, of ships running out to sea, like Virgil's Phaeacum abscondimus arces, Id., Luc.
hidden, concealed, Eur.; ἐν ἀποκρύφωι in secret, Hdt.
c. gen. concealed from, unknown to one, Xen.
obscure, hard to understand, Id.

entry.etym: pass. rare, ἀποθνήσκω being used as pass.
entry.sense: to kill, slay, Hom., Hdt., attic
of judges, to condemn to death, Plat., Xen., etc.
metaph., like Lat. enecare, to weary to death, Eur.
to kill Plat., Xen.
to bear young, bring forth, c. acc., Plut., Luc.:—metaph., ἡ ἁμαρτία ἀπ. θάνατον NTest.
to roll away, NTest.:—Pass., Luc.
to mourn loudly over, τινά Aesch.
a hindrance, Xen.
to hinder or prevent from a thing, τινά τινος Xen.; c. inf., ἀπ. τινὰ ποιεῖν to prevent from doing, forbid to do, μὴ ποιεῖν τι Eur., Xen.
c. acc. only, to keep off, hinder, Orac. ap. Hdt., Thuc.: —absol. to stop the way, Thuc.:—impers., οὐδὲν ἀποκωλύει there is no hindrance, Plat.
to obtain a portion of a thing by lot, τῶν κτημάτων τὸ μέρος ἀπ. Hdt.; generally to obtain, Eur.
to fail in drawing lots, Plut.: generally to be left destitute, Eur.
to kick off or away, shake off, ὕπνον Aesch.
to spurn, Id.
to speak out heedlessly, Luc.
to take or receive from another, παρά τινος Thuc.:— to receive what is one's due, μισθόν Hdt., Xen.; ἀπ. ὅρκους to accept oaths tendered, Dem.
c. gen. to take of, take part of a thing, Thuc.
to hear or learn, Lat. accipio, Plat.
to take back, get back, regain, recover, τὴν τυραννίδα Hdt.
to have an account rendered one, ἀπ. λόγον Aeschin.
to take apart or aside, ἀπ. τινὰ μοῦνον Hdt.; ἀπολαβὼν σκόπει consider it separately, Plat.
to cut off, intercept, arrest, Hdt.; ἀπ. τείχει to intercept by a wall, Thuc.:—Pass. to be arrested or stopped by contrary winds, Hdt.
to make famous:— Pass. to become so, Hdt.
to shine or beam from a thing, of light, Il.; so in Mid., χάρις ἀπελάμπετο grace beamed from her, Hom.
to lap up like a dog, swallow greedily, Ar.
enjoyment, fruition, Thuc., Arist.
c. gen. advantage got from a thing, Xen.; ἀπόλαυσιν εἰκοῦς (acc. absol.) as a reward for your resemblance, Eur.
enjoyment, Aeschin.
devoted to enjoyment, Arist.; producing enjoyment, Id.:—adv., ἀπολαυστικῶς ζῆν to live a life of pleasure, Id.
enjoyed, enjoyable, Plut.
to have enjoyment of a thing, to have the benefit of it, to enjoy, c. gen., Hdt., attic:—with acc. added, ἀπολαύειν τί τινος to enjoy an advantage from some source, Ar., Thuc.
ironically, to have the benefit of, τῶν Οἰδίπου κακῶν Eur.: —absol. to have a benefit, come finely off, Ar.
to pick out from a number, to pick out, choose, Hdt.:—Mid. to pick out for oneself, Id., Thuc.; ἀπολελεγμένοι, attic -ειλεγμένοι, picked men, Hdt., Xen.
like ἀπαγορεύω, to decline, refuse: — Mid. to decline something offered to one, renounce, Plut.:—absol. to give in, Id.
to let drop off, to pour a libation, Hes.:—Pass. to drop or run down from, τινός Od.
to leave over or behind, of meats not wholly eaten, Od.:—Mid. to leave behind one, after death, Hdt.
to leave hold of, lose, βίον Soph.; also, βίοτος ἀπολείπει τινά Id.
to leave behind, as in the race, to distance, and generally to surpass, Xen.; v. infr.
to leave quite, forsake, abandon, of places one ought to defend, Il., Hdt., etc.: to leave one in the lurch, Hdt., Ar.
of things, to leave alone, leave undone or unsaid, Hdt., attic
to leave open, leave a space, Hdt., Xen.
intr. to fail, to be wanting, Od.; of rivers, to fall, sink, Hdt.; of flowers, to begin to wither, Xen.;—also, like ἀπειπεῖν, to fail, flag, lose heart, Hdt., Xen.

to be wanting of or in a thing, c. gen., Thuc.; of measures, ἀπὸ τεσσέρων πήχεων ἀπ. τρεῖς δακτύλους wanting 3 fingers of 4 cubits, Hdt.: c. inf., ὀλίγον ἀπέλιπον ἀπικέσθαι wanted but little of coming, Id.
c. part. to leave off doing, Plat.
to depart from, ἐκ τῶν Συρακουσῶν Thuc., Plat.
Pass. to be left behind, stay behind, Thuc., Xen.
to be distanced by, inferior to, τινος Dem.
to be parted from, be absent or far from, c. gen., Hdt.: to be deprived of, τάφου Soph.; φρενῶν Eur.
to be wanting in, fall short of, παιδείας Dem.; ἀπολειφθεὶς ἡμῶν without our cognisance, Id.; ἀπ. φρενῶν to be bereft of, Eur.
to lick clean, NTest.
a forsaking, abandonment, of a thing, Thuc.: desertion of a husband by his wife, Dem.; of their post by soldiers, Xen., etc.
intr. a falling short, deficiency, Thuc.
chosen out, picked, Thuc., Xen.
unwarlike, unfit for war, Il., Eur.
peaceful, Eur.
not to be warred on, invincible, Aesch.
πόλεμος ἀπόλεμος a war that is no war, a hopeless struggle, Id., Eur.
to peel off, flay, Eur., Ar.
to leave off, desist from a thing, c. gen., Il., Plat.
c. part. to leave off doing, Hom.:—absol. to cease, desist, Id.
to chatter at random, Dem.
an intercepting, cutting off, Thuc.
to drop off, vanish, Ar.
to scream aloud, be obstreperous, Ar.
Pass. to become stone, Strab.
to leave, Plut., Luc.
to slip off or away, Thuc.
c. gen. to slip away from, τινός Ar.
one without city, state or country, an outlaw, Hdt., Soph., etc.
πόλις ἄπολις a city that is no city, a ruined city, Aesch.
to pack oneself off, Ar.
taking no part in public matters, living as a private person, Plut.
Dep. to lick off, αἷμα Il.

to destroy utterly, kill, slay, and of things, to destroy, demolish, waste, Hom., attic; in pregnant sense, γᾶς ἐκ πατρίας ἀπ. to drive me ruined from my fatherland, Eur.; λόγοις ἀπ. τινά Soph.:— to talk or bore one to death, Ar.
to lose utterly, πατέρα, νόστιμον ἦμαρ Hom.

Mid. ἀπόλλυμαι, fut. -ολοῦμαι, ionic -ολέομαι with part. ἀπολεύμενος: aor2 -ωλόμην: perf. -όλωλα: plup. ἀπολώλειν:— to perish utterly, die, Il.; c. acc. cogn., ἀπ. κακὸν μόρον, αἰπὺν ὄλεθρον Od.; to be undone, Id.; ἀπόλωλας you are done for, lost, ruined, Ar.; as an imprecation, κάκιστ’ ἀπολοίμην Id.; in fut. part., ὦ κάκιστ’ ἀπολούμενε oh destined to a miserable end! i. e. oh villain, scoundrel! Ar.
to be lost, slip away, vanish, of the water eluding Tantalus, Od.; of sleep, Il.
of or belonging to Apollo, Pind.
Ἀπολλώνιον, τό, the temple of Apollo, Thuc.
Apollo, son of Zeus and Latona, brother of Artemis, Hom., etc.: in Hom. men who die suddenly are said to be slain by his ἀγανὰ βέλεα; cf. Ἄρτεμις.

to speak in defence, defend oneself, περί τινος about a thing, πρός τι or τινα in answer to.., Thuc., Plat.; ἀπ. ὑπέρ τινος to speak in another's behalf, Hdt.:—absol., Id.; ὁ ἀπολογούμενος the defendant, Ar.
c. acc. criminis, to defend oneself against a thing, explain, excuse, Thuc., Aeschin.
ἀπ. τι ἔς τι to allege in one's defence against a charge, Thuc., Plat.
ἀπ. δίκην θανάτου to speak against sentence of death being passed on one, Thuc.
a plea alleged in defence, Plut.
one must defend, Plat.
a speech in defence, defence, Thuc.
to reckon up, give in an account, Lat. rationes reddere, Xen.: c. acc. rei, to give in an account of the receipts, Aeschin.
to reckon on a thing, calculate that it will be, c. acc. et inf., Dem.
a giving account, statement, Aeschin.
an account kept, record, Luc.
a story, tale, fable, apologue, Plat.
c. acc. rei, to wash off dirt, Il.: Mid. ἅλμην ὤμοιν ἀπολούεσθαι to wash the brine from off my shoulders, Od.
c. acc. pers. to wash clean, Ar.:— Mid. to wash oneself, Il.
c. acc. pers. et rei, Πάτροκλον λοῦσαι ἄπο βρότον to wash the gore off him, Id.
Mid. to bewail loudly, Xen.
in past tenses, to leave off wailing, Thuc.
to wash dirt off oneself, cleanse oneself by bathing, Il.
a destroyer: δαιτῶν ἀπολ. one who destroys the pleasure of dinner, a kill-joy, — or, acc. to others, a devourer of feasts, lick-plate, Od.
release, deliverance from a thing, c. gen., Plut.; κατὰ τὴν ἀπόλυσιν τοῦ θανάτου so far as acquittal from a capital charge went, Hdt.
disposed to acquit:— adv., ἀπολυτικῶς ἔχειν τινός to be minded to acquit one, Xen.
to release on payment of ransom, c. gen. pretii, Philipp. ap. Dem.
a ransoming, Plut.: redemption by payment of ransom, NTest.
to loose from, τί τινος Od.: to undo, Id.
to set free from, release or relieve from, τινὰ τῆς φρουρῆς, τῆς ἐπιμελείας Hdt., Xen.; τι ἀπό τινος Plat.:—Pass. to be set free from, Thuc.
in legal sense, ἄπ. τῆς αἰτίης to acquit of the charge, Hdt., Xen.:—c. inf., ἀπ. τινὰ μὴ φῶρα εἶναι to acquit one of being a thief, Hdt.: then absol. to acquit, Ar.
to let go free on receipt of ransom, hold to ransom, Il.:—Mid. to ransom, redeem, χρυσοῦ by payment of gold, Id.
to discharge or disband an army, Xen.:—generally, to dismiss, Ar.
to divorce a wife, NTest.
Mid. to redeem, v. supr. II.
to do away with charges against one, Lat. diluere, Thuc., Plat.:— absol., ἀπολυόμενος in defence, Hdt.
like Pass. (c. II), to depart, Soph.
Pass. to be released, let off, τῆς στρατηΐης from military service, Hdt.; τῆς ἀρχῆς ἀπολυθῆναι to be freed from their rule, Thuc.:—absol. to be acquitted, discharged, Id., Plat.
of combatants, to be separated, part, Thuc.
to depart, Soph.
Pass. to be grievously insulted, Soph.
to pluck off flowers: generally, to pluck off, cut off, Eur.
the crumb or inside of the loaf, on which the Greeks wiped their hands at dinner, and then threw it to the dogs, dog's meat, Ar.
Pass. to rave, rage to the uttermost, Luc.
a strickle, Ar.
Pass. to show weakness, Plut.
to unlearn, Lat. dediscere, Plat., Xen.
Dep. to announce as a prophet, τὸ μέλλον ἥξειν Plat.
a wiping off, Plut.
Pass. to waste or wither away, die away, of a tranquil death, Xen.
to wipe clean, Dem.:— Mid., Ἀχιλλείων ἀπομάττει you wipe your hands on the finest bread, Ar.

to wipe off or level corn with a strickle (ἀπόμακτρον): χοίνικα ἀπ. to give scant measure, as was done in giving slaves their allowance, Luc.; κενεὰν ἀπομάξαι (sc. χοίνικα) to level an empty measure, i. e. to labour in vain, Theocr.
to take an impression: metaph. to take impression, Ar.
to scourge severely, Hdt.
to behave in unseemly fashion, Hdt.
to fight from the walls, Thuc.; τείχεα ἱκανὰ ἀπομάχεσθαι high enough to fight from, Xen.:—absol. to fight desperately, Id.
ἀπ. τι to fight off a thing, decline it, Hdt.; absol., Id.
ἀπ. τινά to drive him off in battle, Xen.
past fighting, past service, Xen.
Mid. to distribute, Hes.
Pass. to be parted from, Id.
to part or distinguish from a number, Plat.
ἀπ. πρός or ἐπί τι to detach on some service, Polyb.: to impart, Id.
to sleep off care, Ar.
Pass. to be filled to the brim, Plat.
to measure out, Luc.:—Mid., Xen.
to prolong, draw out, λόγον Plat.: absol. to be prolix, Id.:—Pass. to be extended, Luc.
to be very wroth, to perseverere in wrath, Hom.
Mid. to express by imitating or copying, represent faithfully, Xen.
Mid.:— to remember fully, χάριν ἀπ. to recognise, repay a favour, feel gratitude, Il., Thuc.
away from (i. e. without) pay, unpaid, ill-paid, Xen., Dem.
paid off, Dem.
to let out for hire, Thuc.;—c.inf., ἀπ. ποιεῖν τι to contract for the doing of a thing, Lex ap. Dem.
a memorial, Plut.:—in pl. memoirs, Lat. commentarii, as those of Socrates by Xen.
to relate from memory, relate, recount, Plat.
to remember, call to mind, Id.; ὄνομα ἀπεμνημόνευσε τῶι παιδὶ θέσθαι gave his son the name in memory of a thing, Hdt.
ἀπ. τί τινι to bear something in mind against another, Xen.
to bear a grudge against, τινί Hdt.
to take an oath away from a thing, i. e. swear that one will not do it, Od.
to swear one has not done or that it is not so, to deny on oath, Hdt., attic; with μή added, ἀπ. ἦ μὴν μὴ εἰδέναι Xen.; ἀπ. μηδὲ ὀβολόν (sc. ἔχειν) Id.
c. acc. to disown on oath: Mid., ἀπωμόσατο τὴν ἀρχήν renounced it, Plut.
to take a solemn oath, ἦ μήν . . Thuc.
a portion, Anth.
Pass. to be excluded from a thing, c. gen., Thuc.
to be left alone, Plut.

to wipe off or away from, τί τινος Il.:—Mid. to wipe off from oneself, Id.; ἀπομόρξατο δάκρυ wiped away his tears, Od.; absol. in same sense, ἀπομόρξασθαι Ar.; and in Pass., τὴν ὀργὴν ἀπομορχθείς having my anger wiped off, Id.
to wipe the face clean, Il.:—Mid., ἀπομόρξατο παρειάς she wiped her cheeks, Od.
away from the Muses, unaccomplished, rude, Eur.:—adv., ἀπομούσως unfavourably, Aesch.
Dep. to dissuade, Il.
Dep. to bellow loudly, Anth.
verb. Adj. one must wipe one's nose, Eur. From
to wipe the nose, Anth.:— Mid. to blow one's nose, Ar., Xen.
metaph. to make him sharp, sharpen his wits, Plat.; cf. Horace's vir emunctae naris.
to remove, to send away, Il.:—Mid. to wend one's way back, ἀπενάσσατο Hom.
aor1 mid. in trans. sense, ἀπενάσσατο παῖδα sent away her child, Eur.; also, ἀπονασθῆναι, to be taken away, depart from a place, c. gen., Id.
Pass. to become quite torpid, insensible, Plat.
verb. Adj. one must assign, Arist. From
to portion out, impart, assign, τί τινι Hdt. Attic:—Mid. to assign or take to oneself, Plat.; ἀπονέμεσθαί τι to feed on, Ar.: c. gen. partit. to help oneself to a share of a thing, Plat.
Adv. part. pf. pss. of ἀπονοέομαι desperately, Xen.
Mid. to go away, depart, Hom.
to bend away from other objects towards one, turn towards, πρός τι Plat.
to unload:— Mid. to throw off a load from, στέρνων ἀπονησαμένη Eur.
Adv. without fatigue, Hdt.
without toil:— adv. Sup. ἀπονητότατα with least trouble, Hdt.
without suffering, Soph.
Mid. to escape by swimming, to swim away, Luc.
non-exertion, laziness, Xen.: exemption from toil, Plut.
wash off, ἀπονίψαντες βρότον ἐξ ὠτειλῶν Od.:—Mid. to wash off from oneself, ἱδρῶ ἀπενίζοντο θαλάσσηι Il.

to wash clean, properly of the hands and feet, ἀπονίζουσα as I was washing his feet, Od.; ὅταν ἀπονίζηι καὶ τὼ πόδ’ ἀλείφηι Ar.:—Mid. to wash one's hands and feet, χεῖράς τε πόδας τε Od.: absol. to wash one's hands, Ar.; perf. pass. ἀπονενίμμεθα Id.
to have the use or enjoyment of a thing, c. gen., Hom., Soph.; but the gen. is often omitted, ἦγε μὲν οὐδ’ ἀπόνητο married her but had no joy [of it], Od.; οὐκ ἀπώνητο (sc. τῆς πόλεως) Hdt.
water in which the hands have been washed, dirty water, Ar.
Mid. to go away, Theogn.: epic aor1 part. ἀπονισσάμενος, Anth.
Dep. to have lost all sense,
of fear, to be desperate, Xen.; ἄνθρωποι ἀπονενοημένοι desperate men, Lat. perditi, Thuc.
of shame, ἀπονενοημένος an abandoned fellow, Theophr.
loss of all sense,
of fear, desperation, εἰς ἀπ. καταστῆσαί τινα to make one desperate, Thuc.
of right perception, madness, Lat. dementia, Dem.
without toil or trouble, untroubled, quiet, Aesch., etc.
of persons, not toiling, lazy, Xen.
adv. -νως, without trouble, Hdt., Xen.
irreg. comp. ἀπονέστερος, Pind., but -ώτερος, Thuc.
to return, come home, ἂψ ἀπονοστήσας, Il.; ἀπ. ὀπίσω Hdt.
to put asunder, keep aloof from, τινά τινος h. Hom.
to bereave or rob of, ὅπλων τινά Soph.:—Pass. to be robbed of, ἐδωδήν h. Hom.
c. acc. loci, to flee from, shun, Soph.
far apart or aloof, Hom.
prep. with gen. far away from, Id.
to pass a night away from, τινός Plut.
to pare the nails: Pass. to have them pared, Babr.
metaph. to pare down, retrench, τὰ σιτία Ar.
= ὀνυχίζω ΙΙΙ, to try by the nail, ἀκριβῶς ἀπωνυχισμένος, Horace's ad unguem factus, Theophr.
to make one turn his back and flee, τινά Eur.
alien to guests, inhospitable, Soph.:—c. gen. loci, far from a country, Aesch.; πέδου banished from, Id.
to drive from house and home, banish, Plut.:—Pass., γῆς ἀποξενοῦσθαι Eur.
a living abroad, Plut.
to shave off, to cut off, ἀπὸ δ’ ἔξεσε χεῖρα Il.
metaph. to strip off, Luc.
to dry up a river, Hdt.:—Pass. to be dried up, run dry, of rivers, Id.
generally to dry completely, τὰς ναῦς Thuc.
to bring to a point, make taper, Od.
to make sharp and piercing, τὴν φωνήν Plut.
to shave clean, c. dupl. acc., τὸν δοῦλον ἀποξυρήσας τὴν κεφαλήν Hdt.
Mid. to have oneself clean shaved, Plut.
cut sharp off, abrupt, Luc.
to strip off as it were a skin, Il.
to hurl, Luc.:—Pass. to rebound, Plut.
to look about one, as if to flee, ionic 3rd pl. fut. ἀποπαπτανέουσιν Il.
to retire from the way, to go aside to ease oneself, Ar.
a place out of the way: a privy, Ar.

to stop or hinder from, make to cease from a thing, c. gen., πολέμου Il.; πένθεος Hdt., etc.: c. inf. to hinder from doing, Od.:—Mid. and Pass. to leave off or cease from, c. gen., Hom.; ἐκ καμάτων Soph.: absol. to leave off, Theogn.
c. acc. only, to stop, check, Il., Eur.
prep. c. gen. = Lat. ab, from.
OF PLACE:
of Motion, from, away from, Hom., etc.; of warriors fighting from chariots, Hom.
of Position, away from, far from, apart from, ἀπὸ ἧς ἀλόχοιο Il.; ἀπ’ ὀφθαλμῶν far from sight, Id.; ἀπὸ θαλάσσης Thuc., etc.
of the mind, ἀπὸ θυμοῦ away from, i. e. alien from, my heart, Il.; οὐκ ἀπὸ τρόπου not without reason, Plat.; οὐκ ἀπὸ πράγματος Dem.
in partitive sense, αἶς’ ἀπὸ ληΐδος a part from the booty, a share of it, Od.
OF TIME, from, after, ἀπὸ δείπνου after supper, Il.; ἀπὸ δείπνου γενέσθαι to have done supper, Hdt., etc.; ἀφ’ οὗ (sc. χρόνου), Lat. ex quo, Id., etc.
OF ORIGIN, CAUSE, etc.:

of that from which one is born, οὐκ ἀπὸ δρυὸς οὐδ’ ἀπὸ πέτρης not sprung from oak or rock, Od.; τρίτος ἀπὸ Διός third in descent from Zeus, Plat.; οἱ ἀπὸ Σπάρτης the men from Sparta, Hdt.:—metaph. of things, κάλλος ἀπὸ Χαρίτων beauty born of the Graces, such as they give, Od.; γάλα ἀπὸ βοός Aesch.: —of connexion with the leader of a sect, οἱ ἀπὸ Πλάτωνος, Plato's disciples; οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀκαδημίας, ἀπὸ τῆς Στοᾶς, the Academics, the Stoics, Plut., etc.
of the Material from or of which a thing is made, ἀπὸ ξύλου Hdt.; ἀπὸ μέλιτος Theocr.
of the Instrument from or by which a thing is done, ἀπ’ ἀργυρέοιο βιοῖο by [arrow shot from] silver bow, Il.

of the Person from whom an act comes, i. e. by whom it is done, οὐδὲν μέγα ἔργον ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο Hdt.; ἐπράχθη ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ οὐδέν Thuc.;—so that ἀπό came to be used like ὑπό, but implying a less direct agency.
of the Source from which life or power is sustained, ζῆν ἀπὸ ἰχθύων Hdt.; τρέφειν τὸ ναυτικὸν ἀπὸ τῶν νήσων Xen.

of the Cause, Means, or Occasion from, by, or because of which a thing is done, ἀπὸ δικαιοσύνης by reason of justice, Hdt.; ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν λημμάτων moved by, for the same profits, Dem.:—hence in many adverbial usages, ἀπὸ σπουδῆς in earnest, eagerly, Il.; ἀπὸ τοῦ ἴσου, ἀπὸ τῆς ἴσης, or ἀπ’ ἴσης, equally, Thuc., etc.; ἀπὸ γλώσσης by word of mouth, Hdt.; ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ from or of oneself, Thuc.
AS ADVERB, far away, Hom., Hdt.
IN COMPOS.:
from, asunder, as in ἀποτέμνω: away, off, as in ἀποβαίνω.
finishing off, completing, as in ἀπεργάζομαι.
ceasing from, leaving off, as in ἀπαλγέω, ἀπολοφύρομαι.
back again, as in ἀποδίδωμι, ἀπολαμβάνω: also, in full, or what is one's own, as ἀπέχω.
by way of abuse, as in ἀποκαλέω.
almost = a_priv; sometimes with Verbs, as ἀπαυδάω, ἀπαγορεύω; with Adjectives, as ἀποχρήματος, ἀπόσιτος.
ἄπο, by anastrophe for ἀπό, when it follows its Noun, as ὀμμάτων ἄπο Soph.
to make trial, essay, or proof of a thing or person, c. gen., Hdt., attic:—so also in Act., ἀποπειρᾶσαι τοῦ Πειραιῶς to make an attempt on the Peiraeeus, Thuc.
a trial, essay, Hdt., Thuc.
to hew or trim with an axe, Ar.
to send off or away, to dismiss, Hom., Hdt., etc.:—Mid. to send away from oneself, Hdt.; ἀπ. τὴν γυναῖκα to put away, divorce her, Id.: ἀπ. ὕδωρ to get rid of it, Id.
to send back, Od.
to dispatch, Hdt., Ar.
a sending off, dispatching, Hdt.
a divorcing, Dem.
to mourn for, τινά Plut.
to carry over, Plut.
to break wind, Lat. pedo, Ar.
to fly off or away, Hom., Ar.

entry.etym: From pf. pass. part. of ἀποφαίνω
entry.sense: openly, plainly, Dem.
to make to freeze, to freeze, Ar.:—Pass., to be frozen, Xen.: of blood, to curdle, Id.
to leap off from, ἵππου Plut.
to start off from, turn away from, τινός Xen.
absol. to leap off, start off, Plat.
to fill up a number, Hdt.
to satisfy, fulfil, χρησμόν Id.
to satisfy, appease, θυμόν, ἐπιθυμίαν Id., Plat.
to drink up, drink off, Hdt.
to fall off from, ἐκ or ἀπό τινος Od., Hdt.; τινός Hdt.; absol. to fall off, Il.
to trust fully, rely on, τινί Polyb.

to lead astray from, τινός Apoll.:—Pass., to stray away from, σῆς πατρίδος, Τροίηθεν Od.; ἀπὸ θώρηκος ἀποπλαγχθείς having glanced off from the breastplate, of an arrow, Id.; absol. τρυφάλεια ἀποπλαγχθεῖσα a helm struck off or falling from the head, Id.
to lead astray, Aeschin.; metaph. to seduce, beguile, τινά NTest.
a wanderer, fugitive, Anth.
to sail away, sail off, Il., Hdt., etc.
disabled by a stroke,
in mind, struck dumb, astounded, senseless, stupid, Hdt., Dem.
in body, crippled, palsied, Lat. sideratus, Hdt.; ἀπ. τὰς γνάθους struck dumb, Ar.
to fill up, satisfy, Lat. explere, τὰς ἐπιθυμίας Plat.; τοῦτό μοι ἀποπλήρωσον make this complete for me, satisfy me in this, Id.
a filling up, satisfying, Plut.
to strike to earth, disable in body or mind:— Pass. to lose one's senses, become dizzy or astounded, Soph.
Mid. to trot off, Ar.; v. πλίσσομαι.
a sailing away, Hdt.
a voyage home or back, Xen.
to wash away, Od.
to breathe forth fire, etc., Hom.; θυμὸν ἀπ. to give up the ghost, Il.; ἀπ. τὴν δυσμένειαν to get rid of it, Plut.
to blow from a particular quarter, of winds, Hdt.
to smell of a thing, c. gen., Plut.
to choke, throttle, Hdt.; ἀπέπνιγον Ar.; of plants, NTest.: to be choked, suffocated, drowned, Dem.: metaph. to be choked with rage, Id.
to fight off from, τοῦ ὄνου from ass-back, Plat.
far from the city, banished, Aesch., Soph.
a sending away: getting rid of an illness, Luc.
Pass. to depart, go away, Xen.
to soften matters down, Plut.
to buy off or up, Ar.

entry.etym: see also the late form ἀποπρίζω
entry.sense: to saw off, Hdt., Anth.
to take away from, σίτου ἀποπροελών having taken some of the bread, Od.
from afar, afar off, far away, Hom.
far away, Hom.
to send away forward, send on, Od.: to send forth, shoot forth, Id.: to let fall, Id.
far away, afar off, Il.
prep. c. gen. far away from, Id., Eur.
to cut off from, νώτου ἀποπροταμών after he had cut a slice from the chine, Od.
to flee away from, Anth.
out of sight of, far away from, c. gen., Soph.:—absol. out of sight, Id.; ἐξ ἀπόπτου from a distance, Id.
spat out: hence loathed, abominated, Trag.
to spit out, Il.; ἀπ. ἄχνην to vomit forth foam, Id.; absol. to spit, Xen.
to abominate, loathe, spurn, Aesch., Eur.: aor1 ἀπέπτυσα, = Lat. omen absit, Eur.
Mid. to inquire or ask of, ἀπ. [αὐτοῦ] εἰ.. asked of him whether.., Hdt.
to snore to the end, Anth.
to slink away, Anth.
not to be travelled, Plut.
to be without means or resource; and so,

to be at a loss, be in doubt, be puzzled, mostly followed by a relative clause, ἀπ. ὅκως διαβήσεται to be at a loss how he shall cross, Hdt.; ἀπ. ὅ τι χρὴ ποιεῖν Xen.; with an acc. added, ἀπ. τὴν ἔλασιν ὅκως διεκπερᾶι to be at a loss about his march, how he shall cross, Hdt.; and with an acc. only, to be at a loss about it, Id.; c. inf. to be at a loss how to do, Ar., Plat.; ἀπ. περί τινος Plat.:—also absol., οὐκ ἀπορήσας without hesitation, Hdt., etc.:—Mid. in same sense, Id., Plat.
in Pass., of things, to be left wanting, left unprovided for, Xen.
c. gen. rei, to be at a loss for, in want of, Soph., Thuc., etc.
ἀπ. τινι to be at a loss by reason of, by means of something, Xen.
absol. to be in want, be poor, Plat.
inclined to doubt, Plat.
not sacked, unravaged, Il., Hdt., attic
to make straight, guide aright, Soph.
of places, difficulty of passing, Xen.
of things, difficulty, straits, ἐς ἀπορίην ἀπιγμένος, ἀπειλημένος, ἐν ἀπορίηι or ἐν ἀπορίηισι ἔχεσθαι, ἀπορίηισιν ἐνεχέσθαι Hdt.; ἀπ. τοῦ μὴ ἡσυχάζειν impossibility of keeping quiet, Thuc.
of persons, difficulty of dealing with, τινός Hdt.
want of means or resource, embarrassment, difficulty, hesitation, perplexity, Plat., etc.
3 ἀρ. τινός want of a person or thing, Ar., etc.
absol. poverty, Thuc.
to start from a place, Λυκίηθεν Il.
without passage, and so:
of places, impassable, pathless, trackless, Xen., etc.

of circumstances, hard to see one's way through, impracticable, very difficult, Hdt., attic: ἄπορα, τά, straits, difficulties, Hdt., Xen.; so, εἰς ἄπορον ἥκειν, πίπτειν Eur., Ar.; ἐν ἀπόρωι εἶναι at a loss, Thuc.:—comp., ἀπορώτερος more difficult, Id.
hard to get, scarce, Plat.
of persons, hard to deal with, impracticable, unmanageable, Hdt., Plat.: c. inf., ἄπ. προσμίσγειν, προσφέρεσθαι impossible to have any dealings with, Hdt.: so, absol., ἄνεμος ἄπ. Id.
without means or resources, at a loss, helpless, Soph., etc.; ἄπορος ἐπὶ φρόνιμα, ἐπ’ οὐδέν Id.; of soldiers, οἱ ἀπορώτατοι the most helpless, worst equipt, Thuc.
poor, needy, Lat. inops, Id., Plat.
adv. 3 a)po/rws, a)p. e)/xei moi I am at a loss, Eur.: comp. -ώτερον, Thuc.
to dart away, Hom.
to neglect a thing from faintheartedness or laziness, c. gen., Xen.; absol., Plat.
to spirt out, shed about, Hdt.
to bereave one of a thing, c. dupl. acc., Od.
a vessel for sprinkling with holy water, Eur.
to sew up again, Hdt., Aeschin.
to speak in fragments of epic poetry, Xen.
to offer some of a thing, c. gen. partit., Theocr.
to flow or run off, stream forth, Hdt., Aesch.; ἀπό τινος Hdt.; ἔκ τινος Plat.
to fall off, as fruit, feathers, leaves, etc., Hdt., attic
to die away, fade from remembrance, Soph.
a fragment, Plut.
to break off, snap asunder, Hom., etc.; πνεῦμ’ ἀπορρῆξαι βίου to snap the thread of life, Aesch.; ἀπ. βίον Eur.
Pass., aor.2 to be broken off, severed, Hdt., Thuc.; ἀπό τινος Hdt.
intr. in perf. to be broken, Archil.
a forbidding, prohibition, Plat.
a giving up a point, refusal, Id.
forbidden, ἀπόρρητον πόλει though it was forbidden to the citizens, Soph.; τὰ ἀπόρρητα prohibited exports, contraband articles, Ar.

not to be spoken, that should not be spoken, Lat. tacendus, ἀπ. ποιεῖσθαι to keep secret, Hdt.; κύριος καὶ ῥητῶν καὶ ἀπορρήτων, of Philip, like dicenda tacenda, Dem.: ἀπόρρητον, ου, τό, a state-secret, Ar.
of sacred things, ineffable, Eur.
unfit to be spoken, abominable, Plat.
to shrink shivering from a thing, shrink from doing it, c. inf., Od.
to file off, Strab.
to throw away, put away, Il.
to cast forth from one's country, Aesch., Soph.; ἀπερριμμένοι outcasts, Dem.
to disown, renounce, Soph.
to throw aside, set at naught, Aesch.: Pass., ἀπέρριπται ἐς τὸ μηδέν Hdt.
of words, to shoot forth bold, keen words, ἔς τινα at one, Id.:— also, ἀπ. ἔπος to let fall a word, Id.
a flowing off, stream, Eur., Xen.
an efflux, emanation, Plat.
to shriek forth, βοάς Soph.
to swallow some of a thing, c. gen. partit., Xen.
to cleanse thoroughly, Luc.: Mid. to cleanse oneself, Plut.
running, Hes.: ἀπ. σταθμά stables with drains, Xen.
broken off, abrupt, sheer, precipitous, Lat. praeruptus, Od., Xen.
as fem. Subst. a piece broken off, Στυγὸς ἀπορρώξ a branch or off-stream of the Styx, Il.
ἀπ. νέκταρος an efflux, distillation of nectar, Od.
Pass. to be orphaned or bereaved, Aesch.; ἀπό τινος ἀπ. to be torn away from one, NTest.
without purple border, Plut.
Dep. to dance a thing away, i. e. lose by dancing, τὸν γάμον Hdt.
to lie in the open sea, to ride at anchor, Thuc., Dem.
to make clear, Plat.
to put out, extinguish, quench, Ar., Plat., etc.
Pass., with fut. mid. aor2 and perf. act. intr., and aor1 pass.— to be extinguished, go out, cease to exist, Eur., Xen.
to shake off:— Mid. to shake off from oneself, Theogn.; of a horse, to throw his rider, Hdt., Xen.; metaph., ἀποσείεσθαι λύπην Ar.
to make august, glorify, Plat.
Pass., with fut. mid., to give oneself airs, Ar.; τι about a thing, Id.
to chase away, Anth.:—Pass., with 3rd sg. epic aor2 ἀπέσσυτο, aor.1, to dart away, Il.
to give notice by signs, give notice, περί τινος Hdt.: absol. to give a sign, Plat.
c. acc. to indicate by signs, betoken, Plut.:—Mid. to show by signs or proofs, Hdt.
ἀπ. εἴς τινα to allude to him, Thuc.
Mid. to seal up as confiscated, to confiscate, Xen.: of persons, to proscribe, Id.
to lose by mortification, or frost-bite, τοὺς δακτύλους Xen.
to make flat-nosed: Pass., ἀποσεσιμώμεθα τὴν ῥῖνα we have snub noses, Luc.
ἀποσιμοῦν τὰς ναῦς to turn the ships aside, make a sideward movement, so as to avoid the direct shock, Thuc.
abstaining from food, Luc.
to cease speaking, maintain silence, Isocr., Plut.
trans. to keep secret, Luc.
a becoming silent, Plut.
a rhetorical figure, when the sentence is broken off, as in Il. 1. 342, Virgil Aen. 1. 135.
to intercept by trenches, Xen.
to scatter abroad, disperse, Hom., Soph.:—Pass. to straggle from the ranks, of soldiers, Xen.
one must look steadily, Arist.
to pull off:— Mid. to pack up and carry off, to make away with, Luc.
to encamp apart from, τινός Xen.
encamping apart, messing alone, Xen.
to keep apart from, Plut.
= ἀποσκηνέω, Id.
to hurl from above, ἀπ. βέλεα ἔστι to hurl thunderbolts upon, Hdt.
intr. to fall suddenly, like a thunderbolt, ἔς τινα Eur., Aeschin.; ἀπ. ἐς φλαῦρον to come to a sorry ending, Hdt.
to cast a shadow, Plat.
the casting a shadow, ἀπ. γνωμόνων measures of time by the shadow on the sun-dial, Plut.
to be dispersed, Il.; of soldiers, ἀπ. ἔς τι to disperse for a purpose, Hdt.
to be dried up, to wither, Ar.; so perf. ἀπέσκληκα Luc.; fut. ἀποσκλήσω Anth.
to look away from other objects at one, to look steadily, πρός τινα or τι Soph., Plat.; εἴς τι Soph.
c. acc. to look to, regard, Eur.; so in Mid., Plut.
far from the mark, Anth.
to strip off the scalp in Scythian fashion: metaph. in Pass. to be shaved bare, κρᾶτ’ ἀπεσκυθισμένη Eur.

sense.gloss: to carry off as spoil from

entry.sense: to banter, rally, τινά Plat.; ἀπ. εἴς τινα to jeer at one, Luc.
to wipe off dirt, Luc.: Pass. to be wiped clean, Id.
to diminish, Luc.
to be consumed by a slow fire, to pine away, Luc.
to scare away, as one does birds or flies, Ar.; metaph., ἀποσοβῆσαι τὸν γέλων Id.
intr. to be off in a hurry, οὐκ ἀποσοβήσεις; i. e. be off! Id.
torn off or away, ἀποσπάδιον, ου, τό, = ἀπόσπασμα, Anth.
to tear off, Eur.
that which is torn off, a piece, rag, shred, Plat.
a slip torn from a tree, a vine-branch or bunch of grapes, Anth.: and

to tear or drag away from, τινός Soph., Plat., etc.; ἀπ. τινα ἀπὸ γυναικός Hdt.; τὸ τέκνον ἐκ χερῶν Eur.; also c. dupl. acc. to tear a thing from one, Soph.:— ἀπ. τινά to tear him away, Hdt.:—Mid. to drag away for oneself, Plut.:—Pass. to be dragged away, detached, separated from, τινός Pind., Eur.; ἐξ ἱροῦ Hdt.; ἀπὸ τῶν ἱερῶν Thuc.
ἀπ. πύλας to tear off the gates, Hdt.
ἀπ. τὸ στρατόπεδον to draw off the army, Xen.; absol., ἀποσπάσας having drawn off, Id.:—Pass., of troops, to be separated or broken, Thuc.
to pour out wine as a drink offering, Od., Eur.
to be zealous in preventing a thing, Hdt.; c. acc. et inf., a)p. *je/rcea strateu/esqaiἀπ. Ξέρξεα στρατεύεσθαι Id.
to wear quite off, ἀπ. τοὺς ὄνυχας to walk one's toes off, Ar.
standing aloof, Hom.
to let fall drop by drop, distil, Theocr.
intr. to fall in drops, distil, Soph.
defection, Plut.
ἀποστασίου δίκη an action against a freedman for having forsaken or slighted his προστάτης, Dem.: ἀποστασίου βιβλίον, ου, τό, a writing or bill of divorce, NTest.
a standing away from, and so,
a defection, revolt, ἀπό τινος or τινος Hdt., Thuc.; πρός τινα Thuc.
departure from, βίου Eur.
distance, interval, Plat.
one must stand off from or give up a thing, c. gen., Thuc., Dem.
to stand aloof from, depart from, be far from, c. gen., Aesch., Soph.; ἀπ. φίλων to fall off from one's friends, Ar.
absol. to stand aloof or afar off, Aesch.
one who has power to dissolve an assembly, Lycurg. ap. Plut.
a runaway slave: a deserter, rebel, Plut.
of or for rebels, Plut.:—adv., ἀποστατικῶς ἔχειν to be ready for revolt, Id.
to fence off with a palisade, Thuc.
to uncover: to take off a roof, NTest.
to keep out water: metaph. to keep out or off, ὄχλον πύργος ἀποστέγει Aesch.
to keep in water, confine it, check its outflow, Plat.
to go away, to go home, Od., Hdt.; imperat. ἀπόστιχε Il., Hdt.
to send off or away from, γῆς, χθονός Soph., Eur.; ἔξω χθονός Eur.; ἐκ τῆς πόλεως Plat.: absol. to send away, banish, Soph., Eur.:—Pass. to go away, depart, set out, Soph., Eur.
to send off, despatch, on some service, Soph.; of troops and ships, Hdt., Thuc.
intr. to go back, retire, of the sea, Thuc.; of seamen, Dem.
to straiten, block up: Pass., 3rd sg. plup. pass. ἀπεστείνωτο Theocr.
to love no more, Theocr.:—hence to put away from one, reject, Lat. abominari, Aesch.

to rob, despoil, bereave or defraud one of a thing, c. acc. pers. et gen. rei, Hdt., Ar.; also, c. acc. pers. et rei, μή μ’ ἀποστερήσηις ἡδονάν Soph., etc.: absol. to defraud, cheat, Ar.:—Pass. to be robbed or deprived of, c. gen., Ἑλλάδος ἀπεστερημένος Hdt., attic; also c. acc., ἵππους ἀπεστέρηνται Xen.
ἀπ. ἑαυτόν τινος to detach, withdraw oneself from . . , Soph., Thuc.
c. acc. pers. to deprive, rob, Hdt., attic;— τὸ σαφές μ’ ἀποστερεῖ certainty fails me, Eur.
c. acc. rei only, to filch away, withhold, Aesch., etc.
deprivation, τῆς ἀκοῆς Thuc.
a depriver, robber, Plat.
of or for cheating, γνώμη ἀπ. τόκου a device for cheating one of his interest, Ar.; so fem. ἀποστερητρίς.
distance, interval, τοῖς ἀπ. πρὸς τοὺς γονεῖς in point of intervals, in relation to one's parents, Arist.
Mid. to fix firmly, Anth.
to make to shine, Anth.
to be bright from or with oil, c. gen., ἀπ. ἀλείφατος Od.
to scrape with a strigil:— Mid. to scrape oneself clean, Xen.; perf. pass. part. ἀπεστλεγγισμένοι, scraped clean, fresh from the bath, Ar.
at Athens, a magistrate who had to fit out a squadron for service, Dem., Aeschin.
a sending off or away, despatching, Eur., Thuc.
(from Pass.) a going away, an expedition, Thuc.
the office of an apostle, apostleship, NTest.
a messenger, ambassador, envoy, Hdt.
a sacred messenger, an Apostle, NTest.
= στόλος, a naval squadron or expedition, Dem., etc.
to dictate by word of mouth, teach by dictation, γράμματα Plat.
to question sharply or to provoke one to speak, NTest.
to recite, repeat by heart, Plut.
a retired general, Dem.
Dep. to encamp away from, τινός Xen.; ἀπ. πρόσω to encamp at a distance, Id.

to turn one back, i. e. either to turn to flight, put to flight, Hom.; or to turn him back from flight, Xen.; πόδας καὶ χεῖρας to twist back the hands and feet so as to bind them, Od.; so τὸν αὐχένα Hdt.:— to turn back, avert one's face, Od., Eur.: to bring back, recall, Xen.
to turn away, to divert the course of a river, Hdt.: to avert a danger, Aesch., Thuc.
intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν, ἵππον, ναῦν, etc.), to turn back, Hdt., Soph.
Pass., ἀπεστράφθαι τοὺς ἐμβόλους, of ships, to have their beaks bent back, Hdt.; ἀποστραφῆναι τὼ πόδε to have one's feet twisted, Ar.
to turn away from, in abhorrence, Lat. aversari, c. acc., Soph., Eur.; absol., ἀπεστραμμένοι λόγοι hostile words, Hdt.
to turn oneself about, turn back, Xen.; to turn and flee, Id.
ἀποστραφῆναί τινος to fall off from one, desert him, Id.
a turning back, Xen.; ἀποστροφὴν λαμβάνειν to have one's course turned, Plut.
a turning away from, an escape from a thing, c. gen., Aesch., Eur.
a resort, resource, Hdt.:—c. gen. objecti, ὕδατος ἀπ. a resource or means for getting water, Id.; σωτηρίας ἀπ. Thuc.
turned away, Soph.
to hate violently, abhor, loathe, Hdt., Soph.; c. inf. to be disgusted that.., Hdt.
to drive away by force from, τινά τινος Il.
to draw up, contract, of astringents, to dull the sense of taste, Anth.
to squeeze figs, to try whether they are ripe, Ar.
to strip off spoils from a person, to rob or defraud one of a thing, τινά τινος Soph.; τινά τι Eur., Xen.:—Pass., ἀποσυλᾶσθαί τι to be robbed of a thing, Aesch.
put out of the synagogue, NTest.
to whistle aloud for want of thought, Hhymn.:—Pass. to sound like whistling, Luc.
to tear away, Thuc.
to lay bare, Theocr.
to cut the throat of a person, Lat. jugulo, ἀποσφ. τινὰ ἐς ἄγγος, so that the blood runs into a pail, Hdt.: generally, to slay, Ar., Thuc., etc.:—Mid. to cut one's own throat, Xen.
to have the limbs frost-bitten, Hdt.
to fall into convulsions, Plut.
to lead astray, drive away, Od.; ἀπ. τινὰ πόνοιο to baulk them of the fruits of toil, Il.
Pass., aor2 ἀπεσφάλην [α], to be baulked or disappointed of a thing, c. gen., Hdt.: to be deprived of, Aesch.: to fail in reaching, Ἰταλίας Plut.: absol. to be missing or lost, Dem.
to compress, Luc.: Pass., λόγος ἀπεσφιγμένος a close-packed style, Id.
to seal up, Plut.:—so in Mid., Eur.
a forked piece of wood for propping hunting-nets, Xen.
to split or cleave off, Od., Eur.

to sever or detach from, τινὰ ἀπό τινος Hdt.:—Pass., ἀποσχισθῆναί τινος to be separated from . . ., Id.; of a river, to be parted from the main stream, Id.; of a tribe, to be detached from its parent stock, Id.
metaph., ἀπ. τινὰ τοῦ λόγου to cut him off from his speech, interrupt him in it, Ar.
to separate by a cord: generally, to separate, Dem.
to preserve from, heal from or of a thing, τινός Soph.; ἀπ. οἴκαδε to bring safe home, Xen.:—Pass., ἀποσωθῆναι ἐς or ἐπὶ τόπον to get safe to a place, Hdt., Xen.: absol. to get off safe, Hdt.
set apart for a special use, Hdt.
to set apart, assign specially, χώραν τινί Plat.:—Pass., ἀπετέτακτο πρὸς τὸ δεξιόν had his appointed post on the right, Xen.
Mid., ἀποτάσσεσθαί τινι to bid farewell to a person or thing, NTest.
Pass. to be like a bull: δέργμα ἀποταυροῦσθαι to cast savage glances at.., Eur.
to fence off with a ditch, Xen.
to stretch out, extend— Pass., Xen.
to lengthen, extend, prolong, of the line of an army, Id.; of speeches, ἀπ. τὸν λόγον Plat.
so as to fortify, τὸν Ἰσθμόν Hdt.
so as to blockade, τινάς Ar., Thuc., etc.
the walling off a town, blockading, Thuc.
a wall built to blockade, lines of blockade, Thuc., Xen.
intr. to end, εἴς τι in a thing, Plat.
to bring quite to an end, complete a work, Hdt., Xen., etc.:—Pass., perf. part. ἀποτετελεσμένος, perfect, Xen.
to pay or perform what one is bound to pay or perform, as vows to a god, Hdt., Xen.: generally, to accomplish, perform, Xen.
to render or make of a certain kind, τὴν πόλιν ἀπ. εὐδαίμονα to make the state quite happy, Plat.; and Mid., ἄμεμπτον φίλον ἀποτελέσασθαι to make him without blame towards himself, Xen.
to cut off, sever, Il., Hdt., attic:—Pass., τὴν γλῶτταν ἀποτμηθείς having his tongue cut out, Aeschin.
to sever, divide, in a geographical sense, Hdt.:—Pass., of troops, to be cut off from the main body, Xen.
Mid. to cut off for oneself, Il.; c. gen. to cut off a bit of a thing, Hdt.
to cut off, so as to appropriate, βοῦς Hhymn., Hdt.; Φοινίκης ἀπ. to have a slice or portion of Phoenicia, Theocr.; ἀπ. τῶν Ἀθηναίων to cut off power from the Athenians, Thuc.
a failure, Plut.
far from, c. gen., Anth.
far away, Od.
to put away, stow away, Il.
Mid. to put away from oneself, lay aside, of arms and clothes, Id., Hdt.; ἀπ. τὸν νόμον to put aside, i. e. disregard, the law, Thuc.
to avoid, escape, of something odious, Il.
to put by for oneself, stow away, Ar., Xen.
ἀποτίθεσθαι εἰς αὖθις to put off, defer Eur., Xen., etc.
to pluck or pull out, τὰς τρίχας Hdt.; οὐδὲν ἀποτίλας without pulling off any of the fur, Id.
a piece plucked off, Theocr.
to put away from honour, to dishonour, slight, Hhymn.
Mid. to fix a price by valuation, διμνέως ἀποτιμησάμενοι having fixed their price at two minae a head, Hdt.
as attic law term, Act. to borrow money on mortgage; Mid. to lend on mortgage; Pass. of the property, to be mortgaged, Dem.
a mortgage, security, Dem.
a mortgaging, Dem.
the Rom. census, Plut.
put away from honour, dishonoured, Hdt., Soph.
to shake off, Eur.
to pay back, repay, return, τί τινι Il.
to pay for a thing, τι Hom., Aesch., etc.: absol. to make atonement, Il.
to pay in full, Hdt., attic
Mid. ἀποτίνομαι and ἀποτίνυμαι: fut. -τίσομαι:— to get paid one, to exact or require a penalty from a man, ποινήν Il.; δίκην Eur.
c. acc. pers., ἀποτίσασθαί τινα to avenge oneself on another, punish him, Od., Xen.
c. acc. rei, to take vengeance for a thing, punish it, Od.; so, c. gen. rei, Hdt.:—absol. to take vengeance, Theogn.
one must pay, Xen.
epic for ἀποτέμνω, to cut off from, τινά τινος Il.
to cut off, sever, Id.; κλιτῦς ἀπ. to cut up or plough the hill-sides, Id.
one must cut off, τῆς χώρας a portion of it, Plat.
unhappy, ill-starred, Hom., Aesch., Eur.: —comp. -ότερος; Sup. -ότατος, Od.
to make a bold venture, τινί upon one, Thuc.: c. inf., Aeschin.: Pass., τὰ ἀποτετολμημένα what has been hazarded, Plat.
a cutting off, Xen.
cut off, abrupt, precipitous, Hdt.; ἀπότομον ὤρουσεν εἰς ἀνάγκαν, metaph. from one who comes suddenly to the edge of a cliff, Soph.
metaph. severe, relentless, Eur.
to shoot off arrows, Luc.
to shoot a person, τινά τινι Id.
not drinkable, Hdt.
act. never drinking, Id., Plat.:— not drinking, without drink, Soph., Xen.
to turn one away from a thing, c. gen., Il.:— to turn away, deter or dissuade from, Thuc.; also, c. inf., ἀπ. τινὰ ποιεῖν τι Aesch., Dem.
c. acc. pers. only, to turn away, turn back, Il.
c. acc. rei, to turn aside, avert, prevent, Hdt., Plat.; cf. ἀποτρόπαιος, ἀπότροπος.
to turn from others against one, τι ἐπί τινι Soph.:—Mid., ἀποτραπόμενος πρός τι turning away from other objects to this one, Plut.
Mid. and Pass. to turn from, to desist from doing a thing, c. part., Il., c. inf., Eur., etc.:—absol. to stop, desist, Thuc.
to turn away, turn a deaf ear, Il.
c. acc. rei, to turn away from, like Lat. aversari, Aesch., Eur.
to turn back, return, Thuc., Xen.
to run off or away, Hdt., attic
to run hard, of one training for a race, Ar.
to wear out, Od.
to rub clean, to rub down a horse, Xen.
to rub off, Theocr.:—Mid. to get rid of, Dem., Aeschin.: to decline, reject, τὴν πεῖραν Plut.
averting evil, of Apollo, Lat. averruncus, Ar., etc.
pass. that ought to be averted, ill-omened, Luc.
a turning away, averting, κακῶν Aesch., Eur.
a hindering, prevention, Thuc.
(from Mid.) desertion of one's party, Id.
turned away, banished, Od.
from which one turns away, direful, grim, Aesch., Soph.
act. turning away, averting, a thing, c. gen., Aesch., Eur.
reared away from home, Hdt.
= ἀποτρύω, Plut.
to rub away, wear out, Soph.:— Mid., γῆν ἀποτρύεσθαι to vex constantly the earth, by working it, Soph.
to bite or nibble off, Ar.
c. gen. to nibble at, τᾶς αὔλακος οὐκ ἀποτρώγεις, i. e. you don't get on with your swathe, in reaping, Theocr.
Frequentat. of ἀποτρέπω, only in pres., Hom.
to fail in hitting or gaining, to miss, lose, c. gen., Xen., etc.
Pass., τὰ ἀποτετευγμένα things not come to pass, Luc.
absol. to miss one's object, to be unlucky, fail, Xen.: to miss the truth, err, Id.:—c. inf. to fail to do, Id.
to cudgel to death, bastinado, Dem.
Mid. to stamp an impression as on wax, εἴς τι Plat.
Act. ἀπ. σφραγῖδα to impress a seal, Luc.
Mid. to cease to beat oneself, to cease mourning, Hdt.
will mark off, i. e. contract, the boundaries of his fields, Il.: others read ἀπ-ουρήσουσι, = ἀπ-αυρήσουσι (from ἀπ-αυράω) will take away.
far from the boundaries of one's country, c. gen., Soph.
a being away, absence, Aesch., Eur., etc.
without foot or feet, Plat.
without the use of one's feet, halt, lame, Soph.
to cleanse off: Mid., Anth.
to shew fort, display, produce, Hdt., Ar.
to make known, declare, Hdt.: to give evidence of a thing, Id.
to shew by reasoning, shew, represent as doing or being, c. part., Id.; and with part. omitted, ἀπ. ἑωϋτὸν αἴτιον (sc. ὄντα) Id.; so, ἀπ. τινα ἐχθρόν Dem.
c. acc. et inf. to represent that, Plat.; so, ἀπ. ὡς . . , ὅτι . . , Hdt., Thuc.
to give an account of, τὴν οὐσίαν Dem.: to pay in money to the treasury, Id.
to render or make so and so, Ar.
to appoint to an office, Plat.
Mid. to display something of one's own, Aesch. Plat.: absol. to make a display of oneself, shew off, Xen.
to produce evidence, Hdt.
ἀποφαίνεσθαι γνώμην to declare one's opinion, Id., attic:— absol. to give an opinion, Hdt., attic. Hence
used like Act., Plat., Xen.
a declaration, statement, Arist.
a denial, negation, opp. to κατάφασις, Plat.
a sentence, decision of a court, Dem.
a list, inventory, Id.
to deny, οὔτε δοκοῦντ’ οὔτ’ ἀποφάσκοντ’ neither in assent nor denial, Soph.
Mid. to feed on, τι Eur.
to carry off or away, Lat. auferre, Hom., etc.:—Pass. to be carried from one's course, Hdt., Thuc.
to carry or bring back, Il., attic: Pass., of persons, to return, Hdt., Thuc.
to pay back, return, Hdt.: hence to pay what is due, Id.
as attic law term, to give in an accusation, accounts, etc., Dem., etc.
intr. to be off, ἀπόφερ’ ἐς κόρακας Ar.
Mid. to take away with one, Hdt., etc.: to carry off a prize, Theocr.
to take for oneself, gain, obtain, Eur.
to bring back for oneself, Hdt.; ἀπ. βίον μητρί, i. e. to return to her alive, Eur.
to flee from, escape, c. acc., Hdt., etc.:—absol. to get safe away, escape, Id.
as law-term, to escape from, τοὺς διώκοντας Id., attic; also, ἀπ. δίκην Ar., Dem.: —absol. to get clear off, be acquitted, Hdt.
useful in escaping: τὰ ἀπ. means of acquittal, Xen.
an escaping, means of getting off, ἀπ. δίκης acquittal, Ar.
to speak out, declare flatly or plainly, Il.; so in Mid., Id.
to say no, Soph.
c. acc. to refuse, deny, Xen., Plat.
Dep. to speak one's opinion plainly, Luc.:—metaph. to ring, Id.
= ἄφθεγκτος, Eur.
a terse pointed saying, an apophthegm, Xen.
dealing in apophthegms, sententious, Plut.
to destroy utterly, ruin, Aesch., Eur.

Pass., with fut. mid., to be lost, perish, Eur., Thuc.: esp. as interrog. used in an imperat. sense, οὐ γῆς τῆσδ’ ἀποφθαρήσεται; i. e. let him begone with a plague to him, Eur.; so, οὐκ εἰς κόρακας ἀποφθερεῖ; Lat. pasce corvos, Ar.
only in pres. to perish, Il.
trans. to lose, Id.
intr. in pres. to perish utterly, die away, Aesch., Soph.
Causal in fut. -φθιῶ, aor1 -έφθισα [ῑ epic, ι Trag.] to make to perish, waste away, destroy, Hes., Soph.: to lose, βίον Aesch.
Pass., = Act. intr., to perish, die, esp. in epic aor2 -έφθιτο [ι], imperat. -φθίσθω, -φθίμην [ῑ], part. -φθίμενος [ι], also in 3rd pl. epic aor1 ἀπέφθιθεν.
utter destruction, Aesch.
to treat slightingly, make no account of, τι Hdt.
to strip off oneself, Anth.
to cease to go to school, Plat.
unnatural murder, Eur.
payment of what is due, tax, tribute, Hdt., attic
also, return for money spent, profit, Xen., etc.
to fence off, block up, Thuc.: metaph., Soph.
a blocking up, Xen.
ἀποφράσσω, Plat., Dem. —Mid., ἀποφράξασθαι αὐτούς to bar their passage, Thuc.
not to be mentioned: ἀποφράδες ἡμέραι, Lat. dies nefasti, days on which no business was done, Plat.
= ἀποφεύγω, Dem.
an escape or place of refuge, ἀποφυγὰς παρέχειν Thuc.; ἀπ. κακῶν escape from ills, Plat.
to blow away, Ar.
to breathe out life, Luc.
empty, vain, idle, useless, fruitless, Lat. irritus, Od.
Dep., only in pres., to withdraw from a place, c. gen., Od.
to slack away a rope: metaph., ἀποχάλα τὴν φροντίδα Ar.
to unbridle, Xen.
to forge of copper, Xen.
to strip of brass, i. e. money, Anth.
= ἀποσταυρόω, Plut.
living by the work of one's hands, Hdt., Xen.
to vote a charge away from one, acquit him, c. gen., Dem.
c. acc., ἀπ. τινα τῆς ἀρχῆς to depose him from the command, Plut.
of things, to vote against, reject, annul, Ar., Dem.
ἀπ. τι μὴ εἶναι to vote that a thing is not, Dem.
rejection by show of hands, Dem.
to pour out or off, shed, let fall, Od.:—poet. Mid. ἀποχεύομαι, Eur.
abstinence, Plut.
a receipt, quittance, Anth.
Pass. to be bereft of, τινος Ar.
to soften away the colour, shade off, Plat.
to use to the full, c. dat. rei or absol., Thuc.
to suffice, be sufficient, be enough: absol., in persons other than 3rd sg., δύ’ ἀποχρήσουσιν μόνω Ar.; c. inf., ἀποχρέουσι ἑκατὸν νέες χειρώσασθαι are sufficient to subdue, Hdt.
mostly in 3 sing:
to suffice, ποταμὸς οὐκ ἀπέχρησε τῆι στρατιῆι πινόμενος was not enough to supply the army with drink, Id.; ταῦτα ἀποχρᾶι μοι Id., attic

impers., c. inf., ἀποχρᾶι μοι ποιεῖν 'tis sufficient for me to do, Hdt., ; c. part., μέρος ἐχούσηι ἀπόχρη μοι 'tis sufficient for me to have a part, Aesch.;—and without inf., ἀπόχρη τινι it is enough for him, Dem.
Pass. to be contented with a thing, c. dat., Hdt.
impers., οὐκ ἀπεχρᾶτο Id.; ἀπεχρέετο, c. inf., Id.
to abuse, misuse, Lat. abuti, c. dat., Dem.
c. acc. to use up, destroy, Thuc.
ζημία ἀποχρ. a penalty but not of money, Aesch.
enough, sufficiently, Thuc.
to secure by fortifications: metaph. in perf. pass. part., ἀπωχυρωμένος πρός τι secure against a thing, Plat.
to make quite lame, Xen.
Pass. to be made quite lame, Thuc.
to bank up the mouth of a river, Xen.
to go from or away from a place, c. gen., Ar.
absol. to go away, depart, Eur.: to retire, retreat, Thuc., Xen.:— ἀπ. εἴς τι to have recourse to a thing, Dem.
ἀπ. ἐκ . . , to withdraw from a thing, i. e. give it up, Xen.
to pass off from the bowels, Id.: also, τὰ ἀποχωροῦντα excrements, Id.
a going off, retreat, Hdt., Thuc.: a place or means of safety, Hdt.
to part or separate from, τι ἀπό τινος Plat.
the damming up of a river, Plut.
to wipe off, Eur.:—Mid. to wipe or rub off from oneself, Ar.
c. acc. pers. to wipe clean: — Mid. to wipe oneself, wipe one's nose, Id.; also, ἀποψ. τὴν χεῖρα εἴς τι Xen.
Pass. to be quite cheated of a thing, c. gen., Plut.

to vote away from, θάνατον ἀπ. τινός to vote death away from him, refuse to condemn him to death, opp. to καταψηφίζεσθαι, Lycurg.:—hence ἀπ. τινός to vote a charge away from one, i. e. to acquit him, Dem., etc.:—absol. to vote an acquittal, Plat.
to vote the franchise away from one, i. e. to disfranchise by vote, Dem.:— Pass. to be disfranchised, Id.
c. acc. rei, of judges, ἀπ. γραφήν to vote against receiving the indictment, Aeschin.
ἀπ. μὴ ποιεῖν τι to vote against doing, Xen.
to strip bare, Hdt.
c. gen. to strip bare of a thing, c. gen., Aesch.
an outlook, view, prospect, Hdt.
a lofty spot or tower which commands a view, Plut.
to leave off breathing, to faint, swoon, Od., NTest.
c. acc., ἀπέψυξεν βίον breathed out life, Soph.: absol., like ἀποπνέω, Lat. exspiro, to expire, die Thuc.
to cool:— Pass., ἱδρῶ ἀπεψύχοντο χιτώνων they got the sweat dried off their tunics, Il.; ἱδρῶ ἀποψυχθείς Id.; metaph., ἀπεψυγμένοι cold, indifferent, Arist.
impers., ἀποψύχει it grows, cool, the air cools, Plat.
an exclamation, Ar.
idleness, want of energy, Plut.
freedom from politics and business (πράγματα), love of a quiet life, love of ease, supineness, Lat. otium, Ar., Xen.; of states that keep clear of foreign politics, Thuc.

free from business (πράγματα), keeping clear of politics, a good easy quiet man, opp. to πολυπράγμων (a restless meddlesome man), Ar., Thuc., etc.; πόλις ἄπρ. a country that keeps clear of foreign politics, Thuc.; τὸ ἄπραγμον = Lat. otium, Id.; τόπος ἀπρ. a place free from law and strife, Ar.
of things, not troublesome or painful, Xen.; so adv. -μόνως, without trouble, Thuc.
to do nothing, Arist.
to gain nothing, παρά τινος Xen.
act. doing nothing, ineffectual, unprofitable, Il., Dem.

of persons, without success, unsuccessful, ἄπρηκτος νέεσθαι, Lat. re infecta, Il.; and in Prose, ἄπρ. ἀπιέναι, ἀπελθεῖν, ἀποχωρεῖν Thuc.; ἄπρ. γίγνεσθαι to gain nothing, Id.; ἄπρακτον ἀποπέμπειν τινά Id.:—adv. -τως, unsuccessfully, Id.
pass. against which nothing can be done, impracticable, Od.
not to be done, impossible, Theogn.
not done, left undone, Xen.
c. gen., μαντικῆς ἄπρακτος ὑμῖν unassailed by your divining arts, Soph.
a not acting, inaction, Eur., Plat.
rest from business, in pl. holidays, Plut.
want of success, Aeschin.
want of purchasers, no sale, Dem.
unsold, unsaleable, Dem.
unseemly conduct; indecency, impropriety, Plat.
unseemly, unbecoming, indecent, indecorous, Thuc., etc.; τὸ ἀπρεπές = ἀπρέπεια, Id.:— adv. -πῶς, poet. -πέως,Hhymn., Plat.
of persons, disreputable, Theocr.
poet. for ἀπρέπεια, ugliness, Anth.
implacable, Anth.
without purchase-money or ransom, Hom.
= ἀπρίξ, Aesch.
struck unceasingly, Aesch.
with closed teeth, Lat. mordicus: hence fast, tight, ἀπρὶξ συλλαβεῖν Soph.
without set purpose, not deliberate, of actions, Arist.
not planned beforehand, unpremeditated, Arist.
not submitted to the βουλή, Dem.
act. without forethought, Arist.:—adv. -τως, Plat.
without premeditation:— adv. -λως, recklessly, Aesch.
not eager or ready, unready, backward, Hdt., Thuc.
unforeseen, Anth.
without portion or dowry, ἄπροικον τὴν ἀδελφὴν διδόναι to give her in marriage without dowry, Isae.
want of forethought, Plat.
unpremeditated, ἀκρασία Arist.
act. improvident, Xen.:—adv. -τως, Id.
without preface, Luc.
unforeseen, Aesch.
unapproachable, Soph.
without want of more, Luc.
uncongenial to Bacchus: hence, not to the point, out of place, Cic., Luc.
unexpected, unlooked for, Aesch., etc.; ἐξ ἀπροσδοκήτου, Lat. necopinato, Hdt.; so adv. -τως, Thuc.
act. not expecting, unaware, Id.
want of intercourse by speech, Arist.
not to be accosted, savage, Soph.
not to be attained, Pind.
unapproachable, Plut.
unforeseen, Xen.
act. improvident, Dem.
of a trial in support of which no summons has been issued, Dem.
not stumbling, void of offence, Aesch., NTest.
giving no offence, Id.
irresistible, Soph.
holding no communion with others, c. dat., Hdt.
not to be withstood, irresistible, Aesch.
unsociable, Soph.
unapproachable, Strab., Plut.
ἀπροστασίου γραφή, at Athens, an indictment of a μέτοικος for not having chosen a patron from among the citizens, Dem.
unsuitable, dangerous, Eur.
not respecting persons. adv. -τως, without respect of persons, NTest.
without a face, i. e. without beauty of face, Plat.
untouched, undefiled, Il.
offering no excuse, unhesitating, Thuc., Xen. adv. -τως, without disguise, without evasion, honestly, Thuc.
not guarded against, unforeseen, Thuc.
not stumbling, ἀπταιστότερος less apt to stumble, Xen.
without wings, unwinged, in phrase τῆι δ’ ἄπτερος ἔπλετο μῦθος the speech was to her without wings, i. e. did not fly away, sank into her heart, Od.; ἄπτερα πωτήματα wingless flight, Aesch.
unfeathered, of the Harpies, Id.; of arrows, Hdt.
of young birds, unfledged, callow, Eur.:—metaph., φάτις ἄπτ. an unfledged, i. e. unconfirmed, report, Aesch.
unfledged, callow, of young birds, Il.
unwinged, Ar.
undaunted in speech, Il.
subject to the sense of touch, Plat.

entry.etym: v. ἑάφθη for ionic perf. pass.
entry.sense: to fasten, bind fast, Od., Eur.: Mid. to fasten for oneself, Od., Eur.
to join, χορόν Aesch.; πάλην τινὶ ἅπτειν to fasten a contest in wrestling on one, engage with one, Id.
Mid. to fasten oneself to, cling to, hang on by, lay hold of, grasp, touch, c. gen., ἅψασθαι γούνων, as a suppliant, Od.; so, ἅψ. γενείου Id.; ἅπτεσθαι νηῶν Il., etc.:—absol. to reach the mark, Id.

to engage in, take part in, c. gen., βουλευμάτων Soph.; πολέμου Thuc.; ἡμμένος φόνου engaged in . . , Plat.;—but, ἅπτεσθαι τῶν λόγων to lay hold of, dispute the argument of another, Id.; τούτων ἥψατο touched on these points, Thuc.
to set upon, attack, assail, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
to touch, affect, ἄλγος οὐδὲν ἅπτεται νεκρῶν Aesch., etc.
to grasp with the senses, apprehend, perceive, Soph., Plat.
to come up to, reach, gain, Plat., Xen.
Act., also, to kindle, set on fire, Hdt., Thuc.:— Pass., with fut. mid. to be set on fire, catch fire, Od., Hdt.
ἅπτειν πῦρ to light a fire, Eur.:—Pass., ἄνθρακες ἡμμένοι red-hot embers, Thuc.
not liable to fall or fail, Plat.
not secured by gates, Xen.
not girt with towers, Od.

without fire, of pans and tripods, that have not yet been on the fire, fire-new, brand-new, Il.: — without fire, i. e. cold, cheerless, οἶκος Hes.:— ἄπ. χρυσίον unsmelted, Hdt.:— ἄπυρα ἱερά sacrifices in which no fire was used, Pind.; but in Aesch. sacrifices without fire, i. e. that will not burn, or unoffered, neglected:— ἄπ. ἄρδις an arrow-point not forged in fire, i. e. the sting of the gad-fly, Aesch.
not yet exposed to fire, Il.
not heard of, Od.: ἄπυστα φωνῶν speaking what none can hear, Soph.
act. without hearing or learning a thing, Od.; c. gen., Id.
a term of endearment used by children to their father, papa, Theocr.
out of tune, Eur., Luc.
from afar, Soph., Eur.
c. gen. far from, Eur., Thuc.

to thrust away, push back, Il.; to push off, Thuc.: Mid. to push away from oneself, Hom.:—c. gen. to drive away from a place; and in Mid. to drive away from oneself, to expel, banish, Hom., Hdt., etc.
of the wind, to beat from one's course, Od.; so in Mid., Id.
in Mid., also, to reject, decline, refuse to accept, Hdt., attic; ἀπ. δουλοσύνην to shake off slavery, Hdt.
destruction, NTest.
without a lid, Babr.
abjured, declared impossible on oath, βροτοῖσιν οὐδέν ἐστ’ ἀπώμοτον Soph.
of persons, under oath not to do a thing, Id.
a driving away, Thuc.
one must reject, Eur.
thrust or driven away from a place, c. gen., Hdt., Soph.
that can be driven away, Hdt.
Sup. adv. of ἄπωθεν, furthest from, τινός Dem.
comp. adv. of ἄπωθεν, further off, Soph., etc. : proverb., ἀπ. ἢ γόνυ κνήμα Theocr.
to rattle, ring, clash, of armour, Il.; of the teeth, to gnash, Theocr.
Arabia, Hdt., poet. Ἀρραβία, Theocr.
Arabian, Plut.
Arabian, Hdt.
a gnashing or chattering of teeth, Il.
a clashing, clattering, rattling, Aesch.; ἀρ. πετρῶν a crashing shower of stones, Eur.; στέρνων ἀρ. beating of the breast, Lat. planctus, Soph.
pass. prayed to or entreated, Ζεὺς ἀραῖος, = ἱκέσιος, Soph.
prayed against, accursed, laden with a curse or curses, Aesch.; μ’ ἀραῖον ἔλαβες you adjured me under a curse, Soph.
act. cursing, bringing mischief upon a house or person, c. dat., Aesch., Soph.
thin, narrow, slight, slender, Lat. tenuis, Hom.
beaten with the hand, τύμπανα Anth.
to pray to a god, c. dat., Il.:—c. acc. to invoke, Od.
c. acc. et inf. to pray that, Il., Hdt., Soph.:—c. inf. only, to pray to be so and so, Od.

to pray something for one, τί τινι; sometimes in good sense, ἀρ. τινι ἀγαθά Hdt.; but usually in bad, to imprecate upon one, ἀρὰς ἀρ. τινι Soph., etc.; without an acc., ἀρᾶσθαί τινι to curse one, Eur.
c. inf. fut. to vow that one will or would, ἠρήσατο ῥέξειν Il.
interrog. Particle, in accent and sense a stronger form of ἄρα:
when it stands alone it usually expects a negative answer, like Lat. num? attic; so ἆρα μή; num vero? Aesch.:—for an affirmative answer, ἆρ’ οὐ; ἆρ’ οὐχί; nonne vero? is used, Soph., etc.
in prose, ἆρα almost always stands first in the sentence.
EPIC USAGE:
then, straightway, at once, ὣς φάτο, βῆ δ’ ἄρ’ ὄνειρος Il.: next in order, οἱ δ’ ἄρ’ Ἀθήνας εἶχον Id.

where attention is called to something startling, τὸν τρεῖς μὲν ἐπιρρήσσεσκον τῶν ἄλλων, Ἀχιλεὺς δ’ ἄρ’ ἐπιρρήσεσκε καὶ οἶος three men of the common sort were required to do it, but Achilles, mark ye did it single-handed, Id.

in explanation of a thing going before, εἰ μὴ ὑπερφίαλον ἔπος ἔκβαλε, φῆ ῥ’ ἀέκητι θεῶν φυγέειν had he not let fall an impious word, — for he said . . , Id.:—so, ἄρα makes relat. Pron. more precise, ἐκ δ’ ἔθορε κλῆρος, ὃν ἄρ’ ἤθελον αὐτοί just the one, the very one which . . , Id.

ATTIC USAGE, much like οὖν, then, therefore:— less strongly, μάτην ἄρ’ ἥκομεν so then we have come in vain, Soph.; εἰκότως ἄρα οὐκ ἐγίγνετο Xen.:— in questions, to express the anxiety of the questioner, as τίς ἄρα ῥύσεται; oh! who is there to save? Aesch.
POSITION: ἄρα never begins a sentence, cf. οὖν, Lat. igitur.

entry.etym: ᾱρ- mostly in epic: in attic always αρ-.
entry.sense: a prayer, Il., Hdt.
esp. a prayer for evil, a curse, imprecation, mostly in pl., Il., Trag.
the effect of the curse, bane, ruin, ἀρὴν καὶ λοιγὸν ἀμῦναι Il.
Ἀρά personified as the goddess of destruction and revenge, Lat. Dira, Soph.

entry.etym: transitive: aor1 ἦρσα, epic ἄρσα: aor.2 ἤραρον, ionic ἄραρον, inf. ἀραρεῖν, part. ἀραρών:— Pass., aor1 ἤρθην, epic 3rd pl. ἄρθεν.

intransitive: perf. ἄρᾱρα in pres. sense, ionic ἄρηρα, epic part. ἀρηρώς, with fem. ἀρηρυῖα and (metri grat.) ἀραρυῖα: epic plup. ἀρήρειν, ἠρήρειν, with imperf. sense: —of the Pass. we only find epic aor2 part. ἄρμενος, η, ον.
entry.sense: TRANS.:—
to join, join together, fasten, Il.; ἄγγεσιν ἄρσον ἅπαντα pack up everything in the vessels, Od.
to fit together, construct, τοῖχον ἀραρεῖν λίθοισιν Il.
to prepare, contrive, μνηστῆρσιν θάνατον ἀραρόντες Od.
to fit, equip, furnish with a thing, νῆα ἄρσας ἐρέτηισιν Id.
to please, gratify, favour, Pind., Soph.
to make fitting or pleasing, Il.
INTR.:—
to be joined closely together, to be in close order, close-packed, Hom.
to be fixed, of oaths and faith, Trag.:—absol., ἄραρε 'tis fixed, Eur.
to fit well or closely, Hom.: to fit or be fitted to a thing, c. dat., Id.
to be fitted, furnished with a thing, c. dat., Il.; κάλλει ἀραρώς endowed with beauty, Eur.

to be fitting, meet or suitable, agreeable or pleasing, like ἀρέσκω, Od., Hes.:—so in epic aor2 pass. part. ἄρμενος, η, ον, fitting, fitted or suited to, c.dat., Od.; absol. meet, convenient, Lat. habilis, Il.
prepared, ready, Hes.
agreeable, welcome, ἄρμενα πράξαις = εὖ πράξας, Pind.
compactly, closely, strongly, Aesch., Eur.

entry.etym: α euphon. , ῥάσσω, akin to ῥήσσω
entry.sense: to strike hard, smite, (Hom. only has it in the compds. ἀπ-, συν-αράσσω); of horses, ὁπλαῖς ἀρ. χθόνα Pind.; θύρας ἀρ. to knock furiously at the door, Eur.; ἀράσσειν στέρνα, κρᾶτα to beat the breast, the head, in mourning, Lat. plangere, Aesch., Eur.; ἄρασσε μᾶλλον strike harder, Aesch.; ἀρ. ὄψεις, βλέφαρα Soph.
c. dat. modi, ἀράσσειν ὀνείδεσι κακοῖς to throw with reproaches or threats, i. e. fling them wildly about, Id.
Pass. to be dashed against, πρὸς τὰς πέτρας Hdt.; πέτραις Aesch.
accursed, unblest, Il., Soph.
prayed for: hence Ἄρητος, Ἀρήτη, (with changed accent), as prop. n., the prayed-for, like the Hebrew Samuel, Hom.
of or belonging to a spider, Anth.
fem. of ἀράχνης, Lat. aranea, Aesch., Anth.
a spider's web, Id.
a spider, Lat. araneus, Hes.
a spider's web, Lat. aranea, Od., attic
to pray, Od.
to damage, ἀράσοντι, doric for ἀρήσουσι, Inscr.: perf. pass. part. ἀρημένος, βεβλαμμένος, distressed, afflicted, Hom.
a strong shoe or half-boot, used by country-people, hunters, travellers, Aesch., Eur., Theocr., Anth.
name of one of the four old Attic tribes, the workmen, labourers, Eur.
painful, troublous, grievous, Lat. gravis, Il., Ar.:— ἀργαλέον ἐστί, c. dat. et inf., 'tis difficult to do a thing, Hom.; rarely c. acc. et inf., Il.
of persons, troublesome, Theogn., Ar.
of or from Argos, Argive: Ἀργεῖοι in Hom., like Ἀχαιοί, for the Greeks in general: ἡ Ἀργεία (sc. γῆ), Argolis, Thuc.
slayer of Argus, i. e. Hermes, Hom.
the feet of a sheep-skin, and so, generally, offal, Ar.
white, of sheep, Il.; of woollen cloths, Id., Anth.
of the South wind, clearing, brightening, like Horace's detergens nubila caelo, Il.
ἀργέστης Ζέφυρος (parox.), the North-west wind, Hes.
to lie idle, be unemployed, do nothing, Eur., Xen.; γῆ ἀργοῦσα land lying fallow, Id.; ἀργεῖ τὸ ἐργαστήριον the shop is out of work, Dem.
Pass. to be left undone, to be fruitless, Xen.
shining, white, Pind., Aesch.
bright, glancing, of vivid lightning, Hom.
shining, white, of fat, Il.; of a robe, Id.
idleness, laziness, Eur., Dem.
in good sense, rest, leisure, ἔργων from work, Plat.
wielder of bright lightning, Il.
an underground dwelling, Ephorus ap. Strab.
white clay, potter's earth, Arist.
like clay, clayey, Hdt.
white, epith. of Rhodian cities, from their chalky hills, Il.
swift-footed, Il., Soph.
the firstlings at a sacrifice, Od.
from Argos, Soph., Eur.
to take part with the Argives, Xen.
of Argolis, a district in Peloponnesus, Plut.
sub. γῆ, a district in Peloponnesus, Hdt., etc.
as adj., of Argolis, Argolic, Aesch.
making idle, Plut.
shining, bright, glistening, Lat. nitidus, Il.: white, Arist. (Hence come ἄργυρος, ἄργῑλος.）
πόδας ἀργοί, as epith. of hounds, swift-footed, because all swift motion causes a kind of glancing or flickering light, Hom.

not working the ground, living without labour, Hdt.; then, generally, inactive, slothful, idle, lazy, Soph., etc.: —c. gen. rei, idle at a thing, free from it, Eur., Plat.; —also, ἀργότεραι ἐς τὸ δρᾶν Thuc.
of land, lying fallow or untilled, Xen.; of money, unemployed, yielding no return, Dem. —Adv. ἀργῶς Xen.
pass. not done, left undone, Lat. infectus, Soph., Eur.; οὐκ ἐν ἀργοῖς not among things neglected, Soph.

name of several Greek cities, of which the Peloponnesian is the best known, called by Hom. Ἀ. Ἀχαιικόν, to distinguish it from Ἀ. Πελασγικόν. The former name comprehends all Argolis; the latter, all Thessaly.
silver-quinsy, which Demosthenes was said to have, when he abstained from speaking on the plea of quinsy, but really (it was alleged) because he was bribed, Plut.
of or for a money-changer, money-changing, Luc.:—adv. -κῶς, Id.
a money-changer, banker, Lat. argentarius, Plat., Theocr., etc.
ἀργύρεια μέταλλα silver mines, Thuc.; or τὰ ἀργύρεια alone, Xen.
silver, of silver, Lat. argenteus, Hom., etc.
to dig for silver, Strab.
of wrought silver, Eur.
= ἀργύριον, in contemptuous sense, Ar.
of, for or in silver, Plut.
a piece of silver, a silver coin, Ar., etc.
collectively, money, a sum of money, cash, as we also say "silver", Id., Thuc.
= ἄργυρος, silver, Id., Plat.
silver-ore, Xen.
an assayer of silver, Plat.
silver-eddying, of rivers, Il.
like silver, silvery, Eur.
silver-studded, Hom.
a money-chest, Theophr.
a silver-smith, NTest.
to levy money, Xen.
c. acc. pers. to levy money upon, lay under contribution, Thuc.
a levying of money, Xen.
levying money, Ar., Thuc.
silver-footed, Homeric epith. of Thetis.
a worker in silver, Anth.
with silver feet, or legs, Xen.
silver-flowing, Eur.
white metal, i. e. silver, Hom., etc.
silver-money, money, like ἀργύριον, Soph.
robbing of silver, βίος ἀργ. a robber's life, Aesch.
with silver sides, Aesch.
with silver bow, Hom.
silver-shining, Anth.
rich in silver, Xen.
bought with silver, Hdt., Aesch.
silver-white, Hom.
= ἀργύφεος, silver-white, Hom.
of the Argo, Eur.
the Argo or swift, the ship in which Jason sailed to Colchis, Od.
a watering of fields, Strab.
to water, Lat. irrigare, Aesch.
lifted up, on high, Soph., Eur.
taken away utterly, wholly, Lat. raptim, Aesch., Eur., etc.
the point of an arrow, Hdt., Aesch.
a watering-place, Hom.
to water, and so,
of men, to water cattle, Hhymn., Hdt.:—Pass. to drink, ἀρδόμενοι h. Hom.
of rivers, to water land, Lat. irrigare, Hdt., Aesch.:— Pass. to be watered, of countries or crops, Hdt.
metaph. to refresh, cherish, Lat. fovere, Ar., Xen.
name of several fountains, the earliest known in Ithaca, Od.:—the most famous at Syracuse, Strab.
collective noun, menaces, threats, Il.
full of warlike frenzy, Anth.
devoted to Ares, warlike, martial, Lat. Mavortius, Il., Hdt.

Ἄρειος πάγος, ὁ, the hill of Ares, Mars-hill, over against the west side of the Acropolis at Athens, Ἀρήϊος π Hdt.; also Ἄρεος πάγος (where Ἄρεος is gen. of Ἄρης), Soph., Eur. On it was held the highest judicial court, which took cognisance of murder and other capital crimes, Dem.
warlike, bold, Anth.
slain by Ares, i. e. slain in war, Il., Eur.
