= Ἄρειος, Aesch.
better, stouter, stronger, braver, more excellent, Hom., Aesch.
a member of the Areopagus, Aeschin.
the character of an ἄρεσκος, complaisance, obsequiousness, Arist.
an act of obsequiousness, Plut.
agreeably, Eur., Plat.
pleasing, but mostly in bad sense, obsequious, cringing, Arist., Theophr.
to make good, make up, ἂψ ἀρέσαι to make amends, Il.:—Mid., ταῦτα ἀρεσσόμεθα this will we make up among ourselves, Hom.
Mid. to appease, conciliate, αὐτὸν ἀρεσσάσθω ἐπέεσσιν Od.
after Hom., c. dat. pers. to please, satisfy, flatter, Hdt., attic; ταῦτα ἀρέσκει μοι Hdt.;—so, in Mid., Id.
in attic also c. acc. pers., οὐ γάρ μ’ ἀρέσκει γλῶσσά σου Soph.; τουτί μ’ οὐκ ἀρ. Ar.: hence, in Pass., to be pleased, satisfied with a thing, c. dat. rei, Hdt., Thuc.
ἀρέσκει is used, like Lat. placet, to express the resolution of a public body, ταῦτα ἤρεσέ σφι ποιέειν Hdt.:—so in Mid., Thuc.
part. ἀρέσκων, ουσα, ον, grateful, acceptable, Soph., Thuc.
acceptable, pleasing, Hdt., Soph. adv., ἑωυτῶι ἀρεστῶς quite to his own satisfaction, Hdt.
to be fit or proper, to thrive, prosper, Od.
goodness, excellence, of any kind, esp. of manly qualities, manhood, valour, prowess, Hom., Hdt. (like Lat. vir-tus, from vir).
rank, nobility, Theogn., Eur.
in Prose, generally, goodness, excellence in any art, Plat., etc.; of animals or things, Hdt., attic.
in moral sense, goodness, virtue, Plat., etc.:—also character for virtue, merit, Eur., etc.
ἀρ. εἴς τινα service done him, Thuc.; ἀρ. περί τινα Xen.
help, aid, Anth.
a helper, Il.
to help, aid, succour, esp. in battle, c. dat., Il., Hdt.
impers., c. inf., like Lat, juvat, it is good or fit, σιγᾶν ἀρήγει Aesch.
c. acc. rei, to ward off, prevent, τι Aesch.; also, ἀρ. τί τινι to ward off from one, Eur.
swift as Ares, swift in battle, Il.
slain by Ares or in battle, Il.
dear to Ares, favoured of the god of war, Il.
help, succour, τινος from a person, Aesch., Soph.
c. gen. rei, help against a thing, means of averting it, Soph.

entry.etym: short α in Hom., except in voc. Ἆρες: in Aesch. long or short.
entry.sense: Ares, called by the Latins Mars, son of Zeus and Hera, god of war and slaughter, also of strife and pestilence, Hom., Trag.
in Poets, as appellat., war, battle, discord, slaughter, ξυνάγωμεν Ἄρηα Il; Ἄρης ἐμφύλιος, Ἄ. τιθασός civil war, Aesch.
warlike spirit, Trag.
entry.etym: The Root ΑΡ, appears also in ἀρετή, the first notion of goodness (virtus) being that of manhood, bravery in war.

entry.sense: a place for prayer, Plut.
one that prays, a priest, Il.
intr. to be united, Il.
united, ἡμῖν ἄρθμιοι friends with us, in league with us, Od.; ἄρθμια, τά, peaceful relations, friendship, Hdt.
a bond, league, friendship, Hom., Aesch.

a joint, Soph.: esp. the socket of the ankle-joint, Hdt., Soph.:—in pl. joined with some other word, ἄρθρα ποδοῖν the ankles, Id.; ἄρθρων ἤλυσις the legs, Eur.; ἄρθρα τῶν κύκλων the eyes, Soph.; ἄρθρα στόματος the mouth, Eur.
a band for the limbs, fetter, Anth.
to fasten by a joint:— of words, ἡ γλῶσσα ἀρθροῖ τὴν φωνήν the tongue produces articulate sounds, Xen.; but, ἀρθροῦν γλώσσην καὶ νόον to nerve the tongue and mind, Theogn.
well-jointed, well-knit, Xen.
easy to be known, Hom.: well-known, far-famed, Id.; and in bad sense, infamous, Lat. nimium notus, Od.
much weeping, very tearful, Aesch.
much shewn, hence like Lat. digito monstratus, Od.; as Sup. c. gen., ἀριδείκετος ἀνδρῶν most renowned of men, Il.
very distinct, far seen, Simon.
quite clear, manifest, Hdt.
conspicuous, very distinct, of a star, Il.; of a voice, Id.; of persons, conspicuous, remarkable, Id.:—adv., ἀριζήλως εἰρημένα a plain tale, Od.
much to be envied, Ar.
to number, count or reckon up, Od., etc.:—Mid., ἠριθμοῦντο they got them counted, Thuc.
to count out, to pay, Xen., Dem.
to reckon, count as, ἐν εὐεργεσίας μέρει Id.:—Pass. to be reckoned, ἔν τισι Eur.; ἀριθμεῖσθαι τῶν φιλτάτων to be counted as one of one's dearest friends, Id.
a reckoning, number, Aesch.
a counting, reckoning up, Hdt.
of or for reckoning, arithmetical, Plat.: ἡ ἀριθμητική (sc. τέχνη) arithmetic, Id.
easily numbered, few in number, Theocr.: οὐκ ἀριθμητός held in no account, nullo numero habitus, Id.
number, Lat. numerus, Od., etc.; ἀριθμόν in number, Hdt., attic; ἀριθμὸν ἕξ Hdt.; ἐς τὸν ἀρ. τρισχίλια Id.; also, ἓν ἀριθμῶι Id.; so in attic
amount, sum, extent, πολὺς ἀρ. χρόνου Aeschin.; ἀρ. ἀργυρίου a sum of money, Xen.
as mark of station, worth, rank, μετ’ ἀνδρῶν ἀριθμῶι among men, Od.; οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀριθμόν have no account made of them, Eur.; οὐδ’ εἰς ἀριθμὸν ἥκεις λόγων you come not into my account, Id.
mere number, quantity, opp. to quality, worth, ἀριθμὸς λόγων a mere set of words, Soph.; so of men, οὐκ ἀρ. ἄλλως not a mere lot, Eur.; so ἀριθμός alone, like Hor.'s nos numerus sumus, Ar.
a numbering, counting, ἀριθμὸν ποιεῖσθαι τῆς στρατιῆς to hold a muster of the army, Hdt.; παρεῖναι εἰς τὸν ἀρ. Xen.
the science of numbers, numeration, arithmetic, Aesch., Plat.
the Arians or Aryans, old name of the Medes, Hdt.
Ἄριος, η, ον, as adj. Median, Aesch.
insep. Prefix, like ἐρι-, strengthening the notion conveyed by its compd.: of same Root with Ἄρης, ἀρετή.
very distinguished, stately, Hom.
of things, very bright, splendid, Id.
very notable, Hhymn., Tyrtae.
very plain, visible, Theocr.
a carpenter's tool, an auger or drill, Anth.
victorious in the contest, Anth.
best-ruling, epith. of Zeus, Simon.
rich in grapes, Anth.
to take breakfast or luncheon, Lat. prandere, Ar., Xen.:—perf. pass. impers., ἠρίστηταί τ’ ἐξαρκούντως Ar.
excellence, prowess, Soph.: Il. 5, in which the prowess of Diomede is described, is called Διομήδους ἀριστεία.
the prize of the best and bravest, the meed of valour, Hdt., Soph., Plat.:—rarely so in sg., Hdt.
in sg. a monument of valour, memorial, Dem.

left, on the left, Lat. sinister, ἐπ’ ἀριστερά towards, i. e. on, the left, Il.; ἐπ’ ἀριστερὰ χειρός on the left hand, Od.; ἐξ ἀριστερῆς χειρός on the left hand, Hdt.; or simply, ἐξ ἀριστερᾶς Soph.; ἐς ἀριστερήν, ἐν ἀριστερῆι Hdt.
metaph. boding ill, ominous, because to a Greek augur, looking northward, the unlucky signs came from the left, Od.
the best man: used by Hom. mostly in epic pl. ἀριστῆες, the best or noblest, chiefs, princes; so Hdt., etc.
to be best or bravest, Hom.:— to gain the prize for valour, gain the highest distinction, Hdt.
c. gen., ἀριστεύεσκε Τρώων he was the best of the Trojans, Il.; βουλῆι ἀριστεύεσκεν ἁπάντων Id.; c. inf., ἀριστεύεσκε μάχεσθαι was best at fighting, Id.; ἀρ. τι to be best in a thing, Theocr.
to give one breakfast, c. acc. pers., Ar.
best-advising, Plut.
producing the best, Anth.
bearing the best children, Pind.
Pass. to be governed by the best-born, to live under an aristocratical form of government, Ar., Plat.
the rule of the best, an aristocracy, Thuc., Plat., etc.
aristocratical, Plat.
best of prophets, Soph.
best at fighting, Pind.
of the best disposition, Anth.

entry.etym: ᾰ in Epic, α in attic
entry.sense: the morning meal, breakfast, taken at sunrise, Hom., Hdt.; ἄριστα, δεῖπνα, δόρπα θ’ αἱρεῖσθαι τρίτον Aesch.:—later, ἄριστον was the mid-day meal, Roman prandium, Thuc.
to prepare breakfast, τὰ ἀριστοποιούμενα things prepared for breakfast, Xen.:—mostly in Mid. to get one's breakfast, Thuc., Xen.
best in its kind, serving as Sup. to ἀγαθός (cf. ἀρείων):

best, noblest, bravest, Il.; βουλῆι, ἔγχεσιν ἄριστος Hom.; εἶδος ἄριστος Il.:—c. inf. ἄριστοι μάχεσθαι Xen.; ἄρ. διαβολὰς ἐνδέκεσθαι readiest to give ear to calumnies, Hdt.; ἄρ. ἀπατᾶσθαι best, i. e. easiest, to cheat, Thuc.
best, most virtuous, Eur.
of animals and things, best, finest, Hom.
neut. pl. as adv. ἄριστα, best, most excellently, Id., Hdt.
bearing the best children:— fem. ἀριστοτόκεια, Theocr.
pass., born of the best parents, Eur.
won by the stoutest hand, ἀγών Soph.
bearing the best children, Anth.
very slippery or treacherous, Od.
easy to be known, very distinct, manifest, Il.: poet. adv. -δέως, plainly, Theocr.
very thoughtful, wise, Soph.
enough, abundantly, ἀρκούντως ἔχει ’tis enough, Aesch., Thuc.
help, aid, service, Soph.
sufficient, NTest., Anth.
to ward off, keep off, a thing from a person, τί τινι Il.; ἀρκεῖν τὸ μὴ οὐ θανεῖν to keep off death, Soph.
c. dat. only, to defend, assist, succour, Hom., Soph.
to be strong enough, to be sufficient, to suffice, c. inf., Aesch., Soph.; c. part., ἀρκέσω θνήσκουσα my death will suffice, Id.; οὐκ ἤρκουν ἰατροὶ θεραπεύοντες Thuc.
c. dat. to suffice, be enough for, satisfy, τινι Hdt., Soph.: to be a match for, πρός τινα Thuc.
absol. to be enough, be strong enough, avail, hold out, Aesch., etc.:—part., ἀρκῶν, οῦσα, οῦν, sufficient, enough, Hdt., attic
impers., ἀρκεῖ μοι 'tis enough for me, I am content, c. inf., Soph., etc.:—absol., οὐκέτ’ ἀρκεῖ there is no help, Id.; ἀρκεῖν δοκεῖ μοι it seems enough, seems good, Id.
in Pass. to be satisfied with, c. dat. rei, ἔφη οὐκέτι ἀρκέεσθαι τούτοισι Hdt.

sufficient, sure, certain, νῦν ἄρκιον ἢ ἀπολέσθαι ἠὲ σαωθῆναι one of these is certain, either to perish or be saved, Il.; μισθὸς ἄρκιος a sure reward, Hom.; ἄρκιον εὑρεῖν to have enough, Theocr.; σφίσιν ἄρκιος a match for them, Id.
one must begin, Soph.
verb. adj. of ἄρχω, one must govern; and in pass sense, one must be ruled, i.e. obey, Id.
a bear, Od., etc.
ἄρκτος, ἡ, the constellation Ursa Major, also called ἅμαξα, the Wain, (the star just behind is called Ἀρκτοῦρος the Bearward, or Βοώτης the Wagoner), Hom., etc.
the region of the bear, the North, sg., Hdt., Eur.
arcturus (v. ἄρκτος II), Hes.
the time of his rising, the middle of September, Soph.
northern, Luc.
pl., nom. and acc ἄρκυες, -υας, attic contr. ἄρκῡς:— a net, hunter's net, Lat. cassis, Aesch.; oft. in pl., Id., Eur.:—metaph., ἄρκυες ξίφους the toils, i. e. perils, of the sword, Eur.
a line of nets, Xen.
beset with nets, ἀρκυστάτα μηχανά the hunter's toils, Eur.
ἀρκύστατα, τά, a place beset with nets, a snare, Aesch., Soph.
a watcher of nets, Xen.
fitting sustenance, allowance, food, Hes., Theocr.
a covered carriage, borrowed from the Persians, Hdt., Ar.; used by women, Xen.
a chariot, esp. a war-chariot, with two wheels, Hom.; often in pl. for sg., Il., Trag.
chariot and horses, the yoked chariot, Id.: also the team, the horses, Eur., Ar.
of or belonging to a chariot, Xen.; μέλος ἁρμ. a kind of dirge, Eur.
to drive or go in a chariot, Eur.
chariot-driving, Xen.
to go in a chariot, drive it, Hdt., Xen.
a charioteer, Soph., Xen.
driven round by a wheel, of Ixion, Eur.
a chariot race, Strab.
used to describe ὄτοβος, the rattling din of chariots, Aesch.
building chariots: ἁρμ. ἀνήρ a wheelwright, chariot-maker, Il.
to keep chariot-horses, esp. for racing, Xen.
a keeping of chariot-horses, Xen.
the wheel-track of a chariot, Luc.:—Hom. uses poet. form ἁρματροχιή, Il.
the tackling or rigging of a ship, Hes., Theocr.
like ὅπλα, any tools, Anth.
entry.etym: Properly neut. of ἄρμενος, v. ἀραρίσκω B. IV.

entry.sense: fitting together, Theogn.
well-fitting, accordant, agreeable, Id.:—adv. -ως, Plut.
to fit together, join, esp. of joiner's work, Od.; so in Mid. to join for oneself, put together, Id.
generally, to fit, adapt, prepare, make ready, Soph.:—Mid. to suit oneself, πρός τινα Luc.

of marriage, ἁρμόζειν τινὶ τὴν θυγατέρα to betroth one's daughter to any one, Hdt.; also, ἁρμ. γάμους Eur.:—Mid. to betroth to oneself, take to wife, τὴν θυγατέρα τινός Hdt.; (so in Mid., NTest.):— Pass., ἡρμόσθαι θυγατέρα τινὸς γυναῖκα to have her betrothed or married to one, Hdt.
to set in order, regulate, govern, Eur.: Pass., Soph.; κονδύλοις ἡρμοττόμην I was ruled or drilled with cuffs, Ar.:—among the Lacedaemonians, to act as harmostes, ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν Xen.
to arrange according to the laws of harmony, to tune instruments, Plat.:— Pass., ἡρμοσμένος in tune, Id.
intr. to fit, fit well, of clothes or armour, c. dat. pers., Il.
to fit, suit, be adapted, fit for, τινί Soph.
impers. ἁρμόζει, it is fitting, Lat. decet, c. acc. et inf., Id.
part., ἁρμόττων, ουσα, ον, fitting, suitable, Plat.; πρός τι Xen.
just, newly, lately, Aesch., Theocr.
entry.etym: In fact, an old dat. of ἁρμός; cf. οἴκοι, πέδοι.

entry.sense: to join, pile together, Anth.
a fastening to keep ship-planks together, a clamp, Od.
a joining, joint, between a ship's planks, τὰς ἁρμ. ἐπάκτωσαν τῆι βύβλωι caulked the joints with byblus, Hdt.
a frame: metaph., δύστροπος γυναικῶν ἁρμ. women's perverse temperament, Eur.
a covenant, agreement, in pl., Il.:— settled government, order, Aesch.
harmony, as a concord of sounds, first as a mythical personage, Harmonia, Music, companion of Hebe, the Graces and the Hours; child of the Muses, Hhymn., Eur.
metaph., harmony, concord, Plat.
skilled in music, Plat.:— τὰ ἁρμονικά, music, Id.
in pl. the fastenings of a door, Eur.; ἁρμὸς χώματος λιθοσπαδής a fissure in the tomb made by tearing away the stones at their joinings, Soph.
one who arranges or governs, esp. a harmost or governor of the islands and towns of Asia Minor, sent out by the Lacedaemonians during their supremacy, Thuc., Xen.
a commander, Aesch.
a sheep's skin, Ar., Plat.
a young ram or wether, just full grown, Il.; ἀρνειὸς ὄϊς joined, like ἵρηξ κίρκος, Od.
of a lamb or sheep, κρέα Orac. ap. Hdt.; ἄ. φόνος slaughtered, sheep, Soph.
feasting on lambs, Anth.
Dep. opp. to φημί, to deny, disown, Hom., etc.
opp. to δίδωμι, to decline to give, refuse, Od., etc.
absol to say no, decline, refuse, Il.
dependent clauses are put in inf., with or without μή, to deny that, Hdt., attic
a diver, tumbler, Hom.
to butt like a ram, to dive, Lycophr.
to be denied, Soph.
denial, Aesch., Soph.; foll. by τὸ μή c. inf., Dem.
a sheep-skin, Luc.

entry.etym: Prob. akin to ἔριον, εἶρος, wool.
entry.sense: a lamb, Lat. agnus, agna, Il.
a sheep, whether ram or ewe, Hom.

entry.etym: used only in pres. and imperf.
entry.sense: to receive for oneself, reap, win, gain, earn, esp. of honour or reward, Hom., attic:—rarely in bad sense, ἀρνύμενος λώβαν, perh. taking vengeance for my injuries, Eur.
arable, fruitful: metaph. fit for engendering children, Soph., in poet. form ἀρώσιμος.
arable land, corn-land, Lat. arvum, Hom.
a plougher, husbandman, Il., Eur.; Σκύθαι ἀροτῆρες, opp. to νομάδες, Hdt.:—adj., βοῦς ἀροτήρ a steer for ploughing, Hes.
metaph. a father, Eur.
a corn-field, Od.
a crop, fruit of the field, Soph.; metaph., τέκνων ἄροτος Eur.
tillage, ploughing, Hes.; ζῆν ἀπ’ ἀρότου to live by husbandry, Hdt.
the season of tillage, seed-time, Hes.: hence a season, year, Soph.
of corn-land, rustic, Anth.
a ploughman, = ἀροτρευτήρ, Theocr.
belonging to the plough, Anth.
a plougher, who goes backwards and forwards like a runner in the δίαυλος, Anth.
a plough, Lat. aratrum, Hom., etc.
working with the plough, Anth.
to draw the plough, Anth.

of or from the country, rural, rustic, μῦς ἀρ. a field- mouse, Hdt.; ὦ παῖ τῆς ἀρουραίας θεοῦ, of Euripides as the reputed son of a herb-seller, Ar.; ἀρ. Οἰνόμαος, of Aeschines who played the part of Oenomaus in the country, Dem.
tilled or arable land, seed-land, cornland, Lat. arvum, and in pl. corn-lands, fields, Il.: then, generally, land, earth, Id.; πατρὶς ἄρουρα father land, Od.
metaph. of a woman as bearing children, Aesch., Soph.
a measure of land in Egypt, nearly = the Roman jugerum, Hdt.
working in the field, Anth.

entry.etym: The Root is ΑΡΟϜ, cf. ἄρουρα, Lat. arvum.
entry.sense: to plough, Lat. arare, οὔτε φυτεύουσιν, οὔτ’ ἀρόωσιν (epic for ἀροῦσι) Od.: Pass., πόντος ἠρόθη δορί Aesch.
to sow, ἀροῦν εἰς κήπους Plat.
metaph. of the husband, Theogn., Soph.:—Pass., of the child, to be begotten, Id.
a rake, Lat. harpago, Eur.
seizure, rapine, robbery, rape, Solon, Hdt., attic
the thing seized, booty, prey, Aesch., Eur.; ἁρπαγὴν ποιεῖσθαί τι to make booty of a thing, Thuc.; cf. λεία.
greediness, rapacity, Xen.
ravished, stolen, Anth.
a seizing, booty, a prize, NTest.
to snatch away, carry off, Hom., Hdt., etc.:—absol. to steal, be a thief, Ar.
to seize hastily, snatch up, λᾶαν Il.; δόρυ Aesch.; ἁρπ. τινὰ μέσον to seize him by the waist, Hdt.; c. gen. part., ἁρπ. τινὰ ποδός by the foot, Eur.
to seize, overpower, Aesch.: also to seize a post, Xen.
to plunder, πόλεις Thuc., etc.
entry.etym: From Root ΑΡΠ, come also ἅρπη, Ἅρπυιαι, cf. Lat. rapio.

entry.sense: a robber, Il.
rapacious, Luc.
gotten by rapine, stolen, Hes.
to be caught, i. e. to be got by chance, hazardous, Id.
greedy: adv. ἁρπαλέως, greedily, eagerly, Od., Theogn.
attractive, alluring, Od., Pind.
to catch up, be eager to receive, τινὰ κωκυτοῖς Aesch.
to exact greedily, Id.
snatching away men, Aesch.
rapacious, Lat. rapax, Ar., Xen.
as Subst.,
ἅρπαξ, rapine, Hes.
ἅρπαξ, a robber, plunderer, Ar.
robbery, Plat.
carried away, Anth.
a cord, for binding or for snaring game, Xen.: a bowstring, Anth.
a bird of prey, a kite, Il.
a sickle, = δρέπανον, Hes.
the snatchers, a personification of whirlwinds or hurricanes, Od. The Harpies, as described by Virgil, belong to later mythology.
earnest-money, caution-money, deposited by the purchaser and forfeited if the purchase is not completed, Lat. arrhabo, arrha, Isae., NTest.
firm, hard, solid, Plat.
without seam, NTest.
undone, poet. ἄρεκτος, Il.
male, Luc.
of male children, Anth.
a manly look manliness, Plat.
masculine-looking, masculine, manly, Plat., Luc.
unbroken, not to be broken, Hom., Hdt., Aesch., etc.: unwearied, Il.
fierce, savage, Theocr.
unspoken, unsaid, Lat. indictus, Od., etc.; οὐκ ἐπ’ ἀρρήτοις λόγοις not without warning spoken, Soph.
not to be spoken, not to be divulged, of sacred mysteries, Hdt., Eur., etc.; διδακτά τε ἄρρητά τ’, i. e. things profane and sacred, Soph.
unutterable, inexpressible, horrible, Lat. nefandus, Id., Eur.; ἄρρητ’ ἀρρήτων "deeds without a name, " Soph.
shameful to be spoken, Id.; ῥητὰ καὶ ἄρρητα, "dicenda tacenda, " Dem.
in Mathem., ἄρρητα, irrational quantities, surds, Plat.

entry.etym: The meaning of Ἀρρη - is uncertain.
entry.sense: to serve as Ἀρρηφόρος, Ar.
the procession of ἀρρηφόροι Lys.
the festival arrephoria. Ἀρρηφόρια, τά.
at Athens
two maidens of noble birth, chosen in their seventh year, who carried the peplos and other holy things of Athena Polias.
not shivering, daring, Anth.
without power of scenting, Xen.
a wicker basket, Ar., Anth.
not to be in rhythm with, Plat.
want of rhythm or proportion, Plat.
of sounds, not in rhythm or time, unrhythmical, opp. to εὔρυθμος, Plat.:—metaph. in undue measure, Eur.: ill-proportioned, Xen.
unwrinkled, Anth.
ionic for ὀρρωδέω
ionic for ὀρρωδία
without cleft or breach, unbroken, γῆ Soph.
to be weak and sickly, Xen., Dem.
an illness, a sickness, Dem.
a moral infirmity, Plut.
weakness, sickness, Thuc., etc.; ἀρρ.τοῦ στρατεύειν inability to serve, Id.
weak, sickly:— adv., ἀρρώστως ἔχειν to be ill, Aeschin.
in moral sense, weak, feeble, τὴν ψυχήν Xen.:— remiss, εἴς τι in a thing, Thuc.
also, v. ἄρδω.
lying with men, NTest.
male, Lat. mas, Il., etc.; ἄρρην, ὁ, or ἄρρεν, the male, Aesch.; οἱ ἄρσενες the male sex, Thuc.
masculine, strong, Eur.: metaph. mighty, κτύπος ἄρσην πόντου Soph.
of the gender of nouns, masculine, ὀνόματα Ar.
contr. for ἀερσίπους, raising the foot, active, Hhymn., Anth.
a raising of the foot in walking, Arist.
in Prosody, arsis, opp. to thesis.
a Persian measure, artaba, = 1 medimnus + 3 choenices, Hdt.
to cut in pieces, rend asunder, Eur.
a butcher, cook, Xen.
that by which something is hung up, a rope, noose, halter, Aesch., Soph.
to fasten to or hang one thing upon another, τι ἀπό τινος Thuc.: to fasten in a noose, τὴν δέρην Eur.:—Mid., βρόχους ἀρτωμένη fastening halters to one's neck, Id.
Pass. to be hung upon, hang upon, ἠρτῆσθαι ἔκ τινος Id.: hence to depend upon, Lat. pendere ab aliquo, Hdt. Cf. ἀρτέομαι.
safe and sound, Hom.
soundness, recovery, Anth.
a temple of Artemis, Hdt.
Artemis, the Roman Diana, goddess of the chase, daughter of Zeus and Latona, sister of Apollo: in Hom., women who die suddenly are said to be slain by her ἀγανὰ βέλεα: cf. Ἀπόλλων.
prob. a foresail, NTest.
as Pass. to be prepared, get ready, make ready, c. inf., πολεμεῖν ἀρτέοντο, ἀρτέετο ἐς πόλεμον Hdt.; also,
as Mid., c. acc., ναυμαχίην ἀρτέεσθαι to prepare a sea-fight, Id.
entry.etym: Akin to ἀρτύω, not to ἀρτάω.

entry.sense: a hanging ornament, earring, Hdt.; cf. λίθινος.
any hanging weight, Plut.
the wind-pipe or trachea, Plat., etc.; πνεύμονος ἀρτηρίαι the vessels of the lungs, Soph.
an artery, only in late writers.
to play at odd and even, Lat. par impar ludere, Ar.
to count, Anth.
the game of odd and even, Arist.
just steeped, Anth.
just married, Anth.
with beard just sprouting, Anth.
just born, Luc.
newly carved, Theocr.
just born, Anth.
just taught, Anth.
just weeping, ready to weep, Eur.
just stript off or peeled, Anth.
ready for plucking, of tender age, Aesch.
ready of speech, glib or ready of tongue, Il., Pind.
a recent union, ἀνδρῶν ἀρτ., i. e. newly-married husbands, Aesch.
to get ready, prepare, Anth.: so in Mid., Theocr.
just budding or blooming, Anth.
just dead, Eur.
close-glued, clinging close to, ἀρτίκολλος ὥστε τέκτονος χιτών = ἀρτίως κολληθεὶς ὡς ὑπὸ τέκτονος, Soph.
metaph. fitting well together, ἀρτ. συμβαίνει turns out exactly right, Aesch.; ἀρτίκολλόν τι μαθεῖν to hear it in the nick of time, opportunely, Id.
just born, Anth.
having just learnt a thing, c. gen., Eur.
sound of limb, Plat.

complete, perfect of its kind, suitable, exactly fitted; ἄρτια βάζειν to speak to the purpose (cf. ἀρτιεπής), Hom.; ἄρτια ᾔδη thought things agreeable, was of the same mind, Id.:— meet, right, proper, Solon, Theogn.
c. inf. prepared, ready, to do a thing, Hdt.
of numbers, perfect, i. e. even, opp. to περισσός (odd), Plat., etc.
adv. ἀρτίως, just, now first, like ἄρτι, used by Soph. both of present time with pres. and perf.; and of past with imperf. and aor.
just put together or made, Theocr., Anth.
freshly coagulated, Id.
newly gotten, χρήματα Eur.
sound of foot, Od., Hdt.:—generally, strong or swift of foot, Il.
（ἄρτι, πούς) coming just in time, Soph.
adv. just, exactly,
of the present, just now, even now, with pres. and perf., Theogn., Aesch., etc.
of the past, just now, just, with imperf. and aor., Eur., etc.
in late writers of the future, just now, presently, Luc., etc.
equipment, Hdt.
just dug, Anth.
speaking in good idiom, or with precision, Plut.
newly initiated, Plat.
new-born, Anth., Luc.
paroxyt. ἀρτιτόκος, ον, having just given birth, Anth.
just nursed, ἀρτιτρεφεῖς βλαχαί the wailings of young children, Aesch.
just of age, marriageable.
sound of mind, sensible, Od., Eur.: c. gen., γάμων fully conscious of a thing, Aesch.
just born, fresh, Anth.
just opening, Anth.
with the first bloom on, Anth.
fresh-spread, φάρμακον Soph.
a baker, Hdt., Xen.
entry.etym: Prob. for ἀρτοπόπος, from πέπτω, cf. Lat. coquus.

entry.sense: with bread and bottle in it, πήρα Anth.
a baking, Xen.
a bread-maker, baker, Xen.
a baker's shop, bakery, Ar.
a bread-woman, Ar.
to eat wheaten bread, Xen.
a cake or loaf of wheat-bread (barley-bread is μᾶζα), mostly in pl., Od.; ἄρτος οὖλος soft bread, Id.
to eat bread, Hdt.
a bread-eater, Batr.
seasoning, sauce, spice, Batr.
a magistrate at Argos and Epidaurus, Thuc.
Ep. form of ἀρτύω to arrange, prepare, devise, λόχον ἀρτύνειν, Lat. insidias struere, Od.; μνηστῆρσιν θάνατον ἀρτ. Id.:—Mid. to prepare for oneself, Id.
like ἀρτύνω to arrange, devise, prepare, δόλον, ὄλεθρον, γάμον Hom.; so Hdt., attic
a bag or purse, Stesich.
a bucket shaped like a purse, i. e. narrow at top, Ar. (Deriv. unknown.)
Mid. to draw for oneself, Hdt
a cup or ladle, Hdt.
Dim. of ἀρυστήρ, Ar.
a small pail, Ar.
fit to drink, Anth.

to draw water or any liquor for others, Hes., Xen.:—Mid. to draw water for oneself, ἀρυσσάμενος ποταμῶν ἄπο having drawn water from the rivers, Hes.; ἀρύσασθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ ποταμοῦ Xen.; c. acc., ἀρύσασθαι πῶμα Eur.; c. gen. partit., ἀρύτεσθαι Νείλου ὑδάτων to draw of the waters of the Nile, Ar.; ἐς τὸν κόλπον τρὶς ἀρυσάμενος τοῦ ἡλίου having (as it were) drawn the rays of the sun into his bosom, Hdt.
an archangel, NTest.
old-fashioned, antiquated, primitive, ἀρχαϊκὰ φρονεῖν Ar.
of ancient race, of old descent, Soph.
to discuss antiquities or things out of date, Thuc.
dear honey-sweet old songs from Phrynichus' Phoenissae, Ar.
rich from olden time, of old hereditary wealth, Aesch., Soph.
distinguished from olden time, time-honoured, Aesch.
from the beginning:
of things, ancient, primeval, olden, Hdt., attic
like ἀρχαϊκός, old-fashioned, antiquated, primitive, Aesch., Ar.
ancient, former, τὸ ἀρχ. ῥέεθρον Hdt., etc.
of persons, ancient, old, Aesch., Thuc., etc.: οἱ ἀρχαῖοι the Ancients, the old Fathers, Prophets, NTest.
adv. ἀρχαίως, anciently, Dem.; so, τὸ ἀρχαῖον, ionic contr. τὠρχαῖον Hdt., attic τἀρχαῖον Aesch.
in olden style, Plat., Aeschin.
as Subst., τὸ ἀρχαῖον, the original sum, the principal, Lat. sors, Ar., Oratt.
old fashions or customs, Plut.
old-fashioned, Thuc.
to hold the assembly for the election of magistrates, Plut.: to elect, Id.
to canvass for election, Id.
an election of magistrates, Hdt.; mostly in pl., Xen., etc.
the senate-house, town-hall, residence of the chief magistrates, Lat. curia, Hdt., Xen.
the magistracy, Arist.
beginning mischief, Il.
leading the people, a chief, Aesch.
ruling a city, Pind.
a leader, prince, Eur.: as adj., ἀρχ. θρόνος a princely throne, Id.
an archetype, pattern, model, Anth.: the figure on a seal, Luc.
to command, c. dat., Il.
leading the chorus or dance, Eur.
causing the first beginning of a thing, c. gen., Aesch.
to be chief leader, τῶν κάτω Hdt.
to make a beginning, Soph.
a first leader, the founder of a city or family, Hdt., etc.
generally, a leader, prince, chief, Aesch., Soph.
a first cause, author, τύχης, γένους Eur.
beginning, originating a thing, c. gen., Eur.
as Subst., like ἀρχηγέτης, founder, of a tutelary hero, Soph.
a prince, chief, Aesch., Simon., Thuc.
a first cause, originator, τοῦ πράγματος Xen.
from the beginning, from of old, from olden time, Hdt.:—with a neg., ἀρχῆθεν μή not at all, Id.
see ἀρχή I.

a beginning, origin, first cause, Hom., etc.:—with Preps. ἐξ ἀρχῆς = ἀρχῆθεν, from the beginning, from of old, Od., attic; ἐξ ἀρχῆς πάλιν anew, afresh, Ar.:—so, ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς Hdt., Trag.:— κατ’ ἀρχάς in the beginning, at first, Hdt.:—absol. in acc. ἀρχήν, to begin with, first, Id.; ἀρχὴν οὐ absolutely not, not at all, Lat. omnino non, Id., attic; with numerals, ἀρχὴν ἑπτά in all, Hdt.
the end, corner, of a bandage, rope, sheet, Id., Eur., NTest.
the first place or power, sovereignty, dominion, command, Hdt., attic; c. gen. rei, ἀρχὴ τῶν νεῶν, τῆς θαλάσσης Thuc., etc.
a sovereignty, empire, realm, Hdt., Thuc.
in Prose, a magistracy, office, Hdt., attic:—also a term of office, τὴν ἐνιαυσίαν ἀρχήν Thuc.:—these offices were commonly obtained in two ways, χειροτονητή by election, κληρωτή by lot, Aeschin.
in pl., αἱ ἀρχαί (as we say) "the authorities, " i. e. the magistrates, Thuc., etc.
a chief clerk, Plut.
a petty office, petty officer, Ar., Dem.
of the high-priest, NTest.
an arch-priest, chief-priest, Hdt.:— at Rome, the Pontifex Maximus, Plut.:—at Jerusalem, the high-priest, NTest.
the high-priesthood, Plut.
ruling the sea, Anth.
to be ἀρχιθέωρος, Dem.
the chief of a θεωρία or sacred embassy, Andoc., Arist.
of or for rule, royal, Aesch., Thuc.
of persons, fit for rule, skilled in government or command, Xen., Plat.: c. gen. having command of, Arist.
a chief pilot, Plut.
a chief comedian, Plut.
a pirate-chief, Plut.
a Nomad chieftain, Luc.
a chief shepherd, NTest.
the ruler of a synagogue, NTest.
to be the architect, Plut.
generally, to construct, contrive, Ar.
a chief-artificer, master-builder, director of works, architect, engineer, Hdt.
generally, a constructor, author, Eur., Dem.
at Athens, the manager of the state theatre and of the Dionysia, Id.
a chief toll-collector, chief-publican, NTest.
the president of a banquet (triclinium), NTest.
chief of the men at arms, Plut.
of an archon, Anth.
a leader, chief, commander, Il.
a precentor, Byz.
a ruler, commander, chief, captain, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
Ἄρχοντες, οἱ, the chief magistrates at Athens, nine in number, the first being ὁ Ἄρχων or Ἄρχων ἐπώνυμος, the second ὁ Βασιλεύς, the third ὁ Πολέμαρχος, the remaining six οἱ Θεσμοθέται.
title of the chief magistrates in other places, as the Ephors at Sparta, Hdt.

entry.etym: pf. pass. ἦργμαι only in mid. sense
entry.sense: in pass. sense:— to be first,
of Time, to begin, make a beginning, both in Act. and Mid.:

c. gen. to make a beginning of, πολέμοιο, μάχης, etc., Hom.; so Hdt. and attic:—Mid. also in a religious sense, like ἀπάρχεσθαι, ἀρχόμενος μελέων beginning the sacrifice with the limbs, Od.; ἄρχειν σπονδῶν Thuc.
c. gen. also to begin from or with, ἐν σοὶ μὲν λήξω σέο δ’ ἄρξομαι Il.; so, ἄρχεσθαι ἔκ τινος Od.; ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ παιδίων even from boyhood, Hdt.
c. gen. rei et dat. pers., ἄρχ. θεοῖς δαιτός to make preparations for a banquet to the gods, Il.; τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε Id., etc.
c. acc., ἄρχειν ὁδόν τινι, like Lat. praeire viam alicui, to shew him the way, Od.; absol. (sub. ὁδόν), to lead the way, Hom.; then generally ἄρχειν τι Aesch., Soph.
c. inf. to begin to do a thing, Hom., etc.; c. part. of continued action or condition, ἦρχον χαλεπαίνων Il.; ἄρχ. διδάσκων Xen.
absol., ἄρχε begin! Hom.; ἄρχει ἡ ἐκεχειρία Thuc.; ἅμα ἦρι ἀρχομένωι, θέρους ἀρχομένου Id.
of Authority, to lead, rule, govern, only in Act.:
c. gen. to rule, be leader of . . , τινός Hom., attic
c. dat. to rule over, Hom., Aesch.
absol. to rule, govern, Id.: esp. to hold a subordinate office, ὁκοῖον εἴη ἄρχειν μετὰ τὸ βασιλεύειν Hdt.:—at Athens, to be archon, Dem.; cf. ἄρχων.
Pass. to be ruled, governed, Hdt., attic; οἱ ἀρχόμενοι subjects, Xen.
help, aid, succour, protection, Ζηνὸς ἀρωγή aid given by Zeus, Il.; ἐπ’ ἀρωγῆι in anyone's favour, Id.; ἀρ. νόσου, help against . . , Plat.
of persons, an aid, succour, Aesch., Soph.
helper of sailors, Anth.
aiding, succouring, propitious, serviceable, τινι Aesch.; absol., Id., Soph.
c. gen. serviceable towards a thing, Aesch., Soph.; πρός τι Thuc.
as Subst. a helper, aid, esp. in battle, Il.: a defender before a tribunal, advocate, Id.
any spice or sweet herb, Xen.
arable land, corn-land, Lat. arvum, Ar.
radical form of ἀραρίσκω, whence come ἄρθρον, ἁρμόζω, ἄρτι, ἄρτιος, ἀρτύω, etc.
poet. for ἀρόσιμος
poet. for ἄρρωστος, Anth.
not trodden down, Xen.
not having been at Salamis, Ar.
not agitated, tranquil, of the sea:—metaph. of the mind, Eur.
a bathing-tub, Od.
unsandalled, unshod, Bion.
not to be soothed, ungentle, Aesch.
to feel loathing or nausea, to be disgusted or vexed at a thing, c. dat., Theogn.; τὴν ψυχὴν ἀσηθῆναι Hdt.; ἀσώμενος ἐν φρεσί Theocr.
not fleshly, i. e. spiritual, Anth.
without flesh, lean, Xen.
indistinctness, obscurity, Plat.

indistinct to the senses, dim, faint, Thuc.; or to the mind, dim, obscure, Soph., Thuc.; νὺξ ἀσαφεστέρα ἐστίν by night one sees less distinctly, Xen.: —adv. -φῶς, obscurely, ἀσαφῶς ποτέρων ἀρξάντων without knowing which began, Thuc.
unquenchable, inextinguishable, of fire, Il.; of laughter, etc., Hom.; ἄσβ. πόρος ὠκεανοῦ ocean's ceaseless flow, Aesch.
as Subst., ἄσβεστος (sc. τίτανος), unslaked lime, Plut.
ungodliness, impiety, profaneness, Eur., Xen., etc.
to be impious, to act profanely, sin against the gods; εἴς τινα or τι Hdt., Eur.; περί τινα or τι Hdt., Xen.
c. acc. pers. to sin against him, Aesch.; hence in Pass., ἠσέβηται οὐδέν no sin has been committed, Andoc.
an impious or profane act, Thuc., Dem.
ungodly, godless, unholy, profane, Soph.: τὸ ἀσεβές = ἀσέβεια, Xen.
not drawn by traces (but by the yoke), Eur.
to behave licentiously, Plat.:—Pass., of acts, τὰ ἠσελγημένα, outrageous acts, Dem.
licentiousness, Plat., Dem.
licentious, wanton, brutal, Dem.:—adv., ἀσελγῶς πίονες extravagantly fat, Ar.; ἀς. ζῆν Dem.
moonless, νύξ Thuc.
unholy, Soph., Eur.
without leader or shepherd, Il.
unsealed, unmarked, Hdt.
without mark or sign, ἄς. χρυσός uncoined gold, Hdt.; ἄς. ἀργύριον Thuc.; ἄς. ὅπλα arms without device, Eur.
of sacrifices or oracles, giving no sign, unintelligible, Hdt., Trag.
leaving no mark, indistinct, Soph.; of sounds, inarticulate, unintelligible, Hdt.; ἄσημα βοῆς = ἄσημος βοή, Soph.:—generally, unperceived, unnoticed, Aesch., Soph.
of persons, cities, etc., of no mark, unknown, obscure, Eur.
nausea, distress, vexation, Hdt., Eur.
want of strength, weakness, feebleness, sickliness, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; ἀσθένεια βίου poverty, Hdt.
sickness, a disease, Thuc.
to be weak, feeble, sickly, Eur., Thuc., etc.; ἠσθένησε he fell sick, Dem.
without strength, weak, feeble, weakly, Hdt., etc.; ἀσθενέστερος πόνον ἐνεγκεῖν too weak to bear labour, Dem.:— τὸ ἀσθενὲς = ἀσθένεια, Thuc.
of property, weak, poor, Hdt., Eur.; οἱ ἀσθενέστεροι the weaker sort, i. e. the poor, Xen.
insignificant, οὐκ ἀσθενέστατος σοφιστής Hdt.; of streams, petty, small, Id.
adv. ἀσθενῶς, feebly, slightly, Plat.: comp. -έστερον or -έστερα Id., Thuc.
to weaken, Xen.
to breathe hard, gasp for breath, of one out of breath or dying, mostly in pres. part., Il.
short breath, panting, from toil, Il., Aesch.
generally, a breath, breathing, Mosch.: a blast, Anth.
Asiatic, Thuc., etc. also Ἀσιάτης, fem. Ἀσιᾶτις, Ionic Ἀσιήτης Ἀσιῆτις, Aesch., Eur.
Asia, Hdt., attic.
an Asiarch, the highest religious official under the Romans in the province of Asia, NTest.
fem. adj. = Ἀσιανή, Asiatic
(sc. κιθάρα ) the lyre as improved in Lesbos.
of Asian birth, Aesch.
not of iron, Eur.: not made by iron, Anth.
without sword, unarmed, Eur.
not nice as to food, Plut.
unhurt, unharmed, of persons, Od., Hdt.: secure, happy of life and fortune, Aesch.
of things, undamaged, Hdt.
act. not harming, Id.: harmless, Xen.
protecting from harm, Aesch.
adv. ἀσινῶς, innocently, Sup. -εστατα Xen.
Asian, Il.
slime, mud, such as a river brings down, Il.
to abstain from food, fast, Eur., Plat.
want of food, Hdt., Eur.
without food, fasting, Od., attic
the spotted lizard, Lat. stellio, Ar.
unhoed, Theocr.
a poor bed, pallet, Ar.
a bier, Anth.
without winking, with unchanged look, Xen.
not blinking or winking, Ar.
dried up, withered, Od.
neut. ἀσκελές as adv. toughly, obstinately, stubbornly, ἀσκελὲς αἰεί Id.; so, ἀσκελέως αἰεί Il.
without the axe, unhewn, Soph.
inconsiderate, unreflecting, Plat.:—adv. -τως, inconsiderately, Thuc., etc.
unconsidered, unobserved, Xen.
without the implements of his art, Hdt.
unfurnished, unprepared, Soph.: c. gen. unfurnished with a thing, Id.
to work curiously, form by art, fashion, Hom.; ἀσκήσας with skilful art, Id.
of adornment, to dress out, trick out, decorate, adorn, deck, Hdt.: Pass., πέπλοισι Περσικοῖς ἠσκημένη Aesch.:—Mid., σῶμ’ ἠσκήσατο adorned his own person, Eur.
in Prose, to practise, exercise, train, Lat. exercere, properly of athletic exercise:
of the person trained, Ar.; ἀσκεῖν τὸ σῶμα εἴς or πρός τι for an object or purpose, Xen., etc.
of the thing practised, ἀσκ. τέχνην Hdt.; metaph., ἀσκ. τὴν ἀλήθειαν Id.; κακότητα Aesch.; ἀσέβειαν Eur.
c. inf., ἄσκει τοιαύτη μένειν endeavour to remain such, Soph.; ἀσκ. ἀγαθὰ ποιεῖν to make a practice of doing good, Xen.
absol. to practise, go into training, οἱ ἀσκοῦντες those who practise gymnastics, Id.
unhurt, unharmed, unscathed, Hom.
an exercise, practice, Xen.
without tents, Plut.
exercise, practice, training, Thuc., Xen., etc.; in pl. exercises, Plat.:—c. gen., ἄσκ. τινος practice of or in a thing, Id.
generally, a mode of life, profession, art, Luc.
to be practised, Xen.
ἀσκητέον, one must practise, σοφίαν Plat.
one who practises any art or trade, ἀσκ. τῶν πολεμικῶν Xen.: esp. an athlete, one trained for the arena, Ar., Plat.
curiously wrought, Od.: adorned, πέπλωι with a robe, Theocr.
to be acquired by practice, Plat., Xen.
of persons, practised in a thing, c. dat., Plut.
unshaded, Pind.
a name for physicians, Theogn., Soph.
the temple of Asclepius, Luc.
of, belonging to Asclepius, Ἀσκληπίεια (sc. ἱερά) his festival, Plat.
Asclepius, Lat. Aesculapius, a Thessalian prince, famous as a physician, Il.:—later, son of Apollo, tutelary god of medicine.
inconsiderate, heedless, Il.: unregardful of a thing, c. gen., Aesch.
pass. unseen, invisible, Soph.
not to be seen, unintelligible, obscure, Aesch., Soph.: inconceivable, incalculable, Id.
aimless, random, Luc.
a leathern-bag, a wine-skin, Hom.; ἀσκὸς βοός the bag of ox-skin in which Aeolus bottled up the winds, Od.; ἀσκὸς Μαρσυέω a bag made of the skin of Marsyas, Hdt.:— a bladder, Eur.
proverb. usage, ἀσκὸν δείρειν τινά to flay one alive, maltreat wantonly, Ar.; ἀσκὸς δεδάρθαι Solon.
to dance as at the Ἀσκώλια, Ar.
the 2nd day of the rural Dionysia, when they danced upon greased wine-skins, "unctos saluere per utres."
the leather padding of the hole which served for the row-lock, put there to make the oar move easily, Ar.
a song, a lyric ode, or lay, Plat.
twister of song, Ar.
to be well-pleased, Polyb.

entry.etym: ἥδομαι, the perf. part. of which would be ἡσμένος
entry.sense: well-pleased, glad, always with a Verb, φύγεν ἄσμενος he escaped gladly or he was glad to have escaped, Hom., etc.; ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένωι εἴη glad would it make me! Il.; ἀσμένωι δέ σοι νὺξ ἀποκρύψει φάος glad wilt thou be when night shuts out the light, Aesch.: —adv. ἀσμένως, gladly, readily, Id., Eur.: Sup. ἀσμεναίτατα, -έστατα, Plat.
unwisdom, stupidity, Plut., Luc.
unwise, foolish, silly, Theogn.

to welcome kindly, bid welcome, greet, Lat. salutare, τινα Hom., etc.; as the common form on meeting, ἀσπάζομαί σε or ἀσπάζομαι alone, Ar.; πρόσωθεν αὐτὴν ἀσπ. I salute her at a respectful distance, i. e. keep away from her, Eur.:— also to take leave of, Id., Xen.
to embrace, kiss, caress, Ar.; of dogs, Lat. blandiri, Xen.
of things, to follow eagerly, cleave to, Lat. amplector, ἀσπ. τὸν οἶνον Plat.
ἀσπ. ὅτι to be glad that, Ar.
to pant, gasp, struggle convulsively, of the dying, Hom., Hdt.; but, μοῦνος ἤσπαιρε he was the only one who still made a struggle, Hdt.
aspalathus, a prickly shrub, yielding a fragrant oil, Theogn.; used as an instrument of torture, Plat.
of land, unsown, untilled, Od.
of plants, not sown, growing wild, Id.
welcome, gladly welcomed, Hom.
well-pleased, glad, Id.:— adv. -ίως, gladly, Id., Hdt.
a greeting, esp. in pl. embraces, Eur.
a greeting, embrace, salutation, Theogn., NTest.
= ἀσπάσιος, welcome, Od., Hdt. adv. -τῶς, Id.
Aeol. and Dor for ἕως.
to be appeased by no libations, implacable, Dem.
without seed or posterity, Il.

entry.etym: a neut. form used as adv.
entry.sense: hastily, hotly, vehemently, Hom.
unspeakable, unutterable, unspeakably great, Hom.:—neut. as adv. unspeakably, Il.
one that throws away his shield, a runaway, Ar.
shield-bearing, Aesch., Eur.
shield-bearing, a warrior, Il.
clattering with shields, Pind.
the workshop of a shieldmaker, Dem.
a shield-bearer, Eur.
living by the shield, i. e. by war, Eur.
without spot, spotless, Anth., NTest.

a round shield, Lat. clipeus, of bull's hide, overlaid with metal plates, with a boss (ὀμφαλός) in the middle, and fringed with tassels (θύσανοι): different from the oblong shield (ὅπλον, Lat. scutum) used by the ὁπλῖται.
in Prose, used for a body of soldiers, ὀκτακισχιλίη ἀσπίς 8, 000 men-at-arms, Hdt.

military phrases: ἐπ’ ἀσπίδας πέντε καὶ εἴκοσι τάξασθαι to be drawn up 25 deep, Thuc.; so, ἐπ’ ἀσπίδων ὀλίγων τετάχθαι Id.; ἐπ’ ἀσπίδα, παρ’ ἀσπίδα (opp. to ἐπὶ δόρυ) on the left, towards or to the left, because the shield was on the left arm, Xen.; παρ’ ἀσπ. στῆναι to stand in battle-array, Eur.
an asp, an Egyptian snake, Hdt.
one armed with a shield, a warrior, gen. pl. ἀσπιστάων, Il.:—as adj., ἀσπισταὶ μόχθοι τευχέων, i. e. the shield of Achilles, Eur.
κλόνοι ἀσπίστορες turmoil of shielded warriors, Aesch.
without bowels: metaph. heartless, spiritless, Soph.
without drink-offering, of a god, to whom no drink-offering is poured, ἄσπ. θεός i. e. death, Eur.

without a regular truce (which was ratified by σπονδαί), Thuc.; ἀσπόνδους τοὺς νεκροὺς ἀνελέσθαι to take up their dead without leave asked, Id.; τὸ ἄσπονδον a keeping out of treaty or covenant with others, neutrality, Id.
admitting of no truce, implacable, deadly, Lat. internecinus, of war, Aesch., Dem.
not to be zealously pursued, not worth pursuing, Eur.
without zeal, without a struggle, ignobly, Il.
Dim. of Lat. as, a farthing, NTest., Plut.

nearer, very near, Hom.: c. gen., ἆσσον ἐμεῖο nearer to me, Il.; with a double comp., μᾶλλον ἆσσον Soph.:—hence, as a new comp., ἀσσοτέρω, with or without gen., Od.; Sup. ἀσσοτάτω, Anth.; whence adj. ἀσσότατος Id.
(sc. γῆ), ἡ Assyria, the country of the Assyrians, Id.
the Assyrians, Hdt.
unsteady, unstable, Anth.
unsteady, unstable, ἀστέρες Xen.; ὁ δῆμος ἀσταθμητότατον πρᾶγμα Dem.: uncertain of life, Eur.; τὸ ἀστάθμητον uncertainty, Thuc.
not in drops, i. e. in floods, Soph., Plat.
not in drops, gushing, Eur.
not dripping, Plut.
a courier, Persian word, Plut.
not disturbed by faction, Thuc.: of persons, free from party-spirit, not factious, Plat.
to be unstable, NTest.
unstable, Plut.
of raisins, Anth.
as collect. noun, dried grapes, raisins, Lat. uva passa, Hdt.
an ear of corn, Il., Hdt.
uncovered: διὰ τὸ ἀστέγαστον from their having no shelter, Thuc.
Dep. to talk cleverly, Plut.
of the town: hence, like Lat. urbanus, town-bred, polite, courteous, opp. to ἄγροικος, Plat.:— refined, elegant, pretty, witty, clever Ar., Plat.:—ironically, ἀστ. κέρδος a pretty piece of luck, Ar.
unmoved, unshaken, Il.; ἀστεμφὲς ἔχεσκε [τὸ σκῆπτρον] he held it stiff, Id.:— adv., ἀστεμφέως ἐχέμεν to hold fast, Od.: also neut. ἀστεμφές, as adv. stiff, stark, Mosch.
of persons, stiff, unflinching, Theocr.
without sigh or groan, Soph., Eur.
one must sing, Ar., Plat.
uncrowned, Eur.
without love of man, shunning wedlock, Aesch.
without love, implacable, hateful, Soph.
starred, starry, Il.
like a star, glittering, Id.
lightning, Il.
the lightener, of Zeus, Il.
star-faced, bright-shining, Eur.
starry, Id.
without crown, ungarlanded, Eur.
uncrowned, not to be crowned, Plat., etc.
without tombstone, Anth.
fem. of ἀστός, Hdt., etc.
not steady, unstable, Anth., NTest.

entry.etym: The Root is ΣΤΕΡ, α being euphon. , cf. Lat. stella, i. e. sterula.
entry.sense: a star, Il., etc.; cf. ἄστρον.
a flame, light, fire, Eur.
untrodden, Aesch.: desert, pathless, Soph.
not to be trodden, holy, Id.
of a city or town, opp. to country, Aesch.; τὰ ἀστικὰ Διονύσια (also called τὰ κατ’ ἄστυ), Thuc.
like ἀστεῖος, polite, neat, nice, ἀστικά (as adv.) Theocr.
not marked with στίγματα, not tattooed, Hdt.
not scraped clean, Anth.
unequipped, of Charon's boat, used in the same way as γάμος ἄγαμος, Aesch.
without mouth: of horses, hardmouthed, restive, Soph.
of dogs, soft-mouthed, unable to hold with the teeth, Xen.
of metal, soft, incapable of a fine edge, Plut.
without sighs, Anth.
without natural affection, Aeschin.; ὥστοργος (i. e. ὁ ἄστ.) the heartless one, Theocr.
a townsman, citizen, Hom., attic
to miss the mark, to miss, fail, τινος or περί τινος Polyb.; περί τι NTest.
missing the mark, aiming badly at, τινος Plat., Anth.
a mule's saddle, an easy padded saddle, Dem.
not twisted, straight, Plat.
to play with ἀστράγαλοι, Plat.
a playing with ἀστράγαλοι, Arist.
one of the neck-vertebrae, Hom.
the ball of the ankle joint, Lat. talus, Hdt., Theocr.

pl. ἀστράγαλοι, dice or agame played with dice, Il., Hdt.:—they were at first made of knuckle-bones, and never had more than four flat sides, whereas the κύβοι had six. They played with four: the best throw (βόλος), when each die came differently, was called Ἀφροδίτη, Lat. jactus Veneris; the worst, when all came alike, κύων, Lat. canis.
a flash of lightning, lightning, Hdt., attic; in pl. lightnings, Aesch., Soph.
any bright light, NTest.
to carry lightnings, Ar.
lightning-bearing, flashing, Eur.
to lighten, hurl lightnings, of omens sent by Zeus, Il., Ar.
impers., ἀστράπτει it lightens, ἤστραψε it lightened, attic
to flash like lightning, Soph., Eur., etc.:—c. acc. cogn., ἐξ ὀμμάτων δ’ ἤστραπτε σέλας (sc. Τυφών) he flashed flame from his eyes, Aesch.
exemption from service, Ar.
a shunning of service, which at Athens was a heavy offence, φεύγειν γραφὴν ἀστρατείας to be accused of it, Id.; ἀστρατείας ἁλῶναι, ὀφλεῖν to be convicted of it, Oratt.
without service, never having seen service, Ar.
= ἄστροφος Theocr.:—adv. -τεί, Anth.
unbending, inflexible, Id.
near the stars, Aesch.
astronomical, Anth.
astronomy, Xen.
to study astronomy, Ar.
astronomy, Ar., Plat., etc.
skilled in astronomy, pertaining to astronomy, Plat.
an astronomer, Plat., etc.
mostly in pl. the stars, Hom., attic; in sg., mostly of Sirius, Xen., etc.; cf. ἀστήρ.
without turning away, unturning, Lat. irretortus, ὄμματα Aesch.; ἀφέρπειν ἄστρ. to go away without turning back, Soph.
starry, Anth.; ἀστρ. ἀνάγκη the law of the stars, Id.
= ἀστερ-ωπός, Eur.
without bed or bedding, Plat.: metaph. unsmoothed, rugged, Eur.
lord of the city, epith. of certain gods, Aesch.: in Hom. only as prop. n.
crying through the city, of a herald, Il.
near or bordering on a city, Hdt., Aesch.
as Subst. a neighbour to the city, a borderer, Hdt., Thuc.
into, to, or towards the city, Hom.
Pass. to have the streets filled with fugitives, Aesch.
without pillar or prop, Anth.
(sc. πόλις) Athens, the victorious city, Aesch.
to be ἀστυ-νόμος, Dem.
the office of ἀστυνόμος, Arist.
of or for an ἀστυνόμος or his office, Plat.
protecting the city, θεοί Aesch.; ὀργαὶ ἀστ. the feelings of social life, Soph.
as Subst. a magistrate at Athens, who had the care of the police, streets, and public buildings, five for the city and five for Peiraeeus, Plat., etc.
protecting the city, Anth.
a city, town, Hom., etc.; Σούσων ἄ. the town of Susa, Aesch.; ἄ. Θήβης Soph.
the Athenians called Athens Ἄστυ, as the Romans called Rome Urbs, mostly without the Art. (as we speak of "being in town, " "going to town"), Ar.
unshaken, undisturbed, Xen.
not rugged, Theogn., Anth.
not pardoning, relentless, Dem.
unmixed, Anth.
not gathered in, Xen.
not to be compared, unlike, Plut.
not plagued by informers, not calumniated, Aeschin., Luc.
of an asylum, Plut.
not inviolate, Eur.
inviolability, of suppliants, Aesch.
not reasoning justly:— adv., -τως, ἀσυλλογίστως ἔχειν τινός to be unable to reason about a thing, Plut.
safe from violence, inviolate, of persons seeking protection, Eur.:—c. gen., γάμων ἄσυλος safe from marriage, Id.
of places, γῆν ἄσυλον παρασχεῖν to make the land a refuge, Id.
not coming to terms, Thuc.:—adv., -τως ἔχειν to be irreconcilable, Plut.
not to be guessed, unintelligible, Soph.
not paying one's scot or share (συμβολαί), Lat. immunis, δειπνεῖν ἀσύμβολον Aeschin.
want of proportion or harmony, Plat.
having no common measure, τινι with a thing, Plat.; πρός τι Plut.
unsymmetrical, disproportionate, Xen.
not compact, Luc.
without sympathy with, τινι Plut.
inconvenient, inexpedient, useless, Hes.: c. dat. inexpedient for, prejudicial to, Eur., Thuc.; also ἔς or πρός τι Id.:— adv. -ρως, Xen.
not agreeing in sound, Plat.:—metaph. discordant, at variance, τινι with another, Id.; πρός τινα NTest.
not agreeing with, τινος Plut.
unconnected, Xen.
not manifest, Plut.
want of understanding, stupidity, Eur., Thuc.
void of understanding, stupid, Hdt., attic; not to be understood, unintelligible, Eur.
want of experience in a thing, c. gen., Arist.
unaccustomed, inexperienced, unacquainted, with others, Arist.
uncompounded, Plat.
（συντίθεμαι) bound by no covenant, faithless, Dem., NTest.
not easily perceived, Aeschin.
not ranged together; of soldiers, not in battle-order, Xen.
undisciplined, disorderly, Thuc., Xen.
not combined in society, Id.
not put on the tax-roll, free from public burdens, Dem.
not strained, slack:— adv. -νως, lazily, Sup. -ώτατα, Xen.
not arranged, not ready, Xen.
having no cohesion or consistency, Plat.
metaph. incoherent, irregular, Lat. dispar sibi, Ar.; ἀξ. ἄλγος fitful, ever-recurring pain, Aesch.
insolent, degrading, Il.
without convulsion or struggle, of one dying, Aesch., Soph.
unslaughtered, Eur.
a mole, Babr.
security against stumbling or falling, ἀσφ. πρὸς τὸν πηλόν Thuc.: stability, Soph.
assurance from danger, personal safety, security, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; ἀσφ. διδόναι, παρέχειν Xen.
assurance, certainty, ἀσφ. μὴ ἂν ἐλθεῖν αὐτούς certainty that they would not come, Thuc.; ἀσφάλεια λόγου the certainty of an argument, Xen., NTest.
of Poseidon, the securer, Ar.
not liable to fall, immoveable, steadfast, firm, θεῶν ἕδος Od., etc.
of friends and the like, unfailing, trusty, Soph., etc.: c. inf., φρονεῖν γὰρ οἱ ταχεῖς οὐκ ἀσφαλεῖς the hasty in council are not safe, Id.: so of things, sure, certain, Thuc., etc.
assured from danger, safe, secure, Soph., etc.; ἐν ἀσφαλεῖ in safety, Thuc.; τὸ ἀσφαλές = ἀσφάλεια, Id.; ἀσφαλές [ἐστι], c. inf., it is safe to . . , Ar.
ἀσφ. ῥήτωρ a convincing speaker, Id.

epic adv. ἀσφαλέως ἔχειν or μένειν to be, remain fast, firm, steady, Hom.; so neut. ἀσφαλές as adv., Id.; ἀσφ. ἀγορεύει without faltering, Od.; ἔμπεδον ἀσφαλέως without fail for ever, Hom.; still further strengthd., ἔμπεδον ἀσφαλὲς ἀεί Il.
attic adv. ἀσφαλῶς in all senses of the adj., in safety, with certainty, Soph.:—comp. -έστερον, Hdt., Plat.; Sup. -έστατα, Id.
Mid. to make safe, secure, NTest.
asphalt, bitumen, forming in lumps, (θρόμβοι) on the surface of the river Is near Babylon and at Ardericca near Susa, Hdt.
entry.etym: Seems to be a foreign word.

entry.sense: to resound, clang, of armed men, Theocr.
the throat, gullet, Il.
asparagus, Anth.
of asphodel, Luc.
ἀσφόδελος as noun, asphodel, king's-spear, a plant of the lily kind, Hes., Theocr.
oxyt., as adj., ἀσφοδελὸς λειμών the asphodel mead, which the shades of heroes haunted, Od.
without pulse, lifeless, Anth.
to be distressed, grieved, Hom.: to be vexed at a thing, c. gen., Od.
to be vexed at a thing, Aesch., Eur.; τι Id.
not to beheld in or checked, irrepressible, ungovernable, Hom.
without form or figure, Plat.
to behave unseemly, disgrace oneself, to be put to shame, Eur., Plat.
want of form, ungracefulness, Plat.: in moral sense, indecorum, Id.
misshapen, unseemly, shameful, Lat. turpis, Eur.
of persons, ἀσχ. γενέσθαι to be indecorous, Hdt.
to engage, occupy, τινά Luc.

an occupation, business, want of leisure, Thuc.; ἀσχ. ἔχειν φιλοσοφίας πέρι to have no leisure for pursuing it, Plat.; ἀσχ. ἄγειν to be engaged or occupied, Id.; ἀσχ. παρέχειν τινί to cause one trouble, Id.
of persons, without leisure, engaged, occupied, busy, Plat., Dem.; ἄσχ. ἔς τι with no leisure for a thing, Hdt.; ἄσχ. περί τι busy about . ., Plut.:—adv., ἀσχόλως ἔχειν to be busy, Eur.
of actions, allowing no leisure, Id.
the inspissated juice of a Scythian tree, Hdt.
unembodied, incorporeal, Plat.
Dep. to lead a profligate, wasteful life, Arist.
prodigality, wastefulness, Plat.
having no hope of safety, abandoned, profligate, Lat. perditus, Soph., Arist.
act., ἄσωτος γένει bringing ruin on the race, fatal to it, Aesch.
of a soldier, to be undisciplined, disorderly, Xen., Dem.
generally, to lead a disorderly life, Xen.
not in battle-order, of troops, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
undisciplined, disorderly, irregular, lawless, Id., etc.
adv. -τως, in an irregular, disorderly manner, of troops, Id.: comp. ἀτακτότερον, Id.
without pains or patience, indifferent, careless, Thuc.
equal in weight, equivalent, or equal to, τινι Hom.
tender-minded, of a child, Il.
to skip in childish glee, gambol, Il.
. Act. to bring up a child, rear, foster, like ἀτιτάλλω, Soph.:—Pass. to grow up, wax, Hhymn.; the Act. is so used by Hes.
tender, delicate, of young creatures, Hom.; ἀταλὰ φρονέοντες of young, gay spirit, Il.
soft-hearted, Anth.
want of discipline, disorderliness, properly among soldiers, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
generally disorder, irregularity, Plat., etc.
to suffer greatly, be in dire distress, ἀτώμενος Soph., Eur.
not disturbed, without confusion, steady, of soldiers, Xen.
unfearing, fearless, Il.; ἀτ. τῆς θέας having no fear about the sight, Soph.
causing no fear, Aesch.
fearless, undaunted, Soph.
unwincing, unflinching, Pind.

but, yet, Lat. at, to introduce an objection or correction, Il., attic; it always begins a sentence or clause, but is placed after the voc., Ἕκτορ, ἀτάρ που ἔφης still thou didst say, Il.:— ἀτάρ sometimes answers to μέν, more emphatic than δέ, Hom., attic
in attic to mark a rapid transition to another thought, Aesch., etc.; so ἀτὰρ δή Eur.
mischievous, baneful, Hom.
presumptuous sin, recklessness, arrogance, Hom. always in pl.; in sg., Hes., Hdt.
acting presumptuously, in arrogance, Od.

entry.etym: ἄτη, though α does not agree in quantity
entry.sense: presumptuous, reckless, arrogant, Hom., Hdt.
unwedded, virgin, Aesch.
want of burial, Luc.
unburied, Hdt., attic
not to be wetted: metaph. not to be softened, relentless, Soph., Eur.
not to be worn away, indestructible, of iron, Hom.: metaph. stubborn, unyielding, Il.
unwalled, unfortified, Thuc.
not walled in, not blockaded, Id.
not to be guessed, obscure, baffling, Hdt., Thuc.:—adv., ἀτεκμάρτως ἔχειν to be in the dark about a thing, Xen.
of persons, uncertain, inconsistent, Ar.
childlessness, Arist.
without children, childless, Hes., Trag.
in causal sense, destroying children, Aesch.
to make childless:— Pass. to be deprived of children, Anth.
exemption from public burdens (τέλη), Lat. immunitas, granted to those who deserved well of the state, attic; c. gen., ἀτ. στρατηΐης exemption from service, Hdt.
without end or issue, to no purpose, without effect, unaccomplished, Hom.
uninitiated in mysteries, c. gen., Eur.; absol., Plat.
not brought to an end or issue, unaccomplished, Il.
of a person, impracticable, Soph.
endless, eternal, Aesch.
without end, i. e.,
not brought to an end or issue, unaccomplished, Od., Xen.:— incomplete, Soph., Thuc., Plat.
act. not bringing to an end, not accomplishing one's purpose, Pind., Plat., etc.
（τέλος iv) at Athens, free from tax or tribute, scot-free, Lat. immunis, absol., or c. gen., ἀτ. τῶν ἄλλων free from all other taxes, Hdt., attic
of sums, without deduction, nett, clear, ὀβολὸς ἀτ. an obol clear gain, Xen., Dem.
（τέλος v) uninitiated in mysteries, c. gen., Hhymn.
to maltreat, to afflict, perplex, Od.: Pass., c. gen., to be bereft or cheated of a thing, Hom.
strained tight, clinging, of ivy, Soph.: metaph.
of men's minds and speech, intent, earnest, Hes., Plat.; also stiff, stubborn, inexorable, Aesch., Ar.:—adv. ἀτενῶς earnestly, ἀτ. ἔχειν πρός τι Plut.
to look intently, gaze earnestly, εἴς τι Arist.; τινί upon one, NTest.
properly acc. pl. neut. of ὅστε, used as Adv., just as, so as, Il., Hdt., Soph.

in causal sense, inasmuch as, seeing that, Lat. quippe, with part., ἅτε ἔχων Hdt., Thuc., etc.; with gen. absol., ἅτε τῶν ὁδῶν φυλασσομένων quippe viae custodirentur, Hdt.; with the part. omitted, δίκτυα δοὺς [αὐτῶι], ἅτε θηρευτῆι [ὄντι] Id.
unsoftened: metaph. stubborn, unfeeling, merciless, Od., Aesch.
without bounds; ἀτ. πέπλος having no end or issue, inextricable, Aesch.; ἀτέρμονες αὐγαί the countless rays of the mirror, Eur.
Dor for ἕτερος, Ar.
ἅτερος [ᾱ], attic crasis for ὁ ἕτερος, neut. θἄτερον [ᾱ], gen. θἀτέρου, etc.
without, Hom.; ἄτερ Ζηνός without his will, Il.
aloof or apart from, Id., Trag.
unpleasing, joyless, melancholy, Hom., Aesch.; ἀτερπέστερον εἰς ἀκρόασιν less attractive to the ear, Thuc.
unpleasantness, Luc.
to fail in gaining a thing, c. gen., Babr.
not gaining.
unequipped, unarmed, Eur., Anth.
want of art or skill, unskilfulness, Plat.
without art, ignorant of the rules of art, unskilled, empirical, Plat.

adv. of ἀτεχνής, simply, i. e. really, absolutely, Lat. plane, omnino, Ar., Plat., etc.; καλὸν ἀτ. simply beautiful, Ar.:—in comparisons, ἀτεχνῶς ὥσπερ just as, Plat.:—with negat., just not, Ar.; ἀτεχνῶς οὐδείς simply no one, Id.
without rules of art, empirically, Xen., Plat.
in part. ἀτέων, fool-hardy, reckless, Il., Hdt.
not melted or to be melted, Plat.
neglected, Plut.
careless:— adv., ἀτημελῶς ἔχειν Id.
unheeded, uncared for, Xen.
baffled, disappointed, Aesch.
taking no heed, slovenly, Alciphro:—adv., ἀτημελήτως ἔχειν to take no heed of a thing, c. gen., Xen.

bewilderment, infatuation, reckless impulse, caused by judicial blindness sent by the gods, Hom.:—hence Ἄτη is personified as the goddess of mischief or reckless conduct, Ἄτη, ἣ πάντας ἀᾶται Il.: the Λιταί come slowly after her, undoing the evil she has worked, Id.
as a consequence,
reckless guilt or sin, as that of Paris, Id.
bane, ruin, Hom., Trag.:—of persons, a bane, pest, Aesch., Soph.
blinded by ἄτη, hurried to ruin, Theogn.
baneful, ruinous, mischievous, Aesch., Soph.: τὸ ἀτηρόν bane, ruin, Aesch.; ἀτηρότατον κακόν Ar.
Attic:— as Subst. (sub. γῆ), Attica, Eur.
unhonoured, Aesch.
act. not honouring or regarding, τινος Eur.
not to honour, to hold in no honour, θεούς Aesch. : absol. in part., ἀτίζων, unheeding, Il.
untamable, wild, Plut.
to forsake the herd, Theocr.
despising the herd, i.e. straying, feeding alone, Theocr., Anth.

to hold in no honour, to esteem lightly, dishonour, slight, c. acc., Hom., attic: so in Mid., Soph.:—c. acc. cogn., ἔπη ἀτιμάζεις πόλιν thou speakest words in dishonour of the city, Id.:—Pass. to suffer dishonour, Hdt., attic

c. gen. rei, ἀτ. λόγου to treat as unworthy of speech, Aesch.; ἀτ. ὧν = ἀτ. τούτων ἅ, Soph.:—also, μή μ’ ἀτιμάσηις τὸ μὴ οὐ θανεῖν deem me not unworthy to die, Id.; οὐκ ἀτιμάσω προσειπεῖν will not disdain to . . , Eur.
= ἀτιμόω in legal sense, to deprive of civil rights, Xen.
to be despised, Plat.
a dishonourer, Aesch.
to dishonour, treat lightly, Hom.
unhonoured, despised, Il.
（τῑμή II) not valued or estimated, δίκη ἀτ. a cause in which the penalty is not assessed in court, but fixed by law beforehand, Dem.
dishonour, disgrace, Od., Soph., etc.; ἐν ἀτιμίηι τινὰ ἔχειν, ἀτιμίην προστιθέναι τινί Hdt.; ἀτ. τινός dishonour done to one, Eur.
at Athens, the loss of civil rights, Lat. deminutio capitis, Aesch., Oratt.
ἐσθημάτων ἀτ., i. e. ragged garments, Aesch.
sorrowing for dishonour incurred, Aesch.

unhonoured, dishonoured, Il., Trag.; comp. ἀτιμότερος less honourable, Xen.; c. gen. without the honour of . . , not deemed worthy of . . , Aesch.; also, χάρις οὐκ ἄτιμος πόνων no unworthy return for . . , Id.

at Athens, deprived of privileges, Lat. capite deminutus, opp. to ἐπίτιμος, Ar., etc.; also c. gen., ἄτ. γερῶν deprived of privileges, Thuc.; ἄτ. τοῦ συμβουλεύειν deprived of the right of advising, Dem.
（τιμή II) without price or value, οἶκον ἄτιμον ἔδεις thou devourest his substance without payment made, Od.
unrevenged, Aesch.
adv. -μως, dishonourably, ignominiously, Id., Soph.
to dishonour, Aesch.:— Pass. to suffer dishonour or indignity, Hdt., Aesch., Eur.
at Athens, to punish with ἀτιμία (2), Lat. aerarium facere, Ar., Oratt.
unavenged, i. e.,
unpunished, ἀτ. γίγνεσθαι to escape punishment, Hdt., Thuc.:— adv. -τως, with impunity, Plat.
for which no revenge has been taken, ἀτιμώρητον ἐᾶν θάνατον Aeschin.
undefended, unprotected, Thuc.
a dishonouring, dishonour done to, c. gen., τραπέζας, πατρός Aesch.
redupl. form of ἀτάλλω, to rear up a child, foster, cherish, tend, Hom.; of horses, Pass., χῆν’ ἀτιταλλομένην ἐνὶ οἴκωι Od.
unpunished, Aesch.
（τίω) unhonoured, Id.
unhonoured, unavenged, Il.
unpaid, Id. [where ῑ].
sprung from Atlas, of the Pleiads, Hes.
of Atlas, Atlantic, τέρμονες Ἀτλ. the pillars of Hercules, Eur.
θάλασσα ἡ Ἀ. καλουμένη, the Atlantic ocean, Hdt.
Atlas, one of the elder gods, who bore up the pillars of heaven, Od.:—later, one of the Titans, Hes., Aesch.
in hist. writers, Mount Atlas in Africa, regarded as the pillar of heaven, Hdt.
to be unable to bear a thing, to be impatient, Soph.
not to be borne, insufferable, Il., Orac. ap. Hdt., Soph.
not to be dared, ἄτλητα τλᾶσα Aesch.
act. incapable of bearing a thing, c. gen., Anth.
slavery, servitude, Anth.
a slave, servant.
not cut up, unravaged, Thuc., Plut.: of mines, not yet opened, Xen.
undivided, indivisible, Plat.
to smoke, Soph.: of water, to steam, Xen.
steam, vapour, Aesch.
unwalled, Eur.
having never yet brought forth, never having had a child, Hdt., Eur.
not bearing interest, Plat.
not to be endured, insufferable, Pind.: of wicked men, Aesch.
want of daring, cowardice, backwardness, Thuc., Dem.
daring nothing, wanting courage, spiritless, cowardly, Ar., Thuc.:—of women, unenterprising, retiring, Aesch.:—c. inf. not having the heart to do a thing, Id.
uncut, unmown, Soph.
that cannot be cut, indivisible, Plat.; ἐν ἀτόμωι in a moment, NTest.
to be relaxed, exhausted, Plut.
not stretched, relaxed, Arist.
without bow or arrow, Luc.
a being out of the way, and so:
extraordinary nature of a thing, Thuc.
strangeness, oddness, eccentricity, Ar., Plat.
out of place, and so,
strange, unwonted, extraordinary, Eur., etc.
strange, odd, eccentric, δοῦλοι τῶν ἀεὶ ἀτόπων slaves to every new paradox, Thuc.; τῶν ἀτοπωτάτων ἂν εἴη Dem.
unnatural, disgusting, foul, πνεῦμα Thuc.
adv. —πως, marvellously or absurdly, Id., Plat.
not treated tragically, Luc.
a spindle, Hdt., Ar., etc.
an arrow, Soph.; cf. ἠλακάτη.
a thistle-like plant, used for making spindles, Theocr.
properly a path with no turnings, generally a path-way, road, Hom., Hdt., Thuc., etc.
the herb orach.
without neck, Anth.
reality, strict truth, certainty, Hdt.
personified Ἀτρέκεια, severity, Pind.
real, genuine, Il.
strict, precise, exact, ἀριθμός Hdt.:— τὸ ἀτρεκές = ἀτρέκεια, Id.; τὸ ἀτρεκέστερον greater exactness, Id.; τὸ ἀτρεκέστατον Id.
sure, certain, Eur.
used by Hom. mostly in adv. ἀτρεκέως, with ἀγορεύειν, καταλέξαι, to tell truly, exactly; so also Hdt.
also neut. as adv., δεκὰς ἀτρεκές just ten of them, Od.; so, τὸ ἀτρεκές Theogn.

entry.etym: ἀτρέμα used by Poets for ἀτρέμας before a conson., Il.
entry.sense: without trembling, without motion, Hom.; ἀτρέμας εὕδειν Id.; ἀτρέμας ἧσο sit still, Il.; ἀτρέμας ἔχειν to keep quiet, Hdt.; ἀτρ. ἅπτεσθαί τινος gently, softly, Eur.; ἀτρ. πορεύεσθαι to go softly, Xen.
not to tremble, to keep still or quiet, Hes.; οὐδαμᾶ κω ἠτρεμήσαμεν, of a restless people, Hdt. From
not trembling, unmoved, Plat., Xen. adv. ἀτρεμέως Theogn.
a keeping still, ἀτρεμίαν ἔχειν or ἄγειν Xen.
to keep quiet, Theogn., Hdt.; οὐκ ἀτρ. to be restless, Id.
unmoved, immutable, Plut., Luc.
not trembling, unfearing, fearless, Lat. intrepidus, Trag.: c. gen., ἄτρ. μάχας fearless of fight, Aesch.; so, ἄτρ. ἐν μάχαις Soph.; ἄτρ. εὕδειν securely, Id.:—also neut. pl. ἄτρεστα as adv., Eur.
unconquered, Aesch.
not rubbed: of places, not traversed, pathless, Thuc.: of roads, not worn or used, Xen.: generally, fresh, new, Lat. integer, Id.
of hands, not worn by work, Od.; of corn, not threshed, Xen.; ἄτρ. ἄκανθαι thorns on which one cannot tread, or untraversed thorns, Theocr.
intrepid, dauntless, Il.
inflexibility, Theogn.
unchangeable, eternal, Theocr.
inflexible, unbending, Anth.:—hence Ἄτροπος, ἡ, name of one of the Μοῖραι or Parcae, Hes.; v. Κλωθώ.
to pine away, suffer from atrophy, Plut.
not fed, ill-fed, Xen.
yielding no harvest, unfruitful, of the sea, Hom.; of the air, Id.
c. gen., ἀτρ. κακῶν not worn out by ills, Aesch.
not worn away, untiring, unwearied, Aesch.: indefatigable, Plut.
of things, unabating, Soph., Mosch.; of a road, wearisome, Theocr.
the unwearied, a name of Pallas, Hom.
entry.etym: Lengthd. form of ἀτρύτη, as Ἀϊδωνεύς of Ἅιδης.

entry.sense: unwounded, Aesch., Soph.
invulnerable, Eur.
a bird, prob. a kind of partridge; or, as others think, the godwit or redshank, Ar.
a bird, prob. a kind of grouse, attagen Ionicus, Hor.
a salutation used to elders, father, Hom.
a cry of pain or grief, Trag., Ar.
a kind of locust without wings, Hdt.
Ἀττης Ὕης, a form of exorcism, used by the priests of Cybele, Dem.
to side with the Athenians, Thuc., Xen.
a siding with Athens, attachment to her, Thuc.
in the Attic dialect, Dem.
my little Athenian, Ar.
Attic, Athenian, Solon, etc.; ἡ Ἀττική (sc. γῆ), Attica, Hdt., etc.; cf. Ἀτθίς.
Adv. -κῶς in Attic style, Dem.
a comic alteration of Ἀττικός, after the form of Λακονικός, Ar.

Pass. : to be distraught from fear, mazed, bewildered, Hom.; ἀτυζόμενοι πεδίοιο fleeing bewildered o'er the plain, Il.: also to be distraught with grief, ἀτυζόμενος Soph., Eur.: c. acc., ὄψιν ἀτυχθείς amazed at the sight, Il.
in late Ep. we find the Act. ἀτύζω, with 3 sing. aor. 1 opt. ἀτύξαι, to strike with terror, Theocr.
without burial, Anth.
without a tomb, Luc.
not ruled by tyrants, Thuc.
without pride or arrogance, modest, Plat.
to be unlucky or unfortunate, fail, miscarry, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
c. gen., to fail of a thing, fail in getting or gaining it, τῆς ἀληθείας Xen.; so, c. part., Thuc.
ἀτ. πρός τινα to fail with another, i. e. to fail in one's request, Xen.:—Pass., τὰ ἀτυχηθέντα mischances, failures, Dem.
a misfortune, mishap, Oratt.
luckless, unfortunate, Dem., etc.
ill-luck:—a misfortune, miscarriage, mishap, Xen.
again, anew, afresh, once more, Hom., etc.; after numerals, δεύτερον αὖ, τρίτον αὖ, etc., Id.
generally, again, i. e. further, moreover, besides, Lat. porro, Od., attic
in turn, on the other hand, following δέ, Il., attic.
the pleon. phrases, πάλιν αὖ, αὖ πάλιν, ἔμπαλιν αὖ, αὖθις αὖ, αὖθις αὖ πάλιν, are only attic, mostly Trag.
αὖ αὖ, bow wow, of a dog, Ar.
to dry Od., Hdt., Xen.
to dry or parch up, αὐανῶ βίον I shall waste life away, Soph.: Pass., αὐανθείς withered, Aesch.; so in fut. mid., αὐανοῦμαι I shall wither away, Soph.
dry, parched, Hes.; of eyes, dry, sleepless, Anth.
to view in the clearest light, see distinctly, discern, Soph.; so in Mid., Il., Hes.
of the sun, to beam upon, illumine, τινά Eur.

the light of the sun, sunlight, and in pl. his rays or beams, Hom.; ὑπ’ αὐγὰς ἠελίοιο, i.e. still alive, Od.; so, αὐγὰς ἐσιδεῖν, λεύσσειν, βλέπειν Theogn., Aesch., Eur.; but, ὑπ’ αὐγὰς λεύσσειν or ἰδεῖν τι to hold up to the light and look at, Id.; κλύζειν πρὸς αὐγάς to rise surging towards the sun, Aesch.:—metaph., βίου δύντος αὐγαί "life's setting sun, " Id.:— αὐγή the dawn, day-break, NTest.
generally, any bright light, as of fire, Hom.; of lightning, Il.; of the eyes, Soph.; hence αὐγαί, like Lat. lumina, the eyes, Eur.
any gleam on the surface of bright objects, sheen, αὐγὴ χαλκείη Il.; αὐγὰ πέπλου Eur.
to cry out, speak, Hdt.: an aor1 act. αὔδαξα occurs in Anth.
c. acc. rei,
to utter sounds, speak, Il., Eur.
c. acc. rei, to speak or say something, Il., Soph.: so as Dep., Id.:—Pass., ηὐδᾶτο γὰρ ταῦτα so 'twas said, Id.
of oracles, to utter, proclaim, tell of, Id.; to speak out concerning a thing, Aesch.
c. acc. pers.,
to speak to, address, accost, Hom.: to invoke a god, Eur.
c. acc. et inf. to tell, bid, order one to do, Soph.; αὐδ. τινα μὴ ποιεῖν to forbid one to do, Aesch.; αὐδῶ σιωπᾶν Soph.: so as Dep., Id.
to call by name, call so and so, Eur.: Pass., αὐδῶμαι παῖς Ἀχιλλέως Soph.; κάκιστ’ αὐδώμενος most ill reported of, Aesch.
like λέγειν, to mean such an one, Eur.
speaking with human voice, Od.; when θεὸς αὐδήεσσα is applied to Calypso and Circe, it means a goddess who used the speech of mortals, Id.
the human voice, speech, opp. to ὀμφή (a divine voice), Il.
the sound or twang of the bowstring, Od.; of a trumpet, Eur.; of the τέττιξ, Hes.
= φήμη, a report, account, Soph., Eur.
an oracle, Id.
to draw back or backwards, Il.; to draw the bow, Id.: absol., in a sacrifice, to draw the victim's head back, so as to cut its throat, Id.
entry.etym: It can hardly be a compd. of αὖ ἐρύω, for αὖ is never elsewh. used in the local sense of back: perh. for ἀνερύω, i. e. ἀνϝερύω.

entry.sense: self-will, wilfulness, stubbornness, contumacy, presumption, Aesch., etc.
self-willed, wilful, dogged, stubborn, contumacious, presumptuous, Hdt., etc.:— metaph. of things, remorseless, unfeeling, Aesch.:— adv. -δως, Ar.; comp. -έστερον, Plat.
Dep. to be self-willed, Plat.
an act of self-will, wilfulness, Aesch.
self-willed in speech, Ar.
of the same blood, a brother, sister, kinsman, Soph.; so αὔθαιμος, ον, Id.
self-chosen, self-elected, Xen.
by free choice, of oneself, Eur.: independent, Thuc.
of things taken upon oneself, self-incurred, voluntary, Soph., Thuc., etc.
one who calls each thing by its name, Arist.
to have full power over, τινός NTest.

entry.etym: The part -έντης is of uncertain deriv.
entry.sense: one who does anything with his own hand, an actual murderer, Hdt., Eur., etc.:—more loosely, one of a murderer's family, Id.
an absolute master, autocrat, Id.
as adj., αὐθέντης φόνος, αὐθένται θάνατοι murder by one of the same family, Aesch.
made or done on the very day, Aeschin.
adv. αὐθημερόν (oxyt.), on the very day, on the same day, immediately, Aesch., etc.; ionic αὐτημερόν, Hdt.
born on the spot, born in the country, native, Lat. indigena, Hdt.; αὐτ. ποταμοί rivers that rise in the country, Id.; ὕδωρ αὐτ. a natural spring, Id.:— genuine, sincere, Eur.
on the spot, here, there, Hom.; αὖθι ἔχειν to keep him there, as he is, Od.
of Time, forthwith, straightway, Il.
a lengthd. form of αὖ:
of place back, back again, Il.; ἂψ αὖτις Id.; this sense rare in attic
of Time, again, afresh, anew, Hom., attic; strengthd., ὕστερον αὖτις, ἔτ’ αὖτις, πάλιν αὖτις Il., etc.; βοᾶν αὖθις to cry encore! Xen.
of future Time, again, hereafter, Il., Aesch.
of Sequence, moreover, in turn, on the other hand, Id., Soph.
epith. of the Trojans in Il., either
（α copul. , ἰαχή) loud-shouting, noisy, or,
(from α privat. ) noiseless, silent.
tracing furrows, Anth.
a furrow made in ploughing, Lat. sulcus, Hom., etc.; αὔλακ’ ἐλαύνειν to draw a furrow, Hes.
metaph. of a wife as the bearer of children, Soph., Eur.
metaph. also, a furrow in the skin, a gash, wound, Aesch., Eur.
= ὄγμος, a swathe, Theocr. (Prob. from same Root as ὁλκός, Lat. sulcus, from ἕλκω.）
of or belonging to the αὐλή or court, ἐπ’ αὐλείηισι θύρηισι at the door of the court, i. e. the outer door, house- door, Od.; so in Hdt. and attic
to play on the flute, Hdt., Plat., etc.; αὐλ. ἔξοδον to play a finale, Ar.
Pass., of tunes, to be played on the flute, Xen.; but, αὐλεῖται μέλαθρον is filled with music, Eur.
in Pass. also of persons, to be played to, hear music, Xen.
a piece of music for the flute, Ar., Plat.

entry.etym: prob. from ἄημι (ἄϝημι) to blow, for the αὐλή was open to the air
entry.sense: in Hom. the court-yard, surrounded with out-buildings, and having the altar of Ζεὺς Ἑρκεῖος in the middle, so that it was at once the meeting-place of the family, and the cattle-yard, Il.: it had two doors, viz. the house-door (cf. αὔλειος), and another leading through the αἴθουσα into the πρόδομος, Od.
the wall of the court-yard, Il.

after Hom., the αὐλή was the court or quadrangle, round which the house itself was built, having a corridor (περιστύλιον), from which were doors leading into the men's apartments; opposite the house-door (cf. αὔλειος) was the μέσαυλος or μέταυλος (q.v.), leading into the women's part of the house, Hdt., attic
generally, any court or hall, Hom., Trag.
flute-playing, Plat.
a flute-player, Lat. tibicen, Theogn., Hdt., etc.
of or for the flute, Plat.; ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη) flute-playing, Id.
a flute-girl, Lat. tibicina, Ar., Xen., etc.
Αὐλιάδες Νύμφαι Nymphs protecting cattlefolds, Anth.
to lie in the court-yard, of cattle, Od.; to pass the night, lodge, Eur.; of soldiers, to bivouac, Hdt.
a country house, cottage, Hhymn.: a fold, stable, Eur., Xen.
a chamber, cave, grotto, Soph.
of or for farm-yards, rustic, Eur.
Dim. of αὐλός, a small reed, pipe, Theogn.
a place for passing the night in, a tent, roosting-place, Hom., Eur.
a house-mate, Theocr.
a flute-case, Anth.
to make flutes or pipes, Anth.
sc. τέχνη, flute-making, Plat.
a flute-maker, Plat.

a flute or rather clarionet (for it was played by a mouthpiece, γλωσσίς, Aeschin.), Il., etc.; αὐλοὶ ἀνδρήϊοι and γυναικήϊοι, Lat. tibiae dextrae and sinistrae, bass and treble, Hdt.; sometimes one person played two αὐλοί at once, Theocr.; αὐλὸς Ἐνυαλίου, i. e. a trumpet, Anth.:— ὑπ’ αὐλοῦ to the sound of the flute, Hdt.; so, πρὸς αὐλόν, ὑπὸ τὸν αὐλόν Xen.

any tube or pipe, as the socket of a spear-head, the groove into which the tongue of a buckle fitted, Hom.; the pipe of bellows, Thuc.:— αὐλὸς παχύς, in Od., seems to mean a jet of blood through the tube of the nostril.
a hollow way, defile, glen, Hhymn., Hdt., Ar.
a canal, aqueduct, trench, Hdt.
a channel, strait, Aesch.; αὐλῶνες πόντιοι the sea straits, i. e. the Archipelago, Soph.
of a helmet, with a tube in front, to hold the λόφος, Il.
to make large, increase, augment, Hdt., etc. (Hom. only uses ἀέξω).
to increase in power, strengthen, exalt, aggrandise, Hdt., attic: also to promote to honour, glorify, magnify, Trag., Plat.
Pass. to grow, wax, increase, Hes., Hdt., etc.; αὐξ. ἐς πλῆθος, ἐς ὕψος Id.; of a child, to grow up, Id.; ηὐξανόμην I grew taller, Ar.; so with an adj., αὐξάνεσθαι μέγας to wax great, Eur. Hence
= αὔξησις, Plat.
the Goddess of growth, Hdt.
growth, increase, Thuc.; of crops, Hdt.
promoting growth, Xen.
the waxing moon, Anth.
dryness, withering, Aesch.
dry, of timber, Od.: dried, of fruit, Hdt.: withered, of leaves, Ar.:—neut. as adv., αὖον ἀϋτεῖν or αὔειν to ring dry and harsh, of metal, Il.
dried up, exhausted, Theocr.
sleeplessness, Plat.
sleepless, wakeful, of persons, Od., attic: metaph. sleepless, never-resting, πηδάλια Aesch.; κρῆναι Soph.
of sleepless nights, Hom.
ὕπνος ἄϋπνος a sleep that is no sleep, from which one easily awakes, Soph.
air in motion, a breeze, esp. a cool breeze, the fresh air of morning, Lat. aura, Od., Hdt., attic Poets; rare in Prose:—metaph. steam, Ar.
metaph. also, of changeful events, Eur., Ar.; of anything thrilling, Eur.
to-morrow, Lat. cras, Hom., etc.; ἐς αὔριον on the morrow or till morning, Id.
as Subst., the morrow, Il.; in attic, ἡ αὔριον (sc. ἡμέρα) the morrow, Eur.; ἡ αὔρ. ἡμέρα Xen.; ἡ ἐς αὔρ. ἡμέρα Soph.; ὁ αὔριον χρόνος Eur.
sunburnt, squalid, Lat. siccus, Od., Hes.
making the tongue dry and rough, harsh, rough, bitter, Plat.:—metaph. austere, harsh, Id., NTest.
harshness, roughness, οἴνου Xen.: metaph. austerity, harshness, Plat.
carrying one's own message, bringing news of what oneself has seen, Soph., Thuc.; c. gen. rei, λόγων αὐτ. Soph.
self-chosen, left to one's choice, Od., Hhymn.
related as brother or sister, Aesch., Soph.
as Subst. one's own brother or sister, Id.
together with the men, men and all, Polyb.
an own cousin, cousin-german, Aesch., Eur.
sufficiency in oneself, independence, Plat.

sufficient in oneself, having enough, independent of others, Hdt., Plat.; νηδὺς αὐτάρκης acting of itself, Aesch.; χώρα αὐτ. a country that supplies itself, independent of imports, Thuc.; αὐτ. πρός τι strong enough for a thing, Id., Xen.; c. inf. able of oneself to do a thing, Dem.; αὐτ. βοή a sufficient, vigorous shout, Soph.
in one's own power; τὸ αὐτεξούσιον free power, Babr.
offering of oneself, of free will, Hdt., Eur., Thuc., etc.

entry.etym: αὖ, τε, — ωηερε τε is otiose, as in ὅστε
entry.sense: again, Il.
to mark Sequence, again, furthermore, next, Id., Soph.
on the other hand, on the contrary, following μέν like δέ, Hom., attic Poets.
of the same surname with, τινος Eur.
one who rows himself, i. e. rower and soldier at once, Thuc.
to cry, shout, Il., Aesch.:—c. acc. cogn., βοὰν ἀϋτῶ Eur.; ἀϋτεῖ δ’ ὀξύ Aesch.
c. acc. pers. to call to, Il., Eur.:—c. acc. pers. et inf., Eur.
one who has himself heard, an ear-witness, Thuc., Plat.
= αὐθημερόν, on the self-same day, Il.
a cry, shout, esp. battle-shout, war-cry, Hom.: generally a sound, Aesch.

forthwith, straightway, at once, Hom., etc.; which notion is strengthened in αὐτίκα νῦν, μάλ’ αὐτίκα Od.; c. partic., αὐτίκ’ ἰόντι immediately on his going, Id.; so, αὐτίκα γενόμενος as soon as born, Hdt.; αὐτίκα καὶ μετέπειτα now and hereafter, Od.; so, τὸ αὐτίκα and τὸ μέλλον, Thuc.:—with a Subst., τὴν αὐτίχ’ ἡμέραν Soph.; ὁ αὐτίκα φόβος momentary fear, Thuc.
also in a slightly future sense, presently, Lat. mox, Soph., etc.
for example, to begin with, Ar., Plat., etc.; αὐτίκα δὴ μάλα Dem.
breath, Il.; ἀϋτμὴ Ἡφαίστοιο the fiery breath of Hephaestus, Id.; πυρὸς ἀϋτμή Od.; of bellows, Il.; of wind, Od.
odour, scent, fragrance, Hom.
the ideal man, the form of man, Arist.
by a mere shout, at the first shout, αὐτ. ἑλεῖν to take without a blow, Thuc.
self-willing, self-purposing, Aesch.
self-produced: αὐτογέννητα κοιμήματα μητρός a mother's intercourse with her own child, Soph.
to act of one's own judgment, Xen. From
on one's own judgment, at one's own discretion, Arist.: adv. -όνως, Plut.
self-determined, self-willed, Soph.
of a plough, having the share-beam of one piece with the pole, Hes.
self-taught, unpremeditated, Soph.
self-slain or mutually slain, Aesch.
with the very teeth, ὁ αὐτοδὰξ τρόπος your ferocious temper, Ar.
just ten, Thuc.
self-evident, Aesch.
self-taught, Od., Aesch.
with independent jurisdiction, with one's own law-courts, Thuc.

entry.etym: It seems to be lengthd. from αὐτός, as μαψίδιος from μάψ, μινυνθάδιος from μίνυνθα.
entry.sense: straightway, Od.
το αὐτ. the ideal or form of each object, Arist.
a murderer, Soph.
in the same year, Theocr.
in or of the same year: adv. αὐτόετες, in the same year, within the year, Od.
Thais herself, Luc.
voluntarily, Anth.
of one's own will, Anth.

of Place, from the very spot, Lat. illinc, Hom., attic; αὐτ. ἐξ ἕδρης straight from his seat, without rising, Il.; αὐτ. ἐκ Σαλαμῖνος Hdt., etc.; αὐτόθεν from where thou standest, Soph.; αὐτ. βιοτεύειν to find a living from the place, Thuc.:— οἱ αὐτ. the natives, Id.
of Time, on the spot, at once, Lat. illico, Il., Hdt., attic
Adv. for αὐτοῦ, on the spot, Il., Hdt., attic
wrought or done carelessly, slovenly, random, Arist.:—adv. -λως, Id.
an own sister, Od., Eur.
an own brother, Il., etc.
self-condemned, NTest.
going one's own road, Anth.
self-bidden, i. e. unbidden, of one's own accord, Xen., Anth.
= αὐτοκέλευστος, Hdt.
branches and all, Luc.
self-called, i. e. uncalled, unbidden, Aesch., Soph.
with natural hair, shaggy, Ar.
hair or leaves and all, Luc.
ruling by oneself, absolute, autocratic, Eur., Plat.
of or for an autocrat: adv. -κῶς, despotically, Plut.
one's own master:
of persons or states, free and independent, Lat. sui juris, Thuc., Xen.
of ambassadors, possessing full powers, plenipotentiary, Ar., Thuc., etc.
of rulers, absolute, arbitrary, despotic, Id., etc.
of reasoning, peremptory, Id.
c. gen. complete master of, ἑαυτοῦ Id.; τῆς ἐπιορκίας αὐτ. at liberty to swear falsely, Dem.
self-produced, i. e. natural, ἄντρα Aesch.
to slay one another, Soph.
self-slaying; Adv. -νως, with one's own hand, Aesch.:—so χεὶρ αὐτ., of Medea, who slew her own children, Eur.
slaying one another, Aesch.; θάνατος αὐτ. death by each other's hand, Id.
one who steers himself, Anth.
together with the hilt, up to the hilt, Aesch.
one who carries his own oil-flask, a shabby fellow, Dem.
having learnt of oneself, self- taught, Anth.
oneself the witness, an eyewitness, Aesch.
to act of oneself, act unadvisedly, Xen.
of persons, acting of one's own will, of oneself, Il., etc.
of things, self-moving, self-acting, spontaneous, of the gates of Olympus, the tripods of Hephaestus, Il.:—of plants, growing of themselves, Hdt.
without apparent cause, accidental, Id.; αὐτ. θάνατος a natural death, Dem.
αὐτόματον, ου, τό, mere chance, ἀπὸ τοῦ αὐτομάτου or ἀπὸ ταὐτομάτου, Lat. sponte, by chance, naturally, Hdt., Thuc.
adv. -τως = ἀπὸ ταὐτομάτου, Hdt.
self-ruler, name of Achilles' charioteer, Il.
Melinna herself, Anth.
to desert, Hdt., attic; αὐτ. πρὸς τοὺς Πέρσας Hdt.; ἐς Ἀθήνας ἐκ Περσέων Id.
desertion, Thuc.
going of oneself, without bidding: as Subst. a deserter, Hdt., attic
Dep. to live by one's own laws, be independent, Thuc., Dem.
freedom to use one's own laws, independence, Thuc., etc.
living under one's own laws, independent, Hdt., attic
generally, of one's own free will, Soph.
of animals, feeding and ranging at will, Anth.
self-willed, Aesch.
that very night, Il.
of mere wood, Soph.
self-joined, self-built, Anth.
one's own feeling or experience, Polyb.
speaking from one's own feeling or experience:— adv. -θως, Polyb.
an own child, Soph.
for one's own woes, Aesch.
self-produced, as the Athenian olive, Soph.
free as a state, independent, Thuc.
citizen of a free state, Xen.
self-wrought, Anth.
on one's own feet, Luc.
