laurel-bearing, δ. κλῶνες laurel branches borne in worship of Apollo, Eur.
belonging to a laurel, Anth.
delighting in laurel, Anth.
laurel-crowned, Anth.
like laurel: laurelled, Eur.

of savage animals, blood-red, tawny, δαφοινὸν δέρμα λέοντος Il.; δράκων ἐπὶ νῶτα δαφοινός Id.: the form δαφοινεός bears the same sense, εἷμα δαφοινεὸν αἵματι red with blood, Id.; δαφοινὸς ἀετός Aesch., etc.
metaph. savage, cruel, Hhymn., Aesch.
abundant, plentiful, Hdt.:— adv. -έως, in abundance, Theocr.
of persons, liberal, profuse, Plut.:—Sup. adv., δαψιλέστατα ζῆν Xen.
an old Root, δα to learn, Lat. disco, which becomes Causal, to teach, Lat. doceo, in redupl. aor2 δέδαε and in διδάσκω:

to learn, and in perf., to know; c. gen. pers. to learn from one, Od.; c. gen. rei, to hear tidings of a thing, Il. From δέδαα again is formed a pres. mid. inf. δεδάασθαι, to search out, c. acc., Od.—The pres. in this sense is διδάσκομαι.
Causal, in redupl. aor. 2 δέδαον, c. dupl. acc. to teach a person a thing, Od.; c. inf. to teach one to do a thing, Id.—The pres. in this sense is διδάσκω.
a word of doubtful origin, expl. by ἐδόκει, ἀεικέλιος δέατ’ εἶναι he seemed, methought he was, a pitiful fellow, Od.:
to greet, Od.
irreg. partic. of δέχομαι (Ionic δέχομαι), in act. sense, waiting, lying in wait, Il., Hes.;—not to be confounded with attic δεδόκημαι from δοκέω.
resolved form of δῆλος, Il.
an entreaty, Ar.
an entreating, asking: a prayer, entreaty, Dem., NTest.
suppliant, Plut.
a sample, pattern, proof, specimen, Lat. documentum, Eur., Ar., etc.; δείγματος ἕνεκα by way of sample, Dem.
a place in the Peiraeeus, where merchants set out their wares for sale, a bazaar, Xen., Dem.
to make a show of, NTest.
fearful, cowardly, Il.

entry.etym: Dep., only in pres. and imperf.
entry.sense: to meet with outstretched hand, to greet, welcome, δεξιτερῆι δειδίσκετο χειρί Od.; δέπαϊ δειδίσκετο pledged him in a cup, Id.; also, δεδισκόμενος Id.
= δείκνυμι 1, to show, Hhymn.

Dep.:—Causal of δείδω, to frighten, alarm, μὴ δειδίσσεο λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν Il.; Ἕκτορα ἀπὸ νεκροῦ δειδίξασθαι to scare him from the corpse, Id.; οὔ σε ἔοικε δειδίσσεσθαι it beseems not to attempt to frighten thee, Id.:—c. inf., φευγέμεν δειδίσσετο Theocr.:—in attic form, Plat., Dem.

entry.etym: pres. δείδω only in first pers., δέδοικα or δέδια being always used as pres. in attic.
entry.sense: to fear, absol., Hom., etc.; foll. by a prep., δ. περί τινι to be alarmed, anxious about . . , Il., attic; ἀμφί τινι, περί τινος, ὑπέρ τινος Id.:—followed by a relat. clause with μή . . , Lat. vereor ne . . , I fear it is . . , followed by subj.; rarely by ind., δείδω μὴ νημερτέα εἶπεν Od.; δ. μὴ οὐ . . , Lat. vereor ut . . , I fear it is not . . , foll. by subj., Hdt., etc.
c. inf. to fear to do, Il., Thuc.
c. acc. to fear, dread, Hom., etc.
τὸ δεδιός, one's fearing, = δέος, Thuc.
to wait till evening, σὺ δ’ ἔρχεο δειελιήσας Od.
at evening, Theocr.
of or belonging to evening, δείελον ἦμαρ eventide, Od., Theocr.
as Subst. (sub. χρόνος), late evening, εἰσόκεν ἔλθηι δείελος Il.
to point out, shew, in ionic imperf. δεικανάασκεν Theocr.
Hom. uses it only in Mid. = δειδίσκομαι, to salute, greet, δεικανόωντ’ ἐπέεσσιν Od.; δεικανόωντο δέπασσι pledged him, Il.
Lacon. for ὑποκριτής, Lat. mimus, a burlesque actor, Plut.
a representation, exhibition, Hdt.
to bring to light, display, exhibit, Od., etc.:—Mid. to set before one, Il.
to shew, point out, Id., Soph.:—absol., αὐτὸ δείξει experiment will shew, Plat.; so, δείξει alone, Ar.
to point out by words, to tell, explain, teach, Lat. indicare, ὁδόν Od., etc.:— to shew, prove, with part., ἔδειξαν ἕτοιμοι ὄντες shewed that they were ready, Thuc.
of accusers, to inform against, τινά Ar.
to offer, proffer, τὰ πιστά Aesch.: to cause, πήματα Id.

in Mid., like δειδίσκομαι, δεξιόομαι, to welcome, greet, τὼ καὶ δεικνύμενος προσέφη Hom.: —so also in perf. and plup. pass., δείδεκτ’ Ἀχιλῆα he pledged him, drank to him, Il.; τοὺς μὲν κυπέλλοις δειδέχατο Id.; δειδέχαται μύθοισι Od.
to be shown, Xen.
δεικτέον μοι it is my duty to show, Dem.
to be a coward or cowardly, Arist.
lengthd. form of δειλός, wretched, sorry, paltry, mostly of persons, Trag.; also, δ. χάρις a sorry kindness, Aesch.; δ. σποδός paltry dust, Soph., etc. [Penult. is often made short in attic Poets.]
a coward: commonly with a coaxing sense, poor fellow! Ar.
very pitiable, Ar.
afternoon, ἔσσεται ἢ ἠὼς ἢ δείλη ἢ μέσον ἦμαρ Il.; divided into early and late (πρωΐα and ὀψία), περὶ δείλην πρωΐην, or δείλης ὀψίης Hdt.; τῆς δείλης in the course of the afternoon, Xen.
the late afternoon, evening, Id.
cowardice, Hdt., Soph.; δειλίην ὀφλεῖν to be charged with cowardice, Hdt.
fright, faintheartedness, Plut.
to be afraid.
Dep. to verge towards afternoon, δείλετό τ’ ἠέλιος Od.
of persons, cowardly, craven, Il.; hence, vile, worthless, Id.:— δειλός τινος afraid of . . , Anth.
miserable, luckless, wretched, Hom.; with a compassionate sense, like Lat. miser, δειλοὶ βροτοί poor mortals! ἆ δειλέ poor wretch! ἆ δειλοί poor wretches! Id.
of things, miserable, wretched, Hes., Soph.
to be afraid, in a fright, Hhymn., Hdt., etc.
c. acc. to fear a thing, Id., Aesch.
timid, Mosch.
horrible, fearful, Batr., Theogn.
fear, affright, Il., Hdt., attic
an object of fear, a terror, horror, ὦ πῦρ σὺ καὶ πᾶν δ. Soph.: esp. in pl., δειμάτων ἄχη fearful plagues or monsters, Aesch.; δείματα θηρῶν Eur.
frightened, scared, Anth.
to frighten, Hdt., Ar.:— Pass. to be frightened, Aesch., Eur.
fear, terror:— personified Δεῖμος, Il.
contr. for δέον neut. part., v. δεῖ 111.
such an one, a certain one, whom one cannot or will not name, ὁ δεῖνα Ar., etc.; ὁ δεῖνα τοῦ δεῖνος τὸν δεῖνα εἰσαγγέλλει Dem.
δεῖνα in Com. as an interjection, Lat. malum! plague on't! Ar.
a knave, Mosch.
Dep. to complain loudly, Hdt.
to complain loudly of sufferings, Dem.
terrible of foot, Ἀρὰ δ. (as if she was a hound upon the track), Soph.

entry.etym: from δέος, properly δεεινός, cf. ἐλεεινός, ἐλεινός, from ἔλεος
entry.sense: fearful, terrible, dread, dire, Hom., etc.; δεινὸν ἀϋτεῖν, βροντᾶν to shout, thunder terribly, Il.; δεινὸν δέρκεσθαι, παπταίνειν, ἰδεῖν to look terrible, Hom.; but, δεινὸς ἰδέσθαι fearful to behold, Od.; δεινὸς μὲν ὁρᾶν, δεινὸς δὲ κλύειν Soph.:— τὸ δεινόν danger, suffering, awe, terror, Hdt., Aesch., etc.; so, τὰ δεινά Soph., etc.:— οὐδὲν δεινοί, μὴ ἀποστέωσιν no fear of their revolting, Hdt.:— δεινὸν ποιεῖσθαι to take ill, complain of, be indignant at a thing, Lat. aegre ferre, Id., etc.; δεινὰ παθεῖν to suffer dreadful, illegal, arbitrary treatment, attic; so in adv., δεινῶς φέρειν Hdt.; δ. ἔχειν to be in straits, Xen.
with a notion of Force or Power, mighty, powerful, δεινὸν σάκος the mighty shield, Il.

simply, wondrous, marvellous, strange, τὸ συγγενές τοι δεινόν kin has a strange power, Aesch.; δ. ἵμερος, ἔρως, δέος Hdt.; δεινὸν ἂν εἴη, εἰ . . , it were strange that . . , Eur.:—adv. -νῶς, marvellously, exceedingly, δ. μέλας, ἄνυδρος Hdt.

the sense of powerful, wondrous passed into that of able, clever, skilful, Id., attic; esp. of practical ability, opp. to σοφός, Plat.: c. inf., δεινὸς εὑρεῖν clever at inventing, Aesch.; δεινὸς λέγειν Soph.; δεινὸς πράγμασι χρῆσθαι Dem.: also c. acc., δεινὸς τὴν τέχνην Plat.; δ. περί τι or τινος Id.
terribleness, Thuc.: harshness, sternness, severity, νόμων Id.
natural ability, cleverness, shrewdness, Dem.; esp. in an orator, Thuc., Dem.
to make terrible: to exaggerate, Thuc.
exaggeration, Plat.
fierce-eyed, of the Erinyes, Soph.
to make a meal, Hom.: in attic to take the chief meal, to dine, δ. τὸ ἄριστον to make breakfast serve as dinner, Xen.
c. acc., δ. ἄρτον to make a meal on bread, Hes.; also, δ. ἀπό τινος Ar.
meal-time, Od.
a dining-room, Plut.
of or for cookery: adv. -κῶς, like a cook, artistically, Ar.
to entertain at dinner, Od., Hdt.
fishing for invitations to dinner, parasitic, Hes.

in Hom. the principal meal of the day, —sometimes the noonday meal, sometimes = ἄριστον, the morning meal, sometimes = δόρπον, the evening meal. In old attic the midday or afternoon meal, dinner or supper:— ἀπὸ δείπνου straightway after the meal, Il.; καλεῖν ἐπὶ δεῖπνον; δ. παραθεῖναι, etc.
generally, fodder, provender, Il., Aesch.
to give a dinner:— Mid. to dine, Thuc., Xen.
carrying meat-offerings, Plut.

c. acc. pers. et inf., δεῖ τινὰ ποιῆσαι it is binding on one to do a thing, one must, one ought, Lat. oportet, Hom., etc.:—rarely, δεῖ σε ὅπως δείξεις = δεῖ σε δεῖξαι, Soph.: —rarely also c. dat. pers. et inf., there is need for one to do, δεῖ τινὶ ποιήσαι Eur., Xen.
c. acc. rei et inf., δεῖ τι γενέσθαι Thuc., etc.:—for the phrase οἴομαι δεῖν, v. οἴομαι:— when used absol., an inf. may be supplied, μὴ πεῖθ’ ἃ μὴ δεῖ (sc. πείθειν) Soph., etc.

(from δέω2, to want), c. gen. rei, there is need of, there is wanting, Lat. opus est re, οὐδὲν δεῖ τινός Hdt., attic:—phrases, πολλοῦ δεῖ there wants much, far from it; ὀλίγου δεῖ there wants little, all but:— in answers, πολλοῦ γε δεῖ, πολλοῦ γε καὶ δεῖ far from it, Ar., Dem.; πλεῦνος δεῖ it is still further from it, Hdt:— ὀλίγου δεῖν absol., in same sense, Plat.; μικροῦ δεῖν Dem.
with a dat. pers. added, δεῖ μοί τινος, Lat. opus est mihi re, Aesch., Thuc., etc.
with acc. pers. added, δεῖ σε προμηθέως Aesch.

neut. part. δέον, contr. δεῖν, absol., like ἐξόν, παρόν it being needful, quum oporteret, Plat.; οὐκ ἀπήντα, δέον, he did not appear in court, though he ought to have done so, Dem.; so, οὐδὲν δέον there being no need, Hdt.
for δέον, τό, as Subst., v. sub voce.
the ridge of a chain of hills, Hom., Soph.:—in pl., Id., Eur.
heavy on the neck, Anth.

entry.etym: note that we get δέρη not δέρα, even in attic.
entry.sense: the neck, throat, Il., Hdt.; attic Trag.
to cut the throat of a person, behead, σὺ δ’ ἄμφω δειροτομήσεις Hom.
fearing man, Aesch.
fear of the gods, religious feeling, Polyb.: in bad sense, superstition, Theophr.
fearing the gods:
in good sense, like εὐσεβής, pious, religious, Xen.
in bad sense, superstitious, bigoted, Theophr.—comp. -έστερος, somewhat superstitious, NTest.
worth ten oxen, τὸ δεκάβοιον a coin attributed to Theseus, Plut.
the tenth generation, Luc.
the government of the ten, Isocr.
a commander of ten, Lat. decurio, Xen.
one of a decury, Xen.
ten palms long or broad, Hes.
ten-yearly, Plat.
ten years old, Hdt.
of or lasting ten years, πόλεμος Thuc.
to bribe or corrupt judges, Isocr., Aeschin.:—Pass. to be bribed, Plut.
ten-times, Il.
holding ten dinner-couches, Xen.
the tenth, i.e. overwhelming, wave, Lat. fluctus decumanus, Luc.: cf. τρικυμία.
ten months old, Xen.
in the tenth month, Hdt.
weighing or worth ten minae, Ar.
holding ten ἀμφορεῖς (about 90 gallons), Eur.
very long ago, like δωδεκάπαλαι, Ar.
ten cubits long, Hdt.
tenfold, Lat. decuplus, Plat.:— ἡ δεκαπλασία (sc. τιμή) a fine of ten times the amount, Dem.
enclosing ten πλέθρα, Thuc.
a ten-city land, Decapolis, NTest.

entry.etym: Some connect it with δάκτυλος, from the number of the fingers.
entry.sense: ten, Lat. decem, Hom., etc.: —οἱ δέκα the Ten, Oratt.: οἱ δέκα [ἔτη] ἀφ’ ἥβης those who are ten years past 20 (the age of military service), Xen.
the government of ten, Xen.
bribery, Plut.
a lapse of ten seed-times, i. e. ten years, Eur.
a decad: a company of ten, Lat. decuria, Il., Hdt.
a bribed company of ten.
the number ten, Arist.
on the tenth day, Plat.
ten days old, Luc.
worth ten talents: δίκη δεκ. an action in which the damages were laid at ten talents, Aeschin.
the tenths-office, custom-house, Xen.

to exact the tenth part from a man, to make him pay tithe, τούτους δεκατεῦσαι τῶι θεῶι to make them pay a tithe to the god, Hdt.:— also of things, δ. τὰ ἐξ ἀγροῦ ὡραῖα to tithe them (as an offering), Xen.: and so, Pass., δεκατευθῆναι τῶι Διΐ Hdt.: hence proverb., ἐλπὶς ἦν δεκατευθῆναι τὰς Θήβας, i. e. that it would be made to pay tithe, Xen.
a tithe-collector, Dem.
v. δέκατος II.
in the tenth generation, Anth.
tenth, Hom., etc.
δεκάτη, sc. μερίς the tenth part, tithe, Hdt., etc.
δεκάτη (sc. ἡμέρα), the tenth day, Hom.; at Athens, the tenth day after birth, when the child has a name given it, τὴν δ. θύειν to give a naming-day feast, Ar.; τὴν δ. ἑστιᾶσαι ὑπὲρ τοῦ υἱοῦ Dem.
like δεκατεύω, to take tithe of a person, τινα NTest.: Pass. to pay tithe, Id.
consisting of ten tribes, Hdt.
the denarius, = ten χαλκοῖ, Plut.
ten thousand, Il.; cf. ἐννεάχιλοι.
from Deceleia, Id.
Deceleia , a place in Attica, Hdt., Thuc.
a Decelean, Id.
lasting ten years, Soph., Plat.
ten years old, Eur.: fem. δεκέτις, ιδος, Plat.
to be received, Luc.
a receiver: a beggar, Od.
acceptable, NTest.
one who takes upon himself or on his own head, αἵματος δ. νέου Aesch.
ten fathoms long, Xen.
to entice or catch by a bait: — Pass., Xen., Dem.
c. acc. cogn., νῶτον ὑὸς περὶ ἄγκιστρον δ. to put it on the hook as a bait, Hdt.
snapping at the bait, Anth.
a bait, Xen.: metaph., δ. τινος bait for a person, Eur.
indecl., fourth letter of the Gr. alph.: as numeral, δʹ = τέσσαρες and τέταρτος, but ͵δ = 4000.
δ is the medial dental mute, between the tenuis τ and the aspirate θ.
changes of δ in the dialects:
aeolic into β, as σάμβαλον for σάνδαλον:— reversely, ὀβελός becomes ὀδελός in doric
aeolic or doric into ζ, or ζ into δ and σδ, v. ζῆτα II. 2
into θ, as ψεῦδος ψύθος.
into λ, as δαήρ, Lat. levir, δάκρυ lacryma, δασύς λάσιος.
into σ, as ὀδμή ὀσμή, ἴδμεν ἴσμεν.
sometimes δ is inserted to give a fuller sound, (ἀνήρ) ἀνέρος ἀνδρός.
δ is sometimes lost, cf. διωγμός, δίωξις with ἰωκή.
it sometimes represents j. (y), as in ἤδη or δή, Lat. jam.
anything shaped like a Δ, a name for islands formed by the mouths of large rivers, as the Nile, Hdt.
writing on a tablet, recording, Aesch.
a writing-tablet, from the letter Δ (the old shape of tablets), Hdt., Trag.: metaph., δέλτοις φρενῶν on the tablets of the heart, Aesch.
Pass. to grow up to pighood, Ar.
a young pig, porker, Hdt., etc.
Delphic, Aesch.
a temple of Apollo at Athens, τὸ ἐπὶ Δελφινίωι δικαστήριον the law-court there, Plut.
a tripod, Plut.
the dolphin, Hom., etc.

a mass of lead, prob. shaped like a dolphin, hung at the yard-arm, and suddenly let down on the decks of the enemy's ships, Ar.:—hence, κεραῖαι δελφινοφόροι beams with pulleys to let down the δελφίς, Thuc.
Delphi, a famous oracle of Apollo in Phocis at the foot of Parnassus (called Pytho by Hom. and Hdt.), Hhymn., Soph.
the Delphians, Hdt.
king of Delphi, Aesch.
the womb, Arist.

the frame of man, the body, Hom.; rarely of other animals, Od.; properly the living body. — Hom. uses it only in acc. sg., absol., μικρὸς δέμας small in stature; ἄριστος δέμας, δέμας ἀθανάτοισι ἔοικε, etc.
in Trag. as a periphrasis, like κάρα, κτανεῖν μητρῷον δ. Aesch.; Ἡράκλειον δ. Eur.; Δαματρὸς ἀκτᾶς δ., i. e. bread, Id.
as adv., δέμας πυρὸς αἰθομένοιο in form or fashion like burning fire, Lat. instar ignis, Il.
mostly in pl. δέμνια, the bedstead or matrass, Hom.
generally, a bed, bedding, Od., etc.
keeping one to one's bed, μοῖρα δ. a lingering fate, Aesch.
to build, Il., etc.:—Mid., ἐδείματο οἴκους he built him houses, Od.:—generally, to construct, δ. ἀλωήν Hhymn.; δ. ὁδόν, ἁμαξιτόν, Lat. munire viam, Hdt.
to turn the eyes or glance quickly, δενδίλλων ἐς ἕκαστον Il.
a tree, mostly in pl., Hom., Hes., Hdt.
woody, Od.
of a tree, Anth.
to climb trees, Anth.
of a woodman, Anth.
grown with wood, Eur., Ar.
to cut down trees, esp. vines and fruit-trees, Xen.; δ. χώραν to waste a country by cutting down the trees, ap. Dem.

entry.etym: for forms such as δενδρέων cf. δένδρεον
entry.sense: a tree, Ar.; δένδρα fruit-trees (opp. to ὕλη timber), Thuc., etc.
blasting trees, Aesch.
to lay waste a country, Thuc.: metaph., δ. τὰ νῶτα Ar.
bearing trees; Sup. -ώτατος, Plut.
planted with trees, Plut.
tree-like: δενδρ. Νύμφαι wood-nymphs, Anth.
fem. adj. wooded, Eur.
to abuse, revile, τινά Theogn., Soph.; c. acc. cogn., κακὰ ῥήματα δεννάζειν to utter words of foul reproach, Id.
a reproach, disgrace, Hdt.

entry.etym: aor1 part. fem. of δέχομαι, with changed accent
entry.sense: a reservoir, tank, cistern, Hdt., Plat.

the right hand, opp. to ἀριστερά, Il.; ἐκ δεξιᾶς on the right, Ar.; ἐν δεξιᾶι ἔχειν τὰ οὔρεα to keep them on the right, as you go, Hdt.; ἐν δ. λαβεῖν τὴν Σικελίαν Id.; so, ἐν δ. ἐσπλέοντι on your right as you sail in, Id.; used in welcoming, δεξιὰν διδόναι to salute by offering the right hand, Ar.

the right hand given as a pledge or assurance, δεξιαὶ ἧις ἐπέπιθμεν Il.; δεξιὰς δόντες καὶ λαβόντες having exchanged assurances, made a treaty, Xen.; δεξιὰς παρὰ βασιλέως φέρειν μή . . to bring pledges that he would not . . , Id.—Though δεξιά is manifestly fem. of δεξιός, it is always used as a Subst. without χείρ; but δ. χείρ occurs in Soph., Eur., Ar.
receiving sheep, i. e. rich in sacrifices, Eur.
a spearman: in pl. guards, NTest.: others δεξιοβόλοι javelin-men.

to greet with the right hand, welcome, greet (cf. δείκνυμι II), c. acc. pers., Ar., Xen.; c. dat. pers., δεξιοῦσθαι θεοῖς to raise one's right hand to the gods, pay honour to them, Aesch.; c. acc. rei, ἄμυστιν δεξιούμενοι pledging one in a bumper, Eur.:—Plat. has aor1 δεξιωθῆναι in pass. sense.
harnessed by a trace on the right side, of a third horse which was outside the regular pair:— hence, generally, spirited, impetuous, Soph.

on the right hand or side, Lat. dexter, opp. to ἀριστερός, Hom., etc.; τὸ δ. (sc. κέρας) the right of an army, Xen.:—adverb. usages, ἐπὶ δεξιά on the right, Il.; ἐπὶ δεξιόφιν (epic gen.) towards the right, Id.; πρὸς δεξιά Hdt.

fortunate, boding good, of the flight of birds, δεξιὸς ὄρνις, = αἴσιος, Hom. —This sense came from the Greek augurs looking to the North, so that lucky omens, which came from the East, were on the right, while the unlucky ones from the West were on the left.
metaph. dexterous, ready, opp. to σκαιός (sinister, French gauche); and of the mind, sharp, shrewd, clever, Ar., Thuc., etc.:—adv., δεξιῶς; Sup. δεξιώτατα, Ar.
dexterity, cleverness, Hdt., Ar.; opp. to ἀμαθία, Thuc.
receiving fire, Eur.
right, the right, Hom.: δεξιτερή, like δεξιά (sub. χείρ), the right hand, Il.; epic dat. δεξιτερῆιφι Id.
a pledge of friendship, Soph.
a greeting, canvassing, Lat. ambitus, Plut.

entry.etym: neut. part. of the impers. δεῖ, made into a Noun
entry.sense: that which is binding, needful, right, proper, Soph., Xen.; τὰ δέοντα things needful or proper, advantages or duties, Thuc., etc.; ἐν δέοντι (sc. καιρῶι), in good time, Lat. opportune, Eur.; ἐν τῶι δέοντι Hdt.; εἰς τὸ δέον for a needful purpose, Id.; hence (at Athens) the phrase for secret service, εἰς τὸ δέον ἀπώλεσα Ar.
fear, alarm, affright, Hom., etc.; τεθνάναι τῶι δέει τινά to be dead afraid of a person, Dem.
awe, reverence, Aesch.
reason for fear, Il.: a means of inspiring fear, Thuc.
a beaker, goblet, chalice, Hom.
enclitic Particle, joined,

to names of Places in the acc., to denote motion towards that place, οἶκόνδε (attic οἴκαδε) home- wards, ἅλαδε sea- wards, Οὐλυμπόνδε to Olympus, θύραζε (for θύρασδε) to the door, Hom.; sometimes repeated with the possess. Pron., ὅνδε δόμονδε; and sometimes even after εἰς, as εἰς ἅλαδε Od.; in Ἀϊδόσδε it follows the gen., = εἰς Ἅιδου (sc. οἶκον). In attic joined to the names of cities, Ἐλευσῖνάδε, Ἀθήναζε, Θήβαζε (for Ἀθήνασδε, Θήβασδε).
sometimes it denotes purpose only, μή τι φόβονδ’ ἀγόρευε speak not aught tending to fear, Il.
-δε is also used to strengthen certain Pronouns, ὅδε, τοιόσδε, etc.

but: conjunctive Particle, with adversative force: it commonly answers to μέν, and may often be rendered by while, whereas, on the other hand, v. μέν:— but μέν is often omitted, δέ being used merely to pass on from one thing to another; ὣς Ἀχιλεὺς θάμβησεν, θάμβησαν δὲ καὶ ἄλλοι Il.; etc.; κινεῖ κραδίην κινεῖ δὲ χόλον Eur.
δέ is often redundant,

to introduce the apodosis, where it may be rendered by then, yet, εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώωσιν, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι if they will not give it, then I will take it, Il.; so at in Lat., si tu oblitus es, at Dii meminerint Catull.
to resume after interruption caused by a parenthesis, where it may be rendered by I say, now, so then, Hdt.
POSITION of δέ: properly second, being often put between the Art. and Subst., the prep. and case.
a collar, Anth.
throttling, Anth.
a necklace, Eur.: a collar, Xen.
a collar, Anth.
a look, glance, Aesch., Eur.

to see clearly, see, Hom.; δεδορκώς having sight, opp. to τυφλός, Soph.:—hence to be alive, living, Hom., Trag.:—like βλέπω with a neut. adj., δεινόν, σμερδαλέον δ. to look terrible, Hom., etc.; c. acc. cogn., πῦρ δεδορκώς flashing fire from the eyes, Od.; Ἄρη δεδορκότων Aesch.; σκότον δεδ. blind, Eur.
c. acc. to look on or at, Hom., Aesch.:—so, δ. εἴς τινα Eur.; κατά τι Aesch.: generally, to perceive, κτύπον δέδορκα Id.
the skin, hide, of beasts, Lat. pellis, Hom., etc.; δέρμα κελαινόν, of a shield, Il.:—also of skins prepared for bags or bottles, Od.; of a man's skin stript off, Il., Hdt.
later, one's skin, Lat. cutis, περὶ τῶι δέρματι δεδοικέναι Ar.: the shell of a tortoise, Id.
of skin, leathern, Od., Hdt.
a leathern covering: in pl. screens of hide, Thuc.: cf. διφθέρα.
the membrane which contains the bowels, Lat. omentum, δέρτρον ἔσω δύνοντες even to the bowels, Od.
to skin, flay, of animals, Hom., etc.:— ἀσκὸν δεδάρθαι to have one's skin flayed off, Solon; so, δερῶ σε θύλακον I will make a purse of your skin, Ar.
also (like the slang words to tan or hide) to cudgel, thrash, Id.
poet. for δεσμός, a bond, fetter, Od.
a head-band, Il.
to fetter, put in chains, Hhymn., Eur.: to tie together, as corn in the sheaf, Hes.
binding: metaph. binding as with a spell, enchaining, c. gen., ὕμνος δ. φρενῶν Aesch.
pass. bound, in bonds, captive, Soph., Eur., etc.
anything for binding, a band, bond, Hom., etc.: a halter, Il.: a mooring-cable, Od.: a door-latch, Id.; a yoke-strap, Xen.
in pl. bonds, fetters, Aesch., Thuc.: in sg., collectively, bonds, imprisonment, Hdt., etc.
a gaoler, Luc.
a bond, fetter, Aesch.
a prison, Hdt., Thuc.
a prisoner, captive, Hdt., attic
as adj. in chains, fettered, Aesch., fem. δεσμῶτις, Soph.
absol. to be lord or master, gain the mastery, Aesch., Plat.
c. gen. to be lord or master of, Hhymn., Hdt., etc.; δεσπόζειν φόβης to own the lock of hair, Aesch.; metaph. to master, δ. λόγου Id.
c. acc. to lord it over, Eur.
the mistress, lady of the house, Lat. hera, of Penelope, Od.
in attic of goddesses, as Artemis, Soph.; Persephone, Plat.
of or belonging to the master or lord, Hhymn., Aesch.; δ. ἀνάγκαι arbitrary rule, Id.
Subst. = δεσπότης, Tyrtae.
the power of a master over slaves, or the relation of master to slaves, Arist.
absolute sway, despotism, Isocr.
c. gen., Plat.:—Pass. to be despotically ruled, Aesch., Eur.

entry.etym: The latter part -πότης is prob. from same Root as πόσις, and Lat. potis, potior: the syll. δεσ- is uncertain.
entry.sense: a master, lord, the master of the house, Lat. herus, dominus, Aesch., etc.; properly in respect of slaves, so that the address of a slave to his master was ὦ δέσποτ’ ἄναξ or ὦναξ δέσποτα Ar.
of Oriental rulers, a despot, absolute ruler, whose subjects are slaves, Hdt., Thuc.; the pl. is used by Poets of single persons, like τύραννοι, Aesch.
of the gods, Eur., Xen.
generally, an owner, master, lord, κώμου, Aesch., Soph.
of or for a master, δεσποτικαὶ συμφοραί misfortunes that befall one's master, Xen.
of persons, inclined to tyranny, despotic, Plat.

entry.etym: properly fem. of δετός, sub. λαμπάς
entry.sense: sticks bound up, a fagot, torch, Il., Ar.
that which is wet, δεύματα κρεῶν boiled flesh, Pind.
of Place, hither, Lat. huc, with Verbs of motion, Hom., etc.; in a pregn. sense with Verbs of Rest, to (have come hither and) be here, πάρεστι δεῦρο Soph.
used in calling to one, here ! on ! come on ! Lat. adesdum, ἄγε δεῦρο, δεῦρ’ ἄγε, δεῦρ’ ἴθι, δεῦρ’ ἴτω always with a Verb sg. (δεῦτε being used with pl.), Hom.; but with a pl. in Trag.
in arguments, μέχρι δ. τοῦ λόγου up to this point of the argument, Plat.
of Time, until now, up to this time, hitherto, Trag., Plat.: also, δεῦρ’ ἀεί Eur.
deeply dyed, ingrained, fast, of colours, Plat., Luc.
the last, Il.
as pl. of δεῦρο, hither! come on! come here! just like δεῦρο, with pl. imperat., δεῦτ’ ἄγετ’ Il.; δεῦτε φίλοι Id.; δεῦτ’ ἄγε, Φαιήκων ἡγήτορες Od.
the actor who takes second-class parts: metaph. one who seconds a speaker, Dem.
on the second day, agreeing with the subject of the Verb, δευτεραῖος ἦν ἐν Σπάρτηι Hdt.; but also, τῆι δευτεραίηι [sc. ἡμέραι] Id.
sc. δευτερεῖα ἆθλα, the second prize in a contest; hence the second place or rank, δ. νέμειν τινί Hdt.
to be second: δευτ. τινί to play second to . . , Plut.
δευτερόπρωτον, σάββατον the first sabbath after the second day of the feast of unleavened bread, or the first sabbath of the second year (i. e. of the year after the sabbatical year), NTest.
second, being comp. of δύο:

in point of Order, of one who comes in second in a race, Il.: in attic with Art., ὁ δεύτερος Soph., etc.; αἱ δεύτεραι φροντίδες second thoughts, Eur.; proverb., τὸν δ. πλοῦν to try the next best way, Plat.

of Time, δευτέρηι ἡμέρηι on the next day, Hdt.: c. gen., ἐμεῖο δεύτερος after my time, Il.; δευτέρωι ἔτεϊ τούτων in the year after this, Hdt.: in neut. as adv., δεύτερον αὖ, δεύτερον αὖτις secondly, next, afterwards, a second time, Hom., attic; in Prose also δεύτερα:— with Art., τὸ δεύτερον Hdt., Aesch., etc.; τὰ δεύτερα Thuc.; ἐκ δευτέρου for the second time, NTest.
in point of Rank, second, δ. μετ’ ἐκεῖνον Hdt.; c. gen., δεύτερος οὐδενός second to none, Id.; ἡγεῖσθαι δεύτερον to think quite secondary, Soph.
the second of two, δευτέρη αὐτή herself with another, Hdt.
as Subst., δεύτερα, τά, = δευτερεῖα, the second prize or place, Il., Hdt.
to wet, drench, Il.:—Mid., πτερὰ δεύεται ἅλμηι wets his wings in the brine, Od.
to mix a dry mass with liquid, so as to make it fit to knead, δ. ἄρτον ὕδατι Xen.
Causal, to make to flow, shed, αἷμα Soph.
to miss, want, ἐδεύησεν ἱκέσθαι he missed, failed in reaching, Od.
as Dep. = attic δέομαι to feel the want or loss of, be without a thing, c. gen., Il.: to stand in need of, βάκτρου Eur.
to be wanting, deficient in a thing, c. gen., Il.: absol. δευόμενος, in need, Id.
c. gen. pers. to be inferior to, Hom.
to soften by working with the hand, Ar.
for ten days, lasting ten days, ἐκεχειρία δεχ. a truce terminable on giving ten days' notice, Thuc.; σπονδαὶ δεχ. Id.

of things as the object, to take, accept, receive what is offered, Lat. accipere, Hom., etc.:— δ. τί τινι to receive something at the hand of another, Il.; also τί τινος Id.; τι παρά τινος Hom.; τι ἔκ τινος Soph.:—but also, δ. τί τινος to receive in exchange for . . , χρυσὸν φίλου ἀνδρὸς ἐδέξατο Od.:—also, μᾶλλον δ., c. inf., to take rather, to choose to do or be, Xen.; and without μᾶλλον, οὐδεὶς ἂν δέξαιτο φεύγειν Thuc.
to accept graciously, Il.; δ. τὸν οἰωνόν to accept, hail the omen, Hdt., etc.:— to accept or approve, τοὺς λόγους, τὴν ξυμμαχίην Id., Thuc.
simply to give ear to, hear, Lat. accipere, Eur., Thuc.
to take or regard as so and so, μηδὲ συμφορὰν δέχου τὸν ἄνδρα Soph.
of persons, to receive hospitably, entertain, Hom., attic
to greet, worship, Il.; δ. τινα ξύμμαχον to accept as an ally, Thuc.
to receive as an enemy, to await the attack of, Lat. excipere, Il.; of a hunter waiting for game or a wild boar waiting for the hunters, Id.; τοὺς πολεμίους δ. Hdt., etc.
to expect, c. acc. et inf. fut., Od.: or c. acc. to wait for, Id.; μηδὲ συμφορὰν δέχου τὸν ἄνδρα do not expect him to be . . , Soph.
absol. to succeed, come next, δέχεται κακὸν ἐκ κακοῦ Il.; ἄλλος δ’ ἐξ ἄλλου δέχεται ἆθλος Hes.; of places, Ἀρτεμίσιον δέκεται Hdt.
to work or knead a thing till it is soft, κηρὸν δεψήσας Od.; δέψει τὸ δέρμα Hdt.
to bind, tie, fetter, δεσμῶι τινα δῆσαι Il., etc.:—c. acc. only, to bind, put in bonds, Od., attic
metaph. to bind, enchain, γλῶσσα δέ οἱ δέδεται Theogn.; ψυχὰ δέδεται λύπηι Eur.
c. gen. to let or stop one from a thing, ἔδησε κελεύθου Od.
Mid. to bind, tie, put on oneself (cf. ὑποδέω), ποσσὶ δ’ ὑπαὶ ἐδήσατο πέδιλα tied them on his feet, Il.; and in Pass., περὶ κνήμηισι κνημῖδας δέδετο he had greaves bound round his legs, Od.

to lack, miss, stand in need of a person or thing, c. gen., Il., Xen.:— πολλοῦ δέω I want much, i. e. am far from, c. inf., πολλοῦ δέω ἀπολογεῖσθαι I am far from defending myself, Plat.; μικροῦ ἔδεον εἶναι Xen.; and absol., πολλοῦ γε δέω far from it, Plat.; τοῦ παντὸς δέω Aesch.; v. δεῖ II:—so in partic., δυοῖν δέοντα τεσσεράκοντα forty lacking two, thirty-eight, Hdt.; ἑνὸς δέον εἰκοστὸν ἔτος the 20th year save one, the 19th, Thuc.
as Dep. δέομαι: fut. δεήσομαι: aor1 ἐδεήθην:
to be in want or need, κάρτα δεόμενος Hdt.:— to stand in need of a person or thing, c. gen., Id., Soph.; οὐδὲν δέομαί τινος I have no need of him, Thuc.: c. inf., τοῦτο ἔτι δέομαι μαθεῖν Plat.

to ask for a thing from a person, c. dupl. gen. rei et pers., Hdt., Thuc.; also, τοῦτο δέομαι ὑμῶν Plat.; and c. acc. cogn., δέημα or δέησιν δεῖσθαί τινος Ar., etc., rarely with gen. pers. only, δεηθεὶς ὑμῶν having begged a favour of you, Dem.:—c. gen. pers. et inf. to beg a person to do, Hdt., Plat.
entry.etym: The aeolic form δεύω (v. δεύω2) shows that the root of this word was ΔΕϜ.

entry.sense: a bite, sting, Xen.: metaph., δ. λύπης Aesch.
the act of biting: in pl. caustics, Plut.
for a long time, Lat. diu, Hom.

a strengthd. form of δή, really, in very truth, τί δὴ ἀνδρωθέντες δῆθεν ποιήσουσι; what then will they do when they are really grown up? Hdt.:— also epexegetic, Lat. videlicet, that is to say, Aesch., Eur.:—ironically, Lat. scilicet, to imply that a statement is not true, οἵ μιν ἠθέλησαν ἀπολέσαι δῆθεν as he pretended, Hdt.; φέροντες ὡς ἄγρην δῆθεν Id.
to tarry, be long, delay, Il.
taken by the enemy, captive, Eur.; contr. δηιάλωτος Aesch.
destroying her spouse, the wife of Hercules, —her name expressing the legend of his death, Soph.
battle-strife, battle, death, Hom.
to cut down, slay, Il.: to cleave asunder, Id.; savage beast, to rend, tear, Id.; τὸν πώγωνα δεδηιωμένος having had his beard cut off, Luc.
to waste or ravage a country, Hdt., Thuc.; ἄστυ δηιώσειν πυρί Soph.
biting, torturing, c. gen., Eur.
a biter, Anth.
able to bite, biting, stinging, Luc.
quite clearly, manifestly, Soph., Eur., etc.:—also iron., προφάσιος τῆσδε δηλαδή on this pretext forsooth, Hdt.:—in answers, yes of course, Ar.

entry.etym: perf. δεδήλημαι both in act. and pass. sense
entry.sense: Dep.: of persons, to hurt, do a mischief to, Hom.; μή με δηλήσεται (epic for -ηται) Od.; so in Hdt.; to hurt by magic potions, Theocr.
of things, to damage, spoil, waste, καρπὸν ἐδηλήσαντ’ Il.; γῆν δηλησάμενος Hdt.:—esp. in phrase, ὅρκια δηλήσασθαι to violate a truce, Il.
absol. to do mischief, be hurtful, Hom.
a mischief, bane, Od., Soph.
baneful, noxious, βροτῶν δηλήμονα baneful to them, Od.; ἀνθρώπων οὐ δηλήμονες doing men no hurt, Hdt.
mischief, ruin, bane, Hdt.
a destroyer, epic Hom.
a Delian woman, Hhymn., Eur.
Δηλιάς, sc. ναῦς the Delian ship, sent from Athens every fourth year in memory of Theseus, Plat.
Delian, Trag., etc.:—ὁ Δ., name of Apollo, Soph., etc.
a Delian, Hdt., etc.
τὰ Δήλια (sc. ἱερά) the quinquennial festival of Apollo at Delos, Thuc.
Delos-born, Simon.
i. e. δῆλόν [ἐστιν] ὅτι, used parenthetically, quite clearly, manifestly, plainly, Plat., etc.
epexegetically, that is to say, namely, Lat. scilicet, Id., Xen.
to make clear, Plut.
properly, visible, conspicuous, Il.

clear to the mind, manifest, evident, Od.: —δῆλός εἰμι with partic., δῆλός ἐστιν ἀλγεινῶς φέρων i. e. it is clear that he takes it ill, Soph.; δῆλοί εἰσι μὴ ἐπιτρέψοντες it is clear that they will not permit, Thuc.; also, acc. to our idiom, δῆλόν [ἐστιν] ὅτι . . , v. δηλονότι.
δῆλον itself is used like δηλαδή, as αὐτὸς πρὸς αὑτοῦ· δῆλον, all by himself, 'tis manifest, Soph.:—also, δῆλον δέ to introduce a proof, Thuc.

entry.etym: Prob. from δῆλος, because of the legend that it became visible by rising from the sea.
entry.sense: Delos, one of the Cyclades, birthplace of Apollo and Artemis, Od.; called also Ὀρτυγία.

entry.etym: Pass., fut. δηλωθήσομαι and in mid. form δηλώσομαι
entry.sense: to make visible or manifest, to show, exhibit, Soph.:—Pass. to be or become manifest, Id.
to make known, disclose, reveal, Aesch., Soph.
to prove, Id., Thuc.
to declare, explain, set forth, indicate, signify, Id.; c. part., δηλώσω σε κακόν [ὄντα] Soph.; the partic., if it refers to the nom. of the Verb, is itself in nom., δηλώσει γεγενημένος Thuc.
intr. to be clear or plain, Hdt., Plat.
impers., δηλοῖ = δῆλόν ἐστι, Hdt.; fut. δηλώσει Plat.; aor1 ἐδήλωσε Xen.
a pointing out, manifestation, explaining, shewing, Thuc.; δ. ποιεῖσθαι = δηλοῦν, Thuc.
to lead the people, in bad sense, Ar.
c. acc. pers. to win by popular arts, Xen.
leadership of the people, Ar.
fit for or like a demagogue, Ar.
a popular leader, of Pericles, Isocr.: commonly in bad sense, a leader of the mob, a demagogue, such as Cleon, Thuc., Xen.
prayed for by the people: as prop. n. of a king of Sparta, Hdt.
to be demarch, Dem.
the office or rank of δήμαρχος, Dem.: the tribunate, Plut.
tribunician, Plut.
a governor of the people:
at Athens, a demarch, the president of a δῆμος, who managed its affairs, Ar., Dem.
at Rome, a tribune of the plebs, Plut.
a friend of the people, Plat.
confiscation of one's property, Plat.
to declare public property, to confiscate, Lat. publicare, Thuc., etc.
generally, to make public, δεδήμευται κράτος the power is in the hands of the people, Eur.
to speak in the assembly, Lat. concionari, Ar., etc.: Pass., τὰ δεδημηγορημένα public speeches, Dem.
to make popular speeches, to speak rhetorically, use clap-trap, Plat., etc.
a speech in the public assembly, Aeschin.
popular oratory, clap-trap, Plat.
of or for public speaking, qualified for it, Xen.: ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη), = δημηγορία, Plat.
a popular orator, mostly in a bad sense, Plat.:— τιμαὶ δ. a speaker's honours, Eur.

entry.etym: The Deriv. from δῆ = γῆ, quasi Γημήτηρ is improbable, v. δᾶ.
entry.sense: Demeter, Lat. Ceres, goddess of agriculture, mother of Persephone, Hom.
to affect popularity, cheat the people, Ar.
abounding in public, κτήνη δ. cattle of which the people have large store, Aesch.
goods sold by public authority: confiscated goods, Ar.
belonging to the people, public, Od.; αἰσυμνῆται δ. judges elected by the people, Id.; neut. pl. as adv., δήμια πίνειν at the public cost, Il.
ὁ δήμιος (sc. δοῦλος), the public executioner, Plat., etc.
to practise a trade, do work, Plat.
c. acc. rei, to work at, fabricate, Id.
to be one of the δημιουργοί (II), Id.
a making, creating, Plat.
workmanship, handicraft, Id.; δ. τῶν τεχνῶν practising them, Id=Plat..
of or for a δημιουργός or handicraftsman, Plat.

one who works for the people, a skilled workman, handicraftsman, Od., etc.; of medical practitioners, Plat.; of sculptors, Id.:—generally, a framer, maker; λόγων Aeschin.; πειθοῦς δημιουργὸς ἡ ῥητορική Plat.: metaph., ὄρθρος δημιοεργός morn that calls man to work, Hhymn.
the Maker of the world, Xen., Plat.
in some Peloponnesian states, the name of a magistrate, Thuc., Dem.
devourer of the people, Il.
an elder of the people, chief, Il.: δημογ. θεός, = Lat. deus minorum gentium, Anth.
at the public cost, Od.
δημόθεν Εὐπυρίδης an Eupyrian by deme, i. e. by birth, place, Anth.
a public feast, Luc.
uttered by the people, Aesch.; δ. ἀναρχία lawlessness of popular clamour, Id.
friend of the people, Lat. poplicola, Plut.
a mob-flatterer, Luc.
to curry mob-favour, Plut.
of or for a demagogue, Plat.
a demagogue.
ratified by the people, Aesch.
Pass. to have a democratical constitution, live in a democracy, Hdt., Ar., Thuc.
democracy, popular government, Hdt., Thuc.
of or for a democracy, Ar., Plat.
of persons, favouring democracy, Plat.
publicly stoned, δ. φόνος death by public stoning, Soph.
Pass. to talk popularly, Pind., Plat.
a mob-monkey, charlatan, Ar.
made a citizen, not one by birth, Plut.
hurled by the people, Aesch.
to imitate Demosthenes, Plut.
to confiscate, like δημεύω, Xen.: Pass., τὰ δεδημοσιευμένα popular sayings, Arist.
intr. to be in the public service, of physicians, Ar., Plat.: generally, to be a public man, opp. to ἰδιωτεύω, Id.
belonging to the people or state, Lat. publicus, opp. to ἴδιος, Hdt., attic:— δημόσιον εἶναι, γίγνεσθαι to be confiscated, Thuc., Plat.
as Subst., ὁ δημόσιος (sc. δοῦλος), a public servant, as the public crier, Hdt.; a public notary, Dem.
as neut., δημόσιον, ου, τό, the state, Lat. respublica, Hdt., attic
any public building, a public hall, Hdt.
the treasury, elsewhere τὸ κοινόν, Dem.
the public prison, Thuc.
τὰ δημόσια (sc. χρήματα) state-property, Ar.
as fem., ἡ δαμοσία (sc. σκηνή) the tent of the Spartan kings, Xen.
as adv.:
dat. δημοσίαι, ionic -ίηι, at the public expense, Hdt.; by public consent, Dem.; δ. τεθνάναι to die by the executioner, Id.
neut. pl. δημόσια, at the public cost, Ar.
to confiscate, like δημοσιεύω, Thuc.
Pass. to be published, Plat.
a farmer of the revenue, Lat. publicanus, Strab.
fat, Il., Ar., etc.; δίπλακι δημῶι (of sacrificial meat) with fat above and fat below, Il.
a country-district, country, land, Hom.

the people of a country, the commons, Lat. plebs, δήμου ἀνήρ, opp. to βασιλεύς, Il., etc.; of a single person, δῆμος ἐών being a commoner, Il.:—in historians, the commons, commonalty, opp. to οἱ εὐδαίμονες, οἱ παχέες, οἱ δυνατοί, Hdt., Thuc.; of soldiers, opp. to officers, Xen.
like πλῆθος, the commons, the democracy, opp. to οἱ ὀλίγοι, Hdt., Ar., etc.
in Attica, δῆμοι, οἱ, townships or hundreds, = doric κῶμαι, Lat. pagi, ancient divisions of the county, being (in the time of Hdt.) 100 in number, 10 in each φυλή.
at the public cost, public, national, Hdt., Thuc.
common, vulgar, Anth.
one of the people, a commoner, plebeian, Hdt., attic
one of the same people, a fellow-citizen, Eur.
at Athens, one of the same deme, Soph.
of or for the people, in common use, common, δ. γράμματα in Egypt, opp. to the hieroglyphics, Hdt.
of the populace, one of them, Lat. plebeius, Xen., Dem.
on the popular or democratic side, Lat. popularis, Ar., Thuc., etc.: adv. -κῶς, affably, kindly, Dem.
protecting the people, of guardian deities, Soph.; δημοῦχοι γᾶς ruling the people of the land, Id.
a mob-courtier, Eur.
of the people, popular, Plat.
a popular pastime, χαρίτων δαμώματα odes for public performance, Stesich, ap. Ar.
of public use, Plat.
long-lived, Il., Theocr.
old, aged, ancient, Aesch.
a Roman coin, a denary, nearly = Gr. δραχμή, NTest.
counsels, plans, arts, whether good or bad, Hom., Hes.
long, for a long while, Lat. diu, Il.; οὐ δὴν ἦν he was not long-lived, Id.
long ago, Od.
of Place, far, much, δὴν χάζετο Il.
a bite, biting: metaph. of biting jokes, Plut.
Particle used to give greater exactness, to the word or words which it influences (prob. a shortened form of ἤδη, Lat. jam) now, in truth, indeed, surely, really.
Usage of δή with single words:

after Adjectives, οἶος δή, μόνος δή, all alone, Od., etc.; esp. such as imply magnitude, μέγας δή, μικρὸς δή, etc.; often with Superlatives, μέγιστος δή, κράτιστος δή quite the greatest, confessedly the best, Thuc.; so with Numerals, ὀκτώ δὴ προέηκα ὀϊστούς I have shot full eight arrows, Il.; εἷς δή one only, Eur., etc.

after Adverbs, πολλάκις δή many times and oft, often ere now, Lat. jam saepe, Il.; ὀψὲ δὲ δή quite late, Id.; νῦν δή even now, now first, now at length, Xen., etc.:— τότε δή at that very time, Thuc.; αὐτίκα δὴ μάλα on the very spot, Plat.; also, ναὶ δή yea verily, Il.; οὐ δή surely not, Soph.
with Verbs, δὴ γὰρ ἴδον ὀφθαλμοῖσι for verily I saw him, Il.
with Substantives, ἐς δὴ τὸ Ἄργος τοῦτο . . well to this A. they came, Hdt.; τέλος δή its complete end, Aesch.; ironically, Lat. scilicet, εἰσήγαγε τὰς ἑταιρίδας δή the pretended courtesans, Xen.

with Pronouns, to mark strongly, ἐμὲ δή a man like me, Hdt.; σὺ δή you of all persons, Id.; οὗτος δή this and no other, Id.; ὅς δή who plainly, Il.:—with indef. Pronouns, ἄλλοι δή others be they who they may, Id.; δή τις some one or other, Lat. nescio quis, Plat.; δή τι in any way, whatever it be, Il., Hdt.
in reference to whole clauses:
to continue a narrative, so then, so, τότε μὲν δὴ ἡσυχίην εἶχε Hdt.; in summing up, τοιαῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα, Lat. haec hactenus, Aesch.
in inferences, Hdt., etc.; esp. to express what is unexpected, καὶ σὺ δή so then you too! Aesch.
with Imperat. and Subj., ἐννοεῖτε γὰρ δή for do but consider, Xen.; so, ἄγε δή, φέρε δή, ἴθι δή, σκόπει δή, etc.
γε δή to express what follows a fortiori, μετὰ ὅπλων γε δή above all with arms, Thuc.; μή τί γε δή not to mention that, Dem.
καὶ δή and what is more, Il.: so, ἐς Αἴγυπτον ἀπίκετο, καὶ δὴ καὶ ἐς Σάρδις he came to Egypt, and what is more to Sardis also, Hdt.; ἰσχὺς καὶ κάλλος καὶ πλοῦτος δή and above all riches, Plat.
καὶ δή is also in answers, βλέψον κάτω. Answ. καὶ δὴ βλέπω, well, I am looking, Ar.
in assumptions, καὶ δὴ δέδεγμαι and now suppose I have accepted, Aesch.
from any quarter, Lat. undecunque, Aesch.
at some time, once upon a time, Od., Aesch., etc.
εἰ δή ποτε, Lat. si quando, Il.; ὁπόθεν δή ποτε from some quarter or other, Dem.
as interrog., τί δή ποτε; what in the world? quid tandem? Id.; πόσοι δή ποτε; how many do you suppose? Id.
indef. adv., much like δήπου, Ar., Plat.

perhaps, it may be, Il.; in attic doubtless, I suppose, I presume, of course, Lat. scilicet, οὐ δήπου τλητόν Aesch., etc.: often in phrases, ἴστε γὰρ δή που, μέμνησθε γὰρ δή που Dem.; so, as interrog. implying an affirm. answer, τὴν αἰχμάλωτον κάτοισθα δή που; I presume you know, Soph.
to contend, wrangle, Hom.
a fight, battle, contest, Il., Aesch.
long-lived, Aesch.
long, too long, δηρὸν χρόνον Il.; so, δηρὸν (sub. χρόνον) as adv. all too long, Id.; ἐπὶ δηρόν Id.; δαρὸν χρόνον Soph.
certainly, to be sure, of course:
in answers, added to a word which echoes the question, ἴσασιν; do they know? Answ. ἴσασι δῆτα aye they know, Eur.; often with a negat., οὐ δῆτ’ ἔγωγε faith not I, Ar.

in questions, mostly to mark an inference or consequence, τί δῆτα; what then? πῶς δῆτα; ἆρα δῆτα, etc. Trag.:— sometimes it expresses indignation, καὶ δῆτ’ ἐτόλμας; and so thou hast dared? Soph.; ταῦτα δῆτ’ ἀνασχετά; Id.; ironical, τῶι σῶι δικαίωι δῆτ’; your principle of justice forsooth, Id.
in prayers or wishes, ἀπόλοιο δῆτα now a murrain take thee! Ar.; σκόπει δῆτα only look, Plat., etc.
sacred to Demeter, Anth.
Demeter, Hhymn., Soph., etc.
to find, meet with, Hom.
a ship's ladder, Luc.
to make a stride, walk or stand with the legs apart, εὖ διαβάς of a man planting himself firmly for fighting, Il.
c. acc. to step across, pass over a ditch or river, Id.
absol. (θάλασσαν or ποταμόν being omitted), to cross over, Lat. trajicere, ἐς Ἤλιδα Od.; πλοίῳ διαβῆναι Hdt., etc.
to throw over or across, to carry over or across, νέας Hdt.: hence,
seemingly intr., like Lat. trajicere, to pass over, cross, pass, Id.: also c. acc., δ. γεφύρας Eur.; πέλαγος Thuc.
to set at variance, make a quarrel between, ἐμὲ καὶ Ἀγάθωνα Plat.:—Pass. to be at variance with, τινί Id.

to traduce, slander, calumniate, Hdt., etc.; διέβαλον τοὺς Ἴωνας ὡς . . traduced them saying that . . , Id.:—Pass., διαβάλλεσθαί τινι to be filled with suspicion against another, Id.; πρός τινα Id.; ἔς τινα Thuc.
c. acc. rei, to misrepresent a thing, to state slanderously, Hdt., Dem.: to give hostile information, without insinuation of falsehood, Thuc.
to deceive by false accounts, impose upon, τινά Hdt.:—so in Mid., Id.:—Pass., διαβεβλῆσθαι ὡς . . to be slanderously told that . . , Plat.
Dep. to dive for a match: metaph. to contend in foul language with, τινι Dem.
a crossing over, passage, δ. ποιεῖσθαι Hdt.
a means or place of crossing, Id.: δ. ποταμοῦ a ford, Thuc.: a bridge, Xen.
to strut about, Ar.
to weigh in the hand, estimate, Plut.
that can be crossed or passed through, Xen.
sc. ἱερά, τά offerings before crossing the border, τὰ δ. προὐχώρει, τὰ δ. ἐγένετο they were favourable, Thuc., Xen.
to be crossed or passed, fordable, Hdt., etc.; νῆσον δ. ἐξ ἠπείρου easily got at from the main land, Id.
Dep. to maintain strongly, Dem.
the compass, so called from its outstretched legs, Lat. circinus, Ar.
to carry over or across, to transport, δ. τὸν στρατὸν κατὰ γεφύρας Hdt.; ἐς τὴν νῆσον τοὺς ὁπλίτας Thuc.
to eat up, Plat.:—Pass., perf. inf. διαβεβρῶσθαι Luc.
to live through, pass, χρόνον, βίον Plat., etc.:—absol. to spend one's whole life, Id., Xen.
to look straight before one, Plat.
to shout out, proclaim, publish, Aesch.:—Pass. to be the common talk, Luc.
to cry out, Thuc.
Mid. to contend in shouting, Dem.
noised abroad, famous, Plut.
false accusation, slander, calumny, ἐπὶ διαβολῇ εἰπεῖν Hdt.; διαβολὰς ἐνδέχεσθαι to give ear to false accusations, Id.; ἐμὴ δ. the slanders against me, Plat.
a quarrel, enmity, Thuc.
slanderous, backbiting, Sup.; διαβολώτατος Ar.
as Subst. a slanderer, Arist.: the slanderer, the Devil, NTest.
adv. -λως, injuriously, invidiously, Thuc.
eating through, devouring, Soph.
proparox. διάβορος, ον, pass. eaten through, consumed, Id.
to cheat with false hopes, Luc.
Dep. to discuss pro and con, discuss thoroughly, Thuc.
counsel, deliberation, Polyb.
to wet through, soak, Aesch.
very wet, moist, Eur.: ναῦς δ. ships with their timbers soaked and rotten, Thuc.:—metaph., ἔρωτι, μέθῃ δ. Luc.

to thrust through so as to stop up:— Mid., διαβυνέονται ὀϊστοὺς διὰ τῆς ἀριστερῆς they pass arrows through their left hand, Hdt.:—Pass., πηδάλιον διὰ τῆς τρόπιος διαβύνεται is passed through the keel, Id.
to make quite calm, Ar.
to be full of indignation, Dem.
great indignation, Plut.

to give notice by a messenger, to send as a message, Xen.:—generally, to noise abroad, proclaim, Eur., Plat.; c. inf. to order to do, Eur.:—Mid. to pass the word of command from man to man, inform one another, Xen.
a messenger, Lat. internuncius, esp. a secret informant, go-between, spy, Thuc.
to laugh at, τινα Eur., Xen.

Dep.:— to go through, pass, τόσαδε ἔτη Plat.; τὴν νύκτα Xen.: absol. to go through life, survive, live, Ar., etc.; c. part., διαγίγνεσθαι ἄρχων to continue in the government, Xen.; οὐδὲν ἄλλο ποιῶν διαγεγένηται he never did anything else, Id.
to be between, intervene, ap. Dem.
to distinguish, discern, Lat. dignoscere, διαγνῶναι ἄνδρα ἕκαστον Il.; δ. εἰ ὁμοῖοί εἰσι whether they are equals or no, Hdt.; δ. τὸ ὀρθὸν καὶ μή Aeschin.:— δ. τινὰς ὄντας, i. e. δ. οἵτινές εἰσιν, Ar.
to discern exactly, τι Soph.
to resolve, vote to do so and so, c. inf., Hdt.:—Pass., impers. διέγνωστο it had been resolved, Thuc.
as Athen. law-term, to decide a suit, Lat. dijudicare, δίκην Aesch.:— to give judgment, περί τινος Thuc.
Dep. to hold a javelin by the thongPass., perf. part. pass. διηγκυλισμένος, of a man, ready to shoot, Xen.:—so (from δι-αγκυλόομαι), διηγκυλωμένος Id.
to scoop out, Od.
carved in intaglio, engraved, Anth.
to carve in intaglio, Diod.
a decree, resolution, Thuc.
to make known, NTest.
a distinguishing, discernment, Eur., Dem.
power of discernment, Eur.
a resolving, deciding, δ. ποιεῖσθαι to decide a matter, Thuc.; δ. περί τινος Dem.
one must distinguish, Luc.
able to distinguish, Luc.
to murmur among themselves, NTest.
to speak plainly, declare, Hdt.
to speak of, κακῶς δ. τινά Luc.
that which is marked out by lines, a figure, plan, Plat.
a geometrical figure, diagram, Xen., Plat.
a written list, register, Dem.
a decree, edict, Plut.
a marking off by lines, Plat.: a geometrical figure, diagram, outline, Plut.
to mark out by lines, delineate, Plat.
to draw a line through, cross out, strike off the list, Id.; δ. δίκην to strike a cause out of the list, cancel, quash it, Ar.
to lie awake, Ar.
to carry over or across, Od., Thuc., etc.
of Time, to go through, pass, spend, βίοτον, βίον Aesch., etc.

intr. (without βίον) to pass life, live, like Lat. degere, Hdt., etc.:— to delay, put off time, Thuc.:— to continue, Xen.: c. part. to continue doing so and so, δ. μανθάνων Id.; also with adv., ἄριστα Id.
to make to continue or keep in a certain state, πόλιν ὀρθοδίκαιον δ. Aesch.; διῆγεν ὑμᾶς Dem.
to entertain a person, Xen.
a passing of life, a way or course of life, Lat. ratio vitae, Plat., etc.; διαγωγαὶ τοῦ συζῆν public pastimes, Arist.
of or for a passage: τέλος δ. a transit duty, Strab.
Dep. to contend, struggle or fight against, τινι and πρός τινα Xen.
to fight desperately, contend earnestly, Thuc., Xen.
to tear asunder, rend, Il.
Dep.:
in reciprocal sense, to divide among themselves, διὰ κτῆσιν δατέοντο Il., Hes.
in act. sense, to divide, distribute, διὰ παῦρα δασάσκετο (ionic for ἐδάσατο), Il.; διεδάσαντο τὴν ληΐην Hdt.; ἐς φυλὰς διεδάσαντο distributed them among the tribes, Id.
to shew clearly, shew plainly, Hdt.; c. part., διαδεξάτω κηδόμενος let him shew that he cares, Id.:—Pass., διαδεικνύσθω ἐὼν πολέμιος let him be declared the king's enemy, Id.
intr. in forms διέδεξε, ὡς διέδεξε, it was clear, manifest, Id.
as adj., πλοῦτος δ. inherited wealth, Eur.
of good omen, Hdt.
Dep. to see through, οὐδ’ ἂν νῶϊ διαδράκοι would not see us through (the cloud), Il.
bound fast, χαλινοὶ διάδετοι γενύων ἱππείων bits firm bound through the horse's mouth, Aesch.
Dep.:
to receive one from another, Lat. excipere, δ. λόγον to take up the word, i. e. to speak next, Plat.; so διαδέχεσθαι alone, Hdt.
διαδέχεσθαί τινι to succeed one, Xen.
absol. to relieve one another, τοῖς ἵπποις with fresh horses, Id.:—part. perf. pass. διαδεδεγμένος, η, ον, in succession, in turns, Soph.; so, διαδεξάμενος Hdt.
to bind round, τὸ πλοῖον Hdt.:— Pass., διαδεδεμένος fast-bound, Plat.
Dep. to do great harm to, tear to pieces, Od., Theocr.
distinguishable among others, Thuc.
to make manifest, Plut.
a band or fillet: esp. the band round the τιάρα of the Persian king, Xen.
wearing a diadem, Plut.

entry.note: fut. -δράσομαι ionic διαδιδρήσκω ionic -δρήσομαι aor2 -έδραν perf. -δέδρᾱκα
entry.sense: to run off, get away, escape, Hdt.; διαδεδρακότες shirkers, Ar.
c. acc. to run away from, escape from, Hdt.
to give from hand to hand, to pass on, hand over, Lat. tradere, λαμπάδια διαδώσουσιν ἀλλήλοις Plat.:—Pass., of reports, to be spread abroad, Xen.
to distribute, τινί τι Id.
δ. κόρας to cast one's eyes around, Eur.
to give judgment in a case, Plat.: c. acc. rei, to decide, Xen.
Mid. to go to law, τινι with another, Plat.; διαδικάσασθαι τὰ πρὸς ἐμέ to have a matter settled by arbitration, Dem.
to submit oneself to trial, Plat., Xen.
to hold a thing to be right, Thuc.
a suit brought to decide who (of several persons) was entitled to any right or privilege, Oratt.:—metaph., δ. τῷ βήματι πρὸς τὸ στρατήγιον a dispute between the orators and the war-office, Aeschin.
the object of litigation in a διαδικασία, Lys.
to drive horses as in a chariot-race, Eur.
to test closely, Xen.
a distribution, largess, Dem., etc.
a taking from another, Dem.
succession, ἄλλος παρ’ ἄλλου διαδοχαῖς by successions or reliefs, Aesch.; ἐκ διαδοχῆς ἀλλήλοις in turns, Lat. vicissim, Dem.; κατὰ διαδοχήν Thuc.
in military sense, a relief, relay, Xen.
succeeding a person in a thing:
c. dat. pers. et gen. rei, δ. Μεγαβάζῳ τῆς στρατηγίης his successor in the command, Hdt.; θνητοῖς διάδοχοι μοχθημάτων succeeding them in, i. e. relieving them from, toils, Aesch.
c. gen. rei only, δ. τῆς ναυαρχίας succeeding to the command, Thuc.
c. gen. pers. only, φέγγος ὕπνου δ. sleep's successor, light, Soph.
c. dat. pers. only, δ. Κλεάνδρῳ Xen.; so, κακὸν κακῷ δ. Eur.; and in a quasi-act. sense, διάδοχος κακῶν κακοῖς bringing a succession of evils after evils, Id.
absol., διάδοχοι ἐφοίτων they went to work in relays or gangs, Hdt., Thuc.: neut. pl. as adv. in succession, Eur.
a citizen who shirks all state burdens, Ar.

entry.etym: a correction for διεπρήστευσε, which has no meaning.
entry.sense: to run off, go over to, Hdt.
a running about through a city, Aesch.
a foray, Plut.
a passage through, Xen.: an aqueduct, Plut.
running through or about, wandering, Aesch.; λέχος δ. stray, lawless love, Eur.

entry.note: or -δύω more commonly as Dep. διαδύομαι fut. -δύσομαι aor2 διέδυν
entry.sense: to slip through a hole or gap, Thuc., Xen.: absol. to slip through, slip away, Hdt., Ar.
c. acc. to evade, shirk, Dem.
a passage through: in pl. evasions, τινος from a thing, Dem.
Dep. to distribute in presents, Xen.
to discern, distinguish, ἣν ἀρετὴν διαείσεται will discern, test his manhood, Il.:—Pass. to be discerned, Il.
to contend in singing, τινί with one, Theocr.
high in air, transcendental, Luc.
to live through, pass, τὸν βίον Eur.:—then, absol., like Lat. degere, Ar., Xen.
c. part., like διαβιόω, to live by doing so and so, ποιηφαγέοντες διέζωον they supported life by eating grass, Hdt.; also, δ. ἀπό τινος to live off or by a thing, Soph.
Pass. to be disjoined, separated, parted, τινος from one, Aeschin.; ἀπό τινος Xen.
a disjoining, parting, Plat.
a girdle, drawers, Lat. subligaculum, Thuc.
an isthmus, Plut.
to gird round the middle:—Mid. to gird oneself with, ἐσθῆτα, Luc.:— Pass., διεζωσμένοι wearing drawers, Thuc.
metaph. to engirdle, encompass, Plut.
to blow through trees, etc., c. acc., Od., Hes.
Dep. to look through, examine, Plat., Xen.
to fumigate thoroughly, Od.
to warm through, Plat., etc.:— Pass. to be heated, by drinking, Dem.
heated through: of a hot temperament, Arist.
a disposition, arrangement, Plat.
the composition in a work of art, as opp. to εὕρεσις, Id.
a disposition of property, = διαθήκη, Id.
a disposing of, selling, sale, Plut.
a man's disposition, Plat.
an arranger, Hdt.
to run about, Thuc., etc.; of reports, of panic fear, Xen.
to run a race, τινί with or against another, Plat.:—c. acc. cogn., δ. τὴν λαμπάδα to run the torch-race, Plut.
a disposition of property by will, a will, testament, Ar., Oratt.
an arrangement between two parties, covenant, Ar., NTest.
to confound utterly, τινα Thuc.: absol. to make a great noise, Plut.
to look closely into, examine closely, Ar.
to spread a report, give out, Thuc.
mostly in Pass. to be commonly reported, διετεθρύλητο ὡς . . Xen.
to be talked deaf, διαθρυλούμενος ὑπό σου Id.
to break in sunder, break in pieces, shiver, Luc.:—Pass., τριχθά τε καὶ τετραχθὰ διατρυφὲν [τὸ ξίφος] Il.; ἀσπίδες διατεθρυμμέναι Xen.
metaph., like Lat. frangere, to break down by profligate living and indulgence, to enervate, pamper, make weak and womanish, Plat., Xen.: —Pass. to be enervated, pampered, Aesch., Xen.
Mid. to give oneself airs, of a prude, Theocr.; of a singer, διαθρύπτεται ἤδη is beginning her airs, Id.
to become quite clear and fine, ἐδόκει διαιθριάζειν it seemed likely to be fine, Xen.
quite clear and fine, Plut.
blood-stained, Eur.; δίαιμον ἀναπτύειν to spit blood, Plut.
to wet, moisten, Il.:— Mid., διαίνεσθαι ὄσσε to wet one's eyes, Aesch.; absol. to weep, Id.
a dividing, division, of money, Hdt.; of spoil, Xen.; ἐν διαιρέσει [ψήφων] in the reckoning of the votes on either side, Aesch.
to be divided, Plat.
διαιρετέον, one must divide, Id.
divisible, Plat.
divided, separated, Xen.: distributed, Soph.
distinguishable, Thuc.

to take one from another, to cleave in twain, to divide into parts, Il., Hdt.; δ. λαγόν to cut it open, Id.; δ. πυλίδα to break it open, Thuc.; δ. τὴν ὀροφήν to tear it away, Id.; δ. τοῦ τείχους to take down part of the wall, make a breach in it, Id.; τὸ διῃρημένον the breach, Id.

to divide, δύο μοίρας Λυδῶν the Lydians into two parts, Hdt.; so, δ. τριχῆ Plat.; εἰς δύο Dem.:—Mid. to divide for themselves, ναῦς Thuc.: but also to divide among themselves, Hes., Hdt.:—Pass., διῃρημένοι κατ’ ἀναπαύλας divided into relays, Thuc.
to divide into component parts, Plat.
to distinguish, Ar.
to determine, decide, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
to say distinctly, to define, interpret, Hdt., attic
to raise up, lift up, τὸν αὐχένα Xen.
to separate, remove, Plut.:—Mid., διαράμενος (sc. )τὰ σκέλη) taking long strides, Theophr.
δ. τὸ στόμα to open one's mouth, Dem.
Dep. to perceive distinctly, distinguish perfectly, τι Plat.
to rush or dart through or across, Hdt.:c. acc., ὄρη διᾴσσει Soph.; of sound, ἀχὼ διῇξεν μυχόν Aesch.; and c. gen., σπασμὸς διῇξε πλευρῶν Soph.
to make an end of, τινά Soph.
a way of living, mode of life, Hdt., Soph., etc.; δ. ποιεῖσθαι to pass one's life, Hdt.
a dwelling, abode, room, Ar.
at Athens, arbitration, Soph., Ar., Oratt.
to feed in a certain way, to diet, δ. τοὺς νοσοῦντας Plut.
Mid. and Pass. to lead a certain course of life, to live, Hdt., Soph.; δ. νόμιμα to live in the observance of laws, Thuc.
to be arbiter or umpire (διαιτητής), Dem., etc.
c. acc. rei, to determine, decide, Theocr.
mostly in pl. rules of life, a mode or course of life, esp. in regard of diet, Xen.: generally, institutions, customs, Thuc., Xen.
in pl. the dwelling rooms of a house, Xen.
an arbitrator, umpire, Lat. arbiter, Hdt., Plat., etc.
burnt through, very hot, Luc.
to cleanse or purge thoroughly, Plat.
a thorough cleansing, Plat.
Mid. to sit each in his own seat, Plut.
to make to sit apart, set apart, Xen.
to burn through, heat to excess, Hdt.:—metaph. to inflame, excite, Plut.
to reveal to view, Dem.
only in aor1, μῶν τὸν λάρυγγα διεκάναξέ σου; has aught run gurgling through thy throat? Eur.
to expect anxiously, Plut.
to endure to the end, last out, Hdt., Xen.
Mid. to confute thoroughly, τινι NTest.
to determine by lot, Ar.
to cleave asunder, Od.

serving as Pass. to διατίθημι, to be in a certain state, to be disposed or affected so and so, Hdt., etc.: often, like ἔχω, with an adv., ὁρᾶτε ὡς δ. ὑπὸ τῆς νόσου how I am affected by the disease, Thuc.; κακῶς, μοχθηρῶς, φαύλως δ. to be in sorry plight, Plat.: εὖ or κακῶς δ. τινι to be well or ill disposed towards him, Oratt.; ἐπιφθόνως δ. τινι to be envied by him, ὑπόπτως τινι δ. to be suspected by him, Thuc.

of things, to be settled, fixed, or ordered, ὥς οἱ διέκειτο so was it ordered him, Hes.; τὰ διακείμενα certain conditions, settled terms, Hdt.; of a gift, ἄμεινον διακείσεται it will be better disposed of, Xen.
to cut in pieces: metaph., διακέρσαι ἐμὸν ἔπος to make it null, frustrate it, Il.:—Pass., σκευάρια διακεκαρμένος shorn of his trappings, Ar.
an exhortation, command, Plat.
Dep. to exhort, give orders, direct, δ. τινι ποιεῖν τι etc., Hdt., etc.; also, δ. τινί τι (sc. ποιεῖν), Plat.; δ. τινι alone, Id.
to encourage one another, Hdt.; δ. ἀλλήλοις Xen.; δ. ἑαυτῷ Id.
an exhortation, cheering on, Thuc.
διὰ, κενῆς, adv. for διὰ κενῆς πράξεως, in vain, idly, to no purpose, Eur., Ar.
quite empty or hollow; τὸ δ. the gap, vacuum, Thuc.
thin, lank, Plut., Luc.
to change into small coin, Ar.
Dep. to negotiate by herald, πρός τινα Thuc.
to proclaim by herald, ἐν διακεκηρυγμένοις in declared war, Plut.
to sell by auction, Id.
to run all risks, make a desperate attempt, hazard all, Thuc.; πρός τινα Id.; ὑπέρ or πρός τινος Lys., Xen.; περί τινος Dem.:—Pass. of the attempt, to be risked, hazarded, Id.
to move thoroughly:—Pass. to be put in motion, Hdt.
to throw into disorder, confound, τὰ πεπραγμένα Thuc.
to sift thoroughly, scrutinise, Ar.
to lend to various persons:—Pass., διακεχρημένον τάλαντον Dem.

entry.note: fut. άσω epic aor1 part. διακλάσσας
entry.sense: to break in twain, Il.
in Pass., = διαθρύπτομαι: perf. pass. διακεκλασμένος enervated, Luc.
to steal at different times, Dem.; τὸ διακλαπέν the quantity stolen [ by the soldiers] and dispersed, Thuc.
to keep alive by stealth, τινά Hdt.
to keep back by stealth, τὴν ἀλήθειαν Dem.
to assign by lot, allot, Aesch.
to choose by lot, Xen.:—Mid. to cast lots, Thuc., Xen.
to turn away, retreat, Polyb.
a retreat, Plut.
to wash, wash out, Eur.
to pull to pieces, Anth.
to glue together, Luc.
to scrape to nothing, ὄψιν δ. to grind out his eye, Eur.:—Pass. to be shivered, Aesch.
to wear out, wear away, Eur.:—Pass. to be worn out, destroyed, Aesch., Eur.; τὸ χρῶμα διακεκναισμένος having lost all one's colour, Ar.
a carrying over, τινὸς εἰς τόπον Thuc.
to carry over or across, Hdt., Thuc.:—Mid. to carry over what is one's own, Hdt.: —Pass. to be carried over, to pass over, cross, Thuc.
to minister, serve, do service, absol., Eur.; τινι to a person, Dem.; δ. πρός τι to be serviceable towards, Plat.:—Mid. to minister to one's own needs, Soph.; αὑτῶι διακονεῖσθαι Ar.
to be a deacon, NTest.
c. acc. rei, to furnish, supply, Lat. ministrare, τί τινι Hdt.:—Pass. to be supplied, Dem.
servants' business, service, Plat.
the office of a διάκονος, service, Thuc., Plat.
attendance on a duty, ministration, Dem.; ἡ δ. ἡ καθημερινή ministering to daily wants, NTest.; ἡ δ. τοῦ λόγου the ministry of the word, Id.
serviceable, Ar., etc.; comp. -ώτερος, Plat.

entry.etym: Akin to διάκτορος: both perh. from διώκω.
entry.sense: a servant, waiting-man, Lat. minister, Hdt., etc.: a messenger, Aesch., Soph.:—as fem., Dem.
a minister of the church, a deacon, NTest.: as fem. a deaconess, Id.
Mid. to contend with others at throwing the javelin, Xen.
a gash, cleft, Plut.;
to cut in two, cut through, Thuc.
to break through the enemy's line, τὴν τάξιν Xen.: then, to break through the line, Id.
to rumble through, τὴν γαστέρα Ar.
satiated, glutted, τινός with a thing, Hdt.
two hundred, Lat. ducenti: sg. with n. of multitude, ἵππος διακοσία two hundred horse, Thuc.
to divide and marshal, muster in array, Il., Thuc.:—Pass., εἴπερ ἐς δεκάδας διακοσμηθεῖμεν Ἀχαιοί (epic for -είημεν, 1st pl. aor1 opt.) Il.
generally, to regulate, set in order, Hdt., etc.: Mid., μέγαρον διεκοσμήσαντο got it set in order, Od.
a setting in order, regulating, Plat.
battle-order, Thuc.
to hear through, hear out or to the end, τί Xen.:— to hear or learn from another, τί τινος Plat.
c. gen. pers. to be a hearer of, Plut.
to scream continually, Ar.
δ. τινί to match another at screaming, Id.
to hold fast, hold one's own, Plut.
to strike the strings of the lyre, Anth.
to make to flow, Theocr.
to examine or discuss minutely or with precision, τι Xen.:—Pass. to be brought to perfection, Arist.
one must discuss minutely, Plut.
eminently, above all, Lat. eximie, Il., Hdt.

to separate one from another, Il.: to part combatants, and in Pass. to be parted, Hom.; so in fut. mid. διακρῐνέεσθαι, Od.; also, διακριθῆναι ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων Thuc.; διακρίνεσθαι πρός . . to part and join different parties, Id.
Pass. to be dissolved into elemental parts, Plat.
to distinguish, Lat. discernere, τὸ σῆμα Od.; οὐδένα διακρίνων making no distinction of persons, Hdt.: —Pass., διεκέκριτο οὐδέν no distinction was made, Thuc.

to settle, decide, of judges, Hdt., Theocr.:—Mid., νεῖκος δ. to get it decided, Hes.: —Pass. to come to a decision, Il.; περί τινος Plat.: — to contend with one, τινι NTest.; μάχῃ διακρινθῆναι πρός τινα Hdt.
Pass. to doubt, hesitate, NTest.
the mountaineers, one of the three Attic parties after Solon., Ar.
separation, dissolution, Emped.
a decision, judgment, Xen.
one must decide, Thuc.
separated: choice, excellent, Theocr.
a putting off, Dem.
to prove by knocking or ringing, as one does an earthen vessel, Plat.

in Mid. to drive from oneself, get rid of, elude, τινα or τι Hdt., Dem.: to evade his creditor by delays, of a debtor, Id.: absol. to practise evasions, Id.:—Pass., διακρουσθῆναι τῆς τιμωρίας to escape from punishment, Id.
the office of a διάκτορος, service, Anth.
epith. of Hermes, the Messenger or Minister of Zeus, Hom.
to play at dice with, πρός τινα Plut.
to mix one with another, jumble, Dem.
to raise into waves, Luc.
to stoop and creep through a narrow place, Hdt.
to stoop so as to peep in, Ar., Xen.
a hindering, Plat.
one must hinder, Plat.
a hinderer, Hdt., Plat.
to hinder, prevent, τινὰ μὴ ποιεῖν τι Hdt.; or without μή, Eur., Plat.; δ. τινά Thuc.; δ. φόνον Soph.:—Pass., ἃ διεκωλύθη (sc. ποιεῖν) which he was prevented from doing, Dem.
to satirise, Plat.
to divide or part by lot, Hdt., Aesch., Xen.; δῶμα σιδήρῳ δ. Eur.:— to tear in pieces, Id.
to crack asunder, burst, Ar.
to kick away, spurn, Theocr.
to talk over a thing with another, τί τινι Eur.:—Pass. to be much talked of, NTest.

entry.note: fut. -λήψομαι aor2 διέλᾰβον perf. διείληφα perf. pass. -είλημμαι or -λέλημμαι ionic -λέλαμμαι
entry.sense: to take or receive severally, i. e. each for himself, each his share, Xen., etc.
to grasp or lay hold of separately, διαλαβόντες τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας Hdt.:—generally, to seize, arrest, τινά Id.
as a gymnastic term, to seize by the middle, Ar.: metaph. of the soul, διειλημμένη ὑπὸ τοῦ σωματοειδοῦς Plat.

to divide, τὸν ποταμὸν ἐς τριηκοσίας διώρυχας δ. Hdt.:—Pass., ποταμὸς διαλελαμμένος πενταχοῦ divided into five channels, Id.; θώρακες διειλημμένοι τὸ βάρος breast-plates having their weight distributed, Xen.
to mark at intervals, Decret. ap. Dem.
to cut off, intercept, Thuc.
to mark off, distinguish:— Pass. χρώμασι διειλημμένη, marked with various colours, Plat.
to distinguish in thought, Id.: to state distinctly, ap. Dem.
to shine through, to dawn, Ar.
to escape notice, διαλαθὼν εἰσέρχεται Thuc.: c. acc. pers. to escape the notice of, Xen.
grievous, Aesch.
suffering great pain, Plut.
to pick out one from another, to pick out, Hdt., Xen.

Dep. δια-λέγομαι: fut. -λέξομαι and -λεχθήσομαι: aor1 δι-ελεξάμην and διελέχθην: perf. διείλεγμαι: 3rd sg. plup. διείλεκτο: — to converse with, hold converse with, τινί Il., etc.; πρός τινα Plat.; δ. τί τινι or πρός τινα to discuss a question with another, Xen.; δ. τινι μὴ ποιεῖν to argue with one against doing, Thuc.:—absol. to discourse, argue, Plat., Xen.
to use a dialect or language, Hdt.
an interval, Plat.; ἐκ διαλειμμάτων at intervals, Plut.
to leave an interval between:— Pass., διελέλειπτο a gap had been left, Hdt.
of Time, διαλιπὼν ἡμέρην having left an interval of a day, Hdt.; ἀκαρῆ διαλιπών having waited an instant, Ar.; διαλιπών absol. after a time, Thuc.
intr. to stand at intervals, δύο πλέθρα ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων δ. Thuc.
c. part. to cease doing a thing, Xen.
of Time, διαλιπόντων ἐτῶν τριῶν after an interval of three years, Thuc.
to lick clean, Ar.
one must discourse, Plat.
skilled in logical argument, Plat.:— ἡ διαλεκτική (sc. τέχην) the art of discussion, dialectic, Id.: adv. -κῶς, logically, Id.
discourse: discussion, debate, arguing, Plat.
language: the language of a country, dialect: a local word or phrase, Plut.
a way of speaking, enunciation, Dem.
discourse, arguing, Ar.
Dep. to discourse subtly, chop logic, τινι with one, Ar.
one must distinguish, Plat.
interchange, exchange, Eur.
a change from enmity to friendship, a reconciliation, truce, Hdt., Ar.; in pl., Eur.; διαλλαγαὶ πρός τινα Dem.
a substitute, changeling, Eur.
a mediator, Hdt., Aesch.

entry.note: fut. ξω perf. δι-ήλλᾰχα Pass., fut. δι-αλλαχθήσομαι and -αλλᾰγήσομαι aor1 -ηλλάχθην and -ηλλάγην perf. -ήλλαγμαι
entry.sense: Mid. to change one with another, interchange, Hdt.: absol. to make an exchange, Xen.
Act. to exchange, i. e.,
to give in exchange, τί τινι Eur.; τι ἀντί τινος Plat.
to take in exchange, Id.; δ. τὴν χώραν to change one land for another, i. e. to pass through a land, Xen.
simply, to change, τοὺς ναυάρχους Id.

to change enmity for friendship, to reconcile one to another, τινά τινι Thuc.; τινὰ πρός τινα Ar.; or c. acc. pl. only, Eur., etc.: absol. to make friends, Plat.:—Pass. to be reconciled, to be made friends, Aesch., etc.
intr., c. dat. pers. et acc. rei, to differ from one in a thing, διαλλάσσειν οὐδὲν τοῖσι ἑτέροισι Hdt.: absol., τὸ διαλλάσσον the difference, Thuc.
Pass. to be different, Lat. distare, Id.
Dep. to leap across, τάφρον Xen.
Dep. to balance accounts, πρός τινα Dem.
to take full account of, to stop to consider, Id.: to distinguish between, Aeschin.
to converse, debate, argue, περί τινος Xen.
a balancing of accounts, Dem.
a conversation, dialogue, Plat.
Dep. to rail furiously at, τινι Hdt.; διαλοιδορηθείς Dem.
Dep. to maltreat shamefully, undo utterly, Hdt., Eur.
to cheat grossly, Ar.
to falsify, corrupt, Id.
no Act. occurs, but perf. part. διαλελυμασμένος is used in pass. sense, Hdt.; aor1 διελυμάνθην Eur.

a loosing one from another, separating, parting, τῆς ψυχῆς καὶ τοῦ σώματος Plat.; δ. τοῦ σώματος its dissolution, Id.; ἡ δ. τῆς γεφύρας the breaking down the bridge, Thuc.: the disbanding, of troops, Xen.; ἡ δ. τῆς ἀγορᾶς the time of its breaking up, Hdt.; τὴν δ. ἐποιήσαντο broke off the action, Thuc.; δ. γάμου a divorce, Plut.
an ending, cessation, κακῶν Eur.; πολέμου Thuc.: absol. a cessation of hostilities, peace, Dem.
one must dissolve, φιλίαν Arist.
a dissolver, breaker-up, Thuc.
capable of dissolution, Plat.

to loose one from another, to part asunder, undo, Hdt.: to dissolve an assembly, Id., Thuc., etc.; τὴν σκηνὴν εἰς κοίτην δ. to break up the party and go to bed, Xen.; δ. τὴν στρατιάν to disband it, Thuc.:—Pass., of an assembly, to break up, Hdt., etc.: of a man, to die, Xen.
to dissolve into its elements, to break up, Plat.
to put an end to friendship, break off a truce, Thuc., etc.:—so in Mid., διαλύσασθαι ξεινίην Hdt.
to put an end to enmity, Thuc.; and in Mid., Dem., etc.
c. acc. pers. to reconcile, τινὰ πρός τινα Id.; οὐ γὰρ ἦν ὁ διαλύσων Thuc.:—Pass. and Mid., διαλύεσθαι νείκους to be parted from quarrel, i. e. to be reconciled, Eur., Xen., etc.
generally, to put an end to, do away with, διαβολήν Thuc.; so in Mid., Id., etc.
to solve a difficulty, Plat.
δ. τιμάς to pay the full value, discharge a debt, Hdt., etc.: c. acc. pers. to pay him off, Dem.
absol. to slacken one's hold, undo, Theocr.
to fill full of barley meal, Ar.
to grind to powder, utterly destroy, Aesch.
Dep. to determine by an oracle, τι Plat.
to go astray from, τῆς ὁδοῦ Thuc.: to fail of obtaining, τινός Id., Dem.
absol. to fail utterly, Plat.
a total mistake, Plut.; δ. τῶν ἡμερῶν a wrong reckoning of the days, Thuc.
as attic law-term, to use a διαμαρτυρία (q. v.), Dem.
c. inf. to affirm by a διαμαρτυρία that a thing is, c. acc. et inf., Id.: Pass., τὰ διαμαρτυρηθέντα things so affirmed, Isocr.
as attic law-term, evidence given to prevent a case from coming to trial, Dem., etc.
Dep. to protest solemnly, Lat. obtestari, Dem.; δ. μή . . , c. inf., Id.:— δ. τινι μὴ ποιεῖν to protest against his doing, Aeschin.
generally, to protest, asseverate, Plat.
absol. to beg earnestly, conjure, Xen.
to knead thoroughly, knead well, Ar.
to scourge severely, Plat.
to pander, δ. τὴν ἡγεμονίαν γάμοις to bargain away the empire by a marriage, Plut.
one must deny absolutely, Plat.
Dep. to fight or strive with, struggle against, τινι or πρός τινι Hdt., etc.; πρός τι Dem.; δ. μὴ μεταγνῶναι ὑμᾶς I resist to the uttermost your change of opinion, Thuc.; δ. τὸ μὴ θανεῖν Eur.
to fight one with another, Id.
to fight it out, contend obstinately, Lat. depugnare, Ar.
to exert oneself greatly, ὅπως τι γένηται Plat.
in argument, to contend or maintain that . . , δ. τι μὴ εἶναι Thuc.; or without μή, Plat.
to cut through, Il., Eur.
to scrape away, Id.; Mid., διαμᾶσθαι τὸν κάχληκα to get the gravel scraped away, Thuc.
to let go, give up, leave off, Eur.

to exchange, τι πρός τι one thing with another, Plat.; so in Mid., διαμείβεσθαί τί τινος or ἀντί τινος, Solon, Plat.:— διαμεῖψαι Ἀσίαν Εὐρώπης to take Asia in exchange for Europe, i.e. to pass into Asia, Eur.
δ. ὁδόν to finish a journey, Aesch.; so in Mid., Id.
in Mid., also, to alter, Hdt.
Dep. to strive hotly with, τινί Plut.
an exchange, Plut.
to make quite black, Plut.
limb by limb, limb-meal, Od.
a being on the point to do, πολλὴ δ. φυλακῆς long postponement of precautionary measures, Thuc.
to be always going to do, i.e. to delay continually, Thuc.
Dep. to blame greatly, Thuc.
to remain by, stand by, τινί Xen.:— to persevere, ἔν τινι Plat.; ἐπί τινι Xen.:—absol. to stand firm, Dem.:—c. part., δ. λέγων to continue speaking, Id.
to distribute, Plat.
to divide: Mid. to divide or part among themselves, NTest.
division, dissension, NTest.
to measure through, out or off, χῶρον δ. to measure lists for combat, Il.:—Pass., ἡμέρα διαμεμετρημένη measured by the clepsydra, Dem.
to measure out in portions, distribute, Xen., etc.:—Mid. to have measured out to one, receive as one's share, Orac. ap. Hdt., Xen.
measured out or off, Il.
a measured allowance, rations, Plut.
sc. γραμμή the diameter or diagonal of a parallelogram, Plat.; κατὰ διάμετρον diametrically, Id.; so, ἐκ διαμέτρου Luc.
a rule for drawing the diameter, Ar.
Dep. to bring about, contrive, Ar., Plat.
Dep. to deal meanly, πρός τινα Plut.
Dep. to contend hotly, strive earnestly, τινι or πρός τινα Plat.; περί τινος Id.
Dep. to keep in memory, Xen.
to hate bitterly, Arist., Plut.
to cut up piecemeal, Hdt.
to call to mind, remember, Hdt.; c. gen., Plat.; c. acc., Xen., etc.
to record, mention, Thuc.: Pass., διαμνημονεύεται ἔχειν he is mentioned as having, Xen.
to divide, rend asunder, Eur.; so in Mid., Id.
in Mid., also, to portion out, distribute, Od.
right through, through and through, c. gen., Aesch., Eur.; also c. acc., Xen.
of Place, through and through, right through, clean through, c. gen., Il., Soph.:—c. acc., Il., Aesch.
absol. without break, continuously, Hom.
of Time, throughout, for ever, Id.; διαμπερὲς αἰεί for ever and aye, Il.
drenching, Aesch.
to communicate by word, to express in speech, Aesch.: to converse, Plat.
to make mouths (in scorn), Ar.
utterly different, Aesch.
to dispute or disagree, πρός τινα περί τινος Dem.:—Pass., τὰ ἀμφισβητούμενα the points at issue, Id.
a disputing, dispute, Plut.
to read through, Isocr.
Mid. to rest awhile, Plat.
to stop chinks: to caulk ships, Strab.
to maintain a sea-fight, Hdt.
to flow through, percolate, Plut.
two ways, διάνδιχα μερμηρίζειν to halt between two opinions, Il.; διάνδιχα δῶκε gave one of two things, Id.; δ. ἔαξα broke it in twain, Theocr.
a distribution, Plut.
one must distribute, Xen.
distributive, Plat.
Pass. to flutter in the wind, Luc., Anth.
to distribute, apportion, τί τινι Ar., Plat.:—Mid. to divide among themselves, Plat., Arist.:—Pass., aor1 inf. διανεμηθῆναι to be spread abroad, NTest.
Pass. to go through, Anth.
to swim across, ἐς Σαλαμῖνα Hdt.
c. acc. to swim through, Plat.
to adorn with flowers, Luc.:—Pass. to be variegated, Plut.
Pass. with aor2 and perf. act. to stand aloof from, depart from, τινος Thuc.
Dep.: to be minded, intend, purpose to do, c. inf., Hdt., etc.
to think over or of, Lat. meditari, τι Id.: c. acc. et inf. to think or suppose that, Plat.
with adv. to be minded or disposed so and so, καλῶς, κακῶς δ. Id.
a thought, notion, Plat.
of or for thinking, intellectual, Plat., Arist.
a thought, intention, purpose, Hdt., attic; διάνοιαν ἔχειν = διανοεῖσθαι, c. inf., Thuc.
a thought, notion, opinion, Lat. cogitatum, Hdt., Plat.
intelligence, understanding, Id.
the thought or meaning of a word or passage, Id.; τῇ διανοίᾳ as regards the sense, Dem.
to open, Plat
to open and explain, τὰς γραφάς NTest.
a distributer, Plut.
a distribution, Aesch., Plat.
extending throughout, right through, διανταία πληγή a home- thrust, Aesch.; so, διανταίαν οὐτᾶν Id.; δ. βέλος Id.; ὀδύνα Eur.:—metaph., μοῖρα δ. destiny that strikes home, Aesch.
to drain out, exhaust: metaph., like Lat. exhaurire, to drink even to the dregs, endure to the end, Eur.
to pass the night, Xen.

to bring quite to an end, accomplish, finish, κέλευθον, ὁδόν h. Hom., etc.;—hence (ὁδόν omitted), διὰ πόντον ἀνύσσας having finished one's course over the sea, Hes.:—c. part. to finish doing a thing, Od., Eur.
Dep. to fight to the death, Ar.
to attend children: generally, to entertain, amuse, Plut.; δ. τὸν καιρόν, Lat. fallere tempus, Id.
Pass. to go through a course of education, Xen.
to continue wrestling, go on wrestling, Ar.
a hard struggle, Plut.
to distribute by lot, Aesch.
to shiver, shatter, Eur., Ar.
to look timidly round, Plut.
violent contention, NTest.
to deflower a maiden, Hdt.
to stretch out by nailing the extremities, as in crucifixion, Hdt.: to stretch out a hide for tanning, Ar.
to sprinkle, δ. τοῦ ψήγήατος ἐς τὰς τρίχας to sprinkle some dust on the hair, Hdt.
to make to cease:— Mid. to rest between times, pause, Plat.:—Pass. to cease to exist, Xen.
to threaten violently, Hdt.:—so in Mid., Aeschin.
to hunger one against the other, to have a starving-match, διαπεινᾶμες (doric 1st pl.), with a play on διαπίνομεν, Ar.

sense.gloss: through c. gen. through, by means of c. acc.

entry.sense: through.
WITH GEN.:
of Place or Space:

of motion in a line, through, right through, διὰ μὲν ἀσπίδος ἦλθε ἔγχος Il.; δι’ ἠέρος αἰθέρ’ ἵκανεν quite through the lower air even to the ether, Id.; διὰ πάντων ἐλθεῖν to go through all in succession, Xen.
of motion through a space, but not in a line, all through, over, διὰ πεδίοιο Il.; δι’ ἄστεος Od.
of Intervals of Space, διὰ δέκα ἐπάλξεων at every 10th battlement, Thuc.; διὰ πέντε σταδίων at a distance of 5 stades, Hdt.
of Time:
throughout, during, διὰ παντὸς τοῦ χρόνου Hdt.; δι’ ἡμέρης all day long, Id.; διὰ παντός continually, Aesch.; δι’ ὀλίγου for a short time, Thuc.
of the interval between two points of Time, διὰ χρόνου πολλοῦ or διὰ πολλοῦ χρ. after a long time, Hdt.; διὰ χρόνου after a time, Soph.; χρόνος διὰ χρόνου time after time, Id.
of successive Intervals, διὰ τρίτης ἡμέρης every other day, Hdt.; δι’ ἐνιαυτοῦ every year, Xen.
Causal, through, by
of the Agent, δι’ ἀγγέλων by the mouth of messengers, Hdt.; δι’ ἑρμηνέως λέγειν Xen.
of the Instrument or Means, διὰ χειρῶν Soph.; διὰ χειρὸς ἔχειν in hand, Id.
of the Manner or Way, παίω δι’ ὀργῆς through passion, in passion, Soph.; διὰ σπουδῆς in haste, hastily, Eur.

to express conditions or states, δι’ ἡσυχίης εἶναι to be in a state of quiet, to be tranquil, Hdt.; διὰ πολέμου ἰέναι τινί to be at war with one, Xen.; δι’ ἀπεχθείας ἐλθεῖν τινι to be hated by him, Aesch.; δι’ οἴκτου ἔχειν τινά to feel pity for one, Eur., etc.
WITH ACC.:
of Place, in same sense as διά c. gen.:
through, ἓξ διὰ πτύχας ἦλθε χαλκός Il.
throughout, over, ὤικεον δι’ ἄκριας Od.; δι’ αἰθέρα Soph.
of Time, διὰ νύκτα Il.; διὰ ὕπνον during sleep, Mosch.
Causal:

of Persons, through, by aid of, by means of, νικῆσαι διὰ Ἀθήνην Od.; διά σε by thy fault or service, Soph.: through, by reason of, αὐτὸς δι’ αὑτόν for his own sake, Plat.; διὰ τὴν ἐκείνου μέλλησιν Thuc.
of things, which express the Cause, Reason, or Purpose, δι’ ἐμὴν ἰότητα because of my will, Il.; δι’ ἀχθηδόνα for the sake of vexing, Thuc.; διὰ τοῦτο, διὰ ταῦτα therefore; etc.
WITHOUT CASE as Adv. throughout, Hom.
IN COMPOS.:
through, right through, as in διαβαίνω.

in different directions, as in διαπέμπω:— of separation, asunder, as in Lat. dis-, as in διασκεδάννυμι:— at variance, as in διαφωνέω; or of mutual relation, one with another, as in διαγωνίζομαι, διᾴδω.
of preeminence, as in διαπρέπω, διαφέρω.
completion, to the end, utterly, as in διαμάχομαι (cf. Lat. decertare).
to add strength, throughly, out and out, as in διαγαληνίζω.
of mixture, between, partly, as in διάλευκος.
an experiment, trial, Hdt.
Dep. to make trial or proof of, to have experience of a thing, c. gen., Hdt.; c. acc., Thuc.
to drive through, τι διά τινος Eur.
to send off in different directions, send to and fro, send about or round, Hdt., Thuc.
to send over or across, Ar., Thuc.: to transmit, ἐπιστολήν Id.; so in Mid., Id.
to mourn through, ἐνιαυτόν Plut.
to bring to a conclusion, discuss thoroughly, Eur.; διαπέραινέ μοι tell me all, Id.:— Mid., διαπεράνασθαι κρίσιν to get a question decided, Id.
to take across, ferry over, Plut.: —Pass. to go across, Thuc.:— διεπεραιώθη ξίφη swords were unsheathed, Soph.
to go over or across, ῥοάς, οἶδμα Eur.; δ. πόλιν to pass through it, Ar.; also, διαπερᾶν Μολοσσίαν to reign through all Molossia, Eur.
to pass through, pierce, Id.
trans. to carry over, Luc.
to destroy utterly, sack, lay waste, of cities, Hom.
Dep. to slip away one by one, Dem.
to fly through, Il., Eur.: c. acc., Id., Ar.; διὰ τῆς πόλεως Id.
to fly away, vanish, Eur., Plat.
to fix thoroughly:— Mid., δ. σχεδίας to get rafts put together, Luc.
to leap across, τάφρον Ar., Xen.:—absol. to take a leap, Id.
to make very fat, Theocr.
Pass. to be quite full of, τινός Thuc.
to drink one against another, challenge at drinking, Hdt., Plat.
to sell off, Plut.
to fall away, slip away, escape, Xen.
of reports and rumours, to spread abroad, Id.
to fall asunder, crumble in pieces, Plat.
to fail utterly, go quite wrong, Ar., Aeschin.
to entrust to one in confidence, τί τινι Aeschin.: Pass. to have a thing entrusted to one, Dem.
to distrust utterly, τινι Dem.
to form completely, mould, Plut., etc.
