to make very wide, dilate, Xen.
to interweave, to weave together, plait, Hdt.
metaph., δ. τὸν βίον, Lat. pertexere vitam, to finish the web of one's life, Id.: then, simply, to pass life, live, Ar.
to sail across, Thuc.; εἰς Αἴγιναν Ar.: metaph., δ. βίον to make life's voyage, Plat.
Dep. to spar with, skirmish with, τινι Plut., Luc.
to break or cleave in pieces, Il.
as adj. sailing continually, διάπλουν καθίστασαν λεών they kept them at the oar, Aesch.
as Subst., a voyage across, passage, πρὸς τόπον Thuc.
room for sailing through, passage, δυοῖν νεοῖν for two ships abreast, Id.
to blow through: — Pass., αὔραις διαπνεῖσθαι Xen.
to breathe between times, get breath, Plut.
intr. to disperse in vapour, Plat.
to variegate, adorn, Plut.
to carry the war through, end the war, Lat. debellare, Hdt.; δ. τινι to fight it out with one, Xen.:—Pass., διαπεπολεμήσεται πόλεμος the war will be at an end, Thuc.
to carry on the war, continue it, Id.
to spend some time at war, Plut.
a finishing of the war, Thuc.
to besiege continually, to blockade, Thuc.
Dep. to be a political rival, Aeschin.
to carry the procession to an end, Luc.
a sending to and fro, interchange of messages, negotiation, Thuc.
to work out with labour, Lat. elaboro, Plat., etc.:—Mid. to get worked out, Id., Xen.: —Pass. to be managed, governed, Aesch.
Pass. also, to be much grieved, NTest.
intr. to work hard, toil constantly, Xen., Arist.; οἱ διαπονούμενοι the hardworking, hardy, Xen.
hard labour, exercise, Plat.
of persons, exercised, Plut.; τι Id.
of things, toilsome:— adv. -νως, with toil, Id.
beyond sea, Lat. transmarinus, Aesch., Thuc.
to carry over, set across, Xen.
Pass., with fut. mid. and aor1 pass. διεπορεύθην, to pass across, ἐς Εὔβοιαν Hdt.: c. acc. cogn. to go through, βίον Plat.
to be quite at a loss, Plat.:—so in Mid., with aor. and perf. pass., Id.
to raise an ἀπορία, start a difficulty, Arist.:—so in Mid., Plat.: —Pass. to be matter of doubt or question, Id., Arist.
Il., Thuc.:—Pass. to be utterly ruined, Trag.
to carry over or across a river or strait, Hdt.: to carry a message from one to another, Id.
metaph. to translate, interpret, Plat.
δ. ποταμόν, of ferry-boats, to ply across a river, Hdt.
to send off in different directions, dispatch, Dem.
Dep. to examine thoroughly, Plat.
to gain by trading, NTest.
dispatch of business, Plat.

to pass over, c. gen., διέπρησσον πεδίοιο they made their way over the plain, Il.; also, δ. κέλευθον to finish a journey, Od.:—also of Time, c. part., ἤματα διέπρησσον πολεμίζων went through days in fighting, Il.; διαπρήξαιμι λέγων should finish speaking, Od.

to bring about, accomplish, effect, settle, Hdt.; δ. τί τινι to get a thing done for a man, Id.: —so in Mid., Id.; perf. pass. in mid. sense, Plat., etc.:—strictly in sense of Mid., to effect for oneself, gain one's point, Hdt., Xen.: c. inf. to manage that, Id.
to make an end of, destroy, slay, Lat. conficere, in part. perf. pass. διαπεπραγμένος, Trag.
eminent, distinguished, illustrious, Thuc.; τινί or τι in a thing, Eur.; τὸ δ. magnificence, Thuc.
to appear prominent or conspicuous, to strike the eye, Hhymn.; διαπρέπον κακόν Aesch.
to be eminent above others, c. gen., Eur.
Dep. to send embassies to different places, Xen.
to saw quite through, saw asunder, Ar.:—metaph., διεπρίοντο ταῖς καρδίαις were cut to the heart, NTest.
δ. τοὺς ὀδόντας to gnash the teeth, Luc.
right through, c. gen., Hom.
going through, piercing: neut. as adv., πρὼν πεδίοιο διαπρύσιον τετυχηκώς a hill running far into the plain, Il.
of sound, piercing, thrilling, ἤϋσεν διαπρύσιον he gave a piercing cry, Id.
later as adj., of sound, δ. ὄτοβος Soph.; κέλαδος Eur.
metaph., δ. κεραϊστής a manifest thief, Hhymn.
to stutter much, Luc.
to scare away, startle and strike with panic, fear, Od., Eur.
to open and spread out, to unfold, disclose, Soph., Eur.
a fold, folding leaf, Eur.
to spit upon, τινά Dem.
to spar, fight with, τινί Xen.
Dep.:— to search out by questioning, to find out, τι Plat.; τί τινος something from one, Plut.
red-hot, Anaxag. ap. Xen., Eur.
metaph. hot, fiery, Plat.
to set on fire, Eur., in Mid.
to throw a light over, c. acc., Plut.
to sell publicly, Xen.
to strike through, Hes.
to go across, Thuc.
to walk to and fro, Luc.
fleckt with white, Babr.
to divide by joints, to articulate, Plat.:—Pass., perf. part. διηρθρωμένος well-jointed, well-knit, Id.
to endue with articulate speech, Luc.; Mid., φωνὴν διηρθρώσατο invented articulate speech, Plat.
to complete in detail, Arist.
to reckon up one by one, enumerate, Eur.
to draw distinctions, distinguish, Plat.: —Pass. to be distinguished, Aeschin.
to have full strength, be quite sufficient, Xen., etc.; δ. πρός τινα to be a match for, Luc.
in point of Time, to hold out, endure, last, Aesch.; c. part., δ. πολιορκούμενος Xen.
to supply nourishment, τινί Plut.
quite sufficient, Thuc.
lasting, Dem.:—adv. -κῶς, Sup. διαρκέστατα in complete competence, Xen.
to distribute in various places, dispose, Eur.
to tear in pieces, Il.: to efface, τὰ ἴχνη Xen.
to spoil, plunder, πόλιν Hdt.
to seize as plunder, χρήματα Id.
Pass. to flow all ways, Soph.
to dash in pieces, destroy, Hom.:— Pass., c. fut. mid., to be destroyed, perish, Il.; διαρραισθέντας Aesch.

entry.note: fut. διαρ-ρεύσομαι aor2 δι-ερρύην perf. δι-ερρύηκα
entry.sense: to flow through, Hdt.
to slip through, τῶν χειρῶν Luc.
of a vessel, to leak, Id.
of a report, to spread abroad, Plut.
χείλη διερρυηκότα gaping lips, Ar.
to fall away like water, die or waste away, χάρις διαρρεῖ Soph.; of one diseased, Ar.; of money, Dem.
to break through, cleave asunder, Il. (in Mid.), Hdt., Soph.:—Pass. to burst, with eating, Xen.; with passion, Ar.; διαρρᾰγείης, as a curse, "split you!" Id.:—perf. διέρρωγα, in same sense, Plat.
expressly, distinctly, explicitly, Lat. nominatim, Hhymn., attic
a casting about, Xen.

entry.note: poet. δια-ρίπτω ionic imperf. διαρ-ρίπτασκον fut. ψω attic pres. διαρριπτέω
entry.sense: to cast or shoot through, Od.
to cast or throw about, a dog, to wag the tail, Xen.
to throw about, as nuts or money among a crowd, Ar.
intr. to plunge, Xen.
a scattering, Xen.
that through which something flows, a pipe, πνεύματος διαρροαί the wind- pipe, Eur.
to roar through, διαρροθῆσαι κάκην τινί to inspire fear by clamour, Aesch.
diarrhoea, Thuc.
to whizz through, c. gen., Soph.
flowing away, vanishing, Trag.
intersected by streams, Strab.
rent asunder, Eur.
to cut limb from limb, Aesch.
to suspend, interrupt, Plut.
to separate, Id.
to fawn upon, Xen.
grinning like a dog, sneering, Plut.

entry.sense: to shake violently: to reduce to anarchy, Luc.; διασεσαλευμένος unsteady, Id.
to make quite clear, shew plainly, Eur., Plat.
to make quite clear, Xen.
shaken about, Aeschin.
to shake violently, τι Plat., δ.τῇ οὐρᾷ to wag with the tail, i. e. to keep wagging the tail, Xen.
to confound, throw into confusion, Hdt.
to extort money from a person, NTest.
Pass. to dart through, rush across, c. gen., Il.; c. acc., δ. λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν Id.
to mark out, point out clearly, Hdt., Xen.
absol. to beckon, τῇ χειρί Arist.
clear, distinct: neut. pl. as adv., διάσημα θρηνεῖ Soph.
conspicuous, Plut.
to putrefy, decay, Luc.
the festival of Zeus μειλίχιος, Ar.
to hiss or whistle violently, Arist.
to remain silent, Eur., Xen.
trans. to pass over in silence, Eur.
properly, to dose with chervil (σκάνδιξ): in Com. for διευριπιδίζω, to come Euripides over one (his mother was a herb-seller), Ar.
to dig through, c. gen., Plut.
to scatter abroad, scatter to the winds, disperse, Lat. dissipare, Od., Soph.
to disband an army, Hdt.: Pass. to be dispersed, aor. 1 and perf. part. διασκεδασθέντες, διεσκεδασμένοι Id.
to get quite ready, equip, Luc.:—Pass., perf. part. διεσκευασμένοι dressed, Plut.: —Mid. to prepare for oneself, provide, Thuc.: to equip oneself, Xen.
Mid., διασκευασάμενος τὴν οὐσίαν having disposed of one's property, Dem.
Mid. to set all in order, Plat.
to deck out, Luc.
to disperse and retire each to his quarters (σκηναί), to take up one's quarters, Xen.
to leave a comrade's tent, Id.
one must take up one's quarters, Xen.
to prop on each side, to prop up, Anth.
to leap about or away, Plut.
to look at in different ways, to examine or consider well, Hdt., Eur., etc.; also in Mid., διασκοπεῖσθαι πρός τι Thuc.
absol. to keep watching, Xen.
Dep. to watch as from a σκοπιά, to spy out, Il.:— to discern, distinguish, Id.
to scatter abroad, NTest.
Mid. to jest one with another, pass jokes to and fro, Xen.
to wipe or rinse out, Hdt.
to rub well, Ar.
to polish off with the chisel: metaph., Anth.
Dep. to quibble like a sophist, Ar.
to squander away, Plut.
torn to pieces, Eur.
to rend in sunder or in pieces, Aesch.
a gap, Plut.

entry.note: fut. -σπάσω attic -σπάσομαι aor1 -έσπᾰσα Pass., aor1 -εσπάσθην perf. -έσπασμαι

in military sense, to separate part of an army from the rest, Xen.:—Pass., στράτευμα διεσπασμένον scattered and in disorder, Thuc.;—of soldiers, also, to be distributed in quarters, Xen.
metaph. to distract, throw into disorder, Id.
to scatter abroad, throw about, of money, Hdt.; δ. λόγον Xen.: to squander, Soph.:—Pass. to be scattered abroad, aor2 διεσπάρην [ᾰ], Id.; of soldiers, Thuc.
dispersion; collectively, = οἱ διεσπαρμένοι, NTest.
to do zealously: Pass. to be anxiously done or looked to, τί μάλιστα διεσπούδαστο; Dem., who also uses διεσπούδασται in act. sense.
Dep. to order by rule, regulate, Eur.
to form into separate factions, Arist.
a standing aloof, separation, Hdt.
difference, Plat.:—in Thuc. it has a causal sense, an attempt to set some against others.
divorce, Plut.
separative, causing discord, Plut.
to fortify with a palisade: Mid. διασταυρώσασθαι τὸν ἰσθμόν to have it fortified, Thuc.
to go through or across, c. acc., Eur.
to go one's way, Theocr.
to put asunder, tear open, Plut.
to distinguish, define, τὰ λεγόμενα Plat.; so to determine, Id.
to give express orders, in Mid., NTest.
very narrow, Galen.
starred, δ. λίθοις Luc.
an interval, Plat.
to make firm, Anth.
to gleam through, Ar., Anth.
to stuff in between, Hdt.
Mid. to arrange for oneself regularly, regulate exactly, ἀρχήν Aesch.
a notch or nick, Plut.
to serve as a general, assume his duties, Plut.
trans. to conduct a war to its close, Id.
to turn different ways, to twist about, distort, Xen.:—Pass. to be distorted, Plat.: of persons, to have one's eyes distorted, to get a squint, Ar.
metaph. to distort, pervert, Dem.
distortion, Arist.
twisted, distorted, Hdt., Trag.
to tear in pieces: metaph. to pull to pieces, i.e. to disparage, ridicule, Dem.
to throw about like a ball, Eur.
murderous, Anth.
to overturn utterly, Luc.— Pass. to be disappointed of, τινός Aeschin.
any opening made by violence, a cleft, rocky gorge, Hdt.
to scatter as by a sling:— Pass. to fly in pieces, Xen.
Pass.: to be made like a wasp, be pinched in at the waist, Ar.
to form completely: Pass. to be so formed, Plat.
to cleave or rend asunder, Od., Plat., etc.:—Pass. to be cloven asunder, Il.; of soldiers, to be separated, Xen.
to preserve through a danger, Hdt., Eur.:—Pass. to come safe through, arrive in safety, Thuc., Xen.: to recover from illness, Id.
of things, to preserve, maintain, Eur., Xen.: to keep in mind, Id.:—Mid. to retain, Thuc.
to arrange, Xen.
an ordinance, NTest.
disposition, arrangement, of troops, Hdt., Dem.; of topics, Luc.
to throw into great confusion, confound utterly, Xen.
tension, Plat., etc.

entry.note: attic -ττω fut. ξω Pass., aor1 -ετάχθην perf. -τέταγμαι
entry.sense: to appoint or ordain severally, dispose, Hes., Hdt.:—absol. to make arrangements, Xen.:—Mid. to arrange for oneself, get things arranged, Plat.:—Pass. to be appointed, c. inf., Hdt.
to draw up an army, set in array, Id.: also to draw up separately, Id.:—Mid., διαταξάμενοι posted in battle-order, Ar., Xen.; so in perf. pass. διατετάχθαι, Hdt.
Mid. to order by will, Anth.
to fortify by a ditch, Polyb.
to stretch to the uttermost, τόξον Hdt.: to stretch out, τὰς χεῖρας Xen.
intr. to extend, continue, Arist.
Mid. and Pass. to exert oneself, Xen., etc.; διατεινάμενος at full speed, Id.; with all one's force, Theocr.; διατείνεσθαι πρός τι to exert oneself for a purpose, Xen.
to maintain earnestly, contend for, τι Dem.
in strict sense of Mid. to stretch out for oneself, δ. τὰ βέλεα to have their lances poised, Hdt.; δ. τὸ τόξον to have one's bow strung, Id.
to cut off and fortify by a wall, Ar.
to divide as by a wall, Xen.
a place walled off and fortified, Thuc.
Dep. to mark out, Lat. designare, Hes.
to bring to fulfilment, Il.
to bring quite to an end, accomplish, Eur., Xen.

absol., mostly with a part. added, to continue being or doing so and so, Hdt., Plat.:—but the part. is sometimes omitted, δ. πρόθυμος to continue zealous, Thuc.: also simply to continue, go on, persevere, Plat.: to live on, Id.
continuous, incessant, Soph., Plat.
to cut through, cut in twain, dissever, Il., Hdt.; δίχα δ. Plat.:—metaph. to disunite, Aeschin.
to cut up, Hdt.:—Pass., διατμηθῆναι λέπαδνα to be cut into strips, Ar.
to bore through, make a hole in, τι Hdt.
to melt, soften by heat, Ar.
Pass., with perf. -τέτηκα, to melt away, thaw, Xen.
to watch closely, observe, Plat., etc.
to keep faithfully, maintain, Dem., Arist.
δ. ἑαυτὸν ἔκ τινος to keep oneself from . . , NTest.
a portion plucked off, Anth.
to continue to dishonour, Aesch.
to shake asunder, shake to pieces, Od., Eur.:—fut. mid. in pass. sense, Id.
to shake violently, Id.

to cut in twain, διατμήξας having cut [the Trojan host] in twain, Il.; λαῖτμα διέτμαγον I clove the wave, Od.; ὦλκα δ., of ploughing, Mosch.:—Pass., διέτμαγεν (3rd pl. aor2 for -μάγησαν) they parted, Hom.: they were scattered abroad, Il.
Lat. quamobrem? wherefore
to place separately, arrange each in their own places, dispose, τὸ μὲν ἐπὶ δεξιά, τὸ δ’ ἐπ’ ἀριστερά Hdt.; so Xen., etc.

to manage well or ill, with an adv., κράτιστα διατιθέναι τὰ τοῦ πολέμου Thuc.; of persons, δ. τινὰ ἀνηκέστως to treat him barbarously, Hdt., :—Pass., οὐ ῥᾳδίως διετέθη he was not very gently treated or handled, Thuc.
οὕτω διατιθέναι τινά to dispose one so or so, Plat., etc.
to recite, Id.
Mid. to arrange as one likes, to dispose of, τὴν θυγατέρα Xen., etc.
to dispose of one's property, devise it by will, Plat.: ὁ διαθέμενος the devisor, testator, NTest.
to set out for sale, dispose of merchandise, Hdt., Xen.
to arrange mutually, δ. διαθήκην τινί to make a covenant with one, Ar., NTest.; πρός τινα Id.; ἔριν δ. ἀλλήλοις to settle a quarrel with one, Xen.
a severance, Aesch.
that can be shot across, δ. χώρα a place within arrow-shot, Plut.
piercing, galling, Aesch.; δ. φόβος thrilling fear, Id.; of a trumpet, Id.
pass. pierced, bored through, Soph.
to turn away from a thing:—Pass. with fut. mid., aor2 mid. -ετραπόμην and pass. -ετράπην [ᾰ], to be turned from one's purpose, to be perplexed, Dem.
to sustain continually, Thuc., etc.
to run across or over the sea, Od.
metaph. to run through, τὸν βίον, τὸν λόγον Plat.
absol. to run about, Lat. discurrere, Ar., Theocr.
δ. μέχρι to penetrate to, Plut.
to flee all ways, Il.
a way of spending time: hence, a pastime (pass-time), amusement, Ar., Dem.
serious employment, study, Ar., Plat.,
a way of life, living, δ. ἐν ἀγορᾷ Ar.
in bad sense, a waste of time, delay, Eur.; in pl., Thuc.
to rub between, rub hard, rub away, consume, waste, Hom.:—Pass., διατρῐβῆναι to perish utterly, Hdt.
δ. χρόνον, Lat. terere tempus, to spend time, Id., Xen.: Pass., ἐνιαυτὸς διετρίβη Thuc.

absol. (without χρόνον), to waste time, pass it away, οὐ μὴ διατρίψεις; i. e. make no more delay, Ar.; δ. ἐν γυμνασίοις to pass all one's time there, Id.; δ. μετ’ ἀλλήλων to go on talking, Id.: —hence, to employ oneself on or in a thing, ἔν or ἐπί τινι Plat.; περί τι Id.; c. part., δ. μελετῶν Xen.
also absol. to lose time, delay, Il., Ar., etc.: c. gen., δ. ὁδοῖο to lose time on the way, Od.
to put off by delay, to thwart, hinder a thing, Hom.; δ. Ἀχαιοὺς ὃν γάμον put them off in the matter of her wedding, Od.
one must spend time, Arist.
in three divisions, three ways, Il.
various in dispositions, Eur.
sustenance, support, Xen.
of a horse, to trot, Xen.
bearing grapes in succession, Od.
to gnaw through, τὸ δίκτυον Ar.
to form perfectly; δ. νόμους to give them a lasting form, Luc.: metaph. to imagine, Id.
configuration, Plut.
to shine through:— διαυγάζει ἡμέρα day dawns, NTest.
transparent, Anth.
a runner in the δίαυλος, Pind.

a double pipe:— in the race, a double course, in which the runner ran to the furthest point of the στάδιον, turned the post (καμπτήρ), and ran back by the other side, Pind., Soph., Eur.:—metaph., κάμψαι διαύλου θάτερον κῶλον to run the backward course, retrace one's steps, Aesch.; also, δίαυλοι κυμάτων ebb and flow, Eur.; δισσούς ἂν ἔβαν διαύλους they would twice return, Id.
a strait, Id.
to eat through, Hdt.
to shew through, let a thing be seen through, Theocr.
Pass., aor2 -εφάνην [ᾰ], to appear or shew through, νεκύων δ. χῶρος shewed clear of dead bodies, Il.; of things seen through a transparent substance, Hdt.
to glow, to be red-hot, Od.
metaph. to be proved, shew itself, Thuc.: to be conspicuous among others, Id.
absol. in Act. to shew light through, to dawn, ἡμέρα, ἠὼς διέφαινε Hdt.: metaph. to shine through, Xen.
transparency, Plat.
seen through, transparent, Ar., Plat.
red-hot, Hdt.
metaph. transparent, manifest, distinct, Soph., Plat.:—adv. -νῶς, Thuc., etc.
famous, illustrious, Plat.
to shew light through, to dawn, Hdt.
differently from, at odds with, διαφερόντως ἤ . . , Plat.; c. gen., διαφερόντως τῶν ἄλλων above all others, Id.
absol. eminently, especially, Thuc., etc.

entry.note: fut. -οίσω fut. -οίσομαι aor1 -ήνεγκα ionic -ήνεικα aor2 -ήνεγκον perf. -ενήνοχα
entry.sense: to carry over or across, δ. ναῦς τὸν Ἰσθμόν Thuc.: to carry from one to another, κηρύγματα Eur.:—metaph., γλῶσσαν διοίσει will put the tongue in motion, will speak, Soph.
of Time, δ. τὸν αἰῶνα, τὸν βίον to go through life, Hdt., Eur.; absol., ἄπαις διοίσει Id.: —in Mid., διοίσεται will pass his life, Soph.; σκοπούμενος διοίσει Xen.
to bear through, bear to the end, σκῆπτρα Eur., etc.
to bear to the end, go through with, πόλεμον Hdt., Thuc.:— to endure, support, sustain, Lat. perferre, Soph., Eur.
to carry different ways, to toss or cast about, Id.
to spread abroad, Dem.
to tear asunder, Lat. differre, Aesch., Eur.
δ. τὴν ψῆφον to give one's vote a different way, i. e. against another, Hdt.: also simply, to give each man his vote, Eur., Thuc.
intr. to differ, make a difference, Pind., Eur.: c. gen. to be different from, Id., Ar.

impers. διαφέρει, it makes a difference, πλεῖστον δ., Lat. multum interest, βραχὺ δ. it makes little difference, Eur.; οὐδὲν διαφέρει Plat.;—c. dat. pers., διαφέρει μοι it makes a difference to me, Id.; αὐτῷ ἰδίᾳ τι δ. he has some private interest at stake, Thuc.
τὸ δ., τὰ διαφέροντα, the difference, the odds, Id., etc.; but τὰ δ. also simply points of difference, Id.
to be different from a man, i. e. to surpass, excel him, c. gen., Id., Plat.:—in a compar. sense, διέφερεν ἀλέξασθαι ἤ . . it was better to defend oneself than . . , Xen.
to prevail, of a belief, Thuc.
Pass. to differ, be at variance, περί τινος Hdt.; τινὶ περί τινος Thuc.: οὐ διαφέρομαι, = οὔ μοι διαφέρει, Dem.
to flee through, get away from, escape, τινά or τι Hdt., Plat.:—absol. to escape, Hdt., Thuc.; διαφεύγει οὐδὲ νῦν it is not now too late, Dem.
to escape one, escape one's notice or memory, Plat., etc.
an escaping, means of escape, Thuc.
to spread abroad, NTest.

entry.note: fut. -φθερῶ epic -φθέρσω perf. -έφθαρκα and διέφθορα Pass., fut. -φθᾰρήσομαι ionic -φθερέομαι ionic 3rd pl. plup. διεφθάρατο
entry.sense: to destroy utterly, Il., Hdt., attic: to make away with, kill, destroy, ruin, Soph., etc.; δ. χέρα to weaken, slacken one's hand, Eur.: to disable a ship, Hdt.:—absol. to forget, Eur.
in moral sense, to corrupt, ruin, Aesch., Plat., etc.:— esp. to corrupt by bribes, Hdt., Dem.: to seduce, Lys.
οὐδὲν διαφθείρας τοῦ χρώματος having changed nothing of his colour, Plat.

Pass. to be destroyed, crippled, disabled, Hdt.; τὴν ἀκοὴν διεφθαρμένος deaf, Id.: τὰ σκέλεα δ. with their legs broken, Id.; τὰ ὄμματα δ. blind, Plat.; τὰς φρένας Eur.; τὸ φρενῶν διαφθαρέν loss of one's mind, Id.
perf. διέφθορα is intr. in Hom., to have lost one's wits;— but in attic trans., Soph., Eur.
destruction, ruin, blight, death. Hdt., attic
in moral sense, corruption, τῶν νέων Xen.
in pass. sense, ἰχθύσιν διαφθ. a prey for fishes, Soph.; πολεμίοις δ. Eur.
a corrupter, τῶν νόμων Plat.:—as fem. in Eur.
to dismiss, disband, Xen.
to dispute earnestly, Plut.
Dep. to strive emulously, Plut.
to burn through, Plut.:—metaph. to inflame, Id.
to drive mad: Pass., perf. inf. διαπεφοιβάσθαι Soph.
to wander or roam continually, Hdt., Ar.:—of reports, to get abroad, Plut.
difference, distinction, Thuc.
variance, disagreement, Hdt., Eur.
to spread abroad, Od.
to carry away, carry off, Thuc.; esp. as plunder, Hdt.
to plunder, οἶκον, πόλιν Hdt.:—Pass., διαφορεῖσθαι ὑπό τινος Dem.
to tear in pieces, Eur.:—Pass., Hdt.
to carry across from one place to another, Thuc.
a plundering, Plut.
different, unlike, Hdt., Plat., etc.
differing or disagreeing with another, c. dat., Eur.; in hostile sense, at variance with, τινι Hdt., Plat.; c. gen., δ. τινος one's adversary, Dem.
distinguished, remarkable, Plut.
making a difference to one, advantageous, profitable, Thuc.
as Subst., διάφορον, ου, τό,
a difference, Hdt., Eur., Dem.
what concerns one, a matter of importance, Thuc., Dem.
a difference, disagreement, Id.
in reference to money-matters, one's balance, expenditure, Id.
adv. -ρως, with a difference,variously, Thuc.:— δ. ἔχειν to differ, Plat.
excellently, Dem.
difference, Plat.
a partition-wall, barrier, Thuc.
the midriff, diaphragm (Homer's φρένες) , Plat.
to barricade, Plut.
to speak distinctly, tell plainly, Hom.
to let through, let pass, Ar., Thuc.
a refuge, means of escape, τινος from a thing, Plat.
any natural break, a joint, suture, division, Plat., Xen.
to be watched, preserved, Xen.
to watch closely, guard carefully, Hdt., etc.; Mid. to guard for oneself, Eur.
to observe closely, τὰ μέτρα Hdt.
to observe, maintain, τοὺς νόμους Plat.; δ. τὸ μή, c. inf., to guard against being . . , Id.

entry.note: Pass. with aor2 act. διέφῡν perf. διαπέφῡκα
entry.sense: of time, to intervene, Hdt.
to be closely connected with, τινος Plut.
to blow in different directions, disperse, Plat.
to blow through, Luc.
to draw off liquids continually: Pass., of wine, Od.
to draw away, tear away, πολλὸν διήφυσε σαρκὸς ὀδόντι Id.
to be dissonant, Plat.:—generally, to disagree, Id.; τινι with one, Id.
discordant, Luc.
to clear completely, Plut.
Dep. to withdraw, Xen.
to loosen, unbar, Eur.
to make supple by exercise, Xen.
to gape wide, yawn, Ar.
to pass the winter, Thuc., Xen.
to have in hand, conduct, manage, administer, Oratt.:—Pass., Xen.
management, administration, Thuc.
to choose between two persons or things by show of hands, to elect, Dem.; so in Mid., Xen.
election, Dem., Aeschin.
to pour different ways, to disperse, Hdt.:— to cut up a victim, Hom.
to dissolve, break up, destroy, Xen.
metaph. to confound, τὰ βεβουλευμένα Hdt.
Pass. to be poured from one vessel into another, Id.
to run through, spread about, Thuc.
to be dissolved, fall away, of a corpse, Hdt.: to disperse, of soldiers, Xen.
metaph. to be or become diffuse or dissipated, Plat.
διαχοῦν τὸ χῶμα to complete the mound, Hdt., διαχώννυμι later in Strab.
Dep., c. dat. rei, to use constantly or habitually, Hdt.; τῇ ἀληθείῃ δ. to speak the truth, Id.; δ. ἀρετῇ to practise virtue, Id.
like Lat. utor, of passive states, to meet with, suffer under, συμφορῇ, αὐχμῷ Id.
c. acc. pers. to use up, consume, destroy, Id., Thuc.
Pass., perf. -κέχρημαι, to be lent out to different persons, Dem.
interwoven with gold, Dem.
diffusion, Plat.; δ. λαμβάνειν to be spread out, Plut.
merriment, Id.
to go through, pass through: impers., κάτω διεχώρει αὐτοῖς they were suffering from diarrhoea, Xen.
of coins, to be current, Luc.
to separate, Xen.
a cleft, division, Luc.
mostly in pres., to brush or blow away, Ar.
to deceive utterly, Dem.:— Pass. to be deceived, mistaken, Id.; δ. τινος to be cheated of, deceived in a person or thing, Xen., Dem.; περί τι or τινι Arist.
Dep. to vote in order with ballots (ψῆφοι, calculi), Thuc.
to decide by vote, Dem.
a voting by ballot, Xen.
to cause to crumble away, Plut.
to whisper among themselves, Luc.
to cool, refresh:—to dry and clean, ναῦς Thuc.; of misers bringing out their hoards, Xen.
on two legs, Eur.
a double-edged lance, halbert, Plut.
two-pointed, Eur., Anth.
with two eye-balls, Theocr.
speaking two languages, Lat. bilinguis, Thuc.
as Subst., δίγλωσσος, ὁ, an interpreter, Plut.
twice-born, of Bacchus, Anth.
twin: double, Eur.
a lesson, Ar.
one must teach, Plat.
apt at teaching, NTest.
of things, taught, learnt, Soph.
that can or ought to be taught or learnt, Pind., Soph., etc.
of persons, taught, instructed, τινός in a thing, NTest.
teaching, instruction, Eur.
a teaching-place, school, Thuc., Plat., etc.
teaching, instruction, education, Lat. disciplina, Xen., Plat., etc.; διδασκαλίαν ποιεῖσθαι or παρέχειν to serve as a lesson to one, Thuc.
the rehearsing of a dramatic chorus, Plat.: also, the drama itself, Plut.
fit for teaching, capable of giving instruction, instructive, Plat., Xen.
a thing taught, a science, art, lesson, Hdt., Xen.
in pl. a teacher's fee, Plut.
a teacher, master, Hhymn., Aesch., etc.: εἰς διδασκάλου (sc. οἶκον) φοιτᾶν to go to school, Plat.; διδασκάλων or ἐκ διδασκάλων ἀπαλλαγῆναι to leave school, Id.; ἐν διδασκάλων at school, Id.
a dramatic poet was called διδάσκαλος because he taught the actors, Ar.

to teach (i. e. instruct) a person, or teach a thing, Hom., etc.: c. dupl. acc., σε . . ἱπποσύνας ἐδίδαξαν they taught thee riding, Il.; to teach one a thing, Hom., etc.; also, δ. τινὰ περί τινος Ar.:—c. acc. pers. et inf. to teach one to be so and so, Od.; c. inf. only, δίδαξε βάλλειν taught him how to shoot, Il.;—also with inf. omitted, διδάσκειν τινὰ ἱππέα [sc. εἶναι] to train one as a horseman, Plat.; so, δ. τινὰ σοφόν, κακόν Eur.:— Mid. to teach oneself, learn, Soph.: but the usual sense of the Mid. is to have another taught, of a father, to have his son taught, Plat., etc.:—Pass. to be taught, to learn, c. gen., διδασκόμενος πολέμοιο trained in war, Il.; also c. acc., Id., etc.; c. inf., δεδιδαγμένος εἶναι Hdt.; διδάσκεται λέγειν ἀκοῦσαί θ’ Eur.
διδάσκειν is used of dramatic Poets, who originally taught the actors their parts, Hdt., attic

entry.etym: epic redupl. form of δέω, as τίθημι of *θέω
entry.sense: to bind, fetter, Hom.
worth two drachms: with pay of two drachms a day, Thuc.
as Subst. δί-δραχμον, ου, τό, a double-drachm or half-shekel, paid to the temple-treasury at Jerusalem, NTest.
touching both the men, Aesch.
bearing twins, Theocr., Anth.

entry.etym: only in dual nom. and pl. dat.
entry.sense: twin-brothers, twins, Il.
twin-born, Eur.
double, twofold, twain, Hom., attic; διδύμη ἅλς, i. e. the Pontus and Bosporus, Soph.
twin, Id., Eur.:—as Subst., δίδυμοι twins, Il., Hdt.; also δίδυμα, τά, Id.
of persons, in Act. to give bail for another, and in Mid. to take bail for him, Isocr.:— Pass. to be bailed by any one, Thuc.

entry.etym: Redupl. from Root ΔΟ, Lat. do, dare.
entry.sense: Orig. sense, to give, τί τινι Hom., etc.; in pres. and imperf. to be ready to give, to offer, Id.
of the gods, to grant, κῦδος, νίκην, and of evils, δ. ἄλγεα, ἄτας, κήδεα Id.; later, εὖ διδόναι τινί to provide well for . . , Soph., Eur.
to offer to the gods, Hom., etc.
with an inf. added, δῶκε τεύχεα θεράποντι φορῆναι gave him the arms to carry, Il.; διδοῖ πιεῖν gives to drink, Hdt., etc.

Prose phrases, δ. ὅρκον, opp. to λαμβάνειν, to tender an oath; δ. χάριν, = χαρίζεσθαι, as ὀργῆι χάριν δούς having indulged his anger, Soph.;— λόγον τινὶ δ. to give one leave to speak, Xen.; but, δ. λόγον ἑαυτῶι to deliberate, Hdt.
c. acc. pers. to give over, deliver up, Hom., etc.
of parents, to give their daughter to wife, Id.
in attic, διδόναι τινά τινι to grant any one to entreaties, pardon him, Xen.:— διδόναι τινί τι to forgive one a thing, remit its punishment, Eur., Dem.
διδόναι ἑαυτόν τινι to give oneself up, Hdt., etc.
δ.δίκην, v. δίκη IV. 3.
in vows and prayers, c. acc. pers. et inf. to grant, allow, bring about that, Hom., Trag.
seemingly intr. to give oneself up, devote oneself, τινί Eur.
a giving of bail, Dem.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use, διοράω being used instead
entry.sense: to see thoroughly, discern, Ar., Plat.; διιδεῖν περί τινος Id.
perf. δίοιδα, inf. διειδέναι to know the difference between, to distinguish, Eur., etc.: to decide, Soph.
distinctly, Xen.
to go to and fro, roam about, Ar.; of a report, to spread, Plut.
c. acc. to go through, go through a thing, to narrate, describe, discuss, Plat.

entry.note: in Hom. also δια-εῖπον The fut. is δι-ερῶ aor1 pass. δι-ερρήθην.
entry.sense: to say through, tell fully or distinctly, Hom., Soph.: to interpret a riddle, Id.
to speak one with another, converse, διαειπέμεν ἀλλήλοισιν Od.
to keep asunder, separate, Il., Hdt., Thuc.
seemingly intr., to lie between, Xen.
to question closely, Hom., Plat.
to draw across, τὰς νέας τὸν ἰσθμόν Hdt.
to pass or draw through, Xen.
dissembling with one's guests, Ar.
an evasion, Plut.
to run through, Plut.
to break or burst through, Luc.
to go through with, Xen.
to pass out through, pass quite through, c. acc., Hdt.:— to cross over, Aesch.
to pass by, overlook, Ar.
to sail out through, c. acc., Hdt.: absol. to sail out, Id.
in naval tactics, to break the enemy's line by sailing through it, Id., Thuc.
a sailing across or through, passing across or through, Hdt.
a breaking the enemy's line in a sea-fight, Id., Thuc.
prep. through and out of, c. gen., Hom.
to slip out through, c. acc., Plut.
a passage for the stream to escape, Hdt.
to escape completely, Plut.

entry.etym: strengthd. for ἐκχέω Aretae. Cur. M. Ac. 2.5.

entry.sense: a driving through: a charge or exercise of cavalry, Xen.

entry.note: fut. διελάσω attic διελῶ aor1 διήλᾰσα
entry.sense: to drive through or across, c. gen., τάφροιο διήλασεν ἵππους Il.
to thrust through, λαπάρης διήλασεν ἔγχος Id.
δ. τινὰ λόγχῃ to thrust one through with a lance, Plut., Luc.
intr. (sub. ἵππον) to ride through, charge through, Xen.
to refute utterly, Plat.
to draw asunder, widen, Plat.
to pull through a thing, c. gen., Ar.
to keep on drinking, Id.
to sell to different buyers, or sell in lots, Lat. divendere, Eur., Ar.:—metaph. to sell, betray, τινά Soph.
to shew through, Luc.

entry.etym: as if from an Act. δίημι = δίω
entry.sense: to flee, speed, πεδίοιο over the plain, Il.; δίεσθαι to hasten away, Id.
to fear, c. inf., Aesch.
one must excel, Luc.
to live out the year, Hdt.
a looking through entrails, Comic word for sharp-sightedness, Ar.
to rush forth, Theocr.
to go out through, pass through, Il., Hdt.
to go through in detail, recount in full, relate circumstantially, Id., Plat., etc.; δ. περί τινος to go through by way of examining, Eur.
to drive, ride, march through, absol., Hdt.; c. acc. loci, δ. τὰς πύλας Id.
to refute utterly, Luc.
to unroll, untie, Hdt.
to learn by close questioning a person, τινά τι Il.
to go through, pass through, τὸ χωρίον Hdt.
to go through, go completely through, πάντας φίλους Eur., etc.: c. part., δ. πωλέων to be done selling, Hdt.
to go through in succession, διὰ πάντων δ. τῶν παίδων, i. e. killing them one after another, Id.; διὰ πασῶν τῶν ζημιῶν, i. e. trying one after another, Thuc.
to go through in detail, recount in full, Hdt., etc.
intr. to be past, gone by, of time, Id.
to be gone through, related fully, Dem.
to let pass through, Hdt.
intr. (sub. αὑτόν), of a river, to empty itself, Thuc.
detailed, Plut.
a way out through, an outlet, passage, channel, Hdt.; διέξοδοι ὁδῶν passage-ways, Id.
a pathway, orbit, of the sun, Id., etc.
an issue, event, Id.
a detailed narrative, description, Plat.
to finish the web, Plut.
to keep the feast throughout, Thuc.
to manage an affair, order, arrange, Il.; δ. τὰ πρήγματα Hdt.
Dep. to make an end of, kill, destroy, Lat. conficere, Hdt., Soph.:—plup. in pass. sense, διέργαστο τὰ πράγματα, actum erat de rebus, Hdt.; so in aor1 διεργασθεῖτ’ ἄν Eur.
Mid. to lean upon, τινι Eur.
to row about, χερσὶ δ. to swim, Od.
c. acc., δ. τὰς χέρας to swing them about, Eur.
to search through, examine closely, Plat.: also in Mid., Id.
a scout or vidette, Xen.
to strive with one another:— Mid. to contend with, τινί Plut.
an interpreter, NTest.
to interpret, expound, NTest.
fresh, active, nimble, of men, Od.; διερῷ ποδί with nimble foot, Id.

after Hom. = liquidus, wet, liquid, Aesch.; of birds, which float through the air, Ar.; δ. μέλεα of the nightingale'snotes, Lat. liquidae voces, Id.; δ. πώγων of one drowned in the sea, Anth. (The sense of liquid is not in Hom.: his usage seems to connect it with δί-ω, to run, flee.)
to creep or pass through, πῦρ δ., of the ordeal of fire, Soph.
to keep off, to hinder, Plut.

entry.note: fut. διελεύσομαι but attic fut. δίειμι attic imperf. διῄειν aor2 διῆλθον
entry.etym: fut. διελεύσομαι, but δίειμι is attic fut.,διῄειν imperf.
entry.sense: Dep. to go through, pass through, absol. or c. gen., Il., Soph.:—c. acc., also, Il., Thuc., etc.
to pass through, complete, Hdt., Plat., etc.
of reports, βάξις διῆλθ’ Ἀχαιούς Soph.; absol., λόγος διῆλθε went abroad, spread, Thuc., Xen.
of pain, to shoot through one, Soph.; of passion, Id.; ἐμὲ διῆλθέ τι a thought shot through me, Eur.
to go through in detail, tell all through, Aesch., Thuc.
intr. of Time, to pass, elapse, Hdt., Dem.; so, σπονδῶν διελθουσῶν Thuc.; but, διελθὼν ἐς βραχὺν χρόνον having waited, Eur.

entry.etym: διερῶ serving as fut., διείρηκα as perf., of διαγορεύω
entry.sense: to say fully, distinctly, expressly, Plat., Dem.:—Pass., aor1 διερρήθην, perf. διείρημαι, Plat.
to cross-question, τινα Plat.
to ask constantly or continually, Dem.
to eat through, δ. τὴν μήτραν, of young vipers, Hdt.
prudently, Xen.
lasting through the year, Lat. perennis, Thuc.
of or lasting two years, Hdt.:— διετές, Lat. biennium, ἐπὶ διετὲς ἡβᾶν to be two years past puberty, Aeschin.
a space of two years, NTest.
to set right, amend, Luc.
to separate accurately, arrange carefully, Xen.
Dep. to take good heed to, beware of, be on one's guard against, c. acc. or gen., Plat.
one must take heed to, Plat.
to lay asleep, τὸν βίοτον Eur.
to preserve decorum, Plut.
to continue prosperous, Dem.
trans. to keep apart or separate, Lat. distinere, Hdt., Plut.
to keep off, Id.
intr. to go through, hold its way, of arrows and lances, Il.:— to extend or reach, Hdt.
to stand apart, be separated or distant, Theogn., Thuc.; διέχοντες ἤεσαν they marched with spaces between man and man, Id.; σταδίους ὡς πεντήκοντα διέχει is about 50 stades wide, Xen.
of Time, to intervene, Soph.
to differ, Arist.
altogether falsely, Strab.

entry.etym: Prob. redupl. from the same Root as ζητέω.
entry.sense: Dep.
to seek out, look for, τινά Il.

to seek for, seek after a thing, Od.; ἐέδνοισιν διζήμενος seeking to win her by gifts, Id.; δ. τὸ μαντήϊον to seek out, seek the meaning of, Hdt.; ἀγγέλους δ. εἰ . . to inquire of them whether . . , Id.:—c. inf. to seek, desire to do, Id.; c. acc. et inf. to demand or require that, Id.
double-yoked, ἵπποι Il.: double, Anth.
to be in doubt, at a loss, Il., Orac. ap. Hdt. (Prob. from the same Root as δίς; — but)
Mid. δίζομαι, = δίζημαι, Theocr., Bion.
with two lives, Sisyphus, who returned from Hades, Anth.
Dep. to set out in detail, describe in full, Thuc., etc.
narrative, statement, Plat.
to strain through, filter, Lat. percolare, Plat.
to wash out, cleanse, purge, Hdt.
intr., of the liquid, to percolate, Id.
to extend or reach from one place to another, Hdt., Thuc.
c. acc. to go through, pervade, Aesch., Soph.
to pass over, Aesch.
to stay through the day, pass the day, Plat., Xen.

continuous, unbroken, Lat. continuus, Od.; νώτοισι διηνεκέεσσι with slices cut the whole length of the chine, Il.:—adv. διηνεκέως, continuously, from beginning to end, Lat. uno tenore, Od.: also distinctly, positively, Id., Hes.
blown through, wind-swept, Soph.
to make dry land of, Anth.
double, μελάθρων διῆρες an upper story, upper room, Eur.
to transmit the sound of, τι Plut.
between two seas, where two seas meet, NTest.
two-edged, ξίφος Aesch.
two-throned, Ἀχαιῶν δ. κράτος the two-throned might of the Achaeans, i. e. the brother-kings, Aesch.
Bacchus-born, Anth.
the dithyrambic poet who taught his own chorus, Ar.
the dithyramb; a kind of lyric poetry, Hdt., Ar., etc.: its proper subject was the birth of Bacchus, Plat.
with two doors, Plut.: with two leaves, of tablets, Luc.
a double thyrsus, Anth.
to drive or thrust through a thing, c. gen., Od., Eur.; also c. dupl. acc., λόγχην δ. στέρνα Id.
to let people go through a country, give them a passage through, Xen., Dem.:— c. gen., ξυμφορὰς τοῦ σοῦ διῆκας στόματος didst let them pass through thy mouth, gavest utterance to them, Soph.
to send apart, to dismiss, disband, Xen.
to dissolve: in Mid., διέμενος ὄξει having diluted it with vinegar, Ar.
to direct by steering, Anth.
Dep. to go through, penetrate, Plut.:— to reach, with missiles, Thuc.
in speaking, to go through, recount, Il.
of Zeus, Plat.
fallen from Zeus, i. e. from heaven, of streams, fed or swollen by rain, Hom.
generally, divine, bright, pure, Eur.
hovering in air, Hhymn.
one must learn, Eur.
to set apart, to place separately, separate, Thuc., Dem.
to set one at variance with another, τινά τινος Ar., Thuc.; δ. τὴν Ἑλλάδα to divide it into fractions, Hdt.
Mid. and Pass., with aor2, perf., and plup. act., to stand apart, to be divided, Il.; θάλασσα διΐστατο the sea made way, opened, Id.; τὰ διεστεῶτα chasms, Hdt.
of persons, to stand apart, be at variance, Il., Thuc.; διέστη ἐς ξυμμαχίαν ἑκατέρων sided with one or the other party, Id.:—simply to differ, be different, Xen.
to part after fighting, Hdt.
to stand at certain distances or intervals, Id.; of soldiers, δ. κατὰ διακοσίους Thuc.
aor1 mid. is trans. to separate, Plat., Theocr.
Dep. to lean upon, rely on, τινι Aeschin.
to affirm confidently, τι Plat.; δ. τι εἶναι Id.
one must go through, Plat.
to judge, to give judgment on a thing, decide or determine a point, Il., etc.

c. acc. cogn., δίκας δ., to adjudge a penalty, Hdt.; δ. φυγήν τινι to decree it as his punishment, Aesch.; δ. φόνον ματρός to ordain her slaughter, Eur.; δ. τοῦ ἐγκλήματος [sc. δίκην] Xen.:—Pass. to be decided, Thuc.
to pass judgment on, condemn, Soph.
φόνον δ. to plead in a case of murder, Eur.
c. dat. pers. to decide between persons, judge their cause, Τρωσί τε καὶ Δαναοῖσι δικαζέτω Il.; ἐς μέσον ἀμφοτέροισι δικάσσατε Id.: —Pass. to be judged or accused, Xen.
absol. to be judge, give judgment, Il.:— to sit as judges or jurymen, Dem.

Mid. of the culprit, to plead one's own case, defend one's right, have one's case tried, go to law, Od., etc.: —δίκην δικάζεσθαί τινι to go to law with one, Plat.; πρός τινα Thuc.; τινος or περί τινος for a thing, Dem.
righteous judgment, NTest.
Dep. to plead one's cause before the judge, Aeschin.
in Act., οἱ δικαιολογοῦντες advocates, Luc.
strict in public faith, Pind.
to act honestly, Arist.
a just or honest act, Arist.
just or honest dealing, Arist.
in Hom. and early writers,
of persons, observant of custom and social rule, well-ordered, civilised, Od.; so, δικαίη ζόη a regular way of living, Hdt.:—adv., δικαίως μνᾶσθαι to woo in due form, decently, Od.
observant of right, righteous, Hom., etc.:—so of actions, in accordance with right, righteous, Id.
later usage:
of things, even, well-balanced, ἅρμα δίκαιον Xen.:— regular, exact, rigid, ὀργυιαὶ δίκαιαι Hdt.; τῷ δικαιοτάτῳ τῶν λόγων to speak quite exactly, Id.; πάντα δικαίως τετήρηται Dem.
right, lawful, just, τὸ δίκαιον right, opp. to τὸ ἄδικον, Hdt., etc.; also, a right, a lawful claim, Thuc., etc.:—adv. -ως, rightly, justly, Hdt., etc.
of persons, as well as things, like Lat. justus, meet, right, fitting, Aesch.; ἵππον δ. ποιεῖσθαί τινι to make a horse fit for another's use, Xen.
real, genuine, true, Dem., συγγραφεύς Luc.:—adv. -ως, really and truly, Soph.
fair, moderate, like μέτριος, Thuc.: —δικαίως with reason, Soph., Thuc.

in Prose, δίκαιός εἰμι with inf., δίκαιοί ἐστε ἰέναι you are bound to come, Hdt.; δ. εἰμι κολάζειν I have a right to punish, Ar.; δίκαιοί εἰσι ἀπιστότατοι εἶναι they have reason to be most distrustful, Thuc.; δ. ἐστιν ἀπολωλέναι dignus est qui pereat, Dem.:—we should say δίκαιόν ἐστι, which also occurs.
righteousness, justice, Theogn., Hdt., etc.; and
= δικαιοσύνη, Xen., Plat., etc.
to set right: Pass., δικαιωθείς proved, tested, Aesch.

to hold or deem right, think fit, demand, c. inf., Hdt., etc.; inf. omitted, as οὕτω δικαιοῦν (sc. γενέσθαι) Id.:— to consent, δουλεύειν Id.; οὐ δ. to refuse, Thuc.:—c. acc. pers. et inf. to desire one to do, Hdt.
to do a man right or justice, to judge, i. e.,
to condemn, Thuc.: to chastise, punish, Hdt.
to deem righteous, justify, NTest.
an act by which wrong is set right: —a judgment, punishment, penalty, Plat.
a plea of right, Thuc.: justification, NTest.: and
an ordinance, decree, Id.
a setting right, doing justice to: punishment, Thuc.
a deeming righteous, justification, NTest.
a demand of right or as of right, a just claim, Thuc.
judgment of what is right, Id.
a house of correction, Plat.
of persons, skilled in law, versed in pleading, lawyer-like, Plat., Xen., etc.
of things, belonging to trials, judicial, Ar., Plat., etc.: like a lawyer's speech, tedious, Id.
two-headed, (δίς, κάρηνον) Batr., Anth.
one who administers law, a judge, Hom.
a court of justice, Hdt., Ar., etc.: —ὑπὸ δ. ἄγειν, ὑπάγειν τινά Hdt.; εἰς δ. ἄγειν Plat.
the court, i. e. the judges, Ar., Dem.
a judge, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
at Athens, the δικασταί, like the Roman judices, were more like our jurymen (the presiding judge being ὁ κριτής), Soph., etc.
δ. αἵματος an avenger, Eur.
of or for law or trials, practised in them, Xen.
as Subst., τὸ δ. the juror's fee, at first one obol, then three obols, Ar.
a she-judge, Luc.
to throw, cast, Aesch., Eur.
to strike, Pind., Eur.
a mattock, a two-pronged hoe, Soph., Eur.
a digger, Luc.
two-horned, two-pointed, Anth.
two-horned, Hhymn.
custom, usage, αὕτη δίκη ἐστὶ βροτῶν this is the custom of mortals, Od.; ἡ γὰρ δίκη ἐστι γερόντων Id.:—acc. δίκην as adv., after the manner of, c. gen., δίκην ὕδατος Aesch., Plat.
right as dependent on custom, law, right, Hom., etc.
δίκη ἐστι, like δίκαιόν ἐστι, Aesch.: —δίκῃ duly, rightly, Il., Trag.; κατὰ δίκην Hdt.; μετὰ δίκης Plat.; πρὸς δίκης Soph.
a judgment, δίκην εἰπεῖν to give judgment, Il.: pl. righteous judgments, Hom.
after Hom., a lawsuit, properly, a private suit or action, opp. to γραφή (a public suit or indictment), Plat., etc.
the trial of the case, πρὸ δίκης Thuc.

the penalty awarded by the judge, δίκην τίνειν, ἐκτίνειν Hdt., Soph.; δίκην or δίκας διδόναι to make amends, suffer punishment, Lat. poenas dare, Hdt., attic; δίκας δοῦναι, also, to submit to trial, Thuc.: —δίκας λαμβάνειν is sometimes = δ. διδόναι, Lat. dare poenas, Hdt., Dem.; but also like Lat. sumere poenas, to inflict punishment, take vengeance, λαβεῖν δίκην παρά τινος Id.:—also, δίκας or δίκην ὑπέχειν to stand trial, Hdt., Soph.; δίκην παρέχειν Eur.: —δίκην ὀφλεῖν ὑπό τινος to incur penalty, Plat.; δίκην φεύγειν to be the defendant in the trial (opp. to διώκειν to prosecute), Dem.: —δίκας αἰτέειν to demand satisfaction, τινός for a thing, Hdt.; δίκην τίσασθαι, v. τίνω II: —δίκας διδόναι καὶ λαμβάνειν παρ’ ἀλλήλων to have their causes tried, of subject-states whose causes were tried in the courts of the ruling state, Id.
bringing justice, avenging, Ζεύς Aesch.; ἡμέρα δ. the day of vengeance, Id.:—as Subst. an avenger, Id.
a little trial, Ar.
double-folding, of doors or gates, in pl., Od.; rarely in sg., Theocr., Anth.
the composition of lawspeeches, Isocr.
a pleader, advocate, Plut.
to get up a lawsuit, Ar.
two-pointed, two-peaked, Luc.
two-peaked, of Parnassus, Eur.
a pitch-fork, Luc.
co-mate in power, Soph.; δικρατεῖς λόγχαι double-slaying spears, Id.
forked, cloven, bifurcate, Xen.
double-beating, κῶπαι Eur.
of ships, double-oared or with two banks of oars, Xen.
δ. ἁμαξιτός a road for two cars, Eur.
the dictatorship, Plut.
the Roman dictator, Polyb.
to cast the net, Anth.
a fisherman, Anth.
Artemis as goddess of the chase, Hdt., Eur.
woven in meshes, σπεῖραι δ. the net's meshy coils, Soph.
a casting-net, a net, Od., Aesch.: a hunting-net, Hdt., Ar.:—metaph., δ. ἄτης, Ἅιδου Aesch.
Pass. to be caught in a net, Babr.
an unknown Libyan animal, Hdt.
a pair of sculls, Luc.
two-oared, σκάφος Eur.
to say again, repeat, Xen.
repetition, Xen.
double-tongued, doubtful, NTest.
double-pointed, two-fold, Aesch.
double-crested, of Parnassus, Soph.
worth or costing two minae, διμναίους ἀποτιμήσασθαι to value at two minae, Hdt.
a double share, Xen.: double pay, Id.
divided in two, double, Aesch.
= foreg., Aesch.
a whirling round, in dancing, Xen.
to whirl or twirl round, or spin round, Hom.: to drive round a circle, Il.:—Pass. to whirl or roll about, Hom.: of a river, to eddy, Eur.: to whirl round in the dance, Xen.
Pass., also, to roam about, Lat. versari, Od.
intr. in Act., just like Pass. to whirl about, of dancers or tumblers, Il.; of a pigeon circling in its flight, Id.; generally, to roam about, Hom.; δινεύειν βλεφάροις to look wildly about, Eur.
whirling, eddying, Hom.
rounded, Mosch.
a whirlpool, eddy, Lat. vortex, Il., etc.
a whirlwind, Ar.
generally, a whirling, rotation, Id., Plat.: metaph., ἀνάγκης δίναι Aesch.
whirled round, Anth.
a whirling, rotation, Ar.
a round area, where oxen trod out the corn, a threshing-floor, Xen.
a large round goblet, Ar.
eddying; τὰ δινώδη eddies, Plut.
to thresh out on the δῖνος (II),Hes.
turned, rounded, Hom.; νώροπι χαλκῷ δινωτήν [sc. ἀσπίδα] covered all round with brazen plates, Il.
hurled by Zeus, Soph., Eur.
giving birth to Zeus, Eur.
sprung from Zeus, of kings and princes, ordained and upheld by Zeus, Hom.; of gods, Trag.
to travel through, c. acc., Plut.
a way through, thoroughfare, passage, Hdt., etc.; ἄστρων δίοδοι their pathways, Aesch.; δ. αἰτεῖσθαι, to demand a passport or safe-conduct, Ar.
adv. sent from Zeus, by his will or favour, Il., Trag.
to open, Ar., Soph., Eur.

entry.note: imperf. διῴκουν fut. -ήσω aor1 διῴκησα perf. διῴκηκα Pass., aor1 διῳκήθην perf. διῴκημαι
entry.sense: properly to manage a house: then generally, to manage, control, govern, administer, τὴν πόλιν Thuc., etc.; esp. of financial matters, Dem.:—Mid. to manage after one's own will and pleasure, τὰ πράγματα Id.; perf. pass. (in same sense), Id.
to provide, furnish, Id.
to inhabit distinct places, Plat.:— Mid. to live apart, Xen.
government, administration, τῆς πόλεως Plat., etc.; esp. the treasury-department, Dem.; ὁ ἐπὶ τῆς διοικήσεως the controller, treasurer, ap. Dem.
one of the lesser Roman provinces, Cic.
as an Eccles. division, a diocese.
to cause to live apart, Dem.: —Pass., Xen.
a dispersion, Plut.
to build across, wall off, Thuc.
one must move round, Eur.
to shoot an arrow through, c. gen., Od.
absol., καί κεν διοϊστεύσειας thou mightest reach it with an arrow, i. e. but a bow-shot off, Id.
to go through, c. acc., Aesch.
absol. to wander about, Hhymn.
Dep.:— to be quite gone by, of time, Hdt.: of persons, to be clean gone, to have perished, Lat. periisse, Soph., Eur.
to be gone through, ended, Soph., Eur.
a cessation, Thuc.
to slip through, to give one the slip, c. acc., Ar.: absol. to slip away, Luc.
to destroy utterly, bring to naught, Soph., Plat., etc.:—Pass., with fut. -ολοῦμαι, perf. -όλωλα, to perish utterly, come to naught, Trag., Thuc.
to blot out of one's mind, forget, Soph.
to be always evenminded, Plut.
a braggart of the deme Diomeia, Ar.
of or like Diomedes, ἡ Διομήδεια λεγομένη ἀνάγκη, i. e. absolute, fatal necessity, Plat.
Jove-counselled; in Hom. as prop. n. Diomedes.
to swear solemnly, to declare on oath that . . , c. inf. fut., Soph.:—Mid. διόμνυμαι, fut. -ομοῦμαι, Id., Plat., etc.; διομνύμενος on oath, Dem.
to make an agreement, undertake, Xen.:—Pass. to be agreed on, Plat.:—Mid. to agree mutually, to agree upon certain points, take as granted, concede, δ. τι εἶναι Id.; περί τινος Id.
a convention, Polyb.
one must concede, Plat.
to distinguish by a name, Plat.
Pass. to be widely known, Isocr.
to keep the Dionysia: hence to live extravagantly, Luc.
belonging to Dionysus, Thuc., Arist.
sc. ἱερά, τά the feast of Dionysus or Bacchus at Athens, of which there were four: viz.
τὰ κατ’ ἀγρούς or τὰ μικρά, in Poseideon (December).
τὰ ἐν Λίμναις or τὰ Λήναια (in the suburb Λίμναι, where the Λήναιον stood), in Gamelion (January).
τὰ Ἀνθεστήρια in Anthesterion (February).
τὰ ἀστικά or τὰ κατ’ ἄστυ, also called τὰ μέγαλα or simply τὰ Διονύσια, in Elaphebolion (March), when Athens was full of strangers, and new Dramas were performed.
Dionysus, Od., etc.: v. Βάκχος.
son of Zeus, Anth.
δι’ ὅπερ, = διό, Thuc.
that fell from Zeus, Eur.
to be in charge of a ship, ap. Dem.
a ruler, commander, Aesch., Eur.
to watch accurately, spy about, Il.: to look into, στέγος Soph.
a spy, scout, Il.
a looker through, ὦ Ζεῦ διόπτα! says Dicaeopolis, holding up a ragged garment to the light, Ar.
= διοπτήρ., Eur.
an instrument for measuring heights, a Jacob's staff, Polyb.
of, belonging to the use of the διόπτρα, Strab.
to see through, see clearly, Xen.
Conjunct., for δι’ ὅ wherefore, on which account, Lat. quapropter, quocirca, quare, Thuc., Plat., etc.
two fathoms long, high, Hdt.
to judge rightly, Eur.
to make quite straight, set right, amend, δ. ἔριν to make up a quarrel, Eur.:—Mid. to amend for oneself, διορθοῦσθαι περί τινος to take full security for . . , Dem.
a making straight, amendment, Plut.
a making straight, restoration, reform, Arist.
a corrector, reformer, Plut.
to draw a boundary through, divide by limits, separate, Hdt., Plat.
to distinguish, determine, define, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
to determine, declare, Soph.; c. inf. to determine one to be so and so, Dem.; with inf. omitted, μικρὸν καὶ μέγαν διώρισαν με Soph.:—Mid., with perf. pass. in mid. sense, Dem.
absol. to draw distinction, lay down definitions, Id.:—so in Mid., Ar., etc.
to remove across the frontier, to banish, Eur., Plat.: generally, to carry abroad, Eur.; δ. πόδα to depart, Id.
distinction, Plat.
a through-cut, canal, Thuc.
to dig through or across, τάφρον Od.; τοῖχον δ. = τοιχωρυχέω, Hdt., Ar.
Dep. to dance a match with one, τινί Ar.
given by Zeus, Aesch.
a sign from Zeus, an omen from the sky, of a sudden storm, Ar.
the temple of the Dioscuri, Thuc.
the sons of Zeus and Leda, Castor and Pollux, Hhymn.
the constellation named from them, the Twins, Lat. Gemini, Luc.

entry.note: δῖος, δῖα, δῖον (fem. δῖος and δία in Eur.), contr. for δίϊος:
entry.sense: god-like, divine, Il.; δῖα γυναικῶν noblest of women, Od.:—also worthy, trusty, the swineherd, Ib.; of whole nations or cities, Hom.; of a noble horse, Il.
of things, like θεῖος, θεσπέσιος, ἱερός, divine, wondrous, Hom.
in literal sense, of or from Zeus, Aesch.
Conjunct. for διὰ τοῦτο ὅτι, for the reason that, since, Hdt., etc.
indirect, wherefore, for what reason, μανθάνειν διότι Id.
= ὅτι, that, Id., Dem.
cherished by Zeus, of kings and nobles, Hom.
Pass. to be watered by canals (ὀχετοί), Strab.
to trouble or annoy exceedingly, Dem.
with two children, Aesch.
δ. θρῆνος a dirge chanted by one's two children, Id.
two palms broad, Xen.
brandished with both hands, two-handed, Eur.: —δίπαλτος ἄν με φονεύοι would kill me each with two spears, Soph.
two cubits long, broad, etc., Hdt., etc.
double, poet. for διπλάσιος, Anth.
to double, Eur.
intr., τὸ δίπλαζον κακόν the twofold evil, Soph.
twofold, double, in double folds, Il.
as Subst., δίπλαξ, a double-folded mantle, Hom.
in pl. ship-planks (doubled one over the one below), Aesch.
to double, Xen.
Pass. to become twofold, Thuc.
twofold, double, twice as much as, twice as many as, as long as, etc., Hdt., etc.; as comp. foll. by ἤ . . , Id.; or c. gen. twice the size of, Id.
as Subst., διπλάσιον, ου, τό, as much again, Lat. duplum, Id.
διπλασίαν (sc. ζημίαν), ap. Dem.
adv. -ως, doubly, Thuc., Aeschin.
two πλέθρα long or broad, Luc.
twice, twice over, Soph., Eur.
a double cloak, like δίπλαξ, Anth.

twofold, double, Lat. duplex, of a cloak, Hom.; ὅθι διπλόος ἤντετο θώρηξ where the cuirass met [the buckle] so as to be double, Il.:— παῖσον διπλῆν (sc. πληγήν), Soph.; διπλῆ ἄκανθα spine bent double by age, Eur.; διπλῇ χερί by mutual slaughter, Soph.
in pl., = δύο, Aesch., Soph.
double-minded, treacherous, Plat., Xen.
to double, Xen.:—Pass., of a sword, to be bent double, Plut.
to repay twofold, NTest. Hence
a doubled or folded paper, a letter of recommendation, diploma, Cic., Plut.
a compounding of words, Arist.
two feet long, broad, etc., Xen.
an ancient festival of Zeus at Athens, Ar.
like the Διπόλια, i. e. obsolete, out of date, Ar.
with two roads or openings, Eur.
between two rivers, Eur.
two-footed, Lat. bipes, Aesch., Plat., etc.
δίπους, the jerboa, which springs from its two hind feet, like the kangaroo, Hdt.
two feet long, Lat. bipedalis, Plat.

double-folded, doubled, Od.; δ. δελτίον a pair of tablets, Hdt.:—neut. pl. as adv., δίπτυχα ποιήσαντες [τὴν κνῖσαν], having doubled the fat, i. e. putting one layer of fat under the thighs (μηροί) and another over them, Il.,
twofold, Lat. geminus, Eur.: and in pl. = δισσοί, two, Id.
double-gated, with two entrances, Soph.
δίπυλον, ου, τό, a gate at Athens, Plut.
with double flame, Ar.
with two poles, i. e. three horses, Aesch.
twice young, Anth.
with two wives, Anth.
twice dead, Od.
Pass. to be pitched, Eur.
to pitch the quoit (δίσκος), play at quoits, Od.:—Pass. to be pitched, Anth.
a thing thrown, Eur.
two-sceptred, Aesch.
the quoit-thrower, a famous statue by Myron, Luc.
a sort of quoit, made of stone, Od.
anything quoit-shaped, a trencher, Anth.:— a mirror, Id.
a quoit's cast, as a measure of distance, Il.
bringing the discus, Luc.
twenty thousand, Hdt., etc.
inseparable Suffix, signifying motion to a place, like -δε, as in ἄλλυδις, οἴκαδις, χαμάδις
an old nom. for Ζεύς which appears in the oblique cases Διός, Διΐ, Δία, and Lat. Dis, Dies-piter, Djovis.
twice, doubly, Lat. bis, Od., Hdt., attic
joint-ruling, Soph.
two-fold, double, Hdt.
in pl. two, Id., Trag., etc.
metaph. double, divided, doubtful, Aesch., Soph.
to be in doubt, hesitate, Plat.
of two verses, Anth.
as Subst., δίστιχον, ου, τό, a distich, Id.
in pairs, two together, Soph.
double-mouthed, with two entrances, Soph.; δίστομοι ὁδοί branching roads, Id.
of a weapon, two-edged, Eur.
of two syllables, Luc.
two thousand, Hdt.:—sg. with collective nouns, δισχιλίη ἵππος 2000 horse, Id.
worth or weighing two talents, Hdt.: costing two talents, Dem.
to strain off, τι NTest.
to awake from sleep, Luc.
to fill up by weaving, Luc.
two-fold, double, Lat. bifarius, Hdt.
in pl. = δύο, Id.
to search after, Il., Hes.:—ionic διφέω Anth.
a searcher, χρυσοῦ after gold, Anth.
a prepared hide, tanned skin, piece of leather, Hdt.; opp. to δέρρις (an undressed hide), Thuc.:— διφθέραι were used for writing-material in ancient times, before papyrus came in, Hdt.
a leathern garment such as peasants wore, Ar., Plat.
a wallet, bag, Xen.
in pl. skins used as tents, Id.
one clad in leather, Luc.
of tanned leather, Xen.
a seat, chair, Theocr.
chariot-driving, Xen.
a charioteer, Soph.
to drive a chariot, Eur.; αἴγλαν ἐδίφρευε drove his beaming car, Id.
to drive a chariot through, τὸν οὐρανόν, of the Sun, Soph.
a charioteer, Trag.
of a chariot: neut. pl. as adv., δίφρια συρόμενος dragged at the chariot wheels, Anth.
divided in mind, distraught, Aesch.
the chariot-board, on which two could stand, the drive (ἡνίοχος) and the combatant (παραιβάτης), Hom.
the war-chariot itself, Il.:—in Od. a travelling-chariot.
a seat, chair, stool, Hom., attic
to draw a chariot, Anth.
to carry in a chair or litter:— Pass. to travel in one, Hdt.
to carry a campstool, Ar.
carrying a camp-stool; of the female μέτοικοι, who carried seats for the κανηφόροι, Ar.
carrying another upon a δίφρος, Plut.
of double form, Hdt., Soph.
to divide in two, Plat.: δ. τινὰ κατά τινος to divide one against another, NTest.
a double chalcos, = 1/4 of an obol, Anth.
adv. in two, asunder, Od., etc.:—generally, apart, aloof, Hdt., etc.
metaph. in two ways, at variance or in doubt, Hom., etc.
prep. with gen. apart from, Aesch., Soph.:— differently from, unlike, Id.; τοῦ ἑτέρου from the other, Thuc.
πόλεως δ. against the will of, Soph.
besides, except, like χωρίς, Aesch.
a divider, Arist.
cloven-hoofed, Hdt., Eur.
δίχηλον, ου, τό, a forceps, pincers, Anth.
in two, asunder, Aesch., Plat., etc.
in two ways, Id., Dem.
dividing the month in twain, c. gen., of the moon, Eur.
twofold, double, divided, Il.
δ. δεδαίαται they are parted in twain, Od.; δ. κραδίη μέμονε my heart is divided, Il.
to differ in opinion, Xen.
divided between two opinions, Plut.
adv. from both sides, both ways, Aesch., Thuc., etc.
holding 2 χοίνικες, near 3 pints, Ar.
the fullness of the moon, Plut.
dividing the month, i. e. at or of the full moon, Hhymn., Plut.
double-speaking, λέγειν διχόμυθα to speak ambiguously, Eur.
discord, disagreement, Plat.
broken in twain, Eur.
oscillating: adv. -πως, waveringly, doubtfully, Aesch.
a standing apart, dissension, Hdt.: sedition, Solon, Theogn.
to stand apart, disagree, Aesch.; πρός τινα Eur.
to cut in two, cut in twain, Plat., NTest.
cut in half, divided equally, Arist.
at variance, discordant, Aesch.
two-coloured, Luc.
adv. doubly, in two ways, Aesch.
thirsty, Batr.
thirst, Il., etc.; ποτοῦ for drink, Plat.
to thirst, διψάων [ᾱ] Od.; of the ground, to be thirsty, parched, Hdt.
metaph. to thirst after a thing, c. gen., Plat.: later c. acc., Anth., NTest.; c. inf. to long to do, Xen.
thirsty, athirst, and of things, thirsty, dry, parched, Trag.
double-minded, NTest.
at Athens, the allowance of two obols to each citizen during the festivals, to pay for their seats in the theatre, Xen.
a pursuit, chase, Aesch., Eur.
the chase, Xen.
pursuit, persecution, harassing, Aesch., Eur.
with thrilling anguish, Soph.
to push asunder, tear away, Il., Eur.
to thrust through, Plut.
Mid. to push asunder for oneself, force one's way through, break through, c. acc., Hdt., Xen.
to push from oneself, push one another away, of seamen keeping ships from collision, Thuc.:— to drive back, repel, repulse, Hdt., Eur.:—absol. to get rid of danger, Hdt.
to reject, Lat. respuere, Id., Thuc.:—absol. to refuse, Hdt.
a pushing about, a scuffle, Plat.
to be pursued, Hdt., Ar.
διωκτέον, one must pursue, Plat.
a pursuer, Babr.
to pursue aperson, to chase, hunt, Il., etc.:—so in Mid., διώκεσθαί τινα πεδίοιο to chase one over or across the plain, Hom.: — to be a follower of a person, attach oneself to him, Xen.
to pursue an object, seek after, Od., etc.; δ. τὰ συμβάντα to follow or wait for the event, Dem.
to drive or chase away, banish, Od., Hdt.

of the wind, to drive a ship, of rowers, to impel, speed on her way, Od.; of a chariot, to drive, Orac. ap. Hdt.; δ. πόδα to urge on, Aesch.:—then, intr. to drive, drive on, Il.: to gallop, speed, run, Aesch.

as law-term, to prosecute, bring an action against a man, ὁ διώκων the prosecutor (opp. to ὁ φεύγων the defendant), Hdt., etc.; ὁ διώκων τοῦ ψηφίσματος he who impeaches the words of the decree, Dem.; c. gen. poenae, θανάτου or περὶ θανάτου δ. τινά, Lat. capitis accusare, Xen.: but c. gen. criminis, to accuse of, to prosecute for, δ. τινὰ τυραννίδος Hdt.; δειλίας Ar.; φόνου Plat.; but, φόνον τινὸς δ. to avenge another's murder, Eur.
with out-stretched arms, Anth.
far-sounding, enormous, immense, Plat.
an oath taken by both parties before the trial came on, Oratt.
bound by oath, Lat. juratus, c. inf., Soph.
with two names, or, of two persons, named together, Eur.
（διά) far-famed, Plut.
urging on the way, Anth.
horse-driving, Anth.
chase, pursuit, of persons, Thuc.
pursuit of an object, Plat.
as law-term, prosecution, Dem., etc.
to run away, take to flight, flee, like δίεμαι Il.
to be afraid, δίε ποιμένι λαῶν μήτι πάθηι Id.
Causal in Mid., subj. δίωμαι, δίηται, δίωνται, opt. δίοιτο, inf. δίεσθαι, to drive away, chase, put to flight, Hom., Aesch.:—simply to drive horses, Il.
to pursue, give chase, ἐπί τινα Aesch.: δ. λάχος to pursue, discharge an office, Id.
a trench, conduit, canal, Hdt., Thuc.; κρυπτὴ δ. an underground passage, Hdt.
a digging through, Dem.
a pushing off, delaying, Arist.
two-eared: two handled, Plat.
a taming, breaking, ἵππων Il.
a tamer, ἵππων Hhymn.:— fem., νὺξ δμητεῖρα θεῶν Il.
a female slave taken in war, Il.:— then, generally, a female slave, serving-woman, Lat. ancilla, Hom., Trag.
in servile condition, βρέφος Anth.
a slave taken in war, Od.:— then, generally, a slave, Id., Soph., Eur.; epic dat. pl. δμώεσσι Od.
to shake violently, fling down, Il.; τὰ σὰ ῥάκεα δνοπαλίξεις "wrap thy old cloak about thee, " Od.
dark, dusk, murky, Hom., Trag.
darkness, dusk, gloom, Simon., Aesch.
it seemed, Hom.; ὡς ἄν σοι πλήμνη δοάσσεται ἱκέσθαι (epic subj. for -ηται) till the nave appear to graze, Il.: cf. δέατο.
that which seems to one, an opinion, dogma, Plat.
a public decree, ordinance, Xen., Dem.
to decree, δ. τινὰ καλήν to declare her beautiful, Anth.
in Pass., of persons, to submit to ordinances, NTest.
a small abscess, boil, Ar.
a pestle-maker, Plut.
a pestle, Ar., etc.
doubt, perplexity, ἐν δοιῇ Il.
two, both, Il., Hes., etc.: neut. δοιά as adv. in two ways, in two points, Od.
two-fold, double, Anth.
bearing twins, Anth.
= δοιοί, of which it is properly the dual, = δύο, indecl., Hom.
to keep an eye upon, watch narrowly, Il., Pind., Eur.

= videor mihi, to think, suppose, imagine, expect, c. acc. et inf., δοκέω νικησέμεν Il.; οὔ σε δοκέω πείθεσθαι Hdt.; τεκεῖν δράκοντ’ ἔδοξεν she thought a serpent bare young ones, Aesch.; ἔδοξα ἰδεῖν, Lat. visus sum videre, methought I saw, Eur.; ἀείδειν δοκῶ I think to sing, Aesch.
absol. to have or form an opinion, περί τινος Hdt.; in parenthetic phrases, ὡς δοκῶ Trag.; πῶς δοκεῖς; how think you? Eur.
δοκῶ μοι in attic, just like δοκεῖ μοι, as Lat. videor mihi for videtur mihi, I seem to myself, methinks, c. inf., Hdt., etc.; also, I am determined, resolved, c. inf., Ar.
c. inf., also, to seem or pretend to be doing, Lat. simulo, or with a negat. to seem or pretend not to be doing, Lat. dissimulo; ἤκουσά του λέγοντος, οὐ δοκῶν κλύειν Eur.
= videor, to seem to one, δοκέεις δέ μοι οὐκ ἀπινύσσειν Od., etc.
absol. to seem, as opp. to reality, οὐ δοκεῖν, ἀλλ’ εἶναι θέλει Aesch.
to seem good, Lat. placere, εἰ δοκεῖ σοι ταῦτα Id.

impers., δοκεῖ μοι much in the same sense as δοκῶ μοι (supr. I. 3), it seems to me, meseems, methinks, ὥς μοι δοκεῖ εἶναι ἄριστα Il., etc.:—in decrees and the like, ἔδοξε τῆι βουλῆι, placuit senatui, Ar., Thuc., etc.; τὸ δόξαν the decree, Hdt.; τὰ δόξαντα Soph.; παρὰ τὸ δοκοῦν ἡμῖν Thuc.:—so in Pass., δέδοκται, Lat. visum est, Hdt., Trag., etc.
acc. absol. δόξαν, when it was decreed or resolved, δόξαν αὐτοῖς ὥστε διαναυμαχεῖν (i. e. ὅτε ἔδοξεν αὐτοῖς) Thuc.; so, δεδογμένον αὐτοῖς Id.

to be thought or reputed so and so, ἄξιοι δοκοῦντες Id.; οἱ δοκοῦντες εἶναί τι men who are held to be something, men of repute, Plat.; so οἱ δοκοῦντες alone, Eur.; τὰ δοκοῦντα, opp. to τὰ μηδὲν ὄντα, Id.; also in Pass., οἱ δεδογμένοι ἀνδροφόνοι those who have been found guilty of homicide, Dem.
a vision, fancy, Eur.; οἱ δοκήμασιν σοφοί the wise in appearance, Id.
opinion, expectation, Id.
a vision, fancy, Aesch.
wise in one's own conceit, Ar.
an opinion, belief, conceit, fancy, Hdt., Soph.; δ. ἀγνὼς λόγων ἦλθε a vague suspicion was thrown out, Id.
an apparition, phantom, Eur.
good report, credit, Id., Thuc.
to assay or test metals, to see if they be pure, Isocr., etc.
of persons, to put to the test, make trial of, scrutinise, Hdt., Thuc.: —then, to approve, Id., Plat., etc.; c. inf., ἐκπονεῖν ἐδοκίμαζε he approved of their working, Xen.
at Athens, to approve as fit for an office, and in Pass. to be approved as fit, Plat., etc.; c. inf., ἱππεύειν δεδοκιμασμένος Xen.
to examine and admit boys to the class of ἔφηβοι or ἔφηβοι to the rights of manhood; and in Pass. to be so admitted, Ar., etc.; ἕως ἀνὴρ εἶναι δοκιμασθείην Dem.
c. inf. to think fit to do, or with negat. to refuse to do, NTest.
an assay, examination, scrutiny:
of magistrates, to see if they fulfil the legal requirements, Plat., etc.
δ. τῶν ἐφήβων, before admission to the rights of manhood, Dem.
δ. τῶν ῥητόρων, a process to determine the right to speak in the ἐκκλησία or law-courts, Aeschin.
an assayer, scrutineer, Plat., Dem.
an approver, panegyrist, Id.
a test, means of testing, Plat., NTest.
a proof, test: tried character, NTest.
assayed, examined, tested, properly of metals, Dem.
generally,
of persons, approved, esteemed, notable, Lat. probus, Hdt.; δοκιμώτατος Ἑλλάδι most approved by Hellas, Eur.
of things, excellent, notable, considerable, Hdt.
adv. -μως, really, truly, Aesch., Xen.
a bearing-beam, in the roof or floor of a house, Od.: generally, a balk or beam, Il., Thuc.: the bar of a gate or door, Ar.
deceitful, deceptive, treacherous, Hdt., Soph., etc.
stealthy of foot, Soph.
crafty, deceitful, treacherous, Od., Trag.
crafty of mind, Aesch., Eur.
to deal treacherously with one, NTest.
with a long tube or socket, Od.
with tall spear, Il.
long-oared, of a ship, Od.; of men, using long oars, Id.
prolix writing, Anth.
long-necked, Il.
to run the δόλιχος, Aeschin.
running the long course, Plat., Xen.
epith. of ἔγχος, casting a long shadow; or for δολιχ-όσχιος (ὄσχος) long-shafted, Il.
long, Hom.: neut. δολιχόν as adv., Il., Plat.
the long course, opp. to στάδιον, Plat., Xen.
subtle, wily, Od.
of things, craftily contrived, Eur.
crafty of counsel, wily, Hom.
subtle-speaking, or conveyed in crafty speech, Soph.
subtlety, craft, Theogn.
weaving wiles, Sapph., Arist.
treacherous, ensnaring, Soph.
properly, a bait for fish, Od.: then, any cunning contrivance for deceiving or catching, as the Trojan horse, the robe of Penelope Id.:—generally, any trick or stratagem, Il.; in pl., wiles, Id.
guile, craft, cunning, treachery, Lat. dolus, Hom., Trag.
to murder by treachery, Dem.
slaying by treachery, Aesch.
wily-minded, Hhymn.
planning craft, wily-minded, Hom.
craft, subtlety, wiliness, Il.
to beguile, ensnare, take by craft, Hes., Hdt., attic
to disguise, Soph.
a trick, deceit, Aesch.
a secret weapon, poniard, stiletto, Plut.
artful-looking, treacherous, Soph.
a tricking, Xen.
for building, Anth.
home, homeward, Hom.; ὅνδε δόμονδε to his own house, Od.
Lat. domus:
a house, Hom., etc.: also part of a house, a room, chamber, Od.:— hence in pl. for a house, Hom., Trag.
the house of a god, a temple, Hom., Trag.
of animals, a sheep-fold, Il.: a wasps' or bees' nest, Id.
κέδρινοι δόμοι a closet or chest of cedar, Eur.
the house, i. e. the household, family, Trag.:—also one's father's house, Aesch.
a layer or course of stone or bricks in a building, διὰ τριήκοντα δόμων πλίνθου at every thirtieth layer of brick, Hdt.
shaking the house, Aesch.
Dep. to fowl with reed and birdlime, Anth.
a thicket of reeds, Il.
= δόναξ, Anth.
of reed, Anth.
reed-cutting, pen-making, Anth.
reedy, Eur.; δόλος δ., of a reed covered with birdlime, Anth.
producing reeds, Theogn.
green with reeds, Eur.

entry.etym: from δονέω, "a reed shaken by the wind, " cf. ῥίψ from ῥίπτω
entry.sense: a reed, Hom.; δόνακες καλάμοιο reed- stalks, Hhymn.
anything made of reed,
the shaft of an arrow, Il.
a shepherd's pipe, Aesch., Theocr.
a fishing-rod or limed twig (cf. δονακόεις), Anth.
the bridge of the lyre, Ar.
to shake, of wind, Il.; δ. γάλα to shake it, as to make butter, Hdt.
to drive about, Lat. agitare, Od., Pind.:—Pass., ἡ Ἀσίη ἐδονέετο Asia was in commotion, Hdt.; αἰθὴρ δονεῖται Ar.
an agitation, waving, δένδρου Luc.

to think, imagine, suppose, fancy, conjecture, c. acc. et inf., Aesch., etc.; inf. omitted, πῶς ταῦτ’ ἀληθῆ δοξάσω; how can I suppose this to be true? Id.:—Pass., δοξάζεται (sc. εἶναι) is supposed to be, Plat.
c. acc. cogn., δόξαν δοξάζειν to entertain an opinion, Id.
absol. to hold an opinion, Soph., Thuc.
to magnify, extol, Id.
a notion, true or false: and so,

expectation, ἀπὸ δόξης otherwise than one expects, Hom.; παρὰ δόξαν ἤ . . Hdt.; opp. to κατὰ δόξαν, Plat., etc.; ἀπὸ δόξης πεσέειν, Lat. spe excidere, Hdt.; δόξαν παρέχειν τινί to make one expect that, c. inf., Xen.
an opinion, judgment, Pind., attic
like δόκησις, a mere opinion, conjecture, Aesch., etc.; δόξῃ ἐπίστασθαι to imagine, suppose (but wrongly), Hdt.:—also, a fancy, vision, dream, Aesch., Eur.

the opinion which others have of one, estimation, reputation, credit, honour, glory, Lat. existimatio, Solon., Aesch., etc.; δόξαν φέρεσθαι, ἔχειν Thuc., etc.; τινός for a thing, Eur.:—rarely of ill repute, Dem.
the estimate popularly formed of a thing, Id.
of external appearance, glory, splendour, effulgence, NTest.
an opinion, notion, conjecture, Thuc., etc.:— a fancy, Eur.
matter of opinion, conjectural, Plat.
to court popularity, Plut.
thirst for popularity, Plut.
mad desire for fame, Plut.
a would-be philosopher, Anth.
perf. δεδόξωμαι: Pass.:— to have the character or credit of being, c. inf., Hdt.
conceit of wisdom, Plat.
wise in one's own conceit, Plat.
a skin, hide, Theogn., Hdt.
a fighting with spears, Plut.
of a spear's thickness, Xen.
wooden, Anth.
captive of the spear, taken in war, Hdt., Eur.; ionic δουριάλωτον λέχος, of Tecmessa, Soph.
bride of battles, i. e. causing war by marriage, or wooed by battle, of Helen, Aesch.
taken by the spear, Eur.
slain by the spear, Aesch.
spear-headed, Aesch.
won by the spear, Eur.: Hom. has ionic fem. δουρικτητή.
won by the spear, Soph., Eur., δουρίληπτος, Soph.
raging with the spear, Eur.
raging with the spear, Aesch.
master of the spear, Eur.
wielding the spear, ἐκ χερὸς δοριπάλτου, i. e. on the right hand, Aesch.
fallen by the spear, Eur.
toiling with the spear, Aesch., Eur.
scattered by the spear, Anth.
mighty with the spear, Aesch.
crowned for bravery, Anth.
shaken by battle, Aesch.
pierced by the spear, Aesch.
bold in war, Anth.
of an antelope, Theophr.
dice made of the vertebrae of an antelope, Anth.
a kind of deer (so called from its large bright eyes), in Greece, the roe-deer, Eur., Xen.; in Syria and Africa, the gazelle, Hdt. so, δόρξ, δορκός, Eur., etc.; ζορκάς, Hdt.
a leathern bag or wallet, Od.
to take supper, Hom.
supper-time, evening, Ar., Xen.
the eve of a festival, Hdt.
in Hom. the evening meal, whether called dinner or supper, Lat. coena:—later, generally, a meal, Hhymn.
a kind of halbert, Plat.
a spear-friend, i.e., properly, one who having been captive to one's spear becomes one's friend; then generally, a firm friend, Aesch., Soph.: as adj., δόμοι δορύξενοι Aesch.; ἑστία Soph.
a maker of spears, Plut., δορυξός Ar.
a stem, tree, Od.:—commonly a plank or beam, Hom.; δόρυ νήϊον a ship's plank, Id.:— hence,
a ship is called δόρυ, like Lat. trabs, Aesch., Eur.

the shaft of a spear, Il.: then, generally, a spear, pike, Hom., etc.; εἰς δόρυ ἀφικνεῖσθαι to come within a spear's throw, Xen.; ἐπὶ δόρυ to the spear-side, i. e. the right hand, opp. to ἐπ’ ἀσπίδα, Id.:—also, the pole of a standard, Id.
metaph., δουρὶ κτεατίζειν to win wealth by the spear, il.; δορὶ ἑλεῖν Thuc.; in Trag. to express an armed force.
μόχθων δορυσσοήτων, of the toils of battle, Soph.
charging with the lance, Hes., Theogn., δορυσσοῦς, Soph.
to attend as a bodyguard, τινα Hdt., Thuc.: generally, to keep guard over, Dem.:—Pass. to be guarded, Id.
δ. τινι to serve as guard, Xen.
a body of guards, Luc.
guard kept over, τινός Xen.
spear-bearing, Aesch.
as Subst. a spearman, pikeman, Xen.
δορυφόροι, οἱ, the body-guard, of kings and tyrants, Lat. satellites, Hdt., etc.:—metaph., ἡδοναὶ δ. satellite pleasures, Plat.
a giving, Hdt., etc.
a gift, Hom., etc.
to be given, Hdt.
δοτέον, one must give, Id.
a giver, dispenser, Il., Aesch.
to make a slave, treat as such: metaph. to bring into subjection, NTest.
servitude, slavery, bondage, Hdt., etc.
in collect. sense, the slaves, slave-class, Id.
slavish, servile, Od., Theogn., attic
a service, Eur.
a slave, Soph.
one must be a slave, Eur.
to be a slave, τινί to one, Plat., etc.; παρά τινι Dem.; c. acc. cogn., δουλείαν δ. Xen.
to serve or be subject to, opp. to ἄρχω, Hdt., etc.; τῆι γῆι δ. to be a slave to one's land, i. e. submit to indignities that one may keep it, Thuc.
of or for a slave, servile, Xen., Plat.: adv. -κῶς, Xen.
slavish, servile, δούλιον ἦμαρ the day of slavery, Il.: δ. φρήν a slave's mind, Aesch.
a slavish spirit, Plat.
befitting a slave, servile, Hdt., Xen., etc.

properly, a born bondman or slave, opp. to one made a slave (ἀνδράποδον), Thuc.; then, generally, a bondman, slave, Hdt.: Hom. has only the fem. δούλη, ἡ, a bondwoman:—χρημάτων δ. slave to money, Eur.
as adj., δοῦλος, η, ον, slavish, servile, subject, Soph., etc.
τὸ δοῦλον = οἱ δοῦλοι, Eur.: also = δουλεία, Id.
slavery, slavish work, Od., Aesch., Eur.
enslaved, τινι Eur.
to make a slave of, enslave, Hdt., attic:—Pass. to be enslaved, Hdt., Thuc.:—Mid., with perf. pass. to make one's slave, make subject to oneself, enslave, Thuc., etc.
enslaving, subjugation, Thuc.
to sound heavy or dead, δούπησεν πεσών with a thud he fell, Il.; δουπεῖ χεὶρ γυναικῶν falls with heavy sound upon their breast, Eur.
a clatterer, Anth.
any dead, heavy sound, a thud, Il.; of the distant din of battle, the sound of footsteps, of the measured tread of infantry, the hum of a multitude, the roar of the sea, Hom.: rare in Trag.
entry.etym: The form γδουπέω, connects the word with κτύπος.

entry.sense: of planks or beams of wood, ἵππος δ. the wooden horse, Od.
a spear's throw off or distant, only in neut. as adv., Il.
famed for the spear, Hom.
fixed on spears, Aesch.
wood-cutting, Anth.
a case or stand for spears, Od.
cutting wood, Anth.
ionic for δοχεῖον, a holder: μέλανος δ. an ink- horn, Anth.
a receptacle, Eur.
a reception, entertainment, NTest.
the space contained in a hand's breadth, the same as παλαστή, Ar.
across, athwart, aslant, like πλάγιος, Lat. obliquus, Il., Eur.
with slanting, nodding plume, Aesch.
Pass. to turn sideways, δοχμωθείς, of a boar turning to rip up his enemy, Hes.; so of Hermes turning to dart through the key-hole, Hhymn.
Lat. obliquus, δοχμὼ ἀΐσσοντε rushing on slantwise, Il.
as much as one can grasp, a handful, truss of corn, Lat. manipulus, Il.:—also a sheaf, = ἄμαλλα, Xen.
uncut corn, Anth., Luc.
carrying sheaves, Babr.
to collect the corn into sheaves, Il.
a grasping, Eur.
to be ready to do, Il.
a shedragon, Hhymn., Aesch., Eur.
of a dragon, Eur., Anth.
serpent-slayer, Anth.
with snaky locks, Aesch.
snake-like, Eur.
a dragon, or serpent of huge size, a python, Hom., etc.
a deed, act, Aesch., Plat.
an action represented on the stage, a drama, Ar.; δρ. διδάσκειν to bring out a play, v. διδάσκω II:—metaph. stage-effect, Plat.
dramatic work, a drama, Luc.
a running, course, a race, Hdt., Trag.
to run away, Xen.; τινά from one, Plat.; δραπετεύσουσι ὑπὸ ταῖς ἀσπίσιν will skulk behind their shields, Xen.
a runaway, Lat. fugitivus, βασιλέος from the king, Hdt.:— a runaway slave, Id.
as adj., runaway, fugitive, δραπέτης κλῆρος a lot of fugitive kind, i. e. crumbling clod of earth, which could not be drawn out of the urn, Soph.
of or for a δραπέτης, δρ. θρίαμβος a triumph over a runaway slave, Plut.
to have a mind to do, to be going to do, Soph., Eur.
τὸ δρ. activity, Aesch.
a running away, flight, Hdt., Aesch.; in pl., Eur.
Dep.
attic to grasp, c. gen. rei, κόνιος δεδραγμένος clutching a handsful of dust, Il.; so, ἐλπίδος δεδραγμένος Soph.
to lay hold of, τί μου δέδαρξαι; Eur.; δραξάμενος φάρυγος having seized [them] by the throat, Theocr.
c. acc. rei, to take by handsful, Hdt.
to be done, Soph.
δραστέον, one must do, Id., Eur.
vigorous, active, efficacious, Aesch., Eur.: τὸ δρ. activity, energy, Thuc.
in bad sense, audacious, Eur.

entry.etym: metath. for δαρτός, verb. adj. of δέρω,
entry.sense: skinned, flayed, Il.
properly, a handful, like δράγμα:—an Attic weight, a drachm, weighing about 66 1/2 grains, the Aeginetan being = 2/3 Attic.
an Attic silver coin, a drachma, worth 6 obols, i. e. 9 3/4 d., nearly = Roman denarius and Fr. franc, Hdt., etc.
worth a drachma, to the amount of a drachma, Arist.

to do, esp. to do some great thing, good or bad, cf. Lat. facinus, attic; often opp. to πάσχω, ἄξια δράσας ἄξια πάσχων Aesch.; κακῶς δράσαντες οὐκ ἐλάσσονα πάσχουσι Id.; proverb., "δράσαντι παθεῖν" doers must suffer, Id.; πεπονθότα μᾶλλον ἢ δεδρακότα things of suffering rather than of doing, Soph.; so, τὸ δρῶν the doing of a thing, Id.:— εὖ or κακῶς δρᾶν τινα to do one a good or ill turn, Theogn., Soph.
a sickle, reaping-hook, Il.: a pruning-hook, Hes.
bearing a scythe, ἅρμα δ. a scythed car, Xen.
sickle-shaped, Thuc.
a scythe, Xen.
a curved sword, scimitar, Hdt.
a sword-maker, armourer, Ar.
to pluck, epic imperf. δρέπτον, Mosch.: so in Mid., Anth.
to pluck, cull, Lat. carpo, Hdt., Eur., etc.:—metaph. to cull flowers from a field, δρ. λειμῶνα Μουσῶν, of a poet, Ar.
Mid. to pluck for oneself, cull, Od.: metaph., δρεπόμενοι τὰ μέλη Plat.; even, αἷμα δρέψασθαι to shed it, Aesch.
Lat. cultus, Hhymn.
a labourer, working man, Od.: fem. δρήστειρα, a workwoman, Id.
（διδράσκω) a runaway, Babr.: fem. δρῆστις, Anth.
service, Od.
piercing, Mosch.
piercing, sharp, keen, Lat. acer, of a dart, Il.: metaph., δριμεῖα μάχη, δριμὺς χόλος Id.; δριμὺ μένος Od.
of things which affect the eyes or taste, pungent, acrid, as smoke, Ar.; herbs, Xen.; smell, Ar.
metaph. of persons, keen, bitter, Aesch., Ar.; also keen, shrewd, Eur.:— δριμὺ βλέπειν to look bitter, Ar.
pungency: metaph. keenness, vehemence, Plat.
a copse, wood, thicket, δρίος ὕλης copse-wood, Od.; δρίος ὑλῆεν Anth.:—in pl. δρία, τά, (as if from δρίον), Hes., Soph., Eur.
a bath, Aesch.
running at full speed, swift, fleet, Soph., Eur.; δρ. κάμηλος a dromedary, Plut.
running, Eur.; ἄμπυξ δρ. the whirling wheel, Soph.; also with a neut. Noun, Eur.
like φοιτάς, wildly roaming, frantic, Id.
Frequent. of δρᾰμεῖν, to run, only in perf. δεδρόμηκα, aeolic -ᾱκα, Sapph., Babr.
a runner, Eur., Ar.
good at running, swift, fleet, Plat.; τὰ δρομικὰ τοῦ πεντάθλου the race, Xen.
a runner, postman, Aeschin.

a course, running, race, Hom. (v. τείνω); οὐρίῳ δρόμῳ in straight course, Soph.:—of any quick movement, e. g. flight, Aesch.:—of time, ἡμέρης δρ. a day's running, i. e. the distance one can go in a day, Hdt.:— δρόμῳ at a run, Id., attic
the footrace:—proverb., περὶ τοῦ παντὸς δρόμον θεῖν to run for one's all, Hdt.; τὸν περὶ ψυχῆς δρόμον δραμεῖν Ar.
the length of the stadium, a course or heat in a race, Soph.
a place for running, a run for cattle, Od.

a race-course, Hdt.: a public walk, Lat. ambulatio, Eur., Plat.:—proverb., ἔξω δρόμου or ἐκτὸς δρόμου φέρεσθαι, Lat. extra oleas vagari, to get off the course, i. e. wander from the point, Aesch., Plat.; ἐκ δρόμου πεσεῖν Aesch.
dewy, watery, Eur., Ar.
to bedew, besprinkle, Ar.
dew, Lat. ros, Hdt.; in pl., Aesch., etc.
pure water, Aesch., Eur.
of other liquids, δρ. φονία, of blood, Aesch.
any thing tender, like ἕρση II, the young of animals, Id.
like dew, moist, Eur.
a Dryad, nymph whose life was bound up with that of her tree, Plut.; cf. Ἁμαδρυάς.
oaken, Od., Eur.; δρ. πῦρ a wood fire of oak-wood, Theocr.; μέλι δρ. honey from the hollow of an oak, Anth.
an oak-coppice; and, generally, a coppice, wood, only in pl. δρυμά, Hom.; δρυμός in Soph., Eur.
dweller on the oak, τέττιξ Anth.
the woodpecker, Arist. δρυκολάπτης, in Ar.
the props or trestles upon which was laid the keel (τρόπις) of a new ship, Od.: metaph., δρυόχους τιθέναι δράματος to lay the keel of a new play, Ar.; ἐκ δρυόχων from the beginning, Plat.
= δρυμά, woods, Anth.
a kind of woodpecker, Ar.
Lat. druppa, an over-ripe olive, Anth.
to tear, strip, Il.:—Mid., δρυψαμένω παρειάς tearing each other's cheeks, Od.; in sign of mourning, δρύπτεσθαι παρειάν to tear one's cheek, Eur.
