originally a tree (which indeed comes from the same root), commonly the oak, Lat. quercus, Hom., etc.; sacred to Zeus, who gave his oracles from the oaks of Dodona, Od.; hence, αἱ προσήγοροι δρύες, Aesch.:—proverb οὐ γὰρ ἀπὸ δρυός ἐσσι οὐδ’ ἀπὸ πέτρης thou art no foundling from tree or rock, i.e. you have parents and a country, Od.; οὐ νῦν ἐστιν ἀπὸ δρυὸς οὐδ’ ἀπὸ πέτρης ὀαρίζειν it is no time now to talk at ease from tree or rock, Il..
of other trees, πίειρα δρῦς the resinous wood (of the pine), Soph.; of the olive Eur..
metaph. a worn-out old man, Anth.

originally a tree (which indeed comes from the same Root), commonly the oak, Lat. quercus, Hom., etc.; sacred to Zeus, who gave his oracles from the oaks of Dodona, Od.;—hence, αἱ προσήγοροι δρύες Aesch.:—proverb., οὐ γὰρ ἀπὸ δρυός ἐσσι οὐδ’ ἀπὸ πέτρης thou art no foundling from tree or rock, i. e. thou hast parents and a country, Od.; οὐ νῦν ἐστιν ἀπὸ δρυὸς οὐδ’ ἀπὸ πέτρης ὀαρίζειν ’tis no time now to talk at ease from tree or rock, Il.
of other trees, πίειρα δρῦς the resinous wood (of the pine), Soph.; of the olive, Eur.
metaph. a wornout old man, Anth.
a wood-cutter, Il.
a fence or railing, serving as the bar of the law-courts or council-chamber, Ar.; in pl., like Lat. cancelli, Id.
parings, Anth.
to get rid of hair by pitch-plasters, Luc.
the number two, Plat.
to plunge in misery, epic 3rd pl. δυόωσιν Od.
much-suffering, Hhymn.
woe, misery, anguish, pain, Od., Trag.; δυηπᾰθίη, ἡ, misery, Anth.

entry.etym: decl. in pres. and imperf. like ἵσταμαι
entry.sense: Dep.

to be able, capable, strong enough to do, c. inf., Hom., etc.; but the inf. is often omitted, Ζεὺς δύναται ἅπαντα [sc. ποιεῖν] Od.; so also, μέγα δυνάμενος very powerful, mighty, Id.; οἱ δυνάμενοι men of power, Eur., Thuc.; δυνάμενος παρά τινι having influence with him, Hdt., etc.
to be able, i. e. to dare or bear to do a thing, οὐδὲ ποιήσειν δύναται Od.; οὐκέτι ἐδύνατο βιοτεύειν Thuc.
with ὡς and a Sup., ὡς ἐδύναντο ἀδηλότατα as secretly as they could, Id.; ὡς δύναμαι μάλιστα as much as I possibly can, Plat.; or simply ὡς ἐδύνατο in the best way he could, Xen.
to pass for, i. e.
of money, to be worth so much, c. acc., ὁ σίγλος δύναται ἑπτὰ ὀβολούς the shekel is worth seven obols, Id.
of number, to be equivalent to, τριηκόσιαι γενεαὶ δυνέαται μύρια ἔτεα Hdt.

of words, to signify, mean, Lat. valere, Id., etc.; ἴσον δύναται, Lat. idem valet, Id.; τὴν αὐτὴν δύνασθαι δουλείαν to mean the same slavery, Thuc.:—also to avail, οὐδένα καιρὸν δύναται avails to no good purpose, Eur.
impers., οὐ δύναται, c. inf., it cannot be, is not to be, Hdt.

power, might, strength, Hom.: then, generally, strength, power, ability to do a thing, Id.; παρὰ δύναμιν beyond one's strength, Thuc.; ὑπὲρ δ. Dem.; κατὰ δ. as far as lies in one, Lat. pro virili, Hdt.
power, might, authority, Aesch., etc.
a force for war, forces, Xen.
a quantity, Lat. vis, χρημάτων δ. Hdt., etc.
a power, faculty, capacity, αἱ τοῦ σώματος δυνάμεις Plat., etc.; also of plants, etc., Xen.
the force or meaning of a word, Plat., etc.
the worth or value of money, Thuc.
to strengthen: Pass., NTest.
power, lordship, sovereignty, Soph., Thuc., etc.
an oligarchy, Id., Xen.
to hold power or lordship, be powerful, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
a lord, master, ruler, of Zeus, Soph.; οἱ δ., Lat. optimates, Hdt.: in Aesch., the stars are λαμπροὶ δυνάσται.
arbitrary, Arist.
to be powerful, mighty, NTest.
strong, mighty, able, esp. in body, τὸ δυνατώτατον the ablest-bodied men, Hdt.:—of ships, fit for service, Thuc.
c. inf. able to do, Hdt., etc.
powerful, Id.; οἱ δυνατοί the chief men of rank and influence, Thuc.

pass., of things, possible, Lat. quod fieri possit, Hdt., etc.:— δυνατόν [ἐστι], c. inf., Id., Aesch., etc.; ὁδὸς δυνατὴ καὶ τοῖς ὑποζυγίοις πορεύεσθαι practicable, Xen.: —κατὰ τὸ δυνατόν, quantum fieri possit, Plat., etc.; so, ἐς τὸ δ. Hdt.; ὅσον δυνατόν Eur., etc.
adv. -τῶς, strongly, powerfully, Aeschin.; δ. ἔχει it is possible, Hdt.
twelve, Il.

entry.etym: can be indecl., like ἄμφω, by Hom., τῶν δύο μοιράων, δύω κανόνεσσι Il.; so in Hdt. and attic Prose; but declined in Trag.
entry.sense: two, Il., etc.;—in Poets δύο or δύω may be joined with pl. Nouns, δύο δ’ ἄνδρες Id.:— εἰς δύο two and two, Xen.; σὺν δύο two together, Il., Hdt.
unchaste, Luc.
to have bad sport in fishing, Plut.
having seen hard service, Plut.
unhappy in one's brothers, Aesch.
ill-blowing, stormy, of winds, Hom.; epic gen. pl. δυσ-αήων for -αέων, Od.
most miserable, Soph.
most melancholy, Aesch.
not clear, murky, Eur.
living a hard life, most miserable, Aesch., Soph.; αἰὼν δυσαίων a life that is no life, Eur.
very painful, Aesch.
hard-hearted, Soph.
hard to catch or take, ἄγρα Plat.
hard to conquer, tutAesch.; c. gen., δ. κακῶν beyond reach of ills, Soph.
most miserable, Il.
hard to call back, Plut.
hard to bring back or recal, Plut.; poet. δυσαγκόμιστος, Aesch.
hard to sail up, Strab.
to bear ill, Lat. aegre ferre, Thuc.: to be greatly vexed, ἐπί τινι Plut.
hard to overthrow, Plut.
disagreeable to meet, boding of ill, Luc.
hard to look in the face, Plut.
hard to get rid of, Soph.
very disobedient, Anth.
hard to demonstrate, Plat.
hard to answer, Luc.
hard to dissuade, Xen.
hard to appease, implacable, Aesch.: — ill to please, peevish, morose, Eur., Xen.
illpleased, τινι with one, Eur.: τὸ δυσάρεστον displeasure, Plut.
unhappy mother of the noblest son, Il.
hard to govern, Aesch., Plut.
disagreement, Plut.
ill-united, Plut.
ill or hard lodging, Aesch.
δ. ἔρις, an unhappy contest with the flute (αὐλός), Anth.
inhospitable, Soph.
hard to take away, Arist.
most painful, Aesch.
grievous to bear, NTest.
Mid. to make impassable, Xen.
inaccessible, impassable, Xen.
trodden in sorrow, Aesch.
sadly wailing, Aesch.
making life wretched, πενίη Anth.
ill counsel, Aesch., Soph.
of ill soil, unfruitful, Anth.
ill-wedded, Eur.
very ticklish, skittish, Xen.
low birth, Soph., etc.
meanness, Eur.
low-born, Eur., etc.
lowminded, low, mean, Id.
hard to bridge over, Strab.
ignorance, doubt, Eur.
difficulty of knowing, Eur.
hard to seduce by enchantments, Plat.
misery, Eur.
of ill fortune, ill-fated, Trag., etc.
sorely wept, Aesch.
act. sorely weeping, Anth.
ill-wived, ill-wedded, Aesch.
hard to settle, Plut.
hard to decide, Plut.
hard to reconcile, Arist.
hard to search through, Plat.
hard to pass through, Polyb.
bringing evil by one's abode, Aesch.
unshapely, ugly, Hdt., Plat.
meanly clad, Eur.
hard to enter: Sup. -ώτατος, ον, least accessible, Thuc.
hard to sail into, Strab.
hard to avert by sacrifice, Plut.
hard to undo: adv. -τως, indissolubly, Aesch.
hard to wash out, Plat.
hard to pass out from, Eur.
hard to escape from: adv. -τως, Anth.
hard to refute, Luc.
ill-starred Helen, Eur.
hardly hoping, desponding, Aesch., Xen.
= δύσελπις, Plut.
unhoped for, ἐκ δυσελπίστων, unexpectedly, Xen.
hard to walk on, Thuc.
hard to enter, inaccessible, Xen.
dysentery, Hdt., Plat.
hard to speak with, Theophr.
hard to deceive, Plat., Xen.
hard to loose from bonds, Plut.
hard to enumerate, Polyb.
hard to refute, Plat.
hard to unfold, Plut.
hard to investigate, Arist.
hard to tame, Plut.
indissoluble, Eur.
hard to get out of, Arist.
hard to attack secretly, Xen.
unfavourable to love, Anth.
difficulty in acting, Plut.
unfit for work, Plut.
very lonely, desolate, Anth.
very quarrelsome, contentious, Plat.
act. producing unhappy strife, Plut.
shed in unholy strife, Soph.
hard to interpret, NTest.
sick in love with, τινος Eur., Thuc.
hardly loving, stony-hearted, Theocr.
an ill bedfellow, Aesch.
hard to find out, Aesch.
hard to find or get, Xen.
hard to find one's way through, impenetrable, Eur.
exceeding jealous, Od., Plut.:—adv., δυσζήλως ἔχειν πρός τινα Plut.
hard to seek or track, Xen.
wretched, Anth.
hard to heal or cure, Anth.
hard of hearing, Anth.
laying one on a hard bed, of death, Hom., Hes.
sunless, Aesch., Eur.
ungovernable, Luc.
ill-sounding, hateful, Il.
hard to warm: chilly, Il.
to die hard, die a lingering death, Hdt.: to struggle against death, Plat.
bringing a hard death, Eur.
having died a hard death, Anth.
ill to look on, Aesch., Soph.
godless, ungodly, Aesch.; hateful to the gods, Soph.
hard to cure, Soph.
Dep. to be much vexed, Xen.
hard to catch, Plut.
loud-wailing, most mournful, Soph., Eur.
ill-sounding, Aesch. to be dispirited, to despond, Hhymn.
Mid. to be melancholy, angry, Eur.
despondency, despair, Eur., Plat., etc.
desponding, melancholy, repentant, Soph., etc.: τὸ δύσθυμον = δυσθυμία, Plut. adv., -μως, comp. -ότερον, Plat.
hard to heal, incurable, Aesch., Eur.
to have bad omens in a sacrifice, Plut.
dipped in the sea, Anth.
hard to ride in; τὰ δ. parts unfit for cavalry-service, Xen., Plut.
a setting of the sun or stars, Aesch., etc.
the quarter in which the sun sets, the west, Thuc., etc.
hard to satisfy by purification or atonement, Soph., Ar.
hard to hold in, ἵπποι Xen.
noisome from smoke, smoky, Aesch.
hard to endure, Plut.
hard to learn or understand, Isocr. adv., -τως ἔχειν Id.
hard to check, restless, Aesch., Eur.
hard to effect, Xen.
hard to restore or rally, Xen.
not to be despised, Xen.
ill-sounding, shrieking, discordant, Il., Aesch., Eur.
full of misery, Od.
past remedy, Aesch.
hard to move, Plat.:— immovable, resolute, Plut.: inexorable, Anth.
infamous, shameful, Il., Aesch., Xen. adv. -εῶς, Soph., Eur.
ill-fame, an ill name, infamy, Eur., Thuc.; ἐπὶ δυσκλείᾳ tending to disgrace him, Soph.
unsocial, Plat.
to be peevish or discontented,Ar.: to shew displeasure, Xen.
discontent, peevishness, Ar., Plat.
of things, difficulty, Dem.
ill-glued or fastened, loose, Luc.
hard to bend: δ. καμπή an intricate flourish in singing, Ar.
making bed uneasy, Ar.
of persons, properly, hard to satisfy with food; then, generally, hard to please, discontented, fretful, peevish, Eur., Ar., etc.:—adv., δυσκόλως ἔχειν, διακεῖσθαι to be peevish, Plat.
of things, troublesome, harassing, Id.; generally, unpleasant, Dem.:— δύσκολόν ἐστι it is difficult, NTest.:—adv. -λως, hardly, with difficulty, Id.
with ill-formed womb, Anth.
hard to bear, intolerable, Soph., Eur.
bad temperament, Lat. intemperies, of the air, Plut.
of bad temperament, Strab.
hard to discern or interpret, Aesch., Soph.: δύσκριτόν ἐστι, c. inf., Plat. adv. -τως, doubtfully, darkly, Aesch.; δ. ἔχειν to be in doubt, Ar.
arising from the stormy sea, Aesch.
to be stone-deaf, Anth.
hard to tell, Lat. infandus, Aesch.
hard to catch, Luc.
ill-calculating, Soph.
hard for the neck, hard to bear, Theogn., Aesch.
impatient of the yoke: adv., impatiently, Eur.
indissoluble, Aesch., Eur.
to be slow at recognising, Aesch.
hard to learn, Aesch.; δ. ἰδεῖν hard to know at sight, Eur.: τὸ δυσμαθές difficulty of knowing Id.
act. slow at learning, Plat.:—adv., δυσμαθῶς ἔχειν to be so, Id.
slowness at learning, Plat.
to fight in vain against, or, to fight an unholy fight with, τινί Soph.
one must fight desperately with, Id.
hard to fight with, unconquerable, Aesch., Eur., etc.: generally, difficult, Aesch. to bear ill-will, τινί against another, Eur., Dem.
ill-will, enmity, Soph., Eur., etc.

entry.etym: a participial form only in masc.
entry.sense: bearing ill-will, hostile, Od.
full of ill-will, hostile, Il., Hdt., Trag.; rarely c. gen., ἄνδρα δ. χθονός an enemy of the land, Soph.
rarely of things, Id., Xen.
hard to manage: hard to attack, Hdt.
wrathful, Anth.
visited by heavy wrath, Anth.

entry.etym: = δύσις, mostly in pl., Soph., etc.;
entry.sense: ἐπὶ δυσμῇσιν at the point of setting, Hdt.
the quarter of sunset, the west, Id., Aesch.
not a mother, Od.
to be at loss how to do, c. inf., Aesch.
hard to imitate, Luc.
a hard fate, Anth.
ill-fated, ill-starred, Il., Soph.:—adv. -ρως, with ill fortune, Aesch.
badness of form, ugliness, Hdt.
misshapen, ill-favoured, ἐσθής Eur.
unmusical, Anth.
hard to conquer, Plut.
hard to wash out, Soph.
to be ill-affected, τινι Plut.
disaffection, ill-will, malevolence, Soph., Eur.
lawlessness, a bad constitution, Solon.
lawless, unrighteous, Anth.
δύσ-νοστος νόστος, a return that is no return, Eur.
ill-affected, disaffected, τινι Soph., Eur., etc.
unpleasing to marry, Anth.
ill-wedded or ill-betrothed, Eur.
hard to deal with, driving a hard bargain, Plat., Xen.
hard to understand, unintelligible, Eur., Xen.
over heavy, burdensome, Plut.
to make bad way, get on slowly, Plut.
difficult and rugged, Aesch.
hard to pass, scarce passable, Thuc.
to be distressed, to fear, Eur.:— δυσοίζω φόβῳ to tremble with fear at a thing, c. acc., Aesch.
entry.etym: οἴζω is formed from οἶ oh! as οἰμώζω from οἴμοι.

entry.sense: bad to dwell in, Xen.
hard to bear, insufferable, Aesch., Soph. fut. mid. of δύω.
stormy, wintry, Soph.
hard to live with, bringing evil in one's company, Aesch.
scarce-seeing, purblind, Aesch.
hard to see, Xen.
quick to anger, Soph.
with bad anchorage, Aesch.:— τὰ δύσορμα rough ground, where one can scarce get footing, Xen.
act., πνοαὶ δ. that detained the fleet in harbour, Aesch.
ill-omened, boding ill, Aesch., Eur.:— with ill auspices, Plut.
dusky, Eur.
an ill smell, ill savour, Soph.
ill-smelling, stinking, Hdt.
bad for scent, in hunting, Xen.
driven by a too favourable wind, fatally favourable, Soph.
firmness in resisting, Plut.
to suffer a hard fate, Mosch.
to be impatient, ἐπί τινι, πρός τι Plut.
impatient of suffering, Plut.: hardly feeling, impassive, Luc.
hard to wrestle with, Aesch., Eur., Xen.
hard to conquer, Aesch.
hard to wrestle with, Aesch.
incomparable, Plut.
hard to move by prayer, inexorable, Aesch., Plut.
hard to carry along, difficult, Polyb.
hard to appease, Plut.
ill-mated, Soph.
hard to appease, Aesch.
unhappy maiden, Anth.
unhappy Paris, ill-starred Paris, Il.; cf. Δυσελένα.
hard to pass, Xen.
insepar. Prefix, like un- or mis- (in un-lucky, mis-chance), destroying the good sense of a word, or increasing its bad sense.
hardly obeying, self-willed, intractable, Xen.:—adv., δυσπειθῶς ἔχειν Plut.
hard to send away, Aesch.

entry.etym: perh. from same Root as πέμφιξ
entry.sense: of the sea, rough and stormy, Il., Hes.:—metaph, rude, uncourteous, Hes.
bringing sore affliction, direful, Pind.
hard to get through, Eur.
hard to encompass, Arist.
falling out ill, most difficult, Soph. adv. δυσπετῶς, ionic -έως, Aesch.
full of grievous evil, disastrous, Aesch.
squalid, Soph.
wandering in misery, Aesch.
difficulty of sailing, Anth.
bad for sailing, Anth.
difficulty of breathing, Xen.
scant of breath, Soph.
δ. πνοαί contrary winds, Id.
hard to war with, Dem.
unlucky in war, Aesch.
hard to take by siege, Xen.
toilsome, Od.
bringing toil and trouble, Aesch.
laborious, Soph.
toilsome, Soph.
hard to pass, Xen.
difficulty of passing, Xen.
gotten with much labour: τὸ δ. difficulty of getting, Plut.
hard to pass, scarce passable, Xen.
unlucky, ill-starred, unhappy, wretched, Trag.; δ. εὐχαί i. e. curses, Aesch.; comp. δυσποτμώτερος Eur. adv. -μως, Aesch.
unpalatable, Aesch.
to be unlucky, Aesch., Plut.
ill success, ill luck, Aesch., Soph.
base, undignified, Eur.
hard to approach, Thuc.
difficult of access, Eur.
hard to attack, Plut.
hard to get at, difficult of access, Thuc.; of men, unsocial, Id., Xen.
hard to approach, Soph.
hard to look on, horrid to behold, Soph.
hard to get at, Plut.
of ill aspect, Plut.
hard to break, Luc.
impatient of cold, Hdt.
impiety, ungodliness, Trag.
a charge of impiety, Soph.
to think or act ungodly, Trag.
ungodly, impious, profane, Trag.
hard to save, ruined, Theocr.
hard to get a view of, Polyb.
most miserable, Soph., Eur.
hard to make out from the given signs, hard to trace, inexplicable, Trag.
unfortunate in children, Soph.
ill-pleasing, Aesch.
wretched, unhappy, unfortunate, disastrous, mostly of persons, Hom., Trag.; δυστήνων δέ τε παῖδες ἐμῷ μένει ἀντιόωσιν unhappy are they whose sons encounter me, Il.
of things, Trag., Ar.: Sup. adv., δυστανοτάτως Eur.
after Hom., in moral sense, wretched, like Lat. miser (a wretch), Soph.
entry.etym: Prob. for δύσστηνος; but the origin of -στηνος is uncertain.

entry.sense: hard to keep, Plut.
suffering hard things, Hhymn.
hard to bear, Aesch.
an unhappy parent, Anth.
to be in sore travail, of women:— metaph., δυστοκεῖ πόλις Ar.
to speak evil of, τινά τι Soph.
bad of mouth: hardmouthed, Anth.
lamentable, Aesch.
hard to guess, Eur.
hard to hit, Plut.
fed on horrid food, Eur.
hard to deal with, intractable, stubborn, Soph.:—adv. -λως, awkwardly, Xen.
hard to turn, intractable, Eur., Dem.
to be unlucky, unhappy, unfortunate, Hdt., attic; τινι in a thing, Eur.; περί τινος Id.; ἔν τινι Ar.; also, πάντα δυστυχεῖν Eur.
a piece of ill luck, a failure, Plat.
unlucky, unfortunate, Trag., etc.; τὰ δυστυχῆ = δυστυχίαι, Aesch.:—adv. -χῶς, Id.
ill-starred, harbinger of ill, Id.
ill luck, ill fortune, Eur., Thuc., etc.
hard to withstand, Plut.
scarce visible, Plut.
hard to speak, unutterable, Lat. nefandus, Aesch.
to use ill words, esp. words of ill omen, Trag.
trans. to speak ill of, Soph., Eur.
ill language, words of ill omen, Soph.
of ill omen, boding, Hes., Eur.
slanderous, Theogn.
hateful, Aesch., Soph.
to bear with pain, bear ill, Lat. aegre ferre: intr. to be impatient, angry, vexed, Hdt., Soph.; τινι at a thing, Aesch., Eur.; ἐπί τινι Aesch.
hard to bear, Eur.
unsuited to the lyre, Eur.
hard to bear, heavy, Xen.

mostly of sufferings, hard to bear, grievous, Trag.; δύσφοροι γνῶμαι false, blinding fancies, Soph.; τὰ δύσφορα our troubles, sorrows, Id.:— δύσφορόν [ἐστι] Xen.:—adv., δυσφόρως ἔχειν to be hard to bear, Soph.
of food, oppressive, Xen.
(from Pass.) moving with difficulty, slow of motion, Id.
= δυσφροσύνη: in pl. troubles, Hes.
rashly, Aesch.
anxiety, care, Hes., in epic gen. pl. δυσφροσυνάων.
sad at heart, sorrowful, melancholy, Trag.
ill-disposed, malignant, Aesch., Eur.
= ἄφρων, insensate, Aesch., Soph.
hard to keep off or prevent, Eur.
suffering from hard winters, very wintry, freezing, Il., Hdt., Aesch.
a thing hard to be subdued, a hard conquest, Soph.
hard to subdue, Hdt., Dem.
to be unable to endure a thing, bear with an ill grace, Lat. aegre ferre, c. acc., Plat.; c. acc. et part. to be annoyed at his doing, Aeschin.
intr. to feel annoyance, to be discontented, displeased, vexed, τινός for or because of a thing, Plat., etc.; τινί at a thing, Dem.:—Pass. to be hateful, Plut.
c. inf. to scorn to do a thing, Plat.
Causal, to cause vexation, ῥήματα τέρψαντα ἢ δυσχεράναντ’ Soph.
δ. ἐν τοῖς λόγοις to make difficulties in argument, to be captious, Plat.
of things, annoyance or disgust caused by a thing, Soph.
difficulty in doing a thing, Plat.
of persons, peevishness, ill temper: loathing, nausea, Id., Theophr.
hard to take in hand or manage, of things, annoying, vexatious, discomfortable, Trag.: τὸ δυσχερές, = δυσχέρεια, Eur.; δυσχερὲς ποιεῖσθαί τι, Lat. aegre ferre, Thuc.; τὰ δυσχερῆ difficulties, Dem.
of arguments, contradictory, captious, Plat., etc.
of persons, ill tempered, unfriendly, hateful, τινι to one, Soph., Eur., etc.; δ. περί τι fastidious, Plat.
adv., δυσχερῶς ἔχειν to be annoyed, Id.
wintry, troublesome, dangerous, fearful, Lat. horridus, Trag.
mean clothing, Eur.
with little grass, ill off for food, Eur.
to be in difficulty or distress, Polyb.
hard to use, nearly useless, Xen.; intractable, Id.:—adv. -τως ἔχειν to be in distress, Plut.
difficult, rough ground, Xen.
ill-smelling, Hdt., Soph., Thuc.
causing grievous pangs, Anth.
to beat down the price, cheapen, Anth.

sense.gloss: one who beats down the price.

entry.sense: bearing an ill name, ill-omened, Hom., Soph., etc.; esp. bearing a name of ill omen, such as Αἴας, Id.
to put out of countenance, put to shame, τινά Luc.: absol. to be importunate, Plut.
in good authors only:—Pass. to be put out of countenance, to be troubled, Plat.; of animals, to be shy, timid, Xen.
to be ashamed of, τι Plut.
to keep painful watch, Il.
a diver, Hdt.
worth twelve beeves, Il.
twelve months old, Hes.
divided into twelve parts, Anth.
δύο καὶ δέκα, twelve, in all genders, Lat. duo-decim, Hom., etc.
twelve, in all genders, Lat. duo-decim, Hom., etc.
holding 22 measures, Il.
22 cubits long, Il.
Causal in fut. and aor1, to strip off clothes, etc., Od. (in compd. ἐξ-έδῡσα).

non causal forms such as the stems δύω and δῡ́νω: of Places or Countries, to enter, make one's way into, τείχεα δύω (aor2 subj.) Il.; ἔδυ νέφεα plunged into the clouds, of a star, Id.; δῦτε θαλάσσης κόλπον plunge into the lap of Ocean, Id.; δύσεο μνηστῆρας go in to them, Od.: also with a prep., δύσομαι εἰς Ἀΐδαο Id.; δύσετ’ ἁλὸς κατὰ κῦμα Il.; ὑπὸ κῦμα ἔδυσαν Id.; δύσκεν εἰς Αἴαντα he got himself unto Ajax, i. e. got behind his shield, Id.

of the sun and stars, to sink into [the sea, v. supr.], to set, ἠέλιος μὲν ἔδυ Id.; Βοώτης ὀψὲ δύων late- setting Bootes, Od.; πρὸ δύντος ἡλίου Hdt.:—metaph., βίου δύντος αὐγαί Aesch.; ἔδυ δόμος the house sank, Id.
of clothes and armour, to get into, put on, Il.; metaph., εἰ μὴ σύγε δύσεαι ἀλκήν if thou wilt not put on strength (cf. ἐπιειμένος ἀλκήν):—ἀμφ’ ὤμοισιν ἐδύσετο τεύχεα Id.; ὤμοιϊν τεύχεα δῡθι Id.
of sufferings, passions, and the like, to enter, come over or upon, κάματος γυῖα δέδυκε Id.; ἄχος ἔδυνεν ἦτορ, etc., Id.; δῦ μιν Ἄρης the spirit of war filled him, Id.
bent twelve times, δωδεκ. τέρμα the post (in the race-course) that has been doubled twelve times, Pind.
a leader of twelve, Xen.
sold at 12 drachmae, Dem.
twelve palms long, Anth.
conqueror in 12 contests, Anth.
2 years old, Plut.
adv. twelve times, Ar.
of twelve threads, Xen.
knowing twelve arts or tricks, Ar.
with twelve children, Anth.
twelve times long ago, ever so long ago, Ar.
twelve cubits long, Hdt.
formed of twelve united states, Hdt.
twelve, Hom., etc.: v. δυώδεκα.
twelve-oared, Plut.
of twelve pieces of leather, Plat.
the number twelve, Anth.
on the twelfth day, Plat.
twelve days old, Hes. (in epic form δυωδ-).
the twelfth, Hom., etc.: epic δυωδ-, Id.
bearing twelve times a year, Luc.
of twelve tribes, τὸ δ. the twelve tribes of Israel, NTest.
twelve years old, Plut.:—fem. δωδεκέτις, Anth.
of Dodona, Il., Aesch.
Dodona, in Epirus, the seat of the most ancient oracle of Zeus, Hom., etc.
entry.etym: Soph. uses the heterocl. forms Δωδῶνος, -ῶνι, -ῶνα (as if from Δωδών).

entry.sense: a house, Hom., Trag.: part of a house, the chief room, hall, Hom.:—hence in pl. for a single house, Od., Trag.
a house, household, family, Aesch., Soph.
a chamber, bed-chamber, Plat.
fem. adj. of the house, Aesch.
to ruin the house, Aesch.
to build: Mid. to cause to be built, Anth.
a gift, present, esp. a free gift, bounty, Lat. beneficium, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
acc. δωρεάν as adv., as a free gift, freely, Lat. gratis, Hdt.
to no purpose, in vain, NTest.
to give, present, Hes., Pind.:— Pass., aor1 ἐδωρήθην, to be given or presented, Hdt.; of persons, to be presented with a thing, Soph.

also as Mid., Il.; δωρέεσθαί τί τινι to present a thing to one, Lat. donare aliquid alicui, Hdt., Aesch., etc.; also, δ. τινά τινι to present one with a thing, Lat. donare aliquem aliquo, Id.; δ. τινά to make him presents, Hdt.
that which is given, a gift, present, Hdt., Trag.
a giver, Anth.
of persons, open to gifts or presents, Il.
of things, freely given, Soph., Plut.
a Dorian, descendant of Dorus: pl. Δωριεῖς, attic -ῆς, οἱ, the Dorians, Od., Hdt., etc.
to imitate the Dorians in life, dialect, or music, to speak Doric Greek, Theocr.
Doric, Hdt., Trag., etc.
Dorian, Pind., Arist.
fem. adj. Dorian, Hdt., Thuc.: hence,
Δωρὶς νᾶσος the Dorian island, i. e. Peloponnesus, Pind., Soph.
(with or without γῆ) Doris, in Northern Greece, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
Δ. κόρα a Dorian damsel, Eur.
in Dorian fashion: ἡ Δ. ἁρμονία the Dorian mode or measure in music, Plat., etc.
to accept as a present, esp. to take as a bribe, ἀργύριον, χρυσόν Hdt., Plat.
absol. to take bribes, Hdt., Ar.
Pass.,
of persons, to have a bribe given one, δεδωροδόκηνται Dem.
of the bribe, τὰ δωροδοκηθέντα the bribes received, Aeschin.
acceptance of a bribe, corruption, Dem.
a taking of bribes, openness to bribery, Oratt.
in bribe-fashion, Ar., with a play on Δωριστί,
taking presents or bribes, Plat., Dem.
a giver of presents, a giver, Anth.
a gift, present, Hom.: a votive gift, Il.:— δῶρά τινος the gifts of, i. e. given by, him, δῶρα θεῶν Hom.; δῶρ’ Ἀφροδίτης, i. e. personal charms, Il.; c. gen. rei, ὕπνου δ. the blessing of sleep, Id.
δῶρα, presents given by way of bribe, Dem., etc.; δώρων ἑλεῖν τινα to convict him of receiving presents, Ar.
the breadth of the hand, the palm, as a measure of length; v. ἑκκαιδεκάδωρος.
greedy of presents, Hes.
to bring presents, τινί Plat.: to give as presents or bribes, τί τινι Ar.
bringing presents, Pind., Anth.
giving oneself up to justice, abiding by the law, Hdt.
Lat. dos, = δόσις, Hes.
fut. part. of δίδωμι, always going to give: Δώσων as a name of Antigonus II, promiser, Plut.
a giver, Od., Hes.:—so δώτης, ου, Hes.
to receive or collect presents, Hdt.
a gift, present, Hom., Hdt.
giver, a Nereid, Il., Hes.
fit for wearing, ἑᾱνῷ λιτί with linen good for wear, i. e. fine and white, Il.; πέπλος ἑᾱνός a fine, light, veil, Id.; ἑᾱνοῦ κασσιτέροιο tin beat out and so made fit for wear, Id.
as Subst., ἑανός, ὁ, a fine robe, fit for the wear of goddesses and great ladies, Hom.

entry.etym: ἐᾱ́ν contracts into ἤν and ἄν
entry.sense: if haply, if, followed by subj. (whereas εἰ is foll. by ind. or opt.), epic εἴ κε, αἴ κε.
in NTest. ἐάν is used just like the adverb ἄν after relative Pronouns and Conjunctions, as ὃς ἐάν whosoever, ὅσος ἐάν, ὅστις ἐάν, ὅπου ἐάν, etc.
exclam. of surprise or displeasure, ha! oho! Lat. vah! esp. before a question, ἔα, τί χρῆμα; Aesch.; ἔα, τίς οὗτος . . ; Eur.
to pass the spring, Xen.
Lat. vernus, of spring, εἰαρινὴ ὥρη spring- time, Il., etc.:—neut. ἠρινόν, -νά, as adv., in spring-time, Eur.; ἠρινὰ κελαδεῖν, of the swallow, Ar.
flourishing in spring, Mosch.

Lat. ver, spring, ἔαρος νέον ἱσταμένοιο in time of early spring, Od.; ἅμα τῷ ἔαρι at the beginning of spring, Hdt.; ἐξ ἦρος εἰς Ἀρκτοῦρον Soph.:—metaph. of the prime or flower of anything, Hdt., etc.; ἔαρ ὁρᾶν to look fresh and bright, Theocr.; γενύων ἔαρ, i. e. the first down on a youth's face, Anth.
to be suffered, Hdt., Eur.
ἐατέον, one must suffer, Id., Plat.

reflex. Pron. of 3rd pers., Lat. sui, sibi, se, of himself, herself, itself, etc.; first in Hdt. and attic; Hom. has ἕο αὐτοῦ, οἷ αὐτῷ, ἑ αὐτόν:—αὐτὸ ἐφ’ ἑαυτό itself by itself, absolutely, Plat.; so τὸ ἐφ’ ἑαυτόν Thuc.; αὐτὸ καθ’ αὑτό Plat.;— ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ of himself, Thuc., etc.; ἐν ἑαυτοῦ, ἐντὸς ἑαυτοῦ, Lat. sui compos: — παρ’ ἑαυτῷ at his own house, Xen.; often with comp. and Sup., ἐγένοντο ἀμείνονες αὐτοὶ ἑωυτῶν they surpassed themselves, Hdt.; πλουσιώτεροι ἑαυτῶν, i. e. continually richer, Thuc.
in attic αὑτοῦ, sometimes for 1st or 2nd pers., Aesch., Soph.
prob. epic for ἥφθη, aor1 pass. of ἅπτω ἐπ’ αὐτῶι ἀσπὶς ἑάφθη upon him his shield was fastened upon or clung to him, i. e. they fell together, Il.
to let, suffer, allow, permit, Lat. sinere, c. acc. pers. et inf., Hom., attic:—Pass. to be given up, Soph.
οὐκ ἐᾶν not to suffer, and then to forbid, hinder, prevent, c. acc. et. inf., Hom., etc.: often an inf. may be supplied, οὐκ ἐάσει σε τοῦτο will not allow thee [to do] this, Soph.
to let alone, let be, c. acc., Hom., etc.;—absol., ἔασον let be, Aesch.:—Pass., ἡ δ’ οὖν ἐάσθω Soph.
in same sense, c. inf., κλέψαι μὲν ἐάσομεν we will have done with stealing, Il.; θεὸς τὸ μὲν δώσει, τὸ δ’ ἐάσει [sc. δοῦναι] he will give one thing, the other he will let alone, Od.; v. χαίρω fin.
name of Apollo, to whom the Spartans sacrificed on the 7th of every month, Aesch.
on the seventh day, Thuc., Xen.
the number seven or a number of seven, Anth.
a period of seven days, a week Arist.: also of seven years, a septenary, Id.
the seventh, Il.
indecl. seventy, Hdt., etc.
seventy years old: fem. -οῦτις, Luc.
seventh, Lat. septimus, Hom., etc.; ἡ ἑβδόμη the seventh day, Hdt.
the ebony-tree, ebony, Hdt., Theocr.
Hebrew, NTest.
a Hebrew, NTest.
in the Hebrew tongue, NTest.
in or of the land, native, Lat. indigena, Aesch.
of property, in land, consisting of land, Dem., etc.
in or of the earth, Plat.

entry.etym: ἐγ-γείνωνται is 3rd pl. aor1 subj. in causal sense
entry.sense: μὴ μυῖαι εὐλὰς ἐγγείνωνται lest the flies breed maggots in [the wounds], Il.
a mocker, scorner, Eur.
to laugh at, mock, Lat. irridere, τινί Soph., Eur.; κατά τινος Soph.
inborn, native, Lat. indigena, Hdt., attic; θεοὶ ἐγγενεῖς gods of the race or country, Aesch.
born of the same race, kindred, Soph.: —adv. -νῶς, like kinsmen, Id.
of qualities, inborn, innate, Trag.
a comfort for old age, Plut.
to grow old in one, decay, Thuc.

entry.note: ionic and later -γῑ́νομαι fut. -γενήσομαι 3rd pl. epic perf. ἐγγεγάᾱσι
entry.sense: Dep.:— to be born or bred in a place, c. dat., Hom., Hdt.
of qualities, to be inborn, innate, Id., Eur.
of events and the like, to happen in or among, τισι Hdt.
to come in, intervene, pass, of Time, Id., Thuc.
ἐγγίγνεται, impers., it is allowed or possible, c. inf., Hdt., attic

entry.etym: comp. and Sup. adj., from adv. ἐγγύς,
entry.sense: nearer, nearest: neut. ἔγγῑον, ἔγγιστα, as adv., Dem., etc.
to have a sweet taste, Hdt.
to cut in, carve, Hdt.
one who lives by his tongue, Ar.
to talk loudly of, Ar.
a grandson, granddaughter, Plut.
a registering, registration, Dem.
to mark in or on, to paint on, Hdt.
to inscribe, write in or on, Id.:—Pass., ἐγγεγραμμένος τι having something written on it, Soph.; so Virgil flores inscripti nomina.
to enter in the public register, ἐγγρ. τὸν υἱὸν εἰς ἄνδρας Dem.:—Pass., εἰς τοὺς δημότας ἐγγραφῆναι Id.
to enter on the judge's list, to indict, Ar., Dem.
properly, to put into the palm of the hand, put into one's hand, Hom.

entry.etym: the forms ἐν-εγύων, ἐν-εγύησα, ἐγ-γεγύηκα (as if the Verb were a compd. with prep. ἐν or ἐγ) are erroneous:
entry.sense: to give or hand over as a pledge, Lat. spondere, and in Mid. to have a thing pledged to one, accept as a surety, Od., Plat.
of a father to give his daughter in marriage, to plight, betroth, Hdt., Eur.:—Mid. to have a woman betrothed to one, Dem.
Mid. also to pledge oneself, give security, Plat., etc.: c. acc. et inf. fut. to promise or engage that . . , Ar., Xen.
c. acc. rei, to answer for, Dem.
a pledge put into the hand: surety, security, Lat. vadimonium, Od., attic
betrothed, Isae.
one who gives security, a surety, Hdt., attic
of a wife, wedded, Dem.
from nigh at hand, Il., attic
with Verbs of rest, hard by, nigh at hand, Hom.
c. dat., ἐγγύθεν τινί hard by him, Il.; also c. gen., Id.
hard by, near, c. gen., Il.; also c. dat., Id.
of Time, nigh at hand, Id.
to exercise a person in a thing, c. dat., Luc.:—Mid. to practise oneself in, Plut.
giving security, Theogn., Xen.
of Place, near, nigh, at hand, Hom.; c. gen. hard by, near to, Id., Soph.; also c. dat., Eur.
of Time, nigh at hand, Hom., Xen.
of Numbers, etc., nearly, Thuc., Xen.; οὐδ’ ἐγγύς i. e. not by a great deal, nothing like it, Plat., Dem.; ἐγγὺς τοῦ τεθνάναι very nearly dead, Plat.
of Relationship, akin to, Aesch., Plat.
entry.etym: From the same Root as ἄγχι, cf. ἄγχιστος, ἔγγιστος.

entry.sense: forming an angle, esp. a right angle, λίθοι ἐν τομῇ ἐγγώνιοι cut square, Thuc.

entry.etym: ἐγρήγορα used as pres, the pluperfect serves as an imperfect.
entry.sense: Act. to awaken, wake up, rouse, Il., Trag.
to rouse, stir up, ἐγείρειν Ἄρηα to stir the fight, Il., etc.
to raise from the dead, NTest.; or from a sick bed, Id.
to raise or erect a building, Id.
Pass., with perf. act. ἐγρήγορα, to awake, Od., Hdt., etc.: in aor2 also to keep watch or vigil, Il.:—in perf. to be awake, Hom., attic
to rouse or stir oneself, be excited by passion, Hes., Thuc.
laughter-stirring, Anth.
exciting the theatre, Anth.
battle-stirring, Anth.
from which one wakes, ὕπνος ἐγ., opp. to the sleep of death, Theocr.
a waking from sleep, Plat.:— awaking from death, NTest.
light-stirring, ἐγ. λίθος the flint, Anth.
one must raise, Eur.
waking, stirring, τινος Plat.
Dep. to sit or settle oneself in a place, εἰς θᾶκον Ar.:— to encamp in a place, Thuc.
to pass one's youth in, Eur.
Dep. to sit in or on, Xen.: to lie in ambush, Ar.
to erect or set up in, Eur.
to seat in or upon, Plat.:—so in aor1 mid., ναὸν ἐγκαθείσατο founded a temple there, Eur.
Mid. to take one's seat on, Hdt.
to let down: to send in as a garrison, Plut.
to place or establish in a place, as king or chief, Eur., Thuc.: to place as a garrison in a place, Dem.
Pass., with aor2, perf. and plup. act., to be established in a place, Thuc.
to look closely into, Plut.
to remark something in a person or thing, Id.
Mid. to run into harbour, come to anchor, Thuc.
to riot or revel in a thing, Eur.
adv. eagerly, busily, Soph.: wakefully, Eur.
a feast of renovation, esp. that established by Judas Macc. at the re-consecration of the Temple, NTest.
to renovate, consecrate:—Pass., NTest.
to burn or heat in fire, Eur.
to make a fire in a place, Plut.
to lose heart, grow weary, NTest.
to call in a debt, Xen., etc.
to bring a charge against a person, φόνον ἐγκαλεῖν τινι to bring a charge of murder against one, Soph., Plat.:— to accuse, τινί Thuc., etc.:— ἐγκ. τι to bring as a charge, Soph., Thuc.
Pass. to take pride or pleasure in a thing, c. dat., Plut.
an ornament, decoration, Thuc.
a covering, wrapping up, Ar.
to veil in a thing, to wrap up, Ar.: —Pass. to be veiled or enwrapt, Id., Xen.
Mid. to hide oneself, hide one's face, Ar., etc.; of persons at the point of death, Xen., Plat.; as a mark of shame, Id.
to bend in, bend, Xen.
to pour in wine, Eur., Ar.
Dep. to make a sound in a thing, ἐγκ. κόχλῳ to blow on a conch, Theocr.
to gulp in greedily, snap up, Ar.
the brain, Anth.
containing fruit, Soph.
athwart, oblique, Thuc.
to persevere or persist in a thing, c. dat., Thuc., Xen.
c. acc. to await stedfastly, Eur.
absol. to hold out, remain firm, Plut.
a being caught in a place, a being hemmed in, interception, Thuc.
Dep. to reckon in or among, Isae.
Pass. to be mixed in or with, c. dat., Isocr.
to thrust firmly in or into, c. dat., Od.
to fall in or upon, c. dat., Anth.
to interweave, entwine, Xen.
to sew in, Xen.
to fall upon, like lightning: of epidemics, to break out among, Thuc.
trans. to hurl down among or upon, properly of a thunderbolt, Aesch., Soph.
to disperse in or among, Plut.
to implant as a principle in, τί τινι Plut.
to slaughter in a place, Plut.
to cut up among a number, Plat.

Mid., ἱμάντα τέῳ ἐγκάτθεο κόλπῳ (epic aor2 imperat.) put the band upon or round thy waist, Il.; ἄτην ἑῷ ἐγκάτθετο θυμῷ stored up, devised mischief in his heart, Od.; τελαμῶνα ἑῇ ἐγκάτθετο τέχνῃ designed the belt by his art, Id.
to pour in besides, Anth.
to scoff at, τινί Aesch.
to dwell in a place, Hdt.
to build in a place, Thuc.
to immure, Aeschin.
the inwards, entrails, bowels, Lat. intestina, Hom.
to grow old in, ἐν πενίᾳ Plut.
to bind fast in, Plat.
sink beneath, ὕδασιν Anth.
to adapt to, τί τινι Soph.
to burn in, Luc.
Pass. to lie in, c. dat., Theogn.
to lie in bed, sleep, Ar.
to put to bed in a place, Ar.:—Pass. to lie down in, Id.
Pass. to lie down to sleep in a place, Hdt.
to hammer in: ἐγκ. χορείαν τοῖς μύσταις to tread a measure among the mystae, Ar.
to catch in a place, to hem in, Thuc.; ἐγκ. τινὰ ὅρκοις to trammel by oaths, Aeschin.
to build in: Pass., 3rd pl. aor2 ἐγκατελέγησαν were built into the wall, Thuc.
to count among, Luc.: to enlist soldiers, Anth.
to leave behind, Hes., Thuc., etc.
to leave in the lurch, Id., etc.
to leave out, omit, Hdt.
Pass. to be left behind in a race, Id.
a sore from burning, Luc.
to lie in, be wrapped in clothes, Il., Hdt.
ἔγκεισθαί τινι to be involved in a thing, Eur.
to press upon, of troops pressing upon the enemy, Thuc.:—with an adj. or adv., πολλὸς ἐνέκειτο was very urgent, Hdt.; πολὺς ἔγκειται he insists much upon a thing, c. dat., Dem.
to be devoted to one, Theocr.
only in perf. pass. part., ἐγκεκαρμένῳ κάρᾳ with shorn head, Eur.
an encouragement, Xen.
urged on, bidden, commanded, Xen.
fut. sw, to urge on, cheer on, Aesch.; c. dat., Xen.; to sound a charge, Plut.
a sting, Ar.: a goad, Xen.
to mix in, mix, esp. wine, Il.:—Mid. to mix for oneself: metaph. to concoct, Hdt.
to abuse, mock at, τινί Eur.
that which is within the head, the brain, Hom., etc.
the edible pith of young palm-shoots, Xen.
to play the harp among, Hhymn.
to shut in, close gates, Hdt., Plat.
to shut or confine within: Pass., ἑρκέων ἐγκεκλῃμένος (for ἐντὸς ἑρκέων κεκλῃμένος) , Soph.; δόμοις ἐγκεκλῃμένος Id.
generally to confine, γλῶσσαν ἐγκλῄσας Id.
Mid. to shut oneself up in, Xen.
an accusation, charge, complaint, Soph., etc.; ἐγκλήματα ἔχειν τινός = ἐγκαλεῖν τινι, Thuc.; ἔγκλημα διαλύεσθαι Id.
litigious, Arist.
having a lot or share in a thing, c. gen., Soph.; λαχεῖν ἔγκληρά τινι to have an equal share with another, Id.
having a share of an inheritance, an heir, heiress, Eur.
ἔγκληρος εὐνή a marriage which brings wealth, Id.; ἔγκ. πεδία land possessed as an inheritance, Id.
leaning, bent down, Hhymn.
to bend in or inwards, Xen.
Pass. to lean on, rest or weigh upon one, Id.; metaph., πόνος ὔμμι ἐγκέκλιται labour lies upon you, Il.
ἐγκλίνειν νῶτόν τινι to turn one's back towards another, Eur.
intr. to give way, flee, Lat. inclinari, Xen., etc.
to decline, become worse, Plut.
to hollow or scoop out, Hdt.
sinking in hollows, hollow, Plat.
to lull to sleep in a place, Anth.
Pass. to be luxurious as Coesyra (A woman of the Alcmaeonid family), ἐγκεκοισυρωμένη Ar.
serving for a bed, Anth.
to cut or carve upon stone, Hdt.
to fall heavily upon, or to gulp down, swallow up, Ar.
to form a bay, Strab.
Mid. to bind a thing on oneself, gird oneself, NTest.
to be quick and active, make haste, hasten, Hom., Soph., etc.
Mid. to sprinkle sand over oneself before wrestling, Xen.
a tool for cutting stone, chisel, Luc.
a hindrance, NTest.
wearied, Anth.
to hinder, thwart, NTest.
to wrap up in coverlets: Pass., ἐγκεκορδυλημένη Ar.
to arrange in a place, c. dat., Od.
to be indignant at, τινί Aesch.
bearing a grudge, spiteful, malignant, Aesch.
as Subst., a grudge, ἔγκοτον ἔχειν τινί to bear a grudge against one, Hdt.
to cry aloud at one, τινί Ar.; ἐπί τινα Thuc.
mastery over a person or thing, ἐγκρ. ἑαυτοῦ self- control, Plat.
absol. self-control, Lat. continentia, Xen.
in possession of power, Soph.
holding fast, stout, strong, Aesch., Soph.
c. gen. rei, having possession of a thing, master of it, Lat. compos rei, Hdt., Soph.; ναὸς ἐγκρατῆ πόδα the sheet that controls the ship, Id.; ἐγκρατὴς ἑαυτοῦ master of oneself, Plat.
adv. -τῶς, with a strong hand, by force, Thuc.
to reckon in or among Eur.
to admit as elected, εἰς τὴν γερουσίαν Dem.: generally, to admit, accept, Plat.
admission to the contest, Luc.
one must admit, Plat.
to strike on the ground, to beat time, Theocr.:—Mid. to dash one against the other, Eur.
to knock or hammer in, Ar.: to strike, Anth.
to dance, Ar.
to hide or conceal in a place, c. dat., Od.
to keep concealed, Ar.
intr. to keep oneself hidden, act underhand, Ar.
a loaf baked in the ashes, Luc.
Dep. to acquire possessions in a foreign country, Hdt., Dem.
land held in a district by a person not belonging to it, Dem.
tenure of land in a place by a stranger, Xen.:— the right of holding such land, granted to foreigners, Decret. ap. Dem.
to mix up in, Ar.
Pass. to rotate in the sockets: metaph. to turn in, Ar.
circular, rounded, round, Eur., Aeschin.
revolving in a cycle, periodical, Dem.:— ordinary, Lat. quotidianus, Isocr., etc.
to move round in a circle, τι Eur.
Pass. to encircle, φωνή μέ τις ἐγκεκύκλωται a voice has echoed around me, Ar.
Mid. to roam about a place, c. acc., Plut.
a surrounding, Strab.
to roll up in: metaph. in Pass. to be involved in, εἴς τι Xen.
pregnant, Xen.; ἐγκύμων τευχέων big with arms, of the Trojan horse, Eur.
to stoop down and peep in, Plat.; ἐγκ. εἴς τι to look closely into, Hdt.:—absol., ἐγκεκῡφότες stooping to the ground, Ar., Thuc.
to fall in with, light upon, meet with, c. dat., Il., Hes., Hdt.

entry.etym: the augmented tenses are formed as if the Verb were a compound of ἐν and κῶμος, not a deriv. from ἐγκώμιον
entry.sense: to praise, laud, extol one, ἐπί τινι for a thing, Plat.:—Pass. to be praised, Hdt.
（κώμη) in or of the same village, native, Hes.
（κῶμος) of or belonging to a Bacchic revel, in which the victor was led home in procession with music and dancing:—hence
ἐγκώμιον, ου, τό, a song in honour of a conqueror, an eulogy, Ar., Plat.
rousing the din of war, Hes.
rousing the fight, Soph.
stirring up to revelry, Anth.

entry.etym: epic part., as if from a pres. ἐγρηγοράω = ἐγείρομαι
entry.sense: watching, waking, Od.
adv. awake, watching, Il.
to be awake or watchful, Hom.
to put a bit in the mouth of a horse, c. acc., Babr.:—Pass. of horses, to have the bit in their mouths, Hdt., Xen.
in or with brass: moneyed, rich, Anth.
to engrave upon a thing, Plut.
to gape, Luc.
to grin or scoff at one, c. dat., Ar.
Lat. incacare, Ar.: c. acc. to be in a horrid fright at one, Id.
epic form of ἔγχος, a spear, lance, Hom.; gen. pl. ἐγχειάων, dat. ἐγχείῃσι.
to put one's hand in or to a thing, to attempt it, c. dat. rei, Eur., Thuc.; c. inf., Xen., etc.: absol. to make an attempt or beginning, Soph., Thuc.
to lay hands on, attack, assail, τινι Id., Xen.
an undertaking, attempt, Soph., Plat., etc.
a taking in hand, undertaking, Thuc., Plut.
one must undertake, Xen.
an undertaker, an adventurer, Ar.
enterprising, adventurous, Xen.
in the hand, Aesch.
as Subst., ἐγχειρίδιον, ου, τό, a hand-knife, dagger, Hdt.
to put into one's hands, entrust, τί or τινά τινι Hdt., Thuc., etc.: —Pass., ἐγχειρίζεσθαί τι to be entrusted with a thing, Luc.
Mid. to take in hand, encounter, κινδύνους Thuc.
put into one's hands, Hdt.
of an eel, τἀγχέλεια (sub. κρέα) eel's flesh, Ar.
an eel, Lat. anguilla, Il., Ar., etc.
eel-faced, Luc.
eager with the spear, Hom.
entry.etym: The deriv. of -μωρος is uncertain, cf. ἰόμωρος, ὑλακόμωρος.

entry.sense: wielding the spear, Il.

entry.note: fut. -χεῶ aor1 ἐν-έχεα epic ἐν-έχευα epic 3rd sg. subj. ἐγχέῃ epic ἐγχείῃ perf. pass. -κέχῠμαι
entry.sense: to pour in, μέθυ ἐγχ. δεπάεσσι Od.; οἶνον ἐς κύλικα Hdt.; ἐγχεῖν alone, to pour in wine, to fill the cup, Xen., etc.: —Mid. to fill one's cup, Ar.
of dry things, to pour in, shoot in, Od.
with acc. of the cup, to fill by pouring in, Xen.
ἐγχεῖν ὕδωρ τινί, i. e. to fill the κλεψύδρα (q. v.), Dem.
in or of the country, Anth.
a spear, lance, often in Hom., consisting of two parts, αἰχμή and δόρυ, head and shaft, Il.
iI. any weapon, a sword, Soph., Eur.:—metaph., φροντίδος ἔγχος Soph.
entry.etym: Prob. akin to Root ΑΚ, in ἀκή, ἀκών.

entry.sense: the plant alkanet, the root of which yields a red dye, Xen.
to dash against, Lat. impingere, Hdt.:—perf. part. pass., ἔσαν ἐγκεχρημένοι (sc. πόλεμοι) there were wars urged on, Id.
Dep. to expectorate, Luc.
to have need: ἐγχρῄζοντα necessaries, Luc.
to bring near to, τῷ [τέρματι] ἐγχρίμψας so as almost to touch the post, Il.; ἐγχρ. τὴν βᾶριν τῇ γῇ to bring the boat close to land, Hdt.

intr. to come near, approach, τινί Soph.:—so in Pass., ἐγχριμφθεὶς πύλῃσιν Il.; αἰχμὴ ὀστέῳ ἐγχριμφθεῖσα the point driven to the very bone, Id.; ἀσπίδ’ (i.e. ἀσπίδι) ἐνιχριμφθείς dashed against his shield, Id.
rubbed in as an ointment, Theocr.
to rub, anoint, τινί with a thing, Anth.
to sting, prick, τινί Plat.
to be long about a thing, to delay, Thuc.:—Pass. to become chronic, Plat.
Pass. to be engrained: — metaph. to be amalgamated with, c. dat., Arist.
to expose children in an earthenware vessel: hence, to make an end of, Ar.
to give room for doing a thing, to allow, permit, Hdt., Xen.:— ἐγχωρεῖ, impers. it is possible or allowable, c. dat. pers. et inf., Plat., Xen., etc.: absol., ἔτι ἐγχωρεῖ there is yet time, Plat.
in or of the country, Hdt., attic
as Subst. a dweller in the land, inhabitant, Soph., Eur.
τὸ ἐγχώριον as adv. according to the custom of the country, Thuc.
strengthd. form of ἐγώ, Lat. equidem, I at least, for my part, for myself,
pron. of the first person, Lat ego
eatable: ἐδανόν, food, Aesch.
sweet, delicious, Il.
to dash to the ground, NTest.

entry.etym: prob. from same Root as ὀδός, οὖδας
entry.sense: the bottom, foundation, base of anything, Thuc.; ἔδαφος νηός the bottom, hold of a ship, Od.; ἔδ. ποταμοῦ Xen.
the ground-floor, pavement, οἴκου Hdt.; καθαιρεῖν εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος to rase to the ground, Thuc.
ground, soil, land, Aeschin., Dem.
a seat, abode, Aesch.
meat: pl. meats, Batr., Plat.
one must eat, Plat.
an eater, Hdt.
eatable: eaten, consumed, Soph.
meat, food, (ἔδω) Hom.
mostly in pl. ἕδνα, epic ἔεδνα, a wedding-gift, presented by the suitor to the bride or her parents (φερνή being the bride's portion), Hom., Aesch.
of wedding-gifts made to the bride by those of her own household, Od., Eur.
to promise for wedding-presents, to betroth one's daughter, Theocr.:—so in Mid., Od.
in Mid. also, to marry, Anth.
a betrother, Il.
a sitting-place:
a seat, chair, stool, bench, Il.
a seat, abode, dwelling place, Hom., etc.:— a temple, Plat., Xen., etc.
a foundation, base, Hes., Anth.
the act of sitting, οὐχ ἕδος ἐστί 'tis no time to sit still, Il.
to make to sit, place, Anth.
sitting, sedentary, Xen., Plat.
ἑδραία ῥάχις the horse's back on which the rider sits, Eur.
sitting fast, steady, steadfast, Id., Plat.
a foundation, base, NTest.
a seat, abode, Aesch., Soph.
a stay, support, of an anchor, Anth.
a sitting-place:
a seat, chair, stool, bench, Hom.: a seat of honour, Il., Xen.
a seat, of the gods, a sanctuary, temple, Pind., Trag.
the seat or place of anything, Hdt.; ἐξ ἕδρας out of its right place, Eur.:— a foundation, base, Plut.
ἡ ἕδρα τοῦ ἵππου the back of the horse, on which the rider sits, Xen.
ἕδραι are the quarters of the sky in which omens appear, Aesch., Eur.
a sitting, Aesch., Soph.: of a position, γονυπετεῖς ἕδραι kneeling, Eur.
a sitting still, inactivity, delay, Hdt., Thuc.; οὐχ ἕδρας ἀκμή 'tis not the season for sitting still, Soph.
the sitting of a council, Id.
the seat, breech, fundament, Hdt.
to seat or set:—Pass. to sit, in epic forms 3rd pl. pres. and imperf. ἑδριόωνται, ἑδριόωντο, Hom., Hes.; inf. ἑδριάασθαι, Id.
intr. in Act. to sit, Theocr.
a wrestler who throws his adversary by a cross-buttock, Theocr.
food, meat, victuals, Hom., Plat.
fodder for cattle, Il.
a bait for fish, Theocr.
eatable, Hdt., Thuc., etc.: ἐδώδιμα, τά, eatables, provisions, Thuc.
a seat, mostly in pl., abodes, Aesch., Soph.
in a ship, ἑδώλια are the rowingbenches, or rather a half-deck, Hdt., Soph., Eur.

entry.etym: old epic pres. for attic ἐσθίω
entry.sense: to eat, Hom.: of beasts, to eat, devour, Id.; of worms, to gnaw, Id.
to eat up, devour, consume, βίοτον, κτήματα Od.: also, ἄλγεσι θυμὸν ἔδοντες Id.
him, acc. of οὗ.
to seat oneself, sit, ἐν λέκτρωι, ἐπὶ δίφρωι, κατὰ κλισμούς Hom.; ἐπὶ χθονὶ ἑζέσθην they sank to the earth, of a pair of scales, Il.:—cf καθέζομαι.
there is no act. pres., ἕζω, to set, place; though, as if from it, we have trans. tenses εἷσα, mid. εἱσάμην, fut. mid. εἵσομαι, perf. pass. εἷμαι; v. εἷσα.
exclam., like ἔ or ἔ ἔ.
customary, accustomed to a thing, c. gen., Thuc., Plut.
to have long hair, Theocr. once in Hom., to tend, take care of a field.
hair, used by Hom. in pl., either of a horse's mane, or of the horsehair crest on helmets:—later in sg. and pl. of the hair of the head, Aesch., Eur., etc.; of a lion's mane, Theocr.
willing, voluntary, Hes.
willing slavery, Plat.
a willing slave, Plat.
will-worship, NTest.
to be slack in duty, play the coward purposely, Hdt.
wilfully bad or cowardly.
adv. voluntarily, Thuc.
Adv. voluntarily, Hdt.
a volunteer, Od.

entry.etym: later form of ἐθελοντήρ, Hdt., Thuc., etc.

entry.sense: willing to work, Xen.
one who voluntarily charges himself with the office of πρόξενος (q. v.), Thuc.
willing to work, Xen.
voluntary, Xen.
of things, optional, matter of free choice, Id.
to will, wish, purpose; c. acc. et inf. to wish that . . , c. inf. to wish to do, Hom., attic; c. acc., inf. being omitted, τί θέλων (sc. πρᾶξαι) Aesch.
with a negat., almost = δύναμαι, μίμνειν οὐκ ἐθέλεσκον they cared not to make a stand, i. e. they were unable, Il.
of things,
much like μέλλω, merely to express a future event, εἰ θελήσει ἀναβῆναι ἡ τυραννίς if the monarchy will revert, Hdt.
to be wont or accustomed, c. inf., Id., Thuc.
to mean, purport, τί ἐθέλει τὸ ἔπος Lat. quid sibi vult? French que veut-il dire? Hdt., etc.
to gather customarily, Anth.
to accustom, use, ἐθ. τινὰ ποιεῖν τι Plat., Xen.:—Pass. to be or become accustomed or used to do, c. inf., Thuc.
one must accustom, Xen.
to be acquired by habit, Arist.
an ethnarch, NTest., Luc.
foreign, heathen, gentile, NTest.: adv. -νικῶς, Id.
a number of people accustomed to live together, a company, body of men, Il., etc.; ἔθνος λαῶν a host of men, Id.; also of animals, swarms, flocks, Id., Soph.
after Hom., a nation, people, Hdt., etc.:—in NTest. τὰ ἔθνη the nations, Gentiles, i. e. all but Jews and Christians.
a special class of men, a caste, tribe, Plat., Xen.
sex, Id.
custom, habit, Aesch., etc.; ἐν ἔθει εἶναι to be in the habit, Thuc.; ἔθει habitually, Arist.

to be accustomed: the pres. only in partic., κακὰ πόλλ’ ἔρδεσκεν ἔθων much ill he wrought by custom, i. e. was accustomed to work, Il.; otherwise, perf. εἴωθα, ionic ἔωθα is used as a pres., and plup. εἰώθειν, ionic ἐώθεα, as imperf.:— to be wont or accustomed, be in the habit, c. inf., Il., Hdt., etc.:—in part. absol. accustomed, customary, usual, Il., Soph., etc.; in neut., κατὰ τὸ εἰωθός according to custom, παρὰ τὸ εἰωθός contrary to custom, Thuc.
a river-side pasture, meadow, ἐν εἰαμενῇ ἕλεος in a marshy meadow, Il.
Lat. eia, Interj. on! up! away! with imperat., Trag.; εἶα δή come then! Aesch.; εἶα νῦν well now! Ar., etc.
with youthful breasts, Anth.
to drop, let fall in drops, Hom.:—Pass. to trickle down, Hes.
shapely, comely, Od.
like, looking like, Anth.
food, and of horses, fodder, Hom.
knowing or expert in a thing, τινός Anth.
the Roman Idus, Plut.
Lat. videor, to be seen, appear, εἴδεται ἄστρα they are visible, appear Il.
c. inf. to appear or seem to be, τοῦτό μοι κάλλιστον εἴδεται εἶναι Od.; also with inf. omitted, τόγε κέρδιον εἴσατο Id.; also, εἴσατ’ ἴμεν he made a show of going, Id.
in strictly middle sense, c. dat., ἐείσατο φθογγὴν Πολίτηι she made herself like Polites in voice, Il.:—also to be like, Id.

entry.etym: Root ϜΙΔ, Lat. video to see:

not used in act. pres., ὁράω being used instead; but pres. is used in Mid., v. εἴδομαι; aor2 εἶδον retains the proper sense of to see: but perf. οἶδα, (I have seen) means I know, and is used as a pres. The form ὄψομαι is used as fut., ἑόρᾱκα or ἑώρᾱκα as perf.
entry.sense: to see, perceive, behold, Hom., etc.; after a Noun, θαῦμα ἰδέσθαι a marvel to behold, Il.; οἰκτρὸς ἰδεῖν Aesch.
to look at, εἰς ὦπα ἰδέσθαι to look him in the face, Il., etc.
to look so and so, ἀχρεῖον ἰδών looking helpless, Id.
to see mentally, ἰδέσθαι ἐν φρεσίν "to see in his mind's eye, " Hom.
to make an image of a thing, to mould, Plut.
the specific nature of a thing, Strab.
forming a species, specific, Arist.
that which is seen, form, shape, figure, Lat. species, forma, Hom.; absol. in acc., εἶδος ἄριστος, etc.
a form, sort, particular kind or nature, Hdt., etc.
a particular state of things or course of action, Thuc.
a class, kind, sort, whether genus or species, Plat., etc.
knowingly, Aeschin.
Dim. of εἶδος: a short descriptive poem, mostly on pastoral subjects, an idyll, Theocr., etc.
an idol's temple, NTest.
sacrificed to idols: εἰδωλόθυτα, τά, meats offered to idols, NTest.
idolatry, NTest.
an idol-worshipper, idolater, NTest.
an image, a phantom, Hom., Hdt.; βροτῶν εἴδωλα καμόντων phantoms of dead men, Od.; of any unsubstantial form, σκιᾶς εἴδωλον Aesch.; οὐδὲν ἄλλο πλὴν εἴδωλα Soph.
an image in the mind, idea, Xen.:—also a fancy, Plat.
an image, likeness, Hdt.
an image, idol, NTest.
to form an image in the mind, Plat.
formation of images, as in a mirror, Plat.
an image-maker, Plat.

entry.etym: Particle, only used in attic dialogue,
entry.sense: well! Lat. esto! be it so! εἶεν· τί δῆτα; Soph.; εἶεν· καὶ δὴ τεθνᾶσι Eur.
at once, forthwith, Il., Theocr.
would that! Lat. utinam: v. εἰ A. II. 1.
to make like to, represent by a likeness, portray, Xen.; εἰκὼν γραφῆι εἰκασμένη a figure painted to the life, Hdt.; αἰετὸς εἰκασμένος a figure like an eagle, Id.
to liken, compare, τί τινι Aesch., Ar.; εἰκ. τι καί τι Hdt.: to describe by a comparison, Id.:—Pass. to resemble, τινι Eur.

to infer from comparison, form a conjecture, Hdt., Soph.; ὡς εἰκάσαι, so far as one can guess, Hdt.:—c. acc. et inf. to guess that it is so, guess it to be, Id., Thuc.: —εἰκ. τι ἔκ τινος Aesch., Thuc.; ἀπό τινος Id.; εἰκ. τι to make a guess about it, Aesch.
random, purposeless, Luc.
a likeness, image, Xen.
a comparison, a conjecture, Plat.
a likeness, image, Aesch.
a conjecturing, Plut., Luc.
the twentieth day of the month (sub. ἡμέρα), Hes.: the days from 21 to 30 were called αἱ εἰκάδες Ar.
the sixth day of the Eleusinian mysteries, Eur.
one who conjectures, a diviner, τῶν μελλόντων Thuc.
able to represent or conjecture: τὸ εἰκαστικόν the faculty of conjecturing, Luc.
comparable, similar, Soph.
dream-like, Ar.
like, Lat. similis, τινι Hom., Hdt.
of like voice, Anth.
without plan or purpose, heedlessly, rashly, at random, at a venture, Lat. temere, Aesch., etc.
counterfeited, pretended, Anth.
worth twenty oxen, Od.
of twenty years, Hdt.
twenty times, Il.
twenty months old, Anth.
twenty-fold without dispute, Il.
indecl., twenty, Lat. viginti, Il., etc.; also in epic form ἐείκοσι, before a vowel ἐείκοσιν, Id.
of twenty cubits, Hdt.
with twenty oars, Od.

entry.etym: neut. partic. of εἶκα or ἔοικα,
entry.sense: like truth, i. e. likely, probable, reasonable, Lat. verisimile, Trag.
as Subst. εἰκός, τό, a likelihood or probability, τὰ οἰκότα likelihoods, Hdt.; κατὰ τὸ εἰκός in all likelihood, Thuc.; ἐκ τοῦ εἰκότος Id.; ἤν γ’ ἐρωτᾷς εἰκότ’, εἰκότα κλύεις Eur.
reasonable, fair, equitable, Thuc.
one who collects the twentieth, a tax or toll collector, Ar.
the twentieth, Od.; epic also ἐεικοστός, Il.
εἰκοστή, ἡ, a tax of a twentieth, Lat. vicesima, levied by the Athenians on imports and exports from the allies in lieu of tribute, Thuc.
of 20 fathoms, Xen.

entry.etym: adverb of εἰκώς, attic perf. part. of ἔοικα,
entry.sense: in all likelihood, suitably, fairly, reasonably, naturally, Aesch., etc.; εἰκότως ἔχει 'tis reasonable, Eur.; οὐκ εἰκότως un reasonably, Thuc.
a likeness, image, portrait, Hdt., Aesch.
an image in a mirror, Eur., Plat.
a semblance, phantom, Eur., Plat., etc.: an image in the mind, Id.
a similitude, simile, Ar., Plat.

entry.etym: Root ϜΙΚ, cf. Lat. vito for victo ; cf. εἰκαθεῖν
entry.sense: to yield, give way, draw back, retire, Il.
c. dat. pers. et gen. loci, μηδ’ εἴκετε χάρμης Ἀργείοις shrink not from the fight for them, Id.; εἴκειν τινὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ, Lat. concedere alicui de via, Hdt.

with dat. pers. only, to yield to, give way to, either in battle or a mark of honour, Hom.:—then, to give way to any passion or impulse, ὧι θυμῶι εἴξας Il.; αἰδοῖ Od.:—also of circumstances, πενίηι εἴκων Id.; κακοῖς, ἀνάγκηι Aesch.
εἴκειν τινί τι, where the acc. is adverbial, μένος οὐδενὶ εἴκων yielding to none in force, Hom.; c. acc. cogn., εἴξαντας ἃ δεῖ yielding in . . , Soph.
trans. to yield up, give up, εἶξαί τέ οἱ ἡνία give the horse the rein, Il.:— to grant, allow, Lat. concedere, ὁπηνίκ’ ἂν θεὸς πλοῦν ἡμὶν εἴκηι Soph.
impers., like παρείκει, it is allowable or possible, Il.
to revel in a large company, Od.
a feaster, quest, boon-companion, Il.
a feast or banquet, given by a single host, opp. to ἔρανος (q. v.), Hom., Eur.

entry.etym: only in nom. and acc. sg.
entry.sense: a close covering, shelter, defence, εἶλαρ νηῶν τε καὶ αὐτῶν shelter for ship and crew, Il.; εἶλαρ κύματος a fence against the waves, Od.
a commander of a troop of horse, esp. at Thebes, Plut.

entry.etym: A quasiparticipial form, as if ἐληλυθυῖα, the readycomer
entry.sense: Ilithyia, the goddess who comes to aid women in child-birth, Lat. Lucina, Il.:
a lurking-place, den, hole, Theocr.
by twisting round, Anth.
Mid. to bask in the sun, Luc.
the sun's heat or warmth, Ar.
κατ’ εἴλας in troops, Id.
sun-heat, heat, Plat.
unmixed, without alloy, pure, Lat. sincerus, Xen., Plat.; εἰλικρινεῖ τῇ διανοίᾳ χρώμενος using pure intellect, Id.; εἰλ. ἀδικία sheer in justice, Xen.
adv. -νῶς, without mixture, of itself, simply, absolutely, Plat.
entry.etym: The origin of εἰλι- is uncertain.

entry.sense: rolling in their gait, with rolling walk, Hom.
epith. of the plant ἄγρωστις, Theocr., prob. from ἕλος, τείνω spreading through marshes.
a wrapper, Od.
a lurking place, den, Xen.
to roll along (trans.), Il.
intr. to roll or whirl about, of a torch, Hes.
to enfold, enwrap, Il.:—Pass. to be wrapt or covered, νεφέληι εἰλυμένος ὤμους, etc., Hom.
Pass., also, = ἰλυσπάομαι, to crawl or wriggle along, of a lame man, Soph.
in Theocr. εἰλυσθείς means rolled up, crouching.

to roll up, pack close, Lat. conglobare, κατὰ τείχεα λαὸν ἐέλσαι to roll up the host and force it back to the walls, Il.; Ἀχαιοὺς ἐπὶ πρύμνηισιν ἐείλεον Id.; εἰλεῖν ἐν μέσσοισι to coop up or hem in on all sides, Id.; θῆρας ὁμοῦ εἰλεῖν to drive game together, Od.:—Pass. to be cooped or huddled up, εἰς ἄστυ ἄλεν (for ἄλησαν) Id.; νηυσὶν ἐπὶ γλαφυρῆισιν ἐελμένοι Id.:—metaph., Διὸς βουλῆισιν ἐελμένος straitened, held in check by the counsels of Zeus, Id.
to smite, νῆα κεραυνῶι Ζεὺς ἔλσας having smitten the ship with lightning, Id.
to collect: Pass., ἀλὲν ὕδωρ water collected, ponded, Il.
Pass., also, to draw oneself up, shrink up, ἀλῆναι ὑπ’ ἀσπίδι Id.; Ἀχιλῆα ἀλεὶς μένεν collecting himself he waited the attack of Achilles, Id.
Pass. also, to go to and fro, like Lat. versari, Hdt.
to wind, turn round:— Pass. to turn round, revolve, ἰλλομένων ἀρότρων moving to and fro, Soph.; ἕλιξ εἰλεῖται is twined round, Theocr.
a Helot, name of the Spartan serfs, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
the condition of a Helot, Plat.
to be a Helot or serf, Isocr.
of Helots, Plut.
a garment, in pl. clothes, clothing, Hom., etc.
a cover, rug, carpet, Aesch., Soph.

ibo, In Prose εἶμι serves as fut. to ἔρχομαι, I shall go, shall come. to come or go, Hom., etc.; c. acc. cogn., ὁδὸν ἰέναι to go a road, Od.:—in Hom., c. gen., ἰὼν πεδίοιο going across the plain; χροὸς εἴσατο went through the skin.

to go in a ship, Od.; of birds, to fly, Id.: of things, πέλεκυς εἶσι διὰ δουρός the axe goes through the beam, Il.; φάτις εἶσι the report goes, Od.; metaph. usages, ἰέναι ἐς λόγους τινί to enter on a conference with one, Thuc., etc.; ἰέναι ἐς χεῖρας to come to blows, Id.; ἰέναι διὰ δίκης πατρί to contest the point with him, Soph.; ἰέναι διὰ μάχης, διὰ φιλίας to live in conflict, in friendship with others, etc.
the Imperat. ἴθι is used like ἄγε, Lat. age, come, come now, mostly followed by 2nd sg. imperat., ἴθι λέξον Ar., etc.; with 1st pl. ἴθι ἐπισκεψώμεθα Xen.
ἴτω let it pass, well then, Soph., Eur.
the part. is added by Trag. to Verbs, φρονείτω ἰών let him go and think, Soph.

entry.etym: The whole of the pres. ind. (except 2nd sg. εἶ) may be enclitic when εἰμί is the Copula; but the 3rd sg. is written ἔστι in certain cases of emphasis, e. g. ἔστι μοι, I have: when used as Verb Subst., it retains the accent in all persons.
entry.sense: as Substantive Verb, to be, to exist, οὐκ ἔσθ’ οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὐδ’ ἔσσεται Od.; τεθνηῶτος, μηδ’ ἔτ’ ἐόντος Id.; οὐκέτ’ ἔστι he is no more, Eur.; θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες Il.; ἐσσόμενοι posterity, Id.; ζώντων καὶ ὄντων Ἀθηναίων Dem.:—so of cities, etc., ὄλωλεν, οὐδ’ ἔτ’ ἔστι Τροία (cf. Troja fuit), Eur.
of things, to be, exist, εἰ ἔστιν ἀληθέως [ἡ τράπεζα] Hdt.; ἕως ἂν ὁ πόλεμος ἦι so long as it last, Thuc.
to be, opp. to appearing to be, as esse to videri, τὸν ἐόντα λόγον the true story, Hdt.; τὰ ὄντα ἀπαγγέλλειν Thuc.; τῶι ὄντι, Lat. revera, in reality, in fact, Plat.

foll. by the Relative, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅς, no one, Il., etc.; εἰσὶν οἵ, Lat. sunt qui, Thuc., etc.; ἐστὶν ἅ some things, Id.; also ἔστιν οἵ, for εἰσὶν οἵ, Hdt., etc.:—so withrelat. Particles, ἔστιν ἔνθα, Lat. est ubi, Xen., etc.; ἔστιν ὅπη, ἔσθ’ ὅπου, somewhere, or somehow, Plat., etc.; ἔστιν ὅπως in some manner, Hdt., etc.; ἔστιν ὅτε, ἔσθ’ ὅτε, sometimes, Soph., etc.
ἔστι impers., c. inf., like πάρεστι, it is possible, Hom., attic
to be, Copula connecting predicate with subject, both being in the same case, Hom., etc.
sometimes εἶναι with Part. represents finite Verb, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, Aesch.; πεφυκός ἐστι = πέφυκε, Ar.
the Inf. is redundant in some phrases, ἑκὼν εἶναι (v. ἑκών II); τὸ ἐπ’ ἐκείνοις εἶναι quantum in illis esset, Thuc.; τὸ σύμπαν εἶναι Hdt.; τὸ νῦν εἶναι Plat., etc.
of nine years: neut. εἰνάετες, as adv. nine years long, Od.
roaming the sea, of nets, Anth.
as adv. nine nights long, Il.
the ninth day of the month, Hes.
sisters-in-law, Il.
ninth, Il., Hdt.
with quivering foliage, Il.
until, Hom.
strengthd. for εἰ, if really, if indeed, Hom., etc.; also, even if, even though, Id.
in attic if that is to say, implying doubt of the fact, εἴπερ ἦν πέλας if I had been (but I was not), Soph.

entry.etym: pres. in use is φήμι, ἀγορεύω, fut. ἐρέω, ἐρῶ, perf. εἴρηκα
entry.sense: to speak, say, Hom., etc.; in parenthesis, ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν so to say, Lat. ut ita dicam, Thuc., etc.; so, ὡς εἰπεῖν, ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν Id.
c. acc. pers. to speak to, address, accost one, Il.
to name, mention, Id.
to call one so and so, πολλοὶ δέ μιν ἐσθλὸν ἔειπον Od.
c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, to say or tell of one, ἀτάσθαλόν τι εἰπεῖν τινα Id.; κακὰ εἰπεῖν τινα Ar.
at Athens, to propose or move a measure in the ἐκκλησία, Thuc., etc.
if ever, Lat. si-quando, Hom.
indirect, if or whether ever, Id.
if anywhere, if at all, Lat. si-cubi, Hom., etc.; εἴ τί που ἐστίν, if it is any way possible, Od.
a Conditional Conjunction, Lat. si, if; and in indirect questions, whether.
with a verb in protasis, answered by a similar tense in apodosis:
with pres. and fut. ind., to express mere Possibility, εἰ τοῦτο ποιεῖ (or ποιήσει), ἁμαρτάνει (or ἁμαρτήσεται) if he is doing (or shall do) this, he is (or will be) wrong.

with imperf. and aor. ind., to express Impossibility, εἰ τοῦτο ἐποίει, ἡμάρτανεν ἄν if he was doing this, he would be wrong; εἰ τοῦτο ἐποίησεν, ἥμαρτεν ἄν if he did (or had done) this, he would be wrong.
with opt. to express a mere Assumption, εἰ τοῦτο ποιοῖ, ἁμαρτάνοι ἄν if he were to do this, he would be wrong.

with Subjunctive, to express Possibility with some degree of Probability: in this case ἄν is always added, and εἰ ἄν becomes ἐάν, ἤν, ἄν, (epic εἴ κεν), ἐὰν τοῦτο ποιῇ, ἁμαρτήσεται if he do this, he will be wrong.
sometimes the apodosis is omitted, so that εἰ expresses a wish, εἴ μοι γένοιτο φθόγγος if I had a voice, [I would . . ], i. e. Oh that I had a voice! so εἰ γάρ, εἴθε, epic αἰ γάρ, αἴθε.
sometimes the protasis is omitted, εἰ δ’ ἄγε come on, = εἰ δὲ [βούλει], ἄγε, Od.; εἰ δέ, σὺ μὲν ἄκουσον Il.
εἰ δὲ μή = Lat. sin minus, otherwise, for εἰ δὲ μὴ [τοῦτό ἐστι], Hdt., etc.
In Indirect Questions, whether, Lat. an, followed by the ind., subj., or opt., according to the principles of oratio obliqua:
with INDIC. or SUBJ. after primary tenses, οὐκ οἶδ’, εἰ θεός ἐστιν whether he is a god, Il.; οὐκ οἶδ’ εἰ δῶ whether I shall give, Xen.
with OPTAT. after past tenses, ἤρετο εἴ τις ἐμοῦ εἴη σοφώτερος he asked whether any one was wiser than I, Plat.
after Verbs expressive of wonder, indignation, etc., θαυμάζω εἰ μηδεὶς ὀργίζεται, where εἰ nearly = ὅτι, Dem.; ἀγανακτεῖ εἰ μὴ στεφανωθήσεται Aeschin.
a cage, prison, Plat.
a gaoler, Xen.
to shut in or up, epic imperf. ἐέργνυν, Od.
bondage, slavery, Od.
rowing, Od., Hdt., etc.: —metaph., εἰρ. πτερῶν Luc.
in collective sense, the rowers, oarsmen, Lat. remigium, Eur., Thuc.
a boat-song, Plut., Luc.
a harvest-wreath of olive or laurel wound round with wool, borne about by singing boys at the Πυανέψια and Θαργήλια and then hung up at the house door, Ar.
peaceful, peaceable, Hdt.: τὰ εἰρηναῖα the fruits of peace, Id.: adv. -ως, Id.
to bring to peace, reconcile, Babr.
intr. to keep peace, live peaceably, Plat., NTest.
peace, time of peace, Hom., etc.; ἐπ’ εἰρήνης in peace, Il.; εἰρ. γίγνεται peace is made, Hdt.; εἰρήνην ποιεῖν or ποιεῖσθαι to make a peace; εἰρ. ἄγειν to keep peace, Ar.; λύειν to break it, Dem.
of or for peace, peaceful, Plat., etc.: adv. -κῶς, peaceably, Xen.
a peace-maker, Xen.
a guardian of peace, Xen.
a Lacedaemonian youth who had completed his 20th year, when he was entrusted with authority over his juniors, Plut.
a place of assembly, epic gen. pl. εἰράων Il.
one must prevent, Soph.
an inclosure, prison, Hdt.:—also the inner part of the house, the women's apartments, Xen.
dressing wool, Il.
wool-fleeced, woolly, Hom.
wool, Od.
delighting in wool, Anth.
dissimulation, i. e. assumed ignorance, irony, Plat., etc.
Dep. to dissemble, i. e. feign ignorance, Plat., etc.: generally, to dissemble, shuffle, Ar.
dissembling, putting on a feigned ignorance, Plat.: adv. -κῶς, Ar.
a dissembler, one who says less than he thinks, Lat. dissimulator, Arist., etc.

entry.etym: The Root is prob. ΣΕΡ, cf. Lat. sero, serui, σειρά
entry.sense: to fasten together in rows, to string, ἠλέκτροισιν ἐερμένος a necklace strung with pieces of electron, Od.
one who announces, a gentleman usher at the Persian court, Hdt.
at Athens, an impeachment, Brought before the Senate of 500, or (sometimes) the ἐκκλησία, Xen.
to go in and announce a person (cf. εἰσαγγελεύς) , Hdt., Eur., etc.
to announce, report a thing, Thuc.:—Pass., ἐσαγγελθέντων ὅτι . . information having been given that . . , Id.
to impeach, Dem., etc.; cf. εἰσαγγελία.
of or for impeachment, ap. Dem.
to collect into a place, Hom.:— Mid., νέον δ’ ἐσαγείρατο θυμόν he gathered fresh courage, Il.: but also in pass. sense, θοῶς δ’ ἐσαγείρατο λαὸς [εἰς τὰς ναῦς] Od.

to lead in or into, to introduce, c. dupl. acc., αὐτοὺς εἰσῆγον δόμον Od.; also, εἰσάγειν τινὰ ἐς . . , Hdt.; or c. dat., τινὰ δόμοις Eur.:—Mid. to admit forces into a city, Thuc.: also to introduce into a league, Hdt.
ἐσάγειν or ἐσάγεσθαι γυναῖκα to lead a wife into one's house, ducere uxorem, Id.
to import foreign wares, Id., attic; so in Mid., Hdt., etc.
ἰατρὸν εἰσάγειν τινί to call in a physician, Xen.
to introduce new customs, Hdt., Eur.
to bring in, bring forward, esp. on the stage, Ar., Plat.
εἰσάγειν τι ἐς τὴν βουλήν to bring before the Council, Xen.
as law-term, εἰσάγειν δίκην or γραφήν to bring a cause into court, Lat. litem intendere, Aesch., Dem.: εἰς. τινά to bring into court, prosecute, Plat.
one who brings cases into court, Dem.
importation of goods, Plat.
as law-term, a bringing causes into court, Id.
that can or may be imported, Plat.
as law-term, within the jurisdiction of the court, δίκη Dem.
for εἰς ἀεί for ever, Aesch., Soph.
Mid. to take to oneself. Theogn.
to discern, descry, Il.
to bring or carry in, Ar.
to dart in or into, Ar.
to listen or hearken to, c. gen., Theocr.
to throw or hurl javelins at, τινά Hdt.; εἰς τὰ γυμνά Thuc.
absol. to dart or spout, of blood, Eur.
to hearken or give ear to one, Il.; c. acc. rei, Hhymn.; c. gen. pers., Soph., Eur., etc.
in Poets, simply, to hear, Soph., Eur.
c. dat. pers. to hearken to, give heed to, Hdt.
one must bring into court (v. εἰσάγω II. 3), Ar., Xen.

entry.note: fut. -ᾰλοῦμαι epic 3rd sg. aor2 ἐσᾶλτο aor1 mid. -ηλάμην
entry.sense: Dep.:— to spring or rush into, c. acc., Il.; ἐσάλλ. ἐς τὸ πῦρ to leap into it, Hdt.
to go into, enter, Aesch.
to go up to or into, c. acc., Hom.
to force into a thing, to constrain, τινά Aesch.
to lead up into, c. acc., Od.
to look up to, c. acc., Il.
to go up into, c. acc., Il.
right opposite, ἔς. ἰδεῖν to look in the face, Hom.
for εἰς ἅπαξ at once, once for all, Hdt., attic
to drive or force in upon, Hdt.
to look at, view, Anth.
for εἰς αὖθις hereafter, afterwards, Eur., Plat.
for εἰς αὔριον on the morrow, Ar.
to let in, admit, Xen.
to come to, τινά Od.
Dep.:— to come into or to, reach or arrive at a place, c. acc., Od., Eur.; ἐσαπ. ἐς τόπον Hdt.; also c. dat., Id.
to go into a ship, to go on board ship, embark, Od.; ἐσβ. ἐς ναῦν Hdt.
generally, to go into, enter, δόμους Eur.; εἰσβ. κακά to come into miseries, Soph.
Causal in aor1 ἀνέβησα, to make to go into, put on board, Il.
to throw into, put into, foll. by εἰς, Hdt., attic:—Mid. to put on board one's ship, Hdt.
intr. to throw oneself into, make an inroad into, εἰς χώραν Id., attic; πρὸς πόλιν εἰσβ. to fall upon it, Thuc.:—poet., c. acc., to come upon, fall in with, Eur.
of rivers, to empty themselves into, fall into, Hdt.
an entrance, means of entrance, Eur.: embarkation, Thuc.
accessible, Thuc.
Dep.:
to force one's way into, εἰς οἶκον Plut.
to force oneself into the citizenship, Ar.
to put on board ship, τὸν στρατὸν ἐς τὰς νέας Hdt.
generally, to make to go into, ἐς τόπον Id.
to look at, look upon, mostly with εἰς, Hdt.; but c. acc., Eur.
an inroad, invasion, attack, Hdt., Eur.
an entrance, pass, ἡ ἐσβ. ἡ Ὀλυμπική the pass of Mount Olympus, Hdt.: a strait, Eur.:—so in pl., of Thermopylae, Hdt.:—in pl. also, the mouth of a river, Id.
an entering into a thing, a beginning, Eur., Ar.
to write in, inscribe:—Mid., ἐς τὰς σπονδὰς εἰσγράψασθαι to have oneself written or received into the league, Thuc.

entry.note: Dep., with aor2 act. -έδρᾰκον perf. εἰσδέδροκα
entry.sense: to look at or upon, Hom., Eur.
Dep.:— to take into, admit, ἐς τὸ ἱρόν Hdt.; c. acc., Eur.; c. dat., ἄντροις εἰσδέξασθαί τινα to receive him in the cave, Id.; εἰσδ. τινα ὑπόστεγον Soph.
II. 2, of rivers, to flow into, Hdt.
reception, εἰσδοχαὶ δόμων a hospitable house, Eur.

entry.etym: from εἰσδράμεῖν, aor2 inf. of εἰστρέχω
entry.sense: an inroad, onslaught, Eur., Thuc.

entry.note: Dep. εἰσ-δύομαι fut. -δύσομαι with aor2 act. -έδῡν perf. -δέδῡκα
entry.sense: to get or go into, with εἰς, Od., Hdt., etc.
c. acc. to enter, Lat. subire, Il., Hdt.:—of feelings, εἰσέδυ με μνήμη κακῶν Soph.; also c. dat., δεινόν τι ἐσέδυνε σφίσι great fear came upon them, Hdt.

entry.note: inf. -ιέναι serving as fut. to εἰσέρχομαι imperf. εἰσῄειν
entry.sense: to go into, οὐκ Ἀχιλῆος ὀφθαλμοὺς εἴσειμι I will not come before Achilles' eyes, Il.:—more commonly with a prep., εἰς. μετ’ ἀνέρας Od.; παρὰ βασιλέα Hdt.; εἰς . . or πρός . . , Id., attic; εἰς. εἰς σπονδάς to enter into a treaty, Thuc.
of the chorus or of actors, to come upon the stage, to enter, Plat.
as attic law-term, to come into court, Dem.
to enter on an office, ὁ ἐσιών the new king, Hdt.
metaph. to come into one's mind, c. acc., Id., attic, Eur.; also c. dat., Id.:— impers., εἰσῄει αὐτοὺς ὅπως . . , it came into their minds that . . , Xen.
of things, τὰ εἰσιόντα what enters into one, food, Id.
to drive in, of a shepherd driving in his flock, Od.
intr. to row or sail in, Id.: to ride in, Xen.:— to enter in triumphal procession, Plut.
to draw, haul, drag in or into: aor1 -είλκῠσα, Hdt., Ar.
to go on board, Anth.
for hereafter, Soph.
to shut up in (a mummy-case), Hdt.
to go into, Plut.
to go into, get in; aor1 εἰσήρρησα, Ar.
to draw into, Od.

entry.note: fut. -ελεύσομαι aor2 -ήλῠθον, -ῆλθον but attic fut. is supplied by εἴσειμι and imperf. by εἰσῄειν
entry.sense: Dep.:— to go in or into, enter, c. acc., Il., etc.; in Prose, εἰς. εἰς . . , Xen., etc.; εἰς. εἰς τὰς σπονδάς to come into the treaty, Thuc.; εἰς. εἰς τοὺς ἐφήβους to enter the Ephebi, Xen.: of money, to come in, Id.
of the chorus or of actors, to come upon the stage, to enter, Plat., Xen.:— to enter the lists, Soph.
as attic law-term, of the accuser, to come into court, Plat., Dem.

metaph., [μένος] ἄνδρας ἐσέρχεται courage enters into the men, Il.; Κροῖσον γέλως εἰσῆλθεalso c. dat., δέος εἰς. τινι Plat.:—also to come into one's mind, Hdt.; so, impers., εἰσῆλθε αὐτόν, c. inf., it comes into one's head that . . , Id.
still yet, Theocr.
intr. to stretch into, reach, extend, ἐπὶ Αἰθιοπίης towards Ethiopia, Hdt.; θάλαμος ἐσέχων ἐς τὸν ἀνδρεῶνα a chamber opening into the men's apartment, Id.
Dep.:— to bring in, introduce a practice, Hdt.
to propose, Thuc., etc.; εἰσηγουμένου τινός on his motion, Id.
εἰσηγεῖσθαί τινι to represent a matter to a person, Id.
to relate, narrate, explain, τινί τι Plat.
a proposition, motion, Aeschin.
a proposing, moving, Thuc.
one must move, Thuc.
one who brings in, a mover, author, κακῶν Thuc.
to inject by a syringe, Hdt.
to have come in, Ar.:—in fut. to be about to come in, Aesch.
a coming in, entrance, Anth.
to run into, run up to him, Ar.
to leap into or in, Il.; c. acc., ἐσθορεῖν δόμον Aesch.
to build in, Hdt.
Mid. to sit down in, c. acc., Il.
to send into, ἐς τὴν [λίμνην]εἰς. τὸ ὕδωρ, of rivers, Hdt.; εἰς. τοὺς Πέρσας ἐς τὸ τεῖχος to let them in, Id.:—Mid. to let in Xen.
in Mid. also, to betake oneself into, enter, c. acc., Od.
an entrance, Od.
Dep. to go into, penetrate, Hdt.
belonging to entrance:— εἰσιτήρια (sc. ἱερά), τά, a sacrifice at entrance on an office, Dem.
one must go in, Luc.
to haul in as an angler the fish which he has hooked, Ar.
to call in, Ar., Xen.
to go down into, c. acc., Od.
to be put on board ship, Thuc.
to summon by public crier, Soph., Ar.
importation of supplies, Thuc.
to carry into the house, carry in, Hes., Aesch., etc.:—Mid. to bring in for oneself, import, Thuc.:—Pass., εἰσκομίζεσθαι εἰς τόπον to get into a place for shelter, Id.

in a theatre, to turn a thing inwards by machinery, of changing scenes in a theatre: —metaph., δαίμων πράγματα εἰσκεκύκληκεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν some spirit has brought scenes of trouble into the house, Ar.
to look into, Soph.
to touch to the quick, affect greatly, Il.
to put in the hand to feel, ἐσεμάξατο χεῖρας (doric form) Theocr.
Pass. to go into, Anth.
to swim into, Thuc.
to perceive, remark, Hom.

entry.etym: epic Verb, only in pres. and imperf.
entry.sense: to make like (cf. ἴσκω), Od.
to deem like, liken, compare, τινά or τί τινι Hom.
c. acc. et inf. to deem, suppose, Id.
absol., ὡς σὺ ἐΐσκεις as thou deemest, Od.
a way in, entrance, i. e., place of entrance, entry, Od., Hdt., etc.
entrance, a right or privilege of entrance, Id., Xen.
to bring in as a friend, Plut.:— Pass. to become intimate with another, Xen.
to settle in, Anth.
a place for dwelling in, a home, Soph.
to bring in as a settler:—Mid. and Pass. to establish oneself in, settle in, εἰς τόπον Hdt.; c. acc., Plut.
to build into, εἰς τεῖχος Thuc.
to be brought in, Dem.
to go into, enter, c. acc., Od.
until, with subj., Il., (in 3. 409, ποιήσεται is epic for ποιήσηται).
so long as, Il.
in time to come, hereafter, Hhymn., Soph.
visible, Hdt.
a mirror, Pind.

entry.note: epic part. εἰσορόων inf. mid. εἰσοράασθαι fut. -όψομαι aor2 -εῖδον epic inf. -ιδέειν
entry.sense: to look into, look upon, view, behold, c. acc., Hom., etc.:—so in Mid., Il.
to look upon with admiration, Lat. suspicere, θεοὺς ὣς εἰσορόωσιν Id.:—hence to pay regard to, respect, τι Soph., Eur.; so, ἐς. ἔς τι Hdt.; εἰσορ. πρός τι to look at, eye eagerly, Soph.
to look on with the mind's eye, perceive, Id.
of angry gods, to visit, punish, Id.
followed by μή, to take care lest . . , Id.
to bring forcibly into, Anth.:— Pass. to force one's way into, c. acc., Soph.
to bring into port:—Pass.and Mid. to run into port, Xen., Plut.
alike, equal:
of a feast, equal, i. e. equally shared, of which each partakes alike, Il.
of ships, even or well-balanced, Hom.
of a shield, equal all ways, i. e. perfectly round, Il.
of the mind, even, well-balanced, Lat. aequus, Od.
against the time when, Od.
a hollow, recess, Strab.
a spectacle, Eur.
to burst or rush in, Soph.; c. acc. loci, Eur.
to send in, bring in, let in, Eur., Thuc.: to prompt or suborn agents, Soph.
to pass over into, c. acc., Hes.

entry.note: fut. -πτήσομαι acr. 2 εἰσ-επτάμην also in act. form -έπτην
entry.sense: to fly into, c. acc., Il.; metaph. of reports, Hdt.
to leap into, c. acc., Hdt.; εἰς τόπον Xen.
to burst in upon, πρός τινα Dem.
to fall into, but generally with a notion of violence, to rush or burst in, ἐς πόλιν Hdt.; ἐς οἴκημα Thuc.:—poet. c. dat., ἐσπίπτει δόμοις Eur.
simply to fall into, ἐς χαράδρας Thuc.; εἰσπ. εἰς εἱρκτήν to be thrown into prison, Id.; in Poets, c. acc., Eur.
to fall into a certain condition, ξυμφοράν Id.
to fall upon, attack, τινά Hdt., Soph.
εἰσπίτνω, poet. form of εἰσπίπτω, v. πίτνω, Eur.

to sail into, enter εἰς τόπον Thuc.: poet. c. acc., Soph., Eur.:—absol., ἐπ’ ἀριστερὰ ἐσπλέοντι on the left as one sails in, Hdt.; οὐδὲν εἰσπλεῖ nothing comes into port, Thuc.: of corn, to be imported, Dem.
a sailing in of ships, Thuc., Xen.
the entrance of a harbour, Thuc.
to breathe upon, τινά Ar.
one who inspires love, a lover, Theocr.
to give in adoption, εἰσποιεῖν υἱόν τινι Plat.; εἰσπ. ἑαυτὸν Ἀμμῶνι to make himself son to Ammon, Plut.:—Mid. to adopt as one's son, Dem.
generally, εἰσπ. τινας εἰς λειτουργίαν to introduce new persons into the public service, Dem.

entry.etym: a neut. dat. (ἰῷ κίον ἤματι) also occurs in Il.
The orig. form was prob. ΕΝΣ, cf. Lat. unus. The fem. μία points to a second Root, cf. οἶος with μόνος.
entry.sense: one, Hom., etc.; εἷς οἶος, μία οἴη a single one, one alone, Id.; εἷς μόνος Hdt.
with a Sup., like Lat. unus omnium maxime, εἷς ἀνὴρ πλεῖστον πόνον παρασχών Aesch.; κάλλιστ’ ἀνὴρ εἷς Soph.; πάντων εἷς ἀνὴρ τῶν μεγίστων αἴτιος κακῶν Dem.
in oppos., made emphatic by the Art., ὁ εἷς, ἡ μία Hom., attic
with a negat., εἷς οὐδείς nullus unus, no single man, Hdt., Thuc.; οὐχ εἷς, i. e. more than one, Aesch.; and more emphatic, οὐδὲ εἷς, μηδὲ εἷς, v. οὐδείς, μηδείς.
εἷς ἕκαστος each one, each by himself, Lat. unusquisque, Hdt., Plat.
often with κατά, καθ’ ἓν ἕκαστον each singly, piece by piece, Hdt., etc.; so, καθ’ ἕνα, καθ’ ἕν one by one, Plat.
with other Preps., ἓν ἀνθ’ ἑνός above all, Id.: —ἓν πρὸς ἕν, in comparisons, Hdt., Plat.; εἷς πρὸς ἕνα Dem.: —παρ’ ἕνα alternately, Luc.
one, i. e. the same, εἷς καὶ ὅμοιος Plat.: c. dat. one with . . , Eur.
one, as opp. to another; so, ὁ μὲν . . , εἷς δὲ . . , εἷς δ’ αὖ . . , Od.; εἷς μέν . . , ἕτερος δέ . . , Xen.
indefinitely, εἷς τις, some one, Lat. unus aliquis, Soph., Plat.;—then alone, like our indef. Art. a, an, (as faber unus Hor.), Eur.
οὐδὲ εἷς οὐδὲ δύο not one or two only, Dem.
adopted, Dem.
to lead into, Eur.:—Pass. with fut. mid. to go into, enter, Xen.
a getting in or collection of dues, Thuc., Dem.
to get in or exact debts, taxes, dues, Dem.; τινά from a person, Id.:—Mid. to exact for oneself, have paid one, Eur.:—Pass., of the money, to be exacted, Dem.
to stream in or into, Eur., Plat.
to put into, place in, τινα or τι εἰς χεῖράς τινι Hdt., Thuc.; τινὰ ἐς ἅμαξαν Hdt.
ἐστ. ἐς ναῦν to put on board ship, Lat. navi imponere, Id.; τέκνα ἐσθέσθαι (aor2 inf.) to put their children on board, Id.
to shoot arrows at, Hdt.
to run in, Thuc.; c. acc. to run into, Theocr.
to carry into or to, Od., Hdt.
to bring in, contribute, Plat., Xen., etc.:—at Athens, to pay the property-tax (v. εἰσφορά II), Thuc.
to bring (suffering) in or upon, πένθος εἰσφ. δόμοις Eur., etc.
to introduce, bring forward, propose, Hdt.; γνώμην ἐσφ. ἐς τὸν δῆμον Thuc.; εἰσφ. νόμον, Lat. legem rogare, Dem.:—absol., like Lat. referre ad senatum, Thuc.
Mid. with perf. pass. εἰσενήνεγμαι, to carry with one, sweep along, Il.
to bring in for oneself, to import, Hdt., Thuc.
to bring in with one, introduce, Hdt., Eur.
Pass. to be brought in, introduced, Hdt.
to rush in, Thuc.
to go often to or into, Eur., Ar.
PREP. WITH ACC. ONLY. Radical sense, into, and then to:

OF PLACE, the commonest usage, εἰς ἅλα into or to the sea, Hom., etc.:—properly opposed to ἐκ, ἐς σφυρὸν ἐκ πτέρνης from head to foot, Il.; εἰς ἔτος ἐξ ἔτεος from year to year, Theocr.:—then, with all Verbs implying motion or direction, ἰδεῖν εἰς οὐρανόν Il.; εἰς ὦπα ἰδέσθαι to look in the face, Id.:—in Hom. and Hdt. also c. acc. pers., where the attic use ὡς, πρός, παρά.

with Verbs which express rest in a place, when a previous motion into or to it is implied, ἐς μέγαρον κατέθηκε, i. e. he brought it into the house, and put it there, Od.; παρεῖναι ἐς τόπον to go to a place and be there, Hdt.
with Verbs of saying or speaking, λόγους ποιεῖσθαι εἰς τὸ πλῆθος to come before the people and speak, Id., etc.
