elliptical usage εἰς Ἀΐδαο, attic εἰς Ἅιδου [δόμους], ἐς Ἀθηναίης [ἱερόν] to the temple of Athena, etc.; as in Lat. ad Apollinis, ad Castoris (sc. aedem); so with appellatives, ἀνδρὸς ἐς ἀφνειοῦ to a rich man's, Il.
OF TIME,

to denote a certain point or limit of time, to, up to, until, ἐς ἠῶ (attic εἰς τὴν ἕω) Od.; ἐς ἠέλιον καταδύντα till sun-set, Id.; ἐς ἐμέ up to my time, Hdt.:—so with Advs., εἰς ὅτε (cf. ἔς τε) against the time when, Od.; so, εἰς πότε; until when? how long? Soph.; ἐς ὃ until, Hdt.

to determine a period, εἰς ἐνιαυτόν for a year, i. e. a whole year, Hom.; ἐς θέρος ἢ ἐς ὀπώρην for the summer, Od.; εἰς ἑσπέραν ἥκειν to come at even, Ar.; εἰς τρίτην ἡμέραν or εἰς τρίτην alone, on the third day, in three days, Plat.; ἐς τέλος at last, Hdt.; οὐκ ἐς ἀναβολάς with no delay, Id.;—so with Advs., ἐς αὔριον Il.; ἐς αὖθις or ἐσαῦθις Thuc.; εἰς ἔπειτα Soph., etc.; cf. εἰσάπαξ, εἰσότε.
to express MEASURE OR LIMIT, ἐς δίσκουρα λέλειπτε was left behind as far as a quoit's throw, Il.; ἐς δραχμὴν διέδωκε paid them as much as a drachma, Thuc.
with Numerals, ναῦς ἐς τὰς τετρακοσίους to the number of 400, Id.; εἰς ἕνα, εἰς δύο, one, two deep, etc., Xen.
to express RELATION, to or towards, ἁμαρτάνειν εἴς τινα Aesch.; ἔχθρα ἔς τινα Hdt.
in regard to, like Lat. quod attinet ad, εὐτυχεῖν ἐς τέκνα Eur.; ἐς τὰ ἄλλα Thuc.; τό γ’ εἰς ἑαυτόν, τὸ εἰς ἐμέ Soph., Eur.
periphr. for Advs., ἐς κοινόν = κοινῶς, Aesch.; ἐς τὸ πᾶν = πάντως, Id.; εἰς τάχος = ταχέως, Ar.

of an END, ἔρχεσθαι, τελευτᾶν ἐς . . , to end in . . , Hdt., etc.; καταξαίνειν ἐς φοινικίδα to cut into red rags, Ar.:—also, of a Purpose, εἰς ἀγαθόν for good, for his good, Il.; εἰς κάλλος ζῆν to live for show, Xen.
a gathering in, Xen.
at Athens, a property-tax levied to supply a deficit in the revenue, to meet the exigencies of war, Thuc., etc.
to let in, admit, Lat. admittere, Ar., Dem.:—Mid. to bring in with one, Eur.
entry.etym: The Root φρέω, prob. akin to φέρω, is only found in compos. with δια-, εἰσ-, ἐπεισ-, ἐκ-

entry.sense: to put into one's hands, entrust, τί τινι Soph.
to pour in or into, Hdt., Eur.:— Pass. with epic syncop. aor2 ἐσεχύμην [ῠ], to stream in, ἐσέχυντο ἐς πόλιν Il.
in sight of, εἰσωποὶ δ’ ἐγένοντο νεῶν [the Greeks] stood facing the ships, Il.
to within, into, absol., μή πού τις ἐπαγγείλῃσι καὶ εἴσω lest some one may carry the news into the house, Od.; εἴσω ἀσπίδ’ ἔαξε he brake it even to the inside, Il.
c. acc., δῦναι δόμον Ἄϊδος εἴσω Il., etc.; Ἄϊδος εἴσω (sc. δόμον) Id.
= ἔνδον, inside, within, Od., etc.
c. gen., μένειν εἴσω δόμων Aesch.; εἴσω τῶν ὅπλων within the heavy-armed troops, i. e. encircled by them, Xen.
to thrust into:—Mid. to press in, Xen.
to denote Sequence of Time, then, next, Lat. deinde, πρῶτα μὲν . . , εἶτα . . , Soph., Plat., etc.: soon, presently, Soph.

to denote Consequence, and so, then, therefore, accordingly, esp. in questions or exclamations to express surprise or sarcasm, and then . . ? and so . . ? κᾆτ’ οὐ δέχονται λιτάς; Soph.; εἴτ’ οὐκ αἰσχύνεσθε; Dem.

εἰ, τε generally doubled, εἴτε . . , εἴτε Lat. sive . . , sive, either . . , or . . , whether . . , or . . the first εἴτε is sometimes omitted in Poets:—the first εἴτε is sometimes replaced by εἰ, as εἰ . . , εἴτε . . , Hdt., Trag.
also used, like εἰ, in indirect questions, Od., etc.
in customary wise, as usual, Soph., Plat.
the far-working: of Apollo, the far-shooting, far-darting, like ἑκηβόλος, Hom.
from afar, Il.; c. gen., ἕκαθεν πόλιος Id.
= ἑκάς, far off, far away, Od.
far, afar, far off, Lat. procul, Hom., Trag.; οὐχ ἑκάς Thuc.:—c. gen. far from, far away from, Il.; also, ἑκὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ τείχεος Id.
comp. ἑκαστέρω, farther, Od., etc.:—c. gen., Hdt.; also ἑκαστοτέρω Theocr.:—Sup. ἑκαστάτω, farthest, Il., Hdt.; ἑκαστάτω τινός farthest from . . , Id.
of Time, οὐχ ἑκὰς χρόνου in no long time, Id.
adv. from each side, Thuc., Xen.
adv. on each side, Plut.
adv. to each side, every way, Plut.
adv. to each side, Thuc.
adv. everywhere, Thuc., etc.
for each or every one, Od.

every, every one, each, each one, Lat. quisque, Hom., etc.; the sg. is often joined with a pl. Verb, ἔβαν οἴκονδε ἕκαστος they went home every one of them, Il.; ἕκαστος ἐπίστασθε Xen.:—the sg. is also put in apposition with a pl. Noun, Τρῶας ἕκαστον ὑπήλυθε τρόμος (for Τρώων ἕκαστον) fear seized them every one, Il.
in pl. all and each one, Hom.
more definitely, εἷς ἕκαστος, Lat. unusquisque, every single one, Hdt., etc.:— καθ’ ἕκαστον singly, by itself, Lat. singulatim, Plat., etc.
ὡς ἕκαστοι each by himself, Hdt., etc.
adv. each time, on each occasion, Hdt., etc.; ἑκάστοτ’ ἀεί Ar.
of Hecate: Ἑκάταιον or Ἑκάτειον, ου, τό, a statue or chapel of Hecate, Ar.
at each time, Xen.
on each side, on either hand, Lat. utrinque, Hom.: —c. gen. on each side of, Id.
each of two, either, each singly, Hdt., etc.:—in sg., with a pl. noun, like Lat. uterque, ταῦτα εἰπόντες ἀπῆλθον ἑκάτερος Xen.; except when each party is a pl., Plat.
on each side, on either hand, Like the poet. ἑκάτερθεν, Hdt., Thuc.; c. gen., ἑκ. τῆς πόλεως Id.
on each side, Hdt.
to each side, each way, both ways, Plat., Xen.
far-shooting, epith. of Apollo, Hom., Hes.; as Subst. the far-darter, Il.
Hecate, the far-darter, Hes.; later, identified with Artemis.
Ἑκάτης δεῖπνον Hecate's dinner, a meal set out by rich persons at the foot of her statue on the 30th of each month for beggars and paupers, Ar.
hundred-headed, Pind.: so ἑκατογ-κέφαλος, ον, Eur., Ar.
hundred-handed, of Briareus, Il.:— ἑκατόγ-χειρ, Plut.
with 100 benches for rowers, Il.
the month Hecatombaeon, the first of the attic year, answering to the last half of July and the first half of August, attic
properly an offering of a hundred oxen, — but generally, a great public sacrifice:—thus, in Il. we find a hecatomb of twelve oxen, in Od. of eighty-one.
worth a hundred beeves, Il.
measuring a hundred feet, Il.
with a hundred cities, Il.
hundred-footed, Soph.
hundred-gated, Il.
a hundred, Lat. centum, Il., etc.
a term of 100 years, Plat.
rated at 100 talents, Ar.
a hundred times as much or many, Xen.
leader of a hundred, Hdt.
the number a hundred, Hdt.
of 100 fathoms, Ar.
far-shooting, epith. of Apollo, Il.
hundred-mouthed, Eur.
the hundredth, Lat. centesimus, Hdt., etc.; ἐπ’ ἑκατοστά a hundred-fold, Id.
ἑκατοστή, ἡ, the hundredth part, a tax or duty at Athens, Ar., Xen.
to speak out, declare, Aesch.
to step out of or off from a place, c. gen., Il., etc.; ἐκβ. ἐκ . . , Thuc.:—absol. to disembark, dismount, Il., etc.
to go out of a place, c. gen. or ἐκβ. ἐκ . . , Eur., etc.
c. acc. to outstep, overstep, Id., Plat.
in Poets, the instrument of motion is added in acc., ἐκβὰς πόδα Eur.; cf. βαίνω A. II. 3.
metaph.,
to come out so and so, come to pass, turn out, Hdt., Thuc.:— to be fulfilled, of prophecies, Dem.; κάκιστος ἐκβ. to prove a villain, Eur.:— τὰ ἐκβησόμενα things likely to happen, Hdt., etc.
to go out of due bounds, to go far, ἐς τοῦτ’ ἐκβέβηκ’ Eur.
Causal, in aor1 -έβησα, to make to go out, to put out of a ship, Hom., Eur.
to excite to Bacchic frenzy, to make frantic, Eur., Plat.:—Pass. to be frenzied, Id.; so in Mid., Eur.

to throw or cast out of a place, c. gen., Il., etc.; or absol. to throw out, throw overboard, Od.: also, like Lat. ejicere, to throw ashore, Id., Hdt.; but, ἐκβ. ἐς τὸ πέλαγος carry out to sea, Id.:—Mid. to put ashore, Id.
to cast out of a place, banish, Id., etc.
to expose on a desert island, Soph.; to expose a dead body, Id.
to divorce a wife, Dem.
to cast out of his seat, depose a king, Aesch., etc.
to strike out of, Lat. excutere, χειρῶν ἔκβαλλε κύπελλα Od.;—absol., δοῦρα ἐκβ. to fell trees (properly, to cut them out of the forest), Id.
to strike open, break in, πύλας Eur.
to let fall, χειρὸς ἔκβαλεν ἔγχος Il.:—metaph., ἔπος ἐκβ. to let fall a word, Hom., etc.; so, δάκρυα ἔκβ. Od.; ἐκβ. ὀδόντας to cast one's teeth, Eur.
to throw away, reject, Soph., etc.:— to reject a candidate for office, Dem.; to drive an actor from the stage, Lat. explodere, Id.
to lose, properly by one's own fault, Soph., etc.
to produce, of women, Plut.; so, of wheat, ἐκβ. στάχυν Eur.
intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν) to go out, depart, Id.; of a river, to empty, discharge itself, Plat.
a way out, egress, Od., Xen.
a going out of, escape from, c. gen., Eur.
ἐκβῶντας, Foed. in Thuc.
to establish, Plut.; in Mid., Id.
to force out:—Pass., τόξον χειρῶν ἐκβεβιασμένον the bow forced from mine hands, Soph.
to make to step out, Ar.; ἐκβ. ποταμόν to turn a river out of its channel, Hdt.:—metaph., ἐκβ. τινὰ δικαίων λόγων to stop one from discussing the question of justice, Thuc.
to land one from a ship, disembark, Id.
to devour, Soph.
to sprout out, Plat.
one must cast out, Plat.
thrown out or away, Eur.
to gush out, Plut.
to call out, cry aloud, Xen., Plat.
a going out to aid, a sally of the besieged, Thuc.
to march out to aid, Hdt.: to make a sally, Thuc.
to peel, as one does an onion of its outer coats, Ar.
a throwing out, ψήφων ἐκβ. turning the votes out of the urn, Aesch.
a throwing the cargo overboard, Id.
ejectment, banishment, Id., Plat.
a letting fall, δακρύων Eur.
a bringing forth:— ἐκβ. σίτου the time when the corn comes into ear, Thuc.
(from intr. signf. of ἐκβάλλω) a going out, outlet, Lat. exitus, ἐκβ. ποταμοῦ the discharge of a river from between mountains, Hdt.: a mountain-pass, Id.: the mouth of a river, Thuc.
ἐκβ. λόγου a digression, Id.
(from Pass.), that which is cast out, ἐκβ. δικέλλης earth cast or scraped up by a hoe or mattock, Soph.; οὐρεία ἐκβολή children exposed on the mountains, Eur.
a cargo cast overboard, ἐκβολαὶ νεώς wrecked seamen, Id.
cast out of a place, c. gen., Eur.:—as Subst., ἔκβολον, ου, τό, an outcast, Id.:—but, ναὸς ἔκβολα rags cast out from the ship, Id.
to throw out foam, of the sea:—Pass., of ships, to be cast ashore, Hdt.
to strike out by lightning, ἐξεβροντήθη σθένος he had strength struck out of him by lightning, Aesch.
Dep. to bellow forth or aloud, Eur.
anything eaten out, πρίονος ἔκβ. saw- dust, Soph.
to give in marriage, and Pass. to be given in marriage, NTest.:—so, ἐκγαμίσκομαι, Id.
Pass. to exult greatly in, c. acc., Eur.
to laugh out, laugh loud, Od., Xen.: metaph. of a liquid, to rush gurgling out, Eur.

entry.note: later and ionic ἐκ-γίν- fut. -γενήσομαι epic perf. ἐκγέγᾰα 3rd dual ἐκγεγάτην part. -ἐκγεγαώς
entry.sense: Dep.:— to be born of a father, c. gen., Ἑλένη Διὸς ἐκγεγαυῖα Il.
c. dat. to be born to, Πορθεῖ τρεῖς παῖδες ἐξεγένοντο Id.
in aor2 to have gone by, χρόνου ἐκγεγονότος time having gone by, Hdt.: c. gen., ἐκγενέσθαι τοῦ ζῆν to have departed this life, Xen.

impers., ἐκγίγνεται, like ἔξεστι, it is allowed, it is granted, c. dat. pers. et inf., mostly with a negat., οὐκ ἐξεγένετό τινι ποιεῖν it was not granted him to do, Hdt.: absol., οὐκ ἐξεγένετο it was not in his power, Id.
to scoop out: irr. perf. pass. ἐξέγλυμμαι Plat.
to hatch, Plut.
born of, sprung from, τινός Hom.
as Subst. a child, whether son or daughter, Id.; and in pl. ἔκγονοι, descendants, Hdt., etc.; neut., ἔκγονά τινος one's offspring, Aesch.
to write out:—Mid. to write out or copy for oneself, Ar., Dem.
Pass. to be stript utterly, Babr.
to burst into tears, weep aloud, Soph., Eur.
a falling short, being in arrear, Thuc.
to shew forth, exhibit, display, Soph., Eur.
a receiving from another: succession, Hdt.
to strip off the skin from a person, c. acc., Hdt.: also c. acc. rei, to strip off, βύρσαν ἐκδ. Eur.
fastened to, Anth.
Dep.:
mostly of persons,
to take or receive from another, τί τινι Il., Aesch.
to take up, of a successor, τὴν ἀρχὴν παρά τινος Hdt., etc.; often also with the acc. omitted, ἐξεδέξατο Σαδυάττης (sc. τὴν βασιληΐην) he succeeded, Id.
to take up the argument, ὥσπερ σφαῖραν ἐκδ. τὸν λόγον Plat.
to wait for, expect, Soph.
of events, to await, Lat. excipere, Hdt.
of contiguous countries, to come next, Id.
to bind so as to hang from, to fasten to or on, c. gen., Il.: absol., σανίδας ἐκδῆσαι to bind planks (to his back), Od.:—Mid. to bind a thing to oneself, hang it round one, Hdt.
conspicuous, Il.:— quite plain, Dem.
to be abroad, to be on one's travels, Hdt., Soph.
a being abroad, exile, Plat.
from home, gone on a journey, Xen.; ἐκδ. στρατεῖαι service in foreign lands, Thuc.; ἔκδ. φυγή Eur.
c. gen. departed from, Id.
to pass quite over, c. acc., Il.
Pass. to depart from one's accustomed mode of life, change one's habits, Thuc.
change of habits, Plut.
prentice-work, a sampler, Eur.

to teach thoroughly, Lat. edocere, Aesch., etc.; ἐκδ. τινά τι Soph.:—Mid. to have another taught, of the parents, Hdt., Eur.:—Pass., αἰσχρὰ ἐκδιδάσκεται is taught disgraceful things, Soph.; ἐκδιδαχθεὶς τῶν κατ’ οἶκον having learnt of things at home, Id.
c. acc. pers. et inf. to teach one to be so and so, Id.; inf. omitted, γενναῖόν τινα ἐκδ. Ar.

entry.note: ionic -διδρήσκω fut. -δράσομαι aor2 ἐξ-έδραν part. ἐκδράς
entry.sense: to run out from, run away, escape, ἐκ τόπου Hdt.; absol., Ar.
to give up, surrender, esp. something seized unlawfully, Lat. reddere, Il., Hdt.:— ἐκδ. δοῦλον to give up a slave to be examined by torture, Dem.
ἐκδ. θυγατέρα to give one's daughter in marriage, Lat. nuptum dare, Hdt., attic; so in Mid., ἐκδίδοσθαι θυγατέρα Hdt., Eur.
to give out for money, let out for hire, Hdt.:—c. inf., like Lat. locare aliquid faciendum, Dem.
to lend out money on security, such as the cargo of a ship, ap. Dem.
intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν or -ούς) of rivers, to empty themselves, Hdt.
to decide finally, settle, of a judge, Ar.
to avenge, Eur.
an avenger, Eur.
to avenge, punish a crime, NTest.: also to exact vengeance for a crime, Id.
to avenge a person, Id.; ἐκδ. τινὰ ἀπό τινος to avenge one on another, Id.
an avenging, ἐκδίκησιν ποιεῖν τινι to avenge him, NTest.
without law, lawless, unjust, Lat. exlex, Aesch., etc.:—adv. -κως, Id.
maintaining the right, avenging, Anth.
to throw from a chariot, Luc.
to chase away, banish, Thuc.
to shake utterly, confound, Anth.
a giving out or up, surrendering, Hdt., Plat.
a giving in marriage, portioning out, Id.
a lending money on ships or exported goods, bottomry, Dem.
one must give up, Plut.
one must give in marriage, Ar.
given up, delivered over, surrendered, Hdt., attic
a receiving from another, succession, Aesch., Eur.
= προσδοκία, NTest.
a reservoir, Anth.
Pass. to become a very serpent, Aesch.

entry.etym: from ἐκδρᾰμεῖν, aor2 inf. of ἐκτρέχω
entry.sense: a running out, sally, charge, Xen.
a party of skirmishers, Thuc.

entry.etym: from ἐκδρᾰμεῖν, aor2 inf. of ἐκτρέχω
entry.sense: one that sallies out from the ranks, a skirmisher, Thuc., Xen.
that which is stript off, a skin, garment, Anth.
a getting out, way out, Hdt.

entry.note: and -δύνω imperf. ἐξέδῡνον aor2 ἐξέδυν perf. ἐκδέδῡκα
entry.sense: Causal in pres. ἐκδύω, imperf. ἐξέδυον, fut. ἐκδύσω, aor1 ἐξέδῡσα: — to take off, strip off, Lat. exuere, c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, ἐκ μέν με χλαῖναν ἔδυσαν they stripped me of my cloke, Od.: c. acc. pers. only, to strip him, Xen., etc.
Mid. ἐκδύομαι, aor1 ἐξεδυσάμην: — to strip oneself of a thing, put off, Il., etc.: absol. to put off one's clothes, strip, Ar., Xen.
in pres. ἐκδύνωin same sense as Mid. ἐκδύομαι
to put off, Od., Hdt.
in aor2 ἐξέδυν, perf. ἐκδέδῡκα, to go or get out of, c. gen., ἐκδὺς μεγάροιο Od.; ἐκδ. τῆς θαλάσσης to emerge from the sea, Plat.
c. acc. to escape, ἐκδῦμεν ὄλεθρον Il.
Pass. to become a thorough Dorian, Hdt.
from that place, thence, Lat. illinc, opp. to ἐκεῖσε, Soph., etc.
= ἐκεῖ, Aesch., Thuc.:—c. gen., τοὐκεῖθεν ἄλσους on yon side of the grove, Soph.
thence, from that fact, Isocr., Dem.
of Time, thereafter, next, Il.

Demonstr. Pron.: the person there, that person or thing, Hom., etc.: when οὗτος and ἐκεῖνος refer to two things before mentioned, ἐκεῖνος, ille, belongs to the more remote, i. e. the former, οὗτος, hic, to the nearer, i. e. the latter.
like ille, to denote well-known persons, ἐκεῖνος Θουκυδίδης Ar.
with demonstr. force, Ἶρος ἐκεῖνος ἧσται Irus sits there, Od.

in attic the Subst. with ἐκεῖνος properly has the Article, and ἐκεῖνος may precede or follow the Subst., ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ: when the Art. is omitted in Prose, ἐκεῖνος follows the Subst., νῆες ἐκεῖναι Thuc.
adv. ἐκείνως, in that way, in that case, Id.
dat. fem. ἐκείνῃ as adv.,
of Place (sub. ὁδῷ), there, at that place, on that road, Hdt., Thuc.
of Manner, in that manner, Plat., etc.
with Preps., ἐξ ἐκείνου from that time, Xen.; so, ἀπ’ ἐκείνου Luc.: κατ’ ἐκεῖνα in that place, there, Xen.: μετ’ ἐκεῖνα afterwards, Thuc.
there, in that place, Lat. illic, attic
euphem. for ἐν Ἅιδου, in another world, Aesch., etc.; οἱ ἐκεῖ, i. e. the dead, Id.
with Verbs of motion, for ἐκεῖσε, as we say there for thither, ἐκεῖ πλέειν Hdt., etc.
thither, to that place, Lat. illuc, opp. to ἐκεῖθεν, Hom., etc.
to the other world, Eur., Plat.; cf. ἐκεῖ I. 2.
c. gen., ἐκ. τοῦ λόγου from that part of the story, Hdt.
a holding of hands, a cessation of hostilities, armistice, truce, Thuc., Xen.
generally, rest from work, vacation, holiday, Luc.
to boil out or over, break out, of curses, Aesch.
c. gen., εὐλέων ἐξέζεσε boiled over with worms, i. e. bred worms, Hdt.
to seek out, enquire, NTest.
to demand an account of a thing, c. acc., Id.
to rekindle, Ar., Plut.
skill in archery, Il.
far-darting, far-shooting, epith. of Apollo, Il.
a time of sixty years, Plut.

at rest, at one's ease, Lat. securus, of persons enjoying themselves, Hom.; ἕκηλοι συλήσετε ye will plunder them at your ease, i. e. without let or hindrance, Il.; ἕκ. εὕδειν Soph.; neut. as adv., Id.
by means of, by virtue of, by the aid of, Διὸς ἕκητι Od., etc.
= ἕνεκα, on account of, for the sake of, Trag.: also, as to, Lat. quod attinet ad, Aesch., Eur.
Pass. to be amazed, NTest.
amazed, astounded, NTest.
to root out, extirpate, Aesch.
to have full confidence in a person, c. dat., Plut.
Dep. to see out, see to the end, Soph.
to make a public show of, to expose to public shame, NTest.
to make a god of, deify, Luc.: to worship as a god, Plut.
of things, to make matter of religion, Id.
to gain over entirely, Aeschin., Plut.
to reap or mow completely, Dem.
a putting out, exposing, of a child, Hdt., Eur.
out of law, lawless: horrible, Plut.
exposed, Eur.
to run out, make a sally, Xen.
Dep. to hunt out, catch, Xen., Plut., Hdt.
Pass. to become quite savage, Lat. efferari, Eur.
to squeeze much: to distress greatly, Xen.
to die away, γέλῳ (for γέλωτι) ἔκθανον were like to die with laughing, Od.
to be in a death-like swoon, be at the point of death, Soph.
Dep. to feast on, c. acc., Aesch.
to lament aloud, Luc.
to leap out of, c. gen., ἔκθορε δίφρου Il.; κραδίη δέ μοι ἔξω στηθέων ἐκθρώσκει of the violent beating of the heart, Id.:— rarely c. acc., Anth.
to burn as incense, Eur.
out of one's mind, senseless, Lat. demens, Aesch.
very spirited, ardent, Plut.
atonement, Lat. expiatio, Plut.
to offer up, sacrifice, slay, Soph., Eur.
Mid. to atone for, expiate by offerings, Lat. lustrare, expiare, c. acc. rei, Hdt.; but c. acc. pers. to propitiate, appease, Eur.
to burst into loud laughter, Xen.
to cleanse out:
with acc. of the thing cleansed, to clear out ditches, etc., Il.; χθόνα ἐκκαθαίρει κνωδάλων he clears this land of monsters, Aesch.:—Pass. to be purified, Xen.
with acc. of the dirt removed, to clear away, Plat.
to sleep out of one's quarters, Xen.
sixteen palms long, Il.
consisting of sixteen threads, Xen.
indecl. sixteen, Lat. sedecim, Hdt., etc.
sixteen cubits long or high, Decret. ap. Dem.
sixteenth, Hdt., etc.
16 years old, Anth.
out of date, antiquated, Anth.

entry.note: attic ἐκ-κάω fut. -καύσω aor1 part. ἐκκέας
entry.sense: to burn out, Hdt., Eur.
to light up, kindle, Hdt., Ar.
to be faint-hearted, NTest.
Dep. to pull out with a fishing-rod, Ar.
to call out or forth, summon forth, Hom., Hdt., Eur.
Mid. to call out to oneself, Od., Hdt.
to call forth, elicit, Aesch., etc.
c. inf. to call on one to do, Soph.
to uncover, Hdt.: to disclose, Aesch., Soph.:—Mid. to uncover one's head, unveil oneself, Od., Plat.
to grow quite weary of a thing, c. acc., Thuc.; c. part., ἐξέκαμον πολεμοῦντες Plut.; ἐκκ. πληγαῖς to yield to blows, Id.
Mid. to yield as produce, Aesch.
Mid. to enjoy the fruit of, ἄλλης γυναικὸς παῖδας ἐκκ. to have children by another wife, Eur.
to derive advantage from being, c. part., Thuc.
in use, to look down from a place, c. gen., Il.
Pass. to leap down from a place, c. gen., Il.
to pull out the stalk: metaph. to pull up root and branch, Ar.
to boast loudly, c. inf., Eur.
to be cast out or exposed, Hdt.
of public notices, to be set up in public, posted up, Dem.
c. gen. to fall from out, be left bare of, Soph.

to empty out, leave desolate, Aesch.; ἐκκενοῦν θυμὸν ἐς σχεδίαν γέροντος to pour out one's spirit into Charon's boat, i. e. give up the ghost, Theocr.; ἐκκ. ἰούς to shoot all one's arrows, Anth.:—Pass. to be left desolate, Aesch.
to cut off root and branch, Anth.

entry.etym: adverb, part. perf. pass. of ἐκχέω
entry.sense: profusely, Plat.
to enfeeble, exhaust, Aesch.
to proclaim by voice of herald, Soph.
to banish by proclamation, Hdt.:—Pass., ἐξεκηρύχθην φυγάς Soph.
to move out of his lair, to put up, ἔλαφον Soph.: metaph. to stir up, rouse, excite, Plut.
to go out, Od.
to cry aloud, Eur.
to shut out from a place, c. gen., Eur.
metaph. to exclude from a thing, Hdt., Aeschin.:— Pass., ἐκκληϊόμενοι τῇ ὥρῃ being hindered by [want of] time, Hdt.
to steal and bring off secretly, to purloin, Il., Hdt., etc.; ἐκκλ. πόδα to steal away, Eur.: —ἐκκλ. μὴ θανεῖν Id.
ἐκκλ. τινὰ λόγοις to deceive him, Soph.; μὴ ἐκκλέψῃς λόγον disguise not the matter, speak not falsely, Id.

entry.etym: for the odd appearence of the preverb ἐκ in its full force, cf. ἐγκωμιάζω
entry.sense: to hold an assembly, debate therein, Ar., Thuc., etc.
to be a member of the Assembly, ἐκκλ. ἀπὸ τιμήματος οὐθενός Arist.

an assembly of the citizens regularly summoned, the legislative assembly, Thuc., etc.:—at Athens, the ordinary Assemblies were called κύριαι, the extraordinary being σύγκλητοι, ap. Dem.; ἐκκλ. συναγείρειν, συνάγειν, συλλέγειν, ἀθροίζειν to call an assembly, Hdt., etc.; ἐκκλ. ποιεῖν "to make a house, " Ar.; ἐκκλ. γίγνεται, καθίσταται an assembly is held, Thuc.; ἐκκλ. διαλύειν, ἀναστῆσαι to dissolve it, Id., etc.; ἀναβάλλειν to adjourn it, Id.
in NTest. the Church, either the body, or the place.
a member of the ἐκκλησία, Plat.
of or for the ἐκκλησία, Dem.:— τὸ ἐκκλησιαστικὸν [ἄργυρον] the public pay received by each citizen who sat in the ἐκκλησία, Luc.
to summon into court, Aeschin.
selected to judge or arbitrate on a point, ἐκκλ. πόλις an umpire city, Aeschin.: —οἱ ἔκκλητοι, in Sparta, a committee of citizens chosen for special business, Xen.
to bend out of the regular line: intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν) to turn away, give ground, retire, Thuc., Xen.:—also c. acc. to avoid, shun, τι Plat.
to turn aside towards, κατά τι Xen.
to wash out stains, Plat.
to wear out: metaph. of troublesome loquacity, like Lat. enecare, Theocr., in doric fut. 3rd pl. ἐκκναισεῦντι.
to scrape off from, c. gen., Hdt.
Dep. to cheat by juggling tricks, cajole, Ar.
to take out the kernel: metaph., ἐκκ. σφυρόν to put out one's ankle, Ar.; ἐκκ. τὰς πόλεις to sack, gut the cities, Id.
to scrape out, obliterate, Thuc.
to swim out of, c. gen., Eur.
a carrying out, Hdt.: of a corpse, burial, Anth.
to carry out, esp. to a place of safety, Hdt.; ἐκκ. τινὰ ἐκ πρήγματος to keep him out of trouble, Id.: so in Mid., Id., Thuc.
to carry out a corpse, bury, Lat. efferre, Plut.
to endure to the end, τι Eur.
to boast loudly, Soph.
Mid. to set forth in fair terms, Eur.
a cutting out of an arrow-point from the body, Plut.

entry.note: fut. ψω perf. -κέκοφα aor2 pass. ἐξ-εκόπην
entry.sense: to cut out, knock out:—Pass., ἐξεκόπη τὠφθαλμώ he had both his eyes knocked out, Ar.
to cut [trees] out of a wood, to fell (cf. ἐκβάλλω), Hdt., Xen.; ἐκκ. τὸν παράδεισον cut down all the trees in the park, Xen.
metaph. to cut off, make an end of, Hdt., etc.
as military term, to beat off, repulse, Xen.
to cut off, NTest.
to sweep out, to sweep clean, Ar.
to clear of bugs, Anth.
to tell summarily, sum up, Hes.
to raise up, exalt, Plut.
to relieve, Id.
to cry out, Plut.
to hang from or upon a thing; τι ἔκ τινος Ar.
Pass. to hang on by, cling to, c. gen., Thuc.:—metaph. to be devoted to, Eur.
Pass. to hang from, depend upon, c. gen., Plut.
hanging from or upon, τινος Anth.
c. gen., Eur.; ῥόπτρων χέρας ἐκκρημνάμεσθα we hang on to the door-handle by the hands, Id.
to choose or pick out, to single out, Thuc.:—Pass., aor1 part. ἐκκριθείς Soph.
to single out for disgrace, expel, like Lat. tribu movere, Xen.
to secrete, separate, ὅταν ὁ νοῦς ἐκκριθῇ Id.
picked out, select, Aesch., Soph.:—neut. ἔκκριτον, as adv. above all, eminently, Eur.
a beating out, driving away, Xen.
beaten out, embossed, Aesch.
to knock out, τι ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν Xen.
to drive back, repulse, Thuc., Xen.: metaph. to frustrate one of a thing, c. gen., Plut.
to hiss an actor off the stage, explodere, Dem.
to put off, adjourn by evasions, Id.; ἐκκρ. τοὺς λόγους to baffle by putting off, elude, Plat.
Pass. to lose at play, c. acc., Plut.
to tumble headlong out of a chariot, c. gen., Eur.; ἐκκ. ὑπέρ τινος to throw a somersault over a thing, Xen.
to put forth as leaves, Anth.
to wheel out, esp. by means of the ἐκκύκλημα (q. v.): ἀλλ’ ἐκκυκλήθητι come, wheel yourself out! i. e. shew yourself, Ar.
a theatrical machine, which served the purpose of drawing back the scenes, and disclosing the interior to the spectators.
to roll out, Ar.:— to overthrow, Anth.:—Pass., ἐκ δίφροιο ἐξεκυλίσθη rolled headlong from the chariot, Il.
to extricate:—Pass. to be extricated from, τῆσδ’ ἐκκυλισθήσει τύχης Aesch.; ἐκκυλισθῆναι εἰς ἔρωτας to plunge headlong into intrigues, Xen.
to wave from the straight line, of a line of soldiers, Xen.
to keep questing about, of hounds, Xen.
to pursue in the chase, hunt down, τινα Eur.
of a hound, questing about, not keeping on one scent, Xen.
to peep out of a place, c. gen., Babr.
to rush wildly out, Eur.
to make quite deaf, Ar.:—Pass., metaph., ἐκκεκώφηται ξίφη swords are blunted, Eur.
to make quite deaf, Plat.:—Pass. to become so, Luc.
to obtain by lot or destiny, Soph.
to kick out, fling out behind, Ar.
to speak out, blab, divulge, Dem.
to receive from others, receive in full, Soph., etc.
ἔργα ἐκλ. = ἐργολαβέω, to contract to do work, opp. to ἐκδίδωμι (to let it out), Hdt.
to take in a certain sense, to understand, Lat. accipere, Plat.; ἐκλ. τι ἐπὶ τὸ χεῖρον Arist.
to shine or beam forth, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
to escape notice utterly: — Mid., with perf. pass. ἐκλέλησμαι, to forget utterly, c. gen. rei, Soph.

entry.note: with aor1 ἐξέλησα doric ἐξέλᾱσα epic redupl. aor2 ἐκλέλᾰθον
entry.sense: Causal, to make one quite forgetful of a thing, c. gen. rei, Od.: c. acc. rei, ἐκλέλαθον κιθαριστύν made him quite forget his harping, Il.
to cast out from a place, c. gen., Aesch.
to drink off, Ar.

entry.note: fut. ξω perf. pass. ἐξείλεγμαι perf. pass. ἐκλέλεγμαι
entry.sense: to pick or single out, Thuc., Xen.:—Mid. to pick out for oneself, choose out, Hdt., Plat., etc.
Mid. also, ἐκλέγεσθαι τὰς πολιὰς τρίχας to pull out one's gray hairs, Ar.
to levy taxes or tribute, Thuc.; c. acc. pers., ἐκλ. τέλη τινάς to levy tolls on them, Aeschin.; so c. gen. pers., Xen.
to leave out, omit, pass over, Hdt., Aesch., etc.:—Pass., ὄνειδος οὐκ ἐκλείπεται fails not to appear, Aesch.
to forsake, desert, abandon, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
in elliptic phrases, ἐκλείπειν τὴν πόλιν εἰς τὰ ἄκρα to abandon the city and go to the heights, Hdt.; εἴ τις ἐξέλιπε τὸν ἀριθμόν (of the Persian immortals) if any one left the number incomplete, Id.
intr., of the sun or moon, to suffer an eclipse, Thuc.;—in full, ὁ ἥλιος ἐκλιπὼν τὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἕδρην Hdt.; cf. ἔκλειψις.
to die, οἱ ἐκλελοιπότες the deceased, Plat.; in full, ἐκλ. βίον Soph.
generally, to leave off, cease, stop, Hdt., etc.
to fail, be wanting, Eur.
abandonment, τῶν νεῶν Hdt.
(from intr.) of sun or moon, an eclipse, Thuc.
picked out, select, Thuc., Plat., etc.
οἱ ἐκλεκτοί, the elect, NTest.
loosely, carelessly, Plut.
to bring the young brood out of the shell, to hatch, Hdt., Ar.
to make quite white, Eur.
to cease utterly, Soph.
a forgetting and forgiving, Od.
to abandon, Eur.
intr. to cease, Id.
to fatten:—Pass. to grow fat, Plut.

entry.etym: from ἐκλῐπεῖν aor2 inf. of ἐκλείπω
entry.sense: failing, deficient, ἡλίου ἐκλιπές τι ἐγένετο
omitted, overlooked, Id.
a picking out, choice, election, Plat.
that which is chosen out, an extract, choice collection of passages, Hor.
Dep. to compute, calculate, Plut.
to consider, reflect on, τι Hdt., Eur.; περί τινος Thuc.
to reckon on, οὐδεὶς αὑτοῦ θάνατον ἐκλογίζεται Eur.
a computation, calculation, Plut.
to bring forth, Eur., in Mid.:—Pass. to be born, Id.
release or deliverance from a thing, c. gen., Aesch., etc.
feebleness, faintness, Dem.
of or for release:— ἐκλυτήριον, τό, a release, Soph.: an expiatory offering, Eur.
easy to let go, light, buoyant, of missiles, Eur.
adv. ἐκλύτως, remissly, Plut.

entry.note: fut. ύσω perf. pass. ἐκλέλῠμαι aor1 ἐξελύθην
entry.sense: to loose, release, set free, from a thing, c. gen., Aesch., Soph.:—Pass. to be set free, Plat.:— Mid. to get one set free, to release from, c. gen., Od., etc.
to unloose, unstring a bow, Hdt.; ἐκλύσων στόμα likely to let loose the tongue, Soph.
to put an end to, Id., Eur.
to relax, enfeeble:— Pass. to be faint, fail, give way, Dem.
to pay in full, Plut.
Pass. to sustain grievous injuries, Soph.
to lay bare, Soph.
that on or in which an impression is made: also the impression made, an impress, mould, Plat.:—metaph., ἐκμαγεῖον πέτρης counterfeit of rock, of a fisherman who is always on them, Anth.
to drive mad with passion, Eur., Theocr.; ἐκμῆναί τινα δωμάτων to drive one raving from the house, Eur.:—Pass., with perf. 2 act. ἐκμέμηνα, to go mad with passion, be furious, Hdt.
c. acc. rei, ἐκμῆναι πόθον to kindle mad desire, Soph.
an impress, Eur.
to learn thoroughly, and, in past tenses, to have learnt thoroughly, to know full well, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
to examine closely, search out, Hdt., Eur., etc.
to make to wither away, Anth.:— Pass. to wither away, Theocr.
Pass. to go raving mad, Eur.
to bear witness to a thing, c. acc., Aesch.
the deposition of a witness, Dem.
ἐκ-μάσσατο, 3rd sg. aor1, he devised or invented, τι Hhymn.; v. μαίομαι.
to wipe off, wipe away Soph., Eur.:—Mid. to wipe away one's tears, Anth.
of an artist, to mould or model in wax or plaster, Lat.exprimere, Plat.:—Mid., τοκέων ἐκμάσσεται ἴχνη he impresses anew the footsteps of his fathers, i. e. walks in their steps, Theocr.
to make quite drunk, to saturate with a thing, c. gen., Anth.
in perf. 2 ἐξέμμορε τιμῆς obtained a chief share of honour, Od.
to train carefully, τινα Plat.
to learn perfectly, con over, practise, τι Id.
out of tune, dissonant, Plut.
to measure out, measure, χρόνον Eur.:—Mid. to measure for oneself, take measure of, τι Xen.; ἄστροις ἐκμετρούμενος χθόνα calculating its position by the stars, Soph.
of six months, half-yearly, Soph.
to inform of, betray, Plut.
Dep. to wind out like a ball of thread: of an army, to make it defile out of a place, c. gen., Polyb., Plut.
intr., of the army, to defile, Xen.
Dep. to imitate faithfully, represent exactly, Eur., Xen.
to hate much, Plut.
to let out for hire, τί τινι Xen.

entry.note: inf. of aor2 ἐξέμολον epic 3rd sg. ἔκμολε
entry.sense: to go out, go forth, Il.
to teach fully, τινά τι Eur.
to work out with toil, Lat. elaborare, Eur.
to struggle through, πόνους Id.
to win by labour, achieve, Id.
to struggle out of danger, c. acc., Id.
to squeeze out, Il.
to turn up one's nose at, mock at, NTest.
to become quite torpid, Plut.
to go forth to feed: metaph., ἐκνέμεσθαι πόδα to turn away one's foot, Soph.
to hatch, Arist.
to cut the sinews:—Pass., ἐκνενευρισμένοι unnerved, Dem.
to turn the head aside, Xen.
c. acc. to shun, avoid, Orph.
to fall headlong, Eur.
to give one a sign to move away, c. inf., Id.
to swim out, swim to land, escape by swimming, Eur., Thuc.: generally, to escape, Eur.
to sleep off a drunken fit, become sober again, Anth.
Dep., to swim out or away, Luc.
to wash out, purge away, Eur.:—Mid. to wash off from oneself, Lat. diluere, οὐδέποτε ἐκνίψῃ τὰ πεπραγμένα Dem.
to wash clean, purify, Anth.
to achieve by force, Eur.: to carry one's point, Plut.
intr. to win a complete victory: metaph. to gain the upper hand, prevail, Thuc.
unusual, marvellous: adv. -ίως, Ar.; Sup. ἐκνομιώτατα Id.
outlawed, Lat. exlex, Aesch.:—adv. -μως, out of tune, discordantly, Id.
senseless, Lat. amens, Plut.
Dep. to take for one's own, Anth.
willingly, Plut.
of actions, voluntary, Soph., Eur., etc.; τὰ ἑκούσια voluntary acts, opp. to τὰ ἀκούσια, Xen.
rarely, like ἑκών, of persons, willing, acting of free will, Soph., Thuc.
adv. -ίως, Eur., etc.; so, ἐξ ἑκουσίας (sc. γνώμης) Soph.; καθ’ ἑκουσίαν Thuc.
Pass. to be struck with amazement, to wonder greatly, only in part., Hdt.
to wonder at, admire exceedingly, c. acc., Aesch., Eur.
terrible, fearful, of persons; superl. ἐκπαγλότατος Il.:—of things, Od.
as adv. terribly, vehemently, exceedingly, Hom.:—also neut. as adv., ἔκπαγλον and ἔκπαγλα, Il.
in later Poets, marvellous, wondrous, Aesch., Soph.; adv. ἔκπαγλα marvellously, Id.
a nursling, a child, Eur.
to bring up from childhood, educate completely, Eur., Plat.
to rush madly to the fray, Il.
to throw out of a thing, dash one from it, c. gen., Eur.
Mid. to dash out, escape, Plut.
to shake out:—Pass. to spurt out from, c. gen., ἔκπαλτο (syncop. epic aor2 mid. as pass.) Il.
to strike, afflict, Eur.:—Pass., φρένας ἐκπεπαταγμένος stricken in mind, Od.
out of the common path: excessive, vehement, Aesch.
to set quite at rest, put an end to, Eur.:—Mid. to take one's rest, Thuc.
to over-persuade, Soph., Eur.
to tempt, c. acc., NTest.
to make trial of, prove, tempt, c. gen. pers., Hdt.; c. inf., ἐκπειρᾷ λέγειν; art thou tempting me to speak? Soph.
to inquire of another, τί τινος Ar.
'tis permitted, Soph.
of persons, to send out or forth from a place, c. gen., Hom., Aesch., etc.:—Mid., Od., Soph., etc.
to bring out by calling, call or fetch out, Id.; so in Mid., Id.:—Pass. to go forth, depart, Id.
to send forth, dispatch, Thuc.
to send away, cast out, Hdt., Aesch.; to divorce a wife, Hdt.:—so in Mid., Soph.
of things, to send out, send abroad, Il., Hdt.
to send forth, give out, σέλας Aesch.
a sending out or forth, Thuc.
to make quite ripe or mellow, Theophr.

entry.etym: adverb from perf. pass. of ἐκπλήσσω
entry.sense: in panic fear, Dem.

entry.etym: adverb from perf. pass. of ἐκπετάννυμι,
entry.sense: extravagantly, Xen.
to finish off, Eur.:—Pass. to be accomplished, Id., Xen.
a coming out of, δωμάτων Aesch.
to go out over, pass beyond, Od., Aesch.; ἐκπ. βίον to go through life, Eur.
absol. of an arrow, to pass through, pierce, Il.
to go or come out of a place, c. gen., Eur.
to escape like a partridge, Ar.
to destroy utterly, Il., Aesch.
to go out and round, go all round, Xen.
to sail out round, so as to attack in flank, Plut.
more exceedingly, NTest.
more than a year ago, Luc.

entry.note: fut. -πετάσω aor1 pass. ἐξεπετάσθην perf. ἐκπεπέτασμαι
entry.sense: to spread out, of a sail, Eur.; of wings, Anth.; of a net, Orac. ap. Hdt.
metaph., ἐπὶ κῶμον ἐκπετασθείς wholly given up to revel, Eur.
ready to fly out, just fledged, Ar.

entry.note: or -πέταμαι fut. -πτήσομαι aor2 ἐξεπτόμην aor2 -άμην act. ἐξέπτην
entry.sense: to fly out or away, Hes., Eur.
to leap out, Hdt.
to make a sally, Xen.
to leap up, start up, Soph.
a leap out, ὕψος κρεῖσσον ἐκπηδήματος a height too great for out-leap, Aesch.
to spin out:—metaph., of an advocate, αὐτοῦ ἐκπηνιεῖται ταῦτα will wind these things out of him, Ar.
Dep. to gush forth, Aesch.
to fill up a bowl, Eur.; ἐκπ. κρατῆρας δρόσου to fill them full of liquid, Id.
to satiate, Id., Thuc.
to fulfil, Hdt.; ἁμαρτάδα ἐξέπλησε paid the full penalty of sin, Id.
to accomplish, complete, Trag.
to drink out or off, quaff liquor, Od.: so, in perf. pass., ἐκπέποται Id., Hdt.; αἵματ’ ἐκποθένθ’ ὑπὸ χθονός Aesch.
to drain a cup dry, πλῆρες ἐκπ. κέρας Soph.: metaph., ἐκπ. ὄλβον Eur.
to sell out, sell off, Dem.
to fall out of a chariot, c. gen., Hom., etc.; c. dat. pers., τόξον δέ οἱ ἔκπεσε χειρός Il.
of seafaring men, to be thrown ashore, Lat. ejici, Od., Hdt., etc.: of things, to suffer shipwreck, Xen.
to fall from a thing, i. e. be deprived of it, Lat. excidere, τινός or ἔκ τινος Aesch., etc.
to be driven out, of persons banished, Hdt., etc.
to go out or forth, sally out, Id., Xen.
to come out, of votes, Id.
to escape, Thuc.
of oracles, to issue from the sanctuary, be imparted, Luc.
to depart from, digress, Xen., Aeschin.
to fall off, come to naught, NTest.
of actors, to be hissed off the stage, Lat. explodi, Dem.
six plethra long, Eur.
quite full of a thing, c. gen., Eur.
complete, of a body of soldiers, Xen.: abundant, Id.
to sail out, sail away, weigh anchor, Hdt., etc.: c. gen. to sail away from, Soph.
metaph., ἐκπλεῖν τοῦ νοῦ, τῶν φρενῶν to go out of one's mind, lose one's senses, Hdt.
ἐκπλ. τὰς ναῦς to outsail the ships, Thuc.
striking with consternation, astounding, Thuc.
terror-stricken, amazed, Luc.
consternation, Thuc., etc.; ἔκπλ. κακῶν terror caused by misfortunes, Aesch.
to fill quite up, Eur.
to make up to a certain number, Hdt., Soph.
to man completely, ναῦς Hdt.
to fulfil, Id.
ἐκπλ. λιμένα to make one's way over the harbour, Lat. emetiri, Eur.
to strike out of, drive away from, Aesch.:—absol. to drive away, Thuc.

to drive out of one's senses, to amaze, astound, Od., Eur.:—often in aor2 pass., epic ἐξεπλήγην, attic ἐξεπλάγην [ᾰ]; aor1 ἐξεπλήχθην; perf. ἐκπέπληγμαι· — to be panic-struck, amazed, astonied, Il., Soph., etc.; ἐκπλαγῆναί τινι to be astonished at a thing, Hdt., so διά τι, ἐπί τινι, etc.; ἐκπλαγῆναί τινα to be struck with panic fear of . . , Soph., Thuc.
generally, of sudden passion, to be stricken, Aesch., etc.
note also the form ἐκπλήγνυμι, Thuc.
a sailing out, leaving port, Aesch., Thuc., etc.
a passage out, entrance of a harbour, Aesch., Xen.
to wash out, esp. to wash out colours from cloths, Plat.:—Pass. to be washed out, Hdt.
to wash clean, Ar.
to be washed out, of colours, Plat.:— metaph. washed out, Aesch.
to breathe out or forth, Plat.; κεραυνὸς ἐκπνέων φλόγα Aesch.
βίον ἐκπν. to breathe one's last, expire, Id., Eur.; also, ἐκπν. θυμόν, ψυχήν Id.
absol. to cease blowing, to become calm, Id.
to blow outwards, of wind, Hdt., Thuc.: to burst out, Soph.
a breathing out, expiring, Plat.

opp. to ἐμποδών, away from the feet, i. e. out of the way, Hdt., Aesch., etc.:— c. dat., ἐκπ. χωρεῖν τινι to get out of his way, Eur.: —ἐκποδὼν ποιεῖσθαι to put out of the way, Xen.: c. gen., ἐκπ. χθονός far from it, Eur.
to put out:
to put out a child, i. e. give him in adoption, Isae.
Mid. to produce, bring forth, Ar.
to make complete, finish, finish off, Hdt.:—c. gen. materiae, Παρίου λίθου τὰ ἔμπροσθε ἐξεποίησαν they made all the front of Parian marble, Id.
a putting forth, emission, Hdt.
given in adoption, Aeschin.
to excite to war, make hostile, Xen.
to make hostile, to involve in war, Hdt., Thuc.:—Pass. to become an enemy to, be at feud with, τινι Hdt.
a making hostile, Plut.
to force a besieged town to surrender, Thuc., Xen.:—Pass. to be forced to surrender, Thuc.
to walk in state, to strut, Luc.
a sending out or forth, Thuc.

to work out, finish off, Lat. elaborare, Ar.; κἠμὲ μαλθακὸν ἐξεπόνασε σιδαρέω wrought me soft-hearted from iron-hearted, Theocr.; ἐκπ. τινά to deck him out, Eur.:—Pass. to be brought to perfection, Thuc.; ἐκπεπονημένος σῖτος corn fully prepared for use, Xen.; ἐκπεπονῆσθαι τὰ σώματα to be in good training or practice, Id.
to execute, Eur.; so in Mid., Id.
to provide by labour, earn, Id.:—c. acc. et inf. τοὺς θεοὺς ἐκπ. φράζειν to prevail on the gods to tell, Id.
absol. to work hard, Id., Xen.
to work out by searching, to search out, Eur.
of food, to digest it by labour, Xen.
to work at, work well, Theocr.
in Pass. to be worn out, Lat. confici, Plut.
to make to go out, fetch out, Eur.: —Mid., with fut. mid. and aor1 pass., to go out or forth, march out, Xen.
to pillage, Eur., etc.:—Pass., of a person, to be undone, Soph., Eur.
to carry off as plunder, Thuc.
a waster, destroyer, Eur.
to carry away by sea:—Eur. has perf. pass. ἐκπεπόρθμευται in both pass. and mid. sense.
to invent, contrive, Eur.
to provide, furnish, Soph., Ar., etc.:—Mid. to provide for oneself, procure, Thuc.
to commit fornication, NTest.
Dep. to fly out or forth, of snow-flakes, Il.: metaph., πᾶ τὰς φρένας ἐκπεπότασαι (2nd sg. doric perf.); = quae te dementia cepit? Theocr.
to do completely, to bring about, achieve, Lat. efficere, Aesch., etc.; τὸν καλλίνικον ἐξεπράξατε ἐς γόον ye have made the hymn of triumph end in wailing, Eur.
to make an end of, kill, destroy, Lat. conficere, Trag.
to exact, levy, Eur.; c. dupl. acc., χρήματα ἐκπρ. τινά to exact money from a person, Thuc.
to exact punishment for a thing, to avenge, Soph., Eur.:—so in Mid., Hdt.
distinguished out of all, preeminent, remarkable, Il.; μεγέθει ἐκπρεπεστάτα Aesch.; εἶδος ἐκπρεπεστάτη Eur.
= ἔξω τοῦ πρέποντος, unseemly, monstrous, Thuc.: so adv. -πῶς, without reasonable grounds, Id.
to be excellent in a thing, τινί Eur.
a setting on fire, inflaming, Plut.
to buy off, Oratt.
to saw out, Thuc.
beyond the appointed day, too late for a thing, c. gen., Luc.
to be very zealous, Eur.
to send forth, Eur.
Mid. to call to oneself or summon out of, ἐκπροκαλεσσαμένη μεγάρων Od.
to choose out, πόλεος ἐκπροκριθεῖσα Eur.
to forsake, abandon, Od.
to flow forth from, Anth.
to honour above all, Soph.
to flee away from, Anth.
to pour forth, Anth.
Dep. to spread the wings, Luc.
to scare out of, οἴκων με ἐξέπταξας (doric) Eur.
= ἐκπτήσσω Tzetz.:—Pass. to bestruck with admiration, Eur.
to spit out of, c. gen., Od.
to spit in token of disgust, Ar.:— to spit at, abominate, NTest.
Dep.: to search out, make enquiry, Il., Eur.
c. acc. to enquire about, hear of, learn, Soph.; ἐκπ. τινος to make inquiry of him, Ar.
to burn to ashes, consume utterly, Eur.: Pass. to catch fire, be burnt up, Id.

entry.etym: ἐξ before a vowel, ἐγ before β γ δ λ μ
entry.sense: prep. governing GEN. only, Lat. e, exRadical sense, from out of, opp. to εἰς:
OF PLACE:
of Motion, out of, forth from, Hom., etc.: ἐκ θυμοῦ φίλεον I loved her from my heart, with all my heart, Il.
to denote change from one place or condition to another, κακὸν ἐκ κακοῦ one evil from (or after) another, Id.; λόγον ἐκ λόγου λέγειν Dem.
to express distinction from a number, ἐκ πόλεων πίσυρες four out of many, Il.
of Position, like ἔξω, outside of, beyond, ἐκ βελέων out of shot, Id.; ἐκ καπνοῦ out of the smoke, Od.

with Verbs of Rest, ἐκ ποταμοῦ χρόα νίζετο washed his body with water from the river, Id.:—with Verbs signifying to hang or fasten, ἐκ πασσαλόφι κρέμασεν φόρμιγγα he hung his lyre from (i. e. on) the peg, Id.; ἐκ τοῦ βραχίονος ἐπέλκουσα leading it [by a rein] upon her arm, Hdt.:—also, sitting or standing, στᾶς’ ἐξ Οὐλύμποιο from Olympus where she stood, Il.; καθῆσθαι ἐκ πάγων to sit on the heights and look from them, Soph.
OF TIME, ἐξ οὗ or ἐξ οὗτε [χρόνου], Lat. ex quo, since, Hom., attic; ἐκ τοῦ or ἐκ τοῖο from that time, Il.; ἐκ πολλοῦ (sc. χρόνου) for a long time, Thuc.
of particular points of time, ἐκ νέου or ἐκ παιδός from boyhood; ἐξ ἀρχῆς, etc.; so, ἐκ θυσίας γενέσθαι to have just finished sacrifice, Hdt.; ἐκ τοῦ ἀρίστου after breakfast, Xen.
when we say in or by, ἐκ νυκτῶν Od.; ἐκ νυκτός Xen., etc.
OF ORIGIN,
of the Material, out of or of which things are made, ποιεῖσθαι ἐκ ξύλων τὰ πλοῖα Hdt.
of the Father, ἔκ τινος εἶναι, γενέσθαι, φῦναι, etc., Il.; ἀγαθοὶ καὶ ἐξ ἀγαθῶν Plat.
of the Author or Occasion of a thing, ὄναρ ἐκ Διός ἐστιν Il.; θάνατος ἐκ μνηστήρων death by the hand of the suitors, Od.; τὰ ἐξ Ἑλλήνων τείχεα walls built by them, Hdt.
with the agent after Pass. Verbs, where ὑπό is more common, ἐφίληθεν ἐκ Διός they were beloved of (i. e. by) Zeus, Il.

of the Cause, Instrument or Means by which a thing is done, ἐκ πατέρων φιλότητος in consequence of our father's friendship, Od.; so, ἐκ τίνος; ἐκ τοῦ; wherefore? Eur.; ποιεῖτε ὑμῖν φίλους ἐκ τοῦ Μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας make yourselves friends of (i. e. by means of), NTest.
from, i. e. according to, ἐκ τῶν λογίων according to the oracles, Hdt.; ἐκ νόμων Aesch.
periphr. for an adv., (as in Lat. ex consulto, ex composito), ἐκ βίας by force, = βιαίως, Soph.; ἐκ τοῦ φανεροῦ = φανερῶς, Thuc., etc.
with numerals, ἐκ τρίτου in the third place, Eur.
a conflagration, Luc.
discovered, Thuc.
a drinking-cup, beaker, Hdt., Soph., etc.
to scatter out of, make to fall in drops from, Soph.

entry.note: fut. -ρεύσομαι perf. ἐξερρύηκα aor2 pass. ἐξερρύην
entry.sense: in act. sense:— to flow out or forth, Il., Hdt., Plat.
of feathers, to fall off, Ar.
metaph. to fall away, disappear, Lat. effluere, Plat.
c. acc. cogn. to shed, let fall, χάριν Anth.
to break off, snap asunder, Il.; c. gen., ὕδωρ ἐξέρρηξεν ὁδοῖο the water broke off a piece of the road, Id.:—Pass. to break or snap asunder, Hdt.

c. acc. cogn. to let break forth, break out with, Plut., Luc.:—Pass. to break out, of an ulcer, Hdt., Aesch.; of a quarrel, ἐς μέσον ἐξερράγη it broke out in public, Hdt.; of persons, to break out into passionate words, Id.
sometimes also intr. in Act., οὔ ποτ’ ἐκρήξει μάχη Soph.
to root out, NTest.
to fan the flame, stir up, Plut.
to cast forth, Aesch., Soph.
= ἔροος, Plat.
an issue, Id.
a flowing out, outflow, outfall, Hdt.
to drink out, gulp down, Ar.
to deliver, Eur.
to shake violently, Anth.
to shake out of, τί τινος Hdt.:—Pass., Ar.

entry.note: perf. ἐξέσσῠμαι 3rd pl. plup. ἐξέσσῠτο aor1 ἐξεσύθην
entry.sense: to rush out or burst forth from a place, c. gen., Hom.: absol. to rush out, Id.
to disclose, indicate, Soph.
Pass. to be put to utter silence, Anth.
to scatter to the wind, Ar.
to disfurnish of tools and implements, Dem.
to wipe out, wipe clean, Hdt.
to scare away, Anth.
to draw out, Il.; so in Mid., ἐκσπασσαμένω ἔγχεα having drawn out their spears, Id.
to pour out as a libation, Eur.
= ἔξω τῶν σπονδῶν, out of the treaty, excluded from it, Thuc., Xen.
six stades long, Luc.
any displacement: entrancement, astonishment, NTest.; a trance, Id.
inclined to depart from, c. gen., Arist.
to fit out, equip, Soph.
to deck with garlands, Eur.; of suppliants, κρᾶτας ἐξεστεμμένοι Id.; but, ἱκτηρίοις κλάδοισιν ἐξεστεμμένοι with garlands on the suppliant olive-branches, Soph.
a going out on service, Luc.
to march out, Thuc., Xen.
in Mid., absol. to take the field, Hdt., Thuc.
to have ended the campaign, Id.
Dep. with perf. pass. to encamp outside, Thuc., Xen.
to turn out of, root up from a place, c. gen., Il.
to turn inside out, Ar.: metaph. to alter entirely, Id.
to hiss off the stage, Lat. explodere, Dem.
Pass. to be shut out from, Eur.

to preserve from danger, keep safe, Hdt., Soph., etc.; ἐκς. τινά τινος to save one from another, Eur.; ἐκς. τινὰ ἐς φάος to bring one safe to light, Id.:—Mid. to save oneself, Hdt.; or to save for oneself, Aesch.:—Pass. to flee for safety, Id.
to heap or pile up, Eur.
outstretched, Eur.
outstretched, outspread, Il.
on the sixth day, Xen.
= ἕκτος, sixth, Anth.
= e)ktei/nw, to stretch out (on the ground), lay low, Il.:—Pass. to lie outstretched, ἐξετανύσθη Id.
to stretch tight, Od.
to throw into great trouble, to agitate, Plut.
extension, Plat.
to draw out in battle-order, of the officers:—Mid. to draw themselves out, of the soldiers, Xen.
to stretch out, Hdt., attic: τὰ γόνατα ἐκτ. to straighten the knees, Ar.: ἐκτ. νέκυν to lay one dead, Eur.:—Pass. to be outstretched, lie at length, Soph.
to stretch or spread out a net, Aesch.: to extend the line of an army, Eur.
to stretch out, prolong, λόγον Hdt., attic
to put to the full stretch, of a horse put to full speed, Xen.; πᾶσαν προθυμίην ἐκτ. to put forth all one's zeal, Hdt.:—metaph. in Pass. to be on the rack, Soph.
to fortify completely, Thuc., Xen.; τεῖχος ἐκτ. to build it from the ground, Ar.
to generate, Eur., in Mid.
to bring quite to an end, accomplish, Aesch.:—Pass. to be quite the end of, τινός Soph.
to bring quite to an end, to accomplish, achieve, Hom., Hdt.: —Pass., fut. inf. ἐκτελέεσθαι, to be accomplished, Il., etc.
brought to an end, perfect, Aesch.; of corn, ripe, Hes.; of persons, Eur.
to cut out, Il., Hdt.; ὀϊστὸν ἐκτάμνειν μηροῦ to cut an arrow from the thigh, Il.
to cut trees out of a wood, cut down, Id.; of planks, to hew out, hew into shape, ὃς νήϊον ἐκτάμνῃσιν (epic for -τέμνῃ) Id.
to cut away, sever, Pind., Plat.
to castrate, Hdt.
intensity, zeal, earnestness, NTest.
intense, zealous, instant, NTest.
to be held, Ar.
ἑκτέος one must have, Xen.
to burn to ashes, calcine, Strab.
to melt out, destroy, by melting, Eur., Ar.
metaph. to let melt away, let pine or waste away, Eur.
Pass., with perf. ἐκτέτηκα, aor2 ἐξετάκην [ᾰ], to melt, pine or waste away, Id.; τόδ’ μήποτ’ ἐκτακείη may it never melt from my remembrance, Aesch.
those who paid 1/6th of the produce, Plut.
to set out, place outside, Od.: to expose on a desert island or to expose a new-born child, Hdt., attic:—Mid. to export, Plut.
to set up in public, exhibit publicly, νόμους Dem.
to pluck out hair:—Pass., κόμην ἐκτετιλμένος having one's hair plucked out, Anacr.
to honour highly, Soph.
not shewing honour, Soph.
to shake outPass., ἐκ δ’ ἐτίναχθεν (epic for -ησαν) ὀδόντες Il.
to shake off dust from one's feet, NTest.: so in Mid., Id.
to pay off, pay in full, Hdt., attic;— δίκην ἐκτ. to pay full penalty, Eur.; τινός for a thing, Hdt.
Mid. to exact full payment for a thing, avenge, c. acc. rei, Soph., Eur.; to take vengeance on, τινά Id.
to bring forth untimely: to miscarry, Hdt.
from without, outside, c. gen., ἔκτοθεν ἄλλων μνηστήρων outside their circle, apart from them, Od.; πύργων δ’ ἔκτ. βαλών having struck them from the wall, Aesch.
absol. outside, Trag.; ἔκτ. γαμεῖν to marry from an alien house, Eur.
for ἐκ τόθεν, out of, outside, c. gen., Il.
to wind a ball of wool quite off: metaph. to bring quite to an end, Hes., Aesch.
a cutting out, Plut.
castration, Hdt., etc.
a segment, piece, Plut.
a eunuch, Hdt.
fem. adj. cutting down, Anth.
to shoot out, shoot away, Hdt.:— metaph., ἐξετόξευσεν has shot away all its arrows, i. e. has no resource left, Eur.
absol. to shoot from a place, shoot arrows, Xen.
to take oneself from a place, go abroad, like ἀποδημέω, Arist.:—metaph. of a speaker, to wander from the point, Id.
ἠνύσατ’ ἐκτοπίαν φλόγα ye have put away the fire, Soph.
away from a place, away from, c. gen., Soph.
absol. distant, Id.; ἔκτοπος ἔστω let him leave the place, Eur.
foreign, strange, οὐδενὸς πρὸς ἐκτόπου by no strange hand, Soph.
out of the way, strange, extraordinary, Ar.
to kill by piercing, Hhymn.
outwards: c. gen. out of, Od.
outside, c. gen., Hom.:—absol., Od.
to deck out in tragic phrase, exaggerate, Luc.
sixth, Lat. sextus, Hom., etc.
outside, opp. to ἐντός:
as prep. with gen. outside, out of, far from, c. gen., Hom.: outside of, free from, Hdt., attic; ἐκτὸς ἐλπίδος beyond hope, Lat. praeter spem, Soph.
of Time, beyond, Hdt.
except, ἐκτὸς ὀλίγων Xen.
absol., τὰ ἐκτός external things, Eur.
with Verbs of motion, ῥίπτειν ἐκτός to throw out, Soph., etc.
banished from the table, Luc.
turning from the common course, devious, strange, Theogn.
of a horse, to throw the rider over its head, Xen.:—Pass. to break one's neck, Ar.: metaph. to plunge headlong into destruction, Dem.
to make rough, Luc.:—metaph. to exasperate, Plut.
to turn out of the course, to turn aside, c. acc., Hdt., attic:—Pass. and Mid., c. gen. to turn aside from, Soph.: absol. to turn aside, Hdt., Xen.
to turn a person off the road, order him out of the way, Soph.:—Pass. and Mid., ἐκτρέπεσθαί τινα to get out of one's way, avoid him, Dem.
τὴν δρῶσαν ἐκτρέπειν to prevent her from acting, Soph.
ἀσπίδας θύρσοις ἐκτρ. to turn shields and flee before the thyrsus, Eur.
to bring up from childhood, rear up, Hdt., attic:—Mid. for oneself, Hhymn., Soph.
to run out or forth, make a sally, Il., Thuc.
to run off or away, Ar.
to run beyond bounds, exceed bounds, Soph.
to rub out, πῦρ ἐκτρ. to produce fire by rubbing, Xen.:— to rub hard, Soph.
to rub out, i. e. to destroy root and branch, Hdt., Eur.; βίον ἐκτρ. to bring life to a wretched end, Soph.:—Pass., πρόρριζος ἐκτέτριπται Hdt.
to rub constantly, wear out, Eur.
a turning off or aside, Thuc.
(from Mid.) a turning aside, escape, μόχθων from labours, Aesch.
ἐκτρ. ὁδοῦ a place to which one turns from the road, a resting-place, Lat. deverticulum, Ar.
to wear out, exhaust, Thuc.
to eat up, devour, Ar.
a child untimely born, an abortion, NTest.
worked in high relief: ἔκτυπος, ὁ, a figure worked in relief, a cameo, Inscr.
to model or work in relief, Xen.
to make quite blind, Hdt., Xen., etc.
a making blind, Hdt.
a mother-in-law, step-mother, = πενθερά, Il.
a father-in-law, step-father, = πενθερός, Il.
to make quite bright, clear away, Eur.
to shew forth, bring to light, disclose, reveal, make manifest, Il., Hdt., etc.:—Pass. to shew oneself, shine forth, come forth to view, Il.
to exhibit, κακότητα Hdt.
ἐκφ. πόλεμον to declare war, Xen.
shewing itself, manifest, Aesch., Plat.
a declaration, Hdt.
beyond power of speech: adv. -τως, ineffably, impiously, Aesch.
to depreciate, Luc.

entry.note: fut. ἐξοίσω fut. mid. ἐξοίσομαι in pass. sense
entry.sense: to carry out of a place, c. gen., or ἐκ τόπου, Il., Hdt.
to carry out a corpse for burial, Lat. efferre, Il., etc.
to carry off as prize or reward, Id.: so in Mid., Hdt., attic
to carry out of the sea, to throw ashore, Hdt., Eur.:—Pass., with fut. mid., to come to land, be cast ashore, Hdt.
to bring forth,
of women, of the earth, to bring forth, produce, Id.
to bring about, accomplish, Il.
to bring out, publish, Ar.: ἐκφ. χρηστήριον to deliver an oracle, Hdt.:—of public measures, to bring forward, ἐκφ. ἐς τὸν δῆμον Id., Dem.
generally to disclose, tell, betray, Hdt.:—Mid., ἐκφέρεσθαι γνώμην to declare one's opinion, Id.
to put forth, exert, δύνασιν Eur.; and in Mid., Soph.
ἐκφέρειν πόλεμον, Lat. inferre bellum, to begin war, Hdt., Xen.
to bear the marks of a thing, Eur.
Pass. to be carried beyond bounds, be carried away, Soph., Thuc., etc.
to carry to a certain point, Soph., Plat.
intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν) to shoot forth (before the rest), Il.: to run away, Xen.
to come to fulfilment, come to an end, Soph.
to flee out or away, escape, Od., Aesch., etc.:— to be acquitted, Ar.
c. gen. to escape out of, flee from, Hom.
c. acc. to escape, Il., Hdt., etc.
of things, ἐκφεύγει μέ τι something escapes me, Soph., Eur.
to speak out or forth, speak loudly: Mid., ἔπος ἐκφάσθαι (aor2 inf.) Od.
to destroy utterlyPass. ἐκφθείρομαι, to be undone, ruined, Eur.: to vanish, pack off, Ar.
ἐξέφθῐτο οἶνος νηῶν, the wine had all been consumed out of the ships, had vanished from the ships, Od.; 3rd pl. perf. pass. ἐξέφθινται they have utterly perished, Aesch.
to kiss heartily, Anth.
to set on fire, Ar.
to frighten away, affright, Aesch., Plat., etc.; τὸ ἐκφοβῆσαι so as to cause alarm, Thuc.; ἐκφ. τινὰ ἐκ δεμνίων Eur.:—Pass. to be much afraid, to fear greatly, c. acc., Soph.
affrighted, NTest.
to make all red or bloody, Eur.
to go out constantly, be in the habit of going out, Hdt., Eur.
of things, to be spread abroad, Plut.
a carrying out of a corpse to burial, Aesch., Ar.
(from Pass.) of horses, a running away, Xen.
to carry out a corpse for burial, Od.:—generally to carry out, Hdt.:—Mid. to take out with one, Eur., etc.:—Pass. to move forth, Il.
to carry quite out, leave none behind, of earth dug from a trench, Hdt.
Pass. to be cast on shore, Id.
payment on produce, rent, tithe, Hdt.
to be carried out, exportable, Ar.
to be made known or divulged, Eur.
act. prepared to weed out, as a gardener does noxious plants, Aesch.
Pass. to be sold for exportation, to be kidnapped, betrayed, Soph.
to tell over, recount, Aesch., Eur.
a description, Luc.

entry.note: poet. 1st pl. imperf. ἐξεφρείομεν fut. -φρήσω aor1 -έφρησα
entry.sense: to let out, bring out, Eur., Ar.
to think out, discover, Lat. excogitare, Eur., Ar., etc.
out of one's mind, senseless, Dem.: also, frenzied, enthusiastic, of poets, Plat.
to watch carefully, Soph., Eur.
to condemn by leaves, used of the Athen. βουλή, which gave their votes written on olive-leaves, Aeschin.
out of the tribe, alienmetaph. strange, unnatural, Plut.
to blow out, ποταμὸς ἐκφυσᾷ μένος pours forth its strength, Aesch.: metaph., ἐκφ. πόλεμον to blow up a war from a spark, Ar.
to breathe out, ὕπνον ἔκφ. i. e. to snore, Theocr.
to generate from another, to beget, of the male, Soph., etc.
of the female, to bear, Id.: also, to produce a plant, Dem.
Pass., with perf. and aor2 act., to be born from another, c. gen., Il., Soph., etc.; λάλημα ἐκπεφυκός a tattler by nature, Id.
to cry out, Plut.
to let go from, τί τινος Anth.
to unbridle, Plut.
to stuff out, to make vain and arrogant, Eur.

entry.note: fut. -χεῶ aor1 ἐξέχεα epic ἔκχευα mid. ἐκχευάμην
entry.sense: to pour out, properly of liquids, Il., Aesch., etc.: metaph., in Med., ἐκχεύατ’ ὀϊστούς he poured forth his arrows, Od.
of words, Aesch., etc.
to pour out like water, squander, waste, one's substance, Id., etc.

Pass., 3rd pl. plup. ἐξεκέχυντο, epic syncop. aor2 ἐξέχῠτο or ἔκχῠτο, part. ἐκχύμενος [ῠ]:— to pour out, stream out or forth, properly of liquids, Hom.:—metaph. of persons, Id.: —generally, to be spread out, Od.
to be poured out like water, forgotten, Theogn., Plat.
to give oneself up to joy, to be overjoyed, Ar.; ἐκχ. γελῶν to burst out laughing, Anth.
to lie languidly, Id.
to break out of the chorus: Mid. to drive out of the chorus, Eur.
to declare as an oracle, tell out, Soph.
to suffice, Hdt.:— impers., like ἀποχρᾷ, c. inf., κῶς βασιλέϊ ἐκχρήσει; how will it suffice him? how will he be content to . . ? Id.
Dep. to squeeze money from, levy contributions on, τινα Thuc.
a spendthrift, Luc.
poured forth, unconfined, outstretched, Anth.
Pass. to be raised on a bank or mound, Hdt.
to go out and away, depart, emigrate, Hdt.
to slip out of, ἐξεχώρησεν ἐξ ἄρθρων was dislocated, Id.
to give way, Soph., Eur.
to give up the ghost, expire, NTest.
willing, of free will, readily, Hom., etc.
wittingly, purposely, ἑκὼν ἡμάρτανε φωτός Il., attic
in Prose, ἑκὼν εἶναι or ἑκών, as far as depends on my will, as far as concerns me, mostly with a negat., Hdt., Plat.

the olive-tree, Lat. olea, oliva, Hom., etc.; said to have been produced by Athena in her contest with Poseidon, Hdt., Soph.; φέρεσθαι ἐκτὸς τῶν ἐλαῶν to run beyond the olives, which stood at the end of the Athenian race-course, i. e. to go too far, Ar.
the fruit of the olive-tree, an olive, Id.
planted with olives, Anth.
oily, of oil, Anth.
of olive-wood, Hom.
an olive-gatherer, Ar.
olive-oil, Lat. oleum, olivum, Hom.
an oil-merchant, Dem.
the wild olive, Lat. oleaster, Soph.
olive-bearing, Eur.
olive-planted, Eur.
olive-planted, Aesch.
an olive-tree: attic pl. ἐλᾷδες Ar.
an olive-yard, Lat. olivetum: the Mount of Olives, Olivet, NTest.
man-destroying, of Helen, Aesch.
an unknown bird, Ar.
Desiderat. to wish to march, Luc.
riding, Xen.
hurled like thunder, Ar.
a driving away, banishing, Thuc.
(sub. στρατοῦ), a march, expedition, Hdt.: a procession, Xen.:—(sub. ἵππου) a riding, Id.
to make less or smaller, to lessen, diminish, lower, Oratt.: c. gen. to detract from, Thuc.
Pass.
absol. to become smaller, be lessened, suffer loss, be depreciated, Id.: —also to take less than one's due, waive one's rights or privileges, Id.
c. dat. rei, to have the worst of it, to be inferior, τινι in a thing, Id., Xen.
c. gen. pers. to be at disadvantage with a person, Dem.

smaller, less, formed from ἐλαχύς (with Sup. ἐλάχιστος, q. v.), but serving as comp. to μικρός, Il.: ἔλασσον ἔχειν to have the worse, be worse off, τινί in a thing, Hdt., Dem.; so, ἐλάττω γίγνεσθαι Ar.
c. gen. pers. worse than, inferior to, Thuc., etc.; but c. gen. rei, like ἥσσων, subservient to, Xen.
in neut. with Preps., περὶ ἐλάσσονος ποιεῖσθαι to consider of less account, Hdt.; παρ’ ἔλαττον ἡγεῖσθαι Plat.; δι’ ἐλάττονος at less distance, Thuc.
of Number, fewer, οἱ ἐλάσσονες the smaller number, Hdt., Thuc.
neut. ἔλασσον, as adv. less, Aesch., etc.
to drive, Il.; ἐλ. τινα to drive about, of the Furies, Eur.:—Pass., of ships, to be rowed, Hdt.
one must ride, Xen.
the silver fir, pinus picea, Il.
an oar, Hom.: also a ship or boat, like Lat. abies, Eur.
driving away, c. gen., Aesch.
a driver of horses, a charioteer, Il., Aesch.
a sort of broad, flat cake, Ar.
of the fir, Lat. abiegnus, Il., Eur.:— of fir or pine-wood, Od., Eur.
a disadvantage, Dem.

Radic. sense : to drive, drive on, set in motion, of driving flocks, Hom.; so aor. mid. ἠλασάμην Il.: often of chariots, to drive, Id., Hdt.; also, ἐλ. ἵππον to ride it, Id.; ἐλ. νῆα to row it, Od.:—in this sense the acc. was omitted, and the Verb became intr., to go in a chariot, to drive, μάστιξεν δ’ ἐλάαν (sc. ἵππους) he whipped them on, Il.; βῆ δ’ ἐλάαν ἐπὶ κύματα he drove on over the waves, Id.; διὰ νύκτα ἐλάαν to travel the night through, Od.; — to ride, Hdt., etc.; to march, Id.; to row, Od.
in this intr. sense, it sometimes took an acc. loci, γαλήνην ἐλαύνειν to sail the calm sea, i. e. over it, Id.; ἐλαύνειν δρόμον to run a course, Ar.
to drive away, like ἀπελαύνω, of stolen cattle, Hom., Xen.: —so in Mid., Hom.
to drive away, expel, Il., Trag.

to drive to extremities, ἄδην ἐλόωσι πολέμοιο will harass him till he has had enough of war, Il.; ἄδην ἐλάαν κακότητος shall persecute him till he has had enough, Od.:—then in attic to persecute, attack, harass, Soph., etc.
intr. in expressions like ἐς τοσοῦτον ἤλασαν, they drove it so far (where πρᾶγμα must be supplied), Hdt.:—hence, to push on, go on, Eur., Plat.
to strike, ἐλάτηισιν πόντον ἐλαύνοντες, cf. Lat. remis impellere, Il.
to strike with a weapon, but never with a missile, Id.:— c. dupl. acc., τὸν μὲν ἔλας’ ὦμον him he struck on the shoulder, Id.; χθόνα ἤλασε μετώπωι struck earth with his forehead, Od.
to drive or thrust through, δόρυ διὰ στήθεσφιν ἔλασσε Il.; and in Pass. to go through, Id.
in metaph. senses:
to beat with a hammer, Lat. ducere, to beat out metal, Il.; περὶ δ’ ἕρκος ἔλασσε κασσιτέρου around he made a fence of beaten tin, Id.

to draw a line of wall or a trench, Lat. ducere murum, Hom., etc.; τεῖχος ἐς τὸν ποταμὸν τοὺς ἀγκῶνας ἐλήλαται the wall has its angles carried down to the river, Hdt.; ὄγμον ἐλαύνειν to work one's way down a ridge or swathe in reaping or mowing, Il.; ὄρχον ἀμπελίδος ἐλ. to draw a line of vines, i. e. plant them in line, Ar.
κολωιὸν ἐλαύνειν to prolong the brawl, Il.
of a stag, ἐλ. κρέα venison, Xen.
a shooting of deer, Soph.
the ninth month of the Attic year, in which the Elaphebolia were held, answering to the last half of March and first of April, Thuc.
shooting deer, Il., Soph.
deer-killing, Eur.
a deer, whether male, a hart or stag, or female, a hind, Il.:— κραδίην ἐλάφοιο [ἔχων] with heart of deer, i. e. a coward, Id.
deer-hunting, Anth.
lightness: levity, NTest.
= Lat. lev-is light in weight, Il., Hdt., attic:— adv. lightly, buoyantly, Od.
light to bear, not burdensome, easy, Il.; ἐλαφρόν [ἐστι] 'tis light, easy, Aesch., etc.; ἐν ἐλαφρῷ ποιεῖσθαί τι to make light of a thing, Hdt.
light in moving, nimble, Lat. agilis, Hom., Aesch.; ἐλαφρὰ ἡλικία the age of active youth, Xen.; οἱ ἐλαφροί light troops, Lat. levis armatura, Id.
lightminded, thoughtless, Eur.
to make light, lighten, Babr.
the smallest, least, οὐκ ἐλ. Hhymn., Hdt., etc.; ἐλαχίστου λόγου of least account, Id.; περὶ ἐλαχίστου ποιεῖσθαι Plat.
of Time, shortest, δι’ ἐλαχίστου [sc. χρόνου] Thuc.; δι’ ἐλαχίστης βουλῆς with shortest deliberation, Id.
of Number, fewest, Plat.
τὸ ἐλάχιστον, τοὐλάχιστον, at the least, Hdt., Xen., etc.; also ἐλάχιστα, Thuc., Plat.
there is also a new comp. ἐλαχιστότερος, less than the least, NTest.
small, short, little, old epic Positive, whence ἐλάσσων, ἐλάχιστος are formed, Hhymn.: cf. λάχεια.
to wish, long to do a thing, c. inf., Hom: —c. gen. to long for, Id=Hom.: c. acc. to desire, Id=Hom.:—as Pass., νῦν τοι ἐελδέσθω πόλεμος be war now welcome, Il.

entry.etym: only found in epic form ἐέλδωρ, τό,
entry.sense: a wish, longing, desire, Il., Hes.
to take pity on, τινά Hom., Ar.
a kind of owl, Ar.
an elegy, Plut.
a distich consisting of hexameter and pentameter, the metre of the elegy, Thuc.
in pl., ἐλεγεῖα, τά, an elegiac poem, Plat., etc.:—so in sg., Plut.
one who convicts or detects, τῶν ἀποκτεινάντων Antipho.
of persons, fond of cross-questioning or examiningadv. -κῶς, Xen.
proving a wife's fidelity, Anth.
a conviction, NTest.
a song of mourning, a lament: at first without reference to metrical form, later always in alternate hexameters and pentameters, Eur., etc.
reproach, disgrace, Il.
worthy of reproof; of men, cowardly, Il.: —Irreg. Sup. ἐλέγχιστος, Id.

a cross-examining, testing, for purposes of disproof or refutation, ἔχειν ἔλεγχον to admit of disproof, Hdt., Thuc.; ἔλ. διδόναι τοῦ βίου to give an account of one's life, Plat.; εἰς ἔλ. πίπτειν to be convicted, Eur.; οἱ περὶ Παυσανίαν ἔλ. the evidence on which he was convicted, Thuc.
a reproach, disgrace, dishonour, Hom.: of men, κάκ’ ἐλέγχεα base reproaches to your name, Il.
to disgrace, put to shame, μῦθον ἐλ. to treat a speech with contempt, Il.; ἐλ. τινά to put one to shame, Od.
to cross-examine, question, for the purpose of disproving or reproving, to censure, accuse, Hdt., attic; c. acc. et inf. to accuse one of doing, Eur.:—Pass. to be convicted, Hdt., Xen., etc.
of arguments, to bring to the proof, to disprove, confute, Aesch., Dem.:—absol. to bring convincing proof, Hdt.: then generally to prove, Lat. arguere, Thuc.

finding pity, pitied or moving pity, pitiable, piteous, Hom., etc.; ἐλεινὸς εἰσορᾶν piteous to behold, Aesch.; ἐλεινὸν ὁρᾷς thou lookest piteous, Soph.; ἐσθῆτ’ ἐλεινήν Ar.; ποιῶν ἑαυτὸν ὡς ἐλεεινότατον Dem.
shewing pity, pitying, ἐλ. δάκρυον a tear of pity, Od.; οὐδὲν ἐλεεινόν no feeling of pity, Plat.
adv. ἐλεεινῶς, in attic Poets ἐλεινῶς, pitiably, Soph.; neut. pl. ἐλεεινά as adv., Il.
to have pity on, shew mercy upon, c. acc., Od., attic:—Pass. to be pitied, have pity or mercy shewn one, Plat.
absol. to feel pity, Ar.
pity, mercy: a charity, alms (which is a corruption of the word), NTest., etc.
pitiful, merciful, compassionate, Od., Dem.
pity, mercy, Od.
walking the marsh, marsh-dwelling, Aesch.
of the marsh or meadow, ἕλ. δάπεδον the surface of the meads, Ar.
growing or dwelling in the marsh, Aesch., Thuc.
ἐλελεῦ, or doubled ἐλελεῦ ἐλελεῦ, a war-cry, Ar.: generally any cry, Aesch.
to whirl round, Od.
to rally soldiers, Il.: Pass., οἱ δ’ ἐλελίχθησαν Id.
generally, to make to tremble or quake, Id.:—Pass. to tremble, quiver, Id.
Mid. and Pass. to move in coils or spires, of a serpent, Id.
to raise the battle-cry, Xen.: generally, to raise a loud cry, Eur.: —in Mid., of the nightingale, to trill her sad lay, Id.; c. acc., Ἴτυν ἐλελιζομένη trilling her lament for Itys, Ar.
shaking the earth, Soph.
ship-destroying, of Helen, Aesch.
marsh-bred, Il.
piteously, Hes.
a kitchen-table, a board on which meat was cut up, a dresser, Hom.:—also ἐλεόν, τό, Ar.
pity, mercy, compassion, Il., attic; ἔλ. τινος pity for . . , Eur.:—in NTest. also ἔλεος, τό.
an object of compassion, a piteous thing, Eur.
city-destroying, of Helen, Aesch., Eur.
that can be taken or caught, Il.
freedom, liberty, Hdt., Aesch., etc.; δι’ ἐλευθερίας μόλις ἐξῆλθες, i. e. μόλις ἐλευθερώθης, Soph.
licence, Plat.
or ος, η, ον, speaking or acting like a freeman, free-spirited, frank, related to ἐλεύθερος, as Lat. liberalis to liber, Plat., Xen.
freely giving, bountiful, liberal, Id.
of pursuits, fit for a freeman, liberal; τὸ ἐλευθέριον = ἐλευθεριότης, Id.
of appearance, free, noble, Id.
Ζεὺς Ἐλευθέριος Jove the Deliverer, Hdt.
the character of an ἐλευθέριος, liberality, Plat.
having free children, i. e. a free man, Anth.
worthy of a freeman, Plat.

free, opp. to δοῦλος: ἐλεύθερον ἦμαρ the day of freedom, i. e. freedom, Il.; κρητὴρ ἐλεύθερος the cup drunk to freedom, Id.:—of persons, Hdt., attic: —τὸ ἐλ. freedom, Hdt.:—c. gen. free or freed from a thing, Trag.
of things, free, open to all, Xen.
like ἐλευθέριος, fit for a freeman, free, frank, Hdt., attic:—adv., ἐλευθέρως εἰπεῖν Hdt., Soph.
to be free of speech, Aesch., Eur.
bearing himself freely or nobly, of the horse, Xen.

to free, set free, Hdt., Aesch., etc.; ἐλ. τὸν ἔσπλουν to set the entrance free, clear it, Thuc.; ἐλευθεροῖ στόμα he keeps his tongue free, i. e. does not commit himself by speech, Soph.: to free from blame, acquit, τινά Xen.:—Pass. to be set free, Hdt.
c. gen. to set free, loose or release from, Eur.; so, ἐλευθεροῦντες ἐκ δρασμῶν πόδα, i. e. ceasing to flee, Id.
a setting free, Hdt., Thuc.
a liberator, Luc.
to Eleusis, Xen.
of Eleusis, Hhymn., Hdt., etc.
at Eleusis, Andoc., Xen.
from Eleusis, Lys., etc.
Eleusis, an old city of Attica, sacred to Demeter and Proserpine, Hhymn., etc.
a coming:—the Advent of our LORD, NTest.
epic Dep. to cheat with empty hopes, said of the false dreams that come through the ivory gate (ἐλέφας), Od.: generally, to cheat, overreach, Il.
to destroy, Hes.
the commander of a squadron of elephants, Plut.
of ivory, ivory, Lat. eburneus, Ar.
inlaid with ivory, Ar.
ivory-hilted, Luc.
a battle of elephants, Plut.
ivory-footed, Luc.
the elephant, Hdt.
the elephant's tusk, ivory, Il., Hes.
whirling, rolling, Aesch.
a curl, lock of hair, Anth.
a winding, convolution, as of the Labyrinth, Hdt., Xen.
with ever-moving eyelids, quick-glancing, Hhymn.
running in curves, circular, Eur.
of winding or spiral form, Plut.
curved, twisted, wreathed, Hhymn., Soph.; ἑλ. κύτος a wheeled ark, Eur.; σῦριγξ περὶ χεῖλος ἑλικτά moving quickly, Theocr.
metaph. tortuous, Eur.
sc.Ἑλῐκωνιάδες παρθένοι, αἱ, the dwellers on Helicon, the Muses, Hes.: so, Νύμφαι Ἑλικωνίδες, Soph.
Helicon, a hill in Boeotia, Hes.
with rolling eyes, quick-glancing, Il.
to keep holiday, to take rest, be at rest, keep quiet, stand idle, Hdt., Aesch.
c. part. to rest or cease from doing, Id.
with crumpled horns, Anth.
adj. twisted, curved, of oxen, either with twisted, crumpled horns, or rolling as they walk, Hom., etc.:—later, ἕλικα ἀνὰ χλόαν on the tangled grass, Eur.
anything which assumes a spiral shape:
an armlet or ear-ring, Il.
a twist, whirl, convolution, ἕλικες στεροπῆς flashes of forked lightning, Aesch.
the tendril of the vine, Eur.: of ivy, Id.
a curl or lock of hair, Anth.
the coil or spire of a serpent, Eur.
to turn round, to turn a chariot round the doubling-post, Il.; so of the chariot of Day, Aesch., Eur.; ἑλ. κόνιν to roll the eddying dust, Aesch.; ἑλ. δίνας of the Euripus, Eur.; ἑλ. βλέφαρα Id.
of any rapid motion, esp. of a circular kind, ἑλ. πλάταν to ply the oar swiftly, Soph.; ἑλ. πόδα to move the swift foot, Eur.: absol. to dance, Id.
to roll or wind round, as the wool round the distaff, Hdt., Eur.
metaph. to turn in one's mind, revolve, Soph.; ἑλ. λόγους to speak wily words, Eur.
Pass. and Mid. to turn oneself round, turn quick round, turn to bay, Il.; of a serpent, to coil himself, Id.; of a missile, to spin through the air, Id.
to turn hither and thither, go about, Id.:—also, like Lat. versari, to be busy about a thing, Id.
to whirl in the dance, Eur.
Mid. in Act. sense, with a whirl, like a sling, Il.
τὰς κεφαλὰς εἰλίχατο μίτρηισι have their heads rolled round with turbans, Hdt.
whirling the wheel, Aesch.
a creeping plant with yellow flower or fruit, Theocr.
to fester, Aesch.
trailing the robe, with long train, Il.
drawing the hand after it, Anth.
trailing the tunic, with long tunic, Il.
to drag about, tear asunder, Il.: to attempt violence to one, Od.
by dragging or pulling, Hes.
a being carried off, violence suffered, Il.
that which is torn in pieces, a prey, Eur.
one that drags, Anth.
to make wounds or sores: metaph. to rip up old sores, Aeschin.
having power to wound, Aesch.
a wound, Il., attic
a festering wound, ἕλκος ὕδρου the festering bite of a serpent, Il.: of plague-ulcers, Thuc.
metaph. a wound, loss, Aesch., Soph.
to wound sorely, lacerate, Eur.:—metaph., ἑλκ. φρένας οἴκους Id.
one must drag, Plat.
fit for drawing, attractive, Plat.
Dim. of ἕλκος, a slight sore, Ar.
Frequentat. of ἕλκω, to drag about, Il.
to be dragged, Xen.
like a sore, ulcerated, Eur.

to draw, drag, Lat. traho, with a notion of force, ποδὸς ἕλκε began to drag [the dead body] by the foot, Il.; to draw ships down to the sea, Od.; of mules, to draw a chariot, Id.; to draw the plough through the field, Id.
to draw after one, Il.; πέδας ἕλκ. to trail fetters after one, Hdt.
to tear in pieces, Id., Eur.:—Mid., ἕλκεσθαι χαίτας to tear one's hair, Il.
to draw a bow, Hom., etc.
to draw a sword, Soph.; and in Mid., to draw one's sword, Il.
ἕλκ. ἱστία to hoist or haul up the sails, Od.
to hold up scales, so as to poise or balance them, Il.
after Hom., in many ways:
to pull an oar, Hdt.
to drag into court, Ar.: to drag about, esp. with lewd violence, Dem., etc.
to draw or suck up, Hdt.: of persons drinking, to drink in long draughts, quaff, Eur., etc.; ἑλκ. μαστόν to suck the breast, Id.
ἕλκ. βίοτον, ζόην to drag out a weary life, Id.: to drag on, prolong tediously, Hdt.: κόρδακα ἑλκύσαι to dance in long, measured steps, Ar.
to draw to oneself, attract, Hdt., etc.
ἕλκ. σταθμόν to draw down the balance, i. e. to weigh so much, Id.; absol., τὸ δ’ ἂν ἑλκύσηι whatever it weigh, Id.
ἑλκύσαι πλίνθους, like Lat. ducere, to make bricks, Id.
Mid. to draw to oneself, amass riches, Theogn.
ulceration, Thuc.
Pass. to gain distinction, Thuc.
to shine upon, to illuminate:— metaph. in Mid. to distinguish oneself, gain glory in or with a thing, Hdt.
the chief judges at the Olympic games, Pind.
at Sparta, a court-martial to try disputes among the allied troops, Xen.
Hellas, a city of Thessaly, founded by Hellen, Il.
that part of Thessaly in which the Myrmidons dwelt, also called Phthiotis, Hom.
Northern Greece, as opp. to Peloponnesus, Od.
later, the name for Greece, from the South to Epirus and Thessaly inclusively, Hes., Hdt., etc.
as adj. with a fem. Subst. Hellenic, Greek, Id., etc.
hellebore, Lat. veratrum, a plant used as a specific for madness, πῖθ’ ἑλλέβορον drink hellebore, i. e. you are mad, Ar.
the band for binding corn-sheaves, Il.
to leave in, leave behind, Eur.
to leave out, leave undone, Lat. omitto, Soph., etc.
intr. to fall short, fail, Hhymn., Soph.; τὸ ἐλλεῖπον τῆς ἐπιστήμης deficiency of knowledge, Thuc.
c. gen. rei, like δέω, to be in want of, fall short of, lack, Aesch., Thuc.; πολλοῦ ἐλλείπω I am far from it, Aesch.
c. gen. pers. to be inferior to, Plat.
foll. by μή c. inf., τί γὰρ ἐλλ. μὴ παραπαίειν; in what does he fall short of madness? Aesch.
with a part., οὐκ ἐλλείπει εὐχαριστῶν he fails not to give thanks, ap. Dem.
of things, to be wanting or lacking to . . , c. dat., Xen.
Pass. to be left behind in a race, Soph.: to be surpassed, Xen.
to be left wanting, to fail, Id.
commonly talked of, Hdt.
to speak Greek, Plat.:—Pass., Ἑλληνισθῆναι τὴν γλῶσσαν to be made Greeks in language by another, Thuc.
Hellenic, Greek, Hdt., attic
τὸ Ἑλληνικόν the Greeks collectively, Hdt.; the Greek soldiery, Xen.
τὰ Ἑλληνικά the history of Grecian affairs, Thuc.
like the Greeks, Eur., Ar.:—adv. -κῶς, in Greek fashion, Hdt.
Ἑλλήνιον, τό, the temple of the Hellenes in Egypt, Id.
= Ἑλλάς, Eur.
fem. of Ἕλλην, attic.
Ἑλληνίς (v. sub. γυνή) a Grecian woman, Eur.
one who uses the Greek language; i. e., in NTest., a Hellenist, a Greek-Jew.
in Greek fashion, Luc.; Ἑλλ. ξυνιέναι to understand Greek, Xen.
the stewards of Greece, i. e. officers appointed by Athens B. C. 477 to levy the contributions paid by the Greek states towards the Persian war, Thuc.
Hellen, son of Deucalion, Hes.
the Ἕλληνες of Hom. are the Thessalian tribe of which Hellen was the reputed chief (cf. Ἑλλάς 1), Il.
later, Ἕλληνες was the regul. name for Greeks, opp. to βάρβαροι, Hdt., etc.
later still, of Gentiles, Opp. to Jews, NTest.
as adj. = Ἑλληνικός, Thuc., etc.:—even with a fem. Subst., Aesch., Eur.
of the Hellespont, Xen., Ἑλλησπόντιος, η, ον, Hdt., Xen.
a wind blowing from the Hellespont, i. e. from the N. E., Hdt.
the Hellespont or sea of Helle (daughter of Athamas, who was drowned therein), now the Dardanelles, Hom., Hdt., etc.
a collector of harbour-dues, Dem.

pass. wanting, lacking, defective, Thuc., etc.; also c. dat.; τὸ μὴ ἐπιχειρούμενον ἀεὶ ἐλλιπὲς ἦν τῆς δοκήσεως whatever was not attempted was so much lost of their reckoning, Thuc.; τὸ ἐλλιπές defect, failure, Id.
that which is in the lobe of the ear, an earring, Lat. inauris, Luc.
to reckon in, to impute, NTest.
held in account (ἐν λόγῳ), notable, famous, Hdt., Plat.
to fish, Theocr.
a young deer, fawn, Od.
to lie in ambush, Eur.: c. acc. to lie in wait for, Plut.
mute, of fish, Hes.
a lamp-wick, Hdt.
a drawing, dragging, trailing, Plat.
low ground by rivers, a marsh-meadow, Hom., Hdt., etc.
giver of hope, Anth.
to hope for, look for, expect, τι Aesch., etc.: c. inf. fut. or aor. to hope or expect that, Hdt., attic
of evils, to look for, fear, Soph., etc.
with inf. pres. it means little more than to think, deem, suppose, believe that, Hdt., attic
c. dat. to hope in . . , τῆι τύχηι Thuc.; εἴς τινα, ἐπί τινα NTest.

hope, expectation, Od.;in pl., πολλῶν ῥαγεισῶν ἐλπίδων after the wreck of many hopes, Aesch.;—with gen. both of subject and object, Πελοποννησίων τὴν ἐλπίδα τοῦ ναυτικοῦ the hope of the P. in their navy, Thuc.
the object of hope, a hope, Ὀρέστης, ἐλπὶς δόμων Aesch.
apprehension, fear, Id.
to make to hope, πάντας ἔλπει feeds all with hope, Od.
Mid. to hope or expect, indulge hope, Hom., Hdt.; like attic ἐλπίζω.
to expect anxiously, to fear, Hom., Hdt.
generally, to think, deem, suppose, Il.
the tree or stock of the plough, on which the share was fixed, Lat. dentale, Hes.
the case of a spear, Ar.
the body as the case of the soul, Plat. ap. Luc.
a place for holding water, a reservoir, Hdt.

to roll round (cf. εἰλύω):— only in aor1 pass. ἐπὶ γαῖαν ἐλύσθη rolled to the ground, Il.; προπάροιθε ποδῶν Ἀχιλῆος ἐλυσθείς rolled up, crouching before Achilles' feet, Id.; ὑπὸ γαστέρ’ ἐλυσθείς huddled under [the ram's] belly, Od.
= εἰλύω, to wrap up, cover, Apoll.

entry.etym: only in nom. and acc. sg. and pl.
entry.sense: booty, spoil, prey, of unburied corpses, Hom.
in pl., Πατρόκλοιο ἕλωρα penalty for the slaughter of Patroclus, Il.
Reflexive Pronoun of first person, of me, of myself: only used in gen., dat., and acc. sg., Hom., etc.
on foot, by land, Il.
surface, area.

entry.note: fut. -βήσομαι perf. -βέβηκα Homeric part. -βεβαώς aor2 ἐνέβην epic 3rd sg. ἔμβη dual ἔμβητον
entry.sense: to step in, μή τις ἐμβήῃ let none step in (to interfere), Il.
to go on, go quickly, ἔμβητον, says Antilochus to his horses, Id.; ἔμβα advance, Eur.
to step into a ship, embark, go on board, Hom., etc.:—perf. to be mounted on, ἐμβεβαὼς ἵπποισι Il.; also c. acc., Ἴλιον ἐμβεβώς Eur.
to step upon, c. dat., Od., Aesch.
to enter upon, εἰς κίνδυνον Xen.; c. acc., ἐμβ. κέλευθον Eur., Plat.
rarely c. gen. to step upon, γῆς ὅρων Soph.
in Poets, with acc. of the instrument of motion (cf. βαίνω II. 3), ἐμβήσει (2nd sg.) πόδα Eur.
Causal in aor1 ἐνέβησα, to make to step in, put in, Od., Eur.; ἐμβῆσαί τινα εἰς φροντίδα to make him anxious, Hdt.
to throw in, put in, Il., etc.; ἐμβ. τινὰ εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον to throw one into prison, Dem.; ἔμβαλλε χεῖρα δεξιάν, as a pledge of good faith, Soph.
ἐμβ. τινί τι θυμῷ to put it into his mind, Hom.; so, ἐμβ. ἵμερον, μένος τινί Id.; βουλὴν ἐμβ. περί τινος to give one counsel about a thing, Xen.
to throw at, upon or against, νηῒ κεραυνόν Od.; ἐμβ. πληγάς to inflict stripes, Xen.; ἐμβ. πῦρ to apply it, Thuc.:— metaph., ἐμβ. φόβον τινί to strike fear into him, Lat. incutere timorem, Hdt.
intr. (sub. στρατόν) to make an inroad or invasion, Id.
generally to break, burst, rush in, Aeschin.; ἐμβάλωμεν εἰς ἄλλον λόγον Eur.
to strike a ship with the ram, to charge or ram it, c. dat., Hdt., Thuc.
κώπῃ ἐμβάλλειν (sub. χεῖρας) to lay oneself to the oar, Lat. incumbere remis, Od.; and ἐμβάλλειν alone, to lay to, pull hard, Ar.
of a river, to empty itself, Plat.
