Mid. to throw in what is one's own, Dem.
metaph., ἐμβάλλεσθαί τι θυμῷ to lay it to heart, consider it, Il.
c. gen., ἐμβάλεσθε τῶν λαγῴων fall upon the hare's flesh, Ar.
Pass. of ships, to charge, Thuc.
sauce, soup, Xen.
to dip in, Ar.
that on which one goes or steps, ἔμβασις ποδός, i. e. a shoe, Aesch.
the foot, hoof, Eur.
a bath, Anth.
pot-visiter, name of a mouse in Batr.
to step in or on, to frequent, haunt a place, c. acc., of tutelary gods, Aesch., etc.:—c. gen., simply, to set foot upon, Soph.
ἐμβατ. κλήρους to enter on, come into possession of, Eur.; so, ἐμβ. εἴς τι Dem.
a felt-shoe, Hdt., Ar.
to be king in or among others, c. dat., Hom.
of or for marching in, ἐμβ. παιάν a march, Plut.
a half-boot of felt, Xen.
a flat vessel for sauces, Hdt.
to set in or on, Plat.:— to put on board ship, cause to embark, Thuc., Xen.
to lead to a thing, Eur., Dem.
a looking straight at, Xen.
to look in the face, look at, τινι or εἴς τινα Plat.; absol., Xen.
an insertion, τὸ εἰς τὸν σίδηρον ἔμβλ. the shaft fitted into the spear-head, Plut.
to call upon, shout to, τινί Xen.; absol., Thuc.
anything put in: a dibble for setting plants, Anth.
a putting into its place, insertion of a letter, Plat.
intr. a breaking in, inroad into an enemy's country, foray, Xen.
an assault, attack, charge, Eur.:—esp. the charge made by one ship upon another, Aesch., Thuc.; ἐμβολαῖς χαλκόστομοις with shocks of brasen beaks, Aesch.
the stroke of a missile, Eur.
a way into, entrance, pass, Hdt., Xen.
the head of a battering-ram, Thuc.
inserted, intercalated, Hdt.
anything pointed so as to be easily thrust in: τῆς χώρης ἔμβολον a tongue of land, Hdt.
in ships of war, the beak or ram of a ship of war, masc. in Hdt.; neut. in Thuc.
οἱ ἔμβολοι the rostra of the Roman forum, Plut.
the wedge-shaped order of battle, Lat. cuneus, neut. in Xen.
a bolt, bar, neut., Eur.
to dwell on, τινί Luc.
adv. in brief, shortly, Ar., Plat.
boy-like, Anth.
weighty, Hdt., Plat.
metaph., like Lat. gravis, weighty, grave, dignified, Plut.
in bad sense, heavy, grievous, Aesch.
Dep. c. aor. mid. et pass., to snort in, of horses, Aesch.
of persons, to be deeply moved, NTest.
c. dat. pers. to admonish urgently, rebuke, Id.
Pass. to be stricken by lightning, Xen.
thunderstruck, stupefied, stupid, Lat. attonitus, Xen., Dem.
dwelling in sea-weed, Anth.
a young one, Od.
an embryo, Lat. foetus, Aesch.
at the bottom of the sea, Anth.
to stuff in, stop with a thing, Ar.
one who uses emetics, like the Roman gourmands, Plut.
vomiting, Lat. vomitus, Hdt.
Dep. to be mad at a thing, c. dat., NTest.
to vomit, throw up, Il., Hdt., etc.: absol. to vomit, to be sick, Hdt., attic; ἐμ. πτίλωι to make oneself sick with a feather, Ar.
woolly, fleecy, Luc.
ἐν μανίᾳ ὤν, in madness, frantic, raving, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
quickly, readily, hastily, Hom.
entry.etym: Perh. from μαπέειν, μάρπτω, to seize eagerly.

entry.sense: Dep. to knead bread in, Ar.
Dep. to fight a battle in, Hdt.
to smile or be glad at, Xen.
harmony: a stately Tragic dance, Plat.: the tune of this dance, Hdt.
to exercise or train in a thing, Plat.
an exercise, a practice, Anth.
sounding in unison, in tune or time, harmonious, Plut.
metaph., of persons, in tune or harmony, orderly, suitable, proper, Plat.:— graceful, elegant, Id.
adv. -λῶς, ionic -έως, harmoniously, suitably, decorously, Simon. Plat.
in eager haste, eager, of persons, Il.
to be lost in passion, Soph.
abiding in: neut. ἐμμενές as adv., ἐμμενὲς αἰεί unceasing ever, Hom.:—so ἐμμενέως, Hes.
to abide in a place, Thuc.
to abide by, stand by, cleave to, be true to one's word, oath, etc., c. dat., Hdt., attic: also, ἐμμ. ἐν σπονδαῖς Thuc.:—absol. to stand fast, be faithful, Eur.
of things, to stand fast, hold good, be fixed, Aesch., etc.
fit measure, proportion, Plat.
in measure, proportioned, suitable, moderate, Plat.
in metre, metrical, Id.
proportion, fitness, Aristaen.
in a month, done or paid every month, monthly, Soph., Theocr.
with pith in it, Theocr.
Pass. to be mixed or mingled in, Aesch.
intr. in Act. to encounter, c. dat., Soph.
in pay, in receipt of pay, hired, Thuc.
an abiding by, cleaving to, τινος Plat.
abiding by, steadfast, Xen.; ἔμμ. τινι abiding by a thing, Id.
partaking in, endued with a thing, c. gen., Od.
（μόρος) fortunate, Anth.
in bodily form, Plut.
needing to be stopped with lint: metaph., ἔμμοτον τῶνδ’ ἄκος a cure to heal these wounds, Aesch.
toilsome, βίοτος Eur.
to initiate in: Pass., μῶν ἐνεμυήθης δῆτ’ ἐν αὐτῷ τὰ μεγάλα; what, were you initiated at the great mysteries in that shabby coat Ar.

possess. Pron. of first pers., mine, Lat. meus, Hom., etc.; by crasis with the Art., οὑμός, τοὐμόν, τοὐμοῦ, τὠμῷ, τἀμάto strengthen the possessive notion, ἐμὸν αὐτοῦ mine own, Il.; τὸν ἐμὸν αὐτοῦ βίον Ar.
objectively, to me, relating to me, against me, ἐμὴ ἀγγελίη Hom.; τὴν ἐμὴν αἰδῶ respect for me, Aesch.; αἱ ἐμαὶ διαβολαί slanders against me, Thuc.; τοὐμὸν αἷμα πατρός his blood shed by me, Soph.

τὸ ἐμόν, τὰ ἐμά my property, Ar., etc.:—but also, τὰ ἐμά or τὸ ἐμόν, my part, my affairs, my interest, οὕτω τὸ ἐμὸν ἔχει things stand thus with me, Hdt.; ἔρρει τἀμά Xen.;—hence periphr. for ἐγώ or ἐμέ, Soph.; or absol., τό γε ἐμόν, τὸ μὲν ἐμόν, for my part, as far as concerns me, Hdt., etc.
ἡ ἐμὴ (sub. γῆ) my country, Thuc.
Dep. to busy oneself about, take heed of, care for a thing, c.gen., Hom.; once c. acc. pers., Il.
in a state of emotion, much affected by or at a thing, Plut.
mockery, NTest.
to mock at, mock, Lat. illudere, τινί Hdt.: absol., Soph.
to sport in or on a place, c. dat., Eur.
a mocker, deceiver, NTest.
possessed of or practised in a thing, c. gen., Od.
bursting in, sudden, Aesch.
to strike in, stamp, emboss, Anth.
intr. to burst in upon, c. dat., Soph.
to close by stuffing in or caulking, Hdt.
Pass. to be entangled in, Hdt.: absol., ἐμπαλασσόμενοι entangled one with another, Thuc.
adv., in attic and Prose often with the Art., τὸ ἔμπαλιν or τοὔμπαλιν, τὰ ἔμπαλιν or τἄμπαλιν, backwards, back, Hhymn., Hes., etc.
contrariwise, the opposite way, ἐκ τοὔμπαλιν from the opposite side, Thuc.
c. gen. contrary to, Hdt.; τοὔμπ. οὗ βούλονται Xen.
to hold assemblies in, Plut.
to give into another's hands, put into his power to do, c. inf., Thuc.
to behave like one drunken, Luc.
notwithstanding, nevertheless, Hom.; with a negat., not at all, Id.; after a part. with περ, like ὅμως, πίνοντά περ ἔμπης, busy though he was with drinking, Il.:—so in Trag., at any rate, yet.
to sprinkle in or on, Plat.: metaph. to weave as patterns in a web of cloth, Il.
to walk in or into a place, enter, c. acc., Aesch.
to abide by one's oath, Hdt., Xen.
in the ground, firm-set, steadfast, Hom.; of events, sure and certain, Od.
of Time, lasting, continual, Hom.

neut. ἔμπεδον as adv., μένειν ἔμπεδον to stand fast, Il.; θέειν ἔμπεδον to run on and on, run without resting, Id.; strenghd., ἔμπεδον αἰέν Id.:—so in pl., τίκτει δ’ ἔμπεδα μῆλα the flocks bring forth without fail, Od.:—also in attic Poets, of a surety, Soph.; but more often ἐμπέδως, Aesch., Soph.
to fix in the earth: generally, to make firm and fast, establish, Eur., Xen.
experience, Eur., Thuc., etc.
c. gen. rei, experience in, acquaintance with, Thuc., etc.; also, ἐμπ. περί τι Xen.

experienced or practised in a thing, acquainted with it, c. gen., Hdt., attic:—absol., οἱ ἔμπειροι the experienced, Soph., Plat., etc.; ϝαυσὶν ἐμπείροις with ships proved by use, Thuc.:— τὸ ἐμπειρότερον αὐτῶν their greater experience, Id.
adv., ἐμπείρως τινὸς ἔχειν to know a thing by experience, by its issue, Xen.
near, hard by, c. dat., Hes.
to bring near, Hes.:—Pass. to come near, approach, c. gen., Soph.
intr. in Act., like Pass. to approach, c. dat., Hhymn., Soph.
skilled in the use of a thing, c. gen., Anth.; also ἐμπείρᾰμος, Id.
to walk about in, Luc.:— absol. to walk about, Id.
a garment fastened with a brooch on the shoulder, Theocr.
to unfold and spread in or on, Xen.
to fix or plant in, c. dat., Il.:—Pass., with perf. and plup. act. to be fixed or stuck in, to stick in, τινί or ἔν τινι Ar.
to jump upon a person, c. dat., Hdt.
to leap in or into, absol. in aor1 part. ἐμπηδήσας, eagerly, greedily, Luc.
crippled, maimed, Hdt.
Mid. or Pass. to be bitter against a person, c. dat., Hdt.
to drink in, drink greedily, Eur., etc.; ἐμπ. τοῦ αἵματος to drink greedily of the blood, Hdt.
absol. to drink one's fill, Theogn., Xen.

entry.note: imperf. mid. ἐνεπιμπλάμην imperat. ἐμπίπληθι attic ἐμπίπλη fut. ἐμπλήσω perf. ἐμπέπληκα Pass., aor1 ἐνεπλήσθην epic aor2 ἐμπλήμην
entry.sense: to fill quite full, Od., Xen.
c. gen. to fill full of a thing, Hom., etc.
Mid. to fill for oneself or what is one's own, ἐμπλήσατο νηδύν Od.; μένεος ἐμπλήσατο θυμόν he filled his heart with rage, Il.

Pass. to be filled full of a thing, c. gen., Hom.:—metaph., υἷος ἐνιπλησθῆναι to take my fill of my son, i. e. to sate myself with looking on him, Od.; so c. part. to be satiated with doing, Eur., Xen.
c. dat., καρπῷ ἐμπ. to be filled with . . , Hdt.
absol. to eat one's fill, Id., etc.

entry.note: not ἐμπίμπρημι inf. ἐμπιπρᾶν imperf. ἐνεπίμπρων 3rd pl. -πίμπρασαν fut. ἐμπρήσω aor1 ἐνέπρησα Pass., fut. ἐμπεπρήσομαι fut. ἐμπρήσομαι aor1 ἐνεπρήσθην perf. ἐμπέπρησμαι
entry.etym: inf. ἐμπιπρᾶν as if from ἐμπιπράω
Pass., fut. ἐμπρήσομαι in mid. form
entry.sense: to kindle, burn, set on fire, Il., Hdt., Soph.; also c. gen., πυρὸς νῆας ἐνιπρῆσαι to burn them by force of fire, Il.:—Pass. to be on fire, Hdt.
to fall in or upon or into, c. dat., Hom., etc.
to fall upon, attack, Id.; also ἐμπ. εἰς . . , Hdt., etc.; rarely c. acc., Soph., Eur.
to light or chance upon a thing, to fall in with, τινί Hdt., etc.; more commonly ἐμπ. εἰς . . , Lat. incidere in . . , Soph., etc.
to break in, burst in or into, c. dat., Id., etc.; aor2 part. ἐμπεσών violently, Hdt.
ἐμπίτνω poet. for ἐμπίπτω
to fall upon, τινί Aesch., Soph.
a mosquito, gnat, Lat. culex, Ar.
to entrust, τινί τι Plut.:—Pass. to be entrusted with, τι Luc.
to plaster up, Hdt.

entry.note: epic ἐνι-πλέκω fut. ξω Pass., aor2 ἐνεπλάκην part. ἐμπλᾰκείς
entry.sense: to plait or weave in, Lat. implicare, χεῖρα ἐμπλ. to entwine one's hand in another's clothes, so as to hold him, Eur.:—Pass. to be entangled in a thing, c. dat., Soph., Eur.
quite full of a thing, Od., Hdt., etc.
to sail in, πλοίῳ Hdt.: absol., οἱ ἐμπλέοντες the crews, Thuc.
madly, rashly, Od.
easily scared, Plut.
stunned, amazed, stupefied, Lat. attonitus, Xen., Plut.
unstable, capricious, Soph., Eur.
adv. -τως, rashly; τὸ ἐμπλήκτως ὀξύ startling rapidity of action, Thuc.
near, next, close by, c. gen., Il.
besides, except, c. gen., Archil.
amazement, stupidity, Aeschin.
to strike against, fall upon or into, c. dat., Hom.
to be filled with, τινός Plat.
to blow or breathe upon, c. dat., Il., Eur.
absol. to breathe, live, be alive, Aesch., Soph., Plat., etc.; βραχὺν βίοτον ἐμπνέων ἔτι Eur.
c. gen. to breathe of, ἐμπν. φόνου, Lat. caedem spirare, NTest.
trans. to blow into, ἱστίον ἐμπν. to swell the sail, Hhymn.
to breathe into, inspire, μένος or θάρσος τινί Hom.
inbreathing, inspiration, Luc.
with the breath in one, breathing, alive, Hdt., attic
to put the feet in bonds, to fetter, Hdt.: —Pass., ἐμπεποδισμένος τοὺς πόδας Id.
generally, to hinder, thwart, impede, Lat. impedire, τινά Ar., Xen.; πρός τι in a thing, Isocr.:—Pass., Soph.
ὥσπερ ἐμποδίζων ἰσχάδας like one stringing figs or treading figs flat for packing, Ar.
at one's feet, coming in the way, meeting, ap. Plut.
in the way, impeding, c. dat. pers., Eur.:—c. gen. rei, ἐμπ. εἶναι εἰρήνης Thuc.
= ἐν ποσὶν ὤν, but formed by anal. to ἐκποδών:— at the feet, in the way, in one's path, Hdt., etc.

in one's way, i. e. presenting an hindrance, ἐμπ. εἶναι to be in the way, Aesch.; ἐμπ. στῆναί τινι Id.; κεῖσθαι Eur.:—c. inf., ἐμπ. εἶναι τῷ ποιεῖν Xen.; ἐμπ. εἶναι or γίγνεσθαί τινι μὴ πράττειν to prevent a person's doing, Thuc., etc.:— τὸ ἐμπ. the hindrance, obstacle, Hdt.
to make in, Il.:—Pass., χελιδὼν ἐμπεποιημένη introduced by the poet's art, Ar.
to foist in, interpolate, Hdt.
to produce or create in, of states of mind, ἐπιθυμίαν τοῖς Ἀθηναίοις ἐμπ. Thuc.; κακόν τι ἐμπ. ταῖς ψυχαῖς Plat.
of conditions, to introduce, produce, cause, φθόρον, στάσιν Thuc.
concerned in traffic, Ar.
to get by barter or traffic, earn, Soph., Xen.:—Mid., βίοτον πολὺν ἐμπολόωντο they were getting much substance by traffic, Od.
to deal or traffic in a thing, to purchase, buy, Soph.:—metaph., ἐμπ. τὴν ἐμὴν φρένα to make profit of my mind, by dealing with me, Id.
absol. to deal as a merchant, traffic, Ar.:—metaph., ἠμποληκὼς τὰ πλεῖστ’ ἀμείνονα having dealt in most things with success, Aesch.
pertaining to war, Hdt.
a merchant, trafficker, Anth.
matter of traffic, the freight of a ship, merchandise, Soph. (metaph.), Eur.
gain made by traffic, Theophr.
merchandise, Ar., Xen.
traffic, purchase, Eur., Xen.
bought, οὑμπολητὸς Σισύφου Λαερτίῳ the son of Sisyphus bought by or palmed off upon Laertes, Soph.
in the city or state: ὁ ἔμπ. τινι one's fellow-citizen, Soph.
to be one of a state, to be a citizen, hold civil rights, Thuc.
to swagger in procession, Luc.
merchandise, Xen.
Dep.
to travel, Soph.
to travel for traffic, to be a merchant, to trade, traffic, Thuc.
c. acc. rei, to import, Luc.
c. acc. pers. to make gain of, to overreach, NTest.
one must go or tramp, Ar.
commerce, trade, traffic, Hes., etc.
a trade or business, NTest., Anth.
merchandise, Xen., Dem.
commercial, mercantile, Stesich.; ἐμπ. τέχνη = ἐμπορία, Plat.; ἐμπ. δίκαι mercantile actions, Dem.; τὰ ἐμπ. χρήματα money to be used in trade, Id.
imported, foreign, Ar.
Lat. emporium, a trading-place, mart, factory, such as were formed by the Phoenicians and Carthaginians, Hdt., etc.
τὸ ἐμπ., at Athens, the Exchange, where the merchants resorted, Dem.
ἐμπόρια, τά, merchandise, Xen.
one who goes on shipboard as a passenger, Lat. vector, Od.
= ὁ ἐν πόρῳ ὤν, any one on a journey, a traveller, wanderer, Trag.
a merchant, trader, Lat. mercator, Hdt., etc.:—metaph., ἔμπορος βίου a trafficker in life, Eur.
to fasten with a broochPass., εἵματα ἐνεπορπέατο (ionic for -ηντο) they wore garments fastened with a brooch, Hdt.
Empusa, a hobgoblin assuming various shapes, Ar.
practicableadv. -τως, Plut.
to be conspicuous in, c. dat., Aesch.; Βάκχαις among them, Ar.
to be conspicuous or famous for a thing, Trag.
to suit, τινί Plut.
to blow up, inflate, Il.:—Pass., ἐμπεπρημένη ὗς a bloated sow, Ar.
= ἐμπίπρημι, to burn, Il.
a conflagration, Hdt.
to saw into, to gnash the teeth together, Luc.
within the stated time, Luc.
adv.:
of Place, before, in front, Hdt., Xen.: τὸ and τὰ ἔμπροσθεν the front, fore-side, Hdt., etc.; εἰς τὸ ἔμπ. forwards, Id.; ἐκ τοῦ ἔμπρ. opposite, Xen.
of Time, before, earlier, of old, Plat.
as prep. with gen. before, in front of:
of Place, ἐμπρ. αὐτῆς (sc. τῆς νηός) Hdt.
of Time, ἔμπρ. ταύτης (sc. τῆς γνώμης) Id.
fore, front, of an animal's feet, Hdt., Xen.
to spit into, ἐς ποταμόν Hdt.
to spit upon, NTest.
to wrap up inPass., νόος οἱ ἐμπεπύκασται his mind is veiled, dark, Mosch.
suppurating, Soph.
to roast in or on the fire, Ar.
made for standing on the fire, of a tripod, Il.
in the fire, ἡ ἔμπ. τέχνη the work of the fire, the forge, Plat.; also the art of divining by fire, Eur.
exposed to fire or sun, scorched, burnt, Id.
burning, fiery, of the sun, Anth.
lighted, of a lamp, Id.
of or for a burnt-offering, Eur.
as Subst., ἔμπυρα (sc. ἱερά), τά, burnt sacrifices, Soph., Eur.

entry.etym: inf. of aor2 ἐνέφαγον, no pres. ἐνεσθίω being in use
entry.sense: to eat hastily, Xen.
to eat in or upon, Luc.
to let a thing be seen in a mirror, Plat.:— to exhibit, display, Plut., etc.
Pass., with fut. mid. to be seen in a mirror, to be reflected, Plat., Xen.
to become visible, Id.
shewing in itself, reflecting, of mirrors, Plat.

visible to the eye, manifest, esp. of the gods appearing bodily among men, Soph., etc.; so, ἐμφανῆ τινα ἰδεῖν to see him bodily, Id.:—of things, τἀμφανῆ κρύπτειν Id.; ἐμφ. τεκμήρια visible proofs, Id.; τὰ ἐμφ. κτήματα the actual property, Xen.
ποιεῖν τι ἐμφανές to do it in public, Lat. in propatulo, Hdt.; τὸ ἐμφ. opp. to τὸ μέλλον, Thuc.; εἰς τοὐμφανὲς ἰέναι to come into light, Xen.
open, actual, palpable, Ar., Thuc., etc.
manifest, well-known, τὰ ἐμφανῆ Hdt.
adv. -νῶς, ionic -νέως, visibly, openly, Lat. palam, Id., Aesch., etc.; openly, i. e. not secretly or treacherously, Soph.; οὐ λόγοις, ἀλλ’ ἐμφανῶς but really, Ar.
so in neut. adj., ἐξ ἐμφανέος or ἐκ τοῦ ἐμφ., Hdt.; ἐν τῷ ἐμφανεῖ Thuc.
to make manifest, exhibit, ἐμφ. τινὰ ἐπίορκον, φίλον to represent him as . . , Xen.:— Pass. to become visible, NTest.
to make clear or plain, τινί τι Xen.
Pass. to feed in a place, c. dat., Mosch.
likeness, Plut.
answering to, resembling, τινί, Hdt., attic: cf. προσφερής.
to bear or bring in, cf. ἐμφορέω.
ἐνεφέρετο an account was given, Not. ad Polyb.
to fly in or into, Luc.
to be fond of dwelling in, to dwell in, τῇ μνήμῃ Luc.
to kindle in, τινί Anth.
with fire in it, πέτρος Anth.
terrible, Lat. formidolosus, Soph.
Pass. to have the mouth-band on, Ar.
Pass. to be borne about in or on, c. dat., Od.
to pour in, ἄκρατον Diod.:— Mid. and Pass. to take one's fill or make much use of a thing, c. gen., Hdt., Plut.
metaph. to put upon, inflict on, ἐμφορεῖν πληγάς τινι Id.
to object to, throw in one's teeth, Soph.
to block up, Thuc.
to keep guard in a place, Thuc.
on guard in a place; οἱ ἔμφρουροι the garrison, Xen.
pass. garrisoned, Dem.
in one's mind or senses, Aesch., Soph.
alive, Id.
rational, intelligent, Xen., Plat.
sensible, shrewd, prudent, Theogn., Soph., etc.
ἐμφύλιοι, kinsfolk, Soph.; αἷμ’ ἐμφύλιον Id.; γῆ ἐμφύλιος one's native land, Id.
in one's tribe, Ἄρης ἐμφύλιος Aesch.; μάχη Theocr.
of the same tribe or race, Od.
in one's tribe, ἔμφ. στάσις civil strife, Hdt.
to blow in: to play the flute, Ar.
to implant, instil into, Xen.
implanted, innate, natural, Hdt., attic
to implant, τί τινι Od., Xen.
Pass., with perf. ἐμπέφῡκα and aor2 ἐνέφῡν:

to grow in or on, c. dat., ὅθι τρίχες κρανίῳ ἐμπεφύασι (epic for ἐμπεφύκασι) Il.:—of qualities, φθόνος ἐμφύεται ἀνθρώπῳ is implanted in him, Hdt.; οὐδεὶς χαρακτὴρ ἐμπέφυκε σώματι no mark is set by nature on the body, Eur.
to be rooted in, cling closely, ὣς ἔχετ’ ἐμπεφῠυῖα (epic for ἐμπεφῡκυῖα) she hung on clinging, Il.; ἔφυν ἐν χερσί clung to his hand, Od.; ἐμφὺς ὡς βδέλλα clinging like a leech, Theocr.
loud of voice, Xen.
sounding, Anth.
having life in one, alive, living, Hdt., attic
of a speech, animated, Luc.
to animate, Anth.
Lat. in.
PREP. WITH DAT.:
OF PLACE
in, ἐν νήσῳ, ἐν Τροίῃ, etc., Hom., etc.:—elliptic, ἐν Ἀλκινόοιο (sc. οἴκῳ) Od.; εἰν Ἀΐδαο Il.; ἐν παιδοτρίβου at the school of the training master, Ar.
in, upon, ἐν οὔρεσι Hom., etc.
in the number of, amongst, ἐν Δαναοῖς, etc., Hom.; and with Verbs of ruling, ἄρχειν, ἀνάσσειν ἐν πολλοῖς to be first or lord among many, i. e. over them, Id.; cf. ὁ, τό B. III. 3.
in one's hands, within one's reach or power, Lat. penes, Hom., etc.; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν Soph.; ἐν τῷ θεῷ τὸ τέλος ἦν Dem.
in respect of, ἐν γήρᾳ in point of age, Soph.
when ἐν is used with Verbs of motion, where we use the prep. into, the construction is called pregnant, πίπτειν ἐν κονίῃσι to fall [to the dust and lie] in it; οἶνον ἔχευεν ἐν δέπαϊ Od., etc.
OF THE STATE, CONDITION, POSITION, in which one is:
of outward circumstances, ἐν πολέμῳ, etc., Hom.; ἐν λόγοις εἶναι to be engaged in oratory, Plat.; οἱ ἐν τοῖς πράγμασι ministers of state, Thuc.; οἱ ἐν τέλει the magistrates, Id.

of inward states, of feeling, etc., ἐν φιλότητι Il.; ἐν φόβῳ εἶναι to be in fear, ἐν αἰσχύνῃ, etc.; also, ἐν ὀργῇ ἔχειν τινά to make him the object of one's anger, Thuc.; ἐν αἰτίᾳ ἔχειν τινά to blame him, Hdt.
often with a neut. adj., ἐν βραχεῖ = βραχέως, Soph.; ἐν τάχει = ταχέως, Id.; ἐν ἐλαφρῷ ποιεῖσθαι Hdt.; ἐν ἴσῳ = ἴσως, Thuc.

OF THE INSTRUMENT, MEANS or MANNER, in or with, ἐν πυρὶ πρῆσαι Il.; ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς or ἐν ὄμμασιν ὁρᾶν have the object in one's eye, Lat. in oculis, Hom.; ἐν λιταῖς by prayers, ἐν δόλῳ by deceit, Aesch., etc.
OF TIME, in, in the course of, ὥρῃ ἐν εἰαρινῇ Il.; ἐν ἡμέρᾳ, ἐν νυκτί Hdt., attic; ἐν ᾧ (sc. χρόνῳ), while, Hdt.:— ἐν ταῖς σπονδαῖς in the time of the truce, Xen.
in, within, ἐν ἔτεσι πεντήκοντα Thuc.; ἐν τρισὶ μησί Xen.
WITHOUT CASE, AS ADVERB, in the phrase ἐν δέ . . :
and therein, Hom.
and among them, Il.
and besides, moreover, Hom., Soph.
IN COMPOS.:
with Verbs, the prep. retains its sense of being in or at a place, etc., c. dat., or foll. by εἰς or ἐν.
with Adjs., it qualifies, as in ἔμπικρος, rather better; or expresses the possession of a quality, as in ἔναιμος, with blood in it, ἔμφωνος with a voice.
ἐν becomes ἐμ- before the labials β μ π φ ψ; ἐγ- before the gutturals γ κ ξ χ; ἐλ- before λ; and in a few words ἐρ- before ρ.
Pass. to be conceited in or of a thing, τινι Luc.
under a curse, excommunicate, accurst, Lat. piacularis, Hdt., etc.
to offer sacrifice to the dead or manes, Lat. parentare, τινί Hdt., etc.
an offering to the manes, Luc.
an offering to the manes, Plut.
Mid. to take in one's arms, Anth.
to fit thongs (ἀγκύλαι) to javelins, for throwing them by, Xen.
just now, lately, Ar., Plat.
to lead in or on, Lat. inducere, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; mostly c. inf., μαίνεσθαι ἐνάγει ἀνθρώπους (sc. Bacchus) Hdt.
c. acc. rei, to urge on, promote, τὸν πόλεμον Thuc.
Dep. to contend or fight among others, c. dat., Hdt.
γῆ εὐμενὴς ἐναγωνίζεσθαι favourable to fight in, Thuc.
of or for a contest, Plut., Luc.:—of gods who presided over games, Simon., etc.
in the air, Luc.
with blood in one, Hdt.
to slay in battle, generally, to kill, slay, Il., Soph.; of things, to destroy, Od.
ominous, boding, fateful, Lat. fatalis, Od.; neut. ἐναίσιμον and -μα as adv. ominously, Hom.: —in good sense, seasonable, Lat. opportunus, of omens, Il.
of persons, righteous, Hom.
of things, fit, proper, Il.:—adv. -ως, fitly, becomingly, Aesch., Eur.
to fight in, Anth.
Pass. to float or drift about in the sea, c. dat., Eur.
adv. nine times, Od., Plat.
nine thousand, ionic εἰνακισχίλιοι, Hdt.
nine hundred, Hdt., Thuc.
to listen to a thing, c. gen., Soph.
to anoint with ointment, c. dat., Plat.:—Mid. to anoint oneself, Anth.
in accordance with truth: adv. -θως, probably, Luc.
like, resembling, c. dat., Hom.; θεοῖς ἐναλίγκιος αὐδήν like the gods in voice, Od.
in, on, of the sea, Lat. marinus, Od., Aesch., etc.; ἐν. λεώς sea men, Soph.; πόντου εἰναλία φύσις, i. e. fish, Id.
crosswise, Ar.
alternately, Lat. vicissim, πρήσσειν ἐν. to have alternations of fortune, Hdt.

entry.note: attic -ττω fut. ξω perf. -ήλλᾰχα pass. -ήλλαγμαι aor2 -ηλλάγην
entry.sense: to exchange, φόνον θανάτῳ ἐν., i. e. to pay for murder by death, Eur.; ἐνήλλαξεν τὴν ὕβριν diverted his assault, Soph.
Pass. to be changed, τί δ’ ἐνήλλακται τῆς ἡμερίας νὺξ ἥδε βάρος; what heavy change from the day hath this night suffered? Soph.
to have dealings with, τινι Thuc.
Dep.
to leap in or upon, c. dat., Aesch., Soph.
absol. to dance, Ar.
changed, contrary, Theocr., Anth.
to deaden or discourage besides, Plut.
to milk into, γαυλοῖς Od.
engaged in equal contest with, a match for, τινι Plat.
opposite, over against, face to face, c. gen., Il.; ἔν. προσβλέπειν νεκρόν Soph.; ἔν. ἐλθεῖν Eur.
set against, hostile, Anth.:—as adv. face to face, against, μαχέσασθαι, πολεμίζειν Il.
Dep:

to set oneself against, oppose, withstand, τινι Hdt., Thuc., etc.; οὐκ ἐναντιώσομαι τὸ μὴ οὐ γεγωνεῖν I will not refuse to speak, Aesch.; τοῦτό μοι ἐναντιοῦται πράττειν this prevents me from doing, Plat.
to contradict, gainsay, Eur., Thuc., etc.
of the wind, to be adverse, Soph., Thuc.
opposite, Lat. adversus:
of Place, over against, opposite, c. dat., Hom.: fronting, face to face, Od., Eur.:—with Verbs of motion, in opposite directions, meeting, Il.
in hostile sense, opposing, facing in fight, Id., etc.; c. gen., ἐναντίοι Ἀχαιῶν Id., etc.: also c. dat., Id.:— οἱ ἐν. one's adversaries, Aesch., etc.:—generally, opposed to, τινί Soph., Xen.
of qualities, acts, etc., the opposite, contrary, reverse, Aesch., Soph.; mostly c. gen., τὰ ἐν. τούτων the very reverse of these things, Hdt., etc.; also c. dat., Aesch.
in adv. usages:
neut. ἐναντίον, opposite, face to face, Od., attic:—as prep. c. gen. in the presence of, before, Lat. coram, c. gen., Soph., Thuc., etc.
in hostile sense, against, c. gen., Il.; also c. dat., Id., Eur.
contrariwise, in attic τοὐναντίον, on the other hand: so also neut. pl. ἐναντία Hdt., Thuc., etc.
ἐκ τοῦ ἐναντίου, over against, opposite, Lat. ex adverso, e regione, Xen., etc.: so, ἐξ ἐναντίας, ionic -ίης, Hdt., Thuc.
regul. adv. ἐναντίως, contrariwise, c. dat., Aesch.: —also c. gen., Plat.:— ἐν. ἔχειν to be exactly opposed, Dem.
contrariety, opposition, Plat.
in the presence of, c. gen., NTest.
an obstacle, hindrance, Thuc., Dem.
a contradiction, discrepancy, Plat.
a contradiction, Thuc.
Mid. or Pass. to gain distinction among others, ἐναπεδεικνύατο (ionic 3rd pl. imperf.) Hdt.
to die in a place, Hdt., Thuc.
to break off in a wound, c. dat., Plut.
Pass. to be stored up in, c. dat., Plut.
to break off short in a shield, Thuc.
Pass. to perish in a place, c. dat., Xen.
Dep. to defend oneself in, Aeschin.
to wash clean in a thing:—Mid., ἐναπονίζεσθαι τοὺς πόδας ἐν τῷ ποδανιπτῆρι to wash one's feet in the foot-pan, Hdt.
to expire in the act of doing a thing, c. dat., Plut.
Pass. to be suffocated in, Luc.
to indicate or point out in, Plut.
to spend on law in a place, Ar.
to give up the ghost in a place, Hes., Anth.
to bind on or to a person, Eur.:— Pass., perf. ἐνῆμμαι, of persons, to be fitted with, clad in, c. acc., λεοντέας ἐναμμένοι (ionic for ἐνημμ-) Hdt., Ar.
to kindle, set on fire, Id.
the arms and trappings of a slain foe, spoils, booty, Lat. spolia, Il.
to fit or fasten in, Od.
ἐνάρηρα, intr., to be fitted in, Id.
visible, palpable, in bodily shape, properly of gods appearing in their own forms, Hom.; so of a dream or vision, Od., Hdt., etc.; ἐναργὴς ταῦρος in visible form a bull, a very bull, Soph.
manifest to the mind's eye, distinct, Id., Dem.:— adv. -γῶς, manifestly, Aesch., etc.
of words, etc., distinct, manifest, Id., Plat., etc.:—adv., ἐναργέως λέγειν Hdt.
prob. a Scythian word, answering to the Greek ἀνδρόγυνοι, a band who plundered the temple of Aphrodite at Ascalon, Hdt.
wearing the spoils, Anth.
to reckon in or among: to reckon, account, οὐδέν as nothing, Soph.:—Mid., = ἐν ἀριθμῷ ποιεῖσθαι, to make account of, Eur.

to strip a slain foe of his arms (ἔναρα), Lat. spoliare, ἔντεα ἐν, τινά Il.:— hence, to slay in fight, and, generally, to slay, Id., Aesch.:—Pass., νὺξ ἐναριζομένα night when dying, i. e. when yielding to day, Soph.
in the number, to make up the number, Od.: counted among, i. e. among, c. dat., Theocr.
taken into account, Lat. in numero habitus, Il.
to fit or fix in a thing, c. dat., Eur.
metaph. to fit, adapt, τι εἴς τι Plat.; ἐν. αὑτόν to make himself popular, Plut.:—Mid., τὰν Δωριστὶ (sc. ἁρμονίαν) ἐναρμόττεσθαι τὴν λύραν to have it tuned to the Dorian mode, Ar.
intr. to fit, suit, be convenient, Id.:—c. dat. pers. to please, Plut.
in accord or harmony, Luc.
Dep. in sacrifices, to begin the offering, by taking the barley (οὐλοχύται) from the basket (κανοῦν), Eur.:—perf. in pass. sense, Id.
to train or practise in athing, Plut.: Pass. with fut. mid., to be so practised, Luc.
Pass. to fit oneself with a shield, Ar.
to behave oneself unseemly in, Plut.
on the ninth day, Thuc.
ninth, Lat. nonus, Il., Hes.
in pl. = ἐννέα, Anth.
wandering in the fields, Anth.
intr. to dwell or abide in aplace, Soph.
Dep. ἐναυλίζομαι to take up one's quarters in a place during night, to take up nightquarters, bivouac, Hdt., Thuc., Xen., etc.
habitable, Anth.
an abode, Anth.
the bed of a stream, a torrent, mountain-stream, Il.
（αὐλή) in pl. the haunts of the country-gods, Hes., Eur.
on or to the flute: metaph., λόγοι ἔν. words ringing in one's ears, Plat.: hence fresh in memory, Aeschin.
（αὐλή), dwelling in dens, Eur.: in one's den, Soph.
to increase, enlarge, Xen.
exposed to the air, Theophr.
a kindling, Plut.
a spark, remnant, Plut.
on the neck, Anth.
to kindle, ἐν. πῦρ τινι to light one a fire, give him a light, Xen.:— Mid., πῦρ ἐναύεσθαι to get a light, Plut., Luc.
to fasten up in a thing, Hdt.
to let drop into, v. l., Hdt.
with lighted torch, Aesch.
to kindle in: Mid. to burn or glow in, Od.
to bite into, ἐνδ. στόμια γνάθοις to take the bit between the teeth, of runaway horses, Eur.
to weep in: ἐνδ. ὄμμασι to suffuse them with tears, Aesch.
native of the country, Mosch.
Dep. to divide, δὶς τοὔνόμ’ ἐνδατούμενος dividing the name of Polynices (into πολὺ νεῖκος) , Aesch.; ἐνδ. λόγους ὀνειδιστῆρας to distribute or fling about reproaches, Eur.
c. acc. objecti, to speak of in detail, i. e., in bad sense, to reproach, revile, or, in good sense, to tell of, celebrate, Soph.
in need of a thing, c. gen., Hdt., attic
absol. in need, indigent, Xen., Plat., etc.
lacking, deficient, mostly in comp., Hdt., Thuc.; τινι in a thing, Id.:— τὸ ἐνδεές lack, want, defect, deficiency, Id.
inferior to, c. gen., Xen.; τῆς δυνάμεως ἐνδεᾶ πρᾶξαι to act short of your real power, Thuc.; τούτου ἐνδεᾶ ἐφαίνετο (sc. τὰ πράγματα) their power was unequal to the purpose, Id.
insufficient, Id.:—adv., ἐνδεῶς, defectively, insufficiently, Plat.; μὴ ἐνδεῶς γνῶναι to judge not insufficiently, Thuc.
want, need, lack, Thuc., etc.
defect, deficiency, Plat.
want of means, need, poverty, Lat. egestas, Id., Dem.
a proof, token, Dem.
to mark, point out, Lat. indicare, Soph., etc.
as attic law-term, to inform against one, Plat.; so in Mid., Plut.:—in Pass., ἐνδεδειγμένος Plat.; ἐνδειχθέντα δεκάζειν being informed against for bribing, Dem.
Mid. to shew forth oneself or what is one's own, Πηλείδῃ ἐνδείξομαι I will declare myself to Achilles, Il.; ἐνδείκνυσθαι τὴν γνώμην Hdt.
with a part. to shew, give proof of doing, Eur., etc.
c. acc. rei, to display, exhibit, Lat. prae se ferre, Aesch., Thuc.
ἐνδείκνυσθαί τινι to display oneself to one, make a set at him, court him, Dem., Aeschin.
a pointing out as Attic law-term, a laying information against one who discharged public functions for which he was legally disqualified, Dem., etc.
a display of good will, Aeschin.
eleven cubits long, Il.
eleven, Lat. undecim, Hom., etc.
at Athens, οἱ ἕνδεκα, the Eleven, the Police-commissioners, who had charge of the prisons, and the punishment of criminals, Ar., etc.
the number Eleven, Plat.
on the eleventh day, Thuc.
the eleventh, Hom., etc.
continuous, perpetual, Plat., etc. adv. -χῶς, Id.
to wall up, Hdt.
to build in a place, Theocr.
Dep. to grasp with the right hand, Eur.

towards the right hand, from left to right: neut. pl. as adv., θεοῖς ἐνδέξια ᾠνοχόει he filled for the gods from left to right, Il.:—contrary procedure was avoided as unlucky, hence, ἐνδέξια σήματα propitious omens, Id.
= δεξιός, on the right, Eur.
clever, expert, Hhymn.
bound to, entangled in, τινι Anth.
Dep.
to take upon oneself, Lat. suscipere, Hdt.
to accept, admit, approve of, Lat. accipere, Id., Thuc.
to give ear to, believe, Hdt.: absol. to give ear, attend, Eur.
of things, to admit, allow of, Thuc., Plat.:—c. inf., οὐκ ἐνδέχεται μελετᾶσθαι does not admit of being practised, Thuc.

absol. to be possible, ἐνδέχεται Id.: esp. in part. ἐνδεχόμενος, η, ον, possible, ἐκ τῶν ἐνδεχομένων by all possible means, Xen.: —ἐνδέχεται impers., it admits of being, it is possible that, c. acc. et inf., Thuc., etc.
as far as possible, ap. Dem.

to bind in, on or to, τι ἔν τινι Od.; τί τινι Ar., etc.; so in Mid., ἐνεδήσατο δεσμῷ bound them fast, Theocr.; ἐνδησάμενος having packed it up, Ar.:—Pass., ἱρὰ ἐνδεδεμένα ἐν καλάμῃ Hdt.; ἐνδεθῆναι εἰς σῶμα or ἐν τῷ σώματι Plat.
metaph., Ζεύς με ἄτῃ ἐνέδησε entangled me in it, Il.:—Pass., ἐνδεδέσθαι ὁρκίοις, etc., Hdt.; ἐνδεδέσθαι τὴν ἀρχήν to have the government secured, Id.:—Mid. to bind to oneself, Eur.
to be in want of a thing, c. gen., Eur., Plat.; c. inf., τίνος ἐνδέομεν μὴ οὐ χωρεῖν; what do we lack of going? Eur.:—so in Mid., Xen.; and in Pass., στρωμάτων ἐνδεηθέντες Id.
of things, to be wanting or lacking, Hdt.:—impers. ἐνδεῖ, there is need or want, c. gen. rei, Plat., Xen.
visible, manifest, clear, Soph., Thuc.
of persons, manifest, discovered, known, Ar., Thuc.
adv. -λως, Sup. -ότατα, Id.
to live in a place, Lys.
dwelling in a place, a native, Hes., etc.; ἐνδημότατος the greatest "stay-at-home, " Thuc.
of or belonging to a people, national, Id.
to calumniate in a matter, Luc.
to pass the noon, Plut.
Pass. to play the prude towards, trifle with, τινι Theocr.
Dep. to live or dwell in a place, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
to draw an army up in, Hdt.
to spend or consume in doing, χρόνον Ar., Thuc.
absol. (sub. χρόνον), to spend time in a place, Dem.
to waste time by staying in a place, linger there, Thuc., Plat.
to continue in the practice of a thing ἔν τινι Xen.: absol. to dwell upon a point (in speaking), Aeschin.
Verbal Adj. of ἐνδιατρίβω one must dwell upon, τινί Luc.
to stay in the open air; generally, to linger in or haunt a place, c. dat., Anth.:—in Mid., Hhymn.
trans., ποιμένες μῆλα ἐνδιάασκον shepherds were driving their sheep afield, Theocr.
to put on another, τινά τι NTest.:—Mid. to put on oneself, Id.
to give in:
to give into one's hands, give up to, τινά or τί τινι Eur., etc.; a city, esp. by treachery, Thuc., Xen.
like Lat. praebere, to give, lend, afford, ἐνδιδόναι τινὶ χέρα to lend him a hand, Eur.; ἐνδ. λαβήν τινι to give one a handle, Ar.:— to cause, excite, Thuc.
to shew, exhibit, Hdt., Eur., etc.
to allow, grant, concede, Eur., Thuc.
intr. to give in, allow, permit, Hdt.: to give in, give way, Thuc.:— ἐνδ. τινι to yield to, Id.
to pass the day in, Theophr.
to chase, pursue, 3rd pl. imperf. ἐνδίεσαν, epic for ἐνεδίεσαν, Il.
of things, according to right, right, just, legitimate, Trag.:— τὸ μὴ ’νδικον = τὸ ἄδικον, Soph.; μὴ λέγων γε τοὔνδικον not speaking truth, Id=Soph.
of persons, righteous, just, upright, Aesch., etc.; τίς ἐνδικώτερος; who has better right or more reason? Id.
adv. -κως, right, with justice, fairly, Id.
truly, indeed, Eur.
justly, naturally, as one has a right to expect, Trag.
the entrails, or rather the body enclosed in armour, Il.
to revolve, go about, ἐνδινεῦντι, doric for ἐνδινοῦσι, Theocr.
cf. Lat. sub divo, at midday, at noon, Hom., Theocr.
ἔνδῐος, in the open air, Anth.: neut. ἔνδῐον, an abode, Id.
sitting on the same seat with another, c. dat., Xen.
adv. from within, Lat. intrinsecus, Od., Trag., etc.:—c. gen., ἔνδοθεν στέγης from inside the tent, Soph.
like οἴκοθεν, of oneself, by one's own doing, Aesch.
within, c. gen., Il., Hes.
absol., Hdt.; οἱ ἔνδοθεν the domestics, Ar.; or the people inside the city, Thuc.
adv. within, at home, Lat. intus, Hom.
c. gen., Il.
to be in doubt, at a loss how to do a thing, c. inf., Thuc.: absol., οἱ ἐνδοιάζοντες the waverers, Id.:—Pass. to be matter of doubt, ἐνδοιασθῆναι Id.
doubtful, Luc.
doubtful, ambiguous: adv. -τῶς, doubtfully, προθύμως Hdt., Thuc.

entry.etym: aeolic and doric for ἔνδοθι, Theocr.

entry.sense: structure, NTest.
in the inmost part of a dwelling, lurking within, Soph.
in, within, in the house, at home, Lat. intus, Hom., etc.; τἄνδον as adv. in one's heart, Eur.:—οἱ ἔνδον those of the house, the family, Soph.: τὰ ἔνδον family matters, Id.
c. gen., Διὸς ἔνδον in the house of Zeus, Il.; σκηνῆς ἔνδον Soph.; φρενῶν ἔνδον in one's senses, Eur.
held in esteem or honour, of high repute, Xen., Plat.
of things, notable, Aeschin.: —adv. -ξως, hence Sup., ἐνδοξότατα Dem.
quite within, Plut.
to fall in with a heavy sound, Od.
a high shoe, worn by Artemis, Anth.
a thick wrapper worn by runners, after exercise, Juven.
bedewed, Aesch.
the oaken peg or pin by which the yoke is fixed to the pole (ἱστοβοεύς), Hes.
adv. thoughtfully, carefully, sedulously, Hom.
a garment, NTest., Plut.
to strengthen, NTest.
to exercise dominion in or among people, c. dat., Aesch.
to procure by one's authority, Xen.
a putting on, NTest.
to be unlucky in or with, c. dat., Eur.
for putting on, Soph.
put on, Aesch., Eur.
ἔνδυτον (sc. ἔσθημα) , a garment, dress, Id.:—metaph., ἐνδ. σαρκός, i. e. one's skin, Id.
clad in, covered with, στέμμασιν Id.

entry.note: and -δύνω with Mid. ἐνδύομαι fut. -δύσομαι aor1 -εδυσάμην and aor2 act. -έδυν
entry.sense: c. acc., to go into,
of clothes, to put on, Lat. induere sibi, ἔνδυνε χιτῶνα Il.; πέπλον Soph.:—so in Mid., Il., etc.:—perf. ἐνδέδυκα, to wear κιθῶνας Hdt.:—metaph. to put on, assume the person of . . , NTest.
to enter, to press into, c. acc., Il., etc.:—also, ἐνδ. εἰς . . , Thuc., etc.:—also c. dat., Xen.:—absol. to enter, Hdt.
Causal in pres. ἐνδύω, fut. -δύσω, aor1 -έδυσαLat. induere alicui, to put on another, to clothe in, c. dupl. acc., Xen.
to clothe, τινά Hdt.
a sitting in: a lying in wait, ambush, Thuc., Xen.
the men laid in ambush, Id.
to lie in wait for, Lat. insidiari, τινά Dem.: —Pass. to be caught in an ambush, to be ensnared, Xen.
absol. to lay or set an ambush, Thuc., Xen.; so in Mid., Id.:—Pass. to lie in ambush, Id.
an inmate, inhabitant, Soph.
Dep. to have one's abode in a place, c. acc., Aesch.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use, ἐνοράω being used instead
entry.sense: to observe something in a person, τι ἔν τινι Thuc.; τί τινι Xen.: absol. to observe, Soph.
of a sculptor, to work into shape, Anth.
to wrap in: metaph.in Pass. to be engaged in or with, τοῖς πολεμίοις Plut.
to wrap up in a thing, c. dat., Thuc.
to be in a place, c. dat., Hom., etc.: c. dat. pl. to be among, Hdt.
absol. to be there, be in abundance, Od., etc.; σίτου οὐκ ἐνόντος as there was no corn there, Thuc.; ἱερῶν τῶν ἐνόντων of the temples that were in the place, Id.
to be possible, Trag., etc.
impers. c. dat. pers. et inf. it is in one's power, one may or can, Soph., etc.
part. neut. ἐνόν absol. since it was in them, was possible, Luc.
τὰ ἐνόντα all things possible, Dem.
to string on a thing, Pass., Hdt.
prep. with gen., mostly after its case, Il., etc.: on account of, for the sake of, because of, for, Lat. gratia, Id., etc.
as far as regards, as for, ἐμοῦ γε ἕνεκα as far as depends on me, Ar.; εἵνεκέν γε χρημάτων Hdt., etc.
pleon., ἀμφὶ σοὔνεκα Soph.; ὅσον ἀπὸ βοῆς ἕνεκα as far as shouting went, Thuc.
as Conjunct., for οὕνεκα, because, Hhymn.
to drive in or into, c. dat., Il.
to roll up in:—Mid. to wrap oneself in, Hdt.
to vomit in or into, εἴς τι Hdt.
ninety years old, Luc.
to keep holiday in, Plut.
indecl. ninety, Il., etc.
dumb, deaf and dumb, Xen.
Mid. to make an irruption among, Aesop.
to forswear oneself by a god, Aeschin.
Dep. to make or produce in, c. dat., Xen., etc.:—aor1 ἐνειργάσθην in pass. sense, to be placed in, Id.
to work for hire in a place, Hdt.; ἐνεργ. τῇ οὐσίᾳ to trade with the property, Dem.
to tell, tell of, relate, describe, Hom., Trag.:—absol. to tell news or tales, Od.
simply to speak, Hes., Trag.
c. acc. et inf. to bid one do so and so, Soph.
to call so and so, ἐνν. τινὰ δοῦλον Eur.
= προσεννέπω, to address, τινά Soph.
action, operation, energy, Arist.
to be in action, to operate, Arist.; so in Mid., NTest.
of land, productive, Plut.
to make profit of a thing, Aeschin.
at work, working, active, busy, Hdt., etc.: of soldiers, ships, effective, fit for service, Thuc., Xen.
of land, in work, productive, opp. to ἀργός, Id.; ἐν. χρήματα capital which brings in a return, Dem.
adv. ἐνεργῶς with activity, Xen.
to thrust in, fix in, τί τινι Od.:— Mid., ἐνερεισάμενος πέτρᾳ γόνυ having planted his own knee on the rock, Theocr.
to belch on one, c. dat., Ar.
somewhat ruddy, Luc.
adv., from beneath, up from below, Il., Aesch., Eur.
without sense of motion, beneath, below, Hom.; οἱ ἔνερθε θεοί the gods below, Lat. dii inferi, Il.
as prep. with gen. beneath, below, Hom., Trag.
subject to, in the power of, Soph.
Lat. inferi, those below, those beneath the earth, Il., Hes., Aesch.
a fitting in, fastening, Thuc.
lower, of the world below, Il., Aesch.: c. gen. below, Il. Cf. νέρτερος.
a suggestion, κείνης ἐννεσίῃσι (epic dat. pl.) at her suggestion, Il.
a pin, brooch, Il.
to be happy in one's life, Thuc.
to gain glory in another's ill fortune, Dem.
to sleep in or on a thing, c. dat., Od.
Pass. to be blessed in one, c. dat., NTest.
on which one sleeps, for sleeping on, Od.; ἐνεύναια, bed-furniture, Id.
to take a pledge from one, τινός Lex ap. Dem.
c. acc. rei, to take in pledge, Dem., Aeschin.:—Pass. to have one's goods seized for debt, Ar.:—Mid. to have security given one, take it for oneself, Id.
a taking in pledge, a security, pledge, Plat.
a pledge, surety, security, Hdt., Xen.; ἐν. τιθέναι τι to make a thing a pledge, put it in pawn, Ar.
to hold within, χόλον ἐνέχειν τινί to lay up, cherish inward wrath at one, Hdt.
Pass., with fut. and aor. mid., to be held, caught, entangled in a thing, c. dat., Id., Xen.: metaph., ἐνέχεσθαι ἀπορίῃσιν Hdt.; ἐν κακῷ Id.; ἐν θωύματι ἐνέσχετο was seized with wonder, Id.
to be obnoxious, liable or subject to, ζημίᾳ, αἰτίᾳ Plat., etc.
intr. to enter in, pierce, εἴς τι Xen.
to press upon, be urgent against, τινί NTest.
to yoke in, bind, involve in misfortune, Aesch.
to bind fast, Soph.
a place of amusement, Hdt.
kindness, gentleness, Il.
kind, gentle, Hom.
anything driven in: as Subst., ἐνήλατα (sc. ξύλα), τά, the rounds of a ladder, which are fixed in the sides, Eur.
ἀξόνων ἐνήλατα the pins driven into the axle, linchpins, Id.
of age, in the prime of manhood, Plut.
to be seated in, Od.

entry.etym: ἐνήνοθε, 3rd sg. perf. without any pres. ἐνέθω in use: only found in compds.
entry.sense: ἐπενήνοθε, of Thersites' head, ψεδνὴ ἐπ. λάχνη a thin coat of downy hair grew thereon, Il.; of a cloak, οὐλὴ ἐπενήνοθε λάχνη a thick pile was on it, Id.; c. acc., of ambrosial unguent, οἷα θεοὺς ἐπενήνοθε such as is on the gods, Od.
κατενήνοθε, to be over, lie upon, Hes., Hom.
with oars, Plut.
of Place, thither, hither, Lat. illuc, huc, Od., etc.
in attic like ἔνθα, here or there, Lat. hic, Ar., etc.; οἱ ἐνθάδε those here, opp. to οἱ κάτω, Soph.; also the people of this country, Id.
of circumstances, in this case or state, Xen.; so, ἐνθάδ’ ἥκων having come to this point, Soph.; c. gen., ἐνθάδε τοῦ πάθους at this stage of my suffering, Id.
of Time, here, now, Id., Xen.
attic strengthd. for ἐνθάδε, Ar.
to sit in or on a thing, c. dat., Soph.
a sitting in, ἡλίου ἐνθ. a seat in the sun, Soph.
there where, where, stronger form of ἔνθα, Il., etc.: whither, Soph.
to bury in a place: aor2 pass. ἐνετάφην Aeschin.
to be inspired, Hdt.
adv.:
Demonstr.
of Place, there, Lat. ibi, Hom., etc.:—also with Verbs of motion, thither, Lat. illuc, Id.; ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα here and there, hither and thither, Lat. hic illic, huc illuc, Id.
of Time, thereupon, then, just then, Id., etc.
Relat.,
of Place, where, Lat. ubi, Il., etc.;c. gen., γαίας ἔνθα in that spot of earth in which, Soph.; ἔνθα πημάτων κυρῶ at what point of misery I am, Eur.: —with Verbs of motion, whither, Lat. quo, Soph.
of Time, when, Xen.; ἔστιν ἔνθα, Lat. est ubi, sometimes, Soph.
hence, from this quarter, Lat. hinc, Hom., attic; ἐνθένδ’ αὐτόθεν from this very city, Ar.
of Time or Consequence, from that time, Thuc.; ἐνθένδε or τοὐνθένδε, thereafter, Soph., Eur.; τἀνθένδε what followed, the event, Id.
adv.:
Demonstr.,

of Place, Lat. inde, thence, Hom.; ἔνθεν μὲν . . , ἑτέρωθι δέ .. , on the one side and the other, Od.; ἔνθεν καὶ ἔνθεν on this side and on that, Lat. hinc illinc, Hdt., etc.:— c. gen., ἔνθεν καὶ ἔνθεν τῶν τροχῶν on both sides of the wheels, Xen.
of Time, thereupon, thereafter, Il., Aesch.
of occasion, thence, from that point, Od.
Relat., for ὅθεν,
of Place, Lat. unde, whence, from which, Id., Soph.
of occasion, whence, like Lat. unde, Aesch., Eur. Hence
full of the god, inspired, possessed, Trag., Xen.:—c. gen. rei, ἔνθεος τέχνης gifted of heaven with prophetic art, Aesch.
of divine frenzy, inspired by the god, Id.
to heat:—Pass., ἐντεθέρμανται πόθῳ is heated by passion, Soph.
a putting in: also a piece put in, a mouthful, Ar.
lawful, like ἔννομος, Plut.
put in, implanted, Theogn.
full of wild beasts, infested by them, Eur.
metaph. savage, wild, rough, Aesch.: untended, undressed, Soph.
to die in a place, Soph., Eur.
of the hand, to grow torpid in, τινί Id.
to be inspired or possessed by the god, be rapt, be in ecstasy, Xen., Plat.:—c. dat., ἐνθουσιᾶν κακοῖς Eur.
inspired, Plat., etc.
possessed, Plut.
crumbled and put into liquid: τὰ ἔνθρυπτα sops, Dem.
to leap in, on, or among, c. dat., Il., Eur.:— λὰξ ἔνθορεν ἰσχίῳ leapt with his feet against his, Od.
to lay to heart, consider well, reflect on, ponder, Aesch., Thuc., etc.
c. gen., ἐνθυμεῖσθαί τινος to think much or deeply of a thing, Id., Xen.
foll. by a relative, as by ὅτι, to consider that, Ar., etc.
with part., οὐκ ἐντεθύμηται ἐπαιρόμενος was not conscious that he was becoming excited, Thuc.
to take to heart, be hurt or angry at, τι Aesch., Dem.
to think out a thing, form a plan, Thuc.
to infer, conclude, Dem.
a thought, piece of reasoning, argument, Soph., Aeschin.
an invention, device, Xen.
consideration, esteem, Thuc.
one must consider, Dem.
a scruple, misgiving, Thuc.

taken to heart, μή σοι ἐνθύμιος ἔστω take not much thought for him, Od.; ἐνθύμιόν οἱ ἐγένετο he had trouble of heart, Hdt.; τί δ’ ἐστί σοι τοῦτ’ ἐνθύμιον; what is 't that weighs upon thy heart? Soph.; ἐνθύμιον ποιεῖσθαί τι to have a scruple about it, Thuc.
taken to heart, Hdt.
to arm, equip with armour: part. perf. pass. ἐντεθωρακισμένος mailed, Xen.
of a year, one year old, σῦς Od., Dem., etc.
yearly, annual, year by year, Hdt.:—neut. pl. as adv., Hes.
for a year, lasting a year, Eur., Thuc.; κἀνιαύσιος βεβώς gone, absent for a year, Soph.
any long period of time, a cycle, period, περιπλομένων ἐνιαυτῶν as times rolled on, Od.; ἐτῶν ἐνιαυτούς Ar.
= ἔτος, a year, Hom., etc.; ἐνιαυτόν during a year, Od.; τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ every year, Xen.; εἰς ἐνιαυτόν for a year, Il.;— κατ’ ἐνιαυτόν for a year, Thuc.; or every year, attic
to sleep among others, c. dat., Od.
in some places, Hdt.; c. gen. loci, Id.
in some places, here and there, now and then, Plat.
to sweat in, labour hard in, Xen.
to set in a place:—Mid. to found or build for oneself, Hdt.:—Pass. to be placed or settled in a place, Id.
to sit in or on a seat, c. acc., Eur.; c. dat., Plat.
to send in or into, Hom.
to put in, implant, inspire, c. acc. rei et dat. pers., καί οἱ θάρσος ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἐνῆκε Il.; ἐνεὶς λύσσαν Eur.
reversely, c. acc. pers. et dat. rei, to plunge into, τὸν Ζεὺς ἐνέηκε πόνοισι Il.
generally, to throw in or upon, c. dat., Hom.:—of ships, to launch them into the sea, Od.:— metaph. to incite one to do a thing, c. inf., Mosch.
to send into the assembly, employ, Thuc.
to inject poison, Xen.
intr. to press on, Id.
to break in, break off: metaph., ἐνικλᾶν ὅττι νοήσω to frustrate what I devise, Il.
some, Lat. aliqui, = ἔστιν οἵ, Hdt., Xen., etc.
for ἔνι ὅτε = ἔστιν ὅτε, sometimes, Eur., etc.
a rebuke, reprof; also abuse, contumely, Hom.
to ride in, Hdt.
to reprove, upbraid, Lat. objurgo, Hom.
to attack, reproach, Hom.; epic inf. ἐνισσέμεν Il.:—Pass., ἐνισσόμενος misused, Id.
Causal in pres., fut. and aor1 act., and in aor1 mid.:— to put, set, place in, ἐν λίθοις Xen.; ἐς τὰς χώρας Hdt.
aor1 mid. to begin, Dem.
Pass., with aor2 perf., and plup. act.:— to be set in, to stand in a place, c. dat., Eur.; ἐν τῷ νηῷ Hdt.
to be appointed, βασιλεὺς ἐνίστασθαι Id.

to be upon, to threaten, Lat. imminere, c. dat. pers., Id.:—absol. to be at hand, begin, arise, Ar., Dem.:—of time, ὁ ἐνεστὼς πόλεμος the present war, Aeschin.; τὰ ἐνεστηκότα πράγματα present circumstances, Xen.
to stand in the way, resist, τινι Thuc.:—absol. to stand in the way, Id.
Mid., ἐνίσχεσθαι τὴν φωνήν to keep in one's voice, Plut.:—Pass. to be held fast, Hdt., Xen.
a period of nine years, Plat.
nine years old, Hes.
an inmate, inhabitant, Anth.
nine years old, Theocr.:—neut. ἐννάετες, as adv. for nine years, Hes.:—fem. ἐνναέτις
an inhabitant, Anth.
to dwell in a place, c. dat., Eur.; ἐνν. ἐκεῖ Soph.:—c. acc. loci, to inhabit, Mosch.
nine times, Anth.
Pass. to have ships built in it, of a place, Thuc.
worth nine beeves, Il.
nineteen months old, Anth.
indecl. nineteen, Il., etc.
eleven years old, Anth.
with nine springs, name of a well at Athens, also called Καλλιρρόη, Hdt., Thuc.
of nine threads, Xen.
of or in nine months, Hdt.
indecl. nine, Lat. novem, Hom., etc.
nine cubits broad, or long , Il.
a body of nine, Theocr.
epic for ἐνάκις χίλιοι nine thousand, Il.
nine fathoms long, Od.
to hatch young in a place, Ar.
c. acc. to hatch as in a nest, Plat.
to make signs to, to ask by signs, NTest.
of or for nine years, Hom.
epic adv. for nine days, Il.

entry.note: fut. ήσω ionic aor1 part. ἐννώσας perf. ἐννένωκα attic Dep. ἐννοοῦμαι with aor. pass. ἐνενοήθην ionic 3rd sg. plup. ἐννένωτο
entry.sense: to have in one's thoughts, to think, consider, reflect, Hdt., Plat.; ἐνν. μή . . , to be anxious lest . . , Xen.
c. acc. to think or reflect upon, consider, Hdt., Soph.; ἐννοεῖν περί τινος Eur.
c. gen. to have thought of a thing, Id., Xen.
to understand, Trag.
to intend to do, c. inf., Hdt., Soph.
to think of, invent, Lat. excogitare, Id., Xen.
to have in one's mind, to conceive, form a notion of, τι Plat., Xen.
a thought in the mind, notion, conception, Plat.
a thought, intent, design, Eur., Xen.
within the law, lawful, legal, Trag., etc.; ἔννομα πάσχειν to suffer lawful punishment, Thuc.
of persons, keeping within the law, upright, Aesch., etc.:— subject to law, NTest.
the Earth-shaker, name of Poseidon, Hom.
thoughtful, intelligent, sensible, Aesch., etc.; ἔννους γίγνομαι I come to my senses, Eur.
to sleep in or on a place, Soph.

entry.etym: The Root was ϜΕΣ, cf. Lat. vestio
entry.sense: to put clothes on another, c. dupl. acc., κεῖνός σε χλαῖνάν τε χιτῶνά τε ἕσσει he will clothe thee in cloak and frock, Od.

Mid. and Pass., c. acc. rei, to clothe oneself in, to be clad in, put on, to wear, Hom.; ἀσπίδας ἑσσάμενοι, of tall shields which covered the whole person, Il.; [ξυστὰ] εἱμένα χαλκῶι shafts clad with brass, Id.; and by a strong metaph., λάϊνον ἕσσο χιτῶνα thou hadst been clad in coat of stone, i. e. stoned by the people, Id.:—metaph. also, φρεσὶ εἱμένοι ἀλκήν Id.
in the night, by night, nightly, Lat. nocturnus, Hom., Soph.:— ἐννύχιοι dwellers in the realms of Night, the dead, Id.
= ἐννῠ́χιος, Il., Aesch.:—adv. ἔννυχον or -χα, NTest.
epith. of Hades, Soph.
in or on the way, by the way-side, Il., Aesch.:—epith. of gods, who had their statues by the way-side, Lat. triviales, as of Hecate, Soph., Eur.; Ἐνοδία, = Lat. Trivia, Id.
to dwell in a place, c. dat., Eur.; ἐν τόπῳ Xen.; [Θυρέαν] ἔδοσαν ἐνοικεῖν gave it them to dwell in, Thuc.
c. acc. loci, to inhabit, Hdt., Soph., etc.; οἱ ἐνοικοῦντες the inhabitants, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
a dwelling in a place, Thuc.
to settle in a place:—Pass. to be settled in a place, to take up one's abode there, Hdt.; so in Mid., Thuc.
in the house, keeping at home, ἐν. ὄρνις a dunghill cock, Aesch.
as Subst., ἐνοίκιον, ου, τό, house-rent, Dem., Anth.
to build in a place, Thuc.:—Mid., ἐν. τεῖχος to build themselves a fort there, Id.
to build up, block up, Id.
in-dwelling: an inhabitant, Trag., Thuc., etc.
pass. dwelt in, Eur.
to keep house, dwell in a place, Luc.
to pour in wine, Hom.
to fall in, of the ground, Plut.: to slip and fall, Id.
to be well acquainted with a thing, c. dat., Plut.
Mid. to impress, Plut.
a crying, screaming, as of birds, Il.: a war-cry, Id.
generally, a voice, Od., Eur.
of things, a sound, Il., Eur.
ἐνόπλιος (sc. ῥυθμός), ὁ a war-tune, march, Ar., Xen.
in arms, armed, Soph., Eur.
with armed men within, of the Trojan horse, Id.
a mirror, Eur.
to see, remark, observe something in a person or thing, τί τινι Thuc., etc.; τι ἔν τινι Hdt., etc.; c. acc. et part. fut., ἐνεώρα τιμωρίην ἐσομένην he saw that vengeance would come, Id.
to look at or upon, Xen.
bound by oath, Lat. juratus, Soph., Thuc.: c. dat. pers., Lat. addictus, Soph.
that whereto one is sworn, Id., etc.
to bring a ship to harbour:—Pass. to come to anchor, Theogn.
in harbour, Anth.
to arouse, stir up in a person, Il.:—Pass. to arise in or among, ἐνῶρτο γέλως θεοῖσιν Id.
to leap in or upon another, c. dat., Il.
a he-goat, Theocr.
uncastrated, entire, ἔνορχα μῆλα rams, Il.
a shaking, quake, Hes., Eur.
entry.etym: From an obsol. Root *ἐνόθω to shake.

entry.sense: Earth-shaker, of Poseidon, Hom.
= the Lat. annus, a year, hence ἐνιαυτός, cf. ἄφ-ενος, Lat. bi-ennis, etc.
the day after to-morrow, Lat. perendie, only in oblique cases of fem., gen. ἔνης epic ἔννηφι (sub. ἡμέρας) Hes.; doric ἔνας Theocr.; εἰς ἕνην Ar.
belonging to the former of two periods, last year's, ἕναι ἀρχαί last year's magistrates, Dem.:— dat. ἕνῃ as adv., long ago, Ar.
ἕνη καὶ νέα (sc. ἡμέρα), the old and new day, i. e. the last day of the month, which consisted of two halves, one belonging to the old, the other to the new moon, Id.
in heaven, heavenly, Anth.
to trouble, disquiet, annoy, τινά Plat., Xen., etc.:—Pass. to be troubled or annoyed, Id.
c. dat. to give trouble or annoyance to, Id., Dem., etc.
absol. to be a nuisance, Ar.
held in, i. e. liable to, subject to, c. dat., Plat.; ἔν. θανάτου (sc. ζημίᾳ) liable to the penalty of death, NTest.
to sew up in, τι εἴς τι; so Mid., Hdt.: —Pass. to be sewed up in, c. dat., Eur.
to shiver or freeze in a garment, Ar.
to shake in or at, Soph.; κέλαδον ἐνς. πώλοις to drive a sound into their ears, Id.
c. acc. pers. to drive into, ἐνς. τινὰ ἀγρίαις ὁδοῖς Id.
Mid. to intimate, Xen.
to be dry, withered, Anth.
to get ready, prepare, Ar.
to dress in a garment, Plut.; Ἡρακλέα ’νεσκεύασα dressed you up as Hercules, Ar.:—Mid. to dress oneself up in other clothes, Id.: to arm oneself, Xen.: —Pass to be equipped, Hdt.
to hurl, dart in or upon, τί τινι Hdt.
intr. to fall in or on, Id., Soph.
to let fall upon, οὔδει ἐνισκίμψαντε καρήατα, of horses hanging their heads in grief for their master's loss, Il.:—Pass. to stick in the ground, Id.
to harden:—Pass. to become inveterate, of diseases, Xen.
wise in a thing, Anth.
included in a truce or treaty, Thuc.; ἔνσπ. τινί in alliance with one, Eur., Thuc.; and as Subst. an ally, Id.
under truce or safe-conduct, Eur.
to drop in or into a thing, c. dat., Ar.: —Pass. to be instilled into, Od., Hdt.

entry.etym: fut. ξω, = ἐνστάζω, εἴς τι, Ar.

entry.sense: a beginning, plan, management, Aeschin.
an adversary, Soph.
to dress in:—Pass., στολὴν ἐνεσταλμένος clad in a dress, Hdt.
to fix in:—Pass., γαίῃ ἐνεστήρικτο it stuck fast in earth, Il.
Dep. to encamp in, Hdt.;—so in Act., Thuc.
to turn inPass. to turn or move in a place, c. dat., Il.
c. acc. loci, σηκοὺς ἐνστρέφειν to visit them, Eur.
to impress on a thing, c. dat., Anth.

entry.note: fut. σω poet. and ionic for ἐντείνω
entry.sense: to stretch or strain tight with cords or straps, Hom.; ἐντανύσας [τὸν θρόνον ἱμᾶσιν] to cover it with stretched straps, Hdt.
to stretch a cord tight, of the bow-string, Od.: also to stretch a bow tight, i. e. to string it, Id.: —Mid., δυνήσεται ἐντανύσασθαι to string one's bow, Id.
tension; limitation, Plat.
to place or post in:—Pass., σφενδονᾶν ἐντεταγμένος posted to use the sling, Xen.
of Place, here, there, Lat. hic, illic, Hdt., etc.; ἐνταῦθά που here-abouts, Ar.
like ἐνταυθοῖ, with sense of motion towards, hither, thither, Lat. huc, illuc, Il., attic
c. gen., ἐντ. τῆς ἠπείρου Thuc.; ἔντ. τῆς πολιτείας in that department of government, Dem.
of Time, at the very time, then, Aesch., etc.
c. gen., ἐντ. ἡλικίας, Lat. ad hoc aetatis, Plat.
of Sequence, = Lat. deinde, thereupon, then, Hdt.
generally, herein, Soph., Plat., etc.: in this state of things, in this position, Dem.
hither, here, Hom.
to prepare for burial, NTest.
burial, NTest.
of or used in burial: hence as Subst., ἐντάφιον, ου, τό, a shroud, winding-sheet, Simon., Anth.
ἐντάφια, τά, offerings to the dead, obsequies, Soph.
fighting gear, arms, armour, Hom.
furniture, appliances, ἔντεα δαιτός Od.; ἔντεα νηός rigging, tackle, Hhymn.; ἔντη δίφρου the harness, Aesch.

to stretch or strain tightPass., δίφρος ἱμᾶσιν ἐντέταται is hung on tight-stretched straps, Il.; γέφυραι ἐντεταμέναι a bridge with the mooring-cables made taught, Hdt.; ἐντεταμένου τοῦ σώματος being braced up, Plat.
to stretch a bow tight, i. e. string it for shooting (cf. ἐντανύω), Eur.; so in Mid. to string one's bow, Id.:—Pass., τόξα ἐντεταμένα bows ready strung, Hdt.
ἐντείνειν ναῦν ποδί to keep a ship's sail taught by the sheet, Eur.
to tie tight, Id.
metaph. to strain, exert:—so in Mid., φωνὴν ἐντεινάμενος Aeschin.; ἐντεινάμενοι τὴν ἁρμονίαν pitching the tune high, Ar.:—and in Pass., ἐντεινόμενος, on the stretch, eager, Xen.
to carry on vigorously, Plut.
so intr. in Act. to exert oneself, be vehement, Eur.
to stretch out at or against, πληγὴν ἐντείνειν τινί, Lat. plagam intendere, to lay a blow on him, Xen.
to put into verse, Plat.
to build or fortify in a place, Xen.
in Mid. to wall in, i. e. blockade, Thuc.
Dep. to beget children in, Plut.
having children, Luc.
to end one's life in a place, Thuc.
complete, full, Ar., Thuc.
of victims, perfect, unblemished, Soph.
of soldiers and their equipments, in good condition, effective, Thuc.
of men, full-grown, Aesch.
to enjoin, command, τί τινι Hdt., etc.; ἐντέλλεσθαι ἀπὸ γλώσσης to command by word of mouth, Id.:—Pass., τὰ ἐντεταλμένα commands, Id., Xen.
to cut in, engrave upon, ἐν τοῖσι λίθοισι γράμματα Hdt.
to cut up,
to cut up the victim, sacrifice, Thuc.
to cut in, shred in, as herbs in a medical mixture, ἄκος ἐντ. Aesch.
to cut in two, Luc.
the timber of a ship, belly-timber, Ar.
an intestine, piece of gut, ἔντερον οἰός a string of sheep's gut, Od.:—mostly in pl. ἔντερα, the guts, bowels, Il., attic
working in harness, ἡμίονοι ἐντ. draught- mules, Il.
vehemently, vigorously, Hdt.
of Place, hence or thence, Lat. hinc or illinc, Od., etc.
of Time, henceforth, thenceforth, thereupon, Hdt., etc.; τοὐντεῦθεν Eur.; τἀντεῦθεν what remains, Aesch.
Causal, from that source, Thuc.
affable, Plut.
a lighting upon, meeting with, converse, intercourse, τινος with a person, Aeschin.
a petition, Plut.: intercession for a person, NTest.
Pass. to be stewed in beet (τεῦτλον), Ar.
within the province of art, artificial, artistic, Plat.
to pour in while molten, μόλιβδον Plut.
Pass., with perf. act. ἐντέτηκα,
of feelings, to sink deep in, Soph.
of persons, to be absorbed by a thing, Id.
to put in or into a ship, Od., attic; so in Mid., Od.:—then, generally, to put in or into, Hes., Hdt., etc.
metaph. to put into a person, inspire, Theogn., Xen.;— Mid., χόλον ἔνθεο θυμῷ thou didst store up wrath in thy heart, Il.; πατέρας ἔνθεο τιμῇ hold our fathers in honour, Id.
to put in the mouth, τί τινι Ar.; and in Mid., ἐνθοῦ, put in, i. e. eat, Id.
to bear or produce in a place, c. dat., Eur.; ᾠὰ ἐντ. ἐς τὴν ἰλύν to drop eggs into the mud, Hdt.
to create or cause in a person, τί τινι Eur.
perf. part. ἐντετοκώς intr., inborn, innate, Ar.
Lat. incacare, to squirt upon, τί τινι Ar.
to value in or among, Dem.
of persons, in honour, honoured, prized, Soph., etc.:—c. dat. rei, honoured with or in a thing, Eur.:— οἱ ἔντιμοι men in office, men of rank, Xen.
of things, honoured, held in honour, Soph.
adv., ἐντίμως ἔχειν to be in honour, Xen.
an incision, notch, Xen.
an injunction, order, command, behest, Hdt., etc.
cut in pieces, cut up: neut. pl., ἔντομα victims, Hdt.
of persons, well-strung, sinewy: metaph. intense, earnest, eager, vehement, Hdt., attic: —adv. ἐντόνως, eagerly, violently, Thuc., Xen.
in or of a place, Soph.
to carve in relief on a thing, Plut.
from within, Od.: —also = ἐντός, within, absol. or c. gen., Il.
to strut among, τισί Luc.
to turn about τὰ νῶτα Hdt.: to alter, Luc.
Mid. or Pass., aor2 ἐνετράπην [ᾰ], to turn about, linger, hesitate, Soph.
c. gen. pers. to turn towards, give heed to, pay regard to, to respect or reverence, Hom., Trag.
c. inf. to take care that, Theogn.
absol. to feel shame or fear, NTest.
to bring up in the house, Eur.:— so in Mid., Hes.:—Pass. to be reared in a place, c. dat., Eur.
to run in, εἰ ἐντρέχοι ἀγλαὰ γυῖα, if his limbs moved freely in [the armour], Il.
to slip in, enter, Anth.
within, inside, Lat. intus, opp. to ἐκτός:
as prep. with gen., τείχεος ἐντός Il.; ἐντὸς Ὀλύμπου Hes., etc.; ἐντὸς ἐμαυτοῦ in my senses, Hdt.; so absol., ἐντὸς ὤν Dem.:—also with Verbs of motion, τείχεος ἐντὸς ἰέναι Il.
within, i. e. on this side, Lat. citra, ἐντὸς τοῦ Ἄλυος ποταμοῦ Hdt., etc.
of Time, within, ἐντὸς εἴκοσιν ἡμερῶν Thuc.; ἐντὸς ἑσπέρας short of, i. e. before, evening, Xen.
absol. within, ἐντὸς ἐέργειν Hom.; ἐντὸς ἔχειν Thuc.; τὰ ἐντός the inner parts, inwards, Id.
metaph. from the touchstone, proved by rubbing, versed in a thing, c. dat., Soph.
to rub in or into a thing, c. dat., Luc.
metaph., ἐντρ. κόνδυλόν τινι to give him a drubbing, Plut.; so in Mid., Luc.
c. acc. pers. to rub one with cosmetics, Xen.:—Pass. to have cosmetics rubbed in, to be anointed, painted, Id.
to wear away by rubbing, Ar.
a cosmetic, Plut.
to third with water, i. e. to mix three parts of water with two of wine, —with a pun on ἡ Τριτογενής, Ar.
hairy, Anth.
a rubbing in, Xen.
trembling, Plut., NTest.
to keep turning round, of men retreating, Il.
a turning towards, ἐντροπήν τινος ἔχειν respect or reverence for one, Soph.: shame, reproach, NTest.
a trick, dodge, Hhymn.
living in or acquainted with a thing, c. dat., Soph.
as Subst., nursling, Anth.
to revel in a thing, c. dat., Menand.: —absol. to be luxurious, Xen.
to mock at, τινί Eur.
to eat greedily, to gobble up, Ar.:—c. gen. to eat greedily of, Luc.

entry.note: fut. -τεύξομαι aor2 ἐνέτῠχον perf. ἐντετύχηκα aor1 pass. part. ἐντευχθείς
entry.sense: in act. sense:— to light upon, fall in with, meet with a person or thing, c. dat., Hdt., etc.:—absol., ὁ ἐντυχών the first who meets us, any chance person, Thuc.; of thunder, to fall upon, c. dat., Xen.; so of misfortunes, Aesch.
rarely, like τυγχάνω c. gen., λελυμένης τῆς γεφύρης ἐντυχόντες having found the bridge broken up, Hdt.; ἐντυχὼν Ἀσκληπιδῶν having fallen in with them, Soph.
to converse with, talk to, τινί Plat.
to intercede with, intreat, τινί NTest., Plut.:—c. inf. to intreat one to do, Id.
of books, to meet with, Plat.: hence, to read, Luc.
to wrap up, Ar.

entry.note: imperf. ἔντῡνον fut. ἐντῠνῶ aor1 ἔντῡνα ἐντύω imperf. ἔντυον
entry.sense: to equip, deck out, get ready, Hom.; δέπας δ’ ἔντυνον (aor1 imperat.) prepare the cup, i. e. mix the wine, Il.; εὖ ἐντύνασαν ἓ αὐτήν having decked herself well out, Id.:—Mid., ὄφρα τάχιστα ἐντύνεαι (epic for ἐντύνῃ) may'st get thee ready, Od.:—Mid., c. acc., to prepare for oneself, ἐντύνεσθαι δαῖτα, δεῖπνον Hom.
adv., ἐντυπὰς ἐν χλαίνῃ κεκαλυμμένος (of Priam in his grief), wrapt up in his mantle so closely as to shew his limbs, Il.
to cut in intaglio, Plut.
to smoke as one does wasps, Ar.
the Warlike, name of Ares (Mars), Il., Soph., etc.
as appellat. war, battle, Eur.
as adj. warlike, furious, Theocr.
to insult or mock one in a thing, c. dat., Soph.; τινὰ ἐν κακοῖς Eur.
an otter, Hdt.
living in the water, Anth.
with water in it, holding water, ἔν. τεῦχος, i. e. a bath, Aesch.; of countries, well watered, Hdt.; ἔν. φρούριον provided with water, Xen.
of water, watery, Eur.
living in or by water, of Nymphs, Soph.; of plants, Ar.
a thing seen in sleep, ἐνύπνιον ἦλθεν ὄνειρος a dream or vision in sleep came to me, Od.:—hence as adv., ἐνύπνιον ἑστιᾶσθαι "to feast with the Barmecide," Ar.
simply a dream, Hdt., attic
in dreams appearing, Aesch.
to weave in as a pattern:—Pass. to be inwoven, Hdt.
inwoven, Theocr.
Enyo, goddess of war, answering to the Roman Bellona, Il., Aesch.
to thrust in or upon, Plut., Luc.
leader of an ἐνωμοτία, Thuc., Xen.
a band of sworn soldiers, a company in the Spartan army, the λόχος contained 4 πεντηκοστύες, each πεντηκοστύς 4 ἐνωμοτίαι, and each ἐνωμοτία 32 men, Thuc., Xen.
bound by oath, Soph.:—adv. -τως, on oath, Plut.
a conspirator, Id.
in one's face, to one's face, Od.
the face, countenance, dat. ἐνωπῇ as adv., before the face, openly, Il.
the inner wall fronting those who enter a building or the side-walls of the entrance, Hom.
face to face, Theocr.
neut. ἐνώπιον, prep. with gen., like Lat. coram, NTest.
Dep. to hearken to a thing, τι NTest.
information sent out to the enemy, Xen.

to send out tidings, report, of traitors and the like, Il., attic:—Mid. to cause to be proclaimed, Hdt., Soph.; c. inf. to promise to do, Eur.: —Pass. to be reported, Hdt.; impers., ἐξαγγέλλεται it is reported, Id.
a messenger who brings out news from within, an informer, Thuc., etc.
on the Greek stage, ἄγγελοι told news from a distance, ἐξάγγελοι what was a-doing behind the scenes, as in Soph.
told of, denounced, Thuc.
to drive out as accursed:—Pass., aor1 part. ἐξαγισθείς, Aesch.
to lead forth, Hdt.
devoted to evil, accursed, abominable, Dem., Aeschin.
ἐξάγιστα holy things, matters of religion, Soph.
to break and tear away, to rend, Il.
to buy up, Plut.
to redeem, NTest.; so in Mid., Id.
fit to explain, τινος Luc.

entry.etym: the aor. is supplied by ἐξεῖπον, the fut. and perf. by ἐξερῶ, ἐξείρηκα
entry.sense: to tell out, make known, declare, Od.: to betray a secret or mystery, Hdt.
to make savage, Plat.:—Pass. to be or become savage, Id.
to make wild or waste:—Pass. to be or be made so, Aeschin.
like ἐξ-αγριαίνω to make savage, exasperate, Hdt., Eur.
to lead out:
of persons, to lead or carry out from a place, Hom., etc.: to bring forth into the world, Il.: to lead out to execution, Hdt.
to march out (sub. στρατόν), Xen.: generally, to go out, Id.
to eject a claimant from property, Dem., etc.
of merchandise, to carry out, export, Ar., etc.:—Pass., τὰ ἐξαγόμενα exports, Xen.
to draw off water, Id.
of building, to carry further out, Thuc.
to call forth, excite, δάκρυ Eur.:—Mid., γέλωτα ἐξάγεσθαι Xen.
to lead on, carry away, excite, τινά Eur., Thuc.; and in bad sense, to lead on, tempt, Id.:—Pass. to be led on, c. inf., Xen.
a leading out of soldiers, Xen.
a drawing out of a ship to sea, Hdt.
a carrying out, exportation, Id., attic
Dep. to struggle hard, Eur.
beside the mark, irrelevant, Luc.
leader of a body of six, Xen.
to sing out, sing one's last song, of the swan, Plat.
trans. to sing of, laud, Eur.
to make into air, volatilise, Luc.
six years old: fem. ἑξαέτις, Theocr.
of six years, χρόνος Plut.:—adv., ἑξάετες, for six years, Od.
Mid. to seek out and collect, Eur.
to be quite disheartened, Plut.
to wail loudly, Eur.
to make quite bloody, Xen.
epic Dep. to carry off, Od.; c. dupl. acc., ἐξαίνυτο θυμὸν ἀμφοτέρω took away life from both, Il.
a taking out, Hdt.:— a way of taking out, Id.
to be taken out or removed, Xen.
ἐξαιρετέον, one must take out: one must pick out, select, Id.
that can be taken out, removable, Hdt.
ἐξαίρετος, ον taken out, picked out, chosen, Lat. eximius, Hom., etc.
excepted, Eur., Thuc., etc.: special, remarkable, Dem.

entry.note: fut. ήσω aor2 ἐξεῖλον epic ἔξελον inf. ἐξελεῖν Pass., perf. ἐξῄρημαι ionic -αραίρημαι
entry.sense: to take out of a thing, τί τινος Hom., etc.; ἔκ τινος Hdt., etc.:—simply to take out, νηδύν Id.:—Mid. to take out for oneself, Il.; ἐξ. τὰ φορτία to discharge their cargoes, Hdt.

to take from among others, to pick out, choose, Hom., etc.:—Mid. to choose for oneself, carry off as booty, Id.:—Pass. to be given as a special honour, τινι to one, Thuc.; ἐξαραιρημένος Ποσειδέωνι dedicated to him, Hdt.
to take out of a number, to except, Id., attic
to expel people from their seats, Hdt., Thuc.
to take out, remove, Hdt., attic

in Mid. to bereave a person of life, c. dupl. acc., μιν ἐξείλετο θυμόν Il., attic; or c. gen. pers., μευ φρένας ἐξέλετο Il.; rarely c. dat. pers., Id.:—Mid. to take away from one, Soph.:—Pass., ἐξαιρεθέντες τὸν Δημοκήδεα having had him taken out of their hands, Hdt.
in Mid. to set free, deliver, Aesch., Dem.
to make away with, annul, Soph.: to demolish a city, Hdt., etc.
to bring to an end, accomplish, Eur.
to lift up, lift off the earth, Hom., Hdt.; ἐξάραντες having bade me rise (from suppliant posture), Soph.
to raise in dignity, exalt, Hdt., Aeschin.
to raise, arouse, stir up, Theogn., Soph.; ἐξ. σε θανεῖν excites thy wish to die, Eur.
Mid., 3rd sg. aor1 ἐξήρατο, to carry off for oneself, earn, win, gain, Od.
to take on oneself, Soph.
Pass. to be raised, Hdt.: to rise up, rise, Eur.:— to be excited, agitated, Soph.
beyond what is ordained or fated: hence,
lawless, Od.
extraordinary, violent, Hdt., Xen.; ἐξ. φυγή headlong flight, Id.
to rush forth, start out from, c. gen., Il.; ἐκ τοῦ νεώ Ar.:—so in Pass., Il.
to utterly destroy, Aesch.

to demand or ask for from another, c. dupl. acc., τήνδε μ’ ἐξαιτεῖ χάριν Soph.; ἐξ. τινα πατρός to ask her in marriage from . . , Id.:— ἐξ. τινα to demand the surrender of a person, Hdt., Dem.;— σμικρὸν ἐξ. to beg for little, Soph.
Mid. to ask for oneself, demand, Hdt., Soph., etc.
in Mid. also, = παραιτοῦμαι, to beg off, gain his pardon or release, Lat. exorare, Aesch., Xen.; c. inf. to beg that one may obtain, Eur.:—c. acc. rei, to avert by begging, Lat. deprecari, Id.
a demanding one for punishment, Dem.
intercession, Id.
much asked for, much desired, choice, excellent, Hom.
adv. on a sudden, Il., attic; ἐξ. ἀποθανόντος, the moment he is dead, Plat.
Dep. to heal completely, heal the wound, make amends, Il.
c. acc. to appease, Hom.; to make up for, Xen.
to mend clothes, Plat.
a thorough cure, Ar.
sixty thousand, Hdt., Xen.
six times, Lat. sexies, Plat., etc.: poet. ἑξάκι, Anth.
six thousand, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
to dart or hurl forth, Xen.; φάσγανον πρὸς ἧπαρ ἐξ. to strike it home, Eur.
metaph., ἐξ. κῶλον τῆς γῆς i. e. to flee precipitately, Id.; τοὺς πόνους ἐξ. to proclaim loudly, Id.
six hundred, Hdt.
to hear a sound, esp. from a distance, Aesch., Soph.; c. gen. pers., Xen.; rei, Plut.
to make exact, ἐξ. λόγον to make a distinct or precise statement, Soph.
to reach the top of, ἐξ. αἰθέρα to skim the upper air, Eur.
one must march out, Xen.
to blind utterly, Od.
to put an eye quite out, Id.
to sack a city, Il., etc.:—also, to empty a city of its inhabitants, clear it out, so as to plant new settlers in it, μίαν πόλιν ἐξαλαπάξας Od.: generally, to destroy utterly, Il.
an unguent-box, Ar.

entry.note: fut. ψω Pass. perf. ἐξ-ήλιμμαι attic -αλήλιμμαι
entry.sense: to plaster or wash over, Hdt., Thuc.
to wipe out, obliterate, Eur.:— ἐξ. τινά to strike his name off the roll, Ar., etc.
metaph., like Lat. delere, to wipe out, destroy utterly, Aesch., Eur.:—Mid., ἐξαλείψασθαι φρενός to blot it out of one's mind, Id.
Dep. to beware of, avoid, escape, Il.; epic aor1 inf. ἐξαλέασθαι, Hes., Ar., Soph.

entry.note: only in aor1 part. ἐξαλίσας perf. ἐξήλῑκα
entry.sense: to roll out or thoroughly, ἄπαγε τὸν ἵππον ἐξαλίσας take him away when you have given him a good roll on the ἀλινδήθρα, Ar.; ἐξήλικας ἐμέ γ’ ἐκ τῶν ἐμῶν you have rolled me out of house and home, Id.
a complete change, alteration, Plat.
to change utterly or completely, Eur.:—Mid., μηδὲν ἐξαλλάσσεται he sees no change take place, Soph.
to withdraw from a place, c. acc., Eur.
ἐξαλλάσσειν τί τινος to remove from, c. gen., Thuc.
intr. to change, turn another way, move back and forward, Eur.; ποίαν ἐξαλλάξω; which other way shall I take? Id.; ἐξαλλάσσουσα χάρις unusual grace, Id.

Dep.:— to leap out of or forth from a place, c. gen., Il.; προμάχων ἐξάλμενος springing out from the front rank, Id.; ἐξάλατο ναός (doric for ἐξήλατο νηός) Theocr.:—absol. to jump off, hop off, Ar.; ἵν’ ἐξήλλου; to what point didst thou leap forth, i. e. to what misery hast thou come? Soph.; of wheels, to start from the axle, Xen.
to leap up. Id.: of horses, to rear, Id.

entry.note: fut. ύξω aor1 ἐξήλυξα like ἐξαλέομαι
entry.sense: to flee from, c. acc., Eur.; absol. to escape, Aesch., Eur.
to err from the mark, fail, Xen.: to miss one's aim, Soph.
to err, do wrong, sin, Hdt., attic; c. acc. cogn., ἐξ. τι to commit a fault, Hdt., Soph., etc.
in Pass. to be mismanaged, Plat.
an error, transgression, Soph.
to mow or reap out, to finish mowing or reaping, Trag.:—metaph. to cut out, in Mid., Eur.:—Pass., γένους ῥίζαν ἐξημημένος (part. perf.) having the race cut off root and branch, Soph.
= ἐξαφύσσω.
to make to miscarry, Eur.
to make abortive, Ar.
to blunt, weaken, Plut.
to exchange, alter, ἐξαμείψασαι τρόμον having put away fear from one, Eur.:—Mid. to take the place of, c. gen., Id.; so intr. in Act., c. dat., φόνῳ φόνος ἐξαμείβων murder following after murder, Id.
of Place, to change one for another, pass over, c. acc., Aesch., Eur.: absol. to withdraw, depart, Id.
in Mid. also to requite, repay, Aesch.
to milk out, suck out, Aesch.
to press out, Eur.
to be utterly careless of a thing, c. gen., Hdt.
of six metres, hexameter, Hdt., etc.
of, lasting six months: ἑξάμ. (sc. χρόνος), a half-year, Xen.; ἡ ἑξάμ. (sc. ὥρη), Hdt.
to get out of a difficulty, c. gen., Eur.

entry.note: fut. ήσομαι aor1 part. ἐξαμιλλησάμενος and -ηθείς
entry.sense: Dep.:— to struggle vehemently, c. acc. cogn., τὰς τεθρίππους ἁμίλλας ἐξαμιλληθείς having contested the chariot-race, Eur.
to drive out of a place, c. gen., Id.: to drive out of his wits, Id.
aor1 in pass. sense, to be forced out, of the Cyclops' eye, Id.
Mid. to ward off from oneself, drive away, Aesch., Eur.
to gush or cause to gush forth, Aesch.
to read through, Plut.
to force or compel utterly, τινὰ ποιεῖν τι Soph., Eur., etc.; c. acc. only, Soph.
to drive away, Xen.
to bring out of or up from, c.gen., Eur.:—Pass. to put out to sea, set sail, Hdt., etc.
Dep. , to rise out of, emerge from water, c. gen., Od.
to escape from, c. gen., Theogn., Plut.
to boil up with, c. acc. cogn., ἐξαναζέσει χόλον will let fury boil forth, Aesch.
to take out of, c. gen., Hhymn.; Mid., Eur.
Mid. to retreat out of a place by backing water, Hdt.
to spend entirely, Dem.:— to exhaust, Plut.
to destroy utterly, Aesch.:—Pass., Dem.
to set quite free from, c.gen., Il.
entire consumption, Plut.
to hang from or by a thing, c. gen., Eur.:—Mid. to attach to oneself, τι Id.
to rekindle, Anth.
to snatch away, Eur.
to tear away from, Hdt., Eur.: to tear up from, χθονός Id.
a rising up from, resurrection from the dead, NTest.
to crown with wreaths, Eur.
to hurl headlong from a place, c. gen., Aesch.
intr. to spring up from a place, c. gen., Mosch.
all openly, Od.
to bear up out of the water, Plut.
intr. to recover from an illness, Id.
to go out of the way, withdraw, retreat, Hdt.
c. acc. to evade, Thuc.
to reduce to utter slavery, Hdt., Xen., etc.
also as Pass., Hdt., Dem.
a selling for slaves, Hdt.
Pass. to come to man's years, Hdt., Eur.
ὀδόντων ὄφεος ἐξηνδρωμένος having grown to men from serpent's teeth, Id.
to excite, Eur.
to rise from the horizon, of stars, Theocr.
to come back from, ἄγρης Hhymn.
to blow out with wind, inflate, Eur.: —metaph., ἐξηνεμώθην I was puffed up, Id.
to come forth from, c. gen., Eur.
to find out, invent, Soph.
to hold up from: but mostly intr. to jut out from, c. gen., Theocr.

Mid., imperf. and aor2 with double augm. ἐξηνειχόμην, ἐξηνεσχόμην, to bear up against, endure, with part., ἐξανασχοίμην κλύων Soph.; ταῦτα παῖδας ἐξανέξεται πάσχοντας Eur.; ταῦτα δόξαντ’ ἐξηνέσχετο endured that these things should be decreed, Id.
to put out flowers, Xen.
metaph. to burst forth, like an efflorescence, bloom forth, Aesch., Eur.:—of ulcers, to break out, Thuc., Luc.
to send forth, let loose, Il., Soph.:—c. gen. to send forth from, Eur.
to let go, Id.
to slacken, undo, Id.:—and intr. to slacken, relax, Soph.; c. gen., ὀργῆς ἐξανείς Eur.
Causal in pres., imperf., fut. and aor 1,

one must trace out, Luc.
to trace out, Aesch., Eur.
to seek by tracking, Soph.; so in Mid., Id.
of, holding six medimni, Ar.

to make to swell: metaph., μητέρα τάφῳ ἐξογκοῦν to honour her by raising a tomb, Eur.: Pass. to be swelled out, πάντα ἐξώγκωτο he had all his garments stuffed out, Hdt.:—metaph. to be puffed up, elated, Id., Eur.; τὰ ἐξωγκωμένα full-sailed prosperity, Id.; so in fut. mid., Id.
anything swollen, ἐξ. λάϊνον a mound of stones, Eur.
to sell, Eur.
of or belonging to an exit:—as Subst., ἐξόδιον (sc. μέλος), the finale of a tragedy, Plut.: metaph. a catastrophe, Id.
to get out of, c. gen., Soph.
a going out, Hdt., attic
a marching out, military expedition, Hdt., attic
a solemn procession, Hdt., Dem.
a way out, outlet, Lat. exitus, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
like Lat. exitus, an end, close, Thuc., Xen.: the end or issue of an argument, Plat.: absol. departure, death, NTest.
the end of a tragedy, or music played at its close, Ar.
to pain greatly, Eur.
intr. to smell, κακὸν ἐξόσδειν (doric) to smell foully, Theocr.

entry.note: -οισθα, ἔξ-οιδα perf. in pres. sense, plup. ἐξῄδη as impf., 2nd sg. -ῄδησθα:
entry.sense: to know thoroughly, know well, Il., Soph., etc.
to swell or be swollen up, Eur., Luc.
to emigrate, Dem.
Pass. to be completely inhabited, Thuc.
habitable, inhabited, Soph.
to remove one from his home, eject, banish, Eur., Thuc.:—Pass. and Mid. to go from home, remove, emigrate, Ar., Aeschin.
to dispeople, empty, Eur.
to build completely, finish a building, Hdt., Ar.
to wail aloud, Soph.
Pass. to be drunk, perf. part. ἐξῳνωμένος drunken, Eur.
to be brought out: ἐξοιστέον, one must bring out, Eur.
to make wild, madden, Luc.
to go out or forth, ἐξοιχνεῦσι (ionic for -οῦσι), Il.
to have gone out, to be quite gone, Il., Soph.
Dep. to avoid as ill-omened, Plut.
intr., of a ship, to run aground or ashore, Hdt., Aesch.
trans. to run (a ship) aground:—metaph. to drive headlong, Eur.
to glide off, slip away, Il.: to glance off, as a spear from a hard substance, Eur.: to slip out, escape, Ar.:—c. acc. to elude, Id.
to destroy utterly, Od., Eur., etc.
Mid., with perf. 2 ἐξόλωλα, to perish utterly, Soph., etc.
to destroy utterly, NTest.
to howl aloud, Batr.
to smooth away, Babr.
a demand of hostages, Plut.
Mid. to take as hostages, Plut.
to have intercourse, live with, τινί Xen.: to bear one company, Eur.
Mid. to be away from one's friends, be alone in the crowd, Id.
out of one's own society, alien, Soph.
to open the eyes of: Pass. to be restored to sight, Soph. ap. Ar.
metaph. to make clear or plain, Aesch.
to swear in excuse, Dem.: to swear in the negative, ἐξ. τὸ μὴ εἰδέναι Soph.:—mostly in Mid., to deny or disown upon oath, swear formally that one does not know a thing, Dem., etc.
to decline an office by oath that one cannot perform it, Aeschin., etc.
to make quite like, to assimilate, Hdt., Plat.:—Pass. to become or be like, Soph., Eur.
a becoming like, Plut.
Dep. to confess in full, Plut., NTest.
to make full acknowledgments, give thanks, Id.
in Act. to agree, promise, Id.
to wipe off from, Eur.:— Mid. to wipe off from oneself, purge away a pollution, Id.
metaph., ἐξομόρξασθαί τινι μωρίαν to wipe off one's folly on another, i. e. give him part of it, Id.
to stamp or imprint upon, Plat.
c. acc. rei, to cast in one's teeth, Soph., Eur.; ἐξονειδισθεὶς κακά having foul reproaches cast upon one, Soph.:—simply, to bring forward, Lat. objicere, Eur.
c. acc. pers. to reproach, Soph.
to utter aloud, announce, Hom.
to call by name, Plut.
to name, speak of by name, Hom.
by name, calling by name, Hom.
behind, in rear, Il.
as prep. with gen. behind, ἐξ. κεράων Id.
attic for ἐξόπιθεν, Ar.
as prep. with gen., Id.
of Place, backwards, back again, Il.
as prep. with gen. behind, Id.
of Time, hereafter, Od.
to arm completely, accoutre, Hdt., Xen.: —Mid. and Pass. to arm or accoutre oneself, Eur.: to get under arms, stand in armed array, Id., Xen.:— generally, ἐξωπλισμένος fully prepared, all ready, Ar.
a being under arms, Xen.
a getting under arms, Xen.
to bake thoroughly, Hdt., Eur.
to heat violently, Hdt.
to see from afar: Pass., Eur.
to enrage, Xen., Aeschin.:—Pass. to be furious, Batr.
to lift up the voice, to cry aloud, Aesch.
to set upright: metaph. to set right, secure, restore, Soph.: Pass., Eur.
to send beyond the frontier, banish, Lat. exterminare, Eur., etc.
to expose a child, Id.
to get rid of a thing, Plat.
c. acc. loci only, ἄλλην ἀπ’ ἄλλης ἐξ. πόλιν to pass from one to another, Eur.
in Pass. to come forth from, τινος Id.
to exasperate, Aesch.
expelled, banished, Dem.
to adjure, NTest.
an exorcist, NTest.
