to cause to forget a thing, c. gen., Od.: —Pass. to be forgotten, perf. part. ἐπιλελησμένος NTest.

Mid. ἐπι-λήθομαι and -λανθάνομαι, fut. -λήσομαι: aor2 -ελᾰθόμην: with perf. act. -λέληθα and pass. -λέλησμαι: plup. -ελελήσμην: — to let a thing escape one, to forget, lose thought of, c. gen., ὅπως Ἰθάκης ἐπιλήσεται (epic for -ηται) Od.; so Hdt., attic:—also c. acc., Hdt., Eur., etc.:—c. inf., Ar., Plat.
to forget wilfully, ἑκὼν ἐπιλήθομαι Hdt.
obtained as booty, Xen.
to beat time to dancers, Od.
nickname of the Tragic muse, the bombastical, Anth.
caught or detected in anything, Soph.; c. part., ἐπίλαμπτος ἀφάσσουσα caught in the act of feeling, Hdt.
suffering, Dem.
a censurer, Timo ap. Plut.
forgetfulness, NTest.
apt to forget, forgetful, Ar., Plat., etc.; c. gen. rei, Xen., in comp. ἐπιλησμονέστερος, whereas Ar. has ἐπιλησμότατος (as if from ἐπίλησμος).
a seizing, seizure, Plat.
epilepsy, Lat. morbus comitialis.
grazing, Il.
Pass. to be overflowed, Plut.
to make fat or sleek, Plut.
to make signs to one by winking, Od.: to wink roguishly, Hhymn.
Dep., to reckon over, conclude, ὅτι . . Hdt.; ἐπ. τι to take account of a thing, Xen.
a conclusion, inference, Hdt.
barbed, Eur.
still left, remaining, Hdt., attic
of Time, to come, future, χρόνος Hdt., Plat., etc.
to annoy or offend besides, τινα Hdt.
release from a thing, c. gen., Aesch.
to loose, untie, Theocr.: to set free, release, Luc.: so in Mid., Plat.; ἐπιλύεσθαι ἐπιστολάς to open letters, Hdt.
to mock at a thing, Od.
to be mad after, dote upon, c. dat., Il., Ar.:—absol. to be mad, to rage, Aesch.
to attack furiously, τινι Anth.
Dep.
to strive after, seek to obtain, aim at, c. gen., σκοπέλου ἐπιμαίεο make for (i. e. steer for) the rock, Od.; metaph., ἐπιμαίεο νόστου strive after a return, Id.
c. acc. to lay hold of, grasp, ἐπεμαίετο κώπην he clutched his sword-hilt, Id.; χείρ’ (i. e. χειρὶ) ἐπιμασσάμενος having clutched [the sword] with my hand, Id.
to handle, feel, Id.; ἕλκος ἰητὴρ ἐπιμάσσεται will probe the wound, Il.
to learn besides or after, Hdt., Thuc.
to bear witness to a thing, to depose, Plat., etc.
in Mid. to adjure, τινὶ μὴ ποιεῖν τι Hdt.
a witness, testimony, Thuc.
Dep.
to call to witness, appeal to, τοὺς θεούς Xen.:—also, to call a person as one's witness, Lat. antestari, Ar.
to call on earnestly, to conjure, Lat. obtestari, Hdt.; ἐπιμ. τινα μὴ ποιεῖν τι to call on one not to do, Id.
to affirm or declare before witnesses that . . , Dem.
a witness to one's word, Hom.
Mid. to knead again, stroke, Anth.
at the breast, not yet weaned, Trag.
seeking for help, begging, Od.
to help one in war, τῇ ἀλλήλων ἐπιμαχεῖν to make a league for the mutual defence of their countries, Thuc.
a defensive alliance, Thuc., Dem.
easily attacked, assailable, Hdt., Thuc., etc.: of a country, open to attack, Id.
to smile at, ἐπιμειδήσας προσέφη addressed him with a smile, Il.
to smile upon, Xen.
still larger or greater, Democr.
care, attention, attic Prose; also in Hdt.; pl. cares, pains, Xen., etc.:—c. gen. care for a thing, attention paid to it, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; also, περί τινος Id.; πρός τινα or τι Dem.
a public charge or commission, Lat. procuratio, Aeschin.: any pursuit, Lat. studium, Xen., etc.

to take care of, have charge of, have the management of a thing, c. gen., Hdt., attic; περί τινος, ὑπέρ τινος Xen.:—c. acc. et inf. to take care that . . , Thuc., etc.; so, ἐπ. ὅπως Plat.:—absol. to give heed, attend, Hdt.
in public offices, to be curator of, Xen., Plat.
a care, anxiety, Xen.
careful or anxious about, put in charge of a thing, c. gen., Plat., Xen.:— τὸ ἐπιμελές τινος = ἐπιμέλεια, Thuc.
absol. careful, attentive, Ar., Xen.
Pass. cared for, an object of care, Hdt.; ἐπιμελές μοι ἦν it was my business, Id., attic
one must take care, pay attention, Plat., Xen.
one who has charge of a thing, a governor, manager, curator, superintendent, Ar., Xen., etc.
able to take charge, managing, Xen.
to sing to, Aesch.
to desire to do a thing, Soph.

Dep. to cast blame upon a person, c. dat., Od., Hdt., etc.; rarely c. acc. pers., Soph.:—c. gen. rei, to find fault for or because of a thing, complain of it, εὐχωλῆς ἐπιμέμφεται complains of the vow [neglected], Il.:—absol. to find fault, complain, Hdt., etc.
to impute as matter of blame, τί τινι Id.
to stay on, tarry or abide still, Hom., attic; ἐπίμεινον wait, Il.

to continue in a pursuit, ἐπί τινι Plat., etc.
to abide by, ταῖς σπονδαῖς Xen.
c. acc. to await, Eur., Plat.; so c. inf., Thuc.
Mid. to send for a reinforcement, Thuc.
to measure out besides, Hes.:— Pass., ὁ ἐπιμετρούμενος σῖτος the corn paid by measure to the Persians, Hdt.
to add to the measure, give over and above, Plut., Luc.
over-measure, excess, Theocr.
Dep. to contrive against one, τί τινι Od.
Epi-metheus, after-thought, brother of Pro-metheus, fore-thought, Hes.
thoughtful, Theocr.
like Epimetheus, Eust.
longish, oblong, Luc.
flock-protectors, Nymphs, Theocr.
monthly: as Subst., ἐπιμήνια, τά, (sub. ἱερά), monthly offerings, Hdt.
to be angry with, Πριάμῳ ἐπεμήνῐε Il.

to devise besides, Xen.
craftily devising, κακῶν ἐπιμήχανος ἔργων contriver of ill deeds, Orac. ap. Hdt.
to add to by mixing, mix with, τί τινι Plat.
intr. to mingle with others, to have intercourse or dealings with them, τισί Thuc.; πρός τινας Xen.:—so also in Pass., ἐπιμίγνυσθαι ἀλλήλοις Id.; παρ’ ἀλλήλους Thuc.
ἐπιμίσγω,older form of ἐπιμίγνυμι

intr. to have intercourse, παρ’ ἀλλήλους Thuc.:—so Pass. in same sense, c. dat. pers., Od., Hdt., etc.; αἰεὶ Τρώεσς’ ἐπιμίσγομαι I have always to be dealing with the Trojans, am always clashing with them, Il.: absol. to associate together, Hdt., Thuc.

fated, Anth.
to come upon, befall, Soph.
an invader, Aesch.
inclined to blame, Eur.
blameable, unlucky, Aesch.
a staying on, tarrying, delay, Thuc.
to murmur at one's words, Il.
Dep. to say besides, Il.
coming after the fable: τὸ ἐπ. the moral, Luc.
scoffed at, Theogn.
to wink in token of assent, Ar.
blameworthy, Hes., Theocr.
the sea-port where the navy lies, the state harbour, Hdt., Thuc.
a spreading, Plut.
to allot, distribute, Hom.

to turn one's cattle to graze over the boundaries, Plat.:—in Mid., of cattle, to feed over the boundaries, trespass on one's neighbour's lands: metaph., of fire, to spread over a place, Hdt.:—so of an infectious disease, Thuc.; in Pass., ὅρος ἐπινέμεται the boundary is exposed to encroachment, Aesch.: cf. ἐπινομία.
to nod, in token of approval, to nod assent, Il.; ἐπ. τι to approve, sanction, promise, Eur.; ἐπένευσεν ἀληθὲς εἶναι he nodded in sign that it was true, Aeschin.

to incline towards, Ar.
clouded, overcast, ἐπινεφέλων ὄντων (gen. absol.) the weather being cloudy, Hdt.
upon the kidneys, Il.
to allot by spinning, of the Fates, Il.
to heap up or load with a thing, c. gen., Hdt.
to float on the top.
on board ship, Anth.
to heap or pile upon a thing, c. gen., Il.
Dep. to swim upon, Batr.; ἐπενάχετο φωνά the voice came up to earth, Theocr.
of victory, triumphal, Pind., etc.
as Subst., ἐπινίκιον (sc. μέλος), a song of victory, triumphal ode, Aesch.
ἐπινίκια (sc. ἱερά), τά, a sacrifice for a victory or feast in honour of it, Plat., etc.

Dep. to go over, c. gen., Soph.
to visit, Theocr.
to snow upon: impers., ἐπινίφει fresh snow falls, or it keeps snowing, Xen.
to think on or of, contrive, Hdt., attic: —c. inf., Ar.:—absol. to form plans, to plan, invent, Thuc.
to have in one's mind, intend, purpose, Id., etc.: c. inf., Hdt., Xen.
aor1 pass. ἐπινοήθην is used like Act., Hdt.

a grazing over the boundaries: — metaph., ἐπ. πυρός the spreading of fire, Plut.
a grazing over the boundaries: a mutual right of pasture, vested in the citizens of two neighbouring states, Xen.

of or for a bride, bridal, Anth.

on the back, Batr.
inclining to yellow, tawny, of hares, Xen.

a common, Il.
at or over wine, Theogn.
to pour out wine for others, Hhymn.
to swear falsely, forswear oneself, πρὸς δαίμονος by a deity, Il.; c. acc., τοὺς θεούς by the gods, Ar., Xen.

Dep. to have before one's eyes, Il.
an over-keeper, a guardian, watcher, ward, c. gen., ὑῶν ἐπίουρος Od., etc.; c. dat., Κρήτῃ ἐπ. guardian over Crete, of Minos, Il.
for the coming day, sufficient for the day, NTest. (From ἡ ἐπιοῦσα [ἡμέρα] the coming day.)
altogether, Theocr.
to sing a paean over, Plut.
to brandish at or against, Aesch.
ἐπὶ, πᾶν, adv. upon the whole, in general, on the average, Hdt., Thuc.; ὡς ἐπίπαν, also τὸ ἐπ. and ὡς τὸ ἐπ. Hdt.
altogether, Aesch.
to heap up still more, to heap up, Thuc.
Mid. to provide oneself with besides, Xen.
to be present besides or in addition, Thuc.
to march on high ground parallel with one below, Xen., etc.:— to assail in flank, c. dat., Thuc.
to come to one's assistance, Id., Xen.

to sprinkle upon or over, Hdt.
sprinkled overas Subst. ἐπίπαστον, τό, a kind of cake with comfits (or the like) upon it, Ar.
a plaster, Theocr.
to the level of the ground, level, Xen., etc.:—irreg. comp. -πεδέστερος, Id.
to be persuaded to a certain end, Hom.
to trust to, put faith in, c. dat., Aesch.
to comply with, obey, Hes., Soph.
to bring near to, Eur.
Dep., to come to or upon a person, c. dat., Od.; epic syncop. part. aor2 ἐπιπλόμενος, coming on, approaching, ἐπιπλόμενον ἔτος the coming year, Id.; of a storm, like Lat. ingruens, Soph.
to send besides or again, of messages, Hdt.
of the gods, to send upon or to, Id.; esp.by way of punishment, to send upon or against, let loose upon, Eur., Plat.
a sending to a place, Thuc.
to turn dark, of grapes ripening; ἐπιπερκάζειν τριχί to begin to get a dark beard, Anth.

to spread over, Xen.

entry.note: fut. -πτήσομαι aor2 ἐπεπτάμην or -όμην also in act. form ἐπέπτην part. ἐπιπτάς

to fly to or towards, Hom., etc.
c. acc. to fly over, πεδία Eur., Ar.
ἐφίπταμαι, late pres. of ἐπιπέτομαι, Mosch.
to freeze at top, Xen.
to leap upon, assault, Ar., Plat.
to press upon, press down, Od.
Dep. to come near, Od.
to fill full of, τί τινος Ar.
to drink afterwards or besides, esp. to drink after eating, Od., attic
to fall upon or over another, c. dat., Thuc.
to fall upon, attack, assail, τινί Hdt., Thuc., etc.; of storms, Hdt., Plat.: of disease and accidents, Thuc., Eur.

entry.etym: from ἐπί, as δίπλα from δίς
entry.sense: implements, utensils, furniture, moveable property, Hdt., attic
Pass.:— to wander about over, πόντον ἐπιπλαγχθείς Od.
to spread as a plaster over, Hdt.

to applaud loudly, τινί Theocr.
to wreathe into a chaplet, Anth.
Pass. to be interwoven with, Luc.
quite full of a thing, c. gen., Hdt.

entry.note: ionic -πλώω fut. -πλεύσομαι epic 2nd sg. aor2 ἐπέπλως part. ἐπιπλώς aor1 part. ἐπιπλώσας
entry.sense: to sail upon or over, πόντον Hom.
to sail against, to attack by sea, c. dat., Hdt., Thuc.
to sail on board, Id.
to float on the surface, Hdt.
rebuke, reproof, Aeschin.
to fill up again:—Mid., ἐπιπληρωσόμεθα τὰς ναῦς we shall man our ships afresh, Thuc.
to strike at, strike smartly, Il.
to chastise with words, to rebuke, reprove, c. acc., Id., Plat.; also c. dat., Il.
ἐπ. τί τινι to cast a thing in one's teeth, Hdt., Aesch.:— c. acc. rei only, Soph.
the membrane enclosing the entrails, the caul, Lat. omentum, Hdt.
a sailing against, bearing down upon, Thuc., Xen.
of friends, a sailing towards, approach, Thuc.
to breathe upon, to blow freshly upon, Il.; τινί on one, Ar.:— to blow fairly for one, τινί Od.
to blow furiously upon, τινί Hdt., Aesch.
c. acc. to blow over, Hes.
metaph. to excite, inflame, τινά τινι one against another, Eur.; τινὰ αἵματι one to slaughter, Id.
to inspire into, Anth.
a breathing upon, inspiration, Lat. afflatus, Aesch., Plat.
breathed upon, inspired, Plat.
upon the feet, Soph.
to yearn after, Hdt., Plat.
a longing after, NTest.
longed for, desired, NTest.
a chief shepherd, Od.
to come to the surface, float, Xen.
to be uppermost, to be prevalent, Id.
to be forward; c. dat. pers. to behave insolently to, Luc.
to be engaged upon a thing, c. dat., Id.
on the surface, superficial, Luc.:— metaph. superficial, common-place, Dem.
prominent, Xen.
a surface: mostly in gen. ἐπιπολῆς as adv. on the surface, a-top, Hdt., Xen.
ἐπιπολῆς also as prep. c. gen. on the top of, above, Hdt., Ar.
Ἐπιπολαί, αἱ, an eminence near Syracuse, with a flat surface, Thuc.
a companion, Soph.
adverb for ἐπὶ πολύ, to a great extent, generally, Hdt., etc.
to triumph over, τινί Plut.
to toil on, persevere, Xen.
painful, toilsome, laborious, Soph., Thuc., etc.:—rarely in good sense, Xen.: —ἐπίπονόν [ἐστι] 'tis a hard task, Thuc.
of persons, laborious, patient of toil, Ar.
of omens, portending distress, Xen.
adv. -νως, Lat. aegre, Thuc., Xen.:—Sup. -ώτατα, Id.
Dep, to travel, march to, march over, Plut.
any garment buckled over the shoulders, a mantle, Plut.
Dep., to fly or hover over, Aesch.
becoming:— τὸ ἐπιπρεπές, propriety, Luc.
to be manifest on the surface, to be conspicuous, Od., Theocr.
to beseem, fit, suit, τινί Xen.
Dep. to send an embassy, Plut.
to grind the teeth with rage at a thing, Anth.
to throw forward, ap. Plut.
to set out or place before one, τί τινι Il.
to send on one after another, Hhymn.
to send forth, Il.; Μενελάῳ ἐπιπροέμεν ταχὺν ἰόν to shoot an arrow at him, Id.
νήσοισιν ἐπιπροέηκε (sc. τὴν ναῦν) he steered straight for them, Od.

sense.gloss: on, upon with gen., dat., and acc.

entry.sense: prep. with gen., dat., and acc.: Radic. signf. upon.
WITH GEN.:
of Place,

with Verbs of Rest, upon or on, κεῖσθαι ἐπὶ χθονός Il.; ἐφ’ ἵππου on horse-back, etc.; ἐπὶ γῆς upon earth, Soph.; ἐπ’ ἀγροῦ in the country, Od.; also at or near, ἐπὶ Λήμνου off Lemnos, Hdt., etc.:—with Verbs of motion, the sense is pregnant, ἐπ’ ἠπείροιο ἔρυσσαν drew the ship upon the land and left it there, Il., etc.; ἀναβῆναι ἐπὶ τῶν πύργων Xen.

not strictly of Place, μένειν ἐπὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς to remain in the command, Id.; ἐπὶ τῶν πραγμάτων engaged in business, Dem.: —of ships, ὁρμεῖν ἐπ’ ἀγκύρας to ride at (i. e. in dependence on an) anchor, Hdt.
with the person. and reflex. Pron., ἐφ’ ὑμείων by yourselves, Il.; ἐφ’ αὑτοῦ by himself, Thuc.; αὐτὸς ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῦ Xen.
with numerals, to denote the depth of a body of soldiers, ἐπὶ τεττάρων four deep, Id.; ἐπ’ ὀλίγων i. e. in a long thin file, Id.; ἐφ’ ἑνός in single file, Id.
c.gen. pers. before, in presence of, Lat. coram, ἐπὶ πάντων Dem.
with Verbs of observing, in, ὁρᾶν τι ἐπί τινος Xen.
of motion towards, προτρέποντο ἐπὶ νηῶν Il.; πλεῖν ἐπὶ Χίου to sail for Chios, Hdt.; ἡ ἐπὶ Βαβυλῶνος ὁδός the road leading to B., Xen.
of Time, in the time of, ἐπὶ προτέρων ἀνθρώπων Il.; ἐπὶ Κύρου Hdt.; ἐπ’ ἐμοῦ in my time, Id.
in various Causal senses:
over, of persons in authority, ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν ὁπλιτῶν, ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν ἱππέων Dem.; ὁ ἐπὶ τῆς διοικήσεως the paymaster, Id.
κεκλῆσθαι ἐπί τινος to be called after him, Hdt.; ἡ ἐπ’ Ἀνταλκίδου εἰρήνη καλουμένη Xen.
of occasions, and the like, ἐπὶ πάντων on all occasions, Dem.; so in phrases which became adverbial, ἐπ’ ἴσης (sc. μοίρας) equally, Soph.
WITH DAT.:

of Place, upon, ἕξεσθαι ἐπὶ δίφρῳ Il.:—with Verbs of Motion, Id.; in pregnant construction, πέτονται ἐπ’ ἄνθεσιν fly on to the flowers and settle there, Id.:— at or near, ἐπὶ θύρῃσι Id.:— on or over, ἐπ’ Ἰφιδάμαντι over the body of Iphidamas, Id.
in hostile sense, against, Hdt.
towards, in reference to, ἐπὶ πᾶσι Il.; νόμον τίθεσθαι ἐπί τινι to make a law for his case, whether for or against, Plat.
of accumulation, upon, after, ὄγχνη ἐπ’ ὄγχνῃ one pear after another, Od.
in addition to, ἐπὶ τοῖσι besides, ἐπὶ τούτοις attic
of position, after, behind, of soldiers, Xen.
in dependence upon, in the power of, Lat. penes, ἐπί τινί ἐστι 'tis in his power to do, c. inf., Hdt.; τὸ ἐπ’ ἐμοί as far as is in my power, Xen.
of condition or circumstances, Il., etc.; ἐπὶ τῷ παρόντι Thuc.
of Time, ἐπὶ νυκτί by night, Il.; αἰεὶ ἐπ’ ἤματι every day, Od.
after, ἕκτῃ ἐπὶ δεκάτῃ or τῇ ἕκτῃ ἐπὶ δέκα, on the 16th of the month, ap. Dem.; τὰ ἐπὶ τούτοις, Lat. quod superest, Thuc.; τοὐπὶ τῷδε Eur.
in various Causal senses:
of the occasion or cause, ἐπὶ σοί for thee, Il.; μέγα φρονεῖν ἐπί τινι to be proud at or of a thing, Plat.; ἀγανακτεῖν ἐπί τινι Xen.
of an end or purpose, ἐπὶ δόρπῳ for supper, Od.; ἐπὶ κακῷ for mischief, Hdt.; δῆσαι ἐπὶ θανάτῳ Id., Xen.; ἐπ’ ἐξαγωγῇ for exportation, Hdt.
of the condition upon which a thing is done, ἐπὶ τούτοις on these terms, Id.; ἐφ’ ᾧ or ἐφ’ ᾧτε on condition that, Id.; ἐπὶ οὐδενί on no account, Id.; ἐπ’ ἴσῃ καὶ ὁμοίᾳ on fair and equal terms, Thuc.
of price, ἔργον τελέσαι μεγάλῳ ἐπὶ δώρῳ Il.; ἐπὶ πόσῳ; Plat.; ἐπ’ ἀργυρίῳ Dem.; of the interest payable on money, δανείζεσθαι ἐπὶ τοῖς μεγάλοις τόκοις Id.
κεκλῆσθαι ἐπί τινι to be called after, Plat.
of persons in authority, ἐπὶ βουσίν over the kine, Od.; ἐπὶ ταῖς ναυσίν Xen.; οἱ ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν Dem.
WITH ACC.:

of Place, upon or on to a height, ἐπὶ πύργον ἔβη Il.; προελθεῖν ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα Thuc.; ἀναβαίνειν ἐπὶ τὸν ἵππον Xen.: simply to, ἦλθε θοὰς ἐπὶ νῆας Il., etc.:—metaph., ἐπὶ ἔργα τρέπεσθαι Id.; ἐπὶ τὴν τράπεζαν ὀφείλειν to owe to the bank, Dem.

up to, as far as, ἐπὶ θάλασσαν Thuc.:—in measurements, πλέον ἢ ἐπὶ δύο στάδια Xen.; with a neut. adj., ὅσον τ’ ἔπι as far as, Il.; ἐπὶ πᾶν ἐλθεῖν Xen.; ἐπὶ σμικρόν, a little way, a little, Soph.; ἐπ’ ἔλαττον, ἐπ’ ἐλάχιστον Plat., etc.
ἐπὶ πλέον still more, Hdt.; before, Lat. coram, ἦγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὰ κοινά Id.
in Military phrases, ἐπ’ ἀσπίδας πέντε καὶ εἴκοσιν, i. e. 25 in file, Thuc.

towards, to, ἐπὶ δεξιά, ἐπ’ ἀριστερά Hom., etc.:—also in Military phrases, ἐπὶ δόρυ ἀναστρέψαι, ἐπὶ ἀσπίδα μεταβαλέσθαι, to the spear or shield side, i. e. to right or left, Xen.; ἐπὶ πόδα ἀναχωρεῖν to retire on the foot, i. e. facing the enemy, Id.; ἐπὶ τὸ μεῖζον, with exaggeration, Thuc.; ἐπὶ τὰ γελοιότερα so as to provoke laughter, Plat.
in hostile sense, against, Il., etc.

of extension over a space, ἐπ’ ἐννέα κεῖτο πέλεθρα over nine acres he lay stretched, Id.; ἐπὶ πολύ over a large space, Thuc.:—so in many cases, where we say on, rather than over, δράκων ἐπὶ νῶτα δαφοινός Il.; ἵππους ἐπὶ νῶτον ἐΐσας Id.
of Time, for or during a certain time, πολλὸν ἐπὶ χρόνον Id.; ἐπὶ δέκα ἔτη Thuc.
up to or till a certain time, ἐπ’ ἠῶ καὶ μέσον ἦμαρ Od.
in various Causal senses:

of the object or purpose for which one goes, ἐπὶ Τυδῆ for (i. e. to bring) tidings of Tydeus, Il.; ἐλθεῖν ἐπ’ ἀργύριον Xen.:—with neut. Pron., ἐπὶ τοῦτο ἐλθεῖν for this purpose, Id.; ἐπὶ τί; to what end? Lat. quorsum? Ar.; ἐπὶ τόκον for (i. e. to gain) interest, Dem.
as regards, τοὐπ’ ἐμέ, τοὐπί σε Eur.
of persons set over others, ἐπὶ τοὺς πεζοὺς καθιστάναι ἄρχοντα Xen.
according to, by, ἐπὶ στάθμην by the rule, Od.
POSITION:— ἐπί may follow its case, when it becomes ἔπι by anastrophe.
ABSOL., ἐπί without anastrophe, esp. ἐπὶ δέ, and besides, Hdt.
ἔπι, for ἔπεστι, 'tis here, Hom.
IN COMPOS.:

of Place, denoting Rest upon, as in ἐπίκειμαι, or Motion, upon or over, as in ἐπιβαίνω; to or towards, as in ἐπαρίστερος, ἐπιδέξιος; against, as in ἐπαΐσσω, ἐπιστρατεύω; up to a point, as in ἐπιτελέω; over or beyond boundaries, as in ἐπινέμομαι, ἐπεργασία.
Extension over a surface, as in ἐπαλείφω, ἐπάργυρος, ἐπίχρυσος.
Accumulation or addition, as in ἐπιβάλλω, ἐπίκτητος.
Accompaniment, to, with, as in ἐπᾴδω, ἐπαυλέω.
Interest, ἐπίτριτος one and 1/3 more, 1+1/3, Lat. sesquitertius; so ἐπιτέταρτος, etc.
of Time and Sequence, after, as in ἐπιγίγνομαι.

in Causal senses, of Superiority felt over or at, as in ἐπιχαίρω, ἐπιγελάω; of Authority, over, as in ἐπικρατέω, ἐπιβούκολος; of Motive, for, as in ἐπιθυμέω, ἐπιθάνατος; to give force or intensity to the Verb, as in ἐπαινέω, ἐπιμέμφομαι.
to send upon, lay upon, ἑτάροις ἐπὶ χεῖρας ἴαλλεν laid hands upon them, Od.; ἐπίηλεν τάδε ἔργα brought these deeds to pass, Id.; ἐπιαλῶ (sc. τὸ κέντρον) I will lay it on, Ar.
to sleep among, c. dat., Od.
to sleep upon, Anth.
to shout out, to shout applause after a speech, Il.: also simply to shout aloud, Id.
of Place, before, Eur., Xen.; γεωλόφους ἐπ. ποιεῖσθαι to make the hills cover one, Id.
of Degree, ἐπ. εἶναί τινος to be better than another, Eur.
to be before, ἐπ. τοῖς πύργοις to be in a line with them, so as to cover one with the other, Polyb.
to pour forth, Hhymn.
to sneeze at, ἐπέπταρε ἔπεσσιν he sneezed as I spoke the words, a good omen, Od.:—metaph. of the gods, to be gracious to, τινί Theocr.
an over-fold, a flap, Plut., Luc.
Dep. to go about, go through, Lat. obire, c. acc., ἐπεπωλεῖτο στίχας ἀνδρῶν, of the general inspecting his troops, Il.;—but also to reconnoitre an enemy, Id.
a going round, inspection, name given to the latter half of Il. 4.
to urge a horse by the whip, Xen.
to be careless about a thing, Luc.
to sprinkle upon or over, τί τινι Theocr.
to sew or stitch on, NTest.
to recite in accompaniment, Luc.
to offer sacrifices at a place, Od.
to sacrifice besides, Theocr.
leaning towards, Lat. proclivis, Luc.
to lean towards, fall to one's lot, Il.; c. inf., ἐπιρρέπει τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Aesch.
trans., ἐπ. τάλαντον to force down one scale, Theogn.: metaph. to weigh out to one, allot, Aesch.

entry.note: fut. -ρεύσομαι and in pass. form -ρυήσομαι aor2 pass. also in act. sense ἐπερρύην
entry.sense: to flow upon the surface, float a-top, like oil on water, Il.

to flow in besides, flow fresh and fresh, Ar.:—metaph. of large bodies of men, to stream on and on, Il., Hdt.; also, οὑπιρρέων χρόνος onward-streaming time, i. e. the future, Aesch.; ὄλβου ἐπιρρυέντος if wealth flows on and on, increases continually, Eur.
ἐπιρρήγνυμι to rend, Aesch.
to dash to, slam to, πύλας Soph.
intr. to break or burst upon one, Id.
ἐπιρρήσσω, ionic for ἐπιρράσσω
to dash to, shut violently, θύρην Il.
to declaim over, τί τινι Luc.
exclaimed against, infamous, Xen.
shrunk up, Xen.
to cast at another, c. dat., Od.; χεῖρα ἐπ. to lay hand upon, Anth.:—metaph. to throw upon one, τί τινι Aesch.
= ἐπιρ-ρίπτω, only in pres. and imperf., Xen.
intr. to throw oneself upon the track, Xen.
afflux, influx, Aesch.:—metaph., ἐπ. κακῶν Eur.
to shout in answer or in approval (cf. ἐπευφημέω), Trag.; ἐπ. κτύπῳ to answer to, ring with the sound, Aesch.
c. acc., λόγοις ἐπιρροθεῖν to inveigh against him, Soph.
hasting to the rescue, a helper, Il., Hes.: —c. gen. giving aid against, Aesch.
ἐπ. κακά reproaches bandied backwards and forwards, abusive language, Soph.
adv. with noisy fury, Eur.
to shriek at one, c. acc. cogn., ἐπ. φυγάς τινι to shriek or forebode flight at him, Aesch.
to swallow besides, Plut.
to set a dog on one, Ar.
to bring into form, arrange, Luc.
Dep. to save, preserve, Aesch.
flowing in or to: metaph. overflowing, Aesch.
pass. overflowed, Xen.
to add strength to, strengthen or encourage for an enterprise, Hdt., Thuc.

Pass., perf. ἐπέρρωμαι, plup. ἐπερρώμην used as pres. and imperf.: fut. ἐπιρρωσθήσομαι: aor1 ἐπερρώσθην: — to recover strength, pluck up courage, Thuc., Xen.; κείνοις ἐπερρώσθη λέγειν (impers.) they took courage to speak, Soph.
Mid. to flow or stream upon, χαῖται ἐπερρώσαντο ἀπὸ κρατός his locks flowed waving from his head, Il.
to move nimbly, Hes.: c. acc. cogn., ἐπίρρωσαι χορείην urge the rapid dance, Anth.
to apply one's strength to a thing, work lustily at it, c. dat., Od.
a load on a beast's back:—metaph., τοὐπίσαγμα τοῦ νοσήματος the burden of the disease, Soph.
to pile a load upon a beast's back, Hdt.; ἵππον ἐπ. to saddle it, Xen.
waving over the forehead, Luc.
to shake at or against, with the view of scaring, τί τινι Il., Eur.; Πέρσας ἐπ. to hold them out as a threat, Plut.; but, ἐπ. τὴν χεῖρα, in token of assent, Luc.
to set upon one, c. dat., Eur.
to put in motion against, set upon one, c. dat., Od.
Pass. to hurry or hasten to or towards, Hom.; in hostile sense, to rush upon or at, c. dat., Il.

part. perf. pass. ἐπεσσύμενος, with 3rd sg. perf. and plup. ἐπέσσῠται, -το mostly in hostile sense, to rush on, Id.; c. dat., αὐτῷ μοι ἐπέσσυτο Id.; c. acc. to assault, Id.; c. gen., ἐπεσσύμενος πεδίοιο rushing, hurrying over the plain, Id.:—also, without hostile sense, to express rapid motion, ἐπέσσυτο δέμνια swept over the clothes, Od.; c. inf., ἐπέσσυτο διώκειν he hasted on to follow, Il.:—metaph. to be excited, eager, θυμὸς ἐπέσσυται Id.
to set a mark upon a person, of a disease, Thuc., Xen.: Pass. to have a mark set on one, Eur.
to indicate, Plut.
Mid. to mark for oneself, signify, indicate, Plat.
to set one's seal to a thing, approve it, Dem., Aeschin.
any distinguishing mark, a device or badge, the bearing on a shield, the ensign of a ship, Hdt.
having a mark on it, of money, stamped, coined, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; ἀναθήματα οὐκ ἐπ. offerings with no inscription on them, Hdt.
notable, remarkable, Lat. insignis, Id., attic: in bad sense, notorious, Eur.
for ἐπ’ ἴσης, (sc. μοίρας) v. sub ἴσος
to set on a dog, Ar.
to bend inwards: intr. to turn aside one's course, Xen.
Mid.
to furnish oneself with food or provender, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
c. acc. rei, ἐπ. ἄριστον to provide oneself with breakfast, Id.; ἐπις. ἀργύριον Xen.
c. acc. pers. to supply with provisions, Id.
a furnishing oneself with provisions, foraging, Xen.
a stock or store of provisions, Id.
to dig superficially, Anth.
to scatter or sprinkle over:—Pass. to be sprinkled over, τινι Plut.
the first bound, in a horse's gallop, Xen.
to be considered or examined, Thuc., Plat.
neut. ἐπισκεπτέον, one must consider, Id.

entry.etym: a pres., which furnishes its tenses to ἐπισκοπέω, v. σκέπτομαι

entry.sense: to cover over, Anth.
to get ready, to equip, fit out, Thuc., Xen.:—Mid., ἐπισκευάζεσθαι ναῦν to have a ship equipped, Thuc.
τὰ χρήματα ἐφ’ ἁμαξῶν ἐπισκευάσαι to pack them upon wagons, Xen.
to make afresh, to repair, Lat. reficere, Thuc., Xen.
one who equips or repairs, Dem.
repaired, restored, Plat.
repair, restoration, Hdt., Dem.
materials for repair or equipment, stores, Thuc., Dem.
inspection, visitation, Xen., Plut.
investigation, inquiry, Xen.
at or before the tent, i. e. public, Soph.
to be quartered in a place: metaph. to dwell upon, NTest.
to make to lean upon, make to fall upon, Aesch.: impose on, τί τινι Soph.
intr. to fall upon, like lightning: metaph., δεῦρ’ ἐπέσκηψεν it came to this point, Aesch.
to lay it upon one to do a thing, to enjoin, lay a strict charge upon, c. dat. pers. et inf., Id., Soph.; c. acc. et inf., Hdt., Eur.
as Attic law-term, generally in Mid. to denounce a person, so as to begin a prosecution, Plut., etc.:—Pass. to be denounced as guilty of a crime, c. gen., Soph.
an injunction, Plut.
as law-term, a denunciation, Dem.
to throw a shade upon, overshadow, Hdt., NTest.:—Pass., λαθραῖον ὄμμ’ ἐπεσκιασμένη keeping a hidden watch, Soph.
shaded, dark, obscure, Plat.
act. shading, c. gen., χεὶρ ὀμμάτων ἐπίσκιος Soph.
to look upon or at, inspect, observe, examine, regard, Hdt., Eur.: to watch over, of tutelary gods, Soph., Eur.
to visit, Soph., Xen., etc.:—Pass., εὐνὴν ὀνείροις οὐκ ἐπισκοπουμένην visited not by dreams, i. e. sleepless, Aesch.
of a general, to inspect, review, Xen.
to consider, reflect, Soph., Xen.:—Mid. to examine with oneself, meditate, Plat.
a watching over, visitation, NTest.
the office of ἐπίσκοπος, Id.: generally, an office, Id.
a looking at, Anth.
one who watches over, an overseer, guardian, Hom., Soph.:—of tutelary gods, Solon., etc.
c. dat., ἐπ. Τρώεσσι one set to watch them, Il.
a public officer, intendant, sent to the subject states, Ar.
a bishop, NTest.
hitting the mark: metaph. reaching, touching a point, c. gen., Aesch., Soph.:—neut. pl. ἐπίσκοπα, as adv. successfully, with good aim, Hdt.
to throw a shadow over, c. dat., Dem.; ἐπ. τινὶ τῆς θέας to be in the way of one's seeing, Plat.
a darkening, obscurity, of the sun or moon in eclipse, Plut.
in the dark, darkened, Plut.
Dep. to be indignant at a thing, Il.; ἐπισκύσσαιτο (epic aor1 opt.) Od.
to ply with drink in Scythian fashion, i. e. with unmixed wine, Hdt.
to look gloomy or stern, Xen.
the skin of the brows which is knitted in frowning, Il., Ar.
superciliousness, Anth.
to laugh at, quiz, make game of, τινά Plat., Xen.:—absol. to joke, make fun, Ar.; ἐπισκώπτων jestingly, Xen.
mocking, raillery, Plut.
gloomy, Hes.:—adv., ἐπισμυγερῶς ἀπέτισεν sadly did he pay for it, Od.; ἐπισμυγερῶς ναυτίλλεται to his cost doth he sail, Id.
the latch or handle by which a door is pulled to, Hdt.
the angler's rod or line, Anth.
drawn upon oneself, Od.
tight-drawn, of a noose, Eur.
to draw or drag after one, Hdt.; and in Mid., Xen.; ἐπισπάσας κόμης by the hair, having dragged her by the hair, Eur.:—metaph. to bring on, cause, πλῆθος πημάτων Aesch.
to pull to, τὴν θύραν Xen.; ἐπισπασθέντος τοῦ βρόχου the noose being drawn tight, Dem.
to attract, gain, win, Soph.:—so in Mid., ἐπισπᾶσθαι κέρδος Hdt.

in Mid. to draw on, allure, persuade, Thuc.: —c. inf., ἐπισπάσασθαι [ἂν] αὐτοὺς ἡγεῖτο προθυμήσεσθαι he thought it would induce them to make the venture, Id.:—Pass., φοβοῦμαι μὴ πάντες ἐπισπασθῶσιν πολεμῆσαι Dem.
Pass., of the sea, ἐπισπωμένη returning with a rush, Thuc.
in Mid. to become uncircumcised, NTest.
to sow with seed, Hdt.
a libation over a sacrifice, Hdt.
to pour upon or over the head of a victim, at a sacrifice, Hdt., Aesch.:—absol. to make a libation, Hdt.:—metaph., ἐπ. δάκρυ Theocr.
in Mid. to make a fresh treaty, Thuc.
hasty, hurried: adv. -χῶς, Xen.
to urge on horses, Il.; generally, to urge on, press forward, Aesch., Thuc.
intr. to rage furiously, of storms, Od.
to urge on, further or promote an object, Hdt., Soph.: of persons, to urge on, Xen.
intr. to hasten onward, Eur.; ἐπισπ. εἴς τι to be zealous for, aim at an object, Xen.
a renewed or renewable truce, Thuc.
sown afterwards, οἱ ἐπ. posterity, Aesch.
intr. to make haste in a thing, Luc.
rushing, gushing, of tears, Aesch.: violent, sudden, of misfortunes, Id.: c. acc. rushing upon, τὰς φρένας Eur.
standing over each in turn, i. e. one after another, successively, Od.
Dep. to weigh well, ponder, Aesch.
to be quartered upon others, Plut.
Pass. to be assigned as quarters, Id.
a liability to have persons quartered on one, Plut.
at the door, Anth.
to drop over, τί τινι Luc.
to fall in drops over, c. acc., Anth.
a commission, Theophr.
Dep.:
c. inf. to know how to do, to be able to do, capable of doing, Hom., attic
to be assured or believe that a thing is, Hdt.
c. acc. to understand a matter, know, be versed in or acquainted with, Hom., etc.:—after Hom. to know as a fact, know for certain, know well, Hdt., attic
rarely, to know a person, Eur.
c. part., to know that one is, has, etc., Hdt., attic
part. pres. ἐπιστάμενος, η, ον, is often also used as an adj. knowing, understanding, skilful, Hom.:—c. gen. skilled or versed in a thing, Id.:—adv. ἐπισταμένως, skilfully, expertly, Id., Hes.
authority, dominion, Plut.
ἐπ. Ζεύς, ὁ, Jupiter Stator, Plut.
entry.etym: From ἐφίστημι, he that makes to stand firm.

entry.sense: a stopping, halting, a halt, Xen.; φροντίδων ἐπιστάσεις haltings of thought, Soph.
attention, care, anxiety, NTest.
superintendence of works, Xen.
to be set over, c. dat., Soph., Plat.: also to stand by, to support, second, Aesch.
c. gen. to be in charge of, have the care of, Hdt., Xen.
at Athens, to be Ἐπιστάτης or President of the βουλή and ἐκκλησία, Thuc., etc.
one who stands near or by, a suppliant, Od.
in battle-order, one's rear-rank man (as παραστάτης is the right- or left-hand man, προστάτης the front-rank man), Xen.
one who stands or is mounted upon a chariot, c. gen., Soph., Eur.
one who is set over, a commander, Trag.; ἐπιστ. Κολωνοῦ, of a tutelary god, Soph.; ἐπ. ἄθλων president, steward of the games, a training- master, Xen.
at Athens the President of the βουλή and ἐκκλησία, Aeschin., Dem.
an overseer, superintendent, in charge of any public works, Id.
the caldron for the hot bath which stood over the fire, Ar.
one must superintend, c. dat., Plat.; c. gen., Xen.
to tread upon, stand upon a place, c. acc., Soph.
to approach, c. acc., Aesch.
to send to, send as a message or letter, Hdt., attic:—absol. to send a message, write word, Eur., Thuc.

to enjoin, command, τινί τι Id.; τινά τι Xen.; also, ἐπ. τινὶ or τινὰ ποιεῖν τι Soph., Xen.:—so, in Pass., ἐπέσταλτό οἱ . . c. inf., he had received orders to do, Hdt.; ἐπέσταλται τί τινι a matter has been committed to one, Aesch.; τὰ ἐπεσταλμένα orders given, Id.
to order by will, Xen.
to groan over, τινί Aesch.
= ἐπι-στενάζω τινί Aesch.:—absol., Soph.
Mid. to groan in answer, Il.
to groan or sigh in answer, Il.
to lament over, τινί Eur.
c. acc. to lament, Soph.
of bowls, ἐπιστεφέες οἴνοιο crowned (i. e. brimming high) with wine, Hom.
to surround with or as with a chaplet: metaph. in Mid., κρητῆρας ἐπιστέψαντο ποτοῖο crowned them to the brim, filled them brimming high, with wine, Hom.
χοὰς ἐπιστέφειν to offer libations as an honour to the dead, Soph.
Pass. to be set up as a column upon, Anth.
acquaintance with a matter, skill, experience, as in archery, Soph.; in war, Thuc., etc.
generally, knowledge, Soph.: esp. scientific knowledge, science, Plat., etc.
knowing, wise, prudent, ἐπ. βουλῇ τε νόῳ τε Od.
acquainted with a thing, skilled or versed in, c. gen., Thuc., etc.
c. inf. knowing how to do, Plat., etc.— adv., ἐπιστημόνως with knowledge: comp. -έστερον, Xen.; Sup. -έστατα, Plat.
possessed of perfect knowledge, Id.
to make to lean on:—Pass. to lean upon, τινι Luc.
to glisten on the surface, Plut.
in Od. means a shed in which a ship is laid up.
girt up, neatly, of dress, Hes.
secretary: also a courier, Xen.
among the Spartans, a vice-admiral, Id.
a message, command, commission, whether verbal or in writing, Hdt., attic; ἐξ ἐπιστολῆς by command, Hdt.
a letter, Lat. epistola, Thuc., etc.
commanded:— δυνάμεις ἐπ. forces decreed, but never sent, paper-armies, Dem.
to curb in a horse: metaph. to curb, bridle, τινά Ar., Dem.
to put on the mouth-piece of a flute; and of a flute, to stop the voice, Plut.
to throw on his face, τινά Luc.
to strew or spread upon, Od.
to saddle, Luc.
a march or expedition against, Hdt.; c. gen., Thuc.

to march against, make war upon, τινί Eur., etc.:— to make an expedition, εἰς Θετταλίαν Aesch.; c. acc., Soph.:—absol., Aesch.:—so in Mid., with perf. pass., ἐπιστρατεύεσθαι ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον Hdt.; c. dat., Eur., etc.
to be turned towards, to be looked at, conspicuous, Aesch.
turning one's eyes or mind to a thing, attentive, Xen.
earnest, vehement: adv. -φῶς, ionic -φέως, earnestly, sharply, Hdt., Aeschin.
to turn about, turn round, Eur.; ἐπ. τὰς ναῦς to make a sudden tack, Thuc.; but also to put an enemy to flight, Xen.
intr. to turn about, turn round, Il., Hdt., attic:— to return, NTest.
to turn towards, τὸ νόημα Theogn.; πρός τι, εἴς τινα Plut.:— ἐπ. πίστιν to press a pledge upon one, Soph.
intr. to turn towards, Xen.
to turn from an error, to correct, make to repent, Luc.
intr. to repent, NTest.
to curve, twist, torment, Ar.

Mid. and Pass., esp. in aor2 pass. ἐπεστράφην [ᾰ]: — to turn oneself round, turn about, ἐπιστρεφόμενος constantly turning, to look behind one, Hdt.; with acc., θάλαμον ἐπεστράφη turned to gaze on it, Eur.; δόξα ἐπεστράφη turned about, changed, Soph.
to go back-and for-wards, wander over the earth, Hes.:—c. acc. loci, to turn to a place, Eur.
to turn the mind towards, to pay attention to, c. gen., Theogn., Soph.: —absol. to recover oneself, pay attention, Hdt., Dem.
c. acc. to visit, Eur.
part. perf. pass. ἐπεστραμμένος, = ἐπιστρεφής, earnest, vehement, Hdt. Hence
turning this way and that way, right and left, Hom.: also, ἐπ. βαδίζειν back- and for-wards, Hhymn.
a turning about, twisting, Plat.
intr. a turning or wheeling about, of men turning to bay, Soph.; ἐπιστροφαὶ κακῶν renewed assaults of ills, Id.:—of ships, a putting about, tacking, Thuc.
a turn of affairs, reaction, Id.
attention paid to a person or thing, regard, Soph., etc.
a moving up and down in a place, δωμάτων ἐπιστροφαί occupation of them, Aesch.; ξενοτίμους ἐπ. δωμάτων, of the duties of hospitality, Id.
having dealings with, conversant with, c. gen., Od., Aesch.
to visit or frequent a place, c. acc. loci, Od.:—Mid. to go in and out of, frequent, visit, occupy, Aesch., Eur.
the lintel on the top of pillars, the epistyle, architrave, Plut.

sense.gloss: to harass yet more with frivolous accusations.

entry.sense: to collect and bring to a place, to gather together, NTest.
a gathering or being gathered together, NTest.
to renew a war, Plut.
to push forward together, Plut.
to run together to a place, NTest.
the trail or track made by dragging a thing, Xen.
to drag or trail after one, in Mid., Luc.: —Pass. to crawl along, Xen.
to do anything in a slovenly way, to slur over, Lys.; ἐπισύροντες confusedly, Dem.; often in part. perf. pass. slovenly, careless, Luc.
a gathering together against, a riotous meeting, NTest.
to slaughter over or upon, of sacrifices offered at a tomb, Eur., Xen.
to kill after or besides, Id.
prone to fall, unstable, precarious, Plat., Dem.:—adv., ἐπισφαλῶς διακεῖσθαι to be in danger, Plut.
to bind, clasp tight, Anth.
to put a seal on, to confirm, ratify, Anth.
as Dep. to put as a seal upon, impress upon, Plat.; also as Pass. to be impressed, marked, Anth.
one who seals or signs, Luc.
bands, clasps or hooks, which fastened the greaves (κνημῖδες) over the ankle, Il.
the ankle, Anth.
on the ankle, Anth.
near at hand, hard by, Hhymn.
to hold in, check, Aesch.
in a row, one after another, Il.
of Time, by degrees, Theocr.
a thing held out, a pretext, Od.
a checking, hindrance, delay, reluctance, lingering, Od., Thuc.
to make strong or powerful, Xen.
intr. to prevail, be urgent, NTest.
to hold or direct towards, Il.; τινί against one, Hes.
to restrain, withhold, check, Id., attic:—c. gen. to restrain from a thing, Od.
intr. to leave off, stop, wait, Thuc.; imperat. ἔπισχε, hold, Eur.
the metal hoop round the felloe (σῶτρον), the tire of a wheel, Il.
an injunction, command, Plat., Aeschin.
a reserve force, Plut.
a commander, Xen.
drawn up behind, οἱ ἐπίτακτοι the reserve of an army, Thuc.
to labour yet more, Thuc.
to push home a bolt, Od.
an injunction, ἡ ἐπ. τοῦ φόρου the assessment of the tribute, Hdt.
disturbance, confusion, Plat.
to trouble or disquiet yet more, Hdt., Luc.
a helper, defender, ally, Hom.; μάχης ἐπ. in fight, Il.
a master, lord, Orac. ap. Hdt.
a stretching of strings, Plat.

to put upon one as a duty, to enjoin, τί τινι Hdt., etc.:—c. dat. pers. et inf. to order one to do, Id., attic:—absol. to impose commands, Thuc.; τινί on one, Soph.:—Pass. with fut. mid. -τάξομαι, aor1 -ετάχθην, perf. -τέταγμαι:— to accept orders, submit to commands, Eur., Ar.; c. acc. rei, Thuc.:—of things, to be ordered, ὁ στρατὸς ὁ ἐπιταχθεὶς ἑκάστοισι Hdt.; τὰ ἐπιτασσόμενα orders given, Id.
to place next or beside, Id., Xen.:— Mid., τοὺς ἱππέας ἐπετάξαντο they had the cavalry placed next, Thuc.
to place behind, c. gen., Hdt.: absol. to place in reserve, Plut.:—Mid., Xen.
to set in command over, οἱ ἐπιτεταγμένοι set as guards over the waggons, Thuc.
over a tomb, λόγος ἐπ. a funeral oration, spoken over citizens who had fallen in battle, such as that of Pericles in Thuc.
to hasten on, urge forward, Thuc.
to stretch upon or over a place, Hdt.:—Pass., in tmesi, ἐπὶ νὺξ τέταται βροτοῖσι Od.
to stretch as on a frame, tighten, of musical strings, Plat.: metaph. to increase in intensity, to increase, augment, Id.
to urge on, incite, τινὰ ποιεῖν τι Xen.; ἐπ. ἑαυτόν to exert himself, Plut.
Pass. to be stretched as on the rack, Plat.
to be on the stretch, to be strained or contracted, Id.; ἐπ. βιβλίοις to devote oneself to books, Luc.
to hold out, endure, Xen.
to build a fort on the frontier as a basis of operations against the enemy, Thuc., Xen.:—metaph., ἐπ. τυράννους to plant them like such forts, Dem.
the building a fort on the enemy's frontier, the occupation of it, Thuc.
a fort placed on the enemy's frontier, Thuc., Xen., etc.; c. gen., ἐπιτειχίσματα τῆς αὐτοῦ χώρας fortresses which command his country, Dem.
metaph., ἐπ. πρός τι a barrier or obstacle to a thing, Id.
to complete a sacrifice, Plut.
accomplishment, completion, Plut.
to complete, finish, accomplish, Hdt., Thuc.: esp. of the fulfilment of oracles, visions, vows or promises, Id.
to discharge a religious service, Hdt.
to pay in full, Id.:—metaph. in Mid., ἐπιτελεῖσθαι τὰ τοῦ γήρως to have to pay, be subject to, the burdens of old age, Xen.; ἐπ. θάνατον to have to pay the debt of death, Id.
brought to an end, completed, accomplished, Hdt., etc.
to lay upon, enjoin, prescribe, ordain, command, τι or τί τινι Hom.:—c. dat. pers. only, to give orders to, Il.:—c. dat. pers. et inf. to order him to do. Id.:—also in Mid., just like the Act., Id.
Pass. to rise, of stars, Hes.:—metaph., of love, Theogn.
to cut on the surface, make an incision into, gash, Lat. incidere, Hdt., Aeschin.:—Mid., ἐπιτάμνεσθαι τοὺς βραχίονας to gash their arms, Hdt.
to cut short, to abridge, Plut.
at the birth, about to bring forth, Hdt., Luc.
pleasing, delightful, Hhymn., Plut.:—adv. -πῶς, Id.
devoted to pleasure, Id.
Pass. to rejoice or delight in a thing, c. dat., Od., Hes.
Dep.
to contrive for a purpose or to meet an emergency, to invent, Hdt.
to contrive against, τί τινι Luc.
contrivance for a purpose, invention, Thuc.
artificially made, Luc.

made for an end or purpose, fit or adapted for it, suitable, convenient, ἔς τι, πρός τι Hdt., Plat.; c. inf., χωρίον ἐπ. ἐνιππεῦσαι fit to ride in, Hdt.; ἐπ. ὑπεξαιρεθῆναι convenient to be put out of the way, Thuc.; ἐπ. ξυνεῖναι a pleasant person to live with, Eur.; ἐπ. παθεῖν deserving to suffer, Dem., also, ἐπιτήδεόν [ἐστί] μοι, c. inf., Hdt.
useful, serviceable, necessary,

of things, fit or serviceable for, c. dat., Thuc.; ἐστὸ ἐπ. to their advantage, Id.; of treaties, omens, favourable, Hdt.:—esp. as Subst., τὰ ἐπιτήδεια necessaries, provisions, Lat. commeatus, Id., Thuc., etc.
of persons, serviceable, friendly, Hdt., Thuc.; τῷ πατρί conformable to his will, Hdt.: as Subst., c. gen., a close friend, Lat. necessarius, Thuc.
adv. -είως, ionic -έως, studiously, carefully, Hdt.
suitably, conveniently, fitly, Id.;—comp. -ειότερον, Id.
fitness, suitableness, Plat.
Theocr.:—also designedly, deceitfully, Eur.
such as may serve the purpose, enough, or of set purpose, advisedly, studiously, Lat. consulto, de industria, Hom.;—in Hdt. and attic written proparox.,
a pursuit, business, practice, Lat. studium, Thuc., Plat.
devotion or attention to a pursuit, Thuc., Plat., etc.; βιότου ἐπιτηδεύσεις refinements of life, Eur.

entry.note: imperf. ἐπετήδευον aor1 ἐπ-ετήδευσα perf. -τετήδευκα pass. -τετήδευμαι
entry.etym: conjugated as if it were a compd. of ἐπί, τηδεύω, but there is no such Verb; and ἐπιτηδεύω must be formed directly from ἐπιτηδές
entry.sense: to pursue or practise a thing, make a practice of, make it one's business, Lat. studere rei, c. acc., Hdt., attic:—also, ἐπ. τι πρός τι to invent for a purpose, Hdt.\:t—Pass. to be done with pains and practice, to be made so and so by art, Id.; of dogs, to be trained, Xen.
c. inf. to take care to do, use to do, Hdt., Plat.

entry.etym: adverb of ἐπιτήδεος, ionic for ἐπιτήδειος.

entry.sense: overlaid with gold: metaph. counterfeit, Anth.
to melt upon, pour when melted over a thing, Hdt., Plut.
to look out for, Ar., Thuc., etc.

entry.etym: the Pass.is mostly furnished by ἐπίκειμαι
entry.sense: Act. to lay, put or place upon, of offerings laid on the altar, meats on the table, etc., c. dat., Od., attic; also c. gen., Il., Hdt.:—c. acc. only, ἐπ. φάρμακα to apply salves, Il.; ἐπ. στήλην to set it up, Hdt.
to put on a covering or lid, Od.; λίθον ἐπέθηκε θύρῃσιν, i. e. put a stone as a door to the cave, put it before the door, Id.: to put a door to, shut it, Il., Hom.
to put to, grant or give besides, Il.
of Time, to add, bring on, Od.
μύθῳ or μύθοις τέλος ἐπιθεῖναι to put an end to them, Il.
to put on as a finish, ἐπέθηκε κορώνην Id.; ἐπ. κεφαλαῖον (v. sub κεφαλαῖον) Dem.
to impose or inflict a penalty, θωήν σοι ἐπιθήσομεν Od.; δίκην, ζημίαν ἐπ. τινί Hdt.
like ἐπιστέλλω, to dispatch a letter, Id., Dem.
to give a name, Hdt., Plat.
Mid. to put on oneself or for oneself, Il., Eur.
to set oneself to, apply oneself to, employ oneself on or in, c. dat., Hdt., Thuc., etc.
to make an attempt upon, attack, τῇ Εὐβοίῃ Hdt., Thuc., etc.
absol., δικαιοσύνην ἐπιθέμενος ἤσκεε he practised justice with assiduity, Hdt.
to bring on oneself, ἀράς Aesch.: also to cause a penalty to be imposed, Thuc.
to lay commands on, τί τινι Hdt.
to give a name, Od.
to lay a value upon, Lat. aestimare: hence,
to shew honour to, τινά Hdt.
to raise in price:—Pass. to rise in price, Dem.
of judges, to lay a penalty on a person, Hdt.
c. acc. to censure, Dem.; also c. dat., Id.: absol., Thuc.
censure, criticism, Thuc.
a chastiser, censurer, Aesch., Eur.
an avenger, Od.
the condition of an ἐπίτιμος, the enjoyment of civil rights, opp. to ἀτιμία, Aeschin., Dem.
mostly in pl. ἐπιτίμια, τά, the value, price, or estimate of a thing, i. e.,
the honours paid to a person, Soph.
assessment of damages or penalties, Hdt., Eur.; τῶνδε for these things, Aesch.; ἐπ. δυσσεβείας the wages of ungodliness, Soph.; in sg., τοὐπιτίμιον λαβεῖν to exact the penalty, Aesch.
of a citizen, in possession of his rights and franchises (τιμαί), opp. to ἄτιμος, Ar., Thuc.
at the breast, a suckling, Theocr.
to wound on the surface, Anth.
to bear patiently, be patient, Il.
the rising of a star, Eur., Thuc.
to submit or endure to do, c. inf., Od.: absol., ἐπετόλμησε he stood firm, Id.
a cutting on the surface, incision, Aeschin.
an epitome, abridgment, Cic.
on the stretch, strained: —ἐπίτονος (sc. ἱμάς), a rope for stretching or tightening, the back-stay of a mast (opp. to πρότονος), Od.
ἐπίτονοι, οἱ, the sinews of the shoulder and arm, Plat.
Dep. to shoot at, c. dat., Il., Luc.
to make into a tragic story, exaggerate, Luc.: to add in exaggeration, Plut.
on or at table, Luc.
one must permit, Xen.; so in pl. ἐπιτρεπτέα Hdt.

entry.note: ionic -τράπω fut. -τρέψω aor1 -έτρεψα ionic -έτραψα aor2 -έτραπον Pass. and Mid., ionic aor1 -ετράφθην Pass. ionic aor1 -ετράφθην aor2 pass. -ετράπην mid. -ετρᾰπόμην
entry.sense: properly to turn towards, in aor2 mid., θυμὸς ἐπετράπετο εἴρεσθαι thy mind inclined itself to ask, Od.
to turn over to, to commit or entrust to another as trustee, guardian, or vicegerent, Hom., Hdt., attic; c. inf., σοὶ ἐπέτρεψεν πονέεσθαι he left it to you to work, Il.
c. dat. only, to trust to, rely upon, Hom., Hdt.: to refer the matter to a person, leave it to his judgment, Ar., Thuc.:—so in Mid. to entrust oneself, leave one's case to, τινι Hdt.

Pass. to be entrusted, ᾧ λαοί τ’ ἐπιτετράφαται (3rd pl. perf. for ἐπιτετραμμένοι εἰσί) Il.; τῇς (sc. Ὥραις) ἐπιτέτραπται οὐρανός heaven's gate is committed to them (to open and to shut), Id.;—also c. acc. rei, ἐπιτρέπομαί τι I am entrusted with a thing, Hdt., Thuc.
to give up, yield, Ποσειδάωνι νίκην ἐπέτρεψας Il.; ἐπ. τινί c. inf. to permit, suffer, Hdt., attic
intr. to yield, give way, Il., Hdt.
to command, τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Xen.
to rear upon:—generally, to support, maintain, Hdt.
Pass. to grow up after, as posterity, Lat. succrescere, Id.; to grow up as a successor, Id.

entry.note: fut. -δρᾰμοῦμαι aor. -έδρᾰμον aor1 -έθρεξα rarely aor1 -έθρεξα perf. -δεδράμηκα Xen.; poet. δέδρομα
entry.sense: to run upon or at, for the purpose of attack, Il.; of dogs, Od.; so in attic to make an assault upon, τινί Thuc., Xen.
to run after, ἐπιδραμών in haste, eagerly, Hdt., Plat.
to run over a space, Il.: to run over or graze the surface, Id.
to be spread over, of a mist, Od.:—c. acc., οἶδμα ὅταν ἔρεβος ἐπιδράμῃ when the billow runs over the deep, Soph.
to overrun, as an army does a country, Hdt., Thuc.
to run over, to treat lightly of, Lat. percurrere, Xen.
to run close after, Il.
to rub on the surface, to crush, Ar.:—Pass. to be galled, Id.
metaph. to afflict, distress, destroy, ruin, Hdt., Ar.; of an actor, to murder a character, Dem.: —Pass. to be utterly destroyed or undone, Solon., Ar.; ἐπιτριβείης be hung! Ar.
to be trierarch beyond the legal time, Dem.
the burden of a trierarchy continued beyond the legal term, Dem.
rubbed down, well worn: metaph. of persons, practised, cunning, Soph.; οὑπίτριπτος the rogue, Ar.
one and a third, i. e. 1 + 1/3, or 4/3, Plat.
ἐπίτριτον (sc. δάνεισμα), a loan of which 1/3 is paid as interest, i. e. 33 1/3 p. cent., Xen.
delegated, Hdt.
to be a trustee, administrator, guardian, governor, Hdt., Xen.
c. acc. to govern, administer, πατρίδα Hdt., Ar., etc.; ἐπ. τινά to be his guardian, Thuc.:—Pass., κακῶς ἐπιτροπευθῆναι to be ill treated by one's guardians, Dem.
a reference to an arbiter, Thuc., Dem.
an action against a guardian, Id.
one to whom a charge is entrusted, a trustee, administrator, Hdt.: a governor, viceroy, Id., Dem.
a guardian, Hdt., Thuc.
adv. trippingly, fluently, glibly, Hom.
voluble, glib, Luc.
to murmur beside or over, τινί Babr.
to eat with or after, Luc.
properly, to hit the mark: hence to light or fall upon, meet with,
c. dat., Hdt., Thuc., etc.
c. gen., Ar., Thuc.
absol., ὁ ἐπιτυχών, like ὁ τυχών, the first person one meets, any one, Hdt., Plat.
to attain to, reach, gain one's end, c. gen. rei, Xen., Dem.
c. part. to succeed in doing, Hdt.
c. dat. modi, to be successful in a thing, μάχῃ Aeschin.: absol. to succeed, be successful, Plat., Xen.
ἐπ. βιβλίῳ to read it, Luc.
at or over a tomb, Aesch.
crested, a name given to larks, Theocr.
Pass. to be inflamed; ἐπιτεθυμμένος furious, rabid, Plat.
to shew forth, display, shew off, Theogn.:—Pass. to come into light, come suddenly into view, Il., Hdt.: — to present oneself, shew oneself, appear, Id.
intr. to shew light, shine upon, c. dat., NTest.
manifestation, Plut.
visible surface: outward show, distinction, Plat.
coming to light, appearing, of gods, Hdt., etc.
in full view, πόλις ἐπ. ἔξωθεν, of a place commanded by another, Thuc.
manifest, evident, of proofs, Id.
of men, conspicuous, famous, distinguished by rank, Hdt.; notable, for well or ill, Thuc., Xen.
of things, remarkable, Hdt.
adv. -νῶς, openly, Thuc.: Sup. -έστατα, Id.
in the light, alive, Soph.
at the manger, Xen.
to shine upon, τινί NTest.

entry.note: fut. ἐποίσω aor1 ἐπήνεγκα aor2 ἐπήνεγκον
entry.sense: to bring, put or lay upon, τί τινι Il., etc.; ἐπιφέρειν τινὶ πόλεμον, Lat. bellum inferre, to make war upon him, Hdt., attic; so, ἐπ. δόρυ Aesch., etc.:— absol. to attack, assail, Ar.
to bring offerings to the grave, Thuc.
to bring as a charge against, Hdt., attic; so, ἐπ. μωρίην, μανίην τινί to impute it to him, Hdt., etc.
to confer or impose upon, in good or bad sense, Thuc.
to add to, increase, Id.
Mid. to bring with or upon oneself, bring as dowry, Dem.
Pass. to rush upon or after, attack, assault, Il., Hdt., attic
to be borne onwards, Hdt.
to come after or next, ensue, τὰ ἐπιφερόμενα coming events, Id.
to utter words ominous of the event, in Mid., Hdt.
to promise according to an omen, c. inf., Eur.
to assign as authority to a thing, τοὺς θεούς Dem.
c. acc. et inf. to allege that, Plut.
to dedicate or devote to a god, Luc.
a word of ominous import, Thuc.
to reach first, part. aor2 ἐπιφθάς, Batr.
Dep. to utter after or in accordance, Lat. accinere, Aesch., Plat.
to utter, pronounce, Id.
to call to, Luc.
to bear grudge against, τινί Od., Hdt.
liable to envy or jealousy, regarded with jealousy, odious, Hdt., attic:— ἐπίφθονόν ἐστι, c. inf. 'tis invidious, hateful to . . , Hdt., Ar.:— τὸ ἐπίφθονον jealousy, odium, Thuc.
act. bearing a grudge against, τινι Aesch.: absol. injurious, Id.
adv., ἐπιφθόνως διακεῖσθαί τινι to be liable to his hatred, Thuc.; ἐπ. ἔχειν πρός τινα Xen.; ἐπ. διαπράξασθαί τι in an odious manner, Thuc.
to spit at, so as to avert a spell, ἐπιφθύζοισα (doric part.) Theocr.:—also to mutter, Id.
Dep. to labour earnestly at, τινι Xen.
to burn up, consume, Il., Hdt.; ἐπ. τὴν πόλιν to set fire to it, Thuc.
metaph. to inflame, excite, Aesch., Plut.
intr. to be scorching hot, Luc.
frightful, terrible, Aesch.

to come habitually to, visit again and again, τὸ ἐπιφοιτέον or οἱ ἐπιφοιτέοντες the visitors, Hdt.; ὁ ἐπιφοιτέων κέραμος the wine-jars which are regularly imported, Id.; ἐπ. ἐς . . to go about to different places, Thuc.
c. dat., σπάνιος ἐπ. σφι visits them rarely, of the Phoenix, Hdt.
c. acc. pers., of visions, to haunt, Id.
a bringing to or besides: a donative, addition made to one's pay, Thuc.
to put upon, lay over, Hdt., Ar., etc.
in pl. dishes served up besides or after, dessert, Hdt., etc.
carrying towards, Thuc.: favourable, Aesch.
of ground, sloping, Plut.
near the time of bringing forth, Xen.
to say besides, Hdt.
Mid., with aor1 mid. ἐπεφρασάμην and pass. ἐπεφράσθην:
c. inf. to think of doing, take into one's head to do, Hom.
c. acc. to think on, devise, contrive, Od., Hdt.:—absol., ὧδε ἐπιφρασθείς having come to this conclusion, Id.; ἐπιφρασθεῖσα αὐτή by her own mother wit, Id.
to notice, observe, Hom.:— to recognise, Od.:— to acquaint oneself with, take cognisance of, Il.
to block up, Theophr.: —Mid., ἐπ. τὰ ὦτα to stop one's ears, Luc.
to be shrewd, prudent; in part. fem. ἐπιφρονέουσα, carefully, Od.
thoughtfulness, Od.
keeping watch over, τινι Eur.
thoughtful, sage, Od.
distributed to the tribes, Eur.
the small grapes left for gleaners, Anth.: hence, Ar. calls poetasters ἐπιφυλλίδες, mere gleanings.
to plant over or upon a thing, Ar.
to produce on or besides, Theophr.
Pass., with aor2 and perf. act. ἐπέφῡν, ἐπιπέφῡκα, to grow upon, c. dat., Hdt.:— of dogs, to stick close to, Plut.
to be born after, Id.
to mention by name, tell of, Soph.
to say upon or with respect to, τινί or εἴς τι Plut.
to call out or address to, Id.
a witty saying, Plut.
acclamation, a cry, Plut.
to draw towards dawn, NTest.
to rejoice over, exult over, mostly of malignant joy, c. dat., Soph., Dem.; absol., Ar., etc.
rarely in good sense, to rejoice in another's joy, c. acc., σὲ μὲν εὖ πράσσοντ’ ἐπιχαίρω Soph.
to shower hail upon, τινά Luc.
to loosen, slacken, Luc.
intr. to give way, relax, Aesch.
to forge upon an anvil: metaph., ἐπ. τινά to forge or mould to one's purpose, Ar.
covered with copper or brass, Hdt., Ar.
to engrave upon, Plut.
gratifying, agreeable, Aesch.
Dep. to quote as a good joke, Luc.
Dep. to make a present of a thing, c. acc., Xen.
intr., ἐπιχάριτται (Boeot. for ἐπιχάρισαι, aor1 imperat.) τῷ ξένῳ be civil to him, Ar.
pleasing, agreeable, charming, Aesch., Xen.:— τὸ ἐπίχαρι pleasantness of manner, Id.—The comp. and Sup. are ἐπιχαριτώτερος, -τατος (as if from ἐπιχάριτος), Id.: adv. is also ἐπιχαρίτως, Id.
an object of malignant joy, Eur., Theocr.
malignant joy, Eur.
wherein one feels joy, delightsome, Aesch., Soph.
wherein one feels malignant joy, ἐχθροῖς ἐπίχαρτα sufferings that afford triumph to my enemies, Aesch.; οἱ δικαίως τι πάσχοντες ἐπίχαρτοι to see people justly punished is a satisfaction, Thuc.
full to the brim, brim-full, Ar.
to pass the winter at a place, Thuc.
to put one's hand on a thing, c. dat., Od., Ar.
to put one's hand to a work, set to work at, attempt, c. dat., Hdt., attic:—rarely c. acc., Theogn., Plat.:—Pass. to be attempted, Thuc.
c. inf. to endeavour or attempt to do, Hdt., attic
to make an attempt on, to set upon, attack, τινί Hdt., attic; πρός τινα Thuc.;—absol., Hdt., etc.
an attempt, enterprise, Thuc., Xen.
an attempt, attack, Hdt., Thuc.; ἐπ. ποιεῖσθαί τινος to attempt a thing, Id.
one must attempt or attack, τινί Thuc., Plat.
an enterprising person, Thuc.

wages of manual labour: generally wages, pay, guerdon, reward, Ar., Plat.:—also in bad sense, τῆς ὑψηγόρου γλώσσης ἐπ. rewards for proud speech, Aesch.; ξιφέων ἐπ. the wages of the sword, i. e. slaughter by it, Soph.
to vote in favour of a proposed decree, to sanction by vote, Dem.
of magistrates, to admit one elected to office, ap. Dem.
a voting by show of hands, Dem.

entry.note: fut. -χεῶ 2 pers. ἐπιχεῖς aor1 ἐπέχεα epic pres. ἐπιχεύω aor1 ἐπέχευα inf. ἐπιχεῦαι
entry.sense: to pour water over the hands, Hom., attic:—metaph. to pour or shed over, ὕπνον τινί, etc., Hom.
of solids, like χώννυμι, Id.
Mid. to pour or throw over oneself or for himself, Od.
to have poured out for one to drink, ἐπ. ἄκρατόν τινος to drink it to any one's health, Theocr.
Pass. to be poured over, Xen.: aor1 ἐπεχύθην [ῠ], perf. -κέχῠμαι:—metaph., of a crowd of persons, to stream to a place, ἐπέχυντο (epic aor2 pass.), Il.:— to come like a stream over, Hdt.
upon the earth, earthly, as epith. of mortals, Hom.; absol., ἐπιχθόνιοι earthly ones, men on earth, Il.
to make a mock of, τι Plut.: to say scornfully, Babr.
to warm slightly, Luc.
act. producing bile, ποίη ἐπιχολωτάτη Hdt.
to dance to or in honour of a thing, Ar.
to come dancing on, Xen.
to supply besides, τί τινι NTest.: —Pass., Id.
additional help, NTest.

entry.etym: only in imperf. or aor2 ἐπέχραον,
entry.sense: to attack, assault, c. dat., Il.; μητέρι μοι μνηστῆρες ἐπέχραον beset her, Od.
to lend besides, cf. ἐπικίχρημι.
Dep. to make use of besides, c. dat., Eur.
c. dat. pers., Lat. uti, to have dealings with, be friends with, Hdt., Thuc.
Dep. to spit upon, τινι Luc.
smeared over:—metaph. spurious, Lat. fucatus, Luc.
to anoint, besmear, Od.:—Mid. to anoint oneself, Id.
to plaster over, τι ἐπί τι NTest.; τινί with a thing, Luc.
overlaid with gold, Hdt., Xen.
to lay on like colour, Plat.
to smear over, colour on the surface, tinge, τινί with a thing, Luc.
to give way, yield, τινί to one, Soph.
to forgive, Plut.
to come towards, join as an ally, Lat. accedere alicui, Thuc., Xen.
to go against the enemy, Id.
to be in the habit of visiting, Plat.; ἐπ. τοῖς ἄνω πράγμασι to be occupied with, Luc.
in or of the country:
of persons, οἱ ἐπ. the people of the country, natives, Hdt., al.; οἱ ἐπιχώριοι χθονός Soph., Eur.

of things, of or used in the country, Hdt., Ar.;—often, τὸ ἐπιχώριον, τοὐπιχώριον the custom of the country, custom, fashion, Id., Thuc., etc.; ἐπιχώριον ὂν ἡμῖν, c. inf., as is the custom of our country, Thuc.
adv. -ίως, Ar.

to touch on the surface, touch lightly, handle, c. gen., Hes., Hdt., attic; κἂν ὀλίγον νυκτός τις ἐπιψαύσῃσι, i. e. if one gets ever so little of the night, i. e. sleeps ever so little, Theocr.:—metaph. to touch lightly upon, Lat. strictim attingere, Hdt.
intr., ὅστ’ ὀλίγον περ ἐπιψαύῃ πραπίδεσσιν who can reach ever so little way by his wits, Od.
to keep dropping, ὁ θεὸς ἐπιψακάζει, of small rain, 'tis drizzling, Ar.
a curb-chain, Anth.
Dep.
to lie still more, Xen.
to attribute falsehood to, τί τινι Luc.
to falsify a number, Plut.
to feel by passing the hand over the surface, Plat.; ἐπ. τινός to feel for it, Id.
to put a question to the vote (the office of the President) in the Athenian Senate or Assembly, ἐπ. τὰς γνώμας Aeschin., Dem.; c. inf. to put it to the vote that . . , Thuc.
absol. to put the question, Id., Xen.
ἐπ. τινί to put the question for or at the instance of any one, Hdt.
ἐπ. τοὺς παρόντας to put the question to them, take their votes, Plat.
Pass. to be put to the vote, Aeschin.
Mid., of the voters, to vote, Luc.
exposed to blame, blameworthy, Xen.: —adv. -γως, Plut.
act. censorious, Aesch.
to cool, Plut.
places of shelter for ships, roadsteads, Od.
presiding over the furrows, Anth.
Dep. to lament over a thing, Anth.
to go as settler or colonist to a place, to settle in a place, c. acc., Eur.; ἐν τόπῳ Xen.
to be settled with hostile views against, ὑμῖν Thuc.: Pass., ἡ Δεκέλεια τῇ χώρᾳ ἐποικεῖται Deceleia is occupied as a base of operations against the country, Id.
to build up, Thuc.
to build upon, Xen.
to rebuild, Id., Dem.
one who has settled among strangers, a settler, alien, Soph., Plat.
a colonist, Ar., Thuc.
as adj. neighbouring, Aesch.: hence again as Subst. a neighbour, one near, Soph.
to have compassion on, τινά Soph.; absol., Aesch.
to compassionate, c. acc., Soph.
pitiable, piteous, Aesch.
piteous, Aesch.
to lament over, πάθει Aesch.
Dep.
to go towards, approach, c. acc., Od., Theogn.
to approach with hostile purpose, set on, attack, c. acc., Il.
to go over, traverse, Id.
to go round, visit in succession (cf. ἔπειμι (εἶμι ibo) III), of one who hands round wine, ἐπῴχετο οἰνοχοεύων Od.; of a general, to go round, inspect, στίχας Hom.; and absol. to go the rounds, Il.
of Apollo and Artemis to visit with death, Hom.
to go over or ply one's work, Id.; ἱστὸν ἐπ. to ply the loom, Lat. percurrere telam, Id.:—absol. in partic., busily, Il.
to run a ship ashore, Hdt., Thuc.
of the ship, to run aground, Id.
uneven, projecting, Anth.
to slip or glide upon, Anth.
to shout for joy, τινί at or to one, Aesch.; τι over or at a thing, Id.;—also in Mid., Id.
to pour rain upon, Anth.
heavy rain, abundance of wet, wet weather, Ar.
very rainy, Arist.
to swear after, swear accordingly, Od.: to take an oath besides, Thuc.
c. acc. pers., to swear by, Hdt., Eur., etc.: so in Mid., ap. Dem.
c. acc. rei, to swear to a thing, Xen.
c. inf. to swear that, Hdt., Eur.; so in Mid., Dem.
absol. in aor1 part., ἐπομόσας upon oath, Hdt., Xen.
on the navel or central point, on the boss of the shield (Lat. umbo), Il.
to be reproached, shameful, ignominious, Eur., Plat.; ἐπονείδιστόν ἐστι is matter of reproach, Dem.
to give a surname: to name or call so and so, Thuc., Plat.:—Pass. to be named, ἀπό τινος or τινος after one, Thuc., Eur.:— to be surnamed, Thuc.
to pronounce a name, Hdt.
Dep., to regard with awe, to reverence, Od., Theogn.
epic poetry or an epic poem, Hdt.
an epic poet, Hdt.
to roast besides or after, Od.
to look over, overlook, watch, of an overseer, Od., Aesch., etc.:—also, to visit, punish, Id., Plat.
to become an ἐπόπτης, be admitted to the highest mysteries, epic Plat.; proverb. to attain to the highest earthly happiness, Ar.
a cry to mimic that of the hoopoe (ἔποψ), Ar.
of tutelary gods, λιτῶν Aesch.
an overseer, watcher, ἐπ. πόνων a spectator, Aesch.; ἐπ. τῶν στρατηγουμένων Dem.
one admitted to the highest mysteries, Plut.
of or for an ἐπόπτης, τὰ τέλεα καὶ ἐπ. the highest mysteries, Plat.
to hold out to, give yet more, Il.; so in Mid., Solon.
Mid. to stretch oneself towards, ἐπορεξάμενος reaching forward to strike, Il.
metaph. to rise in one's demands, Hdt.
to set upright, of the voice, to lift up, Aesch.; absol., ἐπορθ. γόοις to lift up the voice in wailing, Id.
to utter aloud, Eur.
to stir up, arouse, excite, Il.
to rouse and send against, c. dat., ὕπνον ἐπῶρσε sent sleep upon her, Od.
Pass. ἐπόρνῠμαι, with perf2 act. ἐπόρωρα, 3rd sg. epic aor2 pass. ἐπῶρτο: — to rise against, assault, fly upon one, c. dat., Il.; absol., Id.:—of things, c. inf., Od.
to rush violently at or upon, c.dat., Il.; absol., Id.: to rush after, i. e. to seek him, Id.; of sleep, to overtake, Od.
Dep. to dance to the tune of, c. gen., Dem.
a word, Od., etc.:— a tale, story, lay, Id.
a pledged word, promise, Il., etc.
a word of advice, counsel, Id.
the word of a deity, a prophecy, oracle, Od., Hdt., Trag.:—later also, a saying, saw, proverb, Hdt.
the meaning, substance, subject of a speech, a thing or matter, Il.
Phrases:— ἅμα ἔπος τε καὶ ἔργον ἐποίεε "no sooner said than done," Hdt.
κατ’ ἔπος word by word, exactly, Ar.
οὐδὲν πρὸς ἔπος nothing to the purpose, Plat.
ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν or ὡς εἰπεῖν ἔπος, so to say, as the saying is, Eur., etc.
ἑνὶ ἔπει in one word, briefly, Hdt.
in pl. poetry in heroic verse, epic poetry, opp. to μέλη (lyric poetry), etc., Id., attic: also, generally, poetry, Pind.
in sg. a verse or line of poetry, Hdt., Ar.
to yell out, utter lamentably, Eur.
to stir up, excite, urge on, Hom., Hdt., etc.; c. inf., Il., etc.; c. dat. et inf., ἑτάροισιν ἐποτρῦναι κατακῆαι to urge them to burn, Od.

c. acc. rei, to stir up against, Id.; ἀγγελίας ἐπ. sends urgent messages, Id.; ξύνοδον ἐπώτρυνον τοῖς ὁπλίταις gave the signal for engagement to the men-at-arms, Thuc.:—Mid., ἐποτρυνώμεθα πομπήν let us urge on our escort, Od.:—Pass. to press on, hasten, Aesch.
on the tail, Anth.
in heaven, heavenly, Hom.
οἱ ἐπουράνιοι the gods above, Theocr.:— τὰ ἐπ. the phenomena of the heavens, Plat.
to waft onwards, Luc.

to blow favourably upon, of a fair wind (οὖρος), ἐπ. τὴν ὀθόνην to fill the sail, Luc.:— metaph., φρόνημα ἐπ. to turn one's mind successfully to a thing, Eur.: c. acc. cogn., πνεῦμα αἱματηρὸν ἐπ. τινί (of the Erinyes) to send after him a gale of murderous breath, Aesch.
blowing favourably, Soph.
to owe besides or still, Thuc.
to cast longing glances at, c. dat., or πρός τι Plut.
Pass. with fut. mid., to be carried upon, ride upon, c. dat., Il.; absol., κάμηλον ὥστε ἐποχεῖσθαι a camel to ride on, Xen.
to carry water by sluices or courses, Lat. derivare, Plat.
a check, cessation: the epoch of a star, i. e. the point at which it seems to halt after reaching the zenith, Plut.
on or of the mountains, Anth.
the saddle-cloth, housing, Xen.
mounted upon a horse, chariot, ship, c. gen. vel dat., ναῶν ἔποχοι, ἅρμασιν ἔποχοι Aesch.: metaph., λόγος μανίας ἔπ. words borne on madness, i. e. frantic words, Eur.
absol. having a good seat on horseback, Xen.
pass., ποταμὸς ναυσὶ ἔπ. navigable by ships, Plut.
for eating with bread, Anth.
that can be looked on, Soph.
full in view, conspicuous, Soph.
act. overlooking all things, of gods, Id.
a view over, ἐπ’ ὅσον ἔπ. τοῦ ἱροῦ εἶχε so far as the view from the temple reached, Hdt.; τὴν ἔποψιν τῆς ναυμαχίας ἔχειν to view the sea-fight, Thuc.
the hoopoe, Lat. upupa, Ar.
of seven bulls'-hides, Il.
worth seven δραχμαί, Theocr.
of seven years: neut. ἑπτάετες as adv. for seven years, Od.
seven years old, Plat.:—fem. -έτις, ιδος, Anth.
seventeen, Hdt., etc.
17 feet long, Plat.
seventeenth, Thuc.
twenty-seven years old, Anth.
seventy-thousand, Hdt., etc.
seven times, Lat. septies, Ar., etc.
seven-thousand, Hdt., etc.
with seven couches or beds, Xen.
seven hundred, Hdt., etc.
of seven lances, i. e. seven bodies of spearmen, Soph.
on seven hills, of Rome, Anth.
born in the seventh month, Hdt.
seven-stringed, Luc., Anth.
the seven districts, Plut.
seven, Lat. septem, Hom., etc.
seven cubits long, Hdt., etc.
seven feet long, Il., Hes.
with seven paths, of the Pleiads, Eur.
with seven gates, epith. of Boeotian Thebes, Hom., etc.;—Egyptian Thebes being ἑκατόμπυλοι.
seven-towered, of Thebes, Eur., etc.
seven-mouthed, with seven portals, of Thebes, Eur.
with seven walls, of Thebes, Aesch.
seven-toned, Eur.
seven-toned, Eur.
seven-voiced, Luc.
adv. in seven parts, Od.
seven years old, Ar.; nom. pl. ἑπτέτεις Plat.

entry.note: ἐπύλλιον, ου, τό, Dim. of ἔπος
entry.sense: a versicle, scrap of poetry, Ar.
an assessment of an obol in the drachma, to be paid by the plaintiff, in case he failed to gain 1/5 of the votes, Dem.
a song sung to or over: an enchantment, charm, spell, Od., Hdt., attic: c. gen. objecti, a charm for or against a thing, Aesch.
singing to or over: as Subst. an enchanter, Eur.: c. gen. acting as a charm for or against, Aesch., Plat.
pass. sung or said after, μορφῆς ἐπῳδόν called after this form, Eur.
in metre, ἐπῳδός, ὁ, a verse or passage returning at intervals, a chorus, burden, refrain, as in Theocr. 1.
to cluck, like a sitting bird, Ar.
to push on, thrust in, Plut.
upon the arm, Hhymn.
on the shoulders, Theocr. 1.
on the shoulder, Anth.
the point of the shoulder, where it joins the collar-bone, the acromion, Xen.:— the shoulder, Anth.
the front or the uppermost part of a ship, Id.
the shoulder-strap of a tunic, Eur.
on oath, sworn, Soph.
pass. witness of oaths, Id.

a surname, name given after some person or thing, Lat. cognomen, as Polynices, (from πολύς, νεῖκος), Aesch.; ἐπ. ποιεῖσθαι, θέσθαι to take a surname, Hdt.; καλεῖσθαι ἐπωνυμίην ἐπί τινος after some one, Id.; ἔχειν ἐπ. ἀπό τινος Id., Thuc.; ἐπ. σχεῖν χώρας to have the naming of it, i. e. have it named after one, Id.; with inf. added, ἐπ. ἔχει εἶναί τι he has a name for being, may be said to be, Plat.
generally, a name, Hdt.
called by the name of, τινός Hdt.

given as a name, τῷ Ὀδυσεὺς ὄνομ’ ἐπώνυμος Odysseus is the name given him, Od.; Ἀλκυόνην καλέεσκον ἐπώνυμον Alcyone they called her by name, Il.; Ἀρήτη δ’ ὄνομ’ ἐστὶν ἐπώνυμον Arete (the Desired) is the name given her, Od.
named besides, surnamed, Hdt.
named after a person or thing, c. gen., Id., Trag.; also, ἐπ. ἐπί τινος Hdt.
act. giving one's name to a thing or person, ἐπώνυμον (sc. τὸ σάκος), which gives thee thy name (of Eurysaces), Soph.
at Athens, οἱ ἐπώνυμοι (sc. ἥρωες), the heroes after whom the Attic φυλαί had their names, Dem.
ἄρχων ἐπ. the first Archon, who gave his name to the current year.
to observe, watch, Aesch.
to howl at, Anth.
to be about, be busy with, τεύχε’ ἕποντα busy with his armour, Il.: cf. ἀμφι-έπω, δι-έπω, ἐφ-έπω, μεθέπω, περι-έπω.
Mid. ἕπομαι to follow, whether after or in company with, Hom.; c. dat. pers., Id.:—also ἕπεσθαι ἅμα τινί Il., etc.; μετά τινι or τινα Id., etc.
to follow, as attendants, Od.:— also to escort, attend, by way of honour, Lat. prosequi, Il.
in hostile sense, to pursue, τινι Id.
to keep pace with, ἕπεθ’ ἵπποις Hom.: metaph. of a man's limbs, they do his bidding, Id.
to follow the motions of another, τρυφάλεια ἕσπετο χειρί the helm went with his hand, i. e. came off in his hand, Il.
to follow, obey, submit to, τῶι νόμωι Hdt., attic
simply, to come near, approach, only in imperat., ἕπεο προτέρω come on nearer, Hom.
to follow up, esp. in mind, to understand, Plat.
of Things, as of honour, glory, etc., τούτωι κῦδος ἅμ’ ἕψεται Il., etc.
to follow upon, τῆι ἀχαριστίαι ἡ ἀναισχυντία ἕπ. Xen.

entry.etym: prob. made up by Nicander as present of εἶπον.
entry.sense: to say, Nicander.
beams projecting like ears on each side of a ship's bows, whence the anchors were let down, cat-heads, Eur., Thuc.
to aid or succour one in a thing, τινά τι Soph., etc.; ἐπ. τινα to aid or succour, Id.; also τινι Id., Eur.
δῶρον, ὃ μήποτ’ ἐπωφέλησα ἐξελέσθαι a gift, which would that I never had received, Id.
a help, store, βορᾶς Soph.
help, succour, Anth.
πᾶσαι γὰρ [πύλαι] ἐπώχατο all the gates were kept shut, Il.
the Lat. terra, earth:—hence Adv. ἔραζε.
to earth, to the ground, Hom.; doric ἔρασδε Theocr.
to love, to be in love with, c. gen. pers., Hom., Eur.
of things, to love passionately, long for, lust after, Il., Hdt., attic
c. inf. to desire eagerly, Theogn., Soph., etc.
lay under contribution, τινά Dem.
c. acc. rei, to collect by contributions, to beg, borrow, Aeschin.: metaph. to combine, Anth.:— Mid. to collect for oneself, borrow, Luc.
to assist by contribution, τινί Dem.
lovely, of places, Hom., Theocr.
a meal to which each contributed his share, Lat. coena collaticia, a pic-nic, Od., Eur.

any contribution, Lat. symbola, such as Athenians paid to pay for the support of the poor or state necessities, Ar.; ἐράνους λέλοιπε he has left his subscriptions unpaid, Dem.; ἔρανον φέρειν, simply, to contribute freely, Id.
a kindness, service, favour, Eur., Thuc., etc.
a society of subscribers to a common fund, a club, Dem.
loving money, Xen.
lovely, Xen.:— beloved, desired, Aesch., Xen.: neut. as adv., Anth.
to long for, c. gen., Aesch.
a lover, properly of persons, Ar., etc.:—metaph. of things, τυραννίδος Hdt.; πολέμων Eur.; ἐρ. πραγμάτων = πολυπράγμων, Ar.; ἐρ. τοῦ πονεῖν fond of work, Id.; ἐρ. ἐπαίνου Xen.
beloved, lovely, Plat.
lovely, charming, Hom.; of a man, ἑτάροις ἐρατεινός welcome to his comrades, Od.
epic form of ἐράω, κρειῶν ἐρατίζων greedy after meat, Hom.
lovely, charming, Il., Hes., etc.: —neut. as adv., ἐρατὸν κιθαρίζειν Hhymn.
beloved, Tyrtae.
fair of face, Anth.
Erato, the lovely, one of the Muses, Hes.
one of the Oceanides, Id.
to love, to be in love with, c. gen. pers., Xen., etc.: c. acc. cogn., ἐρᾶν ἔρωτα Eur.:—absol., ἐρῶν a lover, opp. to ἡ ἐρωμένη the beloved one, Hdt.
of things, to love or desire passionately, τυραννίδος Archil.; μάχης Aesch.; and c. inf. to desire to do, Soph., Eur.
to pour out, vomit forth, Aesch.
to work, labour, properly of husbandry, Hes., Thuc., etc.; but also of all manual labour, Od., Hdt.:—also of things, as Vulcan's bellows, Il.
trans. to work at, make, build, Od., attic
to do, perform, accomplish, Hom., attic:—c. dupl. acc. to do something to another, Hdt., etc.; κακὰ ἐργάζεσθαί τινα Soph., Thuc.
to work a material, χρυσὸν εἰργάζετο Od.; ἐργ. γῆν to work the land, Hdt.
to earn by working, χρήματα Id., attic
to work at, practise, Lat. exercere, τέχνην Plat.
absol. to work at a trade or business, to traffic, trade, Dem.
the perf. pass. εἴργασμαι is used in act. sense, as Hdt., Soph.; but also in pass. sense,
to be made or built, ἔργαστο τὸ τεῖχος Hdt.; ἐκ πέτρας εἰργασμένος Aesch., etc.
to be done, Id. —The fut. ἐργασθήσομαι always in pass. sense, Soph., etc.
to sever, cut off, Il.
to hold back, check, Soph., Eur.
a tool, instrument, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
Desiderat. of ἐργάζομαι, to be about to do, Soph.
work, daily labour, business, Lat. labor, Hhymn., attic; δὸς ἐργασίαν, c. inf., Lat. da operam ut . . , NTest.
a working at, making, building, τειχῶν Thuc.; ἱματίων, ὑποδημάτων Plat., etc.
a working of a material, τοῦ σιδήρου Hdt.; τῶν χρυσείων μετάλλων Thuc., Ar., etc.
generally, trade, commerce, Xen., Dem.
a practising, exercising, τῶν τεχνῶν Plat.
a work of art, production, τετράγωνος ἐργ., of the Hermae, Thuc.
of land, arable, Xen., etc.
one must work the land, Xen.
τοὖργον ἔστ’ ἐργ. it must be done or one must do it, Aesch., Eur.
any place in which work is done: a workshop, manufactory, Hdt., attic: a mine, quarry, Dem.:— a butcher's shop, Ar.
a workman, husbandman, Xen.
able to work, working, industrious, Plat., Xen.
producing an income, Plut.
a workman: esp. one who works the soil, a husbandman, Hdt., attic; οὑργάτης λεώς the country- folk, Ar.
as adj. hard-working, strenuous, Xen.
one who practises an art, c. gen., Id.
a doer, worker, Soph., Xen.
given to labour, diligent, active, Plat.; of the Nile, from its activity in depositing silt, Hdt.: adv. -κῶς τι advantageously, Plut.
a husbandman, Theocr.
as adj., active, laborious, Anth.
c. gen. making a thing or practising an art, Id.
a workwoman: as adj. laborious, industrious, active, Hdt., Soph.
c. gen. working at or producing a thing, Aesch.; νέκταρος ἐργ., of bees, Anth.
a work, deed, business, Theogn., Aesch., etc.
to confine, epic imperf. ἐέργνυν, Od.
one who lets out work, opp. to ἐργολάβος, Xen.
to contract for the execution of work, ἐργ. ἀνδριάντας, Lat. statuas conducere faciendas, Xen.:—absol. to work for hire, ply a trade, Dem.
one who contracts for the execution of work, a contractor, Lat. conductor, redemptor, opp. to ἐργοδότης, Plat.
work, Hom., etc.; τὰ σαυτῆς ἔργα κόμιζε mind your own business, Hom.:
in Il. mostly of deeds of war, πολεμήϊα ἔργα Il., etc.; so, ἐν τῷ ἔργῳ during the action, Thuc.; ἔργου ἔχεσθαι to engage in battle, Id.

of works of industry, tilled lands, fields, farms, Hom.; οὔτε βοῶν οὔτ’ ἀνδρῶν ἔργα (cf. Virgil's hominumque boumque labores), Il.; ἔργα Ἰθάκης the tilled lands of Ithaca, Od.; so in attic, τὰ κατ’ ἀγροὺς ἔργα, etc.:—then, generally, property, wealth, possessions, ἔργον ἀέξειν Od.
of women's work, weaving, Hom.

of other occupations, θαλάσσια ἔργα fishing, as a way of life, Od.; periphr., ἔργα δαιτός works of feasting, Il.; so, ἔργα θήρας, etc. Xen., etc.:—in attic also of all kinds of works, such as mines, iron- works, Id., Dem.
a hard piece of work, a hard task, Il.: also, a shocking deed or act, Lat. facinus, Od.:— also, χερμάδιον λάβε Τυδείδης, μέγα ἔργον a huge mass, Il.
a deed, action, often, as opp. to ἔπος, deed, not word, Hom.
a thing, matter, πᾶν ἔργον in every point, Il.; ἄκουε τοὔργον Soph., etc.
Pass. that which is wrought, a work, of the arms of Achilles, Il.; metal-work is called ἔργον Ἡφαίστοιο Od., etc.
the result of work, ἔργον χρημάτων profit on money, Dem.
the following pecul. attic phrases arise from signf. I:
ἔργον ἐστί,
c. gen. pers. his business, his proper work, ἔργον ἀγαθοῦ πολίτου Plat.; so, σὸν ἔργον ἐστί it is your business, Aesch.
c. gen. rei, there is need of, use of a thing, Eur.
c. inf. it is hard work, difficult to do, πολὺ ἔργον ἂν εἴη διεξελθεῖν Xen., etc.; οὐκ ἔργον θρηνεῖσθαι 'tis no use to lament, Soph.
ἔργα παρέχειν τινί to give one trouble, Ar.; ἔργον ἔχειν to take trouble, Xen.
a husbandman, Anth.

entry.etym: for aor2 εἴργαθον v. sub ἐργαθεῖν
Mid. and Pass., fut. ἔρξομαι, attic εἴρξομαι
entry.sense: to bar one's way either by shutting in or shutting out:

to shut in, shut up, Lat. includere, Hom.; ἐντὸς ἐέργειν to enclose, bound, Il.; ἂψ ἐπὶ νῆας ἔεργε drove them to the ships and shut them up there, Id.:—of things, δόμον ἐέργειν to shut it up, Od.: —Pass., ἔρχατο were fenced in, Il.; γέφυραι ἐεργμέναι well-secured, strong-built, Id.
to shut out, Lat. excludere, Hom.; ἐκτὸς ἐέργειν Od.

c. gen. to shut out or keep away from, Il., Hdt., attic; and with Preps., ἔργ. τι ἀπό τινος Il.; c. dat. pers., εἴργειν μητρὶ δόρυ to keep it off from her, Aesch.:— Pass., εἰργόμενον θανάτου short of death, Aeschin.:— Mid. to keep oneself or abstain from, Hdt., Soph.

to hinder, prevent from doing, Theogn.:—Pass., οὐδὲν εἴργεται nothing is barred, i. e. all things are permitted, Soph.:—c. inf., mostly with μή added; εἴργει τόνδε μὴ θανεῖν νόμος Eur.; c. inf. only, οὐδὲν εἴργει τελειοῦσθαι τάδε Soph.
to do work, obsol. Root, for which ἔρδω, ῥέζω, ἐργάζομαι are used in the pres.: for the fut., aor1 and perf., v. ἔρδω.
irksome, troublesome, Xen., etc.

to do, Hom., etc.; often c. dupl. acc., to do something to a person, κακὰ πολλὰ ἔοργεν Τρῶας Il.; also, εὖ or κακῶς ἔρδειν τινά Theogn., etc.; simply, ἔρδ. τινά to do one harm, Soph.; ἔρδ. πήματα to work mischief, Aesch.; ἔρδοι τις ἣν ἕκαστος εἰδείη τέχνην let each man practise the art he knows, Ar.
to make or offer a sacrifice (v. ῥέζω), Hom., Hdt.:— absol., like Lat. facere, operari, Hes.
dark, gloomy, Il., Hes.
a kind of pulse, chick-pea, Lat. cicer, Il., Ar. Cf. ὄροβος.
to grope about in darkness, Ar.
from nether gloom, Eur.
to or into Erebus, Od.
Erebus, a place of nether darkness, above Hades, Hom., etc.:—metaph., ἔρεβος ὕφαλον the darkness of the deep, Soph.
to ask, c. acc. pers. to ask of one, Od.; c. acc. rei, to ask a thing, Hom.; c. dupl. acc., ἐρ. τινά τι to ask one a thing, Od.:—so in Med. Od.

to rouse to anger, rouse to fight, irritate, Hom., Hdt., etc.: to provoke to curiosity, Od.; metaph., ἐρ. χορούς to stir them, Eur.:—Pass. to be provoked, excited, Hdt., Ar.; of fire, φέψαλος ἐρεθιζόμενος ῥιπίδι a spark kindled by the bellows, Id.; αἰθὴρ ἐρεθιζέσθω βροντῆι Aesch.; of one who is out of breath, Eur.
a stirring up, exciting, Ar.
to stir to anger, provoke, irritate, Hom.: c. acc. rei, ἤρεθον ᾠδάν they raised a song, Theocr.
to make one thing lean against another, τι πρός τι or τι ἐπί τινι Hom.; of Atlas supporting heaven, Aesch., Eur., etc.:—generally, to fix firmly, ἐρ. ὄμμα, Lat. figere oculos, εἴς τι Id.
to prop, stay, support, ἀσπὶς ἄρ’ ἀσπίδ’ ἔρειδε, κόρυς κόρυν, ἀνέρα δ’ ἀνήρ, of close ranks of men-at-arms, Il.
to hurl forth, Ar.; and in Mid., Id.
to infix, plant in, τί τινι Soph.; ἐρ. πληγήν to inflict a blow, Eur.
of wagers or matches, to set one pledge against another, Theocr.
intr. to lean against, jostle, c. dat., Od.
to set upon, press hard, c. dat., Il.; εἴς τινα Ar.; absol., of an illness, Aesch.
generally, \6tto go to work, fall to, of eating, Ar.
Mid. and Pass. to lean upon, c. dat., Il.; ἐπί τινος and τινος, Id.: absol. to plant oneself firmly, take a firm stand, Id.; οὔδεϊ χαῖται ἐρηρέδαται their hair rests on the ground, Id.
to be fixed firm, planted, ἔγχος διὰ θώρηκος ἠρήρειστο had been fixed, Id., etc.; λᾶε ἐρηρέδαται the stones are firmly set, Id.
Mid.,
in recipr. sense, to strive one with another, contend, Id.
c. acc. to support for oneself, βάκτρωι ἐρείδου στίβον Eur.; ἐρ. ἐπὶ τοίχωι λίθον Theocr.
heath, heather, Lat. erica, Aesch., Theocr.
to rend, Hes., Aesch.: Pass., ἐρεικόμενος περὶ δουρί Il.
to bruise, pound, shatter, Aesch.
intr. only in aor2 ἤρικον, to be rent, to shiver, Il.
a fallen ruin, wreck, mostly in pl., ναυτικὰ ἐρ. pieces of wreck, Aesch., Eur.; also, οἰκημάτων ἐρ. ruins of houses, Hdt.; ἐρ. πέπλων fragments, Eur.; cf. ἐρείπω.

to throw or dash down, tear down, Il., Hdt.: metaph., ἐρείπει γένος θεῶν τις some god brings the family to ruin, Soph.:—Pass. to be thrown down, fall in ruins, Il.; ἐν ἐρειπίοις νεκρῶν ἐρειφθείς a ruin amid the ruins of the dead, Soph.; ἐρείπεται κτύπος the thunder comes crashing down, Id.
intr., in aor2 ἤριπον, epic ἔριπον, to fall down, tumble, fall headlong, Hom.
a prop, stay, support, Lat. columen, Soph., Eur.:—in pl. the props to keep a boat on shore upright, Theocr.
