thrown down, in ruins, Eur.
overthrowing walls, c. gen., Aesch.
black, swart, dark, Hom., Aesch., etc.:—metaph., ἐρεμνὴ φάτις a dark, obscure rumour, Soph.
Dep. to feed on, c. acc., λωτόν, κρῖ λευκόν, πυρὸν ἐρεπτόμενοι Hom.
to row, Hom., Soph.; of birds flying, πτεροῖς ἐρ. Eur.

trans. to speed by rowing; metaph., γόων ἐρέσσετ’ πίτυλον ply the measured stroke of lamentation, Aesch.:—Pass. to be rowed, Id.; of birds, πτερύγων ἐρετμοῖσιν ἐρεσσόμενοι with the oarage of wings (cf. Virgil's remigio alarum), Id.
generally, to put in quick motion, ply, τὸν πόδα Eur.: —metaph., ἐρ. ἀπειλάς to set threats in motion, Soph.; ἐρ. μῆτιν Id.:—Pass., of a bow, to be plied, handled, Id.
to row through the sea, Anth.
only in pres. to talk lightly, to be jocular, Plat.
trans. to jest upon, quiz, banter, τινά Id.
a rower, Od., Hdt., attic
in pl., also, oars, Anth.
of or for rowers, ἐρ. πληρώματα crews of rowers, Plut.
Lat. remus, an oar, Od., Eur.: —of wings, v. ἐρέσσω II. 1.
to furnish with oars, set to row, Eur.
an Eretrian, Hdt., etc.
to spit or spew out, to disgorge, Lat. eructare, c. acc. Il.:—absol. to belch, Lat. ructare, Od.
metaph. of the sea, to surge, break in foam against the land, Hom.
in aor2 act., to bellow, roar, properly of oxen (cf. ἐρύγμηλος), ἤρυγεν ὡς ὅτε ταῦρος ἤρυγεν Il.
madder, Hdt.
to be red, Luc.
to make red, stain red, Il.:—Pass. to be or become red, Theocr.
inquiry, search, ἔρ. ἔχειν τινός to make search for one, Soph.; ᾄσσειν εἰς ἔρευναν Eur.
to seek or search for, search after, track, Hom., attic; ὧν χρείαν ἐρευνᾶι the things whereof he seeks after the use, i. e. whatever things he finds serviceable, Soph.
to search a place, Hdt., Theocr.
to enquire after, examine, Eur., Plat.
c. inf. to seek to do, Theocr.
one must seek out, Xen.
to cover with a roof, ἔρεψαν ὄροφον made a roof, Il.: θάλαμον ἐρ. Od.
to cover with a crown, to crown, Soph.: —Mid. to crown oneself, Eur.
from Ἐρεχθεύς as a name of the Athenians, Trag.
an ancient hero of Attica, the render (from ἐρέχθω).
to rend, break, Od.:—Pass., of a ship, to be shattered by the winds, Il.
a roofing, roof, Plut.

entry.etym: epic Verb, = ἐρεείνω, ἔρομαι, ἐρωτάω, not to be confounded with ἐρέω, future of ἐρῶ
entry.sense: to ask, enquire, τι about a thing, Hom.
c. acc. pers. to question, μάντιν ἐρείομεν (epic for ἐρέωμεν) Il.; ἀλλήλους ἐρέοιμεν Od.
to be left lonely, go alone, ἐρημάζεσκον (ionic imperf.) Theocr.
desolate, solitary, Mosch.: c. gen. bereft of, Anth.
of places, a solitude, desert, wilderness, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
as a state or condition, solitude, loneliness, ἐρημίαν ἄγειν, ἔχειν to keep alone, Eur.; of persons, isolation, desolation, Soph.; δι’ ἐρημίαν from being left alone, Thuc.
c. gen. want of, absence, Eur., Thuc., etc.; τὴν ἐρ. ὁρῶν τῶν κωλυσόντων seeing that there would be none to hinder him, Dem.; ἐρ. κακῶν freedom from evil, Eur.
a solitary devotee, Theocr.
void of hair, Anth.
chattering in the desert, Anth.
haunting the wilds, Anth.
reft of one's city, Eur.
desolate, lone, lonely, lonesome, solitary:
of places, Hdt., attic; τὰ ἐρ. desert parts, Hdt., etc.; ἡ ἐρῆμος (sc. χώρα), Id.
of persons or animals, Il., Aesch., etc.: desolate, helpless, Soph., Dem.:—neut. pl. as adv., ἔρημα κλαίω I weep in solitude, Eur.
of conditions, Soph.
c. gen. reft of, void or destitute of, Hdt., attic
of persons, with no bad sense, wanting, without, ἐρῆμος ὅπλων Hdt.

ἐρήμη δίκη, ἡ, an undefended action, in which one party does not appear, and judgment goes against him by default, Thuc., etc.: so ἐρήμη or ἔρημος (without δίκη), ἐρήμην εἷλον I got judgment by default, Dem.; ἔρημον ὦφλε he let it go by default, Id.; ἐρήμην κατηγορεῖν to accuse in a case where there was no defence, Plat.
solitude, Anth.
loving solitude, Anth.
to strip bare, to desolate, lay waste, ἱερά Thuc.:—Pass., Hdt., etc.
to bereave one of a thing, c. gen., ἐρ. ναυβατῶν ἐρετμά to leave the oars without men, Eur.:—Pass. to be bereft of, c. gen., Hdt., Aesch.
to set free or deliver from, c. gen., Eur.
to abandon, desert, c. acc., Aesch., Eur.; ἐρ. Συρακούσας to evacuate it, Thuc.
to keep in solitude, isolate, Eur.: —Pass. to be isolated from, c. gen., Hdt.
a desolator, Anth.
to keep back, restrain, check, Hom.; πολλὰ κέλευθος ἐρατύοι let a long distance bar thy approach, Soph.
c. gen. to keep away from, Eur.
with high-arching neck, of horses, Il.
loud-shouting, Anth.
of Zeus, loud-thundering, Il.: loud-sounding, αὐλός Anth.
loud-shouting, Hhymn.
loud-bellowing, Hhymn.: loud-braying, of the trumpet, Anth.
with large clods, very fertile, Od.:—so, ἐρί-βωλος, Hom.
loud-thundering, Hom.
to wrangle, quarrel, dispute, Hom.; c. dat., ἐριδαίνετον ἀλλήλοιϊν Il.; and in Mid., ποσσὶν ἐριδδήσασθαι Ἀχαιοῖς to contend with them in the foot-race, Id.
to provoke to strife, irritate, Il.
intr. = ἐριδαίνω, to contend, Theocr., Mosch.
strongly-built, i. e. unconquerable, or (from δαμάω) all-subduing.
to strive, wrangle, quarrel, τινί with one, Hom., attic; πρός τινα Hdt., Plat.
to rival, vie with, be a match for, τινί Hom.:—c. acc. rei, to contend with one in a thing, Id.;—also, c. dat. rei, Od., attic
absol. to engage in a contest, keep the contest up, Il.
Hom. sometimes uses the Mid., like the Act.
fitting exactly: as epith. of ἑταῖρος, faithful, trusty, Il.; pl. in heterocl. form, ἐρίηρες ἑταῖροι, ἐριήρας ἑταίρους Hom.
very flourishing, luxuriant, of plants, Il., Hes.
a day-labourer, hired servant of any sort; in Il., ἔριθοι are mowers or reapers: later, ἔριθοι, αἱ, spinsters, workers in wool, Dem., Theocr.
much-weeping, Anth.
loud-sounding, Hes.
very famous, glorious, splendid, Hom.
big with young, Aesch.
loud-bellowing, Hom., Hes.
of wool, woollen, Hdt.
the wild fig-tree, Il., Theocr.

the Erinys or Fury, an avenging deity, in sg. and pl., Hom., Trag.:—the number Three first in Eur.; the names Tisiphone, Megaera, Alecto only in late writers. At Athens they were called Εὐμενίδες, Σεμναί.

as appellat., μητρὸς Ἐρινύες curses from one's mother, Hom.; but Ἐρινῦς πατρός the blood-guiltiness of his sire, Hes.; φρενῶν Ἐρινύς distraction, Soph.:—in Trag. persons sent to be curses to men are called Ἐρινύες.
wool, in sg. and pl., Hom., attic:— εἴρια ἀπὸ ξύλου cotton (Germ. Baumwolle, tree-wool), Hdt.
adv., like a wool-dealer, roguishly, Ar.
Homeric epith. of Hermes the ready helper, luckbringer, Il.
to work in wool, Xen.
insepar. prefix, like ἀρι-, to strengthen the sense of a word, very, much.
a broken cliff, crag, scaur, Eur.: a steep side, sheer ascent, Id.
very mighty, of Zeus, Hom., Hes.: of the Furies, Orph.
a cause of quarrel, Il.
loud-thundering, of Zeus, Hes.
strife, quarrel, debate, contention:
in Il. mostly of battle-strife, ἔριδι or ἐξ ἔριδος μάχεσθαι; ἔριδι ξυνιέναι to meet in battle; θεοὺς ἔριδι ξυνελάσσαι to set them a-fighting, etc.
in Od. mostly of contention, rivalry, ἔργοιο in work; ἀέθλων for prizes, etc.:—later much like ἀγών, a contest, ἔριν ἔχειν ἀμφὶ μουσικῇ Hdt.; ἔρις ἀγαθῶν zeal for good, Aesch.
after Hom. of political or domestic strife, discord, quarrel, wrangling, disputation, Hdt., attic
as pr. nom. Eris, a goddess who excites to war, sister and companion of Ares, Il.
of wine, made of fine grapes, Od.
rich in grapes, of Bacchus, Anth.
matter for contest, Soph.
loud-roaring, Hhymn.
highly-prized, precious, Il., Ar.
of a kid, Xen.
Dim. of ἔρῐφος, a kid, NTest.
a young goat, kid, Hom.
ἔριφοι, οἱ, Lat. hoedi, a constellation (rising in Oct.) which brought storms, Theocr.
rich in gold, Anth.
a hurricane, applied to Cleon by Ar.:— deriv. uncertain; for the deriv. in Ar. from ἔριον ὀλλύναι, wool-consumption, is a mere pun.
of or in the ἕρκος or front court, Ζεὺς Ἑρκεῖος, the household god, because his statue stood in the ἕρκος, Od., Hdt., etc.
πύλαι, θύρα ἕρκ. the gates, door of the court, Aesch.; ἑρκεῖος στέγη the court itself, Soph.
a fence, inclosure, Hom.

a fence, hedge, wall, Hom.; esp. round the court-yards of houses, Od.:— also the place enclosed, the court-yard, Hom.; Κίσσινον ἕρκος, i. e. Susa, Aesch.; γαίας ἕρκος a fenced city, Eur.; ἕρκος ἱρόν, i. e. the altar, Soph.; ἕρκος ὀδόντων the ring or wall which the teeth make round the gums, i. e. the teeth, Hom.; σφραγῖδος ἕρκος, i. e. a seal, Soph.
metaph. any fence, ἕρκος ἀκόντων a defence against javelins, Il.; ἕρκος βελέων Id.:—of persons, ἕρκος Ἀχαιῶν, of Ajax, ἕρκος Ἀχαιοῖσιν πολέμοιο, of Achilles, Id.
a net, toils, snare for birds, Od.; mostly in pl., Ar.:—metaph., τῆς Δίκης ἐν ἕρκεσιν Aesch.
watching an enclosure, Anth.

a prop, support, used to keep ships upright when ashore, Il.: metaph. of men, ἕρμα πόληος prop or stay of the city, Lat. columen, Hom.; μελαινέων ἕρμ’ ὀδυνάων, of a sharp arrow, the foundation, i. e. the cause, of pangs, Il.
a sunken rock, reef, on which a vessel may strike, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
a mound, cairn, barrow, Soph.
that which keeps a ship steady, ballast, Plut.
earrings, Hom.
a herd of Hermae, Anth.
a god-send, wind-fall, reputed to be a gift of the god Hermes, as in Latin of Hercules, Soph., Plat.; Ἕρμαια, (sc. ἱερά), τά, a feast of Hermes, Aeschin.
called after Hermes Od., Aesch.
of or from Hermes, gainful, Id.
an hermaphrodite, a person partaking of the attributes of both sexes, so called from Hermaphroditus, son of Hermes and Aphrodite, Luc.
interpretation, explanation, Plat., Xen.
an interpretation, explanation, Eur.
a symbol, monument, Id.

entry.etym: Ἑρμῆς, the messenger of the gods
entry.sense: an interpreter, esp. of foreign tongues, a dragoman, Hdt., Xen.
an interpreter, expounder, Aesch.
of or for interpreting, Luc.
to interpret foreign tongues, Xen.
to interpret, put into words, give utterance to, Thuc., etc.
to explain, Soph., Plat.

Hermes, the Lat. Mercurius, son of Maia and Zeus; messenger of the gods (διάκτορος); giver of good luck (ἐριούνιος, ἀκάκητα); god of all secret dealings, cunning, and stratagem (δόλιος); bearing a golden rod (χρυσόρραπις); conductor of defunct spirits (ψυχοπομπός, πομπαῖος); tutelary god of all arts, of traffic, markets, roads (ἀγοραῖος, ἐμπολαῖος, ὅδιος, ἐνόδιος), and of heralds. His bust, mounted on a four-cornered pillar, was used to mark boundaries. —Proverb., κοινὸς Ἑρμῆς shares in your luck! Theophr.: cf. ἕρμαιον.
Dim. of Ἑρμῆς, a little Hermes, Ar.
a bed-post, Od.
a statuary's shop, Plat.
a carver of Hermae: generally, a statuary, Luc.
of or for a statuary: ἡ -κη (sc. τέχνη), the art of statuary, Luc.
a Hermes-mutilator, Plut.
a young sprout, shoot, scion, Hom.; ἀνέδραμεν ἔρνεϊ ἶσος shot up like a young plant, Il.
metaph. of a child, a scion, Trag.

entry.etym: from ἔργω, ἔρδω or ἔργω, εἴργω
entry.sense: in Hdt., as a translation of the Persian name Darius: either from ἔργω, ἔρδω the worker, doer; or from ἔργω, εἴργω, Lat. coercitor
poet., lovely, charming, Hes., etc.
to ask, enquire, Od., Thuc.
c. acc. objecti, to learn by enquiry, Od.: to ask after or for, Il.
c. acc. pers. to enquire of, question, Id., Hdt.,
c. dupl. acc. to ask one about a thing, Od.
love, desire, Hom., etc.
as nom. pr. Eros, the god of love, Hes.
wool, only occurs in the ionic for εἶρος.
a walking animal, quadruped, Od.; ἑρπετά, opp. to πετεινά, Hdt.
a creeping thing, reptile, Eur., etc.
= ἑρπετόν, of a mouse, Anth.
adj. creeping, Id.
to creep, crawl, of persons weighed down by age or distress.
creeping thyme, Lat. serpyllum, Ar., Theocr.
a crawling child, Anth.

entry.etym: attic aor1 εἵρπυσα, inf. ἑρπύσαι supplied by ἑρπύζω
entry.sense: to creep, crawl, Lat. serpo, repo, and generally to move slowly, walk, Hom., Trag.:—also simply, to go or come, Id.
variously, of a tear, to steal from the eye, Soph.; of reports, to creep on, spread, like Lat. serpit rumor, Id.; ὁ πόλεμος ἑρπέτω let it take its course, Ar.; of calamities, Soph.

entry.etym: part. perf. pass. of ῥώννυμι, used as adj.
entry.sense: in good health, stout, vigorous, opp. to ἄρρωστος, Plat., Dem.; irreg. comp., ἐρρωμενέστερος, Hdt., Xen.: —Sup. -έστατος, Plat.:—adv. ἐρρωμένως, stoutly, manfully, vigorously, Aesch., Ar., etc.
to go slowly, wander about, Od.; of slow, halting gait, whence Hephaestus is called ἔρρων, limping, Il.
to go or come to one's own loss or harm, Id.; ἔρρων ἐκ ναός gone, fallen from a ship, Aesch.

imperat. ἔρρε, Lat. abi in malam rem, away! begone! Il., etc.; so, ἔρροις Eur.; in pl. ἔρρετε Il.; and in 3rd sg. ἐρρέτω, away with him, Hom.; ἐρρέτω Ἴλιον perish Troy! Soph.; ἔρρ’ ἐς κόρακας, Lat. pasce corvos, be thou hung, Ar.; so, οὐκ ἐρρήσετε; οὐκ ἐς κόρακας ἐρρήσετε; Id.

in attic of persons and things, to be clean gone, to be lost, perish, disappear, Trag.; ἐξ οἵων καλῶν ἔρρεις from what fortunes hast thou fallen, Eur.; ἔρρει τὰ ἐμὰ πράγματα, Lat. actum est de me! Xen.
dew, Lat. ros, Hom., etc.:—in pl. rain-drops, Il.
metaph. of young and tender animals, Od.; cf. δρόσος.
dewy, dew-besprent, Il.: metaph. of a corpse, fresh, Id.
= ἐρεύγομαι vomit, eructare, οἶνον ἐρυγγ. Eur.
loud-bellowing, Il.
Pass. to become red with blood, Il.
a redness on the skin, Thuc.; ἐρ. προσώπου a blush, Eur.:—absol. redness, Xen.
Pass. to become red, to blush, Xen.
to be apt to blush, to colour up, Ar., etc.
red-footed:—name of a bird, the redshank, Ar.

entry.etym: ῠ by nature, so that the correct forms of the comp. and Sup. are -ώτερος, -ώτατος
entry.sense: red, Lat. ruber, of the colour of nectar and wine, Hom.; of copper, Il.; of gold, Theogn.; of minium, Hdt.; of blood, Aesch.
Ἐρυθρὴ θάλασσα in Hdt. the Erythraean sea, including not only the Red Sea or Arabian Gulf, but also the Indian Ocean:—Later also of the Persian Gulf, Xen.
to restrain, withhold, epic part. fem. ἐρυκανόως’ Od.
to keep in, hold back, keep in check, curb, restrain, Hom.:—c. gen., μή με ἔρυκε μάχης keep me not from fight, Il.:—c. inf. to hinder from doing, Eur.:—absol. to hinder, Il.
to detain a guest, Hom.:—but also, to detain by force, to withhold, confine, Id.
to ward off, Lat. arcere, ἄκοντα, λιμόν Id.
to keep apart, separate, Il.
Pass. to be held back, detained, Od.:— to hold back, keep back, Id.
to be kept away, Hdt.
ἀνέδην χῶρος ἐρύκεται the place is remissly guarded, i. e. is open to all, Soph.
a fence, guard, ἔρυμα χροός, of defensive armour, Il., Xen.; τὸ ἔρ. τοῦ τείχεος the defence given by it, Hdt.: absol. a bulwark, breastwork, Thuc.
a safeguard, of the Areopagus, Aesch.; παῖδας ἔρ. δώμασι Eur.
with fenced back, of a crab, Anth.
fenced, fortified, by art or nature, Eur., Thuc.; τὰ ἐρυμνά strong positions, Xen.
strength or security of a place, Xen.
chariot-drawing, of horses, Il.
red blight, Lat. robigo, Plat.
ἐρυσίθριξ ψήκτρα, a comb for drawing through the hair, a small-tooth comb, Anth.
preserving ships, Anth.
protecting the city, Il.
a safeguard against witchcraft, Hhymn.
drawn, Soph.

to drag along the ground, drag, draw, a ship in to the sea or on to land, Hom.; νεκρὸν ἐρ., to drag a body away, rescue, Il.; or to drag off for plunder, Id.; of dogs and birds of prey, to drag and tear, Id.:—also, to tear away battlements, Id.
without any sense of violence, φᾶρος κὰκ κεφαλῆς εἴρυσσε drew it over his head, Od.; χλαίνης ἐρύων plucking him by the cloak, Il.; τόξον Hdt.; πλίνθους εἰρύειν, Lat. ducere lateres, Id.
Mid. ἐρύομαι to draw for oneself, Hom.; ἐρύσασθαι νῆας to launch us ships, Il.; ξίφος ἐρύεσθαι to draw one's sword, Id.; ἐρύσσεσθαι τόξον to prepare to draw one's bow, i. e. to string it, Od.
to draw towards oneself, Id.
to draw out of the press, ἐρύσασθαί τινα μάχης Il.; hence, to rescue, deliver, of captives, to redeem, ransom, Id.
simply to protect, guard, of armour, Id.
c. acc. rei, to keep off, ward off, Id.
to thwart, check, curb, Id.
to keep guard upon, watch over, νῆας, δῶμα Od.; εἰρύαται οἴκαδ’ ἰόντα lie in wait for me, Id.; φρεσὶν ἐρύσασθαι to keep in one's heart, to conceal, Id.
to support, hold in honour, with notion of obedience, Id.
Pass. to be drawn ashore, drawn up in line, of ships, Il.; νῆες δ’ ὁδὸν εἰρύαται are drawn up along the road, Od.
Pass. to be kept or shut up, epic 3rd pl. ἐρχατόωντο Od.
to come or go, Hom., etc.
to come or go back, return, Od.; in full, αὖτις, ἄψ, πάλιν ἐλθεῖν Id.
c. acc. cogn., ὁδόν or κέλευθον ἐλθεῖν to go a journey, Hom., Aesch.; ἀγγελίην ἐλθεῖν to go a message, Il.
c. gen. loci, πεδίοιο ἐλθεῖν over or across the plain, Id.

c. part. fut., to denote the object, ἔρχομαι οἰσόμενος I go to fetch, Id.; μαρτυρήσων ἦλθον Aesch., etc.:—like an auxiliary Verb, ἔρχομαι λέξων I am going to tell, I intend to say (as in French je vais dire), Hdt.
the aor. part. ἐλθών is often added to another Verb, κάθηρον ἐλθών come and cleanse, Il., etc.
Post-Homeric phrases:
εἰς λόγους ἔρχεσθαί τινι to come to speech with, Hdt., Soph.
εἰς χεῖρας, so, ἐς μάχην ἐλθεῖν τινι to come to blows with one, Aesch., Hdt.
ἐπὶ μεῖζον ἔρχ. to increase, Soph.; εἰς πᾶν ἐλθεῖν to try everything, Xen.
ἐς τὸ δεινόν, ἐς τὰ ἀλγεινὰ ἐλθεῖν to come into danger, etc., Thuc., etc.
παρὰ μικρὸν ἐλθεῖν, c. inf. to come within a little of, be near a thing, Eur.; παρὰ τοσοῦτον ἦλθε κινδύνου so narrow was her escape, Thuc.
with διά and gen., periphr. for a Verb, διὰ μάχης τινὶ ἔρχεσθαι, for μάχεσθαί τινι, Eur., etc.
the heron or hern, Lat. ardea, Il., Ar.
to rush, rush forth, Hom.; ἠρώησαν ὀπίσσω, of horses, they started back, Il.
c. gen. rei, to draw back or rest from, πολέμοιο, χάρμης Id.; νέφος οὔποτ’ ἐρωεῖ the cloud never fails from (the rock), Od.:—c. acc. to leave, quit, Theocr.
trans. to drive or force back, Il.

any quick motion, rush, force, Il.; mostly of things, δουρός, βελέων ἐρ. Id.; λείπετο δουρὸς ἐρωήν war left a spear's throw behind, Id.; λικμητῆρος ἐρωή the force or swing of the winnower's (shovel), Id.
c. gen. rei, a drawing back from, rest from, πολέμου Id.
a little love, darling, Anth.
one's love: v. ἐράω.

entry.etym: the place of the pres. εἴρω (rare even in epic and never in attic) is supplied by φημί, λέγω or ἀγορεύω; and εἶπον serves as the aor.
entry.sense: I will say or speak, attic: c. acc. pers. to speak of, κακῶς ἐρεῖν τινα Theogn., Eur.; c. dupl. acc., ἐρεῖν τινά τι Id., etc.
I will tell, proclaim, Il., etc.; φόως ἐρέουσα to announce the dawn, Id.; ἐπὶ ῥηθέντι δικαίωι upon clear right, Od.
εἰρημένος promised, μισθός Hes., Hdt.; εἰρημένον, absol., when it had been agreed, Thuc.
to tell, order one to do, c. dat. et inf., Xen.; c. acc. et inf., Id.:—so in Pass., εἴρητό οἱ, c. inf., orders had been given him to do, Hdt.
in Pass. to be mentioned, Id.
simple εἴρω in Ionic and Epic, to say, speak, tell, Od.: so in Mid., Hom.: but in ionic Prose, the Mid. means to cause to be told one, i. e. to ask, like attic ἐροῦμαι.
love, Trag.:— love of a thing, desire for it, τινός Hdt., Aesch., etc.:—in pl. loves, amours, Eur.; in Soph., of passionate joy, cf. φρίσσω II. 3.
as prop. n. the god of love, Eros, Amor, Id., Eur.
Dim. of ἔρως, a little Cupid, Anth.
to ask, τινά τι something of one, Od., Soph., etc.:—Pass. to be asked, τι Xen.
ἐρ. τι to ask about a thing, Aesch.:— Pass., τὸ ἐρωτηθέν, τὸ ἐρωτώμενον the question, Thuc., Xen.
to enquire of a person, question him, Od., Eur., etc.:—Pass. to be questioned, Id.
= αἰτέω, to ask, i. e. to beg, solicit, NTest.
that which is asked, a question, Thuc.; τὰ ἐρ. τοῦ ξυνθήματος asking for the watchword, Id.
a questioning, Plat., Xen.
amatory, Thuc., etc.
of persons, amorous, Plat., Xen.:—adv. -κῶς, Thuc.; ἐρ. ἔχειν τινός to be eager for, Xen.
a loved one, darling, Theocr.
as adj., of love, Anth.
for writing of love, Anth.
beguiling love, Anth.
doric word, a darling, sweetheart, Theocr.
as adj., ἐρωτύλα ἀείδειν to sing love-songs, Bion.
for ever, v. ἀεί.
to clothe:—only used in perf. and plup. pass., ἤσθημαι, ionic ἔσθημαι, clothed or clad, τι in a thing, ἐσθῆτα ἐσθημένος Hdt.; ῥάκεσι ἐσθημένος Id.; ἠσθημένοι πέπλοισι Eur.
a garment, in pl., clothes, raiment, Trag., Thuc., etc.
clothing, raiment, NTest.
dress, clothing, raiment, Hom., Hdt., attic; in pl., of the clothes of several persons, Aesch.
collectively, clothes, Od., Hdt.
to eat, Lat. edo (cf. ἔδω), Hom., etc.; ἐσθ. τινός to eat of a thing (partitive gen.), Xen.:—Pass., οἶκος ἐσθίεται the house is eaten up, we are eaten out of house and home, Od.
metaph., πάντας πῦρ ἐσθίει the fire devours all, Il.; ἐσθ. ἑαυτόν to vex oneself (like Homer's ὃν θυμὸν κατέδων), Ar.; ἐσθ. τὴν χελύνην to bite the lip, Id.
good of his kind, good, brave, Hom., esp. in Il.;—also, rich, wealthy, Hes.: noble, opp. to κακός (v. ἀγαθός 1), εἴτ’ εὐγενὴς πέφυκας εἴτ’ ἐσθλῶν κακή Soph.
of things, Hom., etc.
good, fortunate, lucky, Od., Trag.
as Subst., ἐσθλά, τά, goods, Od.:—but ἐσθλόν, good luck, Hom.
ἐσθλόν [ἐστι], c. inf. it is good, expedient to do, Il.
for ἐστὶν ὅτε, Lat. est quum, there is a time when, i. e. now and then, sometimes, Soph., Xen.
to eat, Hom.: to eat up, consume one's substance, Id.
an impulse, tendency, only in Plat.: but the compd. ἔφεσις is found.
（ἕζω) a sitting. v. εἰσ-.

entry.etym: adverb from perf. pass. part. of σκέπτω
entry.sense: deliberately, Dem.
anything let out, Lat. scaturigo: esp. a swarm of bees or wasps, Hdt., Ar.:—of things, ἑσμοὶ γάλακτος streams of milk, Eur.
producing swarms of bees, Anth.
Lat. vespera, properly fem. of ἕσπερος:
(sub. ὥρα), evening, eventide, eve, Hdt.; ἑσπέρας at eve, Plat., etc.; ἀπὸ ἑσπέρας εὐθύς just at nightfall, Thuc.; πρὸς ἑσπέρᾳ Ar.; ἐπεὶ πρὸς ἑσπέραν ἦν Xen.; ἑσπέρας γιγνομένης Plat.
(sub. χώρα), the west, Lat. occidens, Eur.; ἡ πρὸς ἑσπέρην χώρη the country to the west, Hdt.; τὸ πρὸς ἑσπέρης Id.; τὰ πρὸς ἑσπέραν Thuc.
of Time, at even, at eventide, Hom.; ἑσπέριος ἦλθεν Od., etc.
of Place, western, Lat. occidentalis, Id., Eur.; τὰ ἑσπ. the western parts, Thuc.
in nom. pr., Ἐσπερίδες, αἱ, the Hesperides, daughters of Night, who dwelt in an island in the west, and guarded a garden with golden apples, Hes.
of or at evening, ἕ. ἀστήρ the evening star, Il.; as Subst., without ἀστήρ, Hesperus, esp. of the planet Venus, Eur., Bion.; but, ἕσπ. θεός the god of darkness, i. e. Hades, death, Soph.
as Subst. evening (v. ἑσπέρα), ἐπὶ ἕσπερος ἦλθε Od.; ποτὶ ἕσπερον at eventide, Hes.; also heterog. pl., ποτὶ ἕσπερα Od.
western, Aesch., Soph.

entry.etym: an aor2 used by Hom. only in 2nd pl.
entry.sense: ἔσπετε νῦν μοι, Μοῦσαι tell me now, ye Muses, Il.
hurrying, vehement, eager, impetuous, Il.:— eager, yearning for a thing, c. gen., Hom.; also c. inf., Id.
adv. ἐσσῠμένως, hurriedly, furiously, Id.
on one's feet, Il.
CONJUNCTION, = ἕως:
up to the time that, until, with ind. or opt., etc.; ἔστ’ ἄν, with subj., Aesch., etc.
so long as, while, with same tenses, etc.
ADVERB, even to, up to, ἔστε ἐπί, Lat. usque ad, Xen.:—also of Time, ἔστε ἐπὶ κνέφας Id.
an entertainment, banquet, Eur.
Vesta, daughter of Kronosand Rhea, guardian of the hearth, Hhymn., Hdt., etc.
the hearth of a house, fireside, Hom., Aesch., etc.; the shrine of the household gods, and a sanctuary for suppliants (ἐφέστιοι), ἐπὶ τὴν ἑστίαν καθίζεσθαι Thuc.
the house itself, a dwelling, home (as we say fireside), Hdt., Trag.: metaph. of the last home, the grave, Soph.
a household, family, Hdt.
an altar, shrine, Trag.; γᾶς μεσόμφαλος ἑστ., of the Delphic shrine, Eur.
as nom. pr.
a feasting, banqueting, entertainment, Thuc., Plat.
a Vestal virgin, Plut.
one who gives a banquet, a host, Plat.:—at Athens, the citizen whose turn it was to give a dinner to his tribe, Dem.
to receive at one's hearth or in one's house: to entertain, feast, regale, Hdt., attic:—absol. to give a feast, Plat.
c. acc. cogn., γάμους ἑστιᾶν to give a marriage feast, Eur., Ar.; ἑστ. νικητήρια Xen.

Pass., with fut. mid. ἑστιάσομαι, aor1 εἱστιάθην: perf. εἱστίᾱμαι, ionic inf. ἱστιῆσθαι:— to be a guest, be feasted, feast, Hdt., Plat.; ἑστ. ἐνύπνιον to have a visionary feast, "feast with the Barmecide," Ar.
Pass. to be founded or established (by children), Eur.
guarding the house, a guardian, Eur.
having an altar or hearth, Trag.
a peg at the end of the pole, passing through the yoke and having a ring (κρίκος) affixed, Il.
erringly, amiss, Anth.
the hearth, fire-place, Hom.; the sanctuary of suppliants, καθέζετο ἐπ’ ἐσχάρῃ ἐν κονίῃσιν Od.:— a pan of coals, a brasier, Ar.
πυρὸς ἐσχάραι the watch-fires of the camp, Il.
an altar for burnt-offerings, Od., Soph.
of or on the hearth, Anth.
a pan of coals, Plut.
to be at the edge, on the border, Il.; epic part. ἐσχατόων straying about the edge of the camp, Id.
the furthest part, edge, border, verge, Hom., Hdt., attic: in pl. the borders, Hdt.; the extremities of the world, Id.

entry.etym: prob. from ἐκ, ἐξ, as if ἔξατος,
entry.sense: of Space, as always in Hom. the furthest, uttermost, extreme, Id., Hdt., attic; ἔσχατοι ἄλλων, of the Thracians who were the last in the Trojan lines, Il.; ἔσχατοι ἀνδρῶν, of the Aethiopians, Od.: ἔσχατα, τά, extremities, ἐσχ. γαίης Hes.; τὰ ἔσχ. τοῦ στρατοπέδου Thuc.
the furthest in each direction.
the uppermost, Soph.
lowest, deepest, Lat. imus, ἀΐδας Theocr.
innermost, Lat. intimus, Soph.
the last, hindmost, Id.

of Degree, the uttermost, utmost, last, worst, πόνος, κίνδυνος Plat.:—as Subst., τὸ ἔσχατον, τὰ ἔσχατα, the utmost, Hdt.; of suffering, pain, etc., Id., attic; ἐπ’ ἔσχατα βαίνεις Soph.; ἔσχατ’ ἐσχάτων κακά worst of possible evils, Id.; so in Sup., τὰ πάντων ἐσχατώτατα the extremest of all, Xen.
of Time, last, ἐς τὸ ἔσχ. to the end, Hdt., Thuc.; ἐσχάτας ὑπὲρ ῥίζας over the last scion of the race, Soph.: —neut. ἔσχατον as adv., for the last time, Id.
adv. -τως, to the uttermost, exceedingly, Xen.:—so, ἐς τὸ ἔσχ. Hdt., Xen.
from within, Hdt., attic
within, Hdt., Aesch.:—c. gen., ἔσωθεν ἄντρων Eur.

entry.etym: older form of εἴσω, cf. ἐς, εἰς
entry.sense: comp., ἐσωτέρω τῆς Ἑλλάδος to the interior of Greece, Hdt.
innermost, Lat. intimus
interior, NTest. comp. of ἔσω.
to examine, test, Anth.
a companion, Il.; φόρμιγξ, ἣν δαιτὶ θεοὶ ποίησαν ἑταίρην Od.; πενία σφιν ἑταίρα Theocr.
opp. to a lawful wife, a concubine, a courtesan, Hdt., attic
companionship, association, brotherhood, Hdt., attic
at Athens, a political club or union for party purposes, Thuc., etc.
generally, friendly connexion, friendship, Dem.
of or belonging to companions, Ζεὺς ἑτ. presiding over fellowship, Hdt.; φόνος ἑτ. the murder of a comrade, Anth.
to keep company, of courtesans, Aeschin., etc.
unchastity, Aeschin.
to be a comrade to any one, c. dat., Il.
trans. in Mid. to associate with oneself, choose for one's comrade, ἤ τινά που Τρώων ἑταρίσσαιτο (epic for ἑταιρίσαιτο) Id.
of or befitting a companion: τὸ ἑταιρικόν = ἑταιρεία I.2, Thuc.: hence the ties of party, Id.
of or like an ἑταίρα, meretricious Plut.:— adv. -κῶς, Id., Luc.

a comrade, companion, mate, Hom.; a common way of addressing people, ὦ ’ταῖρε my good friend, Ar.; φίλ’ ἑταῖρε Theogn.; pupils or disciples were the ἑταῖροι of their masters, as those of Socrates, Xen.:—c. gen., δαιτὸς ἑταῖρε partner of my feast, Hhymn.; πόσιος καὶ βρώσιος ἑταῖροι mess mates, Theogn.
metaph. of things, ἐσθλὸς ἑταῖρος, of a fair wind, Od.; c. dat., βίος ὁ σοφοῖς ἕταρος Anth.: as adj. associate in a thing, c. gen., Plat.: Sup., ἑταιρότατος Id.
friendly, a friend, Anth.
yearly, from year to year, Lat. annuus, Aesch., Eur.
of one year, yearling, Xen.
a genuine son of Butes (one of the hereditary priests of Athena Polias), Dem.
true Cretans, of the old stock, Od.
true, real, genuine, Hom.; ἐτεὸν μαντεύεται prophesies truth, Il.; ὡς ἐτεόν περ as the truth is, Hom.
ἐτεόν as adv., in truth, really, verily, Lat. revera, Id.; rightly, Theocr.:—attic as an interrog., often in iron. sense, really? indeed? so? Lat. itane? Ar.

giving strength to one of two, Δαναοῖσι μάχης ἑτεραλκέα νίκην δοῦναι to give victory in battle inclining to the side of the Danai, Il.; ἑτ. σῆμα a sign that victory was changing sides, Id.; so without μάχης, δίδου ἑτεραλκέα νίκην Hom.
act., δῆμος ἑτ. a body of men which decides the victory, Il.
inclining first to one side then to the other, doubtful, Lat. anceps, Hdt.; so in adv., ἑτεραλκέως ἀγωνίζεσθαι, ancipiti Marte pugnare, Id.
on alternate days, day and day about, of the Dioscuri, Od.
of other tongue, ἐν ἑτερογλώσσοις by men of foreign tongue, NTest.
with one side of the mouth harder than the other, ἵππος Xen.
to teach differently, to teach errors, NTest.
zealous for one side, leaning to one side, of the balance:—adv. -λως, unfairly, Hes.
zealous in another pursuit, Anth.
to be yoked in unequal partnership with another, NTest.
coupled with an animal of diverse kind, Lxx.
yoked singly, without its yokefellow, metaph., Ion ap. Plut.
of a different kind, Hdt.
to make of different kind:—Pass. to be changed or altered, to alter, Hdt.
leaning to one side, sloping, Xen.
with sides of uneven length, i. e. oblong, rectangular, Xen.
of money lent on a ship and cargo with the risk of the outward, but not of the homeward, voyage, Dem.

entry.etym: crasis for ὁ ἕτερος, ionic οὕτερος, doric ὥτερος; neut. θάτερον attic, ionic τοὔτερον: pl. ἅτεροι, θάτερα, for οἱ ἕτεροι, τὰ ἕτερα: gen. θατέρου: dat. θατέρῳ: fem. nom. ἁτέρα, dat. θἀτέρᾳ
entry.sense: Lat. alter, the other, one of two, χειρὶ ἑτέρῃ Hom., v. infr. IV; χωλὸς ἕτερον πόδα, etc.:—then of all persons or things of which there are two, Lat. alteruter, Il.; τὴν ἑτ. πύλην one of the two gates, Hdt.; δυοῖν ἀγαθοῖν τὸ ἕτ. Thuc., etc.:—in pl. one of two parties, each of which is pl., Lat. alterutri, Hom.
in double clauses, ἕτερος (in Prose ὁ ἕτερος) is repeated, ἕτερον μὲν ἔδωκε, ἕτερον δ’ ἀνένευσε Il., etc.
often repeated in the same clause, ἐξ ἑτέρων ἕτερ’ ἐστίν one depends upon the other, Od.; ἕτεροι ἑτέρων ἄρχουσι the one rule the other, Thuc.

like Lat. alter, = δεύτερος, second, ἡ μὲν . . , ἡ δ’ ἑτέρη . . , ἡ δὲ τρίτη . . , Od., etc.; ἡ ἑτέρα (sc. ἡμέρα), the second day, i. e. day after to-morrow, Xen.:—so with Pronouns of quantity, ἕτερον τοσοῦτο another of the same size, Hdt.
put loosely for ἄλλος, Lat. alius, another, Hom., attic
other than usual, different, Od., etc.; ἕτ. καὶ οὐχ ὁ αὐτός Dem.:—c. gen. other than, different from, ἑτέρους τῶν νῦν ὄντων Thuc.; so, ἕτερον ἢ . . , Eur.
other than should be, other than good, euphem. for κακός, as Lat. sequior for malus, ἀγαθὰ ἢ θάτερα Dem.; and alone, ἑτ. θυσία Aesch., etc.
Special Phrases:
elliptical, τῇ ἑτέρᾳ (sc. χειρί), epic τῇ ἑτέρῃ or ἑτέρῃφι with one hand, Il.; esp. with the left hand, Hom.
(sub. ἡμέρᾳ) on the next day, Soph., Xen.
(sub. ὁδῷ) 2n another or a different way, Soph., Ar.
Adverbial with Preps.,
ἐπὶ θάτερα to or on the other side, Thuc., etc.
κατὰ θάτερα on the one or other side, Dem.
adv.
of different sort or fashion, Ar.
turning the other way, uncertain, Anth.
one-eyed, Lat. unoculus, luscus, Dem.
of other mind, raving, Anth.
of different voice: foreign, Aesch.
adv.
from the other side, Il.
in pregnant sense with Verbs of rest, as if for ἑτέρωθι, on the other side, opposite, Id.
adv.
on the other side, Od., Hdt.
= ἄλλοθι, elsewhere, Hom., etc.:—c. gen., ἑτ. τοῦ λόγου in another part of my story, Hdt.
at another time, Id.
adv. to the other side, Hom.:— on one side, Id.
in pregnant sense with Verbs of Rest, as if for ἑτέρωθι, on the other side, Il., Dem.
= ἄλλοσε, elsewhither, Il., Hom.
in one or the other way, Plat.
differently, Ar., Dem.

with or without ἄνεμοι, periodic winds: of the Egyptian monsoons, which blow from the North-west during the summer, Hdt.; of northerly winds, which blow in the Aegean for 40 days from the rising of the dog-star, Id., Dem.
lasting a year, a year long, πένθος Eur., Thuc.
every year, annual, Id.
the ἔται were clansmen, i. e. the kinsmen of a great house, cousins, παῖδές τε κασίγνητοί τε ἔται τε Hom.; ἔται καὶ ἀνεψιοί Il.
later, = δημότης, a townsman, neighbour, Thuc.:—in sg. a private citizen, Aesch.
for ὦ τάν or ὦ ’τάν, v. sub τάν.
truth, Anth.
true, Hom.; τοῦτ’ ἀγόρευσον ἐτήτυμον tell me this true, Od.; εἰ λέγεις ἐτήτυμα Soph.
of persons, truthful, Eur.
true, genuine, real, Lat. sincerus, κείνῳ δ’ οὐκέτι νόστος ἐτ. for him there remains no true, real return, Od.; ἐτ. Διὸς κόρα Aesch.; παῖς χρυσός Theocr.
as adv., in neut. ἐτήτυμον, truly, really, in truth and in deed, Hom.:—regul. adv. -μως, Aesch., Soph.
of Time,
of the Present, yet, as yet, still, Lat. adhuc, Il., attic; cf. οὐκέτι.
of the Past, mostly with imperf., ἀήθεσσον γὰρ ἔτι they were yet unaccustomed, Il.; προορωμένοις ἔτι Thuc.
of the Future, yet, further, ἄλγε’ ἔδωκεν, ἠδ’ ἔτι δώσει Il.:—also hereafter, Aesch., Soph.
of Degree, yet, still, besides, further, moreover, Lat. praeterea, insuper, Hom., etc.; ἔτι δέ and besides, nay more, Thuc.
often to strengthen a comp., ἔτι μᾶλλον yet more, Il.; μᾶλλον ἔτι Od.; ἔτι πλέον Hdt., etc.
with the posit., ἔτι ἄνω yet higher up, Xen.
a soup-ladle, Ar.
soup-stirring, τορύνη Anth.
a thick soup of pulse, pea-soup, Ar., Plat.
to make or get ready, prepare, provide, Il., Hdt., attic; c. inf., κάπρον ἑτοιμασάτω ταμέειν Il.
Mid. to cause to be prepared, Id.
with perf. pass. ἡτοίμασμαι, to prepare for oneself, τἄλλα ἡτοιμάζετο made his other arrangements, Thuc.; ἡτοιμασμένοι Xen.
to prepare oneself, c. inf., Id.
at hand, ready, prepared, of food, Od., Hdt.; ἑτ. χρήματα ready money, money in hand, Id.; ἑτ. ποιεῖσθαι to make ready, Id.; ἐξ ἑτοίμου off-hand, forthwith, Xen.:— τὰ ἑτοῖμα what comes to hand, Thuc.
of the future, sure to come, certain, Il.:—also easy to be done, feasible, Id.
of the past, carried into effect, made good, Hom.
of persons or the will, ready, active, zealous, Lat. paratus, promptus, Hdt., Aesch.; εἴς or πρός τι Hdt., Xen.:—c. inf. ready to do, Hdt., attic: τὸ ἕτοιμον readiness, Eur.
adv. -μως, readily, Thuc., etc.
a state of preparation, readiness, Plut.
ready for cutting, Anth.

a year, Hom., etc.; τῶν προτέρων ἐτέων in bygone years, Il.; ἑκάστου ἔτους every year, Plat.; ἀνὰ πᾶν ἔτος Anth.; ἀνὰ πέντε ἔτεα every five years, Hdt.; δι’ ἔτους πέμπτου every fifth year, Ar.; κατὰ ἔτος every year, Thuc.; ἔτος εἰς ἔτος year after year, Soph.; in acc., ἔτος τόδ’ ἤδη δέκατον now for these ten years, Id.
without reason, for nothing, only with negat. οὐκ ἐτός, Lat. non temere, Ar., Plat.; οὐκ ἐτὸς ἄρ’ ἦλθεν it was not for nothing then that he came? Ar.
true, real, actual, ψεύσομαι ἢ ἔτυμον ἐρέω; shall I lie or speak truth? Hom.; οἵ ῥ’ ἔτυμα κραίνουσι those [dreams] have true issues, Od.; ἔτ. ἄγγελος, φήμη Aesch., Eur.
neut. ἔτυμον as adv., like ἐτεόν, truly, really, Hom.; also pl., ἔτυμα Anth.; the regular adv. -μως, Aesch., etc.
working fruitlessly, Hes.
fruitless, useless, unprofitable, Lat. irritus, ἐτώσιον ἄχθος ἀρούρης Il., etc.
Dep. to bring good news, announce them, Ar., Dem., etc.
to proclaim as glad tidings, τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ NTest.
absol. to preach the gospel, Id.:—c. acc. pers. to preach the gospel to persons, Id.;—so also in Act., Id.:— Pass. to have the gospel preached to one, Id.; of the gospel, to be preached, Id.

the reward of good tidings, given to the messenger, Od.; in pl., εὐαγγέλια θύειν to make a thankoffering for good tidings, Xen., etc.; εὐαγγελίων θυσίαι Aeschin.; εὐαγγέλια στεφανοῦν τινα to crown one for good news, Ar.
in Christian sense, the Glad Tidings, i. e. the Gospel (Saxon gode-spell), NTest.
the bringer of good tidings, an evangelist, preacher of the gospel, NTest.
bringing good news, Aesch.
to be pure, holy, Theocr.
free from pollution, guiltless, pure, undefiled, ὅσιος καὶ εὐαγής Lex_solonis; of snow, Eur.
of actions, holy, righteous, Soph., Dem.; —so epic adv. εὐαγέως, Hhymn.
in act. sense, purificatory, Soph.
moving well, nimble, Anth.
bright, far-seen, conspicuous, ἕδραν εὐαγῆ στρατοῦ a seat in full view of the army, Aesch.; πύργον εὐαγῆ a lofty town, Eur.
bright, of clouds, Ar.
easy to bear in the arms, Aesch.
to have good sport, Anth.
good sport, Anth.
lucky in the chase, blessed with success, Soph., Anth.
good education, Aeschin.
easy to lead, easily led, ductile, ἐπί τι, εἴς τι, πρός τι Plat., Xen.
to cry evoe to Bacchus, Soph., Eur.
well ventilated, fresh, airy, Hes.
act., of a wind, favourably blowing, fair, Hdt., Eur.: —metaph. favourable, Soph.
happily won, Anth.
easy to be taken, Hdt.
happy in life, Eur.; of life itself, happy, fortunate, blessed, Aesch., Soph.; ὕπνος εὐ. blessed sleep, Soph.
well-grown, luxuriant, Anth.
of good meal, Anth.
easy to be taken or caught, Xen., etc.
with fine vines, Anth.
easy to call out, of the names of dogs, Xen.
easy to recall, Plut.:—adv., εὐανακλήτως ἔχειν πρός τινα Id.
to abound in men, Plut.
to be in full vigour, Id.
abundance of men, store of goodly men, Xen.; in pl., πληρωμάτων εὐανδρίαις by the crews being able-bodied men, Plut.
manhood, manliness, manly spirit, Eur.
abounding in good men, Tyrtae., Eur., etc.
prosperous to men, Aesch.
flowery, blooming, Anth.
to be flowery or blooming, Luc.
blooming, budding, Od.
rich in flowers, flowery, Theogn., Ar.
flowered, gay-coloured, gay, bright, Plat., Anth.
metaph. blooming, fresh, goodly, Ar.
evan, a cry of the Bacchanals, like εὐοῖ, Eur.
accessible, gracious, Anth.
finely vaulted, Anth.
easy to part with, Xen.
easy to cheat, Plat.
easy to disembark on, convenient for landing, Thuc.
easy to excuse, Plut.
easy to wall off, easy to blockade by circumvallation, Thuc., Xen.
well-pleasing, acceptable, NTest.:—adv., εὐαρεστοτέρως διακεῖσθαί τινι to be more popular with one, Xen.
easy to count, i. e. few in number, Plat.
easy to govern, manageable, of a horse's mouth, Aesch.
with beauteous car, Soph.
easiness of temper, Plat., Dem.
well-joined, harmonious, Eur., Plat.
of men, accommodating, Plat.
rich in sheep or lambs, Anth.
well-ploughed or easy to be ploughed, Anth.
beginning well, making a good beginning, Anth.
a Bacchanalian shout, Eur.
a shout of revelry, Plut.
the Roman ovatio, Plut.
a Bacchanal, Anth.
easy to describe, Hdt.
touching gently: metaph., εὐ.μετάβασις an easy, unforced transition, Luc.:— τὸ εὐαφές delicate touch, Id.:—adv. -φῶς, Id.
easy to carry or move, Hdt.
accessible, passable, Aesch.; comp. -ώτερος, Xen.
with beautiful eyes, Anth.
an Euboean, Hdt., etc.
Euboea, now Negropont (i. e. Egripo or Evripo, from Euripus), an island lying along the coast of Boeotia and Attica, Hom., etc.
Euboean, Hdt., etc.; fem. Εὐβοΐς, Id.; lengthd. Εὐβοιΐς, Soph.
throwing luckily (with the dice): adv., ἦν γὰρ εὐβόλως ἔχων he was in luck, Aesch.
with good pasture, Od.
well-fed, thriving, Theocr.
rich in grapes, Soph.
good counsel, prudence, Aesch., Soph., etc.
well-advised, prudent, Theogn., Hdt., Aesch.
rich in cattle, Hhymn.
well-noosed, well-knit, Anth.
nobility of birth, high descent, Aesch., Eur.; εὐγένεια παίδων = εὐγενεῖς παῖδες, Id.
of a lion, well-maned, Hom.; of men, well-bearded, Plat.
well-born, of noble race, of high descent, Lat. generosus, Trag.; εὐγενές [ἐστι] is a mark of nobility, Hdt.
noble-minded, generous, Soph., Plat.
of animals, high-bred, noble, generous, Theogn., Aesch., etc.; of a country, fertile, Plut.
of outward form, noble, Eur.
adv. -νῶς, nobly, bravely, Id.
adv. well, rightly, to confirm or approve what has been said, Ar., Plat.:—ironically, Eur., Ar.
without a Verb, good! well said! well done! bravo! Lat. euge! Id.
joyous, cheerful, Eur.
sweet-sounding, Ar.
abounding in milk:—a metapl. dat. εὔγλαγι, as if from εὖγλαξ, Anth.
well-carved, well-engraved, Anth.
glibness of tongue, Ar.
good of tongue, eloquent, Aesch.: glib of tongue, voluble, Ar.
sweet sounding, Anth.
act. loosing the tongue, making eloquent, Id.
like εὖχος, a boast, vaunt, Od.
like εὐχή, but always in pl. prayers, wishes, Aesch., Soph.
well-bent, Od.
to be fair and honest, shew good feeling, Plut.
kindness of heart, considerateness, indulgence, Aeschin.
prudence, Plut.
of good feeling, kindhearted, considerate, reasonable, indulgent, Xen., etc.
wise, prudent, thoughtful, Anth.
adv. -μόνως, indulgently, fairly, candidly, Luc.
prudently, Xen.
well-known, familiar, Soph., Eur.
easy to discern, Dem.
well-nailed, well-fastened, Eur.
fruitfulness, Xen.
well-drawn, Luc.; τῶν ὀφρύων τὸ εὔγραμμον their fine lines, Id.
well-painted, Anth.
act. writing well, Id.
well-circling, Anth.
regularity of angels, Eur.
with regular angles, Xen.
beautifully wrought, Anth.
to be prosperous, well off, happy, Hdt., attic:— εὐδαιμονοίης, as a form of blessing, Eur.
prosperity, good fortune, wealth, weal, happiness, Hhymn., Hdt., attic
to call or account happy, Eur., Xen., etc.; c. gen., μοίρας for his fortune, Soph.; ὑπέρ τινος Xen.; ἐπί τινι Dem.
conducive to happiness, Plat.; τὰ εὐδ. the constituents thereof, Xen.
blessed with a good genius; hence fortunate, happy, blest, Lat. felix, Hes., Theogn., Trag., etc.:— τὸ εὔδαιμον = εὐδαιμονία, Thuc.:—adv. -μόνως, Eur., etc.
of outward prosperity, well off, wealthy, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
tearful, lamentable, Aesch.
of much expense, liberal, Plut.
very clear, distinct, far-seen, epith. of Ithaca and other islands, Od.
with goodly feasts, Eur.
well-wooded, abounding in fair trees, Pind., Eur.
quite clear, manifest, Aesch., etc.: εὔδηλός [ἐστι] ποιῶν all may see him doing, Ar.
easy to cross, ποταμός Xen.
easy to misrepresent, Plat.
living temperately, Xen.
easy to reconcile, placable: adv. -τως, Plut.
ruler of the calm, Luc.
fair weather, Xen.
metaph. tranquillity, calm, Aesch., Xen.
Plat.; ἐν εὐδιεινοῖς in sheltered spots, Xen.
righteous dealing, Od.
easily-turning, Anth.
calm, fine, clear, of weather, sea, etc., Xen., Theocr.:—neut. εὔδιον, εὔδια, as adv., Anth.:—irreg. comp. εὐδιαίτερος, Xen.
well-built, Hom.
to be well pleased, ἔν τινι with a person or thing, NTest.
c. inf. to consent to do, be glad to do, Id.
satisfaction, approval, NTest.

entry.etym: the augm. is omitted in ionic
entry.sense: to be of good repute, to be held in esteem, honoured, famous, popular, Theogn., Eur., Ar., etc.: —εὐδ. ἔν τινι to be distinguished in a thing, Hdt., Thuc.; ἐπί τινι Plat.:— εὐδ. παρὰ τῷ βασιλέϊ to have influence with him, Hdt.
good repute, credit, Plat.
in good repute, honoured, famous, glorious, Aesch., Eur.; πρός τι in a thing, Plat.
to be in good repute, to be honoured, famous, Eur., Xen.
good repute, credit, honour, glory, Simon., Dem.
approval, τοῦ πλήθους Plat.
good judgment, Id.
of good repute, honoured, famous, glorious, Theogn., Thuc., etc.; νέες εὐδοξόταται ships of best repute, Hdt.
sharp-sighted, Soph.
running well, swift of foot, Anth.
ἐΰδρ. πόλις a city with fair race-courses, Id.
with plenteous dew, abounding in water, Eur., Ar.
to sleep, lie down to sleep, Hom., etc.; c. acc. cogn., εὕδειν ὕπνον Od., Eur., Theocr.; also, ὕπνωι εὕδειν Soph.; βραδὺς εὕδει, i. e. sleep detains him, Id.
of the sleep of death, Il., Soph.
metaph. to be still, be hushed, of wind, sea, etc., Il., Aesch.; of the mind, to be at ease, content, Plat., Theocr.
richly-robed, Mosch.
with beautiful seat, on stately throne, of gods, Aesch.
of a ship, = ἐΰσσελμος, Theocr.
pass. easy to sit, ἵππος Xen.
well-shaped, goodly, beautiful, beauteous, Il., Hdt., attic
sunny, warm, Lat. apricus, Eur.
well-robed, Aesch.
with or of good wool, fleecy, Anth.:—attic εὔερος, Soph.
easy to refute: easy to test, Plat.
of good hope, hopeful, cheerful, sanguine, Thuc., Xen., etc.:—c. inf. fut., εὔελπις ἰσχύσειν Aesch.; εὔελπις σωθήσεσθαι in good hope to be saved, Thuc.
easy to wipe out, Xen.
easily deceived, Plat., Xen.
a good habit of body, good state of health, high health, Plat.:—generally, vigour, Id.
easy to get out of or escape from, Aesch.
beauty of language, eloquence, Plat.
kind words, Soph.
well-speaking, eloquent, melodious, Xen.
making eloquent, of Helicon, Anth.
pass. well-spoken, acceptable, λόγος Hdt.
easy of attack, Luc.
exposed to treachery or stratagem, Xen.
easy to set upon or attack, Thuc.; εὐεπίθετον τοῖς πολεμίοις easy for them to make an attack, Xen.
easily put in order, docile, Anth.
well-doing, Od., Theogn., etc.
good service, a good deed, kindness, bounty, benefit, Od., Hdt.; εὐ. καταθέσθαι ἔς τινα Thuc.; εὐ. ὀφείλεταί μοι Id., etc.
to do well, do good, Soph.
c. acc. pers. to do good services or shew kindness to one, Aesch., Eur.; εὐεργεσίαν εὐεργ. τινά to do one a kindness, Plat.:—Pass. to have a kindness done one, εὐεργεσίαν εὐεργετηθείς Id.
a service done, kindness, Xen.
a well-doer, benefactor, Soph.; τινί to one, Hdt., Eur.; more commonly, τινός Id., etc.
a title of honour of such persons as had "done the state some service," εὐ. βασιλέος ἀνεγράφη was registered as the King's benefactor, Id.; so Xen., etc.
one must shew kindness to, τοὺς φίλους Xen.
well-wrought, well-made, of chariots, ships, etc., Hom.; of gold, wrought, Od.
well-done: pl. εὐεργέα = εὐεργεσίαι, benefits, services, Id.
doing good or well, upright, Od.
pass. well-wrought, well-tilled, Theocr.
easy to work, Hdt.
well-fenced, well-walled, Hom., Aesch.
act. fencing well, well-closed, of doors, Od.
sprouting well, flourishing, Eur.
well-being, tranquillity, prosperity, Hdt., Aesch.
goodness of season, a good season (for the fruits of the earth), Xen., etc.
easy to find, χώρα εὐεύρετος a place in which it will be easy to find things, Xen.
easy to come at, assailable, accessible, of places, Xen.
emulous in good: adv. -λως, Anth.
of ships, well-benched, Od.
well-girdled, of women, Il.
of men, girt up for exercise, dressed for walking, active, Hor.'s alte praecinctus, Hdt., Thuc.; of light troops, unincumbered, Lat. expeditus, Xen.
metaph. unincumbered, πενία Plut.
quite pure, unmixed, of wine, Eur.; comp. -ότερος and -έστερος.
good government, Od.
goodness of heart, good nature, guilelessness, simplicity, honesty, Hdt., attic
in bad sense, simplicity, silliness, Hdt., attic
good-hearted, open-hearted, simpleminded, guileless, Plat.; τὸ εὔηθες = εὐήθεια, Thuc.
in bad sense, simple, silly, Hdt., attic: —as Subst. a simpleton, Xen.
adv. -θως, Plat.:—comp. -έστερα, Id.; Sup. -έστατα, Eur.
Pass. to play the fool, Plat.
good-natured, Plat.:—adv. -κῶς, Ar.
well-pointed, Il.
inclined to give ear, of gods, Anth.
spinning well, Theocr.
easy to drive or ride over, πεδίον εὐ. a plain fit for cavalry, Xen.
well-sunned, sunny, genial, Lat. apricus, Eur., Ar.; εὐήλιον πῦρ the sun's heat, Eur.:—adv. -ίως, with bright sunshine, Aesch.
to spend the day cheerfully, live happily from day to day, Soph.; ταῖσι Θήβαις εὐημερεῖ τὰ πρὸς σέ 'tis fair weather for Thebes in relation to thee, Id.
to be successful in a thing, gain one's point, Aeschin.
fineness of the day, good weather, εὐημερίας οὔσης Xen.
good times, health and happiness, health and wealth, Eur.
of a fine day, εὐ. φάος a happy day, Soph.
enjoying a lucky day, cheerful, happy, Ar., Plat.
well as to the winds, i. e.,
sheltered from the wind, calm, Eur.
open to the wind, Soph.
obedient to the rein, tractable, Plat.
manliness, manly virtue, Eur.
man-exalting, glorious, Od.
well fitted to the oar, Aesch.
well-rowed, Soph., Eur.
well-fitted, of the oar, well-poised, easy to handle, Od., Eur.
easy to draw out, Hhymn.
with good thread, well-woven, Plat.
act. well-weaving, Anth.
well-sounding, tuneful, Eur.: loud-sounding, Id.
prosperous by sea, δῶρον εὐθ. the gift of seamanship, Soph.
blooming, flourishing, Mosch.
of good courage, Hhymn., Aesch., etc.
giving courage, secure, Xen.
easily won by kindness or attention, Xen.
to set in order, arrange well, Hes., Luc.
well-arranged or easily stowed, Aesch.; εὔθ. σάκος well-fitting, ready for use, Lat. habilis, Id.
sharpening well, Anth.
well-nurtured, thriving, goodly, Eur., Ar.
with distended udder, Eur.
good management, Hes.
a habit of good order, tidiness, Xen.
setting in order, c. gen., δωμάτων εὔθ. Aesch.
to thrive, flourish, prosper, Lat. florere, vigere, Hdt., Aesch., Dem.:—c. dat. to abound in a thing, Hhymn.
Pass. in same sense, οἱ Λακεδαιμόνιοι εὐθηνήθησαν Hdt.; τὴν πόλιν εὐθενεῖσθαι Dem.
easy to catch or win, Anth.
lucky or successful in the chase, Eur.; εὐθ. ἄγρη successful sport, Anth.; εὔθ. κάλαμοι unerring arrows, Id.
（θήρ) abounding in game, good for hunting, Id.
well-stored, precious, Anth.
touching the point, clever, Anth.
in or with easy death, Aesch.
with rich banquet: sumptuous, Aesch.
well-coped, of high walls, Eur.
with beautiful hair: in Il. always of horses, with flowing mane; of dogs, Xen.; of birds, well-plumed, Theocr.
made of good hair, of a fishing line, Anth.
with beautiful throne, Hom.
loud-sounding, Anth.
easily broken, crumbling, Plut.
a direct throw, Plut.
an open, direct trial, on the merits of the case, Dem.
righteous-judging, Aesch., Anth.
accurately wrought, Luc.
quick-killing, mortal, Plut.
fighting openly, Pind.
a fair fight, Plut.
to be of good cheer, Eur., Anth.:— to be gracious, Theocr.
trans. to make cheerful, cheer, delight, τινά Aesch.:—Pass. to be cheerful, Xen.
one must be cheerful, Xen.
cheerfulness, tranquillity, Xen.
bountiful, generous, Od.
of good cheer, cheerful, in good spirits, Xen.:—of horses, spirited, Id.;—adv. -μως, cheerfully, Aesch., Xen.
a setting straight, correction, chastisement, Plat.

at Athens, an examination of accounts, audit, Ar., etc.; in pl., Id., etc.; εὔθυναι τῆς πρεσβείας an account of one's embassage, Dem.; εὐθύνας ἀπαιτεῖν to call for one's accounts, Id.; εὐθύνας διδόναι to give them in, Ar.; εὐθύνας ὀφλεῖν Lys., etc.
a corrector, chastiser, judge, Aesch.
at Athens, an examiner, auditor, Plat.
directing, ruling, Aesch.
εὐθυντηρία, ἡ, the part of a ship wherein the rudder was fixed, Eur.
a corrector, chastiser, Theogn.
a ruler, Eur.
to guide straight, direct, Aesch., Ar.; εὐθ. δόρυ to steer the bark straight, Eur.; εὐθ. πλάταν Id.; εὐθ. χερσί to manage or guide him, Soph.
metaph. to direct, govern, Trag.
to make or put straight, Plat.; εὐθ. δίκας σκολιάς to make crooked judgments straight, Solon.
at Athens, to audit the accounts (cf. εὐθύνα) of a magistrate, call him to account, Plat.
c. gen. to call to account for an offence, εὐθ. τινὰ κλοπῆς Plut.:—Pass., τῶν ἀδικημάτων εὐθύνθη Thuc.
to go straight forward, πότμος εὐθυπορῶν (metaph. from a ship), unswerving destiny, Aesch.
going straight: metaph. straightforward, Plat.
to speak in a straightforward manner, Cic.: to speak off-hand, Plut.
plain-spoken, Cic.
with beautiful shaft, Eur.
straight, direct, Thuc., etc.:— εὐθείᾳ (sc. ὁδῷ) by the straight road, Plat.; so, τὴν εὐθεῖαν Eur.
in moral sense, straightforward, open, frank, Tyrtae., Aesch., etc.; ἀπὸ τοῦ εὐθέος, ἐκ τοῦ εὐθέος openly, without reserve, Thuc.
as adv., εὐθύς properly of Time, εὐθύ of Place:
εὐθύ, of Place, straight, εὐθὺ Πύλονδε straight to P., Hhymn.; εὐθὺ πρὸς τὰ λέχη Soph.; εὐθὺ ἐπὶ Βαβυλῶνος straight towards B., Xen.; so c. gen., εὐθὺ Πελλήνης Ar., etc.
εὐθύς,
of Time, straightway, forthwith, at once, Aesch., etc.; εὐθὺς ἐκ παιδίου Xen.; with a part., εὐθὺς νέοι ὄντες Thuc.; τοῦ θέρους εὐθὺς ἀρχομένου just at the beginning of summer, Id.
rarely, like εὐθύ, of Place, ὑπὲρ τῆς πόλεως εὐθύς just above the city, Id.; τὴν εὐθὺς Ἄργους ὁδόν the road leading straight to Argos, Eur.
of Manner, directly, simply, Plat.
εὐθέως, adv., is used just as the adv. εὐθύς, Soph., etc.; ἐπεὶ εὐθέως as soon as, Xen.
well-fringed, Anth.
right-minded, Aesch.
in a straight direction: in neut. εὐθύωρον as adv. = εὐθύς, Xen.
well-mailed, Anth.
Bacchic, Anth.: fem. εὐιάς Id.
easy to heal, Xen.
very holy, Lat. sacrosanctus, Anth.
Euios, Evius, name of Bacchus, from the cry, εὐοῖ, Soph., Eur.: Εὔιος = Βάκχος, Id.
εὔιος, ον, as adj. Bacchic, Soph., Eur.
of persons, well-horsed, delighting in horses, Hhymn.: Sup., Xen.
of places, famed for horses, Soph.
for good knowledge, Anth.
easy to conquer, Thuc.
easy to keep under, Xen.
to devote one's leisure, εἴς τι NTest.
good season, opportunity, Plat.
well-timed, in season, seasonable, Soph.: neut. εὔκαιρον in season, Anth.:—adv. -ρως, seasonably, opportunely, -ότερον, Plat.
of easy labour, easy, Eur.; εὐκ. ἔργα well-wrought works, Anth.; εὐκ. στέφανος a crown won by noble toils, Id.
well-curved, curved, Od., Mosch., etc.
easy to bend, flexible, Plut.
good of heart, stout-hearted, Lat. egregie cordatus, Soph., etc.; of a horse, spirited, Xen.:—adv. -ίως, with stout heart, Eur.
rich in fruit, fruitful, Hhymn., Soph.; of Demeter, Anth.
easy to overthrow, Xen.
easy to be despised, contemptible, despicable, Xen., Dem.
easy to work: of food, easy of digestion, Xen.
easy of accomplishment, Id.
easy to subdue, Plut.
easy to blame, open to accusation, Thuc.
easy to cleave or split, Od.
well-sounding, melodious, Eur., Ar.
pointed, Anth.
with beautiful horns, Mosch.: —contr. εὔκερως, ων, Soph.
she that lulls or soothes, Hes.
free from care, at one's ease, Lat. securus, Hom., Soph.; εὔκηλοι πολέμιζον were fighting undisturbed, Il.
of night, still, silent, Theocr.
easily moved, εἴς τι Anth.
ivied, Anth.
with beautiful pillars, Eur., Anth.
of good report, famous, glorious, Hom., etc.; εὐκλεέστατος βίος Eur. adv. -εῶς, epic -ειῶς, Il.; κατθανεῖν Aesch.; Sup. εὐκλεέστατα, Xen.
good repute, glory, Hom., Trag.
to praise, laud, Tyrtae.
much-famed, Anth.
to have a good lot, Anth.
fortunate, happy, Anth.
well-spun, Hhymn., Anth.
well-equipped with greaves, well-greaved, epic nom. and acc. pl. ἐϋκνημῖδες, -ῖδας, Hom.
with beautiful legs, Anth.
easy to deal with, Arist.
contentedness, good temper, Plat., etc.
of the body, agility, facility, Plut.
gluing well, sticky, Anth.
of persons, easily satisfied, contented with one's food, Anth., Plut.
easily satisfied, contented, good-natured, peaceable, Lat. facilis, comis, Ar.; c. dat., εὔκολος πολίταις friendly to them, at peace with them, Id.:—adv. -λως, tranquilly, calmly, Plat., Xen.
willing, agile, Anth.
in bad sense, easily led, prone, πρὸς ἀδικίαν Luc.
of things, easy, Plat.
with fair bosom, Anth.
in goodly folds, of a net, Id.
well cared for, Hdt.
fair-haired, Hom., Hes.: of sheep, well-fleeced, Anth.
loud-sounding, Eur.
with easy labour, easy, εὐκοπώτερόν [ἐστι], c. inf., NTest.
well-adorned, Hhymn.
orderly behaviour, good conduct, decency, Eur., Xen., etc.
behaving well, orderly, decorous, Solon., attic, Thuc.; τὸ εὔκοσμον = εὐκοσμία, Thuc.
well, adorned, graceful, Eur.
adv. -μως, in good order, Od.; Sup. -ότατα, Xen.
gracefully, Plut.
with fine horns, esp. of oxen, Hhymn.
a good temperature, mildness, Plat.
= εὔκρατος, Plat.
of persons, mixing readily with others, Anth.
well-mixed, temperate, Plat.
well-struck, well-woven, of the threads of the warp, Anth.
well-watered, Anth.
rich in barley, Theocr., Anth.
to keep distinct, keep in order, Xen.
well-separated, Xen.
well-arranged, in good order, Hdt., Xen.:— regular, steady, of winds, Hes.
accompanied by castanets, Anth.: rattling, πλατάγη Id.
well-hammered, well-wrought, of metal, Soph., Eur.
easy to hide, Aesch.
of or for prayer, votive, Aesch., Ar.: devoted, Eur.:— εὐκταῖα, τά, votive offerings, vows, prayers, Aesch., Soph.
of gods, invoked by prayer, Aesch., Eur.
prayed for, Anth.
wealthy, Aesch., Anth.
with straight fibres, slender, tall, Plut.
wealthy, Pind.
easily gotten, Anth.
expressing a wish, votive, Anth.
well-built, Il.; νῆσος ἐϋκτιμένη furnished with goodly buildings, Od.; ἐϋκτ. ἐν ἀλῳή on well-made threshing-floor, Il.; of a garden, well-wrought, Od.
wished for, ὄφρ’ εὐκτὰ γένηται that what they wish for may happen, Il.
to be wished for, εὐκτὸν ἀνθρώποις Eur.:— εὐκτόν ἐστι, c. inf., Id., Xen.
vowed, dedicated, Anth.
well-rounded, round, of a shield, Il., Aesch.; of a chariot, well-wheeled, Id., Od.
suited to the wine-cup, Anth.
discretion, caution, circumspection, Theogn., Soph., etc.; εὐλάβειαν ἔχειν μή . . = εὐλαβεῖσθαι μή . . , Plat.; εὐλαβείας δεῖται it requires caution, Dem.; ἐπ’ εὐλαβείᾳ by way of caution, Plat.
c. gen. caution or discretion in a thing, Soph.
reverence, piety, περὶ τὸ θεῖον Plut.: absol. godly fear, NTest.
in bad sense, over-caution, timidity, Plut.

to behave like the εὐλαβής, have a care, to be discreet, cautious, circumspect, to beware, Lat. cavere, foll. by μή or ὅπως μή with subj., Soph., Eur., etc.; c. inf., with or without μή, Soph., Eur.:— absol., εὐλαβήθητι Soph.; μηδὲν εὐλαβηθέντα without reserve, Dem.
c. acc. to have a care of, beware of, Aesch., Plat., etc.
to reverence, pay honour to, Id.
to watch for, await quietly, Eur.
taking hold well, holding fast: — then metaph. undertaking prudently, discreet, cautions, circumspect, Plat.
in bad sense, over-cautious, timid, Plut.:—adv. εὐλαβῶς, comp. -εστέρως, Eur.
reverent, pious, religious, devout, NTest.
pass. easy to get hold of, Luc.
one must beware, c. inf., Plat.
one must beware of, c. acc., Id.

entry.etym: Old Lacon. form, prob. akin to αὖλαξ
entry.sense: to plough, Orac. ap. Thuc.
a ploughshare, Orac. ap. Thuc.
entry.etym: Old Lacon. form, prob. akin to αὖλαξ

entry.sense: sweetly-speaking, Anth.
= εὔγλωσσος II, Id.
fruitful in herbs, Anth.
with goodly meadows, Od., Hhymn.
bringing wedded happiness, blessing marriage, Soph.
a worm or maggot, Il., Hdt.
easily taken hold of: adv. -τως so that one can easily take hold, Sup. εὐληπτότατα Xen.
easy to be taken or reduced, Thuc.:— easy to gain or obtain, Luc.
reins, Il.
with good harbours, Eur., Plat.
to speak well of, praise, honour, Trag.; δίκαια εὐλ. τινα to praise him justly, Ar.:—Pass. to be honoured, Soph.
to bless, NTest.
blessed, NTest.
good or fine language, Plat.: a fair speech, specious talk, NTest.
eulogy, panegyric, Pind.; blessing (as an act) or a blessing (as an effect) Id.:— of the alms collected for poor brethren, Id.
rightly reckoning, thoughtful, Arist.
having good reason, reasonable, sensible, Aesch.; εὔλογόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it is reasonable that, Ar.
reasonable, fair, Thuc., etc.: τὸ εὔλ. a fair reason, Id.
adv. -γως, with good reason, reasonably, Aesch., Thuc.; εὐλ. ἔχειν to be reasonable, Plat.
propitious, Plut.
with fine baths, Anth.
well-plumed, Soph.
helping in childbirth, Eur.
playing well on the lyre, skilled in the lyre, Ar., Anth.
easy to untie or loose, Xen.; εὔλ. πρὸς λοιδορίαν easily breaking into abuse, Theophr.
metaph. easily dissolved or broken, Eur., Xen.
readiness in learning, docility, Plat., Anth.
ready or quick at learning, Lat. docilis, Plat., Dem.:—adv. -θῶς, Aeschin.
pass. easy to learn or discern, intelligible, Aesch.: well-known, Soph.
of fine wool, Pind.
abounding in fennel, Anth.
easiness, ease, opportunity, τινος for doing a thing, Soph.
ease of movement, dexterity, Eur.

of condition, ease, comfort, εὐμαρείᾳ χρῆσθαι to be at ease, in comfort, Soph.; but also, εὐμαρίῃ χρᾶσθαι euphem. for alvum exonerare, to ease oneself, Hdt.; εὐμ. πρός τι provision for, protection against, Plat.
easy, convenient, without trouble, Theogn.; εὐμ. χείρωμα an easy prey, Aesch.:— εὐμαρές [ἐστι], c. inf., 'tis easy, Pind., Eur.; so, ἐν εὐμαρεῖ [ἐστι] Id.
adv. -ρῶς, epic -ρέως, mildly, Theogn.
easily, Plat.
an Asiatic shoe or slipper, Aesch., Eur.
of good size, very large, Ar.
well-blackened, inky, Anth.
musical, rhythmical, Arist.
the character of the εὐμενής, goodwill, favour, grace, Hdt., Soph., etc.
a well-wisher, εὐμενέτῃσι (epic dat. pl.) Od.
to be gracious, Theocr.
c. acc. to deal kindly with, Pind.
well-disposed, favourable, gracious, kindly, Hhymn., attic
of places, γῆ εὐμ. ἐναγωνίσασθαι favourable to fight in, Thuc.; of a river, kindly, bounteous, Aesch.; of a road, easy, Xen.
adv. -νῶς, ionic -έως, Aesch., Plat., etc.:—comp. -έστερον, Eur.
Εὐμενίδες sc. θεαί the gracious goddesses, euphem. name of the Ἐρινύες or Furies, Aesch., etc.
Mid. to propitiate, ἥρωας Xen.
easily changed, Arist.
changeable, Plat., Xen., etc.
readily imparting, generous, NTest.
easy to persuade, Arist.
easy to handle or manage, manageable, Plat., Xen.
easy to deal with or master, Thuc., Xen.
well-measured, well-calculated, Aesch.: well-proportioned, Theocr.
of a good length, tall, Plat., Theocr.
rich in sheep, Od., Pind.
easy to spin out, Luc.
of good counsel, prudent, Anth.
inventive skill, Pind., Plut.
of persons, skilful in contriving, ingenious, inventive, Aesch., Plat.
pass., of things, skillfully contrived, ingenious, Ar., Plat.
easily imitated, Plat.
exposed to hatred, Xen.
with fine threads, εὐμίτοις πλοκαῖς = τὸν μίτον εὖ πλέκουσα, Eur.
with beautiful μίτρα, Mosch.
armed with good ashen spear, Hom.; ἐϋμμελίω epic gen., Il.
easy to remember, Dem.; comp. -ότερος, Arist.
easy to remember:—comp. adv. εὐμνημονέστερως ἔχειν to be easier to remember, Xen.
well-remembering, mindful of a thing, c. gen., Soph.
happy possession of a thing, wealth or weal, Luc.
blest with possessions, Plat.
to sing well, Hhymn.
sweetly singing, Anth.
beauty of form, symmetry, Eur., Plat., etc.; symmetry in the σπλάγχνα, which was required for good omens, Aesch.
fair of form, comely, goodly, Hdt., Aesch.
skilled in the arts, esp. in poetry and music: hence musical, melodious, Eur., Anth.
laborious, Anth.
eloquent, Anth.
loud-bellowing, Anth.
to lay or place in ambush, Od.
to put to bed: of animals, to lay their young in a form, Xen.: metaph. of death, to lay asleep, Soph.:—Pass. to go to bed, sleep, Od., attic; of fowls, Od.:—of pain, εὐνασθέντος κακοῦ Soph.
intr., like Pass., to sleep, Id.
well-situated, of cities and houses, Hom.:—so also εὐ-ναιόμενος, Il.
in one's bed, εὐν. λαγώς a hare in its form, Xen.
wedded, Aesch., Eur.
λύπη εὐν. making one keep one's bed (cf. δεμνιοτήρης), Id.; εὐν. πτέρυγες brooding, of a bird on the nest, Anth.
（εὐνή II) of or for anchorage: generally, steadying, guiding a ship, of the rudder, Eur.
good for sleeping in: εὐνάσιμα, τά, convenient sleeping places, Xen.
a sleeping-place, bed-chamber, Trag.
to lay or place in ambush, Od.
to lay asleep, lull to sleep, metaph., εὔνησε γόον Id.:—Pass. to lie asleep, of a dog, to lie kennelled, Soph.: of the winds, Od.
well furnished with ships, Max.
from or out of bed, Od.
marriage, Eur.
a bed, Hom.; εὐνῆς ἐπιβήμεναι Il.; ἐξ εὐνῆς ἀναστᾶσα Id., etc.
the bedding, as opp. to λέχος (the bedstead), Od.
εὐναὶ Νυμφάων their abode, Il.: —of animals, the lair of a deer, Hom.; the seat of a hare, Xen.; the nest of a bird, Soph.
the marriage-bed, Hom., etc.
one's last bed, the grave, Aesch., Soph.
pl. εὐναί, stones used as anchors in the times of Hom. and Hes., and thrown out from the prow, while the stern was made fast to land, ἐκ δ’ εὐνὰς ἔβαλον κατὰ δὲ πρυμνήσι’ ἔδησαν Hom.
a bedfellow, husband, Aesch.:—doric fem. εὐνάτειρα, θεοῦ μὲν εὐν. partner of his bed, Id.; εὐν. Διὸς λεχέων Id.
reft of, bereaved of, c. gen., Hom., Aesch.:—absol. bereaved of children, Id.
a bedfellow, wife, Soph., Eur.
well-spun, Hom.
to be well-inclined, Hdt., attic

good-will, favour, kindness, κατ’ εὔνοιαν out of kindness or good-will, Hdt.; δι’ εὐνοίας Thuc.; δι’ εὔνοιαν Plat.; εὐνοίας ἕνεκα Dem.; μετ’ or ὑπ’ εὐνοίας Id.; ἐπ’ εὐνοίᾳ χθονός for love of fatherland, Aesch.; εὔνοιαν ἔχειν εἴς τινα ap. Dem.:—in pl. feelings of kindness, favours, Aesch.
a gift in token of good-will, esp. of presents to the Athenian commanders from the subject states, Dem.
well-disposed, kindly, favourable, Dem.: —adv., εὐνοϊκῶς ἔχειν τινί or πρός τινα to be kindly disposed to . . , Xen.
Dep.:— to have good laws, to be orderly, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
good order, order, Od., Hdt., attic
personified by Hes. as daughter of Themis.
under good laws, well-ordered, Pind., Plat.

well-minded, well-disposed, kindly, friendly, Hdt., attic; τινι to one, Hdt., etc.; οἱ ἐμοὶ εὖνοι my well-wishers, Xen.; τὸ εὔνουν = εὔνοια, Soph., etc.—comp. εὐνούστερος Id., ionic εὐνοέστερος Hdt.; Sup. εὐνούστατος Ar.
a eunuch, employed to take charge of the women and act as chamberlains (whence the name, οἱ τὴν εὐνὴν ἔχοντες) , Hdt., Ar., etc.
moving well or regularly, εὐνώμᾳ χρόνῳ by the steady march of time, Soph.
well-carded, of wool, Anth.
kind to strangers, hospitable, ἀνδρῶνας εὐξένους δόμων the guest- chambers, Aesch.; λιμὴν εὐξεινότατος ναύταις Eur.
πόντος εὔξεινος the Euxine, now the Black sea, Hdt., etc.:—anciently called ἄξενος, the inhospitable (dictus ab antiquis Axenus ille fuit, Ovid.).
well-planed, well-polished, of carpenters' work, Hom.
just like εὔξεστος, often in Hom.; σκέπαρνον ἐΰξοον an axe with polished haft, Od.
to have a free course or passage, of running water, Dem.
a good journey, wishes for a good journey, Aesch. ap. Ar.
easy to pass, of mountains, Xen.; of a road, easy to travel, Id.
to help on the way, c. dat. pers., Soph.
Pass. to have a prosperous journey, NTest.:—metaph. to prosper, be successful, Hdt., NTest.
producing good wine, Anth.
Bacchanalian exclamation, Lat. evoe, Soph., etc.
wealthy, prosperous, Eur.
easy to concede, indisputable, Plat.
to be well-equipt, Anth.
a good state of arms and equipments, Xen.
well-armed, well-equipt, Ar., Xen.
gentleness of temper, Eur.
good-tempered:—adv. -τως, with good temper, Thuc.
to be faithful to one's oath, Eur., Thuc.
fidelity to one's oath, Pind.
keeping one's oath, faithful to one's oath, Hes., attic
of oaths, εὔορκα ὀμνύναι to swear faithfully, attic; εὔορκόν [ἐστι] it is in accordance with one's oath, no breach of oath, Thuc.; εὔορκα ταῦθ’ ὑμῖν ἐστι Dem.; so in adv., τάδ’ εὐόρκως ἔχει Aesch.
a faithful oath, Aesch.
with good mooring-places, Hom., Soph.
well-moored, of ships, Anth.
abounding in birds, Anth.
well-roofed, Anth.
sweet-smelling, fragrant, Theocr.
with beautiful eyes, Xen.: keen-eyes, Id.
with fine eyebrows, Anth.
to be in good case, Hes.
with goodly banks, fertile, epic Hom.:— generally abundant, rich, Eur.
of the body, compact, firm, strong, Xen., Theocr.
the enjoyment of good things, comfort, ease, Xen.:—esp. in pl. enjoyments, luxuries, ἐν εὐπαθίῃσι εἶναι to enjoy oneself, Hdt.; also delicacies, dainties, Xen.
to be well off, enjoy oneself, make merry, Hdt., Plat.
easily affected, Plut.
a goodly race of children, Eur.; εὐπαιδίαν ἔχων blest in his children, Id.
blest in one's children, i. e. with many or good children, Hhymn., Hdt., attic; γόνος εὔπαις noble offspring, Eur.
handy, skilful, ingenious, inventive, Aesch., Anth.
easy to lead astray, Ar.
placable, Plut.
easy to follow, of an argument, Arist.
easy to convey, Plut.
with beauteous cheeks, Pind.
easily led away, Xen.
constantly attending, τὸ εὐπ. τῷ Κυρίῳ constant waiting on the Lord, NTest.
rendered irritable, Plut.
easily excited, Arist.
with fine purple border, Plut.
of persons, wearing such a garment, Lat. praetextatus, a grandee, Luc.
daughter of a noble sire, Hom.
of places, of a noble father, Eur.
of good or noble sire, of noble family, of persons, Soph., Eur., etc.; εὐπατρίδαι οἶκοι Eur.
at Athens in the old time, the εὐπατρίδαι formed the first class (the Nobles), the γεωμόροι the second, the δημιουργοί the third, Xen.
at Rome, the Patricians, Id.
born of a noble sire, Eur.; τίς ἂν εὔπατρις ὧδε βλάστοι; who could be born so worthy of a noble sire? Soph.; ἐλπίδων εὐπατρίδων of hopes derived from those of noble birth, Id.
born of a noble sire, Aesch.
ready to obey, obedient, τινι Aesch., Plat.; also τινος, Id.
act. persuasive, Aesch.
easily persuaded, Arist.
a word of uncertain meaning in Aesch., either tranquil, placable, as if it were εὐπέμφελον (cf. δυσπέμφελος) , or easy to be sent away (cf. δύσπεμπτος).
with a good father-in-law, Theocr.
beautifully robed, Hom.
easy of digestion, Arist.
easily turned round, Luc.
easy to sketch out, with a good outline, Luc.
easy to pull away, Xen.
easily besetting, NTest.
with beautiful leaves, Anth.
ease, δι’ εὐπετείας easily, Eur.:—pl., εὐπετείας διδόναι to give facilities, Plat.
easiness of getting or having a thing, c. gen., Hdt., Xen.
of the dice, falling well; metaph. favourable, Aesch.; so in adv., εὐπετῶς ἔχειν Id.

easy, without trouble, Lat. facilis, Hdt., attic:—adv. εὐπετῶς, ionic -έως, easily, Hdt., attic; with numerals, ἑξακοσίους ἀμφορέας εὐπ. χωρέει it easily holds 600 amphorae, i. e. full 600, Hdt.:—comp. -εστέρως Id.
of persons, easy-tempered, accommodating, Eur.
of good hard stone, Anth.
well-built, stout, Od.
well-built, Hom.
with beautiful helmet, Anth.
of fine texture, Eur.
with beautiful arms, Eur.
abounding in fountains, Anth.
trustworthy, trusty, Xen.; εὔπιστα things easy to believe, Soph.
act. easily believing, credulous, Arist.
very fat: very rich, Anth.
of a good breadth, Xen.
well filled, Od.
well-plaited, well-twisted, of wicker-work and ropes, Il.; of nets, Eur.
a fair voyage, Il., Soph.
with goodly locks, fairhaired, Hom.; εὐπλ. κόμαι goodly tresses, Eur.
good for sailing, εὔπλοον ὅρμον ἵκοιτο may he reach a friendly port, Theocr.
well-washed, well-cleansed, Od.
favourable to sailing, Anth.
fragrance, Anth.
breathing well, breathing a sweet smell, sweet-smelling, Mosch., Anth.
affording a free passage to the air, Lat. perflabilis, Xen.
goodness of foot, Xen.
beneficent, Arist.
well-made, well-wrought, Od., Hes.
beneficence, Luc.
much varied, variegated, Anth.
rich in wool, fleecy, Aesch.
good at war, successful in war, Hhymn., Xen.
conducting to a happy issue, Aesch., Soph.
to prosper, thrive, be well off, Xen.; ὅθεν ὁ πόλεμος εὐπορεῖ from which sources war is successfully maintained, Thuc.
c. gen. rei, to have plenty of, to have store of, to abound in a thing, c. gen., Xen., etc.
to find a way, find means, Thuc.: c. inf. to be able to do, Plat.
c. acc. rei, to supply, furnish, Thuc., Dem., etc.
an easy way of doing a thing, facility or faculty for doing, c. inf., Thuc.; absol., Xen.:—c. gen. rei, easy means of providing, Thuc., etc.
plenty, store, abundance, wealth, Xen.:— in pl. advantages, Isocr., Dem.
the solution of doubts or difficulties, Xen., etc.
easy to procure;— εὐπόριστα (sc. φάρμακα) τά, common medicines, Plut.
easy to pass or travel through, Aesch.; τὰ εὔπορα open ground, Xen.; εὔπορόν ἐστι διϊέναι Thuc.
easily gotten, easily done, easy, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:— τὸ εὔπορον = εὐπορία, Id.; εὔπορόν ἐστι it is easy, c. inf., Id.
going easily, ready, glib, γλῶττα Ar.
of persons, full of resources or devices, ingenious, inventive, ready, opp. to ἄπορος, Ar., Plat.
εὔπ. τινι well-provided with, rich in a thing, Thuc.:—absol. well off, wealthy, Dem.
adv. -ρως, easily, Xen.; comp. -ώτερον, Plat.
in abundance, εὐπ. ἔχειν πάντα Thuc.
to be lucky, fortunate, Plut.
good fortune, Plut., Luc.
happy, prosperous, Aesch.
easy to drink, pleasant to the taste, Aesch.
with good feet, Xen.
of verses, with good feet, flowing, Anth.
to do well, be well off, flourish, Thuc., Xen., etc.
well-doing, well-being, welfare, success, Thuc., etc.
easy to be done, Xen.
= εὐπραγία, Hdt., Trag.
good conduct, Xen.
with good stem, Anth.
goodly appearance, dignity, comeliness, Thuc.
colourable appearance, speciousness, plausibility, Id., Plat.
well-looking, goodly, comely, of outward appearance, Hdt., attic; εὐπρ. ἰδεῖν fair to look on, Xen.; εἶδος εὐπρεπής Eur.
decent, seemly, fitting, becoming, Hdt., Aesch., Eur.; τελευτὴ εὐπρεπεστάτη a most glorious end, Thuc.
specious, plausible, Hdt., Thuc.; ἐκ τοῦ εὐπρεποῦς in pretence, Id.
adv. -πῶς, ionic πέως, Hdt., Aesch., etc.; comp. -πέστερον, Eur.; Sup. -πέστατα, Thuc.
well-blowing, strong-blowing, Il.
easy of address, i. e. affable, courteous, Eur.; οὐκ εὐπρ. ἆται miseries that forbid my being spoken to, Id.
easy of access, of places, Luc.
of persons, accessible, affable, Lat. qui faciles aditus habet, Thuc., Xen.
of places, easily accessible, Id.
easy of approach: generally, easy, Eur.
to make a fair show, NTest.
lying so as to present a fair face, Aesch.
fair of face, Ar., Xen.: with glad countenance, Soph.
metaph. fair in outward show, specious, Hdt., Eur., etc.
with good pretext, plausible, Thuc.
with goodly stern, Il., Eur.
with goodly prow, Eur.
well-winged, well-plumed, Soph., Eur.; metaph., of high-plumed dames, Ar.
finely branching, of horns, Anth.
well-towered, of fortified towns, Il.

well, Lat. bene, opp. to κακῶς, Hom., etc.; with another adv., εὖ καὶ ἐπισταμένως well and workmanlike, Hom.; so, εὖ κατὰ κόσμον well and in order, Il.:—also, luckily, happily, well off, Od.:—in Prose, εὖ ἔχειν to be well off, attic;c. gen., εὖ ἥκειν τοῦ βίου to be well off for livelihood, Hdt.
εὖ γε, oft. in answers, v. εὖγε.
with Adjectives or Adverbs, to add to their force, εὖ πάντες, like μάλα πάντες, Od.; εὖ μάλα Id.; εὖ πάνυ Ar.; εὖ σαφῶς Aesch.
as Subst., τὸ εὖ the right, the good cause, τὸ δ’ εὖ νικάτω Id.
as the Predicate of a propos., τί τῶνδ’ εὖ; which of these things is well? Id.; εὖ εἴη may it be well, Id.

in Compos., it has all the senses of the adv., but commonly implies greatness, abundance, prosperity, easiness, opp. to δυσ-. (Like α- privat., Lat. in-, δυσ-, it is properly compounded with Nouns only, Verbs beginning with εὖ being derived from a compd. Noun, as, εὐπαθέω from εὐπαθής. εὐ-δοκέω is an exception.)
well-bearded, Anth.
abounding in foals or horses, Il.: breeding noble horses, Soph.
on one side, sideways, Il.
εὐρὰξ πατάξ, an exclamation to frighten away birds, Ar.
a finding, discovery, Plat.
to be discovered, found out, Thuc.
an inventor, discoverer, Plat.
inventive, ingenious, Plat.
discoverable, Xen.
an invention, discovery, Eur., Ar., etc.
c. gen. an invention, for or against a thing, a remedy, Eur., Dem.
that which is found unexpectedly, i. e., much like Ἕρμαιον, a piece of good luck, godsend, windfall, prize, Hdt., Eur., etc.
of a child, a foundling, Soph., Eur.
inventive of words, fluent, Pind.: wordy, sophistical, Ar.
of good leather, Anth.
of or like Euripides, Plat.
little Euripides, term of endearment, Ar.
a place where the flux and reflux is strong, esp. the strait which separates Euboea from Boeotia, where the current was said to change seven times a day, Xen.:—proverb of an unstable man, Aeschin.
generally, a canal, ditch, Anth.
to find, Hom., etc.:—c. part. to find that, Hdt.; and in Pass., ἢν εὑρεθῆις δίκαιος ὤν Soph.
c. inf., εὕρισκε πρῆγμά οἱ εἶναι found that the thing for him was, Hdt.
to find out, discover, Hom., etc.; cf. εὕρημα II:—so in Mid. to find out for oneself, Od.
to devise, invent, Aesch., etc.:—Mid., τὰ δ’ ἔργα τοὺς λόγους εὑρίσκεται deeds make themselves words, i. e. speak for themselves, Soph.
to find, get, gain, procure, Pind., Soph., etc.:—Mid. to get for oneself, bring on oneself, κακὸν εὕρετο Od.; αὐτὸς εὑρόμην πόνους Aesch.
of merchandise, to find a purchaser, to fetch, earn, πολλὸν χρυσίον εὑροῦσα having fetched a large sum, Hdt.; ἀποδίδοται τοῦ εὑρόντος sells for what it will fetch, Xen.
with a good nose, i. e. keen-scented, Aesch., Soph.
to flow well or abundantly; metaph. to go on well, be favourable, Eur.
to be fluent, speak successfully, Plut.
a good flow, free passage, Plat.
fluency, Id.
successful progress, Id.
loud-whizzing, Anth.
in Act. Ap., probably a storm from the East; but the prob. reading is εὐρ-ακύλων, Euro-aquilo, a N. E. wind.
easily inclining, easy-sliding, Anth.
the East wind, or more exactly E. S. E., Lat. Eurus, Il. (Probably akin to ἠώς, ἕως, the morning-wind, as Ζέφυρος is to ζόφος, the evening-wind.)
breadth, width, absol., εὖρος in breadth, Od., Hdt., etc.; so, τὸ εὖρος Xen.; εἰς εὖρος Eur.
well-stitched, Od.
fair-flowing, epic gen. ἐϋρρεῖος ποταμοῖο, contr. for ἐϋρρεέος, Il.
of a good sheep, Anth.
flowing well or plentifully, fair-flowing, Il., Soph., Eur.
of words, flowing, fluent, glib, Id.

entry.etym: fem. adj. used only in nom. and acc.
entry.sense: with wide streets, in epith. of great cities, Hom.
with wide threshing-floor, generally, broad, Anth.
rhythmical order or movement, Plat., etc.
rhythmical, of musical time or cadence, Ar., etc.
well-proportioned, Xen.; of armour, fitting well, Id.
wide-ruling, of Agamemnon, Hom.
with broad meadows, Pind.
broad-fronted, of oxen, Hom.
to broaden, εὐρῦναι ἀγῶνα to clear the arena (for dancing), Od.; τὸ μέσον εὐρύνειν to leave a wide space in the middle, Hdt.
metaph. to extend, Anth.:—Pass. to be spread abroad, Luc.
broad-backed, Soph.
fem. adj. with broad, open ways, only used in gen. fem., χθονὸς εὐρυοδείης Hom.
the far-seeing, of Zeus, εὐρύοπα Ζεύς Hom.; also in voc., εὐρύοπα Ζεῦ Il.;—in Il. there is also an acc. (as if from a nom. εὐρύοψ) εὐρύοπα Ζῆνα.
with broad surface, Anth.
with broad ways, of the sea, where all may roam at will, Hom., etc.
lewdness, Ar.
lewd, filthy, Ar.
with broad gates, Hom.
with broad channel, broadflowing, Il.
broad-flowing, Il. —there is no such verb as εὐρυρέω, v. εὖ fin.
with broad shield, name of Ajax' son, Soph.
of far-extended might, mighty, Hom., Pind.
with wide bier or tomb, Anth.
wide, broad, Hom., etc.
far-reaching, far-spread, κλέος εὐρύ Od.; ἐλπίδες Anth.
as adv. the neut. εὐρύ is mostly used, Il., etc.
broad-breasted, Hes.
wide-mouthed, Xen., etc.
wide, far-honoured, Pind.
with wide quiver, Pind.
broad-growing, of the manner in which the grains of barley are set on the stalk, Od.
wide-mouthed, of cups, Anth.
with wide-streaming hair, Pind.
with broad places, spacious, of cities, Hom., etc.: cf. καλλίχορος.
open space, free room, Hdt., Dem.
of an open field for battle, Xen.; ἐν εὐρυχωρίῃ ναυμαχέειν to fight with plenty of sea-room, Hdt.
roomy, wide, Arist.
abounding in grapes, Anth.
mouldy, dank, οἰκία εὐρώεντα (Virgil's loca senta situ), of the world below, Hom.; τάφον εὐρώεντα Soph.
Europa, Europe, as a geograph. name, first in the Hhymn. to Apollo.
mould, dank decay, Lat. situs, squalor, Theogn., Eur., etc.
stoutness, strength, Plut.
stout, strong, Xen. adv. -τως, Id.
to be or become mouldy, βίος εὐρωτιῶν the life of the unwashed, Ar.
fleshy, in good case, plump, Xen.
reverence towards the gods, piety, religion, Trag.; εὐς. Ζηνός towards him, Soph.; πρὸς εὐσέβειαν = εὐσεβῶς, Id.:—also, like Lat. pietas, reverence towards parents, filial respect, Plat.
credit or character for piety, Soph.
to live or act piously and religiously, Theogn., Soph., etc.; εἴς τινα towards one, Id.; εὐς. τὰ πρὸς θεούς in matters that respect the gods, Id.:—also, εὐς. θεούς to reverence Them, Aesch.
Lat. pius, pious, religious, Theogn., Hdt., attic; εὐσεβὴς χεῖρα righteous in act, Aesch.
of acts, things, etc., holy, hallowed, held sacred, Id., Eur.:— εὐσεβές [ἐστι], c. inf., Anth.; so, ἐν εὐσεβεῖ [ἐστι] Eur.:— τὸ εὐς. =εὐσέβεια, Soph., etc.
adv. εὐσεβέως, attic -βῶς, Pind., etc.; εὐσεβῶς ἔχει, for εὐσεβές ἐστι, Soph.:—comp. -έστερον, Xen.: Sup. -έστατα, Isocr.
well-benched, with good banks of oars, Hom., Eur.
much reverenced, holy, Soph.
of good signs or omens, Eur.
easily known by signs, clear to be seen, Aesch.
clear to understand, distinct, Soph.
to be strong, healthy, Eur.
stout, lively, Anth.
with full bread-basket, Anth.
abounding in chervil, Anth.
swift-springing, bounding, Il.
well-protected, Thuc.
to be well equipt, Soph.
well-shaded, shadowy, Soph.
sharp-seeing, keen-sighted, watchful, Hom.
far-seen or commanding a wide view, Xen.
（σκοπός) shooting well, of unerring aim, Orac. ap. Hdt., Aesch.
happiness, prosperity, Soph.
safe and well, happy, Theocr.
well-turned, wreathing, winding, Anth.
good heart, firmness, Eur.
with healthy bowels, Medic.
metaph. compassionate, NTest.
well-sown, Ar., Anth.

entry.etym: epic neut. ἠΰ (εὖ being used only as adv.)
entry.sense: good, brave, noble, Hom.:—epic gen. pl. ἐάων, of good things, good fortune, Id.
stability: good health, vigour, Anth.
to be steady, favourable, Eur.:— to be calm, tranquil, of the sea, Luc.
well-based, well-built, Hom.
light equipment, Plut.
well-equipt, Aesch.; of troops, light-armed, Lat. expeditus, Thuc., Xen.
well-conducted, favourable, Soph.
well-packed, compact, Plut.
well-behaved, mannerly, Plat.: —in dress, neat, trim, Luc.
rich in corn, Anth.: metaph. blooming, fruitful, Anth.
well-crowned or well-girdled, Hom., Hes.
crowned with walls and towers, Od., Pind.
well-trodden, Anth.
with good stomach: adv., -χως, Anth.
to sing sweetly, Soph.
generally, = εὐφημέω, to refrain from speech, Aesch., Ar.
with mouth of good size, of dogs, Xen.
speaking well, eloquent, Anth.; of the cup, making eloquent, Id.
like εὔφημος, avoiding words of ill omen, περὶ τούτων εὔστομα κείσθω on these things let me keep a religious silence, Hdt.; εὔστομ’ ἔχε peace, be still! Soph.
from a good trunk, Anth.
with goodly colonnades, Anth.
skill in shooting at a mark, good aim, Eur.; χερὸς εὐστ., periphr. for a bow, Id.
metaph. quickness in guessing, sagacity, Arist.
well-aimed, Eur., Xen.
aiming well, Id.:—adv., εὐστόχως βάλλειν Id.
metaph. guessing well, sagacious, Arist.
the place for singeing slaughtered swine, Ar.
well-twisted, of ropes, Od.
well-plied, nimble, πόδες Anth.
well-twisted, of cords, Hom.
curly, of hair, Anth.
well-twisted, Il.
easily turning, active, nimble, Eur.
well spread with clothes, Hhymn.
with goodly pillars, Eur.
easy to divine or understand (cf. συμβάλλω III), Aesch.
easy to deal with, honest, upright, Xen.
