the implements of Bacchus, the thyrsi and torches of the Bacchantes, Il.
to sacrifice, Lys..
an offering or mode of offering, Hdt.
in pl. offerings, sacrifices, sacred rites, Batr., Hdt., attic; θυσίῃσι (ionic dat. pl.) ἱλάσκεσθαι τὸν θεόν Hdt.; θυσίας ἕρδειν, ἐπιτελέειν, ἀνάγειν Id.; of the gods, θυσίαν δέχεσθαι Aesch.
a festival, at which sacrifices were offered, Plat.
the victim or offering itself, Luc.
an altar, NTest.
fit for sacrifice, Hdt., Ar.
sacrificial, Aesch., Soph.
a place for sacrificing, Aeschin.
one must sacrifice, Ar.
a sacrificer, slayer, Aesch., Soph.
of or for sacrifice, Luc.
Act. to offer part of a meal to the gods, Hom. (who used the word only in the sense of offering or burning, never = σφάξαι, to slaughter for sacrifice); θ. πέλανον, δεῖπνα Aesch.; κριθάς, πυρούς Ar.
to sacrifice, i. e. by slaying a victim, τῶι ἡλίωι θ. ἵππους Hdt.; θ. αὑτοῦ παῖδα Aesch.; ἱερεῖα Thuc.:—also simply, to slaughter, slay, Hdt.:—Pass., τὰ τεθυμένα the flesh of the victim, Xen.
absol. to sacrifice, offer sacrifices, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
to celebrate with offerings or sacrifices, c. acc., Hdt., Xen.
c. dupl. acc., εὐαγγέλια θ. ἑκατὸν βοῦς το sacrifice a hundred oxen for the good news, Ar.

Mid. to cause to be offered, to have a victim slain, and so to take the auspices, Hdt., Aesch., etc.:—rarely c. inf., θύομαι ἰέναι I consult the auspices about going, to know whether I may go or not, Xen.; so, θύεσθαι ἐπ’ ἐξόδωι Id.:—metaph. to tear in pieces, Aesch.
to rush on or along, of a rushing wind, Od.; of a swollen river, Il.; of the sea, Od.; δάπεδον αἵματι θῦεν the ground boiled with blood, Id.:—generally, to storm, rage, Il., Aesch.
smelling of incense, sweet-smelling, Od., Eur.
smelling of incense, sweet-smelling, Od., Eur.
that which is burnt as incense; in pl. spices, Hdt.
a penalty, Hom.
a cord, string, Hdt.: a bow-string, Aesch.
a heap, Aesch.
flattery, adulation, Eur., Ar.
a piece of flattery, Ar.; pl. caresses, Eur.
bits of flattery, Ar.
to flatter, fawn on, cajole, wheedle, Lat. adulari, Soph., Eur., etc.; σὺ ταῦτα θώπευ’ be it thine to flatter thus, Soph.:— to caress or pat a horse, Xen.
a breast-work, Aesch.
to arm with a breastplate or corslet, Xen.:—Mid. to put on one's breastplate, Id.: —Pass., θωρακισθείς with one's breastplate on, Id.; οἱ τεθωρακισμένοι cuirassiers, Thuc., Xen.
generally, to cover with defensive armour, ἐθωράκισε πλὴν τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν Xen.
making breastplates, Xen.
a dealer in breastplates, Ar.
wearing a breastplate, a cuirassier, Hdt., Xen.
a breastplate, cuirass, corslet, Lat. lorica, Il.:— the breast and back pieces which composed it were called γύαλα, which were fastened by clasps (ὀχεῖς) on both sides.
the part covered by the breastplate, the trunk, Eur., Plat.
the breastwork of a wall, the outer wall, Hdt.
armed with breastplate, Il.
= θωρακίζω, to arm with breastplate: and, generally, to arm, get men under arms, Il.

Mid. and Pass., θωρήσσομαι, fut. ξομαι: aor1 ἐθωρήχθην:— to arm oneself, put one's harness on, Hom.; τεύχε’ ἐνείκω θωρηχθῆναι I will bring you arms to arm yourselves withal, Od.; πρὸς τοὺς πολεμίους θωρήξομαι Ar.
to make drunk, to intoxicate, Theogn.:— Mid. to drink unmixed wine, to get drunk, Id.
the jackal, Il., Hdt.
a barker, roarer, crier, Anth.
make a noise, of a gnat, to buzz, Aesch.; of men, to cry aloud, shout out, Trag.
c. acc. pers. to call on, call, Soph.; also c. dat., θ. κυσί to shout to dogs, Eur.
a flatterer, fawner, false friend, Hdt.:—as adj., θῶπες λόγοι fawning speeches, Plat.
Comic exclamation for αἰβοῖ, Ar.
to heat, Od.
to melt:—Pass. to be melted, Id.
to warm, cheer, Lat. fovere, θυμὸν ἰαίνειν Id., etc.:—Pass., ἐν φρεσὶ θυμὸς ἰάνθη Id.; μέτωπον ἰάνθη her brow unfolded, Il.; c. dat. rei, to take delight in, Od.
to shout Ἴακχος; c. acc. cogn., ἰακχάζειν φωνήν to utter the cry Ἴακχος, Hdt.
a temple of Bacchus, Plut.
Bacchanalian, Soph.
Iacchus, mystic name of Bacchus, Ar., etc.
a festal song in his honour, Hdt., etc.
a wailing woman, Aesch.
a wail, lament, dirge, Aesch., Eur.
as adj., hapless, melancholy, Theocr.
to send forth, ὀϊστὸν ἀπὸ νευρῆφιν ἴαλλεν Il.; ἐπ’ ὀνείατα χεῖρας ἴαλλον they put forth their hands to the dishes, Hom.; περὶ χερσὶ δεσμὸν ἴηλα threw chains around thy arms, Il.
to attack, assail, ἀτιμίηισιν ἰάλλειν τινά to assail him with reproaches, Od.
to send, Theogn., Aesch.
intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν), to send oneself on, i. e. to flee, run, fly, Hes.
sent forth, Aesch.
a means of healing, remedy, medicine, Hdt., Thuc.
= ἴασις, NTest.
iambic, μέτρον Arist.
as Subst., ἰαμβεῖον, ου, τό, an iambic verse, Ar., Plat.
iambic metre, Arist.
a glutton at iambics, or perhaps a murderer of them, Dem.
to assail in iambics, to lampoon, Arist.
iambic, Arist.
to write iambics, Arist.
a writer of iambics, Arist.
an iambus, a metrical foot consisting of a short and long syll., as ἐγώ, Plat., etc.
an iambic verse, the trimeter or senarius, Hdt., Ar.
an iambic poem, lampoon, Plat.
entry.etym: From ἰάπτω 2, because iambics were first used by the satiric poets Archilochus and Hipponax; criminosi iambi, Hor.

entry.sense: an Ionian, Aesch. [who has gen. pl. Ἰάνων with ᾰ].

entry.etym: Pass., v. infr. [ῑᾱ Hom., etc.,; later also ι]
entry.sense: to heal, cure, Hom., etc.:— metaph., ἀδικίαν ἰᾶσθαι Eur.: proverb., μὴ τῶι κακῶι τὸ κακὸν ἰῶ, i. e. do not make bad worse, Hdt.
the aor1 ἰάθην [ᾱ] is always pass., to be healed, to recover, Andoc., NTest.; so perf. ἴᾱμαι NTest.
O Ionian, Ar.
the Ionians, including, Il.:—in Persian it was = Ἕλληνες, Aesch.:— sg. Ἰάων rare, Theocr.
Ionian, Greek, Aesch.; Athenian, Orac. ap. Plut.
a voice, cry, Orac. ap. Hdt., Aesch., Eur.

to send on, put forth, Hom.; κατὰ χρόα ἰάπτειν (sc. τὰς χεῖρας) to put forth (her hands) against her body, i. e. smite her breasts for grief, Od.: —of missiles, to send forth, shoot, Aesch.; ἰάπτειν ὀρχήματα to begin the dance, Soph.
to assail, attack, Id.: to wound, ἰ. τινὰ ἐς ὀστέον ἄχρις Theocr.; Pass., ἰάπτομαι ἄλγεσιν ἦτορ Mosch.
a people of Southern Italy, Hdt.
the country of the Iapygians, a people of Southern Italy, Hdt.
Iapygian, Thuc.
the NW or WNW wind, Arist.
Ἰάπῠγες, Ion. Ἰήπ-, οἱ, a people of Southern Italy, Hdt.:—ἡ Ἰᾱπυγία, Ion. Ἰηπ-, their country, Id.:—Adj. Ἰᾱπύγιος, α, ον, Iapygian, Thuc.
to be cured, curable, opp. to ἀνίατος, Aesch., Plat., etc.: metaph. appeasable, Eur.
healing, a mode of healing, cure, remedy, Lat. medela, Soph., Plat., etc.
Ionian, Ionic, Hdt., Thuc.
as Subst. (sub. γυνή), an Ionian woman, Hdt.
(sub. γλῶσσα) the Ionic dialect, Luc.
jasper, Plat. (A foreign word.)
in Ionic fashion, Plat.
in the Ionic mode (of music), Id.
in the Ionic dialect, Luc.
Iaso, the goddess of healing, Ar.
doctor, healer, metaph., ἰ. κακῶν Od., Soph.
the art of healing, surgery, Soph.
curable, Pind., Plat.
medical treatment: metaph. a curing, correcting, Arist.
a surgery, Plat., etc.
in Rhet. a means of healing disaffection in the hearers, Arist.
to treat medically, to cure, Plat.:—Pass. to be under medical care, Id.
absol. to practise medicine, Arist.
of or for a surgeon: — ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη), surgery, medicine, Hdt., Plat., etc.
skilled in the medical art, Plat.: metaph., ἰ. περὶ τὴν ψυχήν Id.
physician and seer, of Apollo and Aesculapius, Aesch., Ar.: metaph., Ar.
like ἰατήρ, one who heals, a mediciner, physician or surgeon (for there seems to have been no professional distinction), Il., etc.: — ἰ. ὀφθαλμῶν, ὀδόντων an oculist, dentist, Hdt.
metaph., ἰατρ. πόνων Pind.; ὀργῆς Aesch.
a practiser of medicine, Ar.
alas! ah! woe's me! Ar.; so, ἰατταταιάξ, Id.
exclamation of joy, ho ho! Ar.
a shout in answer to one calling, ho! holla! Ar.
to sleep, to pass the night, Hom.:—c. acc. cogn., ἐννυχίαν τέρψιν ἰαύειν to enjoy the night's sleep, Soph.
an archer, Anth.
to cry, shout, shriek, like ἰάχω, Eur., etc.:—c. acc. cogn., ἰαχεῖν μέλος Id.; ἀοιδάν Ar.
to bewail, lament, Eur.
of things, to sound, Hhymn., Eur.
a cry: the hissing of a serpent, Eur.: the sound of an instrument, Anth.
a cry, shout, wail, shriek, Hom.: also a joyous sound, ἰαχὰ ὑμεναίων Pind., Trag.
to cry, shout, shriek, in sign either of joy or grief, like ἰαχέω, Hom.; of articulate speech, Eur., Anth.
of things, to ring, resound, Hom.; of waves and of fire, to roar, Id.; of a bowstring, to twang, Il.; of hot iron in water, to hiss, Od.
c. acc. cogn., ἰ. ἀοιδήν, μέλος to sound forth a strain, Hhymn.; ἰ. λογίων ὁδόν to proclaim the sense of oracles, Ar.; ἴαχον Ἀπόλλω were sounding his praises, Id.
the ibis, an Egyptian bird, Hdt., Ar.
a mortar, Solon., Anth.
the part behind the thigh and knee, the ham, Lat. poples, Il., Theocr.
of Ida, Il.
causing sweat, Hes.
= εἶδος, form, Pind., Ar., etc.
the look of a thing, as opp. to its reality, Lat. species, γνώμην ἐξαπατῶς’ ἰδέαι outward appearances cheat the mind, Theogn.

a kind, sort, nature, Hdt.; ἐφρόνεον διφασίας ἰδέας they conceived two modes of acting, Id.; τὰ ὄργι’ ἐστὶ τίν’ ἰδέαν ἔχοντα; what is their nature or fashion? Eur.; καινὰς ἰδέας εἰσφέρειν to bring in new fashions, Ar.; πᾶσα ἰδέα θανάτου every form of death, Thuc.
in Logic, = εἶδος, a class, kind, sort, species, Plat.
and, Hom., Soph.
lo, behold, Hom.: later ἴδε.
Ida, i. e. the wooded hill, Mt. Ida, Il.; epic gen., Ἴδηθεν μεδέων ruler of Ida, Id.; as adv. from Ida, Id.
a timber-tree, in pl., Hdt.:—in sg., a wood, ἐν τῇ ἴδῃ τῇ πλείστῃ in the thick of the wood, Id.
as prop. n.,
to follow one's own counsel, take one's own way, Hdt.
holding one's own opinion, Arist.
of peculiar form, Plut.
Mid. to appropriate to oneself, Plat.
one's own, pertaining to oneself: and so,

private, personal, πρῆξις ἥδ’ ἰδίη οὐ δήμιος this business is private, not public, Od.; ἴδιος ἐν κοινῷ σταλείς embarking a private man in a public cause, Pind.; πλοῦτος ἴδιος καὶ δημόσιος private and public wealth, Thuc.; τὰ ἱρὰ καὶ τὸ ἴδια temples and private buildings, Hdt.

τὰ ἴδια, either private affairs, private interests, Thuc.; or one's own property, Id.; ἴδια πράττειν to mind one's own affairs, Eur.; τὰ ἐμὰ ἴδια Dem.:—in sg., τὸ ἡμέτερον ἴδιον Id.; εἰς τὸ ἴδιον for oneself, Xen.; τοὐμὸν ἴδιον for my own part, Luc.
peculiar, separate, distinct, ἔθνος ἴδιον Hdt.; ἴδιοί τινες θεοί Ar.; ἴδιον ἢ ἄλλοι peculiar and different from others, Plat.; strange, unaccustomed, ἰδίοισιν ὑμεναίοισι Eur.
regul. comp. is ἰδιώτερος.; Sup. ἰδιώτατος, Dem.; later ἰδιαίτερος, -αίτατος, Arist.
adv. ἰδίως, especially, peculiarly, Plat., etc.
also ἰδίᾳ, ionic -ίῃ, as adv. by oneself, privately, separately, on one's own account, Hdt., etc.; οὔτε ἰδίᾳ οὔτε ἐν κοινῷ Thuc.; καὶ ἰδίᾳ καὶ δημοσίᾳ Id.:—c. gen. apart from, Ar.
equipt at one's own expense, Plut.; ἰδ. ἔπλευσε sailed in his own ship, Id.
peculiar nature, property, Xen.
to sweat, Od., Ar.
distinction between, Plat.
private life or business, Xen., Plat.
uncouthness, want of education, Luc.
to be a private person, i. e. to live in retirement, Plat., Xen.:—of a country, to be of no consideration, Xen.
to practise privately, of a physician, Plat.
c. gen. rei, to be unpractised in a thing, Id.
a private person, an individual, ξυμφέροντα καὶ πόλεσι καὶ ἰδιώταις Thuc., etc.
one in a private station, opp. to one taking part in public affairs, Hdt., attic; opp. to στρατηγός, a private soldier, Xen.
a common man, plebeian, Plut.
as adj., ἰδ. βίος a private station, homely way of life, Plat.
one who has no professional knowledge, as we say "a layman," ἰατρὸς καὶ ἰδιώτης Thuc.; opp. to ποιητής, a prose-writer, Plat.; to a trained soldier, Thuc.; to a skilled workman, Plat.
c. gen. rei, unpractised, unskilled in a thing, Lat. expers, rudis, ἰατρικῆς Id.; also, ἰδ. κατά τι Xen.
generally, a raw hand, an ignorant, ill-informed man, Id., Dem.
ἰδιῶται one's own countrymen, opp. to ξένοι, Ar.
of or for a private person, private, Hdt., attic
not done by rules of art, unprofessional, unskilful, rude, Plat.:—adv., ἰδιωτικῶς τὸ σῶμα ἔχειν, i. e. to neglect gymnastic exercises, Xen.
knowledge, skill, Hes.
skilled, skilful, τινός in a thing, Anth.
to bend oneself, double oneself up, shrink up, esp. for pain, Il.; ἰδνωθεὶς ὀπίσω bent back, of one throwing up a ball, Hom.
the chief of the Cretans, properly strength of Ida (in Crete), Il.
violent heat, as of the dog-days, Hes.

entry.etym: 2nd sg mid imperat of εἰδόμην, as adv.
entry.sense: lo! behold! see there! Soph.; ἰδού, δέχου there! take it! Lat. en tibi! Id., etc.:— well, as you please! Ar.
in repeating another's words quizzingly, ἰδού γ’ ἄκρατον oh yes, wine, Id.
skill, ἰδρείῃ πολέμοιο Il.
experienced, knowing, skilful, Od.; c. gen. rei, Hes., Trag., etc.; c. inf. knowing how to do, Od.
ἴδρις alone, the provident one, i. e. the ant, Hes.

entry.etym: This Verb, like its oppos. ῥιγόω, is contracted epic into ω and ωι instead of ου and οι, part. fem. ἱδρῶσα Il., lengthd. ἱδρώουσα, masc. acc. ἱδρώοντα, -οντας; but in Xen. we find ἱδροῦντι, not ἱδρῶντι.
entry.sense: to sweat, perspire, Hom. (esp. in Il.); ἵππους ὑπὸ ζυγοῦ ἱδρώοντας Od.; ἱδρώσει τελαμών it shall reek with sweat, Il.; c. acc. cogn., ἱδρῶθ’ ὃν ἵδρωσα Id.
a thing founded or built, a foundation, Plut.
like ἕδος, a temple, shrine, Hdt., Aesch., Eur.
τὸ ἵδρυμα πόλεως the stay, support of thy city, Lat. columen rei, Eur.
a founding, building, of temples, Plat.
Ἑρμέω ἱδρύσιες his statues, Anth.
one must inaugurate a statue, Ar.
pass., ἱδρυτέον one must sit idle, Soph.

to make to sit down, to seat, Hom., etc.; αὐτός τε κάθησο καὶ ἄλλους ἵδρυε λαούς Il.; ἵδρυσε τὴν στρατιήν encamped the army, Hdt.:—Pass. to be seated, sit. still, Il., Eur.; of an army, to lie encamped, Hdt.; ἀσφαλῶς ἱδρυμένος seated, steady, secure, Id.
like Lat. figere, to fix or settle persons in a place, εἰς δόμον Eur.:—Pass. to be settled, Hdt., Soph., etc.
in Mid. to establish, ἱδρ. τινὰ ἄνακτα Eur.; τινὰ ἐς οἶκόν Id.
perf. pass. ἵδρῡμαι, of places, to be situated, to lie, Hdt.
to set up, found, esp. to dedicate temples, statues, Eur., Ar.:—Pass., ἱρόν, βωμὸς ἵδρυται Hdt.:—Mid. to set up for oneself, to found, Id., Eur.; perf. pass. in mid. sense, Hdt., Plat.
sweat, Lat. sudor, Hom., attic
the exudation of trees, gum, σμύρνης Eur.

entry.etym: epic for εἰδυῖα, part. fem. of οἶδα
entry.sense: as adj., ἰδυίῃσι πραπίδεσσιν with knowing, skilful mind, Il.
a hawk, falcon, Il., Ar.
Pass. to be a priest or priestess, Hdt., Thuc.
the priest's office, priesthood, Arist., NTest.
a priesthood, NTest.
priestly, Plut.
to be a priest, NTest.
of or for the priest's office, priestly, Arist., Plut.
devoted to sacred purposes, Luc.
a priestess, Il., attic
a victim, an animal for sacrifice or slaughter, Hom., Hdt., attic
an offering for the dead, Od.
of cattle slaughtered for food, mostly in pl., Hdt., Xen.
a priest, sacrificer, Il., etc.
metaph., ἱερεύς τις ἄτης a minister of woe, Aesch.; and, comically, λεπτοτάτων λήρων ἱερεῦ Ar.
to slaughter for sacrifice, to sacrifice, Hom.
to slaughter for a feast, Od.: Mid. to slaughter for oneself, Id.
hieroglyphic; ἱερογλυφικά (sc. γράμματα) τά, a way of writing on monuments used by the Egyptian priests, Luc.
of prophetic tongue, Anth.
a sacred scribe, a lower order of the Egyptian priesthood, Luc.
offered to a god, ἱερ. καπνός smoke from the sacrifices, Ar.
the herald at a sacrifice, Dem.
sacred or mystical language, Luc.
the holy time of the month, during which the great festivals were held and hostilities suspended, ἱερ. Νεμέας, of the Nemean games, Pind., Thuc.
the holy time of the month, of the Carneian festival at Sparta, Thuc.
to be ἱερομνήμων, Ar.
the sacred Secretary or Recorder sent by each Amphictyonic state to their Council, Dem.:—generally, a recorder, notary, Arist.
conqueror in the games, Luc.
to offer sacrifices, to sacrifice, Dem.
managing sacred rites: at Athens, the ἱεροποιοί were ten magistrates, one from each tribe, who saw that the victims were perfect, Plat., Dem.
beseeming a sacred place, person or matter, holy, reverend, Plat., Luc.; ἱεροπρεπέστατος Xen.

entry.etym: a false form for ἱρουργίη in Hdt.

entry.sense: super-human, mighty, divine, wonderful, Hom.; often like θεσπέσιος, to express wonder or admiration, ἱερὸν τέλος, ἱερὸς στρατός a glorious band, Id.; ἱερὸς δίφρος a splendid chariot, Il.; οὐχ ἱερόν no mighty matter! Theocr.

holy, hallowed, Lat. sacer, Hom., etc.; ἱερὸς πόλεμος a holy war, Ar., etc.: ἱρὰ γράμματα, = ἱερογλυφικά, Hdt.; ἱερὸν τὸ σῶμα διδόναι, of one dedicated to a god, Eur.; ἱερὸς νόμος the law of sacrifice, Dem.; of the Roman Tribunes, to express sacrosanctus, Plut.; for ἱερὰ καὶ ὅσια, v. ὅσιος.
of kings, heroes, etc., from a notion of "the divinity that doth hedge a king,"Pind., Soph.
as Subst.,

ἱερά, ionic ἱρά, τά, offerings, sacrifices, victims, ἱερὰ ῥέζειν, Lat. sacra facere, operari, Il.; ἔρδειν Hes.; θῦσαι Hdt.:—after Hom. the inwards of the victim, the auspices, τὰ ἱερὰ καλὰ ἦν Xen.; or, simply, τὰ ἱερὰ γίγνεται Id.:—generally, sacred things or rites, Lat. sacra, Hdt.
ἱερόν, ionic ἱρόν, τό, a temple, holy place, Id., attic
ἱρὸν τῆς δίκης a sacred principle of right, Eur.
special phrases:
ἱερὸς λόχος, v. λόχος 1. 4.
ἱερὰ νόσος the awful disease, epilepsy, Hdt.
ἡ ἱ. ὁδός the sacred road to Delphi, Id.
ἡ ἱερά (sc. τριήρης), of the Delian ship, or one of the state-ships (Salaminia or Paralos), Dem.
Ἱερὰ νῆσος, one of the Liparean group, Thuc.
adv. -ρῶς, holily, Plut.
to rob a temple, commit sacrilege, Ar., Plat.:—c. acc., ἱερ. τὰ ὅπλα to steal the sacred arms, Dem.
temple-robbery, sacrilege, Xen., Plat.
a temple-robber, sacrilegious person, Lat. sacrilegus, Ar., Plat.
to perform sacred rites: c. acc., ἱερ. τὸ εὐαγγέλιον to minister the gospel, NTest.; so in Mid., ἱερουργίας ἱερουργεῖσθαι Plut.
religious service, worship, sacrifice, Hdt.
to be a hierophant, Luc.
a hierophant, one who teaches the rites of sacrifice and worship, Hdt., Plut.:—at Rome, the Pontifex Maximus, Plut.
the office of hierophant, Plut.
of a hierophant, Luc.; βίβλοι ἱερ. the libri pontificales, Plut. adv. -κῶς, Luc.
a keeper of a temple, temple-warden, Lat. aedituus, Eur.
of hallowed soil, Anth.
to hallow, consecrate, dedicate, Plat.:—perf. pass. inf. ἱερῶσθαι Thuc.
the office of priest, priesthood, Hdt., attic
an ironical exclamation, whew! Lat. hui! Ar.
Causal, to make to sit, Il.
intr. to sit, Lat. sedere, Od.; ἐπ’ ὄμμασι ὕπνος ἱζάνει Il.
of soil, to settle down, sink in, Thuc.

Causal, to make to sit, seat, place, μή μ’ ἐς θρόνον ἷζε Il.; ἵζει μάντιν ἐν θρόνοις Aesch.:—the ionic and poet. aor1 εἷσα is always causal (as in the compds. ἐφ-, καθ-εῖσα), εἷσεν ἐν κλισμοῖς, κατὰ κλισμούς, ἐπὶ θρόνου, ἐς δίφρον Hom.; εἷσέ μ’ ἐπὶ βουσί set me over the oxen, Od.; σκοπὸν εἷσε set as a spy, Il.; λόχον εἷσαν laid an ambush, Id.; εἷσεν ἐν Σχερίηι settled [them] in Scheria, Od.; imperat. εἷσον Id.; part. ἕσας Id.; so in Hdt., τοῦτον εἷσε ἐς τὸν θρόνον Id.; ἐπὶ τὸ δεῖπνον ἵζειν τοὺς βασιλέας Id.; inf. ἕσσαι in Pind.; rare in attic, σὺ γάρ νιν εἷσας ἐς τόδε for thou didst bring it to this, Soph.; cf. καθίζω.
the aor1 mid. εἱσάμην is used in the sense of ἱδρύω, to dedicate temples statues, etc., to gods, Theogn., Hdt.; part. εἱσάμενος Thuc.
intr. to sit, sit down, Lat. sedere, Il.; ἵζειν ἐς θρόνον Od.; ἐς θᾶκον Soph.; also, ἐπὶ θρόνου Hom.; ἐπὶ τὸ δεῖπνον Hdt.; ἐπὶ κώπην, of rowers, Ar.:—c. acc. loci, ἵζειν θρόνον Aesch.; βωμόν Eur.
to sit still, be quiet, Hhymn.

Pass. also in signf. II, to sit, πάροιθ’ ἵζευ ἐμεῖο sit down before me, Il.: to lie in ambush, Id.: of an army, to sit down, take up a position, ἵζεσθαι ἀντίοι τινί Hdt.; ἵζεσθαι ἐν τῶι Τηυγέτωι or ἐς τὸ Τηύγετον Id.
invoked with the cry ἰή, of Apollo, Aesch., etc.
mournful, grievous, Soph.; ἰήιος βοά a cry of mourning, Eur.
to set a going, put in motion, being the Causal of εἶμι (ibo), ἧκα πόδας καὶ χεῖρε φέρεσθαι Od.; ἱ. πόδα Eur.: hence
to send, Hom., etc.

of sounds, to send forth, utter, Id., etc.; Ἑλλάδα γλῶσσαν ἱ. to speak Greek, Hdt.; φωνὴν Παρνησίδα Aesch.; τὸ τᾶς εὐφήμου στόμα φροντίδος ἱέντες, i. e. speaking not in words, but in silent thought, Soph.
to send forth, throw, hurl, of stones or javelins, Hom.; c. gen. pers. to throw or shoot at one, Il.
like βάλλειν, c. dat. instrumenti, ἵησι τῆι ἀξίνηι he throws [at him] with his axe, Xen.
the acc. is often omitted, so that ἵημι sometimes seems intr., to throw, shoot, Hom.; c. gen. objecti, τῶν μεγάλων ψυχῶν ἱείς shooting at great souls, Soph.
of water, to let flow, let burst or spout forth, Il., Aesch., etc.; ὕδωρ omitted, ποταμὸς ἐπὶ γαῖαν ἵησιν the river pours over the land, Od.; so, of fire, Eur.
to let fall, κὰδ δὲ κάρητος ἧκε κόμας made his locks flow down from his head. Od.; ἐκ δὲ ποδοῖιν ἄκμονας ἧκα δύω I let two anvils hang from his two legs, Id.; ἧκαν ἑαυτούς let themselves go, Xen.
Mid. to send oneself, hasten, οἴκαδε ἱέμενος hastening homewards, Hom.; ἱέμενος Τροίηνδε Od.; so, δρόμωι ἵεσθαι ἐπί τινα Hdt.; etc.
metaph. to be set upon doing a thing, to desire to do it, c. inf., ἵετο γὰρ βαλέειν Il.:—c. gen. to long for, ἱέμενοι νίκης Id.:—absol. in part., ἱέμενός περ eager though he was, Od.

the 3rd pl. aor2 mid. ἕντο is used by Hom. in the phrase ἐπεὶ πόσιος καὶ ἐδητύος ἐξ ἔρον ἕντο, when they had put away the desire of meat and drink, i. e. eaten and drunk enough, Virgil's postquam exempta fames epulis.
epith. of Apollo, from the cry ἰὴ παιάν, Hhymn.
a hymn sung to him, Id.
fut. ίσω, to cry ἰὴ παιών! Ar.
Lat. io! exclam. of joy, ἰή, ἰή, ἰή, Ar.; ἰὴ παιών Id.
of grief, Aesch.
Jesus, Greek form of Hebrew Joshua or Jehoshua, Saviour, NTest.

born in lawful wedlock, legitimate, ἀλλά με ἶσον ἰθαιγενέεσσιν ἐτίμα honoured me like his true-born sons, Od.:—so, of a nation, from the ancient stock, genuine, ἰθ. Αἰγύπτιοι Hdt.; of some mouths of the Nile, natural, original, opp. to ὀρυκτά, Id.
to Ithaca, Od.
Ithaca, the home of Ulysses, an island on the West coast of Greece, Hom.:—hence he is called Ἰθᾰκήσιος.
Ithacan, Hom.
a step, motion, Il.
giving right judgment, Hes.
straight-running, Anth.
straight-haired, opp. to οὐλόθριξ (wooly-haired), Hdt.
a fair, stand-up fight, Hdt.
fighting fairly, Simon.

entry.etym: adverb Sup. of ἰθύ: v. ἰθύς I. 2.

entry.sense: a guide, pilot, Anth.
ionic for εὐθύνω, to make straight, straighten, ἐπὶ στάθμην ἴθυνεν by the rule, Od.:—Pass. to run evenly, of horses yoked abreast, Il.

to guide in a straight line, ἵππους ἰθύνομεν (epic for -ωμεν) let us drive them straight, Id.; νῆα ἰθύνει [the pilot] keeps it straight, Id.; βέλος ἴθυνεν she sped it straight, Id.:—Mid. to guide or steer for oneself, ἰθύνετο ὀϊστόν aimed his arrow straight, Od.; πηδαλίωι ἰθύνετο (sc. νῆα) Id.; c. gen., ἀλλήλων ἰθυνομένων δοῦρα as they drove their spears straight at each other, Il.:—Pass., of a boat, to be guided, steered, Hdt.

to guide, direct, rule, Il., Aesch.: of a judge, μύθους ἰθύνειν to rectify unjust judgments, Hes.; ἰθ. τὸ πλέον τινί to adjudge the greater part to him, Theocr.:—Pass., ἰθύνεσθαι θανάτωι to be punished with death, Hdt.
going straight on, Anth.
straight-flying, of a javelin, Il.

of motion, straight, direct, Lat. rectus, used by Hom. in this sense only in adv. ἰθύς (infr. II); ἰθείῃ τέχνῃ straightway, forthwith, Hdt.; ἰθεῖαν (sc. ὁδόν) straight on, Lat. recta (sc. via), Id.; ἐκ τῆς ἰθείης (sc. ὁδοῦ) outright, openly, Id.; κατ’ ἰθὺ εἶναι to be right over against, opposite, Id.

in moral sense, straight, straight-forward, just, ἰθεῖα γὰρ ἔσται [ἡ δίκη] Il.; ἰθείῃσι δίκαις Hes.: so in Sup. adv., δίκην ἰθύντατα εἰπεῖν to give judgment most fairly, Il.; so, πρήξιες ἰθύτεραι [ῠ] Theogn.; ἰθύς τε καὶ δίκαιος Hdt.

ἰθύς, or less commonly ἰθύ, as adv., straight at, right at, c. gen. objecti, ἰθὺς Δαναῶν Il.; ἰθὺς κίεν οἴκου went straight towards the home, Id.; ἰθὺ τοῦ Ἴστρου Hdt.;—also, ἰθὺς πρὸς τεῖχος Il.; ἰθὺς ἐπὶ Θεσσαλίης Hdt.

absol., ἰθὺς φρονέων resolving to go straight on, Il.; ἰθὺς μαχέσασθαι to fight hand to hand, Id.; τέτραπτο πρὸς ἰθύ οἱ, i. e. προσετέτραπτό οἱ ἰθύ, he fronted him face to face, Id.:—of Time, straightway, Hdt.
ἰθέως, regul. adv., Hdt.
a straight course, ἀν’ ἰθύν straight upwards, on high, Hom.
a direct attempt, purpose, πᾶσαν ἐπ’ ἰθύν Id.; γυναικῶν γνώομεν ἰθύν Od.
stretched out, straight, Anth.: upright, perpendicular, Id.
the phallos carried in the festivals of Bacchus: metaph. a lewd fellow, Dem.

to go straight, press right on, Il.; ἴθυσε μάχη πεδίοιο the tide of war set straight over the plain, Id.:—c. gen. objecti, ἴθυσε νεός made straight for the ship, Id.; ἴθυσαν δ’ ἐπὶ τεῖχος Id.; ἴθυσαν πρός . . Hdt.
c. inf. to strive or struggle to do, Od.; ὅκη ἰθύσειε στρατεύεσθαι whichever way he purposed to march, Hdt.
becoming, befitting, sufficing:

of persons, sufficient, competent, c. inf., Hdt.; ἱκ. τεκμηριῶσαι sufficient to prove a point, Thuc.; ἱκ. ζημιοῦν with sufficient power to punish, Xen.; c. acc. rei, ἀνὴρ γνώμην ἱκανός a man of sufficient prudence, Hdt.; ἱκ. τὴν ἰατρικήν sufficiently versed in medicine, Xen.:—c. dat. pers. a match for, equivalent to, εἷς πολλοῖς ἱκανός Plat.:—absol., ἱκανὸς Ἀπόλλων Soph.; ἱκ. ἂν γένοιο σύ Eur.; ἱκανοὶ ὡς πρὸς ἰδιώτας very tolerable in comparison with common men, Plat.

of things, sufficient, adequate, enough, Eur.; ἱκανὰ τοῖς πολεμίοις εὐτύχηται they have had successes enough, Thuc.:—of size, large enough, οὐχ ἱκανῆς οὔσης τῆς Ἀττικῆς Id.; ἱκανά σοι μέλαθρα ἐγκαθυβρίζειν large enough to riot in, Eur.:—of Time, considerable, long, Ar.
sufficient, satisfactory, ἱκανὴ μαρτυρία Plat.:— τὸ ἱκανὸν λαμβάνειν to take security, NTest.
adv. -νῶς, sufficiently, adequately, enough, Thuc., etc.
ἱκ. ἔχειν to be sufficient, to be far enough advanced, Id., Xen., etc.: —Sup. ἱκανώτατα Plat.
sufficiency, fitness, Plat.
a sufficiency, sufficient supply, Id.
to make sufficient, qualify, NTest.

entry.etym: tense other than present and imperfect are supplied by ἱκνέομαι
entry.sense: to come, arrive, Hom., Aesch.: c. acc. to come to, reach, ἱκάνω νῆας Ἀχαιῶν Il., etc.; of a tall tree, δι’ ἠέρος αἰθέρ’ ἵκανεν Id.; ἥβης μέτρον ἱκ. reached, attained to the age of youth, Od.

with a person for the object, often of grief, hardship, and the like, ἄχος κραδίην καὶ θυμὸν ἱκάνει Il.; so, ἄλγος, γῆρας, κάματος, χόλος ἱκάνει τινά Hom.; παλαίφατα θέσφατ’ ἱκάνει με they are fulfilled upon me, Od.
of a suppliant, σὰ γούνατ’ ἱκάνω Il.; cf. ἱκνέομαι ΙΙΙ.
also in Mid., χρειὼ γὰρ ἱκάνεται Id.; τὰ σὰ γούναθ’ ἱκάνομαι Hom.
Icarian, πόντος Ἰκ. the Aegean between the Cyclades and Caria, where Icarus son of Daedalus was drowned, Il.; Ἰκ. πέλαγος Hdt.

entry.etym: poet. and ionic form of εἴκελος,
entry.sense: like, resembling, τινι Il., Hdt., Pind.
to make like, Anth.
the prayer of a suppliant, Eur.; ἱκεσίαισι σαῖς at thy entreaties, Id.
= ἱκετήσιος, Trag.
of or consisting of suppliants, Aesch.
suppliant, of prayers, Soph., Eur.; of persons, Soph., Eur.
supplication, Thuc.; ἱκετείαν ποιεῖσθαί τινος to supplicate him, Id.
a mode of supplication, Thuc.
to be besought or entreated, Luc.
to approach as a suppliant, ἐπεί σε ἱκέτευσα Od.; ἐς Πηλῆ’ ἱκέτευσε Il.; ἱκ. τινὰ γονάτων or πρὸς γονάτων Eur.
to supplicate, beseech one to do a thing, c. acc. et inf., Od., Hdt., attic:—also c. gen. pers. et inf. to beg of one that . . , Eur.
c. acc. rei, to ask a thing as a suppliant, Id., Thuc.
of or fit for suppliants, ἱκτ. θησαυρός, of hair offered to a god, Soph.; ἱκτήριοι = ἱκέται, Id.

ἱκετηρία, ionic -ίη, (sub. ῥάβδος), an olive-branch which the suppliant held as a symbol of his condition, Hdt., Ar., etc.; so, κλάδοι ἱκτήριοι Soph.:—metaph., ἱκετηρίαν δὲ γόνασιν ἐξάπτω σέθεν τὸ σῶμα τοὐμόν I attach my body to thy knees as a suppliant olive-branch, Eur.; so, νομίζετε τὸν παῖδα ἱκτηρίαν προκεῖσθαι Dem.
epith. of Zeus, as tutelary god of suppliants, Od.

one who comes to seek protection, a suppliant or fugitive, who lays his ἱκετηρία on the altar or hearth, after which his person was inviolable; esp. one who seeks purification after homicide, Hom., etc.

entry.etym: fem. of ἱκέτης, Hdt., Soph., etc.

entry.sense: moisture, juice, Il., Hdt.:—comic metaph., τὴν ἰκμάδα τῆς φροντίδος Ar.; i). *b|akxouἰ. Βάκχου, i. e. wine, Anth.; ἰ. δρυός, i. e. gum, Id.
only in the phrase ἴκμενος οὖρος (from ἴκω, ἱκνέομαι) a following, favourable wind, Hom.
to come to a place, c. acc. loci, or foll. by a prep., ἵκετο νῆας or ἐπὶ νῆας Hom., etc.

to come to, ἵκετο χρόα, of a spear, Il.; τέλος ἵκεο μύθων Id.; ἠῶ ἱκέσθαι, i. e. to live till morning, Od.; λέκτροιο θεσμὸν ἱκ., i. e. to wed, Id.; ὅ τι χεῖρας ἵκοιτο, whatever came to hand, Id.; ἱκ. ἐς λόγους τινός to speak with one, Soph., etc.
of suffering, sorrow, etc., to come upon, πένθος ἱκ. τινά Il.; ἄχος, χόλος τινὰ ἱκ. θυμόν or κραδίην Hom.

to approach as suppliant, Id.; τὰ σὰ γοῦνα ἱκόμεθ’ Od.:—hence, like ἱκετεύω, to supplicate, beseech, τὰς θεὰς ἱκνοῦμαι Soph.; καί σε πρὸς θεῶν ἱκνοῦμαι Id.:—c. inf., πάντες σ’ ἱκνοῦνται θάψαι νεκρούς Eur.

impers. like προσήκει, it becomes, befits, φαμὲν ἡμέας ἱκνέεσθαι ἡγεμονεύειν we say that it befits us to take the lead, Hdt.; τοὺς μάλιστα ἱκνέεται (sc. κεκάρθαι) whom it most concerns, Id.; so, ἐς τὸν ἱκνέεται he to whom it belongs, Id.

in part., τὸ ἱκνεύμενον that which is fitting, proper, Id.; ὁ ἱκν. χρόνος the fit, proper time, Id.; τὸ ἱκν. ἀνάλωμα the proportionate expense, Thuc.:—hence adv. ἱκνευμένως, fittingly, aright, Hdt.part.
the half-decks fore and aft of Homeric ships, Hom.: the planks of the deck, Od.
generally, a platform, stage, Hdt.
following closely, Hes.
of Place, close to, hard by, Aesch., Plat.; c. gen., Aesch.
a suppliant, Soph., Eur.
as adj. = ἱκετήριος, Aesch.
a kite, Hdt., Ar., Plat.
the yellow-breasted marten, the marten-cat, (cf. γαλέη), Lat. mustela, Ar.
as adj. suppliant, Eur.
to come to, reach, c. acc. or with a prep., ἵκειν ἐς πατρίδα, ἵκειν κατὰ νῆας or ἵκειν δόμον, Τροίην, κλισίην Hom.
of sufferings, feelings, etc., ὅτε κέν τινα χόλος ἵκοι whenever anger come upon him, Il.; χρειὼ ἵκει με necessity is upon me, Od.
in troops, Lat. turmatim, Il., Hdt.: generally, in abundance, in a mass, Hes.
neut. ἵλεα:—of gods, propitious, gracious, Il., Hes., etc.
of men, gracious, kindly, gentle, θυμὸς ἐνὶ φρεσὶν ἵλαος ἔστω Il.; so in Soph.
cheerful, gay, merry, joyous, Lat. hilaris, Ar., Xen.:— τὸ ἱλαρόν = ἱλαρότης, Plut. adv. -ρῶς, Xen.
cheerfulness, Lat. hilaritas, Plut.
to appease, θεὸν ἱλάσκεσθαι to make him propitious to one, conciliate him, win his favour, Hom.; μολπῆι θεὸν ἱλάσκοντο Il.; ὄφρ’ ἡμῖν Ἑκάεργον ἱλάσσεαι Id.; so of men, Hdt., Plat.
in NTest. to expiate, τὰς ἁμαρτίας.
in NTest. also, an aor1 imperat. pass. ἱλάσθητι, be gracious.
a means of appeasing, Plut.:— a propitiation, NTest.
propitiatory,
(sub. ἐπίθεμα) as Subst., ἱλαστήριον, the mercy-seat, covering of the ark in the Holy of Holies, NTest.
(sub. ἀνάθημα) , a propitiation, Id.
to be gracious, εἴ κεν Ἀπόλλων ἡμῖν ἱλήκῃσι (epic 3rd sg. subj.) Od.
in prayers, be gracious! Od.; doric ἵλαθι Theocr.
a crowd, band, troop of men, Hdt., Soph.: εὔφρονες ἶλαι merry companies, Pind.; also, ἴλη λεόντων Eur.
a troop of horse, Lat. turma, ala, κατ’ ἴλας = ἰλαδόν, Xen.
descendants of Ilos, i. e. Trojans, Eur.
Ilian, Trojan, Anth.
fem. of Ἰλιακός, Hdt., Trag.
as Subst.: Troy, the Troad, Hdt.
(sub. γυνή), a Trojan woman, Eur.
(sub. ποίησις) , the Iliad, Arist.; proverb., Ἰλιὰς κακῶν, i. e. an endless string of woes, Dem.
to be or become dizzy, lose one's head, caused by looking down from a height or by drunkenness, Plat.; by fear, Ar., etc.
a spinning round: esp. a swimming in the head, Lat. vertigo, Plat.
from Troy, Hom.
Ἰλ. πρό before Troy, Od., etc.
destroyer of Troy, Anth.
Ilian, Trojan, Eur.
Ilios or Ilium, the city of Ilus, Troy, Hom., Eur.:— Ἴλιον, ου, τό, Il., Trag.; Ἰλιόφι, τείχεα the walls of Troy, Il.
a rope, band, Il.
muddy, impure, Anth.
mud, slime, dirt, Il., Hdt.
of leathern thongs, Hdt.
a leathern noose, of a polypus' leg, Anth.
the thong of a whip, a whip, Hom.
a leathern strap or thong, Il.: in pl. the traces by which horses were attached to the chariot, Id.: also, the reins, Id., Soph., Eur.
the straps on which the body of the chariot was hung, Il.
the lash of a whip, Id.
the caestus of boxers, consisting of straps put round the hand, Id.
in sg. the magic girdle of Aphrodite, Lat. cestus, Id.
the chin-strap of the helmet, Id.
in Od. a latchet or thong, by which the bolt was shot home into the socket, and which was then fastened to the κορώνη, Od.
after Hom. the thong or latchet of a sandal, Xen.
a dog-leash, Id.: proverb., ἱμὰς κύνειός ἐστι he's as tough as a dog- leash, Ar.
to flog horses, Hom.; generally, to scourge, smite, Il.
a clothes-seller, Luc.

entry.etym: in form a Dim. of ἷμα, i.e. εἷμα
entry.sense: an outer garment, a cloak or mantle worn above the χιτών, the same as Homer's χλαῖνα, Hdt., Ar.:—used of the Roman toga, ἐν ἱματίοις, Lat. togati, Plut.
ἱμάτια, τά, generally, clothes, Hdt., Dem.
generally, a cloth, Hdt.
to take care of clothes, Luc.
clothing, apparel, Theophr.
to long for, yearn after, desire a thing, c. gen., Od., Aesch., etc.:—c. inf. to long or wish to do, Solon, Aesch., etc.
as Dep. to desire, c. gen., ὁππότ’ ἂν ἧς ἱμείρεται αἴης (epic for -ηται) Od.; χρημάτων ἱμ. μεγάλως Hdt.
exciting love or desire, lovely, delightsome, charming, Hom., Theocr.:—Sup. ἱμεροέστατος Theogn.
sweetly blooming, Anth.

a longing or yearning after a thing, Lat. desiderium, c. gen., Il.; γόου ἵμερον ὦρσεν raised [in them] a yearning after tears, i. e. a desire to weep, Id.; and with a second gen., πατρὸς ὑφ’ ἵμερον ὦρσε γόοιο for his father, Od.; ἵμερον ἔχειν = ἱμείρεσθαι, Hdt.:—in pl., πολλοὶ ἵμεροι various emotions, Aesch.
absol. desire, love, Il., etc.
as adj., but only in neut. as adv., ἵμερον αὐλεῖν Anth.; ἵμερα μελίζεσθαι, δακρύειν Id.
of lovely voice or song, Theocr.
longed for, lovely, Il., Hes.
the rope of a draw-well, Ar.
a water-drawer, Ar.
Adverb,
of Place,
demonstr. in that place, there, only in Il. 10. 127.

relat., = ὅπου, in which place, where, Hdt., etc.;—so, ἵνα τε Il.; ἵνα περ Hom.:—c. gen., ἵνα γῆς in whatever part of the land, Hdt.; ἔμαθε ἵνα ἦν κακοῦ in what a calamity, Id.; οὐχ ὁρᾷς ἵν’ εἶ κακοῦ Soph.
= ὅποι, with Verbs of motion, whither, Od.; ὁρᾷς ἵν’ ἥκεις Soph.
of circumstance, when, at which, Od.
Final Conjunction, = ὅπως, that, in order that, Lat. ut, Hom.:
with subj.,
after principal tenses of ind., Id., etc.
after historical tenses, in similes, where the aor. refers to any possible time, Od.
after opt. and ἄν, ἔδωκε μένος, ἵνα γένοιτο she gave him vigour, that he might become, Il.
with opt., after historical tenses, Hom., etc.
with past tenses of ind., to express a consequence which has not followed or cannot follow, ἵν’ ἦν τυφλός in which case he must be blind, Soph., etc.
ἵνα μή as the negat. of ἵνα, that not, Lat. ut ne or ne, Il., attic
elliptical usages,
where the purpose only is stated, Ζεὺς ἔσθ’, ἵν’ εἰδῇς 'tis Zeus, [I tell thee this] that thou may'st know it, Soph.; so, ἵνα συντέμω Dem.
ὅρα or βλέπε being understood, ἵνα ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ see that thou come and lay hands on her, NTest.
ἵνα τί (sc. γένηται); to what end? Ar., Plat.

entry.etym: Dep., hardly used, save in pres. and imperf.
entry.sense: to appear like, look like, ἀθανάτοις ἰνδάλλεται εἰσοράασθαι he is like the immortals to look upon, Od.; ἰνδάλλετο δέ σφισι μεγαθύμῳ Πηλείωνι he seemed to them like the son of P., Il.
to appear, seem, Id.; ὥς μοι ἰνδάλλεται ἦτορ as my heart seems to me [to say], i. e. as the matter seems to me, Od.; ἰνδάλλεται ὁμοιότατος κλητῆρος he seems most like a summoner, Ar.
an appearance, Lat. species, Anth., Luc.
Indian, Hdt., etc.
Indian-killer, Anth.
an Indian, Hdt., etc.
the river Indus, Id.
as adj. = Ἰνδικός, Anth.
the muscle at the back of the neck, the nape of the neck, Il.
a son, Aesch., Eur.:— ἶνις, ἡ, a daughter, Eur.
fibrous, of parts of animals, Xen.
Ino, daughter of Cadmus, worshipped as a sea-goddess by the name of Leucothea, Od., Hes.
of the ibex bounding, springing, Il.
a fowler, bird-catcher, Bion., Anth.
as adj. catching with birdlime, Id.
Ixion, a king of Thessaly: his name prob. was = ἱκέτης, for he was the first homicide, and therefore the first suppliant, Pind., Aesch.
to catch with limed twigs: to catch, Anth.
one who uses birdlime, Anth.
mistletoe, Lat. viscum, Arist.
birdlime prepared from the mistletoe berry, Eur.
metaph., ἐκφυγὼν τὸν ἰξὸν τὸν ἐν πράγματι Luc.
limed, Anth.
the waist, Od.
Bacchus invoked with the cry of ἰώ, Anth.
violet-eyed, Luc.
to shoot arrows, dart, Anth.
shooting arrows, Anth.
shedding venom, poisonous, Id.
dark-haired, Pind.
violet-dark, purple, Od.
holding arrows, Hom.: —as Subst. a quiver, Anth.
like the violet, purple, of the sea, Hom.
violet-coloured, dark, Il.
mixed with poison, Anth.
warlike or ill-fated, miserable; Hom.
shaggy, epith. of the wild goat, Od.
of or called after Io, Ἰόνιος κόλπος or πόρος, the sea between Epirus and Italy, across which Io swam, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
the violet, Theocr.:—once in Hom., λειμῶνες ἴου ἠδὲ σελίνου θήλεον the meadows were blooming with ἴον and parsley;—but whether it is here violet or some other dark blue flower is doubtful.
weaving violets, Anth.
an arrow, Il., Trag.
rust, Theogn., Plat.
poison, as of serpents, Trag.
violet-crowned, Hhymn., Solon., etc.
will, desire, θεῶν ἰότητι by the will or hest of the gods, Hom.
= ἕκατι II, for the sake of, ἰότᾱτι γάμων Aesch.
to side with or imitate the Jews, NTest.
a Jew: Ἰουδαία, a Jewess; ἡἸουδαία (sub. γῆ), Judaea.
the young hair at the side of the face, the whiskers, Od., Aesch.
Interj.
a cry of woe, Lat. heu! Trag.
like ἰώ, a cry of surprise, ho! Aesch., Ar., etc.
arrow-pourer, shooter of arrows, of Artemis, Hom.
entry.etym: Prob. from χέω, not from χαίρω.

entry.sense: -ῑ́, iota demonstrativum, in familiar attic (not in Trag.), is attached to demonstr. Pronouns, to strengthen their force, as οὑτοσί αὑτηΐ τουτί, Lat. hicce; ἐκεινοσί ὁδί ταδί τοσουτονί τοσονδί τυννουτοσί, etc.; also to demonstr. Advs., as οὑτωσί ὡδί ἐνθαδί δευρί νυνί.
baked in the oven, Anth.
one who works at an oven, Luc.
an oven or furnace, Hdt., Ar.
the place of the oven, i. e. the kitchen, Ar.
a lantern, Id.
Pass. to be weighed down, Aesch., Ar.
in a mouse-trap, the piece of wood that falls and catches the mouse: generally any weight, Pind.
three officers at Lacedaemon, who chose 300 ἔφηβοι, to serve as a bodyguard for the kings, Xen.
carrying horses, of ships used as cavalry transports, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
to drive horses, drive a chariot, Il.: later, to ride, Hdt., Ar.
Pass., of the horse, to be ridden or driven, Plat.: to be broken in for riding, Xen.
ἱππάζεσθαι χώραν to ride over a country, Plut.
a horse-cock, gryphon, a fabulous animal, Aesch.

entry.etym: poet. lengthd. form for ἱππεύς, Theocr.

entry.sense: a cry of the Ἱππεῖς, a parody of the boatmen's cry (ῥυππαπαί), Ar.
Dim. of ἵππος, a pony, Xen.
a commander of cavalry, Xen.
to command the cavalry, c. gen., Hdt., Dem.
the office of ἵππαρχος, Xen.
of or for a ἵππαρχος· ἱππαρχικόν ἐστι it is part of his duty, Xen.
a general of cavalry, Hdt.: at Athens there were two, with 10 φύλαρχοι under them, Ar.
riding, horse-exercise, Ar., Xen.
chariot-driving, Luc.
fit for horses, fit for riding, Hdt., Xen.:—metaph., κόλαξιν ἱππάσιμος ridden by flatterers, Plut.
ἱππὰς στολή, a riding-dress, Hdt.
= ἱππευτής, Luc.
as adj. fit for riding, of a horse, Xen.
fond of riding, Plut.
the starting-post in a race, Anth.
a riding or driving of horses, horsemanship, Soph., Eur.
cavalry, Xen.
of a horse or horses, Hom., Soph.; ἵππ. λόφος a horse-hair crest, Il.
horse-love, horse-fever, Ar.
a ride on horseback or journey in a chariot, Eur.
a horseman, either of the charioteer or of the hero who fights from a chariot, Il.
a horseman, i. e. rider, first in Hdt.
in Solon.'s constitution, the ἱππεῖς, attic ἱππῆς, Horsemen or Knights, were the 2d class, required to possess land producing 300 medimni, and a horse, Ar., Thuc.,
at Sparta 300 chosen men, the King's Body Guard, Hdt.
a rider, horseman, Eur.
to be a horseman or rider, to ride, Hdt., attic:—so in Mid., Hdt.
metaph. of the wind, Eur.
to be a trooper, serve in the cavalry, Xen.
of a horse, as we say "the horse rides (i. e. carries his rider) well," Id.
adv. like a horse, Aesch.
as on horseback, like a horseman, Ar.
ἱππ. ὁδός a chariot-road, Il.
to ride or drive, Ar.
a driver of horses, one who fights from a chariot, a Knight, Hom.
fit for horsemanship or driving, of countries, Od.
the mare-milkers, a Scythian or Tartar tribe, Il.
king of horsemen, Aesch.
of a horse or horses, Hdt., attic
of horsemen or chariots, ἱππικὸς ἀγών, δρόμος Hdt., Soph.
skilled in riding, equestrian, Plat.; ἡ ἱππική Ar.
τὸ ἱππικόν, the horse, cavalry, Hdt., Xen.
a course of four stadia, Plut.
adv. -κῶς, like a horseman: Sup. -κώτατα, with best horsemanship, Xen.
of a horse or horses, Eur.; epith. of the Queen of the Amazons, Id.; of Poseidon as creator of the horse, Aesch., etc.
shaggy with horse-hair, Il.
one who fights from a chariot, Hom.: later, a horseman, rider, Aesch.
as adj., ἵππ. κλόνοι the tumult of the horse-fight, Id.
going on horseback, equestrian, Aesch., Soph.
metaph., ῥήματα ἱππ. great high-paced words, bombast, Ar.
a horseman, Aesch.
feeder of horses, Eur.
the ἱπποβόται at Chalcis in Euboea were a class, like the ἱππεῖς at Athens, Lat. Equites, the Knights, Hdt.
grazed by horses, Hom., Eur.
a horse-herd, horse-keeper, Eur.
crane-cavalry, Luc.
vulture-cavalry, Luc.
tamer of horses, Hom.

entry.etym: as fem. without any masc. in use,
entry.sense: bushy with horse-hair, of helmets, Hom.
horse-bands, reins, Eur.
binding horses, Soph.
a driver or rider of steeds, Theocr.
a horse-race or chariot-race, Ar., Thuc.
a light horseman, Hdt.
a chariot-road, Il.
a race-course for chariots, Lat. curriculum, Plat., etc.
forth from the horse, Od.
a horse-beetle, Ar.
travelling by means of horses, a driver of horses, Il.
a horse-centaur, half-horse half-man, Xen.
to groom horses, ἱπποκομεῖν κάνθαρον to groom one's beetle, Ar.
decked with horse-hair, of a helmet, Il., Soph.
a groom or esquire, who attended the ἱππεύς in war, Lat. equiso, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
equipt or furnished with horses, Il.
to be superior in horse, Dem.:— Pass. to be inferior in horse, Thuc.
victory in a cavalry action, Xen.
tremendously steep, ἱππόκρημνον ῥῆμα a neck-breaking word, Ar.
sounding with horses, Eur.
with horse-hair crest, Ar., Anth.
of a meadow, in which horses take mad delight, or, swarming with horses, Soph.
as Subst., ἱππομανές, έος, an Arcadian plant, which makes horses mad, Theocr.
mad love for horses, Luc.
to fight on horseback, Thuc., Xen.
a horse-fight, an action of cavalry, Thuc., etc.
fighting on horseback, a trooper, Simon., Luc.
a horse-ant: pl. ant-cavalry, Luc.
guiding or keeping horses, Soph., Eur.
busied with horses, Il.

a horse, mare, Lat. equus, equa, Hom., etc.:—the pl. ἵπποι in Hom. are the chariot-horses, Il.:—hence ἵπποι is used for the chariot itself, καθ’ ἵππων ἅλλεσθαι, ἐξ ἵππων βῆσαι, ἵππων ἐπεβήσετο Id.:—the art of riding, though known to Hom., was an uncommon practice, cf. κέλης, κελητίζω,
as Collective Noun, ἵππος, ἡ, horse, cavalry, Lat. equitatus, Hdt., attic; always in sg., as ἵππος χιλίη a thousand horse, Hdt.
ὁ ἵππος ὁ ποτάμιος the hippopotamus, Id.
in Compos., it expressed anything large or coarse, as in our horsechestnut, horselaugh, v. ἱππόκρημνος, etc.
a stable:—metaph., Ἀελίου κνεφαία ἱππόστασις the dark stable of the Sun, i. e. the west, Eur.
the art of chariot-driving, horsemanship, Hom.
= ἵππος II, horse, cavalry, Orac. ap. Hdt.
a driver or rider of horses, a horseman, knight, Lat. eques, Hom., Hdt., etc.
as adj., ἱππότης λεώς the horse, the horsemen, Aesch., Soph.
a mounted bowman, horse-archer, Hdt., Thuc.
a breeding or keeping of horses, esp. for racing, Simon., Thuc.
horse-feeding, abounding in horses, Hes.
of persons, breeding and keeping race-horses, Dem., Plut.
horse-pride, i. e. excessive pride, Luc.
fem. adj. horse-tailed, decked with a horse-tail, of helmets, Hom.
a lot of horses out at grass, a troop of horses, Hdt., Xen.
a stable, Eur.
a horse-keeper, Plat.
horse-like, Xen.
a buying of horses, Xen.
to buy horses, Xen.
a place for horses:
a stable, Xen.
a posting-house, station, Id.
fut. ἴψομαι: epic 2nd sg. aor1 ἴψαο: Dep.:— to press hard, oppress, Il., Theocr.
Iris, the messenger of the gods, Il.
as Appellat. ἰρις, ἡ: — the rainbow, iris, in Hom., as in the Bible, a sign to men, τέρας μερόπων ἀνθρώπων Il.
any bright-coloured circle as that round the eyes of a peacock's tail, Luc.
the plant Iris, Theophr.
like an angel, NTest.
like a brother, Eur.
to make equal, to balance, of a person holding scales, Il.; ἰς. τὰς κτήσεις to equalise them, Arist.: —Mid. to make oneself equal to another, Il.
equal in the race: neut. pl. as adv., Anth.
worth its weight in silver, Aesch.
equal freedom of speech, equality, Hdt., Xen.
of the same age with, τινι Xen.
Isthmian, Thuc.
anything on the neck, a necklace, Od.
Ἴσθμια (sc. ἱερά), τά, the Isthmian games, holden on the Isthmus of Corinth, Ar., etc.
Isthmian, Soph.
from the Isthmus, Anth.
on the Isthmus, Anth.
on the Isthmus, ap. Plut.
any narrow passage: esp. a neck of land between two seas, an isthmus, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
ὁ Ἰσθμός was the Isthmus of Corith, Hdt.
like an isthmus, Thuc.
of or for Isis:—fem. Ἰσιάς, άδος, ἡ, Anth.
Isis, an Egypt. goddess, answering to the Greek Demeter, Hdt.
he said, he spake, Od.
to make like, τί τινι Od.; ἴσκε ψεύδεα πολλὰ λέγων ἐτύμοισιν ὁμοῖα speaking many lies he made them like truths, i. e. seemed to speak truth, Id.
to think like, τινά τινι Il.: absol., ἴσκεν ἕκαστος ἀνήρ every one fancied, i. e. took false for real, Od.
to deem, suppose, Anth.
equal to a king, Plut.
like land, Luc.
equality of kind, Plat.
godlike, Aesch.
living on an equality, Thuc.
running equally, of equal length, Anth.
evenly balanced: equal, Anth.
equal to the gods, godlike, Hom., attic
to make equal to the gods, Aesop.
equal to the danger or risk, a match for, Thuc.
equal in property, Plut.
of equal power, possessing equal rights with others, Hdt.
like one's mother, Theocr.
equal in battle, Xen.
equal in size, Xen.
with equal front, Xen.
equal in length, Plat.
to have an equal share, Thuc., Xen.
an equal share, partnership, τινός in a thing, Thuc.
sharing equally or alike, c. gen., Xen.
coextensive, Aesch.; γῆς ἰσόμοιρ’ ἀήρ earth's equal partner air, Soph.
used by Poseidon of himself as ἰσόμορος with Zeus, Il.
dream-like, empty, Aesch.
dying equally or alike, Eur.
Pass. to have equal rights, Thuc.
equality of rights, the equality of a Greek democracy, Hdt., Thuc.
of states, having equal rights, Scol_gr.
like a child, as of a child, Aesch.
a span long, Anth.
equal in the struggle, well-matched, Hdt.
generally, equivalent, Thuc.
level ground, a flat, Il., Xen.
of even surface, level or even with, c. dat., Hdt.
equal in breadth, τινι to a thing, Thuc.
another Plato, Anth.
equal in number or quantity, τινι to a person or thing, Thuc.
like an old man, Aesch.
equipoise, equilibrium, Plat.
equally balanced, in equipoise, of the balance, Plat.; metaph. of fortune, Aesch.; of a conflict, Eur.:—c. dat. equally matched with, Hdt.; so, c. gen., in equipoise with, Thuc.
with equal legs, isosceles, Plat.
of numbers, that can be divided into two equal parts, even (as 6 = 3 + 3), Id.

equal to, the same as, c. dat., or absol. equal, like, Hom., etc.:— ἴσα πρὸς ἴσα "measure for measure, " Hdt.; of the mixture of wine with water, ἴσος οἶνος ἴσῳ ὕδατι κεκραμένος Comici; metaph., μηδὲν ἴσον ἴσῳ φέρων not mixing half and half, i. e. not giving tit for tat, Ar.
equally divided, equal, Hom., Soph.:— τὰ ἴσα an equal share, fair measure, Hdt., Soph.:— ἴσαι (sc. ψῆφοι) votes equally divided, Ar.

at Athens, of the equal division of all civic rights, Thuc., etc.:— τὰ ἴσα equal rights, equality, Dem.:—also, ἡ ἴση καὶ ὁμοία (sc. δίκη) Thuc., etc.; ἐπ’ ἴσῃ τε καὶ ὁμοίῃ on fair and equal terms, Hdt.
of persons, fair, impartial, Soph., Plat., etc.
of ground, even, level, flat, Lat. aequus, εἰς τὸ ἴσον καταβαίνειν, of an army, Xen.
adv., ἴσως, v. sub voc.:—but there are other adverbial forms,
neut. sg., ἶσον Κηρί even as Death, Il.; ἶσον ἐμοί like me, Id., etc.; ἴσον τῷ πρίν equally as before, Eur.; followed by καί, ἴσα καί . . like as, as if, Lat. aeque ac, Soph., etc.:—absol. alike, Id.
with Preps.: —ἀπὸ τῆς ἴσης equally, Lat. ex aequo, Thuc.; ἀπ’ ἴσης Dem.:— ἐν ἴσῳ equally, Thuc., etc.;— ἐξ ἴσου Hdt., attic:— ἐπὶ ἴσης, later ἐπίσης, Hdt., attic
attic comp. ἰσαίτερος Eur., etc.
in equipoise with, equivalent to, τινι Plut., Luc.
the condition of an ἰσοτελής, equality in tax and tribute, Xen.
fulfilled alike, ὁ ἐπίκουρος ἰς., the ally that comes to all alike, of Death, Soph.
paying alike, bearing equal burdens: at Athens, the ἰσοτελεῖς were a class of μέτοικοι, who needed no patron (προστάτης) and paid no alien-tax (μετοίκιον), Lys., etc.
equality, Eur., etc.
equality of privilege, Luc.
held in equal honour, having the same privileges, Plut., etc.
to match oneself with, be a match for, cope with, c. dat., Il.
bearing or drawing equal weights, equal in strength, Od.
level with the brim, Xen.
equally woolly with, τινι Anth.
equal right to vote, Plut.
with or by an equal number of votes, Aesch.
having an equal vote with others, equal in authority, Eur., Thuc.
of equal spirit, κράτος ἰς. Aesch.
of like soul or mind, NTest.
to make equal, Soph., Ar., etc.:—Mid., ὄνυχας χεῖράς τε ἰσώσαντο, i. e. used them in like manner, Hes.:—Pass. to be made like or equal to, c. dat., Od., Soph.
a muscle, esp. the muscle at the back of the neck, Il.:—in pl. the muscles, Hom.
strength, force, Lat. vis, Hom.:—in periphr. like βίη, ἱερὴ ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο the strong Telemachus, Od., etc.

entry.etym: late form of ἵστημι, NTest., etc.

entry.sense: Causal Tenses, to make to stand, Lat. sisto,
intr. to stand, Lat. sto,
Causal, to make to stand, set, Hom., etc.:— to set men in array, post them, Il., Xen.
to make to stand, stop, stay, check, Hom., etc.; στῆσαι τὴν φάλαγγα to halt it, Xen.; στ. τὰ ὄμματα to fix them, of a dying man, Plat.; ἵ. τὸ πρόσωπον, Lat. componere vultum, Xen.

to set up, ἱστ. ἱστόν to set up the loom, or to raise the mast, Hom.; to raise buildings, statues, trophies, etc., Hdt., attic; ἱστάναι τινὰ χαλκοῦν to set him up in brass, raise a brasen statue to him, Dem.
to raise, rouse, stir up, Hom., etc.; φυλόπιδα στήσειν to stir up strife, Od.; in aor1 mid., στήσασθαι μάχην Id.
to set up, appoint, τινὰ βασιλέα Hdt.; Pass., ὁ σταθεὶς ὕπαρχος Id.
to establish, institute a festival, Id., attic
to place in the balance, weigh, Il., etc.; ἱστάναι τι πρός τι to weigh one thing against another, Hdt.

Pass. and intr. tenses of Act. to be set or placed, to stand, Hom.:—often merely for εἶναι, to be there, Od., etc.; with an adv. to be in a certain state or condition, ἵνα χρείας ἕσταμεν in what a state of need we are, Soph., etc.
to lie, be situated, Thuc.
to stand still, stop, halt, Hom.: to stand idle, Il.: to stop, cease, be at rest, Id.
metaph. to stand firm, Xen.
to stand up, rise up, Il.; of a horse, ἵστασθαι ὀρθός to rear up, Hdt.
to arise, begin, Il.

in marking Time, ἔαρος ἱσταμένοιο as spring was beginning, Od.; ἕβδομος ἑστήκει μείς the seventh month began, Il.; τοῦ μὲν φθίνοντος μηνός, τοῦ δ’ ἱσταμένοιο as one month ends and the next begins, Od.; the month in Hom. being divided into two parts, ἱστάμενος and φθίνων; but in the attic Calendar, it fell into three decads, ἱστάμενος, μεσῶν, φθίνων, Hdt., Thuc.
to be appointed, στῆναι ἐς ἀρχήν Hdt.
any web, a sail, ἱστία στέλλεσθαι, μηρύεσθαι, καθελεῖν to lower or furl sail, Od.; ἄκροισι χρῆσθαι ἱστίοις to keep the sails close-reefed, Ar.
the plough-tree or pole, Hes.
the mast-crutch, on which the mast rested when let down, Il.
a hole in the keel for stepping the mast, Od.
the long beams of the loom, Anth.
working at the loom, Anth.
to inquire into a thing, to learn by inquiry, Hdt., Aesch., etc.; to examine, and in perf. sense, to know, Aesch.
c. acc. pers. to inquire of, ask, Hdt., Eur.:—Pass. to be questioned, Eur.
c. acc. pers. also to inquire about one, Soph., Eur.
c. dupl. acc. to inquire of one about a thing, Eur.
absol. to inquire, Hdt.
to narrate what one has learnt, Arist., Luc.
a learning by inquiry, inquiry, Hdt., Plat.
the knowledge so obtained, information, Hdt.
an account of one's inquiries, a narrative, history, Arist.
of or for inquiry: historical, Plut.
anything set upright:
a ship's mast, ἱστὸν στῆσαι or στήσασθαι to step the mast, Hom.:— a rod, pole, Hdt.

the beam of the loom, which stood upright, instead of lying horizontal as in our looms, Hom.; ἱστὸν στήσασθαι to set up the beam and so begin a web, Hes.; ἱστὸν ἐποίχεσθαι to traverse the loom, because the weaver was obliged to walk to and fro, Hom.
the warp that was fixed to the beam, the web, Id.
stretched in the loom, Ar.
to work at the loom, Soph.
weaving, Plat.
a wise man, one who knows right, a judge, Il.
as adj. knowing, Hes.; ἵστωρ τινός knowing a thing, Soph.
staunching blood, Luc.
thin, Od.
to hold back, check, Hom.
c. gen. to cling to, long after, desire eagerly, Id.
to check, hinder, Il.:—c. gen. to keep back from, Hes.
a dried fig, Ar.
the hip-joint, Hom.
in pl. the fleshy parts round the hip-joint, the haunches, hams, Il., Hdt.
to make dry or withered, to dry up, Hdt., attic:—metaph., θυμὸν ἰσχναίνειν to bring down a proud stomach, Aesch.; τὴν τέχνην ἴσχνανα I refined the art (Tragedy), Ar.
with withered cheeks, Anth.
dry, withered, lean, meagre, Ar.
checked in one's voice, stuttering, stammering, Hdt.
to make oneself strong, to be strong, gain force, Xen.
to contend stoutly, to persist obstinately in doing, c. part., Thuc.: esp. to maintain stiffly, obstinately, Id., Plat.
to put firm trust in a thing, c. dat., Dem.
one must maintain, Plat.
strong, mighty, Hdt., Soph.; τὸ ἰσχυρόν strength, vigour, Thuc.; τὰ ἰσχυρότατα your strongest points, Id.:— hard, χθών Aesch.
obstinate, stiff, stubborn, inveterate, excessive, severe, Hdt., Thuc.
adv. -ρῶς, strongly, with all force, Thuc.:— exceedingly, Hdt., Xen.
strength of body, attic, Hes.; a fortified place, Thuc.
might, power, force, Aesch., etc.; κατ’ ἰσχύν perforce, Id.; πρὸς ἰσχύος χάριν Eur.
a force of soldiers, Xen.
to be strong in body, Soph., Xen., etc.
to be strong, mighty, powerful, prevail, Aesch., etc.; πλέον, μεῖζον ἰσχ. Eur.; ἰσχ. παρά τινι to have power or influence with one, Thuc.

entry.etym: a form of ἔχω only in pres. and impf.
entry.sense: to hold, check, curb, keep back, restrain, Hom.:—c. gen. to keep from, Il., Eur., etc.; also, ἴσχ. τινὰ μὴ πράσσειν Id.

intr., ἴσχε hold, stay, stop, Aesch.; of ships, to lie at anchor, Thuc.:—so in Pass., ἴσχεσθ’ Ἀργεῖοι, μὴ φεύγετε Od.; ἴσχεο Hom.:—c. gen., ἴσχεσθαί τινος to desist from, Od.: ἴσχετο impers., here it stopped, Xen.
to hold fast, hold, maintain, Il., Soph.
like ἔχω, to hold or have in possession, to have, Hdt., attic: to have a wife, Hdt.: to have a child, Id.
intr., with an adv., to be so and so, Thuc.
equally, in like manner, Soph.: Sup. ἰσαίτατα Plat.
equally, fairly, equitably, Dem.
probably, perhaps, Hdt., attic;—in attic often joined with ἄν or τάχ’ ἄν, Soph., etc.
with numerals, about, Ar.
Italy, Hdt., etc.
an Italiote, i. e. a Greek inhabitant of Italy, Thuc.:—fem. Ἰταλιῶτις, ιδος, adj. Italian, Id.
= ταῦρος, whence Italy is said to be derived, cf. Lat. vitulus.
Italian:—as adj., Anth.
headlong, hasty, eager, ready for anything, reckless, Lat. audax, Aesch., Dem.
a willow, Lat. salix, Il., Hdt., etc.
a wicker shield, target, Eur.
of willow, Lat. salignus, Hdt.; made of wicker, Theocr.
one must go, Plat.
passable, Anth.
like a cake, Anth.
a cake of sesame and honey, Ar.

entry.etym: Boeot. for ἴστω, 3rd sg. imperat. of οἶδα
entry.sense: ἴττω Ζεύς Zeus be witness! Ar., Plat.
a circle made of willow (cf. ἰτέα): of the felloe of a wheel, Il.:— the edge or rim of a shield, Hes., Hdt.; the round shield itself, Eur., Xen.
a howling, shrieking, yelling, as of men in pain, Orac. ap. Hdt., Soph.
a shouting, shout of joy, Il.
a cry of pain, shriek, Aesch., Eur.
the wryneck, so called from its cry. The ancient witches used to bind it to a wheel, believing that, as it turned, it drew men's hearts along with it, Xen., Theocr.
metaph. a spell, charm, passionate yearning for, c. gen., Aesch.
to shout, yell, Hom.:—later to yell or cry from grief or pain, Aesch., Soph.
entry.etym: ῑ, epic and Pind.; ῐ in Soph.

entry.sense: one who shouts or yells: also, a singer, whistler, piper, Theocr.
stout, strong, stalwart, Il.:—of women, comely, goodly, Hom.
strong-born:—as prop. n. Iphigeneia, Agamemnon's daughter, Trag.; called Ἰφιάνασσα by Hom.
stout, fat, goodly, of sheep, Hom.

entry.etym: epic adv., an old dat. of ἴς,
entry.sense: strongly, stoutly, mightily, Hom.
to fish, angle, epic imperf. ἰχθυάασκον Od.; c. acc. to fish for, epic 3rd sg. ἰχθυάᾳ Id.
to sport, of fish, Hes.
to strike fish, Anth.
striking fish, ἰχθ. μηχανή, of the trident, Aesch.
as Subst. a fisher, angler, Anth.
pass., ἰχθ. θήρα a spoil of speared fish, Id.
fish-eating, Anth.
a little fish, Anth.
holding fish, Anth.
fishy, scaly, i. e. foul, dirty, Ar.
fish-like, of fishes, Hdt.
full of fish, fishy, Hom.
consisting of fish, Anth.
a fisherman, Anth.
plague of fish, of a fisheater, Ar.
feeding fish: full of fish, Plut.
fish-eating:— οἱ Ἰχθ. ἄνδρες the fish-eaters, a tribe on the Arabian Gulf, Hdt.
piercing fish, Anth.
a stealer of fish, Anth.
a fish, Hom., etc.
in pl., οἱ ἰχθῦς the fish-market, Ar.
full of fish, Hdt.
following on the track, Hhymn.
a casting about for the scent, of hounds, Xen.
one who pursues the track, Anth.
the tracker: an Egyptian animal of the weasel-kind, which hunts out crocodile's eggs, the ichneumon, Pharaoh's rat, Arist.
a tracking, Xen.
a tracker, ἰχν. κύων a hound that hunts by nose, Anth.
= ἰχνεύμων, Hdt.
to track out, hunt after, seek out, Soph., Eur.: metaph., τὴν ψῆφον ἰχν. seeking for the vote of condemnation, Ar.
ἰχν. ὄρη to hunt the mountains, Xen.
a track, trace, footstep, Hom.
a kind of fetter or trap, Anth.
to examine the track, Aesch.
a track, footstep, Od., Hdt., etc.: metaph. a track, trace, clue, Trag.
poet. a foot or leg, Eur.
ichor, the etherial juice, that flows in the veins of gods, Il.;—epic acc. ἰχῶ for ἰχῶρα, Id.: later blood, Aesch.
a worm that eats horn and wood, Od.
shelter, Βορέω ὑπ’ ἰωγῇ under shelter from the north-wind, Od.
any loud sound: the shout or cry of men, Il.; the sound of the lyre, Od.; of the wind, of a fire, Il.
rout, pursuit, Il.:— Ἰωκή is personified Id.
entry.etym: metaplast. acc. ἴωκα (as if from ἰώξ), Il.

entry.sense: a violet-bed, Lat. violarium, Ar.
Ionic, Ionian, i. e. effeminate, Ar.
Ion, the son of Xuthus (or Apollo) and Creusa, from whom sprung the Ionian race, Hdt.: —οἱ Ἴωνες the Ionians, etc.
an exclamation of joy, as in Lat. io triumphe! Trag.
of grief or suffering, oh! Id.
Io, daughter of Inachus, Hdt., etc.
the letter iota, proverb. of anything very small, the smallest letter, a jot (the Hebr. yod), NTest.

Ι, ι, ἰῶτα, τό, indecl., ninth letter of the Gr. alphabet: as numeral ιʹ = 10, but ͵ι = 10,000. The ι subscriptum was called ι προσγεγραμμένον, adscriptum, and was so written till the 13th century, τῶι (not τῷ), as is still done in capital letters ΤΩΙ., Changes of ι:

doric, ι for υ in the 3rd pl. and part. pres., as φιλέοισι ἐοῖσα for φιλέουσι, etc.; so also Μοῖσα Ἀρέθοισα for Μοῦσα, etc.:—it was added to α in some Adjs., and in the aor1 part., as μέλαις τάλαις ῥίψαις for μέλας, etc.; and in the acc. pl. fem. of 1st decl., as ταῖς νύμφαις for τὰς νύμφας.
Boeot. and Lacon. as σιός, σεῖος, for θεός, θεῖος.

ῑ easily passes into ει, whence forms like εἴλω ἴλλω, εἴλη ἴλη, εἴρην ἰρήν: ῐ was sometimes exchanged with ε, as in ἑστία, ionic ἱστίη:—often inserted to lengthen the syll., e. g. εἰν εἰς ξεῖνος κεινός πνείω ὑπείρ διαί μεταί παραί, for ἐν, ἐς, etc. The Quantity of ι varies.
the Cabeiri, divinities worshipped in Lemnos and Samothrace, reputed to be sons of Hephaestus or Vulcan, from their skill in working metals, Hdt.
fit for burning, dry, Hom., Theocr.
to laugh aloud, Lat. cachinnari, in epic forms, 3rd pl. καγχαλόωσι Il.; part. καγχαλόων, -όωσα Hom. (Like καχάζω, formed from the sound.)
an urn or box: there were two, in which the dicasts placed their votes of guilty or not guilty, Ar.

Cadmean, Hes., Trag.; poet. Καδμέϊος, Pind., Soph., ionic form Καδμήιος, η, ον Καδμεῖοι, οἱ, the Cadmeans or ancient inhabitants of Thebes, Hom., etc.; also Καδμείωνες, Il.:— ἡ Καδμεία the citadel of Thebes, Xen.:—proverb., Καδμεία νίκη a dear-bought victory (from the story of the Σπαρτοί, or that of Polynices and Eteocles), Hdt.

entry.etym: fem. of Καδμεῖος, Hhymn., Hes.; also in attic, Thuc.

entry.sense: Cadmus-born, Trag.

Cadmus, Od., Hes.: son of the Phoenician king Agenor, brother to Europa, founder of Boeotian Thebes. Cadmus brought from Phoenicia the old Greek alphabet of sixteen letters, hence called Καδμήια or Φοινικήια γράμματα (Hdt.); which was afterwards increased by the eight (so called) Ionic, η ω θ φ χ ζ ξ ψ.
a jar or vessel for water or wine, Lat. cadus, Hdt., etc.
a liquid measure, = ἀμφορεύς, Anth.
an urn or box for collecting the votes, like καδίσκος, Ar.
a Carian woman, Il.
adj. fem. = Καρική, Carian, Hdt.
funeral rites, Lat parentalia, Luc.
to purify, hallow, Luc.:—Pass., μήτηρ πυρὶ καθήγνισται δέμας, i. e. has been burnt on the funeral-pyre, Eur.
to offer as an expiatory sacrifice, Id.
bloodstained, bloody, Eur.
to make bloody, sprinkle or stain with blood, Aesch., Eur.
bloodstained, bloody, Eur.
a pulling down, rasing to the ground, Thuc., Xen.: destruction, NTest.
to be put down, Thuc.
a putter down, overthrower, Thuc.
to be taken or achieved, Thuc.

entry.note: ionic κατ- fut. ήσω fut. 2 καθελῶ aor2 καθεῖλον inf. καθελεῖν Pass., aor1 καθῃρέθην perf. -ῄρημαι
entry.sense: to take down, καθείλομεν ἱστία we lowered sail, Od.; κ. ἄχθος to take a load down, i. e. off one's shoulders, Ar.:—Mid., καταιρεῖσθαι τὰ τόξα to take down one's bow, Hdt.
to put down or close the eyes of the dead, Hom.
of sorcerers, to bring down, Lat. caelo deducere, σελήνην Ar., Plat.
κατά με πέδον γᾶς ἕλοι (in tmesi) may earth swallow me! Eur.
to put down by force, destroy, Od., Trag.: simply to kill, slay, Eur.
in a milder sense, to put down, reduce, Hdt., Dem., etc.: to depose, dethrone, Hdt.; κ. τὸ λῃστικόν to remove it utterly, Thuc.
to rase to the ground, pull down, τὰς πόλεις Id.; τῶν τειχῶν a part of the walls, Xen.
to cancel, rescind, τὸ ψήφισμα Thuc.
as attic law-term, to condemn, Soph.
to reduce in flesh, Plut.
to overpower, seize, κὰδ δέ μιν ὕπνος ᾕρει (in tmesi) Od.; καθ. τινὰ ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ to catch in the act of folly, Soph.: c. gen. partis, κ. τῶν ὤτων to seize by the ears, Theocr.
to fetch down as a reward or prize, καθαιρεῖν ἀγῶνα or ἀγώνισμα Plut.: metaph. to achieve, Pind.; so in Mid., φόνῳ καθαιρεῖσθ’, οὐ λόγῳ, τὰ πράγματα Eur.; in Pass., Hdt.
more rarely like the simple αἱρέω, to take and carry off, seize, Id.
Dep., to leap down, Xen.: metaph. of a storm, to rush down, Il.
of the person or thing purified, to make pure or clean, cleanse, clean, purge, καθήραντες χρόα ὕδατι Od.:— to purge, clear a land of monsters and robbers, Soph.

in religious sense, to cleanse, purify, [δέπας] ἐκάθηρε θεείωι purified it by fumigating with sulphur, Il.; καθ. τινὰ φόνου to purify him from blood, Hdt.; Δῆλον κ. Id.:—Mid. to purify oneself, get purified, Id.; οἱ φιλοσοφίαι καθηράμενοι Plat.:—so Pass., κεκαθαρμένος Id.
to prune a tree, i. e. clear it of superfluous wood, NTest.
metaph., = μαστιγόω, like our vulgar phrase "to rub down, " Theocr.
of the thing removed by purification, to purge away, wash off or away, λύματα Il.; ῥύπα Od.; φόνον Aesch.
c. dupl. acc., αἷμα κάθηρον Σαρπηδόνα cleanse Sarpedon of blood, wash the blood off him, Il.:—Pass., φόνον καθαρθείς Hdt.
on the whole; divisim καθ’ ἅπαν.
once for all, Od., Dem.:—then, like ἁπλῶς, once for all, absolutely, Dem.

for καθ’ ἅ, according as, just as, Xen.:— so καθάπερ, ionic κατάπερ, Hdt., Ar., etc.:—strengthd., καθάπερ εἰ, ionic κατάπερ εἰ, like as if, exactly as, Hdt., Plat.; καθάπερ ἄν Dem.; καθάπερ ἂν εἰ Plat., etc.
to devote, dedicate, offer to a god, τί τινι Hdt., Ar., etc.:—of a burnt offering, Hdt.:— to make offerings to the manes, Lat. parentare, Luc.
generally, to burn, καταγιζομένου τοῦ καρποῦ Hdt.:— to burn a dead body, and even to bury, Plut.:—so, ὅσων σπαράγματ’ ἢ κύνες καθήγισαν whose mangled bodies dogs have buried, i. e. devoured, Soph.
bound with, equipt with a thing, c. dat., Ar.
to fasten, fix or put upon, τί τινι Soph.; so, κ. τι ἀμφί τινι Eur.; ἐπί τι Xen.:—Pass., βρόχῳ καθημμένος (perf. part.) fastened with a halter, i. e. hung, Soph.
to dress, clothe, in Mid., σκευῇ σῶμ’ ἐμὸν καθάψομαι Eur.
intr. in sense of Mid. (II), to lay hold of, τινός NTest.

Mid., καθάπτεσθαί τινα ἐπέεσσι, in good or bad sense, as, σὺ τόν γ’ ἐπέεσσι καθάπτεσθαι μαλακοῖσι or μειλιχίοις do thou accost or address him with gentle words, Hom.; or, ἀντιβίοις ἐπέεσσι καθαπτόμενος assailing or attacking . . , Od.: also without qualifying words, to accost or assail, γέροντα καθαπτόμενος προσέειπεν Id.
c. gen. to assail, attack, upbraid, Hdt., attic;—also, like Lat. antestari, θεῶν καταπτόμενος appealing to them, Hdt.
to lay hold of, τυραννίδος Solon.; βρέφεος Theocr.
of persons, cleanly, neat, nice, tidy, Lat. mundus, Arist.:—adv. -είως or -ίως, Xen., etc.
one must keep oneself clean, Luc.
to be clean or pure, Plat.: —c. gen. to be clean or free from guilt, Plut.; also, κ. ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ (sc. τοῦ σώματος) Plat.; also, καθ. γνώμῃ to be pure or clear in mind, Ar.
to make clean, to cleanse, NTest.:—Pass. to be or become clean from disease, Id.; and of the disease, to be purged away, Id.
cleanliness, purity, Hdt., Xen.
that which is thrown away in cleansing; in pl. the offscourings, refuse of a sacrifice, Aesch.
metaph. a castaway, outcast, Ar., Dem., etc.
in pl. = κάθαρσις, purification, Eur.
purified ground, ἐντὸς καθάρματος within the hallowed space, Ar.
to join or fit to, τί τινι Eur.

a cleansing, purification from guilt, Soph.:—hence, a means of purification, purifying sacrifice, atonement, expiation, καθαρμὸν τῆς χώρης ποιεῖσθαί τινα to make him an atonement for his country, Hdt.; μύσος ἐλαύνειν καθαρμοῖς by purifying rites, Aesch.; θοῦ νῦν καθαρμὸν δαιμόνων avert their wrath by purification, Soph.; καθαρμὸν θύειν to offer a purifying sacrifice, Eur.
applied to rites of initiation, Plat., Dem.
clear of dirt, clean, spotless, unsoiled, Od., Hdt., Eur.

clear, open, free, ἐν καθαρῷ (sc. τόπῳ) in a clear, open space, Il.; ἐν καθαρῷ βῆναι to leave the way clear, Soph.; διὰ καθαροῦ ῥέειν, of a river whose course is clear and open, Hdt.; τὸ ἐμποδὼν ἐγεγόνεε καθαρόν the hindrance was cleared away, Id.:—c. gen., γλῶσσα καθαρὴ τῶν σημηΐων clear of the marks, Id.

in moral sense, clear from shame or pollution, pure, καθαρῷ θανάτῳ Od.: esp. clear of guilt or defilement, clean, pure, Theogn., Aesch.; καθαρὸς χεῖρας Hdt.:—so, of persons purified after pollution, ἱκέτης προσῆλθες κ. Aesch.; of things, βωμοί, θύματα, δόμοι, μέλαθρα Id., Eur.:—c. gen. clear of or from a charge, κ. ἐγκλημάτων, ἀδικίας, κακῶν, etc., Horace's sceleris purus, Plat., Xen.
opp. to θολερός, clear of admixture, clear, pure, of water, Hdt., Eur.; so, κ. φάος, φέγγος Pind.; κ. ἄρτος χρυσός Hdt.; ἀργύριον Theocr.
of birth, opp. to ξένος, pure, , genuine, Pind., Eur.; τῶν Ἀθηναίων ὅπερ ἐστράτευε καθαρὸν ἐξῆλθε, i. e. who were citizens of pure blood, Thuc.:— καθαρόν a real, genuine saying, Id.
without blemish, τὸ καθαρὸν τοῦ στρατοῦ the sound portion of the army, Hdt.
clear, exact, ἂν καθαραὶ ὦσιν αἱ ψῆφοι if the accounts are clear, exactly balanced, Dem.
adv. καθαρῶς, Hes.; καθαρῶς γεγονέναι to be of pure blood, Hdt.
with clean hands, honestly, Theogn., Plat.
clearly, plainly, λέγειν Ar.; γνῶναι, εἰδέναι Id., Plat.
cleanness, purity, in moral sense, Plat.
to snatch down, Eur.
cleansing from guilt or defilement, purifying, Hdt., Soph.:—of sacrifice, αἷμα Aesch.; πῦρ, φλόξ Eur.
c. gen., καθ. φόνου cleansing or purifying from blood, Aesch.; but, κ. οἴκων purifying them, Eur.
as Subst., καθάρσιον (sc. ἱερόν), a purifying sacrifice, Aeschin.:— hence, purification, Hdt.
a cleansing from guilt or defilement, purification, Lat. lustratio, Hdt., Plat.
a cleanser from guilt or defilement, purifier, Soph., Ar., etc.
for cleansing or purifying, Plat.
a seat, κ. τοῦ λαγῶ a hare's seat or form, Xen.
the posture of sitting, ἐν τῇ καθέδρᾳ while they were sitting idle, Thuc.
perf. pass., used impers. it is ordained to one's ruin, Plut., Luc.
to shut in, enclose, confine, imprison, Od., Hdt., attic
Dep.:— to sit down, take one's seat, Hom., Trag.
to sit as suppliants, Eur., Thuc.
to sit down in a country, encamp, Thuc.
for καθ’ εἷς one by one, εἷς καθεῖς, for εἷς καθ’ ἕνα, NTest.
one must keep back, Plut.
to be held back or checked, Dem.: to be retained, Plut.
to wrap with bandages, enfold, swathe, Hdt.:—Pass., τὰς κνήμας ῥάκεσι κατειλίχατο (ionic 3rd pl. plup.), they have their legs swathed in rags, Id.

entry.note: fut. -έλξω Ar. fut. -ελκύσω aor1 καθείλκῠσα perf. -είλκῠκα Pass., aor1 -ειλκύσθην perf. -είλκυσμαι
entry.sense: of ships, to draw them to the sea, launch them, Lat. deducere, Hdt., attic
to draw down or depress the scale, Ar.
for καθ’ ἕν, one by one.
to clothe, v. καταέννυμι.
a holding, retention, Thuc.
to creep down, Ar., Xen.
steadily, calmly, Arist.

entry.etym: syncop. for καθεστηκότα, perf. part. pl. neut. of καθίστημι.

entry.sense: let down, of a fishing-line, Anth.
one must sleep, Plat.

entry.note: ionic κατ-εύδω imperf. καθεῦδον attic also καθηῦδον and ἐκάθευδον fut. καθευδήσω
entry.sense: to lie down to sleep, sleep, Hom., etc.:— ἐκ τοῦ καθεύδοντος (part. neut.) from a sleeping state, Plat.
metaph. to lie asleep, lie idle, Aesch., etc.:—also of things, to sleep, lie still, be at rest, ἐλπίδες καθεύδουσιν Eur.
to discover, Luc.:—Pass., καθευρέθη κοσμοῦσα she was found in the act of adorning, Soph.
Dep., to mock at, Lat. illudere, c. gen., Od.
to boil down, Ar.
metaph. to soften, temper, Xen.
a leader, a guide, Hdt.
Dep.:— to go before, act as guide, lead the way, absol., Hdt., Thuc.; οἱ κατηγεόμενοι the guides, Hdt.:—c. dat. to guide a person, Id.
c. acc. rei, to go before and teach a thing, to explain, expound, Id.
c. gen., καθ. τοῦ λόγου to begin the discourse, Plat.
to be the first to do, to establish, institute, Hdt.; οὐ κατηγήσομαι τὸν νόμον τόνδε τιθείς I will not begin establishing this law, Id.
to squander in luxury, Xen., Plut.
to have come or gone down, esp. to fight, Aesch.
to come down to, come or reach to, Hdt.
to have come to any one, καθῆκεν ἐς ἡμᾶς ὁ λόγος the turn of speaking came to us, Aeschin.
of Time, ὁ χρόνος καθήκει the time is come, Xen.; ὅταν ἐκ τῶν νόμων καθήκῃ when [the time] appointed by the law comes, Dem.
to be meet, fit, proper, τοῦ καθήκοντος χρόνου Soph.; αἱ καθ. ἡμέραι the regular, proper days, Dem.

impers., καθήκει μοι it belongs to me, beseems me, c. inf., οἷς καθήκει ἀθροίζεσθαι whose duty it is to assemble, Xen.:—in part., τὸ καθῆκον, τὰ καθήκοντα, ionic τὰ κατήκοντα, that which is meet, fit or proper, one's due or duty, Hdt., Xen.; also the present state of things, circumstances, Hdt.
to bring the sun down upon, to illuminate, Anth.
to nail on or to, Plut.
to be seated, Hom., etc.
to be seated in court, Ar.; οἱ καθήμενοι the judges, the court, Thuc., etc.
to sit still, sit quiet, Lat. desidere, Hom., Hdt.: in bad sense, to sit or lie idle, Il., etc.
of a besieging army, to sit down or lie before a place, Eur., Thuc.
to lead a sedentary life, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
of people, to be settled, Hdt.
day by day, daily (καθ’ ἡμέραν), Eur.:—later also καθημερινός, ή, όν, Plut.
on this day, Soph.
to make to sit down, Od., Eur.:—Pass. to sit down, settle, Ar.; κ. ἐς Ἀργώ to take one's seat in Argos, Theocr.
to consecrate, dedicate: so in aor1 mid. -ιδρυσάμην and perf. pass. -ίδρῡμαι, Eur.
to sacrifice, offer, Plat., Arist.
to dedicate, devote, hallow, Hdt., attic
a dedication, Aeschin., Plut.
to sit down, θῶκόνδε καθίζανον they went to the council and took their seats, Od.; μάντις ἐς θρόνους κ. Aesch.

entry.note: ionic κατ- imperf. καθῖζον or κάθιζον attic ἐκάθιζον fut. attic καθιῶ doric καθιξῶ aor1 ἐκάθῐσα epic κάθῐσα attic aor1 καθῖσα ionic κατῖσα epic part. καθίσσας doric καθίξας aor1 καθεῖσα aor1 -θεσσα Mid., imperf. ἐκαθιζόμην fut. καθιζήσομαι later καθίσομαι aor1 ἐκαθισάμην
entry.sense: Causal, to make to sit down, seat, Il., Hdt.; καθίσαι τινὰ εἰς θρόνον Xen.
to set or place, Hom.; καθίσαι στρατόν to encamp it, Eur., Thuc.
to set or place for any purpose, post, Od.; καθίσαι φυλάκους, φύλακας to set guards, Hdt., Xen.
to set up, ἀνδριάντα κάθεσσαν Pind.
to make an assembly take their seats, Od.; κ. τὸ δικαστήριον to hold the court, Ar.
to put into a certain condition, κλαίοντά τινα κ. to set him a-weeping, Plat.; also, κλαίειν τινὰ κ. to make him weep, Xen.
intr., like καθέζομαι, to sit down, be seated, take one's seat, sit, Hom., etc.:—c. acc., καθ. τρίποδα, βωμόν, (as we say "to sit a horse"), Eur.
to sit at meals, Lat. discumbere, Xen.
to sit as judge, Hdt., Dem.
to sit down in a country, encamp, Thuc.
to settle, sink in, Plat.
the Mid. is also used in intr. sense, Il., Theocr., etc.; καθίζεσθαι to take their seats (in the theatre), Dem.

entry.note: ionic κατ- fut. καθήσω aor1 καθῆκα epic καθέηκα perf. καθεῖκα
entry.sense: to send down, let fall, Lat. demittere, Hom., etc.; [ἱστία] ἐς νῆας κάθεμεν (1st pl. aor2) we let down, lowered the sails, Od.; κ. ἄγκυραν Hdt.; κ. καταπειρητηρίην to let down a sounding-line, Id.; καθιέναι to sound, Plat.; καθῆκε τὰ σκέλη let down his legs, of one who had been lying down, Id.; κ. δόρυ to let down one's pike, bring it to the rest, Xen.; κ. τὰς κώπας to let down the oars, so as to stop the ship's way, Thuc.:—rarely of striking, δι’ ὀμφαλοῦ καθῆκεν ἔγχος Eur.; γόνυ καθεῖσαν sank on their knee, Id.:— Pass. to come down, of a cow's udder, Hdt.; καθεῖτο τὰ τείχη the walls were carried down to the water, Thuc.
to send down into the arena, enter for racing, ἅρματα, ζεύγη Id.; τοῦτον τὸν λόγον καθεῖκε has entered this plea, Dem.
to set at, Lat. immittere, Luc.:—Pass. to be put in motion, ἡ στρατηλασίη κατίετο ἐς τὴν Ἑλλάδα Hdt.
seemingly intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν), to swoop down like a wind, Ar.; of rivers, to run down, Plat.; κ. εἰς γόνυ to sink on the knee, Plut.
to beg earnestly, Eur.
to offer earnest prayers, Hdt.
Dep., to come down to: metaph. to reach, touch, με καθίκετο πένθος Od.; καθίκεο θυμόν hast touched my heart, Il.; κάρα μου καθίκετο came down upon my head, Soph.
to let down by a rope, Ar.
Dep.:
to ride down, overrun with horse, Hdt.
to ride down, trample under foot, Aesch.

in Causal sense; of Act., pres., imperf., fut.; of Mid., the aor1, and sometimes pres.:— to set down, place, Il.; νῆα κατάστησον stop it, bring it to land, Od.; κ. δίφρον to station it, before starting for the race, Soph.:—Mid., [λαῖφος] κατεστήσαντο steadied the sails, Hhymn.
to bring down to a place, Od., etc.:— to restore, ἐς φῶς σὸν κατ. βίον Eur.:—Pass., οὐκ ἂν χάρις καθίσταιτο would not be returned, Thuc.
to bring before a magistrate or king, Hdt.
of soldiers, to set in order, to set as guards, Xen.
to ordain, appoint, Hdt., etc.:—in aor1 mid. to appoint for oneself, establish, institute, Hdt., Aesch.

esp. of political constitutions, to settle, establish, νόμους Eur., etc.; κατ. πολιτείαν, Lat. constituere rempublicam, Plat., etc.:— so in Mid., φρούρημα γῆς καθίσταμαι Aesch.; καθίστατο τὰ περὶ τὴν Μιτυλήνην Thuc.

to bring into a certain state, κατ. δῆμον ἐς μοναρχίαν Eur.; κ. τινὰ ἐς ἀπόνοιαν, ἐς φόβον, ἐς ἀπορίαν Thuc.; so, κ. τοὺς φίλους ἐν ἀκινδύνῳ Xen.:—also, κ. ἑαυτὸν ἐς κρίσιν to present himself for trial, Thuc.
to make or render so and so, κ. τινα ψευδῆ Soph.; ἄπιστον Thuc.:—rarely c. inf., καθ. τινὰ φεύγειν to make him fly, Id.:—Mid., τὴν ναυμαχίαν πεζομαχίαν καθίστασθαι Id.
τὴν ζόην καταστήσασθαι ἀπ’ ἔργων ἀνοσιωτάτων to get one's living by most unhallowed deeds, Hdt.
to make, continue, Aesch.; so in Mid., Id.
intr. in aor2, perf., and plup. of Act. (also in fut. καθεστήξω), and in all tenses of Mid. (except aor. 1), and all of Pass.:— to be set, set oneself down, settle, arrive, ἐς τόπον Hdt., Soph.
to come before another, stand in his presence, Hdt.; καταστὰς ἐπὶ τὸ πλῆθος ἔλεγε Thuc.
to be set as guard, Hdt., etc.: to be appointed, Eur., etc.
to stand quiet, be calm, of water, Ar.; so, πνεῦμα καθεστηκός Id.; ὁ θόρυβος κατέστη abated, Hdt.; so, of persons, καταστάς composedly, Aesch.; ἡ καθεστηκυῖα ἡλικία middle age, Thuc.

in perf. to come into a certain state, to become, and in aor2 and plup. to be, Hdt., etc.; καταστάντων εὖ τῶν πρηγμάτων being in a good state, Id.; τίνι τρόπῳ καθέστατε; in what case are ye? Soph.; ἀρξάμενος εὐθὺς καθισταμένου (sc. τοῦ πολέμου) from its first commencement, Thuc.

to be established or instituted, to prevail, exist, Hdt., etc.: in perf. part., existing, established, prevailing, τὸν νῦν κατεστεῶτα κόσμον Id.; οἱ καθεστῶτες νόμοι Soph.; τὰ καθεστῶτα the present state of life, Id.; so, τὰ κατεστεῶτα, existing laws, customs, Hdt.
Pass. to stand against, oppose, Τιτήνεσσι κατέσταθεν Hes.
a going down, descent, Luc.: a way down, Id.
a coming back, return, Eur., Thuc.; of an exile, Hdt., Thuc.
as adv. on the whole, in general, for καθ’ ὅλου, Arist., etc.; οὐ καθόλου, not at all, Dem.
to conciliate by daily intercourse, to win the favour of, Arist.
to confess or allow, esp. to one's detriment, Plat.
to promise, vow, Luc.
to betroth, Plut.
to equip or arm fully, τῇ πανοπλίᾳ Aeschin.:—Pass. to be so armed, Xen.
τὸ μὴ καλὸν καθοπλίσασα having taken arms against dishonour, Soph.
adverb for καθ’ ὅ, = καθά, in so far as, according as, Lys., etc.
so that, Plat.
to guide, Plut.
a mode of arming, armour, Xen.

entry.note: ionic κατ- imperf. καθεώρων ionic 3rd sg. κατώρα perf. καθεόρακα fut. κατόψομαι perf. κατῶμμαι aor1 κατώφθην
entry.sense: to look down, Il., Hdt.; so in Mid., Il.
c. acc. to look down upon, ὁπόσους ἠέλιος καθορᾷ Theogn., etc.
to have within view, to perceive, Hdt., Ar., etc.
to look to, observe, Pind., Ar.
to explore, τὰ ἄλλα Hdt.
to bring a ship into harbour, bring to anchor, Plut.:—Pass., with aor1 mid., to come into harbour, put in, Thuc.
metaph., ἐς τάσδε σαυτὸν πημονὰς καθώρμισας hast brought thyself to such miseries, Aesch.
Mid. to dedicate, θεῷ Eur.:—Pass., καθωσιώθη Ar.
κ. πόλιν καθαρμοῖς to purify, Plut.
for καθ’ ὅσον in so far as, inasmuch as, Thuc.
for καθ’ ὅ τι, in what manner, Hdt., Thuc.
to treat despitefully, to insult or affront wantontly, τινά Soph., etc.; also τινός Id.:—Pass., absol., to wax wanton, Id.
full of water, κάθυδρος κρατήρ, poet. for water itself, Soph.
to overshoot completely, Ar.
from above, down from above, Hom., etc.:—c. gen., κ. μελαθρόφιν Od.

on the top or upper side, above, Id.; καθ. ἐπιρρέει floats atop, Il.:— to denote geographical position, Φρυγίη καθύπερθε Id.; c. gen., καθύπερθε Χίου above, i. e. north of, Chios, Od.; τὰ κ. the upper country, i. e. further inland, τὰ κ. τῆς λίμνης Hdt.; καθύπερθε γενέσθαι τινός, properly, of a wrestler who falls atop of his opponent; hence, to have the upper hand of, Id.
of Time, before, c. gen., Id.
highest, ἐν τῇ κατυπερτάτῃ τῆς γῆς Hdt.
to be fast asleep, fall asleep, Hdt., Xen.:—Pass., perf. part. κατυπνωμένος asleep, Hdt.
Dep.:
to subdue by histrionic arts, Dem.
c. inf. to pretend to be some one else, Luc.
to come far behind, Plut.: absol. to be behind-hand, Menand.
to give up treacherously, Dem.; καθ. τὸν ἀγῶνα to conduct it treacherously, compromise it, Dem.; so also in Mid., with perf. pass., Id.
Mid., καθυφίεσθαί τινι to give way to any one, Xen.
above: metaph. having the upper hand, superior, κ. γίγνεσθαι Hdt., Thuc., etc.: c. gen., πόλις κ. τῶν ἀντιπάλων Xen.:—neut. καθυπέρτερον as adv., = καθύπερθε, Theocr.
= καθά, Hdt., NTest.
how, NTest.
a pit at Sparta, into which criminals were thrown, like the Athen. βάραθρον, Thuc., Plut.
for truly, to confirm a proposition, Lat. etenim, Hom., etc.:—also καὶ γὰρ δή for of a surety, Il.; καὶ γάρ ῥα Id.; καὶ γὰρ οὖν, καὶ γάρ τοι, Lat. etenim profecto, Plat., etc.
but also, Hom.
nay further, Hdt.
even if, although, Hom.
