to bear witness against, τινός or κατά τινος Oratt.; c. acc. pers. et inf., καταμαρτυροῦσιν αὐτὸν λαβεῖν Dem.:—Pass. to have evidence given against one, Id.
Pass. also of the evidence, to be given against one, Id.
Dep. to subdue, conquer, Plut.

entry.etym: used by Hom. only once in epic aor1 mid. κατ-ᾰμήσατο
entry.sense: to scrape over, pile up, heap up, Il.
in Act., to cut down, reap like corn (cf. ἀμάω), Soph.
to blunt, or dull, Soph.: aor1 pass. κατημβλύνθην Anth.
Causal, to make quite drunk, Hdt., Plat.
to take no care of, c. gen., Xen.: absol. to pay no heed, be heedless, Soph., Xen.
to spread over with honey, metaph. of the nightingale's voice, Ar.
blamed by all, abhorred, Soph.: neut. pl. as adv. so as to have cause to find fault, Il.
to find great fault with, blame greatly, accuse, Thuc., Plat.
a blaming, finding fault, Thuc.; οὐκ ἔχει τινὶ κατάμεμψιν it leaves him no ground for censure, Id.
to stay behind, stay, Hdt., attic
to remain fixed, continue in a certain state, Xen.
to cut in pieces, Luc.
to distribute, Xen.
to measure out to, Hdt., Xen.
to put in a probe: metaph., κημὸν κ. to use the ballot-box as a probe, i. e. make a peculator disgorge what he has stolen, Ar.
to point out, make known, indicate, Hdt.
to inform against, τινός Xen.
to taint, defile, Pind., Plat.:— Pass. to wear squalid garments as a sign of grief, wear mourning (cf. Lat. sordidatus), Hdt.

entry.note: or -ύω fut. -μίξω epic aor1 part. καμμίξας
entry.sense: to mix up, mingle the ingredients, Il., Ar.
to spend in paying public servants or soldiers, Ar., Aeschin.
liable to blame, inauspicious, Aesch.
better divisim κατὰ μόνας, v. μόνος.
to conquer in single combat, Plut.
to encompass, κ. ἐν τύμβῳ, i. e. to bury him, Eur.
a closing of the eyes, Plut.
to tear, scratch, Theocr.:—Mid., καταμύξατο χεῖρα she scratched her hand, Il.
to make mincemeat of, Ar.

entry.note: fut. ύσω aor1 ἐκάμμῠσα epic inf. καμμῦσαι
entry.sense: to shut or close the eyes, Xen., NTest.:—hence to drop asleep, doze, Batr., Ar.
to put all round, Od.
Dep. to mock at, τινος Plut.
to overpower by force, confine, Eur.
to coerce, τινὰ ἐς ξυμμαχίαν Thuc.
a curse, NTest.
to curse, NTest.
to make to dwell, settle, only used in aor1 κατένασσα Hes.:—Mid., aor1 κατανασσαμένη Aesch.: —Pass. to take up one's abode, dwell, only in aor1 κατενάσθην, Eur.; poet. 3rd pl. κατένασθεν Ar.
to use up, spend, lavish, Xen., Plat.:—Pass., with perf. act., to be lavished, Plat.
to be slothful towards, press heavily upon, c. gen., NTest.
to stamp or beat down firmly, Hdt.
to conquer in a sea-fight, Xen., etc.:—Pass. to be so conquered, Luc.
to distribute, allot, assign, esp. as pasture-land, Hdt., Dem.
to distribute, divide into separate bodies, Xen.:—of a single person, κ. τινὰ εἰς τὴν τάξιν to assign him to his post, Aeschin.
Mid. or Pass. to divide among themselves, Thuc., Plat.
to occupy with cattle, to graze land, Lat. depasci, Isocr.:—metaph. to plunder, Babr.

entry.note: fut. νεύσομαι aor1 κατένευσα epic part. καννεύσας
entry.sense: to nod assent, Il.: c. acc. rei, to grant, promise, Id.; so c. inf., generally, to make a sign by nodding the head, Od.
to heap up, Hdt.
to burn to cinders, Anth.
Pass. to be burnt to cinders,
to cover with snow, Ar.: metaph. to sprinkle as with snow, Luc.
absol., κατανίφει it snows, κεἰ κριμνώδη κατανίφοι even were it to snow thick as meal, Ar.
to observe well, to understand, Hdt., Plat.
to perceive, Thuc.
to learn, Id.
to consider, περί τινος Xen.
observation: means of observing, Plut.
Pass. to be used up or wasted, Od.
to bedew, Eur.
down-hill, Il.
down-hill, downward, steep, Ar.; εἰς τὸ κάταντες downwards, Xen.
metaph. prone, inclined, πρός τι Eur.
better κατ’ ἄντηστιν, so as to face, right opposite, Od.
prep. with gen. straight down from, Od.
= ἀντῑκρύ, right opposite, ἐς τὰ κ. Κυθήρων to the parts opposite Cythera, Thuc.; κατ. ᾗ εἰσρεῖ exactly opposite to the point at which it flows in, Plat.
as adv. of Place, right opposite, ἡ ἤπειρος ἡ κ. Thuc.; ἐκ τοῦ κ. from the opposite side, Plat.
straightforward, downright, Thuc.
over against, right opposite, facing, c. gen., Hdt.; c. dat., Id.; absol., Soph.
to pour water over:—metaph. to pour a flood of words over, τινός Ar.
stupefaction, slumber, NTest.
Pass. to be sorely pricked, κατενύγησαν τῇ καρδίᾳ NTest.
to be stupefied, to slumber, Lxx.
to bring to quite an end: esp.,
to accomplish a certain distance, δρόμον, ὁδόν Hdt., Xen.
(the acc. being omitted) intr. to arrive at a place, Hdt., Soph., etc.
to accomplish, perpetrate, Eur.; κ. αἷμα to murder, Id.
to card or comb well: to tear in pieces, rend in shreds, Eur.; καταξαίνειν τινὰ εἰς φοινικίδα to pound him to red rags, Ar.:—Pass., καταξανθείς crushed to atoms, Soph.; πρὶν κατεξάνθαι Eur.
to wear or waste away, Lat. atterere, Aesch.: Pass., κατεξάνθην πόνοις, δακρύοις Eur.
Pass. to be received as a guest, perf. part. κατεξενωμένος Aesch.
quite or very worthy of, c. gen., Soph.; absol., Eur. adv. -ίως, Id.
to deem worthy, Plat.:—Mid. to hold in high esteem, Aesch.
πολλὰ χαίρειν ξυμφοραῖς καταξιῶ I bid a long farewell to calamities, Id.; σύ τοι κατηξίωσας thou would'st have it so, Soph.
to mock at, τινός Anth.
shutting downwards, καταπακτὴ θύρα a trap-door, Hdt.
to throw in wrestling, Ar.: metaph. to overthrow, Eur., Plat.
Pass. to vault or leap down, οὐρανοῦ ἐκ κατέπαλτο (epic syncop. aor2 for κατεπάλετο), Il.
to besprinkle or bespatter, Ar.:—Pass., καταπαττόμενος Id.
c. acc. rei, to sprinkle or strew over, Id.
besprinkled, Ar.
embroidered, Id.
to trample down, trample under foot, Thuc., etc.; κ. ὑσὶ τὸ σπέρμα to trample down the seed (i. e. have it trampled down) by swine, Hdt.: —Pass., Id., Thuc., etc.
metaph. in tmesi, κατὰ δ’ ὅρκια πιστὰ πάτησαν Il.
a means of stopping, Il.
a putting to rest: a putting down, deposing, Hdt.
a cessation, calm, NTest.

entry.note: poet. καπ-παύω fut. σω epic inf. -παυσέμεν
entry.sense: to lay to rest, put an end to, Hom., Hdt.:— Mid., Eur.
c. acc. pers. to lay to rest, i. e. kill, Il.
to make one stop from a thing, hinder or check from, c. gen., Hom.:—and c. acc. only, to stop, keep in check, Id., Hdt.
like καταλύω, to put down or depose from power, κ. τινὰ τῆς ἀρχῆς, τῆς βασιληΐης Hdt.; κ. τοὺς τυράννους Id.:—Pass., τῆς βασιληΐης κατεπαύθη Id.
to put down, τὴν Κύρου δύναμιν Id.; τὸν δῆμον Thuc.
Pass. and Mid. to leave off from, cease from, τινος Hdt., etc.
absol. to leave off, cease, Ar., etc.
the Act. is also used intr. like Mid., Eur.
to fetter, hamper, Hom.
to persuade, Luc.
to threaten loudly, κατ. ἔπη to use threatening words, Soph.; τὰ κατηπειλημένα the threats uttered, Id.

sense.gloss: down, downwards, with gen. or acc.

entry.sense: prep. with gen. or acc. Radical sense down, downwards.
WITH GENIT.,
denoting motion from above, down from, βῆ δὲ κατ’ Οὐλύμποιο καρήνων Il., etc.
denoting downward motion,
down upon or over, κατὰ χθονὸς ὄμματα πήξας Il.; of the dying, κατ’ ὀφθαλμῶν κέχυτ’ ἀχλύς a cloud settled upon the eyes, Id.; so, ὕδωρ κατὰ χειρός, v. χείρ II. 6.
down into, νέκταρ στάξε κατὰ ῥινῶν Od.; so, κατὰ χθονὸς (or γῆς) δῦναι Trag.; κατὰ χθονὸς κρύπτειν to bury, Soph., etc.

εὔχεσθαι or ὀμόσαι κατά τινος to vow or swear by a thing (because one calls down the vengeance of the gods upon it), Thuc., Dem.:—also to make a vow towards something, i. e. make a vow of offering it, Ar.

in hostile sense, against, Aesch., etc.; esp. of judges giving sentence against a person, Id.; λόγος κατά τινος a speech against one accused, Lat. in aliquem; λόγος πρός τινα an answer to an opponent, Lat. adversus aliquem.
Lat. de, upon, in respect of, concerning, σκοπεῖν κατά τινος Plat.; ἔπαινος κατά τινος praise bestowed upon one, Aeschin., etc.
WITH ACCUS.,
of motion downwards, κατὰ ῥόον down stream, Hdt.; κατ’ οὖρον ἰέναι, ῥεῖν to sail down (i. e. with) the wind, Aesch.
of motion, on, over, throughout a space, Hom., etc.; καθ’ Ἑλλάδα Aesch.; κατὰ γῆν καὶ θάλασσαν by land and sea, etc.: —also to hit upon the shield, Il.
opposite, over against, κατὰ Σινώπην πόλιν Hdt.; ἀνὴρ κατ’ ἄνδρα Aesch.
κατὰ τὸ προάστειον somewhere in the suburb, Hdt.
distributively, of a whole divided into parts, κατὰ φῦλα, κατὰ φρήτρας by tribes, by clans, Il.; κατὰ κώμας κατῳκῆσθαι to live in separate villages, Hdt.; κατ’ ἄνδρα man by man, Id.
so of parts of Time, καθ’ ἡμέραν, κατ’ ἦμαρ day by day, daily, v. ἡμέρα III, ἦμαρ.
of numbers, by so many at a time, καθ’ ἕνα one at a time, Hdt.; κατὰ τὰς πέντε καὶ εἴκοσι μνᾶς πεντακοσίας δραχμὰς εἰσφέρειν to pay 500 drachmae on every 25 minae, Dem., etc.
of direction towards an object, πλεῖν κατὰ πρῆξιν on a business, for or after, Od.; κατὰ ληΐην in quest of booty, Hdt.; κατὰ θέαν ἥκειν to have come for the purpose of seeing, Thuc.
of pursuit, κατ’ ἴχνος on the track, Soph.

according to, κατὰ θυμόν Hom.; καθ’ ἡμέτερον νόον after our liking, Il.; κατὰ μοῖραν as is meet and right, Hom.; so, κατ’ αἶσαν, κατὰ κόσμον Id.; καθ’ ἡδονήν so as to please, Aesch.; κατὰ δύναμιν to the best of one's power, et.

in relation to, concerning, τὰ κατ’ ἀνθρώπους = τὰ ἀνθρώπινα, Aesch.; so, τὸ καθ’ ὑμᾶς as far as concerns you, Hdt.; κατὰ τοῦτο according to this way, in this view; κατὰ ταὐτά in the same way, καθ’ ὅτι so far as, etc.

implying comparison, κατὰ λοπὸν κρομύοιο like the coat of a leek, Od.; κατὰ Μιθραδάτην answering to the description of him, Hdt.; κατὰ πνιγέα very like an oven, Ar.; κηδεῦσαι καθ’ ἑαυτόν to marry in one's own rank of life, Aesch.; κατ’ ἄνθρωπον like a man, as befits a man, Id.; κατ’ ἄνδρα, μὴ θεόν Id.:—after a comp., μείζων ἢ κατ’ ἀνθρώπου greater than befits a man, Hdt.; μείζω ἢ κατὰ δάκρυα too great to weep for, Thuc.
by the favour of a god, κατὰ δαίμονα, Lat. non sine numine, Pind.; κατὰ θεόν Hdt.
of loosely stated numbers, nearly, about, κατὰ ἑξηκόσια ἔτεα 600 years more or less, Id.
of Time, during, sometime in a period, κατὰ τὸν πόλεμον in the course of the war, Id.; καθ’ ἡμέραν by day, Aesch.
about, κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν χρόνον Hdt.; κατὰ Ἄμασιν βασιλεύοντα about the time of Amasis, Id.
used periphr. for Adverbs, as, καθ’ ἡσυχίην, κατὰ τάχος, etc., for ἡσύχως, ταχέως, Id.; κατὰ μέρος partially; κατὰ φύσιν naturally; etc.
Position: when κατά follows its case it is written with anastr. κάτα.
absol. as adv. like κάτω, downwards, Hom.
κατά in Compos.,
downwards, down, as in καταβαίνω.
in answer to, in accordance with, as in κατᾴδω, καταθύμιος.
against, in hostile sense, as καταγιγνώσκω, κατακρίνω.
often only to strengthen the notion of the simple word, as κατακόπτω, καταφαγεῖν.

κατά as a prep. was sometimes shortened, esp. in epic into κάγ, κάκ, κάμ, κάν, κάπ, κάρ, κάτ, before γ, κ, μ, ν, π (or φ), ῥ, τ (or θ), respectively; see these forms in their own places. Mss. and the older Edd. join the prep. with the following word, as καγγόνυ, καδδέ, κακκεφαλῆς, καππεδίον, καπφάλαρα, καρρόον, καττάδε, καττόν, etc. In compd. Verbs, κατά sometimes changes into καβ, καλ, καρ, κατ, before β, λ, ρ, θ, respectively, as κάββαλε, κάτθανε, κάλλιπε, καρρέζουσα; and before στ, σχ, the second syll. sometimes disappears, as in καστορνῦσα, κάσχεθε, κασσύω, as also in Doric forms καβαίνων, κάπετον.
a sounding-line, Hdt.
to overrun with light-armed troops (πελτασταί), Ar.
to be sent down, Luc.
to send down, Hes.; esp. from the inland to the sea-coast, Xen.
to send from head-quarters, to dispatch, Dem.
to mourn for, bewail, Anth.

entry.note: mostly in Mid. -πέρδομαι; aor2 κατέπαρδον perf. καταπέποδρα
entry.sense: to break wind at, τινός Ar.
to boil down, to digest food, Arist.:—metaph. to digest, keep from rising, Lat. concoquere, κ. χόλον Il.; κ. μέγαν ὄλβον, i. e. to bear great fortune meekly, Pind.
to spread out over, Il., Eur.
to spread or cover with, τί τινι Ar., Xen.
a curtain, veil, NTest.

entry.note: fut. -πτήσομαι 3rd sg. aor2 κατέπτατο part. καταπτάμενος subj. κατάπτωμαι also aor2 act. κατέπτην
entry.sense: to fly down, Hdt., Ar., etc.
to stone to death, Xen.
contemptuously, Dem.
to stick fast in the ground, plant firmly, Il., Hdt., etc.
Pass., with perf. and plup. act., to stand fast or firm in, Il.; absol., στήλη καταπεπηγυῖα Hdt.
to leap down, Xen.
to fill full of a thing, c. gen., Plat.
to burn to ashes, Anth.

entry.note: fut. -πίομαι later -πιοῦμαι aor2 κατέπιον epic κάππιον
entry.sense: to gulp or swallow down, Hes., Hdt., attic
metaph., κ. Εὐριπίδην to drink in Euripides, i. e. imbibe his spirit, Ar.
to swallow up, consume, Id.
to spend in tippling, Aeschin.
to sell outright, καταπραθείς Luc.

entry.note: fut. -πεσοῦμαι aor2 κατ-έπεσον poet. κάπ-πεσον 3rd dual καπ-πεσέτην perf. πέπτωκα
entry.sense: to fall or drop down, Hom., Hdt., attic;—used as Pass., κάππεσε = κατεβλήθη, Aesch.
metaph., κάππεσε θυμός their spirit fell, Il.; κ. εἰς ἀπιστίαν Plat.
to have the falling sickness, Luc.
to cover with pitch, to pitch over and burn (as a punishment), Plat.
to trust, Plut.
to plaster over with clay, etc., Hdt., Ar.:—Mid., καταπλάσσεσθαι τὴν κεφαλήν to plaster one's own head, Hdt.; τοῦτο καταπλάσσονται ὅλον τὸ σῶμα this they plaster over their whole body, Id.
plastered over, καταπλαστὸν φάρμακον a plaster, Ar.
to entwine, plait, Hdt.
metaph. to implicate, κ. τινὰ προδοσίᾳ Id.
to finish twining: metaph. to bring to an end, τὴν ζόην, τὴν ῥῆσιν Id.
gen. ω, quite full, τινος of a thing:— fouled or stained with a thing, γῆς κατάπλεως καὶ αἵματος Xen.
to sail down: i. e.,
to sail from the high sea to shore, sail to land, put in, Od., Hdt., attic; νεωστὶ καταπεπλευκώς having lately come ashore, Plat.
to sail down stream, κατ. τὸν Εὐφρήτην Hdt.
to sail back, Id.
amazement, consternation, Thuc.

to strike down: metaph. to strike with amazement, astound, terrify, Thuc., Xen., etc.:—Pass. to be panic-stricken, amazed, astounded, κατεπλήγη (aor2) Il.; attic aor2 inf., καταπλαγῆναι Thuc.; 2nd pl. perf. καταπέπληχθε Id.; c. acc., καταπλαγέντες τὸν Φίλιππον Dem.
stricken with amazement, astounded, Lys.
shy, bashful, Arist.
a sailing down to land, a putting ashore, putting in, Thuc.
a sailing back, return, Xen.
to enrich greatly, Hdt., Xen.
to wash by pouring over, to drench, Xen.
to wash out:—Pass., metaph., τὸ πρᾶγμα καταπέπλῠται the affair is washed out, i. e. forgotten, Aeschin.
a bathing in water, Xen.
to breathe upon or over, c. gen., Eur.
to inspire, Aesch.; θεὸς καταπνεῖ σε Eur.
a blowing, Pind.
-po/das, less correct forms for κατὰ πόδα, κατὰ πόδας.
to war down, i. e. to exhaust by war, subdue completely, reduce, Lat. debellare, Thuc., Xen.: in pres. to attempt to subdue, Thuc.: —Pass., ἐλπίζοντες [τὴν πόλιν] καταπεπολεμῆσθαι Id.
Dep. to subdue by policy, Dem.
less correct form for κατὰ πολύ
to subdue after a hard struggle: — Pass. to be so subdued, Aeschin.
tired, wearied, Plut.
to throw into the sea, drown therein, Dem., καταποντίζω, Hdt., Plat.
one who throws into the sea, Dem.
to prostitute, Hdt.
to accomplish, execute, Xen.
to achieve, gain, Id.:—Mid. to achieve for oneself, Id.:—Pass., τὰ καταπεπραγμένα Id.
to soften down, appease, Plat.
down-turned, of the hand as used in striking or grasping, χειρὶ καταπρηνεῖ with the flat of his hand, Il.; χείρεσσι καταπρηνέσσι Od.
to throw headlong down, Anth.
to saw up, Hdt.
to cut or bite into pieces, Theocr.
to betray utterly, leave in the lurch, Hdt., attic

entry.etym: a fut. without any pres. in use
entry.sense: to do a thing without return, i. e. with impunity, used with a negat., οὐκ ἐμὲ λωβησάμενος καταπροΐξεται he shall not escape for having insulted me, Hdt.; οὐ καταπροΐξονται ἀποστάντες, Id.; οὔ τοι καταπροίξει πολλὰ κλέψας Ar.:— absol., ἐκείνους οὐ καταπροΐξεσθαι ἔφη he said that they should not get off scot-free, Hdt.
c. gen. pers., οὔ τοι ἐμοῦ καταπροίξει you will not escape for this despite done to me, Ar.
winged, Aesch., Eur.

entry.note: fut. -πτήξω 3rd dual epic aor2 καταπτήτην poet. part. καταπτᾰκών perf. κατέπτηχα epic part. καταπεπτηώς
entry.sense: to crouch down, to lie crouching or cowering, Hom., Hes.
c. acc. to cower beneath, Plut.
to be spat upon, abominable, despicable, Aesch., Eur., Dem.
with ample folds, Theocr.
to spit upon or at, esp. as a mark of abhorrence, c. gen., Dem., Aeschin.
to reduce to beggary, Plut.
brutal lust, Ar.
a lewd fellow, Ar.
to make rotten, Hhymn.:— Pass. to become rotten, Il.
very thick, Theocr.
to stud thickly with a thing, Plut.
a curse, κατάρην ποιεῖσθαί τινι to lay a curse upon one, Hdt.; διδόναι τινὰ κατάρᾳ Eur.
Dep.

to call down curses upon, imprecate upon, τί τινι Hom., Hdt.:—c. inf., καταρῶνται ἀπολέσθαι they pray that he may perish, Theogn.:—c. dat. pers. only, to curse, execrate, Hdt., Ar., etc.; later, c. acc. pers., Plut., NTest.
absol. to utter imprecations, Ar.
perf. pass. part. κατ-ηρᾱμένος in pass. sense, accursed, Id.
accursed, abominable, Eur., Ar.; comp. -ότερος Dem.; †sup. -ότατος Soph.
to leave unemployed or idle, Eur.; κ. τὴν γῆν to occupy the ground uselessly, cumber it, NTest.
to make of none effect, Id.:—Pass., καταργηθῆναι to be abolished, cease, Id.; κ. ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου to be set free from the law, Id.
to make to tarry, v. sub ἀπαρτίζω.
only in pl. κατάργματα, the first offerings, Eur.
the purifications made by such offerings, Plut.
to cover with silver:—Pass., καταργυρωμένος (ionic for κατηργ-) silvered, Hdt.
to buy or bribe with silver, κατηργυρωμένος Soph.
to water:—metaph. to besprinkle with praise, Ar.
making one shudder, horrible, Od.
to count or reckon among, Eur., Plat.
to recount in detail, Plat.:—in Mid. to recount, enumerate, Id.
to be fully sufficient, Hdt., Eur.
to deny strongly, persist in denying, Soph.
to plough up, τὴν γῆν Ar.
to lose from carelessness, Xen., Dem.:—Pass., τὰ κατερρᾳθυμημένα things lost through negligence, Dem.
intr. to be very careless, καταρρᾳθυμήσαντες through carelessness, Xen.
to tear into shreds: perf. pass. part. κατερρακωμένος in rags or tatters, Soph.
as adj. down-rushing, τὸν καταρράκτην ὀδόν (attic for οὐδόν) to the downward entrance [of Hades], Soph.
as Subst. broken water, a waterfall, Lat. cataracta, Strab.
a kind of portcullis, Plut.
a sea-bird, so called from rushing down upon its prey, a gull, Ar.
κ. θύρα, a trap-door, Plut.
to stitch on or over, θύρη κατερραμμένη ῥιπὶ καλάμων a frame lashed to a crate of reeds, Hdt.
to stitch tight, Plut.
metaph. to devise, compass, Aesch.
sewn together, patched, Luc.
to pat with the hand, to stroke, caress, like Lat. mulcere, χειρὶ δέ μιν κατέρεξε (epic for κατερρ-) Hom.; also καρρέζουσα (epic for καταρρ-) Il.
to make to incline downwards, make to fall, Soph.
to flow down, Il., Hdt., attic
of men, to stream or rush down, Ar., Thuc.
of fruit, leaves, etc., to fall off, Xen.
to fall in ruins, Dem.
κ. εἴς τινα to come to, fall to the lot of, Theocr., Bion.
κ. φόνῳ to run down with blood, Eur.; so in Mid., Plut.
to break down, τὴν γέφυραν Hdt.; μέλαθρα Eur.
to tear in pieces, rend, Dem.:—Mid., κατερρήξαντο τοὺς κιθῶνας they rent their coats, Hdt.
in Soph. Ant. 675 τροπὰς καταρρήγνυσι [ἡ ἀναρχία] breaks up armies and turns them to flight.
Pass., aor2 κατερράγην [ᾰ], with perf. act. κατέρρωγα: — to be broken down, to be thrown down and broken, Hdt.
to fall or rush down, to break or burst out, of storms, Id.; of tears, Eur.:—metaph., ὁ πόλεμος κατερράγη Ar.
to be broken in pieces, Αἴγυπτος μελάγγαιός τε καὶ κατερρηγμένη with black and crumbling soil, Hdt.
to dash down, break in pieces, τοὺς λοιπούς κατήραξεν ἐς τὸν Κιθαιρῶνα drove them shattered to Cithaerae, Hdt.; τὸ στράτευμα κατηράχθη εἰς τὰ τειχίσματα Thuc.
intr. to fall down, fall headlong, Plut.
to file down:— metaph., κατερρινημένον τι polished, elegant, Ar.
to throw down, overthrow, Aesch.
a running from the head, a catarrh, Plat.
to gulp or swallow down, Xen.
falling away, Soph.
irrigated, watered, Eur.
carried down by water, alluvial, of the Delta, Hdt.
to fear, dread, Hdt.
jagged, broken, Soph.
a landing-place, Thuc.
to hang down from, hang on or append, Plut.
to adjust, χρῆμα κατηρτημένον a well-adjusted or convenient thing, Hdt.
to adjust or put in order again, restore, Hdt.; κ. δίκτυα to put nets to rights, mend them, NTest.:—metaph. to restore to a right mind, Id.
to furnish completely: perf. pass. part. κατηρτισμένος, absol., well-furnished, complete, Hdt., NTest.
restoration, NTest.
a training, education, discipline, Plut.
one who restores order, a mediator, Hdt.
to prepare, dress, of food, Luc.
generally, to train, educate, discipline: — Pass. to be trained, disciplined, Solon., Soph.
c. inf., κ. μολεῖν to procure his coming, Soph.
intr. in part. perf., κατηρτυκὼς ἱκέτης, metaph., a complete suppliant, one who has done all that is required, Aesch.
to defeat in an election, esp. by unfair means, Plut.
less correct form for κατ’ ἀρχάς
to make beginning of a thing, c. gen., Aesch.; ὁδοῦ κατάρχειν to lead the way, Soph.:— rarely c. acc. to begin a thing, Plat.:—c. part. to begin doing, Xen.
to honour, Eur.
Mid. to make a beginning, to begin, like Act., c. gen., Id., Plat.; also c. acc., Eur.: absol., κατάρχεται μέλος is beginning, Id.

in religious sense, to begin the sacrificial ceremonies, Νέστωρ χέρνιβά τ’ οὐλοχύτας τε κατήρχετο Nestor began [the sacrifice] with the washing of hands and sprinkling the barley on the victim's head, Od.; κατάρχομαι I begin the function, Eur.:—c. gen., κατάρχεσθαι τοῦ τράγου to make a beginning of the victim, i. e. consecrate him for sacrifice by cutting off the hair of his forehead, Ar.; πῶς δ’ αὖ κατάρξει θυμάτων; Eur.
to sacrifice, slay, Id.:—Pass., σὸν κατῆρκται σῶμα hath been devoted, Id.
simply, to strike, Plut.
to put out, quench, Lat. extinguere, Il., Eur., etc.:—metaph., ἔστιν θάλασσα, τίς δέ νιν κατασβέσει; who shall dry it up? Aesch.; κ. βοήν, ἔριν to quell noise, strife, Soph.
Pass., aor1 κατ-εσβήθην, with intr. aor2 act. κατέσβην, inf. κατα-σβῆναι, perf. act. κατ-έσβηκα: — to go out, be quenched, Hdt.:—metaph., κλαυμάτων πηγαὶ κατεσβήκασι Aesch.
to shake down, throw down, Thuc.

κατασεῖσαι τὴν χεῖρα to shake or make a motion of the hand; so, κ. τὰ ἱμάτια, by way of signal, Plut.; but also, κ. τῇ χειρί to beckon with the hand, NTest.: absol., κατασείειν τινί to beckon to another, as a sign for him to be silent, Xen.
Pass., to rush back into, c. acc., κῦμα κατέσσυτο (epic aor2) ῥέεθρα Il.
to seal up: Mid. to have a thing sealed up, Plat.
to make rotten, let rot, Xen.:—Pass., aor2 κατ-εσάπην [ᾰ], epic 3rd sg. subj. -σαπήῃ, with perf. 2 act. κατα-σέσηπα, to grow rotten, rot away.
to weaken, Anth.
to pant and struggle against a thing, c. gen., Aesch.
to become silent, Plat.
τυρόν, to Sicilise (i. e. to consume) the cheese (in allusion to the peculations of Laches in Sicily), Ar.
Dep. to eat up, feed on, Hdt.
to be silent about a thing, Dem.
Causal, to make silent, silence, Xen.: Mid. to cause silence, Id.
to dig down, destroy utterly, rase to the ground, overthrow, Hdt., Soph., etc.:— Pass., οἰκία οἱ κατεσκάφη (aor2) Hdt.
a rasing to the ground, destruction, Trag.
γῆς κατασκαφαία grave deep dug in earth, Aesch.; θανόντων ἐς κατασκαφάς, i. e. to the grave, Soph.
dug down, κ. οἴκησις the deep-dug dwelling, i. e. the grave, Soph.
to scatter, or pour upon or over, τι κατά τινος Ar.; also τί τινος, Dem., etc.
κ. φήμην to spread a report against one, Plat.
Mid. to pour or sprinkle about, Xen.
Pass. to become a skeleton, wither or pine away, Aesch.:—so in perf. act. κατέσκληκα and plup. κατεσκλήκει, Babr.
to equip or furnish fully, Dem.; so in Mid., Xen.:—Pass., σκηνὴ χρυσῷ κατεσκευασμένη Hdt., etc.

to get ready, make, build, Id., Plat., etc.:—hence, to prepare, arrange, δημοκρατίαν Xen.; συμπόσιον Plat., etc.: —Mid. to make for oneself, esp. to build a house and furnish it, Thuc.: to pack up, also opp. to ἀνασκευάζεσθαι, Xen.
of fraudulent transactions, to get up, trump up, Id., etc.; of persons, to suborn, Arist.
to make so and so, with a second acc., εἰ μὴ Γοργίαν Νέστορά τινα κατασκευάζεις unless you make Gorgias a kind of Nestor, Plat.: also, to represent as so and so, κ. τινὰ πάροινον, Dem.
in Logic, to construct an argument, Arist.
absol. in Mid. to make ready for doing, ὡς πολεμήσοντες Thuc.; ὡς οἰκήσων Xen.
that which is prepared or made, a building, structure, edifice, Dem.
an arrangement, contrivance, device, Id.
contrivance, Dem.
one must prepare or make, Xen.
preparation, ἐν κατασκευῇ τοῦ πολέμου in preparing for it, Thuc.; the equipment of ships, engines, etc., Id.
any kind of furniture that is fixed, opp. to what is movable (παρασκευή), buildings, fixtures, Id.; but also, like παρασκευή, any furniture, Hdt., Thuc.
the state, condition, constitution of a thing, Eur., Plat.
a device, trick, Aeschin.
to practise much: part. perf. pass. κατησκημένος, regular, ascetic, Plut.
to pitch one's camp or tent, take up one's quarters, encamp, Xen.; generally, to rest, lodge, settle,
a covering, veil, Aesch.
an encamping:—of birds, a resting-place, nest, NTest.
to rush down or fall upon, c. dat., of lightning and storms, Hdt.; of divine wrath, Id.; of the plague, Thuc.:—rarely, κατασκῆψαί τινα to fall on one, Eur.
κ. λιταῖς to storm or importune with prayers, Soph.
to overshadow, cover over, Hes.; κ. κόνει to bury one, Soph.
shaded or covered with something, Hes., Hdt., Aesch.
trans. overshadowing, Aesch., Eur., Ar.
to view closely, spy out, Eur.: to reconnoitre, Xen.:— also in Mid., Id.
a viewing closely, spying, Soph., Eur.; ἐπὶ κατασκοπῇ, κατασκοπῆς ἕνεκα Xen.
one who keeps a look out, a scout, spy, Hdt., Eur.:—in Thuc., a person sent to examine and report, an inspector.
to make jokes upon, to jeer or mock, Hdt.
to disparage, depreciate, Arist.
to burn with a slow fire, burn up, Il.; metaph. of love, Theocr.; in Pass., of a lover, to smoulder away, Id.
Dep. to conquer by sophisms or fallacies, to outwit, Luc.:—also as Pass. to be outwitted, Id.
Dep. to embrace, Plut.
to tear down, pull to pieces, Ar.
to live wantonly, to wanton, Anth.
to draw or pull down, κ. τὰς νῆας to haul ships down to the sea, Hdt.; κ. σημεῖα to pull the flags down (in token of defeat), Thuc.; κ. τινὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἵππου Xen.
to quaff or swallow down, Lat. deglutire, Ar.
to sow thickly: metaph., ἀνίας κ. to sow a crop of sorrows, Soph.
to beget, τέκνα Eur.
to scatter over, as in sowing, c. gen., Plut.
to besprinkle, Anth.
self-devotion, Plut.
to pour as a drink-offering, Lat. libare, Eur., Ar.:—absol. to pour drink-offerings, Hdt.
c. acc., κ. τινὰ δακρύοις to honour with offerings of tears, Eur.; κ. τινά lament with tears, Anth.
to consecrate, Plut., Anth.
to urge on, Ar.;—absol., κατασπέρχον urgent, pressing, causing anxiety, Thuc.
to press, urge, or hasten on, Aeschin.
to throw down in the dust: Pass., perf. part. κατεσποδημένοι Aesch.
Dep., to be very earnest or serious, Hdt.; οὐδαμῶς κατεσπουδασμένος ἀνήρ Id.
of persons,
to let fall in drops upon, pour upon, shed over, τί τινος Eur.
c. dat. rei, to run down with a thing, νόσῳ κ. πόδα to have one's foot running with a sore, Soph.; κ. ἀφρῷ to run down with foam, Eur.
of the liquid,
intr. to drop down, drip or trickle down, Eur., Xen.
trans. to drop down over, wet, ἱδρὼς καταστάζει δέμας Soph.
to form a counter-party in the state, Plut.
Pass. to be factiously opposed or overpowered, Xen., Dem.
trans. a settling, appointing, appointment, institution, Aesch., Dem.; δαιμόνων κατ. their ordinance, Eur.
appointment of magistrates, Plat.
a bringing of ambassadors before the senate or assembly, an introduction, presentation, Hdt.
κ. ἐγγυητῶν a bringing one's bail forward, Dem.
a putting down, calming, Arist.
intr. a standing firm, a settled condition, fixedness, Soph.
a state, condition, Hdt., Eur., etc.
a constitution, system, Hdt., Plat.
one must appoint, Plat., Xen.
an establisher, restorer, Soph.
fitted for calming: τὸ κ. a power to calm, of music, Plut.
to cover over, Hdt., Plat.
a covering, Hdt.
covered in, roofed, Hdt., Plat.
to tread down, κ. πέδον to tread the ground, Soph.
to put in order, arrange, Eur.
to keep down, repress, check, Eur., NTest.
to sigh over or lament, τινά Soph., Eur.; ὑπέρ τινος Eur.
to crown, Anth.
crowned, Soph.; of suppliant branches, wreathed with wool, Eur.
to deck with garlands, crown, wreath, Eur.; κ. νεκρόν (with libations), Id.; κ. τινά to supplicate him, Id.:—Pass., perf. inf., κατεστέφθαι Aeschin.
a condition or state of health, Plut.
established: sedate, Plut.
spotted, speckled, brindled, Eur.
Pass. to be brilliant, Greg.
to send beaming forth, σέλας Hhymn.
intr. to beam brightly, Anth.
to bewail, Anth.
to hurl down lightning, κατὰ τόπον upon a place, Soph.; absol., καταστράπτει it lightens, Plut.
trans. to strike with lightning, dazzle, τὰς ὄψεις Id.
to put into cantonments, encamp, Xen.: to station a fleet, Id.
Mid. to take up quarters, encamp, Id.
to turn down, trample on, Hhymn.: to turn the soil, Xen.
to upset, overturn, Ar.
Mid. to subject to oneself, to subdue, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; κατεστρέψατο ἐς φόρου ἀπαγωγήν subdued and made them tributary, Hdt.; so, Ἰωνίην κατεστρέψατο δασμοφόρον εἶναι Id.
Pass., in aor1 and perf., to be subdued, Id.; ἀκούειν σοῦ κατέστραμμαι am constrained to hear, Aesch.:—but the perf. pass. is also used in sense of Mid., Hdt., Dem.
to turn back, bring back, κατέστρεψε λόγους εἰς φιλανθρωπίαν Aeschin.
to turn round, bring to an end, Aesch.:—absol. to come to an end, die, Plut.
to twist up: metaph., λέξις κατεστραμμένη a close periodic style, opp. to a loose running style (εἰρομένη) Arist.
to behave wantonly towards, τινός NTest.
an overturning, Aesch.
a subduing, subjugation, reduction, Hdt., Thuc.
a sudden turn or end, a close, conclusion, Aesch.; of death, Soph., Thuc.: in drama, the catastrophe, Luc.
that which is spread over: in a ship, the deck, Hdt., Thuc.; οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν καταστρωμάτων the marines, opp. to the rowers, Thuc.

entry.note: and -ύω fut. -στρώσω aor1 pass. -εστρώθην part. fem. καστορνῦσα fut. -στορέσω
entry.sense: to lay low, Eur., Xen.:—Pass., κατέστρωντο οἱ βάρβαροι Hdt.
entry.etym: part. fem. καστορνῦσα as if from καταστόρνυμι
entry.sense: to over-spread or cover with a thing, τί τινι Il.
to spread upon, Od.
to throw down, lay low, Hdt.; καταστ. κύματα, Lat. sternere aequor, Anth.
to shudder at, abhor, abominate, Hom.
very hard or rugged, Hes.
to make sour: Pass., perf. part., τὸ κατεστυμμένον sourness, harshness, Plut.
Dep. to chatter: perf. part. κατεστωμυλμένος a chattering fellow, Ar.
to pull down, lay waste, ravage, Hdt.
to drag away, NTest.

entry.note: later -σφάττω fut. ξω Pass., aor2 κατεσφάγην
entry.sense: to slaughter, murder, Hdt.: Pass., Trag.
to hold back, Od., Soph.; κάσχεθε (epic for κατέσχεθε) , Il.
intr., Θορικόνδε κατέσχεθον they held on their way to Thoricum, Hhymn.
held back, Soph.
to dress up or invest with a certain form or appearance, Isocr., Plut.:—Mid. or Pass. to conform oneself, Plut.
to cleave asunder, split up, Ar.; Mid., κατεσχίσω τὸ ῥάκος Id.; κατασχ. τὰς πύλας to burst them open, Xen.
to pass the time in idleness, χρόνου τι κ. to tarry somewhat too long, Soph.
to rub in pieces, grind down, Hdt.
to draw up in order, arrange, τὴν στρατιάν Xen.
to appoint, ἐπί τι to do a thing, Dem.
κατατάξασθαί τινι to make arrangements with one, Id.
to stretch or draw tight, Il., Hdt.; κ. τὰ ὅπλα to draw the cables taut, Hdt.
to stretch so as to torture, Dem., etc.
to stretch or draw in a straight line, Hdt.
to hold tight down, Plut.
intr. to stretch oneself: hence,
to extend or run straight towards, Lat. tendere, Hdt., Xen.: absol. to extend, Hdt.
to strive against, strive earnestly, be vehement, Eur., Xen.: aor1 part., with all one's might, λέγω κατατείνας Plat.
to cut in pieces, cut up, Hdt., Ar., etc.: so in Mid., Eur.:— Pass., τελαμῶσι κατατετμημένοις with regularly cut bandages, Hdt.; σπλάγχνα κατατετμημένα Ar.
κ. χώρην ἐς διώρυχας to cut it up into ditches or canals, Hdt.; κατετέτμηντο τάφροι ἐπὶ τὴν χώραν Xen.
c. dupl. acc. κ. τινὰ καττύματα to cut him into strips, Ar.:—Pass., κατατμηθείην λέπαδνα may I be cut up into straps, Id.
κ. τὸν Πειραιᾶ to lay it out for building, Arist.:—Pass., ἡ πόλις κατατέτμηται τὰς ὁδοὺς ἰθείας has its streets cut straight, Hdt.
to cut into the ground, κατετέτμηντο τάφροι there were trenches cut, Xen.
trans. to melt away, to make to fall away, Hdt.
Pass., with perf. act. κατατέτηκα, to melt or be melting away, Od., Hdt., attic

entry.note: fut. -θήσω aor2 κατ-έθην epic form pl. κάτ-θεμεν epic form pl. κάτ-θετε epic form pl. κάτ-θεσαν inf. κατ-θέμεν 1st pl. subj. κατα-θείομεν Mid. κατ-θέμεθα, κατ-θέσθην subj epic . καταθείομαι subj epic . καταθείομαι subj. for καταθῶμαι part. κατ-θέμενος
entry.sense: to place, put, or lay down, Hom.

to propose as a prize, Id.; κ. ἄεθλον to propose a contest, Od.; κ. τι ἐς μέσον to put it down in the midst, i. e. for common use, Eur.; but, ἐς μέσον Πέρσῃσι κ. τὰ πρήγματα to communicate power to them, give them a common share of it, Hdt.
to put down as payment, pay down, Id., Ar., etc.:— to redeem a promise, ἃ δ’ ὑπέσχεο ποῖ καταθήσεις; Soph.
to lay up, lay by, Theogn., Hdt.; so in Mid., v. infr. II. 4.
Mid. to lay down from oneself, put off, lay aside, Lat. deponere, of arms or clothes, Hom., etc.
metaph. to put an end to, arrange, settle, τὸν πόλεμον Thuc.
to put aside, treat negligently, Xen.
to lay down in a place, Hes., etc.: of the dead, to bury, Od.

to deposit for oneself, lay up in store (v. supr. I. 4), Id., etc.: —metaph., κατατίθεσθαι κλέος to lay up store of glory, Hdt.; χάριτα or χάριν κατατίθεσθαί τινι or πρός τινα to lay up a store of gratitude or favour, Lat. collocare gratiam apud aliquem, Id., etc.; so, εὐεργεσίαν κ. Thuc., etc.
to deposit in a place of safety, Id., Xen.
to lay up in memory or as a memorial, Theogn., Plat.
to make dirt over, c. gen., Ar.
to wound severely, Xen.
to beggar by usurious interest:—Pass. to be thus beggared, Arist.
abscission, concision, as opp. to true circumcision, NTest.
to strike down with arrows, shoot dead, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
to cover with wounds, Hdt., Thuc.:—of ships, to disable utterly, cripple, Thuc.
to run down, Hdt., Xen.
of seamen, to run to land, to disembark in haste, Xen.:—metaph., κ. ἄστυ to come to a haven in . . , Pind.
trans. to overrun, ravage, χώραν Thuc.
to rub down or away; hence,
of clothes, to wear out, Theogn., Plat.
of persons, to wear out, exhaust, Thuc.: —Pass. to be quite worn out, Ar., Xen.
of Time, to wear it away, get rid of it, Lat. diem terere, Dem., Aeschin.: κ. τὸν βίον to employ it fully, Xen.; so in perf. pass. to pass one's whole time, κατατέτριμμαι στρατευόμενος Id.
of property, to squander, Id.
to squeak or scream loudly, Batr.
to chatter against, τινός Anth.
to wear out, exhaust, Hom., Theocr.:—Pass., κατατρυχόμενοι Eur.
to gnaw in pieces, eat up, Ar.; c. gen., Plut.
to hit one's mark, to be successful, Dem.
to shine upon: Mid. to gaze at, see, Anth.
a shining brightly, Plut.
to speak out, speak plainly, Soph.
to play upon the flute to, τινός Plat.:—Pass., of persons, to have it played to one, Id.:—Pass. to resound with flute-playing, Plut.
c. acc. pers. to overpower by flute-playing:—generally, to overpower, strike dumb, Eur.
Dep., to be under shelter of a hall, house, tent, Soph., Eur.
to exult in a thing, c. dat., Aesch.
to devour, eat up, Il., Hdt.
to spend in eating, waste, devour, Od., Aeschin.
to declare, make known, Pind.
Pass., fut. -φᾰνήσομαι, aor2 κατ-εφάνην [ᾰ], to become visible, appear, Hhymn., Hdt.
to be quite clear or plain, Hdt., Plat.; κατεφάνη τῷ Δαρείῳ τεχνάζειν it was apparent to Darius that he was playing tricks, Hdt.
clearly seen, in sight, Xen.; ἐν καταφανεῖ in an open place, Id.

manifest, evident, καταφανὲς ποιεῖν or ποιεῖσθαί τι Hdt., Xen.; καταφανέστερος εἶναι κακουργῶν Thuc.:—adv. -νῶς, evidently, plainly, Ar.; καταφανέστερον ἢ ὥστε λανθάνειν too manifestly to escape detection, Thuc.
to anoint with drugs or charms, to enchant, bewitch, Plat.
to bewitch with drugs, Hdt.
to protest, promise, Plut.
to depreciate, Plut.
going down, εὖτε ἂν κ. γίνηται ὁ ἥλιος when the sun is near setting, Hdt.; of ground, sloping downwards, Lat. declivis, Xen.
inclined, Lat. proclivis, pronus, πρὸς οἶνον Plut.
to bring down, ἄχος με κατοίσεται Ἄϊδος εἴσω grief will bring me down to the grave, Il.; καταφέρω ποδὸς ἀκμάν I bring down my foot, Aesch.:—Pass. to be brought down by a river, of gold dust, Hdt.
of a storm, to drive ships to land, Thuc.
to pay down, Plut.
Pass. to be weighed down by sleep, NTest.
to carry home, Ar.:—Pass. to return, Id.

to flee for refuge, Hdt.; c. acc., κ. βωμόν to flee for refuge to the altar, Eur.; κ. ἐν τόπῳ to flee and take refuge in a place, Xen.; to flee for protection, ὃς ἂν καταφυγῇ ἐς τούτους Hdt.; so, κ. ἐπί τινα, πρός τινα Dem.
ἐκ τῆς μάχης κ. to escape from . . , Hdt.
to have recourse to, εἰς τοὺς λόγους Plat.; ἐπὶ τὸν δικαστήν Arist.
εἰς τὴν τοῦ βίου μετριότητα to fall back upon, appeal to, Dem.
one must have recourse to, Luc.
flight for refuge, Thuc.
a place of refuge, Id.
to say yes, assent, Soph.
to spread a report abroad, announce, Pind.
to take first possession of, γῆν καταφθατουμένη Aesch.
to destroy or spoil utterly, bring to naught, Aesch., Soph., etc.
to waste away, decay, perish, Hdt., Trag.; κ. νόσῳ, γήρᾳ Soph., Eur.
Causal in fut. κατα-φθίσω [ῑ], aor1 κατ-έφθῐσα, to ruin, destroy, Od., Aesch.

Pass., epic aor2 κατ-εφθίμην [ῐ], inf. καταφθίσθαι; poet. καπ-φθίμενος:— to be ruined, to waste away, perish, ἤϊα πάντα κατέφθιτο the provisions were all consumed, Od.; ὡς καὶ σὺ καταφθίσθαι ὤφελες oh that thou hadst perished, Id.; σεῖο καταφθιμένοιο if thou wert dead, Il.; ἐκεῖ κατέφθιτο there he died, Aesch.; φέγγος ἡλίου κατέφθιτο the sun's light was gone, Id.
destruction, death, Eur.
metaph. confusion, φρενῶν Aesch.
to let slip down, κατηφίει (imperf.) Plat.
to kiss tenderly, to caress, Xen.
to burn down, burn up, consume, πυρί Il., Hes., etc.:—Pass. to be burnt down, Thuc.
to strike with fear, Thuc.:— Pass., c. fut. mid. to be greatly afraid of, τι Ar.; absol., καταφοβηθείς Thuc.
to come down constantly or regularly, as wild beasts from the mountains to prey, Hdt.
to slaughter, Hdt., Eur., etc.
of a river, to carry down gold dust, Hdt.
to pour like a stream over, τί τινος Plat.
to declare, Pind.:—Mid., with aor1 pass. and mid., to consider, think upon, ponder, Hes.; καταφρασθείς observed, Hdt.
shut up, confined, Soph.; πλοῖα κ. decked vessels, Thuc.
to think down upon, i. e. to look down upon, think slightly of, τινός Hdt., Eur., etc.
c. acc. to regard slightly, despise, Hdt., attic:—Pass. to be thought little of, despised, Xen., etc.
absol. to be disdainful, deal contemptuously, Thuc.
c. inf. to think contemptuously that, to presume, καταφρονήσαντες κρέσσονες εἶναι Hdt.; καταφρονοῦντες κἂν προαισθέσθαι Thuc.
c. acc. rei, only in ionic writers (cf. κατανοέω), to fix one's thoughts upon, aim at, Lat. affectare, τὴν τυραννίδα Hdt.: also to observe with contempt, τι Id.
contempt of others, μὴ φρόνημα μόνον, ἀλλὰ καταφρ. not only spirit, but a spirit of disdain, Thuc.
contempt, disdain, Thuc., Plat.
without any bad sense, opp. to αὔχημα, Thuc.
a despiser, Plut.
contemptuous, Arist. adv. -κῶς, Xen.
τὸ ἱμάτιον οὐκ ἀπολώλεκ’, ἀλλὰ καταπεφρόντικα I have not lost it, but I've thought it away, lost it in the schools, Ar.
to burn to ashes, Ar.
a refuge, place of refuge, Hdt., Eur.: c. gen., κ. κακῶν refuge from evils, Eur., Thuc.
a way of escape, excuse, Dem.
in tribes, by clans, Il.
to shed the leaves: metaph. to lose its splendour, Pind.
to plant, Plut., Luc.

entry.note: Pass., with aor2 act. κατ-έφυν perf. -πέφυκα
entry.sense: to be produced, Plut.
all planted with a thing, c. dat., Luc.
to catch in a theft: to catch in the act, detect, discover, Thuc., Xen.
detected: manifest, Plut.
to illuminate, light up, Anth.
to exult over, c. dat., Hdt.; absol., καταχαίρων with malignant joy, Id.
to shower down like hail upon, τί τινος Luc.
overlaid with brass or copper, Eur.; κατ. πεδίον ἀστράπτει the plain flashes with gleaming arms, Id.; δράκων κ. a serpent lapt in mail, i. e. scales, Id.
to cover with brass, Hdt.
Dep.
to do or give up a thing out of courtesy, Aeschin.; κ. τὰ δίκαια to give judgment by private interest, Plat.
to shew favour to a person, c. dat., Dem.
a mockery, Theogn.
to befoul, τινός Ar.

to vote against, to vote in condemnation of, τινός Dem.; c. inf., ἀδικεῖν Εὐάνδρου κατεχειροτόνησεν ὁ δῆμος Id.:—Pass., καταχειροτονηθὲν αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῦτα ἀσεβεῖν a vote of condemnation having been passed against him, and that for sacrilege, Id.
a vote of condemnation, Dem.

entry.note: fut. -χεῶ aor1 κατέχεα epic κατέχευα Pass., 3rd sg. epic aor2 κατέχῠτο Pass., 3rd pl. epic aor2 κατέχυντο
entry.sense: to pour down upon, pour over, τί τινι Hom.; also, κατ. τί τινος Hdt., attic:—Pass., κατὰ ταῖν κόραιν ὕπνου τι καταχεῖται a bit of sleep is poured over the eyes, Ar.
to pour or shower down, Hom.: to throw or cast down, Id.; πέπλον κατέχευεν ἐπ’ οὔδει let the robe fall upon the pavement, Il.
Pass. to be poured over the ground, lie in heaps, ὁ χῶρος, ἐν ᾧ αἱ ἄκανθαι [τῶν ὀφίων] κατακεχύαται (ionic 3rd pl. perf. pass.), Hdt.
to melt down, χρυσὸν ἐς πίθους Id.; and in Mid., χρυσὸν καταχέασθαι to have it melted down, Id.
epic imperf. mid., τέττιξ καταχεύετ’ ἀοιδήν, Hes.
derision, mockery, Ar.
to pass in widowhood, Dem.
sounding, Theocr.
subterranean, Ζεὺς καταχθόνιος, i. e. Pluto, Il.; δαίμονες κ. Dii Manes, Anth.
to mince up as for a sausage, Hdt.
to lavish as χορηγός: generally, to spend lavishly, squander, Plut.
Dep. to besprinkle, Anth.

entry.etym: perf. -κέχρημαι both in act. and pass. senses
entry.sense: Dep.
to make full use of, apply, c. dat., Plat., Dem.
to use to the uttermost, use up, c. acc., Dem.
to misuse, abuse, c. dat., Plat.
of persons, to make away with, destroy, kill, c. acc., Hdt.;—so aor1 καταχρησθῆναι, in pass. sense, Id.
to pretend, allege, Dem.
Act.

entry.etym: only in ionic writers in 3rd sg.
entry.sense: ἀντὶ λόφου ἡ λοφιὴ κατέχρα the mane sufficed them for a crest, Hdt.:—impers., οὐδέ οἱ καταχρήσει ὑμέων ἀπέχεσθαι nor will it suffice him to keep his hands off you, Id.
Pass. to be ill-treated, perf. part. κατηχρειωμένη Anth.
Dep. to spit upon, τινος Ar.
overlaid with gold-leaf, gilded, Luc.
to cover with gold-leaf, gild, Hdt.
to make golden (i. e. splendid), Plut.
to colour:— Pass. to be stained, Eur.
that which is poured over, sauce, Ar.
in pl. handfuls of nuts, figs, etc.; Lat. bellaria, which used to be showered over a bride or a new slave on entering the house (cf. Virg. sparge, marite, nuces), Ar., Dem.
to melt down, Dem.
to cover with a heap, ὁ νότος κατέχωσέ σφεας the South wind buried them in sand, Hdt.; κ. τινὰ λίθοις Ar.
to set in a place, place in position, Xen.:—Pass. to take up a position, Id.
Pass. to resound with music, Plut.
to stroke with the hand, to stroke, caress, καταψῶσα αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφαλήν Hdt.; καταψῶν αὐτὸν [τὸν κάνθαρον], ὥσπερ πωλίον Ar.
to wet by continual dropping, Aesch., Plut.
Dep., to tell lies against, speak falsely of, τινος Ar., Plat., etc.
to allege falsely against, τί τινος Plat., Dem.
to say falsely, pretend, Eur.: to feign, invent, τι Dem.
also as Pass. to be falsely reported: of writings, to be spurious, Plut.
to bear false witness against, τινός Xen.; so in Mid., Dem.:—Pass. to be borne down by false evidence, Plat.
Mid. to vote against or in condemnation of, τινος Plat., Xen.; κ. τινος κλοπήν to find him guilty of theft, Plat.; so in perf. pass., κατεψηφισμένοι αὐτοῦ θάνατον Xen.
Pass., in perf. and aor1 pass., to be condemned, Plat., Dem.:—of the sentence, to be pronounced against, δίκη κατεψηφισμένη τινός Thuc.; κατεψηφισμένος ἦν μου ὁ θάνατος Xen.
to vote in affirmation, Arist.
one must condemn, Xen.
to rub down, pound in a mortar: — Pass. to crumble away, perf. κατέψηκται Soph.
to stroke down, caress, Lat. mulceo, ἵππους Eur.
to cool, chill, Arist.:—Pass., perf. κατέψυγμαι, aor1 κατεψύχθην and 2 κατεψύγην [ῠ]·· — to be chilled, become cold, of persons, Id., Plut.
Pass., of a country, to be dried or parched up, Plut.

entry.etym: adverb from perf. pass. part. of καταβλᾱκεύω
entry.sense: slothfully, tardily, Ar., Anth.
to pledge, betroth, παῖδά τινι Eur.
as attic law-term, to make responsible, to compel to give security, Dem.: —Mid. or Pass. to give or find security, Id.
to seize as a security, Id.
bail or security given, Dem.
to eat up, devour, Il.; metaph., οἶκον, κτῆσιν κατέδειν to eat up house, goods, Od.; ὃν θυμὸν κατέδων eating one's heart for grief, Il.
to let flow down, shed, Od.:—Mid. to flow apace, Hom.; metaph., κατείβετο αἰών life ebbed, passed away, Od.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use, καθοράω being used instead
entry.sense: to look down, Il., Hdt., etc.
c. acc. to look down upon, Ar.: simply to behold, regard, perceive, Theogn., Aesch.; κατιδεῖν βίον to live, Aesch.—Also in aor2 mid. κατειδόμην, inf. κατιδέσθαι, Hdt., Soph.
full of idols, given to idolatry, NTest.
to liken:—Pass., aor1 κατ-εικάσθην, to be or become like, Soph.
to guess, surmise, Hdt.: to suspect evil, Id.
to force into a narrow space, to coop up, ἐς τὸ τεῖχος, ἐς τὸ ἄστυ Hdt.:—Pass., κατειλήθησαν ἐς Διὸς ἱρόν Id.; έν ὀλίγῳ χώρῳ πολλαὶ μυριάδες κατειλημέναι Id.
to cover up, Il.: Pass., ὄρος ψάμμῳ κατειλῡμένον (perf. part.) Hdt.
to go or come down, Hom., etc.:—esp. to go down to the grave, Il.; of a ship, to sail down to land, Od.; of a wind, to come sweeping down, Thuc.
to come back, return, Od.; of exiles, to return home, Hdt., attic

entry.etym: used as aor2 to καταγορεύω. (κατερῶ being the fut.)
entry.sense: to speak against or to the prejudice of, accuse, denounce, τινος Hdt., Eur., etc.
c. acc. to speak out, tell plainly, declare, report, Eur., Ar.
absol. to tell, Hdt., etc.; κάτειπέ μοι tell me, Ar.
to drive into, shut in, Hdt.:—generally, to press hard, reduce to straits, Id.:—Pass. to be hemmed in, kept down, Thuc.; τὸ κατειργόμενον what is done under necessity, Id.
to hinder, prevent, Eur.
Dep. to use irony towards, to dissemble, Plut.
to betray to one's own loss, Anth.
to draw down, Plut.
to convict of falsehood, to belie, Hes.
to disgrace, Pind.
to have compassion upon, τινά Plat.
to hope or expect confidently, Hdt.
to burn up, Eur.
Dep. to kill, slay, murder, Od.:—an aor2 act. κατήνᾰρον occurs in Soph., Anth.
over against, opposite, before, τινί Il., Hes.; τινός Hdt., etc.
to kill outright: aor1 pass. κατηναρίσθην Aesch.; perf. part. κατηναρισμένος Soph.
right over against, right opposite, c. gen., Il.
Pass. with aor2 act. κατ-εξανέστην, to rise up against, struggle against, τινός Plut.
to exercise lordship over, τινός NTest.
to make promises or engagements, τινι with one, Dem.; πρός τινα Aeschin.
to bring one thing quickly upon or after another, to repeat quickly, Ar.
to subdue by charms, τινά Plat.
to press down, depress, Il.
to press much, press hard, drive on, urge on, impel, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
intr. to hasten, make haste, Xen.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use
entry.sense: to kill, slay, Hom., Soph.
Mid. to effect by perjury, Dem.

entry.etym: perf. -είργασμαι both in act. and pass. sense
entry.sense: Dep.
to effect by labour, to achieve, accomplish, Hdt., Soph., etc.:—so perf. κατείργασμαι, Xen.; but in pass. sense, to be effected or achieved, Hdt., Eur.
to earn or gain by labour, to achieve, acquire, τὴν ἡγεμονίην Hdt.; σωτηρίαν Eur.; in pass. sense, ἀρετὴ ἀπὸ σοφίης κατεργασμένη Hdt.
absol. to be successful, Id.
c. acc. pers., like Lat. conficere, to make an end of, finish, kill, Id., Soph., Eur.
to overpower, subdue, conquer Hdt., Ar., Thuc.:—perf. pass. to be overcome, Thuc.; κατείργασται πέδον is subdued, brought under cultivation, Aesch.
to prevail upon, Hdt., Xen.: —aor1 pass., οὐκ ἐδύνατο κατεργασθῆναι could not be prevailed upon, Hdt.
to work up for use, Lat. concoquere, κ. μέλι to make honey, Id.
to grind down:—metaph., κ. θυμόν to fritter it away, smooth it down, Ar.:—Mid. to rend one's garments, in token of sorrow, Hdt., Aesch.
to throw or cast down, Orac. ap. Hdt.:—Pass. to fall in ruins, of Troy, Eur.
intr. in aor2 κατ-ήρῐπον, to fall down, fall prostrate, Il., Theocr.; so in perf., τεῖχος κατ-ερήριπεν Il.
to belch over, τινός Ar.
to cover over, roof, Plut.:—Mid. to roof over for oneself or what is one's own, Ar.

entry.etym: serving as fut. of the aor2 κατεῖπον
entry.sense: to speak against, accuse, τινός Xen., Plat.
c. acc. to denounce, Hdt.
to say or tell plainly, speak out, Id., Eur., etc.:— Pass., κατειρήσεται it shall be declared, Hdt.
to hold back, Hom., Soph.
bruised, ground, of pulse, Ar.
to hold back, detain, Hom., Theogn., Ar.:—Pass., κατερύκεται εὐρέϊ πόντῳ Od.
to draw or haul down, of ships, Lat. deducere naves, Od., Hdt.:—Pass., νηῦς τε κατείρυσται Od.
κ. τόξα to draw a bow, Anth.

entry.note: fut. κατελεύσομαι aor2 κατήλῠθον aor2 κατῆλθον inf. κατελθεῖν
entry.etym: fut. κατελεύσομαι, but in good attic κάτειμι
entry.sense: Dep.
to go down from a place, c. gen., Il.; to go down to the grave, κ. Ἄϊδος εἴσω, Ἄϊδόσδε Id.;—also from high land to the coast, Od.
of things, κατερχομένης ὑπὸ πέτρης by the descending rock, Id.; of a river, κατέρχεται ὁ Νεῖλος πληθύων comes down in flood, Hdt.
to come back, return, πόλινδε Od.: esp. to come back from exile, Hdt., attic; in pass. sense, ὑπό τινος κατελθεῖν to be brought back by him, Thuc.

entry.note: fut. κατέδομαι aor2 κατέφᾰγον perf. κατεδήδοκα epic κατέδηδα perf. pass. κατεδήδεσμαι
entry.sense: to eat up, devour, of animals of prey, Hom.; of men, to eat up, Od., Hdt.
to eat up or devour one's substance, Ar., Dem.
λίθοι κατεδηδεσμένοι ὑπὸ σηπεδόνος corroded, Plat.
always in pl. vows, Aesch.:— votive offerings, Soph.
imprecations, curses, Aesch., Eur.
to be quite successful, carry one's point, Aeschin.
straight forward, Xen.
to make or keep straight, to set right, guide aright, Plat.
intr. to make straight towards a point, Plut.

to put to bed, lull to sleep, Soph.; of death, Id.; ἐκτὸς αὐτὸν τάξεων κατηύνασεν assigned him quarters outside the army, Eur.; κ. τινὰ μόχθων to give one rest from . . , Anth.:—Pass. to lie down to sleep, Il.
one who conducts to bed, a chamberlain, Plut.
to put to sleep, Il.: metaph. to lull pain to sleep, Soph.:—Pass. to be asleep, Od.
to swear solemnly, Gorg. ap. Arist.
to be quite successful, Plut.
to put in order again, Xen.
to be quite successful, prosper, Plut.
to applaud, extol, Plut.
a prayer, vow, Aesch.
Dep. to pray earnestly, Hdt., Trag.; κ. τινι to pray to one, Aesch., Eur.
absol. to make a prayer or vow, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
in bad sense,
c. gen. pers. to pray against one, imprecate curses on one, Lat. imprecari, Plat.; also, κατ. τί τινι Aesch.; c. acc. et inf., Soph.
absol., Eur.
to boast that . . , Theocr.
Dep. to feast and make merry, Hdt.
Dep. to spring down upon, rush upon, κατεπάλμενος (aor2 part. syncop.) Il., Anth.
for κατ-έπαλτο, v. καταπάλλω.
Pass., with aor2 act. to rise up against, NTest.

entry.note: fut. καθέξω fut. κατασχήσω aor2 κατέσχον poet. κατέσχεθον epic 3rd sg. κάσχεθε
entry.sense: trans. to hold fast, Hes.
to hold back, withhold, Hom.:— to check, restrain, control, bridle, Hdt., attic: —Pass. to be held down, to be bound, kept under, Hdt.
to detain, Id., Xen.:—Pass. to be detained, to stay, stop, tarry, Hdt., Soph.
to have in possession, possess, occupy, Trag.
of sound, to fill, ἀλαλητῷ πεδίον κατέχουσι Il.; κ. στρατόπεδον δυσφημίαις to fill it with his grievous cries, Soph.
βιοτὰν κ. to continue a life, Id.
to occupy, be spread over, cover, νὺξ κάτεχ’ οὐρανόν Od.; ἡμέρα κατέσχε γαῖαν Aesch.:—in Mid., κατέσχετο πρόσωπα covered her face, Od.
of the grave, to confine, cover, Hom.
of conditions and the like, to hold down, overpower, oppress, afflict, Od., Soph.: —of circumstances, to occupy or engage one, Hdt.
to occupy, in right of conquest, Id., Soph., etc.
to master, understand, Plat.
in Pass., of persons, to be possessed, inspired, Xen., Plat.
to follow close upon, press hard, Lat. urgere, Xen.
to bring a ship to land, bring it in or to, Hdt.
intr.:
(sub. ἑαυτόν) to control oneself, Soph., Plat.:— to hold, stop, cease, of the wind, Ar.
to come from the high sea to shore, put in, Hhymn., Hdt., attic
to prevail, ὁ λόγος κατέχει the report prevails, is rife, Thuc.; σεισμοὶ κατ. earthquakes prevail, are frequent, Id.
to have the upper hand, Theogn., Arist.
Mid. to keep back for oneself, embezzle, Hdt.
to cover oneself, v. supr. A. II. 4.
to hold, contain, Polyb.
the aor. mid. is also used like a Pass., to be stopped, to stop, Od.:— κατασχόμενος subdued, Pind.
to speak against, to accuse, τινός Hdt.; κατά τινος Xen.
κ. τί τινος, to state or bring as a charge against a person, accuse him of it, Hdt., Soph., etc.

c. acc. rei only, to allege in accusation, allege, Lat. objicere, Eur., Xen., etc.:—Pass. to be brought as an accusation against, Soph., Thuc., etc.:—impers., c. inf., σφέων κατηγόρητο μηδίζειν a charge had been brought against them that they favoured the Medes, Hdt.; so, κατηγορεῖταί τινος ὡς βαρβαρίζει Xen.
absol. to be an accuser, appear as prosecutor, Ar., Plat.
to signify, indicate, prove, Lat. arguo, c. acc. rei, τι Xen.:c. gen. to tell of, Aesch.
an accusation, charge, Plat., Dem.
an accusation, charge, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
an accuser, Hdt., Soph.:— a betrayer, Aesch.
listening: as Subst. a listener, eaves-dropper, Hdt.
hearkening to, obeying, obedient, subject, Id., Soph.; τινός to another, Hdt.; also c. dat., Κύρῳ κ. Id.
giving ear to, εὐχωλῇσι Anth.
the upper story of a house, or a stair-case or ladder, Ar.
to make of small account, take no account of, neglect, Hdt.
a going down, descent, Anth.
hanging down, hanging on their mother's neck, of children, Eur.
to assuage, allay epic 3rd pl. imperf. pass., κατηπιόωντο Il.
to calm, appease, Xen.

covered over, vaulted, overhanging, Hom., Hes.; κ. πέτρος, of a cave, Soph.:— of trees, thick-leaved, Theocr.:— κ. πόδα τιθέναι to keep the foot covered, of Pallas when seated, and the robe falls over her feet, opp. to ὀρθὸν πόδα τ., when she steps forward, Aesch.
covered by a thing, c. dat., σπέος δάφνῃσι κατηρεφές shaded by laurels, embowered in them, Od.; τύμβῳ κ., i. e. buried, Soph.: —also c. gen., covered with or by a thing, Eur.
fitted out or furnished with a thing, c. dat., Eur.:—of ships, furnished with oars, πλοῖον κατῆρες a rowing boat, Hdt.; but, ταρσὸς κ. a well-fitted oar. Eur.
dejection, sorrow, shame, Il., Thuc.
to be downcast, to be mute with horror or grief, Hom., Eur.
with downcast eyes, downcast, mute, Od., Eur.
metaph. dim, obscure, dusk, Anth.
one who causes grief or shame, as Priam calls his sons κατηφόνες, dedecora, Il.
to sound a thing in one's ears, to teach by word of mouth, to instruct, Luc.:—Pass. to be informed, NTest.
in Christian writers, to instruct in the elements of religion, Id.
to harm, hurt, Od., Mosch.
to fill with mud or dirt, Xen.
to make to pine or waste away, Aesch.:—fut. mid. κατισχνᾰνεῖσθαι in pass. sense, Id.
to have power over, overpower, prevail against one, c. gen., NTest.
to come to one's full strength, Soph.
to hold back, Lat. detinere, Il., Hdt.:—Mid. to keep by one, Il.
to occupy: Pass. to be occupied, Od.
to direct or steer to a place, Id., Hdt., etc.
intr., to come down, Hdt.

entry.etym: perf.in pres. sense, plup. κατῄδη in imperf. sense
entry.sense: to know well, understand, Aesch., Soph.
c. acc. pers. to know by sight, recognise, Soph., Eur.
absol. οὐ κατειδώς unwittingly, Eur.
c. part. to know well that, Soph.; c. inf. to know how to do, Id.
to dwell in as a κάτοικος, to settle in, colonise, Hdt., Eur.: generally, to inhabit, Soph., Eur., etc.
absol. to settle, dwell, Soph., Eur., etc.:—so in perf. and plup. pass. to have been settled, to dwell, Hdt.
in Pass., of a state, to be administered, governed, Soph., Plat.
intr. of cities, to lie, be situate, Plat.
a settling in a place, Thuc.
a dwelling-place, abode, NTest.
a settlement, colony: the foundation of a colony, Plut.
living in or about a house, domestic, οἱ κατοικίδιοι home birds, Luc.

to remove to a place, plant, settle or establish there as colonists, κ. τινὰ εἰς τόπον Hdt., Ar.; γυναῖκας ἐς φῶς ἡλίου κατ. Eur.:—also, κ. τινὰ ἐν τόπῳ to settle or plant one in, Soph.; ἐλπίδας ἔν τινι κ. to plant them in his mind, Aesch.
c. acc. loci, to colonise, people a place, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
Pass.,
of persons, to be placed or settled, ἐν τόπῳ Hdt.; ἐς τόπον Thuc.
of places, to have colonies planted there, to be colonised, Id.
to bring home and re-establish there, to restore to one's country, Aesch.
a planting with inhabitants, foundation of a state, colonisation, Thuc., Plat.
to build upon or in a place, Xen.
to build away, i. e. to squander in building, Plut.
to manage well, Plut.
a settler, Aesch.
to ruin utterly, Plut.
to have mercy or compassion on, τινά Hdt., Soph., Eur., etc.
intr. to feel or shew compassion, Hdt.
Soph.:—Mid. to bewail oneself, utter lamentations, Hdt., Aesch.; so in aor1 pass. κατῳκτίσθην, Eur.;—c. acc. rei, as in Act., Aesch.
Causal, to excite pity, Soph.
compassion, Xen.
to bewail, lament, Eur.
Dep. to have gone down, οἱ κατοιχόμενοι the departed, dead, Dem.
to shrink from doing or undertaking, c. inf., Soph., Thuc.;—absol. to shrink back, Aesch., Thuc.
a being possessed, possession (i. e. inspiration), Plat.
capable of being possessed, Arist.
to slip or sink down, Luc.
to destroy utterly:—Pass., with perf. acc. to perish utterly, Aesch.
to shriek over a thing, c. gen., Aesch.
Dep. to bewail, c. acc., Eur., Xen.
Pass. to be rained on, drenched, Anth.
to confirm by oath, τί τινι Ar.; c. inf. to swear that . . , Dem.
c. acc. to call to witness, swear by, τὴν ἐμὴν ψυχήν Eur.:—so in Mid., Dem.
in Mid. also, c. gen. to take an oath against, accuse on oath, Hdt.
Dep. to censure bitterly, depreciate, abuse, Hdt.
very sharp, piercing, of sound, Ar.
to follow hard upon, Hes.
by consequence, behind, after, Theogn., attic:—c. gen., Ar., Plat.
of Time, after, Plat.
behind, after, in the rear, Hom.; c. gen., Od.
of Time, hereafter, afterwards, henceforth, Id.
to spy out, reconnoitre, Xen.:—Pass. to be observed, Soph.
a spy, scout, Hhymn., Hdt., Aesch., etc.
an overseer, τῶν πραγμάτων Aesch.
to be seen, visible, Thuc.
c. gen. in view of or looking down over, Aesch.
to shew as in a mirror:—Mid. κατοπτριζόμενοι τὴν δόξαν beholding as in a mirror, or rather reflecting as a mirror, NTest.
a mirror, Lat. speculum, Eur.
metaph. a mere reflexion (not a reality), Aesch.
to sound with music through, Anth.
celebrating orgies, Anth.
to initiate in orgies, Plut.
to set upright, erect, Eur.:—metaph. to keep straight, set right, Soph.
to accomplish successfully, bring to a successful issue, Plat., Dem.: —Pass. to succeed, prosper, Hdt., Eur.; δρᾶν κατώρθωσαι thou hast rightly purposed to do, Aesch.
intr. as in Pass. to go on prosperously, succeed, Thuc., Xen.; τὸ κατορθοῦν success, Dem.
a setting straight: successful accomplishment of a thing, success, Arist.
likely or able to succeed, Arist.
to rush downwards, Hhymn.
to be dismayed at, dread greatly, c. acc., Hdt.
absol. to be afraid, be in fear, Id.
to bury in the earth, Hdt.; ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν κατώρυξε buried head downwards, Id.; ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ Ar.
Dep. to dance in triumph over, treat despitefully, Lat. insultare, Hdt.
Dep. to contemplate, behold, Anth.

entry.etym: ionic for καθότι or καθ’ ὅ τι.

entry.sense: under the earth, Hhymn.
Pass. to cicatrise, heal over, Anth.
to bring into port with a fair wind: metaph., τάδ’ ὀρθῶς ἔμπεδα κατουρίζει the oracle brings these things safe to port or to fulfilment, or intr. these things come to fulfilment, Soph.
a holding fast, detention, Hdt.
possession by a spirit, inspiration, Plut.
holding down, holding fast, tenacious, Plut.
pass. kept down, held fast, overpowered, overcome, Aesch., Soph.; κάτοχος subject to him, Eur.
in sight of, opposite, τινος Eur.
to spend in eating, Aeschin.

entry.note: epic for κατ-ετάνυσαν 3rd pl. aor1 of κατατανύω.

entry.sense: from below, up from below, Aesch., Plat.:—also, from the low country, from the coast, Hdt.
below, beneath, where κάτω would be required by our idiom, Soph., Plat., etc.
to push down, Il.
head downwards, Ar.
from the shoulder, δίσκος κ. a quoit thrown from the shoulder, i. e. from the upturned hand held above the shoulder, Il.; cf. κατ-ωμᾰδόν
worn or borne on the shoulder, Anth.
from the shoulders, with the arm drawn back to the shoulder, Il.
an accusation on oath, Hdt.
with verbs of Motion, down, downwards, Hom., Hdt., attic
with Verbs of Rest, beneath, below, underneath, opp. to ἄνω, Hes.: —esp. in the world below, Soph., Plat.
geographically below, southward, Hdt.; but also, on the coast, Thuc.
as a prep. c. gen. under, below, Trag.
comp. κατωτέρω, lower, further, downwards, Ar.; c. gen. lower than, below, Hdt.
Sup. κατωτάτω, at the lowest part, Id.
sunk or imbedded in the earth, ἀγορὴ λάεσσι κατωρυχέεσς’ ἀραρυῖα (as if from κατωρυχής), Od.
underground, in caves, Aesch.; ἐκ κατώρυχος στέγης, i. e. from the grave, Soph.
as Subst., κατῶρυξ, a pit, cavern, Id.
a buried treasure, Eur.
lowest, Xen.: neut. pl. as adv., Hdt.
eating with the head down to the ground, gluttonous, Ar.
sunken, Xen.
Mt. Caucasus between the Euxine and Caspian, Hdt.; a gen. Καυκάσιος (as if from Καύκασις) Id.; τὸ Καυκάσιον ὄρος Hdt.
made of a stalk or stick, Luc.
stalk-fungi, Luc.
the shaft of a spear, Il.: the hilt of a sword, Id.
the stalk of a plat, Ar., etc.
burning heat, esp. of the sun, καύματος in the sun-heat, Il.; καῦμ’ ἔθαλπε Soph.
fever-heat, Thuc.:—metaph. of love, Anth.
to burn or scorch up, NTest.:—Pass. to be burnt up, Id.
a thick cloak, Ar.
fit for burning, combustible, Xen.
a burning, Hdt.:—in surgery, cautery, Plat.
Pass. to burn with intense heat, NTest.
fem. adj. burning hot, raging, in gen. καυστείρης κάχης Il.
burnt, red-hot, Eur.
of or from the river Cayster (in Lydia), Ar.
burning heat, NTest.
to cauterise, brand: metaph. in Pass., NTest.
a branding iron, Luc., NTest.
a burner, Pind.
to speak loud, be loud-tongued, Pind.: to boast or vaunt oneself, c. inf., to boast that, Hdt.:— c. acc. to boast of a thing, c. acc., NTest.
a boast, vaunt, Pind.
a subject of boasting, NTest.
boastful, Babr.
reason to boast, NTest.
to laugh aloud, Soph., Theocr. (Formed from the sound, cf. Lat. cachinnari.)
a bad habit of body, opp. to εὐεξία, Plat., etc.
living bad days, wretched, Anth.

entry.etym: redupl. form of χλάζω, only used in pres. and imperf.,
entry.sense: to plash, of wine poured into a cup, Pind.; of the sea, Aesch., Theocr.:—c. acc. cogn., κῦμα ἀφρὸν καχλάζον a wave frothing with foam, Eur.
a pebble in the beds of rivers:—collectively, gravel, shingle, Thuc.
entry.etym: Prob. akin to χάλιξ, Lat. calx, calculus.

entry.sense: unlucky harbourage, Anth.
parched barley, from which pearl-barley (ἄλφιτα) was made, Ar.
suspecting evil, suspicious, Plat.
to split, cleave wood, Od.; of lightning, to shiver, shatter, Id.; of a spear, κέασσε δὲ ὀστέα λευκά Il.; [κεφαλὴ] ἄνδιχα κεάσθη was cloven in twain, Id.
the redcap, redpoll, Ar.
of the size of a grain of millet, Luc.
millet-throwers, Luc.
millet, Hes., Hdt., etc.; of a single grain, Hdt.
anything in small grains, as the spawn of fish, Id.
things of the size of millet-grains:—in Eur., eyelet-holes in the rim of the shield, through which a soldier could view his enemy without exposing his person.
to break asunder, break up, scatter, Hom.:—Pass., κεδασθείσης ὑσμίνης when the battle was broken up, i. e. when the combatants were no longer in masses, Il.
careful, diligent, sage, trusty, Hom., Aesch., Eur.
pass. cared for, cherished, dear, Hom.
of things, κέδν’ εἰδυῖα knowing her duties, Od.; κ. φροντίς, βουλεύματα sage, wise, Aesch.; of news, good, joyful, Id.
cedar resin or oil, Hdt.
of cedar, Il., Eur.
the cedar-tree, Lat. cedrus, Od., Hdt.
anything made of cedar-wood; a cedar-coffin, Eur.; a cedar-box, for a bee-hive, Theocr.
cedar-oil, Luc.
made of or inlaid with cedar-wood, Eur.

to be laid (used as a Pass. to τίθημι), and so to lie, lie outstretched, Hom., etc.; ὁ δ’ ἐπ’ ἐννέα κεῖτο πέλεθρα lay stretched over nine plethra, Od.; κειμένωι ἐπεμπηδᾶν to kick him when he's down, Ar.
to lie asleep, repose, Hom., etc.:—also, to lie idle, lie still, Id.; ὑπὸ γαστέρ’ ἐλυσθεὶς κείμην of Ulysses under the ram's belly, Od.; κακὸν κείμενον a sleeping evil, Soph.
to lie sick or wounded, lie in misery, Hom., Soph., etc.; to lie at the mercy of the conqueror, Aesch.
to lie dead, like Lat. jacere, Hom., Hdt., Trag.
to lie neglected or uncared for, of an unburied corpse, Il.;—so also of places, to lie in ruins, Aesch.
of wrestlers, to have a fall, Id., Ar.
of places, to lie, be situated, Od., Hdt., attic
to be laid up, be in store, of goods, property, Hom.;—also of things dedicated to a god, Hdt.; of money, κείμενα deposits, Id.
to be set up, proposed, κεῖται ἄεθλον Il.; ὅπλων ἔκειτ’ ἀγὼν πέρι Soph.
of laws, κεῖται νόμος the law is laid down, Eur., Thuc.; οἱ νόμοι οἱ κείμενοι the established laws, Ar.; κεῖται ζημία the penalty is fixed by law, Thuc.
of names, κεῖται ὄνομα the name is given, Hdt., Xen.
metaph., πένθος ἐνὶ φρεσὶ κεῖται grief lies heavy on my heart, Od.; ταῦτα θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται, i. e. these things are yet in the power of the gods, to give or not, Il.
κεῖσθαι ἔν τινι to rest entirely or be dependent on him, Pind.; θεῶι κείμεθα Soph.
to be so and so, Hdt., Aesch.:—simply, to be, νεῖκος κ. τισι there is strife between them, Soph.
anything stored up as valuable, a treasure, heirloom, Hom., Hdt., Soph., Eur.
anything stored up as valuable, a treasure, heirloom, Hom., Hdt., Soph., Eur., etc.
the cord or girth of a bedstead, Lat. instita, Ar.
in pl. swathings, grave-clothes, NTest.

to cut the hair short, shear, clip, Il., Hdt., Eur.:— Mid. to cut off one's hair or have it cut off, as in deep mourning, Hom., Eur., etc.:—Pass., βοστρύχους κεκαρμένος having one's locks cut off, Eur.; κεκάρθαι τὰς κεφαλάς to have their heads shorn, in sign of mourning, Hdt.: of the hair, to be cut off, Pind.
to cut or hew out, Il.; ὕλην Soph.

to ravage a country, by cutting down the crops and fruit-trees, Hdt., Thuc.:—Pass., of a country, to be ravaged, Thuc.:—Mid., Ἄρης πλάκα κερσάμενος having had the plain swept clean (by destroying the men), Aesch.
generally, to destroy, and so,
to tear, eat greedily, Lat. depasci, of beasts, Hom.; ἔκειρε πολύκερων φόνον, i. e. he slaughtered many a horned beast, Soph.
of the suitors, to consume, waste one's substance, Od.
βῆ δ’ ἰμέναι κείων he went to lie down, went to bed, Od.; ἴομεν κείοντες Il.
to cleave, Od.
to cleave, radic. form of κεάζω, Od.

entry.etym: an epic perf. part. with no pres. in use
entry.sense: only found in phrase κεκαφηὼς θυμόν breathing forth one's life, Lat. animam agens, Hom.—Commonly referred to κάπτω.
a scream, cry, Ar.
a bawler, Ar.
he who conquers all in bawling, the blusterer, Ar.
a mythical king of Athens, Hdt.: hence
adj. Κεκρόπιος, η, ον Cecropian, Athenian, πέτρα K. the Acropolis, Eur.; (also simply Κεκροπία, ἡ, used for Athens itself, Id.); K. χθών Attica, Id.; Κεκρόπιοι, οἱ, the Athenians, Anth.
fem. Κεκροπίς, name of a tribe, Ar.
Κεκροπίδαι, οἱ, the Athenians, Hdt., Eur.
a woman's head-dress of net, to confine the hair, Lat. reticulum, Il., Anth.
part of the headstall of a bridle, Xen.
the pouch or belly of a hunting-net, Id., Plut.
sounding, noisy, Il.; epith. of Artemis, from the noise of the chase, Hom.:—doric κελαδεννός, Pind.
to sound as rushing water, Orac. ap. Aeschin.:— to shout aloud, in applause, Il.; κ. παιᾶνα to sound the loud paean, Eur.
of various sounds, to utter a cry, cry aloud, Aesch., Ar., etc.; of bells, to ring, tinkle, Eur.; of the flute, κ. φθόγγον κάλλιστον Id.
trans. to sing of, celebrate loudly, τινά Pind., Eur., etc.
a rushing sound, Eur., Ar.
loud-sounding, Pind.
a noise as of rushing waters: a loud noise, din, clamour, Il.
a loud clear voice, a shout, cry, Aesch., Soph., etc.
the sound of music, Eur.
sounding, roaring, Hom., Theocr.
with black (i. e. bloody) spear, Pind.
black with clouds, of Zeus, shrouded in dark clouds, cloudwrapt, Hom.:—generally, dark-coloured, αἷμα Id.; πεδίον κ. black, rich soil, Pind.
black and bloody with gnawing, Aesch.
Pass. to grow black or dark, Aesch.
black, swart, dark, murky, Hom., etc.
black-gleaming, ὄρφνα κ. murky twilight, Ar.
black-hearted, Aesch.
black-coloured, Anth.
black-faced, swarthy, gloomy, Soph.: fem., κελαινῶπις Pind.
to murmur, of running water, Hom.; doric 3rd sg. imperf. κελάρυσδε Theocr.
a cup, jar, pan, Theocr.
the beams in the upright loom of the ancients, between which the web was stretched, Theocr.
a wayfarer, Anth.
road-making, Aesch.
a wayfarer, Anth.

a road, way, path, track, Hom., etc.; ὑγρὰ κέλευθα, ἰχθυόεντα κέλευθα, of the sea, Od.; ἀνέμων κέλευθα or κέλευθοι Hom.; ἐγγὺς γὰρ νυκτός τε καὶ ἤματός εἰσι κέλευθοι i. e. night and day follow closely, Od.; ἄρκτου στροφάδες κ. their paths or orbits, Soph.
a journey, voyage, Hom.; πολλὴ κ., i. e. a great distance, Soph.
an expedition, Aesch.
a way of going, walk, gait, Eur.:—metaph. a way of life, Aesch., Eur.

an order, command, behest, Aesch., Soph., etc.; a call, summons, Aesch.:— the word of command in battle, Hdt.; also the call of the κελευστής (q. v.), which gave the time to the rowers, ἀπὸ ἑνὸς κελεύσματος all at once, Thuc.; ἐκ κελεύσματος at the word of command, Aesch.
an order, command, Eur.
the signalman on board ship, who gave the time to the rowers, Eur., Thuc.
ordered, commanded, Luc.

entry.etym: Frequentat. of κελεύω, as πνευστιάω from πνέω
only used in epic part. (dual), κελευτιόωντε
entry.sense: continually urging on [the men], Il.

to urge or drive on, urge, exhort, bid, command, order, Hom., etc.: c. acc. pers. et inf. to order one to do, Il.; (also c. dat. pers., Hom.):—c. acc. pers. et rei, τί με ταῦτα κελεύεις (sc. ποιεῖν); also c. acc. pers. only, θυμός με κελεύει (sc. φείδεσθαι) Od.; ἐκέλευσε τοὺς ἕνδεκα ἐπὶ τὸν Θηραμένην ordered them [to go] against him, ordered them to seize him, Xen.; c. acc. rei only, to command a thing, Aesch.:—Pass., τὸ κελευόμενον, τὰ -να, commands, orders, Xen.
a courser, riding-horse, Od., Hdt., etc.
a fast-sailing yacht with one bank of oars, a light vessel, Lat. celox, Hdt., Thuc.
to ride, of one who rides one or more horses, leaping from one to the other, Il.
to drive on, νῆα κέλσαι to run a ship to land, put her to shore, Lat. appellere, Od.:—metaph., Ἄργει κ. πόδα Eur.
intr., of ships or seamen, to put to shore or into harbour, Od., Aesch., etc.:—metaph., πᾶ ποτε κέλσαντ’ having reached what port? Aesch.; πᾶ κέλσω; where shall I find a haven? Eur.
to urge on, exhort, command, in Hom.; constructed like κελεύω.
much like καλέω, to call, call to, Il.: also, to call on for aid, Soph.
to call by name, call, Pind.
Celtic, Gallic, fem. Κελτίς, ίδος, Anth.
in the language of the Celts, Luc.
the Kelts or Celts, Hdt., Xen.
a sheath, case, pod, shell, Arist.: the hollow of the eye, Anth.
metaph. of old dicasts, ἀντωμοσιῶν κελύφη mere affidavit- husks, Ar.;—of an old man's boat, which served as his coffin, Anth.
son, Eur.
a young deer, a pricket, Il.:—also κεμμάς, Anth.
emptying vessels: breeding famine, Aesch.
lack of men, dispeopled state, Aesch.
empty of men, dispeopled, Aesch., Soph.
vain-glorious, Il.
dead: κενέβρεια, τά, carrion, dog's-meat, Ar.
to step on emptiness, step into a hole, Plut., Luc.
empty-minded, Theogn., Pind.
the hollow below the ribs, the flank, Hom., Xen.
any hollow, a glen, Anth.
toothless, Anth.
to talk emptily, Arist.
of things, empty, opp. to πλέως or πλήρης, Hom., Hdt., attic
metaph. empty, vain, κενὰ εὔγματα Od.; κ. ἐλπίς Aesch., etc.:—in adverbial usages, neut. pl., κενεὰ πνεύσας Pind.; διὰ κενῆς to no purpose, in vain, Ar., Thuc.
of persons,
c. gen. void, destitute, bereft, τοῦ νοῦ, φρενῶν Soph.; συμμάζων Eur.
empty-handed, Hom., Hdt., attic:— bereft of her mate, λέαινα Soph.: — empty of wit, empty-headed, Id., Ar.
comp. and Sup. κενώτερος, -ώτατος, Plat., etc.
to honour with an empty tomb, Eur.
an empty tomb, cenotaph, Xen.
emptiness, vanity, Plat.
emptiness of mind, Plut.
empty-minded, Aesch.
vain talking, babbling, NTest.

to empty out, drain, opp. to πληρόω, Aesch., Eur., etc.; c. gen. to empty of a thing:— Pass. to be emptied, made or left empty, Soph.; ἐς τὸ κενούμενον into the space continually left empty, Thuc.; c. gen., κεκεινωμένος πάντων stripped of all things, Hdt.
to make a place empty by leaving it, desert it, Eur.
metaph. to make empty, to make of no account or of no effect, NTest.:—Pass. to be or become so, Id.
Centaurian, of Centaurs, Eur.
of or from Centaurs, ἵππος K. a Thessalian horse, Luc.
like a Centaur, i. e. savage, brutal: adv. -κῶς, Ar.
a battle of Centaurs, Plut.
full of Centaurs, Eur.
a Centaur: the Centaurs were a savage Thessalian race, between Pelion and Ossa, extirpated in a war with their neighbours the Lapithae, Hom.
in later Poets they are monsters of double shape, half-man and half-horse, Pind., etc.

entry.etym: epic inf. κένσαι as if from κέντω
entry.sense: to prick, goad, spur on, Il., Ar.
of bees and wasps, to sting, Ar., Theocr.
generally, to prick, stab, Pind., Soph., etc.: to torture, Xen.: metaph., σὺν δόλωι κ. to stab in the dark, Soph.
spurred or goaded on, Il.
to prick, goad or spur on, Xen.; metaph., ἔρως κ. Id.
madly spurring, or spurring to madness, Anth.
any sharp point:
a horsegoad, Lat. stimulus, Il., etc.: also an ox-goad, Plat.; —proverb., πρὸς κέντρα λακτίζειν, v. λακτίζω 2.
metaph. a goad, spur, incentive, Aesch., Eur.
an instrument of torture, Hdt.:—metaph. in pl. tortures, pangs, Soph.
the sting of bees and wasps, Ar.; of a scorpion, Dem.; metaph. of the impression produced by Socrates, ὥσπερ μέλιττα τὸ κ. ἐγκαταλιπών Plat.
the stationary point of a pair of compasses, the centre of a circle, Id.
struck by the goad, Anth.
to furnish with a sting:— Pass. to be so furnished, to sting, Plat.
to strike with a goad, Hdt.
one that bears the marks of the κέντρον, a rogue that has been put to the torture, Ar.
the Lat. Centurio, NTest.
a goader, driver, Il.
an emptying, Plat.
a sea-bird:—metaph. a booby, Ar.
any thing projecting like a horn; a yard-arm, (as Lat. cornua antennarum), Aesch., Thuc., etc.
the projecting beam of a crane, Thuc.
a branching stake of wood, Plut.:— of the forked ends of the ancilia, Id.
the apex of a letter, a dot, tittle, NTest.
the projecting spur of a mountain, Anth.
a bow of horn, Id.
to ravage, despoil, plunder, Hom., Hdt.
of ships, to sink or disable them, Hdt.
of living beings, to assail fiercely, to slaughter, Il., Hdt.
to carry off as plunder, Hdt.
a ravager, robber, Hhymn.
ζωρότερον κέραιε, mix the wine stronger, Il.
the potter's art or craft, Plat.
the potter's quarter: in Athens two places were called Cerameicus, one within and the other without the Dipylon or Thriasian Gate, Thuc., etc.
a potter's work-shop, Aeschin.
name of an Attic deme, Ar., etc.
of clay, earthen, Plat.
a potter, Lat. figulus, Il.: —proverb., κεραμεὺς κεραμεῖ κοτέει ‘two of a trade never agree,’ Hes.
Κεραμεῖς, Att. Κεραμῆς, οἱ, name of an Attic deme, Ar., etc.
to be a potter, work in earthenware, Plat., etc.
c. acc., κ. τὸν κεραμέα to make a pot of the potter, Id.
of or for pottery, Xen., etc.
an earthenware vessel, a jar, Lat. testa, Hdt., Xen.
a roof-tile or coping tile, Ar., Thuc.
potter's earth, potter's clay, Plat.
anything made of this earth, as,
an earthen vessel, wine-jar, Il., Hdt.: also in collective sense, pottery, Ar.; κ. ἐσάγεται πλήρης οἴνου jars full of wine, Hdt.
a tile, and in collective sense, the tiles, tiling, Ar., Thuc.
a jar, used to confine a person in, Il.
to mix, mingle, (cf. κρᾶσις):

mostly of diluting wine with water, Od., attic;—so in Mid., ὅτε περ οἶνον κέρωνται when they mix their wine, Il.; κρητῆρα κεράσσατο he mixed him a bowl, Od.:—Pass., κύλιξ ἴσον ἴσωι κεκραμένη a cup mixed half and half, Ar.
to temper or cool by mixing, θυμῆρες κεράσασα having mixed (the water) to an agreeable temperature, Od.

generally, to mix, blend, temper, regulate, Lat. tempero, of climates, ὧραι μάλιστα κεκραμέναι most temperate seasons, Hdt.; οὐ γῆρας κέκραται γενεᾶι no old age is mingled with the race, i. e. it knows no old age, Pind.:—of tempers of mind, Plat.
generally, to mix, compound, Lat. attempero, ἔκ τινος of a thing, Id.; φωνὴ μεταξὺ τῆς τε Χαλκιδέων καὶ Δωρίδος ἐκράθη Thuc.
polishing or working horn, esp. for bows, Il.
horned, Hom., Theocr.
of horn, made of horn, Anth.
the horn of an animal, as of oxen, Il.; ὀφθαλμοὶ δ’ ὡσεὶ κέρα ἔστασαν his eyes stood fixed and stiff like horns, Od.
horn, as a material, αἱ μὲν γὰρ [αἱ πύλαι] κεράεσσι τετεύχαται, of the horn doors, through which the true dreams came, Id.
anything made of horn,
a bow, Il., Hom., Theocr.
of musical instruments, a horn for blowing, Xen.: a flute, Luc.
a drinking-horn, Xen.
βοὸς κ. a horn guard or pipe to which the leadweight (μολύβδαινα) of a fishing-line was attached, Hom.
κέρατα the horn points with which the writing-reed was tipped, Anth.
an arm or branch of a river, Hes., Thuc.

the wing of an army or fleet, Hdt., attic; κατὰ κέρας προσβάλλειν, ἐπιπίπτειν to attack in flank, Thuc., Xen.; ἐπὶ κέρας ἄγειν to lead towards the wing, i. e. in column, not with a broad front, Lat. agmine longo, Hdt., attic
any projection, e. g. a mountain-peak, Xen.
horned, ἔλαφος Soph., Eur.:—fem. κεραστίς, ίδος, of Io, Aesch.
mixed, mingled, Anth.
horn-bearing, horned, Eur.
the carob or locust-tree (Arab. kharoob):—its fruit
is called St. John's bread, from a notion that it was the fruit he ate in the wilderness, NTest.
of horn, Xen.

entry.etym: Dim. of κέρας, v. sub κερατέα.

entry.sense: made of horns, Plut.
wielding the thunder, Anth.
of a thunderbolt, Aesch., Eur.
thunder-smitten, Soph., Eur.
to hurl the thunderbolt, Anth.
trans. to strike therewith, Il.
hurling the thunder, Anth.
pass. thunder-stricken, Eur.
the lightener and thunderer, Ar.
fighting with thunder, Anth.
a thunderbolt, Lat. fulmen, Hom., etc.: generally, thunder:—but thunder properly was βροντή, Lat. tonitru; lightning was στεροπή, Lat. fulgur.
metaph., κεραυνὸν ἐν γλώσσῃ φέρειν, of Pericles, Plut.
flashing like thunder, Eur.
wielding the thunderbolt, Plut.
to strike with thunderbolts, Hdt.:— Pass., κεραυνωθείς Hes., Plat., etc.

entry.etym: epic radic. form of κεράννυμι, part. κερῶν Od.; Mid., in imperat. κεράασθε, Id.; 3rd pl. imperf. κερόωντο Il.

entry.sense: Cerberus, the fifty-headed dog of Hades, which guarded the gate of the nether world, Hes.; later, with three heads or bodies, Eur.

to gain, derive profit or advantage, κακὰ κ. to make unfair gains, Hes.; κ. ἔκ or ἀπό τινος Hdt., attic; πρός τινος Soph.; τί κερδανῶ; what shall I gain by it? Ar.:—c. part. to gain by doing, οὐδὲν ἐκμαθοῦσα κερδανεῖς Aesch., etc.
absol. to make profit, gain advantage, Hdt., attic:— to traffic, make merchandise, Soph.; κ. ἔπη to receive fair words, Id.
like ἀπολαύω, to gain a loss, reap disadvantage from a thing, as, δάκρυα κ., Eur.; κ. ζημίαν NTest.
having an eye to gain, wily, crafty, cunning, Hom.:—of the fox, Archil. ap. Plat.
of things, gainful, profitable, κερδαλεώτερον Hdt.:— τὸ κ. = κέρδος, Aesch., Thuc.: adv. -λέως, to one's advantage, Thuc.
crafty-minded, Il.

entry.etym: comp. with no Posit. in use, formed from κέρδος
entry.sense: more profitable, Hom., etc.
κέρδιστος, η, ον, Sup. most cunning or crafty, Il.
of things, most profitable, Aesch., Soph.
gain, profit, advantage, Lat. lucrum, Od.; ποιεῖσθαί τι ἐν κέρδει, Horace's lucro apponere, Hdt.; so, κέρδος ἡγεῖσθαι or νομίζειν τι Eur., Thuc.
desire of gain, love of gain, Find., Trag.
in pl. cunning arts, wiles, tricks, Hom.
like κερδαλεότης, cunning, craft: dat. κερδοσύνῃ as adv., by craft, cunningly, Hom.

entry.etym: κερδῷος I from κέρδος, κερδῳος II from κερδώ
entry.sense: bringing gain, of Hermes, Luc., etc.
foxlike, wily, Babr.
the wily one, i. e. the fox, Pind., Ar.
(sc. τέχνη) the art of the shuttle-maker, Arist.
to make the web close with the κερκίς, Plat.
in the loom, the rod or comb by which the threads of the woof were driven home, so as to make the web even and close, Hom., Soph., etc.
any rod, a measuring-rod, Anth.
the great bone of the leg, the tibia, Plut.
the tail of a beast, Ar., Plat., etc.
a light vessel, boat, esp. of the Cyprians, Hdt.
the island Corcyra, now Corfu, Hdt., etc.: —adj. Κερκυραῖος, η, ον Corcyraean, Id., etc.:— τὰ Κερκυραϊκά, the affairs of Corcyra, Thuc.
