entry.sense: a witness, Hes., Theogn.; μάρτυρα θέσθαι τινά Eur.; μ. θεοὺς ποιεῖσθαι Thuc.; μάρτυρι χρῆσθαί τινι Arist.; μάρτυρας παρέχεσθαι to produce witnesses, Plat., etc.; so, μ. παριστάναι Xen.
Dep. to chew, Ar.
a leather strap, thong, Soph.:—metaph. a supple knave, Ar.
Lat. Massilia, Marseilles, Thuc., etc.: the Marseillais were Μασσαλιῶται, or -ῆται, ῶν, οἱ, Dem., etc.

entry.etym: irreg. comp. of μακρός or μέγας
entry.sense: longer, greater, Od.; μάσσον’ ἢ ὡς ἰδέμεν greater than one could see, Pind.; τὰ μάσσω anything more, Aesch.
to handle, touch, in Mid., Anth.: cf. ἐπιμαίομαι.
to work with the hands, to knead dough, Lat. pinso, Ar.; also in Mid., Hdt., Ar.; metaph., μάττειν ἐπινοίας Ar.:—Pass., μᾶζα ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ μεμαγμένη Id.; σῖτος μεμαγμένος dough ready kneaded, Thuc.
that with which one chews, the mouth, Od.
that which is chewed, a mouthful, morsel, Il., Theocr.
only in pres., to mumble, of an old man, Ar.
to seek, search, Eur.
c. acc. to seek or search after:—to crave, need, Pind., Aesch., Xen.
c. inf. to seek or strive to do, Pind., Eur., Xen.
a seeker, searcher, one who looks for, τινος Soph., Eur.
one that always wants whipping, a worthless slave, a sorry knave, Lat. verbero, Ar., Plat.
a scourge-bearer, a sort of policeman, Thuc.

entry.etym: Mid. fut. μαστιγώσομαι in Pass. sense
entry.sense: to whip, flog, Hdt., Plat.
that deserves whipping, Luc.
deserving a whipping, Ar.
to whip, flog, Il., Theocr.: c. inf., μάστιξεν δ’ ἐλάαν (v. ἐλαύνω I. 2), Hom.
a scourger, Aesch.

entry.etym: from same Root as ἱμάς, μάσθλης
entry.sense: a whip, scourge, Hom., Hdt., etc.; ἵππου μ. a horsewhip, Hdt.; ὑπὸ μαστίγων βαίνειν to advance under the lash, of soldiers flogged on, Id.; so, τοξεύειν ὑπὸ μ. Xen.
metaph. a scourge, plague, Il., Aesch.; διπλῇ μ., τὴν Ἄρης φιλεῖ, i. e. fire and sword, Aesch.; μ. Θεοῦ of sickness, NTest.
to gnash the teeth, epic part. μαστιχόων, Hes.
to whip, scourge, Il.:—Mid., οὐρῇ πλευρὰς μαστίεται [the lion] lashing his sides with his tail, Il.
a breast-band, Anth.
one of the breasts, δεξιτερὸν παρὰ μαζόν Il.; βάλε στέρνον ὑπὲρ μαζοῖο struck his chest above the breast, Id.; βάλε στῆθος παρὰ μαζόν Id.
esp. a woman's breast, μαζὸν ἀνέσχε, of Hecuba mourning over Hector, Id.; παῒς δέ οἱ ἦν ἐπὶ μαζῷ Od.; προσέσχε μαστόν, of the mother, Aesch.; of animals, the udder, Eur.
metaph. a round hill, knoll (French mamelon), Pind., Xen.
a piece of wool fastened to the edge of nets, Xen.
a pandaring, Xen.
to play the pandar, Xen.; μ. τινὰ πρὸς τὴν πόλιν to seduce one into public life, Id.
a pandar, Lat. leno, lena, Ar.; metaph., Xen.
the armpit, Lat. ala, axilla, Ar., etc.
a bay, Strab.
to put under the arm-pits: hence, to mutilate a corpse, since murderers had a fancy, that by cutting off the extremities and placing them under the arm-pits, they would avert vengeance, Aesch., Soph.
a broad strap passing round the horse and fastened to the yoke by the λέπαδνον: generally, a girth, girdle, band, Hdt., Aesch.
to speak or work folly, Soph.; σπλάγχνα δ’ οὐ ματᾴζει my heart is not deceived, Aesch.
to talk idly, at random, Strab.
talking idly, at random, NTest.
labour in vain, Strab., Luc.
labouring in vain, Philo.
vain, empty, idle, trifling, frivolous, Theogn., Hdt., attic
thoughtless, rash, irreverent, profane, impious, Aesch.; τὸ μὴ μάταιον seriousness, gravity, Id.
adv. -ως, idly, without ground, Soph.
to be idle, to dally, loiter, linger, Il.; οὐ ματᾷ τοὖργον the work lags not, Aesch.; ματᾶν ὁδῷ to loiter by the way, Id.; φροίμιον ματᾷ is in vain, Id.
to seek, search, Il., Soph.
c. acc. pers. to seek after, seek for, search after, properly of hounds casting for the scent, Aesch.; then generally, Id., Soph., etc.
c. inf. to seek or strive to do, Pind., Soph.
c. acc. loci, to search, explore, Theocr.
in vain, idly, fruitlessly, Lat. frustra, Hhymn., Pind., attic; μ. ὁ μόχθος in vain the labour, Aesch.; with a Noun, τὸ μ. ἄχθος the fruitless burthen, Id.
at random, without reason, Lat. temere, Theogn., Hdt., attic; ὁ νοσῶν μ., of a madman, Soph.
idly, falsely, Lat. falso, Id.; μ. βέβακεν, of a dream, Aesch.
a folly, a fault, Aesch.
a vain attempt, Od.
a devourer of meal, Ar. (A dubious word, said to be derived from μάτιον a measure of meal. Others read ματτυό-λοιχος, a licker up of dainties.)
a dainty dish, Menand.: v. ματιολοιχός.
to darken, to blind, make powerless, Pind., Aesch.
metaph. to make dim or obscure, or forgotten, Hes.:—Pass. to become dim or obscure, Theogn., Aesch.
tomb of Mausolus at Halicarnassus, and, as appellat. a mausoleum, Strab.
a king of Halicarnassus, husband of Artemisia, Hdt.
a large knife or dirk, worn by the heroes of the Iliad next the sword-sheath, Il.: generally, a knife for cutting up meat, Hdt., attic
as a weapon, a short sword or dagger, Hdt., etc.: a sabre or bent sword, opp. to the straight sword (ξίφος), Xen.
a kind of rasor, μιᾷ μαχαίρᾳ with the rasor's single blade, opp. to διπλῆ μ. scissars, Ar.
a rasor, Ar., Luc.
a cutler's factory, Dem.
a cutler, Ar., Dem.
a cutler's shop, Plut.
wearing a sabre, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
Machaon, son of Aesculapius, the first surgeon that we hear of, Il.
one must fight, Arist.
warlike, Il., Anth.

battle, fight, combat, Hom., etc.; μάχαι ναῶν sea fights, Pind.:—with Verbs, μάχην μάχεσθαι to fight a battle, Il., attic; μάχην ἀρτύνειν, ἐγείρειν, ὀρνύμεν, ὀτρύνειν Il.; μάχην συνάπτειν or συμβάλλειν τινί to engage battle with one, Aesch., Eur.; also, διὰ μάχης τινὶ ἀπικέσθαι, ἔρχεσθαι, ἥκειν, μολεῖν Hdt., attic; μάχην νικᾶν to win a battle, Xen.:— μάχη τινός battle with an enemy, Il., etc.
in pl. quarrels, strifes, wranglings, Id., Plat.
= ἀγών, a contest for a prize in the games, Pind.: generally a struggle, Xen.
a mode of fighting, way of battle, Hdt., Xen.
a field of battle, Xen.
a fighter, warrior, Hom.: doric adj., μαχᾱτάς, warlike, Pind.
inclined to battle or war, quarrelsome, Arist.:— μ. ἵπποι restive horses, Plat.
to be fought with, Od.
fit for battle, warlike, Hdt., attic; οἱ μ. the fighting men, soldiery, and in Egypt the warrior-caste, Hdt.; τὸ μ. the effective force, Thuc.
warlike, quarrelsome, Anth.
lewd, lustful, Hes., Luc.
metaph. wanton, luxuriant, insolent, Aesch.
lewdness, lust, wantonness, Il., Hdt.

to fight, Hom., etc.; c. dat. pers. to fight with, i. e. against, one, Id., etc.; μ. ἀντία and ἐναντίον τινός Il.; ἐπί τινι, πρός τινα Id.; but, μ. σύν τινι with the sanction, under the auspices of a deity, Od., Xen.; κατὰ σφέας μαχέονται will fight by themselves, Il.; καθ’ ἕνα μ. to fight one against one, in single combat, Hdt.:— τὸ μήπω μεμαχημένον the force that had not yet come into action, Thuc.
generally, to quarrel, wrangle, dispute with one, to oppose, gainsay, τινι Il., Plat.
to contend for the mastery in games, πὺξ μάχεσθαι Il.; παγκράτιον μ. Ar.
pugnaciously, Strab.
random breezes, squalls, gusts or flaws of wind, Hes.
vain, false, Eur., Theocr.: useless, worthless, Anth.:—adv. μαψιδίως, = μάψ, Hom.
idly talking, μ. οἰωνοί birds whose cries convey no sure omen, Hhymn.
bringing forth in vain, Anth.
in vain, idly, fruitlessly, Il.; μὰψ ὀμόσαι to swear lightly, i. e. without meaning to perform, Id.
vainly, idly, foolishly, thoughtlessly, μὰψ αὔτως Hom.; μάψ, ἀτὰρ οὐ κατὰ κόσμον Id.
idly barking, i. e. repeating a thing again and again, Pind.
very bold, Hes.
high-minded, Hom., Hes.

to look on a thing as too great, to grudge one a thing as too great for him, Il.; so c. inf., μηδὲ μεγήρῃς ἡμῖν τελευτῆσαι τάδε ἔργα grudge us not the accomplishment of these works, Od.; c. acc. et inf., μνηστῆρας οὔτι μεγαίρω ἔρδειν I complain not that the suitors should do, Id.
c. dat. pers. to feel a grudge towards, Il.
absol., ἢ πύξ, ἠὲ πάλῃ, ἢ καὶ ποσίν, οὔτι μεγαίρω I care not (which), Od.
c. gen. rei, βιότοιο μεγήρας grudging him the life [of Antilochus], Il.; οὐ μ. τοῦδέ σοι δωρήματος Aesch.
Pass. to be envied, Anth.
with great hollows, cavernous, of the sea, Od. (cf. βαθυκήτης): of a ship, with large hull, Il.; of a dolphin, with huge maw, Id.
very famous, declined (as if from μεγακλής) μεγακλέος, έϊ, έα, έες, έα, Anth.
unjust in great matters, Arist.
of great strength, ap. Plut.
to boast highly, talk big, Aesch.: —Mid. to boast oneself, Plat.
great boasting, arrogance, Plat.
greatly boasting, very glorious, Pind., Aesch., etc.
magnificent, splendid, Xen.: τὰ μεγαλεῖα mighty works, NTest.:—adv. -ως, splendidly, Xen.
of persons, stately, haughty, Id.
majesty, NTest.
to talk big, boast, Xen.
big talking, Eur., Xen.
talking big, vaunting, boastful, Aesch., Xen.
great manliness, proud self-confidence, haughtiness, Pind., Eur.
very manly, heroic: self-confident, haughty, Pind.
great-hearted, heroic, Hom.
Pass. to be exalted, to bear oneself proudly, Hom.
high-mindedness, Xen.
high-minded, Xen.
full of large trees, Strab.
very glorious, Pind., Plut.
munificence, Luc.
making great presents, munificent, Ar.
performing great deeds, magnificent, Luc.
magnificence, Luc.
very wretched, Theocr.
concealing much: capacious, Pind.
braving great dangers, Arist.
with lofty summits, ap. Arist.
far-ruling, Anth.
of high design, ambitious, Aesch.
receiving high pay, Luc.
greatness of intellect, Plat., Luc.
great-minded, Luc.
epith. of great cities, αἱ μεγαλοπτόλιες Ἀθᾶναι Athens that mighty city, Pind.; ἁ μ. Τροία Eur.
the disposition to do great things, magnificence, Plut.
disposed to do great deeds, forming great designs, Xen.
the character of a μεγαλοπρεπής, magnificence, Hdt., Plat.
befitting a great man, magnificent, Hdt., attic:— τὸ μεγαλοπρεπές, = μεγαλοπρέπεια, Xen.
adv. -ῶς, ionic -έως, Hdt., Xen.: comp. -έστερον Plat., Sup. -έστατα Hdt.
exceeding strong, Pind.
with large heart: high-spirited, Eur.
very lamentable, most piteous, Aesch.
magnificent, Aesch.
greatly adventurous, Luc.
to be high-minded, μ. ἐφ’ ἑαυτῷ to be confident in oneself, Xen.:—Mid., in bad sense, to be arrogant, Plat.
greatness of mind, Plat.; ὑπὸ μεγαλοφροσύνης magnanimously, Hdt.
in bad sense, pride, arrogance, Id.
high-minded, noble, generous, Xen.
in bad sense, arrogant: adv. -όνως, Plat., Xen.
grandiloquence, Luc.
loud-voiced, Dem.
greatness of soul, magnanimity, Arist.:—in bad sense, arrogance, Dem.
of things, magnificence, Id.
high-souled, magnanimous, Dem.:—adv. -χως, Id.
to make great or powerful, to exalt, strengthen, Thuc.:— Pass., μεγαλύνεσθαι ἔκ τινος to gain great glory from . . , Xen.
to make great by word, to extol, magnify, Eur., Thuc., etc.:—Mid. to boast oneself, Aesch., Xen.
to aggravate a crime, Thuc.
with a great name, giving glory, Soph., Ar.

entry.etym: adverb of μέγας, v. μέγας B.
epic and ionic adv. of μέγας,
entry.sense: far and wide, over a vast space, Hom.
= μεγάλως, Hdt. 2. also = μεγαλοπρεπῶς, Id.
greatness, majesty, NTest.
man-exalting, Pind.
toMegara, Ar.
Megara, Hdt., etc.
a citizen of Megara, pl. Μεγαρεῖς or -ῆς, Hdt., etc.
fut. ιῶ, to side with the Megarians or speak their dialect, Ar.
Megarian, Ar., etc.:—fem. Μεγαρίς (sc. γῆ), the Megarian territory, Megarid, Thuc.
from Megara, Ar.
at Megara, Ar.
homewards, home, Od.
a large room or chamber, esp. the hall, Od.
the women's apartment, Id.
in pl. a house, palace, like Lat. aedes, because the house consisted of many rooms, Hom.; ἐν μεγάροις at home, Id.
the oracular chamber in the temple, the sanctuary, shrine, Hdt.; in this sense always, like Lat. aedes, in sg.
Radic. sense, opp. to μικρός, σμικρός, big, great, of men's stature, tall, Hom.; of women, καλή τε μεγάλη τε Od.:—also, great, full-grown, of age as shewn by stature, Id., Aesch.
vast, high, οὐρανός, ὄρος, πύργος Hom.
vast, spacious, wide, πέλαγός, αἰγιαλός, etc., Id.

of Degree, great, strong, mighty, of gods, Id., etc.; μεγάλα θεά, of Demeter and Proserpine, Soph.; μέγας ηὐξήθη rose to greatness, Dem.; βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας, i. e. the King of Persia, le grand monarque, Hdt.; βασιλεὺς μέγας Aesch.; ὁ μ. ἐπικληθεὶς Ἀντίοχος the Great, Polyb.
great, strong, violent, etc., ἄνεμος, λαῖλαψ Hom.; of properties, passions, etc., Id., etc.
of sounds, great, loud, Id., etc.; μὴ φώνει μέγα Soph.;—but, μέγας λόγος a prevailing rumour, Aesch.
great, mighty, weighty, important, μέγα ἔργον Od.; μέγα ποιεῖσθαί τι to esteem of great importance, Hdt.; καὶ τὸ μέγιστον and what is most important, Thuc.
in bad sense, over-great, μέγα εἰπεῖν to speak big, λίην μέγα εἰπεῖν Od.; μέγα, μεγάλα φρονεῖν to have high thoughts, be presumptuous, Soph., Eur.; μεγάλα πνεῖν Eur.
adv. μεγάλως [ᾰ], greatly, mightily, exceedingly, Lat. magnopere, Hom., Aesch.
neut. sg. and pl. μέγα and μεγάλα as adv., very much, exceedingly, Hom.; with verbs of sound, aloud, loudly, Id.; so in attic
of Space, far, μέγα ἄνευθε far away, Il., etc.:—with comp. and Sup. by far, μέγ’ ἀμείνων, ἄριστος, φέρτατος Hom.
degrees of Comparison:

comp. μείζων (for μεγίων), -ον, gen. -ονος, Hom., attic; ionic μέζων, ον, Hdt.; later also μειζότερος, NTest.:— greater, Hom., etc.; also, too great, too much, more than enough, Plat.:—adv. μειζόνως Eur.; ionic μεζόνως Hdt., etc.; also neut. as adv., μεῖζον σθένειν Soph., etc.
Sup. μέγιστος, η, ον, Hom.:—neut. as adv., μέγιστον ἰσχύειν Soph.; with another Sup. μέγιστον ἔχθιστος Eur.:—also in pl., χαῖρ’ ὡς μέγιστα Soph.

greatness, magnitude, size, height, stature, Hom., Hdt., etc.:—of sound, loudness, βοῆς μ. Thuc.:—dat. and acc. are used adverbially, μεγάθεϊ μέγας great in size, Hdt.; μεγάθεϊ μικρός Id.; so, ποταμοὶ οὐ κατὰ τὸν Νεῖλον ἐόντες μεγάθεα rivers not bearing any proportion to the Nile in size, Id.
of Degree, greatness, magnitude, Eur., Thuc., etc.
greatness, i. e. might, power, Eur., Xen.
greatness, magnanimity, Plut.
passing lovely, Hes.
great men, grandees, NTest.
making cities greatest, Pind.
a guardian, Ζεὺς Ἴδηθεν μεδέων guardian of Ida, Il.; δελφίνων μ., of Poseidon, Ar.
fem. μεδέουσα, of Aphrodite, Hhymn.; of Mnemosyne, Hes., etc.
the medimnus, an Attic corn-measure, containing 6 ἑκτεῖς, 48 χοίνικες, 192 κοτύλαι = 6 Roman modii, i. e. very nearly 12 gallons, Hes., attic
to provide for, think on, be mindful of, bethink one of, c. gen., πολέμοιο μεδέσθω Il.; ὡς δείπνοιο μέδηται Od., etc.
to plan, contrive, devise something for one, κακὰ Τρώεσσι μέδεσθαι Il.

entry.etym: only in pres., and mostly in participial Subst. μέδων, οντος, ὁ, like μεδέων, μεδέουσα
entry.sense: a guardian, lord, Ἀργείων ἡγήτορες ἠδὲ μέδοντες leaders and guardians of the Argives, Hom.; μέδων ἁλός lord of the sea, Od.; of Bacchus, ὃ μέδεις Δηοῦς ἐν κόλποις Soph.
to catch in turn, of a game at ball, Od.
to leap or rush upon, c. dat., Il.
to rush after, in a race, Id.

to dispose differently, to correct, Soph.:—Mid., aor1 μεθηρμοσάμην, with perf. pass. -ήρμοσμαι, to dispose for oneself, μεθάρμοσαι νέους τρόπους adopt new habits, Aesch.; μεθηρμόσμεσθα βελτίω βίον Eur.

entry.note: μεθεκτέος, ον verb. adj. of μετέχω
entry.sense: one must have a share of, τινός Thuc.
to draw to the other side, ἡνίας Anth.
participation, Plat.

entry.note: imperf. μεθεῖπον epic -επον fut. -έψω aor2 μετ-έσπον inf. μετασπεῖν part. -σπών mid. -σπόμενος
entry.sense: to follow after, follow closely, Hom.; so in Mid., μετασπόμενος Il.; c. dat., μεθέψομαί σοι Soph.
c. acc. to follow with the eyes, to seek after, Il.
to visit, νέον μεθέπεις; dost thou come but now to visit us? Od.
metaph. to pursue, attend to, Pind.; ἄχθος μεθέπων carrying a burden, Id.
Causal, c. dupl. acc., Τυδείδην μέθεπε ἵππους he turned the horses in pursuit of Tydeides, Il.
happening by day, in open day, Xen., Dem.
remissness, carelessness, Il.
remiss, careless, Hom.
strong drink, καλῶς ἔχειν μέθης to be pretty well drunk, Hdt.; ὑπερπλησθεὶς μέθης Soph.; μέθῃ βρεχθείς Eur.
drunkenness, Plat.
to be come in quest of, τινά Eur., Ar.
Pass. to sit among, c. dat., Od.
migration, Strab.
to place differently, transpose, Plat.: —Pass. to keep moving, Plut.

entry.note: 3 pers. μεθιεῖ 2 pers. μεθιεῖς ionic μετιεῖ or μετίει 3rd pl. μεθιᾶσι ionic μετιεῖσι imperat. μεθίει epic 3rd sg. subj. μεθίῃσι inf. μεθιέναι inf epic -ιέμεναι inf epic -ιέμεν imperf. 3rd sg. μεθίει 3rd pl. μέθιεν fut. μεθήσω epic inf. μεθησέμεναι epic inf -έμεν aor1 μεθῆκα epic μεθέηκα aor 2, imperat. μέθες subj. μεθῶ epic μεθείω opt. μεθείην inf. μεθεῖναι epic μεθέμεν part. μεθείς Mid., fut. μεθήσομαι ionic μετήσομαι 3rd sg. aor2 μεθεῖτο, 2nd pl. μέθεσθε 2nd dual subj. μεθῆσθον, 2nd pl. subj. μεθῆσθε inf. μεθέσθαι Pass., 3rd sg. ionic imperf. μετίετο 3rd pl. perf. μεθεῖνται ionic imperat. μετείσθω ionic part. μεμετιμένος ionic aor1 μετείθην
entry.etym: 2 and 3 pers. μεθιεῖς, μεθιεῖ as if from μεθιέω
entry.sense: trans. to let go, let loose, release a prisoner, Il., etc.: to let a visitor depart, Od.: to dismiss a wife, Hdt.:—c. inf. to let one free to do as he will, allow one to do, Id.; so, ἐλεύθερον μ. τινά Eur.:—Pass. to be let go, dismissed, Hdt.
to give up, abandon, Il.:—metaph., εἴ με μεθείη ῥῖγος if the cold would but leave me, Od.

c. acc. rei, to let a thing go, let it fall, throw, τι ἐς ποταμόν Id., etc.:— also, μ. χόλον to let go, give up one's wrath, Hom.; so, Ἀχιλῆι μεθέμεν χόλον to put away anger in favour of Achilles, Il.; so, μ. καρδίας χόλον to put away anger from one's heart, Eur.; μ. ψυχήν to give up the ghost, Id.:—of liquids, to let flow, let drop, Hdt., attic:—so, γλῶσσαν Περσίδα μ. to let drop, i. e. utter, Persian words, Hdt.:— μ. βλαστόν to let it shoot forth, Id.:— μ. βέλος to let it fly, discharge it, Soph.; μ. ξίφος ἐς γυναῖκα to plunge it into her, Eur. ; ναῒ μεθεῖναι (sc. ἱστία) to give the ship her way, Soph.
to relieve, κῆρ ἄχεος the heart from grief, Il.
to give up, resign, throw aside, Id., attic
to forgive one a fault, remit a debt, Hdt.; τόνδε κίνδυνον μεθείς excusing thee this peril, Eur.
intr. to relax one's energies (where ἑαυτόν may be supplied), to be slack, remiss, lukewarm, dally, Hom.: c. inf. to neglect to do, Il., Hdt., attic
to let, permit, μεθεῖσά μοι λέγειν having left it for me to speak, having allowed me, Soph.
c. gen. rei, to relax or cease from, πολέμοιο, μάχης Il., etc.; μέθιεν χόλοιο Τηλεμάχῳ [the suitors] ceased from wrath in deference to Telemachus, Od.
c. gen. pers. to abandon, neglect, Il.
c. part., κλαύσας μεθέηκε having wept he left off, Id.
the Mid. agrees in construction with the intr. Act., to free oneself from, let go one's hold of, c. gen., παιδὸς οὐ μεθήσομαι Eur., etc.;—the act. would be παῖδα οὐ μεθήσω.
Causal, in pres. and imperf., fut. and aor1, to place in another way, to change, μεταστήσω τοι ταῦτα I will give thee another present instead of this, Od.; μ. τὰ νόμιμα πάντα Hdt.; ὄνομα etc., Eur.
c. gen. partit., οὐ μεθίστησι τοῦ χρώματος he changes nothing of his colour, Ar.
of persons, to set free, νόσου from disease, Soph.; κακῶν, ὕπνου Eur.
to remove, Id., Thuc.:—so in aor1 mid., μεταστήσασθαι to remove from oneself or from one's presence, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
Pass., aor1 μετεστάθην [ᾰ], with aor2, perf., and plup. act.:
to stand among or in the midst of, ἑτάροισι μεθίστατο Il.
to change one's position, remove, depart, Hdt., attic; μ. τυράννοις ἐκποδών to make way for them, Eur.
c. gen. rei, to change or cease from, κότου Aesch.; λύπης, κακῶν Eur.; μ. βίου to die, Id.; μ. φρενῶν to go mad, Id.
to go over to another party, to revolt, Thuc.
of things, to change, alter, sometimes for the better, τῆς τύχης εὖ μετεστεώσης Hdt.; or for the worse, δαίμων μεθέστηκε στρατῷ fortune hath changed for the army, Aesch.
craft, wiliness, NTest.
to treat by method: to use cunning devices, employ craft, Lxx.
to lead another way, Anth.
a following after, pursuit: esp. pursuit of knowledge, scientific inquiry, investigation, method of inquiry, method, Plat., etc.
to hold converse with, τινί Il.
for μεθ’ ὅ after that.

lying between as a boundary, γῆ μεθορία τῆς Ἀργείας καὶ Λακωνικῆς the border country between Argolis and Laconia, Thuc.: in pl. the borders, marches, frontier, Id., Xen., etc.:—also, ἡ μεθορία (sub. χώρα) Plut.
Pass. to rush in pursuit of, make a dash at, Hom.

to remove from one anchorage to another, intr. (sub. νέας), μ. εἰς Σηστόν Xen.: metaph., τοῦ νῦν σκυθρωποῦ μεθορμιεῖ σε will unmoor, i. e. will remove, thee from thy sternness, Eur.:— Mid., μεθορμίσασθαι to seek a refuge, Id.:—Pass. to sail from one place to another, put out from, Hdt.
a water-nymph, Anth.
between-waters, a place in Arcadia, whence the waters ran some north some south (cf. Ital. Inter-amnia), Thuc.
giver of wine, Anth.
wine, mead, Hom.
gushing with wine, Anth.
wine-stricken, Anth.
drunkenness, Theogn.
to make drunk, intoxicate, inebriate, Plat., Luc., etc.
to give to drink: to water, moisten, Anth.
Pass. = μεθύω, to drink freely, to get drunk, Hdt., Xen.; aor1 ἐμεθύσθην, to be drunk, Eur., Dem.; νέκταρος with nectar, Plat.
drunk with cottabus-playing, Ar.
drunken, Ar., etc.
living after, μεθύστεροι posterity, Aesch.
neut. as adv. afterwards, hereafter, Hhymn., Soph.; so long after, so late, Aesch.; οὐ μ. in a moment, Id.: too late, Soph.
intoxicating, Arist.
of men, given to wine, Plat.
reeling-drunk, Anth.

entry.etym: only in pres. and imperf.; the fut. and aor. act. belong to μεθύσκω
entry.sense: to be drunken with wine, Od., etc.; μ. ὑπὸ τοῦ οἴνου Xen.
metaph. of things, βοείη μεθύουσα ἀλοιφῆι an ox-hide soaked in oil, Il.
of persons, to be drunken or intoxicated with passion, pride, etc., Xen., Plat.
to bring the lamb to the scale, and metaph., μ. τὴν τραγῳδίαν to weigh tragedy as you would a lamb, Ar.
bringing the sacrificial lamb (μεῖον) to be weighed, Eupol.

entry.etym: only used in epic 3rd sg. aor1 μείδησε, part. μειδήσας, -σασα
entry.sense: to smile, Hom.: to grin, v. σαρδάνιος. Cf. μειδιάω.
a smile, smiling, Hes.
a smile, Plut., Luc.
soothing things, pleasing gifts, Il.
in sg., a charm, Anth.
anything that serves to soothe, μειλίγματα θυμοῦ scraps to appease the hunger of dogs, Od.:—metaph., γλώσσης μείλιγμα Aesch.
in pl. propitiations, atonements made to the dead, Lat. inferiae, Id.
of a person, a fondling, darling, Id.
a soothing song, Theocr.
able to soothe: μειλικτήρια (sc. ἱερά), τά, propitiations, Aesch.

to make mild, to appease, propitiate, πυρὸς μειλισσέμεν to appease [the dead] by fire, i. e. by funeral rites, Il.; ὀργὰς μ. Eur.:—Mid. to use soothing words, μηδέ τί μ’ αἰδόμενος μειλίσσεο μηδ’ ἐλεαίρων extenuate not aught from respect or pity to me, Od.
gentleness, softness, μειλιχίη πολέμοιο lukewarmness in battle, Il.
gentle, mild, soothing, μειλιχίοις ἐπέεσσι, μ. μύθοις Hom.; and without Subst., προσαυδᾶν μειλιχίοισι to address with gentle words, Il.; αἰδοῖ μειλιχίῃ Od., Hes.; neut. as adv., gently, Mosch.
gracious, Ζεὺς Μειλίχιος the protector of those who invoked him with propitiatory offerings, Thuc., Xen.
μειλίχια ποτά propitiatory drink-offerings, or (as others) honied drinks, honey being mixed in the drink-offerings, Soph.
soft-voiced, Tyrtae.
gentle, kind, like μειλίχιος, Hom., etc.; c. gen., Ἄρτεμις μ. ὠδίνων soother of pangs, Anth.; τὸ μείλιχον gentleness, Theogn.; τὰ μείλιχα joys, Pind.
to have too little, to be poor, Xen.: to be worse off, come short, Id.; c. gen. rei, to be short of a thing, Id.
disadvantage, Xen.
neut. of μείων. less.

μεῖον, ου, the lamb which was offered at the Apaturia, when a boy was enrolled in his φρατρία. It was to be of a certain weight; and the φράτερες, whose perquisite it was, used to cry out μεῖον, μεῖον, too light! cf. μειαγωγέω.
to make smaller, to lessen, moderate, Xen.
to lessen in honour, degrade, Id.
to lessen by word, extenuate, disparage, Id.
Pass. to become worse or weaker, Id.: c. gen. to fall short of, Id.
a boy-cheater, Anth.
Dep. to play the boy, Plut., Luc.
a boy, lad, stripling, Plat.
a little girl, Ar.
a lad, stripling, Plat.
becoming a youth, youthful, Plat.
puerile, Id.
a mere lad, Ar.
a young girl, lass, (μειράκιον being used of boys), Ar., etc.
to receive as one's portion or due, καὶ ἥμισυ μείρεο τιμῆς take half the honour as thy due, Il.
in perf. to have one's share of, c. gen., ἔμμορε τιμῆς he has gotten his share of honour, Hom.

in 3rd sg. perf. pass. εἵμαρται, impers. it is allotted, decreed by fate, Plat.; plup. εἵμαρτο, it was decreed, Hom.; εἵμαρτο Dem., etc.:—part., εἱμαρμένος, η, ον, ordained, destined, allotted, Theogn., Aesch., etc.; ἡ εἱμαρμένη (sc. μοῖρα), that which is allotted, destiny, Plat.
most, Bion.
curtailment:—a fine, Xen.
less, Aesch., etc.: older, Soph.:—neut. μεῖον, as adv., less, μ. ἰσχύσειν Διός Aesch.:— μειόνως ἔχειν to be of less value, Soph.
with black soil, loamy, Hdt.
black-horned, black, Aesch.
the blackcap, Ar.
with black woof: of a ship, with black sails, Aesch.
black-haired, of Centaurs, Hes., Soph., Eur.
black, dark, Aesch., Eur.
entry.etym: Formed from μέλας, with termin. -χιμος, as δύσχιμος from δυσ-

entry.sense: with black raiment, darksome, gloomy, Aesch.
black-cloaked, Mosch.
οἱ M., a Scythian nation, Hdt.
to be atrabilious, Ar., Plat.
atrabilious, choleric, Plat.
dipped in black bile, Soph.
black-skinned, swarthy, Od.
swarthy, Plut., etc.; a heterocl. nom. pl. μελάγχροες, Hdt.
the ceiling of a room, or (rather) the main beam which bears the ceiling, Od.; in Od. 19. 544, the end of this beam outside the house.
generally, a roof, Hom.
a house, hall, Pind., Eur.; mostly in pl., like Lat. tecta, Trag.
to blacken: Pass., μελαίνετο χρόα he had his skin stained black (with blood), Il.; of earth just turned up, Id.; of ripening grapes, Hes.; of a newly-bearded chin, Id.
intr., = Pass., to grow black, Plat., Anth.
darkly deep, Aesch., Eur.
with black soil, Anth.
black clotted, Aesch.: generally, discoloured, Id.
black-robed, Eur.: generally, black, Id.
dark-leaved, Anth.
black-winged, Anth.
whose light is blackness, Eur.
dark-leaved, Anacr.: of places, dark with leaves, Pind., Soph.
with dark aegis, Aesch.
dark-gleaming, Eur.
bound or mounted with black, of swords with black scabbards, Il., Eur.; σάκος μ. an iron-rimmed shield, Aesch.
holding ink, Anth.
black-clad, μ. ἔφοδοι the assaults of the black-robed ones (the Furies), Aesch.
blackness: a black cloud, Xen.
black-hearted, Ar.
black-eyed, Plat.
clad in black death-clothes, Ar.
black-winged, Eur., Ar.
black-eyed, Il.
black-boned, Il.
a sea-fish, the black-tail: fem. μελαν-ουρίς, ίδος, Anth.
black pigment, ink, Dem.
black-walled, Pind.
a black dye, Luc.
black when eaten, Anth.
with black water, κρήνη μελάνυδρος of water which looks black from its depth, Il., Od.
intr. to grow black, Il.
anything black, μ. γραμματόκον a black lead pencil, Anth.

entry.etym: cf. τάλας, the only word like it in form
entry.sense: black, swart, Hom., etc.; μέλαν ὕδωρ of water drawn from a deep well (cf. μελάνυδρος), Od.
black, dark, murky, ἕσπερος, νύξ Hom., etc.
metaph. black, dark, θάνατος, Κήρ, the origin of the metaphor being seen in such phrases as μέλαν νέφος θανάτοιο, Hom.
dark, obscure, Anth.
comp. μελάντερος, η, ον, blacker, very black, Il.; cf. ἠΰτε.
μέλαν, v. sub voc.
Pass., only in pres., to melt, λέβης κνίσην μελδόμενος a pot filled with melting fat, Il.
to care for, be cumbered about a thing, c. gen., Theogn., Theocr.
c. acc. to tend, attend to, Hdt., Theocr.
c. inf., γῆμαι οὐ μελεδαίνει cares not to marry, Theogn.
care, anxiety, Il.; μελεδήματα πατρός anxieties about one's father, Od.:— μελεδήματα θεῶν the care of gods [for men], Eur.
careful, busy, Anth.
care, sorrow, Od., Theocr.
one who takes care of anything, a manager, keeper, μ. τῶν οἰκιῶν a house- steward, Hdt.; ὁ μ. τῶν θηρίων the keeper of the crocodiles, Id.; μ. τῆς τροφῆς one who provides their food, Id.
limb from limb, Shaksp. "limb-meal, " μελεϊστὶ ταμεῖν Hom.
sadly suffering, Aesch.
having laboured wretchedly, Aesch.
idle, useless, Lat. irritus, Hom.: neut. as adv. in vain, Il.
unhappy, miserable, ὦ μέλεοι, τί κάθησθε; Orac. ap. Hdt.; μέλεος γάμων unhappy in marriage, Aesch., etc.; μ. ἔργα, μ. θάνατος Id.
miserable-minded, Eur.
and ὦ μέλε, only in voc., ὦ μέλε, dear!good friend! Ar.
singing with its wings, of the cicada, Anth.
to care for, attend to a thing, c. gen., Hes.
c. acc. rei, to attend to, study, Hdt., Soph.; μ. δόξαν to study, court reputation, Thuc.

to practise an art, Lat. meditari, μαντείαν Hhymn.; μ. τοῦτο (sc. κήρυκα εἶναι) Hdt.; μ. σοφίαν Ar.; ῥητορικήν Plat.:—in attic also, to practise speaking, to con over a speech, Dem.:—Pass., τὸ ναυτικὸν οὐκ ἐνδέχεται ἐκ παρέργου μελετᾶσθαι nautical skill cannot be acquired by occasional practice, Thuc.; εὐταξία μετὰ κινδύνων μελετωμένη discipline won by practice on the battle-field, Id.
c. inf. to practise doing a thing, μ. τοξεύειν καὶ ἀκοντίζειν Xen.; μ. ἀποθνήσκειν Plat.
absol. to practise, exercise oneself, the acc. rei being omitted, Thuc., Xen.; ἐν τῷ μὴ μελετῶντι (= μελετᾶν) by want of practice, Thuc.: —esp. to rehearse a speech, declaim, Plat., etc.
c. acc. pers. to exercise or train persons, Xen.
a practice, exercise, study, Plat., Xen.
care, attention, Hes.; μ. πλεόνων care for many things, Id.; ἔργων μ. attention to action, Thuc.:—but c. gen. subjecti, care paid by one, θεῶν του μελέτῃ Soph.
practice, exercise, Lat. meditatio, Pind.; ἡ δι’ ὀλίγου μ. their short practice, Thuc.; πόνων μελέται painful exercises, of the Spartan discipline, Id.
in a military sense, exercise, practice, drill, Id.
of an orator, rehearsal, Dem.
a pursuit, Pind.
care, anxiety, μελέτῃ κατατρύχεσθαι Eur.
practising diligently, Xen.
one must study, Plat.
a place for practice, Plut.
one who cares for, an avenger, ἀμφί τινα Soph.
the object of care, a darling, of persons, τοὐμὸν μέλ., like Virgil's mea cura, Pind.; ὦ φίλτατον μ. Aesch.
a charge, duty, Id., Soph.
care, anxiety, Aesch., Theocr.
with μ inserted, an object of care or love to men, Pind.
one must take thought for, τινός Plat.
proverbial at Athens for a blockhead (in form a patronymic from Μέλητος), Ar.
the ash, Lat. fraxinus, Il., etc.
an ashen spear, Id.
sweet-toned, Anth.
sweet-sounding, Pind.

entry.note: μελί-γηρυς, doric μελί-γᾱρυς, υος, ὁ, ἡ,
entry.sense: sweet-voiced, melodious, Od., Pind.
honey-tongued, Aesch., Ar.
a song, Mosch.
a pitch-pipe, Id.
to modulate, sing, warble, Theocr.: mostly in Mid., Id., Anth.
trans. to sing of, celebrate in song, Pind., Aesch.
honey-sweet, of wine, Hom.:— metaph., μελιηδέα θυμὸν ἀπηύρα Il.; μ. ὕπνος Od.
honey-fed, Anth.
a honey-comb, Theocr.
sweet-sounding, Pind.
a drink of honey and milk offered to the powers below, Od.
a singer, player, Theocr., Mosch.
melilot, a kind of clover, rich in honey, Cratin., etc.
millet, Lat. panicum, Hdt.: in pl. millet-fields, Xen., Dem.
ashen, Lat. fraxineus, Hom.
millet-eaters, a Thracian tribe, Xen.
with honey-children, of a bee-hive, Anth.
Lat. mel, honey, Hom., etc.
honey-breathing, sweet-breathing, Theocr., Anth.
honey-flowing, Plat.

entry.etym: Dim. of μέλος II, Alcman, Antipho.

entry.sense: a song, Theocr.: a tune, Anth.
a bee, Lat. apis, Hom., etc.
one of the priestesses of Delphi, Pind.
= μέλι, honey, Soph.
of bees, κηρίον μ. a honeycomb, NTest.
fed on by bees, Anth.
keeping bees, :—in Aesch. ap. Ar., the Μελισσονόμοι are priestesses of Artemis.
guardian of bees, Anth.
produced by bees, honied, Anth.
feeding bees, Eur.
dropping honey, Anth.
baulm, Lat. apiastrum, Theocr.
mead, Plut., etc.
honied, i. e. sweet, delicious, Pind.
sweetened with honey, μελιτόεσσα (sc. μᾶζα), a honey-cake, as a sacred offering, Hdt.; attic contr. μελιτοῦττα, Ar.
Pass. to be sweetened with honey, Thuc.
a dealer in honey, Ar.
a bee-keeper, Plat.
like honey: a name of Persephone, Lat. Mellita, Theocr.
a honey-cake, Batr.
honey-voiced, Pind.
sweet to the mind, delicious, Hom., Hes.
honey-pale, Plat., Theocr.
honey-sweet, Theocr.:—metaph., of Sophocles, Anth.:—comp. adv. μελιχρότερον, Id.
yellow as honey, Anth.
a Spartan youth before the age of 20, Plut.
a delay, Eur., Aeschin.
a being about to do, threatening to do, Thuc.
an intention not carried into effect, delay, Id.; διὰ βραχείας μελλήσεως at short notice, Id.
c. gen. rei, a putting off, a delaying to execute, Id.
one must delay, Eur.
a delayer, loiterer, Thuc., Arist.
betrothed, Soph., Theocr.
to be going to conquer, with a play on the name of Νικίας, the Athenian Cunctator, Ar.
of girls, about to be betrothed or wedded, Lat. nubilis, Soph.:—in Soph. Tr. 207, ἀνολολύξατε ὁ μελλόνυμφος, ὁ μ. (sc. χορός) must be taken collectively for αἱ μελλόνυμφοι, the maidens of the house.

to think of doing, intend to do, to be about to do, with inf., mostly inf. fut., τάχ’ ἔμελλε δώσειν he was just going to give, Il.; μέλλεις ἀφαιρήσεσθαι ἄεθλον thou thinkest to strip me of the prize, Id.; often with οὐκ ἄρα, as, οὐκ ἄρ’ ἔμελλες λήξειν; did you not think you might stop? could you not stop? Od., etc.; to be about to do (on compulsion), to be destined to do or to be, τὰ οὐ τελέεσθαι ἔμελλον which were not to be accomplished, Il.; μέλλεν οἶκος ἀφνειὸς ἔμμεναι the house was destined to be wealthy, Od.; εἰ ἐμέλλομεν ἀνοίσειν if we were able to refer, Plat.
to express a certainty, μέλλω ἀπέχθεσθαι Διί it must be that I am hated by Zeus, Il.; μέλλω ἀθανάτους ἀλιτέσθαι I must have sinned against the immortals, Od.

to mark a probability, when it may be rendered to be like to do or be, or expressed by an adv., τὰ δὲ μέλλετ’ ἀκουέμεν belike ye have heard it, Hom.; μέλλεις ἴδμεναι thou art like to know of it, Od.; ἐμέλλετ’ ἆρα πάντες ἀνασείειν βοήν aye, all of you were like to raise (i. e. I thought you would raise) a cry of submission, Ar.

to mark mere intention, to be always going to do without ever doing, and so to delay, put off, hesitate, scruple, mostly with inf. pres., τί μέλλομεν χωρεῖν; Soph.; often followed by μὴ οὐ or μή, τί μέλλομεν μὴ πράσσειν; Eur.

μέλλω often stands without its inf., τὸν υἱὸν ἑόρακας αὐτοῦ; Answ. τί δ’ οὐ μέλλω; why shouldn't I have seen him? i. e. be sure I have, Xen.; οὐδὲν ἐπάθετε οὐδὲ ἐμελλήσατε (sc. παθεῖν) Thuc.:—so, when μέλλω seems to govern an acc., an inf. is omitted, τὸ μέλλειν ἀγαθά (sc. πράσσειν) the expectation of good things, Eur.: hence

the part. μέλλων without an inf. (where εἶναι or γίγνεσθαι may be supplied), ὁ μ. χρόνος the future time, Pind., Aesch.; esp. in neut., τὸ μέλλον, τὰ μέλλοντα things to come, the event, issue, future, Aesch., etc.:—so in Mid., τὰ ἰσχυρότατα ἐλπιζόμενα μέλλεται your strongest pleas are hopes in futurity, Thuc.
μέλλομαι as Pass., ὡς μὴ μέλλοιτο τὰ δέοντα that the necessary steps might not be delayed, Xen.; ἐν ὅσωι ταῦτα μέλλεται while these delays are going on, Dem.
song-writing, Anth.
writing songs, Anth.
to make lyric poems, Ar.
a making of lyric poems or music: the theory of music, as opposed to its practice, Plat.
a maker of songs, a lyric poet, Ar., Plat.
as adj. tuneful, Eur.
a limb, Hom., etc.; μελέων ἔντοσθε within my bodily frame, Aesch.; κατὰ μέλεα limb by limb, like μελεϊστί, Hdt.
a song, strain, Hhymn., etc.:—esp. of lyric poetry, ἐν μέλεϊ ποιέειν to write in lyric strain, Hdt.; μέλη, τά, lyric poetry, the choral songs, opp. to the dialogue, Plat.
the music to which a song is set, the tune, Id.; ἐν μέλει in tune, Id.; παρὰ μέλος, out of tune, Id.
to strike up a strain, chant, Aesch.
the song with the dance, festive sport, κυνῶν μέλπηθρα a sport for dogs, of a corpse, κυσὶ μέλπηθρα γενέσθαι Il.
Melpomene, a Muse, properly the songstress, Hes.: later the Muse of tragedy.
to sing of, celebrate with song and dance, Il., Eur.; μ. τινὰ κατὰ χέλυν Eur.
intr. to sing, Aesch., Eur.;— c. acc. cogn., μ. θανάσιμον γόον Aesch.; ἰαχάν, βοάν Eur.
also as Dep. μέλπομαι to sing to the lyre or harp, Od.; to dance and sing, as a chorus, μετὰ μελπομένηισιν ἐν χορῶι Il.; μέλπεσθαι Ἄρηι to dance a war-dance in honour of Ares, i. e. to fight, Id.
c. acc., as in Act. to sing, celebrate, Hes., Eur.
a ditty, Theocr., Bion.
to sing, chant, Ar.
a singing, chanting, Eur.
a chant, choral song, Plat.
singing, musical, melodious, Eur.

entry.etym: on II., most usual in 3rd sg. and pl. of act. pres. μέλει, μέλουσι.
entry.sense: neuter, with perf. μέμηλα, to be an object of care or thought to anyone, c. dat. pers., ἀνθρώποισι μέλω I am a source of care to men, i. e. am well known to them, Od.; so, Ἀργὼ πᾶσι μέλουσα Id.; νερτέροισι μέλω Eur., etc.

μή τοι ταῦτα μελόντων let not these things be a care to thee, Hom.; πόλεμος ἄνδρεσσι μελήσει Il.; ὧι τόσσα μέμηλε to whom so great things are a care, Od., etc.:—an inf. often stands as nom., οὐκ ἔμελέν μοι ταῦτα μεταλλῆσαι Id.

in attic 3rd sg. is commonly used impers. with the object in gen., and pers. in dat., ὧι μέλει μάχας to whom there is care for the battle, who careth for it, Aesch.; Ζηνὶ τῶν σῶν μέλει πόνων Eur., etc.;—also, μέλει μοι περί τινος Hdt., attic; ὑπέρ τινος Dem.
absol., with a neg., οὐδέν μοι μέλει I care not, Ar.
μέλον ἔστι periphr. for μέλει, as, ἐστί τι μέλον τινί Soph.; τοῦτο ἴσασιν ἐμοὶ μεμεληκός Xen.:—also absol., μέλον γέ σοι since you have thought about it, Plat.

Mid. is used by Poets like Act., to be an object of care, ἐμοὶ δέ κε ταῦτα μελήσεται Il.; τἀνθάδ’ ἂν μέλοιτό μοι what remains should be a care to you, Soph., etc.; rarely impers., μέλεταί μοί τινος Theocr.

in epic Poets are found perf. and plup. pass. μέμβλεται, μέμβλετο, shortd. for μεμέληται, μεμέλητο, with pres. and imperf. sense, οὐκέτι μέμβλετ’ Ἀχιλλεύς (for μέλει) Achilles cares no longer for it, Il.; μέμβλετο οἱ τεῖχος (for ἔμελε) the wall was a care to him, Id.:—the regul. perf. occurs in later Poets, Φοίβωι μεμελήμεθα Anth.; 2 and 3rd sg. plup. μεμέλησο, -ητο, Id., Theocr.

trans., c. gen. of persons, to care for, take care of, take an interest in a thing, πλούτοιο μεμηλώς busied with riches, Il.; πολέμοιο μεμηλώς Id.; θεοὶ τῶν ἀδίκων μέλουσιν Eur.:—absol. to be anxious, μέλει κέαρ Aesch., etc.

Mid. μέλομαι, to care for, take care of, c. gen., Trag.; so in aor1 pass., τάφου μεληθείς having provided for the burial, Soph.:—also μεληθέν, as Pass. cared for, Anth.; and perf. part. μεμελημένος, Id.

entry.etym: found only in perf. μέμαα with pres. sense
entry.sense: to wish eagerly, strive, yearn, desire, c. inf., Hom., etc.: c. gen. to long for, be eager for:—often also with an adv., πῆ μέματον; whither so fast? Il.; πρόσσω μεμαυῖαι pressing forward, Id.; absol. in part., ἔβη μεμαώς he strode on hastily, eagerly, Id.; ἐν πέτρᾳ μεμαώς, of a fisher, expectant, Theocr.
to be bent on doing, to purpose, μεμάασιν αὖθι μένειν Il., etc.
Mid. in doric inf. μῶσθαι, part. μώμενος: — to seek after, covet, c. acc., Theogn., etc.; c. inf. or absol., Aesch.
the Lat. membra_na, parchment, NTest.
a small kind of anchovy, Ar.
carefully, Plat.

entry.etym: adverb perf. pass. part. of μετρέω
entry.sense: according to a stated measure, Luc.
by stratagem, Eur.
the temple of Memnon, in Egypt, Luc.; τὰ βασιλήια τὰ Μεμνόνεια (or Μεμνόνια) Hdt.
the steadfast or resolute (cf. Ἀγαμέμνων), Memnon, son of Eos and Tithonus, killed by Achilles, Od., Hes.

entry.etym: perf. used as pres., but only in sg., the pl. being supplied by μέμαα
entry.sense: to wish eagerly, to yearn, strive, be fain, to do a thing, c. inf., Hom.:—absol., διχθὰ δέ μοι κραδίη μέμονε my heart yearneth with a twofold wish, Il.; μέμονεν ὅγε ἶσα θεοῖσι he puts forth spirit equal with the gods, Id.; τί μέμονας; what wishest thou? Aesch.
to be blamed, blameworthy, Hdt., Eur.; comp. μεμπτότερος Thuc.; οὐ μ. not contemptible, Id.:—adv. μεμπτῶς Plut.
act. throwing blame upon, τινι Soph.; where μεμπτός is fem. for -τή.
to blame, censure, find fault with a person or thing, c. acc., Hes., Hdt., attic
c. dat. pers. et acc. rei, to impute as blameworthy, cast it in his teeth, Lat. exprobrare or objicere alicui, Hdt., attic

c. dat. pers. only, to find fault with, Trag.;—c. gen. rei only, to complain of a thing, Eur., Thuc.; and with both these cases, τοῦδ’ ἂν οὐδεὶς μέμψαιτό μοι no one would find fault with me for this, Aesch.
c. inf. with μή pleonastic, μ. μὴ πολλάκις βουλεύεσθαι to impute blame for doing, Thuc.
to complain of fate, Luc.
to impute as blameworthy, τί τινι ap. Dem.
complaining of one's fate, repining, querulous, Isocr., Luc.
blame, censure, reproof, μ. ἐπιφέρειν τινί Ar.; ἔχειν μ. to incur blame, Eur.
act. cause for complaint, Aesch., Soph.
abiding the spear, staunch in battle, Anth.
to desire earnestly or eagerly, to be bent on doing, c. inf., Hom.; also, c. gen., μ. μάχης to long for battle, Hes.
absol. to be angry, rage, Hom.; but, κτεινόμενος μενέαινε he struggled as he was dying, Il.
standing against the enemy, staunch, steadfast, Il.; doric -δάϊος, Anth.
pr. n. withstanding-men, Hom.: attic Μενέλεως, gen. εω, Trag.; doric dat. Μενέλᾳ, Pind., acc. Μενέλαν Eur.
staunch in battle, steadfast, Il.
pr. n., abider, Il.
one must remain, Plat., Xen.
inclined to wait, patient, Ar.: οἱ καιροὶ οὐ μενετοί opportunities will not wait, Thuc.
staunch in battle, of heroes, Il.:—also μενέχαρμος, ον, Id.
suited to the desires, satisfying, sufficient, plentiful, agreeable to one's taste, Hom.; τάφος μ. a plentiful funeral feast, Il.; μενοεικέα ὕλην great store of wood, Id.

to desire eagerly, to be bent on a thing, c. acc., Hom.: also c. inf. to be eager to do, Id.:—absol., ὧδε μενοινῶν so eager, Il.:— μ. τί τινι to design or purpose something against one, κακὰ Τρώεσσι μενοίνα Od.; c. dat. rei, to strive for a thing, Theogn.
eager desire, Anth.
might, force, strength, prowess, courage, Hom., etc.
strength, as implying life, life itself, Il.: life-blood, Soph.
rage, passion, μένος ἔλλαβε θυμόν Il.; μένεος φρένες πίμπλαντο Id.; μένεα πνείοντες Id.:— μένει in dat. violently, furiously, Aesch.
the bent, intent, purpose of any one, Τρώων μ. αἰὲν ἀτάσθαλον their bent is aye to folly, Il.
μένος is also used in periphr., ἱερὸν μένος Ἀλκινόοιο, i. e. Alcinous himself, Od.; μένος Ἀτρείδαο, Ἕκτορος, etc., Il.

Particle, used to shew that the word or clause with which it stands answers to a following word or clause, which is introduced by δέ. Generally, μέν and δέ may be rendered on the one hand, on the other hand, or as well . . , as, while or whereas, but it is often necessary to leave μέν untranslated.
μέν is not always answered by δέ, but by other equiv. Particles, as ἀλλά, ἀτάρ or αὐτάρ, αὖ, αὖθις, αὖτε; also πρῶτον μέν, εἶτα Soph.; πρῶτον μέν, ἔπειτα Id.; πρῶτον μέν, μετὰ τοῦτο Xen.

the answering clause with δέ is sometimes left to be supplied, ὡς μὲν λέγουσι as indeed they say, (but as I believe not), Eur.; this isolated μέν is often a Pron., ἐγὼ μὲν οὐκ οἶδα I for my part, (whatever others may say), Xen.; οὗτος μέν Plat.
μέν was orig. the same as μήν, and like it is used in protestations, καί μοι ὄμοσσον, ἦ μέν μοι ἀρήξειν and swear to me, that surely thou wilt assist me, Il.
μέν before other Particles: μὲν ἄρα, μέν ῥα accordingly, and so, Hom., etc.
μέν γε, used much like γοῦν, at all events, at any rate, Ar., etc.
μὲν δή to express certainty, Soph., etc.

μὲν οὖν or μενοῦν, a strengthd. form of οὖν, so then, Id.; in replies, it affirms strongly, πάνυ μὲν οὖν Plat., etc.; also it corrects a statement, nay rather, like Lat. imo, imo vero, μου πρὸς τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀποψῶ wipe your nose on my head, Answ. ἐμοῦ μὲν οὖν . . , nay on mine, Ar., etc.; μὲν οὖν δή Soph.:—so in NTest., μενοῦνγε, to begin a sentence, yea rather, Lat. quin imo.
μέν τοι or μέντοι,
conjunctive, yet, but however, nevertheless, tamen, vero, Aesch., etc.

Adverbial, of course, certainly, Plat., etc.; with an imperat., to enforce the command, τουτὶ μέντοι σὺ φυλάττου only take heed . . , Ar.; strengthd. μέντοι γε Xen.:—in narrative, etc., to add something, καὶ φυλάξασθαι μέντοι . . , and of course to take care . . , Id.
wrought by Mentor, Luc.
Lat. maneo, to stay stand fast, abide, in battle, Hom., Aesch.; μ. κατὰ χώραν, of soldiers, Thuc.
to stay at home, stay where one is, not stir, Il.; μ. εἴσω δόμων Aesch.; κατ’ οἶκον Eur., etc.:—but, μ. ἀπό τινος to stay away from, Il.
to stay, tarry, Hom., etc.
of things, to be lasting, remian, last, stand, στήλη μένει ἔμπεδον Il., etc.
of condition, to remain as one was, of a maiden, Il.; ἢ μείνωσιν ὅρκοι if oaths hold good, Eur.; μ. ἐπὶ τούτων to remain contented with.., Dem.
to abide by an opinion, conviction, etc., ἐπὶ τῶι ἀληθεῖ Plat.
impers. c. inf., it remains for one to do, ἀνθρώποισι κατθανεῖν μένει Eur.

trans. to await, expect, wait for, c. acc., Il.; so, like Lat. manere hostem, Hom., etc.:—so, also c. acc. et inf., ἦ μένετε Τρῶας σχεδὸν ἐλθέμεν; wait ye for the Trojans to come nigh? Il.; μένον δ’ ἐπὶ ἕσπερον ἐλθεῖν they waited for evening's coming on, Od.; μένω δ’ ἀκοῦσαι I wait, i. e. long, to hear, Aesch.
bit-stealer, a mouse in Batr.
to divide, distribute, Plat., etc.
Mid., μερίζεσθαί τι to divide among themselves, Theocr., Dem.:—c. gen. rei, to take part in, Arist.
Pass. to be divided, Xen.
to be reckoned as part, Dem.
care, thought, esp. anxious thought, solicitude, Hes., Trag.; μ. τινος care for, Aesch., Soph.: —pl. cares, anxieties, Aesch., Ar.
the thought, mind, Aesch.
to care for, be anxious about, think earnestly upon, scan minutely, Lat. meditari, Soph., Xen.; πολλὰ μ. to be cumbered with many cares, Xen.:—c. inf. to be careful to do, Dem.
anxiety, Soph.
one who is anxious about a thing, c. gen., Eur.
mother of cares, Anth.
a dividing, division, Plat.
a part, portion, share, parcel, Plat.
a contribution, Dem.
a part, division, class, Eur., Dem.
a divider, NTest.
divided, divisible, Plat., Arist.
a partaker in, τινός Dem.
causing anxiety, mischievous, baneful, μέρμερα μητίσασθαι to meditate mischief, Il.; μέρμερα ῥέζειν Id.; πολέμοιο μ. ἔργα Id.
of persons, anxious, peevish, morose, Plat.
epic gen. pl. -άων, poet. form of μέριμνα, care, trouble, Hes., Theogn.
intr. to be full of cares, to be anxious or thoughtful, to be in doubt, Hom.; δίχα or διάνδιχα μερμηρίζειν to halt between two opinions, Id.
trans. to devise, contrive, δόλον ἐνὶ φρεσὶ μερμ. Od.; φόνον ἡμῖν μερμηρίζει Id.
a cord, string, rope, Od.
a part, share, Hdt., etc.
one's portion, heritage, lot, Aesch.; ἀπὸ μέρους from considerations of rank, Thuc.

one's turn, Hdt., etc.; ἀγγέλου μ. his turn of duty as messenger, Aesch.:— ἀνὰ μέρος in turn, by turns, Eur.; so, κατὰ μέρος Thuc.; ἐν μέρει in turn, Hdt., etc.; ἐν τῷ μέρει in one's turn, Id.; παρὰ τὸ μ. out of one's turn, Xen.; πρὸς μέρος in proportion, Thuc.; τὸ μέρος in part, Hdt.

the part one takes in a thing, or the part assigned one, τοὐμὸν μέρος, τὸ σὸν μ. my or thy part, i. e. simply I or me, thou or thee, Soph.; and absol. as adv., τοὐμὸν μ. as to me, Lat. quod ad me attinet, Id.
a part, as opp. to the whole, ἡμέρας μ. Aesch.: a division of an army, Xen.; τὰ πέντε μ. five-sixths, τὰ ὀκτὼ μ. eight-ninths, etc.
ἐν μέρει τινὸς τιθέναι, ποιεῖσθαι to put in the class of . . , consider as so and so, Plat.; ἐν οὐδενὸς εἶναι μέρει to be as no one, Dem.; ἐν προσθήκης μέρει as an appendage, Id.
only in pl. as epithet of men, dividing the voice, i. e. articulate-speaking, endowed, with speech, Hom., Hes.:—hence μέροπες as Subst. = ἄνθρωποι, Aesch., Eur.
a leathern strap, by which the yoke was fastened to the pole, Hes.
a javelin with a strap (ἀγκύλη) for throwing it by, Eur.
half-gray, grizzled, i. e. middle-aged, Il.
between shores, in mid-sea, Aesch.
the inner court, behind the αὐλή, where the cattle were put at night, Il.; of the cave of the Cyclops, Od.
in attic, μέταυλος (with or without θύρα), the door between the αὐλή and the inner part of the house, Ar.; θύραι μέσαυλοι Eur.
to deposit a pledge in the hands of a third party, Plat.: —Mid., μεσεγγυᾶσθαι ἀργύριον to have one's money deposited in the hands of a third party, Dem.
money or a pledge deposited with a third party, Aeschin.
to keep the middle or mean between two, c. gen., Plat.: absol. to stand mid-way, to be neutral, Xen.
adverb
of Space, absol. in the middle, between, οὐδέ τι πολλὴ χώρη μεσσηγύς Il.
c. gen. between, betwixt, μ. γαίης τε καὶ οὐρανοῦ Id., etc.
of Time, meanwhile, meantime, Od.
as Subst., τὸ μεσηγύ the part between, Hhymn.; τὸ μεσηγὺ ἤματος mid-day, Theocr.
middle, middling, Il.
to pass the noon, Lat. meridiari, μεσημβριάζοντα εὕδειν to sleep at noon, Plat.
mid-day, noon, Hdt.; μεσαμβρίης at noon, Id.; τῆς μεσημβρίας Ar.; so, τῇ μεσαμβρίῃ Hdt.; ἐν μεσημβρίᾳ Thuc.; μ. ἵσταται 'tis high noon, Plat.
the parts towards noon, the South, Hdt.

belonging to noon, about noon, noontide, εὖτε πόντος ἐν μεσημβριναῖς κοίταις εὕδοι πεσών Aesch.; μεσημβρινοῖσι θάλπεσι in the noon-day heats, Id.; ὁ μ. ᾠδός, of the cicada, Anth.:— τὸ μεσαμβρινόν noon, Theocr.
southern, Aesch., Thuc.
μεσαμέριον at mid-day, Theocr.
in the middle, midmost, Eur.; Σείριος ἔτι μ. Sirius is still in mid-heaven, Id.
mediation, negotiation, Barb.
to act as mediator, Barb., NTest.
a mediator, umpire, arbitrator, Polyb., NTest.
an interregnum, Plut.
the Roman interrex, one who holds kingly power between the death of one king and the accession of another, Plut.
inland, in the heart of a country, Hdt.; τὴν μ. τῆς ὁδοῦ the inland road, Id.
μεσόγεως As adj., Plat.
as Subst., μεσογαία, the inland parts, interior, Lat. loca mediterranea, Hdt.; so, μεσογεία, ἡ, Thuc., Dem.
drawn in the middle: τὸ μ. a mean proportional found by the μεσόλαβος, Anth.
something built between: in pl., prob., the bays or compartments between the pillars that supported the roof, Od.
a box amidships in which the mast was stepped, Id.
held by the middle, Aesch.
middling white, χιτὼν πορφυρᾶ μ. a tunic of purple shot with white, Xen.
in mid-navel, central, of Apollo's shrine at Delphi (cf. ὀμφαλός), Aesch., Eur.; τὰ μ. γῆς μαντεῖα Soph.
of or at midnight, Pind., Eur.:— neut. as adv., Theocr.
fixed up to the middle, μεσσοπαγὲς δ’ ἄρ’ ἔθηκε ἔγχος drove the spear in up to the middle, Il.
to be half-way, Theophr.
going in the middle, μ. δι’ αἰθέρος through mid- air, Eur.
between rivers: Μεσοποταμία, sc. χώρα, a land between two rivers, esp. that between the Tigris and Euphrates, Mesopotamia, Polyb., Strab.:— Μεσοποταμίτης, [ῑ], ου, ὁ, Luc.

middle, in the middle, Lat. medius, Hom., etc.; μέσον σάκος the middle or centre of the shield, Il.; ἐν αἰθέρι μέσῳ in mid air, Soph.; with the Art. following, διὰ μέσης τῆς πόλεως, ἐν μ. τῇ χώρᾳ Xen.
with a Verb, ἔχεται μέσος by the middle, by the waist, proverb. from the wrestling-ring, Ar.
μ. δικαστής = μεσίτης, a judge between two, an umpire, Thuc.
ὁ μέσος (sc. δάκτυλος) Plat.
of Time, μέσον ἦμαρ mid- day, Hom.; μέσαι νύκτες Hdt.; also, μέσον τῆς ἡμέρας Id.
middling, moderate, μέσος ἀνήρ a man of middle rank, Id.; μ. πολίτης Thuc.; also οἱ διὰ μέσου the moderate or neutral party, Id.
middling, i. e. middling good, Plat.

μέσον epic μέσσον, ου, as Subst. the middle, the space between, ἐν μέσσῳ, for ἐν μεταιχμίῳ, Il.; or without ἐν, ἔνθορε μέσσῳ he leaped into the middle, Id.; οἱ ἐν μ. λόγοι the intervening words, Soph.; τὰ ἐν μ. what went between, Id.; ἐν μ. ἡμῶν καὶ βασιλέως between us and him, Xen.; ἐν μ. νυκτῶν at mid night, Id.; ἆθλα κείμενα ἐν μέσῳ prizes set up for all to contend for, Dem.;—so in pl., κεῖτο δ’ ἄρ’ ἐν μέσσοισι Il.

ἐς μέσον, ἐς μ. ἀμφοτέρων Hom.; ἐς μ. τιθέναι τισί τι to set a prize before all, for all to contest, Lat. in medio ponere, Il.; ἐς τὸ μ. τιθέναι to propose, bring forward in public, Hdt.; ἐς τὸ μ. λέγειν to speak before all, Id.; ἐς μ. Πέρσῃσι καταθεῖναι τὰ πρήγματα to give up the power in common to all, Id.
ἐκ τοῦ μέσου καθέζεσθαι to keep clear of a contest, i. e. remain neutral, Id.
διὰ μέσου = μεταξύ, between, Id., Thuc.; and of Time, meanwhile,Hdt., Thuc.
ἀνὰ μέσον midway between, Theocr.
κατὰ μέσσον, = ἐν μέσῳ, Il.
τὸ μέσον, also, the difference, average, Hdt., Thuc.
the middle state or mean, Lat. mediocritas, Arist.; παντὶ μέσῳ τὸ κράτος θεὸς ὤπασεν Aesch.
adv. μέσον, epic μέσσον, in the middle, Hom.: c. gen. between, οὐρανοῦ μ. χθονός τε Eur.
in attic μέσως, moderately, Id.; καὶ μέσως even a little, Thuc.; μέσως βεβιωκέναι in a middle way, i. e. neither well nor ill, Plat.
irreg. comp. μεσαίτερος (cf. μεσαῖος) Id.; Sup. μεσαίτατος Hdt., etc.
split in two, Anth.
a middle or central position, Plat.
a mean between two extremes, Arist.
a partition-wall, NTest.
to cut through the middle, cut in twain, bisect, Plat., Xen.
cut through the middle, Anth.
mid-heaven, mid-air, NTest.
the sun's place in meridian, Strab.
to form the middle, be in or at the middle, Aesch., Eur.:—of time, ἡμέρα μεσοῦσα mid- day, Hdt.; θέρους μεσοῦντος in mid summer, Thuc.
c. gen. to be in the middle of, τῆς ἀναβάσιος Hdt.; so, c. acc., μεσῶν τὴν ἀρχήν in the middle of his time of office, Aeschin.
midmost, Il.; attic μέσατος, Ar.
from the middle, Anth.
in the middle, Hes.
full, filled, filled full, Ar., etc.
c. gen. full of, filled with a thing, Hdt., Ar.:—metaph., ἀπάτης, ἀπορίας μ. Plat.:—metaph. also, sated with a thing, Eur.; so c. part., μεστὸς ἦν θυμούμενος i. e. had had my fill of anger, Soph.
to fill full of a thing, c. gen., Soph.:—Pass. to be filled or full of, Id.
until, c. gen., μέσφ’ ἠοῦς Il.; with adv., μ. ἐχθές till to-morrow, Theocr.
a passing over, migration, Plut.
change, revolution in government, Plat.
transition from one to another, Luc.
to carry over, shift bring into another place or state Ar., Xen.
to lead in a different direction, Plat.
one must change, trans., τινὰ εἴς τι Plat.
intr., Id.
by way of exchange, Arist.: ἡ μεταβλητική (sub. τέχνη) exchange, barter, Plat.
a change, changing, Pind.
exchange, barter, traffic, Thuc.

(from Mid.) a transition, change, and in pl. changes, vicissitudes, Hdt., Eur.:—c. gen. change from a thing, μ. κακῶν Eur.; rarely change to . . , μ. ἀπραγμοσύνης Thuc.; but this is generally expressed by a prep., ἅμα τῇ μ. ἐς Ἕλληνας their going over to the Greeks, Hdt.; ἡ ἐναντία μ. change to the contrary, Thuc.
μ. τῆς ἡμέρης an eclipse, Hdt.
μ. πολιτείας change of government, a revolution, Thuc.
as military term, a wheeling about, Polyb.; metaph. of a speaker, Aeschin.
to alter one's plans, change one's mind, Od.; but commonly as Dep. μεταβουλεύομαι, Hdt., Eur.; μετ. στράτευμα μὴ ἄγειν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἑλλάδα to change one's mind and not march, Hdt.
changing one's mind, changeful, Ar.
a messenger between two parties, Lat. internuncius, -cia, of Iris, Il.
the second month of the Athen. year, the latter half of August and first of September, so called because then people flitted and changed their neighbours.

entry.note: ionic and later -γῑνώσκω fut. -γνώσομαι aor2 μετέγνων
entry.sense: to change one's mind, to repent, Hdt., attic
c. acc. rei, to change one's mind about a thing, to repent of, μετέγνων τὰ πρόσθ’ εἰρημένα Eur.; μ. τὰ προδεδογμένα to alter or repeal a previous decree, Thuc.
c. inf. to change one's mind so as to do something different, Id.; μετ. ὡς . . , to change one's mind and think that . . , Xen.
repentance, remorse, Soph.
change of mind or purpose, Hdt., Dem.
to write differently, to alter or correct what one has written, Eur., Thuc.; in a trial, to alter the record, Dem.
to translate, Luc.: Mid., τὰς ἐπιστολὰς μεταγραψάμενοι having got them translated, Thuc.
to transcribe, Luc.
to convey from one place to another: metaph., τὴν ψυχὴν ἐς εὐφροσύνην Anth.
intr. to go by another route, change one's course, Xen.
Dep. to share the feast with another, c. dat., Hom.:— to partake of a thing, c. gen., Il.
one must untie, Xen.
in the midst of or among the people, in the country, Od.
to change one's way of life, Luc.
to give part of, give a share of a thing, c. gen., Theogn., Hdt., attic
the part given is sometimes expressed, μ. τὸ τριτημόριόν τινι Hdt.; μ. τὸ μέρος Xen.
pursued, overtaken, Hdt.
to follow closely after, pursue, c. acc., Hdt., Xen.

to change one's opinion:—mostly impers., δείσασα μή σφι μεταδόξῃ in fear lest they should change their mind, Hdt.; c. acc. et inf., μετέδοξέ σοι ταῦτα βελτίω εἶναι you changed your mind and thought that this was better, Luc.:—part., μεταδόξαν when they changed their mind, Dem.; and in Pass., μεταδεδογμένον μοι μὴ στρατεύεσθαι since I have changed my mind and resolved not to march, Hdt.
to change one's opinion, Plat.
in the middle of supper, during supper, Od.
after supper, Anth.
the giving a share, imparting, Xen.
exchange of commodities, Arist.
a contribution, Plut.
one must give a share, τινί τινος Plat., Xen.
falling at haphazard, Hes.
adv. running after, following close upon, Il.
a running after, pursuit, Eur., Xen.
running after, taking vengeance for a thing, c. gen., Soph.
afterwards, in the rear, Hes.
to put to another carriage, Xen.
transposition, Dem.
change of sides or opinions, amendment, Polyb.
a power of changing, Thuc.
to run after, chase, Xen., etc.
to hunt or range over, τὰ ὄρη Id.: absol. to hunt about, range, Id.
to seat oneself with or beside, Od.
to lift up and remove, to shift, Eur.; ψήφισμα μ. repeal a decree, Dem.
intr. to depart, NTest.
to rush after, rush upon an enemy, Hom.
μ. τινά to follow him closely, Pind.
to demand one's share of a thing, c. gen., Hdt.: also μεταιτεῖν μέρος τινός Ar.:—absol., μ. παρά τινος Dem.
to beg of, ask alms of, c. acc. pers., Ar.
to beg, solicit, Luc.
a beggar, Luc.
c. gen. rei, being in part the cause of a thing, accessory to it, c. gen., Hdt., attic: —c. dat. pers., θεοὺς τοὺς ἐμοὶ μεταιτίους νόστου who were accessory to my return, Aesch.
between two armies:—as Subst. μεταίχμιον, ου, τό, the space between two armies, Hdt., Eur.; ἐν μεταιχμίοις δορός Eur.
a disputed frontier, debateable land, Hdt.:—metaph., ἐν μεταιχμίῳ σκότου in the border-land between light and darkness, Aesch.
what is midway between, c. gen., ἀνὴρ γυνή τε χὤτι τῶν μεταίχμιον Id.; πεδαίχμιοι λαμπάδες hanging in mid air, Id.
Mid. to change one's seat, Luc.
to model anew, Anth.
to call away to another place, Aeschin.: to call back, recall, Thuc.
in Mid. to call in a physician, Luc.
to follow after, absol., Il.: c. acc. to chase, Τρῶας μετεκίαθε Id.
to go to visit, Αἰθίοπας μετεκίαθε Od.
to transpose, shift, remove, Hdt.:— Mid. to go from one place to another, Id.
to change, alter, τὴν πολιτείαν Dem.
to be removed, Luc.
to be disturbed, Thuc.
to weep afterwards or too late, Il.:—Mid. to lament after or next, Eur.
Pass. to shift to the other side, Il.
Pass. to change to a state of sleep, to be lulled to sleep, Aesch.
sharing in common, partaking, Aesch.; τινι with another, Id.
to transport, Plat.:—Mid. to cause to be carried over, Lycurg.
to roll to another place, to roll over, Ar.
between the waves, ἄτας μ. between two waves of misery, i. e. bringing a short lull or pause from misery, Eur.
to have a share of a thing allotted one, c. gen., Plat.; also, μ. μέρος τινός Eur.
to have or get a share of, to partake of a thing, c. gen., Hdt., etc.:—Mid., μεταλαμβάνεσθαί τινος to get possession of, lay claim to, Id.
the part received is sometimes added in acc., μ. μοῖραν or μέρος τινός Eur., etc.; μ. τὸ πέμπτον μέρος τῶν ψήφων Plat.
c. gen. pers. to share his society, Xen.: in bad sense, to lay hold of, accuse, Ar.
to take after another, to succeed to, c. acc., Xen.
to take in exchange, substitute, πόλεμον ἀντ’ εἰρήνης Thuc.; μ. τὰ ἐπιτηδεύματα to adopt new customs, Id.; ἱμάτια μ. Xen.
to interchange, Plat.
to leave off, cease from, c. gen., Il.
participation, Plat.; τινος in a thing, Il.
change, μ. τῆς ἡμέρης an eclipse, Hdt.; ἐν μεταλλαγῇ πολυμηχάνου ἀνδρός by having a crafty man for thy master instead [of me], Soph.
c. gen. objecti, μ. πολέμου a change from war, Xen.
changed, altered, Aesch.
to change, alter, Hdt.
to exchange,
to take in exchange, adopt, assume, ὀρνίθων φύσιν Ar.; so, μ. τόπον, χώραν to go into a new country, Plat.
to exchange by leaving, to quit, μ. τὸν βίον Isocr.; so, μεταλλάσσειν alone, Plat.
intr. to undergo a change, Hdt.
to be searched out, Pind.
properly, to search after other things (μετὰ ἄλλα, cf. μέταλλον), to search carefully, to inquire diligently, Od.
c. acc. pers. to inquire of, question, Hom.
c. acc. objecti, to ask about or after, Id.; so, μεταλλῆσαι ἀμφὶ πόσει Od.
c. dupl. acc. to ask one about a thing, ask him a thing, Id.
a searching for metals and the like, mining, Plat.
one who searches for metals, a miner, Strab.
skilled in searching for metals: ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη) the art of mining, Arist.
to get by mining:—Pass. to be got by mining, of metals, Plat., etc.
generally, to explore, Anth.
of or for mines, Dem.
a mine or quarry, ἁλὸς μέταλλον a salt- pit, salt- mine, Hdt.; χρύσεα καὶ ἀργύρεα μέταλλα gold and silver mines, Id.; μέταλλα (alone) silver mines, Xen.; μαρμάρου μ. marble quarries, Strab.
the sense of metal, Lat. metallum, does not occur in classical Greek.
entry.etym: Prob., like μεταλλάω, from μετ’ ἄλλα, a search for other things.

entry.sense: Dep. to search after, chase, Pind.
to learn differently, μετ. γλῶσσαν to unlearn one language and learn another instead, Hdt.; μ. ὕμνον to learn a new strain, Aesch.
to learn to forget, unlearn, Lat. dediscere, Aeschin.
absol. to learn better, Ar.
to exchange, ἐσλὸν πήματος good for ill, Pind.
to change to another form, ἐκ βοὸς μετάμειβε γυναῖκα Mosch.
γᾶν τέκνοις μ. to hand down land to children, Eur.
Mid. to change one's condition, to escape, Pind.; μεταμειβόμενοι in turns. Id.
c. acc., μ. τί τινι to change one thing for another, Eur.

entry.note: imperf. μετ-έμελε fut. -μελήσει aor1 μετεμέλησε fut. -μελήσομαι aor1 -εμελήθην
entry.sense: impers. it repents me, rues me, Lat. poenitet me:—Construction:
c. dat. pers. et gen. rei, μεταμέλει σοι τῆς δωρεᾶς Xen.
oftener, the thing one repents of is in part. agreeing with the dat., μεταμέλει μοι οὕτως ἀπολογησαμένῳ I repent of having so defended myself, Plat.
absol., μ. μοι it repents me, Ar.; ξυνέβη ὑμῖν πεισθῆναι μὲν ἀκεραίοις, μεταμέλειν δὲ κακουμένοις to adopt a measure when your forces are unbroken, and to repent when in distress, Thuc.
part. neut. μεταμέλον absol., since it repented him, Plat.
seldom with a nom., to cause repentance or sorrow, τῷ Ἀρίστωνι μετέμελε τὸ εἰρημένον (for τοῦ εἰρημένου) Hdt., ; οἶμαί σοι ταῦτα μεταμελήσει (for τούτων) Ar.
Dep., to feel repentance, to rue, regret, c. part., μετεμέλοντο οὐ δεξάμενοι they repented that they had not received, Thuc.: absol. to change one's purpose or line of conduct, Xen.
Causal in part. fut. τὸ μεταμελησόμενον that which will cause regret, matter for future repentance, Id.
change of purpose, regret, repentance, Thuc.; μ. ἔχει με = μεταμέλει μοι, Xen.
full of regrets, Arist.
repentance, regret, Thuc.
Dep. to sing or dance among others, c. dat., Hhymn.
to mix among, confound with, τί τινι Od.
to transform: Pass. to be transfigured, NTest.
a transformation, Luc.
Mid., to put on a different dress, μ. δουλείαν to put on the new dress of slavery, Plat.

to change the dress of another, strip off his dress, τινά Plut., Luc.:—metaph. to change, τι εἴς τι Anth.; ἀποδυσάμενος τὸν Πυθαγόραν τίνα μετημφιάσω μετ’ αὐτόν; what body didst thou assume after him? Luc.
borne by the wind, τὰ δὲ πάντα θεοὶ μετ. θεῖεν may the gods give all that to the winds, Il.; ἐς κόρακας βαδιεῖ μεταμώνιος Ar.
bootless, vain, idle, μεταμώνια νήματα vainly-woven webs, Od.; μεταμώνια βάζειν to talk idly, Id.
Pass. to repent of a thing, c. gen., Soph.
to dwell with, τινί Hhymn.
one who dwells with, Hes.
migration, Thuc.
one who has changed his home, a wanderer, immigrant, commonly as a term of reproach, like Scottish land-louper, Il.
wandering, Anth.
a wanderer, Anth.
to pass over to the other side, Ἠέλιος μετενίσσετο the sun was passing over the meridian, Hom.
c. acc. to go after, pursue, Eur.: also to win, get possession of, Pind.
to remove one from his country, Polyb.
Pass. c. aor2 et perf. act. to move off and go elsewhere, to migrate, Hdt., Soph.
to change one's mind or purpose, Plat., Xen.
to repent, Antipho., etc.
after-thought, repentance, Thuc., etc.
to draw from one vessel into another, Anth.
adv.,
of Place, betwixt, between, Il., etc.; with the Art., τὸ μεταξύ Hdt.; ἐν τῷ μ. Thuc.
of Time, between-whiles, meanwhile, Hdt., etc; with pres. part., μεταξὺ ὀρύσσων in the midst of his digging, Lat. inter fodiendum, Id.; μ. θύων Ar.; λέγοντα μ. in the middle of his discourse, Plat.
after, afterwards, NTest.
of Qualities, τὰ μ. intermediate, i. e. neither good nor bad, Plat.
as prep. with gen. between, Hdt., etc.
of Time, ὁ μ. τῆς δίκης τε καὶ τοῦ θανάτου [χρόνος] Plat.; τὰ μ. τούτου meanwhile, Soph.
to educate differently, Luc.
Mid. to rest between-whiles, Il.
rest between-whiles, πολέμοιο from war, Il.
to change a man's persuasion, Ar., Dem.:—Pass. to be persuaded to change, Plat., etc.

sense.gloss: in the midst of, among with gen., dat., and acc.

entry.sense: Prep. with gen., dat., and acc.
WITH GEN. in the midst of, among a number, μετ’ ἄλλων ἑταίρων Od.; πολλῶν μετὰ δούλων Aesch.
in common, along with, μετὰ Βοιωτῶν ἐμάχοντο Il.; μ. ξυμμάχων κινδυνεύειν Thuc.; μετά τινος πάσχειν, στῆναι Aesch., Soph.
with, by means of, ἱκετεύειν μετὰ δακρύων Plat.; μετ’ ἀρετῆς πρωτεύειν Xen.:—as a periphr. for Adverbs, ὁσίως καὶ μετ’ ἀληθείας Plat.
WITH DAT., only poet., mostly epic,
properly of persons, among, in company with, μετὰ τριτάτοισιν ἄνασσεν in or among the third generation Nestor reigned, Il.
of things, μετὰ νηυσί, ἀστράσι among, in the midst of, Hom.; μετὰ πνοιῇς ἀνέμοιο in company with the winds, as swift as they, Id.
between, μετὰ χερσὶν ἔχειν to hold between, i. e. in, the hands, Il.; μετὰ φρεσίν Id.
to complete a number, with, besides, πέμπτος μετὰ τοῖσιν a fifth with them, Hom.;—N. B., μετά is never used with dat. sg., unless of collective Nouns, μετὰ στρατῷ Il.
WITH ACCUS.,
of motion, into the middle of coming among a number, μετὰ φῦλα θεῶν Hom.; μετὰ λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν Il.

in pursuit or quest of, βῆναι μετὰ Νέστορα Id.; in hostile sense. βῆναι μετά τινα to go after, pursue him, Id.;—also, βῆναι μετὰ πατρὸς ἀκουήν to go in search of news of thy father, Od.; πόλεμον μέτα θωρήσσοντο they were arming for the battle, Il.
of mere sequence or succession,
of Place, after, next after, behind, λαοὶ ἕπονθ’ ὡσεὶ μετὰ κτίλον ἕσπετο μῆλα as sheep follow after the bell-wether, Il.
of Time, after, next to, μεθ’ Ἕκτορα πότμος ἑτοῖμος after Hector thy death is at the door, Id.; μετὰ ταῦτα thereupon, thereafter, attic; μεθ’ ἡμέραν in the course of the day, Hdt.
of Worth, Rank, next to, next after, following a Sup., κάλλιστος ἀνὴρ μετ’ ἀμύμονα Πηλείωνα Il.
after, according to, μετὰ σὸν καὶ ἐμὸν κῆρ as you and I wish, Id.; μετ’ ὔλμον by the line of the furrow, Id.
generally, among, between, as with dat., μετὰ πάντας ἄριστος best among all, Il.; μετὰ χεῖρας ἔχειν Hdt.
absol. as ADV. among them, with them, Il.
and then, next afterwards, thereafter, Hom., Hdt.
μέτα for μέτεστι, Od., etc.
IN COMPOS:
of community or participation, as μεταδίδωμι, μετέχω, c. gen. rei.
of action in common with another, as μεταδαίνυμαι, c. dat. pers.
of an interval, as μεταίχμιον.
of succession, as μεταδόρπιος.
of pursuit, as μετέρχομαι.
of letting go, as μεθίημι.
after, behind, as μετάφρενον.
back again, reversely, as μετατρέπω, μεταστρέφω.
most often of change of place, condition, plan, etc., as μεταβαίνω, μεταβουλεύω, etc.
to pass over from one place to another, μετὰ δ’ ἄστρα βεβήκει ( for μετεβεβήκει) the stars had passed over the meridian, Od.; μ. ἐς τὴν Ἀσίην Hdt.: to go over to the other side, Aesch.
to pass from one point to another, μετάβηθι change thy theme, Od.; μεταβάντες changing their course, turning round, Hdt.; μ. ἐκ μείζονος εἰς ἔλαττον Plat.
c. acc., μεταβὰς βίοτον having passed to another life, Eur.
Causal in aor1 μεταβῆσαι, to carry over, to change, Id.
to throw into a different position, to turn quickly, μετὰ νῶτα βαλών Il.; μ. θοἰμάτιον ἐπὶ δεξιάν to throw one's mantle over to the right, Ar.
to turn about, change, alter, Hdt., attic; μ. ὕδατα to drink different water, Hdt.:— μ. ὀργάς to change, i. e. give up, anger, Eur.
intr. to undergo a change, change one's condition, Hdt., Plat.

to change one's course, μεταβαλὼν πρὸς Ἀθηναίους changing his course and turning to the Athenians, Hdt.:—the part. μεταβάλλων or μεταβαλών is used absol., almost like an adv. instead, in turn, Id., Eur.
Mid. to change what is one's own, etc. μ. ἱμάτια to change one's clothes, Xen.; μ. τοὺς τρόπους Ar., etc.
to change one with another, exchange, μ. σιγὰν λόγων to exchange silence for words, Soph.: — to barter, traffic, Xen.
to turn oneself, turn about, Plat.:— to change one's purpose, change sides, Hdt., Thuc.
to turn or wheel about, Xen.
to change by dipping, Plut., Luc.
to be sent for, Thuc.
sent for, Hdt., Thuc.
to send after, Eur., Ar.:— to send for, summon, Lat. arcessere, Hdt., etc.; so in Med: —Pass., aor1 μεταπεμφθῆναι to be sent for, Dem.
Dep. to fly to another place, fly away, Luc.
to leap from one place to another, jump about, Luc.
to fall differently, undergo a change, μ. τὸ εἶδος Hdt., or εἰς ἄλλο εἶδος Plat.: also, to change one's opinion suddenly, Eur., Ar.; εἰ τρεῖς μόναι μετέπεσον τῶν ψήφων Plat.
to change, esp. for the worse, μεταπίπτοντος δαίμονος if fortune changes, Eur.; rarely for the better, Id.:—of political changes, to undergo change or revolution, Thuc.
to mould differently, remodel, Plat.; so in Mid., Anth.
to alter the make of a thing, remodel, alter, Solon., Dem.
Mid. to make a pretence of, lay claim to, pretend to, c. gen., ἀρετῆς Thuc.
Dep.
to go after, follow up, ἔχθραν Lys.
to pursue, punish, Polyb.
a selling by retail, retail-trade, Strab.
distinguished among others, c. dat. pl., Il.
to distinguish oneself or be distinguished among others, c. dat. pl., Hom.
change, Plat.: change of party, Polyb.
the wall between two towers, the curtain, Thuc.
counted among others, c. dat. pl., Hhymn.
to flow differently, to change to and fro, ebb and flow, Arist.
to turn upside down, Dem.
to change the fashion of a thing, to remodel, Hdt., Aesch.:— to reform, amend, Xen.
Pass. to rise high into the air, νέφος μεταρσιωθέν Hdt.,
raised form the ground, high in air, Lat. sublimis, Trag.; λόγοι πεδάρσιοι scattered to the winds, Aesch.; ναῦς ἄρμεν’ ἔχοισα μετάρσια a ship having her sails hoisted, Theocr.
like μετέωρος II. 2, on the high sea, out at sea, Hdt.
metaph. in air, high above this world, Eur.
of things, airy, empty, Id.
in Medic., of the breath, high, quick.

entry.note: epic μετασσεύομαι 3rd sg. epic aor2 μετέσσῠτο
entry.sense: Pass.:— to rush towards or after, Il.:— c. acc. to rush upon, μετέσσυτο ποιμένα λαῶν Id.
to put into another dress (σκευή), to change the fashion of, transform, Xen.
Mid. to pack up so as to shift one's quarters, Luc.
to draw over from one side to another, Soph.
lambs born midway between the πρόγονοι (early-born) and the ἕρσαι (freshlings or lateborn).
a removing, removal, κακοῦ Andoc.
（μεθίσταμαι) a being put into a different place, removal, migration, Plat.; μ. ἡλίου an eclipse, Eur.
a changing, change, Id.; θυμῷ μετάστασιν διδόναι to allow a change to one's wrath, i. e. suffer it to cease, Soph.
a change of political constitution, revolution, Thuc.
one must alter, Isocr.
to go in quest of, τινά Eur.
Mid., to send for, summon, Luc.
only in pres. and imperf., to lament afterwards, Od., Aesch.
to lament after this or next, Eur.
adv. all in a row, Il.
to sigh or lament afterwards, Hes.
to shift one's ground or camp, Polyb.:—so in Mid., Xen.
fit for turning another way, fit for directing, Plat.
to turn about, turn round, turn, Il., Ar.:—Pass. to turn oneself about, turn about, whether to face the enemy or to flee, Il.; then, simply, to turn round, Hdt., Plat.
to pervert, change, alter, Plat., etc.:—Pass., τἀμὰ μετεστράφη my fortunes are changed, Eur.; τὸ ψήφισμ’ ὅπως μεταστραφείη Ar.
intr. to turn another way, change one's ways, Il.; μεταστρέψας contrariwise, Plat.
c. gen. to care for, regard, Eur.
a turning from one thing to another, Plat.
participation, τινος in the nature of a thing, Plat.
to change the form of a person or thing, Plat.
to transfer as in a figure, NTest.
to transpose: Mid. to change one's order of battle, Xen.; μετατάσσεσθαι παρ’ Ἀθηναίους to go over and join them, Thuc.
to place among, τῷ κ’ οὔτι τόσον κέλαδον μετέθηκεν (variant reading: μεθέηκεν) then he would not have caused so much noise among us, Od.
to place differently,
in local sense, to transpose, Plat.
to change, alter, of a treaty, Thuc., Xen.; μ. τὰς ἐπωνυμίας ἐπὶ ὑός to change their names and call them after swine, Hdt.; μ. τι ἀντί τινος to put one thing in place of another, substitute, Dem.
Mid. to change what is one's own or for oneself, τοὺς νόμους, Xen.; μετατίθεσθαι τὴν γνώμην to adopt a new opinion, Hdt.; so, absol., Plat.
μ. [τὸν φόβον] to get rid of, transfer one's fear, Dem.
c. dupl. acc., τὸ κείνων κακὸν τῷδε κέρδος μ. to alter their evil designs into gain for him, Soph.
Pass. to be changed, to alter, Eur.
to bring forth afterwards, Aesch.
Mid., to turn oneself round, turn round, Il.
to look back to, shew regard for, c. gen., Id.
to run after, οὔκουν παρ’ Ἀθηναίων σὺ μεταθρέξει; you run and get it from the Athenians, Ar.
Pass. to turn about, il.
retribution, vengeance for a thing, c. gen., Eur.
a turn of fortune, a reverse, Pind.
turning about, returning, Anth.
turning round upon, Aesch.; ἔργα μετάτροπα deeds that turn upon their author or are visited with vengeance, Hes.; so, μ. αὖραι Eur.; πολέμου μετάτροπος αὔρα Ar.
to look keenly about for, τινά Pind.
to speak among others, to address them, c. dat. pl., Hom.
c. acc. pers. to accost, address, Mosch.
afterwards, Hdt., Aesch.
just after, presently after, Hdt.
to carry over, transfer, Dem.; μ. κέντρα πώλοις to apply the goad to the horses in turn, Eur.
to change, alter, Soph., Dem.; μ. τὰ δίκαια to change, confound, Aeschin.
in Rhetoric, to use a word in a changed sense, to employ a metaphor, Arist.
to speak among others, to address them, c. dat. pl., Hom.
c. acc. pers. to accost, Il.
apt at metaphors, Arist.
metaphorical: adv. -κῶς, Plut.
to paraphrase, to translate, Plut.
Mid. to consider after, ταῦτα μεταφρασόμεσθα καὶ αὖτις Il.
a paraphrasing, Plut.
properly, the part behind the midriff (μετὰ τὰς φρένας), the back, Il., Plat.
to speak among others, c. dat. pl., Il.

entry.note: fut. attic ιῶ aor1 -εχείρισα fut. attic -ιοῦμαι aor1 -εχειρισάμην and -εχειρίσθην perf. -κεχείρισμαι
entry.etym: sometimes active, but more commonly as Dep.
entry.sense: to have or take in hand, handle, administer, manage, Hdt.
to manage, arrange, conduct, Thuc.:—so as Dep., Ar., Xen.
to practise, pursue an art or study, Plat.; c. inf. to study to do, Id.
c. acc. pers. to handle, treat, or deal with in a certain way, χαλεπῶς τινὰ μεταχειρίζειν Thuc.:—of a physician, Plat.
happening afterwards, Luc.
in Hes. = μετάρσιος.
after the time, done later, Luc.
to go to another place, to withdraw, migrate, emigrate, Aesch., Thuc.
to brush against a thing, c. acc., Eur.
to put upon a new register: 3 sg. fut. 2 pass. μετεγγραφήσεται he will be put on a new register, Ar.
to be among, c. dat. pl., Hom.; absol., οὐ παυσωλὴ μετέσσεται no interval of rest will be mine, Il.
impers., μέτεστί μοί τινος I have a share in or claim to a thing, Hdt., attic:—so part. neut. used absol., οὐδὲν Αἰολεῦσι μετεὸν τῆς χώρης since the Aeolians had no share in the land, Hdt.
sometimes the share is added in nom., μέτεστι πᾶσι τὸ ἴσον Thuc.; ἐμοὶ τούτων οὐδὲν μ. Plat.

entry.note: attic fut. of μετέρχομαι imperf. μετῄειν epic aor1 part. μετεισάμενος
entry.sense: to go between or among others, Il.
to go after or behind, follow, Id., Xen.
c. acc. to go after, go in quest of, pursue, Hdt., attic
to pursue with vengeance, Aesch., Thuc.; δίκας μ. τινα (where δίκας is acc. cogn.), to execute judgment upon one, Aesch.
to pursue, go about a business, Eur.
μ. τινὰ θυσίαις to approach one with sacrifices, Hdt.: c. acc. et inf., ἕνα ἕκαστον μετῄεσαν μὴ ἐπιτρέπειν besought each one not to permit, Thuc.
to pass over to another, Ar.
to speak among others address them, c. dat. pl., Hom.
absol. to speak thereafter, afterwards, Id.
to go from one place into another, Hdt.; c. acc., μ. φθόγγον to pass from one note to another, Anth.
to lend out, Plut.
Mid. to pull off one's own clothes and put on others, to assume, Plut.
one must punish, Luc.
to go on board another ship, Plut.
Causal of μετ-εμβαίνω, to put on board another ship, Thuc.
engrafted afresh, Anth.
Causal in aor1, to put other clothes on a person, invest with new power, τινά τι, Luc.
Pass. μετενδύομαι, with aor2 act. μετενέδῡν, to put on other clothes, Strab.
to speak among, τινί Mosch.
to put into another place: Mid., μετεντίθεσθαι τὸν γόμον to shift a ship's cargo, Dem.
Mid. to take out of and put elsewhere, Dem.
Pass. to move from one place to another, Luc.
some among many, certain persons, Hdt.
afterwards, thereafter, Hom.

entry.note: aeolic and doric πεδ-έρχομαι fut. μετελεύσομαι aor2 μετ-ῆλθον perf. -ελήλυθα
entry.etym: in attic, the imperf. and fut. are borrowed from μέτειμι, q. v.
entry.sense: to come or go among others, c. dat. pl. or absol., Hom.; μετελθών having gone between the ranks, Il.
to go to another place, Id.: simply to come next, follow, Pind.
c. acc. to go after, to go to seek, go in quest of Il., attic: generally, to seek for, aim at, Eur., Thuc.
in hostile sense, to pursue, Il., Hdt., attic: c. acc. rei, to seek to avenge, Aesch., Eur.:—then c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, μ. τι τινά to visit a crime upon a person, Eur.
of things, to go after, attend to, to pursue a business, Hom., attic
to approach with prayers, Lat. adire, prosequi, τινα Hdt., Eur.: to court or woo, Pind.
Dep. to change one's wish, to wish something else, Eur.

entry.note: aeolic πεδ-έχω fut. μεθ-έξω perf. μετ-έσχηκα
entry.sense: to partake of, enjoy a share of, share in, take part in, c. gen. rei, Theogn., Aesch.; c. gen. pers. to partake of a person's friendship, Xen.; μ. τῶν πεντακισχιλίων to be members of the 5000 in turn, Thuc.:— with dat. pers. added, μετ. τινός τινι to partake of something in common with another, Pind., Eur.:— often the part or share is added, μ. τάφου μέρος Aesch., etc.
rarely with the acc. only, ἀκερδῆ χάριν μ. Soph.
absol., οἱ μετέχοντες the partners, Hdt.

to raise to a height, raise, Thuc.:—Mid., δελφῖνας μετεωρίζου heave up your dolphins (v. δελφίς II), Ar.:—Pass. to be raised up, to float in mid-air, Lat. suspendi, Id., etc.: of ships, to keep out on the high sea, Thuc.
metaph. to lift up, buoy up with false hopes, Dem.:—Pass. to be elevated, excited, Ar.
to prate about high things, Ar.
one who prates on things above, a star-gazer, visionary, Plat.
to talk of high things, Plat.
discussion of high things, Plat.
one who talks of the heavenly bodies, an astronomer, Plat.
a star-gazer, Plat.
an astrological sophist, Ar.
raised from the ground, hanging, Lat. suspensus, Hdt.;—of high ground, Thuc.

like μετάρσιος, in mid-air, high in air, Lat. sublimis, Hdt., Ar.; Ἀήρ, ὃς ἔχεις τὴν γῆν μ. poised on high, Ar.; τὰ μ. χωρία the regions of air, Id.; τὰ μ. things in heaven above, astronomical phenomena, Id., Plat.
on the high sea, out at sea, of ships, Thuc.
metaph. of the mind, lifted up, buoyed up, on the tiptoe of expectation, in suspense, Lat. spe erectus, Id.
wavering, uncertain, Dem.: —adv., μετεώρως ἔχειν to be in uncertainty, Plut.
an astrological quack, Ar.
swift as wind, Anth.
lifted off the ground, hanging, Il.:—doric πεδάορος Aesch.
metaph. wavering, thoughtless, Hhymn.
= μετοικία 1, Anth.:—the Removal or Captivity of the Jews, NTest.
to change one's abode, remove to a place, c. acc. loci, Eur.:—c. dat. loci, to settle in, Pind.
absol. to be a μέτοικος or settler, reside in a foreign city, Eur., Ar., etc.
change of abode, removal, migration, Thuc.
a settling as μέτοικος, settlement or residence in a foreign city, Aesch., etc.
to lead settlers to another abode, Plut.
in the condition of a μέτοικος, Plut.: — τὸ μ. the list of μέτοικοι, Luc.
the tax paid by the μέτοικοι, Plat.
μετοίκια, ων, τά, the feast of migration, Plut.
emigration, Plut.
an emigrant, Plut.
to build differently, Plut.
changing one's abode, emigrating and settling elsewhere, Hdt.
as Subst. μέτοικος, ἡ, an alien settled in a foreign city, a settler, emigrant, sojourner, Aesch., etc.; μ. γῆς one who has settled in a country, Id.
at Athens, a resident alien, who paid a tax (μετοίκιον), but enjoyed no civic rights, Thuc., etc.
guardian of the μέτοικοι, Xen.
Dep. to have gone after, to have gone in quest of, c. acc. pers., Hom.: c. acc. rei, to seek for, Eur.
with hostile intent, to pursue, Il.
to have gone among or through, Od.
to keep changing from one knee to another, said of a coward crouching in ambush, Il.
