a calling upon, appealing, τινος to one, Thuc.: intreaty, deprecation, Strab.
an exhortation, address, Thuc., Aeschin.: encouragement, NTest.
one must call on, summon, Arist.
hortatory, Plat.
called to one's aid, Lat. advocatus: as Subst. a legal assistant, advocate, Dem.
in NTest., ὁ Παράκλητος, the Intercessor or the Comforter.
bending sideways, turning aside, swerving, οὐκ ἂν ἔγωγε ἄλλα παρὲξ εἴποιμι παρακλιδόν I would not tell you another tale beside the mark, swerving from the truth, Od.
to bend or turn aside, παρακλίνας κεφαλήν Od.; π. τὴν θύραν, τὴν πύλην to set it ajar, Hdt.
metaph., ἄλλῃ παρκλίνουσι δίκας they turn justice from her path, Hes.
to lay beside another:—Pass. to lie down beside, at meals, Lat. accumbere, τινι Theocr.
intr. to turn aside, Il.; παρακλίνασα having swerved from the course, Aesch.
one who lies beside at meals, Xen.
to be past the prime, Xen.
the point at which the prime is past, abatement, Plut.
unwillingness to hear, disobedience, NTest.
Mid. to communicate, τί τινι Pind.
to keep watch beside, Polyb.
one who sleeps beside, a bedfellow, husband, spouse, Il., Hes.
a wife, spouse, Il.; epic dat. παρακοίτῑ Od.
to follow beside, follow closely, c. dat., Dem.: of a physician, π. νοσήματι Plat.; so, π. τοῖς πράγμασιν ἐξ ἀρχῆς Dem.: of an audience, to follow with the mind, Aeschin.
a carrying across, transporting, Thuc.
(from Pass.) a going or sailing across, passage, transit, Id.
to carry along with one, escort, convoy, Eur.
to carry or convey over, to transport, Xen.: generally, to convey, carry, Hdt.: —Mid. to have a thing brought one, Xen.
Pass. to go or sail beside, coast along, τὴν Ἰταλίαν Thuc.
to go or sail across, pass over, Polyb.
to sharpen besides, sharpen also, Xen.:—Pass. to be so sharpened, 3rd pl. perf. pass. παρηκόνηνται Ar.
to throw the dart with others, Luc.
metaph. infatuation, insanity, frenzy, Aesch.
frenzied, frantic, Aesch.; also, παράκοπος φρενῶν Eur.
to strike falsely: Pass., perf. part. παρακεκομμένος, of coin, counterfeit; metaph. of men, ἀνδράρια μοχθηρά, παρακεκομμένα knavish mannikins, base coin, Ar.
Mid. to cheat or swindle out of a thing, π. τινὰ ἀγαθῶν Id.; simply, to cheat, τινά Id.:—Pass. to be cheated, τινι in a thing, Id.
metaph. to strike the mind awry, drive mad, Eur.
a false story, Strab.
one must disobey, τινός Muson. ap. Stob.
to hear beside, esp. to hear accidentally, to hear talk of, c. acc., Hdt.
to hear underhand, overhear from, τί τινος Ar.; τι παρά τινος Plat.
to hear imperfectly or wrongly, misunderstand, Id.
to hear carelessly, take no heed to, c. gen., NTest.
to hang beside, χεῖρα παρακρεμάσας letting the hand hang down, Il.
on the edge of a precipice, Strab.
to draw up in line opposite: Pass., πεζὸς παρακεκριμένος παρὰ τὸν αἰγιαλόν the land force drawn up along the shore, Hdt.; παρεκρίθησαν διαταχθέντες Id.
to pat or clap one, Luc.
a striking falsely: metaph. a cheating, deception, Dem.:— a fallacy, Arist.
to strike aside: to disappoint, mislead, Plat.:—Pass. to be led astray, go wrong, Id., Dem.:—so also in Mid., Isocr.
in Mid. also, to strike away from oneself, parry, Plut.
Dep. to get over and above: in perf. -κέκτημαι, to have over and above, Hdt.
on the sea-side, by the shore, Trag.
to stoop sideways, of the attitude of a bad harp-player, Ar.
to stoop for the purpose of looking at, and so,
to look sideways at, cast a careless glance on a thing, Dem.
to peep out of a door or window, Ar.:— or, of persons outside, to peep in, look in, κατ’ ἄντρον παρκύπτοισα Theocr.; παρέκυψεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον NTest.
to receive from another, of persons succeeding to an office, π. τὴν βασιληίην Hdt.; τὴν ἀρχήν Plat., etc.:—also of persons succeeding by inheritance, Eur., Dem.; π. ἀράς to inherit curses, Eur.
to take upon oneself, undertake, πρᾶγμά τι Ar.: Pass., τὰ παραλαμβανόμενα undertakings, Hdt.
to take in pledge, Id.: also, to take by force or treachery, get possession of, Id., Thuc.
to receive by hearsay or report, to ascertain, π. τὴν ἀλήθειαν Hdt., etc.
to take up, catch up, τὸ οὔνομα τοῦτο Id.
c. acc. pers. to take to oneself, associate with oneself, as a wife or mistress, an adopted son, a partner or ally, Id., Thuc., etc.; as a pupil, Plat.
to invite, Hdt.
to wait for, intercept, Lat. excipere, Id., Xen.: to take prisoner, Polyb.
to escape the notice of, τινά Plat.
to lay beside: Mid. to lie beside or with another, c. dat., ὁ δέ οἱ παρελέξατο λάθρη Il.;epic aor2 παρέλεκτο Hhymn.
παραλέγεσθαι τὴν γῆν to sail or coast along, Lat. legere oram, NTest.
one must pass over, τι Xen.
to leave on one side, leave remaining, Thuc., Xen.: —τοῖς ἐχθροῖς παραλείπεται is reserved for enemies, Dem.
to leave to another, λόγον τινὶ π. to leave him time for speaking, Aeschin.
to leave on one side, pass by, neglect, Eur., Ar., etc.: Pass., εἴ τις παραλείπεται [πρόσοδος] if the revenue is insufficient, Arist.
to pass over, leave untold, omit, Eur., Thuc., etc.: Pass., τὰ παραλειπόμενα omissions, Plat.
to bedaub as with ointment, Arist.
one must produce, μάρτυρας Dem.
to be accepted, Plat.
to talk like a dotard, talk nonsense, Lat. delirare, Ar., etc.
a receiving from another, succession to, τῆς ἀρχῆς Polyb.
the taking of a town, Id.
a chapel of the hero Paralus, Dem.
by the sea, Trag.
ἡ (sc. γῆ or χώρα) the seacoast, sea-board, Hdt., Arist.
the eastern coast of Attica, between Hymettus and the sea, Hdt., Thuc.
a passing from hand to hand, transmission, Aesch.
variation, change, NTest.
an interchange, variation, Strab.
alternation, alternating motion, τῶν σκελῶν Plut.
a change for the worse, alteration, Plat.

entry.note: attic -ττω fut. -ξω aor1 -ήλλαξα Pass., aor1 -ηλλάχθην aor2 -ηλλάγην perf. -ήλλαγμαι
entry.sense: to make things alternate, to transpose, Plat.
to change or alter a little, Hdt., Soph.
of Place, to pass by, go past, elude, Xen.:— to get rid of, Plut.
to go beyond, exceed in point of time, Id.
intr. to pass by one another, to overlap, Hdt.
to differ, vary, Id.:—impers., οὐ σμικρὸν παραλλάττει it makes no small difference, Plat.
π. τοῦ σκοποῦ to go aside from the mark, Id.
to deviate from the course, to be liable to deviation, Id.; λόγοι παραλλάσσοντες delirious, Eur.
to slip aside or away, Aesch.
alternately, in turn, Lat. vicissim, Soph.
in alternating rows, Lat. ad quincuncem dispositi, Thuc.

beside one another, side by side, αἱ παράλληλοι (sc. γραμμαί) parallel lines, Arist.; π. (sub. κύκλος) a parallel of latitude, Strab.; οἱ βίοι οἱ π. the parallel lives of Plutarch, Plut.; ἐκ παραλλήλου parallelwise, Id.
c. dat. parallel to, Polyb.
Dep.:
in keeping accounts, to misreckon, miscalculate, Dem.
to cheat out of a thing, to defraud of, c. dupl. acc., Arist.
to mislead by fallacious reasoning, Aeschin.:—Pass. to be so misled, Arist.
false reasoning, deception, Polyb.
fallacious, Arist.
beyond calculation, unexpected, casual, uncertain, Arist., etc.: —παράλογον, ου, an unexpected event; but, τὰ παράλογα the portions of food given to unexpected guests, Xen.:—adv. παραλόγως Dem.

παράλογος, ὁ, as Subst., an unexpected issue, Thuc.; πολύς, μέγας ὁ π. the event is greatly contrary to calculation, Id.; so, τὸν π. τοσοῦτον ποιῆσαι τοῖς Ἕλλησι caused so great a miscalculation to the Greeks, Id.; ἐν τοῖς ἀνθρωπείοις παραλόγοις by miscalculations such as men make, Id.
by or near the sea, Soph., Eur.: near the salt, (with a pun on ἡ Πάραλος), Ar.
generally, concerned with the sea, naval, Hdt.
ἡ πάραλος γῆ the coast-land of Attica (cf. παράλιος II), Thuc.;—hence οἱ Πάραλοι the people of the coast-land, Hdt., Eur.
ἡ Πάραλος ναῦς, or ἡ Π. alone, the Paralus, one of the Athenian sacred galleys, reserved for state-service, Thuc., Dem.; also Πάραλος (without Art.), Ar.
οἱ Πάραλοι, the crew of the Paralus, Id., Thuc.
dwelling near the Alps, Plut.
to grieve or trouble besides, ἄλλο παρελύπει οὐδέν no disease attacked them besides the plague, Thuc.; ὅταν μηδὲν αὐτὴν παραλυπῇ Plat.; οἱ παραλυποῦντες the troublesome, the refractory, Xen.
of soil, rather poor, Strab.
a loosening by the side: paralysis, palsy, Theophr.
paralytic, NTest.

entry.note: fut. -λύσω aor1 -έλῡσα perf. -λέλῠκα Pass., aor1 -ελύθην perf. -λέλῠμαι
entry.sense: c. acc. rei, to loose from the side, take off, detach, Hdt., etc.
to undo, put an end to, Eur.

c. acc. pers. et gen. rei, to unyoke or part from, πολλοὺς παρέλυσεν θάνατος δάμαρτος Id.; π. τινὰ τῆς στρατηίης to set free from military service, Hdt.; π. τινὰ τῆς στρατηγίης to dismiss from the command, Id.: —τοὺς Ἀθηναίους π. τῆς ὀργῆς to set them free from . . , Thuc.: c. acc. only, to set free, Eur.:—Pass. to be parted from, τινος Hdt.: to be exempt from service, Id.
to loose beside, i. e. one beside another, Xen.
in Pass. to be disabled at the side, to be paralysed, Arist.: generally, to be exhausted, to flag, of camels, Hdt.
to leave on one side, pass by, c. acc. loci, Plut.
to outrun, exceed, excel, σοφίᾳ σοφίαν Soph.
to pass, βίον Anth.
mostly in Mid. to go past, pass by, leave on one side, Od., Hdt., etc.; τὸν παραμειψάμενος Od.; παραμείβεσθαι ἔθνεα πολλά Hdt.;—but, πύλας παραμείψεται shall pass through the gates, Theogn.
to pass over, make no mention of, Lat. praetermitto, Hdt.
to outrun, outstrip, Pind., Eur.
of Time, to pass, go by, Hes.
in a causal sense, to turn aside, divert, Pind.
to pass by and disregard, to be disregardful of, τινός Thuc., Xen., etc.: absol., παρημελήκεε he recked little, Hdt.; παραμελοῦντες being negligent, Plat.:—Pass. to be abandoned, Aesch.
to stay beside or near, stand by another, c. dat., Il., Ar.; παρά τινι Aeschin.:—of slaves, to remain faithful, Plat.; hence Παρμένων, trusty, as a slave's name, Menand.
absol. to stand one's ground, stand fast, Il., Hdt., attic; to remain with the army, Thuc.
to stay at a place, stay behind or at home, Hdt.
to survive, remain alive, Id.
of things, to endure, last, Eur., Xen.
to measure one thing by another, to compare, Plat.
παραμεύεσθαί τινος μορφάν to surpass, Pind.
oblong or oval, Polyb.
extending parallel to the mainland, Strab.
along the thighs; τὰ παραμ. armour for the thighs, cuisses, Xen.
to intermix with, τί τινι Ar.:—Pass., ἡδονὴν παραμεμῖχθαι τῇ εὐδαιμονίᾳ Arist.
to add by mixing, Lat. admiscere, ὕδωρ παραμίσγειν Hdt.:—Pass., ὅ τι αὐτοῖς παραμέμικται Plat.
Dep., to mention besides, to make mention of a thing along with another, c. gen. rei, Hdt., Soph.
to abide, tarry, Od.
staying beside, i. e. steadfast, permanent, Theogn., Pind.
of slaves, trusty, Xen.
out of tune with, discordant with, c. dat., Eur.: absol. harsh, horrid, Aesch.
to wrap a thing round as a cloak: metaph., π. λόγους to use a cloak of words, Eur.
Dep.:

to encourage or exhort one to do a thing, c. dat. pers. et inf., τοῖς ἄλλοισιν ἔφη παραμυθήσασθαι οἴκαδ’ ἀποπλείειν Il.; c. acc. pers., παραμυθοῦ με (sc. ποιεῖν); ὅ τι καὶ πείσεις Aesch.:—c. acc. pers. only, to encourage, exhort, advise, Plat., Xen.
to console, comfort, τινα Hdt., attic
to pacify, παρεμυθεῖτο attempted to pacify them, Thuc.
to assuage, abate, Plut.: to soften down, explain away, Strab.
consolatory, Arist.
encouragement, exhortation, persuasion, Plat.
consolation, diversion, Id.
relief from, abatement of, φθόνου Plut.
an address, exhortation, Plat.
an assuagement, abatement, καμάτων Soph.; πυρσῶν of the fires of love, Theocr.; ἐλπὶς κινδύνῳ π. οὖσα Thuc.
Dep. to bellow beside or in answer, of thunder following on earthquake, Aesch.
to read beside, so as to compare one document with another, π. τῷ ψηφίσματι τοὺς νόμους Aeschin.; π. παρὰ μαρτυρίας τὰς ῥήσεις Dem.
to read publicly, Polyb.
Mid., with aor2 and perf. act., to come forth and appear beside or near, Plut.
to dwell near, c. acc. loci, Soph.
to spend amiss, to waste, squander, Dem.:—Pass., of persons, to be sacrificed uselessly, 3rd pl. aor1 παραναλώθησαν Plut.
useless expense, Plut.
to heap or pile up beside, only in imperf., σῖτον παρενήνεον ἐν κανέοισιν Od.
Dep. to swim along the shore, Od.: to swim beside, τῇ τριήρει Plut.
to subdue to evil, pervert, Aesch.
Dep. to go past, c. acc., Hhymn.
to set up beside: Mid. with aor2 act. to stand up beside, Plut.
trans. to raise in answer, Thuc.
intr. to stand forth beside, Plut.
to think amiss, to be deranged, lose one's wits, Eur., Ar.
derangement, madness, Aesch., Eur., Ar.
to open at the side or a little, set ajar, θύραν Dem.
to transgress the law, act unlawfully, Thuc., Plat.:—Pass., κάθοδος παρανομήθη a return illegally procured, Thuc.
to commit an outrage, ἐς τὸν νεκρὸν ταῦτα παρενόμησε Hdt.; περί τινα Thuc.:—Pass. to be outraged, ill used, Dem.
an illegal act, transgression, Thuc.
transgression of law, decency or order, Thuc., Plat.; ἡ κατὰ τὸ σῶμα π. εἰς τὴν δίαιταν loose and disorderly habits of life, Thuc.
acting contrary to law, lawless, Eur., Plat.
of things, contrary to law, unlawful, Ar., Thuc., etc.:—adv., παρανόμως, illegally, Thuc.

in attic law, παράνομα γράφειν, εἰπεῖν to propose an illegal measure, Dem.; παρανόμων γράφεσθαί τινα to indict one for proposing such a measure, Id.: the indictment itself was παρανόμων γραφή Aeschin.:—in superl., παρανομώτατα γεγραφότα Id.
distraught, Aesch.
sideways, sidewards, Il.
to pass the night beside, Plut.
the bridegroom's friend or best man, who went beside him in his chariot to fetch his bride:—as fem. the bride's-maid, Ar.
half-foreign, counterfeit, Ar.
to graze or rub in passing, Anth.
a knife worn beside the sword, a dirk, Strab.
beside the axle: τὸ π. a linchpin: —παραξόνια, in Ar. Ran., perh., rapid whirlings.
to help to train: to reform gradually, Luc.
to strike on one side: to strike a false note, and metaph. to be infatuated, lose one's wits, Aesch.: —π. τι to commit a folly, Luc.
to fall away from, Lat. aberrare, τῆς ἀληθείας Polyb.
Pass. to bound beside, τινι Eur.
altogether, absolutely, generally with Art., τὸ π. Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—with a negat., τὸ π. οὐδέν not at all, Hdt.; οὔκ εἰμι τὸ π. ἄθεος Plat.
in reckoning, ἐπὶ διηκόσια τὸ παράπαν up to two hundred altogether, Hdt.
to deceive, cajole, Aesch.
to mislead, beguile, Od.:—c. inf. to induce one to do a thing by craft or fraud, Il.
to persuade gradually, win over, beguile, Hom., in epic aor2, 3rd sg. παραιπεπίθῃσιν, part. παρ-πεπῐθών.
to send past, convey past or through, c. acc. loci, Od.
to send by or along the coast, Thuc.
to escort, convoy, of ships of war convoying merchant vessels, Dem.; so in Mid., Id.
to convoy supplies to an army, Xen.
to send troops to the flank, in support, Id.
to pass on to, of an echo, π. στόνον τινί Soph.; θόρυβον π. to waft him applause, Ar.
to send away, dismiss, Philipp. ap. Dem.

sense.gloss: from the side of, c. gen., beside, alongside of, c. dat., to the side of, motion alongside of, c. acc.

entry.sense: prep. with gen., dat., and acc.: Radical sense beside:
WITH GENIT. from the side of, from beside: from, φάσγανον ὀξὺ ἐρυσσάμενος παρὰ μηροῦ Il.
commonly of Persons, ἦλθε πὰρ Διός Id.; ἀγγελίη ἥκει παρὰ βασιλῆος Hdt.; ὁ παρά τινος ἥκων his messenger, Xen.

issuing from a person, γίγνεσθαι παρά τινος to be born from him, Plat.; when it follows a Noun, a particip. may be supplied, ἡ παρὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων δόξα glory from (given by) men, Id.; τὸ παρ’ ἐμοῦ ἀδίκημα done by me, Xen.; παρ’ ἑαυτοῦ διδόναι to give from oneself, i. e. from one's own means, Hdt.
with Verbs of receiving and obtaining, τυχεῖν τινος παρά τινος Od.; εὑρέσθαι τι παρά τινος Isocr.; δέχεσθαι, λαμβάνειν τι παρά τινος Thuc.; μανθάνειν, ἀκούειν παρά τινος Hdt.

with Pass. Verbs, on the part of (not, like ὑπό, of the direct agent), παρὰ θεῶν δίδοταί or σημαίνεταί τι Plat.; τὰ παρά τινος λεγόμενα or συμβουλευόμενα Xen.; φάρμακον πιεῖν παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ by his prescription, Plat.
in poetic passages, for παρά c. dat., near, πὰρ Σαλαμῖνος Pind.; πὰρ Κυανεᾶν σπιλάδων Soph.; παρ’ Ἰσμηνοῦ ῥείθρων Id.
WITH DAT. beside, alongside of, by, with Verbs implying rest, used to answer the question where?
of Places, ἧσθαι πὰρ πυρί Od.; ἑστάναι παρ’ ὄχεσφιν Il.; πὰρ ποσσί at one's feet, Id.; παρὰ ῥηγμῖνι θαλάσσης Id.
of persons, κεῖτο παρὰ μνηστῇ ἀλόχῳ Id.; στῆναι παρά τινι to stand by him, Id.

like Lat. apud, French chez, at one's house, μένειν παρά τινι Id.; οἱ παρ’ ἡμῖν ἄνθρωποι the people here, Plat.; ἡ παρ’ ἡμῖν πολιτεία Dem.:—like Lat. apud for penes, in one's own hands, ἔχειν παρ’ ἑωϋτῷ Hdt.
Lat. coram, before, in the presence of, ἤειδε παρὰ μνηστῆρσιν Od.: before a judge, Hdt., attic; παρ’ ἐμοί, Lat. me judice, Hdt.; εὐδοκιμεῖν, μέγα δύνασθαι, τιμᾶσθαι παρά τινι with one, Plat.
WITH ACCUS. to the side of an object, or motion alongside of it:
of Place,
with Verbs of coming and going, βῆ παρὰ θῖνα Il.; παρ’ Ἥφαιστον to his chamber, Id.; εἰσιέναι παρά τινα to go into his house, Thuc., Plat.
with Verbs of rest, beside, near, by, κεῖται ποταμοῖο παρ’ ὄχθας lies stretched beside the river banks, Il.; παρ’ ἔμ’ ἵστασο come and stand by me, Id.
with Verbs of striking, wounding, βάλε στῆθος παρὰ μαζόν Il.; αἰχμὴ δ’ ἐξεσύθη παρὰ ἀνθερεῶνα Id.
with Verbs of passing by, leaving on one side, Hom.; παρὰ τὴν Βαβυλῶνα παριέναι Xen.
by or beside the mark, πὰρ δύναμιν beyond one's strength, Il.
contrary to, against, παρὰ μοῖραν contrary to destiny, Hom.; παρ’ αἶσαν, παρὰ τὰς σπονδάς Thuc.; παρὰ δόξαν contrary to opinion, Id.; παρ’ ἐλπίδας Soph.

beside, except, οὐκ ἔστι παρὰ ταῦτ’ ἄλλα beside this there is nothing else, Ar.; παρὰ ἓν πάλαισμα ἔδραμε νικᾶν Ὀλυμπιάδα he won the Olympic prize save in one conflict, he was within one of winning it, Hdt.; so, παρὰ ὀλίγον only just, Eur.; παρ’ ἐλάχιστον ἦλθε ἀφελέσθαι was within an ace of taking away, Thuc.; παρὰ τοσοῦτον ἦλθε κινδύνου came within such a degree of peril, i. e. was in such imminent peril, Id.: —opp. to these phrases is παρὰ πολύ by far, δεινότατον παρὰ πολύ Ar.; παρὰ πολὺ νικᾶν Thuc.:—but
παρὰ ὀλίγον ποιεῖσθαι, ἡγεῖσθαι to hold of small account, Xen.; παρ’ οὐδέν ἐστι are as nothing, Soph.
with a sense of alternation, παρ’ ἡμέραν or παρ’ ἦμαρ, doric παρ’ ἆμαρ, day by day, Pind., Soph.; πληγὴ παρὰ πληγήν blow for blow, Ar.
with a sense of Comparison, παρὰ τὰ ἄλλα ζῷα ὥσπερ θεοὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι βιοτεύουσι men beyond all other animals live like gods, Xen.; χειμὼν μείζω παρὰ τὴν καθεστηκυῖαν ὥραν Thuc.
metaph. to denote dependence, on account of, because of, by means of, παρὰ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀμέλειαν Id.; παρὰ τοῦτο γέγονε Dem.
of Time, along the whole course of, during, παρὰ τὴν ζόην Hdt.; παρὰ πάντα τὸν χρόνον Dem.; παρὰ ποτόν while they were at wine, Aeschin.
at the moment of, παρ’ αὐτὰ τἀδικήματα, flagrante delicto, Dem.
POSITION: —παρά may follow its Subst. in all cases, but then becomes by anastrophe πάρα.
πάρα (with anastrophe) also stands for πάρεστι and πάρεισι.
παρά absol., as adv., near, together, at once, in Hom.
IN COMPOS.,
alongside of, beside, παράλληλοι, παραπλέω.
to the side of, to, παραδίδωμι, παρέχω.
to one side of, by, past, παρέρχομαι, παρατρέχω.
metaph.:
aside, i. e. amiss, wrong, παραβαίνω, παρακούω.
of comparison, παραβάλλω, παρατίθημι.
of change, παραλλάσσω, παράφημι.

entry.note: fut. -βήσομαι perf. -βέβηκα perf -βέβαα part. -βεβώς epic -βεβαώς aor2 παρέβην Pass., aor1 pass. παρεβάθην perf. παραβέβασμαι
entry.sense: to go by the side of, c. dat., Ἕκτορι παρβεβαώς standing beside Hector in the chariot, Il.; παρβεβαῶτε ἀλλήλοιιν Id.; so imperf. παρέβασκε is used as = ἦν παραβάτης, Id.

to pass beside or beyond, to overstep, transgress, τὰ νόμιμα Hdt.; δίκην Aesch.; τὰς σπονδάς Ar., Thuc.:—absol., παραβάντες the transgressors, Aesch.:—Pass. to be transgressed, σπονδὰς ἅς γε ὁ θεὸς νομίζει παραβεβάσθαι Thuc.; νόμῳ παραβαθέντι Id.; παραβαινομένων, absol., though offences are committed, Id.
to pass over, omit, Soph., Dem.: οὔ με παρέβα φάσμα it escaped me not, Eur.
to come forward, π. πρὸς τὸ θέατρον to step forward to address the spectators, Ar.; cf. παράβασις III.
that which is spread before a thing, a hanging curtain, Hdt., Ar.:—metaph. a screen, cover, Plat., Dem.
Dep.:— to fly alongside, Arist.
to fly past, to escape, Anth.
to fix or plant beside, Hdt.:—Pass., with perf. 2 πέπηγα, to be fixed in the ground beside, Il.: to be closely annexed to a thing, c. dat., Isocr.
to spring beyond, transgress, τοὺς νόμους Aeschin.
to embitter, provoke, NTest.
provocation, NTest.
Pass. to be inflamed, Xen.
to fall beside, Plut.
to fall in one's way, Hdt., Xen.: —καιρὸς παραπίπτει an opportunity offers, Thuc.: —ὁ παραπεσών, like ὁ παρατυχών, the first that comes, Plat.
c. dat. to befall, Id.
to fall aside or away from, c. gen., Polyb.:—absol. to fall away, NTest.

to make to wander from the right way, to drive seamen from their course, Od.:—metaph. to lead astray, perplex, Id.:—Pass., παρεπλάγχθη ἰός the arrow went aside, Il.; παραπλαγχθῆναι γνώμης to wander from reason, Eur.
almost full, Plat.
to braid or weave in, Strab.
covers for the sides of horses, Xen.
that must be sailed past, Strab.

entry.note: ionic πλώω fut. -πλεύσομαι fut. -οῦμαι epic aor2 παρέπλων
entry.etym: epic aor2 παρέπλων as if from a Verb in μι
entry.sense: to sail by or past, absol., οἴη δὴ κείνῃ γε παρέπλω Ἀργώ was the only ship that sailed past or through that way, Od.; ἐν χρῷ παραπλέοντες sailing past so as to shave closely, Thuc.
to sail along the coast, c. acc. loci, of persons making a coasting voyage, Hdt.
frenzy-stricken, Soph.
stricken sideways, ἠιόνες π. spits on which the waves break obliquely, Od.
metaph. = παράπληκτος, mad, Hdt., Ar.
to be a neighbour, Aesop.

coming near, nearly resembling, such-like, τοιαῦτα καὶ παραπλήσια such and such-like, Thuc.; ναυσὶ παραπλησίαις τὸν ἀριθμόν with ships nearly equal in number, Id.:—with dat., παραπλήσιοι ἀλλήλοις about equal, Hdt.; ὅμοια ἢ π. τούτοις Dem.

foll. by a relat., παρ. ὡς . . , Id.; π. ὥσπερ ἂν εἰ . . , Isocr.:—Neut. παραπλήσια as adv., π. ὡς εἰ . . , perinde ac si . . , Hdt.; so adv. -ίως, Plat.; παραπλησίως ἀγωνίζεσθαι, Lat. aequo Marte contendere, Hdt.
to strike at the side: — Pass. to be stricken on one side: to be deranged, frantic, γέλως παραπεπληγμένος Eur.
a sailing beside, a coasting voyage, τῆς Ἰταλίας towards Italy, Thuc.
a point sailed by or doubled, Strab.
to blow by the side, to escape by a sideway, of the winds confined by Aeolus, Od.
to entangle the feet; generally, to impede, Polyb.:—Pass. to be ensnared, Plat.
at the feet, i. e. present, Pind.
to make falsely: Mid., παραποιησάμενος σφραγῖδα having got a false seal made, Thuc.
to alter slightly, Arist.
to have the benefit of besides, τινός Luc.
to destroy besides:—Mid., with perf. 2 παραπόλωλα, to perish besides, παραπολεῖ (2nd sg. fut.) Ar.
to be ruined undeservedly, Dem.
a convoying, σίτου Decret. ap. Dem.
a procuring, providing, Arist.
that which is procured, supplies, Lat. commeatus, Xen.
escorting, Polyb.
beside or near the sea, Anth.
Dep., with fut. mid. and aor1 pass.,
to go beside or alongside, Polyb.
to go past, c. acc. loci, Id.: to pass, διὰ τῶν σπορίμων NTest.
beside a river, lying on a river, Hdt., Eur.: οἱ π. people who live on a river, Hdt.
to do a thing beside or beyond the main purpose, Hdt.
to help in doing, Soph.
a dishonest embassage, Dem.
to execute an embassy dishonestly, Dem., Aeschin.:—so Dep. παραπρεσβεύομαι, Dem.
saw-dust, metaph., of poetic phrases, Ar.
to fasten beside:—Pass., χερσὶ παραπτομένα πλάτα fitted to the hands, plied by the hands, Soph.; others take it as contr. for παραπετομένα, flying.
a false step, a transgression, trespass, NTest.
a falling beside; κατὰ τὴν π. τινος in the course of an action, Polyb.
Comic word, a sickness which prevented one from being victor at the Πύθια, Anth.
to filch away, Anth.
Pass. to be sewn as a fringe along, Hdt.
to flow beside or past, τόπον or παρὰ τόπον Hdt.: to drift away, NTest.
to slip out or off, Soph., Xen.
to slip in unawares, Dem.
to break at the side, esp. to break a line of battle, Thuc.; and in Pass. to be broken, Id.
Pass., aor2 παρερράγην [ᾰ], with perf. 2 act. παρέρρωγα, to break or burst at the side, Soph., Plut.
φωνὴ παρερρωγυῖα a voice broken (by passion), Theophr.
of persons, that may be moved by words, Il.
of words, persuasive, Id.
to throw beside: metaph. to run the risk of doing a thing, c. part., π. λαμβάνων Soph.: to throw aside, reject, Anth.
anything drawn along the side: a leathern or hair curtain, stretched along the sides of ships to protect the men, Xen.
Pass. to be hung by one's side, Plut.
Mid.:
trans. to fit out for oneself, παραρτέετο στρατιήν was engaged in preparing his army, Hdt.
in pass. sense, to hold oneself in readiness, Id.
of food, to season by additions.
a parasang (the Persian farsang), containing thirty stades, Hdt., Xen.
to stuff in beside, τι παρά τι Hdt.
a topsail, Luc.
fastened alongside, π. ἵππος a horse harnessed alongside of the regular pair, an outrigger:—metaph. a yoke-fellow, true associate, Eur.
to shake at the side, π. τὰς χεῖρας to swing one's arms in running; then (without χεῖρας) φεύγειν παρασείσας, like demissis manibus fugere, i. e. celerrime, Arist.
Mid.:
to set one's seal beside, to counterseal, seal up, Dem.:—perf. part. παρασεσημασμένος in pass. sense, Id.
to note in passing, to notice besides, Arist.
a side-mark: a mark of distinction, the ensign of a ship, Lat. insigne, NTest.: the badge of a soldier, Plut.
marked amiss, falsely struck, counterfeit, of coin, Dem.; metaph. of men, Ar.; so, π. δόξα Eur.; παράσημος αἴνῳ falsely stamped with praise, i. e. praised by a wrong standard, Aesch.
of words, false, incorrect, Anth.
noted, Plut.
to pass by in silence, Strab.
to play the parasite or toad-eater, Luc.
to be honoured with a seat at the public table, Plut.
of a παράσιτος: ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη), the trade of a παράσιτος, toad-eating, Luc.
one who eats at another's table, one who lives at another's expense, a parasite, toad-eater, Com., Luc.
to pass over in silence, Polyb.

entry.note: fut. άσω Pass., perf. παρεσκεύασμαι ionic 3rd pl. plup. παρεσκευάδατο
entry.sense: to get ready, prepare, Hdt., attic
to provide, procure, to get up, Dem.

to make or render so and so, with a Part. or adj., π. τινὰ εὖ ἔχοντα, π. τινὰ ὅτι βέλτιστον Xen.; c. inf., π. τινὰ ὡς μὴ ποιεῖν to accustom him not to do, Id.;—so, π. ὅπως ὡς βέλτισται ἔσονται αἱ ψυχαί Plat.
absol. to make one's friend, Dem.
Mid. and Pass.:
in proper sense of Mid., to get ready or prepare for oneself, Hdt., attic
in Oratt. to procure witnesses and partisans, so as to obtain a false verdict (cf. παρασκευή 1. 3):—absol. to form a party, intrigue, Dem.:—so in Act., Xen.
in Mid., absol. to prepare oneself, make preparations, Hdt., attic
perf. παρεσκεύασμαι is mostly pass. to be ready, be prepared, Hdt., attic; παρεσκευάσθαι τί to be provided with a thing, Plat.:—impers., ὡς παρεσκεύαστο when preparations had been made, Thuc.
anything prepared, apparatus, Xen.
one must prepare or provide, Plat., Xen.
(from Pass.) one must prepare oneself, be ready, Plat.
a provider, τινος Plat.
skilled in providing, τινος Xen.
that can be provided, Plat.

preparation, Hdt., attic; ἐν τούτῳ παρασκευῆς in this state of preparation, Thuc.:— preparation of a speech, Xen.:—with Preps., ἐκ παρασκευῆς of set purpose, μάχη ἐγένετο ἐκ π. a pitched battle, Thuc.; so, ἀπὸ παρασκευῆς Id.; δι’ ὀλίγης παρασκευῆς at short notice, offhand, Id.; ἐν παρασκευῇ in course of preparation, Id.
a providing, procuring, π. φίλων καὶ οὐσίας Plat.
an intrigue or cabal, for the purpose of gaining a verdict or carrying a measure, Dem., etc.
that which is prepared, equipage, Lat. apparatus, Plat., Xen.: an armament, Thuc., Dem.
generally, power, means, Thuc.
among the Jews, the day of preparation, the day before the sabbath of the Passover, NTest.
to pitch one's tent beside or near, Xen.
the side-scenes, Dem.
to throw over one like a tent or curtain, Aesch.
to fall beside, εἴς τι Luc.
to leap upon, Plut.
to give a sidelong glance at, τινά Plat.
c. gen. to miss seeing the force of a thing, Aesch.
to jeer indirectly, Hhymn.
to scare away birds: intr. to stalk haughtily past, Plut.
Dep. to out-do in skill, τινα Arist.

to draw forcibly aside, wrest aside, Soph.: metaph., παρασπᾶν τινα γνώμης Id.; ἀδίκους φρένας παρασπᾷς, i. e. ὥστε εἶναι ἀδίκους, Id.: —Mid., παρασπᾶσθαί τινά τινος to detach him from another's side, Xen.
to bear a shield beside, i. e. to fight beside, stand by, Eur.:—metaph., [τόξα] παρασπίζοντ’ ἐμοῖς βραχίοσι Id.
a companion in arms, Eur.
to act contrary to an alliance or compact, break a treaty, Dem.
trans. to break faith with one, Polyb.:—Pass. to suffer by a breach of faith, Id.
a breach of faith, Polyb.
a breaking of faith, Polyb.
contrary to a treaty, Thuc., Xen.
at one's side, Hom., Theogn.
a putting aside or away, banishing, relegatio, Plat., etc.
a setting out things for sale, retail-trade, Arist.
（παρίσταμαι) intr. a being beside:
a position or post near a king, Xen.
presence of mind, courage, Polyb.: also, desperation, Id.
as law-term, a small money deposit on entering law-suits, Oratt.
to stand by or near, Trag.
to stand by, to support, succour, τινί Aesch., Soph.
anything that stands beside: pl. παραστάδες, doorposts, pilasters, Lat. antae:—also, the space enclosed between the antae, the vestibule, Eur.:—sometimes in sg., Id.
one who stands by, a defender, Eur.
one's comrade on the flank (as προστάτης is one's front-rank-man, ἐπιστάτης one's rear-rank-man), Hdt., Xen.: generally, a comrade, supporter, Hdt., etc.
one's right or left-handman in a chorus, Arist.
fit for standing by:
able to exhort or rouse, c. gen., Polyb., Plut.
having presence of mind, courageous, desperate, Polyb.
a helper, assistant, Soph., Xen.
to go past, pass by, c. acc. loci, Hhymn., Aesch.: absol., Soph.
to pass into, enter, δόμους Id.
to lay flat, lay low, ἐγώ σε παραστορῶ (attic fut.) Ar.
to be at the general's side, interfere with him, Plut.
to encamp opposite to, τινί Polyb.
to turn aside: metaph., perf. pass. part. παρεστραμμένος, perverted, Arist.
π. τὸν τρίβωνα, to wear it crooked, Theophr.
to break contract with, τινα Dem.
Pass. to assemble with others, Andoc.
to sweep away, carry away, of a rapid stream, Ar.
π. ἔπος to drag a word in, use it out of time and place, Aesch.
to make an arrow glance aside, Il.; π. τινά τινος to foil one of [obtaining] a thing, Pind.
to rip up lengthwise, slit up, Hdt.
a placing in line of battle, ἐκ παρατάξεως in regular battle, Thuc., etc.
of marshalling a political party, arrangement, Aeschin., Dem.

to place side by side, draw up in battle-order, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—Mid. to draw up one's men in battle-order, Xen.; so of ships, Thuc.:—Mid. and Pass. to be drawn up along, παρατετάχατο παρὰ τὴν ἀκτήν Hdt.; ἑκατέρωθεν παρατεταγμένοι Thuc.; so, παρετάξαντο ἀλλήλοις Xen.: absol., παρατεταγμένοι or παραταξάμενοι in order of battle, Thuc., Dem.
in Mid. and Pass., also, to stand prepared, παρατετάχθαι πρὸς τὸ ἀποκρίνεσθαι Plat.

to stretch out along or beside, to extend the line of battle, Lat. ordines explicare, Xen.; π. τάφρον to draw a long trench, Id.:—Pass. to be stretched along (v. infr. II. 1): to be stretched at length, laid low, Ar.
to stretch on the rack, torture, Xen.: —Pass. to be half-dead, worn out, Plat.
Pass., παρατείνεσθαι εἰς τοὔσχατον to strain themselves to the uttermost, hold out to the last, Thuc.
to prolong, protract, Arist., Luc.
to apply a figure to a right line, Plat.
of pronunciation, to lengthen in pronunciation, Lat. producere, Luc.
intr. to stretch along, of a wall, a tract of country, Hdt.:— so also in Pass., παρατέταται τὸ ὄρος Id., etc.
of Time, to continue one's life, Luc.
a wall built beside or across, Thuc.

Mid.:—of timber, to work into another form; then, generally, to transform, alter, οὐδέ κεν ἄλλως Ζεὺς παρατεκτήναιτο not even Zeus could make it any way else, Il.; αἶψά κε ἔπος παρατεκτήναιο soon couldst thou dress up some other tale, Od.
Act. to build besides, Plut.

entry.etym: adverb from part. perf. pass. of παρατάσσω
entry.sense: as in battle-array, steadily, Plat.
to watch closely, observe narrowly, to watch one's opportunity, Xen.:—so in Mid., NTest.
to take care, ὅπως μὴ . . Dem.
observation, μετὰ παρατηρήσεως so that it can be observed, NTest.

entry.note: poet. παρ-τίθημι 2nd sg. -τιθεῖς 3rd sg. -τιθεῖ imperf. -ετίθεις imperf. -ετίθει aor1 act. παρέθηκα perf. παρατέθεικα Mid., aor2 παρεθέμην epic part. παρθέμενος
entry.sense: in attic παράκειμαι generally serves as the Pass.:— to place beside, Od., attic:—of meals, to set before, serve up, τί τινι Hom.; οἱ παρατιθέντες the serving-men, Xen.:—Pass., τὰ παρατιθέμενα meats set before one, Id.
generally, to offer, provide, Od., Plat.
to place upon, στεφάνους παρέθηκε καρήατι Hes.
to lay before one, explain, τί τινι Xen., NTest.
to compare, τί τινι Plut.
Mid. to set before oneself, have set before one, Od., Thuc., etc.
to deposit what belongs to one in another's hands, give in charge, commit, Hdt., Xen.; τι εἴς τινα or τινά τινι NTest.
to venture, stake, hazard, παρθέμενοι κεφαλάς, ψυχάς Od.
to employ something of one's own, τι ἔν τινι Plat.
to pluck the hair off, Ar.:— Mid. to pluck out one's hairs, Id.: perf. pass. part. παρατετιλμένος, η, clean-plucked, Id.
foolhardy, Plut.
stretched beside, hanging down by the side, Eur.
to turn aside, Il.; ποταμὸν π. to turn a river from its channel, Lat. derivare, Hdt.; π. ἄλλῃ τὸ ὕδωρ Thuc.:—Pass., παρατρεπόμενος εἰς Τένεδον turning aside to . . , Xen.
to turn one from his opinion, change his mind, Hes.: so in Mid., Theocr.
of things, π. λόγον to pervert or falsify a story, Hdt.
to alter or revoke a decree, Id.
to feed beside another:—Pass., of men not worth their keep, to feed at another's expense, Dem.

entry.note: fut. -θρέξομαι fut. -δρᾰμοῦμαι aor2 παρέδρᾰμον 3rd pl. plup. -δεδραμήκεσαν
entry.sense: to run by or past, Il., Ar.
to outrun, overtake, Il.: π. τὰ τότε κακά to go beyond, exceed them, Eur.
to run through or over, run across (a space of ground expressed or implied), Xen.
to run over, i. e. treat in a cursory way, Isocr.:— to slight, neglect, Theocr.
to escape unnoticed, τινά Polyb.
to start aside from fear, Il.
to rub beside or alongside, π. χρυσὸν ἀκήρατον ἄλλῳ χρυσῷ (sc. εἰς βάσανον) to rub pure gold by the side of other gold on the lapis Lydius and see the difference of the marks they leave, Hdt.
παρατρίψασθαι τὸ μέτωπον, Lat. frontem perfricare, to harden the forehead by rubbing, i. e. to be hardened, dead to shame, Strab.
τί με ταῦτα παρατροπέων ἀγορεύεις; why tell me this, leading me astray? Od.
a turning away, means of averting, θανάτου Eur.
intr. a digression, Luc.
turned aside, lawless, strange, unusual, Plut.
act. averting a thing, c. gen., Eur.
to run past, τινά Anth.: to pass by or over, to leave unnoticed, Id.
to gnaw at the side, nibble at, take a bite of, c. gen., Ar.
θεοὺς θυέεσσι παρατρωπῶς’ ἄνθρωποι turn away the anger of the gods by sacrifices, Il.
to happen to be near, be among others, c. dat., Il.; π. τῷ λόγῳ τῷ πάθεϊ to be present at . . , Lat. interesse, Hdt.
absol. to happen to be present, Id.: of a thing, to offer itself, παρατυχούσης τινὸς σωτηρίας Thuc.

often in partic. παρατυχών, whoever chanced to be by, i. e. the first comer, any chance person, Id.;— so, τὸ παρατυγχάνον or παρατυχόν whatever turns up or chances, πρὸς τὸ παρατυγχάνον as circumstances required, Id.: nom. absol., ἐν τῷ παρατυχόντι Id.: —παρατυχόν, it being in one's power, since it was in one's power to do, c. inf., Id.
to illumine slightly:—Pass. to be illumined, Strab.; and of the sun, to shine, Id.
to address so as to console or encourage, Od.; μὴ ταῦτα παραύδα do not talk me into this, Id.
c. acc. rei, to speak lightly of, μὴ δή μοι θάνατόν γε παραύδα Id.
to lie near a place, c. dat., Eur.
dwelling beside, πάραυλον οἰκίζειν τινά to place one on the borders (of a land), Soph.; βοὴ πάραυλος a cry close at hand, Id.
in like manner, Lat. perinde or (as others) = παραυτίκα, at first, Aesch., Dem.
immediately, forthwith, straightway, Lat. illico, Hdt.; also, τὸ π. Id.; ἐν τῷ π. Thuc.
with Substantives, to express brief duration, Ἅιδην τὸν π. present death, Eur.; ἡ π. λαμπρότης momentary splendour, Thuc.; ἡ π. ἐλπίς Id.
hanging from the neck, Anth.
to shew beside or by uncovering, Hes.
to walk beside and light, light one to a place, Ar.
Pass. to appear by the side, disclose itself, Plat.

entry.etym: only in poet. forms such as παραίφασις, πάρφασις
entry.sense: an address, encouragement, consolation, Il.
allurement, persuasion, said of the cestus of Aphrodite, Id.: deceit, Pind.
to bring to one's side, to hand to, set before one, Hdt., Xen.; π. τὰς κεφαλάς to exhibit them, Hdt.:—Pass. to be set on table, Id.
to bring forward, by way of argument, π. ἐς μέσον Id.: to bring forward, allege, cite, Id., Eur., etc.
to hand over, transmit, Eur.
to carry beside, τί τινι Id.
to carry past or beyond, Plat.; π. τὴν χεῖρα to wave the hand, Dem.:—Pass. to be carried past or beyond, Thuc.; τοῦ χειμῶνος παραφερομένου while the winter was passing, Plut.
to turn aside or away, τὴν ὄψιν π. τινός Xen.: to put away, remove, NTest.
to turn in a wrong direction, Dem.:—Pass. to move in a wrong direction, of paralysed limbs, Arist.
to lead aside, mislead:—Pass. to be misled, err, go wrong, Plat.
to sweep away, of a river, Plut.: —Pass. to be carried away, Anth.
to let pass, Lat. praetermittere, τὰς ὥρας παρηνέγκατε τῆς θυσίας Orac. ap. Dem.:—Pass. to slip away, escape, Xen.
intr. to be beyond or over, ἡμερῶν ὀλίγων παρενεγκουσῶν, ἡμέρας οὐ πολλὰς παρενεγκούσας a few days over, more or less, Thuc.
to flee close past or beyond, παρφυγέειν (epic aor2 inf.) Od.
to speak gently to, to advise, c. dat., Il.:—Mid. to persuade, appease, c. acc., Hom.
to speak deceitfully or insincerely, Pind.; and, in Mid., Id.

entry.note: aor2 παρέφθην part. act.. παραφθάς part mid. -φθάμενος
entry.sense: to overtake, outstrip, Il.; εἰ δ’ ἄμμε παραφθαίησι πόδεσσι (epic 3rd sg. opt.) Id.
Dep.:
to add a qualification, Plat.
to interrupt, Plut.
a going aside: of the mind, derangement, Aesch.
to set before, τί τινι Ar.:—Pass., Hdt.
borne aside, carried away, Plut.
wandering, reeling, staggering, Eur., Luc.
mad, frenzied, Plut., Luc.
a breastwork on the top of a mound, only in pl., Thuc.; in a ship, the bulwarks, Id.: a low screen, Plat.
to enclose with a breastwork, Polyb.
to be beside oneself, be deranged or mad, Hdt., Aesch., etc.; poet. παραιφρ-, Theocr.
derangement, Plat.
to keep guard beside, c. acc., Strab.
wandering from reason, out of one's wits, deranged, Soph., Eur., etc.
an offshoot, Arist.
growing beside: παραφυές, = παραφυάς, Arist.
a guard, watch, garrison, Polyb.
to watch beside, to guard closely, watch narrowly, Xen., etc.
Mid. to be on one's guard, Plat.
to grow beside or at the side, Hdt.
to slacken at the side: of a ship, to let in water, leak, Ar.
to mark with a false stamp, falsify, Luc.
to winter in or at a place, Dem., etc.
a wintering in a place, Polyb.
a dweller by the Achelous, Strab.: —fem. παραχελωῖτις, ιδος, (sc. χώρα) the country along the Achelous, Id.
to pour in beside, pour in, Hdt.
of solids, to heap up on the side, Id.
Pass. to lie spread out near, of a country, Plut.
Dep.:
to use improperly, misuse, abuse, c. dat., Polyb.
π. ἔς τινα to deal wrongly or unworthily with him, Hdt.
= ἐκ παρέργου χράομαι, to treat with contempt, disregard, c. acc., Id.: ionic part. παραχρεώμενοι, of furious combatants, setting nothing by their life, Id.
on the spot, forthwith, straightway, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—with the Art., τὸ π. Hdt., attic; ἐκ or ἀπὸ τοῦ παραχρῆμα off-hand, immediate, Xen.; ἐν τῷ π. Plat., etc.; —ἐς τὸ π. ἀκούειν Thuc.
to give a false oracle, Strab.
of false or altered colour, colourless, faded, Luc.
to corrupt music by the ἁρμονία χρωματική, Arist.
a side embankment, a dyke, Strab.
to throw up beside, Hdt.
to go aside, make room, give place, retire, Ar., etc.: π. τινί to give way, yield, submit, Plat., etc.:— π. τινός to retire from, Dem.
to step aside out of the way for another, as a mark of respect, ὁδοῦ π. πρεσβυτέρῳ Xen.; π. τινί τοῦ βήματος Aeschin.; τῇ πόλει παραχωρῶ τῆς τιμωρίας I leave the task of punishment to the state, Dem.
to concede a thing, c. acc., Plat.
a giving way: c. gen. a retiring from, τῆς ἀρχῆς Plut.
one must give way, Xen.
to touch lightly, Plut.
to stammer out somewhat of the truth, Strab.
cooling, refreshment, consolation, Eur.; ἀλγέων π. Id.; π. τῷ πένθει Dem.
to cool gently: metaph. to console, soothe, Theocr.
wet, damp, Ar.
(sc. δορά) a leopard-skin, Il., Hdt.; doric παρδαλέα, Pind.
leopard-killing, Anth.
gen. εως ionic ιος; dat. ει, the pard, whether leopard, panther, or ounce, Hom., attic
spotted like the pard, Luc.
illegally registered, π. πολίτης an intrusive citizen, Aeschin.
to interpolate, Aeschin.; παρεγγραφεὶς πολίτης = παρέγγραπτος, Id.
to hand over to another, to entrust or commend to his care, Hdt.
as a military term, to pass on the word of command along the line, Lat. imperium tradere per manus, Eur., Xen.
of a general, to give the word to do a thing, command suddenly, π. τινι ποιεῖν τι Xen.
of a general also, to deliver an address before battle, Id.
to pledge one's word, promise, c. acc. et inf. fut., Soph.
a word of command passed on, Xen.
a passing on the word of command, Xen.
to raise partly, Plut.
to make to incline sideways:—Pass. to incline sideways, Plut.
to sit constantly beside, attend constantly, be always near, Lat. assidere, c. dat., Eur.
of judges, to be an assessor, Dem.
sitting beside, as at table, Hdt.: generally, sitting beside, near, τινι Eur.
as Subst. an assessor, coadjutor, associate, foll. by dat. or gen., Pind., Eur.
in Prose, the assessor or coadjutor of a king or magistrate, Hdt.
Dep. to sit beside, Theogn.; cf. παρίζω.
the cheek, mostly in pl., (παρήιον being used by Hom. for sg.), Hom., Trag.
entry.etym: Prob. from παρά, being literally the side of the face.

entry.sense: a reddish-brown snake, sacred to Aesculapius, Ar., Dem.

entry.etym: aor2, παροράω being used as the pres.
entry.sense: to observe by the way, notice, τί τινι something in one, Hdt.
to look past, overlook, disregard, Dem.
to compare, τινί τι Plat.

entry.note: fut. ξω poet. aor2 παρείκᾰθον inf. -αθεῖν
entry.sense: to give way, τινί to one, Soph.: absol. to permit, allow, Plat.; κατὰ τὸ παρεῖκον by such ways as were practicable, Thuc.
impers., παρείκει μοι it is competent, allowable for me, εἴ μοι παρείκοι Soph.; ὅπῃ παρείκοι wherever it was practicable, Thuc.

entry.note: epic 3rd pl. παρέᾱσι subj. παρῶ epic παρέω inf. παρεῖναι epic παρέμμεναι part. παρών epic παρέων imperf. παρῆν epic παρέην 3rd pl. πάρεσαν epic fut. παρέσσομαι
entry.sense: to be by or present, Hom.
to be by or near one, c. dat., Od., Soph., etc.: to be present in or at a thing, Hom., attic
to be present so as to help, stand by, Lat. adesse, τινι Il.
παρεῖναι εἰς . . , to arrive at, to have come to, a place, Hdt.; π. ἐπὶ δεῖπνον Id., attic
of things, to be by, to be ready or at hand, Lat. praesto esse, Od., etc.; εἴ μοι δύναμίς γε παρείη if power were at my command, Id.:—so of feelings, φόβος βαρβάροις παρῆν Aesch.; θαῦμα παρῆν Soph.

of Time, ὁ παρὼν νῦν χρόνος Id.; τὰ παρόντα (ionic παρεόντα) the present state of affairs, present circumstances, Hdt.; ἐκ τῶν παρόντων according to present circumstances, Thuc.; ἐν τῷ παρόντι, opp. to ἐν τῷ ἔπειτα, Id.; πρὸς τὸ π. αὐτίκα Id.
impers., πάρεστί μοι it is in my power to do, c. inf., Hdt., Aesch., etc.; and without dat., παρῆν κλύειν one might hear, Aesch.
part. παρόν, ionic παρεόν, it being possible since it is allowed, Lat. quum liceret, παρεὸν αὐτῷ βασιλέα γενέσθαι Hdt.

entry.etym: used as fut. of παρέρχομαι and παρῄειν as imperf.
entry.sense: to go by, beside or past, to pass by, pass, Od., Plat., etc.:— to go alongside, Thuc.: to march along the coast, of an army, as παραπλέω of a fleet, Id., Xen.
c. acc. loci, to pass by, Hdt.; absol., Id.
of Time, to pass on, pass, Id.
to pass by, overtake, surpass, Xen.
to pass into, enter, Hdt., Eur.
in discourse, to pass on from one part of a subject to another, Ar.
in attic Prose, to come forward, Xen.; πάριτ’ ἐς τὸ πρόσθεν Ar.
to come forward to speak, Plat., Dem.; οἱ παριόντες orators, Dem.
to pass from man to man, Xen.

entry.etym: aor2, with no pres. in use, παρά-φημι or παρ-αγορεύω being used instead
entry.sense: to persuade by indirect means, to talk over, win over, Il., Aesch.; παρειπών by thy persuasions, Il.:—c. acc. cogn. to give such and such advice, αἴσιμα παρειπών Id.
entry.etym: In Il. the first syll. is long, πᾱρειπών, πᾱρειποῦσα, the orig. form having been παρϝειπών.

entry.sense: to fasten in beside, insert, Xen.; νόμους παρείρων if he adds observance of laws, Soph.
to lead in by one's side, bring forward, introduce, Isocr., NTest.
introduced privily, NTest.
Dep. with aor. and perf. act. to come or go in beside or secretly, Polyb., NTest.
to get in by the side, steal in, Polyb.
to flow on beside, Plut.
to bring in beside, π. νόμον to propose a new law to amend another, Lat. subrogare, Dem.
to apply besides, NTest.
a deviation from, c. gen., Arist.; of constitutional forms, τυραννίς is a παρέκβασις from monarchy, oligarchy from aristocracy, Id.
to deviate, Aeschin.
to collect covertly, π. τὰ κοινά to embezzle the public moneys, Dem.
to flee forth from, elude, ἵνα μή σε παρεκπροφύγῃσιν ἄεθλα (epic 3rd sg. aor2 subj.), Il.
to stretch out in line, Polyb.
to accomplish otherwise, Mosch.
one must cause, Xen.
besides or except for, c. gen., NTest.: —absol., τὰ παρεκτός things external, Id.
to turn aside, divert, Eur.
to run out past, Plut.
to pour out by degrees:—Pass., of rivers and lakes, to overflow, Strab.
an overflowing, of rivers, Strab.
to drive by or past, ἐναντίω δυ’ ἅρματε π. to drive them past one another, Ar.; τὰς αἶγας παρελᾶντα (doric pres. part. acc.) Theocr.
intr.,
to drive by, Il.:—then c. acc. pers. to drive past, overtake, Id., Xen.
to row or sail past, Od.; c. acc. pers., Σειρῆνας παρήλασε Id.
to ride by, run by, c. acc., Xen.
more rarely to ride up to, rush towards, Id.: to ride on one's way, Id.

entry.note: fut. ξω also -ελκύσω aor1 παρείλκῠσα perf. pass. παρείλκυσμαι
entry.sense: to draw aside, pervert, Pind.: —Mid. to draw aside to oneself, draw away from, τί τινος Od.
to lead alongside, as one does a led horse, Hdt.; παρέλκειν ἐκ γῆς to tow [boats] from the bank, Id.
κενὰς παρέλκειν (sc. τὰς κώπας) to pull them through the air without dipping them, i. e. to make a mere show of working, Ar.
to drag to one side, put off, μὴ μύνῃσι παρέλκετε put not things off by excuses, Od.
intr. to be prolonged, to continue, Luc.
to put in beside, insert, interpolate, interpose, τι Ar., Dem.; π. ὑποψίας to insinuate suspicions, Aeschin.
to put the auxiliaries in line with the legionaries, Polyb.
intr. to fall into line, to encamp, Id.
to look askance, Eur.
insertion, interpolation, Aeschin.
an encampment, fortress, NTest.
to stuff in, Luc.
to fill secretly with, c. gen., Plut.
Pass. to be inflamed by rubbing, Strab.
to fall in by the way, creep or steal in, Plat., Aeschin.
to traffic underhand in a thing, to smuggle a thing in, Eur.
of small wares: metaph. an appendix, Luc.
Dep. to traffic in besides:—metaph., τὸ τερπνὸν π. to yield delight besides instruction, Luc.
something put in beside, an addition, appendix, Hdt.; παρενθήκην ἔχρησε ἐς Μιλησίους delivered an oracle by way of parenthesis, Id.
to trouble greatly, NTest.:—Pass., καὶ ὑμεῖς παρηνώχλησθε (2nd pl. perf. pass.) Dem.
to swing to and fro, Ar.
to rouse to exertion, Plut.
to lift up beside, Strab.

entry.note: fut. ήσω part. pass. perf. παρεξηυλημένοι
entry.sense: of musical instruments, worn out by being played upon, and so, generally, worn out, Ar.
to go out beside, pass by or alongside of, c. acc. loci, Hdt.: absol., Id., Eur., etc.
to turn aside out of the path, Plat.
to overstep, transgress, Aesch., Soph.
the part of the ship beyond the rowers, at either end, Thuc.
to drive out past, to pass in a race, Il.: to row past, c. acc., Od.: to march by, Hdt.
to march out to meet, ἀλλήλοις Plut.
to go out beside, slip past, Od.; π. τινα, Hdt.
παρεξελθεῖν πεδίοιο τυτθόν to pass over a little of it, Il.
to overstep, transgress, Διὸς νόον Od.; δίκην Soph.
to examine by comparing, Dem.
to find out besides, π. ἄλλον νόμον to find out another different law, Hdt.
to let out beside: of Time, to let pass, Hdt.
as prep.,
c. gen. loci, outside, before, παρὲκ λιμένος Od.; παρὲξ ὁδοῦ out of the road, Il.
like χωρίς, besides, except, exclusive of, παρὲξ τοῦ ἀργύρου Hdt.

c. acc. out by the side of, along side of, παρὲξ ἅλα Il.; παρὲξ τὴν νῆσον away from the island, Od.; παρὲξ δοῦρα out of the way of spears, Id.; παρὲκ νόον out of sense and reason, foolishly, Il.; παρὲξ Ἀχιλῆα without the knowledge of Achilles, Id.
as adv.,
of Place, out beside, στῆ δὲ παρέξ hard by, Il.; νῆχε παρέξ was swimming out along shore, Od.
metaph. beside the mark, παρὲξ ἀγορεύειν Il.
ἄλλα παρὲξ μεμνώμεθα let us talk of something else, Od.; παρὲξ ἢ ὅσον except so long as, Hdt.
c.gen. to step out aside from, deviate from, Hes., Arist.
c. acc. to overstep, transgress, Aesch., Arist.
absol. to deviate, Arist.: to make a digression, Id.
subordinate or incidental praise, Plat.
to correct an inscription, Strab.
Mid. to exhibit out of season, make a display, Luc.
a turning round in passing, Plut.
Dep. to follow along side, follow close, c. dat., Xen.; absol., Plat.
a pottering workman, Eur.

a bye-work, subordinate or secondary business, appendage, appendix, Eur.; πάρεργ’ ὁδοῦ a secondary purpose of my journey, Id.; π. τύχης an unhappy addition to my fortune, Id.; πάρεργα κακῶν things useless to remedy my ills, Id.:— ἐν παρέργῳ as a bye-work, as subordinate or secondary, Lat. obiter, ἐν π. θέσθαι to treat as a bye-work, Soph.; ὡς ἐν π. Eur.; ἐκ παρέργου Thuc.
to creep secretly up to, Theocr.
to pass by, Anth.
to draw along the side, φραγμόν Hdt.
Dep.:— to go by, beside or past, to pass by, pass, Od.; παρῆλθεν ὁ κίνδυνος ὥσπερ νέφος passed away, Dem.
of Time, to pass, Hdt.; ὁ παρελθὼν ἄροτος the past season, Soph.; π. ὁδοί wanderings now gone by, Id.; ἐν τῷ παρελθόντι in time past, of old, Xen.; τὰ παρεληλυθότα past events, Dem.
to pass by, outstrip, Hom., Theogn., attic; τοὺς λόγους τὰ ἔργα παρέρχεται Dem.
to outwit, escape, elude, Il., Hdt., Eur.
to arrive at, π. εἰς . . Hes.
to pass in, ἐς τὴν αὐλήν Hdt.; π. ἔσω or εἴσω to go into a house, etc., Trag.; c. acc., π. δόμους Eur.
to pass without heeding, τεὸν βωμόν Il.: to pass by, pass over, disregard, slight, θεούς Eur.
to overstep, transgress, τοὺς νόμους Dem.
to pass unnoticed, escape the notice of, τουτὶ παρῆλθέ με εἰπεῖν Id.
in attic to come forward to speak, π. εἰς τὸν δῆμον Thuc.; absol., παρελθὼν ἔλεξε τοιάδε Id.
to gnaw or nibble at a thing, c. gen., Ar.
a letting go, remission, NTest.
by or at the hearth, Soph.:— generally, = ἐφέστιος, Id., Eur.
to surpass in reputation, τινα Plut.
to direct, constrain, Soph.
to calm, soothe, Eur.
Pass. to lie beside another, c. dat., Od.
lying beside or with:—metaph., πῆμα πατρὶ πάρευνον Aesch.
the invention of a false pretext, a pretence, Decret. ap. Dem.
to discover besides, invent, Hdt.
Pass. to be discovered besides, aor1 παρευρέθην Id.
to perform one's duty regularly, Polyb.
to put in order, arrange, make ready, Eur.
to arrange badly, neglect, Id.
to lie near to guard, to keep guard, Polyb.

entry.note: fut. παρέξω or παρασχήσω perf. παρέσχηκα aor2 παρέσχον epic inf. παρασχέμεν imperat. παράσχες poet. παρέσχεθον inf. παρασχεθεῖν
entry.sense: Act. to hold beside, hold in readiness, to furnish, provide, supply, Hom., etc.:—absol., πᾶσι παρέξω I will provide for all, Od.
to afford, cause, grant, give, φιλότητα, εὐφροσύνην Hom.; ὄχλον Hdt.; χάριν, εὔνοιαν Soph., etc.

to present or offer for a purpose, c. inf., [ὄϊες] παρέχουσι γάλα θῆσθαι Od.; π. τὸ σῶμα τύπτειν Ar.; π. ἑαυτόν τινι ἐρωτᾶν Plat.:—hence, absol., to submit oneself, ἰατροῖς παρέχουσι ἀποτέμνειν Xen.; πάρεχε ἐκποδών make yourself scarce, Ar.
with reflex. Pron. and a predicative, to shew or exhibit oneself so and so, π. ἑαυτὸν σοφιστήν Plat.; εὐπειθῆ Xen.; π. γῆν ἄσυλον to offer the country as an asylum, Eur.
to allow, grant, σιγὴν παρασχών Soph.;—c. inf. to allow one to do a thing, Id.

impers., παρέχει τινί c. inf. (where ὁ καιρός may be supplied), it is allowed, easy, in one's power to do so and so, Hdt., Eur., etc.:—so neut. part. used absol., παρέχον it being in one's power, since one can, Hdt., Thuc.
in attic to produce a person on demand, Xen., etc.
Mid. παρέχομαι, fut. -έξομαι and -σχήσομαι: perf. pass. (in mid. sense) -έσχημαι:— to supply of oneself or from one's own means, Hdt., etc.
to furnish, produce, κροκοδείλους Id.
to display on one's own part, exhibit, προθυμίαν Id., etc.
in attic law, παρέχεσθαί τινα μάρτυρα to bring forward as a witness, Plat.
to produce as one's own, ἄρχοντα παρέχεσθαί τινα to acknowledge as one's general, Hdt.; π. πόλιν, of an ambassador, to represent a city in one's own person, Thuc.
to offer, promise, Hdt., etc.
to make so and so for or towards oneself, παρασχέσθαι θεὸν εὐμενῆ Eur.
in Arithmetic, to make up, amount to, παρέχονται ἡμέρας διηκοσίας Hdt.
to be past one's prime, to be growing old, Hdt., Thuc.
past one's prime, Anth.

entry.note: imperf. παρηγόρουν fut. -ήσω aor1 -ησα Pass., aor1 -ήθην
entry.sense: to address, exhort, Hdt., Aesch., etc.; c. inf. to advise, Eur.; so in Mid., Hdt.
to console, appease, Aesch.
exhortation, persuasion, Aesch.
consolation, Plut.
consoling, and as Subst. a comforter, Soph.

entry.etym: ionic for παρεῖον which is not in use
entry.sense: the cheek, jaw, Hom.
παρήιον the cheek-ornament of a bridle, Il. Cf. παρειά.

entry.etym: later form of πᾰρήιον, Aesch., Eur.

entry.sense: to have come alongside, i. e. to lie beside, stretch along, Hdt., Thuc.
to pass forth, Soph.
past one's prime, Plut., Anth.
to be seated beside or by, c. dat., Il., Eur.; ἀλλοτρίοισι παρήμενος seated at other men's tables, Od.: generally, to dwell with, σύεσσι π. Id.:—absol. to sit beside or near, Hom.
day by day, daily, Pind.
a coming to shore: a landing place, Aesch.
fem. adj. on the shore, Anth.
in pl. side-traces, i. e. the traces by which the outside horse (παρήορος) was harnessed beside the regular pair, Il.; ἐν δὲ παρηορίῃσι Πήδασον ἵει he harnessed Pedasus with side-traces, Id.
hanging or hung beside: παρήορος (sc. ἵππος) a horse which draws by the side of the regular pair (ξυνωρίς), an outrigger, elsewhere παράσειρος, σειραφόρος, Il.
lying along, outstretched, sprawling, Id., Aesch.
metaph. (from the fact that the ἵππος π. was given to prancing), reckless, distraught, senseless, Il.
maidenhood, virginity, Eur.
of or belonging to a maiden, Pind., Aesch., Eur.
in pl. the pursuits or amusements of maidens, Eur.; so in sg., a maiden's work, Id.
νόθον π. the child of an unmarried woman, Id.
to bring up as a maid, Eur.:—Pass. to lead a maiden life, remain a maid, Hdt., Aesch.; πολιὰ (neut. pl.) παρθενεύεται grows gray in maidenhood, Eur.
παρθένια (sc. μέλη) τά songs sung by maidens to the flute (αὐλὸς παρθένιος) Pind.; so παρθένεια, ων, τά, Ar.
the son of a concubine: Παρθένιαι the youths born at Sparta during the Messenian War, Arist.
of or for a maiden, Plut.
like παρθένειος, of a maiden or virgin, maiden, maidenly, Od., Hes., Aesch., etc.
παρθένιος, the son of an unmarried girl, Il.:—but, π. ἀνήρ the husband of maidenhood, first husband, Plut.
metaph. pure, undefiled, Hhymn.; π. μύρτα, of white myrtleberries, Ar.
the maiden-hero or son of the maiden (Atalanta), one of the Seven against Thebes: [to be pronounced Παρθεννοπαῖος in Aesch.].
one who looks after maidens, a seducer, Il.
a maid, maiden, virgin, girl, Hom., etc.
Παρθένος, as a name of Athena at Athens, of Artemis, etc.
as adj. maiden, virgin, chaste, πάρθενον ψυχὴν ἔχων Eur.: metaph., π. πηγή Aesch.; παρθένοι τριήρεις maiden, i. e. new, ships, Ar.
as masc., παρθένος, an unmarried man, NTest.
of a slaughtered maiden's blood, Aesch.
the maidens' apartments, young women's chambers in a house, mostly in pl., Aesch., Eur., etc.
in sg. the Parthenon or temple of Athena Parthenos in the citadel at Athens, rebuilt under Pericles, Dem.
of maiden aspect, Eur.
a deposit, pledge, Anth.
Parthian, Strab.; Παρθικά, τά, a history of Parthia, Id.; so Παρθίς, ίδος, ἡ, Luc.
to sleep beside, c. dat., Hom.
to set up beside:—in Mid., Anth.
to sit beside another, c. dat., Od., Hdt.
Causal, to seat or make to sit beside, τινά τινι Hdt.: —Mid. παρίζομαι to seat oneself or sit beside, Id., Bion.; aor2 παρ-εζόμην, epic imperat. -εζεο, Hom.

entry.note: 2nd sg. παριεῖς fut. παρήσω aor1 παρῆκα 3rd pl. aor2 παρεῖσαν part. παρείς perf. παρεῖκα Pass., aor1 παρείθην inf. παρεθῆναι aor2 παρείμην perf. παρεῖμαι
entry.sense: to let drop beside or at the side, let fall, Soph., Eur.:—Pass., παρείθη ποτὶ γαῖαν it hung down to earth, Il.
to pass by, pass over, leave out, Lat. omitto, Hdt., Soph.
to pass unnoticed, disregard, let alone, Lat. praetermittere, Hdt., Aesch.; τὰ παθήματα παρεῖς’ ἐάσω Soph.; so in Pass., πόθος παρεῖτο Id.; παρεθῆναι Dem.
c.inf. to omit to do, Plat., etc.; and with a negat. repeated, μὴ παρῇς τὸ μὴ οὐ φράσαι Soph.
of Time, to let pass, τὸν χειμῶνα Hdt.; τὸν καιρόν Thuc.
to relax, slacken, remit, γόον, χόλον Eur.:—Pass. to be relaxed, weakened, exhausted, Id.
τοῦ ποδὸς παριέναι to slack away the sheet, v. πούς II. 2; so metaph., τοῦ μετρίου παρείς letting go one's hold of moderation, i. e. giving it up, Soph.
to remit punishment, to forgive, pardon, Ar.

to yield, give up, Lat. concedere, νίκην τινί Hdt., attic: — to leave a thing to another, σοὶ παρεὶς τάδε Soph.; παρῆκεν, ὥστε βραχέα μοι δεῖσθαι φράσαι left it so that there is need for me to say but little, Id.
to permit, allow, c. dat. pers. et inf., ἄλλῳ παρήσομεν ναυμαχήσειν Hdt.; absol., the inf. being understood, Soph.
to allow to pass, let pass, let in, admit, Hdt., Eur., etc.; so perf. pass. in mid. sense, βαρβάρους εἰς τὰς ἀκροπόλεις παρεῖνται have admitted them into their citadels, Dem.
Mid. παρίεσθαί τινα to obtain leave from him, obtain his consent, Soph., Plat.
to beg to be let off something, οὐδέν σου παρίεμαι I ask no quarter, Plat.: to beg a favour, Id.; παριέμεσθα we ask pardon, Eur.
of Time, to be gone by, Pind.
to ride along or over, πόντον Eur.: to ride alongside, Thuc.
Pass. to make oneself equal to, measure oneself with, c. dat., Hdt., Theocr.
to be made equal or like to, τινι Plat.
in the Parthian tongue, Plut.
the Parthians, Hdt.
Parthia, Strab.
almost equal, evenly balanced, Polyb.: of the clauses of a sentence, Arist.
Causal in pres., imperf., fut. and aor1 to make to stand or to place beside, Polyb.; παραστήσας τὰ ὅπλα having brought his arms into view, Dem.
to set before the mind, present, offer, bring home to the mind, c. inf., Id.; π. τινὶ θαρρεῖν to give one confidence, Aeschin.
to make good, prove, shew, Lys., NTest.
to set side by side, compare, Isocr.
Pass., with aor2, perf. and plup. act., intr., to stand by, beside or near, Hom.; so aor1 pass. part. παρασταθείς, Eur.
to stand by, i. e. to help or defend, τινι Il., Hdt., Trag.
in past tenses, to have come, be at hand, be present, Il.
of events, to be near, be at hand, Hom.; perf. part., Lat. praesens, τὸ χρῶμα τὸ παρεστηκός Ar.; attic also παρεστώς, ῶσα, ός, Trag.; τὰ παρεστῶτα present circumstances, Aesch.; πρὸς τὸ παρεστός Ar.
to come to the side of another, come over to his opinion, Hdt.: absol. to come to terms, surrender, submit, Id., Dem.
to happen to one, Hdt.: to come into one's head, occur to one, δόξα μοι παρεστάθη Soph.:—impers., παρίσταταί μοι it occurs to me, Hdt., Thuc.
absol., παρεστηκός, = παρόν, since it was in their power, since the opportunity offered, Thuc.
Some tenses of Mid., esp. fut. and aor1, are used in causal sense:
to bring forward, produce, Xen.; esp. in a court of justice, Dem.
to bring to one's side, and so,
to bring over by force, bring to terms, Hdt., Soph., etc.
to gain by kindness, win over, Thuc., Dem.
generally, to dispose for one's own views or purposes, Hdt.
at the loom, Anth.
to hold in readiness, Il.: to present, offer, Id.
an even balancing of the clauses in a sentence, Isocr.
one must come forward, Thuc.
Parnassian, Pind.; fem. Παρνᾱσιάς, άδος, ionic Παρνησιάς, Eur.; also Παρνησίς, ίδος, Aesch.
Parnassus, a mountain of Phocis, Od.
Parnes, a mountain of Attica, Ar.:—adj. Παρνήθιος, η, ον, Id.
a locust, Ar.
to pass by, Theocr.
c. acc. to go past, Luc.
a passer-by, wayfarer, Anth.:— fem. παροδῖτις, ιδος, Id.
a by-way, passage, Thuc.
a going by, passing, Id.; ἐν τῇ παρόδῳ as they passed by, Id.
a side-entrance, a narrow entrance or approach, Xen.; λαβεῖν τὰς παρόδους (of Thermopylae), Dem.
a coming forward, esp. before the assembly to speak, Id.
the first entrance of the chorus, their first song, Arist.
to open at the side or a little, half-open, Hhymn., Eur.; παροίξας τῆς θύρας having opened a bit of the door, put it ajar, Ar.
prep. c. gen.
before, in the presence of, Hom.
of Time, π. ἐμοῦ before me, Aesch.
adv.,
of Place, before, in front, Il.
of Time, before this, formerly, Hom., Trag.; οἱ π. men bygone, Pind.; τῆς π. ἡμέρας Eur.
πάροιθεν πρὶν . . , Lat. priusquam, Soph.
to dwell beside, c. acc., π. τὴν Ἀσίαν dwell along the coast of Asia, Isocr.: c. dat. to live near, Thuc.: to dwell among, τισίν Id.; of places, to lie near, Xen.
（πάροικος II) to live in a place, sojourn, NTest.
a neighbourhood, Thuc.
a sojourning in a foreign land, NTest.
to place near:—Pass. to settle near, dwell among, τισίν Hdt.
to build beside or across, Thuc.
dwelling beside or near, c. gen., Aesch., Soph.; c. dat., Thuc.:—absol. a neighbour, Arist.
πάροικος πόλεμος a war with neighbours, Hdt.
as Subst. a sojourner, alien, NTest.
to make proverbial:—Pass. to pass into a proverb, become proverbial, Plat.
Mid. to speak in proverbs, Id.
proverbial: adv. -κῶς, Anth.
παροιμιακόν (sub. μέτρον), a paroemiac, i. e. an Anapaestic dimeter catalectic, used at the end of an Anapaestic system.
a by-word, common saying, proverb, maxim, saw, Aesch., Soph., etc.; κατὰ τὴν π. as the saying goes, Plat.
a parable, NTest.
to behave ill at wine, play drunken tricks, Oratt.
to act like a drunken man, Plut.; παροινήσας in a drunken fit, Plat.
trans. to treat with drunken violence:— Pass. to be so treated, Dem.
drunken behaviour, drunken violence, a drunken frolic, Xen., etc.
addicted to wine, Ar.
= παροινικός, Ar.
befitting a drinking party, Luc.; παροίνια drinking songs, Plut.
the one before or in front, Il.

entry.note: fut. -οιχήσομαι perf. -ῴχηκα ionic -οίχωκα and in late writers -ῴχημαι 3rd sg. ionic plup. -οιχώκεε
entry.sense: to have passed by, παρῴχετο γηθόσυνος κῆρ he passed on, went on his way, Il.
of Time, to be gone by, Id.; ἡ παροιχομένη νύξ the bygone night, Hdt.; ἄνδρες παροιχόμενοι men of by-gone times, Pind.; τὰ παροιχόμενα the past, Hdt.
c. gen., ὅσον μοίρας παροίχῃ how art thou fallen from thine high estate, Eur.
redupl. form of παροχή, a supplying, furnishing, Thuc.
to neglect a little, Xen.
to accompany, Plut., Luc.
to be much like, τινί NTest.
much like, nearly like, closely resembling, τινι Hdt., Thuc.:—absol., Hdt.
of numbers, nearly equal, Xen.
to alter slightly, Strab.
fit for inciting or urging on, Xen., Dem.
exasperating, provoking, Isocr.
to urge, prick or spur on, stimulate, Xen., Dem.
to anger, provoke, irritate, exasperate, πατρὸς μὴ π. φρένα Eur., Thuc.:—Pass. to be provoked, Thuc., etc.
irritation, exasperation, Dem., NTest.: a provoking, NTest.
to disarm, Polyb.:—Pass., Plut.
to be overlooked, Luc.
παροπτέον, one must overlook, Dem.
overlooking, negligence, Plut., Luc.

entry.note: fut. -όψομαι aor2 παρεῖδον aor1 pass. -ώφθην perf. pass. -ῶμμαι
entry.sense: to look at by the way, notice, remark, Xen.; τί τινι something in one, Hdt., Ar.
to overlook, disregard, neglect, Xen., etc.
to see amiss, see wrong, Plat.
to look sideways, Xen.
to provoke to anger, NTest.:—Pass., Dem.
provocation; anger, NTest.
along a mountain, Strab.
to outstep one's boundaries, encroach on a neighbour's property, Anth.
an encroacher, Anth.
to urge on, stimulate, Xen.
to lie at anchor beside or near, Plut.
incitement, Xen.
stimulative, Plut.
to anchor side by side, Lys.
ill-omened, Aesch.
to dig alongside or parallel, Thuc.
to dig one against another, as was done by men in training for a preparatory exercise as the Olympic games.
Dep. to represent by vulgar dancing, Luc.
adv.,
of Time, beforetime, formerly, erst, Hom., Trag.; θεοὶ οἱ πάρος Aesch.; τά τε πάρος τά τ’ εἰσέπειτα Soph., etc.
like πρίν, before, Lat. priusquam, c. inf., πάρος τάδε ἔργα γενέσθαι Il.
anteced. to πρίν γε, πάρος δ’ οὐκ ἔσσεται ἄλλως, πρίν γε . . not until, Id.
before the time, too soon, Id.
rather, sooner, Id.
rarely of Place, first, σοι βαδιστέον π. Soph.
prep., poet. = πρό,
of Place, before, Il., Soph., Eur.
of Time, θανεῖν πάρος τέκνων Eur.
Causal, before, above, in preference to, Id.
for, instead of, ἀδελφῶν πάρος θανεῖν Id.
Paros, one of the Cyclades, famous for its white marble, Hhymn.:—adj. Πάριος, η, ον, Πάριος λίθος Parian marble, Pind., Hdt.
to urge one on to do a thing, Pind.
a being present, presence, Aesch., Eur., etc.; so, πόλις μείζων τῆς ἡμετέρας παρουσίας = ἡμῶν τῶν παρόντων, Thuc.:—of things, κακῶν π. Eur. : —παρουσίαν ἔχειν for παρεῖναι, Soph.
arrival, Id., Eur.:— the Advent, NTest.
Pass. to sit beside in a chariot, τινι Xen.
to turn from its course, divert, Plut.:—metaph., τοῦτ’ αὖ παρωχέτευσας εὖ Eur.
a supplying, furnishing, νεῶν παροχῇ with liability to furnish ships, Thuc.
to move as with a lever, Anth.
one who goes beside another in a chariot, one who attends the bridegroom (v. παράνυμφος), Ar.
Dep. to eat dainties, Luc.
a dainty side-dish, Xen.
an addition to the regular fare, a dainty, metaph., π. χλιδῆς a new relish to luxury, Aesch.
in act. and pass. sense, Dep.: to speak freely, openly, boldly, Plat., etc.
freespokenness, openness, frankness, Eur.; μετὰ παρρησίας Dem.
in bad sense, licence of tongue, Isocr.
a free speaker, Arist.
freespoken, Arist.
to furnish with a hem or border (παρυφή) :—ὅπλα παρυφασμένα armed men hemming in an unarmed crowd, Xen.
a border woven along a robe, Lat. clavus.
to be avoided, Pind.
a song or poem in which serious words become burlesque, a burlesque, parody, Arist.
singing indirectly, obscurely hinting, Eur.
to push aside, reject, slight, Soph., Eur.:—Pass. to be set aside, slighted, Xen., Dem.
Mid. to push away from oneself, reject, renounce, Eur., Aeschin.
of Time, to put off, Plat.
near or on the ocean, Plut.
nearly even or equal, Strab.
= παρ-ώνῠμος, Plat.
as Subst., παρωνύμιον, ου, a derivative, Id.
a surname, Plut.
formed by a slight change, derivative, Aesch.
a district on the side of a mountain, Polyb.
a mountaineer, Anth.
out of season, untimely: neut. πάρωρα as adv., Anth.
the projecting eaves or cornice of a roof, Hdt.
of the ship Argo, a care to all, i. e. known to all, Od.
the finest meal: metaph., ὕπνου οὐδὲ πασπάλη not a morsel of sleep, Ar.
Lat. omnis, all, when used of many; when of one only, all, the whole:
in pl. all, πάντες τε θεοὶ πᾶσαί τε θέαιναι Il.; τῶν Σαμίων πάντες Thuc.; ἅμα πάντες, πάντες ἅμα all together, Il., etc.
with a Sup., πάντες ἄριστοι all the noblest, Lat. optimus quisque, Hom.
all, the whole, πᾶσα ἀλήθεια all the truth, Il.; χαλκέη πᾶσα all of bronze, Hdt.; ἦν ἡ μάχη ἐν χερσὶ πᾶσα all hand to hand, Thuc.; ἡ πᾶσα βλάβη nothing but mischief, Soph.
= ἕκαστος, every, Hom., etc.; πᾶς χώρει let everyone go, Ar.:—also, πᾶς ἀνήρ Soph., etc.; πᾶς τις every single one, Hdt., etc.; πᾶς ὅστις . . Soph.; πᾶν ὅσον Aesch., etc.
When the Art. is used, it is generally put after πᾶς, πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν all his force, Hdt.; πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν Thuc.
πᾶς is put between the Art. and Subst., to denote totality, ὁ πᾶς ἀριθμός Aesch.; τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος Thuc.
as a Subst., τὸ πᾶν the whole, Aesch.; τὰ πάντα the whole, Id.
With Numerals it marks an exact number, ἐννέα πάντες quite nine, full nine, no less, Od.; δέκα πάντα τάλαντα Il.; but, κτήνεα τὰ θύσιμα πάντα τρισχίλια ἔθυσε 3000 of all kinds, Hdt.
with the Article, in all, οἱ πάντες εἷς καὶ ἐννενήκοντα Id.
Special Usages:—in dat. pl. masc. πᾶσι, with or in the judgment of all, Il., Soph.
πᾶσι as neut., in all things, altogether, Soph.
πάντα γίγνεσθαι to become all things, i. e. assume every shape, Od.; εἰς πᾶν ἀφικνεῖσθαι to venture everything, Xen.
πάντα εἶναί τινι to be everything to one, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
πάντα as adv. for πάντως, in all points, entirely, wholly, Od., Soph., etc.:—but, τὰ πάντα in every way, by all means, altogether, Hdt.
neut. sg. τὸ πᾶν the whole, one's all, περὶ τοῦ παντὸς δρόμον θέειν Id.; τοῦ π. ἐλλείπειν Aesch.: — τὸ πᾶν as adv., on the whole, altogether, Soph., etc.; with a negat. at all, Aesch.
πᾶν everything, anything, πᾶν μᾶλλον ἢ στρατιήν anything rather than an army, Hdt.; πᾶν ποιῶν by any means whatever, Plat.; so, πάντα ποιῶν Dem.
ἐπὶ πᾶν on the whole, in general, generally, Plat.
παντὸς μᾶλλον above all, absolutely, necessarily, Lat. ita ut nihil supra, Id.:—in answers, π. γε μᾶλλον yes, absolutely so, Id.

with Preps., ἐς πᾶν κακοῦ ἀπικέσθαι to all extremity of ill, Hdt.; so, εἰς πᾶν ἀφικέσθαι Xen.; ἐς τὸ πᾶν altogether, Aesch.:— ἐν παντὶ ἀθυμίας εἶναι in all extremity of despair, Thuc.:— περὶ παντὸς ποιεῖσθαι to esteem above all, Lat. maximi facere, Xen.:— διὰ παντὸς (sc. χρόνου), or as one word διάπαντος, for ever, continually, Soph., Thuc., etc.: but also, altogether, Thuc., Plat.
pinned down, Aesch.
to pin or fasten to, τί τινι Aesch., Eur.
to drive in like a peg, Aesch.
a peg on which to hang clothes, arms, etc., Hom., etc.; ἀπὸ πασσαλόφι ζυγὸν ᾕρεον Il.; ἀπὸ πασσάλου αἴνυτο τόξον Od.; ἐκ πασσαλόφι κρέμασεν φόρμιγγα Id.
a gag, Ar.
πάσσος, οἶνος, Lat. vinum passum, raisin wine, Polyb.

entry.etym: irreg. epic comp. of παχύς, for παχύτερος or παχίων
entry.sense: thicker, stouter, Od.
to sprinkle, φάρμακα πάσσων laying salves upon a wound, Il.: —c. gen. partit., πάσσε ἁλός sprinkle some salt, Id.
to besprinkle, χρυσῶι, ῥόδοις π. τινά Ar.
metaph. to embroider, broider, Il.; π. ἀέθλους to work battles in embroidery, Id.
a porch, Hdt.: also, a colonnade, piazza, corridor, Xen.
like θάλαμος, an inner room, bridal chamber, Eur., Theocr.; of the cave in which Antigone was immured, Soph.
to be besprinkled, Ar.
a bridal chamber, Luc.
the Hebrew Passover (from pasach to pass over), the paschal supper, NTest.
radical sense, to receive an impression from without, to suffer, as opp. to doing, ἔρξαν τ’ ἔπαθόν τε Od.; δρᾶν καὶ πάσχειν, etc.; ὁμοίως π. τινί to be in the same case with . . , Hdt.
the sense is often limited by some word expressing good or evil:

κακῶς πάσχειν to be ill off, in evil plight, unlucky, Od., etc.; κακῶς π. ὑπό τινος to be ill used, ill treated by . . , Aesch.; often with an adj., κακά, λυγρὰ π. Il., etc.; δεινὰ π. Dem.; also with a Subst., ἄλγεα π. etc., Hom.
εὖ πάσχειν to be well off, in good case, lucky, Theogn., etc.; also, to receive benefits, opp. to εὖ δρᾶν, Aesch., etc.; so, ἀγαθὰ π. Hdt., etc.

without a limiting word, it always refers to evil, being used for κακῶς or κακὰ π., μάλα πολλ’ ἔπαθον Od., etc.; μή τι πάθηις lest thou suffer any ill, Hom.; εἴ τι πάθοιμι or ἤν τι πάθω, a euphemism, if aught were to happen to me, i. e. if I were to die, Hdt., attic
τί πάθω; to express the extreme of perplexity, what is to become of me? what can I do? Hom., etc.; τί πάσχεις; what are you about? Ar.
the interrog. τί παθών; expresses something amiss, τί παθόντες γαῖαν ἔδυτε; what ailed you that you died? Od.

to be affected in a certain way, be in a certain state of mind, entertain certain feelings, Thuc., Plat.; ὅπερ ἂν οἱ πολλοὶ πάθοιεν as would be the case with most men, Thuc.; ἵνα μὴ ταὐτὸ πάθητε τῶι ἵππωι that it be not with you as with the horse in the fable, Arist.; ὑϊκὸν πάσχει he is swinishly disposed, Xen.; so of things, πάσχει τοῦτο καὶ κάρδαμα this is just the way with cress, Ar.
τὰ εὖ πεπονθότα benefits received, Aeschin.; cf. δράω.
to clatter, clash, clap, of the sharp noise caused by the collision of two bodies, Ar.; of waves, to dash, plash, Theocr.: to chatter, as birds, Soph.
trans., τύμπανα π. to beat drums, Luc.
a clatter, crash, of trees falling, Il.; a chattering of teeth, Id.; the plash of a body falling into water, Id.; the rattling or crash of thunder, Ar.: a clashing of arms, Hdt., Trag.
the name of a notorious impostor, Aeschin.
Phoenician deities of dwarfish shape, forming the figure-heads of ships, Hdt.
Scythian word, Hdt.
intr. to beat, knock, Lat. palpito, θυμὸς ἐνὶ στήθεσσι πάτασσεν Il.; κραδίη στέρνοισι πατάσσει (as Shaksp., "my heart knocks at my ribs") Id.
like πλήσσω, to strike, smite, π. τινὰ δορί Eur.; absol., Soph., etc.; of a deadly blow, ἐὰν λίθος ἢ σίδηρος πατάξηι Dem.
πατάξαι θύραν to knock at the door, Ar.
metaph., πατάξαι θυμόν Soph.; π. καρδίαν Ar.
to eat, σπλάγχν’ ἐπάσαντο Il.; c. gen. partit. to eat of, partake of, σίτοιό τ’ ἐπασσάμεθ’ ἠδὲ ποτῆτος Od.; δείπνου πασσάμενος, etc., Id.: absol. to taste food, οὔτι πεπάσμην Id.
to say or call father, Ar.
little father, Luc.
to tread, walk, Pind., Aesch.
trans. to tread on, tread, πορφύρας πατεῖν Aesch.; χῶρος οὐχ ἁγνὸς πατεῖν, i.e. it is holy ground, Soph.; πατεῖν πύλας to pass the gates, Aesch.
to walk in, i. e. to dwell in, frequent, Soph., Theocr.:—metaph., like Lat. terere, εὐνὰς π. to frequent, use, misuse, Aesch.; π. Αἴσωπον to be always thumbing Aesop, Ar.
to tread under foot, trample on, Aesch., Soph., etc.

entry.etym: acc. always πατέρα gen. pl. rarely πατρῶν
entry.sense: a father, Hom., etc.; πατρὸς πατήρ a grandfather, Il.; τὰ πρὸς πατρός = πατρόθεν, by the father's side, Hdt.
among the gods Zeus is called πατήρ, πατὴρ Ζεύς, π. ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε Hom., Hes.; so Ζεὺς π. Aesch.; Ζεῦ πάτερ καὶ θεοί Ar.
a respectful mode of addressing elderly persons, Od.
metaph. the father of anything, Lat. auctor, π. ἀοιδᾶν Pind., etc.
in pl. fathers, i.e. forefathers, Hom.; ἐξ ἔτι πατρῶν as an inheritance from one's fathers, Od.
a treading on, εἱμάτων Aesch.
a trodden or beaten way, path, Hom.: —metaph., ἔξω πάτου out-of-the-way, Luc.
one who slays his father, a parricide, Ar., etc.
one's fatherland, native land, country, home, Il., Trag.: —πατρίς was the common prose form.
fatherhood, descent from a common father, ὁμὸν γένος ἤδ’ ἴα πάτρη Il.: then, like πατριά II, a house, clan, Lat. gens, Pind.
a city of Achaia, now Patras, Thuc.
citizens of Patras, Hdt.
from a race or family, Pind.
lineage, pedigree, by the father's side, Hdt.
= πάτρα II, a clan, house, family, Id., NTest.
the father or chief of a race, a patriarch, NTest.
Comic Dim. of πατήρ, daddy, Ar.
derived from one's fathers, paternal, hereditary, Ar., Thuc., etc.
= πάτριος, of or belonging to one's father, ἡ πατρική (sc. οὐσία) patrimony, Eur.; τὰ πατρικά Anth.
like a father, paternal, Arist.
of or belonging to one's father, Lat. patrius, Pind., Soph., etc.

= πατρικός, derived from one's fathers, hereditary, οἱ π. θεοί Hdt., Ar., etc.: —τὰ πάτρια, Lat. instituta majorum, κατὰ τὰ πάτρια Ar., Thuc., etc.; rarely in sg., τὸ πάτριον παρείς neglecting the rule of our fathers, Thuc. Cf. πατρῷος.
of one's fathers, πατρὶς γαῖα, αἶα, ἄρουρα one's fatherland, country, Hom.
as Subst., like πάτρα, Il., attic

one of the same country, a fellow-countryman, applied to barbarians who had only a common πατρίς, πολῖται being used of Greeks who had a common πόλις (or free state), Plat.; ἵπποι πατρ. Xen.; by a metaph., Mount Cithaeron is the πατριώτης of Oedipus, Soph.

entry.etym: fem. of πατριώτης, π. γῆ = πατρίς, Eur.

entry.sense: from or after a father, πατρόθεν ἐκ γενεῆς ὀνομάξων naming him by descent by his father's name, Il.; ἐμὸς τὰ πατρόθεν mine by the father's side, Soph.; ἀναγραφῆναι π. to have one's name inscribed as the son of one's father, Hdt.
coming from, sent by one's father, π. ἀλάστωρ Aesch.; π. εὐκταία φάτις a father's curse, Id.
a father's brother, Hom., Hes.
Patroclus the friend of Achilles
entry.etym: the obl. cases as if from **patrokleu/s*Πατροκλεύς, gen. Πατροκλῆος, acc. Πατροκλῆα, voc. Πατρόκλεις, Il.; nom. pl. Πάτροκλοι, Ar.;—a nom. Πατροκλῆς, Theocr.

entry.sense: to murder one's father, Aesch.
murder of a father, parricide, Plut.
murdering one's father, parricidal, Trag.; π. μίασμα the pollution of parricide, Aesch.:—but χεὶρ πατροκτόνος a father's murdering hand, Eur.
a parricide, Anth.
a mother's father, Luc.
Pass. to be under a patriarchal government, Plat.
paternal government, Luc.
of or like a πατρονόμος: ἡ -κή (sc. ἀρχή or τροφή) the rule of a father, Plat.
a father's father, Pind.
reft of father, Aesch.
holding from the father: π. παρθένος a sole-heiress, Hdt.
murderer of one's father, Od.
parricidal, Aesch., Eur.:—as Subst. a parricide, Plat.
named after his father, Aesch.

of or from one's father, coming or inherited from him, Lat. paternus, Hom., etc.; ξεῖνος πατρώιος my hereditary friend, Il.; γαῖα πατρωίη one's fatherland, Id.; πατρώια one's patrimony, Id., etc.; π. δόξα hereditary glory, Xen.; Ζεὺς π. also the god who protects a parent's rights, Ar.
like πάτριος, of or belonging to one's father, Pind., Soph.; τὰ πατρώια the cause of one's father, Opp. to τὰ μητρώια, Hdt.
a father's brother, uncle by the father's side, Lat. patruus, Hdt., Pind.
rest, a resting-point, stop, end, pause, Soph.; οὐκ ἐν παύλῃ ἐφαίνετο there seemed to be no end of it, Thuc.
c. gen., π. νόσου cessation of disease or rest from it, Soph.; παῦλάν τιν’ αὐτῶν some means of stopping them, Xen.
seldom, Theogn.
of few words, Anth.
little, small, of Time, short, Hes., Pind.
of number, few, Hom., Hes., etc.: comp. παυρότερος, fewer, Il.;—neut. pl. παῦρα as adv. few times, seldom, Hes., Ar.
stilling the wind, θυσία Aesch.
ending pain, Eur.
curing sickness, Anth.
ending toil or hardship, c. gen., Eur.
one must stop, Plat.
fit for ending or relieving, νόσου Soph.
one who stops, calms, a reliever, νόσου Soph.
like παῦλα, rest, Il.
Causal, to make to cease:

of persons, to bring to an end, check, make an end of (by death), Hom., etc.:—Pass. and Mid. to take one's rest, rest, cease, have done, Il.:—also of things, to make an end of, stop, abate, Id., etc.; π. τόξον to let one's bow rest, Od.; π. τὸν νόμον to annul it, Eur.; π. τυραννίδα to put it down, Dem.

c. acc. pers. et gen. rei, to make to rest, stop, hinder, keep back from a thing, π. Ἕκτορα μάχης, etc., Hom., etc.: —π. τινὰ τῆς βασιλείας to depose one from being king, Hdt., etc.:—Pass. and Mid. to leave off from, rest or cease from, πολέμου Hom., etc.; τῆς μάχης Hdt., etc.; ἐκ τρόχων πεπαυμένοι at rest from play, Eur.
rarely c. gen. rei only, αἴ κέ ποθι Ζεὺς παύσηι ὀϊζύος oh that Zeus would make an end of woe! Od.; φάρμαχ’, ἅ κεν παύσηισι ὀδυνάων Il.

c. part. praes. to stop a person from doing or being, π. τινὰ ἀριστεύοντα to stop him from being first, Id., attic:—Pass. and Mid. to leave off doing or being, ἄνεμος μὲν ἐπαύσατο θύων left off blowing, Od.; the partic. omitted, αἷμα ἐπαύσατο the blood stopt [flowing], Il., etc.
inf. for part., ἔμ’ ἔπαυσας μάχεσθαι Id.; with μή inserted, θνητούς γ’ ἔπαυσα μὴ προδέρκεσθαι Aesch.
intr. in imperat., παῦε cease, leave off, Soph., Ar.; so, παῦε, παῦε τοῦ λόγου Ar.
a Paphlagonian, Il.:—adj. Παφλαγονικός, ή, όν, Xen.
to boil, bluster, of the sea, Il.:— metaph. to splutter, bluster, of the angry Cleon (hence called Παφλαγών), Ar.
a boiling, of the sea:—metaph., παφλάσματα blusterings, Ar.
Paphos, a town in Cyprus celebrated for its temple of Aphrodite, Od.:—adj. πάφιος, η, ον, of Aphrodite, Ar.
massive, Od.
entry.etym: seemingly a poet. form of παχύς, as περιμήκετος of περιμήκης

entry.sense: hoar-frost, rime, Lat. pruina, Od., Aesch.: metaph., κουροβόρος π. the clotted blood of the eaten children, Aesch.

to congeal, make solid: metaph., ἐπάχνωσεν φίλον ἦτορ he made his blood run cold, made it curdle, Hes.; Pass., ἦτορ παχνοῦται his heart is cold and stiff [with grief], Il.; παχνοῦσθαι πένθεσιν, λύπῃ Aesch., Eur.
thickness, Od., Thuc.:— absol., πάχος in thickness, Hdt.
π. σαρκός stoutness, Eur.
with stout calves, Ar.
thickish: adv. -λῶς, coarsely, roughly, Arist.
consisting of thick or coarse parts: metaph. in adv. roughly, Strab.
to thicken, fatten, Plat., Xen.:—Pass. to grow fat, Ar.: to become thick, of the skull, Hdt.
metaph. to increase:—Pass., ὄλβος ἄγαν παχυνθείς Aesch.
metaph. also to make gross or stupid:—Pass., NTest.
