thick, stout, Hom., Hes.:— later, stout, fat, Ar.
of things, thick, massive, Hom., Ar.:—adv. -έως, roughly, of stating or arguing, Arist.; παχύτερον or -έρως, Plat.
of liquids, thick, curdled, clotted, Il., Hdt.
οἱ παχέες the men of substance, the wealthy class, Hdt.; τοὺς παχεῖς καὶ πλουσίους Ar.
in Com. and Prose, thick-witted, gross, dull, stupid, like Lat. pinguis, crassus, Id.
comp. παχύτερος, sup. -ύτατος:—irreg. comp. πάσσων, ον, Od.:—Sup. πάχιστος, Il.
speaking broad or roughly, Strab.
thickness, stoutness, Hdt.
the thickness or sediment of liquor, Id.
to bind with fetters, to bind fast, make fast, Od., Hdt., Aesch.
to shackle, trammel, constrain, Hom., Soph.; c. inf. to constrain one to do a thing, Hom.

a fetter, Lat. pedica, compes, mostly in pl. fetters, shackles, Il., etc.; πεδέων (ionic) ζεῦγος a pair of fetters, Hdt.; metaph., πέδαι ἀχάλκευτοι fetters not forged by smiths, of the robe in which Agamemnon was entangled, Aesch.
a mode of breaking in a horse, Xen.
one fettered, a prisoner, Luc.
a hinderer, Anth.
of or on the plain:— οἱ πεδιακοί the party of the plain, i. e. those who opposed Peisistratus, Arist.; called οἱ ἐκ τοῦ πεδίου by Hdt.; οἱ πεδιεῖς by Plut.
of the plain, Strab.
poet. fem. of πέδιος, = πεδινός, flat, level, Hdt.: ἡ πεδιάς (sc. γῆ) the level country, Id.
on or of the plain, Soph.; λόγχη πεδιάς spearmen on the plain, Id.
abounding in plains, level, Aesch.
mostly in pl. sandals, Hom., Hes., Eur.
any covering for the foot, shoes or boots, Hdt.
metaph., Δωρίῳ πεδίλῳ φωνὰν ἐναρμόξαι, i.e. to adapt the song to Doric rhythm, Pind.; also, ἐν τούτῳ πεδίλῳ πόδ’ ἔχειν to have one's foot in this shoe, i. e. to be in this condition or fortune, Id.
flat, level, Hdt.: comp. πεδινώτερος Plat.
of or on the plain, Xen.
to the plain, Hom., Ar.
dwelling in plains, π. θεοί gods of the country, Aesch.
a plain or flat, and collectively a plain flat open country, Hom., Hes., etc.
earth-walking, Aesch.
from the ground, Hes., Eur.
from the bottom, Pind.: metaph. from the bottom of the heart, Od.
from the beginning, Pind.
on the ground, on earth, Aesch.
lying on the ground, Anth.
to the ground, earthwards, Il., Soph.
to the plain, Od.
the ground, earth, Hhymn., attic; πέδῳ πεσεῖν to fall on the ground, to earth, Aesch.; so, ῥίπτειν πέδῳ Eur.
= πεδίον, Soph., Ar.
earth-treading, Eur.:— on foot, opp. to ἱππηλάτης, Aesch.
digging the soil, Anth.
= πούς, Anth.
metaph. the bottom or end of a body, πέζῃ ἔπι πρώτῃ at the far end, Il.
the edge or border of anything, of a garment, Anth.
a leader of foot, Xen.
trafficking by land, Strab.
the foot-guards in the Macedon. army, the horse-guards being ἑταῖροι, Dem.
to go or travel on foot, walk, opp. to riding, Eur.
to go by land, opp. to going by sea, Xen.; οἱ πεζεύοντες land-forces, Arist.
on foot, of or for a foot-soldier, τὸ πεζικόν the foot, the infantry, Xen.; τὰ π. the evolutions of infantry, Id.
like πεζός, of a land force, opp. to a fleet, Id., Aeschin., etc.
to walk over, Anth.
one who shouts the battle-cry on foot, a foot-soldier, Pind.
to fight by land, opp. to ναυμαχέω, Hdt., Ar.; τισί with others, Thuc.; π. ἀπὸ τῶν νεῶν to fight like soldiers from ship-board, Id.
a battle by land, opp. to ναυμαχία, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
fighting on foot, Luc.
fighting as a soldier, opp. to ναυμάχος, Plut.
commanding by land, Aesch.
to go on foot, Xen.
to go by land, to march, Polyb.
going by land, Anth.; ναύτης ἠπείρου π. πελάγους, of Xerxes, Id.

on foot, πεζοί fighters on foot, opp. to horsemen, Hom.:—also on land, going by land, opp. to sea-faring, Id.:—so, ὁ πεζὸς στρατός, or ὁ πεζός alone, sometimes foot-soldiery, infantry, opp. to cavalry (ἡ ἵππος), Hdt., Xen.
ὁ πεζός, also, a land-force or army, opp. to a naval force, Hdt., Thuc.; so, τὸ πεζόν Hdt.; στρατιὰ καὶ ναυτικὴ καὶ πεζή Thuc.; τὰ πεζὰ κράτιστοι strongest by land, Id.
of animals, land, as opp. to birds and fishes, τὰ π. καὶ τὰ πτηνά beasts and birds, Plat.
metaph. of language, not rising above the ground, prosaic, Luc.
dat. fem. πεζῇ (sub. ὁδῷ) as adv., on foot, Xen.
by land, Thuc.
obeying men, obedient, Aesch.
to obey one in authority, c. dat., π. πατρί Soph.; τοῖς νόμοις Ar.: absol. to be obedient, Arist.:—so in Mid., Hdt.
obedience to command, Aesch., Soph.
obeying readily, Arist.
obedient, Aesch.
Peitho, Persuasion as a goddess, Lat. Suada, Suadela, Hes., Hdt., Trag.
as appellat., the faculty of persuasion, winning eloquence, persuasiveness, Aesch., Plat., etc.
a persuasion in the mind, Aesch.
a means of persuasion, inducement, argument, Eur., Ar.
obedience, Xen.

Act. to prevail upon, win over, persuade, τινά Hom., etc.:—c. acc. pers. et inf. to persuade one to do, Il., etc.; also, π. τινὰ ὥστε δοῦναι, etc., Hdt.; π. τινα ὡς χρή Plat.; π. τινὰ εἴς τι Thuc.; in part., πείσας by persuasion, by fair means, Soph.
Special usages:
to talk over, mislead, ἔληθε δόλωι καὶ ἔπεισεν Ἀχαιούς Od.
to prevail on by entreaty, Hom.
π. τινὰ χρήμασι to bribe, Hdt.; so, π. ἐπὶ μισθῶι or μισθῶι Id., Thuc.: so, πείθειν τινά alone, Xen., NTest.
c. dupl. acc., πείθειν τινά τι to persuade one of a thing, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
Pass. and Mid. to be prevailed on, won over, persuaded, absol., Hom., attic; the imperat. πείθου or πιθοῦ listen, comply, Trag.; c. inf. to be persuaded to do, Soph.; also, πείθεσθαι ὥστε . . Thuc.
πείθεσθαί τινι to listen to one, obey him, Hom., etc.; νῦν μὲν πειθώμεθα νυκτὶ μελαίνηι, of leaving off the labours of the day, Il.; —πάντα πείθεσθαί τινι to obey him in all things, Od., etc.

πείθεσθαί τινι, also, to believe or trust in a person or thing, Hom., etc.: —c. acc. et inf. to believe that, Od., etc.: with an adj. neut., π. τὰ περὶ Αἴγυπτον Hdt.; ταῦτ’ ἐγώ σοι οὐ πείθομαι I do not take this on your word, Plat.

perf. 2 πέποιθα, like the Pass., to trust, rely on, have confidence in a person or thing, Hom., etc.; c. inf., πέποιθα τοῦτ’ ἐπισπάσειν κλέος I trust to win this fame, Soph.; πέποιθα τὸν πυρφόρον ἥξειν Aesch.;— πεπ. εἴς τινα, ἐπί τινα NTest.
perf. pass. πέπεισμαι to believe, trust, c. dat., Aesch., Eur.: c. acc. et inf., πεπ. ταῦτα συνοίσειν Dem.
also ος, ον, hungry, Anth.; π. πίνακες empty dishes, Id.
hunger, famine, Od., Plat.
metaph. hunger or longing for a thing, Plat.

entry.etym: forms in αε contr. into η not ᾱ, as in διψάω
entry.sense: to be hungry, suffer hunger, be famished, Lat. esurio, Hom., etc.: πεινᾶντι (doric for -ῶντι) μὴ προσενθῆις don't go near a hungry man, Theocr.
c. gen. to hunger after, Od.: —metaph., π. χρημάτων, ἐπαίνου Xen., NTest.
to make proof or trial of, τινός Od.:—c. inf. to attempt to do, NTest.:—Pass., πεπειράσθω let trial be made, Ar.
c. acc. pers. to try or tempt a person, put him to the test, NTest.: absol., ὁ πειράζων the tempter, Id.:—Pass. to be sorely tempted, to be tempted to sin, Id.
Peiraeeus, the most noted harbour of Athens; gen. Πειραιέως, attic Πειραιῶς, dat. Πειραιεῖ, acc. Πειραιᾶ, ionic Πειραιέα. — adj. Πειραϊκός, ή, όν, Plut.
over the border, γῆ π. border- country, the march, Thuc.
to fasten by the two ends, to tie fast, σειρὴν ἐξ αὐτοῦ πειρήναντε having tied a rope to him, Od.

a trial, attempt, essay, experiment, Theogn., Soph., etc.; —πεῖραν ἔχειν to be proved, Pind.; but, πεῖραν ἔχειν τινός to have experience of a thing, Xen.; π. ἔχει τῆς γνώμης involves a trial of your resolution, Thuc.; —πεῖράν τινος λαμβάνειν to make trial or proof of . . , Xen., etc.: —πεῖράν τινος διδόναι, Lat. specimen sui edere, Thuc.

with Preps., ἀπὸ πείρης by experiment, Hdt.: —εἰς πεῖράν τινος ἔρχεσθαι, ἰέναι Eur., Thuc.: —ἐν πείρᾳ τινὸς γίγνεσθαι to be acquainted with, associate with one, Xen.: —ἐπὶ πείρᾳ by way of test or trial, Ar.
an attempt on or against one, c. gen., Soph.
generally, an attempt, enterprise, Aesch., Soph.
an end, mostly in pl., πείρατα γαίης the ends of the earth, Hom.:— absol., πείρατα the ends or ties of ropes, Od.; cf. ἐπαλλάσσω.
the end or issue of a thing, Id.; ἑκάστου πείρατ’ ἔειπεν of the issues or chief points, Il.:—pleonastic, πείρατα νίκης = νίκη, πείρατ’ ὀλέθρου
act. that which gives the finish to a thing, πείρατα τέχνης, the finishers of his art (of tools), Od.
trial, temptation, NTest.
tentative, Arist.
one must attempt, Plat.
to be a pirate, Strab.
φόνια πειρατήρια the murderous ordeal, Eur.
a pirate's nest, Strab., Plut.
a pirate, Lat. pirata, i. e. one who attacks ships, Polyb., Plut.
piratical, Plut.: τὰ π. gangs of pirates, Strab.
Act. to attempt, endeavour, try to do, c. inf., Il., Hdt., etc.
c. gen. pers. to make trial of one, Il.: in hostile sense, to make an attempt on, Hom., Hdt.
absol. to try one's fortune, try one's skill in thieving, Hhymn.; ναυσὶ π. to make an attempt by sea, Thuc.; cf. πειρατής.
c. acc. pers. to make an attempt on, Ar.
Dep. in the same sense, c. inf. to try to do, Il., Hdt.;—also foll. by εἰ, to try whether, Il.; by μή, Od.
most commonly, c. gen.,

c. gen. pers. to make trial of one, to see whether he is trustworthy, Hom., Hdt.:—also in hostile sense, to make trial of the strength of an enemy, Il.; π. τῆς Πελοποννήσου to make an attempt on it, Hdt.; τοῦ τείχους Thuc.

c. gen. rei, to make proof or trial of one's strength, Hom.:— to try one's chance at or in a work or contest, Id.:—also to make proof of a thing, to see what it is good for, τόξου, νευρῆς Od.:— to make proof of, have experience of, make acquaintance with others, Hdt., Thuc.
absol. to try one's fortune, try the chances of war, Il.
c. dat. modi, to make a trial or attempt with, ἐπειρήσαντο πόδεσσι tried their luck in the foot-race, Od.; σφαίρηι πειρήσαντο Id.; also, π. σὺν ἔντεσι, σὺν τεύχεσι πειρηθῆναι Il.
c. acc. rei, ἢ ἕκαστα πειρήσαιτο or should examine into each particular, Od.
c. acc. pers. to make an attempt on, Pind.
to attempt, try, prove, c. inf., or absol., Hom.
c. gen. pers. to make trial of, Id.: c. gen. rei, σθένεος καὶ ἀλκῆς Od.
c. acc., π. στίχας ἀνδρῶν to attempt, i. e. attack, the lines, Il.
a wicker-basket fixed upon the ἅμαξα or carriage, being in fact the body of the cart, Hom.

to pierce quite through, fix meat on spits, for roasting, Il.; κρέα ἀμφ’ ὀβελοῖσιν ἔπειραν Id.:—also, διὰ πεῖρεν ὀδόντων ἔγχεϊ he ran him through the teeth with a spear, Id.:— Pass., ἥλοισι πεπαρμένον studded with golden nails, Id.; but, ὀδύνηισι πεπαρμένος pierced with pain, Id.; also, πεπαρμένη περὶ δουρί Id.
metaph., κύματα πείρειν to cleave the waves, Hom.; πεῖρε κέλευθον clave her way [through the sea], Od.
poet. for πειθώ, obedience, ἐν πείσηι κραδίη μένε, i. e. it remained calm, Od.
persuading or controlling mortals, of a king's sceptre, Aesch.
obeying the rein, Pind.
a ship's cable, Od., Aesch.:— generally, a rope, Od. (Properly, that which holds in obedience.)
persuasion, NTest.
one must persuade, Plat.
(from Pass.) one must obey, Soph., Eur.
persuasive, Eur.
a rope, Theocr.
persuasive, Plat.
to shear, clip, Ar.
to comb or card wool, Od.: Mid., χαίτας πεξαμένη when she combed her hair, Il.
to shear sheep, Hes., Theocr.: Mid., πόκως πέξασθαι to have their wool shorn, Simon. ap. Ar.
to form a sea or lake, of a river that has overflowed, Hdt.:—of places, to be flooded, Id.
to keep the sea, cross the sea, Xen.
of the sea, Lat. marinus, Eur.:—of animals, living in the sea, Id.
out at sea, on the open sea, Soph.; of seamen or ships, Thuc., Xen.
fem. adj. of or on the sea, Anth.

the sea, esp. the high sea, open sea, the main, Lat. pelagus, Hom., etc.; joined with other words denoting sea, ἁλὸς ἐν πελάγεσσιν (cf. aequora ponti), Od.; πόντιον π. or πόντου π., Pind.; ἅλς πελαγία Aesch.; ἅλιον π. Eur.: often of parts of the sea (θάλασσα), Αἰγαῖον π. Aesch.; ἐκ μεγάλων πελαγῶν, τοῦ τε Τυρσηνικοῦ καὶ τοῦ Σικελιοῦ Thuc.
metaph., of any vast quantity, π. κακῶν a "sea of troubles, " Aesch.; π. δύης Id.; εἰς τὸ π. τῶν λόγων Plat.; also of great difficulties, Soph.
intr. to approach, come near, draw near or nigh, c. dat., πέλασεν νήεσσι Il.; τούτοις σὺ μὴ π. Aesch., etc.
rarely c. gen., πελάσαι νεῶν to come near the ships, Soph.; πελάζειν σῆς πάτρας Id.
with a prep., π. πρὸς τοῖχον Hes.; εἰς ὄψιν τινός Eur.; c. acc. loci, δῶμα πελάζειν Id.; οὐκέτι πελᾶτε will no more approach me, Soph.
absol., Xen.

Causal, to bring near or to, make to approach, Κρήτηι ἐπέλασσεν (sc. τὰς νέας) Od.; νευρὴν μαζῶι πέλασεν brought the string up to his breast, in drawing a bow, Id.; ἐπέλασσα θαλάσσηι στῆθος, in swimming, Id.; πέλασε χθονί brought them to earth, Il.; π. τινὰ δεσμοῖς Aesch.:—metaph., π. τινὰ ὀδύνηισι to bring him into pain, Il.; ἔπος ἐρέω, ἀδάμαντι πελάσσας having made it firm as adamant, Orac. ap. Hdt.
followed by a prep., με νῆσον ἐς Ὠγυγίην πέλασαν θεοί Od.
in Pass., like the intr. Act. to come nigh, approach, etc., c. dat., Il.; πλῆτο χθονί he came near (i. e. sank to) earth, Id.
rarely c. gen., Soph.
foll. by a prep., πελασθῆναι ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν Id.
to approach or wed, of a woman, Aesch.

entry.etym: collat. form of πελάζω intr., Aesch. ap. Ar., Eur.

entry.sense: any half-liquid substance, of various consistency, as oil, Aesch.; clotted blood, Id.; foam at the mouth, Eur.
a mixture offered to the gods, of meal, honey, and oil, Aesch., Eur.
a young stork, Ar.
τὸ Πελαργικόν the northern slope of the Acropolis at Athens, Ar.; written Πελασγικόν in Hdt., Thuc.
the stork, Lat. ciconia, Ar., etc.
entry.etym: From πελός, ἀργός, properly, the blackandwhite.

entry.sense: like a stork, Strab.
Thessalian, but later for Argive, Eur.:—so Πελάσγιος, η, ον, Aesch., Eur.
Pelasgiotes (in Thessaly), Strab.:—fem. adj. Πελασγίς, ίδος, Hdt.

a Pelasgian; in Il., the Pelasgians appear among the allies of the Trojans; in Od. we hear of them in Crete; but in Il., Achilles prays to Dodonaean Zeus as Pelasgian, and τὸ Πελασγικὸν Ἄργος was Thessalian Argos, the original seat of the Hellenes; Hdt. contrasts them with the Hellenes; but Πελασγοί is used for Greeks in Eur., as in Virg.
near, hard by, close, c. gen., Od., Hdt., Trag.
like ἐγγύς, c. dat., Pind., Aesch.
absol., χριμφθεὶς πέλας Od.; π. στείχειν, παρεῖναι, στῆναι Trag.
οἱ πέλας (sc. ὄντες) one's neighbours, Thuc., etc.: hence one's fellow-creatures, all men, Hdt., Trag.: in sg., ὁ πέλας one's neighbour, any man, Hdt., Eur.
one who approaches or comes near, Soph.: a neighbour, Lat. accola, Aesch.
esp. of one who approaches a woman, τὸν πελάταν λέκτρων Διός, of Ixion, Soph.
one who approaches to seek protection, a dependant, Plat.; the Rom. cliens, Plut.
ordure, Ar.
the wild-pigeon, rock-pigeon, stock-dove, so called from its dark colour, Hom., Soph.
πέλειαι, ῶν, αἱ, name of prophetic priestesses, prob. borrowed from the prophetic doves of Dodona, Hdt.
= πέλεια, Il., Hdt., Trag.
= πέλεια II, Soph.
dove-nurturing, Aesch.
the woodpecker, as if joiner-bird (from πελεκάω), Ar.
to hew or shape with an axe, Lat. dolare, Od. (in epic aor1 πελέκκησε), Ar.
to cut off with an axe, esp. to behead, Polyb.
a water-bird of the pelican kind, Ar.
an axe-handle, Il.
an axe for felling trees, with two edges, opp. to the ἡμιπέλεκκον, Hom., Xen.

a sacrificial axe, Hom.—That it was not, properly, a battle axe appears from the phrase, οὐ δόρασι μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ πελέκεσι to fight not with spears only, but with common axes, i. e. to the last, Hdt.
in Theophr. Char., πέλεκυς as a child's nickname seems to mean a sharp blade.
an axe-bearer, Lat. consul or praetor, before whom axes are carried, Polyb.
to shake, to make to quiver or tremble, Il.; π. [τόξον] to struggle at the bow, in order to bend it, Od.:—Pass. to be shaken, to tremble, quiver, quake, Il.
to shake or drive from his post, Id.: Pass., χασσάμενος πελεμίχθη Id.
livid, Thuc.
livid, Dem.
Lat. pelvis, a wooden bowl, milk-pail, Il., Theocr.
in the Peloponnesian (i. e. Dorian) dialect, Theocr.
Peloponnesian, Strab.
Peloponnesian, inhabitants of the Peloponnese, Hdt., etc.
for Πέλοπος νῆσος, the Peloponnesus, now the Morea, Hhymn., etc.
Lat. pullus, dark-coloured, dusky, ash-coloured, Theocr.
Pelops, i. e. dark-face, son of Tantalus, who migrated from Lydia, and gave his name to Peloponnesus, Il.
to serve as a targeteer, Xen.
one who bears a light shield (πέλτη) instead of the heavy ὅπλον, a targeteer, Lat. cetratus, Eur., Thuc., etc. The peltasts held a place between the ὁπλῖται and ψιλοί.

skilled in the use of the πέλτη, like a targeteer, Plat.:— ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη) the art or skill of a targeteer, Id.: τὸ -κόν, = οἱ πελτασταί, Xen. —Sup. adv., πελταστικώτατα quite in the manner of πελτασταί, in the best style, Id.
a small light shield of leather without a rim (ἴτυς), a target, Lat. cetra, orig. used by the Thracians, Hdt., Eur., etc.
a body of πελτασταί, Eur.
a horse's ornament, Id.
= παλτόν, a shaft, pole, Xen.
bearing a target, Xen.
a kind of axe, Babr.

The orig. sense, to be in motion, appears in Hom., κλαγγὴ πέλει οὐρανόθι πρό the cry goes, rises to heaven, Il.; τῶι δεκάτηι πέλεν ἠώς to him came the tenth morn, Od.; γῆρας καὶ θάνατος ἐπ’ ἀνθρώποισι πέλονται old age and death come upon men, Id.:—this sense of motion is plain in the compd. participles ἐπιπλόμενος, περιπλόμενος.
commonly to be, Hom.; but generally implying continuance, to be used or wont to be, Il.:—the imperf. in pres. sense, ὀϊζυρὸς ἔπλεο thou wast doomed to be, i. e. thou art, Id.
Like πέλωρος, gigantic, Hom.: of things, huge, ἔγχος, λᾶας, κύματα Id.; τὰ πρὶν πελώρια the mighty things, or mighty ones, of old, Aesch.
a monster, prodigy, of the Gorgon, Hom.; of a large stag, Od.; of the animals transformed by Circe, Id.; πέλωρα θεῶν portents sent by the gods, Il.
monstrous, prodigious, huge, gigantic, with collat. notion of terrible, like πελώριος, Hom., Hes.:—neut. pl. as adv., πέλωρα βιβᾷ he strides gigantic, Hhymn.
a portent, prodigy, monster, only in nom. and acc., of the Cyclops, Od.; of Scylla, Id.; even of Hephaestus, Il.
any kind of dressed food; but mostly in pl., pastry, cakes, sweetmeats, Hdt.
a commander of a body of five, Xen.

properly to count on the five fingers, i. e. to count by fives, and then, generally, to count, Aesch.:—so in Mid., ἐπὴν πάσας πεμπάσσεται (epic for πεμπάσηται aor1 subj.) when he has done counting them all, Od.
a body of five, Plat., Xen.
one who counts: used as a Verbal c. acc., μύρια π. reviewing by tens of thousands, Aesch.

on the fifth day, agreeing with the Subject, πεμπταῖοι ἱκόμεσθα on the fifth day we came, Od.; πεμπταῖον ἐγένετο it was on the fifth day, Dem.; π. προκεῖσθαι to have been five days laid out as dead, Ar.
to be sent, Luc.
πεμπτέον, one must send, Xen.
the fifth, oneself with four others, πέμπτος μετὰ τοῖσιν Od.; πέμπτος αὐτός Thuc.; π. σπιθαμή, i. e. 4 cubits and a span, Hdt.; τὸ πέμπτον μέρος a fifth, Plat.
ἡ πέμπτη (sc. ἡμέρα) the fifth day, Hes., Ar.
sent, Thuc.
a five-pronged fork, for stirring the sacrificial fire, Hom.
to send, despatch, Il., etc.; of a ship, to convey, carry, Od.; c. dupl. acc., ὁδὸν π. τινά to conduct one on his way Soph.
to send forth or away, dismiss, like ἀποπέμπω, to send home, Hom.; χρὴ ξεῖνον παρεόντα φιλεῖν, ἐθέλοντα δὲ πέμπειν, "welcome the coming, speed the parting guest, " Od.
of missiles, to discharge, shoot forth, Hes.
of words, to send forth, utter, Aesch., Soph.

to conduct, convoy, escort, Lat. deduco, Hom., etc.; ὁ πέμπων absol., of Hermes, Soph.:— πομπὴν πέμπειν to conduct a procession, Hdt., Thuc.; π. χορούς Eur., Xen.: in Pass., πέμπεσθαι Διονύσωι to be carried in procession in his honour, Hdt.
to send with one, give as provision for a journey, Od., Hdt., etc.
like ἀναπέμπω, to send up, produce, Soph.
in Mid., πέμπεσθαί τινα, = μεταπέμπεσθαι, to send for one, Soph., Eur.
to send for oneself, to send in one's own service or cause some one to be sent, Soph.
a sending, mission, dispatch, Hdt., Thuc.
the class of Penestae, Arist.

a labourer, workman:—the πενέσται were the Thessalian serfs, ascripti glebae, Ar., Xen., etc. Like the Εἵλωτες in Laconia, they were orig. a conquered tribe, afterwards increased by prisoners of war, and formed a link between the freemen and the born slaves.
generally, any slave or bondsman, Eur.:— a poor man, Ar.
one who works for his daily bread, a day-labourer, a poor man, distinguished from πτωχός (beggar), Hdt., Soph., etc.
as adj. of a poor man, δόμος Eur.; ἐν πένητι σώματι Id.: c. gen., π. χρημάτων poor in money, Id.; π. φίλων Plat.:— comp. πενέστερος Xen.; Sup. πενέστατος Dem.
tending the poor, Anth.
sad, mourning, Anth.
a mother-in-law, Lat. socrus, Dem.
a father-in-law, Lat. socer, Hom., etc.:—in pl. parents-in-law, Eur.
generally, a connexion by marriage, e. g. brother-in-law, Id.
to bewail, lament, mourn for, Il.; πενθεῖν τινὰ ὡς τεθνεῶτα Hdt., etc.:—Pass. to be mourned for, Isocr.
lamentation, mourning, Aesch., Eur.
of five days, κατὰ πενθήμερον for alternate spaces of five days, Xen.
consisting of five halves, or two and a half:—in Prosody, τομὴ π. the caesura after two feet and a half, as in hexam. and iamb. verses.
consisting of five half feet, i. e. of 2 1/2 feet, Xen.
lamenting, mourning, Eur.
of or in sign of mourning, Aesch.

sic.seg: penqhthfailing on lembuf [] | /r, h=ros, o(, h(,

entry.sense: a mourner, Aesch.:— fem., κακῶν πενθήτριᾰ, she who mourns for evils, Eur.
of or for mourning, mournful:—adv., πενθικῶς ἔχειν τινός to be in mourning for a person, Xen.
mournful, mourning, sorrowful, Aesch., Eur.
mournful, sorry, wretched, γῆρας Eur.
grief, sadness, sorrow, Hom., etc.; τινός for one, Od.:—esp. of the outward signs of grief, mourning for the dead, Hom., etc.; π. ποιήσασθαι to make a public mourning, Hdt.
a misfortune, Hdt., Pind.
of persons, a misery, Soph.
entry.etym: Related to πάθος, as βένθος to βάθος.

entry.sense: poverty, need, Od., etc.
poor, needy, Od., Theogn.
Dep., used in pres. and impf. :
intr. to work for one's daily bread; generally, to toil, work, labour, Hom.
to be poor or needy, Solon, Eur., etc.
c. gen. to be poor in, have need of, Aesch., Eur.
trans. to work at, prepare, get ready, δαῖτα πένοντο Od.; τί σε χρὴ ταῦτα πένεσθαι; Id.
five drachmae, Xen.
of the weight or value of five drachmae, Hdt.
= πεντετηρίς, Arist.
as adj. coming every fifth year, Pind.
five years old, Hom.
five years old, Hdt.
of Time, lasting five years, Thuc.:— neut. adv. πεντάετες, for five years, Od.
with five zones, Strab.

the contest of the five exercises, Lat. quinquertium, Pind.; πεντάεθλον ἀσκεῖν or ἐπασκεῖν Hdt.—These exercises were ἅλμα, δίσκος, δρόμος, πάλη, πυγμή, the last being exchanged for the ἀκόντισις or ἀκών; they are summed in one pentam., ἅλμα, ποδωκείην, δίσκον, ἄκοντα, πάλην.
one who practises the πένταθλον or conquers therein, Arist.: metaph. of "a jack of all trades, " Xen.
five-pointed, Anth.
five times ten thousand, 50, 000, Hdt.
five times, Pind., Aesch., etc.:—in late Poets πεντάκῐ, Anth.
five thousand, Hdt.
the commander of 500 men, Plut.
five hundred, Od., Hdt.
at Athens, οἱ πεντακόσιοι the senate of 500 (ἡ βουλή), chosen by lot (ἀπὸ κυάμου), 50 from each tribe, Dem., etc.
possessing land which produced 500 medimni yearly, Thuc., Arist.:—acc. to Solon.'s distribution of the Athen. citizens, the πεντακοσιομέδιμνοι formed the first class.
the five-hundredth, one of 500, Ar.
the fifth wave, supposed to be larger than the four preceding, Luc.
in five parts, Strab.
five handbreadths wide, long, Xen.
five cubits long or broad, Hdt.
five-fold, Hdt.; π. τινος five times as large as . . , Arist.
with five berries, Anth.
a magistracy of five, Arist.
five spans long or broad, Xen.
of five stades, Strab.:— also πεντα-σταδιαῖος, Luc.
of five lines or verses, Anth.
with five mouths or openings, of rivers, Hdt.
consisting of five books: as Subst., ἡ π. (sc. βίβλος) the five books of Moses, Pentateuch.
of five-fold nature, five, Anth.
five-fold, in five divisions, Il.
in five places, Hdt.
a squadron of 15 ships, Dem.
fifteen, Hdt., etc.
worth fifteen talents, Dem.
the fifteenth, NTest.
fifty-five years old, Plat.
five, Hom., etc.
with five holes, ξύλον π. a pillory, furnished with five holes, through which the head, arms, and legs of criminals were passed, Ar.
worth or consisting of five talents, Dem.; π. δίκη an action for the recovery of five talents, Ar.
happening every five years, quinquennial, Strab.
a term of five years, Lat. quinquennium, διὰ πεντετηρίδος every five years, Hdt.
a festival celebrated every five years, Id., Thuc.
of five years, σπονδαί Ar.
Dep. to conquer five times, Anth.
worth fifty drachmae, Plat.
fifty years old, Plat.
of or lasting fifty years; fem., πεντηκονταέτιδες σπονδαί Thuc.
of fifty-three years, Polyb.
fifty-headed, Hes.
consisting of fifty children, Aesch.
having fifty children, Id.
fifty, Lat. quinquaginta, Il., etc.
to be a πεντηκόνταρχος, Dem.
the commander of fifty men, Xen., Dem.
the commander of fifty men, an officer in the Spartan army, Thuc., Xen.
of fifty acres of corn-land, Il.
fifty fathoms deep, high, long, Hdt.
(sc. ναῦς), a ship of burden with fifty oars, Pind., Eur., Thuc.
fifty years old, Plat.
five hundred, Od.
Pass. to be charged with the tax πεντηκοστή on any articles, Dem.
a collector of the tax πεντηκοστή, Dem.
fiftieth, Plat.
as Subst., ἡ πεντηκοστή,

(sc. μερίς), at Athens the duty of one-fiftieth, or two per cent., on all exports and imports, Oratt.; εὕρηκε καινὴν ἱππικῆς τινὰ πεντηκοστήν he invented a new two per cent. duty, in lieu of his cavalry service, i. e. paid this instead of it, Dem.
(sc. ἡμέρα), the fiftieth day (after the Passover), Pentecost, NTest.
a number of fifty, esp. as a division of the Spartan army, Thuc.; κατὰ πεντηκοστῦς (acc. pl.) Xen.
(sc. ναῦς), a quinquereme, Hdt.:—so, πεντηρικὸν, πλοῖον, σκάφος Polyb.:—v. τριήρης.
like πεντάοζος, with five branches: Hes. calls the hand πέντοζον, the five-branch.
of five fathoms, Anth.
membrum virile, Ar., etc.
to ripen, make ripe, Hdt.; absol., διασκοπῶν τὰς ἀμπέλους, εἰ πεπαίνουσιν ἤδη, i. e. if the grapes are ripening, Ar.:—Pass. to become ripe, Hdt., etc.
metaph. to soften, assuage anger, Ar., Xen.; of a person, ἢν πεπανθῆις Eur.

entry.etym: rarer collat. form of πέπων, Anth.

entry.sense: to display, manifest, only in Pind.
ripe, Lat. maturus, Anth.
metaph. softened, ὀργή Soph.
pepper, the pepper-tree, Lat. piper.

entry.etym: from πέπλασμαι, perf. pass. of πλάσσω.
entry.sense: artificially, by pretence, Plat., Arist.
in late Poets with heterog. pl. πέπλα, any woven cloth used for a covering, a sheet, carpet, curtain, veil, Il., Eur.
a robe, worn by women over the common dress, and falling in folds about the person, answering to the man's ἱμάτιον or χλαῖνα, Hom., etc.
esp. of the πέπλος of Athena, embroidered with mythol. subjects, which was carried like the sail of a galley in public procession at the Panathenaea, Eur., Plat.
a man's robe, Trag.; esp. of the long Persian dresses, Aesch.
a robe, Trag.

entry.etym: old epic perf. pass. of πνέω, with pres. sense
entry.sense: to have breath or soul, and metaph. to be wise, discreet, prudent, πέπνῡσαι νόωι Il.; inf. πεπνῦσθαι Hom.; 2 sg. plup. with imperf. sense, πέπνῡσο Od.; part. πεπνῡμένος, as adj., sage, wise, sagacious, Hom., Hes.
trust, confidence, boldness, NTest.
of fruit, cooked by the sun, ripe, mellow, Lat. mitis, Hdt., Ar., etc.

metaph. in voc., mostly as a term of endearment, kind, gentle, ὦ πέπον my good friend, Il.; κριὲ πέπον my pet ram, Od.;— in bad sense, soft, weak, Il.; ὦ πέπονες ye weaklings, Id.: —μόχθος πέπων softened pain, Soph., etc.: c. dat., ἐχθροῖς π. gentle to one's foes, Aesch.
from beyond, from the far side, Hdt., Eur.
to bring to an end, finish, accomplish, execute, Trag., etc.:—Pass. to be brought to an end, be finished, πάντα πεπείρανται Od.: to be fulfilled, accomplished, Eur. etc.
in speaking, to end a discourse, finish speaking, Aesch., etc.
to repeat from beginning to end, Ar.:— to relate, Eur.
absol. to effect one's purpose, esp. with a neg., οὐδὲν π. to come to no issue, do no good, make no progress, Eur., Thuc.
intr. to make way, reach or penetrate, Aesch., Plat.
intr. to come to an end, end, Plut.

on the other side:—as Subst., ἡ περαίη (sc. γῆ, χώρα) the opposite country, the country on the other side of a strait, Strab.; ἡ π. τῆς Βοιωτίης χώρης the part of Boeotia over against [Chalcis], Hdt.; ἡ π. τῶν Τενεδίων the coast [of Mysia] opposite Tenedos, Strab.

to carry to the opposite side, carry over or across, στρατιὰν ἐπεραίωσε, Lat. trajecit exercitum, Thuc.:—Pass., with fut. mid., to pass over, cross, pass, Od., Ar., Thuc.;—also c. acc. loci, ἐπεραιώθη τὸν Ἀραξέα Hdt.; τὸ πέλαγος Thuc.
beyond, ὁδοὶ περαίτεραι roads leading further, Pind.
adv. περαιτέρω, further, Eur.; καὶ ἔτι π. Thuc.
c. gen., τῶνδε καὶ π. Aesch.; π. τοῦ μετρίου Xen.; and absol., π. (sc. τοῦ δέοντος) πεπραγμένα beyond what is fit, too far, Soph.
a carrying over, Strab.
on the other side, across, beyond, Lat. trans, c. gen., πέρην ἁλός Il.; τὰ πέρην τοῦ Ἴστρου Hdt.; πόντου πέραν Aesch.
absol. on the other side, Hdt., Xen.

with Verbs of motion, foll. by εἰς, over or across to, πέρην ἐς τὴν Ἀχαιίην διέπεμψαν Hdt.; πέραν εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν διαβῆναι Xen.: also without εἰς, διαβαλόντες πέρην having crossed over to the main land, Hdt.
with the Art., διαβιβάζειν εἰς τὸ πέραν τοῦ ποταμοῦ Xen.; τὰ πέραν things done on the opposite side, Id.:— ἡ πέραν γῆ the country just over the border, the border- country. Thuc.
over against, opposite, c. gen., πέρην Εὐβοίης Il.
= πέρα, beyond, c. gen., π. γε πόντου τερμόνων τ’ Ἀτλαντικῶν Eur.
conclusive, logical, Ar.
beyond, across or over, further, Lat. ultra, Plat.
c. gen., Ἀτλαντικῶν πέρα ὅρων Eur.
of Time, beyond, longer, Xen.
c. gen., π. μεσούσης ἡμέρας Id.
beyond measure, excessively, extravagantly, πέρα λέγειν, φράζειν Soph., etc.

c. gen. more than, beyond, exceeding, π. δίκης, καιροῦ Aesch.; π. τῶν νῦν εἰρημένων Soph.; θαυμάτων π. more than marvels, Eur.:—sometimes the gen. is omitted, ἄπιστα καὶ πέρα things incredible, and more than that, Ar.
also as comp., foll. by ἤ, Soph.
above, higher than, τῶν ἐχθρῶν πέρα Id.
passable, Plut.
a crossing, βίου πέρασις passage from life to death, Soph.
an end, limit, boundary, ἐκ περάτων γῆς Thuc.
an end, finish, οὐ π. ἔχων κακῶν Eur.; πέρας ἐστὶ τοῦ βίου θάνατος Dem.
an end, completion, Luc.
as adv., like τέλος, at length, at last, Aeschin., etc.
on the opposite side:—as Subst., περάτη (sc. χώρα) an opposite land or quarter, esp. of the west, as opp. to the east, ἐν περάτῃ Od.
to drive right through, λευκοὺς ἐπέρησεν ὀδόντας Il.

commonly, to pass across or through a space, to pass over, pass, cross, traverse, περᾶν θάλασσαν, πόντον Od.; πύλας πέρησεν passed through the gates, Il.; τάφρος ἀργαλέη περάαν hard to pass, Id.; τὰς φυλακὰς π. to pass the guards, Hdt.:—metaph., κίνδυνον π. to pass through, i. e. overcome, a danger, Aesch.; π. ὅρκον, prob. to go through the words of the oath, Lat. jusjurandum peragere, Id.
rarely of Time, to pass through, complete, τοῦ βίου τέρμα Soph.; τὴν τελευταίαν ἡμέραν Eur.
intr. to penetrate or pierce right through, of a weapon, Il.; of rain, Od.: to extend to a place, Xen.
to pass across, to pass, δι’ Ὠκεανοῖο Od.; ἐπὶ πόντον Il.; διὰ Κυανέας ἀκτάς through the Symplegades, Eur.
to pass to or from a place, εἰς Ἀΐδαο Theogn.; ἔξω δωμάτων Soph.:—c. acc. loci, π. Δελφούς Eur.
rarely of Time, διὰ γήρως π. Xen.; εὐδαίμων π. to live happy, Orac. ap. Xen.
to pass all bounds, to go too far, Soph.; so, π. ὀργῆς to pass all bounds in anger (or to cease from anger), Id.
with instrument of motion in acc., π. πόδα, ἴχνος Eur.

to carry beyond seas for the purpose of selling, to export for sale; then like πέρνημι, to sell men as slaves, Hom.; π. τινα Λῆμνον to sell one to Lemnos, Il.; or with a prep., π. τινὰ ἐς Λῆμνον Id.; π. τινὰ πρὸς δώματά τινος Od.
Pergamus, the citadel of Troy, Il.; τὸ Πριάμου Πέργαμον Hdt.; τὰ Πέργαμα Soph., Eur., etc.: —then, any citadel, Aesch., Eur.
also Περγαμία, Pind.
a deme of the φυλὴ Ἐρεχθηίς.
at Pergase, Ar.
keeping partridges, Strab.
a partridge, Lat. perdix, Soph.
to break wind, Lat. pedere, Ar.

entry.etym: syncop. aor2 inf. πέρθαι, like δέχθαι from δέχομαι
entry.sense: to waste, ravage, sack, destroy, a town, Hom.
of persons, to destroy, slay, Pind., Soph.:—metaph. of love, Eur.
of things, to destroy, Aesch., Soph.
to get by plunder, Il., Eur.
broken in pieces, Anth.
= περιηγής, quite round, Id.
to purify all round, Luc.
to bend and break all round: Pass., ὂψ περιάγνυται the voice is broken all round, i. e. spreads all round, Il.
to lead or draw round, Hdt.
to lead about with one, have always by one, Xen.; so in Mid., Id.
to turn round, turn about, τὴν κεφαλήν Ar., etc.:— π. τὴν σκυταλίδα to twist it round in order to tighten a noose, Hdt.
to put off, Luc.
to bring round to a point, πρός τι Arist., etc.
c. acc. loci, to go round, περιάγουσι τὴν λίμνην κύκλῳ Hdt.; π. τὰς πόλεις NTest.
a windlass, capstan, Luc.
a going round, a revolution, Plat.
to go about singing, Luc.
that may be taken off, Thuc.

entry.note: fut. ήσω perf. -ῄρηκα aor2 περι-εῖλον inf. -ελεῖν
entry.sense: to take off something that surrounds, take off an outer coat, take away, strip off, τὰ τείχη Hdt., Thuc.; π. τὸν κέραμον taking off the earthen jar into which the gold had been run, Hdt.:—Mid. to take off from oneself, π. τὴν κυνέην to take off one's helmet, Hdt.; βιβλίον περιαιρεόμενος taking [the cover] off the letter, i. e. opening it, Id.:—but Mid. often just like Act. to strip off, take away, Xen., Plat.:—Pass. to be taken off, τοῦ ἄλλου περιῃρημένου when the rest has been taken away, Thuc.
Pass. also c. acc. rei, to be stript of a thing, περιῃρημένοι χρήματα καὶ συμμάχους Dem.; τοὺς στεφάνους περιῄρηνται Id.
one must bring round, Plat.
to be greatly pained at, τινί Thuc.
much pained, very sorrowful, Plat.
to smear all over, anoint, Ar.
before all others; in adv. περίαλλα, before all, Hhymn., Pind.: exceedingly, Soph.
with purple all round, κακοῖς π. double-dyed in villany, Ar.
anything worn about one, an amulet, Anth.
to put round about, π. τινά τι to put a thing round or over one, Ar.:—Mid. to put round oneself, put on, Plat.
to cover all round, Id.
to defend or guard all round, Plut.
hung round one: as Subst., περίαπτον, τό, = περίαμμα, Plat.: an appendage, Arist.
to tie, fasten, hang about or upon, apply to, γυίοις φάρμακα περάπτων (aeolic form) Pind.: —Mid. to put round oneself, put on to wear, Plat.
metaph., π. τιμάς, αἶσχός τινι to attach to one, Ar.; ἀντὶ καλῆς [δόξης] αἰσχρὰν π. τῇ πόλει Dem.
to light a fire all round or in the midst, NTest.
to fit on all round, τί τινι Plut.
to hang round or on:—Pass. to be hung round, c. dat., Plut.
to flash around, c. acc., NTest.
to be busy about a thing, Luc.
put round the neck, Hdt.

to go round, of one defending a fallen comrade, either to walk round and round him, or, like ἀμφιβαίνω, to bestride him, absol., Il.; c. gen., περιβῆναι ἀδελφειοῦ κταμένοιο Id.; also, c. dat., Πατρόκλῳ περιβάς Id.; so, περὶ τρόπιος βεβαῶτα astride of the keel, Od.; c. acc., π. ἵππον to bestride a horse, Plut.
of sound, to come round one's ears, Soph.

to throw round, περὶ χαῖρε βαλών having thrown his arms round him, Od.; χέρας π. τινί Eur.; περὶ δ’ ὠλένας δέρᾳ βάλοιμι Id.; π. τινὶ δεσμά Aesch.; π. ναῦν περὶ ἕρμα to wreck it on a reef, Thuc.:—Mid. to throw round oneself, put on, c. acc. rei, τεύχεα περιβαλλόμενοι putting on their arms, Od.; π. ἔρυμα, ἕρκος, τείχεα to throw round oneself for defence, Hdt.; c. dupl. acc., τεῖχος περιβάλλεσθαι πόλιν to build a wall round it, Id.:—in perf. pass. to have a thing put round one, Plat.; περιβεβλημένος τὸ τεῖχος having his wall around him, Id.
metaph. to put round a person, i. e. invest him with it, π. τινὶ βασιληίην, τυραννίδα Id., Eur.; δουλείαν Μυκήναις Eur.; π. ἀνανδρίαν τινί, i. e. to make him faint-hearted, Id.

reversely, c. dat. rei, to surround, encompass, enclose with, περιβάλλειν βρόχῳ τὸν αὐχένα Hdt.; τινὰ πέπλοις Eur.; π. τινὰ χερσί to embrace, Id.:—metaph., π. τινὰ συμφοραῖς, κακοῖς to involve one in calamities, evils, etc., Id.:—so in Mid. to surround or enclose for oneself, Xen.
π. τινὰ χαλκεύματι to put him round the sword, i. e. stab him, Aesch.

c. acc. only, to encompass, surround, περιβάλλει με σκότος Eur.; π. τινά to embrace him, Xen.; but also to clothe, NTest.:—Pass., τὸ περιβεβλημένον the space enclosed, enclosure, Hdt.:—Mid., ἤλαυνον περιβαλλόμενοι [τὰ ὑποζύγια] surrounding them, Id.
to fetch a compass round, double, c. acc., ἵπποι περὶ τέρμα βαλοῦσαι Il.; of ships, π. τὸν Ἄθων Hdt., etc.
to frequent, be fond of a place, Xen.
Mid. to bring into one's power, aim at, Lat. affectare, as we say "to compass" a thing, π. ἑωυτῷ κέρδεα Hdt.; σωφροσύνης δόξαν π. Xen.:—perf. pass. to have come into possession of a thing, Hdt.
to cloke or veil in words, Plat.
to throw beyond, and so, generally, to excel, surpass, μνηστῆρας δώροισι Od.; or, simply, π. ἀρετῇ to be superior in virtue, Il.
exceeding heavy, Aesch.
to survive, Plut.
looked at from all sides, admired of all observers, Eur., Xen.
intr. to look round about, gaze around, Xen., etc.
trans. to look round at, πάντας Id.: so in Mid., NTest.
to seek after, look about for, τινά or τι Luc.
to gaze on, admire, respect, Soph.; π. βίαν to be jealous of, suspect force, or to covet it, Eur.:—Pass., περιβλέπεσθαι τίμιον, Lat. digito monstrari, Id.
a looking about: close examination, Plut.
poet. περί-βωτος, noised abroad, much talked of, famous, Thuc., Dem.
in bad sense, notorious, scandalous, Dem.:—adv. -τως, notoriously, Aeschin., Dem.
with or amid shouts, epith. of Ares, Soph.
that which is thrown round, a covering, θανάτου περιβόλαια corpse-clothes, Eur.; π. σαρκὸς ἡβῶντα youthful incasements of flesh, i. e. youth, manhood, Id.: a chariot-cover, Plut.

anything which is thrown round, a covering, Plat.; χειρῶν περιβολαί embraces, Eur.; so περιβολαί alone, Xen.; περιβολαὶ χθονός, i. e. the grave, Eur.; π. [ξίφεος] a scabbard, Id.: absol. of walls round a town, ἑπτάπυργοι π. Id.
a space enclosed, compass, οἰκίης μεγάλης περιβολή a house of large compass, Hdt.
a circumference, circuit, Thuc.; π. ποιεῖσθαι to make a circuit, Xen.
metaph.,
a compassing, endeavouring after, τῆς ἀρχῆς, Lat. affectatio imperii, Id.
ἡ π. τοῦ λόγου the whole compass of the matter, long and short of it, Isocr.
going round, compassing, encircling, Eur.
as Subst., περίβολος = περιβολή, ἐχίδνης περίβολοι the spires or coils of a serpent, Id.; in pl. walls round a town, Hdt., Eur.; so in sg., Thuc.
an enclosure, circuit, compass, π. νεωρίων Eur.; of a temple, the precincts, Plut.
to let feed around:—Pass., of cattle, to feed on all round, c. acc., Luc.
round or on the arm, Plut.:— περιβραχιόνιον, ου, an armlet or piece of armour for the arm, Xen.
engulfed by the surge all round, οἴδματα π. waves swallowed up by one another, i. e. wave upon wave, Soph.
to stop up round about, to stuff in all round, τί τινι Luc.

entry.note: ionic and later -γίνομαι fut. -γενήσομαι aor2 -εγενόμην perf. -γέγονα
entry.sense: to be superior to others, to prevail over, overcome, excel, c. gen., ἡνίοχος περιγίγνεται ἡνιόχοιο Il., etc.; rarely c. acc., π. Ἕλληνας Hdt.:—absol. to be superior, prevail, Id., Thuc., etc.
of things, ἤν τι περιγένηταί σφι τοῦ πολέμου if they gain any advantage in the war, Thuc.; π. ὑμῖν πλῆθος νεῶν you have a superiority in number of ships, Id.

to live over, get over, to survive, escape, Lat. salvus evadere, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; οἱ περιγενόμενοι the survivors, Hdt.; also c. gen. rei, περιεγένετο τούτου τοῦ πάθεος he survived this disaster, Id.
of things, to remain over and above, Ar., Xen.
of things also, to be a result or consequence, ἐκ τῶν μεγίστων κινδύνων μέγισται τιμαὶ περιγίγνονται Thuc.; περιγίγνεταί τι the upshot of the matter is so and so, Dem.
full of milk, Il.
Dep. to turn round the eyeballs, glare around, of a lion, Theocr.
ready of tongue, Pind.
to double a headland, Μάλειαν Od.
a line drawn round a ring, Luc.
one must trace out, Plat.
marked round, ἐκ περιγραπτοῦ from a circumscribed space, Thuc.
a line drawn round, an outline, sketch, Plat., Arist.
a circumference, circuit, Arist.
that which is marked by an outline, a contour, π. ποδοῖν Aesch.
dress, Luc.
to draw a line round, mark round, Lat. circumscribo, Hdt.; π. κύκλον to draw a circle round, Id.:—absol. to draw a circle, Ar.
to define, determine, Xen.:—Pass., περιεγέγραπτο, limits had been drawn, Id.
to draw in outline, sketch out, Lat. delineare, Arist.
to enclose as it were within brackets, to cancel, Anth.; π. τινὰ ἐκ πολιτείας to exclude from civic privileges, Aeschin.
very timid or fearful, Hdt.; τινος of or for a person or thing, Thuc.; π. μὴ . . , Id.:— adv. -ῶς, in great fear, Id.

entry.note: fut. -δείσομαι aor1 περιέδεισα epic3 pl. περίδδεισαν part. περιδδείσας perf. περιδέδοικα epic περιδείδια
entry.sense: to be in great fear about, c. gen., Δαναῶν περιδείδια Il.; c. dat. to be in great fear for, Αἴαντι περιδδείσαντες Id.; ἐμῇ κεφαλῇ περιδείδια Id.
with two right hands, i.e. using both hands alike, Il.
very dexterous, Ar.
passed round the neck: as Subst., περιδέραιον, ου, a necklace, Arist., Plut.
to bind, tie round or on, τί τινι Hdt.:—Mid. to bind round oneself, put on, Id., Ar.

entry.etym: Mid. of περιδίδωμι, which does not occur
entry.sense: to stake or wager, c. gen. rei (i. e. pretii), τρίποδος περιδώμεθα ἠὲ λέβητος let us make a wager of a tripod, i. e. let us wager a tripod (to be paid by the loser), Il.; ἐμέθεν περιδώσομαι αὐτῆς I will wager for myself, i. e. pledge myself, Od.; π. πότερον to lay a wager whether, Ar.; so, περιδίδομαι περὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς I stake my head, Id.; c. dat. pers. added, περίδου μοι περὶ θυματιδᾶν ἁλῶν have a wager with me for a little thyme-salt, Id.; περίδου νῦν ἐμοί Id.
to whirl or wheel round, Aeschin.: —Pass. to run circling round, πόλιν περιδινηθήτην (3 dual aor1 pass.) Il.:—so in Mid., Anth.; to spin round like a top, Xen.
a whirling round, Plat.
to be in great fear for, c. dat., only in 3rd sg. imperf., περὶ γὰρ δίε νηυσὶν Ἀχαιῶν Il., etc.
to pursue on all sides, Strab.
Dep. to grasp a thing with the hand, c. gen. rei, Plut.
whirled round, Anth.
a running round, Plut.; π. ποιεῖσθαι to wheel about, Xen.
a revolution, orbit, Eur.
running round, of a chariot-rail, of the nave of a wheel, Il.; of the rim of a shield, Eur.
going about, roaming, Theogn., Ar.
pass. that can be run round, and so standing apart, detached, Hom.
as Subst. that which surrounds, as the rim of a shield, Eur.; the string that runs round the top of a net (cf. ἐπίδρομος), Xen.; a gallery running round a building, Id.
to tear all round, to peel the bark off a tree, Anth.:—Pass., ἀγκῶνας περιδρύφθη (epic aor. 1 pass.) he had the skin all torn from off his arms, Il.
to pull off from round, strip off, περίδυσε χιτῶνας Il.
to fold or wrap round, σακκία περὶ τοὺς πόδας Xen.
to wrap up, swathe:—Mid. to swathe oneself, περιειλάμενος (aor1 part.), Ar.
to be around a place, c. dat., Thuc.; τὰ περιόντα circumstances, Dem.

to be better than, superior to another, surpass, excel, c. gen., Il., Hdt.; περίεσσι γυναικῶν εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε Od.; οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν περὶ δ’ ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι ( = μάχην) Il.; c. dat. rei, σοφίᾳ π. τῶν Ἑλλήνων Plat.: absol. to be superior, Hdt., etc.; ἐκ περιόντος at an advantage, Thuc.
to overlive, outlive, τινι Hdt.: absol. to survive, remain alive, Id., Dem., etc.:—of things, to be extant, to be in existence, Hdt.
to be over and above, to remain in hand, of property, money, etc., Thuc.; οἰόμενοι περιεῖναι χρήματά τῳ imagining that any one has a balance in his hands, Dem.

to be a result or consequence, περίεστιν ὑμῖν ἐκ τούτων what you have got by all this is . . , Id.; τοσοῦτον ὑμῖν περίεστιν τοῦ πρὸς ἐμὲ μίσους you have so much hatred against me left, Philipp. ap. Dem.; c. inf., περίεστι ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς ἐρίζειν it remains for you to quarrel with them, Dem.
to go round fetch a compass, Hdt.; π. κατὰ νώτου τινί to get round and take him in rear, Thuc.:— to go about with idle questions or stories, Dem.
c. acc. loci, to go round, compass, π. τὸν νηὸν κύκλῳ Hdt.; π. φυλακάς to go round the guards, visit them, Id.:—of sounds, αὐλῶν σε περίεισιν πνοή Ar.
to come round to one, in succession or by inheritance, ἢ ἀρχή, βασιληίη περίεισι εἴς τινα Hdt.
of revolving periods, χρόνου περιιόντος as time came round, Id.; περιιόντι τῷ θέρει Thuc.
to insert or fix round, Hdt.
grasping, Luc.
a place for driving round, a roadway, Hdt.
to drive round, τὰς κύλικας π. to push the cups round, Xen.
to drive about, harass, Ar.:—Pass., Hdt.
to draw or build round, περὶ δ’ ἕρκος ἔλασσε Il.:—Pass., περὶ δ’ ἕρκος ἐλήλαται Od.
seemingly intr. (sub. ἅρμα, ἵππον), to drive or ride round, Hdt., attic
to roll or wind round, τι περί τι Hdt.:—Mid., π. ἱμάντας to wind caestus straps round one's arms, Plat.:— Pass. to be wound round, περιελιχθέντα περὶ τὴν γῆν Id.
to drag round, drag about, Xen.
to draw round another way, κύκλῳ π. τινά, Lat. huc illuc ducere, Plat.:—Pass., Id.
to put round, περὶ εἵματα ἕσσον Il.; περὶ τεύχεα ἕσσεν Id.: Mid., χλαῖναν περιέσσασθαι to put on one's cloak, Hes.

entry.note: imperf. -εῖπον fut. -έψω aor2 -έσπον inf. -σπεῖν Mid., fut. -έψομαι Pass., aor1 inf. -εφθῆναι
entry.sense: to treat with great care:
in good sense, εὖ π. τινά to treat him well, Hdt.; ὡς κάλλιστα π. τινά Id.; π. τινὰ ὡς εὐεργέτην Xen.: alone also, to treat with respect or honour, to caress, Lat. colo, foveo, Id.
in bad sense, τρηχέως, κάρτα τρηχέως π. to treat, handle roughly, Hdt.; π. τινὰ ὡς πολέμιον Id.:—Pass., τρηχέως περιεφθῆναι ὑπό τινος Id.
Dep.:

to take more pains than enough about a thing, to waste one's labour on it, with a part., Σωκράτης περιεργάζεται ζητῶν Plat.; περιείργασμαι περὶ τούτων εἰπών Dem.:—c. dat. modi, τῷ θυλάκῳ περιειργάσθαι that they had overdone it with their "sack" (i. e. need not have used the word), Hdt.:—perf. in pass. sense, οὐδὲ περιείργασται nor is there any superfluity, Luc.
to be a busybody, meddle with other folk's affairs, Dem.
over-exactness in doing anything, Luc.
intermeddling, officiousness, Theophr., Luc.
careful overmuch, Lys., etc.
busy about other folk's affairs, meddling, a busybody, Xen.
pass. done with especial care, elaborate, Aeschin., etc.
superfluous, Plat., etc.
curious, superstitious, Plut.
to inclose all round, encompass, Hdt., Thuc.:—Pass., ἐν περιειργμένοις παραδείσοις in enclosed parks, Xen.
Dep.:

to go round, go about, Hdt., attic:— to go about, like a beggar, Xen.; like a canvasser, Lat. ambire, Dem.:—c. part. to go about doing a thing, Plat.:—c. acc. cogn., π. στάδια χίλια Ar.:—c. acc. loci, π. τὸν βωμόν to go round the altar, Id.; τὴν ἀγοράν Dem.
c. acc. pers. to come round, encompass, of sounds, περὶ κτύπος ἦλθε ποδοῖιν the sound of feet came round him, Od.; of the effect of wine, Κύκλωπα περὶ φρένας ἤλυθεν οἶνος Id.
like Lat. circumvenire, to take in, to overreach, cheat, Hdt., Ar.

to go round and return to a point, come round, ἡ βασιληίη περιῆλθε ἔς τινα Hdt.; ἐς φθίσιν περιῆλθε ἡ νοῦσος the disease ended in . . , Id.; c. acc., ἡ τίσις περιῆλθε τὸν Πανιώνιον vengeance came at last upon him, Id.
of Time, to come round, Xen.
to eat all round, eat away, nibble at, Luc.
the surrounding extremities, Hdt.
thoroughly well cooked, Luc.
to encompass, embrace, surround, Plat.
to surround so as to guard, Plut.
in Pass. to be shut in or beleaguered, ὑπό τινος Hdt., Xen.
to embrace, comprise, comprehend, Plat., etc.
to overcome, gain the victory, Thuc.: of an army, to outflank the enemy, Id.
Mid. to hold one's arms round another, take charge of, c. gen. pers., περίσχεο (ionic aor2 mid. imperat.) παιδὸς ἐῆος Il.; c. acc. to protect, Od.
to cling to, be fond of a person or thing, c. gen., Hdt.
c. inf., περιείχετο μὴ ἐκλιπεῖν he was urgent with them that they should not leave him, Id.
very violently, Hhymn.
to boil round, Luc.; poet. -ζείω Anth.
a spare strap, Xen.
a girdle round the loins, apron, Plut.
to gird round oneself, gird oneself with, ἐσθῆτα Plut.; τοῦτον τὸν ἄνδρα περιεζώσατο put him on as a defence, Ar.; περιεζῶσθαι τὴν φορβείαν to have their halter girded round them, Arist.
a ribbon twined round a garland, Theocr.
Dep.:
to lead round, π. τινι τὸ οὖρος to shew one the way round the mountain, Hdt.
to explain, describe, Luc.
like περιγραφή, an outline, contour, Hdt.
a leading round and explaining what is worth notice, a full description, such as is given by guides and cicerones, Luc.:— geographical description, Strab.
= περιαγής II: of the arms, tied behind one, Anth.
one who guides strangers about and shews what is worth notice, a cicerone, showman, Luc.:— a describer of geographical details, Id.
to have come round to one, τὰ σὲ περιήκοντα that which has fallen to thy lot, Hdt.; τοῦτον τὸν ἄνδρα φαμὲν περιήκειν τὰ πρῶτα we say that the greatest luck befel this man, Id.
of Time, to have come round, Plut.
a coming round, encompassing, Plut.
a revolution, Hdt.
to be much aggrieved, to chafe greatly at, c. dat., Hdt.; c. gen. pers. to be aggrieved at or with him, Id. (Deriv. of -ημεκτέω uncertain.)
to ring all round, Il.:—so in Mid., νῆσος περιηχουμένη τῷ κύματι Luc.
a resounding, echoing, Plut.
much alarmed, Plut.
a putting on, NTest.
put round, περιθεταὶ τρίχες false hair, Polyb.
to run round, Hom., Hdt.; c. acc. loci, Hdt., Xen.
to run about, Lat. discurro, Ar., Plat.
to rotate, revolve, ἀσπίδος αἰεὶ περιθεούσης, i. e. as he was always swaying his shield round and round, Hdt.
to go round and observe, Luc.
Pass. to resound with wailing, Plut.
to edge or fence all round, Plut.
very wrathful, Aesch. adv. -μως, Id.; περιθύμως ἔχειν to be very angry, Hdt.
to wound all round, περὶ θυμὸς ἰάφθη (3 sg. aor1 pass.) Theocr.
to ring around, re-echo, Od.; epic imperf. περίαχε [ῑ], for περιίαχε, Hes.
Dep. to sit round about, Hdt.; c. acc., Id.
to ride round, Polyb.
in the trans. tenses, fut. -στήσω, aor1 -έστησα, to place round, π. τί τινι Hdt.; στρατὸν περὶ πόλιν Xen.:—metaph., π. τινὶ πλείω κακά Dem.
to bring round, π. πολιτείαν εἰς ἑαυτόν to bring it round to himself, Arist.:—esp. to bring into a worse state, Aeschin.
in aor1 mid. to place round oneself, Xen.
Pass. and Mid., with aor2 act. -έστην, perf. -έστηκα, plup. -έστηκειν, to stand round about, Il.; κῦμα περιστάθη a wave rose around (epic aor1 pass.), Od.
c. acc. to stand round, encircle, surround, Hom.; μήπως με περιστήως’ ἕνα πολλοί (epic 3rd pl. aor2 subj.), that their numbers surround me not, Il.; metaph., τὸ περιεστὸς ἡμᾶς δεινόν Thuc.
to come round to one, νομίσαντες τὸ παρανόμημα ἐς τοὺς Ἀθηναίους περιεστάναι Thuc.:—c. dat. to come upon one, ἡμῖν ἀδοξία περιέστη Id.; τοῦ πολέμου περιεστηκότος τοῖς Θηβαίοις Dem.

of events, to come round, turn out, esp. for the worse, ἐς τοῦτο περιέστη ἡ τύχη fortune was so completely reversed, Thuc.; τοὐναντίον περιέστη αὐτῷ it turned out quite contrary for him, Id.; c. inf., περιειστήκει τοῖς βοηθείας δεομένοις αὐτοὺς ἑτέροις βοηθεῖν it came round to those who required help to give help to others, Dem.
in late writers, to go round so as to avoid, Luc., NTest.

entry.note: περι-ιτέος, ον, verb. adj. of περίειμι
entry.sense: one must make a circuit, Plat.
on fire all round: adv., περικαῶς ἔχειν τινός to be hot with love for . . , Plut.
to fasten or hang on all round, ἀγγεῖον Plut.
an off-scouring, refuse, NTest.
Dep. to sit down round, Luc.: c. acc. to sit down round a town, Dem.

entry.note: ionic -κάτημαι inf. ῆσθαι ionic 3pl. imperf. περιεκατέατο
entry.sense: to be seated or to sit all round, Hdt.: of an army, to beleaguer, invest a town, Id.; of ships, to blockade, Id.: c. acc. pers. to sit down by one, Id.
to burn round about: — Pass. to be all scorched, Hdt.
to be in extreme ill-luck, Polyb.
extreme ill-luck, Polyb.
very beautiful, Hom.
one must muffle or wrap oneself up, Ar.
to cover all round, Il.
to put round as a covering, αὐτῷ περὶ κῶμ’ ἐκάλυψα put sleep as a cloak round him, Id.; π. τοῖσι πράγμασι σκότον to throw a veil of darkness over . . , Eur.
to bend round: to drive round (sub. ἅρμα or ἵππους), Plat.
to fall in and go to ruin, Lys.
to tear off round about, strip off:—Mid., περικατερρήξατο τὸν ἄνωθεν πέπλον she tore off and rent her outer garment, Xen.

to lie round about, c. dat., εὗρε δὲ Πατρόκλῳ περικείμενον ὃν φίλον υἱόν she found her son lying with his arms round Patroclus, Il.; γωρυτὸς τόξῳ περίκειτο there was a case round the bow, Od.: —absol. to lie or be round, Hes.; τὰ περικείμενα χρυσία plates of gold laid on (an ivory statue), Thuc.
metaph., οὔ τι μοι περίκειται there is no advantage for me, it is nothing to me, Il.
c. acc. rei, to have round one, to wear, mostly in part., περικείμενοι [τελαμῶνας] περὶ τοῖσι αὐχέσι Hdt.; π. δύναμιν invested with power, Plut.; π. ἅλυσιν with a chain round one, NTest.
to shear or clip all round, Hdt.; Mid., περικείρεσθαι τρίχας to have one's hair clipt, Id.
a covering for the head, a helmet, cap, Polyb.; also περικεφάλαιον, ου, τό, Id.
Dep. to be very anxious about a person, c. gen., Od., Pind.:— π. τινι βιότου to take care of a living for him, Od.
exceeding dry, of timber, Od.
surrounded with pillars, Eur.
ruggedness of ground, Polyb.
to break one thing round or on another, τί τινι Plut.; π. τὸν Τίβεριν to divert it, Id.
famed all round, farfamed, Theocr.
to shut in all round, surround on all sides, Hdt., Thuc.; so in Mid., περικλῄσασθαι τὰς ναῦς to get them surrounded, Thuc.; and in Pass., ὑπὸ πλήθους περικλῃόμενοι Id.
sloping on all sides, Plut.
to decline, of the sun, Strab.
Pass. to be washed all round by the sea, of an island, Thuc.; of a strait, Plut.
washed all round by the sea, of islands, Hhymn., Aesch., etc.
heard of all round, famous, renowned, glorious, Lat. inclytus, Hom.
a covering for the leg, Plut.
to scratch all round, keep nibbling; so in aor1 mid. περικνίξασθε, of bees, Anth.
to cry cuckoo all round, Ar.
to carry round, Thuc.:—Pass. to go round, Id.
that which is cut off all round, trimmings, mincemeat, Ar.
very elegant, exquisite, Ar.
a cutting all round, mutilation, Thuc.; trepanning, Plut.
the outline or general form of a person or thing, Polyb.
a section or short passage in an author: a portion of scripture, as the Epistles and Gospels.
to cut all round, clip, mutilate, Dem.: Pass., περιεκόπησαν τὰ πρόσωπα had their faces mutilated, Thuc.
π. χώραν to lay waste an enemy's country, from the practice of cutting down the fruit-trees, Dem.; hence, to plunder a person, Id.:—simply, to take away, intercept, Plut.
round the skull, πῖλος π. a skull cap, Plut.
having full command over a thing, c. gen., NTest.
to hang round, τί τινι Anth.:—Pass. to hang round, to cling to, c. dat., Id.
steep all round, Plut.
to strike off all round: Pass., περικρουσθεῖσα πέτρας τε καὶ ὄστρεα having stones and shells knocked off, stript of them, Plat.
to conceal entirely, Luc., NTest.
dwellers around, neighbours, Hom.; cf. ἀμφικτίονες.
to encircle, encompass: mostly in Mid. to surround an enemy, Hdt., Xen.
intr. to go round, Luc.
an encircling, encompassing, Thuc.
to roll round, Ar.
surrounded by waves, of islands, Eur.
to carouse round, παλαίστρας Ar.
to smear all over with pitch, π. τὰ ἐμβάδια to black shoes, Ar.
to seize around, embrace, Xen.

to encompass or surround an enemy, so as to intercept him, Hdt.; μετεώρους τὰς ναῦς π. to intercept them at sea, Thuc.; ἐπεὰν δὲ αὐτὸν περιλάβῃς when you get hold of him, catch him, Hdt.:—Pass. to be caught, οἴμοι, περιείλημμαι μόνος Ar.
to comprehend, include, of a number of particulars, Isocr., Plat.
very brilliant, Plut.
to beam around, Plut.
c. acc. to shine around, φῶς π. τινά NTest.:—Pass. to be illumined, Plut., Luc.
Pass. to be left remaining, remain over, survive, Il., Hdt., etc.
to lick all round, Ar.
circumlocution, Ar.
to strip off all round, Il., Hdt.
talked of in every club (λέσχη), matter of common talk, Hdt.
embraced or to be embraced, Plut.
to surround with water, insulate, τὴν πόλιν Thuc.
surviving, Plat.
Dep.:
to lick all round, Theocr., Luc.
to lick up, Luc.
to wash all over, Plut.
deeply grieved, Isocr., Arist.
to gaze or peep eagerly round, σκόπελον περιμαιμώωσα (epic part.), Od.
Pass. to rush furiously about, Hes.
to wipe all round, to purify by magic, disenchant by purification, Dem.
fought about, fought for or to be fought for, Ar., Thuc.; οὐ περιμαχητόν not a thing one would fight for, Xen.
to wait for, await, Hdt., Ar., etc.
of events, to await, be in store for, Soph., Plat.
c. inf., οὐ περιμένουσιν ἄλλους σφᾶς διολέσαι they do not wait for others to destroy them, Plat.; μηδ’ ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν [ταῦτα] ἐλθεῖν π. Dem.
absol. to wait, stand still, Hdt., Ar., etc.
full all round, quite full of, τινός Xen.
to measure all round, Luc.
the circumference, Hdt.
excessive, in size or beauty, very large or very beautiful, of Penelope's web, Od.
περίμετρος (sc. γραμμή) = περίμετρον, Polyb.
very tall or high, Hom.
very tall or long, Od.:— very large, huge, Hdt.
Dep. to prepare very craftily, contrive cunningly, Od.
Dep. to roar round, τινα Plut.
to dwell round about or in the neighbourhood, Od.
in pass. sense, to be inhabited, Id.
one of those who dwell round, a neighbour, Il.
to pile round, ὕλην (sc. περὶ τὸν πύργον) Hdt.
π. τὴν οἰκίην ὕλῃ to pile it round with wood, Id.
a supercargo or passenger, Thuc.
to wash off all round:—Pass., περὶ δ’ αἷμα νένιπται Il.
Dep. to come round, of time, Eur.
to contrive cunningly, Ar.
to consider on all sides, consider well, Plut.
quick intelligence: over-wiseness, Thuc.
to go round, to visit or inspect, τὰς παλαίστρας Ar.
absol. to go about, stalk about, Id., Plat.
polished round about, πέτρη Od.
to polish all round, Theocr.
to shave all round, Hdt.:—Pass., περιεξυρημένος τὸν πώγωνα having one's beard clean shaven, Luc.
as prep. round about, all round, c. gen., Hdt., Xen.
c. acc., Hdt., Aesch., Eur.
as adv. round about, all round, Hdt., Trag.: metaph., π. φρονεῖν circuitously, Eur.
a circuit, Strab.
to go all round, c. acc., Plut.
to be periodical, Strab.
a going round, a flank march, Hdt., Thuc.
a way round, the circumference, circuit, compass, τοῦ τείχεος, τῆς λίμνης Hdt.; absol., τὴν π. in circumference, Id.
γῆς π. a chart or map of the earth (cf. πίναξ), Id., Ar.
a going round in a circle, circuit, Plut.
of Time, a cycle or period of time, Pind., Plat., etc.
a prescribed course of life, system, Plat.
a fit of intermittent fever, Dem.
= περιφορά, a course at dinner, Xen.; π. λόγων table-talk, Id.
the orbit of a heavenly body, Id.
a well-rounded sentence, period, Arist.

entry.etym: perf. and plup. in pres. and imperf. sense
entry.sense: to know well how to do, c. inf., περίοιδε νοῆσαι Il.; c. dat., ἴχνεσι γὰρ περιῄδη for he was well skilled in the tracks, Od.:—c. acc. rei et gen. pers., βουλῇ περιίδμεναι ἄλλων (epic inf.) to be better skilled in counsel than others, Il.
to dwell round a person or place, c. acc., Hdt., Xen.
dwelling or lying round about, neighbouring, Hdt., Thuc.
as Subst. (sc. γῆ, χώρα), the country round a town, the suburbs, Thuc.
a town of περίοικοι, a dependent town, Arist.
to build round, Dem.
to enclose by building round, Id.:—Pass. to be built up, walled in, Thuc., Xen.; τὸ περιοικοδομημένον the space built round, the enclosure, Lat. ovile, Hdt.
dwelling round, Hdt.: —οἱ π. neighbours, Id.

in Laconia, οἱ περίοικοι were the free inhabitants, being remnants of the original population, who enjoyed civil but not political liberty, opp. on the one hand to the Spartans, and on the other to the Helots, Id., Thuc.
to slip away all round, slip off, Plut.
a slipping away, Plut.
to be overlooked or suffered, c. part., οὔ σφι περιοπτέα Ἑλλὰς ἀπολλυμένη Hdt.; c. inf., ἡμῖν τοῦτό ἐστι οὐ περιοπτέον, γένος τὸ Εὐρυσθένεος γενέσθαι ἐξίτηλον Id.
to be watched or guarded against, Thuc.
περιοπτέον one must overlook or suffer, Xen.
to be seen all round, in a commanding position, Plut.
conspicuous, admirable, Id.:—adv. -τως, gloriously, Id.

entry.note: imperf. περιεώρων ionic περιώρεον perf. περιεόρᾱκα fut. -όψομαι perf. pass. -ῶμμαι aor1 pass. -ώφθην aor2 περιεῖδον
entry.sense: to look over, overlook, i. e. to allow, suffer:

mostly c. part., οὐ περιεῖδον αὐτὸν ἀναρπασθέντα they did not overlook his being carried off, i. e. did not suffer him to be . . , Hdt.; μὴ περιιδεῖν τὴν ἡγεμονίην αὖτις ἐς Μήδους περιελθοῦσαν Id., etc.; ταῦτα περιιδεῖν γιγνόμενα Dem.; but, εἰ ὑμᾶς τοὺς ἐναντιουμένους περιίδοιμεν if we overlook your opposition, Thuc.
c. inf., περιιδόντες τοὺς Πέρσας ἐσελθεῖν having suffered them to enter, Hdt., etc.:—with the inf. omitted, οὐκ ἄν με περιεῖδες [ποιέειν] Id.; π. τὴν ὕβριν Xen.
to wait for, τὸ μέλλον περιιδεῖν Thuc.
Mid. to look about before doing a thing, to watch the turn of events, to watch and wait, Id.
c. gen. to look round after, watch over, Id.
very angry or wrathful, Thuc. adv. -γῶς, Aesch.
towards morning: τὸ π. dawn, Thuc.
to mark by boundaries, Plut.
a limitation, Plut.
to anchor round, to blockade, Thuc.
to bring round [a ship] to anchor, Dem.:—Mid. to come to anchor, Thuc.
to dig round, π. λίμνην to dig a lake round, Hdt.
to dig up around, Plut.
to dig out around, Id.
Dep. to dance around, Luc.
that which is over and above necessary expenses, surplus, abundance, plenty, Ar., Thuc., etc.

absol. abundance, plenty, wealth, Plat., etc.; ἀπὸ περιουσίας with plenty of other resources, ex abundanti, Thuc., etc.; εἰς περιουσίαν so as to bring advantage, Dem.; ἐκ περιουσίας at an advantage, Id.
superiority of numbers or force, Thuc.
a being saved, survival, τίς οὖν ἡ ταύτης π.; what is its chance of being saved? Dem.
having more than enough: especial, peculiar, NTest.
compass, extent:—a mass, body, Plut.
a portion circumscribed, a section of a book, NTest.
in violent excitement, greatly distressed, Polyb.
absol. passionate, Luc.:— adv. -θῶς, Id.
to look timidly round, Mosch.
to walk up and down, to walk about, Ar., Xen.: generally, to walk, Plat., etc.
metaph. to walk, i. e. live, NTest.
walking about while teaching: hence Aristotle and his followers were called περιπατητικοί, Peripatetics, Cir., Luc.
a walking about, walking, Plat., etc.
a place for walking, a covered walk, Xen.
discourse during a walk, a philosophical discussion, Ar.
οἱ ἐκ τοῦ περιπάτου the Peripatetics, school of Aristotle, because he taught walking in a περίπατος of the Lyceum at Athens, Plut., etc.
to pierce as with a spit: metaph. to pierce, ἑαυτοὺς π. ὀδύναις NTest.

entry.etym: only in epic syncop. part., of Place, c. acc., ἄστυ περιπλομένων
entry.sense: Dep. to move round, be round about, δηίων while the enemy are about the town, Il.
of Time, περιπλομένου δ’ ἐνιαυτοῦ as the year went round, passed, Od., Hes.; περιπλομένων ἐνιαυτῶν Od.; πέντε π. ἐνιαυτούς during five revolving years, Il.

sense.gloss: around, round about with gen., dat., and acc.

entry.sense: prep. with gen., dat., and acc.: Radical sense, round about, all round, whereas ἀμφί properly means on both sides.
WITH GENITIVE:
of Place, round about, around, Lat. circum, Od.
about, near, ἑσδόμεναι περὶ σεῖο Mosch.
Causal, to denote the object about or for which one does something:
with Verbs of fighting or contending, μάχεσθαι περὶ πτόλιος Il.; περὶ Πατρόκλοιο θανόντος Id.; so, τρέχειν περὶ ἑωυτοῦ, περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς Hdt.
about, for, on account of, μερμηρίζειν περί τινος Il.; φροντίζειν περί τινος Hdt.
with Verbs of hearing, knowing, speaking, about, concerning, Lat. circa, de, περὶ νόστου ἄκουσα Od., etc.
rather of the motive, than the object, περὶ ἔριδος μάρνασθαι to fight for very enmity, Il.; περὶ τῶνδε for these reasons, Id.
about, as to, in reference to, οὕτως ἔσχε περὶ τοῦ πρήγματος τούτου Hdt.; so, τὰ περί τινος his circumstances, Thuc.:—also without the Art., ἀριθμοῦ πέρι as to number, Hdt.

like Lat. prae, before, above, beyond, περὶ πάντων ἔμμεναι ἄλλων Il.; τετιμῆσθαι περὶ πάντων Id.; κρατερὸς περὶ πάντων Hom.: in this sense, divided from its gen., περὶ φρένας ἔμμεναι ἄλλων in understanding to be beyond them, Il.
to denote value, περὶ πολλοῦ ἐστὶν ἡμῖν it is worth much to us, Hdt.; περὶ πολλοῦ ποιεῖσθαί τι to reckon a thing for, i. e. worth, much, Lat. magni facere, Id.; περὶ πλείστου ἡγεῖσθαι Thuc.
WITH DATIVE:

of Place, round about, around, of close-fitting dresses, armour, etc., ἔνδυνε περὶ στήθεσσι χιτῶνα Il.; κνημῖδας περὶ κνήμῃσιν ἔθηκεν Id.; περὶ δ’ ἔγχεϊ . . καμεῖται will grow weary by grasping the spear, Id.; περὶ δουρὶ πεπαρμένος spitted upon it, transfixed by it, Id.; πεπτῶς περὶ ξίφει Soph.
of a warrior, standing over or going round a dead comrade so as to defend him (v. ἀμφιβαίνω, περιβαίνω); Αἴας περὶ Πατρόκλῳ βεβήκει Il.
Causal, much like περί c. gen., of an object for or about which one struggles, μαχήσασθαι περὶ δαιτί Od.; περὶ τοῖς φιλτάτοις κυβεύειν Plat.
so also with Verbs denoting fear, ἔδδεισεν δὲ περὶ ξανθῷ Μενελάῳ Il.; δεῖσαι περὶ τῷ χωρίῳ Thuc.

generally, of the cause or occasion, for, on account of, by reason of, Lat. prae, μὴ περὶ Μαρδονίῳ πταίσῃ ἡ Ἑλλάς Hdt.; περὶ σφίσιν αὐτοῖς πταίειν Thuc.:—in Poets also, περὶ δείματι for fear, Pind.; περὶ τάρβει, περὶ φόβῳ Aesch.
WITH ACCUSATIVE:

of Place, properly referring to the object round about which motion takes place, περὶ βόθρον ἐφοίτων came flocking round the pit, Od.; ἄστυ πέρι διώκειν Il.:—hence, near, ἑστάμεναι περὶ τοῖχον Il.; οἳ περὶ Πηνειὸν ναίεσκον Id.; περὶ τὴν κρήνην somewhere near it, Plat.; ἡ περὶ Λέσβον ναυμαχία the sea-fight off Lesbos, Xen.

of persons who are about one, οἱ περί τινα a person's suite, attendants, associates, οἱ περὶ τὸν Πείσανδρον πρέσβεις Thuc.; οἱ περὶ Ἡράκλειτον his school, Plat.; οἱ περὶ Ἀρχίαν πολέμαρχοι Archias and his colleagues, Xen.:—later, οἱ περί τινα periphr. for the person himself, Plut.
of the object about which one is occupied or concerned, περὶ δόρπα πονεῖσθαι Hom.; εἶναι or γίγνεσθαι περί τι Thuc., etc.; ὁ περὶ τὸν ἵππον the groom, Xen.
denoting motion about or in a place, περὶ νῆσον ἀλώμενοι wandering about the island, Od.; χρονίζειν περὶ Αἴγυπτον Hdt.

about, in the case of, τὰ περὶ τὴν Αἴγυπτον γεγονότα Hdt.; εὐσεβεῖν περὶ θεούς Plat.: —also without a Verb, about, in respect of, in regard to, πονηρὸς περὶ τὸ σῶμα Plat.; ἀκόλαστος περὶ ταῦτα Aeschin.; τὰ περὶ τὰς ναῦς naval affairs, Thuc.; τὰ περὶ τοὺς θεούς Xen., etc.
of Time, περὶ λύχνων ἁφάς about the time of lamp-lighting, Hdt.; περὶ μέσας νύκτας about midnight, Xen.; περὶ ἡλίου δυσμάς Id.
of numbers loosely given, περὶ ἑβδομήκοντα about seventy, Thuc.
POSITION: περί may follow its Subst., when it suffers anastrophe, ἥν πέρι, ἄστυ πέρι.
absol., as ADV., around, about, also near, by, Hom.
before or above others, in which case it commonly suffers anastrophe, Τυδείδη, πέρι μέν σε τίον Δαναοί Il.; πέρι κέρδεα οἶδεν Od.
περὶ κῆρι very much in heart, right heartily, περὶ κῆρι φιλεῖν Il.; περὶ κῆρι χολοῦσθαι Id.; so, περὶ σθένεϊ Id.
strengthd. περὶ πρό, where also περί recovers its accent, Id.
IN COMPOS. all its chief senses recur:
all round, as in περιβάλλω, περιβλέπω, περιέχω.
of return to the same point, about, as in περιάγω, περιβαίνω, περιστρέφω.
above, before, as in περιγίγνομαι, περιτοξεύω: also beyond measure, very, exceedingly, as in περικαλλής, περιδείδω, like Lat. per- in permultus, pergratus.
rarely = ἀμφί, as in περιδέξιος.
PROSODY:—though ι in περί is short, περί does not suffer elision. The exceptions to this rule are few.
to announce by messages sent round, Thuc.
absol. to send or carry a message round, Hdt.

c. dat. pers. et inf. to send round orders for people to do something, περιήγγελλον ταῖς πόλεσι στρατιὰν παρασκευάζεσθαι Thuc., etc.; with the inf. omitted, ναῦς περιήγγελλον, Lat. imperabant naves, Id.
to go round and collect money:—in Mid. to do so for oneself, Plat.
sent round: neut. pl. as adv. by sending round, Aesch.
to send round from one place to another, dispatch in all directions, Hdt., Thuc.

of bread, to bake all over, Lat. obcrustare: metaph. to crust or cover over, cook up, Ar.; π. ἀβλαβῶς to cover the men without hurting them, Plut.:—Pass., ῥηματίοις περιπεφθείς (aor1 part.) cajoled by words, Ar.
to spread or stretch around, χέρα τινί Eur.; π. φοινικίδας to spread them out, Aeschin.:— Pass., περιπέπταται ὑγρὸς ἄκανθος is spread round, Theocr.
spread round or over, Ar.
a turning right about, i. e. a sudden change of fortune, such as that on which the plot in a Tragedy hinges, Arist.
falling round, ἀμφὶ μέσσῃ προσκείμενος π. lying with his arms clasped round her waist, Soph.
wrapt in, πέπλοισι Aesch.
ἔγχος π. the sword round which (i. e. on which) he has fallen, Soph.
falling in with danger, etc., c. dat., Dem.; π. γενέσθαι τῇ αἰτίᾳ to become liable to . . , Plut.
changing suddenly, περιπετέα πρήγματα a sudden reverse, Hdt.; π. τύχαι Eur.
Dep.: to fly around, Ar.
very sharp, keen or painful, Il.
to fix round, to make a fence round, c. acc. loci, Pind.:—Pass., with perf. act. περιπέπηγα, to be fixed around, Plut.:—Pass., τὰ ὑποδήματα π. are frozen on the feet, Xen.
to leap round or upon, Luc.
a congealing round, Strab.
Pass. to be filled full, Xen.
to set on fire round about; imperf. περιεπίμπρα Xen.; 3rd pl. -επίμπρασαν Thuc.
to fall around, so as to embrace, τινί Xen.
to fall around, i. e. upon, a weapon, τῷ ξίφει Ar.
c. dat. to fall in with, Hdt., Xen.; of ships meeting by chance at sea, Hdt., Thuc.
to fall foul of other ships, Hdt.; περὶ ἀλλήλας of one another, Id.; also, π. περὶ τόπον to be wrecked on a place, Id.

metaph. to fall in with, fall into, c. dat., π. ἀδίκοισι γνώμῃσι to encounter unjust judgments, Id.; π. δουλοσύνῃ Id.; αἰσχρᾷ τύχῃ Eur.; but, ἑωυτῷ περιπίπτειν to be caught in one's own snare, Hdt.; so, τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ λόγοις περιπίπτειν Aeschin.
to change suddenly, Polyb.
to fall on one side, Plut.
περιπίτνω poet. for περιπίπτω
c. acc., καρδίαν π. to come over or upon the heart, Aesch.
Pass. to wander about a country, c. acc., Hdt.: metaph. to float round about one, as the lion's skin round Hercules, Pind.
absol. to wander about, ταῦτα π. to be in this state of uncertainty, Xen.
to plaster one thing over another, form as a mould or cast round, c. dat., Plat., etc.
intertwining, crossing, of the feet of dancers, Theocr.
to twine or enfold round:—Pass. to fold oneself round, c. dat., ἱστῷ περιπλεχθείς Od.; absol., δίκτυον εὖ μάλα περιπλεκόμενον close folding, Xen.
to complicate, entangle, Luc.
to wrap up in words, Aeschin.
inflammation of the lungs, Plat., Luc.
covering the side, Eur.
to sail or swim round, absol., Hdt., etc.; ἀνὴρ πολλὰ περιπεπλευκώς a man of many voyages, Ar.; c. acc., π. Λιβύην, Πελοπόννησον, etc., Hdt., Thuc., etc.
c. gen. quite full of a thing, Thuc., etc.: c. dat. filled with a thing, Anth.
absol. supernumerary, spare, Xen.
very full of people, Od.
very large, Plut.; comp. -έστερος, Luc.
crossed, Luc.
Dep. to put the legs round or across.
a twining round, entanglement, intricacy, Eur.
entwined, Anth.
a sailing round a place, c. gen., Hdt.; περὶ τόπον Thuc.
the account of a coasting voyage, Luc.
to wash clean, scour well, Dem.
to breathe round or over a place, c. acc., Pind.
sailing round, Anth.
pass. that may be sailed round, Thuc.
much-beloved, Luc.
to make to remain over and above, to keep safe, preserve, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
of money, to save up, lay by, Xen.
to put round or upon, procure, τὴν δυναστείαν ἑαυτοῖς Aeschin.; π. τὰ πράγματα εἰς αὑτούς to get things into their own hands, Thuc.
Mid. to keep or save for oneself, Hdt., etc.:— to compass, acquire, obtain, Thuc., Xen.: —absol. to make gain, Xen.
a keeping safe, preservation, NTest.
(from Mid.) a gaining possession of, acquisition, obtaining, Id.
a possession, Id.
variegated or spotted all over, Xen.
a superintendent of police, Thuc.
to go round or about, wander about, Soph., Eur.
c. acc. loci, to traverse, Plat.; π. στρατόν to prowl about it, Eur.
at Athens, περιπολεῖν τὴν χώραν to patrol the country (v. περίπολος), Xen.
a station for περίπολοι, a guard-house, Thuc.
lying round a place, c. gen., Strab.
going the rounds, patrolling: hence, as Subst.,
a watchman, patrol, Plut., etc.:—at Athens, the περίπολοι were young citizens between 18 and 20, who formed a sort of patrol to guard the frontier, Ar., Thuc.
generally, an attendant, follower, as fem., Soph.
very rascally, as a pun on περιφόρητος, Ar.
Dep. to travel or go about a place, c. acc., Polyb.
περιπορφῠρό-σημος παῖς, Lat. puer praetextatus, Anth.
to hover about, Soph.
edged with purple, π. ἐσθής a robe with a purple border, the Roman toga praetextata or laticlavia, Polyb., etc.
very much, especially, Il.
Pass. to be poured all round, in aor. 1 part., ἔρος θυμὸν περιπροχῠθείς love rushing in a flood over his heart, Il.
to stumble upon, τινί Plut.
to strip off the husk:—perf. pass. part. περιεπτισμένοι free from the chaff, clean winnowed, Ar.
anything folded round, a covering, Eur.
an embracing, Plut.
to enfold, enwrap in a thing, τινά τινι Soph.; πέπλοι περιπτύσσοντες δέμας Eur.; π. γόνυ, δέμας to clasp, embrace it, Id.
as military term, to outflank, Xen.
to fold round, π. χέρας to fold the arms round another, Eur.
something which enfolds, τειχέων περιπτυχαί enfolding walls, Eur.; δόμων Ar.; Ἀχαιῶν ναύλοχοι π. their naval cloak or fence, Eur.
an enfolding, embracing, Id.; ἐν ἡλίου περιπτυχαῖς in all that the sun embraces, i. e. all the world, Id.
folded round, Soph.
φασγάνῳ π. fallen around (i. e. upon) his sword, Id.
a calamity, Plat.
to fear greatly, Anth.
known all round about, Anth.
torn or broken all round, Anth.
to besprinkle all round, esp. in sacred rites:—Mid. to purify oneself, Theophr., Plut.
an utensil for besprinkling, or a vessel for lustral water, Lat. aspergillum, Hdt.
περιρραντήρια ἀγορᾶς the parts of the forum sprinkled with lustral water, Lex ap. Aeschin.
c. acc. to flow round, τὸν δ’ αἷμα περίρρεε Od.; νῆσον π. ὁ Νεῖλος Hdt., etc.:—Pass. to be surrounded by water, Xen.
to slip away on all sides, ἡ ἀσπὶς περιερρύη εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν slipped off his arm into the sea, Thuc.; [αἱ πέδαι] αὐτόμαται π. Xen.
to overflow on all sides, σοὶ περιρρείτω βίος may thy means of living abound, Soph.; οὐδενὸς περιρρέοντος being superfluous, Plut.:—Pass. to be all dripping, ἱδρῶτι with sweat, Id.
of clothes, to rend from round one, to rend and tear off, Dem.:—Mid., περιερρήξατο τοὺς πέπλους tore off his own garments, Plut.:—Pass. to be torn off, Aesch.

to make a stream break or divide round a piece of land, [Βούσιρις] τὸν Νεῖλον περὶ τὴν χώραν περιέρρηξε Isocr.: Pass., κατὰ τὸ ὀξὺ τοῦ Δέλτα περιρρήγνυται ὁ Νεῖλος at the apex of the Delta the Nile is broken round it, i. e. breaks into several branches, Hdt.
to break a thing round or on another, to wreck, τὸ σκαφίδιον πρὸς πέτραν Luc.
doubled round or over a thing, c. dat., περιρρηδὴς τραπέζῃ Od.
entry.etym: The deriv. of -ρήδης is uncertain; perh. from ῥέω.

entry.sense: a flowing round, Plat.
to make to spin round like a top, Plut.
surrounded with water, sea-girt, of islands, Od., Hdt., etc.
act. flowing round, c. gen., περιρρύτων ὑπὲρ ἀκαρπίστων πεδίων Σικελίας over the barren plains that flow round Sicily, i. e. the sea, Eur.
to wag the tail round, fawn upon, c. acc. or absol., Od.
Pass. to be shaken all round, ἔθειραι περισσείοντο (epic for περιεσείοντο) the hair was floating round, Il.
very august, Ar.
much-revered, Aesch.
very famous or n notable, Lat. insignis, Eur., Mosch.
to be exceeding strong, epic part. περισθενέων Od.
exceeding strong, Pind.
dry and hard all round, exceeding hard, of iron, Soph.:—metaph. obstinate, stubborn, Id.
a leg-band, i. e. an anklet or bangle, Menand., Hor.
to be seen on all sides, far-seen, conspicuous, Od.
admired, Anth.
to leap round, c. acc., Anth.
to look round, Soph.
to examine all round, observe carefully, consider well, Hdt., Thuc.: perf. part. περιεσκεμμένος, circumspect, Luc.
a sacrifice in which a puppy was sacrificed and carried about, Plut.
to rattle all round, Luc.
to chase about, π. ποτήριον to push round the wine-cup, Menand.
to run bustling round, τὰς πόλεις Ar.
Dep. to overreach, cheat, Ar.
distraction, Polyb.
to draw off from around, to strip off:—Mid. to strip oneself of, τὴν τιάραν Xen.
to strip bare, Eur.
to draw round, wheel about, of an army, Polyb.: of a horse's bit, οὐ πάνυ π. not pulling it violently round, Luc.:—Mid., περισπώμενος τὰς ὄψεις turning about one's eyes, Id.
to draw off or away, Arist.:—Pass. to be distracted or engaged in business, περί τι NTest.
to wind round, Plut.:—Mid. to surround with soldiers, Id.:—Pass., of soldiers, to form round a leader, τινί Id.; of serpents, to twine round, τινί Luc.
to be much angered, Hdt.
very hasty, π. πάθος a rash, overhasty death, Soph.
great-hearted, Theocr.
to sponge all round, Theophr.
much sought after, much desired, Luc.
surplus, abundance, NTest.
that which remains over, abundance, NTest.
to be over and above the number, c. gen., περιττεύσουσιν ἡμῶν οἱ πολέμιοι the enemy will go beyond us, outflank us, Xen.
absol. to be more than enough, remain over, Id., etc.; τοσοῦτον τῷ Περικλεῖ ἐπερίσσευε such abundance of reason had Pericles, Thuc.
in bad sense, to be superfluous, Soph.
of persons, to abound in a thing, c. dat., NTest.:—also c. gen., π. ἄρτων to have more than enough of bread, Id.
to be superior, have the advantage, Id.; π. μᾶλλον to abound more and more, Id.
Causal, to make to abound, Id.:—Pass. to be made to abound, Id.
over-talking, wordiness, Isocr.
beyond the regular number or size, prodigious, Hes.

out of the common way, extraordinary, uncommon, remarkable, signal, strange, εἴ τι περισσὸν εἰδείη σοφίης if he has any signal gift of wisdom, Theogn.; so, π. λόγος Soph.; οὐ γὰρ περισσὸν οὐδὲν οὐδ’ ἔξω λόγου πέπονθας Eur.
of persons, extraordinary, eminent, remarkable, esp. for learning, Id.
c. gen., περισσὸς ἄλλων πρός τι beyond others in a thing, Soph.; θύσει τοῦδε περισσότερα greater things than this, Anth.; περιττότερος προφήτου greater than a prophet, NTest.

more than sufficient, redundant, superfluous, Xen.; περιττὸν ἔχειν to have a surplus, Id.; c. gen., τῶν ἀρκούντων περιττά more than sufficient, Id.:—often in military sense, οἱ π. ἱππεῖς the reserve horse, Id.; π. σκηναί spare tents, Id.; τὸ π. the surplus, residue, Id.
in bad sense, superfluous, Trag.
excessive, extravagant, περισσὰ μηχανᾶσθαι to commit extravagancies, Hdt.; περισσὰ δρᾶν, πράσσειν to be over busy, Soph.
of persons, extravagant, over-curious, περισσὸς καὶ φρονῶν μέγα Eur.; π. ἐν τοῖς λόγοις Δημοσθένης Aeschin.
in Arithmetic, ἀριθμὸς περιττός is an odd, uneven number, opp. to ἄρτιος, Plat., etc.
adv. περισσῶς, extraordinarily, exceedingly, Hdt., Eur.; π. παῖδας ἐκδιδάσκεσθαι to have them educated overmuch, Eur.; also περισσά, Pind., Eur.
in a peculiar manner, remarkably, περισσότερον τῶν ἄλλων θάψαι τινά more sumptuously, Hdt.
often with a negat., οὐδὲν περισσότερον τῶν ἄλλων Plat.
τὰ περισσά in vain, Anth.
ἐκ περιττοῦ as adv. superfluously, uselessly, Plat.

entry.note: περισσότης, later attic περιττ-, ητος, ἡ,
entry.sense: superfluity, excess, Isocr.
over-wise, Aesch.
standing round about, Il., Hdt., attic
Pass. to be bedewed all round, Anth.
a standing round, a crowd standing round, Lat. corona, Theophr., etc.
circumstances, a state of affairs, Polyb.:—in bad sense, κατὰ τὰς π. in critical times, Id.
outward pomp and circumstance, Id.
surrounded and admired by the crowd, Isocr.
to fence about with a palisade, to entrench, Thuc.:—Mid., περισταυρωσάμενοι having entrenched themselves, Xen.
to go round about, c. acc., Od.
to dress, clothe, wrap up, Pind., Plut.; ἔπηξα δ’ αὐτὸν εὖ περιστείλας I planted the sword having wrapt it well with earth, i. e. planted it firmly, Soph.
to dress or lay out a corpse, Lat. componere, Od., Hdt., attic: simply, to bury, Plat.
metaph. to wrap up, cloak, cover, τἄδικ’ εὖ π. Eur.:—Mid., τὰ σὰ περιστέλλου κακά Id.
to take care of, protect, defend, Hdt., Soph.; π. τοὺς νόμους to maintain the laws, Hdt.; τὰ πάτρια Dem.; π. ἀοιδάν to uphold minstrelsy, Pind.
Mid. to lament vehemently, Plut.
περιστεναχίζομαι Mid. to echo all round, Od.
περιστοναχίζω to groan all round, Hes.
to make narrow, compress: Pass., περιστένεται δέ τε γαστήρ, of wolves, Il.
to sound round about, c. acc., Hhymn.
to bemoan, Luc.
the common pigeon or dove, Hdt., Soph., etc.
a dovecote, Plat.: περιστερῶν, Aesop.
to enwreathe, encircle, Ar.:— Pass., πῖλοι πτεροῖσι περιεστεφανωμένοι Hdt.; οὔρεσι περιεστεφάνωται Θεσσαλίη Id.
wreathed, crowned, ἀνθέων π. with a crown of flowers, Soph.
act. twining, encircling, κισσός Eur.
to enwreathe, surround, νεφέεσσι περιστέφει οὐρανὸν Ζεύς Od.
