of persons, to promote or prefer to honour, Plut.
perf. pass. with mid. sense, προῆκται παῖδας οὕτω ὥστε . . , has had them brought up in such a way that . . , Dem.; but also in pass. sense, τοῖς ἔθεσι προηγμένοι Arist.
intr. to lead the way, go before, advance, Plat., Xen., etc.:—an acc. added, to go before one, NTest.
the trade of a προαγωγός, pandering, Xen., Aeschin.
to prostitute, Lex ap. Aeschin.
metaph., πρ. ἑαυτὸν ὀφθαλμοῖς Ar.
a leading on, promotion, rank, eminence, Polyb.
one who leads on: a pander, pimp, procurer, Ar., Aeschin.
a negotiator, Xen.
one who fights for another, a champion, Plut.
to be the first in wronging:— Pass. to be wronged before or first, Dem., Aeschin.
to sing before, prelude, Aeschin.
Dep.:— to owe one special respect, be under obligations to one, c. dat., Hdt.
a preliminary contest, prelude, Ar., Plat.:— the preparation for a festival, Aeschin.
Dep.:— to fight before, ἐξ ὧν προηγώνισθε = ἐξ ἀγωνῶν οὓς προηγώνισθε, from the contests which you have before had, Thuc.:—perf. also in pass. sense, οἱ προηγωνισμένοι ἀγῶνες Plut.
to fight for or in defence of another, Id.
a choosing one thing before another, an act of deliberate choice, a purpose, resolution, Plat., etc.:— κατὰ προαίρεσιν on purpose, as one will, Arist.
a purpose, plan, or scope of action, a course of life, principle of action, Dem.
in political language, a deliberate course of action, a policy, Id.:—also, a mode of government, such as an oligarchy, Id.; in pl., τὰς κοινὰς πρ. your public principles, your general policy, Id.
a department of government, Id.
a political party, Id.
one must choose, prefer, Plat.
inclined to prefer, deliberately choosing a thing, c. gen., Arist.
absol. purposing, intentional, Id.
deliberately chosen, purposed, Arist.
to bring forth, produce from one's stores, Thuc., Theophr.
to take away first, Babr.
mostly in Mid., fut. -αιρήσομαι: aor2 -ειλόμην: perf. pass. (in mid. sense) -ῄρημαι:— to take away first for oneself, remove out of one's way, Plat.
to choose before or sooner than something else, prefer, τί τινος or τι πρό τινος Id.; τι ἀντί τινος Xen.
c. inf. to prefer to do, Id.: to purpose or propose to do, Dem.
Dep. to perceive or observe beforehand, Thuc., Xen.; πρ. τινος to become aware of a thing beforehand, Thuc.
Dep. to accuse beforehand, τινα εἶναι NTest.
Pass. to be thrown like a javelin before, Luc.
to hear beforehand, Hdt., attic
springing forward, i. e. overhanging, abrupt, Il.
metaph. = προπετής:— comp. adv., προαλέστερον more eagerly, Strab.
Pass: to be convicted beforehand, Dem.
to fail or sin before, NTest.
Mid. to defend oneself or take measures for defence beforehand, Thuc.: —c. acc. to take such measures against others, Id.
to ascend before, so as to preoccupy, τὸν λόφον Thuc.
Mid. to say or sing by way of prelude, Ar.
to lead up before:—Pass. to put to sea before, Thuc.
to take away before, Dem.: to refute by anticipation, Arist.
to use up, spend before: Pass., perf. -ανῃσίμωμαι, ionic -αναισίμωμαι, ἐν τῷ προαναισιμωμένῳ χρόνῳ πρότερον ἢ ἐμὲ γενέσθαι in times past before I was born, Hdt.
to stir up before, Plut.
absol. to make previous movements, Arist.
to examine before, of the measures to be submitted to the vote of the people, Arist.
to use up or spend before, Thuc., Dem.:—Pass. to throw away one's life before, Thuc.
to carry off or arrest beforehand, Dem.; πρ. τῆς παρασκευῆς = ἀναρπάζειν πρὸ τῆς παρασκευῆς, Plut.
to check beforehand, Plut.
to say by way of preface, Plut.
a former departure, Thuc.
to accomplish before, Xen.
to give in before, Isocr.
to go forth to meet, Thuc.
to meet beforehand, Id.
to go away first, Luc.
to give in or fail before, Isocr.; perf. προαπείρηκα Id.
Dep.: to go away before, Thuc., Dem.
Pass. to begin hostilities before, Dem.
to prove before, Isocr.
to die before or first, Hdt., Plat.; of a coward, πρ. ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου, i. e. before his real death, Xen.
to bewail beforehand, Plut.
to grow tired before the end, give up the task of doing, c. inf., Plat.; c. gen., Plut.
to be allotted beforehand, Luc.
to kill beforehand, Luc.
to enjoy beforehand, Plut.
intr. to fail before, i. e. in comparison of, c. gen., Antipho.
Pass.:— to be first destroyed, to perish before or first, Thuc.; μὴ ἡ ψυχὴ προαπολλύηται (as if from -απολλύω) Plat.
to send away before, Thuc.:— Mid., Xen.
to send away, dispatch beforehand, or in advance, Thuc.:—Pass. to be sent in advance, Id.; but, προαποσταλῆναί τινος = ἀποσταλῆναι πρό τινος, Id.
to slay before, Luc.
Mid. to turn aside before, leave off, c. part., προαποτρέπομαι διώκων Xen.
to declare before:—Mid., πρ. τὴν γνώμην to declare one's opinion before, Plat.
to go away before, Thuc.
to snatch away before, Luc.; metaph., πρ. τὸ λεγόμενον to snap at a conclusion, anticipate hastily, Plat.
to train or exercise before, Isocr.
the space immediately in front of or round a town, a suburb, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
to declare before or first, Ar., in the contr. inf. πρωυδᾶν.
to play a prelude on the flute, Arist.
a prelude on the flute, Arist.
Dep. to relate before, Hdt.
Dep. to arrive first, Thuc.
Pass., with perf. and aor2 act.:— to fall off or revolt before, Thuc.
to leave off or desist before, Plat.
as one walks, Hes.; πρ. ἔξαγε lead them out onward, Ar.

entry.note: fut. -βήσομαι perf. -βέβηκα attic aor.2 προὔβην epic part. προβιβάς
entry.sense: to step on, step forward, advance, Hom., etc.:—as a mark of Time, ἄστρα προβέβηκε they are far gone in heaven, i. e. it is past midnight, Il.; ἡ νὺξ προβαίνει the night is wearing fast, Xen.; then of Time itself, τοῦ χρόνου προβαίνοντος as time went on, Hdt.; so, προβαίνοντος τοῦ ἔργου, τοῦ πολέμου Id.; and of persons, τοὺς προβεβηκότας τῇ ἡλικίᾳ advanced in age, Lys., etc.

metaph. of narrative, argument, events, προβήσομαι ἐς τὸ πρόσω τοῦ λόγου Hdt.; πρ. ἐπ’ ἔσχατον θράσους Soph.; τὸ τῆς τύχης ἀφανὲς οἷ προβήσεται Eur.; πρ. πόρρω μοχθηρίας to be far gone in knavery, Xen.; πρ. εἰς τοῦτο ἔχθρας Dem.
to advance, proceed, προέβαινε τὸ ἔθνος ἄρχον the nation kept making advances in dominion, kept extending its sway, Hdt.; μὴ προβαίη μεῖζον ἢ τὸ νῦν κακόν lest it creep on, increase, Eur.
to go before, i. e. to be before or superior to another, c. gen., προβέβηκας ἁπάντων Il.; Τρηχῖνος προβέβηκε he was set over, i. e. ruled, Trachis, Hes.
c. acc. rei, to overstep, τέρμα προβάς (for ὑπερβάς) Pind.
in Poets, πόδα πρ. to advance the foot, Theogn.; τὸν πόδα Ar.; προβὰς κῶλον, ἀρβύλαν προβάς Eur.; v. βαίνω A. II. 3.
Causal, in fut. act., to put forward, advance, τίς τρόπος ἄνδρα προβάσει [ᾱ]; Pind.
of Bacchus, leader of the Bacchanals, Eur.

entry.note: fut. -βᾰλῶ perf. -βέβληκα aor2 προέβᾰλον attic προὔβαλον ionic προβάλεσκον
entry.sense: to throw before, throw or toss to, Lat. projicere, Νότος Βορέῃ προβάλεσκε [σχεδίην] Od.; τοὺς μαζοὺς κυσὶ προέβαλε Hdt.
to put forward, i. e. to begin, ἔριδα προβαλόντες Il.
to put forward as a defence or plea, Soph., Eur.:—Pass., Thuc.
to propose for an office, Andoc.
to propose a problem, riddle (cf. πρόβλημα IV), Ar., etc.
to put forth beyond, τί τινος Soph.
πρ. ἑαυτόν to give oneself up for lost, Lat. spem abjicere, Hdt.; so, πρ. ἐμαυτὸν εἰς δεινὰς ἀράς Soph.
Mid. with perf. pass. (which is used also in pass. sense):— to throw or toss before one, οὐλοχύτας προβάλοντο Hom.: to throw away, expose, Soph.
to lay before or first, θεμείλιά τε προβάλοντο Il.
to set before oneself, propose to oneself, ἔργον Hes.
to propose for election, Lat. designare, Hdt., attic:— Pass. to be so proposed, Hdt.
to throw beyond, beat in throwing; and so, to surpass, excel, c. gen. pers. et dat. rei, ἐγὼ δέ κε σεῖο νοήματί γε προβαλοίμην Il.

to hold before oneself, τὼ χεῖρε Ar.; πρ. τὰ ὅπλα, i. e. to present arms, whether for offensive or defensive purposes, Xen.;—so, in perf. pass., κοντὸν προβεβλημένος having a pole advanced, with levelled pole, Luc.; also, προβεβλημένοι τοὺς θωρακοφόρους having them to cover one in front, Xen.:—absol. to stand in front, stand on the defensive, Id.; προαίρεσις προβεβλημένη a defensive system, Dem.:— c. gen., προβεβλῆσθαί τινος to stand before, shield him, Id.
metaph. to put forward, Id.:— to bring forward or cite in defence, Plat.: to cite as an example, Hdt.:— to use as an excuse or pretext, Thuc.:— προβέβληνται (in mid. sense), Id.
as attic law-term, to present or accuse a person before the Ecclesia by the process called προβολή (v. προβολή IV); ὁ προβαλλόμενος the prosecutor in a προβολή, Dem.:—Pass. to be accused, Xen.
to torture before, Luc.
property in cattle (πρόβατα), cattle, Od.
a keeping of sheep, a shepherd's life, Plut.
property in cattle, a flock of sheep, like the Homeric πρόβασις, Strab.
of or for cattle:— ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη) the art of breeding or keeping sheep, Lat. pecuaria, Xen.
to watch sheep, be a shepherd, Anth.
of sheep or goats:— ἡ προβατικὴ (sc. πύλη) the sheep-gate, NTest.
a little sheep, Lat. ovicula, Ar., Plat.; cf. πρόβατον.
a good judge of sheep: metaph. a good judge of character, Aesch.
a retailer of sheep, Plut.

mostly in pl. πρόβατα, properly, anything that walks forward; in Hom. generally of cattle, flocks and herds; in Hdt. and Pind. also of horses; τὰ λεπτὰ τῶν προβάτων small cattle, i. e. sheep and goats, Hdt.; but in attic always of sheep, Ar., Thuc.
proverb. of stupid, lazy people, πρόβατ’ ἄλλως a set of sheep, Ar.; so, προβατίου βίος, i. e. a lazy do-nothing life, Id.
a sheep-dealer, Ar.

entry.etym: an isolated poet. perf. 2 (προ-βούλομαι does not occur)
entry.sense: to prefer one to another, τινά τινος Il.
a step forward, Ar.
Dep. to force a measure through, Aeschin.
to make step forward, lead forward, lead on, τινά Soph., Ar., etc.:— to lead on, induce, λόγῳ τινὰ πρ. Xen.
to push forward, advance, to exalt, τὴν πατρίδα Polyb.
to teach beforehand, τινά τι LXX.:— Pass., prob. in NTest.
to foresee: so in Mid., NTest.
anything projecting, a headland, promontory, Soph.
anything put before one, a fence, barrier, screen, Hdt., attic; πρ. σώματος, of a shield, Aesch.; προβλήματα ἵππων χαλκᾶ the brasen armour of horses, Xen.
c. gen. a defence against a thing, πέτρων Aesch.; χείματος Eur.; κακῶν Ar.
πρ. φόβου ἢ αἰδοῦς ἔχειν to have fear or shame as a defence, Soph.
anything put forward as an excuse or screen, Dem.; so, πρ. λαβεῖν τινά (as we say) to make a stalking horse of him, Soph.
that which is proposed, a task, business, Eur.
a problem in Geometry, Plat.
problematical, Plut.

sic.seg: problhfailing on lembuf [] | /s, h=tos, o(, h(,

entry.sense: forestretching, jutting, Hom.: προβλῆτες, without Subst., forelands, headlands, Soph.
thrown forth, tossed away, Lat. projectus, Soph.
to go or come forth, to go out of the house, Hom.
to shout before, cry aloud, Il., Soph.
to hasten to aid before, προβωθῆσαι ἐς τὴν Βοιωτίην Hdt.
held out before one, levelled, couched, of a spear, Theocr.: ὁ πρ., alone, a spear, ap. Hdt.

a putting forward, esp. of a weapon for defence, τὰ δόρατα εἰς προβολὴν καθιέναι to bring the spears to the rest, Xen.; ἐν προβολῇ θέσθαι ξίφος to bring it to the guard, Anth.; ἐν προβολῇ ἑστάναι to stand with spear in rest, Plut.:—of a pugilist, a lunging out with the fist, Theocr.
a projection, a jutting rock, foreland or tongue of land, Soph.; Νειλόρυτος πρ. i. e. the Delta of the Nile, Anth.
a thing held before one as a defence, a fence, screen, bulwark, Xen.: c. gen. a defence against, δείματος καὶ βελέων Soph.; θανάτου Eur.
a legal process in which the plaintiff appealed to the Ecclesia to support his suit before bringing it into court, pl. προβολαί, Xen., Dem., etc.
a boar-spear, Xen.
anything that projects:
a jutting rock, foreland, Od.:—metaph. a rock in the path, an obstacle, Dem.; λιμένας προβόλων ἐμπλῆσαι Id.; πρόβολοι ξύλων projecting barriers of wood, Plut.
a defence, bulwark, Xen.: of a person, a shield, guardian, Ar.
a hunting-spear, Hdt.; cf. προβόλαιος.
a means of providing food: an elephant's proboscis, Arist.
an assistant herdsman, Hdt.
at Athens, a preliminary order of the senate, Dem., Aeschin.
to contrive or concert measures before, Thuc.:—Mid. to debate or consider first, Hdt., etc.

of the Senate at Athens, to frame or pass a προβούλευμα, Xen., Dem.; of magistrates, to propose decrees, Thuc.:—impers. in Pass., τῇ βουλῇ προβεβούλευται, c. acc. et inf., it has been decreed that, Xen.
to award by a decree of this kind, Dem.
to have the chief voice in the senate and in passing decrees, Xen.
πρ. τινός to deliberate for one, provide for his interest, Ar., Xen.
forethought, ἐκ προβούλης of malice aforethought, Antipho.
in Aesch., πρ. Ἄτης, = πρόβουλος παῖς Ἄτης, the fore-counselling child of Ate.
debating beforehand:—pl. πρόβουλοι,
commissioners to examine measures before they were proposed to the people, Ar., etc.
deputies of the Ionian states at the Panionium, Hdt.: also the deputies appointed by the Western Greeks to consult on the mode of meeting Xerxes, Hdt.
at Athens, a committee of Ten, appointed before the constitution of the 400, Ar.
πρ. λύχνον to push up the wick of a lamp, to trim it, Ar.
before the altar, σφαγαί Eur.: προβώμια, ων, τά, a space in front of an altar, Id.
(sub. ἑαυτόν) to prepare oneself for tickling, Arist.
a false paunch worn by actors, Luc.
fat-paunch, Anth.
with prominent chin, long-chinned, Theocr.
born before, primaeval, Soph.: —comp. προγενέστερος earlier in birth, i. e. older, Hom.; οἱ πρ. our predecessors, Arist.:—Sup. προγενέστατος, eldest-born, Hhymn.
in pl. forefathers, Eur.

entry.note: ionic and later -γίνομαι fut. -γενήσομαι aor2 -προὐγενόμην perf. προγέγονα and -γεγένημαι
entry.sense: Dep. to come forwards, τάχα προγένοντο quickly they came in sight, Il.
to be born before, exist before, Hdt.; οἱ προγεγονότες θεοί Id.; οἱ πρ. ἄνθρωποι former men, and οἱ προγεγενημένοι Xen.
of events and the like, ταῦτά μοι προὐγεγόνει Plat.; τὰ προγεγενημένα things of old time, Thuc.; προγεγενημένοι πόλεμοι, καιροί Id.

entry.note: ionic and later -γινώσκω fut. -γνώσομαι aor2 -έγνων epic inf. -γνώμεναι
entry.sense: to know, perceive, learn, or understand beforehand, Hhymn., Plat., etc.; absol., Eur.
to foreknow, NTest.
to judge beforehand, Thuc.; to provide, Xen.
a perceiving beforehand, Luc.: in medicine, prognosis of diseases, Anth.

a forefather, ancestor, Hdt., attic; οἱ ἄνωθεν πρ. Plat.; ἐκ προγόνων, Lat. antiquitus, Id.:— also of gods who are the authors or founders of a race; Ζεῦ πρόγονε Eur.; θεοὶ πρόγονοι Plat.:—metaph., πόνοι πρόγονοι πόνων troubles parents of troubles, Soph.
a child by a former marriage, i. e. one's step-son, Lat. privignus, Eur.: fem. a stepdaughter, Plut.
a public proclamation or notice, programm, Dem.
a public notice, Xen.:—esp. a sale of confiscated property, Lat. proscriptio, Strab.
to write before or first, Thuc.
to give public notice of anything, Ar., Dem.:—also to summon by public notice, ἐκκλησίαν Aeschin.:—Pass. to be set forth publicly, NTest.
= Lat. proscribere, Plut.
to write at the head of a list, Id.
to exercise or train beforehand, Luc.

entry.etym: aor2 pass. inf. with act. sense from *προδάω
entry.sense: to know beforehand, part. προδαείς Od.
to lend before or first, Plut.
to spend beforehand, Luc.
to fear prematurely, Soph.
before evening, Theocr.
to shew by way of example, Hdt.; τὸν ζωστῆρα προδέξας having pointed out [the use of] the girdle, Id.
absol. to tell first, Aesch.
to foreshew what is about to happen, Hdt., etc.:—c. acc. et inf. to make known beforehand that . . , Thuc.
to point before one, σκήπτρῳ πρ. (sc. τὴν ὁδόν) to feel one's way with a stick, of a blind man, Soph.
pugilistic term, χερσὶ πρ. to make feints with the hands, make as if one was going to strike, Lat. praeludere, Theocr.:—in war, to make a demonstration, Xen.
to fear beforehand, Hdt.
a foreshewer, Hdt.
Dep. to see beforehand, Aesch.
clear or manifest beforehand, Eur., etc.:— πρόδηλον ἤδη ἦν, ὅτι . . , Xen.; so, πρόδηλα γάρ [ἐστι], ὅτι μέλλουσι Hdt.:— ἐκ προδήλου from a place in sight, Soph.: adv. -λως, Id.
to make clear beforehand, shew plainly, Thuc.
demonstration of the event, Plut.
to go across before others, τάφρον Xen.
to raise prejudices against one beforehand, τινά Thuc.:—Pass. to have prejudices raised against one, Arist.
to perceive or understand beforehand, Thuc.
to make a previous decree, Id.
preparation by diet, Luc.
Mid., with aor1 pass., to speak or converse beforehand, Isocr.
to pull in pieces or ridicule beforehand, Arist.
to ruin beforehand, Isocr.: to bribe beforehand, Dem.:—Pass., Thuc.
to have a previous difference with another, Arist.
to teach one a thing beforehand, τινά τι Soph., Ar.; πρ. τινά Plat.:—c. acc. et inf., πρ. τινὰ σοφὸν εἶναι Soph.:—Mid. to have one taught beforehand, Id.:—Pass. to learn beforehand, Thuc.
to give beforehand, pay in advance, Xen.
to give up to the enemy, deliver up, betray, Lat. prodere, Hdt.:—c. inf., ὃν σὺ προὔδωκας θανεῖν Eur.:—Pass., Hdt., Soph.
to forsake in distress, abandon, Hdt., attic:—Pass., Hdt.
absol. to play false, desert, Id., etc.; προδοῦς’ ἁλίσκεται is convicted of treachery, Soph.; πρ. πρὸς τοὺς κατιόντας to treat treasonably with them, Hdt.
with a thing as subject, to betray or fail one, Xen.:—intr. to fail, Lat. deficere, of a river that has run dry, Hdt.; of a tottering wall, Id.
with a thing as object, to betray, give up, Eur.; χάριν πρ. to be thankless, Id.:—hence, to give up as lost, bid adieu to, ἡδονάς Soph.; τὰς ἐλπίδας Ar.
Dep. to go out through before, Xen.: —metaph. to go through before, τι Aeschin.
Dep.: to work or mould beforehand, Arist.
to discover by searching, Xen.
one sent before to search, Xen.
Dep. to go through before, Xen.
Dep. to relate beforehand, premise, Hdt.
a detailing beforehand, Aeschin.
an advocate, defender, avenger, Aesch.
at Sparta, a young king's guardian, Xen.: regent, Plut.
to regulate, order, govern, manage beforehand, Dem.: Mid. in act. sense, Aeschin.
Dep. to grant beforehand:—Pass. to be granted on both sides beforehand, Arist.
to pursue further or to a distance, Thuc., Xen.

entry.note: only in perf. and plup. pass.
entry.sense: ὥσπερ προεδέδοκτο αὐτοῖς as had been before determined, Thuc.; τὰ προδεδογμένα Id.; προὐδέδοκτο ταῦτά μοι this was my former opinion, Plat.
a place where one lies in wait, lurking-place, Il.
the chamber entered immediately from the αὐλή, serving as the guests' sleeping-room, Hom.
before the house, Anth.
to judge beforehand, Plat., Arist.
a giving up, betrayal, treason, Hdt., Eur., Dem.
payment beforehand, money advanced, earnest-money, Dem.
a betrayer, traitor, Hdt., attic
one who abandons in danger, Aesch.
traitorous, Luc.
a traitress, Eur.
betrayed, Soph., Eur.
serving as a slave, of a shoe, Aesch.

entry.etym: from προδρᾰμεῖν aor2 inf. of προτρέχω
entry.sense: a running forward, a sally, sudden attack, Xen.

entry.etym: from προδρᾰμεῖν aor2 inf. of προτρέχω
entry.sense: running forward, with headlong speed, Trag.
going in advance, Hdt., Eur.:— οἱ πρ. the advanced guard, "the guides, " a corps in the Maced. army, Arr.
metaph. a precursor, Plat.
to wake up before, Arist.
Pass. to be implanted before, Polyb.
to act as president, Aeschin.; πρ. τῆς βουλῆς Dem.
the privilege of the front seats at public games, in theatres, in the public assemblies, given as an honour to ambassadors, etc., Hdt., Ar.
in concrete sense, the front seat, ἐν προεδρίῃ κατήμενος on a chair of state, Hdt.
the office of πρόεδρος (II.), Arist.
one who sits in the first place, a president, Thuc., etc.
in the Athenian ἐκκλησία, the πρυτάνεις in office were called πρόεδροι (v. πρύτανις), ap. Dem.
to stop by standing before, c. acc. et inf., προέεργε πάντας ὁδεύειν Il.
to train beforehand:—Pass. to be so trained, Xen., etc.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use, προοράω being used instead
entry.sense: to see beforehand, catch sight of, Hom., etc.; so in Mid., προϊδέσθαι Od.:—absol. to look forward, Id.
of Time, to foresee, portend, Orac. ap. Hdt., Pind.:—so in Mid., Xen., etc.
to have a care for, provide against, c. gen., ἡμέων οἰκοφθορημένων Hdt.; αὐτῶν (sc. τῶν ἀποβαινόντων) Thuc.:—so in Mid., προϊδομένους αὐτῶν Id.:— to make provision, προϊδέσθαι ὑπέρ τινος Dem.
to conjecture beforehand, Arist.
to go forward, go on, advance, Thuc., etc.
of Time, προϊόντος τοῦ χρόνου as time went on, Hdt.; so, προϊόντος Xen.; προϊούσης τῆς νυκτός Id., etc.
of persons reading, προϊὼν καὶ ἀναγιγνώσκων going on reading, Plat.
to go first, go in advance, Xen.:—c. gen. to go before or in advance of, τῆς στρατιῆς Hdt.
to go forth, Xen.
πρ. εἴς τι to pass on to, begin another thing, Id., Arist.
of an action, to go on well, succeed, Xen.
to be before, Il.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use, πρόφημι, προαγορεύω being used instead
entry.sense: to tell or state before, Plat.: to premise, Aeschin.
to proclaim or declare publicly, Lat. indicere, πόλεμόν τινι Hdt., etc.:— πρ. τινι φόνου to make proclamation of murder against him, Dem.
c. inf. to order or command before, Od., etc.; the inf. is sometimes omitted, πρ. Λυδοῖσι (sc. ποιέειν) τὰ ὁ Κροῖσος ὑπετίθετο Hdt.; πρ. ξεινίην τοῖσι Ἀκανθίοισι, like Lat. imperare frumentum, Id.
to bring in or introduce before, Dem.:—Mid. to bring in beforehand for oneself, to bring in from the country into the town, Hdt.
intr., πρ. ἑαυτοῦ to go on the stage before oneself, Arist.
Dep. to come or go in before, Dem.
to send in before, Xen.
to advance money to pay the εἰσφορά for others, Dem.
money advanced to pay the εἰσφορά for others, Dem.
Dep. to intercept before, Strab.
an introduction, preface, Polyb.
to run out before, sally from the ranks, rush on, Thuc.
to carry out beforehand, Hdt.
to collect moneys not yet due, Dem.
to send out before, Plut.
to sail out before, Plut.
to astound before, Plut., Luc.
a going beyond limits, Strab.
Mid. to set forth before or by way of preface, Polyb.
to run out before, Plut.
to scare away before, Plut., Luc.
a previous panic, Thuc.
a riding forward, Xen.

seemingly intr. (sub. ἵππον) to ride on or forward, Xen.: c. gen. to ride before one, Id.:—Pass., of Time, ὡς πρόσω τῆς νυκτὸς προελήλατο (3rd sg. plup. impers.) as the night was now far advanced, Hdt.
to hope for before, NTest.
to embark first or before, Plut.
to put in or insert before, Arist.
absol., προεμβαλλόντων ἐς τὴν γῆν τῶν κερέων the horns first striking against the ground, of the βόες ὀπισθονόμοι, which by reason of their projecting horns were obliged to graze backwards, Hdt.
of ships, to make the charge (ἐμβολή) first, Thuc.
to put in before, πρ. τινὰ εἰς ἀπέχθειαν to make one hated before, Polyb.
Dep. to begin before, NTest.
Dep. to exhibit oneself or make a demonstration before another, c. dat., Aeschin.
to proclaim, announce, Aesch., Eur.; πρ. τινὶ ὅτι . . Aesch.: c. inf., πρ. τινὰ χαίρειν I publicly bid him hail, Soph., Eur.
a dwelling in a place before, Thuc.
to set at before, τινά τινι Plut.
to converse with before, Plut., etc.; ὄψις πρ. τῆς φωνῆς his face begins to converse before he speaks, Id.
to announce beforehand, Dem.
of pugilists, to move the arms before beginning to fight: also of a speaker, Arist.
to lead or carry out first, Hdt., Thuc.
intr. to advance first, τῷ κέρᾳ with the wing, Thuc.:—so in Pass., Id.
to take out before:—Pass. to be deprived of before, τι Luc.
to dart out before, as out of the ranks in battle, Hdt.; aor1 part. προεξᾴξαντες Thuc.
to do wrong before, Isocr.
Pass., with aor2, perf., and plup. act. to rise and go out before or first, Hdt., Dem.
in a race, to start before the signal is given, Hdt.
to deceive before, Arist.
to send out before, Polyb.
a chair of state, Hdt.
to sally forth from, Thuc.
to ride out before, Plut.
π. πλοίῳ to run out in a ship before, Id.
Dep. to know well before, Aesch.
to investigate before, Eur.
an explorer sent before, Eur.
Dep. to go out before, τῷ πεζῷ with the infantry, Thuc.
to examine before, Luc.
Mid. to enjoin beforehand, Soph.
to set out or start beforehand, Xen.
Mid. to promise before, NTest.
to praise beforehand, Thuc.
to raise the hand against before: metaph. in Pass., ἡ παρασκευὴ προεπανεσείσθη it was in agitation before, Thuc.
to send forward against the enemy, Luc.,
to plot against one beforehand, τινί Thuc.:—Pass. to be the object of such plots, Id.
Pass. to be received as a guest before, Luc.
to be the first to blame, τινί Arist.
to inspect or consider before, Strab., Luc.
Dep. to know or understand beforehand, Plat., Xen.
to be the first to attack, Thuc., Plut., etc.
c. inf. to attempt beforehand, Plut.
to colonise before, Strab.
to do or work at beforehand, Hdt., Xen.:—perf. also in pass. sense, τὰ προειργασμένα former deeds, Thuc.; ἡ προειργασμένη δόξα glory won before, Xen.
to row forwards, Hom.
Mid. to search out first or before, οἱ προερευνώμενοι ἱππεῖς the videttes, Xen.

entry.note: attic contr. -ερῶ perf. προείρηκα pass. -ημαι aor1 pass. προερρήθην contr. προὐρρήθην
entry.sense: to say beforehand, Plat.:—Pass., ἐκ τῶν προειρημένων Id.; τὰ προρρηθέντα Id.; ταῦτά μοι προειρήσθω be said by way of preface, Isocr.

to order one to do a thing beforehand or publicly, τινί c. inf., Hdt.; also, πρ. τινί ὡς . . Id.:—Pass. impers., προείρητο αὐτοῖς μὴ ἐπιχειρεῖν orders had been given them not to attack, Thuc.; τὸ προειρημένον the prescribed implement, Hdt.; δεῖπνον πρ. ordered beforehand, Id.; πόλεμος προερρήθη, Lat. indictus est, Xen.
to draw on or forward, νῆα ἅλαδε προέρυσσεν drew the ship forward, by hauling her from the beach to the sea, Il.
of ships at sea, = προερέσσω, Hom.

entry.etym: like πρόειμι (which serves as the fut.)
entry.sense: Dep.
to go forward, go on, advance, Hdt., Thuc., etc.: —absol., προελθὼν ὁ κῆρυξ ἐκήρυττε Aeschin.
of Time, προελθόντος πολλοῦ χρόνου Thuc.; of persons, προεληλυθὼς τῇ ἡλικίᾳ far advanced in age, Xen.
to go on, in a story or argument, Plat.
metaph., τὰ Περσέων πρήγματα ἐς τοῦτο προελθόντα the power of the Persians having advanced to this height, Hdt.; εἰς πᾶν μοχθηρίας πρ. Dem.; εἰς τοῦτο προβέβηκεν ἔχθρας, ὥστε . . Id.
to go before or first, Xen.; πρ. τινος to go before him, Id.; later, πρ. τινα NTest.
with instr. of motion, πρ. πόδα to advance the foot, Luc.
a throwing away, Arist.
apt to throw away, giving lavishly, profuse, lavish, Xen., etc.; πρ. τινι giving lavishly to . . , Arist.:—adv. -κῶς, Id.
to get ready before:—Mid. to prepare for one's own use or purpose, Hdt.
Dep. to preach the gospel beforehand, NTest.
Dep.:— to take heed, be cautious beforehand, Dem.
Pass. to be traversed before, Strab.

entry.note: contr. προὔχω fut. -έξω aor2 -έσχον mid. -εσχόμην προὐσχόμην
entry.sense: to hold before, so as to protect another, Ar. Xen.:—Mid. to hold before oneself, hold out before one, Hom., Ar.
metaph. in Mid. to put forward, use as a pretext, Soph.; ὅπερ μάλιστα προὔχονται, μὴ ἂν γίγνεσθαι τὸν πόλεμον which is the chief reason they allege, to shew that the war would not arise, Thuc.
to hold forth, offer, Id.
to be possessed or informed of a thing beforehand, Hdt.
to have before others, τιμὴν προέξους’ τῶν ἐνδίκων shall have honour before the righteous, Soph.: absol., ὁ προέχων the first possessor, Arist.
intr. to jut out, project of headlands, towers, hills, Hom., Hdt., etc.

in running, to be the first, have the start, Il.; c. gen., προέχων τῶν ἄλλων getting before the rest, Hdt.; πρ. ἡμέρης ὁδῷ to keep ahead by a day's march, Id.; πρ. τῇ κεφαλῇ to beat by a head, in racing, Xen.;—of Time, προεῖχε [ἡ τριήρης] ἡμέρᾳ καὶ νυκτί started first by a day and night, Thuc.

of rank, c. gen., δήμου προὔχουσιν they are the first or chief of the people, Hhymn.:— absol. to be superior, to be eminent, Thuc.; τὸ προὔχον all that is eminent, Id.; οἱ προὔχοντες the chief men, Id.
to surpass, excel, c. gen., Hdt., attic; πρ. τινὸς τιμήν to be preferred to him in honour, Soph.
rarely c. acc. pers., Xen.:—Pass. to be excelled, NTest.
impers., οὔ τι προέχει it naught avails, c. inf., Hdt.
one who leads as a guide, Dem.
Dep. to go first and lead the way, to be the leader, Hdt., etc.; τινι for a person, i. e. to guide him, Ar., Xen.; πρ. τὴν ὁδόν Xen.
c. gen. to take the lead of, Id.;—later, c. acc., NTest.
of things, to go before, precede, Xen.
part. προηγούμενος, η, ον, going first, τὸ πρ. στράτευμα the van, Id.
one who goes before to shew the way, a guide, Soph.; so προηγητήρ, Eur.
to speak on the part of others, Xen.; πρ. τινί to speak for another, Plut.
a speaking in behalf of others, Luc.
one who speaks in behalf of others, an advocate.
beforehand, antecedently, Plut.
Pass. to be pleased before or first, Arist.
pointed in front, Od.
to have gone before, be the first, Thuc., Xen.
to have advanced, πρ. ἐς βαθὺ τῆς ἡλικίας Ar.; εἰς τοῦτο προήκειν to have come to this pass, Dem.; of Time, τῆς ἡμέρας προηκούσας Plut.
to reach beyond, τῆς ἄρκυος Xen.
to overpower beforehand, Polyb.:—perf. and plup. pass. to be beaten or worsted before, Id.
early growing, Hhymn.
from the foundations or roots, προθελύμνους ἕλκετο χαίτας he tore his hair out by the roots, Il.; προθέλυμνα χαμαὶ βάλε δένδρεα he threw to earth trees uprooted, Id.; ἐφόρει τὰς δρῦς προθελύμνους Ar.
σάκος σάκεϊ προθελύμνῳ φράξαντες fixing shield on shield close-pressed, — where θέλυμνα are the several shields, each overlapping its neighbour, Hom.
to prepare beforehand, Plat.
to court beforehand, Plut.
a placing in public;— of a corpse, the laying it out (cf. προτίθημι II), Plat., Dem.
a public notice, Arist.
the statement of the case, Id.
οἱ ἄρτοι τῆς προθέσεως the loaves laid before, the shewbread, NTest.
a purpose, end proposed, Philipp. ap. Dem.
a supposition, calculation, Polyb.
fore-appointed, Luc.
προθεσμία (sc. ἡμέρα), in attic law, a day appointed beforehand, within which money was to be paid, actions brought, claims made, elections held, Dem., Aeschin.: —generally, an appointed time, Plat.
to foretell, Aesch.
to run before, Il.; πολὺ προθέεσκε (ionic imperf.) he was far ahead, Hom.
to run forward or forth, Xen.
c. acc. to outrun, outstrip, Id.; c. gen., Plut.
τοὔνεκά οἱ προθέουσιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι do they therefore let him speak reproachful words? Il.
to die before, Thuc.
to die for another, c. gen., Eur.
a president, Anth.
to noise abroad beforehand, Luc.
to spring before, forth, forward, only in aor2 part. προθορών, Il.
a preparatory sacrifice, Ar.:— metaph., ἐμὸν θάνατον προθύματ’ ἔλαβεν Ἄρτεμις Eur.

entry.note: imperf. προεθυμεόμην contr. προὐθυμούμην fut. mid. -θυμήσομαι and pass. -θυμηθήσομαι aor1 προὐθυμήθην
entry.sense: to be ready, willing, eager, zealous to do a thing, c. inf., Hdt., attic; also πρ. ὅπως Hdt., attic
absol. to shew zeal, exert oneself, Hdt.:— to be of good cheer, Xen.
c. acc. rei, to be eager or zealous for, promote eagerly, desire ardently, Thuc., etc.
one must be eager, Plat.;and
readiness, willingness, eagerness, zeal, ἧσι προθυμίῃσι [ῑ] πεποιθώς, i. e. πρόθυμος ὤν, Il.; πάσῃ προθυμίᾳ with all zeal, Plat.; ὑπὸ προθυμίας zealously, Id.
c. gen. pers., ἐκ τῆς Κλεομένεος προθυμίης at his desire, Hdt.; κατὰ τὴν τούτου προθυμίην as far as his desire goes, Id.; τοῦ θεοῦ προθυμίᾳ by the will of the god, Eur.
c. gen. rei, προθυμίη σωτηρίης zeal to save him, Hdt.; πρ. ἔργου readiness for action, the will or purpose to act, Soph.
πρ. ἔχειν, = προθυμεῖσθαι, Hdt.; c. inf., Id., attic
good-will, ready kindness, Hdt.
ready, willing, eager, zealous, π. εἰμι, c. inf., = προθυμέομαι, Hdt., attic
c. gen. rei, eager for, Soph., Thuc.
with Preps., πρ. εἴς τι Ar., Thuc., etc.; ἐπί τι, πρός τι Xen.
absol., Hdt., etc.:— τὸ πρόθυμον = προθυμία, Eur.
bearing good-will, wishing well, Soph., Eur., etc.
adv. -μως, readily, zealously, actively, Hdt., etc.; πρ. μᾶλλον ἢ φίλως with more zeal than kindness, Aesch.:—comp. -ότερον, Thuc., etc.:—Sup. -ότατα, Hdt., etc.
before the door; προθύραια, ων, τά, the space before a door, Hhymn.
the front-door, the door leading from the αὐλή, Hom.; also in pl., Id.
the space before a door, a kind of porch or verandah, Lat. vestibulum, Od., Hdt., attic
metaph., Κόρινθος πρόθυρον Ποτειδᾶνος Pind.; πρόθυρα ἀρετῆς Plat.
to sacrifice or offer before, Plat.:—Mid. to have a person sacrificed or slaughtered before, Luc.
to sacrifice for or in behalf of another, c. gen., Eur.; ὑπέρ τινος Id.
to send forth, dismiss, Hom.
to send forward, to send untimely to the nether world, Il., Aesch.
Mid. to sit before, take the first seat, Hdt.

entry.note: 3 pres. προΐει as if from προΐω 3 opt. προΐοι attic imperf. προΐειν attic imperf -εις attic imperf -ει fut. προήσω aor1 προῆκα epic προέηκα 3rd pl. aor2 πρόεσαν opt. προεῖεν imperat. πρόες 3rd sg. προέτω inf. προέμεν for προεῖναι Mid., aor1 προηκάμην 3rd pl. aor2 opt. πρόοιντο πρόειντο Pass., perf. προεῖμαι 3rd sg. plup. προεῖτο
entry.sense: to send before, send on or forward, Hom.: also, to send something to another, ἀγγελίας, φήμην Od.:—Hom. often with an inf. added; αἰετὼ προέηκα πέτεσθαι, οὖρον προέηκεν ἀῆναι Od.
to send away, dismiss, let go, Il.; τήνδε θεῷ πρόες let her go to the god, i. e. in reverence to him, Id.
to let loose, let fall, esp. thoughtlessly, ἔπος προέηκε let drop a word, Od.; πηδάλιον ἐκ χειρῶν προέηκε he let the helm slip from his hands, Id.; δάκρυα προῆκεν Eur.
of missiles, to send forth, shoot or dart forth, Hom.
of a river, ὕδωρ προΐει ἐς Πηνειόν it pours its water into the Peneius, Il.
πρ. τινί ποιεῖν τι to allow one to do, Pind.
to give up, deliver over, betray one to his enemy, Hdt., Thuc.: —Pass. to be given or thrown away, εἰ προεῖτο ταῦτα Dem.
ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτίκα ἡδὺ πρ. αὑτόν to give up or devote oneself to present delights, Xen.
Mid. to send forward from oneself, drive forward, Xen.:—of sounds, to utter, Aeschin., etc.
to give up, let go: to give up to the enemy, Thuc., etc.; πρ. σφᾶς αὑτούς gave themselves up as lost, Id.
to desert, abandon, Id.; οὐδαμῆ προΐεντο ἑαυτούς did not lose themselves (i. e. take bribes), Dem.
to give away, give freely, Thuc., etc.; προέσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων Dem.
to throw off one's clothes, Id.: and, in bad sense, to throw away, τὸν καιρόν Id.; τὰ πατρῷα Aeschin.: absol. to be lavish, Arist.
a second predicate is sometimes added, ἡμᾶς προέσθαι ἀδικουμένους to suffer us to be wronged, Thuc.; προέμενοι αὐτοὺς ἀπολέσθαι Xen.; πρ. τινὶ ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατῆσαι Dem.
to suffer to escape, Polyb.
rarely in good sense, to give over to one, confide to one's care, Xen.
to neglect, disregard, Arist.:— absol. to neglect all advice, to be reckless, Dem.
gratuitous, Anth.
one who asks a gift, a beggar, Od.; ἀνὴρ π. a beggar- man, Id.
a gift, present, προικὸς γεύσασθαι to taste of a present, Od.; προικὸς χαρίσασθαι to give away gratis (προικός being gen. pretii), Id.
a marriage-portion, dowry, Plat., Dem.
the attic used acc. προῖκα as adv., like δωρεάν, as a free gift, freely, at one's own cost, Lat. gratis, Ar., Plat.; πρ. κρίνειν without a gift, unbribed, Dem.
to ride before others, c. gen., Plut.

entry.note: fut. -στήσω aor1 προὔστησα part. προστήσας inf. προστῆσαι
entry.sense: Causal in these tenses, as also in pres. and aor1 mid., to set before or in front, προστήσας [σε] Τρωσὶ μάχεσθαι Il.
to set over others, c. gen., Plat.
Mid., mostly in aor1, to put another before oneself, choose as one's leader, Hdt.: c. gen., προΐστασθαι τουτονὶ ἑαυτοῦ to take as one's leader, Plat.
to put before one, put in front, Hdt., etc.
metaph. to put forward as a pretence, use as a screen, τὰ τῶν Ἀμφικτυόνων δόγματα προστήσασθαι Dem.; c. gen. to use one thing as a pretext for another, Id.
to prefer, value one above another, τινά τινος Plat.
Pass., with aor2 act. προὔστην: perf. προέστηκα, ionic 2nd pl. προέστατε, inf. προεστάναι, part. προεστώς: aor1 pass. προεστάθην:—3 to put oneself forward, come forward, Dem.
c. acc. to approach, Soph.
c. dat. to stand before or face another, Id.

c. gen. to be set over, be the chief power, τῆς Ἑλλάδος, τῶν Ἀρκάδων Hdt.:— to be at the head of a party, act as chief or leader, τῶν παράλων, τῶν ἐκ τοῦ πεδίου Id.; τοῦ δήμου Thuc.: hence absol., οἱ προεστῶτες, ionic -εῶτες, the leading men, chiefs, leaders, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
in various relations, to govern, direct, manage, οὐκ ὀρθῶς σεωυτοῦ προέστηκας you do not manage yourself well, Hdt.; πρ. τοῦ ἑαυτοῦ βίου Xen.

to stand before so as to guard him, Hdt.; πρόστητε τύχης be our defence against fortune, Soph.; ὁ προστὰς τῆς εἰρήνης the champion of peace, Aeschin.;—also, προὐστήτην φόνου were the authors of death, Soph.:—absol., βέλεα ἀρωγὰ προσταθέντα Id.
to hold before, hold out, of boys playing at ποσίνδα, Xen.:—mostly in Mid. to hold out before oneself, stretch forth, χεῖρας Thuc.: c. gen. to hold before, τῶν ὄψεων τὰς χεῖρας Plut.
metaph. in Mid. to put forward, use as a pretext, allege, plead, Hdt., Thuc.
to propose, offer, Id.
Προιτίδες (πύλαι), αἱ, one of the gates of Thebes, called from Proetus, Aesch.
pursuit of the foremost, Hes.
exceeding bad, κακὰ πρόκακα evils beyond evils, Aesch.
to call forth: mostly in Mid., 3 sg. epic aor1 προκαλέσσατο, imperat. προκάλεσσαι: — to call out to fight, challenge, defy, Lat. provoco, Hom.; so, πρ. εἰς ἀγῶνα Xen.
to invite or summon beforehand, τινὰ ἐς λόγους Hdt., Thuc.; ἐς σπονδάς Thuc.; ἐπὶ ξυμμαχίαν Id.
c. acc. et inf. to invite one to do, Id., etc.
absol., αὐτῶν προκαλεσαμένων at or after their invitation, Id.
c. acc. rei, to offer or propose, δίκην Id.; τὰς σπονδάς Ar.; c. acc. pers. added, προκαλεῖσθαί τινα τὴν εἰρήνην to offer one peace, Id.

as attic law-term, to make an offer or challenge to the opponent, such as to submit the case to arbitration, let slaves be put to the torture, Dem.; cf. πρόκλησις: — Pass., πρ. ἐς κρίσιν περί τινος Thuc.
to call up or forth, εὐγένειαν Eur.

entry.etym: only in pres. imperat. προκαλίζεο, epic 3rd sg. imperf. προκαλίζετο
entry.sense: Dep. to call forth or out, challenge, defy, Hom.
Pass. to fall prostrate before another, Isocr., Dem.
anything put before, a curtain, such as was hung in doorways instead of doors, Aesch.
a covering, as a protection, Thuc.
metaph. a screen or cloak, Id., Luc.
to hang before as a covering:— Mid. to put over oneself as a screen or cloak, Eur.; οὐ παρακαλυπτομένα παρηίδος putting no veil over one's face, Id.
to cover over, ἥλιον νεφέλη πρ. Xen.: —Mid., προὐκαλύψατο ὄμματα veiled her eyes, Eur.
to work or toil before, Theogn.
to toil for or in defence of, τινός Soph.
to grow weary, give up, μὴ πρόκαμνε Aesch.; μὴ προκάμητε πόδα Eur.
to have a previous illness, Thuc.;— to be distressed beforehand, Id.
forthwith, straightway, suddenly, in Hdt., πρόκα τε or πρόκατε.
to sleep before or first, Ar.
Dep. to go before and guide, Polyb.; πρ. τῆς κρίσεως to influence it beforehand, Id.
to be seated before, πρὸ τῆς ἄλλης Ἑλλάδος πρ. to lie in front of the rest of Greece, of the Thessalians, Hdt.
c. gen. to be seated or lie before a place, and so, to protect, defend, Id., Thuc.; στρατιᾶς πρ. Eur.
to preside over, τῆς πόλεως Plat.
to sit down or alight before, Il.
to sit in public, sit in state, ἐς θρόνον Hdt.: —so in Mid., Id.
to settle before, Id.
trans. to set over, Polyb.
to let down beforehand: metaph., πόλιν πρ. εἰς ταραχήν to plunge the city into confusion, Dem.; πρ. τινὰ ἐξαπατᾶν to put a person forward in order to deceive, Id.
to set before; so in Mid., Xen.
Pass., with aor2 and perf. act., φυλακῆς μὴ προκαθεστηκυίας no guard having been set beforehand, Thuc.
to examine beforehand, to reconnoitre, Hdt.
to burn before: Pass. to be lighted before, of fires, Xen.
head-foremost, Anth.
to announce or declare beforehand, NTest.
to vote against beforehand, condemn by a prejudgment, c. gen. pers., Dem., etc.; absol., Ar.; μὴ προκατεγνωκέναι μηδέν not to prejudge in any point, Dem.
c. inf., πρ. ἡμῶν ἥσσους εἶναι to prejudge us and say we are inferior, Thuc.
πρ. τί τινος, as, φόνον τινός, to give a verdict of murder against one beforehand, Oratt.
Pass. to get into harbour before, τινος Luc.
a coming into port before, Arr.
to run down before, Xen.
to burn all before one, Xen.
Pass. to lie down before, Luc.
to make to lie down before others, Joseph.:—Pass., = προκατάκειμαι, Luc.
to seize beforehand, preoccupy, Thuc., etc.:—Pass. to be preoccupied, Id.
metaph. to anticipate, frustrate, Id., Aeschin.:—of persons, to anticipate or surprise them, Thuc.
to overpower before, Id.
Pass. to be described beforehand, Hdt.
to terminate beforehand, Polyb.
to break up or annul beforehand, Thuc.; τὸν βίον πρ. τοῦ ἔργου to end his life before finishing his work, Plut.:—Mid., πρ. τὴν ἔχθρην to end their mutual enmity before, Hdt.
to fall down before: λόγοι προκατέπιπτον εἰς τὴν Ῥώμην rumours reached Rome beforehand, Plut.
to sail down before, Polyb.
to complete beforehand, NTest.
to begin a thing before others, to begin hostilities, Polyb.
προκατάρχεσθαί τινι τῶν ἱερῶν to serve one with the first portion of the victim (one of the privileges of the citizens of the mother-city in their colonies), Thuc.
to prepare beforehand, Xen.
previous preparation, a preface, introduction, Polyb.
to escape to a place of safety before, Thuc.
Dep. to use up beforehand, Dem.
to hope beforehand, Polyb.
to eat up beforehand, Luc.
to hold or gain possession of beforehand, preoccupy, Thuc., Xen.:—Mid. to hold down before oneself, Hhymn.
to bring accusations beforehand, Dem.
a previous accusation, Thuc.
to be set before one, of meats, Hom., Hdt.
to lie exposed, of a child, Hdt.:— to lie dead, Aesch., Soph.; ὁ προκείμενος the corpse laid out for burial, Soph., etc.

to be set before all, as the prize of a contest, Hes.:—metaph. to be set before all, be set forth, proposed, Lat. in medio poni, γνῶμαι τρεῖς προεκέατο three opinions were set forth, proposed, Hdt., etc.:—of contests, struggles, πόνος τε καὶ ἀγὼν πρόκειται Plat.:—in partic., ἄεθλος προκείμενος a task proposed, Hdt., etc.; τὰ προκείμενα, opp. to μέλλοντα, Soph.; τὸ προκείμενον πρῆγμα the matter in hand, Hdt.

to be set forth beforehand, to be prescribed, αἱ προκείμεναι ἡμέραι the prescribed days, Id.; so, ἐνιαυτοὶ πρόκεινται ἐς ὀγδώκοντα are set, fixed at, Id.; of laws, νόμοι οἱ προκείμενοι Soph.; of penalties, Thuc.
to lie before, lie in front of, c. gen., Αἴγυπτος προκειμένη τῆς ἐχομένης γῆς Hdt.; τὰ προκείμενα τῆς χώρας ὄρη Xen.
to precede, γράμμα πρ. an initial letter, Anth.
conducting, τινος Mosch.
to empty beforehand, Luc.
Dep. to take care of, take thought for, τινος Aesch., Soph.
to be anxious for, τινός Soph.: also, τί ποτ’, ὦ τέκνον, τάδε κηραίνεις; why art thou thus anxious? Eur.
Dep. to negotiate by herald, Aeschin.
to proclaim by herald, proclaim publicly, Soph.: c. acc. rei, Id.
to run risk before others, brave the first danger, bear the brunt of battle, Thuc., Dem.; τῷ βαρβάρῳ against the barbarians, Thuc.
to move forward, τὸν στρατόν Xen.: to urge on, ἵππον Id.:—Pass. with fut. mid. to advance, Id.
to weep beforehand or openly, Soph., Eur.
trans. to lament beforehand, Hdt., Eur.
a calling forth, challenging, challenge, ἐκ προκλήσιος upon or by challenge, Hdt.
an invitation, offer, proposal, Thuc., etc.

as law-term, a challenge offered to the opponent, for the purpose of bringing disputed points to issue, somewhat like the Roman sponsio, Dem., etc.; πρ. προκαλεῖσθαι to make such a challenge, δέχεσθαι to accept it, Id.
calling forth, challenging: προκλητικόν, τό, a challenge, Plut.
to lean forward, Soph.
heard formerly, of olden time, Il.
to hear beforehand, Aesch.
a covering for the leg, Polyb.
a watch kept before a place; in pl., like Lat. excubiae, Polyb.
one who keeps watch before a place, Polyb.
to chastise beforehand, Arist.
to flatter beforehand, Plat.
a robe falling over the breast, Theophr.
to bring forward, produce, Luc.
Pass. to be carried before to a place of safety, Hdt.
the forelock of a horse, Xen.
progress on a journey, generally, progress, advance, Polyb.; in pl., Plut., Luc.
to cut away in front: hence to forward a work (the metaph. being prob. taken from pioneers), Pass. to be forwarded, to advance, prosper, Hdt.
with neut. Adjs., τὰ πολλὰ προκόψας’ having made most things ready, Eur.; τί ἂν προκόπτοις; what good would you get? Id.; οὐδὲν προὔκοπτον they were making no progress, Xen.

c. gen. rei, τοῦ ναυτικοῦ μέγα μέρος προκόψαντες having made improvements in their navy to a great extent, Thuc.; ἡμῶν προκοπτόντων τῆς ἀρχῆς ἐκείνοις since we promote the increase of their empire, Id.; ἐπὶ πλεῖον πρ. ἀσεβείας having advanced further in impiety, NTest.
absol., ἡ νὺξ προέκοψεν the night is far spent, Id.; πρ. σοφίᾳ to advance in wisdom, Id.
prejudgment, prejudice, NTest.

to choose before others, choose by preference, prefer, select, Hdt., attic:—Pass. to be preferred before others, τὰ προκεκριμένα the most eminent, Hdt.: c. inf., τοῦτο προκέκριται εἶναι κάλλιστον Xen.; inf., τὸ ἐμὲ προκριθῆναι ἄρχοντα Id.
c. gen. to prefer before others, Plat.:—Pass., τῶν ἄλλων προκεκρίσθαι Hdt.
c. acc. et inf. to judge or decide beforehand that . . , Xen.
chosen before others, select, Plat.

ranged at regular intervals, like steps or battlements (v. κρόσσαι); of ships drawn up on the beach, ranged in a row, Il.; πρόκροσσαι ἐς πόντον ἐπὶ ὀκτώ ranged in rows turned seawards eight deep, Hdt.; of a cup, πέριξ αὐτοῦ γρυπῶν κεφαλαὶ οἱ πρόκροσσοι ἦσαν the heads of griffins were set at intervals round it, Id.
Pass. to roll at the feet of another, Lat. provolvi ad genua alicujus, τινι Ar.; τινος Dem.
Pass. to roll forward, of a wave, Il.
to stoop and bend forward, to peep out, Ar.
Pass. to be confirmed before, NTest.
Procyon, a star which rises (about the middle of July) before the dog-star, Hor.
πικροὶ Καλλιμάχου πρόκυνες, a nickname of the Grammarians, snappers and snarlers, Anth.
the prelude sung by a κῶμος, Pind.
of a sword, grasped by the hilt, drawn, Aesch., Eur.:—metaph. ready, Aesch.
Dep. to receive beforehand or by anticipation, τινος some of a thing, Eur.
to prate before, Anth.
to take or receive before, Eur., Dem., etc.
to take or seize beforehand, Dem.; πρ. ὅπως . . to provide that . . , Dem.; προλαβὼν προεγνωκότας ὑμᾶς first procured your vote of condemnation, Id.
to take before, take in preference, τι πρό τινος Soph.
to take away or off before, προὔλαβον μόγις πόδα Eur.
to be beforehand with, anticipate,
c. acc. pers. to get the start of, Xen., Dem.:—also c. gen. pers., Dem.
c. acc. rei, Eur.
c. gen. spatii, πρ. τῆς ὁδοῦ to get a start on the way, Hdt.; πρ. τῆς φυγῆς Thuc.
absol., πολλῷ προὔλαβε was far ahead, Id.:— to anticipate the event, prejudge, Dem.; προλαβόντες by anticipation, Xen.
to repeat from the origin, Isocr.
to choose before others, prefer: Pass., Ἀθηναίων προλελεγμένοι Il.; πασᾶν ἐκ πολίων πρ. Theocr.
to foretell, announce beforehand, of an oracle, Hdt., attic
to state publicly, proclaim, c. acc. et inf., Aesch., etc.
πρ. τινὶ ποιεῖν τι to order him to do, Xen.— to caution, warn, Thuc.
to denounce punishment, πρ. δεσμόν τινι Dem.
to go forth and leave, to leave behind, forsake, abandon, Hom., etc.; μῆτίς σε προλέλοιπε prudence hath forsaken thee, Od.; χώραν πρ. to abandon one's post, Thuc.
c. inf. to omit to do a thing, Theogn., Soph.
of things, to desert, fail one, Plat.
intr. to cease or fail beforehand, Ἀτρείδαις οὐ προλείπει φόνος Eur.; εἴ τῳ προλείποι ἡ ῥώμη Thuc.; of persons, to faint, fall into a swoon, Eur.
Dep. to hold conversations with one before, c. dat. pers., Hdt.
to see before oneself or in front, Soph.
in Trag. and old Com. Poets, the prologue, that portion of the play that comes before the first chorus, Arist.; but from the time of Eur., a narrative of facts introductory to the plot, Ar.
to lay an ambuscade beforehand: — Pass., αἱ προλελοχισμέναι ἐνέδραι the ambush that had before been laid, Thuc.
to beset with an ambuscade, Id.
Dep. to destroy beforehand, Polyb.
Pass. to feel pain before, Plat.
previous distress, Plat.
to soften beforehand: so in Mid., Plut.
a tree, prob. a kind of willow, Anth.
to learn beforehand, and (in aor2 προὔμαθον) to know beforehand, Pind., Thuc., etc.:—c. acc. to learn by rote, Ar.: c. inf., προὔμαθον στέργειν τάδε Soph.
the right of consulting the Delphic Oracle first, Hdt., Dem.
Dep. to prophesy, Hdt.:c. acc. to foretell, predict, Luc.
a prophet or prophetess, Eur.
the title of the Pythia or Delphic priestess, who gave out the answers of the oracle, Hdt., Thuc.; so of the priestess at Dodona, Hdt.
as adj. prophetic, δίκη πρ. justice giving presage of the issue, Soph.; θυμὸς πρ. "my prophetic soul, " Eur.; c.gen., τούτων πρ. οὖσα prophetic, foreboding of a thing, Aesch.
Dep. to witness beforehand, NTest.
to fight in front, Xen.
a bulwark, rampart, Lat. propugnaculum, Hdt., Xen.; πρ. τοῦ τείχεος Hdt.
to fight before, Τρωσί in front of the Trojans, as their champion, Il.; also, to fight as champion with another, Ἀχιλῆι Id.
Dep. to fight before, ἁπάντων before all, Il.
to fight for or in defence of, τινος Ar.
fighting before or in front: πρόμαχοι, οἱ, the foremost fighters, champions, Hom.; ἐν προμάχοισιν among the foremost, Il.:—as adj., πρ. δόρυ the champion spear, Soph.
fighting for, πόλεως, δόμων Aesch.
to practise beforehand: c. inf., Xen.
name of a prophetess of Dodona, presage, Hdt.
to take thought before, NTest.
before or on the forehead:— προμετωπίδιον, ου, the skin or hair of the forehead, Hdt.
a frontlet for horses, Xen.
the festival of Prometheus, Xen.

Dep to take care beforehand, to provide for, c. gen., Hdt.; ὑπέρ τινος, περί τι Plat.; absol., Aesch.: —generally, to take heed, Lat. cavere, πρ. μὴ . . Hdt.: —c. acc. to shew regard or respect for, Id., Plat.
foresight, forethought, Hdt., Eur., etc.; ἐν προμηθίῃ ἔχειν τινά to hold in consideration, Hdt.; προμηθίαν ἔχειν τινός Eur., Plat.

entry.note: Προμήθειος, α, ον, and ος, ον,
entry.sense: Promethean, Anth.
Προμήθεια, τά, the festival of Prometheus, Xen.

Prometheus, son of the Titan Iapetus and Themis, inventor of many arts: he is said to have made man from clay, and to have furnished him with the ἔντεχνον πῦρ stolen from Olympus: hence also his name (from προμηθής), opp. to his careless brother Ἐπιμηθεύς, — forethought and afterthought, Hes., Aesch., etc.
as appellat. forethought, Aesch.
forethinking, provident, cautious, Thuc.; τὸ προμηθές, = προμήθεια, Id.: c. gen. troubling oneself about a thing, Soph.
shrewdly, warily, with allusion to the name Prometheus, Ar.
prolonged, elongated, Plut.
to denounce beforehand, τινί τι Soph.: to indicate before, τι Plut.
first mother of a race, formed like προπάτωρ, Aesch., Eur.
Dep. to contrive beforehand, Luc.
to mingle beforehand:—Pass., παλλακίδι προμῐγῆναι (aor2 inf.) to have intercourse with her before, Il.
Pass. to be hired beforehand, Plut.
Dep.
to woo or court for another, ἡ προμνησαμένη = προμνήστρια, Xen.
generally, to solicit, Id., Plut.
προμνᾶταί τί μοι γνώμα my mind forebodeth somewhat, Soph.
one by one, one after the other, Od.
entry.etym: Perh. from μένω, for προμενετῖνοι — each waiting for the one before.

entry.sense: a woman who woos or courts for another, a match-maker, Ar., Plat.; metaph., κακῶν πρ. of one who brings about evil, Eur.
before the destined term, i. e. untimely, of death, Anth.
an approach, of the foot of a mountain, Anth.; the mouth of a river, Id.
the foremost man, = πρόμαχος, Hom.; πρ. τινί opposed to another in the front rank, Il.:— generally, a chief, Lat. primus, princeps, Trag.; πάντων θεῶν θεὸς πρόμος, of the Sun, Soph.
to work beforehand, Eur.
before a temple, esp. of gods whose shrines or statues stood before the temple, as of Athena at Delphi, Hdt.; Παλλὰς προναία Aesch.
as Subst., πρόναος, = πρόδομος, the hall of a temple, through which one went to the ναός or cella, Hdt.
to fight at sea for or in defence of, c. gen., Hdt.
to assign beforehand, τί τινι Pind.; καθαρὰς χεῖρας πρ. to present unspotted hands, Aesch.
Mid. to go forward in grazing: hence to gain ground, creep onward, of war, etc.
to stoop or bend forward, Plat.; of a rider, Xen.; of rowers, Id.
to fast before, Hdt.
to gain a victory beforehand, Thuc.

entry.note: fut. ήσω fut. ήσομαι aor1 mid. προὐνοησάμην and pass. προὐνοήθην perf. προνενόημαι
entry.sense: to perceive before, foresee, Il., Thuc., Arist.; προνοῶν ὅτι . . foreseeing that . . , Xen.
to think of or plan beforehand, provide, Od.:—absol. to be provident, take measures of precaution, Eur., Thuc.: —πρ. ὅτι . . , to provide, take care that . . , Thuc.; ὅπως . . , Xen., etc.
c. gen. to provide for, take thought for, Id.
in same sense, Dep. προνοοῦμαι
Act. to provide, Thuc., etc.:—c. inf. to take care to do, Eur.
c. gen. to provide for, Thuc., etc.
one must provide, Xen.
provident, cautious, wary, Xen.
of things, shewing forethought or design, Id.: adv. -κῶς, Id.
foresight, foreknowledge, Aesch., Soph.

foresight, forethought, forecast, Soph.; ἐκ προνοίας with forethought, purposely, Lat. consulto, Hdt.; ἀπὸ προνοίας τίνων by their precautions, Thuc.:—esp. of crimes committed with design or malice prepense, ἐκ προνοίας τραύματα Aeschin.; τὰ ἐκ πρ., opp. to ἀκούσια, Arist.:— πρόνοιαν ἔχειν (or ἴσχειν) τινός to take thought for . . , shew care for . . , Eur., etc.; περί τινος Soph.; c. inf., πολλὴν πρ. εἶχεν εὐσχήμως πεσεῖν Eur.
divine providence, Hdt., attic

entry.etym: = προνομή II, Plut.; of a fly, Luc.

entry.sense: to go out for foraging, Polyb.
a foraging, a foraging expedition, foray, Xen.: in pl., foraging parties, Id.
an elephant's trunk, Polyb.
= προ-νομία, Luc.
a privilege, Strab., Luc.
earnest-money, Luc.
careful, Hdt.:—comp. προνούστερος, Soph.
stooping forwards, with head inclined, Lat. pronus, στείχει πρ., of one in deep grief, Eur.; πρ. ἐστι, of one dying, Id.; so, πρ. λαβεῖν to take her as she fell fainting forward, Aesch.
metaph. inclined, ready, πρ. ἐς τὸ λοιδορεῖν Eur.
the front of a house (cf. ἐνώπια), Eur.: metaph. in sg., χώρας Πελοπίας πρ., of Troezen, the outer portal of Peloponnesus, Id.
as adj. in front, before the door, Id.
proxeny, i. e. a compact between a State and a foreigner, Lat. hospitium, Thuc., etc.; προξενίᾳ πέποιθα I trust my public friendship, Pind.; τινὰ πρ. ἐξευρήσεις; what protector wilt thou find? Eur.

a public ξένος, public guest or friend, made so by an act of the State, such as was the King of Macedon to the Athenians, Hdt.; —the word expressed the same relation between a State and an individual of another State, that ξένος expressed between individuals of different States.—The πρόξενος enjoyed his privileges on the condition of entertaining and assisting the ambassadors and citizens of the State which he represented, so that the πρόξενοι answered to our Consuls, Agents, Residents, though the πρόξενος was always a member of the foreign State.
generally, a patron, protector, Aesch.: as fem. a patroness, Soph.
to travel before, Luc.
to travel before, Luc.
to prepare the way before, prepare or pave the way, τινί for another, Arist.
c. acc. to prepare beforehand, Plut.:—Pass. to be prepared before, Arist.: part. προωδοποιημένος, η, ον, prepared, ready, Id.
the roe-deer, Od.: cf. προκάς.

entry.note: fut. ήσω imperf. προὐξένουν fut. -ήσω perf. προὐξένηκα
entry.sense: to be any one's πρόξενος, διὰ τὸ προξενεῖν ὑμῶν because he is your πρόξενος, Xen.; πρ. τῶν πρέσβεων to act as πρ. to the envoys of a friendly State, Dem.:—generally, to be one's protector, patron, Eur.
from the duties of a πρόξενος (signf. II),

to manage or effect anything for another, Id.; πρ. θράσος to lend daring, Soph.; πρ. τιμήν τινι to procure it for him, Plut.:—also in bad sense, πρ. κίνδυνόν τινι to put danger upon one, Xen.:—also, c. dat. et inf., πρ. τινὶ ὁρᾶν to be the means of his seeing, Soph.; πρ. τινὶ καταλῦσαι βίον to grant one to die, Xen.:—also, πρ. τινί to be one's guide, Soph.
to introduce or recommend to another, Plat., Dem.
going before: οἱ πρ. a party of soldiers in advance, Xen.
a going on, advance, progress, Xen.
to know beforehand, Hdt., attic
to build before:—Pass., Luc.

entry.note: attic contr. φροιμιάζομαι fut. άσομαι perf. πεφροιμίασμαι
entry.sense: Dep.:— to make a prelude, preamble or preface, Aesch., Xen.

c. acc. to say by way of preface, premise, φροιμιάζομαι θεούς begin by invoking them, Aesch.; τί φροιμιάζει; Eur.:—perf. in pass. sense, πεφροιμιάσθω τοσαῦτα let so much be said by way of preface, Arist.
an opening or introduction to a thing; in Music, a prelude, overture, Pind.; in poems and speeches, a proem, preface, preamble, introduction, Lat. exordium, Id., Xen.
metaph. of any prelude or beginning, φροίμιον χορεύσομαι Aesch.; μηδέπω ’ν προοιμίοις only just beginning, Id.; εἴ τι τοῦδε φρ. ματᾷ if any part of this presage be vain, Id.
generally, a hymn, Thuc., Plat.
Dep. to have gone on before, Xen.
to swear before or beforehand, Dem.
to testify on oath before that . . , c. acc. et inf., Aesch., Dem.
to grant or concede beforehand, Plat.:—Pass., προωμολόγηταί τι εἶναι Id.
one must look to, be careful of, c. gen., Hdt.
foreseen, manifest, Hdt., attic
to be foreseen, Xen.
to see before one, see what is just before the eyes, Thuc.: to look forward to, Xen.:—absol. to look before one or forward, Id.
to see before, foresee, τὸ μέλλον Hdt., attic:—absol., τὸ προορᾶν σευ your foresight, Hdt.
c. gen. to provide or make provision for, Id.
in attic also in Mid., with perf. and plup. pass., to look before one, Xen.
to foresee, Thuc., Dem.
to provide for, Thuc., Dem.
to determine beforehand, to predetermine, pre-ordain, NTest.
to drive forward:—Pass. to move forward, push on, Xen.;—so intr. in Act., Id.
one who leads the dance, Luc.

to owe beforehand: πρ. κακόν τινι to owe one an ill turn, i. e. to deserve evil at his hands, Eur.; πρ. κακὸν ταῖς πλευραῖς to owe one's ribs a mischief, i. e. deserve a beating, Ar.:—Pass. to be due beforehand, of debts, ὁ προοφειλόμενος φόρος the arrears of tribute, Hdt.; ἔχθρη προοφειλομένη εἴς τινα the hatred one has long had reason to feel, Id.; εὐεργεσία προὐφειλομένη a kindness that has long remained as a debt, Thuc.
= ὀφείλω I, to be due beforehand, Eur.
a foreseeing, Thuc.; οὐκ οὔσης τῆς προόψεως since there was no seeing, Id.
prominent, Luc.
preparatory teaching, Plat.
to teach beforehand:—Pass., Plat.
very long ago, Ar.
a great-grandfather, Oratt.
prep. with gen., before, in front of, Hom.; πρ. ποδῶν at one's feet, i. e. close at hand, Id.; ἠιόνος πρ. before, i. e. along the shore, Il.; πρ. νεός before, i. e. beyond the ship, Od.
before the time of, Aesch.
as adv.,
of Place, in front, in advance, forward, before, Hom., Hes.
of Time, before, formerly, Hom., Aesch.
prep. with gen. before, in front of, Hes., Eur.
adv., before, sooner, Aesch.
to put beside beforehand:—Mid. to do so for oneself, Thuc.
to prepare beforehand, Thuc., etc.:—Mid. to prepare for oneself, Id.:—Pass., ἐκ πολλοῦ προπαρεσκευασμένοι Id.
to offer before, Xen.
to supply before, Id.
πρόπαν ἦμαρ all day long, Hom.; νῆας προπάσας all the ships together, Il.; πρόπασα χώρα, γαῖα Aesch.; πρόπαντος χρόνου Id.; πρ. στόλος Soph.; πρόπαντα κακὰ κακῶν Id.: neut. πρόπαν, as adv., Eur.
to suffer first or beforehand, Hdt., Thuc., etc.: to be ill-treated before, ὑπό τινος Thuc.:—also, ἀγαθὸν πρ. Xen.
the first founder of a family, forefather, Hdt., Eur.:—in pl. ancestors, forefathers, Hdt., etc.; ὦ Ζεῦ, προγόνων προπάτωρ Soph.
to persuade beforehand, Luc.
before, Lat. prae:
PREP. WITH GENIT.:
of Place, before, in front of, πρὸ ἄστεος, πρὸ πυλάων Hom.; οὐρανόθι πρό Il.; χωρεῖν πρὸ δόμων to come out in front of, Soph.
before, in front of, for the purpose of shielding or guarding, στῆναι πρὸ Τρώων Il.:— in defence of, for, μάχεσθαι πρὸ γυναικῶν Id.; ὀλέσθαι πρὸ πόληος, Lat. pro patria mori, Id.
πρὸ ὁδοῦ further on the road, i. e. forwards, onward, Il.: (hence φροῦδος).

of Time, before, πρὸ γάμοιο Od.; πρὸ ὁ τοῦ ( = ὁ πρὸ τοῦ) ἐνόησεν one before the other, Il.; πρὸ τοῦ θανάτου Plat., etc.; πρὸ πολλοῦ long before, Hdt.; τὸ πρὸ τούτου before this, before, Thuc.; πρὸ τοῦ (often written προτοῦ) before, Hdt., attic
in other relations:

of Preference, before, sooner or rather than, κέρδος πρὸ δίκας αἰνῆσαι to praise sleight before right, Pind.; πᾶν πρὸ τῆς παρεούσης λύπης anything before, rather than their actual grievance, Hdt.; πρὸ πολλοῦ ποιεῖσθαι to esteem above much, i. e. very highly, Isocr.; so, πρὸ πολλῶν χρημάτων τιμᾶσθαι Thuc.: redundant, after a comp., ἡ τυραννὶς πρὸ ἐλευθερίης ἀσπαστότερον Hdt.
of Cause or Motive, Lat. prae, for, out of, from, πρὸ φόβοιο for fear, Il.; πρὸ τῶνδε there fore, Soph.
POSITION: never after its case, except after the epic gen. Ἰλιόθι πρό, οὐρανόθι πρό, ἠῶθι πρό.
πρό, absol. as adv.:
of Place, before, in front, forth, forward, Il.
of Time, before, beforehand, Od.: before, earlier, Hes.: prematurely, Aesch.
with other Preps. ἀποπρό, διαπρό, ἐπιπρό, περιπρό, προπρό, it strengthens the first prep.
πρό IN COMPOS.
with Substs., to denote
position before or in front, πρόθυρον, προπύλαια.
priority of rank, πρόεδρος; or of order, προοίμιον.
standing in another's place, πρόμαντις, πρόξενος.
with Adjs., to denote
proximity, readiness, πρόχειρος, πρόθυμος.
forth from, προθέλυμνος, πρόρριζος.
prematureness, πρόμοιρος, πρόωρος.
with Verbs,
of Place, before, forwards, προβαίνω, προβάλλω: also before, in defence, προκινδυνεύω.
forth, προέλκω, προφέρω:—also publicly, προειπεῖν.
giving away, προδίδωμι.
before, in preference, προαιροῦμαι, προτιμάω.
before, beforehand, προαισθάνομαι, προνοέω, προοράω.
to announce beforehand, Xen.
a previous trial or venture, πρόπειραν ποιεῖσθαι ἔν τινι, Lat. periculum facere in . . , Hdt.; πρ. ποιεῖσθαι εἰ . . , Thuc.
only in neut. pl. πρόπεμπτα as adv. five days before, on the fifth day, Lex ap. Dem.

entry.note: fut. ψω aor1 προέπεμψα contr. προὔπεμψα
entry.sense: to send before, send on or forward, Hom., Hdt., attic; πρ. ἄχη to cause them, Soph.
of things, to send forth, Aesch.; ἰοὺς πρ. to shoot forth arrows, Soph.

to conduct, attend, escort, Hdt., attic: — to follow a corpse to the grave, Aesch.; τιμὰς θεοῖς πρ. to carry offerings in procession, Id.; jocosely, τὸν ἕνα ψωμὸν ἐνὶ ὄψῳ πρ. to let one piece of bread be attended by one condiment, Xen.
to pursue, Id.
two years ago, Plat., Dem., etc.
to spread out before, Xen.
reckless haste, vehemence, rashness, indiscretion, Dem., etc.
falling forwards, inclined forward, Lat. proclivis, Xen.
thrown away, κεῖται προπετές [τὸ κάταγμα] Soph.
drooping, at the point of death, Id.; cf. προνωπής.
metaph.,
being upon the point of, πρ. ἐπὶ πολιὰς χαίτας Eur.; τύμβου πρ. παρθένος Id.
ready for, prone to a thing, ἐπί or εἴς τι Xen.; πρός τι Plat.
headlong, precipitate, rash, reckless, violent, Aeschin., ; ἡ πρ. ἀκρασία Arist.; of a lot, drawn at random, Pind.:—of persons, οἱ θρασεῖς προπετεῖς Arist.
adv. -τῶς, forwards, Xen.
headlong hastily, Id., etc.; πρ. ἔχειν to be rash, Id.
to spring before, τῶν ἄλλων Luc.
to spring forward from, c. gen., Babr.
to bespatter with mud or to trample in the mire: metaph. to treat with contumely, to abuse foully, τινά Soph., Thuc., etc.:—Pass., ἰδὼν προπεπηλακισμένην [τὴν φιλοσοφίαν] Plat.
c. acc. rei, to throw in one's teeth, Dem.
contumelious treatment, Hdt., Plat. Dem.
contumeliously, Dem.

entry.note: imperf. προὔπῑνον fut. -πίομαι aor2 προὔπιον perf. προπέπωκα
entry.sense: to drink before another, c. gen., Luc.

to drink to another, drink to his health, pledge him, Lat. propinare, because the custom was to drink first oneself and then pass the cup to the person pledged, προπίνω σοι Xen.; also, πρ. φιλοτησίας τινί (v. φιλοτήσιος II), Dem.

on festal occasions it was a custom to make a present of the cup to the person pledged, τὰ ἐκπώματα ἐμπιμπλάς προὔπινε καὶ ἐδωρεῖτο Xen.: hence, simply, to give freely, make a present of, πρ. τὴν ἐλευθερίαν Φιλίππῳ to make liberty a drinking-present to Philip, give it carelessly to him, Dem.; Pass., c. gen. pretii, προπέποται τῆς αὐτίκα χάριτος τὰ τῆς πόλεως πράγματα the interests of the state have been sacrificed for mere present pleasure, Id.
to fall or throw oneself forward, as in rowing, προπεσόντες ἔρεσσον, like Lat. incumbere remis, Od.:—of suppliants, to fall prostrate, Eur.
to rush forward, rush headlong, Soph., Theocr.
to move forwards, advance before the rest, Polyb.: to project, Id.
προπίτνω poet. for προπίπτω
to fall prostate, ἐς γᾶν Aesch., Soph.
to trust or believe beforehand, Xen., Dem.
to sail before, Thuc.
sailing before or in advance, αἱ πρόπλοι νῆες the leading ships, Thuc.
to advance the foot, Il.
better written divisim πρὸ ποδῶν.
to do before or beforehand, Hdt.; absol., προποιῆσαι to make the first move, Thuc.
to prepare beforehand, plup. pass. προεπεποίητο Hdt.

to make war for or in defence of another, τινός Isocr., etc.; ὑπέρ τινος Plat.: absol., οἱ προπολεμοῦντες the guards or defenders of a country, Id.; τὸ προπολεμῆσον the body intended to act as guards, Arist.
service done, πρ. δάφνης its service or use, = πρόπολος δάφνη, Eur.
employing oneself before:
a servant that goes before one, an attendant, minister, Aesch., Eur., etc.: a rower, Pind.
one who serves a god, a minister, Hhymn., Ar.:—generally, a temple-servant, bedel, like νεωκόρος, Hdt., Ar., etc.
as adj. ministering to a thing, devoted to it, Pind.
to go before in a procession, τινός before him or it, Luc.
an attending, escorting, Xen.:— a processional escort, Plut.
escorting, esp. in a procession, Xen.: c. acc., πρ. χοάς carrying drink-offerings in procession, Aesch.
as Subst. a conductor, escort, attendant, Id., Xen.
to work or labour beforehand, Xen.
to work for or instead of another τινός Id.
c. gen. rei, to work for, work so as to obtain, τῶν εὐφροσυνῶν Id.
c. acc. rei, to obtain by previous labour, Luc.:—Pass., τὰ προπεπονημένα the things so obtained, Xen.
Mid. to sink under affliction, Soph.
the fore-sea, i. e. the Sea of Marmora, that leads into the Pontus, Hdt., Aesch.
Pass., with aor1 mid., to go before or forward, Xen.
to come forward, Polyb.
to be promoted, advance, Id.
Pass. to be provided beforehand, Luc.
a drinking to one, Polyb.
one who drinks healths, προπόται θίασοι bands of revellers, Eur.
the projecting foot of a mountain, its lowest part, Polyb., etc.
to do before, Arist., Luc.
to exact, Aesch.
metaph. friendly, kindly, Pind.
with the face downwards, Lat. pronus, Il.; φασγάνῳ προπρηνέϊ with the edge of the sword, Od.:—neut. προπρηνές as adv., forward, Il.
Pass. to keep rolling before another, roll at his feet, c. gen., προπροκυλινδόμενος πατρὸς Διός Il.; absol. roaming on for ever, Od.
away from the stern, πρ. ἐκβολὰν φέρει, of throwing over the freight to save the vessel, metaph. in Aesch.
before the gate, of the statues of gods, Ar.
προπύλαια, ων, τά, the gateway of temples, Hdt., Ar., etc.:—in sg., Anth.
in pl., like προπύλαια, Hdt., Soph., etc.; in sg., Anth.
Dep.:— to learn by inquiring before, hear beforehand, Hdt., Thuc.
offered for the towers, i. e. for the city, θυσίαι Aesch.
to flow forward, flow amain, of rivers, Hom.
a foretelling, prediction, a previous instruction or warning, Thuc.
public notice, a proclamation, πολεμεῖν ἐκ προρρήσεως Dem.
proclaimed, commanded, Soph.
by the roots, root and branch, utterly, Lat. radicitus, Il.; πρόρριζόν τινα ἀνατρέπειν Hdt.; ἐκτρίβειν Eur.; πρόρριζος ἔφθαρται Soph.
the fore-sabbath, eve of the sabbath, NTest.
to announce, τινά τινι Luc.
to denounce, τῇ βουλῇ τινά Plut.
to be called or named, Plat.
προσαγορευτέον, one must call, τινά τι Arist.

entry.note: fut. σω aor1 -ηγόρευσα fut. and perf. προσερῶ, προσείρηκα aor1 pass. προσηγορεύθην
entry.sense: to address, greet, accost, Lat. salutare, Hdt.: Pass., δυστυχοῦντες οὐ προσαγορευόμεθα in misfortune we are not spoken to, Thuc.
c. dupl. acc. to address or greet as so and so, Δίκαν δέ νιν προσαγορεύομεν Aesch.; τὸν αὐτὸν πατέρα πρ. Xen.: —c. inf., πρ. τινὰ χαίρειν to bid one hail or farewell, Ar.
to call by name, call so and so, τὸν Ἀγαμέμνονα πρ. ποιμένα λαῶν Xen.; τί τὴν πόλιν προσαγορεύεις; Plat.

entry.note: fut. ξω aor2 προσήγᾰγον rarely aor1 προσῆξα προσάξομαι
entry.etym: fut. mid. προσάξομαι in pass. sense
entry.sense: to bring to or upon, τίς δαίμων τόδε πῆμα προσήγαγε; Od.; θυσίας πρ. τινί Hdt.; πρ. πάντα to furnish, supply, Xen.
to put to, add, ἅμα ἠγόρευε καὶ ἔργον προσῆγε Hdt.
to put to, bring to, move towards, apply, like Lat. applicare, τὴν ἄνω γνάθον πρ. τῇ κάτω Id.; ὀφθαλμὸν πρ. κεγχρώμασι to apply the eye closely to the eyelet-holes, Eur.
of meats, to set before, βρώματά τινι Xen.
metaph., πρ. ὅρκον τινί to put an oath to him, make him take it, Hdt.
in military sense, to bring up for the attack, move on towards, τῇ Ποτιδαίᾳ τὸν στρατόν Thuc.; στρατιὰν πρ. πρὸς πολεμίους, πρ. μηχανὰς πόλει Id.
metaph., τὰς ἀνάγκας Id.; πρ. τόλμαν to apply or put forth daring, Eur.
πρ. φόρον to bring in tribute, Thuc.
to bring to or before, τῷ Κύρῳ τοὺς αἰχμαλώτους Xen.: to introduce, τινὰ πρὸς τὸν δῆμον, πρὸς τὴν βουλήν Thuc.; πρ. τοὺς πρέσβεις Dem.
Pass. to attach oneself to, τινι Id.
seemingly intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν, στρατόν, etc.), to draw near, approach, esp. in a hostile sense, Xen.
(sub. ναῦν) to bring to, come to land, Polyb.
Mid. to bring or draw to oneself, attach to oneself, bring over to one's side, Lat. sibi conciliare, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; πάντων πρ. ὄμματα to draw all eyes upon oneself, Xen.
absol. to draw to oneself, embrace, Eur., Ar.
c. inf. to induce one to do a thing, ἡ Σφὶγξ σκοπεῖν ἡμᾶς προσήγετο Soph.; προσάξομαι δάμαρτ’ ἐᾶν σε will induce her to suffer thee, Eur.
to take to oneself, to take up, ὀστᾶ Id.; τὰ ναυάγια Thuc.:— to procure, import, Xen.; τὰ προσαχθέντα imports, Id.
one who brings to: πρ. λημμάτων one who hunts for another's profit, a jackal, Dem.
a bringing to or up to, a bringing up, Polyb.
a bringing to, acquisition, ξυμμάχων Thuc.
(intr.) a solemn approach, as at festivals or in supplication, Hdt.
approach, access to a person, esp. to a king's presence, Xen., NTest.
attractive, persuasive, Thuc., Luc.
to sing to, Theocr.
πρ. τραγῳδίαν to sing the songs in a Tragedy to music, Ar.
to harmonise, chime in, τινί with one, Soph.; absol., Plat.
to raise high in air, Aesch.
Mid. to choose for oneself, ἑαυτῷ πρ. τινα to take for one's companion or ally, Lat. cooptare, Hdt.
generally, to choose in addition to, τινά τινι Thuc., Xen.
to rush to, Od.; ὀμίχλη πρ. ὄσσοις a cloud comes over my eyes, Aesch.
to ask besides, αἷμα πρ. to demand more blood, Aesch.; πρ. μισθόν to demand higher pay, Xen.
c. acc. pers. to importune, ask an alms of, Hdt.: c. acc. rei, to beg for a thing, Eur.: c. dupl. acc. to beg somewhat of one, Id., Xen.:—absol. to beg hard, to be importunate, Eur., Ar.
a beggar, Luc.
to accuse besides, τινα Plut.
to shoot like a javelin, Luc.
to hear besides, Xen.
Dep. to skirmish with besides, Polyb.
one must bring to or near, Plat.
one must introduce, Arist.
to rub or smear upon, τί τινι Od.
Dep. to jump up at one, like a dog, Xen.
near the Alps, Strab.
Mid., to answer, τινα Theocr.
Pass, with fut. mid. to yield milk besides, Theocr.
to come to aid, τινί Il.
to put on over, τί τινα Ar.
to go up or mount besides, Xen.:— to rise higher, as a swollen river, Polyb.: metaph., πρ. τῷ Ῥωμύλῳ to go back to Romulus, Plut.

a going up, ascent, κλίμακος προσαμβάσεις ascent by means of ladders, i. e. scaling ladders, Aesch., Eur.; πρ. Eur.; τειχέων πρ. a place where they may be approached, Id.; δωμάτων πρ. i. e. the steps leading to the house, Id.
to read besides, Aeschin.
to force or constrain besides, Thuc.
to bring under command or discipline, Id.
c. acc. et inf. to force one to do, Hhymn.; πρ. τινὰ παρεῖναι, ὁμολογεῖν Xen.; but inf. omitted, τοὺς μὴ δεχομένους τὰς σπονδὰς πρ. (sc. δέχεσθαι) Thuc.
to announce besides, Plat.
to record besides, Luc.
seemingly intr. πρ. τῇ γῇ to put back to land, Plut.
to lift up besides: Mid. to take upon oneself besides, πόλεμον Thuc.
to destroy besides, τἀληθές Arist.
of an oracle, to give an answer besides, Plat.; πρ. τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Dem.
Pass. to be spent besides, Hdt.
to disclose besides, Strab.
that on which one leans, Anth.
to take in besides, Dem.:—Pass., πλειόνων προσαναλαμβανομένων εἰς τὴν σύγκλητον, of a batch of new senators, Plut.
to recal to strength: intr. to recover, Polyb.
to lavish or consume besides, Plat., Dem.
Mid. or Pass. to sleep beside, τινι Plut.
to fill up or replenish besides, Arist., NTest.:—Mid. to add so as to fill up, Plat.
to break off besides, Plut.
to shake up or about besides:— Pass. to be roused still further, Polyb.; δίκαι αὐτῷ προσανεσείοντο were being promoted against him, Plut.
to hold back besides, τὸν ἵππον Plut.
to rise up towards, Eur.
Mid. to take an additional burthen on oneself, Xen.; but, πρ. τί τινι to contribute of oneself to another, NTest.
προσανατίθεσθαί τινι to take counsel with one, Id.
to run back, retrace past events, Polyb.
Mid. to rub oneself upon or against a thing, to frequent the gymnasium, Theophr.
to declare, publish, order besides, Xen.
to creep up to, Plut.
to ask or inquire further, Plat.
to find out besides, Strab.
to wait patiently for a thing, c. dat., Polyb.:—also c. acc., Id.
rising up against, uphill, steep, Lat. adversus, Pind., Thuc.
metaph. arduous, irksome, adverse, Hdt., Eur., etc.
of persons, adverse, hostile, τινί to one, Eur.; πρ. πρός τι setting oneself against it, Xen.
Mid. to take hold of one another, τῶν χειρῶν by the hands, Strab.
to demand besides, Polyb.
to announce besides, Xen.
to require from as a duty besides, Luc.
to deceive besides, Strab.
to threaten besides, ap. Dem.
Pass. to rely mainly upon, Polyb.
to throw away besides, Ar.
to demonstrate besides, Plat.
to declare besides, Strab.
to pay as a debt besides, Dem.
to add by way of completing, Strab.
Dep. to answer with some addition, Plat.
to kill besides, Xen.
to destroy besides or also, Hdt., Eur.:—Mid. aor2 -ωλόμην: perf. -όλωλα:— to perish besides or with others, Hdt., Dem.
to lose besides, τὴν ἀρχήν Hdt., Plat.
to send away or off besides, Ar.
to propose a further difficulty, Arist.
to despatch besides, Thuc.
to defraud of besides, τῆς νίκης Dem.
to estimate besides, Dem.
to pay besides, Plat.
to carry off besides:—Pass. to be returned besides as liable to taxation, Dem.
one must apply, τινί τι Plat.
to fasten or attach to, attribute, τί τινι Il., Soph., etc.:—in bad sense, to fix upon, μή τι χρέος ἐμᾷ πόλει προσάψῃς Soph.
c. acc. only, to apply, Eur.
to deliver or confide to, ναυτικόν τινι Xen.
intr. to be added, εἰ κακοῖς κακὰ προσάψει Soph.
Mid. to fasten oneself upon, to lay hold of, reach, touch, Xen.
to meddle with, c. gen., Aeschin.
to fit to:—intr., to be fitted to, ἐπίσσωτρα προσαρηρότα tires firmly fitted, Il.: an ionic perf. pass. προσαρήρεται Hes.
to dash against, πρ. ναῦς σκοπέλοις Plut.
to yield needful aid, succour, assist, τινί Soph.; absol., Id., Eur.
towards the north, Strab.
to fit to, attach closely to, τί τινι Eur.; εἴς τι Plat.
metaph. to adapt, Id.
c. acc. only, πρ. τὴν χεῖρα to fit it on to the stump, Xen.; πρ. δῶρα to add fitting gifts, Soph.
intr. to attach oneself: to suit or agree with a thing, τινί Plat.; πρός τι Xen.
to fasten or attach to, τί τινι Babr.:—Pass. to be fastened or attached to, προσηρτημένον τῷ καλῷ τὸ ἀγαθόν Xen.: to accrue to one, λῆμμα προσήρτηται Dem.
to deprive of civil rights besides, Dem.: Pass., perf. part. προσητιμωμένος Id.
Pass. to wither away upon, πέτραις Aesch.
to speak to, address, accost, τινά Il., Trag.
c. acc. to address words to one, Il.
to speak of, τύχαν σέθεν Eur.:—Pass., ἀδελφὴ προσηυδώμην was addressed as sister, Soph.
near a farm-yard, rustic, Eur.
to burn against, πρὶν πυρὶ θερμῷ πόδα τις προσαύσῃ Soph.
to take away besides, Dem.
Dep. to arrive at a place or to arrive and join a force, Thuc.
to approach, τινα Anth.
to cause to revolt besides, Thuc.

entry.note: fut. -βήσομαι aor2 προσέβην 3rd sg. aor1 mid. προσεβήσατο epic -ετο
entry.sense: to step upon, Hom., Il.; πρὸς τὸ κάτω τοῦ τόξου τῷ ἀριστερῷ ποδὶ πρ., so as to get a purchase in drawing it, Xen.
to go to or towards, approach, c. acc. loci, Hom., etc.; —c. dat., Plat.
to mount, ascend, Hdt., Soph.
absol. to step on, advance, Soph.
metaph. to come upon, τίς σε προσέβα μανία; Id.; ἄλλοις ἄλλα πρ. ὀδύνα Eur.

to strike or dash against, τί τινι Il.; ἀψῖδα πέτρῳ πρ. letting it dash against, Eur.; τὸν πρὶν ὄλβον ἕρματι πρ. to wreck his happiness on a rock, Aesch.; πρ. θηρία τινί to set them on him, Dem.; πρ. δόρυ τινί Eur.:—without any notion of violence, to put to, apply, μαλακὰν χέρα πρ. [ἕλκει] of a surgeon, Pind.; πρ. παρειὰν παρηίδι Eur.; ὄμματα τέκνοις Id.

to assign to, procure for, κέρδος τινί Hdt.; πρ. Λακεδαιμονίοις Ὀλυμπιάδα to give them the honour of an Olympic victory, Id.; πρ. κακὸν τῇ πόλει Aesch.; εὔκλειαν σαυτῇ Soph.; πρ. δεῖμά τινι, Lat. incutere timorem alicui, Eur.
with acc. of the object struck, ἀρούρας προσβάλλειν, of the Sun, to strike the earth with his rays, Hom.; of smells, βροτοῦ [ὀσμὴ] με προσέβαλε Ar.
metaph. to attend to a thing or to add, Soph.
μή μ’ ἀνάγκῃ προσβάλῃς τάδ’ εἰκαθεῖν do not drive me by force to give way, Id.
intr. to strike against, to make an attack or assault upon, τινί Aesch., etc.; πρὸς τὸ τεῖχος Hdt.:—absol. to attack, charge, Id.; προσβαλὼν αἱρεῖ τὴν πόλιν by assault, Xen.
to put in with a ship, ἐς τὸν λιμένα Thuc.; πρὸς Τάραντα Id.; c. dat., Σικελίᾳ Id.
Mid. to throw oneself upon, attack, τινα Il.
a means of approach, access, Hdt., Thuc.; προσβάσεις πύργων means of approaching the towers, Eur.
accessible, τινι Xen.; χωρίον ἔνθα οὐ προσβατὸν θανάτῳ where was no point accessible by death, Id.
Dep. to compel, constrain, τινα Ar.
aor1 προσβιασθῆναι, in pass. sense, to be forced or hard pressed, Thuc.
to make to approach, bring nearer, τινά Plat.
metaph. to bring over, persuade, εὖ προσβιβάζεις με Ar., Xen.: of things, πρ. τι κατὰ τὸ εἰκός to bring it into accordance with probability, Plat.
to live longer, Plut.
to look at or upon, τινά Trag.:—rarely c. dat., Xen., Plut.
of things, to regard, Soph., Dem.
Mid. to call to oneself, call in, Hdt.
to come to aid, come up with succour, προσβωθῆσαι ἐς τὴν Βοιωτίην Hdt.: absol., Thuc.
a putting to, application, e. g. of the touchstone (v. βάσανος), Aesch.; of the cupping-glass, Arist.; φίλιαι πρ. προσώπων, of kisses, Eur.; absol. a kiss or embrace, Id.
(from intr. sense) a falling upon, an attack, assault, Hdt., etc.; πρ. Ἀχαιΐς an assault of the Achaeans, Aesch.
generally, attacks, assaults, visitations, προσβολαὶ Ἐρινύων Id.; μιασμάτοιν Id.

without any hostile sense, an approach, a means of approach, προσβολὴν ἔχειν τῆς Σικελίας to afford a means of entering Sicily, Thuc.:—of ships, a landing-place, place to touch at, Id.; ἐν προσβολῇ εἶναι to be a place for ships to touch at, Id.
exposed to the north, Eur.
somewhat shallow, Strab.
near the earth, near the ground, Luc.
to look laughing at one, τινά Hdt., Eur., etc.; c. acc. cogn., προσγελᾶτε τὸν πανύστατον γέλων smile your last smile upon me, Eur.
metaph., like Lat. arrideo, to delight, ὀσμὴ βροτείων αἱμάτων με προσγελᾷ Aesch.
Dep.
to come or go to, to attach oneself to another, τινι Hdt., etc.; τοῖς προσγιγνομένοις by the reinforcements, Thuc.
generally, to be added, accrue, Lat. accedere, Hdt., Eur., etc.
to come to, happen to, τινι Soph.
to write besides, add in writing, Dem.:—Pass., τὰ προσγεγραμμένα conditions added to a treaty, Xen.:—Mid. to cause to be registered besides, Dem.
to exercise at or in a thing, Plat.:—Pass., προσγεγυμνασμένος πολέμῳ Plut.
to lend besides: Mid. to have lent one, i. e. to borrow, besides, Xen.
to spend besides, Luc.
a reception, Soph.
needing besides, yet lacking, τινος Plat.

entry.note: doric ποτι-δέρκομαι fut. -δέρξομαι aor2 act. -έδρᾰκον aor1 pass. -εδέρχθην perf. -δέδορκα
entry.sense: Dep.
to look at, behold, Od., Aesch., etc.
to look closely, Soph.
tied to a thing, τινι Eur.

entry.note: ionic -δέκομαι fut. -δέξομαι epic aor2 part. sync. ποτιδέγμενος
entry.sense: Dep.
to receive favourably, accept, Hdt.: to receive hospitably, Soph., etc.: to admit into a place, Thuc.: to admit to citizenship, Plat.
to admit an argument, Id.

epic part. ποτιδέγμενος, waiting for or expecting, Hom.; so, προσδεκομένους τοιοῦτο οὐδέν Hdt.; τῷ Νικίᾳ προσδεχομένῳ ἦν was according to his expectation, Thuc.: —c. acc. et inf. fut. to expect that . . , Hdt., etc.
absol. to wait patiently, Hom.
to bind on or to attach, Hdt.
act.
to need besides, c. gen., Eur.
impers. προσδεῖ there is still need of, c. gen. rei, Thuc., Xen., etc.; c. inf., ἔτι προσδεῖ ἐρέσθαι Plat.
dep. προσ-δέομαι.
