of persons, to call together, Eur.:—so in Mid., Od., etc.: —Pass. to come together, assemble, Hdt., attic
to collect, get together, στασιώτας Hdt.; σ. στρατόν to levy an army, Lat. conscribere, Thuc.
partner of the bed, Eur.
adv. collectively, in sum, in short, Theogn., Aesch., etc.
to finish together with, c. dat., Anth.
one must seize together, Eur.
to be seized, Luc.
a partner, accomplice, assistant, Aesch.; τινός in a thing, Eur., etc.
a taking together: a seizing, arresting, ποιεῖσθαι ξύλληψιν to arrest, Thuc.
conception, Plut.
a gathering, collecting, Thuc.: metaph., ἐν γενείου ξυλλογῇ τριχώματος in the first harvest of a beard, i. e. in early manhood, Aesch.
a levying of soldiers, Lat. conscriptio, Xen.
a summary, recapitulation, Dem.
(from Pass.) an assembly, meeting, Hdt., Lys.
Dep.
to collect and bring at once before the mind, to compute fully, sum up, Hdt., Dem.
to collect or conclude from premisses, Lat. colligere, Plat., Dem.
to conclude by way of syllogism, Arist.:—perf. in pass. sense, συλλελογισμένα logically concluded, Id.
collected from divers places, Luc.
computation, Plat.
a conclusion, inference from premisses, Id.
to be concluded, Plat.
neut. συλλογιστέον one must compute or conclude, Arist.
of or for concluding, syllogistic, Arist.:—adv. -κῶς, Id.
an assembly, Hdt., attic; σύλλογον ποιεῖσθαι to convene an assembly, opp. to διαλύειν, Hdt., etc.:— a muster of forces, Xen.
metaph. collectedness, presence of mind, Eur.
Mid. or Pass. to bathe together, Plut.
to incorporate soldiers, Plut.
a soldier of the same λόχος, Hdt.
to hurt or mortify together, σ. τινα αὑτῷ to make him share one's grief, Arist.
Pass., fut. -λυπηθήσομαι and in mid. form -λυπήσομαι: — to sympathise or condole with, τινί Hdt., attic
Pass. to go mad with, τινι, Anth.
to help in loosing, Eur.:— to help to solve a difficulty or end a quarrel, Soph.
to rest under the same roof, Aesch.; cf. καταλύω.
paring the nails, Anth.

entry.note: fut. -βήσομαι perf. -βέβηκα 3rd pl. sync. -βεβᾶσι ionic inf. -βεβάναι aor2 συνέβην inf. συμβῆναι 3rd sg. aor1 subj. ξυμβᾰθῇ perf. inf. βεβάσθαι
entry.sense: Pass., to stand with the feet together, opp. to διαβαίνειν, Xen.
to stand with, so as to assist, Soph.; σ. κακοῖς, i. e. increase them, Eur.
to meet, τινί Xen.; συμβέβηκεν οὐδαμοῦ has never come in my way, has had naught to do with me, Eur.
metaph. to come together, come to an agreement, come to terms, Lat. convenire, τινί with another, Hdt., attic; c. inf., σ. ὑπήκοοι εἶναι Thuc.; Pass., of the terms, to be agreed on, Id.
of things, to coincide or correspond with, c. dat., Hdt., attic:—absol., Trag., etc.
to fall to one's lot, c. dat. pers., Eur., Dem.

of events, to come to pass, happen, Lat. contingere, Aesch., Plat., etc.:—impers., συνέβη μοι, c. inf., it happened to me to do a thing, Hdt., etc.; also c. acc. it happened that I did, Id., Thuc., etc.: ξυμβαίνει c. inf. it happens to be, i. e. it is so and so, Plat.: —τὸ συμβεβηκός a chance event, contingency, Dem.; so, τὰ συμβαίνοντα Xen.; τὰ συμβάντα Id.
joined with Adverbs or Adjectives, to turn out in a certain way, ὀρθῶς συνέβαινε Hdt.; κακῶς, καλῶς ξυμβῆναι Xen., etc.
of consequences, to result, follow, Thuc.: so, of logical conclusions, Plat.
to join in the feast of Bacchus or Bacchic revelry, Eur., Plat.
joining in Bacchic revelry, Eur.

entry.note: fut. -βᾰλῶ aor2 -έβᾰλον inf. -βᾰλεῖν fut. -βέβληκα Pass., aor1 -εβλήθην aor2 συμβλήτην, -βλήμεναι, Mid. σύμβλητο, -βληντο, -βληται, -βλήμενος with fut. συμβλήσομαι 2nd sg. συμβλήσεαι
entry.sense: to throw together, dash together, Il., Eur., etc.: to unite their streams, of rivers, Il.: —so in Mid., Hdt.
to throw together, collect, Xen.
intr. to come together, meet, Aesch., Soph., Xen.
to close the eyes, in sleep or death, Aesch.; but, ποῖον ὄμμα συμβαλῶ; how shall I meet her eyes with mine? Eur.
generally, to join, unite, σ. σχοινία to twist ropes, Ar.; ξ. δεξιάς to join hands, Eur.; σ. λόγους Id.:—Pass., κριθὰς ἵπποις συμβεβλημένας barley thrown in heaps before them, Xen.

σ. συμβόλαιά τινι or πρός τινα to make a contract with a person, to lend him money on bond, Dem.; συμβόλαιον εἰς τἀνδράποδα συμβεβλημένον money lent on the security of the slaves, Id.; absol., in same sense, Plat.

to contribute, lend, Xen.:—so in Mid., Hdt., etc.; τὸ μὴ ἀγανακτεῖν ἄλλα πολλὰ συμβάλλεται many circumstances contribute to my feeling no vexation, Plat.; συμβάλλεσθαι εἰς or πρός τι to contribute towards, Hdt., attic; c. gen. partit., ξυμβάλλεται πολλὰ τοῦδε δείματος many things contribute [their share] of this fear, i. e. join in causing it, Eur.
συμβάλλεσθαι γνώμας to add one's opinion to that of others, Hdt.

συμβάλλειν λόγους to converse, and συμβάλλειν, absol., like Lat. conferre for conferre sermonem, σ. πρός τινα NTest.:—so in Mid., συμβάλλεσθαι λόγους Xen.; συμβάλλεσθαί τι to have something to say, Plat., etc.
to bring men together in hostile sense, to set them together, match them, Il., etc.:—Mid. to join in fight.
intr. to come together, engage, Il.: to come to blows, τινί with another, Hdt., Aesch.
σ. μάχην, Lat. committere pugnam, Eur.; ἔχθραν σ. τινί Id.;— metaph., συμβαλεῖν ἔπη κακά to bandy reproaches, Soph.
Mid. to fall in with one, meet him by chance, c. dat., Hom., who uses epic aor2 ξύμβλητο and fut. συμβλήσομαι solely in this sense.
to put together, and in Pass. to correspond, tally, Aesch.
to compare, τί τινι Hdt.; ἓν πρὸς ἕν Id.; τι πρός τι Plat.:—Pass., τὸ Βαβυλώνιον τάλαντον συμβαλλόμενον πρὸς τὸ Εὐβοεικόν the Babyl. talent being compared with, reduced to, the Euboic, Hdt.
in Mid. to put together, reckon, compute, Id.
to compare one's own opinion with facts, and so to conclude, infer, conjecture, interpret, Pind., Soph., etc.:—so in Mid. to make out, understand, Hdt.
in Mid. to agree upon, fix, settle, Xen.
a chance, casualty, Luc.
II, to wish to make a league or covenant with another, τινί Thuc.
to rule or reign together with, τινί Luc.
an agreement, arrangement, treaty, Hdt., Eur.; δὸς ξύμβασιν τέκνοις make them friends, Eur.
tending to agreement, conciliatory, ξυμβ. λόγοι Thuc.; οὐδὲν πράξαντες ξυμβατικόν having effected nothing towards an agreement, Id.:—adv., -κῶς ἔχειν to be inclined to agreement, Plut.
hit by several arrows at once, Polyb.
Pass. to be forced together, to be reduced or extorted by force, Dem.
to bring together: Pass. to be joined or knit together, framed, NTest.
metaph. to bring together, reconcile, Hdt.; σ. τινά τινι to reconcile one to another, Thuc.
to put together, compare, examine, Plat.
to prove logically, Arist., NTest.
to teach, instruct, NTest.
leading to reconciliation, Plut.
a companion, partner, Arist.: a husband or wife, Anth.
to live with another, c. dat., Dem.; in pl. to live together, ὡς κοινῇ συμβιωσόμενοι Plat.
one must live with, τινί Arist.

entry.note: συμβλητός, ή, όν verb. adj. of συμβάλλω
entry.sense: comparable, capable of being compared, absol. or c. dat., Arist.
to shout together with, τινί Xen.
c. acc. to call on others at once, Id.
joint aid or assistance, Thuc.
to render joint aid, join in assisting, Thuc., Xen.
like σύμβολον, a mark or sign to conclude from, a token, Hdt.: a symptom, Soph.

at Athens, a contract, covenant, bond, in acknowledgment of a loan, Oratt.; in pl., of a single contract, Plat., etc.; τὰ Ἀθήναζε καὶ τὰ Ἀθήνηθεν συμβ. a bond for money lent on freights to and from Athens, Dem.
generally, an engagement, Eur.
intercourse, Plut.
of or concerning contracts, Thuc.
to meet or fall in with, τινί Aesch.
a coming together, meeting, joining, Xen.: the juncture of two parts, the end, Lat. commissura, Hdt., Plat.
in hostile sense, an encounter, engagement, battle, Hdt., Aesch.
= συμβόλαιον II, a contract, covenant, Arist.; in Ar. Ach. there is a play on signfs. II and III, encounter and accounts, charge and charges.
in pl., συμβολαί were contributions for a common meal, πίνειν ἀπὸ συμβολῶν, like de symbolis esse in Terent., attic; the entertainment itself, a picnic, Xen.
signifying by a sign or symbol, symbolical, figurative, Luc.
a sign or token by which one infers a thing, Trag.; λαμπάδος τὸ σύμβολον the token of the beacon-fire, Aesch.:—often in pl., of marks on the body, Eur.; of omens, Aesch.
a pledge or pawn, on which money was advanced, Lys.
in pl. tallies, Lat. tesserae hospitales, i.e. the halves of a bone or coin, which two persons broke between them, each keeping one piece, Hdt., Eur., etc.
at Athens, a ticket, counter, Lat. tessera, such as were given to the dicasts, on presenting which they received their fee, Dem.
a permit or licence to reside, given to aliens, Ar.; a ticket given by each person who joined in a picnic, to be presented for payment at the end (cf. συμβολή IV), Id.
in Eccl. the distinctive mark of Christians, a confession of faith, a creed, Lat. symbolum.

in legal phrase, σύμβολα were covenants between two states for protection of commerce, Dem., etc.; σύμβολα ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς πόλιν to make a commercial treaty with a state, τὰ σ. συγχέειν to violate such treaty, Id.
an augury, omen, Aesch., Xen.
advice given, Xen., Arist.
to be given as advice, Thuc.
-τέον, one must advise, τινί Isocr.
of or for advising, deliberative, of orators, Arist.
to advise, counsel, Lat. consulere alicui, c. dat. pers. et inf., to advise one to do a thing, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
without the inf., σ. τινί τι Hdt., Plat.; σ. τι to recommend a measure, Hdt., attic:—Pass., τὰ συμβουλευόμενα the advice given, Xen.
absol. to advise, give advice, Soph.; ὁ συμβουλεύων or -εύσας, an adviser, Lat. auctor sententiae, Arist.
Mid. to consult with a person, i. e. ask his advice, Lat. consulere aliquem, c. dat., Hdt., etc.: absol. to consult, deliberate, Xen.
counsel, consultation, deliberation, debate, Plat.
advice or counsel given, Hdt., Xen.; in pl. counsels, Xen.
counsel, NTest.
a council, Plut.
Dep.
to will or to wish with another, c. dat., Eur.
to agree with, τινι Plat.:—absol. to consent, Id.

an adviser, counsellor, Hdt., Soph., etc.; as fem., Xen.:—c. gen. pers. one's adviser, Aesch., etc.; also, σ. τινι Ar., etc.:—but c. gen. rei, σ. λόγου τοῦδέ μοι γένεσθε be my counsellors in this matter, Aesch.; also, περί or ὑπέρ τινος Id., Isocr.:— ξύμβουλός εἰμι = συμβουλεύω, to advise, c. inf., Aesch.
to cram or huddle together, Ar.
worshipped on a common altar, Strab.
a fellow-disciple, Plat.

entry.note: aor. 2 συνεμάνην intr. perf. act. συμμέμηνα
entry.sense: Pass., to be mad together, join in madness, τινι with one, Luc.
to learn along with another, c. dat., Xen.: absol. to share in the knowledge of a thing, Soph.; ὁ συμμαθών one that is accustomed to a thing, Xen.
to seize or grasp together, Hom.
to bear witness with or in support of another, c. dat., Soph., Thuc.; τι to a fact, Solon., Xen.; also, σ. τινι πάντα ὡς ἀληθῆ λέγει Xen.
a fellow-witness, Soph.
to whip or lash along with or together, Luc.
to be an ally, to be in alliance, Aesch., Thuc.:—generally, to help, aid, succour, τινί Soph., etc.:—Pass. to be assisted, Luc.
an alliance offensive and defensive (opp. to an ἐπιμαχία, defensive), Hdt., etc.: συμμαχίαν ποιεῖσθαι πρός τινα Id.; τινί Thuc.
generally, the duty of an ally, Aesch.
= τὸ συμμαχικόν, the body of allies, Hdt., Thuc.: also, the country of one's allies, Thuc.
an allied or auxiliary force, Id., Xen.
of or for alliance, θεοὶ ξ. the gods invoked at the making of an alliance, Thuc.
τὸ συμμαχικόν, the auxiliaries, allied forces, Hdt., Thuc.
a treaty of alliance, Thuc.: τὰ -κά matters respecting alliances, Xen.
adv. -κῶς, like an ally, Isocr.
allied, Thuc., Xen.; ξ. πόλις an allied state, Thuc.; also ἡ σ. (without πόλις) Id.
= τὸ ξυμμαχικόν, the body of allies, Id.

entry.note: fut. οῦμαι aor1 συνεμαχεσάμην perf. συμμεμάχημαι
entry.sense: Dep.:— to fight along with others, to be an ally, auxiliary, Xen.: generally, to help, succour, τινι Id.; τὸ οἰκὸς ἐμοὶ συμμάχεται probability is on my side, Hdt.
fighting along with, allied with, τινι Hdt., attic: as Subst. an ally, and in pl. allies, Hdt., attic
of things, συμμάχῳ δορί Aesch.; νόμος σύμμαχος τῷ θέλοντι Hdt.; c. gen. rei, ἀρετὴ τῶν ἔργων σύμμαχος Xen.
to sway jointly, Anth.
to help in changing, 3rd sg. συμμεθιστᾷ (from -ιστάω) Strab.
Pass., with aor2 et perf. act., to change places along with another, Plut.
to exercise or practise with or together, Anth.
to hold together, keep together, Thuc., etc.: of treaties or agreements, to hold, continue, Hdt., Thuc.
to distribute in shares: Mid. to take share in or with, c. dat., NTest.
a being in the same meridian, Strab.
to change along with other things, τί τινι Anth., Plut.:—Pass. to change sides and take part with, τινί Aeschin.
intr. in Act. to change with or together, Arist.
Pass. to change one's habits along with another, c. dat., Plut.
to change along with others, c. dat., Aeschin.
Pass. to be borne off together, Plut.
Dep. to take charge of a thing with others, Isae.
to partake of a thing with others, take part in it with others, c. dat. pers. et gen. rei, Eur.; with gen. rei only, Id., Xen.
Pass. to be raised together, Strab.
to emigrate along with another, c. dat., Plut.
partaking with another in a thing, the partner of another, NTest.
to measure by comparison with another thing:—Pass.,
ἦμαρ συμμετρούμενον χρόνῳ this day measured by calculation of time, Soph.
absol. to be commensurate with, Id.
οἷς ὁ βίος ξυνεμετρήθη who had their life measured out, Thuc.
Mid. to measure for oneself, compute exactly, Hdt.; ξυνεμετρήσαντο [τὸ τεῖχος] ταῖς ἐπιβολαῖς τῶν πλίνθων calculated its height by counting the courses of bricks, Thuc.
commeasurement, Thuc.
commensurability, Arist.
symmetry, due proportion, Plat., etc.

commensurate with another thing, Eur.: exactly fitting, Aesch.; τῷδε τἀνδρὶ ξ. being of like age with, Soph.; ποίᾳ σύμμετρος τύχῃ; coincident with what chance? i. e. in the very nick of time, Id.; v. infr. III. 2.
commensurable, Arist.
in measure with, proportionable, exactly suitable, Isocr., etc.
absol. in right measure, in due proportion, symmetrical, opp. to ὑπερβάλλων and ἐλλείπων, Plat., etc.
generally, fitting, meet, due, Aesch.;— σύμμετρος ὡς κλύειν within fit distance for hearing, Soph.
adv. -τρως, Isocr., etc.
in due time, Eur.
Dep. to take counsel with or together, Il.
Dep.
to help to provide or procure, Xen.
to form plans with another, c. dat., Plut.
promiscuously with others, c. dat., Hdt.
commingled, promiscuous, Soph., Eur., etc.
c. dat. commingled with, Aesch.

entry.note: and -ύω 3rd sg. imperat. συμμίγνυ epic and ionic, pres. συμμίσγω fut. -μίξω Mid., fut. -μίξομαι
entry.etym: Mid., fut. -μίξομαι also in pass. sense
entry.sense: to mix together, commingle, Hhymn.; to mix one thing with another, τί τινι Hdt., attic; c. acc. only, συμμίξαντες τὰ στρατόπεδα having combined them, Hdt.:—Pass., of a river, to be mingled with another river, c. dat., Il.: to join forces, of two armies, Thuc.:—metaph., οὐδείς [ἐστι] τῷ κακὸν οὐ συνεμίχθη there is none who has not misery as an ingredient in his nature, Hdt.; συμμιγέντων τούτων πάντων when all these things happened together, Id.
to unite, θεοὺς γυναιξί Hhymn.:—Pass. to have intercourse with, c. dat., Hdt., Aesch.
metaph., σ. τινὰ τύχᾳ to make him acquainted with fortune, Pind.; πρῆγμα συμμῖξαί τινι to communicate a matter to another, Hdt.

intr. in Act. to have intercourse with, to associate or communicate with others, c. dat., Theogn., Hdt., etc.; σ. πρός τινα to join him, Xen.:—generally, to meet for conversation or traffic, Hdt.; σ. τινί to converse with, Id., Eur.
in hostile sense, to meet in close fight, come to blows, engage, τινί with one, Hdt., etc.
generally, to meet, Xen.
commingled, promiscuous, Hes., Soph.: esp. of troops, irregular, Hdt., Thuc. adv. -τως, Strab.
a joint-imitator, NTest.
Pass. to bear in mind with, Dem.
commixture, τινος πρός τι Plat.
intercourse, Plut.
to join with in hating, Polyb.

a co-partnership or company: at Athens, after 377 B. C., the 1200 wealthiest citizens were divided into 20 συμμορίαι or companies, 2 in each tribe (φυλή); each being called on in its turn to discharge extraordinary expenses, Xen., Dem.
united for purposes of taxation, Thuc.
Pass. to be conformed to, τινι NTest.
conformed to, c. gen., NTest.
to share in toil with, τινί Eur.
to initiate together, Plut.
to be shut up, to close, be closed, of wounds, Il.; συμμεμυκώς with closed eyes, Plat.
fellow-feeling, sympathy, Arist.
to sympathise, Isocr., etc.
sympathizing with, τινί Arist.: absol. sympathetic, Id.
to sing paeans with, τινί Dem.
to teach together, educate at the same time, Xen.: Pass. to be educated with others, Isocr.
to play or sport with another, c. dat., Soph.; absol., Hdt.; c. acc. cogn., μετ’ ἐμοῦ σύμπαιζε τὴν ἑορτήν keep the feast together with me, Ar.
a playmate, playfellow, Plat.:— fem. συμπαίστρια, ἡ, Ar.
to dash against, τί τινι Soph.
intr. to dash together, Eur.
to attend a solemn assembly with another, c. dat., Plut.
to cram in along with, τινά τινι Luc.
to help in canvassing for an office, c. dat., Plut.
Dep.
to be ready at the same time, of fruit ripening, Hdt.
to stand by another, to come in to assist, Thuc.
to shew incidentally at the same time, Strab.
to run along together, Dem.
to join in recommending, τί τινι Ar.: to join in approving, τι Id.
to make to sit beside: so in Mid., Dem.
Mid. also to sit close beside, Plat.
to invite together or at the same time, Xen., Plat.
to ask for at the same time, τι ἀπό τινος Xen.
Dep. to join in exciting, Isocr.
to follow in a parallel line with, keep up with, τινί Isocr., etc.: absol., Xen.
to carry along the coast with one, of a commander, Thuc.; Pass. of the ships, Id.
to bend oneself along with, Luc.
to take along with one, take in as an adjunct, Plat.
to stay along with or among others, c. dat., Thuc.
to mix in together, Ar.
to express assent also, Arist.
Dep. to swim beside together, Luc.
to escort along with others, τὴν παραπομπήν Aeschin.; τὴν ὄψιν σ. τινί to follow him with one's eyes, Plut.
to perish along with or besides, Dem.
to assist in getting ready or bringing about, Xen., Dem.
to stand by so as to assist, c. dat., Aesch.; absol., Ar.
one who stands by to aid, a joint helper or assistant, Soph., Ar.
Pass. to be set in array with others, fight along with them, c. dat., Isocr.
to keep watch together, Dem.
to place alongside of others, Polyb.
to bring up or keep at the same time, of dogs and other animals, Xen.
to run along with, Plut.
to carry along together: — Pass. to rush along together, Xen.
to be present also or at the same time, Xen., etc.
to stand by, to come to help, τινι Id., Dem.
to go beside also or together, 3 sg. imperf. συμπαρῄει, Xen., Aeschin.
Dep. to go in along with, Luc.
Dep. to go along with, accompany, c. dat., Xen., etc.
to assist in causing, φόβον τινί Xen.; in procuring, ἀσφάλειάν τινι Id.
Dep. to fly along with, Luc.
to place beside one also, Pind.
Pass., c. aor2 et perf. act., to stand beside, assist, τινι Soph.
to provoke with or together, Xen.
to urge on with or together, Plut.
acquainted with, τινι Pind.
to pierce through together, Plut.
to send with or at the same time, Hdt., attic
to help in conducting, Lys.
trans. to join in mourning for a thing, τι Isocr.
intr. to mourn together with, τινί Aesch.; absol., Eur.
Dep. to be poor along with another in a thing, τινί τινος Plat.
to join or assist in accomplishing, Eur.:—Mid., συμπεραίνεσθαί τινι ἔχθραν to join fully in enmity with another, Dem.
to decide or conclude absolutely, σ. φροντίδα to make up one's mind, Eur.; κλῇθρα μοχλοῖς σ. to make the doors doubly sure by bars, Id.:—Pass. to be quite finished, Xen.
a conclusion, Arist.
conclusive: adv. -κῶς, Arist.
to destroy with or together, Eur.
to carry about with or together, Xen.:—Pass. to go round with or together, Id.:— Mid. to lead about with oneself, Id.
an assistant in converting others, Plat.
to go round with another, c. dat., Xen.
to run about together, Luc.
to comprehend in a treaty with others, Philipp. ap. Dem.
Mid. to take part together in a thing, c. gen., Luc.
to go round together with, follow along with, τινί Luc.
to walk round or about with, τινί Plat.: absol., οἱ συμπεριπατοῦντες their companions in walking round, Arist.
inter-connexion, Luc.
to help in procuring, Polyb.
to run round together, Luc.
to carry round along with or together, Plat.
Pass. to be carried round together, Id.
συμπεριφέρεσθαί τινι to have intercourse with one, Polyb.: to adapt oneself to circumstances, c. dat., Aeschin.
to be well acquainted with things, Polyb.
Pass. to go about with any one to one's own ruin, Luc.
to pin together, Plut.
Dep. to fly with or together, Luc.
to put together, construct, frame, Pind., Eur., etc.:—Mid. to construct for oneself, Luc.
to make solid, congeal, condense, Il.
put together, constructed, framed, Hdt., Ar.
to press or squeeze together, to grasp closely, Plat.:—Pass. to be squeezed up, Xen.
to drink together, join in a drinking bout, Hdt., Ar., etc.
to fall together, meet in battle, come to blows, Lat. concurrere, Hom., Hdt.: σ. ἐς νείκεα Hdt.: to encounter, κλύδωνι Eur.; νηί Thuc.
generally, to fall in with, meet with accidents, misfortunes, c. dat., Hdt., Soph.
of ailments, events, to fall upon, happen to, c. dat. pers., Aesch., Isocr.; also ἔς τινα Hdt.
absol. to happen or fall out at the same time, concur, Id.
c. part, like τυγχάνω, τόδε συνέπεσε γενόμενον Id.
impers., συνέπεσε, it happened, fell out, came to pass, c. inf., Id.; ξυνέπεσεν εἰς τοῦτο ἀνάγκης ὥστε . . matters came to such a pass that . . , Thuc.; or c. acc. et inf., Id.
to coincide, agree or be in accordance with, τινί Hdt.: absol. to agree exactly, Id.; ἐμοὶ σὺ συμπέπτωκας ἐς ταὐτὸν λόγου have come to exactly the same point with me, Eur.
to fall together, i. e. fall in, collapse, of a house, Lat. concidere, Id., Thuc.; σῶμα συμπεσόν a frame having collapsed from disease, Plat.
συμπίτνω poet. for συμπίπτω, when the penult. is to be short
to fall or dash together, of waves, Aesch.
to concur, Id.; c. dat., Eur.
Pass. to wander about with, Polyb.
to mould or fashion together, γαίης of clay, Hes.:—Pass., Ar.
of speakers and writers, ξυνομολογοῦντες καὶ ξ. by agreeing on an hypothesis and a fiction, Plat.
metaph. to feign or fabricate together, Dem.
to sound by striking together, σ. χερσί to clap with the hands, Il.
several together, Lat. complures, Arist.
to twine or plait together, Plat.; τινί with a thing, Theocr.; συμπλέκοντες τὼ χεῖρε εἰς τοὐπίσω joining their hands behind them, Thuc.
Pass. to be twined together, entwined, entangled, Eur.; ἴχνη συμπεπλεγμένα tracks entangled, crossing in different directions, Xen.

of persons wrestling, to be locked together with another, c. dat., Hdt.: generally, to be engaged in close fight, Dem.: of a ship, to be entangled with her opponent, Hdt.:—then, metaph. to be entangled in, τῇ Σκυθῶν ἐρημίᾳ συμπλακῆναι Ar.; συμπεπλέγμεθα ξένῳ we are entangled or engaged with him, Eur.; of war, to be engaged in, Dem.
intr. in Act., = Pass., Eur.
quite full, Xen.
to sail in company with, τινί Hdt., etc.; absol., Thuc.

striking or dashing together, ξυμπληγάδες πέτραι the justling rocks, i. e. the Κυάνεαι νῆσοι, which were supposed to close in on all who sailed between them, Eur.; also Ξυμπληγάδες (without πέτραι) Id.; also in sg., Id.
with clapping of hands, Theocr.
to multiply or increase together, Xen.
to help to fill or increase, Hdt.
to help to fill, σ. τοῖσι Ἀθηναίοισι τὰς νέας to help them in manning the ships, Hdt.
to fill up, ξ. ἑξήκοντα ναῦς to man them fully, Thuc.
sailing with or together, συμπλ. φιλία friendship of shipmates, Arist.
an intertwining, complication, Plat.
a close struggle or engagement, Id.
sailing with one in a ship, a shipmate, Hdt.; c. dat. pers., Eur.:—poet. of ships, Anth.
metaph. a partner or comrade in a thing, c. gen., Soph.
to breathe together with, τινί Anth.: metaph., ἐμπαίοις τύχαισι σ. to go along with the sudden blasts of fortune, to yield or bow to them, Aesch.
absol. to agree together, conspire, Dem.
to throttle, choke, press closely, NTest.
animated by one breath, in accord with, τινι Anth.
to tie the feet together, bind hand and foot, Ar.:—Pass. to be entangled in a net, Xen.
metaph. to entangle, Lat. impedire, Plat.
to help in doing a thing, Isae.
Pass. to feed together, Eur.
to join in war, Thuc., Xen., etc.; τινί with one, Xen.
to unite into one city:—Pass., Strab.
to join in besieging, to besiege jointly, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
a federal union of states, a confederacy, league, Polyb.
to live as fellow-citizens or members of one state, τισί with others, Thuc.:—Mid., οἱ συμπολιτευόμενοι one's fellow-citizens, Isocr.
a fellow-citizen, Eur.
many together, Plat.
to accompany in a procession, to escort, Aeschin.
to work with or together, to take part in labouring, τινί with one, Aesch., Soph., etc.: also, σ. κακοῖς to take part in evils, Eur.:—absol. to labour or suffer together, Soph., etc.
Dep. to join others in villainy, c. dat. pers., Isocr.
Dep.: to go or journey together, Eur.; τινι with one, Xen., etc.
to come together, of the Senate, Polyb.
to help to destroy, c. dat. pers., Eur.; οἱ συμπεπορθημένοι involved in like ruin, Strab.
to help in procuring, Thuc.:— Mid. to do so for oneself, Id.
a drinking together, Pind.
to be a συμποσίαρχος, Arist.
the president of a drinking-party, toastmaster, Lat. magister bibendi, Xen., etc.
a drinking-party, symposium, Theogn., Hdt., etc.
the room in which such parties were given, drinking-room, Luc.
a fellow-drinker, boon-companion, Hdt., Eur.
of or for a συμπόσιον, convivial, jolly, Ar.; σ. ἁρμονίαι airs suited for drinking songs, Plat.:— συμποτικός a jolly fellow, Ar.:—comp. -ώτερος, Sup. -ώτατος, Luc.
Dep. to assist in transacting business, c. dat. pers., Plut.
all together, all at once, all in a body, Hom., Hdt., attic; in attic, the Art. is often added in the case of Numerals, πέντ’ ἦσαν οἱ ξύμπαντες Soph.
with collective nouns, the whole, ὁ σ. στρατός Hdt.; στρατὸς σ. Soph.; ξύμπασα πόλις the state as a whole, Thuc.; ξ. γνώμη the general scope (of a speech), Id.
τὸ σύμπαν the whole together, the sum of the matter, Hdt.; τὸ ξύμπαν εἰπεῖν Thuc.
τὸ σύμπαν, as adv. altogether, on the whole, in general, Id., etc.
to suffer together, be affected by the same thing, Plat.
to have a fellow-feeling, sympathise, feel sympathy, Id.
to strike with or together, Eur.
to tread together, trample under foot, Babr.:—Pass. to be trampled under foot, Aeschin.
to bind together:—metaph. of frost, to benumb, Xen.
to join or assist in persuading, Xen.;—also, σ. τοῦ μὴ ἀθυμεῖν to help in persuading against despair, Thuc.:—Pass. to allow oneself to be persuaded at the same time, Aeschin.
a helper, assistant, Hdt., Xen.: c. gen. rei, σ. ὁδοῦ a companion in travel, Soph.

to join or help in doing, τί τινι Aesch., Eur., etc.; σ. τινὶ τἀγαθά to assist one in procuring what is good, Arist.: —c. acc. rei only, Soph.; σ. εἰρήνην to help in negotiating peace, Xen.; c. dat. pers. only, to act with, cooperate with, τινί Thuc., etc.
absol. to lend aid, cooperate, Soph., Xen., etc.; οἱ ξυμπράσσοντες the confederates, Thuc.
intr., σὺν κακῶς πράσσοντι συμπράσσειν κακῶς to share in another's woe, Eur.
Mid. to assist in avenging, συνεπρήξαντο Μενέλεῳ τῆς Ἑλένης ἁρπαγάς Hdt.
befitting, Aesch.
to befit, beseem, Pind.
a fellow-ambassador, Aeschin.
to be a fellow-ambassador, be joined or associated with on an embassy, Dem., Aeschin.: Mid. to join in sending an embassy, Thuc.

entry.etym: = συμπρεσβευτής, but only in pl., Thuc., Dem., etc.

entry.sense: a fellow-presbyter, NTest.

entry.etym: aor2 inf., no pres. in use, cf *πρίαμαι
entry.sense: to buy together, buy up, Arist.
to lead forward together: intr. to move forward with or together, Plut.
a joint-president, Aeschin.
Dep. to have equal desire with, share in eagerness with, τινι Thuc.: absol., Xen.
c. acc. rei, to join zealously in promoting, Id.
c. dat. rei, to take zealous part in, Luc.
c. inf. to share in the desire that . . , Thuc., Xen., etc.
to help in furnishing with means, Eur.
to join in escorting, Hdt., Ar., etc.; σ. τινὰ ναυσίν Thuc.
to clash against, τινί Aesop.
to fold together, fold up and lay by, Soph.
a chance, casualty, Arist.: in bad sense, a mishap, mischance, Thuc.
a collapsing, Strab.
a meeting, Polyb.: in hostile sense, an attack, Id.
pressed together, compressed, Xen.
Dep. to inquire about with another, τί τινι Eur.
to burn up with or together, Eur.
manifest at the same time, quite manifest, Arist.

entry.etym: adverb from part. pres. of συμφέρω
entry.sense: profitably, Isocr.
united, banded together, Il.

entry.note: fut. συνοίσω aor1 συνήνεγκα ionic -ήνεικα aor2 -ήνεγκον perf. -ενήνοχα
entry.sense: Act.,
to bring together, gather, collect, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
to contribute, Aesch., Eur.
to bring into conflict, Aesch.
to bear along with or together, Xen.:—of sufferings and labours, to bear jointly, help to bear, Soph., Eur.: to bear with, excuse, Aesch.
intr. to confer a benefit, be useful or profitable, Hdt., attic
impers. it is of use, is profitable, expedient, c. inf., Aesch., etc.

part. συμφέρων, ουσα, ον, useful, expedient, fitting, Soph., etc.:—in neut. as Subst., συμφέρον, οντος, τό, use, profit, advantage, expediency, Lat. utile, Id., Thuc., etc.:—also in pl., τὰ συμφέροντα Soph., etc.; also in aor. part., τό τῳ ξυνενεγκόν Thuc.
intr., also,
to work with, agree with, assist, τινί Soph., Eur., etc.: — to bear with, give way, τινί Soph.
to fit, suit, τινί Ar., Xen.
of events, to happen, take place, turn out, c. inf., Hdt.
Pass. συμφέρομαι, fut. συνοίσομαι: aor1 -ηνέχθην, ionic -είχθην: perf. -ενήνεγμαι:— to come together, to meet in battle, engage, Lat. congredi, Il., Thuc.: simply, to meet, Plat.
to come to terms, be of one mind or to agree with, τινι Hdt.: —absol. to agree together, be of one mind, concur, come to terms, Id., Soph., etc.
c. dat. rei, to adapt oneself to, acquiesce in, Plat.;—also, συμφέρεται ὡυτὸς εἶναι is found to be one and the same, Hdt.; οὐ συμφέρεται περί τινος does not agree with their story, Id.
of events, to happen, turn out, occur, come to pass, Id., Ar., etc.
impers. it happens, falls out, Hdt.
to flee along with, τινί Hdt., Eur., etc.; σὺν φεύγουσι συμφεύγειν Eur.
to be banished along with or together, ξυνέφυγε τὴν φυγὴν ταύτην shared in this banishment, Plat.
to assent, approve, or agree fully, Aesch., etc.
c. acc. rei, to concede, agree to, grant, Plat., Xen.; absol., ξύμφημί σοι I grant you, Plat.; ξύμφαθι ἢ ἄπειπε say yes or no, Id.
c. acc. et inf. to agree that . . , Soph., Plat.
c. inf. fut. to promise, Xen.
Dep. to sound with, accord with, τινι Plut.
to destroy together or altogether, Eur., Luc.
to decay along with, poet. aor2 pass. συνέφθῐτο, Anth.
sounding together, in concert, Aesch.
to love mutually, Soph.
to be candidate for an honour along with another, Plut.
to take part in a dispute with, side with, τινί Plat., etc.
absol. to join in a disputation, Plut.
to join in philosophic study, Arist.
Dep. to join in zealous efforts, Plut.
to burn to cinders, Eur., Theocr.
to frighten at the same time: — Pass. to be afraid at the same time, Thuc.
to go regularly to a place together, Hdt.: esp. to go to school together, Ar., Dem., etc.; τινί with one, Luc.
a going to school together, Aeschin.
a school-fellow, Plat., Xen.
to join another in killing, c. dat., Eur.
an event, circumstance, chance, hap, Hdt., attic; αἱ ξ. τῶν βουλευμάτων the results, issues of the counsels, Soph.; ξυμφορᾶς ἵν’ ἕσταμεν in what a hazardous state we are, Id.
esp. a mishap, mischance, misfortune, Hdt., attic; συμφορῇ χρῆσθαι to be unfortunate, Hdt.
in good sense, good luck, a happy issue, Trag.
a Lacedaemonian officer, a sort of aide-de-camp, Xen.
to bring together, to gather, collect, heap up, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—Pass. to be collected, Plat.
a bringing together, Plut.
brought together, collected, σ. δεῖπνον, σ. ἑστίασις a meal to which each guest contributes, Lat. coena collatitia, Arist.
happening with, accompanying, λιμὸς ἀεργῷ σύμφορος ἀνδρί hunger is the sluggard's companion, Hes.; c. gen., πενίης σύμφορα Id.

useful, profitable, expedient, suitable, good, c. dat., Id., Thuc.:— σύμφορόν ἐστι = συμφέρει, c. inf., Hdt.; Πλούτῳ συμφορώτατον Ar.:— τὰ σύμφορα what is expedient, Soph., Thuc., etc.; τὸ ὑμέτερον ξ. your plea of expediency, Thuc.:—adv., συμφόρως ἔχειν to be expedient, Xen.; comp. συμφορώτερον, Thuc.; Sup. -ώτατα, Eur., etc.
rarely of persons, ξυμφορώτατοι προσπολεμῆσαι most convenient to make war upon, Thuc.
one who joins in considering, a counsellor, Il.
in accord with, c. gen., Anth.
Mid.:— to join in considering, to take counsel with, c. dat., Od.
τίς τοι συμφράσσατο βουλάς; who imparted his counsels to thee? Id.
to contrive, Hes., Soph.
Act. to mention at the same time, Strab.
to press or pack closely together, Hdt., Xen.
absol. of troops, to close their ranks, form in close order, Xen.
to block up, close, Id.
to be of one mind with, to agree, Polyb.
to consider well, ἃ δέον ἦν ποιεῖν Plut.
to collect oneself, Id.
to have a joint care for, τινός Luc.
watching with, μέλαθρον σύμφρουρον ἐμοί the chamber that keeps watch with me, i. e. in which I lie sleepless, Soph.
of one mind, brotherly, Aesch.:— favouring, propitious, Id.
a fellow-exile, Eur., Thuc.
born with one, congenital, natural, Plat., etc.
adapted by nature, Plut.
attached, adhering, τινί to a thing, Anth.
a fellow-watchman or guard, Thuc., Plat., Xen., etc.
to keep guard along with others, Hdt.: to guard with others, τι Xen.
of the same φυλή, Lat. contribulis: generally, a fellow-countryman, NTest.
of the same stock or race, οἱ σύμφυλοι his congeners, Babr.
commingled, confounded, Eur.
to knead together: beat black and blue, Theocr.:—Pass., Eur.; ψυχὴ συμπέφυρται μετὰ τοῦ κακοῦ Plat.
to blow together:—hence, like Lat. conflare, to beat up, contrive, Ar.
Pass., of the wind, to blow at the same time, Plut.
to plant along with or together: metaph. to have a hand in contriving, Soph.:—Pass. to be implanted also, Xen.

born with one, congenital, innate, natural, inborn, inbred, Pind., Plat.; σ. αἰών our natural age, i. e. old age, Aesch.; νεικέων σ. τέκτων the natural author of strife, i. e. cause of strife natural to the race, Id.; ἐς τὸ σ. according to one's nature, Eur.
c. dat. natural to, Lys.
to make to grow together, Plat.
Pass., with perf. act. συμπέφῡκα, aor2 συνέφῡν:— to grow together, Id., Xen.
to grow to or into, σ. ἀλλήλοις Plat.
to grow up with one, to become natural, Arist.
to agree in sound, be in harmony, Plat.
metaph. to agree with, hold the same opinions with, τινί Id.
to make an agreement or bargain with any one, πρός τινα Xen.; σ. τινί δηναρίου to agree with one for a denarius, NTest.: Pass., συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν it was agreed between you, Id.
to conspire, Arist.
concord or unison of sound, Plat.
metaph. harmony, agreement, Id.
agreeing in sound, in unison, Hhymn., Ar.: generally, echoing to cries, Soph.
metaph. harmonious, friendly, Pind., Soph.; σ. τινι in harmony or agreement with, Plat.
to touch one another, Xen.
to sweep away, of a rapid river, Hdt.
to reckon together, count up, NTest.
voting with, τινι Plat., etc.; σ. τινί τινος voting with one for a thing, Id.:—absol. voting together, of the same opinion, Dem.
to make a noise together, Polyb.
of one mind, at unity, NTest.
a fellow messenger or ambassador, Hdt.
a confined space, Babr.

entry.note: fut. -αγερῶ aor1 συνήγειρα epic ξυνάγειρα Pass., 3rd pl. aor1 συνάγερθεν
entry.sense: to gather together, assemble, Il., Hdt.:—esp. to collect an army, Hdt.:—Pass. to gather together, come together, assemble, Il.; συναγρόμενοι, epic syncop. aor2 pass. part., those assembled, an assembly, Id.
to collect the means of living, Od.; and in Mid. to collect for oneself, Id.
metaph., σ. ἑαυτόν to collect oneself, Plat.:—so in Pass., Id.
to break together, break to pieces, shiver, shatter, Hom.

entry.etym: the fut. in use is συνερῶ
entry.sense: to join in advocating, advocate the same thing with, τί τινι Thuc., Xen.
to join in advising another, τινί Lys.
σ. τινί to speak with or in behalf of a person, support him, advocate his cause, Thuc.: so, c. dat. rei, σ. τινὸς σωτηρίᾳ Dem.
to join in the chase, Anth.

entry.note: imperf. -ῆγον doric -ᾶγον epic -ᾰγον fut. συνάξω aor2 συνήγαγον perf. συνῆχα and συναγήοχα Pass. συνῆγμαι
entry.sense: to bring together, gather together, collect, convene, Hom., Hdt., attic
in hostile sense, to join battle, begin the battle-strife, Il.:—also like συμβάλλω, to match two warriors one against the other, Aesch.:—hence intr., σ. εἰς μέσσον to engage in fight, Theocr.
to bring together, join in one, unite, Hhymn. ( i.e., h. Merc.), Aesch.;— σ. γάμους to contract a marriage, Xen.
to receive into one's house, NTest.
to gather together stores, crops, etc., Xen., etc.
to draw together, so as to make the extremities meet, Hdt., Thuc.: also to draw together, narrow, contract, Hdt.
to contract the brows, Ar.; σ. τὰ ὦτα to prick the ears, of dogs, Xen.
to collect from premises, i. e. to conclude, infer, Lat. colligere, Arist.
one who brings together, a convener, Lys.
one who unites, Plat.
a bringing together, uniting, Plat.
a place of assembly, synagogue, NTest.
σ. πολέμου a levying of war, Thuc.
a gathering in of harvest, Polyb.
a drawing together, contracting, σ. στρατιᾶς a forming an army in column, Plat.; σ. τοῦ προσώπου a pursing up or wrinkling of the face, Isocr.
a collection of writings, Arist.
a conclusion, inference, Id.
bringing together, uniting, Plat.
to share in the anxiety, Polyb.
Dep.
to contend along with, to share in a contest, τινι with one, Thuc., etc.:—generally, ξ. τινι to share in the fortunes of another, Id.
to help, succour, τινι Dem.
absol. to fight on the same side, Thuc.
one who shares with another in a contest, a fellow-combatant, coadjutor, Plat., etc.; τινός for a thing, Aeschin., Dem.
one that has a brother or sister, Xen.
to join in wrong or injury, τινί with another, Thuc., Xen.; absol., Thuc., Xen.:— Pass. to be wronged alike, Dem.
to sing with or together, Aeschin.; σ. ᾠδάν Ar.
generally, to be in accord with, τινί Soph., Plat.
trans. to celebrate together, τινά Theocr.
to raise up together, Il.
to bind or yoke together, Id.; —Mid., συναείρεται ἵππους Id.
to strive together, τινί for a thing, NTest.
to strive or labour with others, τισί Id.
to gather together, assemble, of soldiers, Xen., Plat., etc.
of things, in Pass., τὸ κεφάλαιον τούτων ξυνηθροισμένων the sum of these collected amounts, Plat.
of a single person, οὐ ξυνήθροισται στρατῷ has not joined the main army, Eur.
a collection, union, Babr.
to play with, τινί Mosch.
Adv. pressing violently together, Hes.
of common blood, kindred, Soph., Eur.
as Subst. a kinsman, kinswoman, esp. a brother, sister, Soph.
Ζεὺς ξ. as presiding over kindred, Id.; νεῖκος ξ. strife between kinsmen, Id.
to join in praising, Aesch.
to consent, absol., Id., Soph., etc.; σ. τινί to agree with a person, Hdt.
c. acc. rei, to agree to, promise, Soph., Xen., etc.: to grant at once, Xen.
c. inf. to agree or consent to do, Id.
Dep. to take up, Il.

entry.note: fut. ήσω fut. 2 συνελῶ aor2 συνεῖλον epic σύνελον
entry.sense: to grasp or seize together, to seize at once, Od., Thuc.
to bring together, bring into small compass; in speaking, ξυνελὼν λέγω briefly, in a word, Thuc.; ὡς συνελόντι εἰπεῖν Xen.; so, συνελόντι alone, Dem.
to make away with, crush, ὀφρῦς σύνελεν λίθος Il.:—metaph. to make an end of, τὸν πόλεμον Plut.:—Pass., Thuc.
to help to take or conquer, Hdt., Thuc.
to take up together, Arist., Plut.; σ. λόγον μετά τινος to balance accounts with another, NTest.
Mid. to take part in a thing, c. gen., Thuc.
c. acc. rei, to help in bearing, Id., Dem.; also to engage in a thing, undertake it, Aesch., Eur.
τῶν σκελῶν σ. to catch by both legs, Plut.
Pass., συναίρεσθαι εἰς τὸ αὐτό to be joined together, unite, Xen.
to contribute, assist, Dem.
Dep. to perceive also or at the same time, Arist.
Dep. to accuse along with, Plut.

c. gen. rei et dat. pers. being the cause of a thing jointly with another, σ. τινι ἀθανασίας helping him towards immortality, Isocr.; σ. τινος γενέσθαι τινί to share in the guilt of a thing with another, Id.
c. gen. rei only, being joint-cause of, accessory to, contributing to, Dem., etc.:—as Subst., ἡ ξυναιτία φόνου accomplice in murder, Aesch.:—absol., οὐκ αἰτίων, ἀλλ’ ἴσως ξυναιτίων Plat.
to fight with or together, Anth.
a fellow-prisoner, NTest.
Pass. to be held suspended together with, c. dat., Plat.
to bloom at the same time, Anth.
to live dissolutely with another, Plut.
to follow closely, to accompany, τινί Ar., Thuc.
σ. λόγῳ to follow an argument completely, Plat.
to throw a javelin along with or at once, Antipho.
to shoot down, τινά Polyb.
to hear along with or at the same time, Xen.; σ. ἀλλήλων to hear each other, Id.
Dep. to be a fellow-hearer, Plat.
one must bring together, Plat.
one must conclude, Arist.
able to bring together, τὸ σ. power of accumulation in oratory, Luc.
to cry aloud together, Polyb.
c. acc. to greet aloud, Eur.
to share in suffering, sympathise, Soph.:—absol., οἱ ξυναλγοῦντες those who are partners in sorrow, Id.
c. dat. rei, to sympathise, shew sympathy at or in, Aesch., Eur.
joint grief:—in pl., = αἱ συναλγοῦσαι, partners in pain, Eur.
to smear or gloss over, Arist.
to bring together, collect, Hdt.:—Pass. to come together, assemble, Id., Xen., etc.; of a single person, to associate with others, NTest.
an interchange of words for purposes of conciliation, Soph., Eur.: absol. a reconciliation, making of peace, Thuc.: pl. a treaty of peace, Xen.
generally, commerce, intercourse, Eur.

intervention, δαιμόνων ξυναλλαγαῖς by special interventions of the deities, Soph.; νόσου ξυναλλαγῇ by intervention of disease, Id.: generally, the issue of intervention, a contingency, incident, Id.; ὀλεθρίαισι συναλλ. with destructive issues, Id.
a mutual agreement, covenant, contract, Dem., etc.: in pl. dealings between men, Arist.
exchange, Plat.
to bring into intercourse with, associate with, τινά τινι Aesch.:—Pass. to have intercourse with, τινί Soph., Eur.
to reconcile, τινά τινι Thuc.:—Pass. and Mid. to be reconciled, to make a league or alliance with, πρός τινα Id., Xen.; absol. to make peace, Thuc., Xen.
intr. to have dealings with another, Soph., Eur.
to enter into engagements or contracts, Dem., Arist.
Dep. to leap together, Luc.
to thresh out together, to grind to powder, crush, shiver, Theocr.
to wander about with another, c. dat., Plut.
together, Anth., Luc.; τινί with one, Theocr.
Dep. to contend or struggle together, Eur.
to cover up closely, to wrap up, Aesch.:—Mid., τί συναμπίσχει κόρας; why dost veil thine eyes? Eur.
both together, Theogn., Hdt., attic:—sg. in collective sense, τὸ ξ. = συναμφότεροι, Plat.; τοῦτο συναμφότερον this united power, Dem.
both together, Plat., etc.
to go up with or together into central Asia, Hdt., Xen.; τινί with one, Xen.
to cry out together, Xen.
to join or assist in compelling, Isocr., Dem.:—Pass. to be compelled at the same time, Dem.
to execute by force also, Isocr.:— Pass., ὅρκοι συνηναγκασμένοι extorted oaths, Eur.
to register or record together:— Pass., συναναγραφῆναι ἐν τοῖς συμμάχοις Aeschin.
to carry back together:—Pass. to retire together, Polyb.
Pass. also, to go to sea together, Dem.
to give back along with, Luc.
to set out along with, Plut.
to destroy together with, τινά τινι Polyb.
to destroy altogether or utterly, Isocr.:—Pass., Thuc.
to give the same answer, Plat.
Pass. to recline together at table, NTest.
Pass. to be mixed up with, τινι Luc.
to expend together or in company, Dem.
to help by spending money, Xen.
to mix up together: Pass. to be associated with others, c. dat., Luc.
Pass. to take rest with others, NTest.
to assist in persuading, τινὰ ποιεῖν τι Thuc., etc.
to send up together, Plut.
to entwine together with, τί τινι Luc.
to join in exacting payment, Xen.
to throw up together, Luc.
to dig up besides, Strab.
to draw up together, Luc.
to rule with, Anth.
to turn back together, intr., Plut.
Pass. and Mid. to live along with or among others, c. dat., Id.
to melt with or together, Plut.
to dedicate along with, Luc.
a rising together, Strab.
to run up with, Plut.
Dep. to cry out or speak together, Plut.
to knead up together:—Pass to wallow together, Luc.
Dep. to cough up together, Luc.
to make to stand up or rise together, Xen.: to assist in restoring, Id.
Pass. with aor2 act., to rise at the same time, Id.; τινι with one, Id.

entry.note: epic 3rd dual imperf. -αντήτην fut. -ήσω aor1 -ήντησα perf. -ήντηκα
entry.sense: to meet face to face, of two persons, Od.; of many persons, to meet together, assemble, Philipp. ap. Dem.
like ἀντάω, to meet with, meet, τινί Eur., Ar.; so in Mid., Il.:—c. acc. cogn., συναντᾶν συνάντησιν Eur.
c. dat. rei, to come in contact with, φόνῳ Id.
to befal, of accidents, etc., τινί Plut., NTest.
a meeting, Eur.
to drain along with, σ. πόνους τινί to join him in bearing all his sufferings, Lat. una exhaurire labores, Eur.
Dep. to fall in with, meet, absol. or c. dat., Hom., etc.; in hostile sense, to meet in battle, Il.: metaph., φόρμιγγι σ. to approach (i. e. use) the lyre, Pind.
συνανύτω, to come to an end with, c. dat., Aesch.
συνανύω to arrive together, Plut.
to join in requiring, Xen.
to lead away with another, c. dat., Xen.; absol., Id.
Pass. to be led away likewise, NTest.
to accommodate oneself to a thing, c. dat., Id.
intr. to sail or march away together, Luc.
to correspond exactly with, lie over against, τινί Strab.
all together, mostly in pl., Hdt., etc.:—in sg., with collective Nouns, τὸ συνάπαν στράτευμα Id.
to threaten at the same time, Luc.
Dep. to help in completing, Plat.
Dep. to become an enemy together, Plut.
to disembark together with, τινί Hdt.
Mid. to enter one's name together with others, as a candidate, Plut.
to be abroad together, Arist.
those who live abroad together, Arist.
to run away along with, ξυναποδρᾶναί τινι (aor2 inf.), Ar.
to join in reprobating, τι, Xen.
to die together with another, c. dat., Hdt.: absol. to die with one, Plat.
to go as colonists together, Luc.
to cease from weariness together, Eur.
to kill together, Aeschin.
to receive in common or at once, Xen.
to shine forth together, Luc.
to destroy together, σ. τοὺς φίλους to destroy one's friends as well as oneself, Thuc.; σ. τὰ χρήματα to lose the money also, Dem.:—Pass. to perish together, Thuc.; τινι with one, Hdt.
Dep. to join in defending, Dem.
Pass. to fade away and die together, Xen.
to bend away together, τοῖς σώμασιν αὐτοῖς ἴσα τῇ δόξῃ ξυναπονεύοντες swerving with their bodies in sympathy with their thought, Thuc.
to send off together, Xen.
to break together, Plut.
to put out with or together, τί τινι Anth.:—Pass., with aor2 act. -έσβην, perf. -έσβηκα, to be put out together, Plut.
to despatch together with another, c. dat., Thuc., Xen.
to help to strip or cheat, τινά τινος one of a thing, Dem.
Mid. to assert likewise or together, to agree in asserting, Isocr., etc.

to tie or bind together, to join together, unite, σ. χέρα, in sign of friendship, Eur.; ἰδού, ξύναψον (sc. τὴν χέρα) Id.; but, σ. χεῖρά τινος ἐν βρόχοις to bind it fast, Id.:— σ. πόδα or ἴχνος τινί to meet him, Id.; σ. κῶλον τάφῳ to approach the grave, Id.; so, φόνος σ. τινὰ γᾷ Id.:— ξ. βλέφαρα to close the eyes, Id.; σ. στόμα to kiss one, Id.:— σ. κακὰ κακοῖς to link misery with misery, Id.; but, σ. κακόν τινι to link him with misery, Id.: σ. τινὶ δαῖτα to give one a meal, Id.: proverb., σ. λίνον λίνῳ to join thread to thread, i. e. to compare things of the same sort, Plat.
to connect in thought, to combine, Id.: σ. μηχανήν to frame a plan, Aesch.; σ. ὄναρ εἴς τινα to connect it with him, refer it to him, Eur.; ξυνῆψε πάντας ἐς μίαν βλάβην involved them in one loss, Id.
in hostile sense, σ. εἰς μάχην to bring into action, Hdt.; ἐλπὶς πόλεις ξυνῆψε engaged them in conflict, Eur.
σ. μάχην to join battle, Hdt.; τινί with one, Aesch.; πρός τινα Thuc.: also (without μάχην) to engage, Hdt., Ar.:—Pass., νεῖκος συνῆπταί τινι πρός τινα Hdt.
in friendly sense, to unite, Xen.: —Pass., συνάπτεσθαί τινι to have intercourse with, Anth.
c. acc. rei, σ. μῦθον, ὅρκους Eur.; σ.τινὶ γάμους, λέκτρα, κῆδος to form an alliance by marriage, Id.: ξυνάπτεσθαι κῆδος τῆς θυγατρός to get one's daughter married, Thuc.
intr.:
in local sense, to border on, lie next to, Hdt.; Τήνῳ συνάπτει Ἄνδρος Aesch.
of Time, to be nigh at hand, Pind.; so of events, λύπη σ. τινί Eur.
metaph. of thoughts, to meet together, Arist.:— to be connected with, πρός τι Id.
of persons, σ. λόγοισι to enter into conversation, Soph.; so, ἐς λόγους ξ. τινί Eur.; also, σ. εἰς χορεύματα to join in the dance, Id.; σ. ἐς χεῖρα γῇ, i. e. to come close to land, Id.
τύχα ποδὸς ξυνάπτει μοι, i. e. I have come in good time, Id.
Mid. to be next to, connected with, τινι Xen.
to take part with one, to assist, τινι Eur.; absol., Aesch.
to bring upon oneself, πληγάς Dem.
to push away together, Luc.
intr. in perf. συνάρηρα, to hang together, Hhymn.
to dash together, dash in pieces, shiver, shatter, Hom.; σ. οἶκον, πόλιν Eur.: —Pass. to be shattered, Od., Hdt.; συναράσσεσθαι κεφαλάς to have their heads dashed together, Hdt.
to please or satisfy together, c. dat., Dem.
impers., like Lat. placet, συναρέσκει μοι I am content also, Xen.
linked together with, Aesch.
to reckon in, to take into the account, enumerate, Isae.; so in Mid., Aeschin.:—Pass. to be counted with others, to be taken into account, Arist.
to take breakfast or luncheon with, τινί Ar., Aeschin.
to do brave deeds together, Eur.
Dep. to acquiesce along with, τινι Theophr.

entry.note: attic -όττω doric fut. -όξω Pass., perf. -ήρμοσμαι aor1 -ηρμόσθην
entry.sense: in physical sense, to fit together, Thuc.; συναρμόζειν βλέφαρα to close them, Eur.:—Pass., λίθοι εὖ συνηρμοσμένοι Hdt.
to put together, so as to make a whole, σκάφος, ἵππον Eur.:—Pass., οὐ καλῶς συνηρμοσμένα Dem.
to combine in act or thought, Solon., Plat.
metaph. to adapt one thing to another, εὐχερείᾳ σ. βροτούς, i. e. to make them indifferent to crime, Aesch.:—Pass., πρὸς παρόντα συνηρμοσμένος Xen.
intr. to fit together, agree, Plat., Xen.
Pass. to be fitted or framed together, NTest.
one who fits together, λίθων Luc.
a joint-governor, Id.
to seize and carry clean away, Trag., etc.:— Pass., Soph.
ξ. χεῖρας to seize and pin them together, Eur.
metaph., σ. φρενί to seize with the mind, grasp, Soph., Ar.
to knit or join together, Eur., Luc.:—Pass. to be closely engaged or entangled, Thuc.: to be attached to, combined with, τινί Arist.: to hang close on an enemy's rear, Plut.
joint administration, Strab.
in pl., αἱ συναρχίαι, the collective magistracy, Arist.
a partner in office, colleague, Arist.
to rule jointly with, τινί Hdt.
absol. to be a colleague in office, Thuc.: ὁ συνάρχων a colleague, Id.
to join in practising, Isocr., Dem.
to keep the shields close together, stand in close order, Xen.
to be a shield-fellow or comrade, Eur.
= συνασπιδόω, Luc.
a shield-fellow, comrade, Soph.
to sympathise indignantly with a thing, c. dat., Aesch.
Pass. to do business with, τινι Plut.
Pass. to be disgraced with, τινι Plut.
to dry quite up, Eur.:—Pass. to be dried up also, Plat.
to speak together: to agree, confess, allow, Soph.
to accompany on the flute, Luc.
a concert of flutes, Ar.
metaph., δύσορνις ἅδε ξ. δορός this ill-omened concert of battle. of the single combat of the brothers, Aesch.
(from αὐλή) a dwelling together, Arist.
Pass. to congregate, Babr.
dwelling with, living in the folds with (sc. ταῖς ποίμναις), Soph.: metaph., θείᾳ μανίᾳ ξ., i. e. afflicted with madness, Id.
to increase or enlarge along with or together, Xen.:—Pass. to increase or wax larger together with a thing, c. dat., Hdt., Eur.
to join or assist in increasing, Xen., Arist.
in concert with the flute: generally, sounding in unison, Ar.: generally, in harmony with, τινι Eur.
common growth, Polyb.
to take away together:—Mid. to assist in rescuing, Thuc.
Pass. to perish with, τινι Strab.
to draw into revolt together, Thuc.:—Pass., ionic συναπίσταμαι, with aor2 and perf. act., to fall off or revolt along with others, c. dat., or absol., Hdt., Thuc.
Dep.:— to be grieved with or together, to condole with, τινι Hdt., Dem., etc.; c. dat. rei, at a thing, Xen.
to kill with the rest, kill also, Soph.
to entertain together, σ. γάμους τινί to share a marriage feast with one, Eur.
a companion at table, Aesch.
to bite together, συνδ. τὸ στόμιον of a horse, to take the bit in his teeth, Xen.
to weep with or together, Eur.
c. acc. to lament together, Plut.
Mid. to collect by borrowing, Plut.
to dine or sup with another, c. dat., Xen.; μετά τινων Dem.:—absol. to dine or sup with others, Xen., etc.; οἱ ξυνδειπνοῦντες the members of a picnic party, Id.
a common meal or banquet, Lat. convivium, Plat.
a companion at table, Lat. conviva, Eur., Xen.
to bribe all together, Xen., Aeschin.
thickly-wooded, Babr.
Dep. to join in begging, τί τινος something of a person, Dem.
heterog. pl. σύνδεσμα, a bond of union, bond, fastening, Eur., Thuc.: metaph., good men are called ὁ ξ. τῆς πόλεως the bond that keeps the state together, Plat.
in Grammar, a conjunction, Arist.
a fellow-prisoner, Thuc., Plat.
bound hand and foot, Soph.
as Subst. σύνδετον, ου, a band, Eur.

to bind or tie together, of two or more things, συνέδησα πόδας Od.; τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας Plat.; δέλτον σ. to fasten up the tablets, Eur.:—Pass., ἰσχία μὴ συνδεδεμένα flanks not drawn up, of dogs, Xen.
of persons, to bind hand and foot, Il., Hdt., etc.
to bind up a wound, Il.
generally, to bind together, unite, Eur., Plat.
Mid., σύνδησαι πέπλους gird up thy robes, Eur.
quite clear or manifest, Arist.
to make altogether clear, Arist.
to join in seeking popularity, Plut.
to go through or cross over together, Thuc., Xen.
to convey over together: absol., Lat. una trajicere, συνδ. τὸν κόλπον to cross the gulf together, Thuc.
to accuse along with, Dem.:—Pass. to be accused together, Thuc.
to carry through or over together, Xen.
to join with others in determining or decreeing, Thuc.
to go through together: absol. (sc. τὸν βίον) to live together, Arist.
Pass. to dwell with or together, Thuc., Isocr.
a living together, intercourse, Plut.
a joint arbitrator, Dem.
one who lives with another, a companion, Luc.
to share in danger, Hdt., Plat.
Pass. to cross over together, Plut.
to set in order together, Plat., Plut.
a fellow -διάκτορος, i. e. a mate of Hermes, Luc.
to help in reconciling, τινὰ πρός τινα Dem.
to help in putting an end to, Isocr.
to help in reconciling, Dem.
Mid. to help to pay, Luc.
to stand one's ground with others, Xen.
to call to remembrance along with or together, Dem., Aeschin.
to turn every way together, Polyb.
Dep. to deliberate with, τινι Polyb.
to sail through together, Luc.
to carry on a war along with, νῆες αἱ ξυνδιαπολεμήσασαι ships which remained with him throughout the war, Thuc.
to start doubts or questions together, Plut.
to accomplish together, or besides, Isocr., Luc., etc.
Mid. to negotiate at the same time, Xen.
to look through or examine along with, τί τινι or μετά τινος Plat.:—so in pres. mid., Id.
to distort together:—Pass. to be twisted together with, τινί Plut.
to assist in preserving, Thuc., Dem.
to endure hardship with or together, Plat.
to continue with to the end, Plat.
to assist in maintaining, Polyb.
to pass or spend time with or together, Aeschin.
absol. (sub. βίον) to live constantly with, οἱ τῷ Σωκράτει συνδιατρίβοντες his disciples, Xen.
to occupy oneself with a thing, c. dat., Isocr.
to bear along with one, Luc.
to bear to the end along with, help in maintaining, Hdt., Ar.
Pass. to perish along with, τινι Isocr.
to be in winter quarters along with or together, Plut.
to assist in accomplishing, Hdt.
to rush out through together, Plut.
to go through together with, Xen.
to spend the day with, τινί Xen.
to be assessor to a judge, Lys.
a fellow-dicast or juryman, Ar.
to act as one's advocate, Aesch., Xen., etc.; σ. τινί Plat.; Ζεύς σοι τόδε συνδικήσει Zeus will be thy advocate herein, Eur.
to be one of the public advocates, Dem.
one who helps in a court of justice, an advocate, Lat. patronus, Aesch., Dem.
at Athens, the σύνδικοι were public advocates appointed to represent the state, Dem.
after the 30 Tyrants, the σύνδικοι were judges to determine disputes about confiscated property, Lys.
belonging jointly to, σ. Ἀπόλλωνος καὶ Μοισᾶν κτέανον their joint possession, Pind.:—adv. συνδίκως, with joint sentence, jointly, Aesch.
to administer together with another, c. dat., Dem.
to examine together, Isocr.
Pass. to be determined also, Strab.
to play at quoits with, τινί Luc.
to chase away together, join in the chase, Thuc.
as law-term, to join in the prosecution, Lex ap. Dem.
to seem good also, ταῦτα κἀμοὶ συνδοκεῖ Ar.; ταῦτα ξυνέδοξε τοῖς ἄλλοις Thuc.:—absol., in answers, ξυνεδόκει ἡμῖν ταῦτα; were we agreed on these points? i. e. we were agreed, Plat.
impers. it seems good also, Eur., Ar., etc.:—so, absol., in part., συνδοκοῦν ἅπασιν ὑμῖν since you all agree, Xen.; συνδόξαν τῷ πατρί since the father approved, Id.
so in perf. pass. part., λόγος τοῖς ἐπιεικεστάτοις συνδεδογμένος in which they also agree, Plat.
to examine together, Isocr.
to join in approving, Arist.
to agree with, τῷ σώματι Porph. in Stob.
Pass. to be glorified together, NTest.
to be a fellow-slave with, τινί Eur.
a fellow-slave, Hdt., Eur., etc.: a special fem. συνδούλη in Babr.
to do together, help in doing, Soph., Thuc.; σ. τί τινι Eur.; ξ. αἷμα καὶ φόνον to help in bloodshed and murder, Id.; τὸ συνδρῶν χρέος the joint necessity, Id.
αἱ σ. πέτραι, = συμπληγάδες, Eur.; σ. Κυάνεαι Theocr.
a tumultuous concourse of people, ap. Arist.
of things, ἡ σ. τοῦ λόγου its conclusion, moral, Anth.
running together, meeting, σ. πέτραι, = συνδρομάδες, Pind.
as Subst. a place where several roads meet, Strab.
running along with, close-following, Anth.:—adv. συνδρόμως Aesch.
to join two and two, couple, Arist.: —Pass. to be coupled with something else, Id.
in Pass. to be coupled, to pair, Xen.
a being taken two together, Arist.
a coupling, pairing, Id.
paired, σ. ἄλοχος one's wedded wife, Eur.
disposed to live in pairs, Arist.
two together, two and two, in pairs, Lat. bini, Hhymn., Hdt., Plat.
to share in misfortune, Eur.
twelve in all, Eur.
to draw near together, Polyb.
a drawing near together, of constellations, Strab.
to join in betrothing, Plut.
of Place, near together, Thuc., etc.; σ. ἀλλήλων or ἀλλήλοις Arist.:— τὸ σ. nearness, proximity, Id.
of Time, Id.
of Quality, οἱ σ. persons of similar rank, Id.; ἡ σ. αἰτία the proximate cause, Id.
to help in raising, NTest.:—Pass. to rise together, Id.
to sit together, sit in council, Aeschin.; οἱ συνεδρεύοντες members of council, Dem.
to hold a council, deliberate, Id.
a sitting together, a circle of friends, Xen.:— gregariousness, which in birds was a favourable omen, Aesch.
a council, Aeschin.
a body of men assembled in council, a council-board, council, Xen., etc.; of the Roman Senate, Polyb.; the Jewish Sanhedrim, NTest.:—esp. of a congress of Allies or Confederates, Hdt., Dem., etc.
a council-chamber, Hdt., Xen.
sitting with in council, of persons, Hdt.; ἐκ ξυνέδρου καὶ τυραννικοῦ κύκλου, = ἐκ κύκλου τῶν συνεδρευόντων τυράννων, Soph.
as Subst. one who sits with others, a councillor, Id.; σύνεδροι select commissioners, Thuc., etc.
twenty together, by twenties, Lat. viceni, Od.
to have the same wish, to consent, Xen.: —in Poets συνθέλω, Soph., Eur.

to accustom, σ. τινὰ ποιεῖν τι to accustom him to do . . , Dem., Aeschin.:—Pass. to become used or habituated, and in aor1 and perf. to have become so, be so, Thuc., Plat.; c. inf., συνειθίσθην ποιεῖν τι Xen.:—also impers., συνειθισμένον ἦν it had become the custom, Lys.
one must accustom oneself, Plat.
self-consciousness: conscience, NTest.
to crowd together, Hdt.; of things, to bind tight together, Id.:—Pass. to be crowded or pressed together, Xen., etc.

to be with, be joined or linked with a thing, c. dat., Od.; periphr. for a simple Verb, σ. ὀνείρασιν to dream, Aesch.; σ. νόσῳ = νοσεῖν, Soph.; κακοῖς πολλοῖς ξ. to be acquainted with miseries, Id.; σ. πράγμασι to be engaged in business, Ar.; σ. ἡδοναῖς, λύπαις, δείμασι Plat.;—reversely, ἐμοὶ ξύνεστιν ἐλπίς Eur.; and absol., ἆται ἀεὶ ξυνοῦσαι Soph.; ὁ χρόνος ξυνὼν μακρός Id.
to have intercourse with a person, live with, τινι Id., Eur., etc.; μετά τινος Ar.
to live with a husband, = συνοικέω, Hdt.
to attend, as to a pupil attends a master, Xen., etc.; of the teacher, Id.:— οἱ συνόντες associates, disciples, partisans, Plat.
to have dealings with, τινι Thuc.; σ. ἵπποις to have to do with them, Plat.
to take part with, τινι Aesch., etc.
to go or come together, to assemble, Il., Hdt., Thuc.
in hostile sense, to meet in battle, Il., etc.: of states, to engage in war, Thuc.
in peaceable sense, to come together, meet to deliberate, Id.
of revenue, to come in, Hdt.
to speak with any one, confirm what another says, Isocr.: to agree with, τινί Xen.
to advocate another's cause, Dem.; generally, to help, further, Isocr.
to help to tell, Eur.
to string together, Lat. connectere, Ar., Plat.
to string words together, Dem., etc.: then, seemingly intr. (sub. λόγους) to speak on and on, go on without pausing, Xen.
to bring in together, Xen.
to embark in a ship with others, σ. πλοῖον ναύταισι Aesch.; σ. ταὐτὸν σκάφος Eur.
intr. to make an inroad into a country together, join in an inroad, Hdt., Thuc.
Dep. to enter along with or together, δόμους Eur.; ἐς οἴκους Id., etc.
to fall or be thrown into with others, Xen.
to rush in together, of soldiers pursuing the besieged to the gates and getting in with them, Hdt., Thuc.
to sail into together, Xen.
to help one (τινί) in exacting money from another (τινά), Dem.
to join in paying the war-tax (εἰσφορά), Xen.
to go out together, Xen.
to cast out along with, τί τινι Hdt.
to assist in casting out or expelling, Xen.
to help in bringing out, Xen.
to be abroad with, τινί Plut.
a fellow-traveller, NTest.
to give out or give up together Plut.
to help a poor man in portioning out his daughter, Dem.
Mid. to put off at the same time, Hdt.
to faint along with, σ. τῷ πώματι, i. e. to drink till wine and drinker fail together, Eur.
sixteen together, by sixteens, Dem.
to set on fire together, Plut.
to help to steal away, Eur.; σ. γάμους to help in concealing the marriage, Id.
to frequent the ἐκκλησία together, Plut.
to carry out along with, Plut.
to help in carrying out, help in achieving, Eur.; σ. τινὶ κακά to help one in bearing evils, Id.
to help to cut away, Xen.
Pass. to be driven from one's purpose together, Plut.
chosen along with, τισί NTest.
Pass. to be dissolved together, Anth.
to send out together, Xen.
to come out together, Xen.
to drink off together, Xen.
to rush out together with others, c. dat., Plut.
to be driven out or banished together, Id.
to disappear together, Luc.

of voting tablets, to come out in agreement, to happen to agree, Hdt.; αἱ πλεῖσται γνῶμαι συνέπιπτον ναυσιμαχέειν agreed in advising to fight, Id.; then of persons, οἱ πολλοὶ σ. Θεμιστοκλέα κρίνοντες agreed in choosing, Id.
c. dat. to come out equal to another, run a dead heat with him, συνεξέπιπτε τῷ πρώτῳ Id.
to be thrown out together, to be rejected, Luc.
to sail out along with, τινί Hdt., Thuc.
to breathe one's last along with another, c. dat., Eur.
to help in working out, Eur.: to help in achieving or effecting, Id.
without acc., σ. τινί to assist to the utmost, Id.
to assist in supporting, συνεκπονοῦσα κῶλον Id.
to help in procuring or supplying, τί τινι Xen.
one must drink off at the same time, Ar.
Mid. to assist in avenging, Hdt.
to help in delivering, Soph.
to arrange in line with, Xen.
one must keep together, Xen.
to bring forth together, Arist.
to pay along with or together, to help in paying, Dem.
Pass. to be furious together, Plut.
to rear up along with or together, Plat.:—Pass. to grow up with, τινί Eur.
to sally out together, Xen.
to carry out together, esp. to burial, to attend a funeral, Thuc.
to pour out together, Anth.
to drive together, Il., Xen.; σὺν δ’ ἤλας’ ὀδόντας gnashed his teeth together, Od.
to match in combat, set to fight, Hom.:—intr., ἔριδι ξυνελαυνέμεν to meet in quarrel, Il.
to join in freeing from another, c. gen., Hdt.:—absol. to join in freeing, Id., Thuc.
to roll together:—Pass. to involve oneself in a thing, c. dat., Soph.
intr. to coil itself up, of a serpent, Eur.
one must draw together, Xen.
to draw together, to draw up, contract, Ar.
to draw out along with, to help to draw out, Id., Xen.
to embark together, τινί with one, Luc.
to help in applying, Ar.
intr. to fall upon also, to join in attacking, Xen.; to make a joint inroad, Dem.
a throwing in together, σ. κώπης the regular dip of all the oars together, to the sound of the κέλευσμα, Aesch.
a junction, fastening, Id.
to burn together, Eur.
to fall in or upon together, Luc.
to fall on or attack together, Plut.
a fellow-traveller, companion, attendant, Trag., Plat.:—metaph., λύπη δ’ ἄμισθος ἐστί σοι ξ. Aesch.; c. gen. rei, σ. χορείας partner in the dance, Ar.
to give in together, Plut.
to strike or dash against a thing, c. dat., Hes.
to lead out together, Hdt.: Pass. to be carried away together, Anth.
to take out together, to help in removing, Hdt.:— Mid., Eur.: to take away also, Xen.
to help in taking, Eur., Xen.
to assist in raising: Pass., aor1 part. συνεξαρθείς being lifted up at once, Plut.; being excited at the same time, Luc.
to follow constantly, to attend everywhere, Polyb.
to hear all together, Soph.
to abolish together, Plut.
to have part in a fault, Thuc., etc.; τινί with one, Dem., etc.
to remove together, Babr.
to stir up together, Plut.
Pass., with aor2 and perf. act., to rise up at the same time, rise and come forth with, Id.
to rise in rebellion, revolt together, Id.
to cheat together or also, Dem.
to go out along with or together, Thuc.; c. dat., Xen.
to drive out along with or together, Aesch.
to draw out together, Anth.
Dep.:— to go or come out with, τινι Hdt., Eur.
to search out and examine along with or together, Plat.:—Pass., οἱ συνεξεταζόμενοι μετά τινος or τινι his party or adherents, Dem.
to assist in finding out, Eur., Isocr.
Pass. to be civilised together, Plut.
to trace out along with, τί τινι Plut.
to help to urge on, Isocr.
intr. to rush forth or sally out together, Xen.
to thrust out together, Strab.
a joining, joint, Il.
to lead together against, Thuc.
to join in bringing in a foreign force to aid, Id.
Dep. to join in stirring up a contest besides, Polyb.
to join in celebrating, Eur.
to approve, together, give joint assent, consent, Aesch., Xen.;—c. inf., σ. μάχεσθαι to join in the recommendation to fight, Thuc.;— σ. τι to consent or agree to, Id.
to join in praising, τινα Xen., Plat.
joining in approbation of a thing, συν. εἶναι to give one's consent to a thing, τινι or absol., Hdt.; c. acc. et inf. to consent that . . , Id.
to raise or lift at the same time, Xen.:—Pass. to be elevated together with, τινί Luc.
to urge on together or also, Xen.:— Pass. to rise together with others, c. dat., Plut.
Dep. to accuse also of a thing, τινά τινος Thuc.
Pass. to continue soaring over, Plut.
to follow closely, Plat.
to join in repelling, τινά Thuc.

sense.gloss: to make to rise up against together.

entry.sense: Pass., with aor2 act., to join in a revolt, Hdt., Thuc.; τινι or ἅμα τινι Hdt.
to join in reestablishing, Dem.
to join in attacking, τινι Thuc.
to rush in upon together, Plut.
Mid. to help to bring in, Xen.
to drink off together, Anth.
to help to make light, i. e. to assist in bearing, Hdt.
to help in inflicting, πληγήν Plut.; σ. ὑπόνοιάν τινι to help to fix a suspicion on him, Id.
c. acc. pers. to transfix, συνεπερείσας τῇ ῥύμῃ τοῦ ἵππου charging him with all the force of his horse, Id.
to contend also with, τινί Anth.
to help to direct or guide, τι Plut.
Dep. to join in prayer, Thuc.; but c. inf. fut. to make a vow also to do a thing, Xen.
to join in a chant or chorus, Xen.
to resound with a thing, Luc.
to mount together, τοῦ τείχους on the wall, Plut.
to apply one's mind also, to consider a thing together, Polyb.
to coincide with, καιροῖς Id.
Pass. to be damaged together with, τινι Arist.
to join in plotting against another, Xen.
a fellow-registrar, fellow-clerk, Isocr.
to point out together, Polyb.
to ascribe to divine interposition, Plut.
to desire along with, τινί τινος Xen.
Pass. to join in attacking, Ar.
to break down at once, Plut.
to help to adorn, Xen., Arist.
to join as an ally, help to relieve, Xen.
to lighten at the same time, Plut.
to help in relieving, Id.
to move backwards and forwards together with, Xen.
to help to conceal, Plut.

Mid. to take part in together, have a share in, partake in, c. gen. rei, Hdt., Thuc.: σ. τινί τινος to take part with or assist one in a thing, Luc.; σ. τινι τοῦ φόβου to contribute towards increasing their fear, Thuc.
c. gen. pers. to take the part of, Plut.
Act. in same sense, λόγῳ καὶ ἔργῳ συνεπιλαμβάνειν τινί to take part with him in word and deed, Thuc.
Dep. to join in taking care of or attending to, τινος Thuc., Xen.; σ. τῆς στρατιᾶς to have joint charge of the army, Xen.; absol., Id.
a coadjutor, Xen.
to incline towards together, Plut.
to help to strengthen, Plut.
to examine together with, τί τινι Xen.
to draw on together, Plut.
Mid. to draw on along with one, esp. to ruin, Plat., Dem., etc.
to join in forcing onward, Xen.
Dep. to be privy to, Xen., Luc.
to act as a common patron, Plat.
to send with or together, Luc.
to join in making war, τινί with another, Thuc., Dem.
to turn at the same time, Plat.
to help to make attentive, Plut.
to join in supporting, Xen.
to help to aggravate, Polyb.
to help to accomplish, Plut.
to join in performing, παιᾶνα θεῷ Xen.
to help in putting on, Plut.
Mid. to join in attacking, τινι Thuc.; ξ. τῷ ἔργῳ to fall to the work together, Id.
to join in chiding, Plut.
to destroy at once, Xen.
a joint guardian, Dem.
to join in applying, Plut.
to attack together, Polyb.
Dep. to join in lying, Luc.
to join in ratifying a law, Arist.
Dep.
to follow along with, follow closely, absol., Od., Thuc., etc.; c. dat., Hdt., etc.; οὔ σοι τῷ βίῳ ξυνέσπετο (thy fortunes) remained not constant to thy life, Soph.
σ. τῷ λόγῳ to follow the argument to its consequences, Plat.: —absol., ξυνέπομαι I follow, i. e. understand, Id.
to swear besides, Xen.
to join in contributing, to collect, Luc.:—Mid. to receive contributions, Plut.
a joint lover, Xen.
to pour together, gather together, συνερᾶσαι τοὺς λόγους Isocr.
to love together with, τινί Eur.; so in epic mid. inf. συνέρασθαι, Bion.
Dep.
to work with, cooperate, Soph.; σ. πρός τι to contribute towards or to a thing, Xen.
aor1 -ειργάσθην, perf. -είργασμαι in pass. sense, λίθοι ξυνειργασμένοι stones wrought so as to fit together, i. e. in ashlar-work, Thuc.; συνειργάσθη ἔργον it was wrought, Anth.
a fellow-workman, helpmate, coadjutor, Soph., Eur.; c. gen. an accomplice or assistant in a thing, Eur.
to work together with, help in work, cooperate, Eur., Xen., etc.;— generally, to cooperate with, assist, τινί Dem.
assistance, support, Polyb.
joint working, cooperation, Arist.; in bad sense, conspiracy, collusion, Dem.

working together, joining or helping in work, and as Subst. a fellow-workman, helpmate, coadjutor, accomplice, Eur., Thuc., etc.; c. dat. pers., Eur., Thuc.:—c. gen. rei, σ. τείχεος helping to make it, Pind.; σ. ἀδίκων ἔργων, ἀρετᾶς helping towards them, Eur.; σ. τινί τινος helping a person in a thing, Xen.; εἴς or πρός τι Id.
of the same trade as another, a fellow-workman, colleague, Dem.

entry.note: old form of attic συνείργω fut. συνείρξω epic συνεέργω imperf. συνέεργον or συνεέργᾰθον
entry.sense: to shut up or enclose together, Hom., Soph.
to fasten together, Od.:— to unite, Plat.
to join in a work, help, τινί Soph.
to set firmly together, Od.: to bind together, bind fast, Eur.:—Pass., συνερεισθεὶς χέρας δεσμοῖς with one's hands tight bound, Id.
σ. τὸν λογισμόν to reason closely, Plut.
intr. to meet in close conflict, Id.
to speak with or together, advocate, support in a speech, c. dat., Xen., Dem.
a helpmate, Od., Ar.; σ. τέχναι assistant arts, Plat.; σ. ἄτρακτος Anth.
of a speaker, driving his opponent into a corner, cogent, Ar.
close union, wedlock, Plat.
Dep. with aor2 and perf. act.:— to go together or in company, Il.
to come together, assemble, Hdt., Eur., etc.; σ. ἐς τωὐτό Hdt.; σ. ἐς λόγους τινί Id.; simply, σ. τινι to have dealings or intercourse with, Soph.
in hostile sense, to meet in battle, Hdt.; also of the battle, μάχη ὑπό τινων ξυνελθοῦσα engaged in, contested by them, Thuc.
to come together, be bonded together, Eur., Plat.: to form a league, Dem.
c. acc. cogn., ταύτην τὴν στρατείαν ξυνῆλθον joined in this expedition, Thuc.; so, τὸ σὸν λέχος ξυνῆλθον shared thy bed, Soph.
of things, to be joined in one, Id., Eur.; of numbers, to make up a sum, Hdt.
of events, to concur, happen together, Id.
to ask with or at the same time, Luc.
to establish a point by means of question and answer, Id.
（εἶμι ibo) a coming together, union, ξύνεσις δύω ποταμῶν Od.
（συνίημι) quick comprehension, mother-wit, intelligence, sagacity, Thuc.; of animals, Plat.
c. gen. rei, intelligence in a thing, sagacity in respect to it, Id.; περί τινος Thuc.
conscience, = συνείδησις, Eur.
a branch of art or science, Arist.

entry.note: συνεστέος, ον, verb. adj. of σύνειμι
entry.sense: one must associate with, τινί Plat.
steadfastly, gravely, Arist.
to entertain in one's house, Anth.:—Pass. to feast along with or together, Dem.

sharing one's hearth or house, a fellow-lodger, guest, Lat. contubernalis, Soph., Eur.; —ξυνέστιοι πόλεος his fellow- citizens, Aesch.:—c. dat. pers., σ. σοι καὶ ὁμοτράπεζος Plat.; c. dat. rei, ξ. ἐμοὶ θοίνῃ associates with me in the feast, Eur.
of Zeus, guardian of the hearth, Aesch.
in a close packed manner, tersely, Arist.
a party, banquet, Hdt.
a companion, partner, comrade, Hdt.
intelligent, sagacious, wise, Lat. prudens, Hdt., Pind., etc.; τὸ συνετόν = σύνεσις, Eur., Thuc.:—c. gen. rei, intelligent in a thing, ξυνετὸς πολέμου Eur.; also c. acc., τὰ οἰκτρὰ ξ. Id.
pass. intelligible, Theogn., Hdt., etc; act. and pass. senses conjoined, εὐξύνετος ξυνετοῖσι βοά Eur.
adv. -τῶς, intelligently, Id.
intelligibly, Plut.
to share in happiness, Xen.
to consent to a thing, c. dat., NTest.
to sympathise with, τινί Id.
to sleep with, Hdt., Soph.
τοῦ ξυνεύδοντος χρόνου in the time coincident with sleep, Aesch.
to enjoy the day or be happy together, Plut.
Pass. to lie with, Pind., Soph.
a bed-fellow, husband, consort, Eur.
a wife or concubine, Id.
a consort, Pind., Trag.
to derive profit together, Dem.
to help to contribute, Dem.
c. gen. rei, to assist by contributing towards, Id.
to help in contriving, Plut.
to be fortunate together, Eur.
Dep. to pray with or together, Eur.; ταὐτὰ δὴ ξ. I join in the same prayer, Id.
Pass. to fare sumptuously or feast together, τινι with one, Luc.
Dep.:
c. gen. rei, to take part in, ἔργου Pind.; τοὺς συνεφαπτομένους those who take part in [the war], Aeschin.
c. gen. pers. to join one in attacking, Hdt.
to wait to fight the conqueror, Polyb.:— σ. τινί to watch closely, Id.
to draw after or along with one together, Plat.
Dep.:— to follow together, Hdt.; τινι with one, Xen.
at the age of youth together, a young comrade, Aeschin.
to set on the watch together, make attentive, Polyb.:—then (sub. τὸν νοῦν), to attend to, observe along with, Id.
Pass. συνεφίστᾰμαι, with aor2 act. to stand over, superintend along with or together, Thuc.
to rise up together, κατά τινος against one, NTest.
continuity, Arist.
connexion or sequence of words or arguments, Luc.
continued attention, perseverance, Dem.
holding together:
of space, continuous, contiguous, Thuc., Plat.:—c. dat. continuous with or contiguous to, in a line with, Hdt., Eur.
of Time, continuous, unintermitting, Xen.; τὸ ξυνεχές = συνέχεια, Thuc.
of persons, constant, persevering, Xen.
adv. σῠνεχῶς, ionic -έως:
of Time, continually, Hes.; Sup. -έστατα Xen.
with Numbers, continuously, Ar., Thuc.
in epic συνεχές as adv., Il.; συνεχὲς αἰεί unceasing ever, Od.
entry.etym: σῡνεχές Hom., and σῡνεχέως Hes., the first syll. being lengthd.

entry.sense: to join in hating, Anth.

entry.etym: fut. mid. in pass. sense, Dem.
entry.sense: to hold or keep together, Il.: to enclose, encompass, embrace, Hes., Plat.

to keep together, keep from dispersing, of soldiers, Xen., Dem.: —then, σ. πόλιν to keep the state together, keep it from falling to pieces, Eur.; καὶ θεοὺς καὶ ἀνθρώπους ἡ κοινωνία ξ. Plat.; σ. τὴν πολιτείαν Dem.; so, ξ.τὴν εἰρεσίαν to keep the rowers together, make them pull in time, Thuc.
to constrain or force one to a thing, NTest.
to compress, oppress, Id.: Pass. to be constrained, oppressed, afflicted, Hdt., attic
intr. to meet, εἰς ἕν Arist.
to fall in with, c. dat., Babr.
a young friend, Eur.
to be an advocate, σ. τινί to be his advocate, plead his cause, Ar., Aeschin.; also σ. ὑπέρ τινος Dem.; περί τινος Arist.
σ. τῷ κατηγόρῳ to second the accuser, Soph.
advocacy of another's cause, a speech in his behalf, Aeschin.
of or for a συνήγορος:—τὸ συνηγορικόν the advocate's fee, being a drachma per diem paid to the public συνήγοροι, Ar.
speaking with, of the same tenor with, Soph.
as Subst. one who speaks with another, an advocate, Aesch.:—at Athens the συνήγοροι were of two kinds,
public advocates, ten being appointed annually to represent the state, Ar., Dem., etc.
private advocates, counsel, who were not allowed to take a fee, Dem.
Dep.
to rejoice together, Plat., Xen., etc.: —σ. τινι to rejoice with, sympathise with, Hdt., attic
c. dat. rei, to rejoice at a thing, be pleased, gratified, Arist.; ἐπί τινι Xen.
c. dat. pers. et rei, Soph.
to make pleasant to the taste:— generally, to help in cheering, Arist.
habitual intercourse, acquaintance, society, intimacy, Lat. consuetudo, Aeschin., etc.
habit, custom, habituation, Hhymn., Plat.: c. gen., ἔργου habituation to a thing, Dem.
the customary use of a phrase, Aeschin.
dwelling or living together, accustomed or used to each other, Hes.: like each other in habits, Thuc., Plat.:— σ. τινί intimate with one, Plat.
habituated, accustomed, τινί to a thing, Id.
of things, habitual, customary, usual, ordinary, Soph., Thuc.; τὸ ξύνηθες ἥσυχον your habitual quietness, Thuc.; τὸ σύνηθες custom, Xen.
adv. -θως, habitually, as is usual, Aeschin.
to have come together, to be assembled, to meet, Thuc.
σ. εἰς ἕν to meet in a point, Xen.
of like or equal age, Lat. aequalis, a playmate, comrade, Aesch., Anth.

entry.etym: from same root as ἤλυθον, aor2 of ἔρχομαι
entry.sense: a meeting, assembly, Anth.
a daily companion, Arist.
to pass the day together or with, τινί Xen., etc.
used in pl., like συνθῆκαι, agreements, covenants, solemn promises, Il.

entry.note: συνήορος, doric and attic συνάορος, ον,
entry.sense: linked with, accompanying, c. dat., Od., Pind.
absol. joined in wedlock, and as Subst. a consort, Eur.
to assist in rowing: generally, to assist, befriend, τινί Soph.
thickly covered, Hdt., Plut.:— metaph., ξυνηρεφὲς πρόσωπον her clouded face, Eur.
Pass. to be conquered together, Xen.
to sound together or in unison, Plut.
to ring with, echo to, c. dat., Theophr.
to sit with, σ. νυκτί to take counsel with the night, Eur.
sitting with or together with, Ζηνὶ σύνθακος θρόνων partner with Zeus of his throne, Soph.:— generally, a partner, Eur.
to warm together:—metaph. to warm or soothe by flattery besides, Aesch.
to bury together, join in burying, Aesch., Trag., Plat., etc.; τινά τινι one with another, Eur.:—Pass. to be buried with, τινί Hdt., Thuc., etc.
Dep.
to view together, of spectators at games, Plat., Xen.
to examine together, Xen.
a fellow-spectator, Plat.
to reap together, Ar.
mostly in pl., like συνθῆκαι, a covenant, treaty, Il.; epic gen. pl. συνθεσιάων Id.
a putting together, composition, combination, Plat.; γραμμάτων συνθέσεις, i. e. syllables and words, Aesch.:—also, of an author's composition, Isocr.
metaph., like συνθεσία, an agreement, treaty, Pind., Plut.
Lat. synthesis was a suit of clothes, Mart.; esp. a loose gown, worn at dinner-parties, Id.
