one must compound, Plat.
skilled in putting together, constructive, Plat., Luc.
put together, composite, compound, Plat., Xen.: complex, Arist.
put together, fictitious, Aesch.
metaph. agreed upon, ἐκ συνθέτου by agreement, Lat. ex composito, Hdt.
to run together with: metaph., οὐχ ἡμῖν συνθεύσεται ἥδε γε βουλή this counsel will not run smoothly, will not succeed, for us, Od.
to run together, meet in one point, Xen.
to act as θεωρός or go to a festival together, Lys.; τινί with one, Ar.
a composition, of words and sentences, Luc.
a conventional agreement, convention, compact, Plat., Arist.; ἐκ συνθήκης, ex composito, by agreement, Plat.; κατὰ συνθήκην conventionally, Arist.

the article of a compact or treaty, Thuc.:—mostly in pl. the articles of agreement, and collectively, a contract, compact, covenant, treaty, Hdt., attic; συνθήκας ποιέεσθαί τινι Hdt., Ar.; ἐκ τῶν συνθηκῶν according to the covenant, Isocr.; κατὰ τὰς σ. Thuc.
anything agreed upon, a preconcerted signal, Hdt., Thuc.; so, δέλτον ἐγγεγραμμένην ξυνθήματα having symbols inscribed upon it, Soph.
a watchword, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; σ. παρέρχεται the word is passed round, Xen.; σ. παραδιδόναι, παραγγέλλειν to pass it, Id.
any token or sign, Soph.
= συνθῆκαι, an agreement, covenant, Plat.; σ. ποιεῖσθαι Xen.; ἀπὸ συνθήματος by agreement, Lat. ex composito, Hdt., Thuc.; so, ἐκ σ. Hdt.
one who joins in quest of, τινός Xen.
to hunt together, join in the chase, Xen.; τινί with one, Id.
to catch or find together, in Mid., Soph.:—Pass., χεῖρες συνθηρώμεναι hands caught and bound together, Id.
hunting with, τινι Xen.: absol. hunting in company, Anth.
c. gen. joining in quest of, Xen.
a partner in the θίασος: generally, a fellow, comrade, Ar.
to crush together:—Pass. to be broken in pieces, NTest.
to press together, compress, Arist.

to die with or together, Aesch., Soph., etc.; c. dat., θανόντι συνθανεῖν Soph.:—of things, συνθνήσκουσα σποδός embers expiring with (the flames), Aesch.; ἡ γὰρ εὐσέβεια σ. βροτοῖς accompanies them even in death, Soph.
a partaker in a feast, Eur.
Pass. to be broken in pieces, shivered, Eur.
to break in pieces, shiver, Eur.
mourning with, τινι Anth.: a partner in mourning, Arist.
to share in a triumph, Plut.
enthroned with, τινι Anth.
sounding together with, accompanying, c. dat., Anth.
to break in pieces: to crush, NTest.
to offer sacrifice together, join in sacrifice, Aeschin.; τινί with one, Eur.
a fellow-priest, Plut.
to sink in, collapse, Theocr., Plut.
to sink, of the wind, Luc.
a settlement, collapse, Plut.
to sit together, to hold a sitting, Hdt.

entry.note: attic ξυν 2 pers. -ίης 3rd sg. and pl. -ιεῖ, -ιοῦσι imperat. ξυνίει 3rd sg. subj. -ίῃ inf. -ιεῖ epic -ῑέμεν part. -ιείς imperf. συνίην or -ίειν 3rd pl. ξυνίεσαν epic ξύνιεν fut. συνήσω aor1 συνῆκα epic ξυνέηκα aor2 imperat. συνές part. συνείς Mid., 3 sg. aor2 ξύνετο, 1st pl. subj. συνώμεθα
entry.sense: to bring or set together, in hostile sense, like Lat. committere, ἔριδι ξυνέηκε μάχεσθαι Il.
Mid. to come together, come to an agreement, Id.
metaph. to perceive, hear, c. acc. rei, Hom., etc.; c. gen. pers., Il.; rarely c. gen. rei, Id.
to understand, ξ. ἀλλήλων to understand one another's language, Hdt.; mostly c. acc. rei, Id., attic:—absol., τοῖς ξυνιεῖσι to the intelligent, Theogn.
to pertain to, interest, Arist.
a joint commander of horse, Hdt.
a comrade in cavalry service, Dem.
to set together, combine, associate, unite, band together, Hdt., Thuc.; μαντικὴν ἑαυτῷ συστῆσαι to bring prophetic art into union with himself, i. e. to win, acquire it, Hdt.
to put together, organise, frame, Thuc., Dem.:— to contrive, σ. θάνατον ἐπί τινι Hdt.; σ. τιμάς to settle prices, Dem.; so in aor1 mid., Isocr.
to bring together as friends, introduce or recommend one to another, τινά τινι Plat., etc.: Pass., συνεστάθη Κύρῳ Xen.
of a debtor, to offer another as a guarantee, τινά τινι Isocr.
Pass., with aor2 act. συνεστάθη Κύρῳ Xen.
of part. συνεστηκώς, contr. συνεστώς, ῶσα, ώς or ός, ionic συνεστεώς, εῶσα, εώς: also fut. mid. συστήσομαι: — to stand together, Hdt., Xen.; of soldiers, to form in order of battle, Xen.

in hostile sense, πολέμοιο συνεσταότος when battle is joined, Il.:—so, of persons, συνίστασθαί τινι to meet him in fight, be engaged with, Hdt., attic:—absol., συνεστηκότων τῶν στρατηγῶν when the generals were at issue, Hdt.
to be involved in a thing, λιμῷ καὶ καμάτῳ Id.; συνεστῶτες ἀγῶνι Thuc.
to form a league or union, Id.; τὸ ξυνιστάμενον the conspirators, Ar.; so, οἱ ξυνεστῶτες, τὸ συνεστηκός Thuc., Aeschin.
generally, to be connected or allied, as by marriage, c. acc. cogn., λέχος Ἡρακλεῖ ξυστᾶσα Soph.
to be put together, organised, framed, Xen.
to arise, become, take place, Dem.
to hold together, endure, continue, Hdt.: in military sense, ξυνεστὼς στρατός a well-disciplined army, Eur.; στράτευμα συνεστηκός a standing army, Dem.
to be compact, solid, firm, Xen.
to be contracted, ξυνεστὸς φρενῶν = σύστασις B. II. 2, Eur.
knowing along with another, conscious, ὡς θεοὶ ξυνίστορες as the gods are witnesses, Soph., etc.
c. acc. (with the verbal constr.), πολλὰ συνίστορα κακά conscious of many evils, Aesch.
to help to dry up:—metaph. to join with in reducing, Eur.
to help to strengthen, Xen.
to be afflicted, Plat.
to dwell with others, c. dat., Aesch., Soph.
to pack tight together, Hdt.
a shipmate, Soph.
to engage in a sea-fight along with others, c. dat., Hdt., Ar.
a shipmate, Soph., Eur.
to tend together, of the shepherd: generally, to make one's associate, Plut.
to incline to a point, converge, Plut.
to consent, agree, Soph.
cloudy, overcast, Thuc.
to collect clouds, Ar.:—impers. συννεφεῖ it is cloudy (cf. ὕει), Arist.
metaph. of persons, συννεφοῦσα ὄμματα wearing a clouded look, Eur.
clouded over, cloudy:—of persons, gloomy, Eur.
to pile or heap together, heap up, Hdt.:—Pass., perf. part. ξυννενημένος Thuc.; ionic 3rd pl. perf. pass. συννενέᾰται Hdt.
to swim together or with, Luc.
Dep. to swim with, τινι Luc.
to have part in a victory with, τινί Eur.
to meditate or reflect upon a thing, Soph., Plat.:—so in Mid., Eur.
to perceive by thinking, comprehend, understand, Plat., etc.:— so in Mid., Ar.
meditation, deep thought, Soph., etc.; συννοίῃ ἐχόμενος wrapt in thought, Hdt.
anxious thought, anxiety, Aesch., Eur.; συννοίᾳ οἷον δέδρακε by remorse for the deed, Eur.
feeding together, gregarious, Ar., etc.: metaph., ἄταισι σύννομοι associated with miseries, Aesch.
σ. τινί τινος partner with one in a thing, λέκτρων ξύννομε partner of the bed, Id.: metaph., θαλάσσης σύννομοι πέτραι, of the Symplegades which lie between two seas, Eur.
absol. as Subst., σύννομος, a partner, mate, of soldiers, Aesch., Soph.; of a wife, Soph.
in deep thought, thoughtful, Isocr.
thoughtful, circumspect, Arist.
to be sick or ill together, Eur.; τινί with one, Id.
helping to deck a bride, Eur.
to travel in company, Plut.
a journey in company, Cic.
a party of travellers, caravan, Strab., NTest.
the member of a σύνοδος, Anth.
to travel together, τινί with one, Luc.
a travelling together, Babr.
a fellow-traveller, Xen., Luc.
an assembly, meeting, Hdt., attic; ξύνοδοι political unions, Ar., Thuc.
a national meeting, like πανήγυρις, Thuc., Arist.
in hostile sense, a meeting of two armies, Ar., Thuc., etc.
of things, a coming together, in-coming, χρημάτων σύνοδοι Hdt.
a meeting, junction, κυάνεαι σύνοδοι θαλάσσης, of the straits of the Hellespont, Eur.; ἡ ξ. τοῦ πλησίον ἀλλήλων τεθῆναι the junction resulting from approximation, Plat.

entry.note: 1st pl. ξύνισμεν 3rd pl. -ίσᾱσι imperat. ξύνισθι inf. -ειδέναι plup. with imperf. sense, συνῄδειν attic -ῄδη dual -ῄστην pl. -ῇσμεν, -ῇστε, -ῇσαν ionic 2nd pl. -ῃδέᾰτε fut. συνείσομαι rarely συνειδήσω
entry.etym: perf. with pres. sense, there being no pres. συνείδω
entry.sense: to share in knowledge, be cognisant of a thing, be privy to it, Lat. conscius esse, Hdt., attic
ἑαυτῷ συνειδέναι τι to be conscious of a thing, Ar., Plat., etc.:—with part., which may be
in nom., ξ. ἐμαυτῷ οὐδ’ ὁτιοῦν σοφὸς ὤν Plat.; without the reflex. Pron. to be conscious that, ξύνοισθά γ’ εἰς ἔμ’ οὐκ εὔορκος ὤν Eur.
in dat., ξ. ἐμαυτῷ οὐδὲν ἐπισταμένῳ I am conscious that I know nothing, Plat.
in acc., ξύνοιδ’ Ὀρέστην σε ἐκπαγλουμένην I know well that thou admirest him, Aesch.
absol. ξυνειδώς, an accomplice, ξ. τις Thuc.; also, ὁ ξ. τινι Id.
neut. τὸ συνειδός = συνείδησις, joint knowledge, consciousness, Dem.
to bind together as friends or kinsmen, to associate or combine with, τινά τινι Plut., etc.: Pass. to be closely united, Arist.
to dwell together, Plat., etc.; σ. τινί to live with, Aesch., etc.
to live together in wedlock, cohabit, Hdt., Eur., etc.; τούτων συνοικησάντων γίνεται Κλεισθένης from their marriage sprang Cleisthenes, Hdt.
metaph., ἄχθος ᾧ ξυνοικεῖ the grief with which he is associated, Soph.; so, σ. φόβῳ Eur.; ἡδοναῖς, ἀμαθίᾳ Plat.; ἱππικοῖς ἐν ἤθεσι ξ. being versed in the ways of horses, Eur.
reversely, with the thing as subject, γῆρας ἵνα πάντα κακὰ κακῶν ξυνοικεῖ old age with which all evils are associated, Soph.; of the poisoned robe of Hercules, to cling closely, Id.
c. acc. loci, to colonise jointly with, Κυρηναίοισι σ. Λιβύην Hdt.:—Pass., of a country, to be thickly peopled, Xen.
that with which one lives, a housefellow, Hdt.
cohabitation, πωλέεσθαι ἐπὶ συνοικήσι (ionic for -ήσει), Hdt.
a house-fellow, Aesch.
= συνοίκησις, Παλλάδος δέξομαι ξυνοικίαν will accept the offer of living with her, Aesch.
a body of people living together, a settlement, community, Plat.
a house in which several families live, a house divided into flats, Lat. insula, opp. to οἰκία (a dwelling occupied by one family), Thuc., Xen., etc.
a back-room, outhouse, Ar.
to make to live with, Isocr.; σ. τινὶ τὴν θυγατέρα to give him one's daughter in marriage, Hdt.

to combine in one city, unite under a capital or metropolis, ξ. πάντας (sc. ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας) Thuc.:—Pass., ξυνοικισθείσης πόλεως the city having been regularly formed, opp. to κατὰ κώμας οἰκίζεσθαι, Id.
to join in peopling or colonising a country, Eur., Thuc.
generally to unite, associate, Plut.
a joint lodging: pl. συνοίκια (sc. ἱερά), τά, a public feast in memory of Theseus' uniting all Attica under Athens, celebrated on the 17th Boedromion, Thuc.
union with the capital, Thuc.
a living together, marriage, Plut.
= συνοίκισις, Id.
a fellow-colonist, Pind.
to build together, Plut.:— metaph. in Pass. to be edified together, of believers, NTest.
Pass. to be built in with other materials, λίθοι ξυνῳκοδομημέναι Thuc.
dwelling in the same house with others, c. dat., Aesch.; ξ. εἰσιέναι to enter the house as an inmate, Soph.:—of persons living in the same country, a fellow-inhabitant, denizen, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
metaph. associated with, wedded to, used to, of persons, ξ. ἀλλαγᾷ βίου Soph.; κακῷ Plat.:—of things, associated with, σκότῳ λιμὸς ξύνοικος Aesch., etc.
living at home together: c. gen., σ. κακῶν a partner in mischief, Eur.
to have compassion on, τινά Xen.
Dep. to hold the same opinion with others, to assent, Plat.
to slip and fall together, Plut., etc.
to destroy together, Bion.:—Mid., aor2 -ωλόμην, to perish along with, τινι Eur.
to raise a loud cry together, Xen.
all together, Plat., etc.
τὸ σύνολον, as adv. on the whole, in general, altogether, Id., etc.:—reg. adv. συνόλως, Isocr.
one of the same blood, a brother or sister, Aesch., Eur.
to make quite level, Plut.
to follow along with, attend on, τινί Solon.; absol., Eur.
a comrade, Theocr.
to converse with, τινί NTest.
to swear together, Xen., Plut.
to promise by oath, τί τινι Soph.; ξυνώμοσαν θάνατον πατρί joined in swearing death against him, Aesch.
to join in a league or confederacy, Id., Thuc.
to form a confederacy with others, c. dat., Thuc.: in bad sense, to conspire, Hdt., Ar., etc.
to be similarly affected with, τινί Arist.

to say the same thing with, to agree with, τινί Hdt., Xen., etc.:— to confess together, confess, concede, αὐτὰ ταῦτα Thuc.:—of disputants, to agree upon certain points, c. acc., Xen., Plat.;— so in Mid., Plat.:—Pass., τὰ ἄλλα συνωμολόγηται Xen., etc.
to agree to do, promise, τί τινι Id.
to come to terms with, make a covenant with, Id.
to abut upon a place, c. dat., NTest.
having the same name with, c. gen., Anth.
a companion, Plat.
under arms together, allied, Eur.
seeing the whole together, taking a comprehensive view, Plat.
that can be seen at a glance, in full view, Arist.
to see together or at the same time, Xen.
to see in one view, see at a glance, whether with the eyes or mind, Plat., Dem.:—in speaking, to take a general view, Isocr., etc.
Dep.:— to be angry together with, τινι Isocr., Dem., etc.
to be conterminous, Polyb.
dawning along with, σύνορθρον αὐγαῖς dawning with the first beams of day, Aesch.
to rouse or stir up together, Il.:—Pass., συνορινόμεναι φάλαγγες the lines with one impulse, Id.
bound together by oath, Xen.
to bring to anchor together, Xen.
Pass. to start or set forth together, (in poet. aor2 part. συνόρμενος), Aesch.
conterminous with, τῇ Ἀττίκῃ or τῆς Ἀττίκης Plut.: metaph., κόνις πηλοῦ κάσις ξύνουρος dust twin-sister of mud, Aesch.

a being with, social intercourse, society, conversation, communion, Hdt., attic; ἡ τοῦ θείου σ. communion with the divinity, Plat.; so, τῆς νόσου ξυνουσίᾳ by long intercourse with the disease, Soph.; ἡ πρὸς Σωκράτην σ. αὐτοῖν their intercourse with him, Xen.; in pl., ξυνουσίαι θηρῶν, = οἱ ξυνόντες θῆρες, Soph.
intercourse with a teacher, attendance on his lectures, Xen.
cohabitation, Plat., Xen.
a society, company, party, Hdt., Plat., etc.
a companion, disciple, Xen.
suited for society, sociable, Ar.
Pass. to have the brow knitted, ξυνωφρυωμένη with knitted brow, Soph.; ξυνωφρυωμένῳ προσώπῳ with frowning countenance, Eur.
with meeting eyebrows, Theocr.
Pass. to travel together in a chariot, Plut.
holding together, Anth.
a being held together, ἐν ξυνοχῇσιν ὁδοῦ at a narrow part of the road, Il.
constraint, affliction, anguish, NTest.
joined together: metaph. agreeing with, suiting, Eur.

entry.etym: epic intr. perf. of συνέχω, for συνόκωχα
entry.sense: to be held together, ὤμω ἐπὶ στῆθος συνοχωκότε shoulders contracted upon the chest, Il.
a general view, Plat.
prep. with dat., Lat. cum
along with, in company with, together with, δεῦρ’ ἤλυθε σὺν Μενελάῳ Il.

with collat. notion of help, σὺν θεῷ with God's help or blessing, (the God being conceived as standing with one), Hom., etc.; σὺν θεῷ εἰρημένον spoken as by inspiration, Hdt.: so, σὺν δαίμονι, σὺν Διί, σὺν Ἀθήνῃ Il.; so also, σύν τινι εἶναι or γίγνεσθαι to be with another, i. e. on his side, of his party, Xen.; οἱ σύν τινι any one's friends, followers, Id.

endued with, ἄκοιτις σὺν μεγάλῃ ἀρετῇ Od.: of things that belong or are attached to a person, στῆ σὺν δουρί Il.; σκῆπτρον, σὺν τῷ ἔβη Id.; αὐτῇ σὺν φόρμιγγι Id. (here, in attic, the σύν is often omitted).
of two or more things taken together, θύελλαι σὺν βορέῃ, ἄνεμος σὺν λαίλαπι Id.; also of coincidence in point of time, ἄκρᾳ σὺν ἑσπέρᾳ Pind.

of connexion or consequence, σὺν μεγάλῳ ἀποτῖσαι to pay with a great loss, i. e. suffer greatly, Il.; σὺν τῷ σῷ ἀγαθῷ to your advantage, Lat. tuo cum commodo, Xen.; σὺν μιάσματι attended with pollution, Soph.:— and, generally, in accordance with; σὺν δίκᾳ Pind., σὺν κόσμῳ, σὺν τάχει, etc., nearly = Advs. δικαίως, κοσμίως, ταχέως, attic.
with, by means of, σὺν νεφέεσσι κάλυψεν γαῖαν Od., Pind.; πλοῦτον ἐκτήσω σὺν αἰχμῇ Aesch.
with Ordin. Numerals, ἐμοὶ σὺν ἑβδόμῳ, i. e. myself with six others, Id.
σύν AS ADV. together, Aesch., Soph.
besides, also, likewise, Od., Trag.
IN COMPOS.
with, along with, together, Lat. con-:—in Compos. with a trans. Verb, as κτείνω, σύν may refer to two things, to kill one person as well as another, or, to join with another in killing.
of the completion of an action, altogether, completely, as in συμπληρόω, συντέμνω.
joined with numerals, σύνδυο two together or by twos, two and two; so σύντρεις, σύμπεντε, etc., like Lat. bini, terni, etc.
συν- before β μ π φ ψ, becomes συμ-; before γ κ ξ χ, συγ-; before λ, συλ-; before σ, συσ-, but before στ, συ-, as συστῆναι.
to be vexed along with, τινί Polyb.
to love along with, τινί Polyb.
that which is put together in order:
a body of troops, squadron, contingent, Xen.
the constitution of a state, σ. πολιτείας a form of constitution, Isocr.
an arrangement of musical notes, Arist.
a regular collection of writings, a work, book, doctrine, Plut.
= σύνταξις II. 3, Aeschin.
the leader of a σύνταγμα (I), Luc.
to endure hardships together, share in misery, Soph.
to stretch together, πολλῶν πείρατα συντανύσαις (doric for -ύσας) bringing together the issues of many events, Pind.
a putting together, arranging, arrangement, organisation, order, Thuc., Xen.: rule, Dem.
a systematic treatise, Arist.: a narrative, Polyb.
grammatical construction, syntax, Luc.
a body of troops, ἡ εἰς μυρίους σ. their contingent towards 10, 000, Xen.
a covenant, contract, Dem.
an assigned impost, contribution, Id., Aeschin.
a payment, allowance, pension, Dem.

to throw all together into confusion, to confound, disturb, trouble, Lat. conturbare, Il., Hdt., attic:—Pass., αἰθὴρ πόντῳ ξυντετάρακται air is confounded with sea, Aesch.: to be thrown into confusion, of soldiers, Thuc.; of social order, Soph., Thuc.; metaph. of persons, to be confounded, greatly troubled, much distressed, Hdt.

to put in order together, esp. of soldiers, to draw up, put in array, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; σ. πεζοὺς τῷ ἱππικῷ to draw up the foot in line with the horse, Xen.:—Pass. to be drawn up in line, Eur., etc.; μάλιστα ξυντεταγμένοι παντὸς τοῦ στρατοῦ in the best order of all the army, Thuc.: —so in Mid. to form in line, συνταξάμενοι τισι or μετά τινων with others, Xen.;—but the Mid. is also trans., συνταξάμενος τὴν φάλαγγα having drawn up his phalanx, Id.
in Pass., of single persons, to be collected, resolute, steady, Thuc., Xen.
to arrange, organise, Plat.:—in bad sense, to concoct, Aeschin.:—Pass. to be organised, Arist.; οἱ συντεταγμένοι the conspirators, Xen.
of taxation, to fix or assess a payment, Aeschin.:—Pass. to be organised for paying contributions, Dem.:—Mid. to agree to such assessment, Id.
c. inf. to ordain, prescribe, τινὰ ποιεῖν τι Xen., Aeschin.; of a physician, θεραπείαν σ. τινί Plut.:—Pass. to be prescribed, ταῦτα τῷ ναυάρχῳ συνετάχθη Dem.
Mid. to agree together, Id.
Mid. also, σ. τινι to take leave of one, bid him farewell, Anth.
to hurry on, τι Hdt.
intr., ὁ βίος συνταχύνει life hastens to an end, Id.
to stretch together, strain, draw tight, brace up, Eur., Plat.
to strain to the uttermost, urge on, exert, Eur.; γνώμῃ συντεταμένῃ with earnest purpose, Xen.
intr. in Act. to exert oneself, strive, hasten, Lat. contendere, Plat., Plut.
to direct earnestly to one point, Plat.
intr. to direct all one's powers to one object, to be bent upon doing a thing, c. inf., Eur.; σ. εἴς τι Dem.; πρός τι Isocr., etc.
to help to build a wall or fortification, Thuc., Xen.
Dep. to conjecture from signs or symptoms, to calculate, Thuc., Xen.
to breed children with, ἀνδρί Xen.
to belong to, Pind.
a joint payment, joint contribution for public burdens, Dem.; εἰς σ. ἄγειν τὰς χορηγίας, i. e. to leave the choregia to be defrayed by subscription, Id.
at Athens, a partnership for bearing public burdens, Decret. ap. Dem.
generally, a company, of the gods, who separately were called τέλειοι, Aesch.
combination of efforts, the consummation of a scheme, Polyb.
to bring quite to an end, complete, accomplish, σ. τὴν δαπάνην to make up the whole expense, Dem.; σ. εἰς τὰ ἑκατὸν ἅρματα to make up the number of 100 chariots, Xen.:—so in Mid., Polyb.
to pay towards common expenses, contribute, Aeschin., Dem.

since at Athens all citizens were classed acc. to the contributions to which they were liable, σ. εἰς . . meant to belong to a class, be counted in it, σ. εἰς ἄνδρας Isocr.; εἰς τοὺς νόθους Dem.:—hence σ. εἰς Ἀθήνας, εἰς τὸ Ἀρκαδικόν, used of a number of small states tributary or subject to a larger, Thuc.; c. dat., σ. Θηβαίοις Isocr.
joining in payment, a contributor, Dem.
belonging to the same συντέλεια (II) or company, Id.:—metaph., [οὔτε] Πάρις, οὔτε σ. πόλις neither Paris nor his associate city, Aesch.
tributary, Dem.
to cut in pieces: to cut down, cut short, Lat. conci_dere, Thuc.:—metaph. to curtail, abridge, Aesch., Ar.:—esp. of expenses, Thuc., Xen.: of persons, to cut off, Soph.
σ. χιτῶνας to cut out, shape them, Xen.
seemingly intr. (sub. ὁδόν) to cut the road short, cut across, Hdt.:—so, of speech, to cut the matter short, speak briefly, Eur.
really intr., τοῦ χρόνου συντάμνοντος as the time became short, Hdt.
to whistle an accompaniment, Theophr.
to border on, τινί Polyb.
bordering on, close together, Anth.

entry.etym: adverb from part. perf. pass. of συντάσσω
entry.sense: in set terms, Plat.

entry.etym: adverb from part. perf. pass. of συντείνω
entry.sense: earnestly, eagerly, vigorously, Ar., Plat.

to bore through so as to meet, σ. τοὺς μυχοὺς ἀλλήλοις carrying their creeks through so as to meet one another, Hdt.; ἕτερον [μέταλλον] συντρῆσαι εἰς τὰ τῶν πλησίον to run another gallery into one's neighbour's mines, Dem.:—Pass. to be carried by a connecting channel or duct, Plat., Arist.
metaph., δι’ ὤτων συντέτραινε μῦθον let the word pierce through thy ears, Aesch.
to join in plots with, τινί Plut.
practising the same art, c. gen. one's mate or fellow-workman, Ar.
to fuse into one mass, to weld together, Lat. conflare, Plat.
to melt down, dissolve: metaph. to make to waste or pine away, Eur.

Pass. συντήκομαι, aor1 -ετήχθην, aor2 -ετάκην [ᾰ]: and in same sense intr. perf. act. συντέτηκα:— to be fused into one mass: metaph., σ. τινι to become absolutely one with another, c. dat., Eur., Plat.
to melt away, disappear, Xen.:— metaph. to waste or fall away, Eur.
to preserve together: Pass., NTest.
to watch one's opportunity, Plut.
to put together, Hdt., Xen., etc.; σ. ἄρθρα στόματος to close the lips, Eur.
in Arithm. to add together, Hdt., Eur., etc.: also συντιθεὶς γέλων adding laughter, Soph.
to put together, of builders, Thuc., Xen.
to construct, frame, build, Hdt.:— σ. τι ἀπό or ἔκ τινος to compose or make one thing of another, Id.
to construct or frame a story, Eur., Ar., etc.:—of an author, to compose, Thuc.
to frame, devise, contrive, ὁ συνθεὶς τάδε the framer of this plot, Soph.; σ. ψευδεῖς αἰτίας Dem.
to put together, take in, comprise, Eur.; ἐν βραχεῖ ξυνθεὶς λόγῳ putting things shortly together, Soph.
Mid. συντίθεμαι, to put together for oneself, i. e. to observe, take heed to, σύνθετο βουλήν, ἀοιδήν Hom.; and, simply, to perceive, hear, ὅπα σύνθετο Od.: absol., σύνθεο take heed, Hom.
to set in order, organise, Xen.
to conclude, form, ἄνδρεσσι κακοῖς συνθέμενοι φιλίην Theogn.; συντίθεσθαι συμμαχίην Hdt.; σ. ναῦλον to agree upon the fare, Xen.:—Pass., τοῦ συντεθέντος χρόνου at the time agreed upon, Plat.
c. inf. to covenant or agree to do, Hdt., Thuc.
absol. to make a covenant, Hdt., Xen.
to honour together or alike, Lys.
to estimate together:—Mid., συνετιμήσαντο ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ ταύτην τὴν εἰσφοράν they fixed this as the estimate of my contribution, Dem.
to shake to the foundations, σὺν δὲ μάχαν ἐτίναξε, i. e. closed with him, Theocr.
to wound in many places, Xen.
to venture together:—doric 2nd sg. aor2 συν-έτλας, Eur.
conciseness, Plat., Arist.
Lat. concisus, cut short, abridged, shortened, esp. of a road, σ. ἀτραπός a short cut, Ar.; συντομώτατον the shortest cut, Hdt.; τὰ ξυντομώτατα Thuc.; ἡ σύντομος (sub. ὁδός) Hdt.
of language, concise, brief, curt, short, Aesch., Eur., etc.
of Time, ξυντομωτάτη διαπολέμησις Thuc.
adv. -μως, concisely, shortly, briefly, Aesch., etc.:—so also neut. pl. σύντομα Soph.: comp. and Sup. -ώτερον, -ώτατα, Isocr.; also -ωτάτως, Soph.
of Time, shortly, immediately, Id., Xen., etc.
intense application or exertion, Arist.
strained tight, ἔχειν τὸ σ. to be strained tight, Xen.
intense, impetuous, violent, Soph.
of persons, earnest, serious, severe, vehement, Plat., etc.: so of Music, severe, Arist.:—adv. -νῶς, intensely, eagerly, severely, Plat.; so neut. pl., σύντονα Eur.:—comp. -ώτερον, Arist.
to act tragedy together, Luc.
a messmate, Xen.; βίον σ. ἔχειν to live with one, Eur.
three together, by threes, Od.
to feed together or besides, Xen.
Pass. to grow up together, Id.; τινι with one, Eur.
of feelings or sentiments, to grow up with, Arist., Plut.: to be organised, of bodies, Plat.
to run together so as to meet, to encounter, Il.:—metaph., εἰπὲ τῷ μόρῳ συντρέχει say with what death she has met, Soph.
to assemble, gather together, Hdt.; of clouds, to gather, Id.; of liquids, to be mingled with, c. dat., Soph.
to come together, concur, agree, Hdt., Xen.
to concur, coincide, of time, Eur., Dem.; σ. τινί to concur or coincide with, Soph.
to run alongside, Xen.
to shatter as with a trident, Eur.
to rub together, σ. τὰ πυρεῖα to rub dry sticks together to procure a light, Luc.
to shiver to atoms, Ar., etc.; σ. τὰς ναῦς to stave them in, by running them aground, Thuc.
of persons, to beat to a jelly, crush, Lat. contundere, Eur.:—c. gen. partis, συντρίβειν τῆς κεφαλῆς Isocr.; and in Pass., συντριβῆναι τῆς κεφαλῆς to have one's head broken, Ar.
a partner in the equipment of a trireme, Dem.
to be a συντριήραρχος, Lys.
a being reared together, common nurture, Plut.
a brood, Anth.
brought up together with another, c. dat., Hdt., Ar.:—often of domestic animals, Hdt., Xen.:—absol., τὸ σ. γένος the people bred up with me, Soph.
generally, living with, Id.; σ. ὄμμα the eye or presence of a companion, Id.; σ. ὢν (sc. ἀνάγκαις) being born to difficulties, Eur.
of things, having grown up with one, congenital, natural, Soph.; τὰ ξύντροφα every-day evils, Thuc.:— σ. τινι natural or habitual to, τῇ Ἑλλάδι πενίη σύντροφος Hdt.
act. a helping in the preservation, τινος of a thing, Xen.
to run together, Plut.

to meet with, fall in with, τινί Hdt., Soph., etc.: οἱ συντυχόντες, of two persons meeting, Hdt.; but, ὁ συντυχών, like ὁ τυχών, the first that meets one, any one, Eur.; ὁ ἀεὶ ξυντυχών Id.; so of things, τὸ συντυχόν what first comes to hand, anything common, mean, bad, Hdt., Xen.
rarely, like τυγχάνω, c. gen., which is governed by σύν, συντυχὼν κακῶν ἀνδρῶν having like others met with evil men, Soph.

of accidents, to happen to, befall, τὰ συντυχόντα σφι Hdt.:—absol. to happen, fall out, εὖ ξυντυχόντων if things go well, Aesch.; ὁ ξ. κίνδυνος Thuc.:—impers., συνετύγχανε, συνέτυχε it happened that . . , c. inf., Id.
to join in slaying tyrants, Luc.
to make into cheese together: hence, comically, τἀκ Βοιωτῶν συντυρούμενα the troubles that are being concocted on the part of the Boeotians, Ar.

an occurrence, a hap, chance, event, incident, Solon., Hdt., attic; ὡς ἑκάστοις τῆς ξυντυχίας ἔσχεν according to the circumstances of each party, Thuc.; κατὰ συντυχίην by chance, Hdt.:—in pl. the chances of life, circumstances, Thuc.
sometimes a happy chance, success, Pind., Hdt.;—or a mishap, misfortune, Eur.
to indicate together, τί τινι Polyb.
Mid. to undergo together, Plut.
Dep. to play a part along with others: to help another in maintaining a thing, Plut.
Mid. to help in composing, Plut.
to cooperate with, τινί NTest., Luc.
to weave together: metaph. to frame with art, devise cunningly, Od., Luc.:—Pass., ὥστε ταῦτα συνυφανθῆναι so that this web was woven, i. e. this business undertaken, Hdt.
to be in travail together, Eur.
singing or sounding in unison with, responsive, Eur.
absol. in harmony, accordant, Plat.
metaph. according with, in harmony with, τινί Hdt., Eur., etc.
to force together, compress forcibly, Xen.
a being leagued by oath, conspiracy, Ar., Thuc., etc.; ξ. δήμου καταλύσεως for putting down the democracy, Thuc.
a confederacy, Id.
a body of men leagued by oath, a political union or club, Id., Plat.
a fellow-conspirator, confederate, Hdt., attic
leagued by oath: ξυνώμοτον, τό, a confederacy, Thuc.
Dep. to collect by offering money, σ. ἵππον to hire a body of cavalry, Hdt.
to buy up, Lat. coemere, Xen., etc.:—the perf. συνεώνημαι is pass., ὁ συνεωνημένος σῖτος corn bought up Lys.; but act. in Dem.
a synonym, Arist.
of like name, Eur., Arist.
one who drives a συνωρίς, Luc.
to yoke together:—Mid., ξυνωρίζου χέρα join thy hand with mine, Eur.
Dep. to drive a pair, Ar.
a pair of horses, Lat. biga, Eur., Ar.
generally, a pair or couple of anything, Trag.; ποδοῖν ξυνωρίς a coupling fetter for the feet, Aesch.
to join in aiding or relieving, τινά Xen.; rarely τινί, Soph.
of Time, perpetually, continually, Hes.
slaughter of swine, Anth.
swine-slayer; fem. συοφόντις, Anth.
subst. Pron. of the second pers., thou, you.
strengthd. by compos. with the enclit. γε, σύγε, (like ἔγωγε) thou at least, for thy part, in Hom., etc., doric τύγα Theocr.
Dual nom. and acc. σφῶι, you two, both of you, Hom.
Pl. ye, you, Hom., etc.,
[χώρα] the territory of Syracuse, Thuc.
Syracusan, and as Subst. a Syracusan.
ionic Συρήκουσαι, doric Συράκοσαι, and Σῠράκοσσαι, Syracuse, Hdt., etc.
a Syrian woman, Ar.
properly συρόγαστρος, trailing the belly, as a worm, Anth.
dragging, in a long line, Aesch.
(sc. γῆ) Syria, Hdt., etc.: Σ. ἡ Παλαιστίνη Palestine, Id.: Κοίλη Σ. the district between Libanus and Anti-libanus, Strab.
the sound of a pipe, Eur., Ar.
a whistling, hissing, Xen.
a pipe:
a musical pipe, a shepherd's pipe, Panspipe, Il., Hes., attic
anything like a pipe:
a spear-case, = δορατοθήκη, Il.
the hole in the nave of a wheel, Trag.
a duct or channel in the body, in pl. the nostrils, Soph.
to play the σῦριγξ, to pipe, Eur., Theocr.; c. acc. cogn., συρίζων ὑμεναίους Eur.
to whistle, hiss, Aesch., Ar.:—c. acc. cogn., συρίζων φόνον hissing forth murder, Aesch.
to hiss an actor, Lat. explodere, Dem.
to speak like a Syrian, Luc.
to speak like a Syrian, Luc.
Syrian-born, Orac. ap. Hdt.
of or from Syria, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
a piper, Luc.
adv. in the Syrian language, Σ. ἐπίστασθαι to understand Syrian, Xen.
purge-plant, a name given to the radish, as used by the Egyptians (v. μελανοσυρμαῖος), Hdt., Ar.
to take a purge, Hdt.
anything trailed or dragged:
a theatric robe with a long train, syrma in Juven.:— periphr., σ. τερηδόνος a long woodworm, Anth.
sweepings, refuse, litter, Heraclit. ap. Arist.
any lengthened sweeping motion, Lat. tractus, the track of meteors, Plat.; of storms, Anth.; the trail of a serpent, Plut.
a Syrian, Hdt., attic
Syros, one of the Cyclades, Strab.; called Σῠριή, in Od.
a Syro-phoenician, Luc.: fem. Συροφοίνισσα, NTest.
a dashing together, Plut.
to sew or stitch together, sew up, Lat. consuo, Hes., Hdt.
to do sacrifice together, Anth.
to flow together or in one stream, Plat.:—metaph. of men, to flow or stream together, Hdt., Xen.
to float together with, Luc.

entry.note: or -ύω fut. -ρήξω Pass., perf. -έρρηγμαι aor2 -ερράγην intr. perf. 2 -έρρωγα
entry.sense: to break in pieces, Plut.:—Pass., κακοῖσι συνέρρηκται he is broken down by sufferings, Od.
to dash together: Pass., of war, to break out, Plut.

intr. to break out together, break forth, of rivers, συρρήγνυσι ἐς τὸν Ἕρμον break into the Hermus, join it, Hdt.: so perf. συνέρρωγα (in pres. signf.) and plup. (in imperf.), ὁ πόλεμος ξυνερρώγει the war broke out, Thuc.
like συρράσσω, to meet in battle, engage, Plut.
Pass. to have the roots united, Luc.
the Syrtis, name of two large sand-banks (Major and Minor) on the coast of Libya, Hdt., etc.
anything swept together, sweepings, refuse, rubbish, litter, Lat. quisquiliae, Hes.
metaph. a mixed crowd, mob, rabble, Plat.: of a single person, one of the mob (cf. Hor. plebs eris), Id.
jumbled together, promiscuous, Luc.
to help in scattering, to toss about, Ar.
to make ready by putting together, to pack up baggage for another, Xen.
to help in preparing, τὸ δεῖπνόν τινι Ar.:—in bad sense, to contrive, concert, get up, Dem.

Mid., with perf. pass. συσκεύασθαι, to pack up one's baggage, to pack up, Lat. convasare, vasa colligere, Thuc., Xen., etc.: part. aor1 mid. and perf. pass. all packed up, in marching order, ready for a start, Xen.; also c. acc., συνεσκευασμένος τὰ ἑαυτοῦ ἐνθάδε with all his goods packed up and brought hither, Lys.
to contrive, get up, organise, Dem.
to bring together, scrape up for one's own use or advantage, σ. χρήματα Lycurg.
to arrange for one's own interests, band together, Dem.
to draw, drag, or trail along, Theocr.:—Pass. to trail along, Anth.
to drag by force, hale, Theocr.:—of rivers, to sweep or carry down with them, Anth.:—Pass. to be swept away, Plut.
a packing up, getting ready, for a journey or march, Xen.
Dep. to contrive, organise, Dem.
to live in the same tent with another, to mess together, Xen.; τινί with one, Id.
a dwelling in one tent: of soldiers, a messing together, Xen.
one who lives in the same tent, a messmate, Lat. contubernalis, Thuc., Xen.
to shade quite over, throw a shade over, shade closely or thickly, Hes.; γένυν σ., i. e.to get a beard, Eur.: metaph., συσκηνῶσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας Dem.
intr. to be thick-shaded, Eur.
closely shaded, thickly shaded, Xen.; σύσκιόν τι a closely-shaded place, Luc.
to contemplate along with or together, Plat.
to grow quite dark: impers., συσκοτάζει it grows dark, Thuc., Xen.
to look gloomy together, Xen.
to tear in pieces, NTest.
drawn together, closed by drawing together, Plat.
to draw together, draw up, contract, Plat., Luc.
to draw together by stitching, sew together, Xen.
in Mid. to draw along with one, Plut.
Pass., of soldiers, to be formed in close order (v. σπεῖρα II), Xen.; σ. ἐπὶ τόπον to march in such order to a place, Id.
to be coiled up, Luc.
to sow together, Luc.
to join in making a libation, Dem., Aeschin.
to assist zealously, τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Hdt.
to join in eating the sacrificial meat (τὰ σπλάγχνα), Ar.
to make haste together, to join in zealous exertion, Ar., Xen.: c. acc. rei, to pursue or execute zealously together with, τί τινι Xen.
Pass. to feel flattered by a thing, Polyb.
to join in celebrating, θυσίας θεῷ Eur.
to urge on together, βοῶν κάρηνα Hhymn.
Mid. to join in singing, Dem.
a fixed sign or signal, NTest.
a pledge, Anth.
to mess with, τινί Ar.:—absol. in pl. to mess together, Plat., Dem.
a messing together, a public mess, Xen.
a common meal, public mess, such as were used in Crete and Lacedaemon, Hdt., Plat., etc.
a messroom, common-hall, Eur., Plat.
one who eats together, a messmate, Theogn., Hdt., attic
to help to save or preserve, Eur., Thuc.
united in one body, NTest.
to be a partner in temperance, Eur.
standing close together, hand to hand, Thuc.
a fellow-rioter, NTest.
a putting together, composition, Arist.; σ. προσώπου a studied expression of countenance, of Pericles, Plut.
a bringing together, introduction, recommendation, Polyb., Plut.
（συνίσταμαι) a standing together, meeting: in hostile sense, close combat, conflict, Hdt.; metaph., σ. γνώμης a conflict of mind, intense anxiety, Thuc.
a meeting, a knot of men, Eur.; κατὰ ξυστάσεις γιγνόμενοι forming into knots, Thuc.: a political union, Dem.
friendship or alliance, Polyb.: a conspiracy, Plut.
construction, structure, constitution, Plat., Arist.: absol. a political constitution, Plat.
metaph. of the mind, σ. φρενῶν contraction, sternness, sullenness, Eur.
a member of the same faction, a partisan, Hdt.
standing together, planted closely, Arist.
to join in faction or sedition, take part therein, Thuc.
introductory, σ. ἐπιστολή a letter of introduction, NTest.
Pass. to be crucified with, τινι NTest.
to cover entirely, τινί with a thing, Plat.:—Pass., Xen.
to draw together, draw in: to shorten sail (sub. τὰ ἱστία), Ar.: to draw soldiers into a fort, Plut.
to contract, reduce, Plat., Dem.:—Pass. to cower together, Eur.; ξυστέλλεσθαι ἐς εὐτέλειαν to retrench, Thuc.
metaph. to lower, humble, abase, Isocr.:—Pass., Eur.
Pass., also, to be wrapped up, shrouded, Id.; aor2 part. συσταλείς, tucked up, ready for action, Ar.
to lament with, τινί Eur.; absol., NTest.
Pass. to wear a crown with, τινι Dem.
a whole compounded of parts, a system, Plat.:— a composition, Arist.
an organised government, constitution, Id.
a body of soldiers, a corps, Polyb.
of the Roman Senate, Plut.
to correspond to, τινί NTest.
a coordinate series, Arist.
standing in the same row, coordinate, correspondent, opp. to ἀντίστοιχος (standing in opposite rows), Arist.
a drawing together, contraction, limitation, Plut.
to put together, fabricate, Eur.
to unite, τινά τινι Anth.
a common campaign, Xen.

entry.note: fut. -εύσω and as Dep. συστρατεύομαι fut. -εύσομαι
entry.sense: act. and Dep. to make a campaign or serve together, to join or share in an expedition, absol., Hdt., Thuc., etc.; τινί with another, Hdt., Thuc.
to be the fellow-general of, τινός Dem.
a joint-commander, Eur., Thuc., etc.
a fellow-soldier, Lat. commilito, Xen., etc.
Dep. to encamp along with, τινι or σύν τινι Xen.
anything twisted up together: a body of men, a crowd, concourse, Polyb.

to twist up into a ball, Lat. conglobare: of animals, to gather themselves together, in preparing to spring, Plat.: of soldiers, σ. ἑωυτούς to collect themselves, rally, Hdt.: Pass., συστραφέντες in a body, Id.; ἐπὶ πεντήκοντα ἀσπίδων συνεστραμμένοι ἦσαν they were formed in a mass 50 deep, Xen.
of soldiers, also, συστρέφειν ἐπὶ δόρυ to wheel them to the right, Id.; σ. τὸν ἵππον to turn him sharply, Plut.
to form into an organised whole, unite, Hdt.:—Pass. to unite, club together, conspire, Thuc., Aeschin.
of sentences, narratives, and the like, to compress, Arist.: absol., συστρέψας γράφει writes briefly, curtly, Aeschin.:—Pass., ῥῆμα βραχὺ καὶ συνεστραμμένον a short and pithy saying, Plat.
a dense mass of men, a gathering of people, Hdt.
a sudden storm, Polyb.
to slay along with: Pass., aor2 inf. συσφαγῆναι to be slain with another, τινι Eur.
to condense:—Pass., Anth.
to conform one thing to another, τι πρός τι Arist.:—Pass. to form oneself after another, to be conformed to his example, NTest.
to be a fellow-pupil or companion in philosophy, to pass one's time with or together, Plut.
a hog-sty, Od.; συφεόνδε to the sty, Id.
a herd of swine, Anth.
a swineherd, Hom.
of Time, long, Hdt., etc.; σ. λόγος a long speech, Plat.

of Number, many, Hdt., Ar., etc.; many days together, Ar.:—c. gen., συχναὶ τῶν νήσων Hdt.:—absol., συχνοί many people together, Ar., etc.:—with sg. nouns, much, great, Id., Plat., etc.; τὸ πολίχνιον συχνὸν ποιεῖν to make the small town large, Plat.:—c. gen., τῆς μαρίλης συχνήν Ar.
the adv. συχνῶς (Antipho.) is rare, the neut. συχνόν, συχνά being used instead, often, much, Plat.: far, Xen.
dat. συχνῷ with comp. adj., νεώτερος ἐμοῦ καὶ συχνῷ younger by a good deal, Dem.
a bowl for catching the blood of the victim in sacrifices, Eur.
= σφάγιον, the victim, Id.
a slayer, butcher, Eur.: a murderer, cut-throat, Dem.:—in Soph., ὁ σφαγεὺς ἕστηκε the slayer is set, i. e. the sword on which Ajax is about to throw himself:— a sacrificial knife, Eur.
slaughter, butchery, in sg. and pl., Trag., Plat., etc.; αἵματος σφαγή the blood gushing from the wound, Aesch.; καθάρμοσον σφαγάς close the gaping wound, Eur.
the throat, the spot where the victim is struck (cf. Lat. jugulum, jugulari), in pl., Id., Thuc.
Dep. to slay a victim, sacrifice, Hdt., Xen.
in Act. Ar., Plut.:—hence aor1 pass. part. σφαγιασθείς, slain, sacrificed, Hdt., Xen.
a slaying, sacrificing, Eur., Plut.
a victim, offering, Soph., Eur.: —mostly in pl., Hdt., Aesch., etc.
slaughter, sacrifice, in pl., Eur.
slaying, slaughtering, σφ. μόρος slaughter, Soph.
a sacrificial knife, Eur.
only in pres. and imperf. to struggle, plunge, of horses, Aesch., Xen.; cf. ἀσφάδαστος.
to struggle, shew impatience, Plut.
a spasm, convulsion, Plat.
to slay, slaughter, properly by cutting the throat (v. σφαγή II), Hom.
esp. to slaughter victims for sacrifice, Il., Eur.
generally to slay, kill, first applied to human victims, Pind., Trag.; σφ. τινὰ ἐς τὸν κρητῆρα so that the blood run into the bowl, Hdt.
a ball, playing-ball, Od., Plat.
any ball: the terrestrial globe, the earth, Strab.
like a globe or ball, ἧκε δέ μιν σφαιρηδὸν ἑλιξάμενος Il.
to play at ball, Plat.
globular, spherical: τὰ σφαιρικά the doctrine of the spheres, astronomy, Anth.
a playing at ball, Arist.
a ball-court, Theophr.
ball-like, spherical, Plat.; σφαιροειδές, τό, a rounded end (cf. σφαιρόω II), Xen.
to make spherical, Strab.
to make spherical:—Pass. to be rounded, στήθεα ἐσφαίρωτο his chest was round and arched, Theocr.
Pass., also, ἀκόντια ἐσφαιρωμένα spears with buttons at the point, like our foils, Xen., Arist.
with a button at the end, Xen.
to be gangrened, ἐσφακέλισε τὸ ὀστέον Hdt.
gangrene:—generally, a spasm, convulsion, Aesch., Eur.: metaph., σφ. ἀνέμων the convulsive fury of winds, Aesch.
likely to make one stumble or trip: metaph. slippery, perilous, dangerous, Lat. lubricus, Hdt., Eur., etc.:— σφαλερόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it is dangerous to . . , Plat., etc.
（σφάλλομαι) ready to fall, tottering, reeling, staggering, Aesch., Soph.; σφ. σύμμαχοι Dem.

Lat. fall-o (the sigma being lost):—to make to fall, throw down, overthrow, properly by tripping up, to trip up in wrestling, Hom., Pind., Eur., etc.; σφ. ναῦς to throw her on her beam-ends, Plut.; ἵππος σφ. τὸν ἀναβάτην throws him, Xen.:—Pass. to be tripped up, Ar.; of a drunken man, σφαλλόμενος reeling, staggering, Id.

generally, to cause to fall, overthrow, defeat, Hdt., Soph., Thuc.:—Pass. to be overthrown, to fall, fail, be undone, become helpless, Hdt., attic; τόδ’ ἐσφάλη this mishap took place, Soph.; οὔ τι μὴ σφαλῶ γ’ ἐν σοί I shall not fail in thy business, Id.
to baffle, foil, balk, disappoint, Hdt., Soph.:—Pass. to err, go wrong, be mistaken, Hdt., Soph.
the Pass. is also used c. gen. rei, to be balked of or foiled in a thing, ἦ καὶ πατήρ τι σφάλλεται βουλευμάτων; Aesch.; σφάλλεσθαι γάμου Eur.; τῆς δόξης Thuc.
Dep., to burst with a noise, to crackle, sputter, ῥίζαι σφαραγεῦντο the roots of his eye crackled or hissed (when Ulysses burnt them with the hot stake), Od.
to be full even to bursting, Id.
to stir up with noise and bustle, Hes.
furious, Anth.
in Hom. only as adv. vehemently, eagerly.

entry.etym: the use of σφι, σφιν as dat. sg. for οἱ is rare, Hhymn., Aesch., Soph.
Acc. σφέᾰς, mostly enclit. pronounced as a long syllable, Hom., Hdt.
entry.sense: masc. and fem. pl. of the Pron. of 3rd person, they, = αὐτοί, Hdt., attic
in Hom. this Pron. is always personal, and therefore he uses no neut.; but Hdt. has neut. pl. σφέα.

this Pron. is used both for the demonstr. αὐτοί, they, and for the reflex. αὑτῶν, etc., themselves;— in the latter case often strengthd. σφῶν αὐτῶν, σφέας αὐτούς, σφᾶς αὐτούς, Hes.; sometimes for ἀλλήλους, Id.
rarely for 2nd pers. pl., μετὰ σφίσιν for μεθ’ ὑμῖν, Il.; σφέας for ὑμᾶς, Hdt.
a footstool, Od.: epic pl. σφέλα Id.
of maple wood: metaph. of persons, "hearts of oak, " Ar.
the maple, Lat. acer, Theophr.
to sling, to use the sling, Thuc., Xen.
to strike by slinging, Babr.
to throw as from a sling:—Pass., Eur.
to move like a swing, to swing to and fro, Id.
Lat. funda (the σ being lost), a sling, Il.: metaph., σφενδόνας ἀπ’ εὐμέτρου with well-measured throw, as from a sling, Aesch.
the hoop of a ring in which the stone was set as in a sling, esp. the broader part round the stone, as in Lat. funda for pala annuli, Eur., Plat.
the stone or bullet of the sling, Xen.; τοιαύταις σφ., of hailstones, Ar.
a slinger, Hdt., Thuc.
of or for slinging.:— ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη), the art of slinging, Plat.
to make one's own, appropriate, usurp, Plat.:—so, as Dep. σφετερίζομαι, Xen., Dem.
appropriation, ἐπὶ σφετερισμῷ ἑαυτοῦ for one's own use and advantage, Arist.
an appropriator, Arist.

entry.etym: possessive adj. of 3rd pers. pl. σφείς
entry.sense: their own, their, Lat. suus, Hom., etc; strengthd., αὐτῶν σφετέρῃσιν ἀτασθαλίῃσιν Od.;—in Prose, the gen. ἑαυτῶν is more common, but σφέτερος occurs in Thuc., etc.; τὸ σφέτερον their own feelings, their own business, Id., Plat.; οἱ σφέτεροι their own people, Thuc.
also of 3rd sg., his or her own, his, her, for ἑός, ὅς, Hes., Pind., Aesch.
in Poets sometimes of other persons:
of 2nd pl., = ὑμέτερος, your own, your, Lat. vester, Il., Hes.
of 2nd sg., = σός, thine own, tuus, Theocr.
of 1st sg., = ἐμός, mine own, meus, Id.
of the 1st pl., = ἡμέτερος, our own, noster, Xen.
a wasps' nest, Eur., Ar.
a piece of wood pointed like a wasp's tail, a pointed stick or stake, Ar.
to make like a wasp, i. e. to pinch in at the waist: generally, to bind tightly, Anth.
Pass., πλοχμοί, οἳ χρυσῷ τε καὶ ἀργύρῳ ἐσφήκωντο (3rd pl. plup.) braids of hair, which were bound tightly with gold and silver, Il.
wasp-like, pinched in at the waist like a wasp, Ar.
the point of a helmet where the plume is fixed in, Ar.
with peaked head, Strab.
with peaked beard, Luc.
a wedge, Ar., etc.;—used as an instrument of torture, Aesch.

entry.note: σφήξ, σφηκός, doric σφάξ, σφᾱκός, οῦ, ὁ,
entry.sense: a wasp, Lat. vespa, Il., Hdt., attic
a Sphettian, Ar. Aeschin.
in or at Sphettos, Aeschin.; Σφηττόθεν from Sphettos, Plut.
a deme of the Acamantian φυλή in Attica, Strab.
a bracelet, necklace, Luc.
to bind tight, bind fast, Aesch., Theocr.:—Pass., Theocr.
a band, lace, Anth.
tight-bound: neut. pl. σφιγκτά as adv., Anth.

Sphinx, a she-monster, Hes.; in Trag. represented as proposing a riddle to the Thebans, and murdering all who failed to guess it; Oedipus guessed it, and she thereupon killed herself. (Prob. form σφίγγω, the throttler.)
very, very much, exceedingly, violently, Hdt., Soph., etc.: with Adjs., σφ. ὑπέρτεροι far superior, Pind.; σφ. ἄδικος Plat.:—with a Subst., τὴν σφόδρα φιλίαν Id.
σφόδρα γε, καὶ σφ. γε, in answers, most certainly, Id.
vehement, violent, excessive, Thuc., etc.
of men, violent, impetuous, Plat.: also strong, robust, Xen.
vehemence, violence, Xen.
Pass. to be or become vehement, σφοδρύνεσθαι τινι to put unbounded trust in a thing, Aesch.
a kind of beetle, Ar.
like σφόνδυλος, a vertebra, Il.
twirled on a spindle, Anth.
a vertebra, Ar.:—in pl. the backbone, spine, or the neck, Eur.
Lat. verticillus, the round weight attached to a spindle, Plat.
their, their own, belonging to them, Il., etc.
in sg. his or her, his own or her own, Theogn.
Comic name for a coxcomb, a long-haired fop with rings and natty nails, Ar.
to seal, Eur.:—Mid. to seal for oneself, have sealed, Plut.: —Pass., perf. part. ἐσφραγισμένος sealed up, kept under seal, Aesch.
to mark as with a seal, to mark, Anth.; δεινοῖς σημάντροισιν ἐσφραγισμένοι, of wounded persons, Eur.
metaph. to set a seal on, confirm, stamp with approval, NTest., Anth.: Mid. to assure of a thing, c. acc. rei, NTest.: to limit, Anth.
to seal or accredit as a faithful servant, as a believer, τινά NTest.
an impression of a signet-ring, a seal, Eur., Xen.
a seal, signet, seal-ring, Hdt., Ar., etc.
the gem or stone for a ring, Hdt., Luc.
the impression of a signet-ring, a seal, Soph., Thuc.:—metaph., σφρηγὶς ἐπικείσθω τοῖσδε, as a warrant, Theogn.; γλώσσῃ σφρ. ἐπικείσθω Anth.
to be full to bursting: of young persons, high-fed horses, etc., to be plump, fresh, vigorous, to be in full health and strength, Lat. vigere, Eur., Ar., etc.
metaph., σφριγῶν μῦθος a vigorous, violent speech, Eur.
a throbbing of parts, pulsation, vibration, Plut.
like the pulse, Arist.
metaph. to be in full vigour, Aesch.
to throb, beat, of the pulse, Plat.: to be feverish, Theocr.
a hammer, Od., Hdt.
a beetle, mallet, for breaking clods of earth, Hes., Ar.
wrought with the hammer, beaten out, as opp. to cast metal (χωνευτός), Hdt., Aesch., etc.
metaph. wrought as of iron, rigid, Luc.
the ankle, Il., attic
metaph, the foot of a mountain, Pind., Anth.; also, Λιβύας ἄκρον σφυρόν the very furthest part of Libya, Theocr.

entry.etym: possess. adj. of σφῶι, Pron. of 2nd pers. dual
entry.sense: of you two, σφωίτερον ἔπος the word of you two, Il.; for 2nd pers. sg., thine own, thine, thy, Theocr.
of 3rd pers. sg., his or her own, Lat. suus, Id.
a honey-cell, and in pl. a honeycomb, Lat. favus, Ar., Theocr.
properly to let loose: hence to slit, open, Ar.; σχ. φλέβα to open a vein, Xen., etc.:—of flowers, σχ. κάλυκας Anth.
to let fall, drop, Xen.
to let go, σχάσας τὴν φροντίδα having let the mind go, given it play, Ar.; σχ. τὰς μηχανάς to let off the engines, Plut.

to check, stop, stay, Lat. inhibere, κώπαν σχάσον, i. e. cease rowing, Pind.; σχάσον ὄμμα lower thine eyes, Eur.:—Mid., σχασάμενος τὴν ἱππικήν having dropt one's horsemanship, "given up the turf," Ar.
a forked stick used to prop nets, Xen.
gently, thoughtfully, Xen.
to do a thing off-hand, Plat.
a raft, float (such as was made off-hand, cf. σχέδιος II), Od., Thuc.; generally, a boat, ship, Eur., Theocr.
a bridge of boats, of the bridge of Xerxes, Hdt., Aesch.
of Place, near, close at hand, Lat. cominus, Il.
of Time, straightway, at once, Babr.
of Place, hand to hand, in or for close combat, Aesch.
of Time, on the spur of the moment, off-hand, Anth.
properly, from nigh at hand, nigh at hand, near, Lat. cominus, Hom.; c. gen., Od.
of Place, close, near, hard by, nigh, Lat. cominus, Hom., Hes.; σχεδὸν οὔτασε Il.; c. gen., γαίης σχ. Od.; c. dat., νῆσοι σχεδὸν ἀλλήλῃσι Il.
with Verbs of motion, σχ. ἐλθεῖν, ἰέναι Hom.
metaph. of relationship, Od.
of Time, [θάνατος] δή τοι σχ. ἐστιν Il.; σοὶ δὲ γάμος σχ. ἐστι Od.
of Degree, nearly, all but, almost, just, σχ. ταὐτά Hdt.; σχ. πάντες Id., etc.
with Verbs, esp. of saying or knowing, σχ. ἐπίσταμαι satis scio, Soph.; σχ. οἶδα Eur.
to hold, Hom.
simply to have, Pind., Aesch.
to hold back, keep away or off, Hom.; αἷμα ἔσχεθον staunched the blood, Il.
ribs of beef, Ar.
a pair of pincers or tongs, Anth.
Scheria, the island of the Phaeacians, Od.: supposed to be the same as Corcyra, Corfu.
found only in dat., ἐν σχερῷ in a line, one after another, uninterruptedly, successively, Pind.; cf. ἐπισχερώ.
a state, condition, Luc.
generally, the nature quality, fashion of a thing, Aesch., Xen., etc.
a check, remedy, λιμοῦ against hunger, Eur.
to complain of hardship, to complain angrily, inveigh bitterly, Ar., Oratt.
passionate complaint, Thuc., Arist.
of persons, properly, unwearying, σχέτλιος ἐσσι Il.
in bad sense, unflinching, cruel, merciless, Hom.: —so in attic, wicked, Dem., etc.:—of beasts, savage, Hdt.

like τλήμων, miserable, wretched, unhappy, Aesch., Eur.; often with a notion of contempt, ὦ σχετλιώτατε ἀνδρῶν O most wretched fool! Hdt.; ὦ σχέτλιε Soph.; c. gen., ὦ σχετλία τῶν πόνων O wretched for thy sufferings, Eur.

of things, σχ. ὕπνος cruel sleep, during which Odysseus was abandoned by his companions, Od.; σχέτλια ἔργα cruel, shocking doings, Id.; σχέτλια παθεῖν Eur., etc.; σχ. καὶ δεινά Ar.: also, σχέτλια [ἐστί], c. acc. et inf., Soph.
adv. -ίως, Isocr.
like Lat. habitus, form, shape, figure, Eur., Ar., etc.; as a periphr., σχῆμα πέτρας = πέτρα, Soph.; σχ. δόμων Eur.
form, figure, appearance, as opp. to the reality: a show, pretence, Thuc.; ἔχει τι σχῆμα Eur.
the bearing, look, air, mien of a person, Hdt., Soph.: in pl. gestures, Xen.
the fashion, manner, way of a thing, σχ. στολῆς fashion of dress, Soph.; σχ. βίου, μάχης Eur.: absol. dress, equipment, Ar., Plat.
the form, character, characteristic property of a thing, Thuc.; βασιλείας σχ. the form of monarchy, Arist.
a figure in dancing, Ar.: in pl. pantomimic gestures, postures, Id., etc.

entry.etym: Pass., perf. ἐσχημάτισμαι Arist., v. infr. II.; but in sense of Mid., v. I. 2
entry.sense: intr. to assume a certain form, figure, posture or position, Plat.: absol. to gesticulate, dance figures, Ar.:—Mid., προστάσεως ἣν σχηματίζονται of the pompous appearance which they assume, Plat.

in Mid. also, to demean oneself in a certain way, make a show of being or doing, ὡς εἰδὼς ἐσχημάτισται he made as if he knew him, Id.; c. inf., σχηματίζονται ἀμαθεῖς εἶναι they pretend to be ignorant, Id.

trans. to give a certain form to a thing, to form, fashion, Plut.:—Mid., σχηματίζεσθαι κόμην to arrange one's hair, Eur.:—Pass. to be fashioned, Aesch.; also to deck out, dress up, embellish, Luc.; to gesticulate, Xen.
the figures of a dance, Hdt.
the assumption of a certain form or appearance, deportment, Plat.
in bad sense, assumption of manner, pretence, Id.
to bring into a certain form: Pass. to take a certain shape or posture, Xen.
a piece of wood cleft off, a lath, splinter, Lat. scindula, Od., Ar.: in pl. cleft wood, fire-wood, Hom.
an arrow, Anth.
to split, cleave, Hes.; ἔσχισε δώδεκα μοίρας, i. e. divided them into twelve parts, Hhymn.; σχ. κάρα πελέκει Soph.

generally, to part, separate, Νεῖλος μέσην Αἴγυπτον σχίζων Hdt.:—Pass., ἐσχίσθη ὁ ποταμός Id.; Νεῖλος σχίζεται τριφασίας ὁδούς branches into three channels, Id.; ἐσχίζοντό σφεων αἱ γνῶμαι their opinions were divided, Id.
with a squill-shaped (i. e. peaked) head, epith. of Pericles, Plut.
the mastich-tree, Lat. lentiscus, Theocr.
its fruit, Hdt.
a squill, = σκίλλα, Ar.
a cleaving, cleavage, parting, division, Plat.
a cleft, a rent in a garment, NTest.
division of opinion, schism, Id.
a cleaving, Aesch.
parted, divided, Soph., Eur.
made of rushes, Eur.
a cord, Hdt., etc.
a fencing with ropes: in pl. roping, rope-fences, Plut.
made of rushes, Anth.
the sedge-bird, Arist.
an effeminate air on the flute, Plut.
a rope-dancer, schoenobates in Juven.
a rush, Lat. juncus, scirpus, Hdt., Ar., etc.
a reed, used as an arrow or javelin, Batr., Ar.
a place where rushes grow, a rushbed, Od., Pind.
a rush-rope, and generally, a rope, cord, Orac. ap. Hdt.
a fence round a garden, Anth.
a land-measure, = 2 Persian parasangs, = 60 stades, Hdt.
stretched outlike a measuring line, drawn in a straight line, Hdt.; σχοινοτενὲς ποιήσασθαι to draw a straight line, Id.
to have leisure or spare time, to be at leisure, Thuc., etc.:—c. inf. to have leisure or time to do a thing, Xen.
to loiter, linger, delay, Eur., Dem.
σχ. ἀπό τινος, Lat. vacare a re, to have rest or respite from a thing, cease from doing, Xen.
σχολάζειν τινί, Lat. vacare rei, to have leisure or opportunity for a thing, to devote one's time to it, Dem.; πρός τι Xen.
also c. dat. pers. to devote himself to, τοῖς φίλοις Id.: esp. of scholars, σχ. τινί to devote oneself to a master, attend his lectures, Id.; and absol. to give lectures, Plut.
of a place, to be vacant or unoccupied, Id.
at one's leisure, leisurely, tardy, Thuc., Xen.:—adv. -ως, Id.; comp. σχολαίτερα Hdt.; or -αίτερον, Thuc.; Sup. -αίτατα, Xen.
leisureliness, laziness, Thuc.
a place for passing leisure in, Plut.
one who lives at ease, Plut.
as adj. leisurely, idle, βίος Id.
enjoying leisure, Lat. otiosus, Arist.; τὸ σχολαστικόν leisure, Id.
devoting one's leisure to learning, a scholar, Plut.: —in bad sense, a pedant, simpleton, Luc.

spare time, leisure, rest, ease, Lat. otium, Hdt., etc.; σχολὴν ἄγειν and ἔχειν to be at leisure, keep quiet, Eur., etc.; σχ. ποιεῖσθαι to find leisure, Xen.; σχ. λαβεῖν Eur.; σχολή [ἐστί] μοι I have time, Ar., etc.:—with a prep., ἐπὶ σχολῆς at leisure, at a fit time, Eur.; κατὰ σχολήν Id.
c. gen. rest from a thing, σχολῇ κακοῦ Soph.; so, σχ. ἀπό τινος Plat.
idleness, Eur.
that in which leisure is employed, esp. a learned discussion, lecture, Plat., etc.
a place for lectures, a school, Arist., etc.
σχολῇ as adv. in a leisurely way, tardily, like σχολαίως, Soph., Thuc., etc.

at one's leisure, i. e. scarcely, hardly, not at all, Soph., etc.; σχολῇ γε Id.:—to introduce an a fortiori argument, εἰ αὗται μὴ ἀκριβεῖς εἰσί, σχολῇ αἱ ἄλλαι if these are not exact, hardly can the rest be so, Plat.
a short note, scholium, Luc.
to save, keep:
of persons, to save from death, keep alive, preserve, Hom., attic
of things, to keep safe, preserve, Hom.:—Mid. to keep or preserve for oneself, Soph., etc.
to keep, observe, maintain laws, etc., Trag.:—Pass., Thuc.
to keep in mind, remember, Eur., Plat.:—so in Mid., Soph., Plat.

with a sense of motion to a place, to bring one safe to, τὸν δ’ ἐσάωσεν ἐς ποταμοῦ προχοάς Od.; σω. τινὰ πρὸς ἤπειρον Aesch.:—in Pass. to come safe, escape to a place, ἐς οἶκον Hdt.; ἐπὶ θάλατταν Xen.
to carry off safe, rescue from danger, ἐκ πολέμου Il.; ἐκ θανάτοιο Od.; ἀπὸ στρατείας Aesch.:—c. gen., ἐχθρῶν σῶσαι χθόνα to rescue the land from enemies, Soph.; Pass., σωθῆναι κακῶν Eur.
c. inf., αἵ σε σώζουσιν θανεῖν who save thee from dying, Id.
absol., τὰ σώσοντα what is likely to save, Dem.
to have strength, Aesch.
c. inf. to be in a condition to do, Soph.
the stout, strong one, of Hermes, Il.
to do like Socrates, to Socratize, Ar.
Socrates: gen. Σωκράτους: acc. Σωκράτην Xen., but also (as if of 3rd decl.) Σωκράτη Ar., Plat.
dear little Socrates, Ar.
Socratic, of Socrates, Arist., etc.; οἱ Σωκρ. the philosophers of his school, Luc. adv. -κῶς, more Socratico, Cic.
a channel, gutter, pipe, Hdt.
the body of a man: in Hom. always the dead body, corpse, carcase, whereas the living body is δέμας.
the living body, Hes., Hdt., attic; τὸ σ. σώζειν or -εσθαι to save one's life, Dem., Thuc.; ἔχειν τὸ σ. κακῶς, ὡς βέλτιστα, to be in a bad, a good state of body, Xen.
body, as opp. to the soul (ψυχή), Plat., etc.; τὰ τοῦ σ. ἔργα bodily labours, Xen.; τὰ εἰς τὸ σ. τιμήματα bodily punishments, Aeschin.
periphr., ἀνθρώπου σῶμα = ἄνθρωπος, Hdt.; esp. in Trag., σῶμα θηρός = ὁ θήρ, Soph., etc.:—often of slaves, σ. αἰχμάλωτα Dem., etc
generally, a body, i. e. any material substance, Plat., etc.
the whole body or mass of a thing, ὑπὸ σώματι γῆς Aesch.; τὸ σ. τῆς πίστεως the body of the proof, Arist.
to exercise the body, Xen.:— metaph., σ. τὸν πόλεμον to train oneself for war, Plut.
bodily exercise, training of the body, esp. of an athletic kind, Xen., etc.
of or for the body, bodily, Lat. corporeus, Arist.:—adv. -κῶς, NTest.
bodily, corporeal, material, Arist.
a poor body, Isocr.
of the nature of a body, bodily, material, Plat.
to make into a body, to consolidate, organise, Polyb.
to provide with bodily strength, to recruit, Id.
to corrupt the body, Aesch.
a place where a body is kept, a sepulchre, Luc.
a basket or box, Babr.
masc. adj. heaped up: ὁ σωρείτης [συλλογισμός] a sorites or heap of syllogisms, the conclusion of one forming the premiss of the next, Luc.
a heap, pile, Xen.
to heap one thing on another, Lat. coacervare, Arist., NTest.
to heap with something, c. dat., Anth.
by heaps, in heaps, Anth.
a heap, Lat. acervus, Hes., etc.
generally, a heap, quantity, Ar.
saving the city, Ar.

entry.etym: the ionic σόος, is used by Hom. in all cases except the nom. sg. σῶς.
σῶος, used by attic writers only in pl. σῶοι, σῶαι, σῶα.
the radic. form σάος, occurs in the comp. σᾰώτερος, v. sub σάος.
entry.sense: radic. sense safe and sound, alive and well, in good case, Lat. salvus, Hom., Hdt., Thuc.
of things, sound, whole, safe, Hom.
of events, safe, sure, certain, νῦν σῶς αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος Il.
one must save, Eur.
a reward for saving one's life, a thankoffering for deliverance, σῶστρα τοῦ παιδὸς θύειν Hdt.; σ. τίνειν Luc.
a reward for bringing back lost cattle or slaves, Hdt., Xen.
fem. of σωτήρ, Hdt., Eur., etc.
epith. of goddesses (cf. Juno Sospita), Pind., Ar.
a saving, deliverance, preservation, safety, Lat. salus, Hdt., attic; σ. τινὶ διδόναι, φέρειν Eur.; σωτηρίαν ἔχειν Soph., etc.
a way or means of safety, Aesch., Eur., etc.
a safe return, ἡ ἐς τὴν πατρίδα σ. Thuc.; ἡ οἴκαδε σωτηρία Dem.; also, νόστιμος σ. Aesch.
of things, a keeping safe, preservation, τινός of anything, Hdt., Aesch., etc.
security, guarantee for safety, σ. ἔστω τινός guarantee for the safe keeping of a thing, ap. Dem.; σωτηρίαι τῆς πολιτείας ways of preserving it, Arist.
security, safety, Thuc.

saving, delivering, Thuc., Plat., etc.; ἐλπὶς σπέρματος σωτηρίου hope of seed to preserve the race, Aesch.:—c. dat. bringing safety or deliverance to one, Id., Eur.:—comp. -ιώτερος, η, ον, more likely to bring safety, Xen.
of persons, much like σωτήρ, Soph., Eur.
as Subst., σωτήρια, ων, τά, like σωτηρία, deliverance, safety, Aesch., Soph.; so in sg., πόλεως σ. Aesch.
σωτήρια (sc. ἱερά), τά, a thankoffering for deliverance, Xen.
a saviour, deliverer, preserver, c. gen. subjecti, τῆς Ἑλλάδος saviour of Greece, Hdt.; also c. gen. objecti, σ. νόσου, κακῶν a preserver from disease, ills, Soph., Eur.

epith. of protecting gods, esp. of Ζεὺς Σωτήρ, Pind., Trag.: to him the third cup of wine was dedicated, τρίτον Σωτῆρι σπένδειν Pind., etc.; proverb., τὸ τρίτον τῷ σωτῆρι the third (i. e. the lucky) time, Plat.; of other gods, as of Apollo, Hermes, Aesch.; even with fem. deities, Τύχη σωτήρ, for σώτειρα, Id.
in NTest. the Saviour.
in Poets, as an adj., saving, Aesch.; with fem. Subst., σωτῆρες τιμαί the office or prerogative of saving, of the Dioscuri, Eur.
to be sound of mind, Hdt.
to be temperate, discreet, shew self-control, Aesch., Ar., etc.; σ. περὶ τοὺς θεούς Xen.
to come to one's senses, learn self-control, Hdt., etc.
Pass., τὰ σεσωφρονημένα μοι things I had done with discretion, Aeschin.
an instance of temperance, Xen.
one must be temperate, Luc.
to recal a person to his senses, to chasten, Eur., Xen., etc.:—Pass. to be chastened, to learn self-control, Thuc., etc.
of passions, to correct, moderate, Xen.; so, σ. ἀμπνοάς to pant less violently, Eur.; ἐς εὐτέλειαν σ. to reduce expenses, Thuc.
naturally temperate, moderate, sober, Xen., etc.:—adv. -κῶς, Ar.
one that makes temperate, a chastener, chastiser, Thuc., Plat., etc.
soundness of mind, moderation, discretion, Od., Theogn., attic
moderation in desires, self-control, temperance, chastity, sobriety, Lat. temperantia, modestia, Ar., Plat., etc.

entry.note: σώ-φρων, epic σᾰό-φρων, ονος, ὁ, ἡ,
entry.sense: of sound mind, Lat. sanae mentis:— hence sensible, discreet, wise, Hom., Hdt., Xen.
of things, σώφρονα εἰπεῖν Eur.; ἄλλο τι σωφρονέστερον γιγνώσκειν Thuc.:— σῶφρόν ἐστι, c. inf., Id.
having control over the sensual desires, temperate, self-controlled, moderate, chaste, sober, Trag., Plat., etc.:—so, σ. γνώμη Aesch.; σ. ἀριστοκρατία Thuc.
τὸ σῶφρον = σωφροσύνη, Eur., Thuc., etc.
adv. -όνως, Hdt.—comp. σωφρονέστερον, Thuc.; so, ἐπὶ τὸ σωφρονέστερον Hdt.:—but -εστέρως, Eur.:—Sup. -έστατα, Isocr.
= Lat. tabula, a dice-table, Anth.
comic word, formed after Καλλιόπη, a game at dice, Anth.
the office or rank of ταγός, Xen.
to be Chief of Thessaly, Xen.:— Pass. to be united under one ταγός, Id.
Mid. to let soldiers be posted or stationed, Aesch.
to be ruler, ἁπάσης Ἀσίδος τ. Aesch.
a frying-pan, saucepan, Ar., Luc.
an array, command:— collectively, ξύμφρων ταγά the chiefs of one mind, Aesch.
that which has been ordered or arranged: esp.,
an ordinance, ἐκ δυοῖν τ. from a combination of two constitutions, Arist.
a body of soldiers, a regiment or brigade, Xen., etc.: —the Roman manipulus, Polyb.
a commander, chief, Aesch., Eur.
esp. the Chief of Thessaly, Xen.
holding command, Aesch.
Taenarus, the southern point of Laconia, Pind., etc.: neut. Ταίναρον, ου, τό, Strab.
a band, riband, fillet, esp. a head-band, worn in sign of victory, Xen., Plat., etc.
a strip or tongue of land, Plut., etc.
a dealer in ταινίαι, Dem.
to bind with a head-band, as a conqueror, Thuc., Xen.: Pass. to be crowned, Ar.
melting in the mouth, tender, Com.: of eyes, melting, languishing, Anth.

fit for ordering or arranging, esp. in war, τ. ἀνήρ a tactician, Xen.; τακτικὸν ἡγεῖσθαί τι to think it a good piece of tactics, Id.; οἱ τ. ἀριθμοί the regular battalions, Id.: τὰ τακτικά the art of drawing up soldiers in array, tactics, Id.
ordered, prescribed, τ. ἀργύριον a stated sum, Thuc.; σῖτος τ. a fixed quantity of corn, Id.; τ. ὁδός a prescribed way, Dem.
enduring labour, drudging, of mules, Hom., Hes.; of Hercules, Theocr.
to go through hard labour, to suffer hardship or distress, Eur., Thuc., etc.
trans. to weary, wear out, Isocr.:—in Pass. to be worn out, be sore distressed, Ar., etc.
hard work, hardship, suffering, distress, Thuc.; in pl. hardships, Hdt.
bodily suffering or pain, caused by disease, Thuc.
suffering, miserable, Aesch., etc.:—adv. -ρως, Thuc.
of things, τ. βίος Soph.; πράγματα Ar.
suffering in mind, wretched, Soph., Eur.: daring, Soph.:—voc. ταλαῖφρον, Id.
patient of heart, stouthearted, of Hercules, Hes.: of Oedipus, much-enduring, miserable, Soph.
to weigh or measure out, Anth.
worth a talent, Dem.
a balance, Theogn., Ar.:—in pl. a pair of scales, Il., etc.
anything weighed,
a definite weight, a talent, in Hom. of gold; but the weight of the Homeric talent is unknown.

in later times the τάλαντον was both a weight and a sum of money represented by that weight of silver:—the Attic talent weighed about 57.75 lbs. avoird., and its value in our money was about 200 l. There was, of course, no such coin as a talent. For purposes of coinage, a talent of silver was coined into 6000 drachmae.
holding the balance: metaph., Ἄρης τ. who turns the scale in battle, Aesch.
subject to many trials, much-suffering, of Ulysses, Od.:—hence, vagrant, vagabond, Anth.
patient in woe, Od.
quasillus, Theocr., Anth.
a basket, Lat. qualus, Od.; πλεκτὸς τάλ. a basket of wicker-work, in which new-made cheeses were placed so as to let the whey run off, Hom.
wool-spinning, Xen., etc.
of or for wool-spinning, Xen.
to spin wool, Xen., Luc.
of or for wool-spinning, Xen.
a wool-spinner, Plat.
patient of mind, stout-hearted, Il.; epith. of Ulysses, Hom.

suffering, wretched, Lat. miser, Od., Trag.; ὦ τάλας ἐγώ Soph.; ὦ τάλαιν’ ἐγώ Aesch.; ὦ τάλαν Soph.;—c. gen. causae, τάλαιν’ ἐγὼ τῆς ὕβρεως wretched that I am for this insolence, Ar.:—in bad sense, τάλαν wretch! Od.—comp. τᾰλάντερος, η, ον: Sup. τᾰλάντατος, η, ον, Ar.
entry.etym: τᾰλᾱς; doric also τᾰλᾰς: voc. τάλᾰν.

entry.sense: with shield of tough bull's-hide, Il.; τ. χρώς a thick tough hide, Anth.:— neut. as adv., ταλαύρινον πολεμίζειν to fight toughly, stoutly, Il.
a marriageable maiden, Soph.
cutting the skin, wounding, Il.
a housekeeper, housewife, Hom., Xen.

one who carves and distributes, a dispenser, Il., Pind., Ar.:—of Zeus, as the dispenser of all things to men, Il.; so Aeolus is τ. ἀνέμων Od.:—of kings or rulers, a controller, director, Pind.; τ. κώμων master of the revels, Id.; τ. Διός the priest of Zeus, Id.: τ. Μοισᾶν, i. e. a poet, Id.; οἶκος τ. στεφάνων that hath store of crowns, Id.; τῆς τε ἐπιθυμίας καὶ τῆς τύχης τ. controller both of his desire and of fortune, Thuc.; τ. τριαίνης, of Poseidon, Ar.
in Prose, a controller of payments, treasurer, Hdt.; τ. τοῦ ἱροῦ the controller of the sacred treasure in the citadel of Athens, Id.
at Rome, the quaestor, Plut.
stewardship, management, economy, Xen.
the office of paymaster, as a polit. term, Arist.
at Rome, the quaestorship, Plut.
a treasury, Thuc., etc.
a magazine, Xen.
of or for stewardship:—at Rome, belonging to the quaestorship, Plut.
to be controller of receipts and expenditure, to be treasurer, paymaster, Ar., Dem.:—c. gen., τ. τῆς Παράλου to be paymaster of the Paralus, Dem.
at Rome, to be quaestor, Plut.

trans. to deal out, dispense, Plat., etc.:—Pass., τοὺς νόμους τεταμιεύμεθα we have the laws dealt out, Lys.:—Mid., ταμιεύεσθαι εἰς ὅσον βουλόμεθα ἄρχειν to control the limits to which we mean to extend our sway, Thuc.
of keeping house, to regulate, manage, Ar., Xen.:— Pass., χώρα ταμιευομένα τινί governed or possessed by one, Pind.
to store up, Dem.; Ζηνὸς ταμιεύεσκε γονάς she was the depository of it, Soph.
rennet, Theocr.
the district of Tanagra, Plut.
a man of Tanagra, Xen.
a town of Boeotia, Hdt., etc.
of Tanagra, Hdt.
with long point or edge, Il.
far-bellowing, Anth.
long-necked, Ar.
stretched, outstretched, tall, long, taper, Il.; πλόκαμος τ. long flowing locks, Eur.; τ. αἰθήρ outspread ether, Id.; τ. γῆρας long old age, Anth.
stretching the feet, long-striding, longshanked, Hhymn., Od.
far-sighted, Emped.
laying one out at length, epith. of death, Hom.
a town in lower Egypt, the Hebrew Zoan, Strab.:— ὁ Τανίτης, νόμος the Tanite nome, Hdt.

entry.etym: only in phrase, ὦ τᾶν or ὦ τάν
entry.sense: sir, my good friend, Soph., Eur., Plat., etc.; used in addressing several persons, ὦ τᾶν, ἀπαλλαχθῆτον Ar.
of or belonging to Tantalus, Eur.
son of Tantalus, Aesch.
daughter of Tantalus, i. e. Niobe, Anth.
entry.etym: From *τλάω, prob. in relation to his long endurance of torment.

entry.sense: Pass. to be balanced or swung, ἐπὶ γᾷ πέσε τανταλωθείς fell with a swing upon earth, Soph.
Tantalus, king of Phrygia, ancestor of the Pelopidae, Od.
long-tongued, chattering, Od.
with long point, Il.
running at full stretch, Aesch.
with flowing hair, Pind.
like ταναήκης, with long point or edge, Hom.
tapering, Il.
of extended age, Anth.
long-haired, shaggy, Hes.
Pass., to be stretched, Il.
long-stretched, tall, ἰτέαι Anth.
now, at present, v. νῦν I.
with flowing peplos, Hom.
in long plaits, Anth.
long-sided, enormous, Anth.

entry.etym: shorter form of τανυσίπτερος, Hes., Pind.

entry.sense: with far-stretching roots, Hes.
with extended wings, long-winged, Od., Hes., Ar.
a stretching, stringing, Od.
with taper ancles, Hes.
of trees, with long-stretched bark, i. e. of tall or slender growth, Il.
with long-pointed leaves, of the olive, Od.
with thick foliage, leafy, Theocr.

to stretch, strain, stretch out, Il.; τ. βιόν to string a bow, Od.; and in Mid., τόξον τανυσσάμενος having strung his bow, Il.:—of putting the strings to a harp, ἐτάνυσσε χορδήν Od.; τ. κανόνα to push the weaving-bar tight, i. e. to weave, Il.; ὅπως τανύσηι when he reins in [the horses], Id.; ἐπὶ Ἀκράγαντι τανύσσας (sc. ὀϊστούς) having aimed them, Pind.:—Pass., γναθμοὶ τάνυσθεν (for ἐτανύσθησαν) the hollow cheeks filled out, Od.; to run at full stretch, of horses galloping, Hom.
metaph. to strain, make more intense, μάχην Il.; ἔριδα πολέμοιο πεῖραρ τάνυσσαν strained the tug of war, Id.

to stretch out, lay along, lay, Hom.; τ. τινὰ ἐν κονίηις, ἐπὶ γαίηι to lay one in the dust, stretch him at his length, Id.:—Pass. to lie stretched out, Id.: to extend, Od.; ἐπὶ χθονὶ κεῖτο τανυσθείς Il.:—also, τρίβος τετάνυστο the path stretched away, Theocr.
to be a taxiarch, Ar., Thuc., etc.
the office of taxiarch, Arist.
the commander of a squadron, Hdt.
at Athens, the commander of a τάξις ( I. 4), the corresponding cavalry- officers being φύλαρχοι, Ar.: generally an officer, Xen.
commanding a λόχος or division, Anth.
Pass. to engage in battle, Pind.
an arranging:
in military sense:
a drawing up, the order or disposition of an army, Thuc., Xen., etc.; τὰ ἀμφὶ τάξεις tactics, Xen.
battle array, order of battle, Lat. acies, κατὰ τάξιν Hdt.; ἐν τάξει Thuc., etc.
a single rank or line of soldiers, Lat. ordo, ἐπὶ τάξεις ὀλίγας γίγνεσθαι to be drawn up a few lines deep, Id.

a body of soldiers, a squadron, Aesch., Soph.: at Athens, the quota of infantry furnished by each φυλή (cf. ταξίαρχος II), Lys.: of smaller bodies, a company, cohort, Xen.; so of ships, a squadron, Aesch.:—generally, a band, company, Id.
a post or place in the line of battle, Lat. statio, Hdt.; μένειν ἐν τῇ ἑωυτοῦ τάξει, opp. to ἐκλείπειν τὴν τ., Id.
generally, an arrangement, order, Plat., etc.
order, regularity, Id.
τ. τοῦ φόρου an assessment of tribute, Xen.: an arrangement with creditors, Lex ap. Dem.
a political order, a constitution, Arist.
metaph. from I. 5, the post or position one holds, Aesch., etc.; ἐν Θετταλῶν τάξει, ἐν ἐχθροῦ τ. viewed as Thessalians, as an enemy, Dem.; ἐν ἐπηρείας τάξει by way of insult, Id.
one's duty towards another, ἡ ὑπέρ τινος τ. Id.; ἡ εὐνοίας τ. the duty of good-will, Id.
a class of men, as of magistrates, Xen., Dem.
the yew-tree, Lat. taxus.
low:
of Place, lying low, Hdt.; ταπεινὰ νέμεσθαι to live in low regions, Pind.; of stature or size, low, Xen.

of the condition of persons, brought down, humbled, submissive, Hdt., Aesch., etc.: of low rank, lowly, mean, Lat. vilis, Eur., etc.: small, poor, weak, Id., Dem.:—adv., ταπεινῶς πράττειν to be poorly off, Isocr.
of the spirits, humbled, dejected, Thuc., Xen.
in moral sense, partly bad, mean, base, abject, Xen., etc.; partly good, lowly, humble, Id., NTest.
of things, mean, low, poor, τ. σχῆμα mean apparel, Xen.: of style, low, poor, Arist.; adv., ταπεινῶς λέγειν Id.
lowness of stature, Hdt.
of condition, low estate, abasement, Thuc., Isocr.
lowness of spirits, dejection, Xen.
in moral sense, baseness, vileness, Plat.
lowliness, humility, NTest.
lowly in mind, Plut.
to lower:—Pass., πᾶν ὄρος ταπεινωθήσεται NTest.
metaph. to lessen, τὸν φθόνον Plut.: to disparage, Polyb.
to humble, abase, Xen., Aeschin.:—Pass., Plat., Xen.
in moral sense, to make lowly, to humble, NTest.:—Pass. to humble oneself, Id.
humiliation, abasement, defeat, Plat.
low estate, low condition, NTest.
a carpet, rug, Lat. tapes, Hom., Ar.
at first, Il.
disquietude, Eur.
disturbance, confusion, Aesch., Eur.
disturbing, c. gen., τῆς ψυχῆς Plut.
a tool for stirring with, Ar. τᾰράκτωρ, ὁ, poet. for ταράκτης, Aesch.
Tarentine, Strab.; T., a Tarentine, Hdt.
heart-troubling, Ar.
troubling the horse-array, of Cleon as a foe to the Ἱππεῖς, Ar.
Tarentum, a town of Magna Graecia, Hdt., Thuc.

to stir, stir up, trouble, in a physical sense, ἐτάραξε πόντον Od.; ὁμοῦ τ. τήν τε γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλατταν Ar.; βροντήμασι κυκάτω πάντα Aesch.; πάντα τ., of a speaker, to jumble up, Dem.; δεινὰ τ. makes "confusion worse confounded," Soph.
to trouble the mind, confound, agitate, disturb, disquiet, Trag., Plat., etc.: absol. to cause confusion, Plat.
of an army, to throw into disorder, Hdt., Xen., etc.:—Pass. to be in disorder, Hdt., Thuc.
of political matters, to agitate, distract, Ar.:—Pass. to be in a state of disorder or anarchy, Thuc., Dem.
ταράττεσθαι ἐπὶ τῶν ἵππων to be shaken in one's seat on horseback, Xen.
to stir up mud, raise by stirring up, Ar.: metaph., τ. νεῖκος, πόλεμον Soph., Plat.; Pass., πόλεμος ἐταράχθη Dem.
intr. perf. τέτρηχα, to be in disorder or confusion, be in an uproar, τετρήχει δ’ ἀγορή Il.; ἀγορὴ τετρηχυῖα Id.
trouble, disorder, confusion, Pind., Thuc., etc.
of an army or fleet, Thuc., etc.; ἐν τῇ ταραχῇ in the confusion, Hdt.
political confusion, tumult, and in pl. tumults, troubles, Id., attic; τ. γίγνεται τῶν ξυμμάχων πρὸς τοὺς Λακεδαιμονίους Thuc.
troublous, turbulent, Hdt.; ἴχνη τ. uncertain, baffling, Xen.
troubled, disordered, Arist.
of an army, Thuc., Xen.
adv., ταραχωδῶς ζῆν to live in a state of confusion, Isocr.; τ. ἔχειν πρός τινα to be rebelliously disposed, Dem.; Sup. -έστατα Isocr.
frighted, fearful, Hhymn., Soph.

intr. to be frightened, alarmed, terrified, Hom.; τ. φόβῳ Soph., Eur.:— absol. to shew fear, Il., Aesch.; τὸ ταρβεῖν a state of fear, Eur.; μή με ταρβήσας προδῷς from fear, Soph.; τεταρβηκώς fear-stricken, Eur.
c. acc. to fear, dread, Il., Aesch., etc.
to stand in awe of, revere, Aesch.
fright, alarm, terror, Il., Trag., etc.
awe, reverence, τινός for one, Aesch.
an object of alarm, a fear, alarm, Soph., Eur.
affrighted or affrighting, Aesch.
a preserving, pickling: in pl., αἱ Ταριχεῖαι factories for salting fish, Hdt., Strab.
embalming, of mummies, Hdt.
pickling, salting, of fish, Id.
an embalmer, of mummies, Hdt.
to preserve the body by artificial means, to embalm, of the Egyptian mummies, Hdt., Plat.
to preserve meat or fish by salting, pickling, or smoking, Plat.:—Pass., [ἰχθύας] ἐξ ἅλμης τεταριχευμένους Hdt.; τεμάχη τεταριχευμένα preserved meat, Xen.
metaph. in Pass. to shrivel up, Aesch.; τεταριχευμένος stale, Dem.
the salt-fish market, Theophr.
to sell salt fish, Plat.
to be engaged with the embalming of corpses, Luc.
a dealer in salt fish, Plut., etc.
a dead body preserved by embalming, a mummy, Hdt.
meat or fish preserved by salting, pickling, or smoking, Id.
a stand or frame of wicker-work, a crate, Lat. cratis, Od., Thuc.:— generally, a basket, Ar.
a mat of reeds, built into brickwork to bind it together, Hdt.
any broad flat surface, as,
τ. ποδός the flat of the foot, the part between the toes and the heel, Il., Hdt.
τ. κωπέως the flat or blade of an oar, Lat. palmula, Hdt.: absol. an oar, Eur.:—in collective sense, the oars on one side of a ship, Thuc.
τ. πτέρυγος the flat of the wing, a wing, Anth.: of a peacock's tail, Mosch.
Tartarean, horrible, Eur., Luc.

entry.note: Τάρτᾰρος, ἡ· heterog. pl. Τάρταρα, ων, τά,
entry.sense: Tartarus, a dark abyss, as deep below Hades as earth below heaven, the prison of the Titans, Il., Hes., etc.:—later, the nether world, like Ἅιδης, Hes., Aesch.
to cast into Tartarus or hell, NTest.
Tartessian, Hdt., Ar.
a city of Spain at the mouth of the Baetis, the Tarshish of Scripture, Hdt., Strab.
a thicket, Il.

thick, close, Aesch.; pl. masc. and neut., like Lat. frequentes, ταρφέες ἰοί thick-flying arrows, Il.; ταρφέα δράγματα Id.:— neut. pl. ταρφέα as adv. ofttimes, often, Hom.:— ταρφειαί in Il. must belong to a nom. ταρφειός, unless we write ταρφεῖαι, from ταρφύς.
to bury solemnly, Il.
tension, intensity, force, Plut.; Ὀφρύων τ. a raising of the eye-brows, Anth.

to arrange, put in order, Hdt., etc.: esp. to draw up in order of battle, to form, array, marshal, both of troops and ships, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—Pass. to be drawn up, Hdt.; ἐπὶ τεττάρων ταχθῆναι in four lines, Xen.; κατὰ μίαν τεταγμένοι in single column, Thuc.: absol., τεταγμένοι in rank and file, opp. to ἄτακτοι, Id., etc.:—Mid. to fall in, form in order of battle, Id.
to post, station, Hdt., Aesch., etc.:—Pass., Hdt., etc.; ἐς τὸ πεζόν or ἐς π. τετάχθαι or ταχθῆναι to serve among the infantry, Id.; c. acc. cogn., τάξιν τινὰ ταχθῆναι Plat.

to appoint to any service, military or civil, τ. τινὰ ἐπί τινος one over a thing, to a service or task, Dem., etc.; ἐπί τινι Aesch., etc.; ἐπί τι Ar., etc.; πρός τι Xen.:—Pass., τετάχθαι ἐπί τινι to be appointed to a service, Hdt., etc.; ἐπί τι Ar.
c. acc. et inf. to appoint one to do a thing, Xen.; and in Pass. to be appointed to do Aesch., etc.:—also (sine inf.), οἱ τεταγμένοι βραβεῖς Soph.; πρέσβεις ταχθέντες Dem.

c. acc. et inf. also, to order one to do a thing, Hdt., Soph., etc.; also, τ. τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Hdt., etc.:—Pass., ἐτάχθην or τέταγμαι ποιεῖν τι Id.:—also impers., ἴωμεν, ἵν’ ἡμῖν τέτακται (sc. ἰέναι) Soph.; οἷς ἐτέτακτο βοηθεῖν Thuc.
to assign to a class, τ. εἰς τάξιν τινά Xen.; τ. ἑαυτόν τινων to act as one of a set, Dem.:—Pass., πρὸς τὴν ξυμμαχίαν ταχθῆναι to join it, Thuc.
c. acc. rei, to place in a certain order, χωρὶς τ. τι Hdt.; πρῶτον τ. τι Xen.
to appoint, ordain, order, prescribe, Soph., Plat.:—Pass., τὸ ταχθέν Soph.; τὰ τεταγμένα Xen.

of taxes or payments, to appoint or fix a certain payment, τ. τινὶ φόρον Aeschin., etc.; with an inf. added, χρήματα τάξαντες φέρειν Thuc.; τάσσειν ἀργυρίου to fix the price, Id.:—Pass., τὸ ταχθὲν τίμημα Plat.:—Mid. to take a payment on oneself, i. e. agree to pay it, φόρον τάξασθαι Hdt.; χρήματα ἀποδοῦναι ταξάμενοι Thuc.
in Mid., also, generally, to agree upon, settle, Plat.
to impose punishments, τ. δίκην Ar.; τιμωρίαν Dem.:—so in Mid., Hdt.
in perf. part. pass. fixed, prescribed, ὁ τεταγμένος χρόνος Id., etc.; ἡ τετ. ἡμέρα, ἔτος Xen., etc.; ἡ τετ. χώρα Id.
Mount Taygetus, between Laconia and Messenia, Od., Hdt., etc.
Τ, τ, ταῦ, τό, indecl., nineteenth letter of the Gr. alphabet: as numeral τʹ = 300, but ͵τ = 300,000.
τ is the tenuis dental mute, related to the medial δ and the aspirate θ.
Changes of τ:
aeolic and doric, τ for σ, as τύ (Lat. tu, thou) for σύ; τοί τέ τῦκον φατί for σοί σέ σῦκον φησί.
in new attic, as in doric and Boeot., ττ for σς, mostly in Verbs, πράττω for πράσσω, etc.
in ionic the tenius τ for its aspirate θ, as αὖτις for αὖθις; so, the tenuis remains unchanged before an aspirate, as κατεῖλον, κατ’ ἡσυχίην.
the Poets, metri grat., insert τ after π at the beginning of some words, e. g. πτόλις, πτόλεμος.
the letter τ, Plat.
of bulls, oxen, or cows, Lat. taurinus, Trag.
of bull's-hide, Il.
a bull-driver:—a Thessalian bull-fighter, tauridor, Anth.
epith. of Poseidon in Boeotia, because bulls were offered to him, Hes.
like a bull, savagely, Ar., Plat.
slaughtering bulls, τελετὴ τ. a sacrifice of a bull, Anth.
devouring bulls, Anth.
with bull's paunch: metaph. enormous, Anth.
bull-binder, in fem. -δέτις, ιδος, Anth.
bull-horned, Eur.
to slaughter bulls, Aesch.
slaughtering bulls, Soph.
bull-formed, Eur.
Pass. to become savage as a bull, Aesch., Eur.; ταυροῦσθαι ὄμμα τινί to cast savage glances on one, Eur.
sprung from a bull, of bees, Theocr.
a name of Artemis, —either worshipped at Tauris, or hunting bulls, Eur.;—so ταυροπόλα (doric for -πόλη), Soph.
bull-footed, Eur.
