an interchange, exchange, change, Eur.
that which is exchanged, νόμισμα ὑπάλλαγμα τῆς χρείας money is the exchangeable representative of demand, Arist.
to exchange, Luc.
under the Alps;— ἡ ὑπαλπεία (sc. χώρα) sub-Alpine Italy, Plut.
a shunning, escape, Hom.
to avoid, shun, flee from, escape, Hom.
to read by way of preface, premise by reading, Aeschin.
to waste away, spend or consume gradually, Thuc., Plut., etc.
a rising up from one's seat, Plat.
one must rise up, Xen.
to retire slowly, Thuc.
under a man, subject to him, married, NTest., Plut.
to come on, creep on, Luc.
Pass. to be somewhat distressed, opt. -ιῷντο Ar.
to remit or relax a little, Plut.:—intr., τοῦ φόβου ὑπανέντος (aor2 part.) Id.
Pass. with aor2 and perf. act. to rise, stand up, Theogn.; of game, to start up, to be sprung, Xen.
ὑπ. τῆς ἕδρης to rise up from one's seat to make room or shew respect to another, Lat. assurgere alicui, Hdt., Ar., etc.
to open from below: to open underhand or secretly, Dem.
to come or go to meet, either as a friend or in arms, τινί Xen., etc.:—also c. gen., Soph.
metaph. to meet, reply or object to, τινί Eur.
to come or go to meet, step forth to meet, encounter, absol., Il., Aesch., etc.: c. dat., Aesch., Xen., etc; also c. acc., Hdt., Plut.
with caverns underneath, Strab.
to threaten underhand, τινί Xen.
to depart stealthily or slowly, to withdraw, retreat, Thuc.
intr. to move off secretly, sneak away from, c. gen., Ar.
having silver underneath; hence,
containing silver, veined with silver, πέτρα, χθών Eur.:— containing a proportion of silver, metaph. of men, Plat.
sold or hired for silver, mercenary, venal, Pind.
one must begin, Plat.
towards the north, Plut.
with a lamb under it, i. e. suckling a lamb or (metaph.) a babe, Eur.
a waking vision, opp. to ὄναρ (a dream), οὐκ ὄναρ, ἀλλ’ ὕπαρ no illusive dream, but a reality, Od.; so Pind., Aesch.
the acc. is used as adv., in a waking state, awake, Plat.; ὄναρ ἢ ὕπαρ ζῆν to pass life asleep or awake, Id.
ὕπαρ in reality, actually, Id.
the beginning: ἐξ ὑπαρχῆς, from the beginning, afresh, anew, Lat. denuo, Soph., Dem.
commanding under another, a lieutenant, lieutenant-governor, viceroy, Hdt., etc.

entry.note: fut. ξω aor1 ὑπῆρξα Pass., perf. ὕπηργμαι ionic -αργμαι
entry.sense: to begin, make a beginning, absol., Od., Eur., etc.
c. gen. to make a beginning of, ἀδικίης Hdt.; πολλῶν κακῶν Eur., etc.
c. part to begin doing, ὑπῆρξαν ἄδικα ποιεῦντες Hdt.; ὑπάρχει εὖ ποιῶν τινα Xen.

c. acc., ὑπ. εὐεργεσίας εἴς τινα or τινι to begin [doing] kindnesses to one, Dem., Aeschin.:—Pass. to be begun, τὰ ἔκ τινος ὑπαργμένα (ionic for ὑπηργ-) Hdt.:—impers., ὑπῆρκτο αὐτοῦ a beginning of it had been made, Thuc.
to begin to be, come into being, arise, spring up, Aesch., etc.

to be in existence, to be there, to be ready, Hdt., attic;—c. gen., ὑπάρχει τῶνδε there is store of these things, Aesch.:—oft. in part., ἡ ὑπάρχουσα οὐσία the existing property, Isocr.; τὰ ὑπ. ἁμαρτήματα Thuc.; τῆς ὑπ. τιμῆς for the current price, Dem.
simply to be, Trag., Thuc., etc.
sometimes with a part., much like τυγχάνω, τοιαῦτα [αὐτῷ] ὑπῆρχε ἐόντα Hdt.; ὑπ. ἐχθρὸς ὤν Dem.
like ὑπόκειμαι II. 2, to be laid down, to be taken for granted, Plat.; τούτων ὑπαρχόντων = quae cum ita sint, Id.
to belong to, fall to one, accrue, ὑπάρχει τινί τι one has, Hdt., Thuc.; ἡ ὑπάρχουσα φύσις your own proper nature, its normal condition, Thuc.
of persons, ὑπ. τινί to be devoted to one, Xen., Dem.; καθ’ ὑμῶν ὑπάρξει ἐκείνῳ he will be on his side against you, Dem.
often in neut. pl. part., τὰ ὑπάρχοντα,
existing circumstances, present advantages, Thuc., Xen., etc.
what belongs to one, one's possessions, means, Thuc., etc.
impers., ὑπάρχει, the fact is that . . , c. acc. et inf., Soph.
it is allowed, it is possible, c. dat. et inf., ὑπ. μοι εἶναι or ποιεῖν τι Thuc., Plat.:— absol., ὥσπερ ὑπῆρχε as well as was possible, Thuc.
in neut. part., like ἐξόν, παρόν, etc., ὑπάρχον ὑμῖν πολεμεῖν since it is allowed you to make war, Id.
under shield, covered with a shield, τὸν ὑπ. κόσμον the arms of Ajax, Soph.; ὑπ. κοῖτον ἰαύειν to sleep an armed sleep, sleep in arms, Eur.: neut. pl. ὑπασπίδια as adv., Il.
to serve as shield-bearer, τινί Pind., Eur.
a shield-bearer, armour-bearer, esquire, Hdt., Eur., etc.
to be consul, Plut.
(sc. χορδή), the lowest note of the three which formed the Gr. scale (v. μέση, νεάτη), Plat.
of consular rank, Lat. consularis, Plut.

like Lat. summus for supremus, the highest, uppermost, of Zeus, ὕπατος κρειόντων, θεῶν ὕπ., Hom.; οἱ ὕπατοι the gods above, Lat. superi, opp. to οἱ χθόνιοι, Lat. inferi, Aesch.; ὕπατός τις some god above, Id.
simply of Place, ἐν πυρῇ ὑπάτῃ on the very top of the funeral pile, Il.
of Time, last, Lat. supremus, Soph., Anth.
of Quality, highest, best, Pind.
c. gen., like the prep. ὑπό, ὕπατος χώρας supreme over the land, Aesch.; ὕπατοι λεχέων high above the nest, Id.
as Subst., ὕπατος, the Roman consul, Polyb., etc.
to play on the flute in accompaniment, Luc.
under or in the court, c. gen., σκηνῆς ὕπαυλος under shelter of the tent, Soph.
under the neck, Anth.: as Subst., ὑπαυχένιον, ου, a cushion for the neck, Luc.
Pass., with aor2 and perf. act., to step back slowly, to withdraw, Antipho.
somewhat frothy, ὄμμα ὕπ. an eye dim with tears, Eur.
somewhat stupid, Hdt.
ὒ, ὖ, a sound to imitate a person snuffing a feast, Ar.

having given surety, liable to be called to account or punished, responsible, Aesch.; ὑπ. πλὴν θανάτου liable to any punishment short of death, Hdt.: c. dat., τὸ γὰρ ὑπέγγυον δίκᾳ καὶ θεοῖσιν liability to human and divine justice, Eur.
to pour in yet more, Plut.
to view from below, to behold, Eur.
metaph. to mistrust, suspect, Id.:— ὑφοράω is used as pres.
Soph., Plat.
one must yield, Soph., Plat.

entry.note: epic ὑπο-είκω imperf. ὑπόεικον fut. ὑπείξω epic ὑπείξομαι, ὑποείξομαι aor1 ὑπεῖξα epic ὑπόειξα
entry.sense: to retire, withdraw, depart, νεῶν from the ships, Il.; ὑπ. τινὶ ἕδρης to retire from one's seat for another (cf. ὑπανίσταμαι), Od.; ὑπ. τινὶ λόγων, i. e. to allow him to speak first, Xen.

to yield, give way, τιμαῖς ὑπ. to give way to authority, Soph.; ὑπ. τινί Xen.: absol. to give way, comply, Hom., etc.; τὸ ὑπεῖκον, = οἱ ὑπείκοντες, Eur.:—c. inf., νῶν ὑπεῖκε τὸν κασίγνητον μολεῖν concede to us that he may come, Soph.
c. acc., χεῖρας ἐμὰς ὑπόειξε he scaped my hands, Il.
to be under, Lat. subesse, c. dat., Il.; πολλῇσι [ἵπποις] πῶλοι ὑπῆσαν under many mares were sucking foals, Id.; of horses, to be under the yoke, to be yoked in the chariot, Hdt.
to be or lie underneath, Id., Aesch.
to be laid down, ὑπόντος τοῦδε this being granted, Eur.
to remain concealed, lurk, Xen.
of things, to be left remaining, remain, be at command, Hdt., attic
to be subjected or subject, Eur.
to steal secretly upon one, Lat. subire, c. acc., Ar.
to depart gradually or secretly, Hdt.

entry.etym: aor2 with no pres. in use, ὑπαγορεύω being used instead
entry.sense: to say as a foundation or preface, to premise, suggest, Eur., Thuc., etc.
to subjoin, add, Ar., Dem.
to suggest an explanation, explain, interpret, Soph., Plat.
used when a long syll. is needed before a vowel, e. g. ὑπεὶρ ἅλα Hom.
to get in secretly, to slip or steal in, Hdt.
Dep. to enter secretly, to come into one's mind, Luc.
combustible matter, fuel, Xen.:—metaph. an incentive, Lat. fomes, ἔρωτος Id.
Pass. to be carried out to a place of safety, to be stowed safe away, Hdt., Thuc.
to bend aside, escape, Ar.: c. acc. to shun, avoid, Plut.
to carry out or away secretly, Thuc., etc.:—Mid., ὑπεκκομίσασθαι πάντα to get all one's goods carried secretly out, Hdt.
to carry off underhand, Eur.
to loosen or weaken gradually, Plut.
to send out secretly, Thuc., Eur.: —Pass., c. acc. loci, τὸ Φωκέων πέδον ὑπεξεπέμφθην I was sent out secretly to Phocis, Soph.
to sail out secretly, Plut.
to run forth from under, outstrip, Il.:—absol. to run on before, Hom.
to loose from under, ἡμιόνους μὲν ὑπεκπροέλυσαν ἀπήνης loosed the mules from under the carriage-yoke, Od.
to flow forth under, Od.
to flee away secretly, escape and flee, Hom.
to flow out under:—metaph. to pass away gradually, Plat.: to slip out, Plut.
Pass. to be gradually broken away, Plut.
to cast down out of, Plut.
to save by drawing away from, Aesch.: absol., αὐτὸν ὑπεξεσάωσεν (epic for -έσωσεν) Il.
Mid. to bring one's goods to a place of safety, carry safely away, ἔστ’ ἂν τέκνα ὑπεκθέωνται (3rd pl. aor2 subj.) Hdt.; so in attic:— Pass. to be carried out to a place of safety, Hdt.
to turn gradually or secretly from a thing, τί τινος Soph.:—Mid. to turn aside from, c. acc., Plat.; c. inf., ὑπεκτραπέσθαι μὴ οὐ ξυνεκσώζειν to decline the task of helping to save, Soph.
to run out from under, escape from, c. acc., Hdt., Soph., etc.;—c. inf., ἢν ἐγὼ μὴ θανεῖν ὑπεκδράμω Eur.
to run out beyond, Soph.
to carry out a little, ὑπεξέφερεν σάκος lifted it a little outwards, so that Teucer could take shelter under it, Il.
to carry out from under, υἱὸν ὑπεξέφερε πολέμοιο Id.: to carry away, bear onward, Od.
intr., ὑπ. ἡμέρης ὁδῷ to get the start by a day's journey, Hdt.
to flee away or escape secretly, Hom., Soph.
mostly c. acc. to escape from, Il., Thuc.
to slacken gradually, Anth.
to withdraw or retire slowly or unnoticed, Hdt.:—c. dat. pers. to retire and give place to another, Plat.; ὑπ. τῷ θανάτῳ to make way for death, i. e. to escape it, Id.
(sub. τὸν ἵππον) to ride up so as to meet, Xen.
he hangs down his head, stands with head hung down, Il.
Dep. to oppose secretly, Plut.
poet. prep. with gen. out from under, from beneath, away from, Il.
Dep. to have under one, of a cow, πόρτιν μαστῷ ὑπ. to have a calf under her udder, Anth.
Mid., with aor2 act., to slip out of, escape, c. acc., Eur.; c. gen., Plut.; absol., ὑπεκδύς having slipped out, Hdt.
to run off secretly or gradually, Plut.
to uncover below or a little, Anth.
set over against, meeting, ἀλλήλοισιν Hes.
set against, opposite, of enemies in battle, Thuc.; οἱ ὑπ. the enemy, Xen.
opposed, opposite: c. dat. opposite or contrary to, Hdt., Xen.: —as Subst., τὸ ὑπεναντίον τούτου πέφυκε the contrary hereto generally happens, Hdt.; τὰ ὑπ. τούτων on the contrary, Id.
adv. -ίως, in a manner contrary to, τῷ νόμῳ Aeschin.
to give way a little, Thuc.
an undergarment, Anth.
Pass., ὑπενδεδυμένοι χιτῶνας having tunics on under their arms, Plut.
underneath, beneath, Hom., Ar.
under the earth, in the nether world, Lat. apud inferos, Od.
as prep., c. gen., under, beneath, Hom., Pind.
to carry out from under, esp. out of danger, Hom., Hdt.
ὑπ. πόδα to withdraw gradually, retire slowly, Eur.; and so, without πόδα, Hdt., Xen.
to take away from below, αἷμα ὑπ. to drain away blood, Soph.
to make away with, to destroy gradually, Eur.; τοὐπίκλημ’ ὑπεξελών having done away with the charge, Soph.:—Pass., Hdt., Thuc.
Mid. to take out privily for oneself, steal away, Il.
to put aside, except, exclude, Plat., Dem.
to ascend to the summit, Eur.

entry.note: aor inf act ὑπ-εξᾰλέασθαι Hes. ὑπ-εξᾰλύσκω
entry.sense: Dep. to flee out from under, avoid, c. acc., Il., Hes.
to step suddenly back, Theocr.
Pass. to put out to sea secretly, Thuc.
to come up from under, emerge, ὑπεξαναδὺς ἁλός Il.; ὑπ. κεφαλῇ to duck or stoop so as to avoid a blow, Theocr.
ὑπ. τινι to rise and make room for him, Plut., Luc.
to drain out from below, exhaust, Eur.
to go away secretly, withdraw gradually, Hdt.; ὑπ. τινί to make way for one, give way to him, Dem.:—of fire or snow, to disappear gradually, Plat.
to drive away gradually, Hdt.
to draw out from under, draw away underhand, Hdt.
to go out from under: to go out secretly, withdraw, retire, Thuc., Dem.:—rarely c. acc. pers. to withdraw from, escape from, Thuc.
to rise up and quit one's settlements, to emigrate, Hdt.
to go out to meet, Id.
intr. to withdraw or retire secretly, Hdt.
Pass., with aor2 and perf. act., to depart secretly, ὑπ. τῆς ἀρχῆς to give up all claim to it, like Lat. abdicare se magistratu, Hdt.; so c. inf., ὑπ. ἄρχειν Luc.
c. acc. to go out of the way of, to give place to, make way for, Xen.: c. dat. to yield to, give way to, Plut.
above measure simple or silly, Dem.
Dep.
to be exceedingly pleased, Plat.
to admire above measure, τινος for a thing, Luc.
to be exceeding angry or vexed at a thing, c. gen., Plat.; c. dat., Aeschin.
to love exceedingly, make much of, Dem.
to be in great distress, Plat., Dem.
blowing hard, Il.
to have over-much blood, Xen.
to lift or raise up over, Plat.:— Mid. or Pass. to lift oneself above, to exalt oneself, be exalted, NTest.
intr.,
c. acc. to climb or get over, pass over, Lat. transcendere, Xen.; ὑπ. τὴν ἄκραν to double the cape, Id.:—as military term, to outflank, Id.
to transcend, excel, outdo, τινά τινι one in a thing, Dem.
to overshoot, go beyond, exceed, καιρόν Aesch.
to overflow, Dem.
exceeding foul or ugly, Xen.
Pass. to feel much ashamed, Aeschin.
Pass. to hang or be suspended over, project over, τινος Hdt.
in nautical language, c. gen. loci, to lie off a place, τῇσι νηυσὶ ὑπεραιωρηθέντες Φαληροῦ Hdt.
past the bloom of youth, NTest.
to overshoot, i. e. to outdo, c. acc., Ar.; ὑπ. τινὰ κλέπτων to outdo one in stealing, Id.
exceedingly exact, Luc.
to mount and climb over, c. acc., Xen.
to project, beetle over, c. gen., Eur.
over or upon the heights, οἱ Ὑπεράκριοι, = οἱ Διάκριοι, the highlanders or inhabitants of the Attic uplands, opp. to the richer classes of the plains and coasts, Hdt.
τὰ ὑπ. the heights above the plain, the uplands, Id.
over or on the top: adv., ὑπεράκρως ζῆν to carry everything to excess, Dem.
to feel pain for or because of, τινός Soph., Eur.
to grieve exceedingly, τινί at a thing, Hdt., Arist.:—absol., Eur.
exceeding grievous, Soph.
exceeding strong, Plut.

entry.note: aor1 -ηλάμην syncop. 3rd sg. aor2 ὑπερ-ᾶλτο part. -άλμενος
entry.sense: Dep.:— to leap over or beyond, c. gen., Il.; also c. acc., Id.; so Xen.
above others, exceeding great, Pind.
transalpine, Strab.
Pass. to be surpassed in impudence, Ar.
exceeding impudent, Dem.
Pass. to exert oneself excessively, Luc.
superhuman, Luc.
Pass., with aor2 and perf. act. to stand up or project beyond, Luc.
Pass. to be very leaky, ὑπ. ἅλμῃ to be water-logged, Luc.
of a ship, quite full of water (ἄντλος), water-logged, Plut.:—metaph. overcharged, ὑπέραντλος συμφορᾷ Eur.; ταῖς φροντίσιν Plut.
over, above, Luc.
Pass. to be deceived excessively, Anth.
to die for, τινός Xen.; ὑπέρ τινος Plat.
Mid. to answer for one, defend him, τινος Ar.
Dep., with fut. and aor1 mid. to speak in behalf of, defend, τινος Hdt., Xen.
to be exceeding afraid, τῇ Ἑλλάδι for Hellas, Hdt.
an upper rope: pl. ὑπέραι, the braces attached to the ends of the sailyards (ἐπίκρια), by means of which the sails are shifted fore and aft, to catch the wind, Od.
exceeding weak, Arist.
panting exceedingly, Xen.
Dep. to be exceeding fond of, τινα Xen.
beyond measure, absurd, Dem.
carrying the use of the Attic dialect to excess, Luc.: adv. -κῶς, Id.
shining exceedingly, Luc.
to increase above measure:—Pass. to be so increased, Andoc.
intr. to increase exceedingly, NTest.
to be overproud, Thuc.
over-boastful, overproud, Soph., Xen.; ὑπέραυχα βάζειν Aesch.
overburdened, Theocr.
Pass. to be exceedingly grieved at a thing, c. dat., Hdt., Soph.

entry.note: fut. -βήσομαι aor2 ὑπερ-έβην epic ὑπέρ-βην epic 3rd pl. ὑπέρβᾰσαν
entry.sense: to step over, mount, scale, c. acc., ὑπ. τεῖχος Il., etc.; ὑπ. δόμους to step over the threshold of the house, Eur.; ὑπ. τοὺς οὔρους to cross the boundaries, Hdt.:—of rivers, to go over their banks, overflow, Id.
to overstep, transgress, τοὺς νόμους Id., Soph.; τοὺς ὅρκους Dem.: absol. to transgress, trespass, sin, ὅτε κέν τις ὑπερβήῃ (epic aor2 subj.) Il.
to pass over, pass by, leave out, omit, Hdt., Dem.
to go beyond, to surpass, outdo, c. acc., Plat.; absol., Theogn.
Causal in aor1, to put over, Xen.
exceedingly, Plat.
to throw over or beyond a mark, to overshoot, c. acc., Il.
ὅτε μέλλοι ἄκρον [λόφον] ὑπερβαλέειν when he was just about to force the stone over the top, Od.
intr. to run beyond, overrun the scent, of hounds, Xen.
to outstrip or pass, τινάς Soph.
metaph.:
to overshoot, outdo, surpass, prevail over, c. gen., βροντῆς ὑπερβάλλοντα κτύπον Aesch.; also c. acc., ὑπ. τινά τινι to outdo one in a thing, Eur.
to go beyond, exceed, c. acc., Hes., etc.; ὑπ. ἑκατὸν ἔτεα to exceed 100 years, in age, Hdt.; ὑπ. τὸν χρόνον, i. e. be too late, Xen.:—also c. gen., Plat.

absol. to exceed all bounds, Aesch., Eur., etc.; οὐχ ὑπερβαλών keeping within bounds, Pind.: to be in excess, Arist.:—often in part., ὑπερβάλλων, ουσα, ον, exceeding, excessive, Aesch., Plat.; τὰ ὑπερβάλλοντα an over-high estate, Eur.; τὸ ὑπ. αὐτῶν such part of them as is extraordinary, Thuc.
to go on further and further, προέβαινε ὑπερβάλλων he went on bidding more and more, Hdt.; ᾔτει τοσαῦτα ὑπερβάλλων Thuc.
to pass over, cross mountains, rivers, etc., c. acc., Aesch., Eur.; also c. gen., Eur.:—of ships, to double a headland, c. acc., Hdt., Thuc.:—absol. to cross over, Hdt., Xen.
of water, to run over, overflow, c. acc., Hdt.
of the Sun, to be at its height or its utmost heat, Id.
Mid., with perf. pass., = A. II, to outdo, overcome, conquer, τινα Hdt., Soph., etc.:—absol. to be conqueror, to conquer, Hdt.
to exceed, surpass, τινα Id., Ar., etc.:—absol. to exceed, Hdt.:—perf. pass. part., ὑπερβεβλημένη γυνή an excellent, surpassing woman, Eur.
to overbid, outbid, τινα Xen.
to put off, postpone, Hdt.;—but, ἢν ὑπερβάλωνται κείνην τὴν ἡμέραν συμβολὴν μὴ ποιεύμενοι if they let that day pass without fighting, Id.:— absol. to delay, linger, Id., Plat.
exceeding heavy, Aesch.
a transgression of law, trespass, Hom., Soph.: also in pl., Il.
transgression, Theogn.
to bepassed or crossed, scaleable, of a wall, Thuc.
transposed, of words, Plat.
act. going beyond, τῶνδ’ ὑπερβατώτερα going far beyond these, Aesch.
beyond all measure, immoderately, Arist.
Dep. to press exceeding heavily, of the plague, Thuc.
to carry over, c. dupl. acc., Luc.
of overwhelming strength or might, Pind.
in bad sense, overweening, lawless, wanton, Hom.:—neut. ὑπέρβιον as adv., Il.
immoderately, excessively, Theogn.
a throwing beyond others: an overshooting, superiority, Thuc.

excess, over-great degree of a thing, Plat.; in various phrases, χρημάτων ὑπερβολῇ πρίασθαι to buy at an extravagant price, Eur.; οὐκ ἔχει ὑπερβολήν it can go no further, Dem.; εἴ τις ὑπ. τούτου if there's aught beyond (worse than) this, Id.; ὑπερβολὴν ποιεῖσθαι to go to all extremities, to put an extreme case, Id.; foll. by a gen., ὑπ. ποιεῖσθαι ἐκείνων τῆς αὑτοῦ βδελυρίας to carry his own rascality beyond theirs, Id.; ἐπέφερον τὴν ὑπ. τοῦ καινοῦσθαι pushed on their extravagance in revolutionising, Thuc.

with a prep. in Adverbial sense, = ὑπερβαλλόντως, εἰς ὑπερβολήν in excess, exceedingly; c. gen. far beyond, τοῦ πρόσθεν εἰς ὑπ. πανοῦργος, i. e. far more wicked, Eur.:— καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν τοξεύσας with surpassing aim, Soph.; καθ. ὑπ. extravagantly, Isocr., etc.
overstrained phrase, hyperbole, Id., Arist.
a crossing over mountains, Xen.
(from Mid.) a deferring, delay, Hdt., Dem.
the Hyperboreans, an imaginary people in the extreme north, distinguished for piety and happiness, Pind., Hdt.;— τύχη ὑπερβόρεος, proverb. of more than mortal fortune, Aesch.
to boil or foam over, in aor. pass., Anth.
to be overfull, Luc.
Dep.
to work under, plough up, prepare for sowing, Xen.
to subdue, reduce: perf. in pass. sense, to be subdued, Eur.
to do underhand or secretly, Plut.
= ὑπηρετέω, to do a service: perf. in pass. sense, πόλλ’ ὑπείργασται φίλα many kind acts have been done, Eur.
above measure ridiculous, Dem.
to overfill, overload, Xen.
exceeding old, of extreme age, Luc.: τὸ ὑπέργηρων extreme old age, Aesch.
very hairy, Xen.
above all fear, undaunted, Il.
to fear for one, c. gen., Aesch., Soph.: absol. to be in exceeding fear, Hdt.
to be much afraid of, τινά Hdt.
exceeding alarming, Dem., Luc.
lying above one on the right hand, Xen.:—simply, lying above, ὑπ. χωρίον higher ground, Id.; τὰ ὑπερδέξια Id.; ἐξ ὑπερδεξίου from above, Id.: —c. gen. commanding from above, Polyb.
metaph. having the advantage in a thing, Id.: victorious over, τινος Plut.
to bind over, τί τινι Anth.
Pass. to exert oneself above measure, Dem., Luc.
to plead for, act as advocate for, τινός Plat.; ὑπ. τὸ φεύγειν τινός to advocate his acquittal, Aesch.
more than just, severely just, Pind.; κἂν ὑπέρδικ’ ᾖ be they never so just, Soph.; adv. -κως, Aesch.
to stimulate a little, Babr.
to put under as a support, Pind., Plat.
to under-prop, support, Plut.
high-land, of the Phaeacians, Od.
to subvert:—Pass., Plut.
intr. in aor2 ὑπήρῐπον, to tumble, fall down, Il.
on yon side, beyond, c. gen., NTest.
to seek to win by excessive attention, Aeschin.
super-abundantly, NTest.
to go beyond all bounds, Luc.
to frighten beyond measure:— Pass. to be in amazement, Xen.; ὑπερεκπεπληγμένος Φίλιππον admiring him exceedingly, Dem.
to stretch beyond measure, ἑαυτόν NTest.
to pay for any one, τινός Luc.
Pass. to run over, NTest.
exceeding light or nimble, Xen.
to fill over-full:—Pass. to be overfull, τινος of a thing, Xen., Luc.
Pass. to be filled quite full, Luc.
to intercede, ὑπέρ τινος for one, NTest.
above 6000, Dem.
to praise above measure, Hdt., Ar.
to desire exceedingly, Xen.
to eat away from under, κονίην ὑπέρεπτε ποδοῖιν Il.
Dep. with aor2 and perf. act.:— to pass over a river, c. acc., Xen.
to surpass, excel, Pind.
to eat immoderately, Xen.
exceeding noble, Arist.
to be exceeding happy, Arist.
Pass. to rejoice exceedingly, Luc.
to hate exceedingly, Soph.

entry.note: epic ὑπειρ-έχω epic imperf. ὑπείρ-εχον aor2 ὑπερ-έσχον poet. -έσχεθον
entry.sense: to hold one thing over another, τί τινος Il., Ar.; ὑπ. χεῖρά τινος to hold the hand over him, so as to protect, Il., Theogn.; also c. dat. pers., Hom.
to have or hold above, ὑπείρεχεν εὐρέας ὤμους he had his broad shoulders above the rest, i. e. over-topped them by the head and shoulders, Il.

intr. to be above, rise above the horizon, Od.: to be above water or the ground, Hdt.;—c. gen., ὑπερέσχεθε γαίης rose above, overlooked the earth, Il.; [σταυροὺς] οὐχ ὑπερέχοντας τῆς θαλάσσης Thuc., etc.
in military phrase, to outflank, c. gen., Xen.
metaph. to overtop, exceed, outdo, c. acc., Aesch., Eur.:—also c. gen., Plat., etc.
absol. to overtop the rest, be prominent, Hdt., Xen.: to prevail, οἱ ὑπερσχόντες the more powerful, Aesch.; ἐὰν ἡ θάλαττα ὑπέρσχῃ to be too powerful, Dem.
c. gen. rei, to rise above, Ar.
c. acc. to get over, cross, Thuc.
to boil over: metaph., of a man, Ar.
Pass. to be overjoyed at, τινι Hdt.; c. part., ὑπερήδετο ἀκούων he rejoiced much at hearing, Id.
exceeding well, excellently, Xen., Dem.
exceeding sweet, Luc. adv. -έως, Xen.; Sup. -ήδιστα, Luc.
a being over the day: as law-term, the latest day for payment, Dem.
forfeiture of recognisances, a distress, Id.
over the day for payment, after which the debtor became liable to have his goods seized, Dem.; ὑπερήμερον λαμβάνων τινά, i. e. having a right to distrain upon him, Id.
metaph., ὑπ. τῆς ζωῆς past the term of life, Luc.; ὑπ. τοῦ βίου beyond the term of human life, Id.
above half, more than half, Hdt.; τινος of a thing, Xen.
somewhat desolate, Plut.

entry.etym: part. with no pres. in use
entry.sense: exceedingly manly:—but always in bad sense, overbearing, overweening, Hom.
in Com. phrase, excelling men, thinking oneself more than man, Ar.

entry.note: ὑπερ-ήνωρ, doric ὑπερ-ᾱ́νωρ, ορος, ὁ, ἡ,
entry.sense: overbearing, overweening, Hes., Eur.

entry.note: used by Hom. only in part.
entry.sense: much like ὑπερηνορέων overweening, arrogant, Il.
trans. to treat disdainfully, Luc.
arrogance, disdain, Xen., Dem.:—c. gen. objecti, contempt towards or for another, Plat., Dem.

entry.etym: prob. for ὑπερφανής, η being inserted.
entry.sense: in bad sense, overweening, arrogant, haughty, Hes., Aesch., Dem.; οἰκίαι ὑπερηφανώτεραι Dem.;—so in adv., ὑπερηφάνως ἔχειν to bear oneself haughtily, Plat.; ὑπ. ζῆν to live prodigally, Isocr.
in good sense, magnificent, splendid, Plat.
above the coast-land, Hdt.
to wonder exceedingly, Hdt., Luc.
most admirable, Anth.
from above or merely above, Il.: of the body, above, in the upper parts, opp. to ἔνερθε, Id.
from heaven above, i. e. from the gods, Hom.
of Degree, yet more, Soph.
c. gen. above, over, Pind., Aesch., etc.; ὕπ. γίγνεσθαί τινος to get the better of one, Eur.; also, ὕπερθεν εἶναι ἢ . . , to be above or beyond, i. e. worse than . . , Id.
postponement, Polyb.
to run beyond, ὑπ. ἄκραν to double the headland, proverb. of escaping from danger, Aesch.
to outstrip, outdo, c. acc., Eur.
to die for another, c. gen. or absol., Eur.

entry.note: fut. -θοροῦμαι epic -θορέομαι aor2 -έθορον epic ὑπέρ-θορον inf. -θορεῖν ionic -θορέειν
entry.sense: to overleap, leap or spring over, c. acc., Il., etc.;—also c. gen., Eur.
high-spirited, high-minded, daring, Hom., Hes., etc.
in bad sense, overdaring, overweening, Hes. — overspirited, of a horse, Xen.
vehemently angry:—adv., ὑπερθύμως ἄγαν in over- vehement wrath, Aesch.
the lintel of a door or gate, Lat. superliminare, Od., Hes.
to shout above, out-shout, c. gen., Anth.
to outdo, Od.

entry.note: Pass., in the phrase, πόδες ὑπερικταίνοντο
entry.sense: the feet went exceeding swiftly, Od.
patronym. of Ὑπερίων, Hyperion's son, i. e. Ἥλιος, Od., Hes.

entry.etym: later form for ὑπερπέτομαι, Plut., Luc.

entry.sense: Pass., with aor2 and perf. act.:— to stand over another, c. gen., Hdt.: esp. to stand over one for protection, protect, τινος Soph.
knowing too well, c. gen., Soph.
exceeding strong, Xen.
to be above, to prevail over, c. gen., Hes.
to protect, τινός Anth.
Hyperion, the Sun-god, joined with Ἥλιος, or alone for Ἥλιος, Hom. Some derive it from ὑπὲρ ἰών, he that walks on high: others simply bring Ὑπερίων from ὑπέρ, the God above.
to sit over or upon, ἐπί τινος Xen.:—metaph. to sit over and watch, keep an eye on, τινος Id.
exceeding beautiful, Arist.
to suffer or labour for, τινός Eur.
to get down over, get quite over, c. acc., Il.; c. gen., Anth.
exceedingly absurd, Aeschin.
Pass. to lie or sit above, at table, c. gen., Plut., Luc.
very distressing, Luc.
to run bubbling over, Luc.
Dep.
to lie or be situate above, Isocr.
to be postponed, Luc.
Pass. to be quite empty, Galen.
an outflanking on one wing, Polyb.
to overflow, Strab.
to flatter immoderately, Dem.
to carry over, Strab.
overweening, arrogant, Aesch.
overstepping all bounds, extravagant, arrogant, Aesch., Soph.:—adv. -πως, excessively, Aesch.
to over-fill or glut, τινά τινος one with a thing, Theogn.
exceeding angry, cruel, Aesch.:— adv. -τως, Eur.
to hang up over, ὑπ. ἄτην τινί Pind.:—Pass. to impend, Theogn.
Dep. to acquire over and above, Soph.
exceeding famous or renowned, only in acc., ὑπερκύδαντας Ἀχαιούς Il.; ὑπερκύδαντα Μενοίτιον Hes.
to stretch and peep over, Plat.; c. gen., Luc.
to step beyond, overstep, c. acc., Anth.
exceeding bright, Ar.
of sound, very clear or loud, Dem.
Pass. to make a splendid show: to shew great eagerness, Xen.
exceedingly, beyond all doubt, NTest.
Pass. to be vexed beyond measure, Hdt.
to be overfull of barley bread (μᾶζα), to be wanton from high feeding, Luc.
Pass. to be or go stark mad, Ar.
to fight for or on behalf of, τινός Soph., Eur.; σὺ ταῦτα τοῦδ’ ὑπερμαχεῖς ἐμοί; dost thou fight thus for him against me? Soph.
inclined to fight for, Plut.
Dep. = ὑπερμαχέω, Plut.; τάδ’ πατρὸς ὑπερμαχοῦμαι will fight this battle for him, Soph.
a champion, defender, Anth.
immensely great, Ar.
Pass.:— to get (and in aor. to be) excessively drunk, Hdt.
part. with no pres. in use, exceeding mighty, Od.
exceeding mighty, exceeding strong, Hom., Hes.
beyond all measure, excessive, Plat.
exceeding long, Aesch.; ἡ βασιλέος χεὶρ ὑπ. the king's arm is very long, reaches very far, Hdt.
exceeding high, of mountains, Id.
ὑπερμάκης βοά a cry exceeding loud, Pind.
ὑπὲρ μόρον.
above the clouds, Luc.
to haul ships over land, Strab.
to be more than conqueror, NTest.
beyond the south wind, i. e. at the extreme south, Hdt.
of excessive bulk, swollen to a great size, Xen., Dem.
immoderate, excessive, Plat.
to be much swollen, of a river, Anth.
to dwell above or beyond, c.gen., Hdt.; also c. acc., Id.
dwelling above or beyond, c. gen., Hdt.
overweening confidence in arms, proud defiance, presumptuousness, ὑπεροπλῑ́ῃσι [epic dat. pl., with ῑ], Il.

entry.note: fut. ίσομαι 3rd sg. epic aor1 opt. -οπλίσσαιτο
entry.sense: Dep. to vanquish by force of arms, or (from ὑπέροπλος) to treat scornfully, Od.
proudly trusting in force of arms, defiant, presumptuous, ὑπέροπλον εἰπεῖν (as adv.) to speak defiantly, presumptuously, Il.; ἠνορέη, βίη ὑπέροπλος Hes.
of conditions, excessive, overwhelming, Pind.
a contemner, disdainer of a thing, c. gen., Soph., Thuc.: absol. disdainful, haughty, Theocr., Arist.
disposed to despise others, contemptuous, disdainful, Isocr., Dem.:—adv. -κῶς, Xen.
disdainful, Anth.; neut. pl. as adv., Soph.

entry.note: ionic -έω fut. -όψομαι aor2 -εῖδον inf. -ῐδεῖν aor1 pass. ὑπερώφθην
entry.sense: to look over, look down upon, c. acc., Hdt.
to overlook, slight, despise, Id., Thuc., etc.:—also c. gen. to shew contempt for, Xen.
to drive beyond the frontier, banish, Plat.; in Pass., Aeschin.
over the boundaries or confines, living abroad, Dem., Theocr.; ὑπ. ἀσχολία occupation in foreign parts, Thuc.; τὰ ὑπ. foreign affairs, Arist.
ἡ ὑπερορία (sc. γῆ), the country beyond one's own frontiers, a foreign country, Plat., Xen.
foreign to the purpose, outlandish, out-of-the-way, Aeschin.
Pass. to rise and hang over, c. dat., Soph.
to be much afraid, τινός for one, Eur.
a pestle to bray and pound with, Hes., Hdt.
anything shaped like a pestle, a club, cudgel, Plut., Luc.
above the heavens, Plat.
a projection, an eminence, Polyb.
metaph. preeminence, superiority, ἡ δὲ νίκη ὑπεροχή τις Arist.
prominent, eminent, distinguished above others, c. gen., Il.; absol., Hdt.; ὑπέροχος βία overbearing force, Soph.
contempt, disdain for a person or thing, c. gen., Thuc., etc.: absol. haughtiness, arrogance, Isocr.
very frosty: τὸ ὑπ. excessive frost, Xen.
to be grievously distressed, ὑπερπαθήσας’ Eur.
to overstrike, i. e. to surpass, exceed, c. gen., Ar.; c. acc., Dem.
to strew or scatter over, Anth.
Mid. to abound more and more, NTest.

sense.gloss: over, above, w. gen, over, beyond, w. acc.

entry.sense: Lat. super:—hence are formed comp. and Sup. ὑπέρτερος, -τατος.
WITH GENIT.,
of Place, over, above:
in a state of rest, στέρνον ὑπὲρ μαζοῖο Il.; ὑπὲρ κεφαλῆς στῆναί τινι to stand over his head, Hom.: of countries, above, further inland, οἰκέοντες ὑπὲρ Ἁλικαρνησσοῦ μεσόγαιαν Hdt.
in a state of motion, over, across, ὑπὲρ θαλάσσης καὶ χθονὸς ποτωμένοις Aesch.
over, beyond, ὑπὲρ πόντου Od.

metaph., from the notion of standing over to protect, for, for defence of, in behalf of, ἑκατόμβην ῥέξαι ὑπὲρ Δαναῶν Il.; θύειν ὑπὲρ τῆς πόλεως Xen.; ὑπὲρ τῆς πατρίδος ἀμύνειν to fight for one's country, etc.
for the sake of a person or thing, λίσσεσθαι ὑπὲρ τοκέων, ὑ. πατρὸς καὶ μητρός Il.
c. inf. for the purpose of, ὑπὲρ τοῦ μηδένα ἀποθνήσκειν to prevent any one from dying, Xen.
for, instead of, in the name of, ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ Thuc.; στρατηγῶν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν acting as general by commission from you, Dem.
like περί, on, of, concerning, Lat. de, ὑπὲρ σέθεν αἴσχεα ἀκούω Il.; τὰ λεγόμενα ὑπέρ τινος Hdt.
WITH ACC., expressing that over and beyond which a thing goes,
of Place, over, beyond, Hom., Plat.
of Measure, over, above, exceeding, beyond, ὑπὲρ τὸ βέλτιστον Aesch.; ὑπὲρ ἐλπίδα Soph., etc.
of transgression, beyond, contrary to, ὑπὲρ αἶσαν, ὑπὲρ μοῖραν, ὑπὲρ ὅρκια Il.
of Number, above, upwards of, ὑπὲρ τεσσεράκοντα Hdt., Xen.; ὑπὲρ τὸ ἥμισυ more than half, Xen.
of Time, beyond, i. e. before, earlier than, ὁ ὑπὲρ τὰ Μηδικὰ πόλεμος Thuc.
POSITION: ὑπέρ may follow its Subst., but then by anastrophe becomes ὕπερ, Hom., Trag.
AS ADV. over much, above measure, ὑπὲρ μὲν ἄγαν Eur.; written ὑπεράγαν, Strab., etc.
IN COMPOS.,
of Place, over, beyond, in ὑπερ-βαίνω, ὑπερ-πόντιος.
for, in defence of, in ὑπερ-ασπίζω, ὑπερ-αλγέω.
above measure, in ὑπερ-ήφανος, ὑπερ-φίαλος.
beyond all measure, NTest.

entry.note: aor2 -επτάμην and in act. form -έπτην doric -έπτᾱν

entry.sense: to stretch over, Luc.
flying over or above, Strab.:—metaph. high-flying, Luc.
to fly over, of a spear, Hom.
c. acc. to fly over or beyond, Od.; also c. gen., Plut.
to leap over, c. acc., Ar.
metaph. to overleap, transgress, Dem., Aeschin.
exceeding sharp in temper, Aesch.
to overfill: Pass., aor1 ὑπερεπλήσθην, to be overfull, Arist.;—c. gen., ὑπερπλησθεὶς μέθης Soph.
to drink overmuch, Xen.
to fall over, run over, project, Strab.
of Time, to be past, gone by, Hdt.
to abound exceedingly, NTest.
superabundant, ὑπερπλήθη ἐξημαρτηκώς having done more misdeeds than enough, Dem.
to fill overfull, Xen.:—Pass. to be overfull, to be gorged, Id.
over-wealthy, exceeding rich, Arist.
to be exceeding rich, Ar.
to overflow, Strab.
overmuch, in pl. over many, Aesch., Xen.
to labour beyond measure, take further trouble, Xen.
to bear or endure for others, Soph.
in Mid. c. gen. pers., Id.
quite worn out, Plut.
over the sea, Aesch.; φοιτᾷς ὑπερπόντιος Soph.
from beyond the sea, i. e. foreign, strange, Pind.
exceeding poor, Arist.
to make very much of one, to fondle and caress him, Ar.
to blush scarlet for another, c. gen., Ar.
Mid. to be exceeding solemn or pompous, Xen.
exceeding wise or clever, Ar., Plat.
to take exceeding great pains, Luc.
uppermost, highest, supreme, Il., etc.
of age, eldest, Pind.

trans. to stretch or lay over, Hdt.: to hold out over to, τί τινι Eur.; ὑπ. σκιὰν σειρίου κυνός to stretch over [the house] a shade from the sun, Aesch.; ὑπ. χεῖρά τινος to stretch the hand over one for protection, Eur.; ὑπ. πόδα ἀκτῆς to stretch one's foot over the beach, i. e. pass over it, Id.
to strain to the uttermost, Plut.
intr. to stretch or jut out over, Thuc.:—also c. acc., ὑπ. τὸ κέρας to outflank the enemy's wing, Xen.
metaph. to exceed the measure or number of, c. gen., Dem.;— c. acc. to exceed, τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην φύσιν Arist.
to overleap, c. acc., Aesch.
leaping over the strait, Aesch.
c. gen. rising or appearing above, Eur.; ἄθλων ὑπερτελής having reached the end of labours, Soph.

to appear above, ὑπερτείλας ὁ ἥλιος the sun when he is well above the horizon, Hdt.; ὑπ. ἐκ γαίας to start from the ground, Eur.; c. gen., φαρέων μαστὸς ὑπερτέλλων appearing above her dress, Id.; κορυφῆς ὑπερτέλλων πέτρος hanging over the head [of Tantalus], Id.
stretching over, laid over, Aesch.
the upper part or body of a carriage, Od.
over or above, upper, κρέα ὑπέρτερα flesh from the outer parts of a victim, opp. to the σπλάγχνα or inwards, Od.
metaph. higher, nobler, more excellent, Il.: stronger, mightier, Soph.
c. gen. victorious or triumphant over, Pind., Eur.; οὐδὲν οἶδ’ ὑπέρτερον I know nothing further, more certain, Soph.
neut. as adv., better than, c. gen., Id.
to melt exceedingly, Strab.
to set higher, erect, Anth.
to set on the other side, carry over, Plut.
in Mid. to hold over, so as to protect, Anth.
metaph., παντὶ θεὸν ὑπερτιθέμεν to set God over all, Pind.
to communicate a thing to another, ὑπερετίθεα (ionic imperf. for -ετίθην) τὰ ἔμελλον ποιήσειν Hdt.:—so in Mid., esp. in order to ask advice, Id.
to honour exceedingly, τινά Soph.
overstrained, strained to the utmost, at full pitch, exceeding loud, Aesch., Ar.
to run over or beyond, outrun, escape, c. acc., Theogn., Eur.
to excel, surpass, τινά Eur.: absol. to prevail, Id.
to overstep, transgress a law, Soph.
to blush a little, Ar.
somewhat red, reddish, Thuc., Plat.
exceeding high, Xen.
to exalt exceedingly, τινά NTest.
Pass. to shew oneself over or above a place, c. gen., Thuc.
to extend the phalanx so as to outflank the enemy: generally, to outflank, Xen.; c. gen., ὑπ. τοῦ στρατεύματος Id.
appearing over or above, out-topping others, Xen.
above speech, unspeakable, Pind.
to bear or carry over a place, ὑπ. τὸν ἰσθμὸν τὰς ναῦς Thuc.:—Pass., [αἱ ναῦς] αἱ ὑπερενεχθεῖσαι τὸν ἰσθμόν Id.

intr. to rise above, to surpass, excel, have the advantage over, τινός τινι one in a thing, Hdt., Ar.; also c. acc. pro gen., ὑπερφέρεις τόλμῃ τόλμαν Eur.: absol. to excel, have preeminence, Hdt., Soph.
Dep. to sound above, τὰ ἔργα ὑπ. τοὺς λόγους Luc.
Pass. to die for or in behalf of, ὑπερέφθιτο (poet. aor2) πατρός Pind.
overbearing, overweening, arrogant, Hom.:—adv. -λως, exceedingly, Id.: arrogantly, Od.
entry.etym: Deriv. uncertain: perh. an epic form either of ὑπέρβιος or of ὑπερφυής.

entry.sense: to love beyond measure, Ar., Xen.
Pass. with fut. mid., to be overfrightened, fear exceedingly, Aesch., Xen.
very fearful, timid, Xen.
to carry over, Xen.
to be over-proud, to have high thoughts, Aesch.; ὑπ. τινί to be proud in or of a thing, Hdt., Plat.
c. acc. to look down upon, despise, Aesch., Ar.:—Pass. to be despised, Thuc.
c. gen. to think slightly of, Eur., Ar.
over-proud, haughty, disdainful, arrogant, Aesch., Eur.: neut. pl. ὑπέρφρονα as adv., Soph.
in good sense, ἐκ τοῦ ὑπέρφρονος from a sense of superiority, Thuc.
overgrown, enormous, Hdt., Ar.
monstrous, marvellous, extraordinary, Hdt., Ar.:—joined with a relat., ὑπερφυὴς ὅσος extraordinary how great, i. e. extraordinarily great, Ar., Plat.
adv. -ῶς, over-much, marvellously, strangely, exceedingly, Ar., Plat.; in affirm. answers, ὑπερφυῶς μὲν οὖν Plat.
Pass., with aor2 and perf. act., to surpass, excel, c. acc., Hdt.
Pass. to be inflated excessively, Luc.
to outbawl, τινά Luc.
to rejoice exceedingly at a thing c. dat., Eur.; c. part., μανθάνων ὑπ. Xen.
to be over-wanton or arrogant, Soph.
Dep. with aor2 and perf. act.:— to go or come under, enter, Lat. subire, c. acc., Od., Aesch.
of involuntary feelings, to come upon, steal over one, c. acc., Τρῶας τρόμος ὑπήλυθε Il.; ὑπῆλθέ με φόβος Soph., etc.
of persons, to creep into another's good graces, to fawn on, cringe to, c. acc., Ar., Plat.
to undermine, beguile, Soph., Eur.
to advance slowly, of an army, Xen.
over head and ears in debt, Dem.
very frigid, Luc.
to start back, recoil, Il.
the upper part of the mouth, the palate, Il.
from an upper room, Od.
the upper part of the house, the upper story or upper rooms, where the women resided, Hom.:—in attic, an attic, garret, Ar. (v. ὑπερῷος).
being above, Plut.
entry.etym: From ὑπέρ; -ῷος being a term., as πατρῴος, μητρῴος from πατήρ, μήτηρ.

entry.sense: to reply by a question, Plat.

liable to give account for one's administration of an office, accountable, responsible, Hdt., Aesch., etc.:— ὑπεύθυνοι, οἱ, at Athens, magistrates who had to submit their accounts to public auditors (λογισταί), Ar., etc.
c. gen. responsible for, ὑπ. ἀρχῆς ἑτέρας ap. Dem.; of slaves, σῶμα ὑπ. ἀδικημάτων their body is liable for their misdeeds, i. e. they must pay for them with their body, Id.
c. dat. responsible to another, dependent on them, Lat. obnoxius, Id., Aeschin.

entry.note: fut. ὑφ-έξω aor2 ὑπέσχον poet. ὑπέσχεθον
entry.sense: to hold or put under, ὑποσχὼν θηλέας ἵππους (cf. Virgil supposita de matre), Il.: to hold out the hand to receive something, Id., Dem.: to hold a cup under another vessel, while something is poured into it, Hdt., Ar.; ὑπ. μαστόν, of the mother giving suck, Eur.
to supply, afford, furnish, Pind.; ὑπ. τινί [φόβον] to occasion him fear, Thuc.:— ὑπ. ἑαυτόν submit oneself to another, Xen., Plat.
to uphold, support, c. acc., Hdt.

Lat. sustinere, to undergo, be subject to, suffer, Soph., Eur.; ὑπ. δίκην τινός to have to give an account of a thing, Hdt., attic; ὑπ. δίκην to undergo a trial, Thuc.; ὑπ. λόγον τινί to render account to another, Plat., Xen., etc.
to sustain, maintain, λόγον an argument, Arist.
giving ear, listening to, τινι Anth.
obedient, subject to another, c. gen., Hdt., Aesch., etc.; so, c. dat., Eur., Xen.
c. dat. rei, ναυσὶν ὑπ. liable to furnish ships, Thuc.
absol. as Subst., ὑπήκοοι, οἱ, subjects, Id., etc.; ἡ ὑπήκοος (sc. χώρα); τὸ ὑπήκοον = οἱ ὑπ., Id.
lifted or wafted by the wind, Theocr.
full of wind, ὑπ. ᾠόν a wind-egg, which produces no chicken, Ar.:— metaph. vain, idle, empty, Luc.; of men, braggart, Plut.
under the wind, under shelter from it, Soph., Theocr.; ἐκ τοῦ ὑπηνέμου on the lee-side, Xen.: metaph. gentle, Eur.
swift as the wind, Anth.
the hair on the under part of the face, the beard, Ar.
one that is just getting a beard, with one's first beard, Hom., Plat.:—generally bearded, Anth.
about dawn, towards morning, early, Hom.; στίβη ὑπηοίη morning frost, Od.
the body of rowers and sailors, the ship's crew, Thuc., etc.
service, Ar., etc.
the cushion on a rower's bench, Thuc.
= ὑπηρετικὸν πλοῖον, Strab.
to do service on board ship, to do rower's service:— hence to be a servant, do service, serve, Soph., Ar.

c. dat. to minister to, serve, Lat. inservire, Hdt., attic; ὑπ. τοῖς τρόποις to comply with, humour his ways, Ar.; ὑπ. τῶι λόγωι to second, support it, Eur.: — ὑπ. τινί τι to help one in a thing, Soph., Ar., etc.
absol. to serve, lend aid, Soph.:—Pass. to be done as service, Hdt., Isocr.
service rendered, service, Plat.; ποδῶν ὑπ. feet that serve one, Soph.
service, Arist.
properly an under-rower, under-seaman, v. ὑπηρεσία.
generally an underling, servant, attendant, assistant, Lat. apparitor, Hdt., attic:—c. gen. objecti, ὑπ. ἔργου a helper in a work, Xen.
at Athens,
the servant who attended each man-at-arms (ὁπλίτης) to carry his baggage and shield, Thuc.
ὁ τῶν ἕνδεκα ὑπ. the assistant of the Eleven, employed in executions, Plat.
one must serve, τινί Arist.
of or for the ὑπηρέται, menial, Plat.; ὅπλα ὑπ. the arms of the hired soldiery, Xen.
of or for service, doing service, Plat., etc.
subordinate, Arist.
κέλης ὑπ. a cockboat, attending on a larger vessel, Xen.; τὸ ὑπ. (sc. πλοῖον) an attendant vessel, despatch-boat, tender, Dem.
to sound under or in answer, to echo, respond, Hes.
to force underneath, properly of a dog putting its tail between the legs: metaph., σοὶ ὑπίλλουσι στόμα keep down their tongue before thee, i. e. fawn and cringe before thee, Soph.

entry.note: contr. -οῦμαι poet. ὑπίσχομαι fut. ὑποσχήσομαι aor2 ὑπεσχόμην perf. ὑπέσχημαι
entry.sense: 3 sg. plup. ὑπέσχητο: — to promise or engage to do a thing, Il., attic;—in attic also, sometimes, to take upon oneself, i. e. to undertake to do, to promise a thing, c. acc., Hom.; with inf. aor., Xen.
absol. to promise, make promises, Hdt.
with inf. pres. to profess that one is, profess to be, Id., Plat.: also to profess to do a thing, Plat., Xen.
to sleep, Hom.
drowsy, Anth.
she that gives sleep, Eur.
to fight with sleep, withstand sleep, Xen.
giver of sleep, Aesch.

sleep, slumber, Hom., etc.; χάλκεος ὕπνος, i. e. the sleep of death, Il.:— ὕπνος τινὰ ἐπέρχεται, ἐπορούει, ἱκάνει, αἱρεῖ, λαμβάνει Hom., etc.; εἰς ὕπνον πεσεῖν Soph.:— ἐν ὕπνῳ in sleep, Eur.;— καθ’ ὕπνον Soph.;— περὶ πρῶτον ὕπνον about one's first sleep, Ar.
Sleep, twin-brother of Death, Il.
scaring in sleep, Anth.
to put to sleep:— Pass. to fall asleep, sleep, Hdt.
sleepy, drowsy, Eur., Plat.
to be sleepy or drowsy, Aesch., Plat.: simply, to sleep, Eur.
somewhat estranged from the Muses, Plat.
anything put under: a framework to support a couch, a rocking apparatus, Xen.

to go or stand under: metaph., τεσσαράκοντα πόδας ὑποβὰς τῆς ἑτέρης [πυραμίδος] τωὐτὸ μέγαθος having gone 40 feet below the like size of the other pyramid, i. e. building it 40 feet lower, Hdt.; μικρὸν ὑποβάς, a little below (in the book), Strab.
to throw, put or lay under, Od.; τί τινι Eur.
to lay under, as a foundation, Aeschin.
to subject, submit, ἐχθροῖς ἐμαυτόν Eur.
Mid. to substitute another's child for one's own, Lat. supponere, Hdt., Plat., etc.
to suggest, whisper, as a prompter does, Il., Plat., etc.: Mid. to make false suggestions, Soph.
in Mid. to appropriate, Plut.
to speak a little like a foreigner, speak rather broken, Plat.
a going down: a crouching down, esp. of a horse that lowers itself to take up the rider, Xen.
under the depths, Anth.
to have a slight cough, Luc.
to bring down: Mid. to crouch down, of a horse that stoops to take up the rider, Lat. subsidere, Xen.

to look up from under the brows at, glance at, to look askance at, eye suspiciously or angrily, Lat. limis oculis suspicere, Plat.; also ὑπ. ἐλεεινά to cast piteous glances, Anth.:—Pass. to be looked at with suspicion, Eur.
adv. throwing in covertly, i. e. by way of caution or reproof, or by way of interruption, Il.
askance, Hhymn.
to be put under, Xen.
put in another's place, counterfeit, suborned, false, Soph.
actively, a throwing or laying under, Plat.
a substitution by stealth, esp. of supposititious children, Id.
a suggesting, ἐξ ὑποβολῆς by admonition, Xen.
the subject-matter of a speech, Luc.
substituted by stealth, supposititious, of children, Hdt., Plat.
to roar or rumble beneath, Aesch.
to wet or moisten a little:—Pass., perf. part. ὑποβεβρεγμένος somewhat drunk, Luc.
under water, Hdt.
neut. pl. ὑπόβρυχα as adv., under water, Od., Hdt.
the paunch, Lat. abdomen: the paunch of the tunny, a favourite dish at Athens, Ar.

entry.note: ὑπό-γειος, ionic and late attic -γαιος, ον,
entry.sense: under the earth, subterraneous, Hdt., etc.
to laugh slily, Lat. subridere, Plat.
to entreat by touching the chin, Aeschin.
Dep.:— to grow up after or in succession, Lat. subnasci, Il., Hdt.
somewhat gray, Xen.
to glance furtively, Mosch.
to sweeten a little: metaph. to coax and smooth down, τινά Ar.
to bend gradually, Hhymn.
an under-secretary, Ar., etc.
to serve as under-secretary, τινί Oratt.
one who writes under another's orders, a secretary, amanuensis, Plut., Luc.
a signed bill of indictment, Plat.
an outline, τενόντων ὑπογραφαί traces of feet, Aesch.: — an outline, sketch, Lat. adumbratio, Plat., etc.
a painting under of the eyelids, Xen.
to write under an inscription, subjoin or add to it, Thuc.; ὑπογράψας ἐπιβουλεῦσαί με having added (to the accusation) that . . , Dem.:— Mid. to bring an additional accusation against him, Eur.
to sign, subscribe:—Mid., ὑπ. τὰς καταβολάς to sign and so make oneself liable, Dem.
to write from dictation, Plut.
to write under, i. e. to trace letters for children to write over, Plat.: metaph., νόμους ὑπ. to trace out laws as guides of action, Id.
to trace in outline, sketch out, Lat. adumbrare, Id., etc.
ὑπογράφειν or -γράφεσθαι τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς to paint under the eyelids, Luc.
under one's hand, nigh at hand, Isocr., Dem.
just out of hand, fresh, new, Lat. recens, Isocr., Dem.; ὑπόγυιόν ἐστι ἐξ οὗ . . , it is a very short time since . . , Isocr.
sudden, Arist.:— ἐξ ὑπογύου off hand, on the spur of the moment, Xen., Plat.
of persons, ὑπ. τῇ ὀργῇ in the first burst of anger, Arist.
to light, kindle under, Il.
to weep a little or secretly, Luc.

to master or weaken beneath one, Il.:— Pass., ὑποδάμνᾰμαι (as if from ὑποδάμνημι) to be overcome, let oneself be overpowered or overcome, Od.; aor1 part. ὑποδμηθεῖσα (v. δαμάζω), of a woman, subdued by a man, yielding to him, Hhymn., Hes.: —Mid., ἔρως φρένας ὑποδάμναται Theocr.
Comic name of a bird in Ar., fear-ling.
somewhat deficient, inferior; mostly in comp. ὑποδεέστερος, Hdt., Plat.; ἐκ πολλῷ ὑποδεεστέρων with resources much inferior, Thuc.:—adv. -εστέρως, Id.
a token, mark, Xen.:— a pattern, Polyb.

entry.note: fut. σω aor1 ὑπέδεισα epic -έδδεισα epic perf. ὑπαιδείδοικα perf. 2 ὑπο-δείδια 3rd pl. plup. ὑπεδείδισαν
entry.sense: trans. to cower under or before, or to fear secretly, c. acc., Hom.:—so of birds, to cower beneath, αἰγυπιὸν ὑποδείσαντες Soph.
absol., Od.; cf. ὑποδεδιώς.
to shew secretly, Hdt.; ὑποδέξας ὄλβον having given a glimpse of happiness, Id.; ὑπ. ἀρετήν to make a shew of virtue, Thuc.
absol. to indicate one's will, Xen.
to shew by tracing out, mark out, Hdt.: absol. to set a pattern, Xen.
generally, to teach indirectly or by indication, Isocr.; c. inf., NTest.
to be traced out, Polyb.
to be somewhat cowardly, Aeschin.
to stand in secret awe of, τινά Hdt.
to lay as a foundation, Hdt.
the reception of a guest, means of entertainment, πᾶσά τοι ἔσθ’ ὑποδεξίη [ῑ, metri grat.], Il.
capacious, Hdt.
a putting on one's shoes, Arist., Luc.
as concrete, = τὰ ὑποδήματα, footgear, boots and shoes, Plat., Xen.

entry.note: ionic -δέκομαι fut. -δέξομαι aor.1 -εδεξάμην and in pass. form -εδέχθην 3rd sg. epic aor2 ὑπέδεκτο 2nd pl. imperat. ὑπόδεχθε inf. ὑποδέχθαι part ὑποδέγμενος
entry.sense: Dep.
to receive beneath the surface, Il.
to receive into one's house, receive hospitably, Hom., etc.; ὁ ὑποδεξάμενος one's host, Isocr.
to give ear to, hearken to, εὐχάς Hes.; τοὺς λόγους Hdt.
to take in charge as a nurse, Hhymn., Plat.
metaph., πῆμα ὑπέδεκτό με sorrow was my host, Od.; στυγερὸς ὑπεδέξατο κοῖτος a hateful nest awaited them, of ensnared birds, Id.
to take upon oneself, undertake a task, promise, Hom.; with inf. fut., Hdt., etc.; less often with inf. aor., Id.; ὑπ. μεγάλα τινί to make him great promises, Id.
to admit, allow a charge, Id.; οὐκ ὑπ. to refuse to admit, deny, Id.
to submit to, bear patiently, Od.
like Lat. excipere,
to wait for, abide the attack of, Hes., Xen.:—of hunters, to lie in wait for game, Xen.
to come next to, border upon, Hdt.
of a woman, to conceive, Xen.
to bind or fasten under, Hdt.

esp. to underbind, i. e. to shoe, because the sandals or shoes were bound on with straps, Plat.:—Mid. to bind under one's feet, put on shoes, Ar., Xen., etc.; also c. acc., ὑποδησάμενος κοθόρνους Hdt.:—so in perf. pass., ὑποδήματα ὑποδεδεμένος with shoes on one's feet, Plat.; and absol., ὑποδεδεμένοι with their shoes on, Xen.; so, ὑποδεδεμένοι τὸν ἀριστερὸν πόδα with shoes on the left foot, Thuc.
to shew privately, Plut.

a sole bound under the foot with straps, a sandal, ποσὶν ὑποδήματα δοῦσα (i. e. δέουσα) Od.; ποσὶν ὑποδήματα δοίην (i. e. δεοίην) Id., etc.; ὑπόδημα κοῖλον, or ὑπόδημα alone, = Lat. calceus, a shoe or half-boot, Ar., etc.
an under-teacher, of a chorus, Plat.
to give way, Arist.
brought to trial or liable to be tried, Lys., etc.: —τινος for a thing, Aesch., Oratt.; ὑπόδικός τινι liable to action from a person, Dem., etc.
clothed in skins, Luc.
an under-servant, Od.
a remission, Aesch.
a reception, entertainment, Hdt., Eur., etc.; εἰς ὑποδοχὴν τοῦ στρατεύματος for the reception of the army (in hostile sense), Thuc.
a harbouring of runaway slaves, Id.
means for entertaining, Plut.
acceptance, support, Aeschin.
a supposition, assumption, Dem.
a receptacle, reservoir, Arist.
adv. only in phrase ὑπόδρα ἰδών looking from under the brows, looking askance, grimly, Il.
an under-servant, attendant, assistant, Od.
a running under or into the way of a thing, Antipho.
running under, πέτρος ὑπ. ἴχνους a stone in the way of his foot, Eur.
somewhat moistened or dewy, Theocr.
to serve, be serviceable to, τινί Od.
a garment under a coat of mail, Plut.

entry.note: -δύνω fut. -δύσομαι aor1 -εδυσάμην epic 3rd sg. -εδύσετο aor.2 act. -έδυν perf. -δέδῡκα
entry.sense: to put on under, κιθῶνας ὑποδύνειν τοῖσι εἵμασι Hdt.
to slip in under, Id.:—also to assume secretly, slip into, c. acc., Id.:—also to slip from under, Xen.
metaph. to undergo danger, Hdt.
Mid. ὑποδύομαι
to go under, get under, sink beneath, Lat. subire, c. acc., Od.; ὑπ. ὑπὸ τὴν ζεύγλην Hdt.:—so, ὑπ. ὑπὸ τῶν κεραμίδων to creep under, Ar.; φέρει τινὰ ὑποδεδυκότα underneath it, Id..
to put one's feet under a shoe, to put it on, Id.
metaph. to put on a character (because the actor's face was put under a mask), Plat., Arist.
c. gen. to come from under, come forth from, Od.
to go under so as to bear, to bear on one's shoulders, Il.
to enter into war, Hdt.
metaph. to undergo danger, c. acc., Xen.; ὑπ. αἰτίαν to make oneself subject to . . , Dem.
c. inf. to undertake to do, Hdt.
of feelings, to steal over one, c. acc., Aesch.:—c. dat., πᾶσιν ὑπέδυ γόος sorrow stole upon all, Od.
absol. to slip or slink away, Dem.
absol., ὀφθαλμοὶ ὑποδεδυκότες sunken eyes, Luc.
an under-priest or priestess, Hdt.

entry.note: and -ύω fut. -ζεύξω Pass., aor2 ὑπεζύγην perf. -έζευγμαι
entry.sense: to yoke under, put under the yoke, ὑπ. ἵππους ἡμιόνους Od.:—Pass. to be yoked under, submit to, ἀνάγκαις Aesch.; πόνῳ Soph.
a beast for the yoke, a beast of burden, Lat. jumentum, Theogn., Hdt., etc.
the diaphragm, midriff, Arist.
in pl. braces passed under the hull of a vessel, so as to undergird her (cf. ὑποζώννυμι II), Plat.
to undergird, Plut.:—Pass., ζειρὰς ὑπεζωσμένοι girt with ζειραί, Hdt.
to undergird or frap a ship (v. ὑπόζωμα II), Polyb., NTest.

entry.etym: less attic form for ὑπόζωμα (II ), Plut.

entry.sense: to heat inwardly, Aesch.:—Pass. to glow under a thing, c. dat., Anth.
to heat a little:—Pass. to grow somewhat hot, be heated, Il.
somewhat hot or passionate, Hdt.
that which is placed under, a foundation, hypothesis, supposition, Lat. assumptio, Plat.
the subject under discussion, the question, Xen., Dem., etc.
that which is laid down as a rule of action, a principle, Dem.: generally, a purpose, plan, design, Plat.
a cause, pretext, Plut.
one must assume, Arist.
to run in under, make a secret attack, Pind.
to run in before, to supplant, Ar.
of dogs, to run in too hastily, Xen.
a suggestion, counsel, warning, piece of advice, Hdt., Arist.
a pledge, a mortgage, Dem.
a suggestion, hint, warning, ὑποθημοσύνῃσιν Ἀθήνης (epic dat. pl.) Hom.; Ἑρμοῦ ὑποθημοσύνῃ Xen.
to press under or gently, Luc.
to begin to make a clamour, Thuc.
Pass., to be delicate or remiss, Plut.
an unknown bird, Ar.
to flatter a little, win by flattery, Ar.:—absol. to use flattery, Hdt.
Mid. to arm oneself in secret, Il.
to sound forth in answer, Anth.
to dwell under: to lie hidden, Anth.
to build under a place, c. gen., Luc.
to keep the house, stay at home: — metaph. to lurk, lie hidden, Luc.
trans. to engage in or plot underhand, Plut.
c. acc. pers. to work secretly upon, Id.; νόσος ὑπ. αὐτούς crept in among them, Id.
to wail softly, to whimper, Luc.
Dep.
to be seated in a place, station oneself, Hdt.
to sit or lie in ambush, Xen.
c. acc. pers. to lie in wait for, Hdt.
to place in ambush:—Mid. to lie in ambush, Xen.
to burn by applying fire below, Hdt.: to offer secret sacrifices, Aesch.
to light under, Luc.
to bend short back, turn in under, Il.
intr. to turn short back, double as a hare, Xen.:—metaph., c. acc., to fall short of, καιρόν Aesch.
a garland worn on the neck, Sapph..
in the heart, Theocr.
to descend by degrees or stealthily, Hdt., Thuc.: to come down a little, Xen.
Pass. to lie down under, to submit, yield, τινι to one, Plat.:—absol. to give in, Dem.
below, under, c. gen., Plat.
to lie under or beneath, Il., Thuc.; c. dat., Plat.
in various metaph. senses,
to be put under the eyes or mind, i. e. to be submitted or proposed to one, Pind.; αἱ ὑποκείμεναι ἐλπίδες one's present hopes, Dem.; ὑπόκειταί μοι ὅτι . . I have laid down the rule, that . . , Hdt.

to be laid down or assumed as an hypothesis, Plat., etc.; τούτων ὑποκειμένων = Lat. his positis, Id.; impers., ὑπόκειται a rule is laid down, Dem.; ὑποκείσθω ὅτι . . let it be granted that . . , Arist.
to be suggested, Hdt.
to be left at bottom, left remaining, Thuc., Dem.
to be subject to, submit to, τινι Plat.: absol. to be submissive, Id.
to be left behind in pledge, to be pledged or mortgaged, τινος for a certain sum, Dem., etc.; ὑποκείμενοι, of persons, bound for payment of a sum of money, Id.
to underlie, as a substratum, Plat., etc.
to be subordinate, Id.
Mid. to make known by voice of herald or crier, to have a thing proclaimed or cried, esp. for sale, Aeschin.; σεαυτὸν ὑπ. to advertise yourself, Plat.
to move lightly, Ζεφύρου ὑποκινήσαντος (sc. τὸ κῠμα) Il.
metaph. to urge gently on, Plat.
intr. to move a little, stir a finger, Hdt., Ar.
metaph. to be deranged, Plat.
to shed secret tears, Aesch.
to steal underhand, filch, Babr.: —Pass. to be stolen away, Pind.
ὑποκλέπτεσθαί τι to be defrauded of a thing, Soph.
Pass. to recline or lie down under, c. dat., σχοίνῳ ὑπεκλίνθη Od.
Pass. to be driven in confusion before one, τινι Il.
Pass. to lurk in secret places, Od.
to wash from below, Anth.
to tickle or excite a little, Pind.:— Pass. to be somewhat excited, Xen.
under the folds of the robe, Anth.
somewhat tired, Xen.
to cut beneath, to hamstring, Plut.
Dep.
to talk child's language,
trans. to call by endearing names, Ar.
to call by a fair name, gloss over or palliate, Plat., Dem.
reversely, to call something good by a bad name, to nickname, Xen.
intr. to use diminutives, Arist.
a coaxing or endearing name, Aeschin.
= ὑποκόρισμα, Plut.
the use of diminutives, Arist.
to soothe with soft names, Pind.
somewhat light or fickle, Plut.
the stand of a κρατήρ, Hdt.
of stringed instruments, to answer in sound, i. e. to sound in harmony with, τινί Pind.

entry.etym: later also aor1 and perf. pass. in mid. sense
entry.sense: to reply, make answer, answer, Hom., Hdt.
to expound, interpret, explain, Od., Ar.:—the attic word in this sense is ἀπο-κρίνομαι.

of actors, to answer on the stage: hence to play a part, τὴν Ἀντιγόνην ὑποκέκριται Dem.; ὑπ. τὸ βασιλικόν to take the king's part, Arist.; ὑποκρ. τραγῳδίαν, κωμῳδίαν to play a tragedy, a comedy, Id.; absol. to play a part, be an actor, Id.
to represent dramatically: hence to exaggerate, Dem.
metaph. to play a part, to feign, pretend, c. inf., Id.

entry.etym: rarer form for ὑπόκρισις II, Anth.

entry.sense: in ionic a reply, answer, Hdt.
in attic the playing a part on the stage, the actor's art, Arist.
an orator's delivery, declamation, Id.
metaph. the playing a part, hypocrisy, Phocyl.
an interpreter or expounder, Plat., Luc.
one who plays a part on the stage, a player, actor, Ar., Plat., etc.
metaph. a pretender, dissembler, hypocrite, NTest.
belonging to ὑπόκρισις (II), having a good delivery, Arist.
suited for speaking or delivery, ὑποκριτικωτάτη λέξις Id.: ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη), the art of delivery, Id.
metaph. pretending to a thing, c. gen., Luc.
to strike gently, Anth.: to beat time, give the time, Plut.
metaph. to break in upon, interrupt, c. acc., Ar.
in Mid. to find fault with, attack, Id.
to hide under or beneath, ἄχνῃ ὑπεκρύφθη [the ship] was hidden beneath the spray, Il.
to croak faintly, as a sick person, Luc.
running on wheels, Od.
Mid. to conceive, become pregnant, ὑποκῡσᾰμένη (not -κυσσαμένη), Hom., Hes.
to stoop under a yoke, οἱ Μῆδοι ὑπέκυψαν Πέρσῃσι bowed to the Persian yoke, Hdt.: absol., of suppliants, to bow down, Ar., Xen.
c. acc., ὑπ. τὰν τύλαν to stoop the shoulder so as to let a load be put on, Ar.
somewhat humped, Strab.
the thigh of an animal, Xen.
to ridicule a little, Luc.
somewhat deaf, Ar., Plat.
to take up by getting under, as the dolphin did Arion, Hdt.: to receive into its bosom, NTest.
to bear up, support, Hdt.
to take by the hand, Plat.

to seize or come suddenly upon, of fear, Hom.; of a fit of madness, a pestilence, Hdt.; δυσχωρία ὑπελάμβανεν αὐτούς, i. e. they came suddenly into difficult ground, Xen.; then, of events, to follow next, come next, Hdt.
to take up the discourse and answer, to reply, rejoin, retort, Thuc., Plat., etc.:— absol., in dialogue, ἔφη ὑπολαβών, ὑπ. ἔφη, ὑπ. εἶπεν he said in answer, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
to take up, interrupt, Xen.
to take up the conqueror, fight with him, Lat. excipere, Thuc.
to take up a charge, Id.
= ὑποδέχομαι, to receive and protect, Xen.
to accept or entertain a proposal, Hdt., Dem.

to take up a notion, assume, suppose, c. inf., Hdt., Plat.:—the inf. omitted, to conceive of a thing as being so and so, Plat.; καίπερ ὑπειληφὼς ταῦτα though I assume this to be so, Dem.: —Pass., τοιοῦτος ὑπολαμβάνομαι Isocr.
to apprehend a thing, Eur., Plat.
to suspect, disbelieve, Xen.
to take secretly, Thuc.
to draw off from duty, seduce, Id.
ὑπ. ἵππον, as a term of horsemanship, to hold up or to check the horse, Xen.
shining with inferior lustre, Hes.
to shine under, shine in under, Xen.:—so in Mid., Anth.
to shine a little, begin to shine, just appear, τὸ ἔαρ ὑπέλαμπε Hdt.; ὑπ. ἡ ἡμέρα Plut.
to pour secret libations, Aesch.
to leave remaining, Od., Thuc., etc.
of things, to fail one, ὑπολείψει ὑμᾶς ἡ μισθοφορά Lys.
Pass., c. fut. mid., to be left remaining, Hom., Hdt.
of things, to remain in force, Thuc.
to stay behind, Od.: c. gen., ὑπολείπεσθαι τοῦ στόλου to stay behind the expedition, i. e. not to go upon it, Hdt.
to be left behind in a race, Ar.: of stragglers in an army, to lag behind, Xen.; ὑπ. μικρὸν τοῦ στόματος to fall behind the front rank, Id.
metaph. to be inferior to, τινός Arist.
absol. to fail, come to an end, Soph.:— ὑπ. τινά ὁ λόγος fails him, Arist.
Mid. to leave behind one, Hdt.; ὑπολείπεσθαι αἰτίαν to leave cause for reproach against oneself, Thuc.
somewhat fine, Luc.
Pass. to become white underneath or somewhat white, Il.
the vessel under a press to receive the wine or oil, a vat, Lat. lacus, NTest.
one must suppose, understand, think of, Plat.
a taking up, esp. a taking up the word, taking up the matter where another leaves off, Plat.:— a rejoinder, reply, Isocr.
a taking in a certain sense, an assumption, conception, Dem.
a hasty judgment, suspicion, Luc.
somewhat less or fewer, Il.
somewhat stony, Luc.
to leave behind, NTest.
to slip or slide gradually, Luc.
somewhat smooth, worn smooth, Ar.
somewhat lickerish or dainty, Luc.
to take account of, τινός Arist.
Dep.:— to take into account, take account of, Plat., Dem.
one must take into account, Plat.
held accountable or liable, Dem.; ὑπόλογον ποιεῖσθαι to hold responsible, Plat.; οὐδέν σοι ὑπόλογον τίθεμαι I put down nothing to your account, Id.
a taking into account, a reckoning, account, ὑπόλογον ποιεῖσθαί τινος, Lat. rationem habere rei, Dem.; ἐν ὑπολόγῳ ποιεῖσθαί τι Lys.
left behind, staying behind, Hdt.; οἱ ὑπ. those who remained alive, Id.
of things, ὑπ. τὸ βάραθρον γίγνεται the pit still remains, Ar.; ὅσα ἦν ὑπ. all that remained to be done, Thuc.
an under-λοχαγός, a lieutenant, Xen.
under the lyre; δόναξ ὑπ. a reed to which the lower ends of the strings were attached, Ar.

entry.note: fut. σω aor1 ὑπ-έλῡσα perf. ὑπο-λέλῠκα Pass., perf. -λέλῠμαι 3rd pl. epic aor2 ὑπ-έλυντο
entry.sense: to loosen beneath or below, ὑπέλυσε γυῖα made his limbs give way under him, Il.:—Pass., γυῖα ὑπέλυντο Id.
to loose from under the yoke, Hom., Thuc.:— to loose from bonds, Od.; in Mid., τὸν ὑπελύσαο δεσμῶν thou didst free him from bonds by stealth, Il.
to untie a person's sandals from under his feet, take off his shoes, Aesch., Ar.:—Mid. to take off one's sandals or shoes, or to have them taken off, Ar.
c. acc. pers. to unshoe him, take off his shoes, Plat.
the parts under the breast, Bion.
somewhat long, longish, Ar.
Pass. to grow cowardly by degrees, Xen.
somewhat mad, in comp. ὑπομαργότερος, Hdt.
to smear or rub underneath, Theocr.
mixed with rain, θέρος ὑπ. a rainy summer, Plut.
to smile a little or gently, Anacreont.
somewhat less:— ὑπομείονες, subordinate citizens, opp. to ὅμοιοι, Xen.
Dep. to blame a little or secretly, Plut.
somewhat discontented with his lot, Cic.
one must sustain, abide, endure, Thuc., etc.
patient of, τῶν δεινῶν Arist.
to stay behind, survive, Od., Hdt., attic
trans.,
c. acc. pers. to await another, to await his attack, bide the onset, Il., Hdt.; ὑπ. τὰς Σειρῆνας to abide their presence, Xen.
c. acc. rei, to be patient under, abide patiently, submit to, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; ὑπ. τὴν κρίσιν to await one's trial, Aeschin.: to wait for, τὴν ἑορτήν Thuc.
absol. to stand one's ground, stand firm, Il., Hdt., etc.; ὑπομένων καρτερεῖν to endure patiently, Plat.
c. inf. to submit or dare to do a thing, wait to do, persist in doing, like Lat. sustinere, Od., Xen.

so with part. relating to the subject, εἰ ὑπομενέουσι χεῖρας ἀνταειρόμενοι if they shall dare to lift their hands, Hdt.; ὑπομένει ὠφελούμενος he submits to be helped, Plat.:—with part. relating to the object, ὑπ. Ξέρξεα ἐπιόντα to await his attack, Hdt., etc.
to add by mixing, Lat. admisceo, τί τινι Plat.
intr. to run close under a place, c. dat., Thuc.
Act.,
to remind one of a person or thing, τινά τινος Od., Thuc.; ὑπ. τινά τι Thuc., Xen.: ὑπ. τινά to put him in mind, Plat.
c. acc. rei, to bring back to one's mind, mention, suggest, τι Hdt., Soph., etc.; τινί τι Aesch.
c. gen. rei, to remind one of, to make mention of, Thuc., etc.
Pass. or Mid. to call to mind, remember, Xen.
to make mention, περί τινος Aesch.
serving for pay, hired, Luc.
Dep. to court clandestinely, ὑπεμνάασθε (epic 2nd pl. imperf.) γυναῖκα Od.
a remembrance, memorial, Thuc., etc.
a note, memorandum, Dem.:—in pl. memoranda, notes, minutes, Lat. commentarii, Plat.
a reminding, Thuc., etc.
a mentioning, ὑπ. ποιεῖσθαί τινος to make mention of a thing, Id.; ὑπ. κακῶν a tale of woe, Eur.
Mid. to betroth, Arist.:—Pass., ὑπομνηστευθείς one betrothed, Id.
Mid.
to make oath that a person cannot appear in court: to apply for a postponement of the trial, Dem.:—Pass., ὑπομοσθέντος τούτου this affidavit being put in by way of excuse, Id.
to bar proceedings by an affidavit in a γραφὴ παρανόμων, Xen.
a remaining behind, Arist.
a holding out, patient endurance, Id.:— the enduring to do, αἰσχρῶν ἔργων Theophr.
rather stupid or silly, Luc.
to dwell under a place, c. acc., Anth.
Mid. to eat away beneath or secretly, Anth.
under the clouds, Luc.
under the promontory Neium, lying at its base, Od.
Dep. to swim under water, dive, Plut.
to snow a little: impers., ὑπένιφε it was snowing a little, Thuc.:—Pass., νὺξ ὑπονιφομένη a snowy night, Id.
to think secretly, suspect, Hdt., Eur., etc.:—c. acc. pers. et inf. to suspect that . . , Hdt.; τῶν λεγόντων ὑπενοεῖτε you feel suspicious of the speakers, Thuc.
generally, to suspect, conjecture, form guesses about, Ar.: absol., ὑπονοοῦντες by conjecture, Plat.
a hidden thought: hence,
a suspicion, conjecture, guess, supposition, Ar., etc.; ὑπόνοιαι τῶν μελλόντων notions formed of future events, Thuc.
the real meaning of a thing, the true intent, deeper sense, Xen., Plat., etc.
by means of pipes, Thuc.
underground, Strab.
ὑπόνομος, ὁ, as Subst. an underground passage, mine, Thuc.
a water-pipe, Xen.
to be rather sickly, Luc.
to go back, retire, Hdt.:— to go down, sink, settle, Id.
subsidence, of the sea, Plut.
to prick or sting underneath: generally, to sting, Theocr.
to fall asleep gradually, Plat.
wooden underneath, i. e. of wood covered with a coat of metal, Xen.
to shave or cut off some of the hair: —Pass., perf. part. ὑπεξυρημένος shorn or shaven, Luc.
under the rasor, Anth.
to scrape slightly, Anth.
to go down voluntarily in wrestling, Luc.
to strew under, Hdt.
to be hungry, to begin to be hungry, Ar.
sent covertly, as a spy, Xen.
to send under: Pass. to be sent beneath, σκότον Eur.
to send secretly: to send as a spy, send in a false character, Thuc., Xen.
to break wind a little, Ar.
to begin to turn colour, of grapes, Od.
to spread out under, Od.
somewhat rocky, Hdt.
to play the ape a little, Ar.
to fill by degrees:—Pass., πώγωνος ἤδη ὑποπιμπλάμενος now beginning to have a thick beard, Plat.; ὑποπίμπλαμαι τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς δακρύων have my eyes filling with tears, Luc.
in Pass. of women, τέκνων ὑποπλησθῆναι to become mothers of many children, Hdt.
to set on fire below, τὴν ὕλην Hdt.
to burn as on a funeral-pyre, τινάς Id.
to drink a little, drink moderately, Plat.
to drink slowly, go on drinking, Ar., Xen.
ὑπο-πεπωκώς rather tipsy, Ar., Xen.
to fall under or down, to sink in, Plut.
to fall down before any one, c. acc., Plat.: —hence, to be subject to him, fall under his power, Isocr.; of a flatterer, to cringe to, τινί Dem.; c. acc. ὑποπεσὼν τὸν δεσπότην Ar.
to fall behind another, Dem.
to get in under or among, Thuc.
of accidents, to happen, fall out, Isocr.
of persons, to fall under a punishment, c. dat., Plut.
of places, to lie under or below, c. dat., Polyb.
under mount Placus, in the Troad, Il.
pretty full, c.gen., δείματός εἰμι ὑπ. am somewhat afraid, Hdt.
to sail under, ὑπ. τὴν Κύπρον, i. e. under the lee of Cyprus, NTest.
to blow gently, NTest.

sense.gloss: from under, by, c. gen. under, c. dat., towards c. acc.

entry.sense: Lat. sub, prep. with gen., dat. and acc.
WITH GEN.,

of Place, from under, ῥέει κρήνη ὑπὸ σπείους Od.: of rescuing from under another's power, after the Verbs ἐρύεσθαι, ἁρπάζειν, Il.; ἵππους λῦσαν ὑπὸ ζυγοῦ they loosed the horses from under the yoke, Hom.
under, beneath, μοχλὸν ὑπὸ σποδοῦ ἤλασα thrust the bar in under the embers, Od.; ὑπὸ στέρνοιο τυχήσας having hit him under the breast, Il.; ὑπὸ χθονός Hom., etc.

of the Agent, with pass. Verbs, by, Lat. a or ab, ὑπό τινος δαμῆναι Il.; ὑφ’ ἑαυτοῦ by one's own action, i.e. of oneself, Thuc.; so also, with neut. verbs, φεύγειν ὑπό τινος, i. e. to flee before him, Il.; ἔπαινον ἔχειν ὑπό τινος Hdt.
of things as well as persons, ὡς διάκειμαι ὑπὸ τῆς νόσου Thuc.; ἐνδακρύειν χαρᾶς ὕπο Aesch.; μαίνεται ὑφ’ ἡδονῆς Soph.; ὀρύσσειν ὑπὸ μαστίγων to dig under fear of scourges, Hdt.

of accompanying music, to the sound of, κωμάζειν ὑπ’ αὐλοῦ Hes.; πίνειν ὑπὸ σάλπιγγος Ar.: then, of anything attendant, δαΐδων ὑπὸ λαμπομενάων ἠγίνεον by torchlight, Il.; ὑπ’ εὐφήμου βοῆς θῦσαι to offer a sacrifice accompanied by it, Soph.; ὑπὸ πομπῆς in or with solemn procession, Hdt.
WITH DAT. of Place or Position, ὑπὸ ποσσί Il.; ὑπὸ πλατανίστῳ Id.; ὑπ’ Ἰλίῳ under its walls, Eur.; ὑφ’ ἅρμασι under, i. e. yoked to, the chariot, Il.
ὑπὸ χερσί τινος δαμῆναι to be subdued under, i. e. by force of his arms, Id.; ὑπὸ δουρὶ δαμῆναι Id.
of the person under whose power or influence a thing is done, φέβεσθαι ὑπό τινι to flee before him, Id.; ὑπὸ πομπῇ τινος βῆναι to go under his convoy, Id.
expressing subjection, ὑπό τινι under one's power, Od.; εἶναι ὑπό τινι to be subject to him, Thuc.; ἔχειν ὑφ’ ἑαυτῷ to have under one, Xen.
of things coming under a class, ἐργασίαι ὑπὸ ταῖς τέχναις Plat.
as in A. II. 3, ὑπ’ αὐλητῆρι πρόσθ’ ἔκιον advanced to the music of the flute-player, Hes.: generally, of attendant circumstances, ἐξ ἁλὸς εἶσι πνοιῇ ὕπο Ζεφύροιο Od.; ὑπὸ σκότῳ, νυκτί Aesch.
WITH ACCUS. of Place, towards and under, ὑπὸ σπέος ἤλασε μῆλα drove them under, i.e. into, the cave, Il.; ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἤγαγεν Od.; ὑπὸ δικαστήριον ἄγειν to bring under or before the tribunal, Hdt.
like ὑπό c. dat. without sense of motion, ὑπ’ ἠῶ τ’ ἠέλιόν τε everywhere under the sun, Il.; ὑπὸ τὴν ἄρκτον Hdt.; τὸ ὑπὸ τὴν ἀκρόπολιν Thuc.
of subjection, ποιεῖσθαι ὑπὸ σφᾶς Id., etc.

of Time, like Lat. sub, just after, just about, ὑπὸ νύκτα towards night, Il.; ὑπὸ ταῦτα about that time, Hdt.; ὑπὸ τὸν νηὸν κατακαέντα about the time of its burning, Il.; ὑπὸ τὸν σεισμόν about the time of the earthquake, Thuc.
of accompaniment, ὑπὸ αὐλὸν διαλέγεσθαι Xen.
ὑπό τι, as adv. to a certain degree, in some measure, Lat. aliquatenus, Plat.
POSITION: ὑπό can always follow its Subst., becoming by anastrophe ὕπο.
AS ADV., under, below, beneath, Hom.
behind, Hdt.
secretly, unnoticed, Il.
IN COMPOSITION:
under, both of rest and motion, as ὕπ-ειμι, ὑπο-βαίνω.
of the casing or covering of one thing with another, as ὑπό-χρυσος.
to express subjection, ὑπο-δαμνάω, ὑφ-ηνίοχος.
somewhat, a little, ὑπο-κινέω, ὑπό-λευκος: underhand, secretly, ὑπο-θωπεύω.
a footstool, Luc.
to put under:—Mid. to subject to oneself, Luc.
to produce gradually, Plut.
in Mid. to gain by underhand tricks, to win over, τινά Dem.
in Mid. to assume, affect, Plut.
somewhat gray, Luc.
Dep. to go beneath the ground, Plut.
with a calf under her, of a cow:— metaph. of a woman, Hes.
Dep. to buy under the price, Theophr.
to gnash the teeth secretly, Luc.
winged, Hdt., Soph., etc.; of a ship, Pind.
metaph. swift-flying, soaring, Id.; ὑπ. φροντίς flighty, giddy thought, Aesch.
to be suspicious, Xen.; also, ὑπ. εἴς τινα to have suspicions of him, Thuc.
to suspect, guess, suppose, Xen.
trans. to suspect, hold in suspicion, Soph., Thuc.; ὑπ. τινὰ εἴς τι of something, Hdt., etc.:—Pass. to be suspected, mistrusted, Thuc.; impers., ὡς ὑπωπτεύετο as was generally suspected, Xen.
c. acc. pers. et inf. to suspect that, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
c. acc. rei, to look suspiciously on, Thuc.:—but also, ὑπ. τι to suspect something, Eur., Xen.
suspicious, jealous, Soph., Thuc.: of a horse, shy, Xen.
to crouch or cower beneath, like hares or birds, πετάλοις ὑποπεπτηῶτες (epic part. perf. for ὑποπεπτηκότες), Il.; ὑποπτήξας τάφῳ Eur.
metaph. to crouch before another, bow down to, τινί Xen.; also, ὑπ. τινά Aesch., Xen.:—absol. to be modest or shy, Xen.
looked at from beneath the brows, i. e. viewed with suspicion or jealousy, Lat. suspectus, Aesch., Thuc.; c. inf., ὑπ. αὐτοῖς μὴ πέμψαι suspected by them of not having sent, Thuc.
of things, τάδ’ ἦν ὕποπτα Eur.; ὕποπτον καθεστήκει it was a matter of jealousy, Thuc.
adv., ὑπόπτως διακεῖσθαι or ἔχειν to lie under suspicion, Id., Xen.
act. suspecting, suspicious of a thing, c. gen., Eur.:— τὸ ὕποπτον suspicion, jealousy, Thuc.; τῷ ὑπ. μου from suspicion of me, Id.:—adv. with suspicion, Id.; ὑπ. ἔχειν πρός τινα Dem.
a joint, τοῦ θώρακος Plut.
under the bottom, Anth.
with a foal under her, Strab.
to fan from below or gently, Anth.
to rouse secretly or gradually, Hom.; τοῖον γὰρ ὑπώρορε Μοῦσα such was the Muse's power to move, Od.:—Pass. to rise secretly or gradually, Id.
ὑπ. βοά the soft note of the pipe, Eur.
to stitch underneath: metaph., ὑπ. λόγον to make up a story, Eur.
to flow under or beneath, Plut.
to flow gradually away, Id.: metaph. to stream gradually to a place, Luc.
metaph. also, to slip or glide into unperceived, Lat. subrepere, Plat., Dem.
to slip away, of time, Ar.; of flowers, to perish, Theocr.; of the hair, to fall off, Luc.; and of friends, Id.
to make to burst downwards: — Pass., οὐρανόθεν ὑπερράγη (aor2) αἰθήρ ether was cleft from beneath the sky, Il.
with a lamb under it, Il.
to fan from below or gently, Anth.
to throw under, ὑπ. τινὰ τοῖς θηρίοις to throw him to the wild beasts, Plut.
to dig under, undermine, Hdt.
Dep. to dance with or to music, Aesch.:—c. acc. cogn., ὄρχησιν ὑπ. Plut.
to sing and dance a character, of a pantomimic actor, Luc.
a hyporcheme or choral hymn to Apollo, mostly in Cretic verses, Plat.
somewhat rotten, Luc.
to prelude on the trumpet, Anth.
dragged alongside, Eur.
to shake below: ὑποσσείουσιν ἱμάντι they set it in motion below by the thong by which an auger is turned, Od.
to give secret signs of, to indicate or intimate, Thuc.
in military sense, σάλπιγγι ὑπ. to make signal by sound of trumpet, Id.
to be silent during, Aeschin.
having a mixture or proportion of iron in it, Plat.
to pass over in silence, Aeschin.
to halt a little, Luc.
to stir underneath, poke up, τὸ πῦρ Ar.
to dig under, ὑπ. μακρὰ ἅλματα to mark a long leap by a line, Pind.
to trip up one's heels, upset, Lat. supplantare, Dem., Luc.
metaph., ὑπ. καὶ ἀνατρέπων Plat., Dem.
under shade, Plut.
guilty of a slight solecism, Cic.
to be scant or stinted of a thing, c. gen., Aesch.
of things, to be lacking, left undone, Soph.
to draw away from under, Plat., Dem.
to withdraw secretly, ὑπέσπασε φυγῇ πόδα withdrew his foot secretly, stole away, Eur.
to sow secretly, Anth.

under a treaty, bound or secured by treaty, Hdt., Xen.:—esp. of taking up the dead from a field of battle, τοὺς νεκροὺς ὑποσπόνδους ἀποδιδόναι to allow a truce for taking up the dead, Thuc.; τοὺς νεκροὺς ὑπ. κομίζεσθαι, ἀναιρεῖσθαι to demand a truce for so doing, in acknowledgment of defeat, Hdt., Xen., etc.
sediment, Plat.; ἐν τῇ Ῥωμύλου ὑποστάθμῃ, in faece Romuli, Plut.
that which settles at the bottom, sediment, Arist.
anything set under, subject-matter of a speech or poem, Polyb., etc.
the foundation or ground of hope, confidence, assurance, NTest.
substance, the real nature of a thing, essence, Id.
that which stands under, a support, prop, Plut.
to be borne or endured, Eur.
Pass. to grow up or wax gradually like ears of corn, Od.
to support from underneath, Aesch.
under the roof, in or into the house, Soph.
to hide under, Xen.
to draw in, ἱστίον ὑπέστειλε made him furl his sail, Pind.
to draw back for shelter, Plut.; ὑπ. ἑαυτόν to shelter oneself behind, τινί Id.; also to withdraw himself, NTest.
Mid., ὑποστέλλεσθαί τι to cloak a thing through fear, to prevaricate, dissemble, Eur., Plat., etc.; μηδὲν ὑποστειλάμενος without dissimulation, Dem.
to moan in an undertone, Soph.
to groan under the weight of, τι Aesch.
to groan beneath one, c. dat., Il., Hes.
to moan in a low tone, begin to moan, Soph.: to grumble, Ar.
to underprop, sustain, Luc.
a shrinking back, evasion, NTest.

entry.note: -στόρνυμι -στρώννυμι -ύω fut. -στορέσω aor1 -εστόρεσα also -στρώσω aor1 -έστρωσα perf. ὑπέστρωκα pass. ὑπέστρωμαι
entry.sense: to spread, lay or strew under, esp. of bed-clothes, δέμνια ὑποστορέσαι Od.; λέκτρα ὑποστρῶσαί τινι to make his bed for a man, i. e. serve him as a wife, Eur.:—Pass., αἱ εὐναὶ ὑποστόρνυνται Xen.; ᾗ χαλκὸς ὑπέστρωται which has copper laid under it, ap. Hdt.
to serve as lieutenant under another, c. dat., Xen.
a lieutenant-general, Xen.
to turn round about, turn back, ἵππους Il.; Βακχίαν ὑποστρέφων ἅμιλλαν bringing back the Bacchic struggle, i. e. changing sorrow into tumultuous joy, Soph.
intr. to turn about, turn short round, Il., Hdt., attic:—so in Pass., αὖτις ὑποστρεφθείς Il., etc.
generally, to return, Od., Hdt.; so in fut. mid., Od.
to turn away, and so elude an attack, Eur., Xen.
part. ὑποστρέψας as adv. reversely, Ar.
to agitate inwardly, Aesch.
a turning about, wheeling round, Hdt.: ἐξ ὑποστροφῆς, of the chariot, after turning round the meta at the end of the δίαυλος, i. e. turning sharply round, Soph.:— on the contrary, ap. Dem.
that which is spread under, a bed, litter, Xen.
to be somewhat astringent, Plut.
to confuse a little:—Pass. to be somewhat confused, Luc.
to whistle gently, rustle, Aesch.
to drag down, Plut., Luc.
to bind tight below, Anth.

an undertaking, engagement, promise, Hom., Hdt., attic; ὑπ. ἀπολαβεῖν to receive the fulfilment of a promise, Xen.; ἀπαιτεῖν τὰς ὑπ. to demand their fulfilment, Arist.; ὑπ. ψεύδεσθαι to fail in its performance, Aeschin.
a profession (as a mode of life), Luc.
subordination, subjection, submission, NTest.
to stir up, trouble from below or a little, Ar.:—Pass. to be somewhat troubled, Luc.
to shrink before, τινά Il.
under Tartarus, of the Titans, Il., Hes.
extension, πεδίων ὑποτάσεις the plains that stretch below, Eur.
to place or arrange under, τί τινι Plut.
to post under, to subject, ἑαυτόν τινι Id.; ἑαυτῷ τὰ πάντα NTest.:—Pass. to be obedient, τινι Id.
to stretch under, put under, ἀντηρίδας ὑπ. πρὸς τοὺς τοίχους to fix stay-beams so as to strengthen the ship's sides, Thuc.
to strain tight, Ar.: metaph. to intensify, Soph.
to hold out hopes, to offer to do a thing, c. inf., Hdt., Thuc.:—also, ὑπ. τινὶ μισθούς Ar.; ἐλπίδας Dem.
to suggest, ὑπ. τινὶ λέγειν Eur.
to build a wall under or across, build a cross-wall, Thuc.
the building of a cross-wall, Thuc.
a cross-wall, Thuc.
to pay off, discharge a payment, Hdt., Xen., etc.; absol. to pay tribute, Thuc.
subject to pay taxes, taxable, tributary, Lat. vectigalis, Thuc.; in full, ὑποτελὴς φόρου Id.
act. receiving as payment, c. gen., Luc.

entry.note: ionic -τάμνω fut. -τεμῶ fut. -τεμοῦμαι aor2 ὑπ-έτᾰμον epic inf. -ταμέειν perf. -τέτμηκα Pass., aor1 -ετμήθην perf. -τέτμημαι
entry.sense: to cut away under, cut away, Hom.: Pass., Aeschin.
to cut underhand or unfairly, of a leather-seller, Ar.
to cut off, intercept, Xen.: so in Hdt.; ὑποτέμνεσθαι τὰς ὁδούς to cut off one's way, stop one short, Ar.; ὑποτέμνεσθαί τινα to intercept him, Xen.
to place under, τί τινι Il.:—Mid. to place under one's feet, Xen.

to place under as a foundation or beginning, Id., Dem.:—Pass. to be laid down, assumed, Plat.:—Mid. to lay down as a principle, take for granted, assume, Id., Dem.; c. acc. et inf. to assume or suppose that . . , Plat.

to hold out under, present, Luc.: metaph. to suggest, Eur., etc.:—so in Mid. to suggest, hint a thing to one, ὑποθέσθαι τινὶ βουλήν Il.; ἔπος, ἔργον ὑποθέσθαι τινί to suggest a speech, an action, to any one, advise or counsel him thereto, Hom., Hdt., etc.
c. dat. pers. only, ὑποθέσθαι τινί to advise, admonish one, Od., Ar., etc.: c. inf. to advise one to do a thing, Hdt., Thuc.
to propose, σκοπόν as a mark or aim, Arist.:—Mid. to propose to oneself, Isocr.
to put down as a deposit or stake, to pawn, pledge, mortgage, Hdt., Aeschin., etc.:—in Mid., of the mortgagee, to lend money on pledge, Dem.
